body.text: // divyāvadānam//
body.translated_text: // <s>Divyāvadāna</s> (Divine Legends) //

body.text: namaḥ śrīsarvabudhhabodhisattvebhyaḥ/
body.translated_text: Homage to the glorious <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all!

body.text: 001.000. div1 koṭikarṇāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 001.000. The <s>Koṭikarṇāvadāna</s> (Legend of <s>Koṭikarṇa</s>).

body.text:
001.001. buddho bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
001.001. asmāt parāntake vāsavagrāme balaseno nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
001.003. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
001.003. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
001.004. so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīnāyācate ārāmedavatāṃ vanadevatāṃ śṛṅgāṭakadevatāṃ balipratigrāhikāṃ devatām/
001.005. sahajāṃ sahadharmikāṃ nityānubaddhāmapi devatāmāyācate/
001.006. asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante/
001.007. duhitaraśceti/
001.007. tacca naivam/
001.007. yadyevamabhaviṣyat, ekaikasya putrasahasramabhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaścakravartinaḥ/
001.008. api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrāa jāyante duhitaraśca/
001.009. katameṣāṃ trayāṇām? mātāpitarau raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharavḥ pratyupasthito bhavati/
001.010. eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraśca/
001.011. sa caivamāyācanaparastiṣṭhati//
body.translated_text: 001.001. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. 001.001. In the distant <s>Parāntaka</s> [region], in the village of <s>Vāsava</s>, there lived a householder named <s>Balasena</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great resources, of extensive and vast possessions, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera). 001.003. He had brought a wife from a family of equal standing. 001.003. He sported, enjoyed, and took pleasure with her. 001.004. Being without a son and desiring a son, he prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other [deities] — the garden deities, the forest deities, the crossroad deities, and the deities who receive offerings. 001.005. He also prayed to the deity who is innate, who shares in one’s <s>dharma</s>, who is perpetually attached [to one]. 001.006. And there is this common saying in the world that sons and 001.007. daughters are born through the power of prayer. 001.007. But this is not so. 001.007. For if it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). 001.008. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. 001.009. Which three? The father and mother are passionate and have come together; the mother is healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>Gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) is present. 001.010. From the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. 001.011. And he continued, intent upon prayer.

body.text:
001.012. anyatamaśca sattvaścaramabhavikaśca hitaiṣī gṛhītamokṣamārgāntonmukho na nirvāṇe bahirmukhaḥ saṃsārādanarthikaḥ sarvabhavagativyupapattiparānmukho 'ntimadehadhārī anyatamāt sattvanikāyāccyutvā tasya prajāpatyāḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ/
001.014. pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye piṇḍatajātīye mātṛgrāme/
001.014. katame pañca? raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti, viraktaṃ jānāti/
001.015. kālaṃ jānāti, ṛtuṃ jānāti/
001.015. garbhamavakrāntaṃ jānāti/
001.016. yasya sakāśād garbhamavakrāmati taṃ jānāti/
001.016. dārakaṃ jānāti dārikāṃ jānāti/
001.017. saceddārako bhavati, dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati/
001.017. saceddārikā bhavati, vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati/
001.018. sā āttamanāttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati--diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhasva/
001.018. āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā/
001.019. yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati, niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyati/
001.019. so 'pi āttamanāttamanā udānam udānayati--apyevāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam/
001.020. jāto me syānnāvajātaḥ/
001.021. kṛtyāni me kurvīt/
001.021. bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt/
001.021. dāyādyaṃ pratipadyeta/
001.021. kulavaṃśo me cirasthitiko bhaviṣyati/
001.022. asmākaṃ cāpyatītakālagatānāmalpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā dakṣiṇāmādeśayiṣyati--idaṃ tayoryatratatropapannayorgacchatoranugacchatviti/
001.024. āpannasattvāṃ ca tāṃ viditvā upariprasādatalagatāmayantritāṃ dhārayati śīte śītopakaraṇairuṣṇa uṣṇopakaraṇairvaidyaprajñaptairāhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyaistiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukaṣāyavivarjitairāhāraiḥ, hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasamiva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcānmañcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭham{na}vatarantīmupa{madha?}rimāṃ bhūmim/
001.027. na <2>cāsya amanojñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya/
body.translated_text: 001.012. Now, a certain being, one in his final existence, well-wishing, who had grasped the path to liberation, facing toward <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and not away from it, disenchanted with <s>Saṃsāra</s>, turned away from all modes of existence and rebirth, bearing his last body — having passed away from a certain class of beings, descended into the womb of that wife of his (<s>Prajāpati</s>). 001.014. There are five distinctive characteristics in certain women of a specific lineage: 001.014. What are the five? She knows a man who is passionate; she knows one who is passionless. 001.015. She knows the [right] time; she knows the fertile season. 001.015. She knows when a conception has descended [into the womb]. 001.016. She knows from whom the embryo descends. 001.016. She knows if it is a boy; she knows if it is a girl. 001.017. If it is a boy, he rests leaning to the right side of the womb. 001.017. If it is a girl, she rests leaning to the left side of the womb. 001.018. She, delighted and overjoyed, announced to her husband: ‘Rejoice, noble son! May you prosper! 001.018. I have become pregnant. 001.019. And since [the child] rests leaning to my right side, it will certainly be a boy.’ 001.019. He too, delighted and overjoyed, uttered an exclamation: ‘May I indeed see the face of a son, long desired! 001.020. May there be born to me [a son], not a still-born [child]! 001.021. May he perform my duties! 001.021. May he repay what I have nurtured! 001.021. May he receive the inheritance! 001.021. May the lineage of my family endure for a long time! 001.022. And may he, having given gifts and performed meritorious deeds, whether few or many, on behalf of us who have departed and passed away, dedicate the merit, [saying]: “May this [merit] follow those two, wherever they may be reborn.”’ 001.024. And having learned that she was pregnant, he kept her on the upper terrace of the mansion, attended to her with care — with cooling provisions in the cold [season], warming provisions in the heat, and with foods prescribed by physicians: not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent — foods free from [excess of] bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent [flavors]; her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> garden, descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, [touching] only the uppermost floor. 001.027. And no unpleasant sound was allowed to reach her ears — all for the maturation of the embryo.

body.text:
002.001. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
002.002. dārako jātaḥ/
002.002. abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇaviśālalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūruttuṅganāso ratnapratyuptikayā karṇikayā āmuktayālaṃkṛtaḥ/
002.004. balasenena gṛhapatinā ratnaparīkṣakā āhūyoktāḥ/
002.004. bhavantaḥ, ratnānāṃ mūlyaṃ kuruta iti/
002.005. na śakyate ratnānāṃ mūlyaṃ kartumiti/
002.005. dharmatā yasya na śakyate mūlyaṃ kartuṃ tasya koṭimūlyaṃ kriyate/
002.006. te kathayanti--gṛhapate, asya ratnasya koṭirmūlyamiti/
002.007. tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya trīṇi saptakāni ekaviṃśatidivasāni vistareṇa jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti/
002.009. ayaṃ dārakaḥ koṭimūlyayā ratnapratyuptikayā āmuktayā jātaḥ, śravaṇeṣu ca nakṣatreṣu/
002.009. bhavatu dārakasya śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇa iti nāma/
002.010. yasminneva divase śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo jātaḥ, tasminneva divase balasenasya gṛhapaterdvau preṣyadārakau jātau/
002.011. tenaikasya dāraka iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam, aparasya pālaka iti/
002.012. śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradatto dvābhyāmaṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyām/
002.013. so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
002.015. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam//
body.translated_text: 002.001. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. 002.002. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, of fair complexion, golden-colored, with a head shaped like a parasol, with long arms, with a broad and wide forehead, with joined eyebrows, with a prominent nose, adorned with an ear-ornament set with jewels. 002.004. The householder <s>Balasena</s> summoned the gem-appraisers and said: ‘Sirs, determine the value of the jewels.’ 002.005. ‘It is not possible to determine the value of the jewels.’ 002.005. It is the custom that when the value of something cannot be determined, a value of one <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) is assigned. 002.006. They said: ‘Householder, the value of this jewel is one <s>koṭi</s>.’ 002.007. His kinsmen, having assembled and gathered, celebrated the birth festival for twenty-one days — three times seven — in elaborate fashion, and established a name: ‘What shall be the name of the boy?’ 002.009. ‘This boy was born wearing a jewel-set ear-ornament worth one <s>koṭi</s>, and under the <s>Śravaṇa</s> constellation.’ 002.009. ‘Let the boy’s name be <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>.’ 002.010. On the very day that <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> was born, on that same day, two servant-boys were born to the householder <s>Balasena</s>. 002.011. He established the name of one as <s>Dāraka</s> (Boy) and of the other as <s>Pālaka</s> (Protector). 002.012. <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two shoulder-nurses, two play-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two milk-nurses. 002.013. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. 002.015. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

body.text:
002.016. sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyām upanyastaḥ, saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyām/
002.017. so 'ṣṭāsu parīkṣāsūdghaṭako vācakaḥ piṇḍataḥ paṭupracāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
002.018. tasya pitrā trīṇi vāsagṛhāṇi māpitāni haimantikaṃ graiṣmikaṃ vārṣikam/
002.018. trīṇi udyānāni māpitāni haimantikaṃ graiṣmikaṃ vārṣikam/
002.019. trīṇi antaḥpurāṇi pratyupasthāpitāni jyeṣṭhakaṃ madhyamaṃ kanīyasam/
002.020. sa upariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
002.021. balaseno gṛhapatir nityameva kṛṣikarmānte udyuktaḥ/
002.021. sa koṭikarṇastaṃ pitaraṃ paśyati nityaṃ kṛṣikarmānte--udyuktam/
002.022. sa kathayati--tāta, kasyārthe tvaṃ nityameva kṛṣikarmānte udyuktah? sa kathayati--putra, yathā tvamupariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍasi ramasi paricārayasi, yadyahamapi evameva krīḍeyaṃ rameyaṃ paricārayeyam, nacirādevāsmākaṃ bhogāstanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādāyaṃ gaccheyuḥ/
002.025. sa saṃlakṣayati--mamaivārthaṃ codanā kriyate/
002.026. sa kathayati--tāta yadyevam, gacchāmi, mahāsamudramavatarāmi/
002.026. pitā kathayati--putra tāvantaṃ me ratnajātamasti/
002.027. yadi tvaṃ tilataṇḍulakolakulatthanyāyena ratnāni parimokṣyase, tathāpi me ratnānāṃ parikṣayo na syāt/
002.028. sa kathayati--tāta anujānīhi māma, paṇyamādāya mahāsamudramavatarāmīti/
002.029. balasenena tasyāvaśyaṃ nirbandhaṃ jñātvānujñātaḥ/
002.029. balasenena gṛhapatinā vāsavagrāmake ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtam--yo yuṣmākamutsahate śroṇena koṭikarṇena sārthavāhena sārdhamaśulkenātarapaṇyena mahāsamudramavatartum, sa mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānayatu/
002.031. pañcabhirvaṇikśatairmahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānītam/
002.032. balaseno nāma gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati--<3>kīdṛśena yānena śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo yāsyati? sa saṃlakṣayati--saced hastibhiḥ, hastinaḥ sukumārā durbharāśca, aśvā api sukumārā dubharāśca, gardabhāḥ smṛtimantaḥ sukumārāśca/
body.translated_text: 002.016. When he had grown up, he was instructed in writing, in arithmetic, in calculation, in seals and stamps, in deposits, in consignments, in the appraisal of goods, and in the appraisal of gems. 002.017. He became accomplished in all eight examinations — a teacher, competent in summary and skilled in practice. 002.018. His father had three residential houses built for him: one for the winter, one for the summer, and one for the rainy season. 002.018. Three gardens were made: for the winter, summer, and rainy season. 002.019. Three harems were provided: the senior, the middle, and the junior. 002.020. He, stationed on the upper terrace of the mansion, sported, enjoyed, and took pleasure with purely instrumental music. 002.021. The householder <s>Balasena</s> was perpetually engaged in farming work. 002.021. <s>Koṭikarṇa</s> saw his father perpetually engaged in farming work. 002.022. He said: ‘Father, for whose sake are you perpetually engaged in farming?’ He replied: ‘Son, just as you sport, enjoy, and take pleasure on the upper terrace of the mansion with purely instrumental music, if I too were to sport, enjoy, and take pleasure in the same way, before long our possessions would dwindle, be exhausted, and come to an end.’ 002.025. He reflected: ‘This exhortation is directed at me.’ 002.026. He said: ‘Father, if that is so, I shall go and venture upon the great ocean.’ 002.026. The father said: ‘Son, I possess such a store of gems. 002.027. Even if you were to spend the gems at the rate of sesame, rice, jujube, and horse-gram, the store of my gems would not be exhausted.’ 002.028. He said: ‘Father, permit me! Taking merchandise, I shall venture upon the great ocean.’ 002.029. <s>Balasena</s>, recognizing his firm insistence, gave permission. 002.029. The householder <s>Balasena</s> had a bell-proclamation made in the village of <s>Vāsava</s>: ‘Whoever among you is willing to venture upon the great ocean with the caravan-leader <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, without toll and without transport-fee, let him prepare merchandise for the ocean voyage.’ 002.031. Five hundred merchants prepared merchandise for the ocean voyage. 002.032. The householder <s>Balasena</s> reflected: ‘By what conveyance shall <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> travel?’ He considered: ‘If by elephants — elephants are delicate and difficult to maintain; horses too are delicate and difficult to maintain; donkeys are mindful but delicate.’

body.text:
003.003. gardabhayānena gacchatviti/
003.003. sa pitrā āhūyoktah--putra na tvayā sārthasya purastād gantavyam, nāpi pṛṣṭhataḥ/
003.004. yadi balavāṃścauro bhavati, sārthasya purastānnipatati/
003.004. durbalo bhavati, pṛṣṭhato nipatati/
003.005. tvayā sārthasya madhye gantavyam/
003.005. na ca te sārthavāhe hate sārtho vaktavyaḥ/
003.006. dāsakapālakāvapi uktau--putrau, yuvābhyāṃ na kenacit prakāreṇa śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo moktavya iti//
body.translated_text: 003.003. ‘Let him go by donkey-conveyance.’ 003.003. He was called by his father and told: ‘Son, you must not go at the front of the caravan, nor at the rear. 003.004. If a robber is strong, he attacks the front of the caravan. 003.004. If he is weak, he attacks the rear. 003.005. You must go in the middle of the caravan. 003.005. And if the caravan-leader is killed, you must not take charge of the caravan.’ 003.006. <s>Dāsaka</s> and <s>Pālaka</s> too were told: ‘Sons, you two must not abandon <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> under any circumstances.’

body.text:
003.008. athāpareṇa samayena śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ kṛtakautukamaṅgalasvastyayano mātuḥ sakāśamupasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya kathayati--amba gacchāmi, avalokitā bhava, mahāsamudramavatarāmi/
003.010. sā ruditumārabdhā/
003.010. sa kathayati--amba kasmād rodasi/
003.010. mātā sāśrudurdinavadanā kathayati--putra, kadācidahaṃ putrakaṃ punarapi jīvantaṃ drakṣyāmīti/
003.011. sa saṃlakṣayati--ahaṃ maṅgalaiḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
003.012. iyamīdṛśamamaṅgalamabhidhatte/
003.012. sa ruṣitaḥ kathayati--amba, ahaṃ kṛtakautūhalamaṅgalasvastyayano mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
003.013. tvaṃ cedṛśānyamaṅgalāni karoṣi/
003.013. apāyān kiṃ na paśyasīti/
003.014. sā kathayati--putra, kharaṃ te vākkarma niścāritam/
003.013. atyayamatyayato deśaya/
003.015. apyevaitat karma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchet/
003.015. sā tenātyayamatyayato kṣamāpitā/
003.015. atha śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ kṛtakautūhalamaṅgalasvastyayanaḥ śakaṭairbhārairmoṭaiḥ piṭakairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiḥ prabhūtaṃ samudragamanīyaṃ paṇyamāropya mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
003.017. so 'nupūrveṇa grāmanagaranigamapallipattaneṣu cañcūryamāṇo mahāsamudrataṭamanuprāptaḥ/
003.018. nipuṇataḥ sāmudram yānapātraṃ pratipādya mahāsamudramavatīrṇo dhanahārakaḥ/
003.019. so 'nuguṇena vāyunā ratnadvīpamanuprāptaḥ/
003.019. tena tatropaparīkṣyopaparīkṣya ratnānāṃ tad vahanaṃ pūritaṃ tadyathā tilataṇḍulakolakulatthānām/
003.020. so 'nuguṇena śroṇaḥ saṃsiddhayānapātro jambudvīpamanuprāptaḥ/
003.021. sa sārthastasminneva samudratīre āvāsitaḥ/
003.021. sau śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo 'pi sārthavāho dāsakapālakāvādāya sārthamadhyādekānte 'pakramya āyaṃ vyayaṃ ca tulayitumārabdhaḥ/
003.023. paścāt tenāsau dāsako 'bhihitah--dāsaka, paśya sāthaḥ kiṃ karotīti/
003.023. sa gataḥ/
003.023. yāvat paśyati sthorāṃ lardayantaṃ sārtham/
003.024. so 'pi sthorāṃ lardayitumārabdhaḥ/
003.024. dāsakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--pālakaḥ sārthavāhaṃ śabdāpayiṣyati/
003.025. pālako 'pi saṃlakṣayati--dāsakaḥ sārthavāhaḥ śabdāpayiṣyatīti/
003.026. sa sārthaḥ sarātrimeva sthorāṃ lardayitvā saṃprasthitaḥ/
003.026. so 'pi gāḍhanidrāvaṣṭabdhaḥ śayitaḥ/
003.027. sa sārthastāvad gato yāvatprabhātam/
003.027. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, kva sārthavāhah? purastād gacchati/
003.028. purastād gatvā pṛcchanti--kva sārthavāhah? pṛṣṭhata āgacchati/
003.028. pṛṣṭhato gatvā pṛcchanti--kva sārthavāhah? madhye gacchati/
003.029. madhye gatvā pṛcchanti/
003.029. yāvat tatrāpi nāsti/
003.029. dāsakaḥ kathayati--mama buddhirutpannā--pālakaḥ sārthavāhaṃ śabdāpayiṣyati/
003.030. pālako 'pi kathayati--mama buddhirutpannā--dāsakaḥ sārthavāhaṃ śabdāpayiṣyati/
003.031. bhavantaḥ, na śobhanaṃ kṛtam yadasmābhiḥ sārthavāhaśchoritaḥ/
003.032. āgacchata, nivārtāmaḥ/
003.032. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, yadi vayaṃ nivartiṣyāmaḥ/
body.translated_text: 003.008. Then, on another occasion, <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, having performed the auspicious rites and benedictions, approached his mother, fell at her feet, and said: 'Mother, I am going. Give me your blessing — I am setting out upon the great ocean.' 003.010. She began to weep. 003.010. He said: 'Mother, why do you weep?' 003.010. The mother, with tears and a sorrowful face, said: 'Son, will I ever see my boy alive again?' 003.011. He reflected: 'I have set out with auspicious [rites]. 003.012. She utters such inauspicious words.' 003.012. He said angrily: 'Mother, I have set out upon the great ocean with the auspicious rites and benedictions performed. 003.013. And you utter such inauspicious things! 003.013. Do you not see the dangers [in this]?' 003.014. She said: 'Son, harsh speech has been uttered by you. 003.013. Confess this transgression as a transgression! 003.015. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> (deed) may go to diminution, exhaustion, and wearing away.' 003.015. She was asked for forgiveness by him, confessing the transgression as a transgression. 003.015. Then <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, having performed the auspicious rites and benedictions, loading abundant ocean-going merchandise onto carts, loads, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, set out upon the great ocean. 003.017. Traveling gradually through villages, towns, market-towns, hamlets, and cities, he reached the shore of the great ocean. 003.018. Having carefully procured a seaworthy vessel, the wealth-seeker embarked upon the great ocean. 003.019. With a favorable wind, he reached the Jewel Island. 003.019. There, having examined and inspected [the goods], he filled that vessel with gems, [packed] like sesame seeds, rice grains, jujubes, and horse-gram. 003.020. With a favorable [wind], <s>Śroṇa</s>, with his vessel successfully [sailed], reached <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. 003.021. The caravan encamped on that very seashore. 003.021. Then <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, the caravan-leader, taking his slave and servant, withdrew to one side from the midst of the caravan and began to tally income and expenditure. 003.023. Afterward, he told his slave: 'Slave, go see what the caravan is doing.' 003.023. He went. 003.023. He saw that the caravan was dancing the <s>sthorā</s> (a wild dance). 003.024. He too began to dance the <s>sthorā</s>. 003.024. The slave reflected: 'The servant will inform the caravan-leader.' 003.025. The servant also reflected: 'The slave will inform the caravan-leader.' 003.026. The caravan danced the <s>sthorā</s> all night long and then set out. 003.026. And he [Śroṇa] lay sleeping, seized by deep slumber. 003.027. The caravan had gone as far as dawn. 003.027. They said: 'Sirs, where is the caravan-leader?' 'He goes ahead.' 003.028. Going ahead, they asked: 'Where is the caravan-leader?' 'He comes behind.' 003.028. Going behind, they asked: 'Where is the caravan-leader?' 'He goes in the middle.' 003.029. Going to the middle, they asked. 003.029. He was not there either. 003.029. The slave said: 'The thought arose in me: the servant will inform the caravan-leader.' 003.030. The servant also said: 'The thought arose in me: the slave will inform the caravan-leader.' 003.031. 'Sirs, we have done something terrible — the caravan-leader has been abandoned by us! 003.032. Come, let us turn back.' 003.032. They said: 'Sirs, if we turn back,

body.text:
004.001. <4>sarva evānayena vyasanamāpatsyāmaḥ/

004.003. śroṇasya koṭikarṇasya mātāpitṛbhyāṃ śrutam--śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo 'bhyāgata iti/

004.007. tābhyāmeka āgatya kathayati--ayaṃ śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo 'bhyāgata iti/

004.008. apara āgatya kathayati--amba, diṣṭyā vardhasva, ayaṃ śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo 'bhyāgata iti/
004.009. tasya tāvabhisāraṃ dattvā pratyudgatau na paśyataḥ/
004.010. tau na kasyacit punarapi śraddadhātumārabdhau/
004.010. tābhyāmudyāneṣu svakasabhādevakuleṣu cchatrāṇi vyajanāni kalaśāni upānahāni cākṣarāṇi abhilikhitāni dattāni sthāpitāni--yadi tāvacchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo jīvati, laghu āgamaya, kṣipramāgamaya/
004.012. atha cyutaḥ kālagataḥ, tasyaiva gatyupapattisthānāt sthānāntaraviśeṣatāyai/

body.translated_text: 004.001. we shall all fall into calamity because of this! 004.001. Come, let us at least make a pact: none of us shall inform <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>'s parents until the merchandise has been distributed.' 004.002. Having made the pact, they went. 004.003. <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>'s parents heard: '<s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> has returned!' 004.004. They said: 'He comes behind.' 004.005. Going behind, they asked: 'Where is the caravan-leader?' 'He goes ahead.' 004.006. They were led about in confusion until the merchandise was distributed. 004.006. Afterward, they said: 'Mother, the caravan-leader was forgotten by us.' 004.007. One of them came and told the parents: 'This <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> has returned!' 004.008. Having given him a reward, they went out to meet [their son] — but they did not see him. 004.008. Another came and said: 'Mother, rejoice! This <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> has returned!' 004.009. Having given him a reward, they went out to meet [their son] — but they did not see him. 004.010. They could no longer bring themselves to believe anyone. 004.010. By the two [parents], in gardens, in their own assembly-halls, and in temples, parasols, fans, water-pots, sandals, and inscriptions were placed and deposited [with the prayer]: 'If <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> is alive, bring him quickly, bring him swiftly!' 004.012. 'But if he has died, has passed away — then for the sake of his gaining a superior destination from whatever station of rebirth he has attained.' 004.013. The two [parents], weeping with grief, became blind.

body.text:
004.014. śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ sārthavāho 'pi sūryāṃśubhiḥ spṛṣṭa ātāpitaḥ prativibuddho yāvat sārthaṃ na paśyati nānyatra gardabhayānameva/
004.015. sa taṃ gardabhayānamabhiruhya saṃprasthitaḥ/
004.016. rātrau ca vātena pravāyatā vālukayā mārgo vyapoḍhaḥ pithitaḥ/
004.016. te ca gardabhāḥ smṛtimanto gandhamāghrāyāghrāya śanairmandamandaṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
004.017. sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kasmādete śanairmandamandaṃ gacchantīti kṛtvā pratodayaṣṭyā tāḍitāḥ/
004.018. te saṃbhrāntā ākulībhūtāḥ smṛtibhraṣṭā unmārgeṇa saṃprasthitāḥ, yāvadanyatamāśāṭavīṃ praviṣṭāḥ/
004.019. te tṛṣārtā vihvalavadanā jihvāṃ nirnāmayya gacchanti/
004.020. tān dṛṣṭvā tasya kāruṇyamutpannam/
004.020. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi etān notsrakṣyāmi, anayena vyasanamāpatsye/
004.021. ko 'sau nirghṛṇahṛdayastyaktaparalokaśca ya eṣāṃ pratodayaṣṭiṃ kāye nipātayiṣyati? tena ta utsṛṣṭāh--adyāgreṇa acchinnāgrāṇi tṛṇāni bhakṣayata anavamarditāni, pānīyāni pibata anāvilāni, caturdiśaṃ ca śītalā vāyavo vāntviti/
004.024. sa tānutsṛjya padbhyāṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
004.024. yāvat paśyati āyasaṃ nagaramuccaṃ ca pragṛhītaṃ ca/
004.025. tatra dvāre puruṣastiṣṭhati kālo raudrāścaṇḍo lohitākṣa udviddhapiṇḍo lohalaguḍavyagrahastaḥ/
004.026. sa tasya sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
004.026. upasaṃkramya taṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchati--asti atra bhoḥ puruṣa pānīyamiti/
004.027. sa tūṣṇīṃ vyavasthitaḥ/
004.027. bhūtastena pṛṣṭah--astyatra nagare pānīyamiti/
004.028. bhūyo 'pi sa tūṣṇīṃ vyavasthitaḥ/
004.028. tena sārthavāhena tatra praviśya pānīyaṃ pānīyam iti śabdo niścāritaḥ/
004.029. yāvat pañcamātraiḥ pretasahasrairdagdhasthūṇāsadṛśairasthiyantravaducchritaiḥ svakeśaromapraticchannaiḥ parvatodarasaṃnibhaiḥ sūcīchidropamamukhairanuparivāritaḥ śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ/
004.031. te kathayanti--sārthavāha kāruṇikastvam/
004.031. asmākaṃ tṛṣārtānāṃ pānīyamanuprayaccha/
004.031. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, ahamapi pānīyameva mṛgayāmi/
004.032. kuto 'ham yuṣmākaṃ pānīyamanuprayacchāmīti? <5>te kathayanti--sārthavāha, pretanagaramidam, kuto 'tra pānīyam? adyāsmābhirdvādaśabhirvarṣaistvatsakāśātpānīyaṃ pānīyamiti śabdaḥ śrutaḥ/
body.translated_text: 004.014. <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> the caravan-leader, touched and heated by the rays of the sun, awoke — and saw neither the caravan nor anything else except the donkey-cart. 004.015. He mounted that donkey-cart and set out. 004.016. At night, the wind blowing had swept and buried the road under sand. 004.016. But the donkeys, being creatures of memory, went on slowly and gently, sniffing and sniffing the scent [of the trail]. 004.017. The caravan-leader reflected: 'Why do they go so slowly and gently?' and struck them with the goad-stick. 004.018. They became agitated, confused, lost their memory, and set off on the wrong path — until they entered a certain wilderness. 004.019. They went on, tormented by thirst, with distressed faces, sticking out their tongues. 004.020. Seeing them, compassion arose in him. 004.020. He reflected: 'If I do not release them, I shall fall into calamity because of this. 004.021. Who is that person of pitiless heart, who has abandoned the next world, who would bring down the goad-stick upon their bodies?' So he released them [saying]: 'From today onward, eat uncut-tipped grass, drink unstirred water, and [enjoy] the cool breezes blowing from the four directions.' 004.024. Having released them, he set out on foot. 004.024. Then he saw an iron city, tall and imposing. 004.025. At the gate stood a man — dark (<s>Kāla</s>), terrible, fierce, red-eyed, with a raised topknot, with an iron club grasped in his hand. 004.026. He approached that man. 004.026. Having approached, he asked the man: 'Sir, is there water here?' 004.027. He stood silent. 004.027. He asked again: 'Is there water in this city?' 004.028. Again, he stood silent. 004.028. The caravan-leader, entering [the city], cried out: 'Water! Water!' 004.029. Thereupon, <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> was surrounded by about five thousand <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), resembling burnt pillars, towering like bone-machines, covered by their own hair and body-hair, resembling the interiors of mountains, with mouths like needle-holes. 004.031. They said: 'Caravan-leader, you are compassionate! 004.031. Give us water — we are tormented by thirst!' 004.031. He said: 'Sirs, I too am searching for water. 004.032. How can I give you water?' They said: 'Caravan-leader, this is the City of the Dead (<s>Pretanagara</s>). Where would there be water here? For twelve years now, we have heard from you [this] cry: "Water! Water!"'

body.text:
005.002. sa kathayati--ke yūyaṃ bhavantaḥ, kena vā karmaṇā ihopapannāh? śroṇa duṣkuhakā jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyāḥ/
005.003. nābhiśraddadhāsyasi/

body.translated_text: 005.002. He said: 'Who are you, sirs, and by what <s>karma</s> have you been born here?' '<s>Śroṇa</s>, we are deceitful <s>Jāmbūdvīpaka</s> humans. 005.003. You will not believe us.' 005.003. 'Sirs, I am an eyewitness — why would I not believe?' They spoke this verse: 005.005. 'We were abusers, we were wrathful, we were envious, we were cheaters and swindlers; 005.006. and not even the slightest gift was given by us — therefore we have come to the world of the dead. // 1 //'

005.017. asmākaṃ tṛṣārtānāṃ pānīyamanuprayaccha/

body.translated_text: 005.007. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, go! You are one called greatly meritorious.' 005.007. 'Has anyone been seen by you who entered the city of the dead (<s>pretanagara</s>) and came out safe and well?' He set out, and then he saw that man. 005.008. That one said to him: 'Good sir, oh, if only you had told me that this was a city of the dead — I would not have entered here!' 005.009. He said to him: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, go! You are one called greatly meritorious, since you entered the city of the dead and came out safe and well.' 005.011. He set out. 005.011. Then he saw another city — made of iron, lofty and well-fortified. 005.011. There too, at the gate, stood a man — terrible, of fierce aspect, red-eyed, with a muscular body, a club of iron in his hand. 005.012. He (<s>Śroṇa</s>) approached him. 005.013. Having approached, he said thus: 'O man, is there water in this city?' He stood silent. 005.014. He asked again: 'O man, is there water in this city?' He stood silent. 005.015. He entered there and cried out: 'Water! Water!' 005.015. He was surrounded by many thousands of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) — resembling burnt pillars, raised up like skeletal machines, covered with their own hair and body-hair, resembling the interiors of mountains, with mouths like needle-holes. 005.017. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, you are compassionate! 005.017. Give us water, we who are tormented by thirst!' He said: 'I too am searching for water myself. 005.018. How can I give you water?' They said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, this is a city of the dead! 005.019. Where is water here? For twelve years now, we have heard the cry "Water! Water!" from your direction.' 005.020. And he said: 'Who are you, and by what deed were you born here?' They said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are wicked deceivers. 005.021. You will not believe us.' 005.021. And he said: 'I am an eyewitness. 005.022. Why would I not believe?' They spoke a verse: 005.023. 'Intoxicated with the pride of health, intoxicated with the pride of useless wealth, 005.024. not even a trifle of charity was given — by which we have come to the world of the ancestors.' // 2 //

body.text:
005.025. śroṇa gaccha, puṇyakarmā tvam/
005.025. asti kaścit tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ śrutaḥ sa pretanagaraṃ praviśya kvastikṣemābhyāṃ jīvannirgacchan? sa saṃprasthitaḥ/
005.026. yāvat tenāsau puruṣo dṛṣṭaḥ/
005.026. sa tenoktah--bhadramukha, aho bata yadi tvayā mamārocitaṃ syād yathedaṃ pretanagaramiti, naivāhamatra praviṣṭaḥ syām/
005.028. sa kathayati--śroṇa gaccha, puṇyamaheśākhyastvam/
005.028. asti kaścit tvayā dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā pretanagaraṃ praviśya svastikṣemābhyāṃ jīvan nirgacchan? sa saṃprasthitaḥ/
005.029. yāvat paśyati sūryasyāstagamanakāle vimāna, catasro 'psarasah abhirūpāḥ prāsādikā darśanīyāḥ/
005.030. ekaḥ puruṣo 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikah aṅgadakuṇḍalavicitramālyābharaṇānulepanastābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
005.032. sa tairdūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ/
005.032. te taṃ pratyavabhāṣitumārabdhāḥ/
005.032. svāgatam <6>śroṇa, māsi tṛṣito bubhukṣito vā? sa saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ devo 'yaṃ vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā bhaviṣyati/
body.translated_text: 005.025. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, go! You are one of meritorious deeds. 005.025. Has anyone been seen or heard of by you who entered the city of the dead and came out safe and well, alive?' He set out. 005.026. Then he saw that man. 005.026. He said to him: 'Good sir, oh, if only you had told me that this was a city of the dead — I would never have entered here!' 005.028. He said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, go! You are one called greatly meritorious. 005.028. Has anyone been seen or heard of by you who entered the city of the dead and came out safe and well, alive?' He set out. 005.029. Then he saw, at the time of sunset, a celestial palace (<s>vimāna</s>), four <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) — beautiful, lovely, pleasant to behold — 005.030. and one man, handsome, comely, and pleasant to behold, adorned with bracelets, earrings, garlands of various kinds, ornaments, and unguents, sporting, delighting, and being attended to together with them. 005.032. He was seen by them from afar. 005.032. They began to address him: 005.032. 'Welcome, <s>Śroṇa</s>! Are you thirsty or hungry?' He reflected: 'Surely this must be a god, or a <s>nāga</s> (serpent-being), or a <s>yakṣa</s> (nature spirit).'

body.text:
006.002. āha ca--ārya tṛṣito 'smi, bubhukṣito 'smi/
006.002. sa taiḥ snāpito bhojitaḥ/
006.002. sa tasmin vimāne tāvat sthito yāvat sūryasyābhyudgamanakālasamayaḥ/
006.003. sa tenoktah--śroṇa avatarasva, ādīnavo 'tra bhaviṣyati/
006.004. so 'vatīrya ekānte vyavasthitaḥ/
006.004. tataḥ paścāt sūryasyābhyudgamanakālasamaye tadvimānamantarhitam/
006.005. tā api apsaraso 'ntarhitāśca/
006.005. catvāraḥ śyāmaśabalāḥ kurkurāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ/
006.006. taistaṃ puruṣamavamūrdhakaṃ pātayitvā tāvat pṛṣṭavaṃśānutpāṭyotpāṭya bhikṣito yāvat sūryasyāstagamanakālasamayaḥ/
006.007. tataḥ paścāt punarapi tadvimānaṃ prādurbhūtam, tā apsarasaḥ prādurbhūtāḥ/
006.008. sa ca puruṣastābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
006.008. sa teṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati--ke yūyam, kena ca karmaṇā ihopapannāh? te procuh--śroṇa duṣkuhakā jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ/
006.010. nābhiśraddadhāsyasi/
006.010. sa cāha--ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī, kathaṃ nābhiśraddadhāsye? śroṇa, ahaṃ vāsavagrāmake aurabhraka āsīt/
006.011. urabhrān praghātya praghātya māṃsaṃ vikrīya jīvikāṃ kalpayāmi/
006.012. āryaśca mahākātyāyano mamānukampayā āgatya kathayati--bhadramukha, aniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇaḥ phalavipākaḥ/
006.013. virama tvamasmāt pāpakādasaddharmāt/
006.013. nāhaṃ tasya vacanena viramāmi/
006.014. bhūyo bhūyaḥ sa māṃ vicchandayati--bhadramukha, aniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇo phalavipākaḥ/
006.015. virama tvamasmāt pāpakādasaddharmāt/
006.015. tathāpi ahaṃ na prativiramāmi/
006.015. sa māṃ pṛcchati--bhadramukha, kiṃ tvametānurabhrān divā praghātayasi āhosvidū rātrau? mayoktah--ārya divā, praghātayāmīti/
006.017. sa kathayati--bhadramukha, rātrau śīlasamādānaṃ kiṃ na gṛhṇāsi/
006.017. mayā tasyāntikād rātrau śīlasamādānaṃ gṛhītam/
006.018. yattad rātrau śīlasamādānaṃ gṛhītam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena rātrāvevaṃvidhaṃ divyaṃ sukhaṃ pratyanubhavāmi/
006.019. yanmayā divā urabhrāḥ praghātitāḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena divā evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavāmi/
006.020. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
006.021. divasaṃ paraprāṇapīḍako rātrau śīlaguṇaiḥ samanvitaḥ/
006.022. tasyaitatkarmaṇaḥ phalaṃ hyanubhavāmi kalyāṇapāpakam//3//
body.translated_text: 006.002. And he said: 'Noble one, I am thirsty and hungry.' 006.002. He was bathed and fed by them. 006.002. He stayed in that celestial palace until the time of sunrise. 006.003. He (<s>Śroṇa</s>) was told by him: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, descend — danger will come here.' 006.004. Having descended, he stood to one side. 006.004. Then, after that, at the time of sunrise, that celestial palace vanished. 006.005. Those <s>apsarases</s> too vanished. 006.005. Four dark-spotted dogs appeared. 006.006. Having thrown that man face-down, they tore and devoured his spine until the time of sunset. 006.007. Afterward, that celestial palace appeared again, and those <s>apsarases</s> appeared again. 006.008. And that man sported, delighted, and was attended to together with them. 006.008. He (<s>Śroṇa</s>) approached them and said: 'Who are you, and by what deed were you born here?' They said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are wicked deceivers. 006.010. You will not believe us.' 006.010. And he said: 'I am an eyewitness — how would I not believe?' '<s>Śroṇa</s>, I was a sheepherder in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. 006.011. Slaughtering sheep again and again, I earned my livelihood by selling the meat. 006.012. And the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, out of compassion for me, came and said: "Good sir, the ripening of this deed's fruit is undesirable. 006.013. Desist from this evil, unrighteous conduct!" 006.013. I did not desist at his word. 006.014. Again and again he dissuaded me: "Good sir, the ripening of this deed's fruit is undesirable. 006.015. Desist from this evil, unrighteous conduct!" 006.015. Even so, I did not desist. 006.015. He asked me: "Good sir, do you slaughter these sheep during the day or at night?" I said: "Noble one, during the day." 006.017. He said: "Good sir, will you not take the moral precepts (<s>śīlasamādāna</s>) for the night?" 006.017. I took the moral precepts from him for the night. 006.018. Because of that deed — having taken the moral precepts at night — I experience such divine happiness at night as its karmic fruition. 006.019. Because I slaughtered sheep during the day, I experience such suffering during the day as its karmic fruition. 006.020. And he spoke a verse: 006.021. "By day, one who injures the lives of others; at night, endowed with the virtues of moral conduct — 006.022. the fruit of that deed, both auspicious and sinful, I experience." // 3 //

body.text:
006.023. śroṇa, gamiṣyasi tvaṃ vāsavagrāmakam? gamiṣyāmi/
006.023. tatra mama putraḥ prativasati/
006.023. sa urabhrān praghātya praghātya jīvikāṃ kalpayati/
006.024. sa tvayā vaktavyah--dṛṣṭaste mayā pitāa/
006.025. kathayati--aniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇaḥ phalavipākaḥ/
006.025. viramāsmāt pāpakādasaddharmāt/
006.025. bhoḥ puruṣa, tvamevaṃ kathayasi--duṣkuhakā jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā iti/
006.026. nābhiśraddadhāsyati/
006.026. śroṇa, yadi na śraddadhāsyati, vaktavyastava pitā kathayati--asti sūnādhastāt suvarṇasya kalaśaḥ pūrayitvā sthāpitaḥ/
006.028. tamuddhṛtyātmānaṃ samyaksukhena prīṇaya/
006.028. āryaṃ ca mahākātyāyanaṃ kālena kālaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādaya, asmākaṃ ca nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādeśaya/
006.029. apyevaitat karma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchet/
006.030. sa saṃprasthitaḥ/
006.030. yāvat sūryasyābhyudgamanakālasamaye paśyati aparaṃ vimānam/
006.031. tatra ekā apsarā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā, ekaśca puruṣa abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikah aṅgadakuṇḍalavicitramālyābharaṇānulepanastayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate <7>paricārayati/
body.translated_text: 006.023. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, will you go to <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>?' 'I will.' 006.023. 'There my son lives. 006.023. He earns his livelihood by slaughtering sheep again and again. 006.024. You should tell him: "Your father has been seen by me. 006.025. He says: The ripening of this deed's fruit is undesirable. 006.025. Desist from this evil, unrighteous conduct!"' 006.025. 'O man, you yourself say: "The humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are wicked deceivers." 006.026. He will not believe.' 006.026. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, if he does not believe, tell him: "Your father says: There is a pot of gold placed full beneath the slaughter-bench. 006.028. Take it out and gratify yourself properly with happiness. 006.028. And attend upon the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> from time to time with alms-food, and in our name, make a merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). 006.029. Perhaps this deed may become attenuated, diminished, and exhausted."' 006.030. He set out. 006.030. Then, at the time of sunrise, he saw another celestial palace. 006.031. There, one <s>apsaras</s> — beautiful, comely, and pleasant to behold — and one man, handsome, comely, and pleasant to behold, adorned with bracelets, earrings, garlands of various kinds, ornaments, and unguents, was sporting, delighting, and being attended to together with her.

body.translated_text: 007.001. Having seen him from afar, he began to address [<s>Śroṇa</s>]: 007.001. 'Welcome, <s>Śroṇa</s>! Are you not thirsty? Are you not hungry?' He reflected: 'Surely this must be a god, or a <s>nāga</s>, or a <s>yakṣa</s>.' 007.003. He said: 'I am thirsty and hungry.' 007.003. He was bathed and fed by him. 007.003. He stayed in that celestial palace until the time of sunset. 007.004. He was told by him: 'Descend — danger will come here.' 007.005. Having seen the danger, he descended and stood to one side. 007.005. Then, after that, at the time of sunset, that celestial palace vanished. 007.006. That <s>apsaras</s> too vanished. 007.006. A great centipede appeared. 007.006. Having coiled its body around that man's body seven times, it stayed devouring his brain, until the time of sunrise. 007.008. Afterward, that celestial palace appeared again. 007.009. That <s>apsaras</s> also appeared again. 007.009. And that man — handsome, comely, and pleasant to behold — was sporting, delighting, and being attended to together with her. 007.010. He (<s>Śroṇa</s>) approached him and asked: 'Who are you, and by what deed were you born here?' He said thus: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, the humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are wicked deceivers. You will not believe.' 007.011. He said: 'I am an eyewitness — why would I not believe?' He said: 'If so — I was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, an adulterer. 007.013. And the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, out of compassion for me, came and said: "Good sir, the ripening of this deed's fruit is undesirable. 007.014. Desist from this evil, unrighteous conduct!" 007.014. At his word, I did not desist. 007.015. Again and again he dissuaded me. 007.015. Even so, I did not desist from that evil, unrighteous conduct. 007.016. He asked me: "Good sir, do you go to another's wife during the day or at night?" I told him: "Noble one, at night." 007.017. He said: "Good sir, during the day, will you not take the moral precepts?" I took the moral precepts from him for the day. 007.018. Because I took the moral precepts from the noble <s>Kātyāyana</s> for the day, I experience such divine happiness during the day as its karmic fruition. 007.020. Because I committed adultery at night, I experience such suffering at night as its karmic fruition. 007.021. And he spoke a verse: 007.022. "At night, infatuated with another's wife; during the day, endowed with the virtues of moral conduct — 007.023. the fruit of that deed, both auspicious and sinful, I experience." // 4 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śroṇa</s>, you will go to <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. There my son, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, is an adulterer. He is to be told: 'Your father has been seen by me.' He says: 'The fruit-ripening of this action is undesirable. Desist from this sinful, unrighteous conduct.' 'Sir, you speak thus — the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are deceitful tricksters. Who will believe this of mine?' <s>Śroṇa</s>, if he will not believe, he is to be told: 'Your father placed a golden pot, having filled it, beneath the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> (fire-sacrifice altar). Having dug it up, gratify yourself properly with comfort. And provide the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food from time to time. And in our name, give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee). Perhaps this <s>karma</s> (action) may go to diminution, exhaustion, and consumption.' He set forth. Then he sees a celestial mansion (<s>vimāna</s>). There, a woman — beautiful, lovely, attractive, adorned with armlets, earrings, various garlands, ornaments, and unguents. At the four feet of her couch, four <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) stand bound. She, having seen him from afar, began to address him: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, welcome!'

body.text:
008.001. mā tṛṣito 'si mā bubhukṣito 'si vā? sa saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ devīyaṃ vā nāgī vā yakṣī vā bhaviṣyati/
008.002. sa kathayati--ārye, tṛṣito 'smi bubhukṣito 'smi/
008.002. tayāsāvudvartitaḥ snāpita āhāro dattaḥ/
008.003. uktaṃ ca--śroṇa, yadi ete kiṃcinmṛgayanti, mā dāsyasīti uktvā teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ karmasvakaṭāṃ pratyakṣīkartukāmā vimānaṃ praviśyāvasthitā/
008.004. te mṛgayitumārabdhāh--śroṇa kāruṇikastvam/
008.005. bubhukṣitā vayam/
008.005. asmākamanuprayaccha/
008.005. tenaikasya kṣiptam--busaplāvī prādurbhūtā/
008.006. aparasya kṣiptam--ayoguḍaṃ bhakṣayitumārabdhaḥ/
008.006. aparasya kṣiptam--svamāṃsaṃ bhakṣayitumārabdhah--aparasya kṣiptam--pūyaśoṇitaṃ prādurbhūtam/
008.007. sā visragandhena nirgatā/
008.008. śroṇa nivāritastvaṃ mayā/

008.010. sa āha--ke yūyam, kena vā karmaṇā ihopapannāh? tayoktam--śroṇa, duṣkuhakā jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā iti nābhiśraddadhāsyasi/
008.011. ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī kasmānnābhiśraddadhāsye? sā kathayati--ahaṃ vāsavagrāmake brāhmaṇī āsīt/
008.012. mayā nakṣatrarātryāṃ pratyupasthitāyāṃ praṇītamāhāraṃ sajjīkṛtam/
008.013. āryamahākātyāyano mamānukampayā vāsavagrāmake piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
008.014. sa mayā dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaścittaprāsādikaḥ/
008.014. cittamabhiprasannaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa mayā prasādajātayā piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ/
008.015. tasyā mama buddhirutpannā--svāminamanumodayāmi, prāmodyamutpādayiṣyatīti/
008.016. sa snātvā āgataḥ/
008.016. mayoktam--āryaputra, anumodasva, mayāryo mahākātyāyanaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ/
008.017. sa ruṣito yāvad brāhmaṇānāṃ na dīyate, jñātīnāṃ vā jñātipūjā na kriyate, tāvattvayā tasmai muṇḍakāya śramaṇakāyāgrapiṇḍakaṃ dattam? so 'marṣajātaḥ kathayati--kasmāt sa muṇḍakaḥ śramaṇako busaplāvīṃ na bhakṣayatīti? tasya karmaṇo vipākenāyaṃ busaplāvīṃ bhakṣayati/
008.020. mama buddhirutpannā--putramapi anumodayāmi, prāmodyamutpādayiṣyatīti/
008.021. so 'pi mayoktah--putra, anumodasva, mayāryo mahākātyāyanaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ/
008.021. so 'pi ruṣito yāvad brāhmaṇānāṃ na dīyate, jñātīnāṃ vā jñātipūjā na kriyate, tāvattvayā tasmai muṇḍakāya śramaṇakāyāgrapiṇḍaṃ dattam? so 'pi amarṣajātaḥ kathayati--kasmāt sa muṇḍakaḥ śramaṇako 'yoguḍaṃ na bhakṣayatīti? tasya karmaṇo vipākenāyamayoguḍaṃ bhakṣayati/
008.024. nakṣatrarātryāṃ pratyupasthitāyāṃ mama jñātayaḥ praheṇakāni preṣayanti/
008.025. tāni ahaṃ snuṣāyāḥ samarpayāmi/
008.025. sā praṇītāni praheṇakāni bhakṣayitvā mama lūhāni upanāmayati/
008.026. ahaṃ teṣāṃ jñātīnāṃ saṃdiśāmi--kiṃ nu yūyaṃ durbhikṣe yathā lūhāni praheṇakāni preṣayata? te mama saṃdiśanti--na vayaṃ lūhāni preṣayāmaḥ, api tu praṇītānyeva praheṇakāni preṣayāmaḥ/
008.029. mayā snuṣābhihitā--vadhūke, mā tvaṃ praṇītāni praheṇakāni bhakṣayitvāsmakaṃ lūhāni upanāmayasi? sā kathayati--kiṃ svamāṃsaṃ na bhakṣayati yā tvadīyāni praheṇakāni bhakṣayatīti? iyaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena svamāṃsāni bhakṣayati/
008.032. nakṣatrarātryāṃ pratupasthitāyāṃ praṇītāni praheṇakāni dattvā jñātīnāṃ preṣayāmi/
008.033. sā dārikā tāni praṇītāni praheṇakāni mārge 'ntarbhakṣayitvā teṣāṃ lūhāni upanāmayati/
body.translated_text: 'Are you not thirsty, are you not hungry?' He considers: 'Surely this one must be a goddess, or a <s>nāgī</s> (serpent-woman), or a <s>yakṣī</s> (nature-spirit).' He says: 'Noble lady, I am thirsty, I am hungry.' By her he was anointed, bathed, and given food. And she said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, if these ones beg for anything, do not give it' — having said this, wishing to make them witness the results of their own <s>karma</s> (actions), she entered the celestial mansion and remained there. They began to beg: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, you are compassionate. We are hungry. Give something to us.' He threw [food] to one — a flood of chaff appeared. He threw to another — that one began to eat an iron ball. He threw to another — that one began to eat his own flesh. He threw to another — pus and blood appeared. She came out because of the foul smell. '<s>Śroṇa</s>, you were warned by me. Why did you give to them? What does he say? — This one is my husband, this one is my son, this one is my daughter-in-law, this one is my maidservant.' He said: 'Who are you, and by what <s>karma</s> have you been reborn here?' She said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are deceitful tricksters — you will not believe it. I am an eyewitness — why would I not believe it?' She says: 'I was a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (brahmin woman) in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. When a <s>nakṣatra</s>-night (constellation festival night) had arrived, I prepared fine food. The venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, out of compassion for me, entered <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s> for alms. He was seen by me — pleasing in body and pleasing in mind. Having seen my mind filled with faith, I, with devotion arisen, provided him with alms-food. This thought arose in me: I shall make my husband rejoice — he will produce gladness. He came after bathing. I said: Noble husband, rejoice! The venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> has been provided with alms-food by me. He became angry: While it is not given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, while honor is not done to kinsmen, you have given the first alms-food to that shaven mendicant? He, filled with indignation, says: Why does that shaven mendicant not eat chaff? By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, this one eats chaff. The thought arose in me: I shall make my son rejoice too — he will produce gladness. He too was told by me: Son, rejoice! The venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> has been provided with alms-food by me. He too became angry: While it is not given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, while honor is not done to kinsmen, you have given the first alms-food to that shaven mendicant? He too, filled with indignation, says: Why does that shaven mendicant not eat an iron ball? By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, this one eats an iron ball. When a <s>nakṣatra</s>-night had arrived, my kinsmen sent gifts. I entrust those to my daughter-in-law. She, having eaten the fine gifts, offers me the inferior ones. I send word to those kinsmen: Why do you send inferior gifts as if in a famine? They send word to me: We do not send inferior ones; rather, we send fine gifts indeed. I said to my daughter-in-law: Daughter-in-law, do you eat the fine gifts and offer us the inferior ones? She says: May she eat her own flesh who eats your gifts! By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, she eats her own flesh.

body.text:
009.001. <9>te mama saṃdiśanti--kiṃ nu tvaṃ durbhikṣe yathā lūhāni asmākaṃ praheṇakāni preṣayasi? ahaṃ teṣāṃ saṃdiśāmi--nāhaṃ lūhāni perṣayāmi, api tu praṇītānyevāhaṃ preṣayāmīti/
009.002. mayā dārikābhihitā--dārike, mā tvaṃ praṇītāni praheṇakāni bhakṣayitvā teṣāṃ lūhāni upanāmayasi/
009.004. sā kathayati--kiṃ nu pūyaśoṇitaṃ na bhakṣayati, yā tvadīyāni praheṇakāni bhakṣayatīti? tasya karmaṇo vipākeneyaṃ pūyaśoṇitaṃ bhakṣayati/
009.005. mama buddhirutpannā--tatra pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇīyām yatraitān sarvān svakaṃ svakaṃ karmaphalaṃ paribhuñjānān paśyeyamiti/
009.006. yayā mayāryamahākātyāyanaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādya praṇīte trāyastriṃśe devanikāye upapattavyam, sāhaṃ mithyāpraṇidhānavaśāt pretamaharddhikā saṃvṛttā/
009.008. śroṇa, gamiṣyasi tvaṃ vāsavagrāmakam? tatra mama duhitā veśyaṃ vāhayati/
009.009. sā tvayā vaktavyā--dṛṣṭāste mayā pitā mātā bhrātā bhrāturjāyā dāsī/
009.010. te kathayanti--aniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇaḥ phalavipākaḥ/
009.010. viramāsmādasaddharmāt/
009.010. bhagini, tvameva kathayasi--duṣkuhakā jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, nābhiśraddadhāsyanti/
009.011. śroṇa, yadi na śraddadhāsyati, vaktavyā--tava paurāṇe paitṛke vāsagṛhe catvāro lohasaṃghāṭāḥ suvarṇasya pūrṇāstiṣṭhanti, madhye ca sauvarṇadaṇḍakamaṇḍaluḥ/
009.013. te kathayanti--tamuddhṛtyātmānaṃ samyaksukhena prīṇaya, āryaṃ ca mahākātyāyanaṃ kālena kālaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādaya, asmākaṃ ca nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādeśaya/
009.015. apyevaitat karma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchet/
009.015. tena tasyāḥ pratijñātam/
009.016. evaṃ tasya paribhramato dvādaśa varṣā atikrāntāḥ//
body.translated_text: They send word to me: Why do you send us inferior gifts as if in a famine? I send word to them: I do not send inferior ones; rather, I send fine ones indeed. I said to the maidservant: Maidservant, do you eat the fine gifts and offer them the inferior ones? She says: May she eat pus and blood who eats your gifts! By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, she eats pus and blood. The thought arose in me: May I be reborn there where I can see all of them experiencing the fruit of their own <s>karma</s>. Although by providing the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food I should have been reborn in the excellent heaven of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, through my wrong aspiration I became a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) of great supernatural power. <s>Śroṇa</s>, will you go to <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>? There my daughter conducts a life of prostitution. She is to be told by you: Your father, mother, brother, sister-in-law, and maidservant have been seen by me. They say: The fruit-ripening of this <s>karma</s> is undesirable. Desist from this unrighteous conduct. Sister, you yourself say: The people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are deceitful tricksters — they will not believe it. <s>Śroṇa</s>, if she will not believe, she is to be told: In your ancestral paternal dwelling-house, there stand four iron chests full of gold, and in the middle a golden staff and water-pot. They say: Having dug those up, gratify yourself properly with comfort, and provide the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food from time to time, and in our name give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee). Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may go to diminution, exhaustion, and consumption. He made a promise to her.

body.text:
009.017. tayoktah--śroṇa, gamiṣyasi tvaṃ vāsavagrāmakam? bhagini, gamiṣyāmi/
009.017. sa tasminneva vimāne uṣitaḥ/
009.018. tayā teṣāmeva pretānāmājñā dattā--bhavanto gacchata, śroṇaṃ koṭikarṇaṃ suptameva vāsavagrāmake paitṛke udyāne sthāpayitvā āgacchata/
009.019. sa tairvāsavagrāmake paitṛke udyāne sthāpitaḥ/
009.020. sa prativibuddho yāvat paśyati ghaṇṭāchatrāṇi vyajanāni, akṣarāṇi likhitāni--yadi tāvacchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo jīvati, laghvāgamanāya, kṣipramāgamanāya, cyutaḥ kālagato gatyupapattisthānāt sthānāntaraviśeṣatāyai/
009.022. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi ahaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ mṛta eva gṛhītaḥ, kasmādbhūyo 'haṃ gṛhaṃ praviśāmi? gacchāmi, ārya mahākātyāyanasyāntikāt pravrajāmīti/
009.024. atha śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
009.025. adrākṣīdāyuṣmān mahākatyāyanaḥ śroṇaṃ koṭikarṇaṃ dūrādeva/
009.025. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ śroṇaṃ koṭikarṇamidamavocat--ehi śroṇa, śvāgataṃ te/
009.026. dṛṣṭaste śroṇa ayaṃ lokaḥ paraśca lokah? sa kathayati--dṛṣṭo bhadanta mahakātyāyana/
009.027. labheyāhaṃ bhadanta mahākātyāyana svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
009.028. careyamahaṃ bhavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
009.028. sa āryeṇoktah--śroṇa, tāṃ tāvat pūrvikāṃ pratijñāṃ paripūraya/
009.029. yathāgṛhītān saṃdeśān samarpayeti/
009.029. sa tasyairabhrikasya sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
009.030. viramāsmādasaddharmāt/
009.031. bhoḥ puruṣa, adya mama piturdvādaśavarṣāṇi kālagatasya/
009.032. asti kaścid dṛṣṭaḥ paralokāt punarāgacchan? bhadramukha, eṣo 'hamāgataḥ/
009.032. nāsau śraddadhāti/
009.033. bhadramukha, yadi na śraddadhāsi, sa tava pitā kathayati--asti sūnādhastāt suvarṇasya kalaśaḥ/
body.translated_text: She said: <s>Śroṇa</s>, will you go to <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>? Sister, I will go. He stayed in that very celestial mansion. By her, a command was given to those very <s>pretas</s>: Go, place <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, while still sleeping, in the paternal garden at <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, and come back. He was placed by them in the paternal garden at <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. Having awakened, he sees bells, parasols, fans, and inscriptions written: If <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> is still alive — for his swift coming, for his quick coming; if deceased, passed away — for distinction of destination from the place of rebirth. He considers: If I have been regarded as dead by my parents, why should I enter the house again? I shall go and take ordination in the presence of the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. Then <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> approached the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. The venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> saw <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> from afar. And having seen him, he said this to <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>: Come, <s>Śroṇa</s>, welcome to you. <s>Śroṇa</s>, have you seen this world and the next world? He says: I have seen them, venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. May I, venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, obtain ordination, full admission, and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline). May I practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in your presence. The venerable one said: <s>Śroṇa</s>, first fulfill that prior promise — deliver the messages as received. He approached that barber. Desist from this unrighteous conduct. Sir, it has been twelve years since my father passed away. Is there anyone who has been seen returning from the next world? Good sir, it is I who have come. He does not believe it. Good sir, if you do not believe, your father says: There is a golden pot beneath the butcher's shop.

body.translated_text: 010.001. <s>Pūrṇa</s> stands [here]. 010.001. ‘Unearth it and make yourself properly comfortable. 010.001. And provide the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food from time to time, and dedicate the merit in our name. 010.002. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may go to diminution, exhaustion, and wearing away.’ 010.003. He reflected: ‘Never before have I heard such a thing. 010.003. Let me see — if it turns out to be true, all this will be confirmed.’ 010.004. He went and dug. 010.004. And indeed, everything was exactly as described. 010.004. So he believed. 010.005. Afterward, he went to the adulterer. 010.005. Having approached, he said: ‘Good sir, I have seen your father.’ 010.006. He said: ‘The fruit-ripening of that <s>karma</s> is unpleasant. 010.006. Desist from this evil, wicked practice.’ 010.007. He said: ‘Sir, it has been twelve years since my father died. 010.007. Has anyone been seen by you who went to the other world and returned?’ ‘Good sir, I myself have come [from there].’ 010.008. He did not believe. 010.009. He said: ‘Good sir, if you do not believe, your father placed a pot filled with gold beneath the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> [fire-altar].’ 010.010. He said: ‘Unearth it and make yourself properly comfortable, provide the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food from time to time, and dedicate the merit in our name. 010.011. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may go to diminution, exhaustion, and wearing away.’ 010.012. He reflected: ‘Never before have I heard such a thing. 010.013. Let me see — if it turns out to be true, all this will be confirmed.’ 010.013. He went and dug. 010.013. And indeed, everything was exactly as described. 010.014. So he believed. 010.014. He went to that courtesan. 010.014. Having approached, he said: ‘Sister, I have seen your mother, father, brother, brother’s wife, and maidservant.’ 010.015. They say: ‘The fruit-ripening of that <s>karma</s> is unpleasant. 010.016. Desist from this evil, wicked practice.’ 010.016. She said: ‘Sir, it has been twelve years since my parents died. 010.017. Has anyone been seen by you who went to the other world and returned?’ He said: ‘I myself have come [from there].’ 010.018. She did not believe. 010.018. He said: ‘Sister, if you do not believe, in your ancestral paternal house stand four iron chests filled with gold, and in the middle a golden water-pot with a golden staff. 010.020. They say: “Unearth it and make yourself properly comfortable, provide the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> with alms-food from time to time, and dedicate the merit in our name. 010.022. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may go to diminution, exhaustion, and wearing away.”’ 010.022. She reflected: ‘Never before have I heard such a thing. 010.023. Let me see — if it turns out to be true, all this will be confirmed.’ 010.023. She went and dug. 010.023. And indeed, everything was exactly as described. 010.024. So she believed. 010.024. <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> reflected: ‘This entire world believes in gold, but no one trusts my word alone.’ 010.025. Thereby he became [spiritually] disillusioned. 010.025. In childhood, his teeth had been bound with gold [caps]. 010.026. By that [mark], she recognized him. 010.026. ‘Could it be that the noble <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> [is recognized by] your sisterly folk?’ 010.027. She went and informed his parents: 010.027. ‘Mother! Father! <s>Koṭikarṇa</s> has come!’ 010.028. Many others also informed them. 010.028. They did not believe anyone. 010.028. They said: ‘Daughter, you too are raising our hopes falsely.’ 010.029. Then he himself went. 010.029. Standing in the entrance-vestibule, he cleared his throat. 010.030. That great soul had a golden voice. 010.030. By his sound, the entire house was filled. 010.030. He was recognized by them through his voice. 010.031. They embraced him by the neck and began to weep. 010.031. By their tears, the cataracts [on their eyes] burst open. 010.032. They began to see. 010.032. He said: ‘Mother, father, give me permission. 010.032. I shall go forth from the household life to the homeless life, with complete faith.’

body.text:
011.001. tau kathayatah--putra āvāṃ tvadīyena śokena rudantāvandhībhūtau/
011.001. idānīṃ tvāmevāgamya cakṣuḥ pratilabdham/
011.002. yāvadāvāṃ jīvāmaḥ, tāvanna pravrajitavyam/
011.002. yadā kālaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, tadā pravrajiṣyasi/
011.003. tenāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasyāntikāddharmaṃ śrutvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, mātāpitarau ca śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau/
011.004. āgamacatuṣṭayamadhītam, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
011.005. mātāpitarau satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau//
body.translated_text: 011.001. They said: ‘Son, we two, weeping from grief over you, became blind. 011.001. Only now, upon your return, have we regained our sight. 011.002. As long as we two live, you must not go forth [as a monk]. 011.002. When we die, then you may go forth.’ 011.003. Then, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, he realized the fruit of <s>Srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry), and established his parents in the refuges (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>) and the training-precepts (<s>śikṣāpada</s>). 011.004. He mastered the four <s>Āgamas</s> (canonical collections) and realized the fruit of <s>Sakṛdāgāmi</s> (once-returning). 011.005. He established his parents in the truths (<s>satyas</s>).

body.text:
011.006. apareṇa samayena tasya mātāpitarau kālagatau/
011.006. sa taṃ dhanajātaṃ dīnānāthakṛpaṇebhyo dattvā daridrānadaridrān kṛtvā yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
011.007. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt/
011.008. ekānte sthitaḥ śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇa āyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamidamavocat--labheyāhamāryamahākātyāyana svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām, yāvaccareyāhaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
011.010. sa āyuṣmatā mahākātyāyanena pravrajitaḥ/
011.011. tena pravrajya mātṛkādhītā, anāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
011.011. asmāt parāntakeṣu janapadeṣvalpabhikṣukam/
011.012. kṛcchreṇa deśavargo gaṇaḥ paripūryate/
011.012. sa traimāsīṃ śrāmaṇero dhāritaḥ/
011.012. dharmatā khalu yathā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dvau saṃnipātau bhavataḥ/
011.013. yaccāṣāḍhyāṃ varṣopanāyikāyām yacca kārtikyāṃ pūrṇamāsyām/
011.014. tatra ye āṣāḍhyāṃ varṣopanāyikāyāṃ saṃnipatanti, te tāṃstānuddeśayogamanasikārānudgṛhya paryavāpya tāsu grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu varṣāmupagacchanti/
011.015. ye kārtikyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ saṃnipatanti, te yathādhigatamārocayanti, uttare ca paripṛcchanti sūtrasya vinayasya mātṛkāyāḥ/
011.017. evameva mahāśrāvakāṇāmapi/
011.017. atha ye āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikā bhikṣavas tāṃstānuddeśayogamanasikāraviśeṣān gṛhya paryavāpya tāsu tāsu grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu varṣāmupagatāḥ, te trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayāt kṛtacīvarā niṣṭhitacīvarāḥ samādāya pātracīvaram yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
011.021. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
011.021. ekānte niṣadya yathādhigatamārocayanti, uttare ca paripṛcchanti/
011.022. deśavargo gaṇaḥ paripūrṇaḥ/
011.022. sa tenopasampāditaḥ/
011.023. tena tṛtīyapiṭakamadhītam/
011.023. sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
011.023. arhan saṃvṛttas traidhātukavītarāgo yāvad abhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: 011.006. After some time, his parents passed away. 011.006. Having given that store of wealth to the destitute, the helpless, and the wretched — having made the poor no longer poor — he approached the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. 011.007. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, he stood to one side. 011.008. Standing to one side, <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> said this to the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: ‘May I, O venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, receive the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, so that I may lead the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the Blessed One.’ 011.010. He was given the going-forth by the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. 011.011. Having gone forth, he mastered the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the <s>Abhidharma</s> matrix) and realized the fruit of <s>Anāgāmi</s> (non-returning). 011.011. But in these outlying <s>Parāntaka</s> regions, there were few monks. 011.012. With difficulty was the local quorum for the <s>Saṅgha</s> assembled. 011.012. He was kept as a <s>Śrāmaṇera</s> (novice) for three months. 011.012. It is indeed the rule that the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> have two assemblies: 011.013. one at the <s>Āṣāḍhī</s> (the rainy-season entry) and one at the full moon of <s>Kārtikī</s>. 011.014. Those who assemble at the <s>Āṣāḍhī</s> rainy-season entry, having taken up and mastered various topics, practices, and contemplations, enter the rains-retreat in those villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and capital cities. 011.015. Those who assemble at the full moon of <s>Kārtikī</s> report what they have attained and ask further questions regarding the <s>Sūtra</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the <s>Mātṛkā</s>. 011.017. So too for the great disciples. 011.017. Then, the monks who were co-residents and pupils of the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having taken up and mastered the special topics, practices, and contemplations, and having entered the rains-retreat in those various villages, towns, market-towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, after the passage of the three months of the rains-retreat, having made their robes and completed their robes, taking their bowls and robes, approached the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. 011.021. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> and sat to one side. 011.021. Sitting to one side, they reported what they had attained and asked further questions. 011.022. The local quorum for the <s>Saṅgha</s> was assembled. 011.022. He was given full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>) by him. 011.023. He mastered the third <s>Piṭaka</s> (basket [of scriptures]). 011.023. Through the abandonment of all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), he realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an <s>Arhat</s>). 011.023. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in the three realms, [with all the attainments] up to being one worthy of veneration.

body.text:
011.025. athāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikā āyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanam yāvattāvat paryupāsyāyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamidamavocan--dṛṣṭo 'smābhirupādhyāyaḥ paryupāsitaśca/
011.027. gacchāmo vayam, bhagavantaṃ paryupāsiṣyāmahe/
011.027. sa cāha--vatsā evaṃ kurudhvam/
011.027. draṣṭavyā eva paryupāsitavyā eva hi tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ/
011.027. tena khalu punaḥ samayena śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt saṃnipatitaḥ/
011.029. athāyuṣmāñ śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇa utthāyāsanād ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamyāyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamidamavocat--dṛṣṭo mayopādhyāyānubhāvena sa bhagavān dharmakāyena, no tu rūpakāyena/
011.032. gacchāmi upādhyāya, rūpakāyenāpi taṃ bhagavantaṃ drakṣyāmi/
011.032. sa <12>āha--evaṃ vatsa kuruṣva/
body.translated_text: 011.025. Then the co-residents and pupils of the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having attended upon the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> for some time, said this to the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: ‘We have seen and attended upon our preceptor. 011.027. We shall now go and attend upon the Blessed One.’ 011.027. He said: ‘Sons, do so. 011.027. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly and fully enlightened ones, must indeed be seen and attended upon.’ 011.027. At that time, <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> was seated and assembled in that very congregation. 011.029. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and making a salutation with joined hands toward the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, bowing down, said this to the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: ‘Through the blessing of my preceptor, I have seen that Blessed One in his <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of teaching), but not in his <s>Rūpakāya</s> (physical body). 011.032. I shall go, preceptor, and see that Blessed One in his physical body as well.’ 011.032. He said: ‘Son, do so.’

body.text:
012.001. durlabhadarśanā hi vatsa tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhās tadyathā audumbarapuṣpam/
012.002. asmākaṃ ca vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandasva, alpābādhatāṃ ca yāvat sukhasparśavihāratāṃ ca/
012.003. pañca praśnāṃśca pṛccha--asmāt parāntakeṣu bhadanta janapadeṣu alpabhikṣukam/
012.004. kṛcchreṇa daśavargagaṇaḥ paripūryate/
012.004. tatrāsmābhiḥ kathaṃ pratipattavyam? kharā bhūmī gokaṇṭakā dhānāḥ/
012.005. asmākamaparāntakeṣu janapadeṣu idamevamrūpamāstaraṇaṃ pratyāstaraṇaṃ tadyathā avicarma gocarma cchāgacarma/
012.006. tadanyeṣu janapadeṣu idamevamrūpamāstaraṇaṃ pratyāstaraṇaṃ tadyathā erako merako jandurako mandurakaḥ/
012.007. evamevāsmāt parāntakeṣu janapadeṣvidamevamrūpamāstaraṇaṃ pratyāstaraṇaṃ tadyathā avicarma pūrvavat/
012.008. udakastabdhikā manuṣyāḥ snātopavicārāḥ/
012.008. bhikṣurbhikṣoścīvarakāni preṣayati itaścyutāni tatrāsamprāptāni kasyaitāni naiḥsargikāni/
012.009. adhivāsayati āyuṣmāñchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇa āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
012.010. athāyuṣmāñchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇas tasyā eva rātreratyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vāsavagrāmakaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
012.012. yāvadanupūrveṇa śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
012.012. athāyuṣmāñchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisāmayya pādau prakṣālya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
012.013. upasaṃkramyaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
012.014. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma--gaccha ānanda tathāgatasya śroṇasya ca koṭikarṇasyaikavihāre mañcaṃ prajñāpaya/
012.015. evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmānānandastathāgatasya śroṇasya ca koṭikarṇasya yāvat prajñāpya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
012.016. upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat--prajñapto bhadanta tathāgatasya śroṇasya koṭikarṇasya vihārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, yāvadvihāraṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ/
012.019. yāvat paśyati smṛtiṃ pratimukhamupasthāpya/
012.019. athāyuṣmānapi śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya yāvat pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya/
012.021. tāṃ khalu rātriṃ bhagavān āyuṣmāṃśca śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇa āryeṇa tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsitavān/
012.022. atha bhagavān rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaye āyuṣmantaṃ śroṇaṃ koṭikarṇamāmantrayate sma--pratibhātu te śroṇa dharmo yo mayā svayamabhijñāyābhisambudhyākhyātaḥ/
012.023. athāyuṣmāñ śroṇo bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśah asmāt parāntikayā guptikayā udānāt pārāyaṇāt satyadṛṣṭaḥ śailagāthā munigāthā arthavargīyāṇi ca sūtrāṇi vistareṇa svareṇa svādhyāyaṃ karoti/
012.025. atha bhagavāñchroṇasya koṭikarṇasya kathāparyavasānaṃ viditvā āyuṣmantaṃ śroṇaṃ koṭikarṇamidamavocat--sādhu sādhu śroṇa, madhuraste dharmo bhāṣitaḥ praṇītaśca, yo mayā svayamabhijñāyābhisambudhyākhyātaḥ/
012.028. athāyuṣmataḥ śroṇasya koṭikarṇasyaitadabhavat--ayaṃ me kālo bhagavata upādhyāyasya vacasārocayitumiti viditvotthāyāsanād yāvad bhagavantaṃ praṇamyedamavocat--asmāt parāntakeṣu janapadeṣu vāsavagrāmake bhadantamahākātyāyanaḥ prativasati, yo me upādhyāyaḥ/
012.031. sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandate alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchati yāvat sparśavihāratāṃ ca/
012.032. pañca ca praśnān pṛcchati vistareṇoccārayitavyāni/
012.032. atha bhagavāñcchroṇaṃ koṭikarṇamidamavocat<13>--akālaṃ te śroṇa praśnavyākaraṇāya/
body.translated_text: For <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) are indeed rare to behold, child, just like the <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree) flower. And in our words, bow with your head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), and ask about his good health and comfortable dwelling. And ask five questions: In our outlying provinces (<s>parāntaka</s>), venerable sir, there are few <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). With difficulty is a group of ten completed. How should we proceed there? The ground is rough and thorny like cow-hooves. In our outlying provinces, the bedding and covering is of this kind, namely sheepskin, cowhide, and goatskin. In other provinces, the bedding and covering is of this kind, namely <s>eraka</s>, <s>meraka</s>, <s>janduraka</s>, and <s>manduraka</s> [types of grass mats]. But in our outlying provinces, the bedding and covering is of this kind, namely sheepskin, as before. The people are fond of bathing and walk about after bathing. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> sends robes to another <s>bhikṣu</s>, and they are lost in transit, not having arrived there — to whom are these to be forfeited (<s>naiḥsargika</s>)? The venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> consented to the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> by silence. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, at the passing of that very night, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s> for alms. Gradually he reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, having put away his bowl and robe and having washed his feet, approached the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Having approached, he sat down to one side. There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, prepare a bed in a single dwelling for the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>. 'Yes, venerable sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having prepared [the dwelling] for the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: The dwelling for the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> has been prepared, venerable sir. He approached, entered the dwelling, and sat down. He then established mindfulness face to face. And the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> also, having washed his feet outside the dwelling, entered the dwelling and sat down, crossing his legs, establishing mindfulness face to face. That night, the <s>Bhagavat</s> and the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> spent in noble silence. Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, at the time of dawn, addressed the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>: Let the <s>Dharma</s> occur to you, <s>Śroṇa</s>, which was by me personally realized, fully awakened to, and declared. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>, given opportunity by the <s>Bhagavat</s>, recited aloud at length the <s>Pārāntika Guptikā</s>, the <s>Udāna</s>, the <s>Pārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Satyadṛṣṭa</s>, the <s>Śailagāthās</s>, the <s>Munigāthās</s>, and the <s>Arthavargīya Sūtras</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, knowing the end of <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>'s discourse, said this to the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>: Excellent, excellent, <s>Śroṇa</s>! The <s>Dharma</s> has been spoken by you sweetly and excellently, which was by me personally realized, fully awakened to, and declared. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s> thought: This is the time for me to report the words of my preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) to the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Knowing this, he rose from his seat, bowed to the <s>Bhagavat</s>, and said: In the outlying provinces of <s>Parāntaka</s>, at <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, venerable sir, dwells the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, who is my preceptor. He bows with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> and asks about good health and comfortable dwelling. And he asks the five questions, which are to be recited at length. Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> said this to <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>: It is not the time, <s>Śroṇa</s>, for answering the questions.

body.text:
013.001. saṃghamelakas tatra kālo bhaviṣyati praśnasya vyākaraṇāya/
013.002. atha bhagavān kālyamevotthāya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
013.003. athāyuṣmāñcchroṇaḥ koṭikarṇo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt/
013.004. ekāntasthito bhagavantamidamavocat--asmāt parāntakeṣu janapadeṣu vāsavagrāmake bhadantamahākāyāyanaḥ prativasati, yo me upādhyāyaḥ/
013.005. sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandate alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchati yāvat sparśavihāratāṃ ca/
013.006. pañca ca praśnāti vistareṇoccārayitavyāni yathāpūrvamuktāni yāvat kasya naiḥsargikāni/
013.007. bhagavānāha--tasmādanujānāmi/
013.008. pratyantimeṣu janapadeṣu vinayadharapañcamenopasampadā, sadā snātaḥ, ekapalāśike upānahe dhārayitavye na dvipuṭāṃ na tripuṭām/
013.009. sā cet kṣayadharmiṇī bhavati, tāṃ tyaktvā punar navā grahītavyā/
013.010. bhikṣurbhikṣoścīvarakāni preṣayati itaścyutāni tatrāsamprāptāni na kasyacinnaiḥsargikāṇi/
013.011. āyuṣmān upālī buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati--yaduktaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā pratyantimeṣu janapadeṣu vinayadharapañcamenopasampadam, tatra katamo 'ntaḥ katamaḥ pratyantah? pūrveṇopāli puṇḍavardhanaṃ nāma nagaram, tasya pūrveṇa puṇḍakakṣo nāma parvataḥ, tataḥ pareṇa pratyantaḥ/
013.013. dakṣiṇena śarāvatī nāma nagarī, tasyāḥ pareṇa sarāvatī nāma nadī, so 'ntaḥ, tataḥ pareṇa pratyantaḥ/
013.015. paścimena sthūṇopasthūṇakau brāmaṇagrāmakau, so 'ntaḥ, tataḥ pareṇa pratyantaḥ/
013.015. uttareṇa uśīragiriḥ so 'ntaḥ, tataḥ pareṇa pratyantaḥ//
body.translated_text: When the <s>Saṃgha</s> (monastic community) assembles, that will be the time for answering the questions. Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>, having risen early in the morning, sat down on a prepared seat before the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>. Then the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, having approached the <s>Bhagavat</s> and having bowed with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, stood to one side. Standing to one side, he said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: In the outlying provinces of <s>Parāntaka</s>, at <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, venerable sir, dwells the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, who is my preceptor. He bows with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> and asks about good health and comfortable dwelling. And the five questions are to be recited at length as previously stated, up to: to whom are they forfeited? The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: Therefore I permit ordination (<s>upasampada</s>) in outlying provinces with a quorum of five including a <s>Vinaya</s>-holder (one learned in monastic discipline); [one may be] always bathed; sandals of single <s>palāśa</s> (leaf-leather) may be worn, not double-layered nor triple-layered. If those [sandals] are subject to wear, having discarded them, new ones are to be taken.
