When a <s>bhikṣu</s> sends robes to another <s>bhikṣu</s>, and they are lost in transit, not having arrived there — they are not to be forfeited by anyone. The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>: It was said by the <s>Bhagavat</s>, venerable sir, that ordination in outlying provinces is with a quorum of five including a <s>Vinaya</s>-holder. What is the interior (<s>anta</s>), and what is the outlying (<s>pratyanta</s>)? To the east, <s>Upāli</s>, there is a city called <s>Puṇḍavardhana</s>; to its east is a mountain called <s>Puṇḍakakṣa</s>; beyond that is the outlying region. To the south, there is a city called <s>Śarāvatī</s>; beyond it is a river called <s>Sarāvatī</s> — that is the interior; beyond that is the outlying region. To the west are the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> villages <s>Sthūṇa</s> and <s>Upasthūṇaka</s> — that is the interior; beyond that is the outlying region. To the north is <s>Uśīragiri</s> — that is the interior; beyond that is the outlying region.

body.text:
013.017. kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā śroṇena koṭikarṇena karma kṛtamiti vistaraḥ/
013.017. bhagavānāha--bhūtapūrvam yāvat kāśyapo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho bhagavāñ śāstā loka utpannaḥ/
013.019. tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ dvau jāyāpatikau/
013.019. tābhyāṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāntike śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni udgṛhītāni/
013.020. yadā kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣu nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā kṛkinā catūratnamayaṃ caityaṃ kāritaṃ samantādyojanamuccatvena/
013.022. tena tatra khaṇḍasphuṭapratisaṃskaraṇāya ye pūrvanagaradvāre karapratyāyā uttiṣṭhante, te tasmin stūpe 'nupradattāḥ/
013.023. yadā kṛkī rājā kālagataḥ, tasya putraḥ sujāto nāṃnā sa rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
013.024. tasyāmātyaiḥ stokāḥ karapratyāyā upanāmitāḥ/
013.025. so 'mātyānāmantrayate--kiṃkāraṇamasmākaṃ bhavadbhiḥ stokakarapratyāyā upanāmitāh? kimasmākaṃ vijite karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante? te kathayanti--deva, kutaḥ karapratyāyā prajñāpitāḥ/
013.028. yadi devo 'nujānīyāt, te vayaṃ tān karapratyāyān samucchindāmaḥ/
013.028. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yanmama pitrā kṛtam, devakṛtaṃ na tu brahmakṛtaṃ tat/
013.029. te saṃlakṣayanti--yadi devo 'nujānīte, vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmo yathā svayameva te karapratyāyā notthāsyanti/
013.030. taiḥ sa dvāre baddhvā sthāpitaḥ/
013.031. na bhūyaḥ karapratyāyā utthiṣṭhante/
013.031. tasmin stūpe caṭitakāni prādurbhūtāni/
013.032. tau jāyāpatī vṛddhībhūtau tatraiva stūpe parikarma kurvāṇau tiṣṭhataḥ/
013.032. uttarāpathāt sārthavāhah <14>paṇyamādāya vārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ/
body.translated_text: What <s>karma</s>, venerable sir, was done by the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>? — this at length. The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: In the past, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened one (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), <s>Bhagavat</s>, teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a married couple. By them, the going for refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>) and the training precepts (<s>śikṣāpada</s>) were taken up in the presence of the perfectly enlightened <s>Kāśyapa</s>. When the perfectly enlightened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, having accomplished the entire <s>Buddha</s>-work, passed into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>), a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) made of four [types of] jewels was built by King <s>Kṛkin</s>, one <s>yojana</s> in height on all sides. By him, the taxes (<s>karapratyāya</s>) collected at the eastern city-gate were assigned to that <s>stūpa</s> for repair of cracks and damages. When King <s>Kṛkin</s> passed away, his son named <s>Sujāta</s> was established in the kingdom. His ministers presented him with meager taxes. He addressed the ministers: Why have you presented us with meager taxes? Do taxes not arise in our dominion? They say: Your Majesty, from where have the taxes been allocated? If Your Majesty permits, we shall discontinue those taxes. He says: Sirs, what was done by my father was divinely ordained, not humanly ordained. They consider: If His Majesty permits, we shall act so that those taxes will not arise of their own accord. By them, a [barrier] was set up, blocking that gate. Taxes no longer arose. Cracks appeared in that <s>stūpa</s>. That elderly married couple continued performing maintenance (<s>parikarma</s>) on that very <s>stūpa</s>. A caravan-leader from the northern route (<s>Uttarāpatha</s>), having brought merchandise, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

body.text:
014.001. tenāsau dṛṣṭaḥ stūpaḥ/
014.001. caṭitasphuṭitakaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
014.001. sa dṛṣṭvā pṛcchati--amba tāta kasyaiṣa stūpa iti/
014.002. tau kathayatah--kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya/
014.003. kena kāritah? kṛkinā rājñā/
014.003. na tena rājñāsmin stūpe khaṇḍasphuṭapratisaṃskārakaraṇāya kiṃcit prajñāptam? tau kathayatah--prajñāptam/
014.004. ye pūrvanagaradvāre karapratyāyāste 'smin stūpe khaṇḍasphuṭapratisaṃskaraṇāya niryātitāḥ/
014.005. kṛkī rājā kālagataḥ/
014.005. tasya putraḥ sujāto nāma, sa rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
014.006. tena te karapratyāyāḥ samucchinnāḥ/
014.006. tenāsmin stūpe caṭitasphuṭitakāni prādurbhūtāni/
014.007. tasya ratnakarṇikā karṇe āmuktikā/
014.007. tena sā ratnakarṇikāvatārya tayordattā/
014.008. amba tāta anayā karṇikayāsmin stūpe khaṇḍasphuṭapratisaṃskāraṃ kurutamiti/
014.008. yāvadahaṃ paṇyaṃ visarjayitvā āgacchāmi/
014.009. tataḥ paścād bhūyo 'pi dāsyāmi/
014.009. taistāṃ vikrīya tasmin stūpe khaṇḍasphuṭitapratisaṃskāraḥ kṛtaḥ/
014.010. aparamutsarpitam/
014.010. athāpareṇa samayena sārthavāhaḥ paṇyaṃ visarjayitvā āgataḥ/
014.011. tena sa dṛṣṭaḥ stūpo 'secanakadarśanaḥ/
014.011. dṛṣṭvā ca bhūyasyā mātrayābhiprasannaḥ/
014.012. sa prasādajātaḥ pṛcchati--amba tāta yuṣmābhiḥ kiṃciduddhārikṛtam/
014.013. tau kathayatah--putra nāsmābhiḥ kiṃciduddhārikṛtam/
014.013. kiṃ tvaparamutsarpitaṃ tiṣṭhati/
014.014. tena prasādajātena yattatrāvaśiṣṭam aparaṃ ca dattvā mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam--anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyam/
014.015. evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām/
014.016. evaṃvidhameva śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
014.016. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau sārthavāhaḥ, eṣa evāsau śroṇaḥ koṭikarṇaḥ/
014.017. yadanena kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya stūpe kārāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ/
014.018. mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
014.019. ahamanena kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena sārdhaṃ samajavaḥ samabalaḥ samadhuraḥ samasāmānyaprāptaḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ/
014.020. iti bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ dharmāṇāmekāntaśuklo vipākaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
014.022. tasmāttarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
014.023. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: 014.001. He saw that <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary monument). 014.001. It had become cracked and chipped. 014.001. Having seen it, he asked: 'Mother, father — whose is this <s>stūpa</s>?' 014.002. They said: 'Of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>).' 014.003. 'By whom was it built?' 'By King <s>Kṛkin</s>.' 014.003. 'Did that king not make any provision for the repair of cracks and chips in this <s>stūpa</s>?' They said: 'He did make provision. 014.004. The tax-revenues from the eastern city-gate were allocated for the repair of cracks and chips in this <s>stūpa</s>. 014.005. King <s>Kṛkin</s> passed away. 014.005. His son, named <s>Sujāta</s>, was established in the kingdom. 014.006. By him those tax-revenues were abolished. 014.006. Therefore, cracks and chips appeared in this <s>stūpa</s>.' 014.007. He had a jeweled ear-ornament fastened to his ear. 014.007. Having removed that jeweled ear-ornament, he gave it to the two [parents]. 014.008. 'Mother, father — with this ear-ornament, carry out the repair of cracks and chips in this <s>stūpa</s>. 014.008. I shall come back after selling the merchandise. 014.009. After that, I shall give even more.' 014.009. Having sold it, they carried out the repair of cracks and chips in that <s>stūpa</s>. 014.010. There was a surplus left over. 014.010. Then, on another occasion, the caravan-leader, having sold his merchandise, returned. 014.011. He saw that <s>stūpa</s> — beautiful to behold, like a freshly watered [garden]. 014.011. Having seen it, he was filled with even greater devotion. 014.012. Filled with faith, he asked: 'Mother, father — have you set aside anything?' 014.013. They said: 'Son, we have not set aside anything. 014.013. But there is a surplus left over.' 014.014. Filled with faith, he gave whatever remained there plus additional [offerings], performed a great worship, and made an aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): 'By this root of merit, may I be born in a wealthy family, of great riches, of great resources. 014.015. And may I be a recipient of such <s>dharmas</s> (teachings). 014.016. And may I attend upon just such a Teacher — may I delight [in him] and not turn away!' 014.016. What do you think, monks? He who was that caravan-leader — that was none other than this <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>. 014.017. Because he performed service to the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and made an aspiration, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was born in a wealthy family, of great riches, of great resources. 014.018. Having gone forth in my teaching, by the complete abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. 014.019. I, together with <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, am of equal speed, equal strength, equal sweetness, and equal common attainment — [thus] the Teacher was delighted in, not turned away from. 014.020. Thus, monks, for exclusively dark <s>dharmas</s>, the ripening is exclusively dark; for exclusively bright <s>dharmas</s>, the ripening is exclusively bright; for mixed [<s>dharmas</s>], the ripening is mixed. 014.022. Therefore, monks, having rejected exclusively dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, you should direct your efforts solely toward exclusively bright <s>karmas</s>. 014.023. Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.'

body.text: 014.024. bhikṣava ūcuh--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā śroṇena koṭikarṇena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena dṛṣṭa eva dharme apāyā dṛṣṭāh? bhagavānāha--yadanena māturantike kharavākkarma niścāritam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena dṛṣṭa eva dharme apāyā dṛṣṭā iti//
body.translated_text: 014.024. The monks said: 'Venerable sir, what <s>karma</s> was performed by the venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa</s>, by the ripening of which he saw calamities in this very life?' The Blessed One said: 'Because he uttered harsh speech to his mother, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he saw calamities in this very life.'

body.text:
014.027. idamavocadbhagavān/
014.027. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: 014.027. Thus spoke the Blessed One. 014.027. Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 014.028. iti śrīdivyāvadāne koṭikarṇāvadānaṃ prathamam//
body.translated_text: 014.028. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Koṭikarṇāvadāna</s> (Legend of <s>Koṭikarṇa</s>) is the first.

body.text:
015.000. div2 pūrṇāvadānam/
015.001. bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
015.001. tena khalu samayena sūrpārake nagare nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
015.003. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kulatramānītam/
015.004. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
015.004. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
015.005. sā aṣṭānāṃ navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
015.005. dārako jātaḥ/
015.006. tasya trīṇi saptakāni ekaviṃśatidivasāni vistareṇa jātasya jātamahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti/
015.007. jñātaya ūcuh--ayaṃ dārako bhavasya gṛhapateḥ putraḥ, tasmādbhavatu bhavileti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
015.008. bhūyo 'pyasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ/
015.009. tasya bhavatrāteti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
015.009. punarapyasya putro jātaḥ/
015.010. tasya bhavanandīti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
015.010. yāvadapareṇa samayena bhavo gṛhapatir glānaṃ saṃvṛttaḥ/
015.011. so 'tyarthaṃ paruṣavacanasamudācārī yataḥ, patnyā putraiścāpyupekṣitaḥ/
015.011. tasya preṣyadārikā/
015.012. sā saṃlakṣayati--mama svāminā anekairupāyaśatairbhogāḥ samudānītāḥ/
015.013. sedānīṃ glānaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
015.012. saiṣa patnyā putraiścāpyupekṣitaḥ/
015.013. na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yadahaṃ svāminamadhyupekṣeyamiti/
015.014. sā vaidyasakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--ārya jānīṣe tvaṃ bhavaṃ gṛhapatim? jāne, kiṃ tasya? tasyaivaṃvidhaṃ glānyaṃ samupajātam/
015.015. sa patnyā putraiścāpyupekṣitaḥ/
015.015. tasya bhaviṣajyam (bhaiṣajyam) vyapadiśeti/
015.016. sa kathayati--dārike tvameva kathayasi--sa patnyā putraiścāpyupekṣita iti/
015.017. atha kastasyopasthānaṃ karoti? sā kathayati--ahamasyopasthānaṃ karomi/
015.018. kiṃ tvalpamūlyāni bhaiṣajyāni vyapadiśeti/
015.018. tena vyapadiṣṭam--idaṃ tasya bhaiṣajyamiti/
015.018. tatastayā kiṃcit svabhaktāttasmādeva gṛhādapahṛtyopasthānaṃ kṛtam/
015.019. sa svasthībhūtaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ahaṃ patnyā putraiścādhyupekṣitaḥ/
015.020. yadahaṃ jīvitaḥ, tadasyā dārikāyāḥ prabhāvāt/
015.020. tadasyāḥ pratyupapakāraḥ kartavya iti/
015.021. sā tenoktā--dārike, ahaṃ patnyā putraiścāpyupekṣitaḥ/
015.021. yat kiṃcidahaṃ jīvitaḥ, sarvaṃ tava prabhāvāt/
015.022. ahaṃ te varamanuprayacchāmīti/
015.022. sā kathayati--svāmin, yadi me parituṣṭo 'si, bhavatu me tvayā sārdhaṃ samāgama iti/
015.023. sa kathayati--āryaputra, dūramapi paramapi gatvā dāsyevāham, yadi tu āryaputreṇa sārdhaṃ samāgamo bhavati, evamadāsī bhavāmīti/
015.026. tenāvaśyaṃ nirbandhaṃ jñātvā abhihitā--yadā saṃvṛttā ṛtumatī tadā mamārocayiṣyasīti/
015.026. sā apareṇa samayena kalyā saṃvṛttā ṛtumatī/
015.027. tayā tasyārocitam/
015.027. tato bhavena gṛhapatinā tayā sārdhaṃ paricāritam/
015.028. sā āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
015.028. yameva divasamāpannasattvā saṃvṛttā tameva divasamupādāya bhavasya gṛhapateḥ sarvārthāḥ sarvakarmāntāśca paripūrṇāḥ/
015.029. sā tvaṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
015.030. dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśīrṣaḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāsaḥ/
015.031. yasminneva divase <16>dārako jātaḥ, tasminneva divase bhavasya gṛhapaterbhūyasyā mātrayā sarvārthāḥ sarvakarmāntāḥ paripūrṇāḥ/
body.translated_text: 015.000. The <s>Pūrṇāvadāna</s> (Legend of <s>Pūrṇa</s>). 015.001. The Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. 015.001. At that time, in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, there lived a householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great resources, of extensive and vast possessions, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), comparable to the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. 015.003. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. 015.004. He sported, enjoyed, and took pleasure with her. 015.004. As he sported, enjoyed, and took pleasure, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. 015.005. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. 015.005. A boy was born. 015.006. On his twenty-one days — three times seven — having celebrated the birth festival in elaborate fashion, a name was established: 'What shall the boy's name be?' 015.007. The kinsmen said: 'This boy is the son of the householder <s>Bhava</s>; therefore let his name be <s>Bhavila</s>.' Thus the name was established. 015.008. Again, as he sported, enjoyed, and took pleasure, a son was born to him. 015.009. His name was established as <s>Bhavatrāta</s>. 015.009. Yet again, a son was born to him. 015.010. His name was established as <s>Bhavanandī</s>. 015.010. Then, on another occasion, the householder <s>Bhava</s> fell ill. 015.011. Because he was exceedingly harsh in speech, he was neglected by his wife and sons. 015.011. He had a maidservant. 015.012. She reflected: 'My master accumulated wealth by hundreds of means. 015.013. Now he has fallen ill. 015.012. He has been neglected by his wife and sons. 015.013. It would not be fitting for me to neglect my master.' 015.014. She went to a physician and said: 'Noble sir, do you know the householder <s>Bhava</s>?' 'I do — what about him?' 'Such an illness has afflicted him. 015.015. He has been neglected by his wife and sons. 015.015. Prescribe medicine for him.' 015.016. He said: 'Girl, you yourself say that he has been neglected by his wife and sons. 015.017. Then who attends to him?' She said: 'I attend to him. 015.018. But prescribe inexpensive medicines.' 015.018. He prescribed: 'This is his medicine.' 015.018. Then she, taking some from her own food-ration and from that very household, attended to him. 015.019. He recovered and reflected: 'I was neglected by my wife and sons. 015.020. That I am alive — that is by the power of this maidservant. 015.020. I should repay her favor.' 015.021. He told her: 'Girl, I was neglected by my wife and sons. 015.021. That I am alive at all — it is all by your power. 015.022. I shall grant you a boon.' 015.022. She said: 'Master, if you are pleased with me, let there be union between you and me.' 015.023. He said: 'Noble son, even if I were to go far, to the ends [of the earth], I would still be a slave-woman; but if there is union with the noble master, thus I would become a non-slave.' 015.026. Having recognized her firm insistence, he told her: 'When you have become fertile, you shall inform me.' 015.026. On another occasion, she became healthy and fertile. 015.027. She informed him. 015.027. Then the householder <s>Bhava</s> took pleasure with her. 015.028. She became pregnant. 015.028. From the very day she became pregnant, from that day onward, all the enterprises and works of the householder <s>Bhava</s> were fulfilled. 015.029. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. 015.030. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, of fair complexion, golden-colored, with a head shaped like a parasol, with long arms, with a broad forehead, with joined eyebrows, with a prominent nose. 015.031. On the very day the boy was born, on that very day, the enterprises and works of the householder <s>Bhava</s> were fulfilled to an even greater degree.

body.text:
016.002. tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasāni vistareṇa jātasya jātamahaṃ kṛtvā pūrvavat yāvatpūrṇeti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
016.003. pūrṇo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dvābhyāmaṃsadhātībhyāṃ datto vistareṇa yāvadāśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam/
016.004. yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ, tadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ hastiparīkṣāyāmaśvaparīkṣāyāṃ kumāraparīkṣāyāṃ kumārikāparīkṣāyām/
016.006. aṣṭāsu parīkṣāsūddhaṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
016.007. tato bhavena gṛhapatinā bhavilādīnāṃ putrāṇām yathānupūrvyā niveśāḥ kṛtāḥ/
016.008. te patnībhiḥ sārdhamatīva saṃraktā nivṛttā maṇḍanaparamā vyavasthitāḥ/
016.009. tato bhavo gṛhapatiḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ/
016.009. sa putrairdṛṣṭaḥ puṣṭaśca--tāta, kasmāttvaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthita iti/
016.010. sa kathayati--putrakāḥ, na tāvanmayā niveśaḥ kṛto yāvatsuvarṇalakṣaḥ samudānīta iti/
016.011. te yūyaṃ nirastavyāpārāḥ patnīṣvatyarthaṃ saṃraktā maṇḍanaparamā vyavasthitāḥ/
016.012. mamātyayāt gṛhaṃ śocanīyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
016.012. kathaṃ na cintāparo bhaviṣyāmīti? bhavilena ratnakarṇikā pinaddhā/
016.013. sa tāmavatāryadārukarṇikāṃ pinahya pratijñāmārūḍhah--na tāvat ratnakarṇikāṃ pinahyāmi yāvat suvarṇalakṣaḥ samupārjita iti/
016.014. apareṇa stavakarṇikā/
016.015. apareṇa trapukarṇikā/
016.015. teṣām yāstāḥ saṃjñā bhavilo bhavatrāto bhavanandīti tā antarhitāḥ/
016.016. dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇīti prādurbhūtāḥ/
016.016. te paṇyamādāya mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
016.016. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--tāta, ahamapi mahāsamudraṃ gacchāmīti/
016.017. sa kathayati--putra bālastvam/
016.017. atraiva tiṣṭha, āvāryāṃ vyāpāraṃ kuru/
016.018. sa tatraivāvasthitaḥ/
016.018. te 'pi saṃsiddhayānapātrā āgatāḥ/
016.018. mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya kathayanti--tāta kalyatāmasmadīyaṃ paṇyamiti/
016.019. ten kalitam--ekaikasya suvarṇalakṣāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
016.020. pūrṇenāpi tatraiva dharmeṇa nyāyena vyavahāritāḥ sātirekāḥ suvarṇalakṣāḥ samudānītāaḥ/
016.020. pūrṇo 'pi pituḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--tāta, mamāpi kalyatāmāvārīsamutthitaṃ dravyamiti/
016.021. sa kathayati--putra tvamatraivāvasthitaḥ/
016.022. kiṃ tava kalyate? sa kathayati--tāta kalyatām/
016.022. tathāpi jñātaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
016.023. kalitam yāvannyāyopārjitasya suvarṇasya mūlyaṃ varjayitvā sātiriktā lakṣāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
016.024. bhavo gṛhapatiḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ saṃlakṣayati--puṇyamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvo yenehaiva sthiteneyatsuvarṇaṃ samupārjitamiti/
016.025. yāvadapareṇa samayena bhavo gṛhapatirglānaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
016.025. sa saṃlakṣayati--mamātyayādete bhedaṃ gamiṣyanti/
016.026. upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyamiti/
016.026. tena te 'bhihitāh--putrakāḥ, kāṣṭhāni samudānayateti/
016.027. taiḥ kāṣṭhāni samudānītāni/
016.027. sa kathayati--agniṃ prajvālayateti/
016.028. tairagniḥ prajvālitaḥ/
016.028. bhavo gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--ekaikamalātamapanayateti/
016.029. tairapanītam/
016.029. so 'gnir nivārṇaḥ/
016.029. sa kathayati--putrakāḥ, dṛṣṭo vah? tāta dṛṣṭaḥ/
016.029. sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
016.030. jvalanti sahitāṅgārā bhrātaraḥ sahitāstathā/
016.031. pravibhaktā niśāmyanti yathāṅgārastathā narāḥ//1//
body.translated_text:
016.002. His kinsmen, having assembled and gathered, celebrated the birth festival for twenty-one days — three times seven — in elaborate fashion, and as before, the name '<s>Pūrṇa</s>' was established.
016.003. The boy <s>Pūrṇa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses, including two shoulder-nurses, and in elaborate fashion he grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.
016.004. When he had grown up, he was instructed in writing, arithmetic, calculation, sealing, extraction, deposit, assessment of goods, appraisal of gems, appraisal of elephants, appraisal of horses, appraisal of boys, and appraisal of girls.
016.006. In all eight appraisals he became skilled, eloquent, learned, and shrewd in practice.
016.007. Then the householder <s>Bhava</s> arranged marriages for his sons <s>Bhavila</s> and the others in due order.
016.008. They, together with their wives, became exceedingly attached, idle, and devoted to adornment.
016.009. Then the householder <s>Bhava</s>, resting his cheek on his hand, sat absorbed in worry.
016.009. He was seen by his sons and asked: 'Father, why are you sitting with your cheek on your hand, absorbed in worry?'
016.010. He said: 'Sons, I have not yet arranged a marriage [for the youngest], since a hundred thousand gold pieces have not yet been accumulated.'
016.011. 'You have abandoned all enterprise, become excessively attached to your wives, and are devoted to adornment.
016.012. After my death, the household will fall into ruin.
016.012. How should I not be absorbed in worry?' <s>Bhavila</s> put on a jewel-set ear-ornament.
016.013. He took it off, put on a wooden ear-ornament, and made a vow: 'I shall not put on the jewel ear-ornament until I have earned a hundred thousand gold pieces.'
016.014. Another [put on] a clay ear-ornament.
016.015. Another [put on] a tin ear-ornament.
016.015. Their previous names — <s>Bhavila</s>, <s>Bhavatrāta</s>, <s>Bhavanandī</s> — disappeared.
016.016. [The names] 'Wooden-Ear' (<s>Dārukarṇī</s>), 'Clay-Ear' (<s>Stavakarṇī</s>), and 'Tin-Ear' (<s>Trapukarṇī</s>) arose [instead].
016.016. They, taking merchandise, set out for the great ocean.
016.016. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'Father, I too will go to the great ocean.'
016.017. He said: 'Son, you are [too] young.
016.017. Stay right here; carry on the business at the shop.'
016.018. He remained right there.
016.018. They too returned, having successfully completed their sea voyage.
016.018. After relieving their fatigue from the journey, they said: 'Father, tally up our merchandise.'
016.019. He tallied it — each one had accumulated a hundred thousand gold pieces.
016.020. <s>Pūrṇa</s> too, right there, had accumulated more than a hundred thousand gold pieces through righteous and lawful commerce.
016.020. <s>Pūrṇa</s> also fell at his father's feet and said: 'Father, please tally the goods I have raised from the shop as well.'
016.021. He said: 'Son, you stayed right here.
016.022. What is there for you to tally?' He said: 'Father, please tally it.
016.022. Even so, it will be known.'
016.023. It was tallied, and excluding the cost-price of the goods lawfully earned, more than a hundred thousand [gold pieces] had been accumulated.
016.024. The householder <s>Bhava</s>, filled with joy and delight, reflected: 'This being is named Great Lord of Merit (<s>Puṇyamaheśa</s>), for even while staying here, he has earned this much gold.'
016.025. Then, at another time, the householder <s>Bhava</s> fell ill.
016.025. He reflected: 'After my death, these [sons] will fall into discord.
016.026. A stratagem must be devised.'
016.026. He addressed them: 'Sons, gather firewood.'
016.027. They gathered firewood.
016.027. He said: 'Light a fire.'
016.028. They lit a fire.
016.028. The householder <s>Bhava</s> said: 'Remove one firebrand each.'
016.029. They removed [them].
016.029. The fire went out.
016.029. He said: 'Sons, did you see?' 'Yes, father, we saw.'
016.029. He recited a verse:
016.030. 'Embers burn when together; brothers are likewise when united.
016.031. Separated, they are extinguished — as with embers, so with men.' // 1 //

body.text:
017.001. <17>putrakāḥ, na yuṣmābhirmamātyayāt strīṇāṃ śrotavyam/
017.002. kuṭumbaṃ bhidyate strībhirvāgbhirbhidyanti kātarāḥ/
017.003. durnyasto bhidyate mantraḥ prītirbhidyate lobhataḥ//2// iti//
body.translated_text:
017.001. 'Sons, after my death you must not listen to women.
017.002. A family is split apart by women; the timid are split by [harsh] words.
017.003. A poorly kept counsel is split apart; affection is split by greed.' // 2 //

body.text:
017.004. te niṣkrāntāḥ/
017.004. bhavilastatraivāvasthitaḥ/
017.004. sa tenoktah--putra, na kadācit tvayā pūrṇo moktavyaḥ/
017.005. puṇyamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvaḥ/
017.005. ityuktvā--
017.006. sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ/
017.007. samyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam//3//
body.translated_text:
017.004. They went out.
017.004. <s>Bhavila</s> remained right there.
017.004. He [<s>Bhava</s>] said to him: 'Son, you must never abandon <s>Pūrṇa</s>.
017.005. This being is named Great Lord of Merit (<s>Puṇyamaheśa</s>).'
017.005. Having said this —
017.006. 'All accumulations end in loss; all elevations end in a fall.
017.007. All unions end in separation; and life ends in death.' // 3 //

body.text:
017.008. iti kāladharmeṇa samyuktaḥ/
017.008. tair nīlapītalohitāvadātairvastraiḥ śibikāmalaṃkṛtya mahatā saṃskāreṇa śmaśānaṃ nītvā dhmāpitaḥ/
017.009. tataste śokavinodanaṃ kṛtvā kathayanti--yadā asmākaṃ pitā jīvati, tadā tadadhīnāḥ prāṇāḥ/
017.010. yadidānīṃ nirastavyāpārāstiṣṭhāmaḥ, gṛḥpamavasādaṃ gamiṣyati/
017.011. na śobhanaṃ bhaviṣyati/
017.011. yannu vayaṃ paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gacchāma iti/
017.011. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--yadyevamahamapi gacchāmīti/
017.012. te kathayanti--tvamatraivāvāryāṃ vyāpāraṃ kuru, vayameva gacchāma iti/
017.013. te paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ/
017.013. pūrṇo nyastasarvakāryastatraivāvasthitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
017.008. Thus he was joined with the law of time [i.e., he died].
017.008. They adorned a bier with blue, yellow, red, and white cloths, carried him to the cremation ground with great ceremony, and cremated him.
017.009. Then, having dispelled their grief, they said: 'When our father was alive, our livelihood depended on him.
017.010. If we now remain idle, the household will fall into decline.
017.011. That will not be good.
017.011. Let us take merchandise and go to another country.'
017.011. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'If so, I too will go.'
017.012. They said: 'You stay right here and carry on the business at the shop; we ourselves will go.'
017.013. They took merchandise and went to another country.
017.013. <s>Pūrṇa</s>, having been entrusted with all affairs, remained right there.

body.text:
017.014. dharmatā khalu īśvaragṛheṣu divasaparivyayo dīyate/
017.014. tāsteṣāṃ patnyo dārikāḥ parivyayanimittaṃ preṣayanti/
017.015. pūrṇo 'pi dhanibhiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairanyaiścājīvibhiḥ parivṛto 'vatiṣṭhate/
017.016. tāstvavakāśaṃ na labhante/
017.016. yadā te upasthāya prakrāntā bhavanti, tadā tāsāṃ divasaparivyayaṃ dadāti/
017.016. tā dārikāściracirādāgacchantītyupālabhyante/
017.017. tā evamarthaṃ vistareṇārocayanti/
017.018. tāḥ kathayanti--evaṃ hi teṣāṃ bhavati, yeṣāṃ dāsīputrāḥ kuleṣvaiśvacaryaṃ vaśe vartayantīti/
017.019. bhavilapatnyā dārikā abhihitā--tvayā kālaṃ jñātvā gantavyamiti/
017.019. sā kālaṃ jñātvā gacchati, śīghraṃ labhate/
017.020. anyāścirayanti/
017.020. tābhiḥ sā pṛṣṭhā--tayā samākhyātam/
017.020. tā api tayā sārdhaṃ gantumārabdhāḥ/
017.021. tā api śīghraṃ pratilabhante/
017.021. tāḥ svābhinībhiruktāh--kimatra kāraṇamidānīṃ śīghramāgacchatheti/
017.022. tāḥ kathayanti--ārogyaṃ jyeṣṭhabhavikāyāa bhavatu/
017.022. yadā tasyā dārikā gatā bhavati, tadā labhyate/
017.023. vayaṃ tayā sārdhaṃ gacchāma iti/
017.023. tāḥ saṃjātāmarṣāḥ kathayanti--evaṃ hi teṣāṃ bhavati yeṣāṃ dāsīputrāḥ kulesvaiścaryaṃ vaśe vartayantīti/
017.024. yāvadapareṇa samayena bhavilo bhavatrāto bhavanandī ca sahitāḥ samagrāḥ saṃmodamānā mahāsamudrāt saṃsiddhayānapātrā āgatāḥ/
017.026. bhavilena patnī pṛṣṭā--bhadre, śobhanaṃ pūrṇena pratipālitā tvamiti? sā kathayati--yathā bhrātrā putreṇa veti/
017.027. te anye 'pi svāmibhyāṃ pṛṣṭe kathayatah--evaṃ hi teṣāṃ bhavati, yeṣāṃ dāsīputrāḥ kuleṣvaiścaryaṃ vaśe vartayantīti/
017.028. tau saṃlakṣayatah--suhṛdbhedakāḥ striyo bhavantīti/
017.029. yāvadapareṇa samayena kāśikavastrāvārī udghāṭitā/
017.029. tatsamanantaraṃ bhavilasya putro gataḥ/
017.030. sa pūrṇena kāśikavastrayugenācchāditaḥ/
017.030. anyābhyāṃ dṛṣṭvā svaputrāḥ preṣitā yāvat kāśikavastrāvārī ghaṭṭitā, phuṭṭakavastrāvārī udghāṭitā/
017.031. te ca daivayogāt saṃprāptāḥ/
017.031. te pūrṇena phuṭṭakairvastrairācchāditāḥ/
017.032. te dṛṣṭvā svāminoḥ kathayatah--dṛṣṭam yuvābhyāmapareṣāṃ kāśikavastrāṇi<18> dīyante, pareṣāṃ phuṭṭakānīti/
body.translated_text:
017.014. Now, it is the custom that in the households of lords, a daily allowance is given.
017.014. The wives of those [brothers] sent maidservants to [receive] the daily allowance.
017.015. But <s>Pūrṇa</s> was always surrounded by wealthy men, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, and other businessmen.
017.016. The maidservants could not find an opportunity [to approach him].
017.016. When those [visitors] had come and departed, then he would give them their daily allowance.
017.016. The maidservants were scolded [by their mistresses] for taking so long to return.
017.017. They explained the matter in detail.
017.018. They [the wives] said: 'This is what happens when the sons of slave-women exercise lordship in [noble] households.'
017.019. <s>Bhavila</s>'s wife instructed her maidservant: 'You should go at the right time.'
017.019. She went at the right time and received [the allowance] quickly.
017.020. The others were delayed.
017.020. They asked her, and she explained.
017.020. They too began going along with her.
017.021. They too received [their allowance] quickly.
017.021. Their mistresses asked them: 'What is the reason you now return quickly?'
017.022. They said: 'Good health to the senior sister <s>Bhavika</s>!
017.022. When her maidservant has gone, [the allowance] is given.
017.023. We go along with her.'
017.023. They, filled with resentment, said: 'This is what happens when the sons of slave-women exercise lordship in [noble] households.'
017.024. Then, at another time, <s>Bhavila</s>, <s>Bhavatrāta</s>, and <s>Bhavanandī</s>, united and all together, returned joyfully from the great ocean, having successfully completed their sea voyage.
017.026. <s>Bhavila</s> asked his wife: 'Dear one, were you well looked after by <s>Pūrṇa</s>?' She said: 'As by a brother, as by a son.'
017.027. The other two were also asked by their husbands, and they said: 'This is what happens when the sons of slave-women exercise lordship in [noble] households.'
017.028. The two reflected: 'Women are the splitters of friendship.'
017.029. Then, at another time, a sale of <s>Kāśika</s> cloth was opened.
017.029. Immediately after, <s>Bhavila</s>'s son came.
017.030. He was dressed by <s>Pūrṇa</s> in a pair of <s>Kāśika</s> garments.
017.030. When the other two [wives] saw this, they sent their sons, but the <s>Kāśika</s> cloth sale had closed and the coarse-cloth sale had opened.
017.031. And they arrived by chance [at that time].
017.031. They were dressed by <s>Pūrṇa</s> in coarse garments.
017.032. They saw and told their husbands: 'Look, you two — others are given <s>Kāśika</s> garments, while ours are given coarse cloth.'

body.text:
018.001. tābhyāmanusaṃjñaptirdattā/
018.001. kimetadeva bhaviṣyati? nūnaṃ kāśikavastrāvārī ghaṭṭitā, phuṭṭakavastrāvārī udghāṭiteti/
018.002. yāvadapareṇa samayena śarkarāvārī udghaṭitā/
018.003. bhavilasya ca putro gataḥ/
018.003. tena śarkarākho{mo}dako labdhaḥ/
018.003. taṃ dṛṣṭvā anyābhyāṃ svaputrāḥ preṣitāḥ/
018.004. te daivayogād guḍāvāryāmudghāṭitāyāṃ gatāḥ/
018.004. tairguḍo labdhaḥ/
018.004. tābhistaṃ dṛṣṭvā svāminau tathā tathā bhagnau yathā gṛhavibhāgaṃ kartumārabdhau/
018.005. tau parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurutah--sarvathā vinaṣṭā vayam, gṛhaṃ bhājayāmeti/
018.006. ekaḥ kathayati--jyeṣṭhataraṃ śabdayāmaḥ/
018.006. ekaḥ kathayati--vicārayāmastāvat kathaṃ bhājayāmeti/
018.007. tau svabuddhyā vicārayataḥ/
018.007. ekasya gṛhagataṃ kṣetragataṃ ca, ekasyāvārīgataṃ deśāntaragataṃ ca, ekasya pūrṇakaḥ/
018.008. yadi jyeṣṭhataro gṛhagataṃ kṣetragataṃ ca grahīṣyati, śaknumo vayamāvārīgatena deśāntaragatena cātmānaṃ saṃdhārayitum/
018.010. athāvārīgataṃ deśāntaragataṃ ca grahīṣyati, tathāpi vayaṃ śknumo gṛhagatena kṣetragatena cātmānaṃ saṃdhārayitum, pūrṇakasya ca māryādābandhaṃ kartumiti/
018.011. tāvevaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kṛtvā bhavilasya sakāśaṃ gatau/
018.012. bhrātaḥ, vinaṣṭā vayaṃ bhājayāmo gṛhamiti/
018.012. sa kathayati--suparīkṣitaṃ kartavyam, gṛhabhedikāḥ striyo bhavantīti/
018.013. tau kathayatah--pratyakṣīkṛtamasmābhiḥ, bhājayāmeti/
018.014. sa kathayati--yadevam, āhūyantāṃ kulānīti/
018.014. tau kathayatah--pūrvamevāsmābhirbhājitam/
018.015. ekasya gṛhagataṃ kṣetragataṃ ca, ekasyāvārīgataṃ deśāntaragataṃ ca, ekasya pūrṇakaḥ/
018.016. sa kathayati--pūrṇasya pratyaṃśaṃ nānuprayacchatha? tau kathayatah--dāsīputraḥ saḥ/
018.016. kastasya pratyaṃśaṃ dadyāt? api tu sa evāsmābhirbhājitaḥ/
018.017. yadi tavābhipretaṃ tameva gṛhāṇeti/
018.017. sa saṃlakṣayati--ahaṃ pitrā abhihitah--sarvasvamapi te parityajya pūrṇo grahītavya iti/
018.018. gṛhṇāmi pūrṇamiti viditvā kathayati--evaṃ bhavatu mama pūrṇaketi/
018.019. yasya gṛhagataṃ kṣetragataṃ ca, sa tvaramāṇo gṛhaṃ gatvā kathayati--jyeṣṭhabhavike nirgaccha/
018.020. sā nirgatā/
018.020. mā bhūyaḥ pravekṣyasi/
018.021. kasyārthāya? asmābhirbhājitaṃ gṛham/
018.021. yasyāvārīgataṃ deśāntaragataṃ ca, so 'pi tvaramāṇa āvārīṃ gatvā kathayati--pūrṇaka avatareti/
018.022. so 'vatīrṇaḥ/
018.022. mā bhūyo 'bhirokṣyasi/
018.022. kiṃ kāraṇam? asmābhirbhājitam/
018.023. yāvat bhavilapatnī pūrṇakena sārdhaṃ jñātigṛhaṃ saṃprasthitā/
018.024. dārakā bubhikṣitā roditumārabdhāḥ/
018.024. sā kathayati--pūrṇa, dārakāṇāṃ pūrvabhakṣikāmanuprayaccheti/
018.025. sa kathayati--kārṣāpaṇaṃ prayaccha/
018.025. sā kathayati--tvayā iyatībhiḥ suvarṇalakṣābhirvyavahṛtam, dārakāṇāṃ pūrvabhikṣikāpi nāsti? pūrṇaḥ kathayati--kimahaṃ jāne yuṣmākaṃ gṛhe īdṛśīyamavasthā bhaviṣyatīti/
018.027. yadi mayā jñātamabhaviṣyat, mayā anekāḥ suvarṇalakṣāḥ saṃhāritā abhaviṣyan/
018.028. dharmataiṣā striya ārakūṭākārṣāpaṇān vastrānte badhnanti/
018.028. tayārakūṭamāṣako dattah--pūrvabhakṣikāmānayeti/
018.029. sa tamādāya vīthīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
018.029. anyatamaśca puruṣaḥ samudravelāpreritānāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ bhāramādāya śītenābhidruto vepamāna āgacchati/
018.030. sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaśca--bhoḥ puruṣa, kasmādevaṃ vepase? sa kathayati--ahamapi na jāne/
018.031. mayā cāyaṃ bhāraka utkṣipto bhavati, mama cedṛśī samavasthā/
018.032. sa dāruparīkṣāyāṃ kṛtāvī/
018.032. sa tat kāṣṭhaṃ nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ/
018.032. paśyati tatra <19>gośīrṣacandanam/
body.translated_text: 018.001. A signal was given by those two [wives]. 018.001. 'What will come of this? Surely the fine-cloth shop has been interfered with, and the coarse-cloth shop has been opened!' 018.002. Then, on another occasion, the sugar shop was opened. 018.003. And <s>Bhavila</s>'s son went [there]. 018.003. He obtained sugar confections. 018.003. Seeing that, the other two [wives] sent their own sons. 018.004. By chance, they arrived when the molasses shop had been opened. 018.004. They obtained molasses. 018.004. Those two [wives], seeing that, provoked their husbands to such a degree that they began to divide the household property. 018.005. The two consulted with each other: 'We are completely ruined! Let us divide the household.' 018.006. One said: 'Let us call the eldest brother.' 018.006. The other said: 'Let us first consider how we shall divide.' 018.007. The two deliberated by their own judgment. 018.007. For one — the house property and the field property; for another — the shop property and the goods abroad; and for one — <s>Pūrṇaka</s> [the slave]. 018.008. 'If the eldest brother takes the house property and the field property, we can sustain ourselves with the shop property and the goods abroad.' 018.010. 'But if he takes the shop property and the goods abroad, even so we can sustain ourselves with the house property and the field property, and also impose restrictions on <s>Pūrṇaka</s>.' 018.011. Having thus conferred, the two went to <s>Bhavila</s>. 018.012. 'Brother, we are ruined — let us divide the household.' 018.012. He said: 'This should be done with careful examination — women are home-wreckers.' 018.013. The two said: 'We have verified it with our own eyes. Let us divide.' 018.014. He said: 'If so, let the family elders be summoned.' 018.014. The two said: 'We have already made the division ourselves. 018.015. For one — the house property and field property; for another — the shop property and goods abroad; and for one — <s>Pūrṇaka</s>.' 018.016. He said: 'Will you not give <s>Pūrṇa</s> his share?' The two said: 'He is a slave-woman's son! 018.016. Who would give him a share? Rather, he himself has been allotted by us. 018.017. If you wish, take him yourself.' 018.017. He reflected: 'My father told me: "Even giving up all your possessions, <s>Pūrṇa</s> should be taken."' 018.018. Knowing this, he said: 'Let it be so — <s>Pūrṇaka</s> is mine.' 018.019. The one who received the house property and field property, hurrying home, said: 'Eldest sister-in-law, leave!' 018.020. She left. 018.020. 'You shall not enter again!' 018.021. 'For what reason?' 'The household has been divided by us.' 018.021. The one who received the shop property and goods abroad also hurried to the shop and said: '<s>Pūrṇaka</s>, come down!' 018.022. He came down. 018.022. 'You shall not go up again!' 018.022. 'For what reason?' 'The household has been divided by us.' 018.023. Then <s>Bhavila</s>'s wife, together with <s>Pūrṇaka</s>, set out for her relatives' house. 018.024. The children, hungry, began to cry. 018.024. She said: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, give the children their morning meal!' 018.025. He said: 'Give me a coin (<s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>).' 018.025. She said: 'You, who dealt in so many hundreds of thousands of gold coins — there is not even a morning meal for the children?' <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'How was I to know that such a situation would arise in your household? 018.027. If I had known, I would have saved many hundreds of thousands of gold coins.' 018.028. It is the nature of women to tie copper coins in the hem of their garments. 018.028. She gave him a copper coin: 'Bring the morning meal.' 018.029. Taking it, he set out along the street. 018.029. And a certain man, carrying a load of wood washed ashore by the sea, came shivering, distressed by the cold. 018.030. He was seen by <s>Pūrṇa</s> and asked: 'Sir, why do you tremble so?' He said: 'I too do not know. 018.031. When I lifted this load, this condition of mine [arose].' 018.032. He [<s>Pūrṇa</s>] was skilled in the examination of timber. 018.032. He began to inspect that wood. 018.032. He saw there — <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood (ox-head sandalwood)!

body.text:
019.001. sa tenābhihitah--bho puruṣa, kiyatā mūlyena dīyate? pañcabhiḥ kārṣāpaṇaśataiḥ/
019.002. tena taṃ kāṣṭhabhāraṃ gṛhītvā tadgośīrṣacandanamapanīya vīthīṃ gatvā karapatrikayā catasraḥ khaṇḍikāḥ kṛtāḥ/
019.003. taccūrṇakasyārthaṃ kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa vikrītaṃ vartate/
019.003. tatastasya puruṣasya pañcakārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāni/
019.004. uktaṃ ca--enaṃ kāṣṭhabhārakamamuṣmin gṛhe bhavilapatnī tiṣṭhati tatra naya, vaktavyā pūrṇena preṣiteti/
019.005. tenāsau nīto yathāvṛttaṃ cārocitam/
019.005. sā urasi prahāraṃ dattvā kathayati--yadyasāvarthātparibhraṣṭaḥ, kiṃ prajñayāpi paribhraṣṭah? pakvamānayeti pācanaṃ preṣitam/
019.007. tadeva nāsti yat paktavyamiti/
019.007. pūrṇena śeṣakatipayakārṣāpaṇairdāsadāsīgomahiṣīvastrāṇi jīvitopakaraṇāni pakvamādāyāgatya dampatyorupanāmitavān/
019.008. tena kuṭumbaṃ saṃtoṣitam//
body.translated_text: 019.001. He was asked by him: 'Sir, for how much will [this load] be sold?' 'For five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.' 019.002. Having taken that load of wood from him, he removed the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood, went to the street, and with a hand-saw made four blocks from it. 019.003. The powder alone was sold for a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>. 019.003. Then he gave five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> to that man. 019.004. And he said: 'Take this load of wood to the house where <s>Bhavila</s>'s wife is staying, and tell her: "Sent by <s>Pūrṇa</s>."' 019.005. It was taken by him, and the events were reported as they happened. 019.005. She, striking her chest, said: 'If he has lost his wealth, has he lost his intelligence too? Bring [something] cooked!' — and she sent [someone] to cook. 019.007. 'But there is nothing to cook!' 019.007. <s>Pūrṇa</s>, with the remaining <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, purchased slaves, maidservants, cows, buffaloes, garments, and provisions for livelihood, brought cooked [food], and presented it to the couple. 019.008. With that, the household was gratified.

body.text:
019.009. atrāntare saurpārakīyo rājā dāhajvareṇa viklavībhūtaḥ/
019.009. tasya vaidyairgośīrṣacandanamupā diṣṭam/
019.010. tato 'mātyā gośīrṣacandanaṃ samanveṣayitumārabdhāḥ/
019.010. tairvīthyāṃ pāramparyeṇa śrutam/
019.010. te pūrṇasya sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayanti--tavāsti gośīrṣacandanam? sa āha--asti/
019.011. te ūcuh--kiyatā mūlyena dīyate? sa āha--kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa/
019.012. taiḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa gṛhītvā rājñaḥ pralepo dattaḥ, svasthībhūtaḥ/
019.013. rājā saṃlakṣayati--kīdṛśo 'sau yasya gṛhe gośīrṣacandanaṃ nāsti/
019.013. rājā pṛcchati--kuta etat? deva pūrṇāt/
019.014. āhūyatāṃ pūrṇakaḥ/
019.014. sa dūtena gatvā uktah--pūrṇa, devastvāṃ śabdāpayatīti/
019.015. sa vicārayitumārabdhah--kimarthaṃ māṃ rājā śabdāpayati? sa saṃlakṣayati--gośīrṣacandanenāsau rājā svasthībhūtaḥ/
019.016. tadarthaṃ māṃ śabdāyati/
019.016. sarvathā gośīrṣacandanamādāya gantavyam/
019.017. sa gośīrṣacandanasya tisro gaṇḍikā vastreṇa pidhāyaikaṃ pāṇinā gṛhītvā rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
019.018. rājñā pṛṣṭah--pūrṇa, asti kiṃcid gośīrṣacandanam/
019.018. sa kathayati--deva idamasti/
019.019. kimasya mūlyam? deva suvarṇalakṣāḥ/
019.019. aparamasti? deva asti/
019.019. tena tāstisro gaṇḍikā darśitāḥ/
019.020. rājñāmātyānāmājñā dattā--pūrṇasya catasraḥ suvarṇalakṣāḥ prayacchateti/
019.021. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--deva, tisro dīyantām/
019.021. ekagaṇḍikā devasya prābhṛtamiti/
019.021. tatastasya tisro dattāḥ/
019.022. rājā kathayati--pūrṇa, parituṣṭo 'ham/
019.022. vada kiṃ te varamanuprayacchāmīti/
019.022. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--yadi me devaḥ parituṣṭo devasya vijate 'paribhūto vaseyamiti/
019.023. rājñā amātyānāmājñā dattā--bhavantaḥ, adyāgreṇa kumārāṇāmājñā deyā na tvevaṃ pūrṇasyeti/
019.024. yāvanmahāsamudrāt pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni saṃsiddhayānapātrāṇi sūrpārakaṃ nagaramanuprāptāni/
019.025. vaṇiggrāmeṇa kriyākāraḥ kṛtah--na kenacidasmākaṃ samastānāṃ nirgatyaikākinā vaṇijāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkramitavyam/
019.026. gaṇa eva saṃbhūya bhāṇḍaṃ grahīṣyatīti/
019.027. apare kathayanti--pūrṇamapi śabdāpayāmaḥ/
019.027. anye kathayanti--kiṃ tasya kṛpaṇasyāsti yaḥ śabdāyata iti/
019.028. tena khalu samayena pūrṇo bahirnirgataḥ/
019.028. tena śrutaṃ mahāsamudrāt pañca vaṇikchatāni saṃsiddhayānapātrāṇi sūrpārakaṃ nagaramanuprāptānīti/
019.030. so 'praviśyaiva nagaraṃ teṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
019.030. pṛcchati--bhavataḥ, kimidaṃ dravyamiti? te kathayanti--idaṃ cedaṃ ceti/
019.031. kiṃ mūlyam? te kathayanti--sārthavāha, dūramapi paramapi gatvā tvameva praṣṭavyaḥ/
019.032. yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi ucyatāṃ mūlyam/
019.032. tairaṣṭādaśa suvarṇalakṣā mūlyamupadiṣṭam/
019.032. sa <20>kathayati--bhavantastisro lakṣā avadraṃgaṃ gṛhṇīta, mamaitat/
body.translated_text: 019.009. Meanwhile, the king of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> became afflicted with a burning fever. 019.009. <s>Gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood was prescribed for him by the physicians. 019.010. Then the ministers began to search for <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood. 019.010. By word of mouth along the street, they heard [about it]. 019.010. They went to <s>Pūrṇa</s> and asked: 'Do you have <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood?' He said: 'I do.' 019.011. They said: 'For how much will it be sold?' He said: 'For a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.' 019.012. Having purchased it for a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, they applied it as an ointment to the king, [and] he was restored to health. 019.013. The king reflected: 'What kind of person is this, in whose house there is no <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood?' 019.013. The king asked: 'Where did this come from?' 'Your Majesty, from <s>Pūrṇa</s>.' 019.014. 'Summon <s>Pūrṇaka</s>.' 019.014. A messenger went and told him: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, the king summons you.' 019.015. He began to deliberate: 'For what purpose does the king summon me?' He reflected: 'The king has been restored to health by the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood. 019.016. It is for that purpose he summons me. 019.016. By all means, I should go taking <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood.' 019.017. He covered three blocks of <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood with cloth, held one in his hand, and went to the king's presence. 019.018. The king asked: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, is there any <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood?' 019.018. He said: 'Your Majesty, here it is.' 019.019. 'What is its price?' 'Your Majesty, hundreds of thousands of gold coins.' 019.019. 'Is there more?' 'Your Majesty, there is.' 019.019. He showed those three blocks. 019.020. The king gave orders to the ministers: 'Give <s>Pūrṇa</s> four hundred thousand gold coins.' 019.021. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'Your Majesty, let three [hundred thousand] be given. 019.021. One block is a gift for Your Majesty.' 019.021. Then three [hundred thousand] were given to him. 019.022. The king said: '<s>Pūrṇa</s>, I am pleased. 019.022. Tell me — what boon shall I grant you?' 019.022. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'If Your Majesty is pleased with me, may I live without being slighted in Your Majesty's domain.' 019.023. The king gave orders to the ministers: 'Sirs, from today onward, orders are to be given to the princes, but not in this manner to <s>Pūrṇa</s>.' 019.024. Then five hundred merchants, with their vessels successfully [returned], arrived at the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> from the great ocean. 019.025. The merchant-guild made a resolution: 'None of us shall separately approach the merchants alone — 019.026. the guild itself, having assembled together, shall purchase the merchandise.' 019.027. Others said: 'Let us summon <s>Pūrṇa</s> too.' 019.027. Others said: 'What does that pauper have? Why summon him?' 019.028. Now at that time, <s>Pūrṇa</s> had gone outside [the city]. 019.028. He heard that five hundred merchants with successful vessels had arrived at the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> from the great ocean. 019.030. Without even entering the city, he went directly to their presence. 019.030. He asked: 'Sirs, what merchandise is this?' They said: 'This and this.' 019.031. 'What is the price?' They said: 'Caravan-leader, even if you go far and wide, you yourself are the one to be asked.' 019.032. 'Even so, state the price.' 019.032. They quoted eighteen hundred thousand gold coins as the price. 019.032. He said: 'Sirs, take three hundred thousand as an advance payment — this [merchandise] is mine.'

body.text:
020.001. paṇyamavaśiṣṭaṃ dāsyāmi/
020.001. tathā bhavatu/
020.002. tena tisro lakṣā ānāyya dattāḥ/
020.002. svamudrālakṣitaṃ ca kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ/
020.002. tato vaṇiggrāmeṇāvacarakāḥ puruṣāḥ preṣitāh--paśyata kiṃ dravyamiti/
020.003. tairgatvā pṛṣṭāh--kiṃ dravyam? idaṃ cedaṃ ca/
020.004. asmākamapi pūrṇāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi tiṣṭhanti/
020.004. pūrṇāni vā bhavantu mā vā/
020.004. api vikrītam/
020.005. kasyāntike? pūrṇasya/
020.005. prabhūtamāsādayiṣyatha pūrṇasyāntikād vikrīya/
020.005. te kathayanti--yattenāvadraṅge dattaṃ tad yūyaṃ mūlye 'pi na dāsyatha/
020.006. kiṃ tenāvadraṅge dattam? tisraḥ suvarṇalakṣāḥ/
020.007. sumuṣitāstena bhrātaraḥ kṛtāḥ/
020.007. tairāgatya vaṇiggrāmasyārocitam/
020.007. tatpaṇyaṃ vikrītam/
020.008. kasyāntike? pūrṇasya/
020.008. prabhūtamāsādayiṣyanti pūrṇasyāntike vikrīya/
020.008. yātenāvadraṅge dattaṃ tadyūyaṃ mūlye 'pi na dāsyatha/
020.009. kiṃ tenāvadraṅge dattam? tisraḥ suvarṇalakṣāḥ/
020.010. sumuṣitāstena te bhrātaraḥ kṛtāḥ/
020.010. sa tairāhūyoktah--pūrṇa vaṇiggrāmeṇa kriyākāraḥ kṛtah--na kenacidekākinā grahītavyam/
020.011. vaṇiggrāma eva grahīṣyatītyeva/
020.011. kasmātte gṛhītam? sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yadā yuṣmābhiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtastadā kimahaṃ na śabdito mama bhrātā vā? yuṣmābhireva kriyākāraḥ kṛto yūyameva pālayata/
020.013. tato vaṇiggrāmeṇa saṃjātāmarṣeṇa ṣaṣṭeḥ kārṣāpaṇānāmarthāyātape dhāritaḥ/
020.014. rājñaḥ pauruṣeyairdṛṣṭaḥ/
020.014. tai rājñe ārocitam/
020.014. rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, śabdayataitān/
020.015. taiḥ śabditāḥ/
020.015. kathayati rājā--bhavantaḥ, kasyārthe yuṣmābhiḥ pūrṇa ātape vidhāritah? te kathayanti--deva vaṇiggrāmeṇa kriyākāraḥ kṛto na kenacidekākinā paṇyaṃ grahītavyamiti/
020.017. tadanenaikākinā gṛhītam/
020.017. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--deva, samanuyujyantām yadaibhiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtastadā kimahamebhiḥ śabdito mama bhrātā vā? te kathayanti--deva neti/
020.019. rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, śobhanaṃ pūrṇaḥ kathayati--sa tairvrīḍitairmuktaḥ/
020.019. yāvadapareṇa samayena rājñastena dravyeṇa prayojanamutpannam/
020.020. tena vaṇiggrāma āhūyoktah--bhavantaḥ, mamāmukena dravyeṇa prayojanam/
020.021. anuprayacchateti/
020.021. te kathayanti--deva pūṇasyāsti/
020.021. rājā kathayati--bahvantaḥ, nāhaṃ tasyājñāṃ dadāmi/
020.022. yūyameva tasyāntikāt krītvānuprayacchata/
020.022. taiḥ pūrṇasya dūtaḥ preṣitah--vaṇiggrāmaḥ śabdayatīti/
020.023. sa kathayati--nāhamāgacchāmi/
020.023. te vaṇiggrāmāḥ sarva eva saṃbhūya tasya niveśanaṃ gatvā dvāri sthitvā tairdūtaḥ preṣitaḥ/
020.024. pūrṇa, nirgaccha vaṇiggrāmo dvāri tiṣṭhatīti/
020.025. sa sāhaṃkāraḥ kāmakāramadattvā nirgataḥ/
020.025. vaṇiggrāmaḥ kathayati--sārthavāha yathākrītakaṃ paṇyamanuprayaccha/
020.026. sa kathayati--ativāṇijako 'ham yadi yathākṛtaṃ paṇyamanuprayacchāmīti/
020.026. te kathayanti--sārthavāha, dviguṇamūlyena dattam/
020.027. pañcadaśa lakṣāṇi teṣāṃ vaṇijyaṃ dattamavaśiṣṭaṃ svagṛhaṃ praveśitam/
020.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ śakyamavaśyāyabindunā kumbhaṃ pūrayitum? mahāsamudramavatarāmīti/
020.029. tena sūrpārake nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ saurpārakīyā vaṇijaḥ/
020.030. pūrṇaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudramavatarati/
020.030. yo yuṣmākamutsahate pūrṇena sārthavāhena sārdhamaśulkenāgulmenātarapaṇyena mahāsamudramavatartuṃ sa mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānayatviti/
020.032. pañcamātrairvaṇikśatairmahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānītam/
020.032. tataḥ pūrṇaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kṛtakutūhalamaṅgalasvastyayanah<21> pañcavaṇikśataparivāro mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: 020.001. ‘I will give the remaining merchandise.’ 020.001. ‘So be it.’ 020.002. He brought and gave three hundred thousand [coins]. 020.002. And having sealed it with his own seal, he departed. 020.002. Then the merchant guild sent scouts: ‘Go see what goods [he has].’ 020.003. They went and asked: ‘What goods?’ ‘Such and such.’ 020.004. ‘Our storehouses and granaries are also full.’ 020.004. ‘Whether they are full or not — 020.004. has it been sold?’ 020.005. ‘To whom?’ ‘To <s>Pūrṇa</s>.’ 020.005. ‘You will obtain a great deal by selling through <s>Pūrṇa</s>.’ 020.005. They said: ‘What he gave as advance payment, you would not give even as the full price.’ 020.006. ‘What did he give as advance payment?’ ‘Three hundred thousand gold [coins].’ 020.007. ‘He has cheated us and made us fools!’ 020.007. They went and reported to the merchant guild. 020.007. ‘That merchandise has been purchased.’ 020.008. ‘By whom?’ ‘By <s>Pūrṇa</s>.’ 020.008. ‘You will obtain a great deal by selling through <s>Pūrṇa</s>.’ 020.008. ‘What he gave as advance payment, you would not give even as the full price.’ 020.009. ‘What did he give as advance payment?’ ‘Three hundred thousand gold [coins].’ 020.010. ‘He has cheated us and made us fools!’ 020.010. He was summoned by them and told: ‘<s>Pūrṇa</s>, the merchant guild made a pact: no one shall purchase goods alone. 020.011. Only the merchant guild itself shall make purchases. 020.011. Why did you purchase [on your own]?’ He said: ‘Sirs, when you made the pact, was I summoned, or was my brother? You yourselves made the pact — you yourselves keep it!’ 020.013. Then the merchant guild, filled with anger, made him stand in the sun for a penalty of sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>. 020.014. He was seen by the king’s men. 020.014. They reported it to the king. 020.014. The king said: ‘Sirs, summon them.’ 020.015. They were summoned. 020.015. The king said: ‘Sirs, for what purpose have you made <s>Pūrṇa</s> stand in the sun?’ They said: ‘Your Majesty, the merchant guild made a pact that no one shall purchase goods alone. 020.017. But he purchased alone.’ 020.017. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: ‘Your Majesty, let them be questioned — when they made the pact, was I summoned, or was my brother?’ They said: ‘No, Your Majesty.’ 020.019. The king said: ‘Sirs, <s>Pūrṇa</s> speaks well.’ He was released by them, ashamed. 020.019. Later, on another occasion, the king had need of that merchandise. 020.020. He summoned the merchant guild and said: ‘Sirs, I have need of such-and-such merchandise. 020.021. Provide it.’ 020.021. They said: ‘Your Majesty, <s>Pūrṇa</s> has it.’ 020.021. The king said: ‘Sirs, I give no order to him. 020.022. You yourselves purchase from him and provide it.’ 020.022. They sent a messenger to <s>Pūrṇa</s>: ‘The merchant guild summons you.’ 020.023. He said: ‘I shall not come.’ 020.023. All the merchants of the guild together went to his dwelling, stood at the door, and sent a messenger: 020.024. ‘<s>Pūrṇa</s>, come out — the merchant guild stands at the door.’ 020.025. He, proudly and freely, came out. 020.025. The merchant guild said: ‘Caravan-leader, provide the merchandise at the purchase price.’ 020.026. He said: ‘I would be a poor merchant if I provided the merchandise at the purchase price.’ 020.026. They said: ‘Caravan-leader, give it at double the price.’ 020.027. Fifteen hundred thousand [coins] were given to those merchants; the remainder he brought into his own house. 020.028. He reflected: ‘Can one fill a pot with drops of dew? I shall venture upon the great ocean.’ 020.029. He had a bell-proclamation made in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>: ‘Hear, O merchants of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>! 020.030. The caravan-leader <s>Pūrṇa</s> ventures upon the great ocean. 020.030. Whoever among you is willing to venture upon the great ocean with the caravan-leader <s>Pūrṇa</s>, without toll, without escort-fee, and without transport-fee, let him prepare merchandise for the ocean voyage.’ 020.032. About five hundred merchants prepared merchandise for the ocean voyage. 020.032. Then the caravan-leader <s>Pūrṇa</s>, having performed the rites of curiosity, auspiciousness, and benediction, accompanied by five hundred merchants, ventured upon the great ocean.

body.text:
021.001. maṅgalasvastyayanaḥ pañcavaṇikśataparivāro mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
021.001. sa saṃsiddhayānapātraśca pratyāgataḥ/
021.002. evam yāvat ṣaṭkṛtvaḥ/
021.002. sāmantakena śabdo viśrutaḥ/
021.002. pūrṇaḥ ṣaṭkṛtvo mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ saṃsiddhayānapātraśca pratyāgata iti/
021.003. śrāvasteyā vaṇijaḥ paṇyamādāya sūrpārakaṃ nagaraṃ gatāḥ/
021.004. te mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya yena pūrṇaḥ sārthavāhastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
021.004. uapsaṃkramya kathayanti--sārthavāha mahāsamudramavatarāmeti/
021.005. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, asti kaścidyuṣmābhirdṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā ṣaṭkṛtvo mahāsamudrātsaṃsiddhayānapātrāgataḥ saptamaṃ vāramavataran? te kathayanti--pūrṇa, vayaṃ tvāmuddiśya dūrādāgatāḥ/
021.007. yadi nāvatarasi, tvameva pramāṇamiti/
021.007. sa saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpyahaṃ dhanenānarthī tathāpyeṣāmarthāyāvatarāmīti/
021.008. sa taiḥ sārdhaṃ mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
021.009. te rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaye udānāt pārāyaṇāt satyadṛśaḥ sthaviragāthāḥ śailagāthā munigāthā arthavargīyāṇi ca sūtrāṇi vistareṇa svareṇa svādhyāyaṃ kurvanti/
021.010. tena te śrutāḥ/
021.010. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, śobhanāni gītāni gāyatha/
021.011. te kathayanti--sārthavāha, naitāni? kiṃtu khalvetadbuddhavacanam/
021.012. sa buddha ityaśrutapūrvaṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā sarvaromakūpāni āhṛṣṭāni/
021.012. sa ādarajātaḥ pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, ko 'yaṃ buddhanāmeti/
021.013. te kathayanti--asti śramaṇo gautamaḥ śākyaputraḥ śākyakulātkeśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi ācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ/
021.015. so 'nuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambuddhaḥ/
021.015. sa eṣa sārthavāha buddho nāma/
021.016. kutra bhavantaḥ sa bhagavānetarhi viharati? sārthavāha, śrāvstyāṃ jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
021.017. sa taṃ hṛdi kṛtvā taiḥ sārdhaṃ mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ saṃsiddhayānapātraśca pratyāgataḥ/
021.017. bhrātāsya bhavilaḥ saṃlakṣayati--parikhinno 'yaṃ mahāsamudragamanena, niveśo 'sya kartavya iti/
021.018. sa tenoktah--bhrātaḥ, kathaya katarasya dhaninaḥ sārthavāhasya vā tavārthāya duhitaraṃ prārthayāmīti/
021.019. sa kathayati--nāhaṃ kāmairarthī/
021.020. yadyanujānāsi, pravrajāmīti/
021.020. sa kathayati--yadāsmākaṃ gṛhe vārtā nāsti, tadā na pravrajitaḥ/
021.021. idānīṃ kāmārthaṃ pravrajasi/
021.021. pūrṇaḥ kathayati--bhrātaḥ, tadānīṃ na śobhate, idānīṃ tu yuktam/
021.022. sa tenāvaśyaṃ nirbandhaṃ jñātvānujñātaḥ/
021.022. sa kathayati--bhrātaḥ, mahāsamudro bahvādīnavo 'lpāsvādaḥ/
021.023. bahavo 'vataranti, alpā vyuttiṣṭhanti/
021.023. sarvathā na tvayā mahāsamudramavatartavyam/
021.023. nyāyopārjitaṃ te prabhūtaṃ dhanamasti, eṣāṃ tu tava bhrātṛrṇāmanyāyoparjitam/
021.024. yadyete kathayanti ekadhye vasāmeti, na vastavyam/
021.025. ityuktvopasthāyakamādāya śrāvastīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
021.025. anupūrveṇa śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ//
body.translated_text: 021.001. Having performed the rites of auspiciousness and benediction, accompanied by five hundred merchants, he ventured upon the great ocean. 021.001. He returned with a successful voyage and vessel. 021.002. Thus, up to six times. 021.002. The fame spread far and wide: 021.002. ‘<s>Pūrṇa</s> has ventured upon the great ocean six times and returned with a successful voyage and vessel.’ 021.003. The merchants of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, taking merchandise, went to the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>. 021.004. Having recovered from the fatigue of the road, they approached the caravan-leader <s>Pūrṇa</s>. 021.004. Having approached, they said: ‘Caravan-leader, we wish to venture upon the great ocean.’ 021.005. He said: ‘Sirs, has anyone been seen or heard of by you who, having returned six times from the great ocean with a successful voyage and vessel, ventured a seventh time?’ They said: ‘<s>Pūrṇa</s>, we have come from afar for your sake. 021.007. If you do not venture, you yourself are the authority.’ 021.007. He reflected: ‘Though I have no need of wealth, still, for their sake I shall venture.’ 021.008. He set out with them upon the great ocean. 021.009. They, at dawn, recited aloud at length from the <s>Udāna</s>, the <s>Pārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Satyadŕś</s>, the <s>Sthaviragāthās</s>, the <s>Śailagāthās</s>, the <s>Munigāthās</s>, and the <s>Arthavargīya Sūtras</s>. 021.010. He heard them. 021.010. He said: ‘Sirs, you sing beautiful songs.’ 021.011. They said: ‘Caravan-leader, these are not [songs]! Rather, these are the words of the <s>Buddha</s>.’ 021.012. He, upon hearing the word ‘<s>Buddha</s>’ — never heard before — felt all his pores bristle with joy. 021.012. With reverence arising, he asked: ‘Sirs, who is this one called <s>Buddha</s>?’ 021.013. They said: ‘There is the <s>Śramaṇa Gautama</s>, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, who, having gone forth from the <s>Śākya</s> clan, having shaved his hair and beard, having put on saffron robes, went forth from the household life to the homeless life with complete faith. 021.015. He has fully awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttara samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). 021.015. He, caravan-leader, is the one called <s>Buddha</s>.’ 021.016. ‘Sirs, where does that Blessed One now dwell?’ ‘Caravan-leader, at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.’ 021.017. Keeping that in his heart, he ventured with them upon the great ocean and returned with a successful voyage and vessel. 021.017. His brother <s>Bhavila</s> reflected: ‘He is weary from the ocean voyage; a household should be established for him.’ 021.018. He (<s>Bhavila</s>) said to him: ‘Brother, tell me — from which wealthy man’s or caravan-leader’s [family] shall I seek a daughter for your sake?’ 021.019. He said: ‘I have no desire for sensual pleasures. 021.020. If you give permission, I shall go forth [as a monk].’ 021.020. He said: ‘When there was no livelihood in our household, you did not go forth [then]. 021.021. Now you wish to go forth for the sake of pleasures!’ 021.021. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: ‘Brother, at that time it was not fitting; now, however, it is appropriate.’ 021.022. He (<s>Bhavila</s>), recognizing his firm insistence, gave permission. 021.022. He (<s>Pūrṇa</s>) said: ‘Brother, the great ocean has many dangers and little reward. 021.023. Many venture forth; few emerge. 021.023. You must never venture upon the great ocean. 021.023. You have abundant wealth, rightfully earned; but these brothers of yours have wealth wrongfully earned. 021.024. If they say, “Let us live together,” you should not live [with them].’ 021.025. Having said this, taking his attendant, he set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s>. 021.025. Gradually he reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text:
021.026. śrāvastyāmudyāne sthitena anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapaterdūto 'nupreṣitaḥ/
021.026. tena gatvā anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapterārocitam--gṛhapate, pūrṇaḥ sārthavāha udyāne tiṣṭhati gṛhapatiṃ draṣṭukāma iti/
021.028. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ jalayānena khinna idānīṃ sthalayānenāgataḥ/
021.029. tataḥ pṛcchati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiyatprabhūtaṃ paṇyamānītam/
021.029. sa kathayati--kuto 'sya paṇyam? upasthāyakadvitīyaḥ/
021.030. sa cāhaṃ ca/
021.030. anāthapiṇḍadaḥ saṃlakṣayati--na mama pratirūpam yadahaṃ pradhānapuruṣamasatkāreṇa praveśayeyamiti/
021.031. sa tena mahatā satkāreṇa praveśita udvartitaḥ snāpito bhojitaḥ/
021.032. svairālāpeṇāvasthitayoranāthapiṇḍadaḥ pṛcchati--<22>sārthavāha, kimāgamanaprayojanam? apūrveṇa gṛhapate icchāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvamiti/
body.translated_text: 021.026. While staying in a garden at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, he sent a messenger to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. 021.026. He (<s>the messenger</s>) went and informed the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: ‘Householder, the caravan-leader <s>Pūrṇa</s> is staying in the garden and wishes to see the householder.’ 021.028. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> reflected: ‘Surely, weary from the sea-voyage, he has now come by land.’ 021.029. Then he asked: ‘Good sir, how much merchandise has he brought?’ 021.029. He said: ‘Where would he have merchandise? He is accompanied only by his attendant. 021.030. He and I.’ 021.030. <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> reflected: ‘It is not fitting for me to receive an eminent man without proper honor.’ 021.031. He received him with great honor — he was anointed, bathed, and fed. 021.032. As they sat together in familiar conversation, <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> asked: ‘Caravan-leader, what is the purpose of your visit?’ ‘It is a new purpose, householder — I wish to receive ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full admission (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.’

body.text:
022.002. tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ pūrvaṃ kāyamabhyunnamayya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prasāryodānamudānayati--aho buddhaḥ/
022.003. aho dharmaḥ/
022.003. aho saṃghasya svākhyātatā/
022.003. yatredānīmīdṛśāḥ pradhānapuruṣā vistīrṇasvajanabandhuvargamapahāya sphītāni ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi ākāṅkṣanti svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvamiti/
022.005. tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛḥpatiḥ pūrṇaṃ sārthavāhamādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
022.006. tena khalu samayena bhagavānanekaśatāyā bhikṣupariṣadaḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati/
022.007. adrākṣīd bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ saprābhṛtamāgacchantam/
022.008. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣa bhikṣavo 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ saprābhṛta āgacchati/
022.009. nāsti tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhaḥ prābhṛto yathā vaineyaprābhṛta iti/
022.010. tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā pūrṇena sārthavāhena sārdhamekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
022.011. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavantamidamavocat--ayaṃ bhadanta pūrṇaḥ sārthavāha ākāṅkṣati svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
022.012. taṃ bhagavān pravrājayatu upasampādayedanukampāmupādāyeti/
022.013. adhivāsayati bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena/
022.014. tato bhagavān pūrṇaṃ sārthavāhamāmantrayate--ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacaryamiti/
022.014. sa bhagavato vācāvasāne muṇḍaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ saṃghāṭiprāvṛtaḥ pātrakarakavyagrahastaḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśrurvarṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣorīryāpathenāvāsthitaḥ/
022.017. ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaśca saṃghāṭiparītadehaḥ/
022.019. sadyaḥ praśāntendriya eva tasthau evaṃ sthito buddhamanorathena//4//
body.translated_text: 022.002. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, first raising his body upright and extending his right arm, uttered an inspired exclamation (<s>udāna</s>): 'Oh, the <s>Buddha</s>! 022.003. Oh, the <s>Dharma</s>! 022.003. Oh, how well-proclaimed is the <s>Saṃgha</s>! 022.003. For now such eminent men, abandoning their extensive circle of kinsmen and relatives and their abundant treasuries and storehouses, desire ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full admission (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline)!' 022.005. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, taking <s>Pūrṇa</s> the caravan-leader, approached the Blessed One. 022.006. At that time, the Blessed One was seated before an assembly of many hundreds of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. 022.007. The Blessed One saw the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> coming with an offering. 022.008. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, this householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> comes with an offering. 022.009. There is no offering for the <s>Tathāgata</s> such as an offering of one who is to be trained.' 022.010. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having worshiped the feet of the Blessed One, sat down to one side together with <s>Pūrṇa</s> the caravan-leader. 022.011. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, this <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the caravan-leader, desires ordination, full admission, and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. 022.012. May the Blessed One ordain him, may he give him full admission, out of compassion!' 022.013. The Blessed One consented to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> by his silence. 022.014. Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Pūrṇa</s> the caravan-leader: 'Come, <s>bhikṣu</s>, practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>)!' 022.014. At the conclusion of the Blessed One's words, he became tonsured, clothed in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (monastic robe), with bowl and water-pot in hand, with hair and beard as if shaved seven days ago, standing in the deportment of a monk who has been ordained for a hundred years. 022.017. Called 'Come!' by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he became tonsured, his body covered with the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>; 022.019. he stood at once with senses calmed — thus established by the <s>Buddha</s>'s wish. // 4 //

body.text:
022.021. athāpareṇa samayenāyuṣmān pūrṇo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
022.021. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt/
022.022. ekānte sthita āyuṣmān pūrṇo bhagavantamidamavocat--sādhu me bhagavāṃstathā saṃkṣiptena dharmaṃ deśayatu yathāhaṃ bhagavato 'ntikāt saṃkṣiptena dharmaṃ śrutvaiko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā vihareyam/
022.024. yadarthaṃ kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśrūṇi avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi ācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ dṛṣṭadharme svayamabhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya pravrajayeyam--kṣīṇā me jātiruṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparamasmādbhavaṃ prajānāmīti/
022.027. evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇamidamavocat--sādhu pūrṇa, sādhu khalu tvaṃ pūrṇa yastvamevaṃ vadasi--sādhu me bhagavāṃstathā saṃkṣiptena dharmaṃ deśayatu pūrvavadyāvannāparamasmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti/
022.029. tena hi pūrṇa śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye//
body.translated_text: 022.021. Then, on another occasion, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> approached the Blessed One. 022.021. Having approached, he worshiped the feet of the Blessed One with his head and stood to one side. 022.022. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the <s>Dharma</s> in brief, in such a way that I, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> in brief from the Blessed One, might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, with a resolute mind. 022.024. For the purpose for which sons of good family, having shaved their hair and beard, putting on saffron robes, with right faith go forth from home to homelessness — may I, having directly known and realized in this very life that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, having attained full admission, go forth [knowing]: "Birth is exhausted for me, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know no further existence."' 022.027. When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>: 'Good, <s>Pūrṇa</s>! Good indeed, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, that you speak thus: "May the Blessed One teach me the <s>Dharma</s> in brief" — as before, up to "I know no further existence." 022.029. Then, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, listen, and attend well and carefully — I shall speak.'

body.text:
022.031. santi pūrṇa cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇīṣṭakāni kāntāni priyāṇi manāpāni kāmopasaṃhitāni rañjanīyāni/
022.032. tāni cedbhikṣurdṛṣṭvābhinandati abhivadāti adhyavasyati adhyavasāya <23>tiṣṭhati, tāni abhinandato 'bhivadato 'dhyavasato 'dhyavasāya tiṣṭhata ānandī bhavati/
body.translated_text: 022.031. There are, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, lovely, dear, pleasant, connected with sense-desire, alluring. 022.032. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, having seen them, delights in them, welcomes them, clings to them, and remains clinging to them — for one who delights, who welcomes, who clings, who remains clinging, delight arises.

body.text:
023.001. ānandyānandīsaumanasyaṃ bhavati/
023.002. nandīsaumanasye sati sarāgo bhavati/
023.002. nandīsarāge sati nandīsarāgasamyojanaṃ bhavati/
023.003. nandīsarāgasamyojanasamyuktaḥ pūrṇa bhikṣurāarannirvāṇasyocyate/
023.003. santi pūrṇa śrotravijñeyāḥ śabdāḥ, ghrāṇavijñeyā gandhāḥ, jihvāvijñeyā rasāḥ, kāyavijñeyāni spraṣṭavyāni, manovijñeyā dharmā iṣṭāḥ kāntāḥ priyā manāpāḥ kāmopasaṃhitā rañjanīyāḥ/
023.006. tāṃśca bhikṣurdṛṣṭvā pūrvavad yāvadārānnirvāṇasyeti ucyate/
023.006. santi tu pūrṇa cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi iṣṭāni kāntāni priyāṇi manāpāni pūrvavad yavat śuklapakṣeṇāntike nirvāṇasyeti ucyate/
023.008. anena tvaṃ pūrṇa mayā saṃkṣiptenāvavādena coditaḥ/
023.008. kutrecchasi vastuṃ kutrecchasi vāsaṃ kalpayitum? anenāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā saṃkṣiptenāvavādena codita icchāmi śroṇāparāntakeṣu janapadeṣu vastuṃ śroṇāparāntakeṣu janapadeṣu vāsaṃ kalpayitum/
023.010. caṇḍāḥ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntikā manuṣyā rabhasāḥ karkaśā ākrośakā roṣakāḥ paribhāṣakāḥ/
023.011. sacet tvāṃ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyā saṃmukhaṃ pāpikayā asatyayā paruṣayā vācā ākrokṣyanti roṣayiṣyanti paribhāṣiṣyante, tasya te kathaṃ bhaviṣyati? sacenmāṃ bhadanta śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ saṃmukhaṃ pāpikayā asātyayā paruṣayā vācā ākrokṣyanti roṣayiṣyanti paribhāṣiṣyante, tasya mamaivaṃ bhaviṣyati--bhadrakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, snigdhakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, ye māṃ saṃmukhaṃ pāpikayā asatyayā paruṣayā
vācā ākrośanti roṣayanti paribhāṣante/
023.017. no tu pāṇinā vā loṣṭena vā praharantīti/
023.017. caṇḍāḥ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ pūrvavat yāvat paribhāṣakāḥ/
023.018. sacet tvāṃ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ pāṇinā vā loṣṭena vā prahariṣyanti, tasya te kathaṃ bhaviṣyati? sacenmāṃ bhadanta śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ pāṇinā vā loṣṭena vā prahariṣyanti, tasya mamaivaṃ bhaviṣyati--bhadrakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, snehakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, ye māṃ pāṇinā vā loṣṭena vā praharanti, no tu daṇḍena vā śastreṇa vā praharantīti/
023.022. caṇḍāḥ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ pūrvavad yāvat paribhāṣakāḥ/
023.023. sacet tvāṃ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyā daṇḍena vā śastreṇa vā prahariṣyanti, tasya te kathaṃ bhaviṣyati? sacenmāṃ bhadanta śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyā daṇḍena vā śastreṇa vā prahariṣyanti, tasya mamaivaṃ bhaviṣyati--bhadrakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, snehakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, ye māṃ daṇḍena vā śastreṇa vā praharanti, no tu sarveṇa sarvaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayanti/
023.027. caṇḍāḥ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyā yāvat paribhāṣakāḥ/
023.027. sacet tvāṃ pūrṇa śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayiṣyanti, tasya te kathaṃ bhaviṣyati? sacenmāṃ bhadanta śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ jīvitād vyaparoyiṣyanti, tasya me evaṃ bhaviṣyati--santi bhagavataḥ śrāvakā ye anena pūtikāyenārdīyamānā jehrīyante, vijugupsamānāḥ śastramapi ādhārayanti, viṣamapi bhikṣayanti, rajjvā baddhā api mriyante, prapātādapi prapatantyapi/
023.032. bhadrakā bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyakāḥ, snehakā <24>bata śroṇāparāntakā manuṣyāḥ, ye māmasmāt pūtikalevarādalpakṛcchreṇa parimocayantīti/
body.translated_text: 023.001. When there is delight, delight-elation arises. 023.002. When there is delight-elation, passion arises. 023.002. When there is delight-passion, the fetter of delight-passion arises. 023.003. Bound by the fetter of delight-passion, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> is said to be far from <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. 023.003. There are, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, sounds cognizable by the ear, smells cognizable by the nose, tastes cognizable by the tongue, tangibles cognizable by the body, and <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) cognizable by the mind — desirable, lovely, dear, pleasant, connected with sense-desire, alluring. 023.006. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, having perceived them, [acts] as before, up to: he is said to be far from <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. 023.006. But there are, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, lovely, dear, pleasant — as before, up to: he is said to be near <s>Nirvāṇa</s> by the bright path. 023.008. By this, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, you have been instructed by me with a brief admonition. 023.008. Where do you wish to dwell? Where do you wish to make your residence?' 'By this brief admonition, venerable sir, having been instructed by the Blessed One, I wish to dwell in the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions, I wish to make my residence in the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions.' 023.010. 'The <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people are fierce, <s>Pūrṇa</s> — violent, harsh, abusive, wrathful, and reproachful. 023.011. If, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people abuse, provoke, and reproach you to your face with evil, untrue, harsh words — how will it be for you?' 'If, venerable sir, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people abuse, provoke, and reproach me to my face with evil, untrue, harsh words, then I shall think thus: Good indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, gentle indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, who abuse, provoke, and reproach me to my face with evil, untrue, harsh words — 023.017. but do not strike me with fists or clods!' 023.017. 'The <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people are fierce, <s>Pūrṇa</s> — as before, up to: reproachful. 023.018. If, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people strike you with fists or clods — how will it be for you?' 'If, venerable sir, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people strike me with fists or clods, then I shall think thus: Good indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, gentle indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, who strike me with fists or clods — but do not strike me with sticks or weapons!' 023.022. 'The <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people are fierce, <s>Pūrṇa</s> — as before, up to: reproachful. 023.023. If, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people strike you with sticks or weapons — how will it be for you?' 'If, venerable sir, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people strike me with sticks or weapons, then I shall think thus: Good indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, gentle indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, who strike me with sticks or weapons — but do not completely deprive me of life!' 023.027. 'The <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people are fierce, <s>Pūrṇa</s> — up to: reproachful. 023.027. If, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people completely deprive you of life — how will it be for you?' 'If, venerable sir, the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people completely deprive me of life, then I shall think thus: There are disciples of the Blessed One who, being afflicted by this foul body, feel disgust and revulsion — who take up weapons, who consume poison, who die bound by ropes, who leap from precipices. 023.032. Good indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, gentle indeed are the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> people, who release me from this foul carcass with little difficulty!'

body.text:
024.002. sādhu sādhu pūrṇa, śakyastvaṃ pūrṇa anena kṣāntisaurabhyena samanvāgataḥ śroṇāparāntakeṣu janapadeṣu vastuṃ śroṇāparāntakeṣu vāsaṃ kalpayitum/
024.003. gaccha tvaṃ pūrṇa, mukto mocaya, tīrṇastāraya, āśvasta āśvasaya, parinirvṛtaḥ parinirvāpayeti//
body.translated_text: 024.002. 'Good, good, <s>Pūrṇa</s>! You, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, endowed with this fragrance of patience (<s>kṣāntisaurabhya</s>), are able to dwell in the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions, to make your residence in the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions. 024.003. Go, <s>Pūrṇa</s>! Being liberated, liberate [others]; having crossed over, help [others] cross; being comforted, comfort [others]; having attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, lead [others] to <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>!'

body.text:
024.005. athāyuṣmān pūrṇo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
024.006. athāyuṣmān pūrṇastasyā eva rātreratyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
024.007. śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātraḥ pratikrāntaḥ/
