024.008. yathāparibhuktaśayanāsanaṃ pratisamayya samādāya pātracīvaram yena śroṇāparāntakā janapadāstena cārikāṃ carañ śroṇāparāntakāñ janapadānanuprāptaḥ/
024.010. athāyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śroṇāparāntakaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
024.011. anyatamaśca lubdhako dhanuṣpāṇirmṛgayāṃ nirgacchati/
024.011. tena dṛṣṭaḥ/
024.011. sa saṃlakṣayati--amaṅgalo 'yaṃ muṇḍakaḥ śramaṇako mayā dṛṣṭa iti viditvā ā karṇād dhanuḥ pūrayitvā yenāyuṣmān pūrṇastena pradhāvitaḥ/
024.013. sa āyuṣmatā pūrṇena dṛṣṭaḥ/
024.013. dṛṣṭvā cettarāsaṅgaṃ vivartya kathayati--bhadramukha, asya duṣpūrasyārthe praviśāmi, atra prahareti/
024.014. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
024.015. yasyārthe gahane caranti vihagā gacchanti bandhaṃ mṛgāḥ saṃgrāme śaraśaktatomaradharā naśyantyajasraṃ narāḥ/
024.017. dīnā durdinacāriṇaśca kṛpaṇā matsyā grasantyāyasam asyārthe udarasya pāpakalile dūrādihābhyāgataḥ//5// iti//
body.translated_text: 024.005. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, having rejoiced at and approved of the words of the Blessed One, having worshiped the feet of the Blessed One with his head, departed from the presence of the Blessed One. 024.006. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, at the passing of that very night, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. 024.007. Having walked through <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms, having completed his meal-duty, having returned from the alms-round after the meal, 024.008. having put away the sleeping-place as it had been used, having taken up his bowl and robe, he went on a wandering tour toward the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions and reached the <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> regions. 024.010. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> for alms. 024.011. A certain hunter, bow in hand, was going out to hunt. 024.011. He saw him [<s>Pūrṇa</s>]. 024.011. He reflected: 'This inauspicious shaven little <s>śramaṇa</s> has been seen by me!' — and knowing this, he drew his bow to the ear and ran toward the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>. 024.013. He was seen by the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>. 024.013. Having seen him, turning back his upper robe, he said: 'Good-faced one, it is for the sake of this insatiable [belly] that I enter [here] — strike here!' 024.014. And he spoke a verse: 024.015. 'For its sake, birds wander in thickets; for its sake, deer go into bondage; in battle, men bearing arrows, spears, and lances perish ceaselessly; 024.017. wretched, wandering in foul weather, miserable fish swallow iron [hooks] — for the sake of this belly, this pool of sin, I have come here from afar.' // 5 //

body.text:
024.019. sa saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ pravrajita īdṛśena kṣāntisaurabhyena samanvāgataḥ/
024.019. kimasya praharāmīti matvā abhiprasannaḥ/
024.020. tato 'syāyuṣmatā pūrṇena dharmo deśyitaḥ, śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeśeṣu ca pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
024.021. anyāni ca pañcopāsakaśatāni kṛtāni pañcopāsikāśatāni/
024.021. pañcavihāraśatāni kāritāni, anekāni ca mañcapīṭhavṛṣikoccakabimbopadhānacaturasrakaśatāni anupradāpitāni/
024.023. tasyaiva ca trimāsasyātyayāt tisro vidyāḥ kāyena sākṣātkṛtāḥ/
024.023. arhan saṃvṛttaḥ/
024.024. traidhātukavītarāgo yāvat sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: 024.019. He [the hunter] reflected: 'This renunciant is endowed with such a fragrance of patience (<s>kṣāntisaurabhya</s>). 024.019. Why should I strike him?' — thinking thus, he was filled with faith. 024.020. Then the <s>Dharma</s> was taught to him by the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and he was established in the taking of refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>) and the training-rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>). 024.021. Five hundred lay male devotees (<s>upāsakas</s>) were made, and five hundred lay female devotees (<s>upāsikās</s>). 024.021. Five hundred monasteries (<s>vihāras</s>) were built, and many hundreds of beds, seats, rugs, cushions, images, pillows, and square mats were provided. 024.023. And at the end of just three months, the three knowledges (<s>tisro vidyāḥ</s>) were directly realized by him in person. 024.023. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — 024.024. free from passion toward the three realms, up to: he became worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

body.text:
024.025. yāvadapareṇa samayena dārukarṇibhrātrorbhogāstanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatāḥ/
024.025. tau kathayatah--gato 'sau asmākaṃ gṛhāt kālakarṇiprakhyaḥ/
024.026. āgaccha, ekadhye prativasāmaḥ/
024.026. sa kathayati--kataro 'sau kālakarṇiprakhyah? tau kathayatah--pūrṇakaśrīḥ/
024.027. sā mama gṛhānniṣkrāntā/
024.028. nāsau kālakarṇiprakhyaḥ/
024.028. tau kathayatah--śrīrvā bhavatu kālakarṇī vā, āgaccha ekadhye prativasāmaḥ/
024.029. sa kathayati--yuvayoranyāyopārjitaṃ dhanam, mama nyāyopārjitam/
024.029. nāham yuvābhyāṃ sārdhamekadhye vāsaṃ kalpayāmīti/
024.030. tau kathayatah--tena dāsīputreṇa mahāsamudramavatīryāvatīrya bhogāḥ samudānītā yena tvaṃ bhuñjāno vikatthase/
024.031. kutastava sāmarthyaṃ mahāsamudramavatartumiti/
024.031. sa tābhyāṃ mānaṃ grāhitaḥ/
024.032. sa saṃlakṣayati--ahamapi mahāsamudramavatarāmi/
024.032. pūrvavat yāvanmahāsamudramavatīrṇah<25>/
body.translated_text: 024.025. After some time, the possessions of <s>Dārukarṇī</s>'s two brothers dwindled, diminished, and were exhausted. 024.025. The two said: 'That one resembling <s>Kālakarṇī</s> (goddess of misfortune) has left our house. 024.026. Come, let us live together.' 024.026. He said: 'Who is that one resembling <s>Kālakarṇī</s>?' The two said: '<s>Pūrṇaka</s>'s fortune (<s>śrī</s>).' 024.027. 'She has departed from my house. 024.028. She is no <s>Kālakarṇī</s>.' 024.028. The two said: 'Be it fortune or misfortune, come, let us live together.' 024.029. He said: 'Your wealth is unjustly earned, mine is justly earned. 024.029. I will not arrange to live together with you two.' 024.030. The two said: 'It was by that slave-woman's son, descending again and again into the great ocean, that the riches were brought back — on which you feast and boast. 024.031. Where do you have the ability to descend into the great ocean?' 024.031. His pride was aroused by those two. 024.032. He reflected: 'I too shall descend into the great ocean.' 024.032. As before, [the narrative proceeds] until he descended into the great ocean.

body.text:
025.001. yāvattadvahanaṃ vāyunā gośīrṣacandanavanamanupreritam/
025.001. karṇadhāraḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yattat śrūyate gośīrṣacandanavanamiti, idaṃ tat/
025.002. gṛhṇantu atra yatsāramiti/
025.002. tena khalu samayena gośīrṣacandanavanaṃ maheśvarasya yakṣasya parigraho 'bhūt/
025.003. sa ca yakṣāṇām yakṣasamitiṃ gataḥ/
025.003. tato gośīrṣacandanavane pañcamātrāṇi kuṭhāraśatāni voḍhumārabdhāni/
025.004. adrākṣīdapriyākhyo yo yakṣo gośīrṣacandanavane pañcamātrāṇi kuṭhāraśatāni vahataḥ/
025.005. dṛṣṭvā ca yena maheśvaro yakṣaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
025.006. upasaṃkramya maheśvaram yakṣamidamavocat--yat khalu grāmaṇīrjānīyā gośīrṣacandanavane pañcamātrāṇi kuṭhāraśatāni vahanti/
025.007. yatte kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tatkuruṣveti/
025.007. atha maheśvaro yakṣo yakṣāṇāṃ samitimasamitiṃ kṛtvā saṃjātāmarṣo mahāntaṃ kālikāvātabhayaṃ saṃjanya yena gośīrṣacandanavanaṃ tena saṃprasthitaḥ/
025.009. karṇadhāreṇārocitam--śṛṇvantu bhavanto jāmbudvīpakā vaṇijah--yattat śrūyate mahākālikāvātabhayamiti, idaṃ tat/
025.010. kiṃ manyadhvamiti? tataste vaṇijo bhītāstrastāḥ saṃvignā āhṛṣṭaromakūpā devatāyācanaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ/
025.012. śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādyā suramanujoragayakṣadānavendrāḥ/
025.014. vyasanamatibhayaṃ vayaṃ prapannā vigatabhayā hi bhavantu no 'dya nāthāḥ//6//
body.translated_text: 025.001. Then that vessel was driven by the wind to the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest. 025.001. The helmsman said: 'Sirs, that which is heard of as the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest — this is it. 025.002. Take whatever is valuable here.' 025.002. Now at that time, the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest was the domain of the <s>yakṣa</s> (nature spirit) <s>Maheśvara</s>. 025.003. And that <s>yakṣa</s> had gone to the assembly of the <s>yakṣas</s>. 025.003. Then, in the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest, about five hundred axes began to be wielded. 025.004. A <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Apriya</s> saw the five hundred axes being wielded in the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest. 025.005. Having seen [this], he approached the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>. 025.006. Having approached, he said this to the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>: 'Know, O chief, that in the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest, about five hundred axes are being wielded. 025.007. Whatever is your duty or obligation — do that.' 025.007. Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>, leaving the <s>yakṣa</s>-assembly without [completing] the assembly, filled with anger, raising a great fearsome black-storm, set out toward the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest. 025.009. The helmsman announced: 'Listen, <s>Jambudvīpan</s> merchants — that which is heard of as the great black-storm terror — this is it! 025.010. What do you think?' Then those merchants, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, began to pray to the deities. 025.012. '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other lords of gods, humans, serpents, <s>yakṣas</s>, and demons — 025.014. we have fallen into calamity and great fear; may our protectors be free from fear today!' // 6 //

body.text:
025.016. kecinnamasyanti śacīpatiṃ narā brahmāṇamanye hariśaṃkarāvapi/
025.018. bhūmyāśritān vṛkṣavanāśritāṃśca trāṇārthino vātapiśācadasthāh(yakṣāh?)//7//
body.translated_text: 025.016. Some men bow to <s>Śacīpati</s> (<s>Indra</s>), others to <s>Brahmā</s>, and to <s>Hari</s> and <s>Śaṃkara</s> too; 025.018. [they pray to deities] dwelling on the earth and those dwelling in groves of trees — seeking protection, bitten by the wind-demon (<s>vātapiśāca</s>) [or: <s>yakṣas</s>]. // 7 //

body.text:
025.020. dārukarṇī alpotsukastiṣṭhati/
025.020. vaṇijaḥ kathayanti--sārthavāha, vayaṃ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptāḥ/
025.021. kimarthamalpotsukastiṣṭhasīti? sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, ahaṃ bhrātrā abhihitah--mahāsamudro 'lpāsvādo bahvādīnavaḥ/
025.022. tṛṣṇāndhā bahavo 'vataranti, svalpā vyutthāsyanti/
025.022. na tvayā kenacit prakāreṇa mahāsamudramavatartavyamiti/
025.023. so 'haṃ tasya vacanamavacanaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
025.024. kimidānīṃ karomi? kastava bhrāatā? pūrṇaḥ/
025.024. vaṇijaḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, sa evāryapūrṇaḥ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ/
025.025. tameva śaraṇaṃ prapadyāma iti/
025.025. tairekasvareṇa sarvairevaṃ nādo muktah--namastasmai āryāya pūrṇāya, namo namastasmai āryāya pūrṇāyeti/
025.026. atha yā devatā āyuṣmatī pūrṇe 'bhiprasannā, sā yenāyuṣmān pūrṇastenopasaṃkrāntā/
025.027. upasaṃkramya āyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇamidamavocat--ārya, bhrātā te kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ, samanvāhareti/
025.028. tena samanvāhṛtam/
025.029. tata āyuṣmān pūrṇastadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte śroṇāparāntake 'ntarhito mahāsamudre vahanasīmāyāṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā avasthitaḥ/
025.030. tato 'sau kālikāvātaḥ sumerupratyāhata iva pratinivṛttaḥ/
025.031. atha maheśvaro yakṣaḥ saṃlakṣayati--pūrvam yat kiṃcidvahanaṃ kālikāvātena spṛśyate, tattūlapicuvata kṣipyate viśīryate ca/
025.032. idānīṃ ko yogo yena kālikāvātah <26>sumerupratyāhata iva pratinivṛttah? sa itaścāmutaśca pratyavekṣitumārabdho yāvat paśyati āyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇaṃ vahanasīmāyāṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvāvasthitam/
body.translated_text: 025.020. <s>Dārukarṇī</s> stood with little concern. 025.020. The merchants said: 'Caravan-leader, we have come into difficulty, strait, and distress. 025.021. Why do you stand with so little concern?' He said: 'Sirs, I was told by my brother: "The great ocean has little pleasure and many dangers. 025.022. Many, blinded by craving, descend into it; few will escape. 025.022. You must not, by any means, descend into the great ocean." 025.023. And I, having disregarded his word, descended into the great ocean. 025.024. What shall I do now?' 'Who is your brother?' '<s>Pūrṇa</s>.' 025.024. The merchants said: 'Sirs, that is the noble <s>Pūrṇa</s> himself — the one called "of great merit." 025.025. Let us take refuge in him alone!' 025.025. Then, with one voice, all of them uttered this cry: 'Homage to that noble <s>Pūrṇa</s>! Homage, homage to that noble <s>Pūrṇa</s>!' 025.026. Then the deity who was devoted to the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> approached the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>. 025.027. Having approached, she said this to the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>: 'Noble one, your brother has come into difficulty, strait, and distress — consider [him]!' 025.028. He considered [the situation]. 025.029. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> attained a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) of such a kind that, with his mind concentrated, he disappeared from <s>Śroṇāparāntaka</s> and appeared in the great ocean at the boundary of the vessel, seated cross-legged. 025.030. Then that black-storm turned back, as if repelled by <s>Sumeru</s>. 025.031. Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Maheśvara</s> reflected: 'Previously, whatever vessel was touched by the black-storm was tossed about like a tuft of cotton and shattered. 025.032. Now, what power is this by which the black-storm has turned back as if repelled by <s>Sumeru</s>?' He began to look this way and that — then he saw the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> seated cross-legged at the boundary of the vessel.

body.text:
026.002. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ kathayati--ārya pūrṇa, kiṃ viheṭhayasīti? āyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ kathayati--jarādharmo 'ham/
026.003. kiṃ māmeva viheṭhayasi? yadi mayedṛśā guṇagaṇā nādhigatāḥ syurbhrātā me tvayā nāmāvaśeṣaḥ kṛtaḥ syāt/
026.004. maheśvaro yakṣaḥ kathayati--ārya idaṃ gośīrṣacandanavanaṃ rājñaścakaravartino 'rthāya dhāryate/
026.005. kiṃ manyase grāmaṇīḥ kiṃ varaṃ rājā cakravartī uta tathagato 'rhan samyaksambuddha? kim ārya bhagavāṃl loka utpannah? utpannaḥ/
026.007. yadi evam yadaparipūrṇaṃ tatparipūryatām/
026.007. tataste vaṇijo gatapratyāgataprāṇā āyuṣmati pūrṇe cittamabhiprasādya tadvahanaṃ gośīrṣacandanasya pūrayitvā saṃprasthitāḥ/
026.008. anupūrveṇa sūrpārakaṃ nagaramanuprāptāḥ//
body.translated_text: 026.002. Having seen him, he said again: 'Noble <s>Pūrṇa</s>, why do you cause trouble?' The venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: 'I am subject to the law of old age. 026.003. Why do you alone cause me trouble? If I had not attained such a host of virtues, my brother would have been destroyed by you, leaving not even his name.' 026.004. The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Maheśvara</s> said: 'Noble one, this <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood forest is maintained for the sake of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) king. 026.005. What do you think, chief — which is superior: a <s>Cakravartin</s> king or a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly and fully enlightened one (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)?' 'Noble one, has the Blessed One arisen in the world?' 'He has arisen.' 026.007. 'If so, let what is unfilled be filled!' 026.007. Then those merchants, their lives having been returned to them, having placed their faith in the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, filled that vessel with <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood and set out. 026.008. Gradually they reached the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.

body.text:
026.010. tata āyuṣmān pūrṇo bhrātuḥ kathayati--yasya nāṃnā vahanaṃ saṃsiddhayānapātramāgacchati, tattasya gamyaṃ bhavati/
026.011. tvameṣāṃ vaṇijāṃ ratnasavibhāgaṃ kuru/
026.011. ahamanena gośīrṣacandanena bhagavato 'rthāya candanamālaṃ prāsādaṃ kārayāmīti/
026.012. tena teṣāṃ vaṇijāṃ ratnaiḥ saṃvibhāgaḥ kṛtaḥ/
026.013. tata āyuṣmān pūrṇo gośīrṣacandanena prāsādaṃ māpayitumārabdhaḥ/
026.013. tena śilpānāhūyoktāh--bhavantaḥ, kiṃ divase divase pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni gṛhṇīdhvamāhosvit gośīrṣacandanacūrṇasya biḍālapadam? te kathayanti--ārya gośīrṣacandanacūrṇasya biḍālapadam/
026.015. yāvat alpīyasā kālena candanamālaḥ prāsādaḥ kṛtaḥ/
026.016. rājā kathayati--bahvantaḥ, śobhanaṃ prāsādam/
026.016. sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhataḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
026.017. yattatra saṃkalikā cūrṇaṃ cāvaśiṣṭam, tat piṣṭvā tatraiva pralepo dattaḥ/
026.018. te ca bhrātara parasparaṃ sarve kṣamitā uktāśca--buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamupanimantrya bhojayata/
026.018. ārya, kutra bhagavān? śrāvastyām/
026.019. kiyaddūramitaḥ śrāvastī? sātirekam yojanaśatam/
026.019. rājānaṃ tāvadavalokayāmaḥ/
026.020. evaṃ kuruta/
026.020. te rājñaḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
026.020. upasaṃkramya śirasā praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā kathayanti--deva, icchāmo vayaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamupanimantrya bhojayitum/
026.021. devo 'smākaṃ sāhāyyaṃ kalpayatu/
026.022. rājā kathayati--tataḥ śobhanam/
026.022. tathā bhavatu/
026.022. kalpayāmi/
026.022. tata āyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ śaraṇapṛṣṭhamabhiruhya jetavanābhimukhaṃ sthitvā ubhe jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya puṣpāṇi kṣiptvā dhūpaṃ saṃcārya ārāmikena ca sauvarṇabhṛṅgāraṃ grāhayitvā ārādhituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
026.025. viśuddhaśīlaṃ suviśuddhabuddhe bhaktābhisāre satatārthadarśin/
026.027. anāthabhūtān prasamīkṣya sādho kṛtvā kṛpāmāgamanaṃ kuruṣva//8// iti/
026.029. tatastāni puṣpāṇi buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvenopari puṣpamaṇḍapaṃ kṛtvā jetavane gatvā sthitāni dūupo 'bhrakūṭavadudakaṃ vaidūryaśalākāvat/
026.030. āyuṣmānānando nimittakuśalaḥ/
026.031. sa kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--kuto bhagavan nimantraṇamāgatam? sūrpārakāt ānanda nagarāt/
026.032. kiyaddūre bhadanta sūrpārakaṃ nagaram? sātirekam ānanda <27>yojanaśatam/
body.translated_text: 026.010. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> said to his brother: 'The vessel that arrives successfully in someone's name — that belongs to that person. 026.011. You distribute the gems among these merchants. 026.011. I shall have a sandalwood-garland palace built with this <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood for the sake of the Blessed One.' 026.012. By him, a distribution of gems was made among those merchants. 026.013. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> began to have a palace built with <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood. 026.013. He summoned the craftsmen and asked: 'Sirs, will you take five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> per day, or a cat's footprint of <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood powder?' They said: 'Noble one, a cat's footprint of <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood powder.' 026.015. In a very short time, the sandalwood-garland palace was built. 026.016. The king said: 'Sirs, a splendid palace! 026.016. It has been completed perfectly in all respects.' 026.017. Whatever filings and powder remained there, those were ground and applied as a coating right there. 026.018. And the brothers all forgave one another and were told: 'Invite the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> and offer them a meal.' 026.018. 'Noble one, where is the Blessed One?' 'At <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' 026.019. 'How far from here is <s>Śrāvastī</s>?' 'More than a hundred <s>yojanas</s>.' 026.019. 'Let us first consult the king.' 026.020. 'Do so.' 026.020. They approached the king. 026.020. Having approached and bowed their heads in obeisance, they said: 'Your Majesty, we wish to invite the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> and offer them a meal. 026.021. May Your Majesty arrange assistance for us.' 026.022. The king said: 'Excellent! 026.022. Let it be so. 026.022. I shall arrange it.' 026.022. Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, having ascended to the roof-terrace, standing facing the <s>Jetavana</s>, placing both knees on the ground, scattering flowers, burning incense, and having the park-keeper hold a golden water-pitcher, began to propitiate [the Buddha]: 026.025. 'O you of pure conduct and supremely pure wisdom, ever perceiving the good in the offering of devotion, 026.027. having observed those who are without a protector, O holy one, having shown compassion, make [your] coming!' // 8 // 026.029. Then those flowers, by the power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and by the power of the deities, formed a flower-pavilion above and went and stood in the <s>Jetavana</s>; the incense [rose] like a cloud-peak, the water like a <s>vaidūrya</s>-gem rod. 026.030. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was skilled in reading signs. 026.031. He, with cupped hands, asked the Blessed One: 'From where, Blessed One, has an invitation arrived?' 'From the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>.' 026.032. 'How far away is the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, venerable sir?' 'More than a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.text:
027.001. gacchāmah? ānanda, bhikṣūnārocaya--yo yuṣmākamutsahate śvaḥ sūrpārakaṃ nagaraṃ gatvā bhoktum, sa śalākāṃ gṛhṇātu iti/
027.002. evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya śalākāṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastāt sthitaḥ/
027.003. bhagavatā śalākā gṛhītā, sthavirasthaviraiśca bhikṣubhiḥ//
body.translated_text: 027.001. 'Shall we go?' '<s>Ānanda</s>, announce to the monks: "Whoever among you is willing to go to the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> tomorrow and eat, let him take a ballot-stick (<s>śalākā</s>)."' 027.002. 'So be it, venerable sir.' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, took a ballot-stick and stood before the Blessed One. 027.003. The Blessed One took a ballot-stick, and [so did] the senior elder monks.

body.text:
027.004. tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ kuṇḍopadhānīyakaḥ sthaviraḥ prajñāvimuktas tasyāmeva pariṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt/
027.005. saṃnipatitaḥ/
027.005. so 'pi śalākāṃ gṛhītumārabdhaḥ/
027.005. tamāyuṣmānānando gāthayā pratyabhāṣata--
027.007. naitadbhoktavyamāyuṣman kośalādhipatergṛhe/
027.008. agāre vā sujātasya mṛgārabhavane 'thavā//9//
body.translated_text: 027.004. Now at that time, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, known as <s>Kuṇḍopadhānīyaka</s>, an elder liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>), was seated in that very assembly. 027.005. He had gathered [with the others]. 027.005. He too began to take a ballot-stick. 027.005. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> addressed him with a verse: 027.007. 'This is not to be eaten, O venerable one, in the house of the lord of <s>Kosala</s>, 027.008. or in the dwelling of <s>Sujāta</s>, or in the mansion of <s>Mṛgāra</s>.' // 9 //

body.text:
027.009. sādhikam yojanaśataṃ sūrpārakamitaḥ puram/
027.010. ṛddhibhiryatra gantavyaṃ tūṣṇī tvaṃ bhava pūrṇaka//10// iti//
body.translated_text: 027.009. 'The city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> is more than a hundred <s>yojanas</s> from here; 027.010. one must go there by supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) — be silent, <s>Pūrṇaka</s>!' // 10 //

body.text:
027.011. sa prajñāvimuktaḥ/
027.011. tena ṛddhir notpāditā/
027.011. tasyaitadabhavat--yena mayā sakalaṃ kleśagaṇaṃ vāntaṃ charditaṃ tyaktaṃ pratiniḥsṛṣṭam, so 'haṃ tīrthikasādhāraṇāyām ṛddhyāṃ viṣaṇṇaḥ/
027.012. tena vīryamāsthāya ṛddhimutpādya yāvadāyuṣmānānandas tṛtīyasthavirasya śalākāṃ na dadāti, tāvat tena gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya śalākā gṛhītā/
027.014. tato gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
027.015. vapuṣmattayā śrutena vā na balātkāraguṇaiśca gautama/
027.016. prabalairapi vānmanorathaiḥ ṣaḍabhijñatvamihādhigamyate//11//
body.translated_text: 027.011. He was liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>). 027.011. Therefore he had not produced supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>). 027.011. This thought arose in him: 'I who have vomited, expelled, abandoned, and discharged the entire mass of defilements — am I to be dejected over supernatural powers that are common even to <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics)?' 027.012. Having applied himself with vigor, he produced supernatural powers. Before the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> could give the ballot-stick to the third elder, he, extending his arm like an elephant's trunk, took the ballot-stick. 027.014. Then he spoke a verse: 027.015. 'Not by bodily beauty, not by learning, not by the qualities of force, O <s>Gautama</s>, 027.016. nor even by powerful wishes — is the sixfold superknowledge (<s>ṣaḍabhijñatva</s>) attained here.' // 11 //

body.text:
027.017. śamaśīlavipaśyanābalairvividhairdhyānabalaiḥ parīkṣitāḥ/
027.018. jarayā hi nipīḍitayauvanāḥ ṣaḍabhijñā hi bhavanti madvidhāḥ//12// iti//
body.translated_text: 027.017. Tested by the powers of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), by the various powers of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), 027.018. those whose youth is crushed by old age become possessed of the six superknowledges (<s>ṣaḍabhijñā</s>), those of my kind. // 12 // Thus.

body.text:
027.019. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ caityaśalākāgrahaṇe/
027.020. tatprathamataḥ śalākāṃ gṛhṇatām yaduta pūrṇaḥ kuṇḍopadhānīyakaḥ sthaviraḥ/
027.020. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha ānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya/
027.021. kiṃ cāpi uktaṃ mayā--praticchannakalyāṇairvo bhikṣavo vihartavyaṃ vivṛtapāpairiti, api tu tīrthikāvastabdhaṃ tannagaram/
027.023. yo vo yasyā ṛddherlābhī, tena tayā tatra sūrpārakaṃ nagaraṃ gatvā bhoktavyamiti/
027.023. evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati--āyuṣmantaḥ, bhagavānevamāha--kiṃ cāpi uktaṃ mayā praticchannakalyāṇairvo bhikṣavo vihartavyamiti pūrvavat yāvat gatvā bhoktavyamiti/
027.026. tataḥ sūrpārakarājñā sūrpārakanagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ candanavāripariṣiktaṃ nānāvidhasurabhidhūpaghaṭikāsamalaṃkṛtamāmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpaṃ nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇaṃ ramaṇīyam/
027.028. sūrpārakasya nagarasyāṣṭādaśa dvārāṇi/
027.028. tasyāpi rājñaḥ saptadaśa putrāḥ/
027.029. pratyekamekaikasmin dvāre paramayā vibhūtyā rājaputrā vyavasthitāḥ/
027.029. mūladvāre ca mahatā rājānubhāvena sūrpārakādhipatī rājā āyuṣmān pūrṇo dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇī ca vyavasthitaḥ/
027.031. yāvat patracārikā ṛddhyā haritacārikā bhājanacārikāścāgatāḥ/
027.031. tān dṛṣṭvā rājā kathayati--bhadanta pūrṇa, kiṃ bhagavānāgatah? āyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ kathayati--mahārāja <28>patracārikā haritacārikā bhājanacārikāścaite, na tāvat bhagavān/
body.translated_text: 027.019. There the Blessed One addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: ‘This, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, is the foremost among my <s>bhikṣu</s> disciples in the taking of the <s>caitya</s>-lot (<s>caityasalaka</s>). 027.020. He who takes the lot first is the Elder <s>Pūrṇa Kuṇḍopadhānīyaka</s>.’ 027.020. There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: ‘Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, announce to the <s>bhikṣus</s>. 027.021. Although I have said: “You <s>bhikṣus</s> should dwell with your virtues concealed and your faults revealed,” nevertheless, that city [of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>] is dominated by heretics (<s>tīrthikas</s>). 027.023. Whoever among you has attained whichever supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), by that [power], going to the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, should take his meal.’ 027.023. ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, announced to the <s>bhikṣus</s>: ‘Venerable ones, the Blessed One says thus: Although I have said that you <s>bhikṣus</s> should dwell with your virtues concealed’ — as before, up to — ‘going [there], should take his meal.’ 027.026. Then, by the king of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> was cleared of stones, gravel, and debris, sprinkled with sandalwood water, adorned with incense-burners of various kinds of fragrant incense, hung with streaming silk banners and garlands, strewn with various flowers — delightful. 027.028. The city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> had eighteen gates. 027.028. That king too had seventeen sons. 027.029. One by one, at each gate, the princes were stationed with supreme splendor. 027.029. And at the main gate, with great royal majesty, stood the lord of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, the king, the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Dārukarṇī</s>, <s>Stavakarṇī</s>, and <s>Trapukarṇī</s>. 027.031. Then those traveling by leaf [through the air], those traveling by greenery, and those traveling by vessel arrived through supernatural power. 027.031. Seeing them, the king said: ‘Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, has the Blessed One arrived?’ The venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: ‘Great king, these are the leaf-travelers, greenery-travelers, and vessel-travelers — the Blessed One has not yet [arrived].’

body.text:
028.001. yāvat sthavirasthavirā bhikṣavo 'nekavidhābhirdhyānasamāpattibhiḥ saṃprāptaḥ/
028.002. punarapi pṛcchati--bhadanta pūrṇa, kiṃ bhagavānāgatah? āyuṣmān pūrṇaḥ kathayati--mahārāja na bhagavān, api tu khalu sthavirasthavirā eva te bhikṣava iti/
028.004. athānyatamopāsakastasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
028.005. siṃhavyāghragajāśvanāgavṛṣabhānāśritya kecit śubhān kecidratnavimānaparvatatarūṃścitrān rathāṃścojjvalān/
028.007. anye toyadharā ivāmbaratale vidyullatālaṃkṛtā ṛddhyā devapurīmiva pramuditā gantuṃ samabhyudyatāḥ//13//
body.translated_text: 028.001. Then elder monks arrived, having attained various <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) absorptions and attainments. 028.002. Again he asked: ‘Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, has the Blessed One arrived?’ The venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: ‘Great king, the Blessed One [has not arrived]; rather, these are the elder monks.’ 028.004. Then a certain lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>) spoke this verse at that moment: 028.005. ‘Some, mounted on auspicious lions, tigers, elephants, horses, <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), and bulls; some on splendid jewel-palaces, mountains, trees, and brilliant chariots; 028.007. others, like rain-clouds in the sky, adorned with lightning-creepers, joyfully preparing to go to the city of the gods by supernatural power. // 13 //’

body.text:
028.009. gāṃ bhittvā hyutpatantyeke patantyantye nabhastalāt/
028.010. āsane nirmitāścaike paśya ṛddhimatāṃ balam//14// iti//
body.translated_text: 028.009. ‘Some burst forth through the earth; others descend from the vault of the sky; 028.010. and some, seated on magically created seats — behold the power of those possessed of supernatural abilities! // 14 //’ Thus.

body.text:
028.011. tato bhagavān bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviśya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
028.012. yāvad bhagavatā gandhakuṭyāṃ sābhisaṃskāraṃ pādo nyastaḥ, ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātah--iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī calati saṃcalati saṃpracalati/
028.014. vyadhati pravyadhati saṃpravyadhati/
028.014. pūrvadigbhāga unnamati, paścimo 'vanamati/
028.015. paścima unnamati, pūrvo 'vanamati/
028.015. dakṣiṇa unnamati, uttaro 'vanamati/
028.015. uttara unnamati, dakṣiṇo 'vanamati/
028.016. anta unnamati, madhyo 'vanamati/
028.016. madhya unnamati, anto 'vanamati/
028.016. rājā āyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇaṃ pṛcchati--ārya pūrṇa, kimetat? sa kathayati--mahārāja, bhagavatā gandhakuṭyāṃ sābhisaṃskāraḥ pādo nyastaḥ, tena ṣaṭvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ/
028.018. tato bhagavatā kanakamarīcivarṇaprabhā utsṛṣṭā yayā jambudvīpo vilīnakanakāvabhāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
028.019. punarapi rājā vismayotphullalocanaḥ pṛcchati--ārya pūrṇa, idaṃ kim? sa kathayati--mahārāja bhagavatā kanakamarīcivarṇaprabhā utsṛṣṭeti//
body.translated_text: 028.011. Then the Blessed One, having washed his feet outside the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), entered the <s>vihāra</s>, set his body upright, established mindfulness before him, and sat down on the prepared seat. 028.012. When the Blessed One placed his foot with deliberate intention in the Perfumed Chamber (<s>gandhakuṭī</s>), there occurred a sixfold earthquake of the earth — this great earth trembled, shook, and quaked; 028.014. it vibrated, rumbled, and thundered; 028.014. the eastern part rose up, the western part sank down; 028.015. the western part rose up, the eastern part sank down; 028.015. the southern part rose up, the northern part sank down; 028.015. the northern part rose up, the southern part sank down; 028.016. the periphery rose up, the middle sank down; 028.016. the middle rose up, the periphery sank down. 028.016. The king asked the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>: ‘Noble <s>Pūrṇa</s>, what is this?’ He said: ‘Great king, the Blessed One has placed his foot with deliberate intention in the Perfumed Chamber; therefore a sixfold earthquake of the earth has occurred.’ 028.018. Then the Blessed One emitted a radiance of the color of golden rays, by which <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became illuminated as if suffused with molten gold. 028.019. Again the king, with eyes wide open in wonder, asked: ‘Noble <s>Pūrṇa</s>, what is this?’ He said: ‘Great king, the Blessed One has emitted a radiance of the color of golden rays.’

body.text:
028.021. tato bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāraḥ pañcabhirarhacchāntaiḥ sārdhaṃ sūrpārakābhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
028.022. atha vā jetavananivāsinī devatā, sā bakulaśākhāṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataśchāyāṃ kurvantī pṛṣṭataḥ saṃprasthitā/
028.023. tasyā bhagavatā āśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhakī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tayā devatayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā śrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
body.translated_text: 028.021. Then the Blessed One, tamed and with a tamed retinue, tranquil and with a tranquil retinue, together with five hundred <s>Arhats</s> who were tranquil, set out toward <s>Sūrpāraka</s>. 028.022. And the deity dwelling in the <s>Jetavana</s>, grasping a <s>bakula</s>-tree branch, making shade for the Blessed One, followed behind. 028.023. Having known her disposition, her element, and her nature, the Blessed One gave her such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, that deity, splitting apart the mountain of the belief in a self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, with the thunderbolt of knowledge (<s>jñānavajra</s>), realized the fruit of <s>Srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry).

body.text:
028.025. yāvadanyatamasmin pradeśe pañcamātrāṇi ghariṇīśatāni prativasanti/
028.026. adrākṣustā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam/
028.028. sahadarśanācca tāsāṃ bhagavati mahāprasāda utpannaḥ/
028.029. dharmataiṣā--na tathā dvādaśavarṣābhyastaḥ śamathaścittasya kalyatāṃ janayati aputrasya ca putralābho daridrasya vā nidhidarśanaṃ rājyābhinandino vā rājyābhiṣeko yathopacitakuśalamūlahetukasya sattvasya tatprathamato buddhadarśanam/
028.031. tato bhagavāṃstāsāṃ vinayakālamavekṣya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya <29>prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
body.translated_text: 028.025. In a certain place, about five hundred housewives dwelt. 028.026. They beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty subsidiary characteristics, adorned with an aura extending one <s>vyāma</s> (fathom), of a radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. 028.028. And upon seeing him, great faith in the Blessed One arose in them. 028.029. It is the law of nature that tranquility practiced for twelve years does not produce such well-being of mind as occurs when a childless person obtains a son, or when a destitute person finds a treasure, or when one who delights in kingship is consecrated as king — nor as the first sight of a <s>Buddha</s> [produces] for a being whose roots of merit have been accumulated. 028.031. Then the Blessed One, discerning the proper time for their guidance, sat down on a prepared seat before the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text:
029.001. tā api bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
029.001. tato bhagavatā tāsāmāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā yāvat srotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
029.003. tā dṛṣṭasatyās trirudānamudānayanti--idamasmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ na rājñā neṣṭasvajanabandhuvargeṇa na devatābhir na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇairyad bhagavatāsmākaṃ tatkṛtam/
029.005. ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitānyapāyadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitā vayaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu atikrāntātikrāntāḥ/
029.006. etā vayaṃ bhagavataṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmo dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
029.007. upāsikāścāsmān bhagavān dhārayatu/
029.007. tata utthāyāsanāt yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocan--aho bata bhagavānasmākaṃ kiṃcidatra prayacchet yatra vayaṃ kārāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ/
029.009. tato bhagavatā ṛddhyā keśanakhamutsṛṣṭam/
029.009. tābhirbhagavataḥ keśanakhastūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
029.010. tatastayā jetavananivāsinyā tasmin stūpe yaṣṭyāṃ sā bakulaśākhāropitā/
029.010. bhagavāṃścoktah--bhagavan, ahamasmin stūpe kārāṃ kurvantī tiṣṭhāmīti/
029.011. sā tatraiva āsthitā/
029.012. tatra kecit ghariṇīstūpa iti saṃjānate, kecit bakulamedhīti, yamadyāpi caityavandakā bhikavo vandante/
029.013. tato bhagavān saṃprasthitaḥ//
body.translated_text: 029.001. They too, having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, sat down to one side. 029.001. Then the Blessed One, having known their dispositions and latent tendencies, their elements and natures, [gave such a teaching that] they realized the fruit of <s>Srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry). 029.003. They, having seen the truth, uttered three times this exclamation: ‘This, venerable sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the king, nor by cherished kinsmen and relatives, nor by deities, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us: 029.005. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; the doors to the lower realms have been shut; and we have been established among gods and humans, having gone beyond, far beyond!’ 029.006. ‘We go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>. 029.007. May the Blessed One consider us as lay women devotees (<s>upāsikās</s>).’ 029.007. Then, rising from their seats, making a salutation with joined hands toward the Blessed One, bowing, they said this to the Blessed One: ‘Ah, if only the Blessed One would give us something here upon which we may perform worship!’ 029.009. Then the Blessed One, by supernatural power, released [some of] his hair and nails. 029.009. By them, a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary shrine) of the Blessed One’s hair and nails was established. 029.010. Then, by that <s>Jetavana</s>-dwelling deity, on the mast of that <s>stūpa</s>, that <s>bakula</s>-tree branch was planted. 029.010. And she said to the Blessed One: ‘Blessed One, I shall remain here, performing worship at this <s>stūpa</s>.’ 029.011. She remained there. 029.012. Some call it the Housewives’ <s>Stūpa</s>; others call it the <s>Bakula</s>-tree [shrine] — which even today the <s>bhikṣus</s> who worship <s>caityas</s> (shrines) venerate. 029.013. Then the Blessed One set out.

body.text:
029.014. yāvadanyasminnāśramapade pañca ṛṣiśatāni prativasanti/
029.014. tatteṣāmāśramapadaṃ puṣpaphalasalilasampannam/
029.015. te tena madena mattā na kiṃcinmanyante/
029.015. tato bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ vinayakālamavekṣya tadāśramapadamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
029.016. upasaṃkramya tasmādāśramapadāt puṣpaphalamṛddhyā śāmitam, salilaṃ śoṣitam, haritaśāḍvalaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sthaṇḍilāni pātitāni/
029.017. tataste ṛṣayaḥ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparā vyavasthitāḥ/
029.018. tato bhagavatā abhihitāh--maharṣayaḥ, kimarthaṃ cintāparāstiṣṭhateti/
029.018. te kathayanti--bhagavaṃstvaṃ dvipādakaṃ puṇyakṣetramiha praviṣṭo 'smākaṃ cedṛśī samavasthā/
029.019. bhagavānāha--kim? te kathayanti--bhagavan, puṣpaphalasalilasampannamāśramapadaṃ vinaṣṭam yathāpaurāṇaṃ bhavatu/
029.021. bhavatu ityāha bhagavān/
029.021. tato bhagavatā ṛddhiḥ prasrabdhā, yathāpaurāṇaṃ saṃvṛttam/
029.021. tataste paraṃ vismayamupagatā bhagavati cittamabhiprasādayāmāsuḥ/
029.022. tato bhagavatā teṣāmāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā taiḥ pañcabhirṛṣiśatairanāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, ṛddhiścābhinirhṛtā/
029.024. tato yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocan--labhema vayaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
029.026. carema vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
029.026. tataste bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitāh--eta bhikṣavaścarata brahmacaryamiti/
029.027. bhagavato vācāvasāne muṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ saṃghāṭiprāvṛtāḥ pātrakaravyagrahastāḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśravo varṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣorīryāpathena avasthitāḥ/
029.029. ehīti coktā hi tathāgatena muṇḍāśca saṃghāṭiparītadehāḥ/
029.031. sadyaḥ praśāntendriyā eva tasthurevaṃ sthitā buddhamanorathena//15//
body.translated_text: 029.014. In another hermitage, five hundred sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>) dwelt. 029.014. That hermitage was endowed with flowers, fruits, and water. 029.015. They, intoxicated with that pride, thought nothing [of others]. 029.015. Then the Blessed One, discerning the proper time for their guidance, approached that hermitage. 029.016. Having approached, he caused the flowers, fruits, and verdure to vanish from that hermitage by supernatural power; the water dried up, the green lawns turned black, and the [ritual] platforms collapsed. 029.017. Then those sages, resting their cheeks on their hands, stood absorbed in anxiety. 029.018. Then the Blessed One said to them: ‘Great sages, why do you stand absorbed in anxiety?’ 029.018. They said: ‘Blessed One, you, a two-footed field of merit, have entered here, and yet such is our condition!’ 029.019. The Blessed One said: ‘What [do you mean]?’ They said: ‘Blessed One, our hermitage, endowed with flowers, fruits, and water, has been ruined. Let it become as it was before!’ 029.021. ‘So be it,’ said the Blessed One. 029.021. Then the Blessed One relaxed his supernatural power, and [the hermitage] became as it was before. 029.021. Then they, overcome with supreme wonder, generated faith in the Blessed One. 029.022. Then the Blessed One, having known their dispositions and latent tendencies, their elements and natures, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, those five hundred sages realized the fruit of <s>Anāgāmi</s> (non-returning), and produced supernatural power as well. 029.024. Then, making a salutation with joined hands toward the Blessed One, bowing, they said this to the Blessed One: ‘May we, venerable sir, receive the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and the status of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. 029.026. May we lead the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the Blessed One.’ 029.026. Then they were addressed by the Blessed One with the formula ‘Come, <s>bhikṣus</s>’ (<s>ehibhikṣukā</s>): ‘Come, <s>bhikṣus</s>, lead the holy life.’ 029.027. At the conclusion of the Blessed One’s words, they became tonsured, clad in the monastic robe, with bowls held in their hands, with hair and beard as if shaved seven days before, standing with the deportment of a <s>bhikṣu</s> ordained for a hundred years. 029.029. ‘Having been told “Come” by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured, with bodies wrapped in the monastic robe, 029.031. at once they stood with senses tranquil — thus established by the aspiration of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 15 //’

body.text:
030.001. <30>tairyujyamānairghaṭamānairvyāyacchamānairidameva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ pūrvavat yāvadabhivādyāśca saṃvṛttāḥ/
030.002. yasteṣām ṛṣiravavādakaḥ sa kathayati--bhagavan, mayā anena veṣeṇa mahājanakāyo vipralabdhaḥ/
030.002. tam yāvadabhiprasādayāmi paścāt pravrajiṣyāmīti/
030.003. tato bhagavān pañcabhirṛṣiśataiḥ pūrvakaiśca pañcabhirbhikṣuḥśatairardhacandrākāropagūḍhastat eva ṛddhyā upari vihāyasā prakrānto 'nupūrveṇa musalakaṃ parvatamanuprāptaḥ/
030.005. tena khalu samayena musalake parvate vakkalī nāma ṛṣiḥ prativasati/
030.006. adrākṣīt sa ṛṣirbhagavantaṃ dūrādeva dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ pūrvavat yāvat samantato bhadrakam/
030.007. sahadarśanāccānena bhagavato 'ntike cittamabhiprasāditam/
030.007. sa prasādajātaścintayati--yannvahaṃ parvatādavatīrya bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi/
030.008. bhagavān vaineyāpekṣayā atikramiṣyati/
030.009. yannvahamātmānaṃ parvatānmuñceyamiti/
030.009. tena parvatādātmā muktaḥ/
030.009. asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
030.010. bhagavatā ṛddhyā pratīṣṭaḥ/
030.010. tato 'sya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā vakkalinā anāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, ṛddhiścābhinirhṛtā/
030.012. tato bhagavantamidamavocat--labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ pūrvavat yāvat bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā pravrājito yāvadevaṃ sthito buddhamanorathena//
body.translated_text:
030.001. As they strove, exerted, and endeavored, this very group of five [attained the fruits] as before, and they became worthy of veneration.
030.002. The one among those sages who was their instructor said: 'Blessed One, I have deceived a great multitude of people with this guise.
030.002. Let me first win back their favor; afterward I shall go forth [as a monk].'
030.003. Then the Blessed One, accompanied by the five hundred sages and the previous five hundred monks, surrounded by a half-moon formation, departed from that very place by supernatural power through the sky, and in due course arrived at Mount <s>Musalaka</s>.
030.005. At that time, a sage named <s>Vakkalī</s> was dwelling on Mount <s>Musalaka</s>.
030.006. That sage saw the Blessed One from a great distance, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, as before, auspicious in every way.
030.007. At the very sight, his mind was filled with serene faith in the Blessed One.
030.007. He, born of faith, thought: 'Let me descend from the mountain and approach the Blessed One for an audience.
030.008. [But] the Blessed One, out of regard for those to be trained, will pass by.
030.009. Let me rather throw myself from the mountain.'
030.009. He threw himself from the mountain.
030.009. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are of unfailing mindfulness.
030.010. He was caught in mid-air by the Blessed One's supernatural power.
030.010. Then the Blessed One, having known his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, <s>Vakkalī</s> realized the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and supernatural power was also manifested [in him].
030.012. Then he said to the Blessed One: 'May I, Venerable Sir, obtain ordination, full admission, and the state of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,' as before, and the Blessed One ordained him with the 'Come, O monk' ordination, and he remained thus, with his aspiration set upon the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text:
030.014. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śraddhādhimuktānām yaduta vakkalī bhikṣuriti/
030.015. tato bhagavān bhikṣusahasraparivṛto vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi kurvan sūrpārakaṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ/
030.016. bhagvān saṃlakṣayati--yadi ekena dvāreṇa praviśāmi, apareṣāṃ bhaviṣyati anyathātvam/
030.017. yannvaham ṛddhyaiva praviśeyamiti/
030.017. tata ṛddhyā upari vihāyasā madhye sūrpārakasya nagarasyāvatīrṇaḥ/
030.018. tataḥ sūrpārakādhipatī rājā āyuṣmān pūrṇo dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇī te ca saptadaśa putrāḥ svakasvakena parivāreṇa yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ, anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi/
030.020. tato bhagavānanekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairanugamyamāno yena candanamālaḥ prāsādas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
030.021. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
030.022. sa janakāyo bhagavantamapaśyaṃś candanamālaṃ prāsādaṃ bhettumārabdhaḥ/
030.022. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--yadi candanamālaḥ prāsādo bhetsyate, dātṛrṇāṃ puṇyāntarāyo bhaviṣyati/
030.023. yannvahamenaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ nirminuyāmiti/
030.024. sa bhagavatā sphaṭikamayo nirmitaḥ/
030.024. tato bhagavatā tasyāḥ pariṣad āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ/
030.026. kaiścinmokṣabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāni utpāditāni, kaiścinnirvedhabhāgīyāni, kaiścit srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam, kaiścidanāgāmiphalam, kaiścit sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścit śrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittānyutpāditāni/
030.030. yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitā//
body.translated_text:
030.014. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'This, O monks, is the foremost among my monks who are devoted through faith, namely the monk <s>Vakkalī</s>.'
030.015. Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a thousand monks and performing various miraculous displays, arrived at the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.
030.016. The Blessed One reflected: 'If I enter by one gate, the others will be displeased.
030.017. Let me rather enter by supernatural power.'
030.017. Then, by supernatural power, he descended through the sky into the middle of the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.
030.018. Then the lord of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, the king, the Venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Dārukarṇī</s>, <s>Stavakarṇī</s>, <s>Trapukarṇī</s>, and those seventeen sons, each with their own retinue, approached the Blessed One, along with many hundreds of thousands of living beings.
030.020. Then the Blessed One, followed by many hundreds of thousands of living beings, approached the <s>Candanamāla</s> palace.
030.021. Having approached, he sat down on a seat prepared in front of the community of monks.
030.022. The multitude, unable to see the Blessed One, began to break open the <s>Candanamāla</s> palace.
030.022. The Blessed One reflected: 'If the <s>Candanamāla</s> palace is broken, it will be an obstacle to the merit of the donors.
030.023. Let me rather transform it into crystal.'
030.024. It was transformed into crystal by the Blessed One.
030.024. Then the Blessed One, having known the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament of that assembly, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of living beings attained great distinction.
030.026. By some, roots of merit pertaining to liberation were generated; by some, those pertaining to penetration; by some, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) was realized; by some, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); by some, the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>); by some, through the abandonment of all defilements, <s>Arhatship</s> was realized; by some, minds were set upon the <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening; by some, upon the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening; by some, minds were set upon the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>).
030.030. For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: 030.031. atha dārukarṇī stavakarṇī trapukarṇī ca praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya āsanāni prajñāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayanti--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālam <31>manyata iti/
body.translated_text: 030.031. Then <s>Dārukarṇī</s>, <s>Stavakarṇī</s>, and <s>Trapukarṇī</s>, having prepared excellent food, both hard and soft, and having set out seats, announced the time to the Blessed One through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the Blessed One now do as he sees fit.'

body.text:
031.001. tena khalu samayena kṛṣṇagautamakau nāgarājau mahāsamudre prativasataḥ/
031.001. tau saṃlakṣayatah--bhagavān sūrpārake nagare dharmaṃ deśayati/
031.002. gacchāvaḥ, dharmaṃ śroṣyāva iti/
031.002. tatastau pañcanāgaśataparivārau pañcanadīśatāni saṃjanya sūrpārakaṃ nagaraṃ saṃprasthitau/
031.003. asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
031.004. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--imau kṛṣṇagautamau nāgarājau yadi sūrpārakaṃ nagaramāgamiṣyataḥ, agocarīkariṣyataḥ/
031.005. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanamāmantrayate--pratigṛhāṇa mahāmaudgalyāyana tathāgatasyātyayikapiṇḍapātam/
031.006. tatkasya hetoh? pañca me maudgalyāyana ātyayikapiṇḍapātāḥ/
031.007. katame pañca? āgantukasya gamikasya glānasya glānopasthāyakasyopadhivārikasya ca/
031.007. asmiṃstvarthe bhagavānupādhau vartate/
031.008. atha bhagavān maudgalyāyanasahāyo yena kṛṣṇagautamakau nāgarājau tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
031.009. tau kathayatah--samanvāharata nāgendrau sūrpārakaṃ nagaramagocarībhaviṣyati/
031.010. tau kathayatah--tādṛśena bhadanta prasādena vayamāgatā yanna śakyamasmābhiḥ kuntapipīlikasyāpi prāṇinaḥ pīḍāmutpādayituṃ prāgeva sūrpārakanagaranivāsino janakāyasyeti/
031.012. tato bhagavatā kṛṣṇagautamakayor nāgarājayostādṛśo dharmo yaṃ śrutvā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatau, dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gatau, śikṣāpadāni ca gṛhītāni/
031.013. bhagavān bhaktakṛtyaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
031.014. ekaiko nāgaḥ saṃlakṣayati--aho bata bhagavān mama pānīyaṃ pibatu iti/
031.015. bhagavān saṃlakṣayti--yadi ekasyeiva pānīyaṃ pāsyāmi, eṣāṃ bhaviṣyati anyathātvam/
031.015. upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyamiti/
031.016. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanamāmantrayate--gaccha maudgalyāyana, yatra pañcānāṃ nadīśatānāṃ saṃbhedaḥ, tasmādudakasya pātrapūramānaya/
031.017. evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yatra pañcānāṃ nadīśatānāṃ saṃbhedastatrodakasya pātrapūramādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
031.019. upasaṃkramya bhagavata udakasya pātrapūramupanāmayati/
031.020. bhagavatā gṛhītvā paribhuktam/
031.020. āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ saṃlakṣayati--pūrvamuktaṃ bhagavatā--duṣkarakārakau hi bhikṣavaḥ putrasya mātāpitarau āpyāyakau poṣakau saṃvardhakau stanyasya dātārau citrasya jambudvīpasya darśayitārau/
031.022. ekenāṃśena putro mātaraṃ dvitīyena pitaraṃ pūrṇavarṣaśataṃ paricaret, yadvā asyāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ maṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvarta iti, evamrūpe vā vividhaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayat, neyatā putreṇa mātāpitaroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syādupakṛtaṃ vā/
031.025. yastu asāvaśrāddhaṃ mātāpitaraṃ śraddhāsampadi samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati, duḥśīlaṃ śīlasampadi, matsariṇaṃ tyāgasampadi, duṣprajñaṃ prajñāsampadi samādāpayati vinayati niveśayati pratiṣṭhāpayati, iyatā putreṇa mātāpitroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syādupakṛtaṃ veti/
031.028. mayā ca mātur na kaścidupakāraḥ kṛtaḥ/
031.028. yadahaṃ samanvāhareyaṃ kutra me mātā upapanneti/
031.029. samanvāhartuṃ saṃvṛttaḥ paśyati marīcike lokadhātau upapannā/
031.030. sa saṃlakṣayati--kasya vineyā? paśyati bhagavataḥ/
031.030. tasyaitadabhavat--dūraṃ vayamihāgatāḥ/
031.031. yannvahametamarthaṃ bhagavato nivedayeyamiti bhagavantamidamavocat--uktaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā pūrvam--duṣkarakārakau hi bhikṣavaḥ putrasya mātāpitarau iti/
031.032. tanmama mātā marīcike lokadhātau upapannā, <32>sā ca bhagavato vineyā/
body.translated_text:
031.001. At that time, two <s>Nāga</s> kings named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s> dwelt in the great ocean.
031.001. They reflected: 'The Blessed One is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.
031.002. Let us go; we shall hear the <s>Dharma</s>.'
031.002. Then those two, accompanied by five hundred <s>Nāgas</s>, producing five hundred rivers, set out for the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.
031.003. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are of unfailing mindfulness.
031.004. The Blessed One reflected: 'If these two <s>Nāga</s> kings, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s>, come to the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>, they will cause devastation.'
031.005. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Accept, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s emergency alms-food.
031.006. For what reason? There are, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, five kinds of emergency alms-food for me.
031.007. Which five? For a newcomer, for a traveler, for the sick, for an attendant of the sick, and for a provisions-keeper.
031.007. In this matter, the Blessed One is engaged in the role of provisions-keeper.'
031.008. Then the Blessed One, together with <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, approached the two <s>Nāga</s> kings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s>.
031.009. They said: 'Be mindful, O <s>Nāga</s> lords — the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s> will be made uninhabitable [by floods].'
031.010. They said: 'We have come, Venerable Sir, with such faith that we are unable to cause harm even to a single ant, let alone to the people dwelling in the city of <s>Sūrpāraka</s>.'
031.012. Then the Blessed One taught such <s>Dharma</s> to the two <s>Nāga</s> kings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Gautamaka</s> that, upon hearing it, they took refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and accepted the precepts.
031.013. The Blessed One began to take his meal.
031.014. Each <s>Nāga</s> reflected: 'Oh, if only the Blessed One would drink my water!'
031.015. The Blessed One reflected: 'If I drink the water of only one, the others will be displeased.
031.015. A skillful means must be devised.'
031.016. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Go, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, to where the five hundred rivers converge, and from there bring a bowl-full of water.'
031.017. 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> replied to the Blessed One, went to where the five hundred rivers converged, took a bowl-full of water, and approached the Blessed One.
031.019. Having approached, he offered the bowl-full of water to the Blessed One.
031.020. The Blessed One accepted and drank it.
031.020. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> reflected: 'The Blessed One has previously said: "Difficult to repay, O monks, are a son's mother and father — they are his nourishers, his sustainers, his raisers, the givers of milk, and those who show him this beautiful <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
031.022. Even if a son were to carry his mother on one shoulder and his father on the other for a full hundred years, or were to establish them in sovereignty over this great earth with its gems — pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, emerald, <s>musāragalva</s>, ruby, and right-spiraling conch — and in such manifold lordship, even so the son would not have repaid or made recompense to his mother and father.
031.025. But he who leads his faithless mother and father to the endowment of faith, persuades, guides, and establishes them in it; leads the unvirtuous to the endowment of virtue, the miserly to the endowment of generosity, and the unwise to the endowment of wisdom — persuades, guides, and establishes them — by this much has a son repaid and made recompense to his mother and father."
031.028. But I have done no service to my mother.
031.028. Let me investigate: where has my mother been reborn?'
031.029. He investigated and saw that she had been reborn in the <s>Marīcika</s> world-system.
031.030. He reflected: 'Whose disciple is she to be trained?' He saw: the Blessed One's.
031.030. He thought: 'We have come far from here.
031.031. Let me report this matter to the Blessed One.' He said to the Blessed One: 'It was said, Venerable Sir, by the Blessed One previously: "Difficult to repay, O monks, are a son's mother and father."
031.032. Now my mother has been reborn in the <s>Marīcika</s> world-system, and she is one to be trained by the Blessed One.'

body.text:
032.001. tadarhati bhagavāṃs tāṃ vinetumanukampāmupādāyeti/
032.001. bhagavān kathayati--maudgalyāyana, kasya ṛddhyā gacchāmah? bhagavan madīyayā/
032.002. tato bhagavānāyuṣmāṃśca mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ sumerumūrdhni pādān sthāpayantau saṃprasthitau/
032.003. saptame divase marīcikaṃ lokadhātumanuprāptaḥ/
032.004. adrākṣīt sā bhadrakanyā āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ dūrādeva/
032.004. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ sasambhramāt tatsakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati--cirādbata putrakaṃ paśyāmīti/
032.005. tato janakāyaḥ kathayati--bhadanto 'yaṃ pravrajito vṛddhaḥ/
032.006. iyaṃ ca kanyā/
032.006. kathamasya mātā bhavatīti? āyuṣmān maudgalyāyanaḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, mama ime skandhā anyāḥ saṃvṛddhāḥ/
032.007. tena mameyaṃ māteti/
032.008. tato bhagavatā tasyā bhadrakanyāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tayā bhadrakanyayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśaulaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
032.010. sā dṛṣṭasatyā trirudānamudānayati pūrvavat yāvat pratiṣṭhāpitā devamanuṣyeṣu/
032.011. āha ca--
032.012. tavānubhāvātpihitaḥ sughoro hyapāyamārgo bahudoṣaduṣṭaḥ/
032.013. apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaṃ ca mayopalabdham//16//
body.translated_text:
032.001. 'Therefore, may the Blessed One, out of compassion, deign to train her.'
032.001. The Blessed One said: '<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, by whose supernatural power shall we go?' 'By mine, Blessed One.'
032.002. Then the Blessed One and the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, placing their feet on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, set out.
032.003. On the seventh day, they arrived at the <s>Marīcika</s> world-system.
032.004. That virtuous maiden saw the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> from a great distance.
032.004. Upon seeing him, she rushed to his presence and said: 'After so long, I see my dear son!'
032.005. Then the people said: 'This venerable one is an aged renunciant.
032.006. And this is a young maiden.
032.006. How can she be his mother?' The Venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said: 'Good people, these aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) of mine have grown differently.
032.007. Therefore she is my mother.'
032.008. Then the Blessed One, having known the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament of that virtuous maiden, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the four noble truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>) that, upon hearing it, that virtuous maiden, shattering with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain-peak of the view of the perishable body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty summits, realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
032.010. She, having seen the truth, uttered three exclamations as before, and was established among gods and humans.
032.011. And she said:
032.012. 'By your power, the terrible road to the lower realms, defiled with many faults, has been blocked;
032.013. the meritorious path to heaven has been opened, and I have attained the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' // 16 //

body.text:
032.014. tvadāśrayāccāptamapetadoṣaṃ mamādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ/
032.015. prāptaṃ ca kāntaṃ padamāryakāntaṃ tīrṇā ca duḥkhārṇavapāramasmi//17//
body.translated_text: By taking refuge in you, my vision, now purified and perfectly clear, has been obtained, free from all faults; and I have attained the beloved state cherished by the <s>Āryas</s> (noble ones), and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering. //17//

body.text:
032.016. jagati daityanarāmarapūjita vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya/
032.017. bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana saphalamadya mune tava darśanam//18//
body.translated_text: O you who are worshipped by <s>Daityas</s>, humans, and <s>Amaras</s> (gods) in the world, free from birth, old age, death, and disease, whose sight is exceedingly rare even in thousands of existences — fruitful indeed is your <s>darśana</s> (sight) today, O sage! //18//

body.text:
032.018. atikrāntāhaṃ bhadanta atikrāntā/
032.018. eṣāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
032.019. upāsikāṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāmabhiprasannām/
032.020. adhivāsayatu me bhagavānadya piṇḍapātena sārdhamāryamahāmaudgalyāyaneneti/
032.020. adhivāsayati bhagavāṃs tasyā bhadrakanyāyāstūṣṇībhāvena/
032.021. atha sā bhadrakanyā bhagavantamāyuṣmantaṃ ca mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhātahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
032.024. bhagavatā tasyā dharmo deśitaḥ/
032.024. āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pātragrāhakaḥ pātraṃ niryātayati/
032.025. bhagavatā abhihitah--maudgalyāyana gacchāmaḥ/
032.026. gacchāmo bhagavan/
032.026. kasya ṛddhyā? tathāgatasya bhagavataḥ/
032.026. yadi evam, samanvāhara jetavanam/
032.027. āgatāḥ smo bhagavan, āgatāḥ/
032.027. maudgalyāyanastato vismayāvarjitamatiḥ kathayati--kiṃ nāmeyaṃ bhagavann ṛddhih? manojavā maudgalyāyana/
032.028. na mayā bhadanta vijñātamevaṃ gambhīramevaṃ gambhīrā buddhadharmā iti/
032.029. yadi vijñātamabhaviṣyat, tilaśo 'pi me saṃcūrṇitaśarīreṇānuttarāyāḥ samyaksambodheścittaṃ vyāvartitamabhaviṣyat/
032.030. idānīṃ kiṃ karomi dagdhendhana iti//
body.translated_text: I have been saved, Venerable Sir, saved! I go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks). Accept me as an <s>upāsikā</s> (lay devotee), from this day forward, as long as I live and breathe, one who has gone for refuge and is full of faith. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept my offering of food today together with the noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to that <s>Bhadrakanyā</s> (virtuous maiden) by remaining silent. Then that <s>Bhadrakanyā</s>, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> were comfortably seated, satisfied and refreshed them with her own hands with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft. Knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating, that his hands were washed and the bowl removed, she took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught her the <s>Dharma</s>. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, as the bowl-bearer of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, handed over the bowl. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, let us go." "Let us go, <s>Bhagavān</s>." "By whose supernatural power?" "By that of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>." "If so, fix your mind on <s>Jetavana</s>." "We have arrived, <s>Bhagavān</s>, we have arrived!" <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, his mind overcome with wonder, said: "What is this supernatural power called, <s>Bhagavān</s>?" "It is swift as thought, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>." "I had not understood, Venerable Sir, how profound — how profound the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are!" "Had you understood, even with your body crushed to sesame-sized pieces, your mind would have turned away from supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>)." "Now what can I do? I am like burnt fuel."

body.text: 032.031. tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā pūrṇena karma kṛtam yenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ, kiṃ karma kṛtam yena <33>dāsyāḥ kukṣau upapannaḥ, pravrajya ca sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam? bhagavānāha--pūrṇena bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitāani avaśyambhāvīni/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> was performed by the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> that he was born in a wealthy, greatly rich, and greatly prosperous family? What <s>karma</s> was done that he was born from the womb of a slave-woman, and that, having gone forth, he realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "The <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated by the monk <s>Pūrṇa</s>, whose requisites have been gathered and whose conditions have ripened, stand present like a flood, and must inevitably bear fruit."

body.text:
033.003. pūrṇena karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni/
033.003. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
033.007. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatairapi/
033.008. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//19//
body.translated_text: The <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated by <s>Pūrṇa</s> [himself]. Who else will experience their results? O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated, whether wholesome or unwholesome, ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); when they meet the right conditions and the right time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. //19//

body.text:
033.009. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'sminneva bhadrakalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca/
033.011. buddho bhagavān vārāṇasīṃ nagarīmupaniśritya viharati/
033.012. tasyāyaṃ śāsane pravrajitaḥ/
033.012. tripiṭakasaṃghasya ca dharmavaiyāvṛtyaṃ karoti/
033.012. yāvadanyatamasyārhata upadhivāraḥ prāptaḥ/
033.013. sa vihāraṃ saṃmarṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
033.013. vāyunetaścāmutaśca saṃkāro nīyate/
033.013. sa saṃlakṣayati--tiṣṭhatu tāvad yāvadvāyurupaśamaṃ gacchatīti/
033.014. vaiyāvṛtyakareṇāsaṃmṛṣṭo vihāro dṛṣṭaḥ/
033.015. tena tīvreṇa paryavasthānena kharavākkarma niścāritam--kasya dāsīputrasyopadhivāra iti/
033.015. tena arhatā śrutam/
033.015. sa saṃlakṣayati--paryavasthito 'yam/
033.016. tiṣṭhatu tāvat/
033.016. paścāt saṃjñāpayiṣyāmīti/
033.017. yadā asya paryavasthānaṃ vigataṃ tadā tasya sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati--jānīṣe tvaṃ ko 'hamiti? sa kathayati--jāne tvaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajito 'hamapīti/
033.018. sa kathayati--yadyapyevaṃ tathāpi tu yanmayā pravrajya caraṇīyaṃ tatkṛtamahaṃ sakalabandhanābaddhaḥ/
033.019. kharaṃ te vākkarma niścāritam/
033.020. atyayamatyayato deśaya/
033.020. apyevaitatkarma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchediti/
033.021. tenātyayamatyayato deśitam/
033.021. yattena naraka upapadya dāsīputreṇa bhavitavyam, tannarake nopapannaḥ/
033.022. pañca tu janmaśatāni dāsyāḥ kukṣau upapannaḥ/
033.022. yāvadetarhyapi carame bhave dāsyā eva kukṣau upapannaḥ/
033.023. yat saṃghasyopasthānaṃ kṛtam, tenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ/
033.024. yattatra paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam, tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
033.025. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntaśuklo vipākaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
033.027. tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
033.028. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: Long ago, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (fortunate aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. [<s>Pūrṇa</s>] had gone forth in his dispensation and served the <s>Tripiṭaka</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> (community versed in the three baskets). Then a certain <s>Arhat</s>'s turn for maintenance duty arrived. He began to sweep the monastery, but the wind carried the refuse here and there. He thought: "Let me wait until the wind subsides." The duty-officer saw that the monastery was left unswept. With intense vexation, he uttered harsh speech: "Whose turn is it, this son of a slave-woman?" That <s>Arhat</s> heard this. He thought: "This one is overcome by defilement. Let it be; I shall instruct him later." When his vexation had subsided, [the <s>Arhat</s>] approached him and said: "Do you know who I am?" He replied: "I know — you have gone forth in the dispensation of the perfectly awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and so have I." [The <s>Arhat</s>] said: "Even so, nevertheless, I have accomplished what was to be done after going forth. I am freed from all bonds. You have uttered harsh speech. Confess your transgression as a transgression, so that this <s>karma</s> may become attenuated, diminished, and exhausted." He confessed his transgression as a transgression. Because of that, he was not reborn in hell, where he would have been a slave-woman's son. But for five hundred births he was born from the womb of a slave-woman. Even now, in his final birth, he was born from the womb of a slave-woman. Because he served the <s>Saṃgha</s>, he was born in a wealthy, greatly rich, and greatly prosperous family. Because he studied, recited, and gained skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (textual divisions), he realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> in my dispensation. Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, entirely black <s>karmas</s> have entirely black results; entirely white <s>karmas</s> have entirely white results; and mixed <s>karmas</s> have mixed results. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, having abandoned entirely black <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, effort should be made toward entirely white <s>karmas</s> alone. Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train yourselves.

body.text:
033.029. idamavocadbhagavān/
033.029. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>bhikṣus</s>, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 033.030. iti śrīdivyāvadāne pūrṇāvadānaṃ dvitīyam//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pūrṇāvadāna</s> (the narrative of <s>Pūrṇa</s>), the second, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text:
034.001. div3 maitreyāvadānam/
034.002. yadā rājñā bhāgadhena ajātaśatruṇā vaidehīputreṇa naukramo mātāpitrormāpitastadā vaiśālakairlicchavibhirbhagavato 'rthe naukramo māpitaḥ/
034.003. nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--vayaṃ vinipatitaśarīrā yannu vayaṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇa bhagavantaṃ nadī{dīm} gaṅgāmuttārayema iti/
034.004. taiḥ phaṇasaṃkramo māpitaḥ/
034.005. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--rājagṛhāt śrāvastīṃ gantum yo yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣava utsahate rājño māgadhasyājātaśatrorvaidehīputrasya nausaṃkrameṇa nadīgaṅgāmuttartum, sa tena taratu, yo vā bhikṣavo vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnāṃ nausaṃkrameṇa, so 'pi tenottararu/
034.007. ahamapi āyuṣmatā ānandena bhikṣuṇā sārdhaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇa nadīṃ gaṅgāmuttariṣyāmi/
034.008. tatra kecit rājño māgadhasyājātaśatrorvaidehīputrasya nausaṃkrameṇottīrṇāḥ, kecit vaiśālikānāṃ licchavīnāṃ nausaṃkrameṇa/
034.010. bhagavānapi āyuṣmatā ānandena sārdhaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇasaṃkrameṇottīrṇaḥ/
034.010. athānyatamopāsakastasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
034.012. ye tarantyarṇavaṃ saraḥ setuṃ kṛtvā visṛjya palvalāni/
034.013. kolaṃ hi janāḥ prabandhitā uttīrṇā medhāvino janāḥ//1//
body.translated_text: <s>Divyāvadāna</s> 3: The <s>Maitreyāvadāna</s> (narrative of <s>Maitreya</s>). When King <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, had a boat-bridge constructed in honor of his parents, then the <s>Vaiśālikas</s>, the <s>Licchavis</s>, had a boat-bridge constructed for the sake of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-kings) considered: "We are beings whose bodies have fallen low; let us ferry the <s>Bhagavān</s> across the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by a bridge of hoods." They constructed a hood-bridge. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "To go from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to <s>Śrāvastī</s> — whichever of you <s>bhikṣus</s> is able to cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by the boat-bridge of King <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, let him cross by that; or whichever <s>bhikṣu</s> [wishes to cross] by the boat-bridge of the <s>Vaiśālika</s> <s>Licchavis</s>, let him also cross by that. I myself, together with the monk, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, shall cross the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> by the hood-bridge of the <s>Nāgas</s>." There, some crossed by the boat-bridge of King <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>; some by the boat-bridge of the <s>Vaiśālika</s> <s>Licchavis</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> also, together with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, crossed by the hood-bridge of the <s>Nāgas</s>. Then a certain <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee) spoke this verse on that occasion: "Those who cross the flood and the lake, having made a bridge and leaving behind the pools — indeed, people bind a raft, but the wise have already crossed over." //1//

body.text:
034.014. uttīrṇo bhagavān buddho brāhmaṇastiṣṭhati sthale/
034.015. bhikṣavo 'tra parisnānti kolaṃ badhnanti śrāvakāḥ//2//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> has crossed over; the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> stands on firm ground. The <s>bhikṣus</s> bathe here; the <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) tie a raft. //2//

body.text:
034.016. kiṃ kuryādudapānena āpaścet sarvato yadi/
034.017. chittveha mūlaṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ kasya paryeṣaṇāṃ caret//3// iti//
body.translated_text: What use is a well if water is available on all sides? Having cut the root of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) here, for whom would one search? //3//

body.text:
034.018. adrākṣīdbhagavānanyatamasmin bhūbhāge unnatonnataṃ pṛthivīpradeśam/
034.018. dṛṣṭvā ca punarāyuṣmantamāmantrayate--icchasi tvamānanda yo 'sau yūya ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasraṃ tiryak ṣoḍaśapravedho nānāratnavicitro vitaḥ, taṃ draṣṭum? etasya bhagavan kālaḥ, etasya sugatasamayaḥ, yo 'yaṃ bhagavān yūpamucchrāpayet, bhikṣavaḥ paśyeyuḥ/
034.022. tato bhagavatā cakrasvatikanandyāvartena jālāvanaddhenānekapuṇyaśatanirjātena bhītānāmāśvāsanakareṇa pṛthivī parāmṛṣṭā/
034.024. nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--kimarthaṃ bhagavatā pṛthivī parāmṛṣṭeti? yāvat paśyanti yūyaṃ draṣṭukāmāḥ/
034.024. tatastairucchrāpitaḥ/
034.024. bhikṣavo yūpaṃ draṣṭumārabdhāḥ/
034.025. āyuṣmānapi bhaddālī alpotsukaḥ pāṃsukūlaṃ sīvyati/
034.025. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--ārohapariṇāhaṃ nimittaṃ bhikṣavo yūpasya gṛhṇīta, antardhāsyatīti/
034.026. antarhitaḥ/
034.027. bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--paśya bhadanta bhikṣavo yūpaṃ paśyanti/
034.027. āyuṣmānapi bhaddālī alpotsukaḥ pāṃsukūlaṃ sīvyati/
034.028. kiṃ tāvat vītararāgatvādāhosvit paryupāsitapūrvatvāt? tadyadi tāvad vītarāgatvāt, santyanye 'pi vītarāgāḥ/
034.029. atha paryupāsitapūrvatvāt? kutra kena paryupāsitamiti/
034.030. bhagavānāha--api bhikṣavo vītarāgatvādapi paryupāsitapūrvatvāt/
034.030. kutrānena paryupāsitam?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw an uneven tract of ground in a certain region of the earth. Having seen it, he again addressed the venerable [<s>Ānanda</s>]: "Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to see that sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) which rises a thousand <s>vyāmas</s> upward and extends sixteen [<s>vyāmas</s>] laterally, adorned with various gems?" "This is the time for that, <s>Bhagavān</s>; this is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> raise the <s>yūpa</s> so that the <s>bhikṣus</s> may see it." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> touched the earth with his <s>cakrasvatika</s>-<s>nandyāvarta</s>-marked hand, covered with a web [of light], born of innumerable hundreds of merits, which gives assurance to the frightened. The <s>Nāgas</s> considered: "For what purpose has the <s>Bhagavān</s> touched the earth?" "Those of you who wish to see, behold!" Then they raised it up. The <s>bhikṣus</s> began to look at the <s>yūpa</s>. The venerable <s>Bhaddālī</s>, being of few desires, was sewing his rag-robe. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Take note of the height and circumference of the <s>yūpa</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for it will disappear." It disappeared. The <s>bhikṣus</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Look, Venerable Sir — the <s>bhikṣus</s> are looking at the <s>yūpa</s>, but the venerable <s>Bhaddālī</s>, being of few desires, is sewing his rag-robe. Is it because of dispassion, or because he has attended upon [such a post] before?" "If it is because of dispassion, there are others who are dispassionate too. If it is because he has attended upon one before, where and by whom was it attended upon?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is both because of dispassion and because he has attended upon one before. Where did he attend upon it?"

body.text:
035.001. <35>bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo rājābhūta praṇādo nāma śakrasya devendrasya vayasyakaḥ/
