035.001. so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitah--anekadhanasamudito 'hamaputraśca/
035.002. mamātyayād rājavaṃśasamucchedo bhaviṣyatīti/
035.003. tataḥ śakreṇa dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaśca--mārṣa, kasmāt tvaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparastiṣṭhasīti? sa kathayati--kauśila, anekadhanasamudito 'hamaputraśca/
035.005. mamātyayād rājavaṃśasyocchedo bhaviṣyati/
035.005. śakraḥ kathayati--mārṣa, mā tvaṃ cintāparastiṣṭha/
035.006. yadi kaścit cyavanadharmā devaputro bhaviṣyati, tatte putratve samādāpayiṣyāmīti/
035.007. dharmatā khalu cyavanadharmaṇo devaputrasya pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhavanti--akliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi saṃkliśyanti, amlānāni mālyāni mlāyante, daurgandhaṃ mukhānniścarati, ubhābhyāṃ kakṣābhyāṃ svedaḥ pragharati, sve cāsane dhṛtiṃ na labhate/
035.009. yāvadanyatamasya devaputrasya pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhūtāni/
035.010. sa śakreṇa devendreṇoktah--mārṣa, praṇādasya rājño 'grāmahiṣyāḥ kukṣau pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhāṇeti/
035.011. sa kathayati--pramādasthānaṃ kauśikam/
035.011. bahukilbiṣkāriṇo hi kauśika rājānaḥ/
035.012. mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kṛtvā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyāmīti/
035.012. śakraḥ kathayati--mārṣa, ahaṃ te smārayiṣyāmi/
035.013. pramattāḥ kauśalika devā ratibahulāḥ/
035.013. evametanmārṣa/
035.013. tathāpi tvahaṃ bhavantaṃ smārayāmi/
035.014. tena praṇādasya rājño 'gramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau pratisaṃdhirgṛhītā/
035.014. yasminneva divase pratisaṃdhirgṛhītā, tasmin divase mahājanakāyena praṇādo muktaḥ/
035.015. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
035.016. dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāsaḥ/
035.017. tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti/
035.018. jñātaya ūcuh--yasminneva divase 'yaṃ dārako mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ, tasminneva divase mahājanakāyena nādo muktaḥ/
035.019. yasminneva divase jātastasminneva divase mahājanakāyena nādo muktaḥ/
035.020. tasmāt bhavatu dārakasya mahāpraṇāda iti nāma/
035.021. tasya mahāpraṇāda iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
035.021. mahāpraṇādo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradatto dvābhyāṃsaṃdhātrībhyāṃ dvāghyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyām/
035.023. so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarṇpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
035.024. āśu vardhate hradasthāmiva paṅkajam/
035.024. yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ/
035.025. saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ hastiparīkṣāyāmaśvaparīkṣāyāṃ kumāraparīkṣāyāṃ kumārīparīkṣāyām/
035.026. so 'ṣṭāsu parīkṣāsūdghaṭṭako vācakaḥ paṭupracāraḥ paṇḍitaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
035.027. sa yāni tāni rāajñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhnābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryasthāmavīryamanuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamabhinirjityādhyāsatāṃ pṛthag bhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni, tadyathā--hastiśikṣāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe śare dhanuṣi prayāṇe niryāṇe 'ṅkuśagrahe pāśagrahe tomaragrahe yaṣṭibandhe padabandhe śikhābandhe dūravedhe marmavedhe 'kṣuṇṇavedhe dṛḍhaprahāritāyāṃ pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān</s> said: In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), there was a king named <s>Praṇāda</s>, a friend of <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s> (gods). He was without a son, yet longing for a son, and placing his chin on his hand, he stood absorbed in worry: "I am endowed with abundant wealth, yet I am sonless. After my death, the royal lineage will be destroyed." Then <s>Śakra</s> saw him and asked: "Dear sir, why do you stand with chin in hand, absorbed in worry?" He replied: "O <s>Kauśika</s>, I am endowed with abundant wealth yet I am sonless. After my death, the royal lineage will be destroyed." <s>Śakra</s> said: "Dear sir, do not stand absorbed in worry. If there is some <s>devaputra</s> (son of a god) destined to fall from heaven, I will persuade him to become your son." Indeed, it is a natural law that five premonitory signs appear in a <s>devaputra</s> destined to fall: his unsoiled garments become soiled, his unwilted garlands wilt, a foul smell issues from his mouth, sweat flows from both armpits, and he finds no comfort on his own seat. Then the five premonitory signs appeared in a certain <s>devaputra</s>. He was told by <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>: "Dear sir, take rebirth in the womb of King <s>Praṇāda</s>'s chief queen." He replied: "That is a place of heedlessness, O <s>Kauśika</s>. For kings are great sinners, O <s>Kauśika</s>. Let me not rule unrighteously and become destined for hell." <s>Śakra</s> said: "Dear sir, I will remind you." "The gods are heedless, O <s>Kauśika</s>, given to pleasures." "That is so, dear sir. Nevertheless, I will remind you." Then he took rebirth in the womb of King <s>Praṇāda</s>'s chief queen. On the very day he took rebirth, a great outcry was released by a large assembly of people for <s>Praṇāda</s>. She gave birth after eight or nine months. A boy was born, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair-complexioned, golden in color, with a head shaped like an umbrella, long arms, a broad forehead, joined eyebrows, and a prominent nose. His relatives, having gathered together, determined a name: "What shall be the name of the boy?" The relatives said: "On the very day this boy descended into his mother's womb, on that very day a great outcry was released by the assembly. And on the very day he was born, on that very day too a great outcry was released." Therefore they gave the boy the name <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> (Great Outcry). King <s>Praṇāda</s> established the prince <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>. And <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>, saw that <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> was established and said: "Dear sir, I have persuaded you into the sonship of King <s>Praṇāda</s>. Do not rule unrighteously, lest you become destined for hell." He replied: "So be it."

body.text:
035.032. dharmatā khalu na tāvat putrasya nāma prajñāyate yāvat tāto jīvati/
035.032. apareṇa samayena <36>praṇādo rājā kālagataḥ/
body.translated_text: Indeed, it is a natural law that a son's name is not recognized as long as the father lives. After some time, King <s>Praṇāda</s> passed away.

body.text:
036.001. mahāpraṇādo rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
036.001. sa yāvattāvad dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā adharmeṇa kārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
036.002. tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇoktah--mārṣa, mayā tvaṃ praṇādasya rājñaḥ samādāpitaḥ/
036.003. mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāraya, mā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyasīti/
036.004. sa yāvattāvad dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā punarapi adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
036.004. dvirapi śakreṇoktah--mārṣa, mayā tvaṃ praṇādasya rājñaḥ putratve samādāpitaḥ/
036.005. mā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāraya, mā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyasīti/
036.006. sa kathayati--kauśika, vayaṃ rājānaḥ pramattā iti ratibahulāḥ kṣaṇād vismarāmaḥ/
036.007. kiṃcittvamasmākaṃ cihnaṃ sthāpaya, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā dānāni dāsyāmaḥ, puṇyāni kārayiṣyāma iti/
036.008. na ca śakyate vinā nimittena puṇyaṃ kartum/
036.008. tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇa viśvakarmaṇo devaputrasyājñā dattā--gaccha tvaṃ viśvakarman rājño mahāpraṇādasya niveśane/
036.009. divyaṃ maṇḍalavāṭaṃ nirmiṇu, yūpaṃ cocchrāpaya/
036.010. ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasreṇa tiryak ṣoḍaśapravedhaṃ nānāratnavicitraṃ sarvasauvarṇamiti/
036.011. tato viśvakarmaṇā devaputreṇa mahāpraṇādasya rājño niveśane divyo maṇḍalavāṭo nirmito yūpaścocchritaḥ/
036.012. ūrdhvaṃ vyāmasahasraṃ nānāratnavicitro divyaḥ sarvasauvarṇaḥ/
036.012. tato mahāpraṇādena rājñā dānaśālā māpitā/
036.013. tasya mātulo 'śoko nāma yūpasya paricārako vyavasthitaḥ/
036.014. tato yūpadarśanodyuktaḥ sarva eva jambudvīpanivāsī janakāya āgatya bhuktvā yūpaṃ paśyati, svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti/
036.015. tataḥ kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ/
036.015. rājñaḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante/
036.016. amātyaiḥ stokāḥ karapratyāyā upanītāḥ/
036.016. mahāpraṇādo rājā pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, kasmāt stokāḥ karapratyāyā upanītāh? deva, jambudvīpanivāsī janakāya āgatya bhuktvā yūpaṃ paśyati, svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti/
036.018. kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ/
036.018. rājñaḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhanta iti/
036.019. rājā kathayati--samucchidyatāṃ dānaśāleti/
036.019. taiḥ samucchinnā/
036.019. tato 'pyasau janakāyaḥ svapathyadanamādāya bhuktvā yūpaṃ nirīkṣamāṇastiṣṭhati, svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti/
036.021. kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ/
036.021. tathāpi karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante/
036.021. rājā pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, dānaśalāḥ samucchinnāḥ/
036.022. idānīṃ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhanta iti/
036.022. amātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, janakāyaḥ svapathyadanamādāya bhuktvā yūpaṃ nīrīkṣamāṇastiṣṭhati, svakarmānuṣṭhānaṃ na karoti/
036.023. kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchinnāḥ, yataḥ karapratyāyā nottiṣṭhante/
036.024. tato rājñā mahāpraṇādena dānāni dattvā puṇyāni kṛtvā sa yūpo nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāmāplāvitaḥ/
036.025. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau māpraṇādasyāśoko nāma mātulaḥ, eṣa evāsau bhaddālī bhikṣuḥ/
036.026. tatrānena paryupāsitapūrvaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> was established in the kingdom. For a while he ruled the kingdom righteously, but then began to rule unrighteously. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>, said: "Dear sir, I persuaded you into the sonship of King <s>Praṇāda</s>. Do not rule unrighteously, lest you become destined for hell." For a while he ruled the kingdom righteously, but then again began to rule unrighteously. A second time <s>Śakra</s> said: "Dear sir, I persuaded you into the sonship of King <s>Praṇāda</s>. Do not rule unrighteously, lest you become destined for hell." He replied: "O <s>Kauśika</s>, we kings are heedless and given to pleasures; we forget in an instant. Please establish some sign for us, upon seeing which we will give gifts and perform meritorious deeds." For it is not possible to perform merit without a cause. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the <s>devas</s>, gave a command to the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Viśvakarman</s>: "Go, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, to the palace of King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>. Construct a divine circular enclosure and erect a sacrificial post, one thousand fathoms high, sixteen measures across, adorned with various jewels, entirely made of gold." Then the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Viśvakarman</s> constructed a divine circular enclosure in King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>'s palace and erected the sacrificial post, one thousand fathoms high, adorned with various jewels, divine and entirely golden. Then King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> established a hall of giving. His maternal uncle named <s>Aśoka</s> was appointed as caretaker of the sacrificial post. Then, eager to see the sacrificial post, all the people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> came and, having eaten, would gaze at the post and not perform their own work. Thus agricultural activities ceased. The king's tax revenues did not come in. The ministers brought only meager tax revenues. King <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> asked: "Gentlemen, why are only meager tax revenues brought?" "Your Majesty, the people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> come and, having eaten, gaze at the post and do not perform their own work. Agricultural activities have ceased. The king's tax revenues do not come in." The king said: "Let the hall of giving be demolished." They demolished it. Yet the assembly of people would bring their own food and eat it while gazing at the post.

body.text:
036.027. kutra bhadanta asau yūpo vilayaṃ gamiṣyati? bhaviṣyanti bhikṣavo 'nāgate 'dhvani aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣo manuṣyāḥ/
036.028. aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ śaṅkho nāma rājā bhaviṣyati samyamanī cakravartī caturantavijetā dhārmiko dharmarājā saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ/
036.029. tasyemānyevaṃ rūpāṇi sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti/
036.030. tadyathā--cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam/
036.031. pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
036.032. sa imāmeva samudraparyantāṃ pṛthivīmakhilāmakaṇaṭakāmanutpīḍāmadaṇḍenāśasreṇa dharmeṇa <37>samayena abhinirjityādhyāvasiṣyati/
body.translated_text: "Where, Venerable One, will that sacrificial post disappear?" "In the future, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), humans will have a lifespan of eighty thousand years. When humans have a lifespan of eighty thousand years, there will be a king named <s>Śaṅkha</s>, a righteous <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a sovereign ruler, conqueror of the four quarters, a righteous king of <s>dharma</s>, endowed with seven treasures. He will have these seven treasures of such form: namely, the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh. And he will have a full thousand sons, heroes, brave, of excellent form, crushers of enemy armies. He will conquer this entire earth, bounded by the ocean, without thorns, without oppression, without punishment or sword, by <s>dharma</s> and righteous authority, and will dwell therein."

body.text:
037.001. śaṅkhasya rājño brahmāyur nāma brāhmaṇaḥ purohito bhaviṣyati/
037.002. tasya brahmavatī nāma patnī bhaviṣyati/
037.002. sā maitreyāṃśena sphuritvā putraṃ janayiṣyati maitreyaṃ nāma/
037.003. brahmāyurmāṇavo 'śītimāṇavakaśatāni brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayiṣyati/
037.003. sa tān māṇavakān maitreyāya anupradāsyati/
037.004. maitreyo māṇavo 'śītimāṇavakasahasrāṇi brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayiṣyati/
037.005. atha catvāro mahārājāścaturmahānidhisthāh--
037.006. piṅgalaśca kaliṅgeṣu mithilāyāṃ ca pāṇḍukaḥ/
037.007. elāpatraśca gāndhāre śaṅkho vārāṇasīpure//4//
body.translated_text: King <s>Śaṅkha</s> will have a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priest) named <s>Brahmāyus</s> as his chaplain. He will have a wife named <s>Brahmavatī</s>. She, having been inspired by a portion of <s>Maitreya</s>, will give birth to a son named <s>Maitreya</s>. The young <s>Brahmāyus</s> will teach the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priestly) <s>mantras</s> (sacred hymns) to eight hundred students. He will entrust those students to <s>Maitreya</s>. The young <s>Maitreya</s> will teach the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>mantras</s> to eighty thousand students. Then the four great kings will guard the four great treasures: <s>Piṅgala</s> in <s>Kaliṅga</s>, <s>Pāṇḍuka</s> in <s>Mithilā</s>, <s>Elāpatra</s> in <s>Gāndhāra</s>, and <s>Śaṅkha</s> in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

body.text:
037.008. enaṃ ca yūpamādāya śaṅkhasya rājña upanāmayiṣyanti/
037.008. śaṅkho 'pi rājā brahmāyuṣe brāhmaṇāyānupradāsyati/
037.009. brahmāyurapi brāhmaṇo maitreyāya māṇavāyānupradāsyati/
037.009. maitreyo 'pi māṇavasteṣāṃ māṇavakānāmanupradāsyati/
037.010. tataste māṇavakāstam yūpaṃ khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ chittvā bhājayiṣyanti/
037.011. tato maitreyo māṇavakastasya yūpasyānityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tenaiva saṃvegena vanaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati/
037.011. yasminneva divase vanaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati, tasminneva divase maitreyāṃśena sphuritvā anuttaraṃ jñānamadhigamiṣyati/
037.013. tasya maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddha iti saṃjñā bhaviṣyati/
037.013. yasminneva divase maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddho 'nuttarajñānamadhigamiṣyati, tasminneva divase śaṅkhasya rājñaḥ saptaratnānyantardhāsyante/
037.014. śaṅkho 'pi rājā aśītikoṭṭarājasahasraparivāro maitreyaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajiṣyati/
037.015. yadapyasya strīratnaṃ viśākhā nāma, sāpi aśītistrīsahasraparivārā maitreyaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajiṣyati/
037.017. tato maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddho 'śītibhikṣukoṭiparivāro yena gurupādakaḥ parvatastenopasaṃkramiṣyati, yatra kāśyapasya bhikṣorasthasaṃghāto 'vikopitastiṣṭhati/
037.018. gurupādakaparvato maitreyāya samyaksambuddhāya vivaramanupradāsyati/
037.019. yato maitreyaḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ kāśyapasya bhikṣoravikopitamasthisaṃghātaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇinā gṛhītvā vāme pāṇau pratiṣṭhāpya evaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati--yo 'sau bhikṣavo varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma śāstā loka utpannastasyāyaṃ śrāvakaḥ kāśyapo nāṃnā alpecchānāṃ saṃtuṣṭānāṃ dhūtaguṇavādināmagro, nirdiṣṭaḥ/
037.022. śākyamuneḥ parinirvṛtasyānena śāsanasaṃgītiḥ kṛtā iti/
037.023. te dṛṣṭvā saṃvegamāpatsyante--kathamidānīmīdṛśenātmabhāvenedṛśā guṇagaṇā adhigatā iti/
037.024. te tenaiva saṃvegenārhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti/
037.025. ṣaṇṇavatikoṭyo 'rhatāṃ bhaviṣyanti dhūtaguṇasākṣātkṛtāḥ/
037.025. yaṃ ca saṃvegamāpatsyante, tatrāsau yūpo vilayaṃ gamiṣyati//
body.translated_text: And taking this sacrificial post, they will present it to King <s>Śaṅkha</s>. King <s>Śaṅkha</s> too will give it to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Brahmāyus</s>. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Brahmāyus</s> too will give it to a young man named <s>Maitreya</s>. <s>Maitreya</s> the young man will give it to those young students. Then those young students, having cut that sacrificial post piece by piece, will distribute it. Then the young man <s>Maitreya</s>, having seen the impermanence of that sacrificial post, will resort to the forest with that very spiritual urgency. On the very day he resorts to the forest, on that very day, having manifested with the portion of <s>Maitreya</s>, he will attain unsurpassed knowledge. His designation will be <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One). On the very day <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> attains unsurpassed knowledge, on that very day the seven treasures of King <s>Śaṅkha</s> will disappear. King <s>Śaṅkha</s> too, accompanied by eighty thousand vassal kings, will go forth following <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> who has gone forth. As for his jewel-woman named <s>Viśākhā</s>, she too, accompanied by eighty thousand women, will go forth following <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> who has gone forth. Then <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>, accompanied by eighty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of monks, will approach <s>Gurupādaka</s> mountain, where the undisturbed bone-relics of the monk <s>Kāśyapa</s> remain. <s>Gurupādaka</s> mountain will open up for <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>. Then <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>, having taken the undisturbed bone-relics of the monk <s>Kāśyapa</s> with his right hand and placed them on his left palm, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to his disciples thus: "O monks, in a time when people lived a hundred years, a teacher named <s>Śākyamuni</s> arose in the world. This was his disciple named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, foremost among those of few desires, the contented, and the advocates of <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities)." He was so designated by <s>Śākyamuni</s>. After <s>Śākyamuni</s> attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), this one performed the compilation of the teaching. Seeing this, they will be filled with spiritual urgency, thinking: "How were such collections of virtues attained with such a bodily form?" With that very spiritual urgency, they will directly realize <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat). Ninety-six <s>koṭis</s> of <s>arhats</s> will come into being, having directly realized the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities). And when they attain that spiritual urgency, at that point the sacrificial post will dissolve.

037.027. ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo dvayo ratnayoryugapalloke prādurbhāvāya? bhagavānāha--praṇidhānavaśāt/
037.028. kutra bhagavan praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam?
037.029. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani madhyadeśe vāsavo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
037.030. tasya sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ/
037.030. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
037.031. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
037.031. uttarāpathe dhanasaṃmato nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
037.033. tasyāpi sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ/
037.033. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchatīti/
037.033. atīva <38>śasyasampattirbhavati/
body.translated_text: "What, Venerable One, is the cause, what is the condition for the simultaneous appearance in the world of two jewels?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "By the power of a vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>)." "Where, <s>Bhagavan</s>, was the vow made?" "Once upon a time, O monks, in a past era, in <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the Middle Country), a king named <s>Vāsava</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. His trees always bore flowers and fruit. The god (<s>Deva</s>) gave timely and proper showers of rain. The harvest was exceedingly abundant. In <s>Uttarāpatha</s> (the Northern Region), a king named <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. His trees also always bore flowers and fruit. The god gave timely and proper showers of rain. The harvest was exceedingly abundant.

body.text:
038.001. yāvadapareṇa samayena vāsavasya rājñaḥ putro jāto ratnapratyuptayā śikhayā/
038.002. tasya vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā ratnaśikhīti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
038.002. so 'pareṇa samayena jīrṇāturamṛtaṃsaṃdarśanādudvigno vanaṃ saṃśritaḥ/
038.003. yasminneva divase vanaṃ saṃśritastasminneva divase 'nuttaraṃ jñānamadhigatam/
038.004. tasya ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddha iti saṃjñodapādi/
038.004. athāpareṇa samayena dhanasaṃmato rājā upariprāsādatalagato 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtastiṣṭhati/
038.005. so 'mātyānāmantrayate--bhavataḥ, kasyacidanyasyāpi rājño rājyamevamṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
038.007. sadāpuṣpaphalā vṛkṣāḥ/
038.007. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchatīti/
038.008. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati yathā asmākamiti? madhyadeśād vaṇijaḥ paṇyamādāyottarāpathaṃ gatāḥ/
038.009. te kathayanti--asti deva madhyadeśe vāsavo nāma rājā iti/
038.009. sahaśravaṇādeva dhanasaṃmatasya rājño 'marṣa utpannaḥ/
038.010. sa saṃjātāmarṣo 'mātyānāmantrayate--saṃnāhayantu bhavantaścatruaṅgaṃ balakāyam/
038.011. rāṣṭrāpamardanamasya kariṣyāma iti/
038.011. tato dhanasaṃmato rājā caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ madhyadeśamāgatya gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe kūle 'vasthitaḥ/
038.013. aśrauṣīdvāsavo rājā--dhanasaṃmato rājā catruaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ madhyadeśamāgatya gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe kūle 'vasthita iti/
038.014. śrutvā ca punaḥ so 'pi caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyamaśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ patikāyaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare kūle 'vasthitaḥ/
038.016. atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastayorvinayakālaṃ jñātvā nadyā gaṅgāyāstīre rātriṃ vāsamupagataḥ/
038.017. ratnaśikhinā samyaksambuddhena laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam/
038.017. dharmatā khalu yadā buddhā bhagavanto laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti, tasmin samaye śakrabrahmādayo devā bhagavataścetasā cittamājānanti/
038.019. atha śakrabrahmādayo devā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
038.020. upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
038.020. teṣāṃ varṇānubhāvena mahānudārāvabhāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
038.021. dhanasaṃmatena rājñā dṛṣṭaḥ/
038.021. dṛṣṭvā ca punaramātyān pṛcchati--kimayaṃ bhavanto vāsavasya rājño vijite mahānudārāvabhāsah? te kathayanti--deva, vāsavasya rājño vijite mahānudārāvabhāsah? te kathayanti--deva, vāsavasya rājño vijite ratnaśikhī nāma samyaksambuddhah utpannaḥ/
038.023. tasya śakrabrahmādayo devā darśanāyopasaṃkramanti/
038.024. tenaivodārāvabhāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
038.024. maharddhiko 'sau mahānubhāvaḥ/
038.024. tasyāyamanubhāva iti/
038.025. dhanasaṃmato rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yasya vijite īdṛśaṃ dvipādakaṃ puṇyakṣetramutpannam, yaṃ śakrabrahmādayo 'pi devā darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti, tasyāhaṃ kīdṛśamanarthaṃ kariṣyāmi? tena tasya dūto 'nupreṣitaḥ/
038.027. vayasya, āgaccha/
038.027. na te 'haṃ kiṃcit kāriṣyāmi iti/
038.027. puṇyamaheśākhyastvam, yasya vijite dvipādakaṃ puṇyakṣetraṃ ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho 'yam/
038.028. śakrabrahmādayo devā darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti/
038.029. kiṃ tu kaṇṭhāśleṣaṃ te datvā gamiṣyāmi/
038.029. evamāvayoḥ parasparaṃ cittasaumanasyaṃ bhavatīti/
038.030. vāsavo rājā viśvāsaṃ na gacchati/
038.030. sa yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
038.031. upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
038.032. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--<39>mama bhadanta dhanasaṃmatena rājñā saṃdiṣṭam--priyavayasaya āgaccha, na te 'haṃ kiṃcit kariṣyāmi/
body.translated_text: After some time, a son was born to King <s>Vāsava</s>, with a crest studded with jewels. Having performed his birth celebration in detail, the name <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> was established for him. He, at a later time, being distressed by seeing old age, sickness, and death, resorted to the forest. On the very day he resorted to the forest, on that very day he attained unsurpassed knowledge. The designation <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) arose for him. Then at another time, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having ascended to the upper terrace of his palace, stood surrounded by a group of ministers. He addressed the ministers: "Sirs, does any other king also have a kingdom so prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people, with trees always bearing flowers and fruit, with the god giving timely and proper showers of rain, and with exceedingly abundant harvests, as ours?" Merchants from <s>Madhyadeśa</s>, having taken their wares, had gone to <s>Uttarāpatha</s>. They said: "Your Majesty, there is in <s>Madhyadeśa</s> a king named <s>Vāsava</s>." Upon hearing this, resentment arose in King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>. Having become resentful, he addressed the ministers: "Sirs, let them equip the fourfold army! We shall devastate his realm." Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having equipped the fourfold army -- elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry -- came to <s>Madhyadeśa</s> and stationed himself on the southern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. King <s>Vāsava</s> heard: "King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having equipped the fourfold army -- elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry -- has come to <s>Madhyadeśa</s> and stationed himself on the southern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>." Having heard this, he too equipped the fourfold army -- elephant corps, cavalry, chariot corps, and infantry -- and stationed himself on the northern bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Then <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>, knowing that the time for their disciplining had come, spent the night on the bank of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> produced a worldly thought. Indeed, it is the nature of things that when the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, produce a worldly thought, at that time <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods know the mind of the Blessed One with their own minds. Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> and sat down to one side. By the splendor of their radiance, a great and noble illumination arose. King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> saw it. Having seen it, he asked his ministers: "Sirs, what is this great and noble illumination in the domain of King <s>Vāsava</s>?" They said: "Your Majesty, in the domain of King <s>Vāsava</s>, a <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> has arisen. <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods come to see him. That is the source of this noble illumination. He is of great supernatural power, of great might. This is his power." King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> said: "Sirs, in whose domain such a two-footed field of merit has arisen, whom even <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods come to see -- what harm could I do to him?" Then he sent a messenger to him: "Dear friend, come! I will do you no harm. You are one of great merit and lordship, in whose domain the two-footed field of merit, <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>, has appeared. <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods come to see him. But I wish to give you an embrace and then depart. Thus may mutual goodwill of mind arise between us." King <s>Vāsava</s> did not trust him. He approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Vāsava</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>: "Venerable Sir, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> has sent me this message: 'Dear friend, come! I will do you no harm."

body.text:
039.002. kaṇḍhā kaṇḍhāśleṣaṃ śleṣaṃ datva agamiṣyāmi/
039.002. evamāvayoḥ parasparaṃ cittasaumanasyaṃ bhavatīti/
039.002. tatra mayā kathaṃ pratipattavyam? ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati--gaccha mahārāja, śobhanaṃ bhaviṣyati/
039.004. bhagavan, kiṃ mayā tasya pādayor nipatitavyam? mahārāja, balaśreṣṭhā hi rājānaḥ/
039.004. nipatitavyam/
039.005. atha vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
039.006. yena dhanasaṃmato rājā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
039.006. upasaṃkramya dhanasaṃmatasya rājñaḥ pādayor nipatitaḥ/
039.007. tato dhanasaṃmatena rājñā kaṇḍhe śleṣaṃ dattvā viśvāsamutpādya preṣitaḥ//
body.translated_text: "I will give an embrace and then depart. Thus may mutual goodwill of mind arise between us." How should I act in this matter?" <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> said: "Go, great king, it will be auspicious." "<s>Bhagavan</s>, should I fall at his feet?" "Great king, kings are indeed supreme in power. You should bow down." Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>, rose from his seat and departed. He approached King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>. Having approached, he fell at the feet of King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, having given him an embrace, inspired trust in him, and sent him off.

body.text:
039.008. atha vāsavo rājā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
039.008. upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
039.009. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo vāsavo rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--kasya bhadanta sarve rājānaḥ pādayor nipatanti? rājño mahārāja cakravartinaḥ/
039.011. atha vāsavo rājā utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena ratnaśikhī tathāgataḥ samyaksambuddhastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
039.013. atha vāsavo rājā tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñāpya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam, yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti/
039.016. atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena rājño vāsavasya bhaktabhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
039.018. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
039.018. atha rājā vāsavo ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
039.020. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ samatarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--anenāhaṃ bhadanta kuśalamūlena rājā syāṃ cakravartīti/
039.023. tatsamanantaraṃ ca śaṅkha āpūritaḥ/
039.023. tato ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho vāsavaṃ rājānamidamavocat--bhaviṣyasi mahārāja aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śaṅkho nāma rājā cakravartīti/
039.024. tata uccaśabdo mahāśabdo jātaḥ/
039.025. dhanasaṃmato rājā kolāhalaśabdaṃ śrutvā amātyān pṛcchati--kimeṣa bhavanto vāsavasya rājño vijite kolāhalaśabdaḥ śrūyate iti? tairāgamya niveditam--deva, ratnaśikhinā samyaksambuddhena vāsavo rājā cakravartirājye vyākṛta iti janakāyo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditaḥ/
039.028. tena kolāhalaśabdo jāta iti/
039.028. atha dhanasaṃmato rājā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
039.029. upasaṃkramya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
039.030. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo dhanasaṃmato rājā ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--kasya bhadanta sarve cakravartinaḥ pādayor nipatanti? tathāgatasya mahārāja arhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya/
039.032. atha dhanasaṃmato rājā utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhastenāñjalim<40> praṇamya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
body.translated_text: 039.008. Then King <s>Vāsava</s> approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>). 039.008. Having approached, he worshiped the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with his head and sat down to one side. 039.009. Seated to one side, King <s>Vāsava</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One: 'At whose feet, venerable sir, do all kings prostrate?' 'At the feet of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), O great king.' 039.011. Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One: 'May the Blessed One consent to a meal tomorrow in my inner palace, together with the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks)!' 039.013. Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food and drink, rising at dawn, having arranged seats and set out water-vessels, informed <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, of the time by a messenger: 'It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready — may the Blessed One come at whatever time he deems fit.' 039.016. Then <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, surrounded by the community of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the meal-offering of King <s>Vāsava</s>. 039.018. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks. 039.018. Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, knowing <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, to be comfortably seated, served and satisfied him with his own hands with pure and excellent food and drink. 039.020. Having served and satisfied [the Buddha] with his own hands in many ways with pure food and drink, knowing the Blessed One <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, to have finished eating, with washed hands and bowl removed, he prostrated at his feet and began to make an aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): 'By this root of merit, venerable sir, may I become a <s>Cakravartin</s> king!' 039.023. Immediately after that, a conch was sounded. 039.023. Then <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said this to King <s>Vāsava</s>: 'You shall become, O great king, among people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, a <s>Cakravartin</s> king named <s>Śaṅkha</s>.' 039.024. Then a loud, great cry arose. 039.025. King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, hearing the tumultuous cry, asked his ministers: 'Sirs, what is this tumultuous cry heard in the domain of King <s>Vāsava</s>?' They came and reported: 'Your Majesty, <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has prophesied that King <s>Vāsava</s> will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> — the people are delighted, pleased, and joyful. 039.028. Hence the tumultuous cry.' 039.028. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> approached <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. 039.029. Having approached, he worshiped the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with his head and sat down to one side. 039.030. Seated to one side, King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One: 'At whose feet, venerable sir, do all <s>Cakravartins</s> prostrate?' 'At the feet of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, O great king.' 039.032. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said this to <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One: 'May the Blessed One consent to a meal tomorrow in my inner palace, together with the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>!'

body.text:
040.002. adhivāsayati ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddho dhanasaṃmatasya rājño 'pi tūṣṇībhāvena/
040.003. atha dhanasaṃmato rājā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanaṃ viditvā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasyāntikāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: 040.002. <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, consented to King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s> also by his silence. 040.003. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, knowing the silent consent of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having worshiped the feet of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with his head, departed from the presence of <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

body.text:
040.006. atha dhanasaṃmato rājā tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya ratnaśikhinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam, yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti/
040.009. atha ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena dhanasaṃmatasya rājño bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
040.010. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
040.011. atha dhanasaṃmato rājā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ tatpramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
040.013. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpya saṃpravārya ratnaśikhinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ pādayor nipatya sarvamimaṃ lokaṃ maitreṇāṃśena sphuritvā praṇidhānaṃ kartumarabdhah--anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena śāstā loke bhaveyaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti/
040.016. ratnaśikhī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati--bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ mahārāja aśītivarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ maitreyo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyakasmbuddha iti/
040.018. tatpraṇidhānavaśād dvayo ratnayorloke prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text: 040.006. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food and drink, rising at dawn, having arranged seats and set out water-vessels, informed <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, of the time by a messenger: 'It is time, venerable sir; the meal is ready — may the Blessed One come at whatever time he deems fit.' 040.009. Then <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, surrounded by the community of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the meal-offering of King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>. 040.010. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks. 040.011. Then King <s>Dhanasaṃmata</s>, knowing <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, together with the foremost community of monks to be comfortably seated, served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent food and drink. 040.013. Having served and satisfied [them] with his own hands in many ways with pure and excellent food and drink, knowing <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, to have finished eating, with washed hands and bowl removed, he prostrated at his feet, and having pervaded this entire world with a share of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I become a Teacher in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One!' 040.016. <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said: 'You, O great king, shall become, among people whose lifespan is eighty thousand years, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Maitreya</s>.' 040.018. By the force of that aspiration, the manifestation of two jewels will arise in the world.

body.text:
040.019. idamavocadbhagavān/
040.019. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: 040.019. Thus spoke the Blessed One. 040.019. Delighted in mind, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 040.020. iti śrīdivyāvadāne maitreyāvadānaṃ tṛtīyam//
body.translated_text: 040.020. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Maitreyāvadāna</s> (Legend of <s>Maitreya</s>) is the third.

body.text:
041.001. div4 brāhmaṇadārikāvadānam/
041.002. bhagavān nyagrodhikāmanuprāptaḥ/
041.002. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya nyagrodhikāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
041.002. kapilavastuno brāhmaṇasya dārikā nyagrodhikāyāṃ niviṣṭā/
041.003. adrākṣīt sā brāhmaṇadārikā bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam/
041.005. sahadarśanādasyā etadabhavat--ayaṃ sa bhagavāñ śākyakulanandanaścakravartikulād rājyamapahāya sphītamantaḥpuraṃ sphītāni ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi pravrajita idānīṃ bhikṣāmaṭate/
041.006. yadi mamāntikātsaktukabhikṣāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt, ahamasmai dadyāmiti/
041.007. tato bhagavatā tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya pātramupanāmitam--yadi te bhagini parityaktam, ākīryatāmasmin pātra iti/
041.008. tato bhūyasyā mātrayā tasyāḥ prasāda utpannaḥ/
041.009. jānāti me bhagavāṃścetasā cittamiti viditvā tīvreṇa prasādena bhagavate saktubhikṣāṃ dattavatī/
041.010. tato bhagavatā smitamupadarśitam/
041.010. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātāḥ puṣparāgapadmarāgavajravaiḍūryamusāragalvārkalohitakādakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti, kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti/
041.013. yā adhastādgacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahava huhuvamutpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmamavīciparyantān narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti, ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti/
041.016. tenānugatāsteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmin kṣaṇe kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ, te pratiprasrabhyante/
041.017. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavantam itaścyutā āhosvidanyatropapannā iti/
041.018. teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavānnirmitam {darśanam} visarjayati/
041.019. teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati--na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, nāpyanyatropapannā iti/
041.020. te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti/
041.022. yā upariṣṭādgacchanti, tāścāturmahārājikān devān gatvā trāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino devān brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānabhṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśānakaniṣṭhaparyantān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyudghoṣayanti/
041.026. gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante--
041.027. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
041.028. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//1//
body.translated_text: 041.001. The <s>Brāhmaṇadārikāvadāna</s> (Legend of the Brahmin Girl). 041.002. The Blessed One had arrived at <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>. 041.002. Then the Blessed One, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Nyagrodhikā</s> for alms. 041.002. The daughter of a brahmin of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was dwelling in <s>Nyagrodhikā</s>. 041.003. That brahmin girl saw the Blessed One adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), his body radiant with the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), adorned with a halo extending a fathom, surpassing the radiance of a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on every side. 041.005. At the very sight, this thought arose in her: 'This is the Blessed One, the delight of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, who renounced sovereignty from a <s>Cakravartin</s> lineage, abandoning the flourishing inner palace and the flourishing treasuries and storehouses, went forth — and now wanders for alms. 041.006. If he would accept from me an offering of barley-flour, I would give it to him.' 041.007. Then the Blessed One, knowing her mind with his own mind, held out his bowl: 'Sister, if you have [food] to spare, let it be poured into this bowl.' 041.008. Then an even greater degree of faith arose in her. 041.009. 'The Blessed One knows my mind with his mind!' — knowing this, with intense devotion she gave the Blessed One an offering of barley-flour. 041.010. Then the Blessed One displayed a smile. 041.010. It is the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) that at whatever time <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that time, rays — blue, yellow, red, and white, of the color of ruby, lotus-ruby, diamond, lapis lazuli, coral, moonstone, agate, and right-spiraling conch-shell, and of gold and silver — issue from their mouths; some go downward, some go upward. 041.013. Those that go downward, going to the hells up to <s>Avīci</s> — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall having become warm. 041.016. By that [light], the distinctive torments of those beings in that moment ease and subside. 041.017. This thought arises in them: 'Have we, sirs, died from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' 041.018. For the purpose of generating faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a magical creation. 041.019. Having seen the magical creation, this thought arises in them: 'We have indeed not died from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.' 041.020. They, having generated faith in the magical creation, having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in that hell, take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. 041.022. Those [rays] that go upward, going to the gods — the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, the <s>Yāma</s>, the <s>Tuṣita</s>, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the <s>Parīttābha</s>, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, the <s>Anabhraka</s>, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, the <s>Abṛha</s>, the <s>Atapa</s>, the <s>Sudṛśa</s>, the <s>Sudarśana</s>, up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' 041.026. And they speak two verses: 041.027. 'Strive! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>! 041.028. Shake off the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut! // 1 //'

body.text:
041.029. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
041.030. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//2//
body.translated_text: 041.029. 'He who shall practice diligently in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, 041.030. having abandoned the cycle of birth (<s>saṃsāra</s>), shall make an end of suffering. // 2 //'

body.text:
042.001. <42>atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchanti/
042.002. tadyadi bhagavānatītaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante/
042.003. anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastādantardhīyante/
042.003. narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante/
042.004. tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante/
042.004. pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante/
042.005. manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunorantardhīyante/
042.006. balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante/
042.006. cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante/
042.007. śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante/
042.008. pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante/
042.008. yadi anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante//
body.translated_text: Then those rays, having pervaded the three-thousand great-thousand world system, followed behind the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) closely. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wished to make a prediction about the past, they disappeared behind him. If he wished to predict the future, they disappeared in front of him. If he wished to predict rebirth in hell, they disappeared at the soles of his feet. If he wished to predict rebirth as an animal, they disappeared at his heels. If he wished to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they disappeared at his big toe. If he wished to predict rebirth as a human, they disappeared at his knees. If he wished to predict the sovereignty of a minor <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they disappeared in his left palm. If he wished to predict the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s>, they disappeared in his right palm. If he wished to predict the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappeared in his mouth. If he wished to predict the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha), they disappeared at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows). If he wished to predict supreme perfect awakening, they disappeared at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance).

body.text:
042.010. atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyorṇāyāmantarhitāḥ/
042.010. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--
042.012. nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkramitaḥ kalāpaḥ/
042.014. avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāt divākareṇodayatā yathaiva//3//
body.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, disappeared at his <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "A cluster of manifold rays, adorned with a thousand colors, has issued from your mouth, illuminating all the directions on every side, just as the sun does when it rises."

body.text:
042.016. gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣate--
042.017. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
042.019. nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ//4//
body.translated_text: And he spoke two verses: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, having abandoned wretchedness and pride, being the supreme cause in the world, the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) who have conquered their enemies, do not display a smile as white as a conch shell or lotus fiber without reason."

body.text:
042.021. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīra buddhyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
042.023. dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//5//
body.translated_text: "Having yourself realized the truth at that moment through your wisdom, O steadfast one, O <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the sake of listeners who are eager, O bull among sages, with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, dispel the doubt that has arisen."

body.text:
042.025. nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ/
042.027. yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ//6// iti/
042.029. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametat/
042.029. nāhetupratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
042.030. samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
042.030. dṛṣṭā tavaiṣā sā ānanda brāhmaṇadārikā, yayā <43>prasādajātayā mahyaṃ saktubhikṣānupradattā ? dṛṣṭā bhadanta/
body.translated_text: "Not without cause do the fully awakened protectors, firm as ocean, salt-water, or mountain-king, display a smile. The multitudes of people desire to hear about the one for whose sake those steadfast ones display a smile." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is so, <s>Ānanda</s>, it is so. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones display a smile. Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priestly) girl who, with faith arisen, offered me a gift of barley-meal?" "I saw her, Venerable One."

body.text:
043.001. asāvānanda brāhmaṇadārikā anena kuśalamūlena trayodaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati/
043.002. kiṃ tarhi devāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca saṃvācyasaṃsṛtya paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścima ātmabhāvapratilambhe suparṇihito nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati/
043.004. sāmantakena śabdo visṛtah--amukayā brāhmaṇadārikā prasādajātayā bhagavate saktubhikṣā pratipāditā, sā bhagavatā pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛteti/
043.006. tasyāśca svāmī puṣpasamidhāmarthāyāraṇyaṃ gataḥ/
043.006. tena śrutaṃ mama patnyā śramaṇāya gautamāya saktubhikṣā pratipāditā, sā ca śramaṇena gautamena pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛtā iti/
043.008. śrutvā punaḥ saṃjātāmarṣo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
043.008. bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya bhagavantamidamavocat--agamadbhavān gautamo 'smākaṃ niveśanam? agamaṃ brāhmaṇa/
043.010. satyaṃ bhavate tayā mama patnyā saktubhikṣā pratipāditā, sā ca tvayā pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛtā iti? satyaṃ brāhmaṇa/
043.011. tvaṃ gautama cakravartirājyamapahāya pravrajitaḥ/
043.011. kathaṃ nāma tvametarhi saktubhikṣāhetoḥ saṃprajānan mṛṣāvādaṃ saṃbhāṣase, kaste śraddhāsyati iyatpramāṇasya bījasyetat phalamiti? tena hi brāhmaṇa tvameva prakṣyāmi, yathā te kṣamate tathaivaṃ vyākuru/
043.014. kiṃ manyase brāhmaṇa asti kaścittvayā āścaryādbhuto dharmo dṛṣṭah? tiṣṭhantu tāvat bho gautama anye āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ/
043.015. yo mayā asyāmeva nyagrodhikāyāmāścaryādbhuto dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ, sa tāvacchrūyatām/
043.016. asyāṃ bho gautama nyagrodhikāyāṃ pūrveṇa nyagrodho vṛkṣo yasya nāṃneyaṃ nyagrodhikā, tasyādhastāt pañca śakaṭaśatāni asaṃsaktāni tiṣṭhanti anyonyāsambādhamānāni/
043.018. kiyatpramāṇaṃ tasya nyagrodhasya phalam? kiyat tāvat? kedāramātram/
043.018. no bho gautama kiliñjamātram/
043.019. tailikacakramātram/
043.019. śakaṭacakramātram/
043.019. gopiṭakamātram/
043.019. bilvamātram/
043.020. kapitthamātram? no bho gautama sarṣapacatuṣṭayabhāgamātram/
043.020. kaste śraddhāsyati iyatpramāṇasya bījasyāyaṃ mahāvṛkṣo nirvṛtta iti? śraddadhātu me bhavān gautamo mā vā/
043.021. naitat pratyakṣaṃ kṣetram/
043.022. tāvadbho gautama nirupahataṃ snigdhamadhuramṛttikāpradeśaṃ bījaṃ ca navasāraṃ sukhāropitam/
043.023. kālena ca kālaṃ devo vṛṣyate, tenāyaṃ mahānyagrodhavṛkṣo 'bhinirvṛttaḥ/
043.023. atha bhagavānasminnutpanne gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
043.025. yathā kṣetre ca bījena pratyakṣastvamiha dvija/
043.026. evaṃ karmavipākeṣu pratyakṣā hi tathāgatāḥ//7//
body.translated_text: "That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> girl, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, will for thirteen <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) not fall into a woeful state. Rather, having transmigrated among gods and humans, in her final existence, final abode, final birth, upon obtaining her final bodily form, she will become a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) named <s>Suparṇihita</s>." The report spread in the vicinity: "A certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> girl, with faith arisen, offered barley-meal to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> has predicted her attainment of solitary awakening." Her husband had gone to the forest for the purpose of gathering flowers and firewood. He heard: "My wife has offered barley-meal to the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>, and the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> has predicted her attainment of solitary awakening." Having heard this, filled with anger, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having exchanged various words of greeting and pleasantry with the <s>Bhagavān</s> face to face, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Did Master <s>Gautama</s> come to our house?" "I did, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." "Is it true that my wife offered you barley-meal, and you predicted her attainment of solitary awakening?" "It is true, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." "You, <s>Gautama</s>, renounced the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s> and went forth as a renunciant. How then can you now deliberately speak falsehood for the sake of barley-meal? Who will believe that such a fruit comes from a seed of such small measure?" "In that case, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, I will ask you; answer as you see fit. What do you think, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, have you ever seen any wondrous, marvelous thing?" "Let alone other wondrous, marvelous things, O <s>Gautama</s>. Just hear what wondrous, marvelous thing I have seen at this very <s>nyagrodhikā</s> (banyan grove). In this <s>nyagrodhikā</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>," he described seeing a great banyan tree grown from a tiny seed.

body.text:
043.027. yathā tvayā brāhmaṇa dṛṣametadalpaṃ ca bījaṃ sumahāṃśca vṛkṣaḥ/
043.029. evaṃ mayā brāhmaṇa dṛṣṭametat alpaṃ ca bījaṃ mahatī ca saṃpat//8// iti//
body.translated_text: "Just as you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, have seen this -- a small seed and a great tree -- so too have I, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seen this: a small seed and a great fruit."

body.text: 043.031. tato bhagavatā mukhāt jihvāṃ nir namayya sarvaṃ mukhamaṇḍalamācchāditam yāvat keśaparyantamupādāya, sa ca brāhmaṇo 'bhihitah--kiṃ manyase brāhmaṇa yasya mukhāt jihvāṃ niścārya sarvam <44>mukhamaṇḍalamācchādayati, api tvasau cakravartirājyaśatasahasrahetorapi saṃprajānan mṛṣāvadāṃ bhāṣeta? no bho gautama/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> extended his tongue from his mouth and covered his entire face up to the hairline. And he addressed that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: "What do you think, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>? Would one who can extend his tongue from his mouth and cover his entire face deliberately speak falsehood, even for the sake of a hundred thousand <s>cakravartin</s> kingdoms?" "No indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>."

body.text:
044.002. tato 'nveva gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
044.003. apyeva hi syādanṛtābhidhāyinī mameha jihvārjavasatyavāditā/
044.005. tadevametanna yathā hi brāhmaṇa tathāgato 'smītyavagantumarhasi//9//
body.translated_text: Then he spoke a verse: "Could this tongue of mine, straight and truth-speaking, be one that speaks falsehood? It is precisely so, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; you should understand that I am a <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.text:
044.007. atha sa brāhmaṇo 'bhiprasannaḥ/
044.007. tato 'sya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam--atikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta atikrāntaḥ/
044.010. eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
044.010. upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatamabhiprasannam/
044.011. atha sa brāhmaṇo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was filled with faith. Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, delivered such a teaching on the penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> shattered the mountain of the view of a self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), risen to twenty peaks, with the thunderbolt of knowledge, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>): "I have crossed over, Venerable One, I have crossed over! I go for refuge to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks). May you regard me as a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) from this day forward, for as long as I live, as one who has gone for refuge and is filled with faith." Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rose from his seat, and departed.

body.text:
044.013. idamavocadbhagavān/
044.013. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), with minds uplifted, rejoiced in the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 044.014. iti śrīdivyāvadāne brāhmaṇadārikāvadānaṃ caturtham//
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Brāhmaṇadārikā-avadāna</s> (Story of the Brāhmaṇa Girl), the fourth, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text:
045.001. div5 stutibrāhmaṇāvadānam/
045.002. atha bhagavān hastināpuramanuprāptaḥ/
045.002. anyatamo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ dūrādeva dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva parvataṃ samantato bhadrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhagavantamabhigamya gāthābhiḥ stotumārabdhah--
045.004. suvarṇavarṇo nayanābhirāmaḥ prītyākaraḥ sarvaguṇairupetaḥ/
045.006. devātidevo naradamyasārathis tīrṇo 'si pāraṃ bhavasāgarasya//1// iti//
body.translated_text: The fifth: <s>Stutibrāhmaṇa-avadāna</s> (Story of the Praising Brāhmaṇa). Now the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Hastināpura</s>. A certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), his body radiant with eighty minor characteristics, adorned with an aura extending a fathom, his brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain, auspicious on all sides -- having seen him, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and began to praise him with verses: "Golden in color, delightful to the eyes, a source of joy, endowed with all virtues, a god beyond gods, the charioteer who tames men, you have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of existence."

body.text:
045.009. tato bhagavatā smitamupadarśitam/
045.009. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, pūrvavad yāvad bhagavata ūrṇāyāmantarhitāḥ/
045.010. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--
045.012. nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānnṣkramitaḥ kalāpaḥ/
045.014. avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva//2//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. Indeed, it is a natural law that whenever the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, display a smile, as described before, the rays disappeared at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "A cluster of manifold rays, adorned with a thousand colors, has issued from your mouth, illuminating all the directions on every side, just as the sun does when it rises."

body.text:
045.016. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
045.017. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
045.019. nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ//3//
body.translated_text: And he spoke a verse: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, having abandoned wretchedness and pride, being the supreme cause in the world, the <s>Jinas</s> who have conquered their enemies, do not display a smile as white as a conch shell or lotus fiber without reason."

body.text:
045.021. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīra buddhyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
045.023. dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//4//
body.translated_text: "Having yourself realized the truth at that moment through your wisdom, O steadfast one, O <s>śramaṇa</s>, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the sake of listeners who are eager, O bull among sages, with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, dispel the doubt that has arisen."

body.text:
045.025. nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ/
045.027. yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ//5// iti//
body.translated_text: "Not without cause do the fully awakened protectors, firm as ocean, salt-water, or mountain-king, display a smile. The multitudes of people desire to hear about the one for whose sake those steadfast ones display a smile."

body.text:
045.029. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametat/
045.029. nāhetupratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
045.030. dṛṣṭaste ānanda brāhmaṇo yena tathāgato gāthayā abhiṣṭutah?<46> dṛṣṭo bhadanta/
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is so, <s>Ānanda</s>, it is so. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones display a smile. Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> was praised with a verse?" "I saw him, Venerable One."

body.text:
046.001. asau anena kuśalamūlena viṃśatikalpaṃ vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati/
046.002. kiṃ tu devāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca gatvā saṃsṛtya paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe stavārho nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati/
046.003. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--paśya bhadanta anena brāhmaṇena bhagavānekayā gāthayā stuto bhagavatā ca pratyekāyāṃ bodhau vyākṛta iti/
046.005. bhagavānāha--na bhikṣava etarhi, yathā atīte 'dhvani anenāhamekayā gāthayā stutaḥ, mayā ca pañcasu grāmavareṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
046.006. tacchṛṇu{ta}, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru{ta}, bhāṣiṣye//
body.translated_text: That one, by this root of merit, will not go to a state of ruin for twenty <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages). Rather, having gone through the realms of gods and humans and transmigrated, in his last abode, his last elevation, his last attainment of a bodily form, he will become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) named <s>Stavārha</s> (Worthy of Praise). The monks, having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "Behold, Venerable One, this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a single verse, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> predicted his attainment of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Not only now, O monks. In a past era too, he praised me with a single verse, and I established him in five excellent villages. Listen to this, pay careful and thorough attention, and I shall speak."

body.text:
046.008. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
046.009. sa cātīva kavipriyaḥ/
046.009. vārāṇasyāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ kaviḥ/
046.010. sa brāhmaṇyocyate--brāhmaṇa śītakālo vartate/
046.010. gaccha, asya rājñaḥ kaccidanukūlaṃ bhāṣitaṃ kṛtvā kadācit kiṃcit śītatrāṇaṃ saṃpadyata iti/
046.011. sa saṃprasthitaḥ/
046.012. yāvadrājā hastiskandhārūḍho nirgacchati/
046.012. sa brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ tāvadrājānaṃ stunomi āhosvid hastināgamiti/
046.013. tasyaitadabhavat--ayaṃ hastināgaḥ sarvalokasya priyo manāpaśca/
046.014. tiṣṭhatu tāvadrājā, hastināgaṃ tāvadabhiṣṭaumīti/
046.014. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
046.015. erāvaṇasyākṛtitulyadeho rūpopapanno varalakṣaṇaiśca/
046.017. lakṣe praśasto 'si mahāgajendra varṇapramāṇena surūparūpa//6// iti//
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O monks, in a past era, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. He was exceedingly fond of poets. In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who was a poet. His wife said to him: "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the cold season is upon us. Go and speak some pleasing words to this king; perhaps you may obtain some protection against the cold." He set out. Just then the king was coming out, mounted on the shoulder of an elephant. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> considered: "Should I now praise the king or the elephant?" He thought: "This elephant is dear and pleasing to all people. Let the king wait; I shall first praise the elephant." And he recited a verse: "With a body equal in form to <s>Erāvaṇa</s>, endowed with beauty and excellent marks, you are celebrated among a hundred thousand, O great lord of elephants, of beautiful form in color and measure."

body.text:
046.019. tato rājā abhiprasanno gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
046.020. yo me gajendro dayito manāpaḥ prītiprado dṛṣṭiharo narāṇām/
046.022. taṃ bhāṣase varṇapadāni tasya dadāmi te grāmavarāṇi pañca//7// iti//
body.translated_text: Then the king, greatly pleased, recited a verse: "This lord of elephants who is dear to me and pleasing, who brings joy and captivates the eyes of men -- you have spoken words of praise about him; I give you five excellent villages."

body.text:
046.024. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau hastināgaḥ, ahameva tena kālena tena samayena/
046.025. tadāpyahamanenaikayā gāthayā stutaḥ, mayā cāyaṃ pañcagrāmavareṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
046.025. etarhi anenaikagāthayā stutaḥ, mayāpi cāyaṃ pratyekabodhau vyākṛta iti//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, O monks? That elephant was none other than myself at that time, in that era. Then too I was praised by him with a single verse, and I established him in five excellent villages. Now too, having been praised by him with a single verse, I have predicted his attainment of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening."

body.text:
046.027. idamavocadbhagavān/
046.027. āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Those monks, with uplifted minds, rejoiced in the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 046.028. iti śrīdivyāvadāne stutibrāhmaṇāvadānaṃ pañcamam//
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Stutibrāhmaṇāvadāna</s> (Story of the Praising Brahmin) is the fifth.

body.text:
047.001. div6 indranāmabrāhmaṇāvadānam/
047.002. bhagavāñ śrughnāmanuprāptaḥ/
047.002. śrughnāyāmindro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati/
047.002. sa ca rūpayauvanaśrutamanuprāpto na mamāsti kaścit tulya ityatīva vikatthate/
047.003. bhagavāṃścānyatamasmin pradeśe purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati/
047.004. aśrauṣīdindro nāma brāhmaṇah--śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrughnāmanuprāpta iti/
047.005. tasyaitadabhavat--śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrūyate 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādika iti/
047.006. gacchāmi paśyāmi kiṃ mamāntikādabhirūpatara āhosvinneti/
047.007. sa nirgato yāvat paśyati bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasarātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam/
047.009. dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--kiṃ cāpi śramaṇo gautamo mamāntikādabhirūpataraḥ, noccatara iti/
047.010. sa bhagavato mūrdhānamavalokayitumārabdho yāvanna paśyati/
047.010. sa ūrdhvataraṃ pradeśamārūḍhaḥ/
047.011. tatra bhagavānindraṃ brāhmaṇamāmantrayate--alaṃ brāhmaṇa, khedamāpatsyase/
047.011. yadi sumerumūrdhānamapi abhiruhya tathāgatasya mūrdhānamavalokayasi, tathā sutarāṃ khedamāpatsyase, na ca drakṣyasi/
047.013. api tu na tvayā śrutaṃ sasurāsurajagadanavalokitamūrdhāno buddhā bhagavanta iti? api tu yadīpsasi tathāgatasya śarīrapramāṇaṃ draṣṭum, tava gṛhe 'gnihotrakuṇḍaṃ tasyādhastādgośīrṣacandanamayī yaṣṭirupatiṣṭhate, tāmuddhṛtya māpaya/
047.015. tattathāgatamātāpaitṛkasyāśrayasya pramāṇamiti/
047.015. indro brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--etadasyāścaryaṃ na kadācinmayā śrutam, gacchāmi paśyāmīti/
047.016. tvaritatvaritagato 'gnihotrakuṇḍakasyādhastāt khanitumārabdhaḥ/
047.017. sarvaṃ tathaiva/
047.017. so 'bhiprasannaḥ/
047.017. sa saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ sarvajñaḥ/
047.018. gacchāmi paryupāsitumiti/
047.018. sa prasādajāto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
047.019. upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
047.020. tato bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yathaindreṇa brāhmaṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
047.022. sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ kathayati--atikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta, atikrāntaḥ/
047.023. eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
047.023. upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatam/
047.024. abhiprasanno 'thendro brāhmaṇa utthāyāsanāt ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt, ahaṃ gośīrṣacandanamayyā yaṣṭyā mahaṃ prajñapayeyamiti/
047.026. bhagavānāha--gaccha brāhmaṇa anujñātaṃ prajñapayasi/
047.027. tatastena viviktāvakāśe mahatā satkāreṇāsau yaṣṭirucchrāpitā, mahaśca prajñapitaḥ/
047.028. anyairapi brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ kuśalamadhiṣṭhānāya bhavatviti viditvā kulā baddhā(?)/
047.029. indreṇa brāhmaṇena yaṣṭyā mahaḥ prajñapita iti indramaha indramaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text: The <s>Indranāmabrāhmaṇāvadāna</s> (Story of the Brahmin Named Indra). The <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Śrughna</s>. In <s>Śrughna</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Indra</s> resided. He, having attained beauty, youth, and learning, boasted exceedingly: "There is no one equal to me." The <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated on a prepared seat in a certain place before the assembly of monks, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Indra</s> heard: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has arrived at <s>Śrughna</s>." He thought: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is said to be handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. I shall go and see whether he is more handsome than me or not." He went out and saw the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with eighty secondary characteristics, ornamented with a fathom-wide halo, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, he thought: "Although the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is more handsome than me, he is not taller." He began trying to see the top of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s head, but could not see it. He climbed to a higher spot. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Indra</s>: "Enough, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, you will exhaust yourself. Even if you climb to the summit of <s>Sumeru</s> and look at the top of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s head, you will become all the more exhausted and still will not see it. But have you not heard that the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, have heads that cannot be seen by the world including its gods and <s>asuras</s>? However, if you wish to see the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, in your house there is a fire-altar, and beneath it stands a staff made of <s>gośīrṣa</s> (ox-head) sandalwood. Pull it out and measure it. That is the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body inherited from his mother and father." The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Indra</s> thought: "This is amazing; I have never heard of this before. I shall go and see." Going quickly, he began to dig beneath the fire-altar. Everything was exactly as described. He was filled with faith. He thought: "Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is omniscient. I shall go and attend upon him." Born of faith, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he exchanged various pleasant and delightful conversation with the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having understood his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching on the penetration of the Four Noble Truths that the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Indra</s>, having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of a personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truths, he said: "I have transgressed, Venerable One, I have transgressed! I go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks. May you accept me as a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) from this day forward, as long as I live, as one who has gone for refuge." Filled with faith, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Indra</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "If the <s>Bhagavān</s> would permit, I would set up a festival with the sandalwood staff." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Go, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, you are permitted to set it up." Then he erected the staff in a secluded open space with great honor, and established a festival. Other <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders too, understanding it to be for the benefit of merit, bound their families to it. Because the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Indra</s> established the festival with the staff, it became known as the <s>Indramaha</s> (Festival of Indra).

body.text:
047.030. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--āgamaya ānanda yena toyikā/
047.030. evaṃ bhadanteti āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt/
047.031. atha bhagavāṃstoyikāmanuprāptaḥ/
047.031. tasmiṃśca pradeśe brāhmaṇo lāṅgalaṃ vāhayati/
047.032. athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaih <48>samalaṃkṛtamaśītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam/
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Toyikā</s>." "So be it, Venerable One," the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Toyikā</s>. In that place, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was driving a plough. Then he saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with eighty secondary characteristics, ornamented with a fathom-wide halo, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides.

body.text:
048.002. dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--yadi bhagavantaṃ gautamamupetyābhivādayiṣyāmi, karmaparihāṇirme bhaviṣyatīti/
048.003. atha nipetyābhivādayiṣyāmi, puṇyaparihāṇirbhaviṣyati/
048.003. tat ko 'sau upāyaḥ syāt yena me karmaparihāṇir na syānnāpi puṇyaparihāṇiriti/
048.004. tasya buddhirutpannā--atrastha evābhivādanaṃ karomi/
048.005. evaṃ na karmaparihāṇir na puṇyaparihāṇiriti/
048.006. tena yathāgṛhītayaiva pratodayaṣṭyā tatrasthenaivābhivādanaṃ kṛtam--abhivādaye buddhaṃ bhagavantamiti/
048.007. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--bhavakṣayakaraḥ kṣaṇam/
048.007. eṣa brāhmaṇaḥ/
048.007. sacedasyaivaṃ samyaksampratyayajñānadarśanam ahamanenopakrameṇa vandito bhaveyam, evamanena dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ vandanā kṛtā bhavet/
048.010. tatkasya hetoh? asminnānanda pradeśe kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopito 'sthisaṃghātastiṣṭhati/
048.011. athāyuṣmānānando laghuladhveva caturguṇamuttarāsaṅgaṃ prajñapya bhagavantamidamavocat--niṣīdatu bhagavān prajñapta evāsane/
048.012. evamayaṃ pṛthivīpradeśo dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ paribhukto bhaviṣyati, yacca kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena, yaccaitarhi bhagavatā iti/
048.014. niṣaṇṇo bhagavān prajñapta evāsane/
048.014. niṣadya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--icchatha kālaḥ, etasya sugata samayaḥ, yaṃ bhagavān bhikṣūṇāṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaṃ śarīrasaṃghātamupadarśayet/
048.017. dṛṣṭvā bhikṣavaścittamabhiprasādayiṣyanti/
048.017. tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam/
048.017. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavanto laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti, tasmin samaye kuntapipīlikā api prāṇino bhagavataścetasā cittamājānanti/
048.019. nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā laukikacittamutpāditamiti? paśyanti--kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātamavikopitaṃ draṣṭukāma iti/
048.021. tatastaiḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaśarīrasaṃghāta ucchrāpitaḥ/
048.021. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--udgṛhṇīta bhikṣavo nimittam/
048.022. antardhāsyati/
048.022. antarhitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Having seen him, he considered: "If I go and pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Gautama</s>, my work will suffer loss. But if I do not go and pay homage, my merit will suffer loss. What method could there be by which neither my work nor my merit suffers loss?" He had an idea: "I will pay homage standing right here.
