Thus there will be neither loss of work nor loss of merit." With the very goad-stick in his hand, standing right there, he paid homage: "I bow to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>." There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "A moment destroys existence. This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> -- if he had the right understanding and knowledge that 'I have been venerated by him through this method,' then he would have paid homage to two <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> (Perfectly Awakened Ones). For what reason? In this place, <s>Ānanda</s>, the undisturbed bone-relics of <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> stand." Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, swiftly folding the upper robe into four, prepared a seat and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> sit on the prepared seat. Thus this spot of earth will have been used by two <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> -- by <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> and now by the <s>Bhagavān</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> sat on the prepared seat. Having sat down, he addressed the monks: "Do you wish, monks -- is this the right time, is this the occasion -- that the <s>Bhagavān</s> show to the monks the undisturbed bodily relics of <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>? Having seen them, monks, you will fill your minds with faith." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought. Indeed, it is the nature of things that when <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, produce a worldly thought, at that time even creatures as small as ants can understand the mind of the Blessed One with their own minds. The <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent beings) considered: "For what reason has the <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought?" They saw: "He wishes to see the undisturbed bodily relics of <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>." Then they raised up the undisturbed bodily relics of <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: "Take note, O monks, of this sign. It will disappear." And it disappeared.

body.text:
048.023. rājñā prasenajitā śrutaṃ bhagavatā śrāvakāṇāṃ darśanāyāvikopitaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātaṃ samucchritamiti/
048.024. śrutvā ca punaḥ kutūhalajātaḥ sahāntaḥpureṇa kumārairamātyairbhaṭabalāgrair naigamajānapadaiśca draṣṭuṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
048.025. evaṃ virūḍhakaḥ, anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ, ṛṣidattaḥ purāṇasthapitaḥ, viśākhā mṛgāramātā, anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kutūhalajātāni draṣṭuṃ saṃprasthitāni pūrvakaiśca kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni/
048.027. yāvadasau anatarhitaḥ/
048.027. taiḥ śrutam--anatarhito 'sau bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghāturavikopita iti/
048.029. śrutvā ca punasteṣāṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyamutpannam--vṛthā asmākamāgamanaṃ jātamiti/
048.029. athānyatamena copāsakena sa pradeśaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtaḥ/
048.030. evaṃ ca cetasā cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--asmānme padāvihārāt kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
048.031. atha bhagavāṃstasya mahājanakāyasyāvipratisārasaṃjananārthaṃ tasya copāsakasya cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text:
048.023. King <s>Prasenajit</s> heard that the Blessed One had raised up the undisturbed body-aggregate of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, for the viewing of his disciples.
048.024. Having heard this, overcome with curiosity, he set out to see it, together with his inner palace, princes, ministers, military commanders, and townspeople and countryfolk.
048.025. Likewise <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, <s>Ṛṣidatta</s> the former chief-builder, <s>Viśākhā</s> the mother of <s>Mṛgāra</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of living beings, overcome with curiosity, set out to see it, impelled by their former roots of merit.
048.027. But by then, he [the relic-body] had disappeared.
048.027. They heard: 'The undisturbed body-aggregate of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, raised by the Blessed One, has disappeared.'
048.029. Having heard this, grief and dejection arose in them: 'Our coming has been in vain.'
048.029. Then a certain lay devotee circumambulated that spot.
048.030. And he formed this thought in his mind: 'How much merit will accrue to me from this single step of circumambulation?'
048.031. Then the Blessed One, in order to prevent regret in that great multitude and having perceived with his mind the thought of that lay devotee, recited a verse:

body.text:
049.001. <49>śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
049.003. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ padāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān//1//
body.translated_text:
049.001. 'Hundreds of thousands of gold coins of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold cannot equal [the merit of]
049.003. one who, with a serene mind, performs a single step of circumambulation at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines, being wise.' // 1 //

body.text:
049.005. anyatamena upāsakena tasmin pradeśe mṛttikāpiṇḍo dattaḥ/
049.005. evaṃ ca cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--padāvihārasya tāvadiyat puṇyamākhyātaṃ bhagavatā anyatra/
049.006. mṛttikāpiṇḍasya kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃstasyāpi cetasā cittamājñāya bhāṣate--
049.008. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
049.010. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitta āropayenmṛttikapiṇḍamekam//2//
body.translated_text:
049.005. A certain lay devotee placed a lump of clay at that spot.
049.005. And he formed this thought: 'The Blessed One has declared elsewhere such great merit for a single step of circumambulation.
049.006. How much merit will there be from [offering] a lump of clay?' Then the Blessed One, having perceived with his mind the thought of that one too, spoke:
049.008. 'Hundreds of thousands of gold coins of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold cannot equal [the merit of]
049.010. one who, with a serene mind, places a single lump of clay at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines.' // 2 //

body.text:
049.012. tataḥ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmṛttikāpiṇḍasamāropaṇaṃ kṛtam/
049.012. aparaistatra muktapuṣpāṇyavakṣiptāni, evaṃ ca cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--padāvihārasya mṛttikāpiṇḍasya ceyat puṇyamuktaṃ bhagavatā, asmākaṃ tu muktapuṣpāṇāṃ kiyat puṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
049.016. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
049.018. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittah āropayenmuktasupuṣparāśim//3//
body.translated_text:
049.012. Then, having heard this, many hundreds of thousands of living beings placed lumps of clay [there].
049.012. Others scattered loose flowers there and formed this thought: 'The Blessed One has declared such merit for a step of circumambulation and for a lump of clay; how much merit will there be for our loose flowers?'
049.016. Then the Blessed One, having perceived with his mind their thought too, recited a verse:
049.016. 'Hundreds of thousands of gold coins of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold cannot equal [the merit of]
049.018. one who, with a serene mind, scatters loose flowers at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines, being wise.' // 3 //

body.text:
049.020. aparaistatra mālāvihāraḥ kṛtaḥ, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--muktapuṣpāṇāṃ bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam/
049.021. asmākaṃ mālāvihārasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
049.023. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇavāhā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
049.025. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto mālāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān//4//
body.translated_text:
049.020. Others made a garland-offering there, and formed this thought: 'The Blessed One has declared such merit for loose flowers.
049.021. How much merit will there be from our garland-offering?' Then the Blessed One, having perceived with his mind their thought too, recited a verse:
049.023. 'Hundreds of thousands of cart-loads of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> cannot equal [the merit of]
049.025. one who, with a serene mind, makes a garland-offering at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines, being wise.' // 4 //

body.text:
049.027. aparaistatra pradīpamālā dattā, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--mālāvihārasya bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam/
049.028. asmākaṃ pradīpadānasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text:
049.027. Others offered a row of lamps there, and formed this thought: 'The Blessed One has declared such merit for a garland-offering.
049.028. How much merit will there be from our lamp-offering?' Then the Blessed One, having perceived with his mind their thought too, recited a verse:

body.text:
050.001. <50>śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇakoṭyo jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
050.003. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ pradīpadānaṃ prakaroti vidvān//5//
body.translated_text:
050.001. 'Hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> cannot equal [the merit of]
050.003. one who, with a serene mind, makes an offering of lamps at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines, being wise.' // 5 //

body.text:
050.005. aparaistatra gandhābhiṣeko dattaḥ/
050.005. evaṃ cetasā cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--pradīpasya bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam/
050.006. asmākaṃ gandhābhiṣekasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
050.008. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇarāśayo jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
050.010. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto gandhābhiṣekaṃ prakaroti vidvān//6//
body.translated_text:
050.005. Others offered a perfume-anointment there.
050.005. They formed this thought: 'The Blessed One has declared such merit for a lamp-offering.
050.006. How much merit will there be from our perfume-anointment?' Then the Blessed One, having perceived with his mind their thought too, recited a verse:
050.008. 'Hundreds of thousands of heaps of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> cannot equal [the merit of]
050.010. one who, with a serene mind, makes a perfume-anointment at <s>Buddha</s>-shrines, being wise.' // 6 //

body.text:
050.012. aparaistatra cchatradhvajapatākāropaṇaṃ kṛtam/
050.012. evaṃ ca ... cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
050.013. tiṣṭhantaṃ pūjayedyañca yañcāpi parinirvṛtam/
050.014. samaṃ cittaṃ prasādyeha nāsti puṇyaviśeṣatā//7//
body.translated_text:
050.012. Others raised parasols, banners, and flags there.
050.012. Likewise ... having perceived with his mind their thought, he recited a verse:
050.013. 'Whether one worships [a <s>Buddha</s>] while living or one who has attained final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
050.014. if the mind is equally serene, there is no difference in merit.' // 7 //

body.text:
050.015. evaṃ hyacintiyā buddhā buddhadharmā^pyacintiyā/
050.016. acintiye prasannānāṃ vipāko 'pi acintiyaḥ//8//
body.translated_text:
050.015. 'For <s>Buddhas</s> are inconceivable, and the qualities of <s>Buddhas</s> are also inconceivable;
050.016. for those who have serene faith in the inconceivable, the fruit [of that faith] is also inconceivable.' // 8 //

body.text:
050.017. teṣāmacintiyānāmapratihatadharmacakravartinām/
050.018. samyaksambuddhānāṃ nālaṃ guṇapāramadhigantum//9// iti//
body.translated_text:
050.017. 'Of those inconceivable ones, whose turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel is unobstructed,
050.018. the Perfectly Awakened Ones — one cannot reach the far shore of their virtues.' // 9 //

body.text:
050.019. tato bhagavatā tasya mahājanakāyasya tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ/
050.021. kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau, kaiścinmūrdhāgatāni, kaiścinmūrdhānaḥ, kaiściduṣṇagatānyāsāditāni, kaiścit satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayaḥ, kaiścitsrotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścit sakṛdāgamiphalam, kaiścit sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
050.023. yadbhūyasā buddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇāḥ saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitāḥ//
body.translated_text:
050.019. Then the Blessed One gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> to that great multitude that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of living beings attained great distinction.
050.021. By some, minds were set upon the <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening; by some, upon the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening; by some, upon the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>); by some, the summit-stage was reached; by some, the summits [were attained]; by some, the heat-stage was realized; by some, the forbearances conforming to truth; by some, the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) was realized; by some, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>); [by some, the fruit of non-returning; by some, <s>Arhatship</s> was realized].

body.text:
050.025. atha anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavantamidamavocat--yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt, atra mahaṃ prajñāyeyam/
050.026. anujānāmi gṛhapate, prajñāpayitavyam/
050.026. tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā mahaḥ prajñāpitaḥ/
050.027. toyikāmaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text:
050.025. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said to the Blessed One: 'If the Blessed One would permit, I would like to establish a festival here.'
050.026. 'I permit it, householder; it should be established.'
050.026. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> established the festival.
050.027. It became known as the '<s>Toyikā</s> festival' (<s>Toyikāmaha</s>).

body.text:
050.028. idamavocadbhagavān/
050.028. āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
050.028. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
050.028. The monks, delighted, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

body.text: 050.029. iti śrīdivyāvadāne indranāmabrāhmaṇāvadānaṃ ṣaṣṭham//
body.translated_text: 050.029. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Indranāmabrāhmaṇāvadāna</s> (The Legend of the Brahmin Named Indra) is the sixth.

body.text: 051.001. div7 nagarāvalambikāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 051.001. The <s>Nagarāvalambikāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Nagarāvalambikā</s>).

body.text:
051.002. atha bhagavān kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
051.002. śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
051.003. aśrauṣīdanāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatih--bhagavān kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
051.004. śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārām iti/
051.005. śrutvā ca punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
051.005. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
051.006. ekāntaniṣaṇṇamanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
051.007. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
051.008. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatih utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhuktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena iti/
051.010. adhivāsayati bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena/
051.011. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yena svaniveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
051.013. upasaṃkramya dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--na tāvadbhoḥ puruṣa tīrthyānāṃ praveśo dātavyo yāvad buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktaṃ bhavati/
051.014. tataḥ paścādahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ dāsyāmīti/
051.015. evamāryeti dauvārikaḥ puruṣo 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ pratyaśrauṣīt/
051.016. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīyaṃ kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
051.018. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapaterbhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
051.020. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
051.020. atha anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
051.022. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya//
body.translated_text:
051.002. Now the Blessed One, wandering on a teaching tour through the <s>Kośala</s> countries, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
051.002. He was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
051.003. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard: 'The Blessed One, wandering on a teaching tour through the <s>Kośala</s> countries, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
051.004. He is dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.'
051.005. Having heard, he approached the Blessed One.
051.005. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.
051.006. The Blessed One instructed, guided, inspired, and gladdened the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
051.007. Having instructed, guided, inspired, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
051.008. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, rising from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said: 'May the Blessed One consent to a meal tomorrow at my residence, together with the community of monks.'
051.010. The Blessed One consented to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> by silence.
051.011. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, understanding the Blessed One's consent by his silence, approved and rejoiced at the Blessed One's words, bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, departed from the Blessed One's presence, and went to his own dwelling.
051.013. Having arrived, he addressed the doorkeeper: 'Good man, do not allow entry to non-Buddhist ascetics until the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks has eaten.
051.014. After that, I shall give to the non-Buddhist ascetics.'
051.015. 'Yes, noble sir,' the doorkeeper replied to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
051.016. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, rising early in the morning, set out seats, placed water vessels, and announced the time to the Blessed One through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the Blessed One now do as he sees fit.'
051.018. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by a company of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached the place of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s meal-offering.
051.020. Having approached, he sat down on a seat prepared in front of the community of monks.
051.020. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, knowing that the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks was comfortably seated, served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft.
051.022. Having served and satisfied them in many ways with pure and excellent food with his own hands, knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating and had washed his hands and put away his bowl, he took a low seat and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
051.025. athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapo 'nyatamasmādāraṇyakācchayanāsanāt dīrghakeśaśmaśrurlūhacīvaro jetavanaṃ gataḥ/
051.026. sa paśyati jetavanaṃ śūnyam/
051.026. tenopadhivārikaḥ pṛṣṭah--kutra buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgha iti/
051.027. tena samākhyātam--anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhāpatinopanimantrita iti/
051.027. sa saṃlakṣayati--gacchāmi, tatraiva piṇḍapātaṃ paribhokṣyāmi, buddhapramukhaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ paryupāsiṣyāmīti/
051.028. so 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ gataḥ/
051.029. ato dauvārikena uktah--ārya tiṣṭha, mā pravekṣyasi/
051.030. kasyārthāya? anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā ājñā dattā--mā tāvat tīrthyānāṃ praveśaṃ dāsyasi, yāvadbuddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktam/
051.031. tataḥ paścāt tīrthyānāṃ dāsyāmi iti/
051.031. athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ saṃlakṣayati--tasya me lābhāḥ sulabdhāḥ, yanmāṃ śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ śramaṇaśākyaputrīya<52> iti na jānante/
body.translated_text:
051.025. Now the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, from a certain forest dwelling, with long hair and beard and wearing ragged robes, went to the <s>Jetavana</s>.
051.026. He saw the <s>Jetavana</s> empty.
051.026. He asked the provisions-keeper: 'Where is the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks?'
051.027. He was told: 'They have been invited by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.'
051.027. He reflected: 'I shall go there; I shall take my alms-food there and attend upon the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks.'
051.028. He went to the dwelling of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
051.029. There the doorkeeper said: 'Venerable sir, stop; you may not enter.'
051.030. 'For what reason?' 'The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> has given the order: "Do not allow entry to non-Buddhist ascetics until the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks has eaten.
051.031. After that, I shall give to the non-Buddhist ascetics."'
051.031. Then the Venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> reflected: 'What good fortune for me that faithful <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders do not recognize me as a disciple of the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Śākyaputra</s>!'

body.text:
052.001. gacchāmi, kṛpaṇajanasyānugrahaṃ karomīti viditvā udyānaṃ gataḥ/
052.001. sa saṃlakṣayati--adya mayā kasyānugrahaḥ kartavya iti/
052.002. yāvadanyatamā nagarāvalambikā kuṣṭhābhidrutā sarujārtā pakvagātrā bhikṣāmaṭati/
052.003. sa tasyāḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
052.003. tasyāśca bhikṣāyāmāyāsaḥ saṃpannaḥ/
052.004. tayā āyuṣmān mahākāśyapo dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaścittaprāsādikaḥ śāntena īryāpathena/
052.005. sā saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ mayā evaṃvidhe dakṣiṇīye kārā kṛtā, yena me iyamevamrūpā samavasthā/
052.005. yadi āryo mahākāśyapo mamāntikādanukampāmupādāya ācāmaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt, ahamasmai dadyāmiti/
052.007. tata āyuṣmatā mahākāśyapena tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya pātramupanāmitam--yadi te bhagini parityaktam, dīyatāmasmin pātra iti/
052.008. tatastayā cittamabhiprasādya tasmin pātre dattam/
052.009. makṣikā ca patitā/
052.009. sā tāmapanetumārabdhā/
052.009. tasyāstasminnācāme 'ṅguliḥ patitā/
052.009. saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpyāryeṇa mama cittānurakṣayā na cchoritaḥ, api tu na paribhokṣyatīti/
052.010. athāyuṣmatā mahākāśyapena tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya tasyā eva pratyakṣamanyatamaṃ kuḍyamūlaṃ niśritya paribhuktam/
052.012. sa saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpi āryeṇa mama cittānurakṣayā paribhuktam, nānenāhāreṇāhārakṛtyaṃ kariṣyati iti/
052.013. athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapastasyāścittamājñāya tāṃ nagarāvalambikāmidamavocat--bhagini prāmodyamutpādayasi, ahaṃ tvadīyenāhāreṇa rātriṃdivasamatināmayiṣyāmi iti/
052.014. tasyā atīva audbilyamutpannam--mamāryeṇa mahākāśyapena piṇḍapātaḥ pratigṛhīta iti/
052.015. tata āyuṣmatī mahākāśyape cittamabhiprasādya kālaṃ gatā tuṣite devanikāye upapannā/
052.016. sā śakreṇa devendreṇa dṛṣṭā ācāmaṃ pratipādayantī cittamabhiprasādayantī kālaṃ ca kurvāṇā/
052.017. no tu dṛṣṭā kutropapannā iti/
052.018. sa narakān vyavalokayitumārabdho na paśyati, tiryak ca pretaṃ ca manuṣyāṃścāturmahārājikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāvanna paśyati/
052.019. tathā hyadhastāddevānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate no tūpariṣṭāt/
052.020. atha śakro devānāmindro yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
052.020. upasaṃkramya gāthābhigītena praśnaṃ papraccha--
052.022. carataḥ piṇḍapātaṃ hi kāśyapasya mahātmanaḥ/
052.023. kutrāsau modaye nārī kāśyapācāmadāyikā//1//
body.translated_text: "I shall go and render aid to wretched people," he thought, and went to a park. He reflected: "To whom should I render aid today?" Meanwhile, a certain city-dwelling woman, afflicted with leprosy, in pain and distress, her limbs decayed, was wandering about begging for alms. He approached her, and she was exhausted from begging. She saw the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, pleasing in body and mind, with a peaceful deportment. She reflected: "Surely I have not rendered service to such a worthy recipient, and therefore this is my condition. If the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> would accept my rice-water out of compassion for me, I would give it to him." Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having understood her thought with his mind, extended his bowl: "If you have something to spare, sister, give it in this bowl." Then, having generated faith in her mind, she gave it in that bowl. A fly fell into it. As she began to remove it, her finger fell off into the rice-water. She thought: "Although the noble one has not rejected it out of consideration for my feelings, he will surely not consume it." Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having understood her thought with his mind, in her very sight leaned against a certain wall and consumed it. She thought: "Although the noble one consumed it out of consideration for my feelings, he will not be able to sustain himself on such food." Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, having understood her thought, said to that city-dwelling woman: "Sister, generate joy — I shall sustain myself day and night on your food." Great elation arose in her: "The noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> has accepted my alms-food!" Then, having generated faith toward the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, she passed away and was reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, had seen her offering rice-water, generating faith, and passing away, but did not see where she was reborn. He began looking through the hells but did not see her; nor among animals, nor <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), nor humans, nor the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, nor the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, and so on he did not see her. For the knowledge-vision of lower gods extends only downward, not upward. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and asked a question through a verse: "As <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the great soul, was walking for alms, where does that woman rejoice — she who gave rice-water to <s>Kāśyapa</s>?" //1//

body.text:
052.024. bhagavānāha--
052.025. tuṣitā nāma te devāḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhayaḥ/
052.026. yatrāsau modate nārī kāśyapācāmadāyikā//2// iti//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Those gods called <s>Tuṣita</s>, endowed with the fulfillment of all desires — there that woman rejoices, she who gave rice-water to <s>Kāśyapa</s>." //2//

body.text:
052.027. atha śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhavat--ime ca tāvanmanuṣyāḥ puṇyāpuṇyānāmapratyakṣadarśino dānāni dadati, puṇyāni kurvanti/
052.028. ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśanena puṇyānāṃ svapuṇyaphale vyavasthitaḥ kasmāt dānāni na dadāmi, puṇyāni vā na karomi? ayamāryo mahākāśyapo dīnānāthakṛpaṇavanīpakānukampī/
052.030. yannvahamenaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādayeyam/
052.030. iti viditvā kṛpaṇavīthyāṃ gṛhaṃ nirmitavān/
052.031. avacīravicīrakaṃ kākābhilīnakaṃ nātiparamarūpaṃ kuvindaṃ cātmānamabhinimārya udūḍhaśiraskaḥ saṇaśāṭikānivāsitaḥ sphaṭitapāṇipādo vastraṃ vāyitumārabdhah<53>/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, thought: "These humans, who do not directly perceive the fruits of merit and demerit, give gifts and perform meritorious deeds. I, who directly perceive the fruits of merits and am established in the fruit of my own merit — why do I not give gifts or perform meritorious deeds? This noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> is compassionate toward the destitute, the helpless, the wretched, and the lowly. Let me offer him alms-food." Having resolved thus, he created a house in the street of the poor. Having transformed himself into a weaver — shabby, with crows roosting about, of not-too-fine appearance — with disheveled hair, wearing a hempen garment, with cracked hands and feet, he began to weave cloth.

body.text:
053.001. śacī api devakanyā kuvindanaryā veśadhāriṇī tasarikāṃ kartumārabdhā/
053.001. pārśve cāsyā divyā sudhā sajjīkṛtā tiṣṭhati/
053.002. athāyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ kṛpaṇānāthavanīpakajanānukampako 'nupūrveṇa tadgṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
053.003. duḥkhitako 'yamiti kṛtvā dvāre sthitena pātraṃ prasāditam/
053.004. śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa divyayā sudhayā pūritam/
053.004. athāyuṣmato mahākāśyapasyaitadabhavat--
053.006. divyaṃ cāsya sudhābhaktamayaṃ ca gṛhavistaraḥ/
053.007. suviruddhamiti kṛtvā jāto me hṛdi saṃśayaḥ//3// iti//
body.translated_text: <s>Śacī</s>, the divine maiden, also assumed the guise of a weaver-woman and began to prepare the shuttle. And beside her, divine <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia) stood prepared. Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, compassionate toward the destitute, helpless, and lowly people, arrived in due course at that house. Thinking "This is a suffering person," he stood at the door and extended his bowl. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, filled it with divine <s>sudhā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> thought: "This divine ambrosia-food and this elaborate household — these are contradictory, and doubt has arisen in my heart." //3//

body.text:
053.008. dharmatā hyeṣā--asamanvāhṛtya arhatāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate/
053.008. sa samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ/
053.009. yāvat paśyati śakraṃ devendram/
053.009. sa kathayati--kauśika, kiṃ duḥkhitajanasyāntarāyaṃ karoṣi, yasya te bhagavatā dīrgharātrānugato vicikitsākathaṃkathāśalyaḥ samūla ārūḍho yathāpi tattathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena/
053.011. ārya mahākāśyapa kiṃ duḥkhitajanasyāntarāyaṃ karomi? ime tāvat manuṣyāḥ puṇyānāmapratyakṣadarśino dānāni dadati puṇyāni kurvanti/
053.012. ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī eva puṇyānāṃ kathaṃ dānāni na dadāmi? nanu coktaṃ bhagavatā--
053.014. karaṇīyāni puṇyāni duḥkhā hyakṛtapuṇyatā/
053.015. kṛtapuṇyāni modante asmimlloke paratra ca//4//
body.translated_text: For this is the rule: without deliberate attention, the knowledge-vision of <s>Arhats</s> does not activate. He began to apply deliberate attention, and then he saw <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods. He said: "<s>Kauśika</s>, why do you create an obstacle for suffering people? The <s>Bhagavān</s> has long since uprooted your thorn of doubt and uncertainty, just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One [has done]." "Noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, how am I creating an obstacle for suffering people? These humans, who do not directly perceive the fruits of merits, give gifts and perform meritorious deeds. I, who directly perceive [the fruits], how can I not give gifts? Has not the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Meritorious deeds should be performed, for it is painful to be without merit. Those who have performed meritorious deeds rejoice in this world and the next.'" //4//

body.text:
053.016. tataḥ prabhṛti āyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ samanvāhṛtya kulāni piṇḍapātaṃ praveṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
053.017. atha śakro devendra ākāśasthaścāyuṣmato mahākāśyapasya piṇḍapātaṃ carato divyayā sudhayā pātraṃ pūrayati/
053.018. āyuṣmānapi mahākāśyapaḥ pātramadhomukhaṃ karoti/
053.018. annapānaṃ choryate/
053.018. etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti/
053.019. bhagavānāha--tasmādanujānāmi piṇḍopadhānaṃ dhārayitavyamiti//
body.translated_text: From then on, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> began to enter households for alms-food only after deliberate examination. But <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, standing in the sky, would fill the bowl of the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> with divine <s>sudhā</s> as he walked for alms. The venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> would turn his bowl upside down, and the food and drink would spill out. The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore I prescribe that an alms-food cover should be kept."

body.text:
053.021. sāmantakena śabdo visṛtah--amukayā nagarāvalambikayā āryo mahākāśyapa ācāmena pratipāditaḥ, sā ca tuṣite devanikāye upapannā iti/
053.022. rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena śrutam--amukayā nagarāvalambikayā āryo mahākāśyapa ācāmena pratipāditaḥ/
053.023. sā tuṣite deve upapannā iti/
053.024. śrutvā ca punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
053.024. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
053.025. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati, anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
053.027. atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavānāryamahākāśyapamuddiśya bhaktaṃ saptāhena iti/
053.029. adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitas tūṣṇībhāvena/
053.030. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
053.031. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastāmeva rātriṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīyaṃ kālyamevotthāya āsanāni <54>prajñāpya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
body.translated_text: The news spread in all directions: "Such-and-such a city-dwelling woman offered rice-water to the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and she was reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods." King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> heard: "Such-and-such a city-dwelling woman offered rice-water to the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and she was reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods." Having heard this, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat down to one side. The <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>; having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal dedicated to the noble <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> for seven days." The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the king by remaining silent. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, understanding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, that very night, prepared excellent hard and soft food, and rising early in the morning, arranged seats, set out water-pots, and announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: "It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come when he thinks it is time."

body.text:
054.002. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
054.004. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
054.004. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
054.006. anyatamaśca kroḍamallako vṛddhānte cittamabhiprasādayaṃstiṣṭhati--ayaṃ rājā pratyakṣadarśīm eva puṇyānāṃ sve puṇyaphale pratiṣṭhāpito 'tṛpta eva puṇyairdānāni dadāti, puṇyāni karoti/
054.008. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nekaparyāyeṇa buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastāt niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
054.011. tato bhagavatā abhihitah--mahārāja, kasya nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśāmi? kiṃ tava, āhosvidyena tavāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtamiti? rājā saṃlakṣayati--māṃ bhagavān piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte/
054.013. ko 'nyo mamāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasaviṣyatīti viditvā kathayati--bhagavan yena mamāntikāt prabhūtataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasūtaṃ tasya bhagavān nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatu iti/
054.014. tato bhagavatā kroḍamallakasya nāṃnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā/
054.015. evam yāvat ṣaḍdivasān/
054.015. tato 'nyadivase rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitah--mama bhagavān piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte, kroḍamallakasya nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśati iti/
054.017. so 'mātyairdṛṣṭaḥ/
054.017. te kathayanti--kimarthaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthita iti? rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kathaṃ na cintāparastiṣṭhāmi, yatredānīṃ sa bhagavān mama piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṅkte, kroḍamallakasya nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmāmādiśatīti? tatraiko vṛddho 'mātyaḥ kathayati--alpotsuko bhavatu/
054.020. vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmo yathā śvo bhagavān devasyaiva nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatīti/
054.021. taiḥ pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā yataḥ śvo bhavadbhiḥ praṇīta āhāraḥ sajjīkartavyaḥ prabhūtaścaiva samudānayitavyo yathopārdhaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātre patati upārdhaṃ bhūmau iti/
054.023. amātyairaparasmin divase prabhūta āhāraḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ praṇītaśca/
054.023. tataḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pariveṣitumārabdhaḥ/
054.024. upārdhaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātre patati, upārdhaṃ bhūmau/
054.025. tataḥ kroḍamallakāḥ pradhāvitāh--bhūmau nipatitaṃ gṛhṇīma iti/
054.025. te pariveṣakair nivāritāḥ/
054.026. tataḥ kroḍamallakaḥ kathayati--yadyasya rājñaḥ prabhūtamannam, svāpateyamasti, santyanye 'pi asmadvidhā duḥkhitakā ākāṅkṣante/
054.027. kimarthaṃ na dīyate? kimanenāparibhogaṃ choritena iti/
054.027. tasya kroḍamallakasya cittavikṣepo jātah--na śakyaṃ tena tathā cittaṃ prasādayitum yathā pūrvam/
054.028. tato rājā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣuasaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā na mama nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśatīti viditvā dakṣiṇāmaśrutvaiva praviṣṭaḥ/
054.030. tato bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya nāṃnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā--
054.031. hastyaśvarathapattiyāyino bhuñjānasya puraṃ sanairgamam/
054.032. paśyasi(?) phalaṃ hi rūṣkikāyā alavaṇikāyāḥ kulmāṣapiṇḍikāyāḥ//5//
body.translated_text: 054.002. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the forenoon and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by the assembly of monks and preceded by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, approached the meal-offering of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>. 054.004. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. 054.004. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, knowing the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hand satisfied and regaled them with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft. 054.006. And a certain <s>kroḍamallaka</s> (pig-wrestler) stood at the edge of the crowd, generating faith in his mind: "This king, a direct witness of merits, established in the fruit of his own merit, still unsatiated with merits, gives gifts and performs meritorious deeds." 054.008. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>, having in many ways satisfied and regaled the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, with his own hand, knowing the Blessed One had finished eating, having washed his hands and set aside the bowl, took a lower seat and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. 054.011. Then the Blessed One addressed him: "Great King, in whose name shall I dedicate the merit (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>)? In yours, or in the name of the one from whom more abundant merit has arisen in your presence?" The king reflected: "The Blessed One partakes of my meal-offering. 054.013. Who else could produce more abundant merit than me?" Having considered this, he said: "Blessed One, let the Blessed One dedicate the merit in the name of the one from whom more abundant merit has arisen in my presence." 054.014. Then the Blessed One dedicated the merit in the name of the <s>kroḍamallaka</s>. 054.015. Thus it continued for six days. 054.015. Then on another day, the king, placing his chin on his hand, stood absorbed in thought: "The Blessed One partakes of my meal-offering, yet dedicates the merit in the name of the <s>kroḍamallaka</s>." 054.017. The ministers saw him. 054.017. They asked: "Why do you stand absorbed in thought with chin resting on hand?" The king said: "Gentlemen, how should I not be absorbed in thought, when the Blessed One partakes of my meal-offering yet dedicates the merit in the name of the <s>kroḍamallaka</s>?" Then a certain aged minister said: "Do not be concerned. 054.020. We shall arrange it so that tomorrow the Blessed One dedicates the merit in Your Majesty's name alone." 054.021. They gave orders to the servants: "Tomorrow you must prepare fine and abundant food, and serve it such that half falls into the monks' bowls and half falls on the ground." 054.023. The next day, the ministers had abundant and excellent food prepared. 054.023. Then they began to serve the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> comfortably seated. 054.024. Half fell into the monks' bowls, half on the ground. 054.025. Then the <s>kroḍamallakas</s> rushed forward: "Let us take what has fallen on the ground!" 054.025. They were blocked by the servers. 054.026. Then the <s>kroḍamallaka</s> said: "If this king has abundant food and personal provisions, there are others like us, wretched ones, who also desire it. 054.027. Why is it not given? What is the use of throwing it away unenjoyed?" 054.027. The mind of that <s>kroḍamallaka</s> became disturbed — he was no longer able to generate faith as before. 054.028. Then the king, having fed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, knowing "He does not dedicate the merit in my name," entered [his quarters] without even hearing the dedication. 054.030. Then the Blessed One dedicated the merit in the name of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> — 054.031. "For one who feasts while his elephant, horse, chariot, and infantry forces move slowly toward the city, 054.032. the fruit of an unsalted barley-cake is [even] greater; 054.033. thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks regarding future [rebirths]. 054.034. One who has little and gives from that little — of such a one, the fruit cannot be measured as so much — 054.035. just as one cannot easily count the water-drops when a full water-vessel is overturned." // 12 //

body.text:
055.001. <55>athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--bahuśo bahuśo bhadanta bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya niveśane bhuktvā nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiṣṭā/
055.002. nābhijānāmi kadācidevamrūpāṃ dakṣiṇāmādiṣṭapūrvām/
055.003. bhagavānāha--icchasi tvamānanda rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyālavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāmārabhya karmaplotiṃ śrotum? etasya bhagavan kālaḥ, etasya sugata samayaḥ/
055.005. ayaṃ bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyālavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāmārabhya karmaplotiṃ varṇayet, bhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti iti/
055.006. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--
055.007. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karpaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati/
055.007. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
055.008. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
055.008. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ/
055.009. sa unnīto vardhitaḥ paṭuḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
055.009. yāvadasau gṛhapatiḥ patnīmāmantrayate--bhadra, jāto 'smākamṛṇahārako dhanahārakaśca/
055.010. gacchāmi paṇyamādāya deśāntaramiti/
055.011. sā kathayati--āryaputra, etat kuruṣva iti/
055.011. sa paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gataḥ/
055.011. tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannaḥ/
055.012. alpaparicchado 'sau gṛhapatiḥ/
055.012. tasya gṛhapaterdhanajātaṃ parikṣīṇam/
055.012. so 'sya putro duḥkhito jātaḥ/
055.013. tasya gṛhapatervayasyakaḥ/
055.013. tena tasya dārakasya mātā abhihitā--ayaṃ tava putraḥ kṣetraṃ rakṣatu, ahamasya sukhaṃ bhuktena yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyāmi/
055.014. evaṃ bhavatu/
055.015. sa tasya kṣetraṃ rakṣitumārabdhaḥ/
055.015. sa tasya sukhaṃ bhaktakena yogodvahanaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
055.015. yāvadapareṇa samayena parvaṇī pratyupasthitā/
055.016. tasya dārakasya mātā saṃlakṣayati--adya gṛhapatipatnī suhṛtsambandhibāndhavāḥ saha śramaṇabrāhmaṇabhojanena vyagrā bhaviṣyati/
055.017. gacchāmi sānukālaṃ tasya dārakasya bhaktaṃ nayāmi iti/
055.018. sā sānukālaṃ gatvā gṛhapatipatnyā etamarthaṃ niveśayati/
055.018. sā ruṣitā kathayati--na tāvacchramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo dadāmi jñātīnāṃ vā, tāvat preṣyamanuṣyāya dadāmi? adya tāvat tiṣṭhatu, śvo dviguṇaṃ dāsyāmīti/
055.020. tatastasya dārakasya mātā saṃlakṣayati--mā me putro bubhukṣitakaḥ sthāsyatīti/
055.021. tayā ātmano 'rthe 'lavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā saṃpāditā/
055.022. sā tāmādāya gatā/
055.022. tena dārakeṇa dūrata eva dṛṣṭā/
055.022. sa kathayati--amba, asti kiṃcinmṛṣṭaṃ mṛṣṭam? sā kathayati--putra, yadeva prātidaivasikaṃ tadapyadya nāsti/
055.023. mayā ātmano 'rthe 'lavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍikā sādhitā/
055.024. tāmahaṃ gṛhītvā āgatā/
055.024. etāṃ paribhuṅkṣveti/
055.025. sa kathayati--sthāpayitvā gacchasveti/
055.025. sā sthāpayitvā prakrāntā//
body.translated_text: 055.001. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Many times, venerable sir, the Blessed One has eaten at the residence of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s> and dedicated the merit in his name. 055.002. I do not recall [the Blessed One] ever having dedicated a merit of such a kind before." 055.003. The Blessed One said: "Do you wish, <s>Ānanda</s>, to hear the story of the deeds (<s>karmaploti</s>) regarding King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>'s unsalted barley-cake?" "<s>Blessed One</s>, this is the time; <s>Sugata</s>, this is the occasion. 055.005. Let the Blessed One narrate the story of the deeds regarding King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kosala</s>'s unsalted barley-cake — having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will retain it." 055.006. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the monks: 055.007. "Once upon a time, monks, in a certain small village a householder dwelt. 055.007. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. 055.008. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. 055.008. While he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, a son was born to him. 055.009. The son was raised, grew up, and became clever. 055.009. Then that householder addressed his wife: 'My dear, a debt-payer and wealth-bringer has been born to us. 055.010. I shall take merchandise and go to another country.' 055.011. She said: 'Do so, noble husband.' 055.011. He took merchandise and went to another country. 055.011. There, through misfortune, he fell into ruin. 055.012. That householder had few possessions. 055.012. The wealth of that householder was exhausted. 055.012. His son became miserable. 055.013. The householder had a friend. 055.013. That friend addressed the boy's mother: 'Let this son of yours guard the fields, and I will arrange for his comfortable sustenance.' 055.014. 'So be it.' 055.015. He began guarding his fields. 055.015. He began arranging for his comfortable sustenance. 055.015. Then, after some time, a festival day arrived. 055.016. The boy's mother reflected: 'Today the householder's wife will be occupied with feeding relatives, kinsmen, family members, along with <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' 055.017. 'Let me go and take food to the boy in a timely manner.' 055.018. She went in a timely manner and presented the matter to the householder's wife. 055.018. She, angered, said: 'I have not yet given to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, or kinsmen, and I should give to a slave's child? Let it be for today; tomorrow I will give double.' 055.020. Then the boy's mother reflected: 'Let not my son remain hungry!' 055.021. She prepared an unsalted barley-cake from her own portion. 055.022. She took it and went. 055.022. The boy saw her from afar. 055.022. He said: 'Mother, is there something delicious, really delicious?' She said: 'Son, even the everyday [food] is not available today. 055.023. I have prepared an unsalted barley-cake from my own portion. 055.024. I have brought it. 055.024. Eat it.' 055.025. He said: 'Set it down and go.' 055.025. She set it down and departed."

body.text:
055.026. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prantaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
055.027. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddhastatpradeśamanuprāptaḥ/
055.027. sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaścitraprāsādikaśca śānteryāpathavartī/
055.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--nūnaṃ mayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūte dakṣiṇīye kārā na kṛtā, yena me īdṛśī samavasthā/
055.029. yadyayaṃ mamāntikādalavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍikāṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt, ahamasmai dadyāmiti/
055.030. tato 'sau pratyekabuddhastasya daridrapuruṣasya cetasā cittamājñāya pātraṃ prasāritavān--bhadramukha, sacette parityaktam, dīyatāmasmin pātra iti/
055.032. tatastena tīvreṇa prasādena sā alavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā tasmai pratyekabuddhāya pratipāditā//
body.translated_text: 055.026. In the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, delighting in secluded dwellings and resting places, sole worthy recipients of offerings in the world. 055.027. Then a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> arrived at that place. 055.027. The boy saw him — pleasing in body, pleasing in appearance, moving with peaceful deportment. 055.028. He reflected: "Surely it is because I have not made offerings to such a true, worthy recipient that I am in this condition. 055.029. If this one would accept my unsalted barley-cake, I would give it to him." 055.030. Then that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, knowing the mind of that poor man with his own mind, extended his bowl: "Friend, if you have renounced it, place it in this bowl." 055.032. Then, with intense faith, he offered that unsalted barley-cake to that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.

body.text:
056.001. <56>kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau daridrapuruṣaḥ, eṣa evāsau rājā prasenajit kauśalastena kālena tena samayena/
056.002. yadanena pratyekabuddhāyālavaṇikā kulmāṣapiṇḍakā pratipāditā, tena karmaṇā ṣaṭkṛtvo deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān, ṣaṭkṛtvo 'syāmeva śrāvastyāṃ rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ, tenaiva ca karmaṇā avaśeṣeṇa etarhi rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
056.005. so 'sya tamahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi--
056.006. hastyaśvarathapattiyāyino bhuñjānasya puraṃ sanairgamanam/
056.007. paśyasi phalaṃ hi rūkṣikāyā alavaṇikāyā kulmāṣapiṇḍakāyāḥ// iti/
056.008. sāmantakena śabdo visṛtah--bhagavatā rājñaḥ prasenajito 'lavaṇikāṃ kulmāṣapiṇḍakāmārabhya karmaplotirvyākṛtā iti/
056.009. rājñāpi prasenajitā śrutam/
056.009. sa yena bhagavāṃsetenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
056.010. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
056.010. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdaraśyati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
056.012. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
056.012. atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanādekāṃsamutterāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃs traimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgheneti/
056.015. adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
056.015. tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena buddhamukhāya bhikṣusaṃghāya traimāsyaṃ śatarasaṃ bhojanaṃ dattam/
056.016. ekaikaśca bhikṣuḥ śatasahasreṇa vastreṇācchāditaḥ/
056.017. tailasya ca kumbhakoṭiṃ samudānīya dīpamālā abhyudyato dātum/
056.018. tatra bhakte pūjāyāṃ ca mahān kolāhalo jātaḥ/
056.018. yāvadanyatamā nagarāvalambikā atīva duḥkhitā/
056.019. tayā kroḍamallakena bhikṣāmaṭantyā uccaśabdhaḥ śrutaḥ/
056.019. śrutvā ca punaḥ pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, kimeṣa uccaśabdo mahāśabda iti/
056.020. aparaiḥ samākhyātam--rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena buddhapramukho bhikṣuasṃghastraimāsyaṃ bhojitaḥ, ekaikaśca bhikṣuḥ śatasahasreṇa vastreṇa ācchāditaḥ, tailasya kumbhakoṭiṃ ca samudānīya dīpamālā abhyudyato dātumiti/
056.022. tatastasyā nagarāvalambikāyā etadabhavat--ayaṃ tāvadrājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ puṇyairatṛpto 'dyāpi dānāni dadāti, puṇyāni karoti/
056.024. yannvahamapi kutaścit samudānīya bhagavataḥ pradīpaṃ dadyāmiti/
056.024. tayā khaṇḍamallake tailasya stokam yācayitvā pradīpaṃ prajvālya bhagavataścaṅkrame dattaḥ/
056.025. pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam--anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yathāyaṃ bhagavāñ śākyamunirvarṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma śāstā loka utpannaḥ, evamahamapi varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunireva śāstā bhaveyam/
056.028. yathā cāsya dāriputramaudgalyāyanāgrayugaṃ bhadrayugamānando bhikṣurupasthāyakaḥ, śuddhodanaḥ pitā, mātā mahāmāyā, rāhulabhadraḥ kumāraḥ putraḥ/
056.029. yathāyaṃ bhagavān dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāsyati, evamahamapi dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāpayeyamiti/
056.030. yāvat sarve te dīpā nairvāṇāḥ/
056.031. sa tayā prajvalitaḥ pradīpaḥ prajvalatyeva/
056.031. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatām--na tāvadupasthāyakāḥ pratisamlīyante na yāvadbuddhā bhagavantaḥ pratisamlīnā iti/
056.032. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ saṃlakṣayati--asthānamanavakāśo yadbuddhā bhagavanta āloke śayyāṃ kalpayanti/
056.033. yannvahaṃ dīpam <57>nirvāpayeyamiti/
body.translated_text:
056.001. <56>"What do you think, monks? He who was that poor man — he is none other than King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> at that time, in that era.
056.002. Because he offered an unsalted <s>kulmāṣapiṇḍaka</s> (barley-cake) to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), by that deed he exercised sovereign lordship and dominion six times among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, and six times in this very <s>Śrāvastī</s> he was a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, and by the remainder of that very deed he has now become a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head.
056.005. It is with reference to him that I speak —
056.006. 'Moving slowly through the city while enjoying elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry;
056.007. Behold the fruit of a coarse, unsalted barley-cake!' Thus.
056.008. Throughout the region the word spread: 'The Blessed One has declared the <s>karmaploti</s> (karmic account) of King <s>Prasenajit</s> beginning with the unsalted barley-cake.'
056.009. King <s>Prasenajit</s> also heard this.
056.009. He approached the Blessed One.
056.010. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
056.010. To King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>.
056.012. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
056.012. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, rising from his seat and arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, said to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept from me, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community of monks), the three-monthly provision of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines for the sick.'
056.015. The Blessed One accepted King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>'s [invitation] by silence.
056.015. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> gave to the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks) headed by the <s>Buddha</s> a feast of a hundred flavors for three months.
056.016. Each monk was covered with a garment worth a hundred thousand.
056.017. And having gathered ten million jars of oil, he prepared to offer a garland of lamps.
056.018. There, at the offering of food and worship, a great commotion arose.
056.018. Meanwhile, a certain woman dependent on the city was exceedingly poor.
056.019. She, begging for alms with a broken bowl, heard the loud sound.
056.019. Having heard it, she asked: 'Good people, what is this loud, great sound?'
056.020. Others told her: 'King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> has fed the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for three months, and each monk has been covered with a garment worth a hundred thousand, and having gathered ten million jars of oil, he is prepared to offer a garland of lamps.'
056.022. Then that city-dwelling woman thought: 'This King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, unsatisfied with merit, even now gives gifts and performs meritorious deeds.
056.024. Let me too, having gathered something from somewhere, offer a lamp to the Blessed One.'
056.024. She obtained a small amount of oil in a broken vessel by begging, lit a lamp, and placed it on the Blessed One's walking path.
056.025. Falling at his feet, she made an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, just as this Blessed One, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, has arisen as a Teacher named <s>Śākyamuni</s> among people with a lifespan of a hundred years, so may I too become a Teacher, a <s>Śākyamuni</s>, among people with a lifespan of a hundred years.
056.028. And just as he has <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> as his foremost pair, his excellent pair, <s>Ānanda</s> as his attendant monk, <s>Śuddhodana</s> as his father, <s>Mahāmāyā</s> as his mother, and <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> as his princely son —
056.029. just as this Blessed One will attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> having made a distribution of relics, so may I too attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> having made a distribution of relics.'
056.030. Eventually all those lamps were extinguished.
056.031. But the lamp lit by her continued to burn.
056.031. It is indeed the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, that attendants do not retire until the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, have retired.
056.032. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> considered: 'It is impossible and inconceivable that <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, should compose themselves to sleep in the light.
056.033. Let me extinguish <57>the lamp.'

body.text:
057.001. sa hastena nirvāpayitumārabdho na śaknoti/
057.001. tataścīvarakarṇikena, tato vyajanena, tathāpi na śaknoti nirvāpayitum/
057.002. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--kimetadānandeti/
057.003. sa kathayati--bhagavan, mama buddhirutpanā--asthānamanavakāśo yadbuddhā bhagavanta āloke śayyāṃ kalpayanti/
057.004. yannvahaṃ dīpaṃ nirvāpayeyamiti/
057.004. so 'haṃ hastena nirvāpayitumārabdho na śaknomi, tataścīvarakarṇikena, tato vyajanena, tathāpi na śaknomīti/
057.005. bhagavānāha--khedamānanda āpatsyase/
057.006. yadi vairambhakā api vāyavo vāyeyuḥ, te 'pi na śaknuyur nirvāpayituṃ prāgeva hastagataścīvarakarṇiko vyajanaṃ vā/
057.007. tathā hi--ayaṃ pradīpastayā dārikayā mahatā cittābhisaṃskāreṇa prajvalitaḥ/
057.008. api tu ānanda bhaviṣyatyasau dārikā varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhaḥ/
057.009. śāriputramaudgalyāyanau tasyāgrayugaṃ bhadrayugam, ānando bhikṣurupāsakaḥ, śuddhodanaḥ pitā, mahāmāyā mātā, kapilavastu nagaram, rāhulabhadraḥ kumāraḥ putraḥ/
057.011. sāpi dhātuvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā parinirvāsyatīti//
body.translated_text:
057.001. He began to extinguish it with his hand but could not.
057.001. Then with the corner of his robe, then with a fan — still he could not extinguish it.
057.002. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'What is this, <s>Ānanda</s>?'
057.003. He said: 'Blessed One, the thought arose in me — it is impossible and inconceivable that <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, should compose themselves to sleep in the light.
057.004. Let me extinguish the lamp.
057.004. I began to extinguish it with my hand but could not, then with the corner of my robe, then with a fan — still I could not.'
057.005. The Blessed One said: 'You will exhaust yourself, <s>Ānanda</s>.
057.006. Even if the <s>Vairambhaka</s> (cosmic) winds were to blow, even they could not extinguish it — how much less a hand, the corner of a robe, or a fan?
057.007. For this lamp was lit by that girl with a great mental resolve.
057.008. Moreover, <s>Ānanda</s>, that girl shall become, among people with a lifespan of a hundred years, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>.
057.009. <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> shall be her foremost pair, her excellent pair; <s>Ānanda</s> shall be her attendant monk; <s>Śuddhodana</s> her father; <s>Mahāmāyā</s> her mother; <s>Kapilavastu</s> her city; <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> her princely son.
057.011. She too shall attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> having made a distribution of relics.'

body.text:
057.012. idamavocadbhagavān/
057.012. āttamanasaste ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
057.012. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
057.012. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 057.013. iti śrīdivyāvadāne nagarāvalambikāvadānaṃ saptamam//
body.translated_text: 057.013. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Nagarāvalambikāvadāna</s> (The Story of the City-Dwelling Woman), the seventh.

body.text: 058.001 div8 supiryāvadāna
body.translated_text: 058.001. Chapter 8: The <s>Supriyāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Supriyā</s>).

body.text:
058.002. buddho bhavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ paurairbrāhmaṇairgṛhapatibhiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavāṃl lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ/
058.005. tatra khalu varṣāvāsaṃ bhagavānupagto jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
058.006. atha tadaiva pravāraṇāyāṃ pratyupasthitāyāṃ saṃbahulāḥ śrtāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
058.007. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānto niṣaṇṇāh
058.008. ekāntaniṣaṇṇān saṃbahulāñ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
058.010. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
058.011. atha saṃbahulāḥ/
058.011. śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakāntāḥ, yenāyuṣmānānandastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
058.012. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
058.013. saṃbahulāñ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇija āyuṣmānānando dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
058.015. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
058.016. atha te vaṇija utthāyāsanebhyah ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmānānandastenānñjaliṃ praṇamya āyuṣmantamānandamidamavocan -- kiṃcitte āryānanda śrutaṃ varṣoṣito bhagavān katameṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyatīti, yadvayaṃ tadyātrikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīmahe ? dharmatā caiṣā ṣaṇmahānagaranivāsino vaṇijo yasyāṃ diśi buddhā bhagavanto gantukāmā bhavanti, tadyātrikabhāṇḍaṃ samudānayanti/
058.020. sa kathayati -- buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ kiṃ na pṛcchatha ? durāsadā hi buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ/
058.021. na śaknumo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ praṣṭum/
058.021. mamāpi bhavanto durāsadā hi buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ/
058.022. ahamapi na śaknomi bhagavantaṃ praṣṭum/
058.022. yadi bhadantānandasyāpi durāsadā buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ, kathaṃ bhadantānando jānīte 'mukāṃ diśaṃ bhagavān gamiṣyatīti ? nimittena vā bhavantaḥ parikathayā vā/
058.024. kathaṃ nimittena ? yāṃ diśaṃ bhagavān gantukāmastato 'bhimukho niṣīdati, evaṃ nimittena/
058.025. kathaṃ parikathayā ? teṣāṃ janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate, evaṃ parikathayā/
058.026. kutomukho bhadantānanda bhagavān niṣīdati, katameṣāṃ ca janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate ? magadhābhimukho bhavanto bhagavān niṣīdati, māgadhakānāṃ janapadānāṃ varṇaṃ bhāṣate/
058.027. api tu bhavanto 'ṣṭādaśānuśaṃsā buddhacārikāyām/
058.028. katame 'ṣṭādaśa ? nāgnibhyaṃ nodakabhyaṃ na siṃhabhyaṃ na vyāghrabhyaṃ na dvīpitarakṣuparacakrabhyaṃ na caurabhayaṃ na gulmatarapaṇyātiyātrābhyaṃ na manuṣyāmanuṣyabhayam/
058.030. kālena ca kālaṃ divyāni rūpāṇi dṛśyante, divyāḥ śabdāḥ śrūyante, udārāś cāvabhāsāḥ prajñnyāyante, ātmavyākaraṇāni ca śrūyante, dharmasambhoga āmiṣasambhogo'/
058.031. pābādhā ca buddhacandrikā//
body.translated_text:
058.002. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, guild-masters, caravan leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, received robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines for the sick, together with the community of disciples.
058.005. There indeed the Blessed One had entered the rains-retreat at <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
058.006. Then, when the <s>Pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) was at hand, a number of merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> approached the Blessed One.
058.007. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
058.008. To the merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>.
058.010. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
058.011. Then the merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having approved and rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, departed from the presence of the Blessed One, and approached the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
058.012. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and sat down to one side.
058.013. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>.
058.015. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
058.016. Then those merchants, rising from their seats and arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, joining their palms toward the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, said to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Has the noble <s>Ānanda</s> heard in which provinces the Blessed One, having spent the rains, will undertake a wandering tour, so that we may gather our travel merchandise? For it is customary that the merchants dwelling in the six great cities gather travel merchandise for whatever direction the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, wish to go.'
058.020. He said: 'Why do you not ask the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One? For <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are difficult to approach and difficult to confront.'
058.021. 'We are unable to ask the Blessed One.'
058.021. 'Good people, for me too, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are difficult to approach and difficult to confront.
058.022. I too am unable to ask the Blessed One.'
058.022. 'If even for the noble <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are difficult to approach and difficult to confront, how then does the noble <s>Ānanda</s> know which direction the Blessed One will go?' 'By signs, good people, or by conversation.'
058.024. 'How by signs?' 'Whichever direction the Blessed One wishes to go, he sits facing that direction — thus by signs.'
058.025. 'How by conversation?' 'He speaks in praise of those provinces — thus by conversation.'
058.026. 'Which direction is the Blessed One facing, noble <s>Ānanda</s>, and which provinces does he praise?' 'Good people, the Blessed One sits facing <s>Magadha</s> and speaks in praise of the provinces of <s>Magadha</s>.'
058.027. 'However, good people, there are eighteen benefits of traveling with a <s>Buddha</s>.
058.028. What eighteen? There is no danger from fires, no danger from floods, no danger from lions, no danger from tigers, no danger from leopards, bears, rival armies, no danger from thieves, no danger from toll-stations, excessive taxes, or transit duties, no danger from human or non-human beings.
058.030. And from time to time, divine forms are seen, divine sounds are heard, magnificent radiances appear, and prophecies for oneself are heard; there is the enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s> and the enjoyment of material goods.
058.031. And there is freedom from illness — the cooling moonlight of the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text:
059.001. <059>atha saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijah āyuṣmatah ānandasya bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya āyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntāḥ/
059.003. dhartā khalu buddhā bhagavanto jīvanto dhriyanto yāpayanto mahākaruṇayā saṃcodyamānāḥ parānugrahapravṛttāḥ kālena kālamaraṇyacārikāṃ caranti, nadīcārikāṃ parvatacārikāṃ śmaśānacārikāṃ janapada cārikāṃ caranti/
059.005. asmiṃstvarthe buddho bhagavān magadheṣu janapadacārikāṃ cartukāmastadeva pravāraṇāṃ pravārayitvā āyuṣmantamānadāmāmantrayate sma -- gaccha ānanda, bhikṣūṇāmārocaya itaḥ saptame divase tathāgato magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cāriṣyati/
059.007. yo yuṣmākam utsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ janapadacārikāṃ cartum, sa cīvarakarma karotu/
059.008. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati -- bhagavānāyuṣyanta itaḥ saptame divase magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
059.009. yo yuṣmākamutsahate bhagavatā sārdhaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum, sa cīvarakarma karotu/
059.011. atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ saṃbahulaiśca śrāvastīnivāsibhirvaṇigbrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ sārdhaṃ magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then the numerous merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having rejoiced in and approved of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>'s words, bowed their heads at the feet of the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, rose from their seats, and departed. Indeed, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, while living, sustaining, and maintaining themselves, impelled by great compassion and devoted to benefiting others, from time to time undertake wanderings in the wilderness, wanderings along rivers, wanderings in the mountains, wanderings in cremation grounds, and wanderings through the countryside. In this connection, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wishing to undertake a countryside wandering in <s>Magadha</s>, having performed the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony), addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and inform the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) that in seven days the <s>Tathāgata</s> will undertake a wandering through the countryside of <s>Magadha</s>. Whoever among you is able to travel with the <s>Tathāgata</s> on the countryside wandering, let him prepare his robe-work." "So be it, Venerable One." The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having acknowledged the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s instruction, informed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Venerable ones, in seven days the <s>Bhagavān</s> will undertake a wandering through the countryside of <s>Magadha</s>. Whoever among you is able to travel with the <s>Bhagavān</s> on a wandering through the countryside of <s>Magadha</s>, let him prepare his robe-work." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, attended by the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>, together with numerous merchants, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, set out on a wandering through the countryside of <s>Magadha</s>.

body.text:
059.013. atha saṃbahulāśca śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
059.013. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantamidamavocan -- adhivāsayatvasmākaṃ bhagavān yāvacca śrāvastī yāvacca rājagṛham, atrāntarā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
059.016. adhivāsayati bhagavān saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvastīnivāsināṃ vaṇijāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena/
059.017. atha saṃbahulāḥ śrāvastīnivāsino vaṇijo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ//
body.translated_text: Then numerous merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from us, for the entire distance from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick, together with the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted from the numerous merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> by his silence. Then the numerous merchants dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, understanding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s acceptance through his silence, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text:
059.019. atha saṃprasthite buddhe bhagavati antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca rājagṛham, atrāntarānmahāṭavyāṃ caurasahasraṃ prativasati/
059.020. adrākṣīttaccaurasahasraṃ bhagavantaṃ sārthaparivṛtaṃ bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtam/
059.021. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ parasparaṃ kathayanti -- gaccatu bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ/
059.021. śeṣaṃ sārthaṃ muṣi ṣyāmaḥ/
059.022. ityanuvicintya sarve javena prasṛtā yena sārthaḥ/
059.022. bhagavatā abhihitah -- kimetadbhavantaḥ samārabdham ? caurāḥ kathayanti -- vayaṃ smo bhadanta caurā aṭavīcarāḥ/
059.023. nāsamākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyā na gaurakṣyam/
059.024. anenopakrameṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ/
059.024. gacchatu bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ/
059.024. śeṣaṃ sārthaṃ muṣiṣyāmaḥ/
059.025. bhagavānāha -- mamaiṣa sārthaḥ saṃniśritaḥ/
059.025. api tu sakalasya sārthasya parigaṇayya suvarṇaṃ gṛhṇīdhvam/
059.026. tathā bhavatviti caurasahasreṇa pratijñnātam/
059.026. asmin sārthe ye upāsakā viṇijastaiḥ kṛtsnasya sārthasya mūlyaṃ gaṇayya caurāṇāṃ niveditam iyanti śatāni sahasrāṇi ceti/
059.028. tatasteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ sārthaniṣkrayārthaṃ bhagavatā nidhānaṃ darśitam/
059.029. tatastena caurasahasreṇa sārthamūlyapramāṇaṃ suvarṇaṃ gṛhītam, avaśiṣṭaṃ tatraivāntarhitam/
059.029. evaṃ bhagavatā sārthaścaurasahasrāt pratimokṣitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then, as the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, had set out, in the great forest between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a thousand bandits were dwelling. That thousand bandits saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> surrounded by the caravan and attended by the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. Having seen him, they said to one another: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s>. We will rob the rest of the caravan." Having thus considered, they all rushed swiftly toward the caravan. The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed them: "What is this undertaking of yours, good sirs?" The bandits replied: "We are bandits, Venerable One, roaming the forest. We have no farming, no trade, no cattle-herding. We sustain our livelihood by this means. Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s>. We will rob the rest of the caravan." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "This caravan has taken refuge with me. However, calculate the value of the entire caravan and take gold instead." "So be it," the thousand bandits agreed. The lay-follower merchants in the caravan calculated the value of the entire caravan and reported it to the bandits: "It is so many hundreds and thousands." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> revealed a treasure to the bandits as ransom for the caravan. The thousand bandits took gold equal to the value of the caravan, and the remainder disappeared right there.

body.text:
059.031. anupūrveṇa bhagavān rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
059.031. punarapi bhagavān sārthaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃgha puraskṛto rājagṛhāt śrāvastīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
059.032. tathaiva caurasahasrasakāśāt sārtho niṣkrītaḥ/
body.translated_text: Gradually the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Once again the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the caravan and attended by the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>, set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. In the same manner, the caravan was ransomed from the thousand bandits.

body.text:
060.001. <60>evaṃ dvitricatuṣpanñcaṣaḍvārāṃśca cairasahasrasakāśādāgamanagamanena sārthaḥ paritrāto mūlyaṃ cānupradattam/
060.002. saptaṃ tu cāraṃ bhagavān sārtharahito bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ śāvastyā rājagṛhaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
060.003. adrākṣīccaurasahasraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sārthavirahitaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtam/
060.003. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ parasparaṃ saṃlapanti -- bhagavān gacchatu, bhikṣusaṃghaṃ muṣiṣyāṃḥ/
060.004. tatkasya hetoh ? eṣo hi bhagavān suvarṇapradaḥ/
060.005. ityuktvā sarvajavena pradhāvitā bhikṣūn muṣitumārabdhāḥ/
060.005. bhagavatā cābhihitāh -- vatsāḥ, mama ete śrāvakāḥ/
060.006. caurāḥ kathayanti -- jānāsyeva bhagavān -- vayaṃ caurā aṭavīcarāḥ/
060.007. nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vaṇijyā na gaurakṣyam/
060.007. anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ/
060.008. tato bhagavatā caurāṇāṃ mahānidhānaṃ darśitam, evaṃ coktāh -- vatsāḥ, yāvadāptaṃ dhanaṃ gṛhṇītheti/
060.009. tatastena caurasahasreṇa tasmānmahānidhānādyāvadāptaṃ suvarṇamādattam, avaśiṣṭaṃ tatraivāntarhitam/
060.010. atha bhagavāṃstaccaurasahasram yāvadāptaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā tato 'nupūrveṇa rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
060.011. tatasteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ buddhirutpannā -- yā kācidasmākaṃ śrīsaubhāgyasampat, sarvāsau buddhaṃ bhagavantamāgamya/
060.012. yannu vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghamasmin pradeśe bhojayema iti/
060.012. atrāntare nāsti kiṃcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāmekarakṣāṇāmekavīrāṇāmadvayavādināṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ trividhadamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupritiṣṭhitānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśāradānāmudārārṣabhasamyaksiṃhanādanādināṃ panñcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ panñcaskandha vimocakānāṃ panñcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍāyatanabhedakānāṃ saṃghātavihāriṇāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇayaśasāṃ
saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānāṃ saptasamādhipariṣkāradāyakānāmāryāṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāmāryamārgapudgalanāyakānāṃ navānupūrvasamāpattikuśalānāṃ navasamyojanavisamyojanakānāṃ daśadikparipūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣtānāṃ trīrātrestrirdivasasya ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivasena buddhacakṣuṣā lokam
vyavalokayantikasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayāmi, kasyāvaropitāni vivardhayāmi, kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ, kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ, kaṃ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhāt parimocayāmi, ko 'pāyaniṃnaḥ, ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ, ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ, kamahamapāyād vyutthāpya svarge mokṣaphale ca pratiṣṭhāpayāmi, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayacchāmi, kasya buddhotpādavibhūṣitaṃ lokaṃ saphalīkaromi, kamāryadhanavirahitamāryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭāpayeyam, ko hīyate ko vardhate/
060.027. apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ/
060.028. na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet//1//
body.translated_text: Thus, two, three, four, five, and six times, by going and coming from the thousand bandits, the caravan was protected and the ransom paid. But on the seventh occasion, the <s>Bhagavān</s> set out from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to <s>Rājagṛha</s> without a caravan, attended only by the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. The thousand bandits saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, without a caravan, surrounded by the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. Having seen him, they said to one another: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass; we will rob the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>. Why? For this <s>Bhagavān</s> is a giver of gold." Having said this, they rushed with all speed and began to rob the <s>bhikṣus</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed them: "Dear ones, these are my <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples)." The bandits replied: "You know well, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that we are bandits, roaming the forest. We have no farming, no trade, no cattle-herding. We sustain our livelihood by this means." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> revealed a great treasure to the bandits and said: "Dear ones, take as much wealth as you can carry." The thousand bandits took as much gold as they could carry from that great treasure, and the remainder disappeared right there. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having satisfied the thousand bandits with as much wealth as they could carry, gradually arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Then a thought arose in the minds of those bandits: "Whatever prosperity, good fortune, and wealth we have, all of it depends on the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Let us approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> and go forth into homelessness." They approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and requested ordination. The <s>Bhagavān</s> ordained them, and through diligent practice they attained <s>arhatship</s> (the state of a worthy one).

body.text:
060.029. yathā hi mātā priyamekaputrakaṃ hyavekṣate rakṣati cāsya jīvitam/
060.031. tathaiva vaineyajanaṃ tathagato hyavekṣate rakṣati cāsya saṃtatim//2//
body.translated_text: Just as a mother watches over her beloved only son and protects his life, so too the <s>Tathāgata</s> watches over those to be trained and protects their continuity.

body.text:
061.001. <61>sarvajñnasaṃtānanivāsinī hi kāruṇyadhenurmṛgayatyakhinnā/
061.003. vaineyavatsān bhavaduḥkhanaṣṭān vatsān praṇaṣṭaniva vatsalā gauḥ//3//
