body.translated_text: The cow of compassion, dwelling in the lineage of the Omniscient One, tirelessly seeks out those to be trained who are lost in the suffering of existence, like an affectionate cow seeking her lost calves.

body.text:
061.005. tato bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ vaineyakālamapekṣya rājagṛhādanupūrveṇa bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣugaṇapuraskṛto dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāraścandanaścandanaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāraḥ pūrvavat yāvanmahākaruṇayā samanvāgatas tāṃ sālāṭavīmanuprāptaḥ/
061.008. adrākṣīttaccaurasahasraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ dūrādevāgacchantam/
061.008. dṛṣṭvā ca punaścittānyabhiprasādya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
061.009. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantamidamavodcan -- adhivāsayatu asmākaṃ bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
061.011. adhivāsayati bhagavāṃstasya caurasasrasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
061.011. atha caurasahasraṃ bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato'ntikān prakrāntam//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, watching for the proper time to train those bandits, gradually set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, surrounded by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, attended by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> -- tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; cool as sandalwood, with a retinue cool as sandalwood; liberated, with a liberated retinue; reassured, with a reassured retinue -- as before, endowed with great compassion, he arrived at that <s>Sāla</s> forest. The thousand bandits saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approaching from afar with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s>. Having seen him, with minds filled with faith, they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from us a meal tomorrow in our dwelling, together with the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted from the thousand bandits by his silence. Then the thousand bandits, understanding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s acceptance through his silence, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text:
061.013. atha taccaurasahasraṃ tāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñnapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya, bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati -- samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyase/
061.015. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena tasya caurasahasrasya bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
061.017. atha taccaurasahasraṃ buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṃghasya candanodakena pādau prakṣālayāmāsa/
061.018. atha bhagavān prakṣālitapāṇipādaḥ purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñnapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
061.019. niṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcatarāṇyāsanāni gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
061.019. atha bhagavatā teṣāmāśayānuśayaṃ viditvā dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñnātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tena caurasahasreṇa tasminnevāsane niṣaṇṇena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñnānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
061.024. dṛṣṭasatyāśca kathayanti -- idamasmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ na rājñnā na devatābhir na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair neṣṭair na svajanabandhuvargeṇa yadasmābhirbhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitramāgamya/
061.025. uddhṛto narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ pādaḥ, pratiṣṭhāpitā devamanuṣyeṣu, paryantīkṛtaḥ saṃsāraḥ, ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, uttīrṇā aśrusāgarāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ/
061.027. labhema vayaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
061.028. carema vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
061.028. tato bhagavatā brahmeṇa svareṇābhihitāh -- eta vatsāḥ, carata brahmacaryam/
061.029. vācāvasāne bhagavato muṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgāḥ samaloṣṭakānñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñnāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhāḥ/
061.031. sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyāśca saṃvṛttāḥ//
body.translated_text: Then those thousand thieves, that very night, having gathered pure and excellent hard and soft foods, rising early in the morning, preparing seats, setting up water vessels, announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: "It is time, Venerable One; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come when he considers it the proper time." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by a group of monks and preceded by the monastic community, approached the place where the meal of those thousand thieves was prepared. Then those thousand thieves washed the feet of the monastic community headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with sandalwood-scented water. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, his hands and feet washed, sat on a prepared seat before the monastic community. Having understood that the monastic community headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was seated, they served and satisfied them with their own hands with pure and excellent hard and soft foods. Having understood that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten, that his hands were washed and his bowl set aside, they took lower seats and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having understood their dispositions and latent tendencies, knowing their natures and characters, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, hearing it, those thousand thieves, seated on those very seats, having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of a personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truths, they said: "This, Venerable One, was not done for us by our mothers, nor by our fathers, nor by kings, nor by deities, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, nor by loved ones, nor by the group of kinsmen and relatives -- that which was accomplished by us through coming to the <s>Bhagavān</s> as our virtuous friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). Our feet have been pulled out from the hells, animal realms, and hungry ghost realms; we have been established among gods and humans; <s>saṃsāra</s> has been brought to its end; the oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the seas of tears have been crossed; the mountains of bones have been surmounted. May we, Venerable One, obtain ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full ordination (<s>upasampadā</s>), and the state of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May we practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said in a voice like <s>Brahmā</s>'s: "Come, dear ones, practice the holy life." At the conclusion of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, they became tonsured, free from passion toward the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, their minds as equal as the sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the eggshell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained knowledge, supernatural powers, and analytical insights, turned away from worldly gain, profit, and honor. They became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

body.text:
062.001. <62>bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh -- paśya bhadanta bhagavatā idaṃ caurasahasraṃ saptavāraṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā atyantaniṣṭhe 'nuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitam/
062.003. bhagavānāha -- na bhikṣava etarhi, yathā atīte 'pyadhvani mayā asyaiva caurasahasrasya sakāśādanekabhāṇḍasahasraḥ sārtho niṣkrītaḥ, na ca śakitāḥ saṃtarpayitum/
062.004. tato mayā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairdevamanuṣyaduṣprāpyāṃ śakrabrahmādyairapi duradhigamāṃ badaradvīpayātrāṃ varṣaśatena sādhayitvā etadeva caurasahasramārabhya kṛtsno jāmbudvīpaḥ suvarṇarajatavaiḍūryasphaṭikādyai ratnaviśeṣairmanorathepsitaiścopakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ saṃtarpayitvā daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ karmapathaiḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
062.007. tacchruṇuta -- bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminneva jambudvīpe vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati sma ṛddhaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskaradurbhikṣarogāpagatam/
062.010. priyamivaikaputrakamiva rājyaṃ kārayati/
062.010. tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ priyaseno nāma sārthavāhaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
062.012. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
062.012. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍate ramate paricārayati/
062.013. atha anyatama udārapuṇyamaheśākhyaḥ sattvo 'nyatamasmāt praṇītāddevanikāyāccayutvā tasyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ/
062.014. panñcāveṇīyā dharmā ihaikatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme/
062.015. katame panñca? raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti, kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti, garbhamavakrāntaṃ jānāti, yasyāḥ sakāśādgarbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti, dārakaṃ jānāti dārikāṃ jānāti/
062.017. saceddārako bhavati, dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati/
062.017. saceddārikā bhavati, vāmaṃ kukṣiṃniśritya tiṣṭhati/
062.018. sā āttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati -- diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhasva, āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā/
062.019. yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati, niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyati/
062.020. so 'pyāttamanāttamanā udānamudānayati -- apyevāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam/
062.021. jāto me syānnāvajātaḥ/
062.021. kṛtyāni me kuryāt/
062.021. bhṛtaḥ pratibharet/
062.021. dāyādyaṃ pratipadyeta/
062.022. kulavaṃśo me ciraṣṭhitikaḥ syāt/
062.022. asmākaṃ cāpyatītakālagatānāmuddiśya dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādiśet -- idaṃ tayoryatratatropapannayorgacchatoranugacchatviti/
062.024. āpannasattvāṃ caināṃ viditvā upariprāsādatalagatāmayantritāṃ dhārayati -- uṣṇa uṣṇopakaraṇaiḥ śīte śītopakaraṇairvaidyaprajñnaptairāhārair nātiśītair nātyuṣṇair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyaistiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitairāhāraiḥ/
062.026. hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīmapsarasamiva nandanavanacāriṇīṃ manñcānmanñcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭhamanavatarantīmadharimāṃ bhūmim/
062.027. na cāsyākiṃcidamanojñnaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya/
062.028. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
062.029. dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāso dṛḍhakaṭhinaśarīro mahānagnabalaḥ/
062.031. tasya jñnātayaḥ saṃgamya samāgamya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatirātriṃdivasāni tasya jātasya jāto mahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti -- kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma? ayaṃ dārakaḥ priyasenasya <63>sarthavāhasya putraḥ/
body.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "Behold, Venerable One, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has satisfied these thousand thieves seven times with wealth and established them in the ultimate, unsurpassed <s>yogakṣema</s> (security from bondage), <s>nirvāṇa</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Not only now, O monks. In a past era too, I ransomed a caravan of many thousands of goods from these very thousand thieves, but was not able to satisfy them. Then, through hundreds of thousands of difficult austerities, having accomplished the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> (Jujube Island) -- which is difficult for gods and humans to reach and hard even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others to attain -- over a hundred years, beginning with these very thousand thieves, I satisfied the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with special jewels such as gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), crystal, and other desired and wished-for provisions, and established them in the ten wholesome courses of action. Listen to this: Once upon a time, O monks, in a past era, in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, and free from strife, quarrels, disturbances, tumults, thieves, famine, and disease. He ruled the kingdom as if it were his beloved only son. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a caravan-leader named <s>Priyasena</s> dwelt, who was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He enjoyed himself with her, delighted, and attended to her. Then a certain being of great and noble merit, having fallen from a certain exalted divine assembly, descended into the womb of his wife. There are five distinctive characteristics in a certain wise woman of noble birth. What five? She knows a passionate man; she knows the time; she knows the season; she knows when conception has occurred; she knows from whom the conception has come; she knows whether it is a boy or a girl. If it is a boy, it rests against the right side of the womb. If it is a girl, it rests against the left side. She, delighted, informed her husband: "Rejoice, noble husband! I have become pregnant. And since it rests against my right side, it will certainly be a boy." He too, overjoyed, uttered an exclamation of joy: "May I indeed see the face of a son long desired! May a son be born to me, not a stillborn child. May he perform my duties. When nourished, may he provide for me. May he receive the inheritance. May our family lineage endure for a long time. And when we have passed away, may he give gifts and make merit on our behalf, dedicating the merit by name: 'May this reach those two, wherever they have been reborn.'" Knowing her to be pregnant, he kept her on the upper terrace of the palace, carefully attended -- in heat with warm provisions, in cold with cool provisions, with foods prescribed by physicians, neither too cold nor too hot, neither too bitter nor too sour, neither too salty nor too sweet, neither too pungent nor too astringent, avoiding bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent foods, her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> garden, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the ground below. And she heard no unpleasant sounds, all for the sake of the maturation of the embryo. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born -- handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair-skinned, golden-complexioned, with a parasol-shaped head, long arms, broad forehead, joined eyebrows, prominent nose, firm and strong body, with the strength of a great <s>nāga</s>. His relatives, gathering and assembling, for three times seven -- twenty-one nights and days -- having celebrated the birth festival of the newborn, established a name: "What shall be the boy's name? This boy is the son of the caravan-leader <s>Priyasena</s>."

body.text:
063.001. tadbhavatu dārakasya nāma supriya iti/
063.001. supriyo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhya upanyasto dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāmaṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām/
063.003. so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhurunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiṣcottaptottapairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
063.004. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam//
body.translated_text: "Therefore let the boy's name be <s>Supriya</s>." The boy <s>Supriya</s> was entrusted to eight nurses -- two milk-nurses, two body-nurses, two cleaning-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, clarified butter, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

body.text:
063.005. yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ/
063.005. saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse
063.006. nikṣepe hastiparīkṣāyāmaśvaparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ vastraparīkṣāyāṃ puruṣaparīkṣāyāṃ strīparīkṣāyām/
063.007. nānāpaṇyaparīkṣāsu paryavadātaḥ sarvaśāstrajñnaḥ saravakalābhijñnaḥ sarvaśilpajñnaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñnaḥ sarvagatigatijñnah uddhaṭṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ paramatīkṣṇaniśitabuddhiḥ saṃvṛtto 'gnikalpa iva jñnānena/
063.009. sa yāni tāni rājñnāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhnābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryasthāmavīryamanuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamabhinirjityādhyāvasatāṃ pṛthagbhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni, tadyathā hastigrīvāyām aśvapṛṣṭhe rathe tsarudhanuḥṣu upayāne niryāṇe 'ṅkuśagrahe tomaragrahe chedye bhedye muṣṭibandhe padabandhe dūravedhe śabdavedhe'kṣuṇṇavedhe marmavedhe dṛḍHaprahāritāyām/
063.013. panñcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ/
063.013. dharmatā caiṣā -- na tāvat putrasya nāma nirgacchati yāvat pitā dhriyate/
063.014. athāpareṇa samayena priyasenaḥ sārthavāho glānībhūtaḥ/
063.014. sa mūlagaṇḍaputrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva/
063.016. sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ/
063.017. samyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam//4//
body.translated_text: When he had grown up, he was put to study writing, arithmetic, calculation, sealing, withdrawing deposits, keeping deposits, elephant-assessment, horse-assessment, gem-assessment, wood-assessment, cloth-assessment, man-assessment, and woman-assessment. He became accomplished in the examination of various wares, a knower of all <s>śāstras</s> (sciences), skilled in all arts, a knower of all crafts, understanding the cries of all creatures, knowing all paths and destinations -- he became sharp, eloquent, learned, skilled in conduct, of supremely keen and sharpened intellect, like fire in his knowledge. In those skills and crafts that belong to kings, <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors) anointed on the head, who have attained sovereignty, strength, and might over their territories, who have conquered and settled upon a great expanse of earth -- namely, on the elephant's neck, on horseback, in a chariot, with sword and bow, in advancing, in retreating, in wielding the goad, in wielding the lance, in cutting, in piercing, in fist-fighting, in foot-fighting, in long-distance shooting, in sound-targeted shooting, in unerring shooting, in vital-point shooting, in firm striking -- he became skilled in five areas. And this is the natural law: a son's name does not become widely known as long as his father lives. Then at a later time, the caravan-leader <s>Priyasena</s> fell ill. Though attended with medicines of roots, tubers, leaves, flowers, and fruits, he only declined further. All accumulations end in decay; all that rises high ends in a fall; all unions end in separation; and life ends in death.

body.text:
063.018. iti sa kāladharmeṇa samyuktaḥ/
063.018. kālagate priyasene sārthavāhe brahmadattena kāśirājñnā supriyo mahāsārthavāhatve 'bhiṣiktaḥ/
063.019. tena sārthavāhabhūtena iyamevamrūpā mahāpratijñnā kṛtā -- sarvattvā mayā dhanena saṃtarpayitavyāḥ/
063.020. alpaṃ ca deyaṃ bahavaśca yācakāḥ/
063.020. tato 'lpairahobhistaddhanaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam/
063.021. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati -- alpaṃ ca deyaṃ bahavaśca yācakāḥ/
063.022. tato 'lpairahobhistaddhanaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam/
063.022. yannvahaṃ sāmudram yānapātraṃ samudānīya mahāsamudramavatareyaṃ dhanahārikaḥ/
063.023. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sāmudrayānapātraṃ samudānīya pañcamātrairvaṇikśataiḥ sārdhaṃ mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
063.024. tato 'nupūrveṇa ratnadvīpaṃ gatvā ratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā svastikṣemābhyāṃ mahāsamudrāduttīrya sthalajairvahitrairbhāṇḍamāropya vārāṇasyabhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
063.026. aṭavīkāntāramadhyagataścaurasahasreṇāsāditaḥ/
063.026. tataste caurā muṣitukāmāḥ sarvajavena prasṛtāḥ/
063.027. supriyeṇa ca sarvāhenāvalokyābhihitāh -- kimetadbhavantaḥ samārabdham? caurāḥ kathayanti -- sārthavāha, tvamekaḥ svastikṣemābhyāṃ gaccha, avaśiṣṭaṃ sārthaṃ bhuṣiṣyāmaḥ/
063.028. sārthavāhaḥ kathayati mamaiṣa bhavantaḥ sārthaḥ saṃniśritaḥ/
063.029. nārhanti bhavanto muṣitum | evamuktāścaurāḥ kathayanti -- vayaṃ smaḥ sārthavāhacaurā aṭavīcarāḥ/
063.030. nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyā na gaurakṣyam/
063.030. anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ/
063.031. teṣāṃ supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- sārthasya mūlyaṃ bhavanto gaṇyatām/
063.032. ahameṣāmarthe mūlyaṃ dāsyāmīti/
063.032. tataste vaṇijaḥ parasparaṃ mūlyaṃ gaṇayitvā caurāṇāṃ nivedayanti<64> -- iyanti śatāni sahasrāṇi ceti/
body.translated_text: Thus he was joined with the law of time [i.e., he died]. When the caravan-leader <s>Priyasena</s> had passed away, <s>Supriyo</s> was anointed as chief caravan-leader by <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king of <s>Kāśī</s>. Having become the caravan-leader, he made this great vow: "All beings must be satisfied by me with wealth." But the gifts were few and the beggars were many, so within a few days that wealth was exhausted and depleted. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> reflected: "The gifts are few and the beggars are many; within a few days that wealth has been exhausted and depleted. Let me procure an ocean-going vessel and venture upon the great ocean to bring back wealth." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having procured an ocean-going vessel, ventured upon the great ocean together with about five hundred merchants. Having gradually reached the Jewel Island and gathered gems, he safely crossed back over the great ocean, loaded the merchandise onto land vehicles, and set out toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. While passing through the midst of a forest wilderness, he was beset by a thousand robbers. Those robbers, wishing to plunder, rushed forward with full speed. <s>Supriyo</s>, looking all around, addressed them: "Sirs, what is this that you have undertaken?" The robbers replied: "Caravan-leader, you alone may go safely; we shall enjoy the rest of the caravan." The caravan-leader said: "Sirs, this caravan has taken refuge with me. You should not rob them." Thus addressed, the robbers replied: "We are forest-roaming caravan-robbers. We have neither farming, nor trade, nor cattle-herding. By this we make our livelihood." The caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> said to them: "Sirs, let the value of the caravan be calculated. I shall give the price on their behalf." Then those merchants, having calculated the price among themselves, reported to the robbers: "It is so many hundreds and thousands."

body.text:
064.001. tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena bhāṇḍaniṣkrayārthe svaṃ dravyamanupradattam/
064.002. caurasakāśāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ/
064.002. evaṃ dvistriścatuḥpanñcaṣaḍvārāṃs tasyaiva caurasahasrasya sakāśāt supriyeṇa sārthavāhena sārthaḥ paritrāto mūlyaṃ cānupradattam/
064.003. yāvat saptaṃ tu vāraṃ supriyaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
064.004. tataḥ saṃsiddhayānapātro 'bhyāgato 'ṭavīkāntāramadhyagatastenaiva caurasahasreṇāsāditaḥ/
064.005. tataste caurā muṣitukāmāḥ sarvajavena prasṛtāḥ/
064.006. supriyeṇa ca sārthavāhenāvalokyābhihitāh -- supriyo 'haṃ bhavantaḥ sārthavāhaḥ/
064.006. caurāḥ kathayanti -- jānāsyeva mahāsārthavāha vayaṃ caurā aṭavīcarāḥ/
064.007. nāsmākaṃ kṛṣir na vāṇijyaṃ na gaurakṣyam/
064.008. anena vayaṃ jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ/
064.008. tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena pūrvikāṃ pratijñnāmanusmṛtya dṛḍhapratijñnena tasya caurasahasrasya bhāṇḍamanupradattam/
064.009. supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati -- ime caurā labdhaṃ labdhamarthajātasaṃnicayaṃ kurvanti/
064.010. mayā ca mahatī pratijñnā kṛtā sarvasattvā dhanena mayā saṃtarpayitavyā iti/
064.011. so 'hamimaṃ caurasahasraṃ na śaknomi dhanena saṃtarpayitum/
064.011. kathaṃ punaḥ sarvasattvān dhanena saṃtarpayiṣyāmīti cintāparo middhamavakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> gave his own property as ransom for the merchandise. The caravan was rescued from the robbers. Thus, two, three, four, five, and six times, the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> rescued the caravan from that same band of a thousand robbers and gave the ransom price. Then, for the seventh time, the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> ventured upon the great ocean. Having returned with a successful voyage, while passing through the forest wilderness, he was again beset by that same band of a thousand robbers. Those robbers, wishing to plunder, rushed forward with full speed. The caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, looking around, addressed them: "Sirs, I am the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>." The robbers replied: "We know well, great caravan-leader — we are forest-roaming robbers. We have neither farming, nor trade, nor cattle-herding. By this we make our livelihood." Then the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, remembering his former vow, being firm in his resolve, gave the merchandise to that band of a thousand robbers. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> reflected: "These robbers hoard whatever wealth they obtain. And I have made a great vow: all beings must be satisfied by me with wealth. I am unable to satisfy even this band of a thousand robbers with wealth. How then shall I satisfy all beings with wealth?" Consumed by anxiety, he fell asleep.

body.text:
064.013. atha tasya mahātmana udārapuṇyamaheśākhyasyodāracetasopapannasya sarvasattvamanorathaparipūrakasya lokahitārthamabhyudgatasya anyatarā maheśākhyā devatā upasaṃkramya samāśvāsayati -- mā tvaṃ sārthavāha khedamāpadyasva/
064.015. ṛddhiṣyati te praṇidhiriti/
064.015. asti khalu mahāsārthavāha asminneva jambudvīpe badaradvīpo nāma mahāpattano 'manuṣyāvacarito maheśākhyamanuṣyādhiṣṭhitaḥ/
064.016. santi tasmin badaradvīpe pradhānāni ratnāni sarvasattvavicitramanorathaparipūrakāṇi/
064.017. yadi mahāsārthavāho badaradvīpayātrāṃ sādhayet, evamimāṃ mahatīṃ pratijñnāṃ pratinistareta/
064.018. iyaṃ hi mahāpratijñnā śakrabrahmādīnāmapi dustarā, prageva manuṣyabhūtasya/
064.019. ityuktavā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā/
064.019. na ca śakitā supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena sā devatā praṣṭum -- katarasyāṃ diśi badaradvīipaḥ kathaṃ vā tatra gamyata iti/
064.021. atha supriyasya sātrthavāhasya suptapratibuddhasya etadabhavat -- aho bata me sā devatā punarapi darśayet, diśaṃ copāyaṃ ca vyapadiśed badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyeti cintāparo middhamavakrāntaḥ/
064.023. atha sā devatā tasya mahātmana udārapuṇyamaheśākhyasya dṛḍhodārapratijñnasyodāravīryaparākramanāmanikṣiptotsāhatāṃ viditvā upasaṃkramya evamāha -- mā tvaṃ sārthavāha khedamāpadyasva/
064.025. asti khalu mahāsārthavāha paścime digbhāge panñcāntaradvīpaśatāni samatikramya sapta mahāparvatāḥ, uccaiśca pragṛhītāśca sapta ca mahānadyaḥ/
064.026. tān vīryabalena laṅghayitvā antaroddānamanulomapratilomadvayamāvartaḥ śaṅkhanābhaḥ śaṅkhanābhī ca nīlodastārakākṣaśca parvatau nīlagrīva eva ca vairambhā tāmrāṭavī vemṇugulmaḥ sapta parvatāḥ sakaṇṭakāḥ kṣāranadī triśaṅkuh ayaskilamaṣṭādaśavakro nadīślakṣṇa eva ca dhūmanetramudakaṃ saptaśīviṣaparvatā nadī bhavati paścimā/
064.029. anulomo pratilomo nāma mahāsamudraḥ/
064.030. anulomapratilome mahāsamudre manuṣyānavacarite anulomapratilomā vāyavo vānti/
064.031. tatra yo 'sau puruṣo bhavati maheśākhyo maheśākhyadevatāparigṛhītaḥ, sa mahatā puṇyabalena vīryabalena cittabalena mahāntaṃ plavamāsthāya anulomapratilomamahāsamudramavatarati<65>/
body.translated_text: Then, a certain great deity named <s>Maheśākhyā</s> approached that great soul, renowned for his magnificent merit, endowed with a noble mind, fulfiller of the wishes of all beings, who had arisen for the welfare of the world, and consoled him: "Do not despair, caravan-leader! Your aspiration will be fulfilled. There is indeed, O great caravan-leader, in this very <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a great port called <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, uninhabited by humans, presided over by a great deity named <s>Maheśākhya</s>. In that <s>Badaradvīpa</s> there are excellent gems that fulfill the various wishes of all beings. If the great caravan-leader were to undertake the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, he could fulfill this great vow. For this great vow is difficult even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others, let alone a mere human." Having said this, that deity vanished on the spot. And the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> was unable to ask that deity: "In which direction is <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, and how does one get there?" Then, upon waking, the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> thought: "If only that deity would appear to me again and point out the direction and the means for reaching the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>!" Consumed by this thought, he fell asleep again. Then that deity, knowing the firm and noble resolve, the exalted vigor and courage, and the sustained enthusiasm of that great soul renowned for his magnificent merit, approached and said: "Do not despair, caravan-leader! There is indeed, O great caravan-leader, in the western direction, beyond five hundred intervening islands, seven great mountains, lofty and towering, and seven great rivers. Having crossed them by the power of vigor, [one encounters] an intermediate garden, the forward-and-reverse double whirlpool, <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s> and <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s>, the mountains <s>Nīloda</s> and <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, and <s>Nīlagrīva</s>, the <s>Vairambhā</s> [winds], the Copper Forest, the Bamboo Thicket, seven thorny mountains, an alkaline river, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, an iron-staked eighteen-bend [path], a smooth river, the Smoke-Eye Water, seven serpent mountains, and the last river. The forward-and-reverse great ocean [lies beyond]. In that great ocean, uninhabited by humans, forward-and-reverse winds blow. There, the man who is called <s>Maheśākhya</s>, supported by a deity named <s>Maheśākhya</s>, by the power of great merit, vigor, and mental strength, mounts a great raft and enters the forward-and-reverse great ocean.

body.text:
065.001. sa yanmāsena gacchati, tadekena divasena pratyāhriyate/
065.001. evaṃ dvis triḥ/
065.001. hriyamāṇaśca pratyāhriyamāṇaśca yadi madhyamāmudakadhārāṃ pratipadyate, evamasau maitrībalaparigṛhīto lokahitārthamabhyudgamyottarati, nistarati, abhiniṣkramati/
065.003. anulomapratilomaṃ mahāsamudraṃ samatikramya anulomapratilomo nāma parvataḥ/
065.004. anulomapratilome mahāparvate 'manuṣyāvacarite 'nulomapratilomā nāma vāyavo vānti, yaiḥ puruṣastimirīkṛtanetro naṣṭasaṃjñnaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate/
065.005. sa vīryabalenātmānaṃ saṃdhārya tasmādeva mahāparvatādamoghāṃ nāmauṣadhīṃ samanviṣya gṛhītvā netre anñjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya anulomapratilomaṃ nāma mahāparvatamabhiniṣkramitavyam/
065.007. sacedetaṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhate, nāsya saṃmoho bhavati, svastikṣemeṇātikramatyanulomapratilomaṃ mahāparvatam/
065.008. sacedevaṃ vidhiṃ vā nānutiṣṭhati auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate, labdhvā vā na gṛhṇāti, sa ṣaṇmāsān muhyati, unmādamapi prāpnoti, ucchritya vā kālaṃ karoti/
065.010. anulomapratilomaṃ mahāparvataṃ samatikramya āvarto nāma mahāsamudraḥ/
065.011. tatra vairambhakā vāyavo vānti yaistadudakaṃ bhrāmyate/
065.011. tatra yo 'sau puruṣo bhavatyudārapuṇyavipākamaheśākhyo devatāparigṛhītaḥ, sa mahatā puṇyabalena vīryabalena cittabalena kāyabalena mahāntaṃ plavamāsthāya āvartaṃ mahāsamudramavarati/
065.013. sa ekasminnāvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate/
065.014. yojanaṃ gatvā dvitīye āvarte unmajjate/
065.015. sa tasminnapyāvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate/
065.015. evaṃ dvitīye tṛtīye caturthe panñcame ṣaṣṭhe āvarte saptakṛtvo bhrāmayitvā nirudhyate, yojanaṃ gatvā unmajjate/
065.016. evamasau maitrībalaparigṛhīto lokahitārthamabhyudgata uttarati nistaratyabhiniṣkrāmati/
065.017. āvartaṃ mahāsamudramabhiniṣkramya āvarto nāma parvato 'manuṣyāvacaritaḥ/
065.018. tatra śaṅkho nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharo mahābalo mahākāyaḥ/
065.019. tasyopariṣṭādyojanamātre śaṅkhanābhī nāmauṣadhī divā dhūmāyate rātrau prajvalati/
065.020. sā nāgaparigṛhītā tiṣṭhati/
065.020. sa khalu nāgo divā svapiti rātrau carati/
065.020. tatra tena puruṣeṇa divā sukhasuptasya nāgasya ātmānaṃ samanurakṣatā nāgaśarīramaviheṭhayatā auṣadhibalena mantrabalena puṇyabalena śaṅkhanābhī auṣadhī grahītavyā/
065.022. gṛhītvā netre anñjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya āvartaḥ parvato 'dhiroḍhavyaḥ/
065.023. sacedetāṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhati, svastikṣemeṇātikrāmati āvartaṃ parvatamaviheṭhitaḥ śaṅkhanābhena rākṣasena/
065.024. sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati, auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate, labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti, tamenaṃ śaṅkhanābho rākṣasaḥ panñcatvamāpādayati/
065.025. āvartaṃ parvatamatikramya nīlodo nāma mahāsamudraḥ/
065.026. gambhīro 'yaṃ gambhīrāvabhāsaḥ/
065.026. nīlode mahāsamudre tārākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raktanetraḥ pradīptaśiroruho vikṛtacaraṇadaśananayanaḥ parvatāyatakukṣiḥ/
065.027. sacet svapiti, vivṛtānyasya netrāṇi bhavanti, tadyathā acirodito bhāskaraḥ/
065.028. audārikāścāsya āśvāsapraśvāsā gurugurukāḥ pravartante yathā meghasya garjato 'śanyāṃ ca sphūrjatyāṃ śabdaḥ/
065.030. yadā jāgarti, nimīlitānyasya bhavanti netrāṇi/
065.030. tatra tena puruṣeṇa tasmādeva samudrakūlānmahāmakarināmauṣadhīṃ samanviṣya gṛhya netre anñjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya mahānataṃ plavamāsthāya suptaṃ tārākṣaṃ dakarākṣasaṃ viditvā pūrvabuddhabhāṣitāmeraṇḍāṃ nāma mahāvidyāmuccārayatā <66>mantrapadāṃ dakarākṣasasamīpena gantavyam
body.translated_text:
065.001. What he traverses in a month, he is carried back in a single day.
065.001. Thus twice, thrice.
065.001. Being carried forward and pulled back, if he reaches the middle current of water, then this man, sustained by the power of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), having risen up for the welfare of the world, crosses over, gets through, and emerges.
065.003. Having crossed the <s>Anulomapratilomasamudra</s> (Forward-Backward Ocean), there is a mountain called <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s> (Forward-Backward).
065.004. On the great mountain <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s>, uninhabited by humans, winds called <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s> blow, by which a man's eyes become blinded with darkness and he stands having lost consciousness.
065.005. Sustaining himself by the force of his energy, he must search for and obtain from that very great mountain the herb called <s>Amoghā</s> (Unfailing), anoint his eyes, bind it to his head, touch it [to his body], and then traverse the great mountain <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s>.
065.007. If he follows this procedure, he will not be bewildered, and he crosses the great mountain <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s> safely and securely.
065.008. If he does not follow this procedure, or does not obtain the herb, or having obtained it does not take it, he is bewildered for six months, may even go mad, or dies outright.
065.010. Having crossed the great mountain <s>Anulomapratilomaḥ</s>, there is a great ocean called <s>Āvarta</s> (Whirlpool).
065.011. There the <s>Vairambhaka</s> winds blow, by which the water is whirled about.
065.011. There, that man who is called 'Great Lord of Noble Merit-Fruit,' sustained by the deities, by the great power of merit, energy, mind, and body, mounting a great raft, enters the <s>Āvarta</s> ocean.
065.013. In one whirlpool he is spun around seven times and submerged.
065.014. Having gone one <s>yojana</s>, he surfaces in the second whirlpool.
065.015. In that whirlpool too he is spun around seven times and submerged.
065.015. Thus in the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth whirlpools he is spun around seven times and submerged, and having gone one <s>yojana</s>, he surfaces.
065.016. Thus this man, sustained by the power of loving-kindness, having risen up for the welfare of the world, crosses over, gets through, and emerges.
065.017. Having emerged from the <s>Āvarta</s> ocean, there is a mountain called <s>Āvarta</s>, uninhabited by humans.
065.018. There dwells a <s>Rākṣasa</s> named <s>Śaṅkha</s> — fierce, a slayer of others, of great strength and great body.
065.019. Above it, at a distance of one <s>yojana</s>, there is an herb called <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s> (Conch-Navel) which smokes by day and glows by night.
065.020. It stands under the protection of a <s>Nāga</s>.
065.020. That <s>Nāga</s> sleeps by day and roams by night.
065.020. There, that man, while the <s>Nāga</s> is happily sleeping by day, protecting himself and not harming the <s>Nāga</s>'s body, must seize the herb <s>Śaṅkhanābhī</s> by the power of herbs, the power of mantras, and the power of merit.
065.022. Having seized it, he should anoint his eyes, bind it to his head, touch it [to his body], and ascend the mountain <s>Āvarta</s>.
065.023. If he follows this procedure, he crosses the mountain <s>Āvarta</s> safely and securely, unharmed by the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s>.
065.024. If he does not follow this procedure, or does not obtain the herb, or having obtained it does not take it, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Śaṅkhanābha</s> puts him to death.
065.025. Having crossed the mountain <s>Āvarta</s>, there is a great ocean called <s>Nīloda</s> (Blue-Water).
065.026. It is deep, with a deep appearance.
065.026. In the great ocean <s>Nīloda</s> dwells a <s>Rākṣasa</s> named <s>Tārākṣa</s> (Star-Eyed) — red-eyed, with blazing hair, with deformed feet, teeth, and eyes, with a belly as vast as a mountain.
065.027. When he sleeps, his eyes are open, like the newly risen sun.
065.028. His inhalations and exhalations are heavy and powerful, like the sound of a thundering cloud when lightning strikes.
065.030. When he is awake, his eyes are closed.
065.030. There, that man must search for and obtain the great herb called <s>Mahāmakarī</s> from the shore of that very ocean, anoint his eyes, bind it to his head, touch it [to his body], and mounting a great raft, knowing that the water-<s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Tārākṣa</s> is asleep, reciting the great <s>vidyā</s> (spell) called <s>Eraṇḍā</s>, previously spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>, must pass by the water-<s>Rākṣasa</s> while chanting the mantra-syllables.

body.text:
066.001. sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati, auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate, labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti, tamenaṃ tārākṣo dakarākṣasa ojaṃ vā ghaṭṭayati, cittaṃ vā kṣipati, sarveṇa vā sarvaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayati/
066.003. nīlodaṃ mahāsamudraṃ samatikramya nīlodo nāma mahāparvataḥ/
066.003. tatra nīlagrīvo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati panñcaśataparivāra ugratejā raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ/
066.004. nīlodo mahāparvata ekanīlo 'khaṇḍo 'cchidro 'suṣiraḥ saṃvṛta ekaghanaḥ/
066.005. apīdānīmanimiṣaṃ paśyato netrāṇi vyābādhayate, mūrcchāṃ ca saṃjanayati/
066.006. tasyopariṣṭādyojanamātre 'moghā nāmauṣadhī vicitrarūpā/
066.007. sā nāgaparigṛhītā tiṣṭhati/
066.007. sa khalu nāgo dṛṣṭiviṣo 'pi śvāsaviṣo 'pi sparśaviṣo 'pi daṃṣṭrāviṣo 'pi/
066.008. yadā svapiti, tadā dhūmāyate/
066.008. yaḥ khalu tena dhūmena mṛgo vā pakṣī vā spṛśyate, sa panñcatvamāpadyate/
066.009. tatra tena puruṣeṇa śiraḥsnātenopoṣitena maitrāyatā karuṇāyatā avyāpannena cittenātmānaṃ samanurakṣatā nāgaśarīramaviheṭhayatā auṣadhī grahītavyā/
066.010. netre anñjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya anena vidhinā jānatānuṣṭhitena nīlodaḥ parvato 'bhiroḍhavyaḥ/
066.011. timiraṃ na bhaviṣyati, mūrcchā ca na bhaviṣyati/
066.012. na cāsya guhyakāḥ śarīre prahariṣyanti/
066.012. sacedetāṃ vidhiṃ nānutiṣṭhati, auṣadhīṃ vā na labhate, labdhāṃ vā na gṛhṇāti, tamenaṃ nīlagrīvo rākṣasaḥ panñcatvamāpādayiṣyati/
066.014. nīlodaṃ parvataṃ samatikramya vairambho nāma mahāsamudraḥ/
066.014. vairambhe mahāsamudre vairambhā nāma vāyavo vānti yaistadudakaṃ kṣobhyate, yatrāgatirmakarakacchapavallakaśiśumārādīnāṃ pretapiśācakumbhāṇḍakaṭapūtanādīnāṃ kaḥ punarvādo manuṣyāṇām/
066.016. tamutsṛjya uttareṇa vairambhasya mahāsamudrasya mahatī tāmrāṭavī anekayojanāyāmavistārā/
066.017. tasyāstāmrāṭavyā madhye mahat sālavanaṃ mahaccodapānam/
066.018. tatra tāmrākṣo nāma ajagaraḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ paramadurgandhaḥ panñcayojanāyāmaḥ/
066.019. sa ṣaṇmāsān svapiti/
066.019. yadā svapiti, tadā asya yojanaṃ sāmantakena lālāsya spharitvā/
066.020. tiṣṭhati, yadā jāgarti, alpāsya lālā bhavati/
066.020. tasyopariṣṭānmahān veṇugulmaḥ/
066.021. tasmin veṇugulme mahatyaśmaśilā/
066.021. tāṃ viryabalena utpāṭya guhā/
066.021. tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ saṃmohanī nāmauṣadhī/
066.022. sā rātriṃdivasaṃ prajvalati/
066.022. tāṃ gṛhītvā netre anñjayitvā śirasi baddhvā samālabhya suptaṃ tāmrākṣamajagaraṃ viditvā auṣadhībalena mantrabalena vā ajagarabhavanasamīpena gantavyam/
066.024. sacedetāṃ vidhimanutiṣṭhati, svastikṣemābhyāmatikramya aviheṭhitastāmrākṣeṇājagareṇa tataḥ paścānmūlaphalāni bhakṣayatā gantavyam/
066.025. mahatīṃ tāmrāṭavīmatikramya sapta parvatāḥ kaṇṭakaveṇupraticchannāḥ/
066.026. tatra tena puruṣeṇa tāmrapaṭṭaiḥ pādau baddhvā tān parvatān vīryabalena laṅghayitvā sapta kṣāranadyaḥ/
066.027. tāsāṃ tīre mahāśālmalīvanam/
066.027. tataḥ śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā abhiruhyātikramitavyā aspṛśatā pānīyam/
066.028. sacet spṛśet, tadaṅgaṃ śīryate/
066.028. sapta kṣāranadīḥ samatikramya triśaṅkur nāma parvataḥ/
066.029. triśaṅkau parvate triśaṅkavo nāma kaṇṭakāstīkṣṇāḥ sutīkṣṇāḥ/
066.030. tatastena puruṣeṇa tāmrapaṭṭairvetrapāśaiḥ pādau baddhvā atikaramitavyam/
066.030. triśaṅkuparvatamatikramya triśaṅkur nāma nadī/
066.031. triśaṅkavo nāma kaṇṭakāstīkṣṇā aṣṭādaśāṅgulā udake 'ntargatāstiṣṭhanti/
066.031. tatra tena puruṣeṇa śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā atikramitavyamaspṛśatā pānīyam/
066.032. sacet patati, <67>tatraivānayena vyasanamāpadyate/
body.translated_text:
066.001. If he does not follow this procedure, or does not obtain the herb, or having obtained it does not take it, the water-<s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Tārākṣa</s> either saps his vitality, drives him mad, or kills him outright.
066.003. Having crossed the great ocean <s>Nīloda</s>, there is a great mountain called <s>Nīloda</s>.
066.003. There dwells a <s>Rākṣasa</s> named <s>Nīlagrīva</s> (Blue-Throat), with a retinue of five hundred — of fierce power, fearsome, a slayer of others.
066.004. The great mountain <s>Nīloda</s> is entirely blue, unbroken, without cracks, without hollows, compact, a single mass.
066.005. Even gazing at it without blinking causes pain to the eyes and produces fainting.
066.006. Above it, at a distance of one <s>yojana</s>, there is an herb called <s>Amoghā</s> (Unfailing), of wondrous form.
066.007. It stands under the protection of a <s>Nāga</s>.
066.007. That <s>Nāga</s> is poisonous by sight, poisonous by breath, poisonous by touch, and poisonous by fang.
066.008. When it sleeps, it smokes.
066.008. Whatever deer or bird is touched by that smoke is killed.
066.009. There, that man, having bathed his head, having observed a fast, with a mind extended in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), with an unmalicious mind, protecting himself and not harming the <s>Nāga</s>'s body, must seize the herb.
066.010. Having anointed his eyes and bound it to his head and touched it [to his body], by this procedure, performed with knowledge, the mountain <s>Nīloda</s> must be ascended.
066.011. There will be no darkness, and there will be no fainting.
066.012. Nor will the <s>Guhyakas</s> (spirits) strike his body.
066.012. If he does not follow this procedure, or does not obtain the herb, or having obtained it does not take it, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Nīlagrīva</s> will put him to death.
066.014. Having crossed the mountain <s>Nīloda</s>, there is a great ocean called <s>Vairambha</s>.
066.014. In the great ocean <s>Vairambha</s>, the <s>Vairambha</s> winds blow, by which the water is agitated — a place inaccessible to sea-creatures, tortoises, crocodiles, and <s>Śiśumāras</s> (dolphins), to <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Kaṭapūtanas</s> — how much more so for humans.
066.016. Leaving that behind, to the north of the <s>Vairambha</s> ocean there is a great copper forest, many <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth.
066.017. In the middle of that copper forest there is a great <s>Śāla</s> grove and a great pond.
066.018. There dwells a python called <s>Tāmrākṣa</s> (Copper-Eyed) — fierce, a slayer of others, exceedingly foul-smelling, eighteen <s>yojanas</s> in length.
066.019. He sleeps for six months.
066.019. When he sleeps, his drool spreads for one <s>yojana</s> around.
066.020. When he is awake, his drool is scant.
066.020. Above him is a great bamboo thicket.
066.021. In that bamboo thicket is a great stone slab.
066.021. Uprooting it by the force of energy, [there is] a cave.
066.021. In that cave is an herb called <s>Saṃmohanī</s> (Bewildering).
066.022. It blazes day and night.
066.022. Having taken it, anointed the eyes, bound it to the head, and touched it [to the body], knowing the python <s>Tāmrākṣa</s> to be asleep, one must pass near the python's abode by the power of herbs or the power of mantras.
066.024. If he follows this procedure, he crosses safely and securely, unharmed by the python <s>Tāmrākṣa</s>; after that, he must proceed eating roots and fruits.
066.025. Having crossed the great copper forest, there are seven mountains covered with thorny bamboo.
066.026. There, that man, having bound his feet with copper plates, must leap over those mountains by the force of energy. [Beyond them are] seven alkaline rivers.
066.027. On their banks is a great <s>Śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton) forest.
066.027. From the planks of <s>Śālmalī</s> wood, he must fashion a raft, board it, and cross without touching the water.
066.028. If he touches it, that limb dissolves.
066.028. Having crossed the seven alkaline rivers, there is a mountain called <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
066.029. On Mount <s>Triśaṅku</s>, there are thorns called <s>Triśaṅku</s> — sharp, extremely sharp.
066.030. There, that man, having bound his feet with copper plates and cane ropes, must cross over.
066.030. Having crossed Mount <s>Triśaṅku</s>, there is a river called <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
066.031. The thorns called <s>Triśaṅku</s>, sharp, eighteen finger-breadths long, stand submerged in the water.
066.031. There, that man must fashion a raft from <s>Śālmalī</s> planks and cross without touching the water.
066.032. If he falls in, right there he meets with calamity and disaster.

body.text:
067.001. yathā triśaṅkuḥ parvataḥ, evaṃ triśaṅkukā nāma nadī/
067.001. evamayaskilaḥ parvato 'yaskilā nāma nadī/
067.002. ayaskilānadīmatikarmya aṣṭādaśavakro nāma parvataḥ/
067.003. ucchritaśca sarvataḥ saṃvṛto 'dvārakaśca/
067.003. asya na kiṃcit nistaraṇamanyatra vṛkṣāgrād vṛkṣamadhiruhya gantavyam/
067.004. aṣṭādaśavakraṃ parvatamatikramya aṣṭādaśavakrikā nāma nādī grāhamakarākulā saṃvṛtā ca/
067.005. tatra vetrapāśaṃ baddhvā atikramitavyam/
067.005. sacet patati, anayena vyasanamāpadyate/
067.006. aṣṭādaśavakrikāṃ nadīmatikramya ślakṣṇo nāma parvataḥ/
067.006. ślakṣṇaḥ parvato mṛdurucchrito 'dvārakaśca/
067.007. na cāsya kiṃcinnistaraṇam/
067.007. tatrāyaskīlānāṃ koṭyātikramitavyam/
067.007. ślakṣṇaṃ parvatamatikramya ślakṣṇā nāma nadī grāhamakarākulā/
067.008. saṃvṛtā ca sā nadī/
067.008. tatra vetrapāśān baddhvā atikaramitavyam/
067.009. sacet patati, anayena vyasanamāpadyate/
067.009. ślakṣṇāṃ nadīmatikramya dhūmanetro nāma parvato dhūmāyate saṃdhūmāyate/
067.010. yena khalu tena dhūmena mṛgā vā pakṣiṇo vā spṛśyante, panñcatvamāpadyante/
067.011. dhūmanetraḥ parvata ucchrito mahāprapāto 'dvārakaśca/
067.011. tatra tena puruṣeṇa guhā paryeṣitavyā/
067.012. guhāṃ samanviṣya tenātra guhādvāramauṣadhibalena mantrabalena ca moktavyam /
067.012. sā ca khalu guhā āśīviṣaparipūrṇā tiṣṭhati/
067.013. te khalu āśīviṣā dṛṣṭiviṣā api, sparśaviṣā api/
067.014. dhūmanetrasya parvatasyopariṣṭānmahadudakapalvalam/
067.014. tasminnudakapalvale mahatyaśmaśilā/
067.014. tāṃ vīryabalenaotpāṭya guhā/
067.015. tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ saṃjīvanī nāmauṣadhī jyotīrasaśca maṇirdīpaprabhāsaḥ/
067.016. tāmauṣadhīṃ gṛhītvā saśīrṣapādaṃ samālabhya tāṃ cauṣadhīṃ gṛhītvā guhā praveṣṭavyā/
067.016. auṣadhībalena mantrabalena auṣadhīprabhāvāccāśīviṣāḥ kāye na kramiṣyanti/
067.017. evaṃ hi tasmāt parvatānnistaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati/
067.018. dhūmanetraparvatamatikramya saptāśīviṣaparvatāḥ/
067.018. auṣadhībalena mantrabalena ca saptāśīviṣaparvatā atikramitavyāḥ/
067.019. saptāśīviṣaparvatānatikramya saptaśīviṣanadyaḥ/
067.019. tīkṣṇagandhā nāma tatrāśīviṣāḥ/
067.020. tatra tena puruṣeṇa māṃsapeśyanveṣitavyā/
067.020. tāsāmāśīviṣanadīnāṃ tīre śālmalīvanam/
067.021. tataḥ śālmalīphalakaiḥ plavaṃ baddhvā māṃsapeśyā ātmānamācchādya adhiroḍhavyam/
067.022. tatastā āśīviṣā māṃsagandhena pārāt pāraṃ gamiṣyanti/
067.022. saptāśīviṣamatikramya mahān sudhāvadātaḥ parvataḥ, uccaśca pragṛhītaśca/
067.023. so 'dhiroḍhavyas tatra drakṣyasi mahāntaṃ sauvarṇabhūmiṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ puṣpaphalacchāyāvṛkṣopaśobhitam/
067.024. rohitakāñ janapadān ṛddhāṃśca kṣemāṃśca subhikṣāṃśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṃśca/
067.025. rohitakaṃ ca mahānagaraṃ dvādaśayojanāyāmaṃ saptayojanavistṛtaṃ saptaprākāraparikṣiptaṃ dvāṣaṣṭidvāropaśobhitaṃ bhavanaśatasahasravirājitaṃ suviviktarathyāvīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇam/
067.027. vīṇā vallikā mahatī sughoṣakaiḥ śrotrābhirāmaiśca gītadhvanibhiranuparataprayogaṃ nānāpaṇyasaṃvṛddhaṃ nityapramuditajanaughasaṃkulaṃ tridaśendropendrasadṛśodyānasabhāpuṣkariṇīsampannaṃ kādambahaṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākopaśobhitataḍāgaṃ rohitakaṃ mahārājādhyuṣitaṃ mahāpuruṣavaṇignisevitam/
067.030. yatra maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ prativasati abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī dvīpāntaradvīpagamanavidhijñno mahāsamudrayānapātrayāyī<68>/
body.translated_text: Just as there is the <s>Triśaṅku</s> mountain, so there is a river named <s>Triśaṅkukā</s>. Likewise, as there is the <s>Ayaskila</s> mountain, so there is a river named <s>Ayaskilā</s>. After crossing the river <s>Ayaskilā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Aṣṭādaśavakra</s> (Eighteen Bends). It is lofty, enclosed on all sides, and without an entrance. There is no way to cross it except by climbing from treetop to treetop. After crossing the <s>Aṣṭādaśavakra</s> mountain, there is a river named <s>Aṣṭādaśavakrikā</s>, teeming with crocodiles and sea-monsters, and enclosed. It must be crossed by tying a cane rope. If one falls, one meets with calamity and disaster. After crossing the river <s>Aṣṭādaśavakrikā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Ślakṣṇa</s> (Smooth). The <s>Ślakṣṇa</s> mountain is smooth, lofty, and without an entrance. There is no way to cross it. It must be crossed using the tips of iron stakes. After crossing the <s>Ślakṣṇa</s> mountain, there is a river named <s>Ślakṣṇā</s>, teeming with crocodiles and sea-monsters. That river is enclosed. It must be crossed by tying cane ropes. If one falls, one meets with calamity and disaster. After crossing the river <s>Ślakṣṇā</s>, there is a mountain named <s>Dhūmanetra</s> (Smoke-Eye) which smokes and fumes. Whatever animals or birds are touched by that smoke, they perish. The <s>Dhūmanetra</s> mountain is lofty, with a great precipice, and without an entrance. There, the man must search for a cave. Having found the cave, the cave entrance must be opened by the power of herbs and the power of <s>mantras</s> (sacred incantations). That cave is filled with venomous serpents. Those serpents are poisonous both by sight and by touch. Above the <s>Dhūmanetra</s> mountain there is a great pool of water. In that pool there is a great stone slab. That must be uprooted by the force of strength, revealing a cave. In that cave there is an herb named <s>Saṃjīvanī</s> (Life-Restoring), and a gem called <s>Jyotīrasa</s> (Light-Essence), the lamp-radiant one. Having taken that herb and anointing oneself from head to foot, and taking that herb, one must enter the cave. By the power of the herb, the power of <s>mantras</s>, and the efficacy of the herb, the venomous serpents will not attack the body. Thus there will be passage from that mountain. After crossing the <s>Dhūmanetra</s> mountain, there are seven serpent mountains. By the power of herbs and <s>mantras</s>, the seven serpent mountains must be crossed. After crossing the seven serpent mountains, there are seven serpent rivers. There are serpents named <s>Tīkṣṇagandha</s> (Sharp-Scented). There, the man must obtain a piece of flesh. On the banks of those serpent rivers is a <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree) forest. Then, having made a raft from <s>śālmalī</s> planks and covering oneself with the piece of flesh, one must embark. Then those serpents, drawn by the scent of flesh, will carry one from shore to shore. After crossing the seven serpent rivers, there is a great mountain, white as plaster, lofty and towering. That must be ascended. There you will see a great golden land, a region of earth adorned with flowering and fruit-bearing shade trees, and the prosperous, peaceful, well-provisioned, and densely populated countryside of <s>Rohitaka</s>. And the great city of <s>Rohitaka</s>, twelve <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in length, seven <s>yojanas</s> in width, surrounded by seven ramparts, adorned with sixty-two gates, resplendent with hundreds of thousands of dwellings, with well-arranged streets, avenues, crossroads, and market-squares, filled with the sounds of <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), flutes, and great drums, with music pleasing to the ears in unceasing performance, flourishing with various merchandise, always bustling with joyful crowds, endowed with parks, assembly halls, and lotus-ponds like those of <s>Tridaśendra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, with ponds adorned by geese, swans, sheldrakes, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds -- <s>Rohitaka</s>, the residence of great kings, frequented by great merchant-men, where dwells <s>Magha</s> the caravan-leader, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, wise, discerning, intelligent, wealthy, of great riches, of great fortune, of vast and extensive possessions, with wealth rivaling that of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, one who knows the methods of traveling between islands and continents, a voyager upon the great ocean.

body.text:
068.001. sa te badaradvīpamahāpattanasya pravṛttimākhyāsyati, nimittāni, ca darśayiṣyati/
068.002. yathoktaṃ ca vidhimanuṣṭhāsyasi, na ca khedamāpatsyase/
068.002. evaṃ mahāsārthavāha paramaduṣkarakāraka imāṃ sumerumalayamandarasadṛśīṃ dṛḍhāṃ pratijñnāṃ nistariṣyasi/
068.003. iyaṃ ca mahāpratijñnā śakrabrahmādīnāmapi duṣkarā, prāgeva manuṣyabhūtānām//
body.translated_text: "He will tell you the details of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> and will show you the signs. And you will follow the prescribed method and will not meet with failure. Thus, O great caravan-leader, doer of the most difficult deeds, you will fulfill this firm vow, equal to <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, and <s>Mandara</s>. This great vow is difficult even for <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others, let alone for those who are mere humans."

body.text:
068.005. ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā/
068.005. atha supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ suptapratibuddho devatāvacanaṃ śrutvā paramavismayamāpannaścintayati -- nūnamanayā devatayā anekairevaṃvidhaiḥ paramaduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitapūrvā bhaviṣyati/
068.007. yadi tāvat sādhitā, duṣkarakārikā iyaṃ devatā/
068.008. atha sādhyamānā, dṛṣṭāḥ paramaduṣkarakārakāste manuṣyāḥ, yairanekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitā/
068.009. atiduṣkaraṃ caitadasmābhiḥ karaṇīyam/
068.009. athavā yadyapyahaṃ lokahitārthe pratipadyeyam, saphalo me pariśramaḥ syāt/
068.010. yathā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpamahāpattanayātrāṃ sadhayiṣyāmi, paraṃ lokānugrahaṃ kariṣyāmi/
068.011. te 'pi manuṣyāḥ, yairanekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpayātrā sādhitapūrvā/
068.012. ahamapi manuṣyaḥ/
068.012. taiḥ sādhitā/
068.012. kasmādahaṃ na sādhayiṣyāmītyanuvicintya supriyo mahāsārthavāho dṛḍhapratijñno dṛḍhavīryaparākramo 'nikṣiptotsāha udārapuṇyavipākamaheśākhyo/
068.014. lokahitārthamabhyudgato yathopadiṣṭoddeśasmṛtiparigṛhīto dṛḍhapratijñnāṃ samanusmṛtya mahatā vīryabalena ekākī advitīyavyavasāyo yathopadiṣṭāni panñcāntaradvīpaśatāni samatikrāmati/
068.016. sapta mahāparvatān, sapta mahānadyo vistareṇa sarvāṇi saṃkaṭāni yathoktena vidhinā mūlakandaphalāhāro guṇavati phalake baddhvā paripūrṇairdvādaśabhirvarṣai rohitakaṃ mahānagaramanuprāptaḥ/
068.018. udyāne sthitvā anyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate -- kaścidbhoḥ puruṣa asmin rohitake mahānagare magho nāma sārthavāhaḥ prarivasati? sa evamāha -- asti bhoḥ puruṣa/
068.019. kiṃ tarhi mahāvyādhinā grastaḥ/
068.020. sthānametadvidyate yattenaivābādhena kālaṃ kariṣyatīti/
068.020. atha supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasyaitadabhavat -- mā haiva magho mahāsārthavāho 'dṛṣṭa eva kālaṃ kuryāt/
068.021. ko me vyapadeśaṃ kariṣyati tasya badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyeti viditvā tvaritatvaritam yena maghasya sārthavāhasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
068.023. sa dvāre nivāryate, na labhate praveśaṃ mahāsārthavāhadarśanāya/
068.024. dharmatā khalu kuśalā bodhisattvāsteṣu teṣu śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu/
068.024. tato vaidyasaṃjñnāṃ ghoṣayitvā praviṣṭaḥ/
068.025. adrakṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāho 'riṣṭādhyāyeṣu viditavṛttāntah -- maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ ṣaḍbhirmāsaiḥ kālaṃ kariṣyatīti viditvā supriyo mahāsārtahvāho 'dhītya vaidyamatāni svayameva mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyānyānulomikāni vyapadiśati sma vyādhivyupaśamārtham/
068.028. paraṃ cainaṃ toṣayati citrākṣaravyanñjanapadābhidhānaiḥ, śāstrabaddhābhiḥ, kathābhiḥ, nānāśrutimanorathākhyāyikābhiḥ saṃranñjayati/
068.029. dākṣyadākṣiṇyacāturyamādhuryopetamupasthānakarmaṇi satputra iva pitaraṃ bhaktyā gauraveṇa śuśrūṣate/
068.030. tato maghasya sārthavāhasya kṣemaṇīyataraṃ cābhūdyāpanīyataraṃ ca/
068.031. saṃjñnā anena pratilabdhā/
068.031. atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ pratilabdhasaṃjñnaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat -- kuto bhavāñ jñnānavijñnānasampanno 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paṇḍito vyakto <69>medhāvī paṭupracāraḥ sarvaśāstrajñnaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ sarvakalābhijñnaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñna iṅgitajñna? kiṃ jātyā bhavān? kiṃgotrah? kena vā kāraṇena amanuṣyāvacaritaṃ deśamabhyāgatah? evamūktaḥ supriyaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha/
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that <s>devatā</s> (deity) disappeared right there. Then the caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, having awakened from sleep and hearing the deity's words, was filled with supreme wonder and thought: "Surely this deity must have previously accomplished the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many such supremely difficult hundreds of thousands of hardships. If she has accomplished it, this deity is a doer of difficult deeds. But if it was being accomplished by others, then those humans are seen to be doers of supremely difficult deeds, who accomplished the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many difficult hundreds of thousands of hardships. This is extremely difficult for us to accomplish. But then, if I were to undertake this for the benefit of the world, my effort would be fruitful. Just as I will accomplish the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many difficult hundreds of thousands of hardships, I will render supreme benefit to the world. Those humans too accomplished the journey to <s>Badaradvīpa</s> through many difficult hundreds of thousands of hardships. I too am a human. They accomplished it. Why should I not accomplish it?" Reflecting thus, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, of firm resolve, of firm heroic valor, with unflagging enthusiasm, renowned for the ripening of his noble merit, arose for the benefit of the world. Holding in memory the instructions as directed, recalling his firm resolve, by great strength and heroism, alone, with singular determination, he crossed the five hundred intermediate islands as instructed, the seven great mountains, the seven great rivers, and in full detail all the dangerous passages according to the prescribed method, subsisting on roots, bulbs, and fruits, binding himself to a sturdy plank, and after a full twelve years arrived at the great city of <s>Rohitaka</s>. Staying in a garden, he addressed a certain man: "Sir, does a caravan-leader named <s>Magha</s> dwell in this great city of <s>Rohitaka</s>?" He replied: "He does, sir. However, he is afflicted by a severe illness. It is possible that he will die from that very ailment." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> thought: "May the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> not die without my having seen him. Who will give me directions for the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>?" Knowing this, he hastened quickly to the dwelling of the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>. He was stopped at the gate and could not gain entry to see the great caravan-leader. It is a natural law that <s>bodhisattvas</s> are skilled in all arts and crafts. Then, having announced himself as a physician, he entered. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, versed in the treatises on fatal signs, saw and understood the situation: the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> would die within six months. Knowing this, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>, having studied medical treatises, himself prescribed roots, bulbs, leaves, flowers, fruits, and appropriate medicines for the alleviation of the illness. Furthermore, he delighted him with discourses adorned with elegant letters, words, and verses, bound in the form of treatises, and entertained him with various stories and tales pleasing to the ear. With skill, courtesy, cleverness, and sweetness in his attendant service, he tended him like a devoted son tending his father, with devotion and respect. Then the condition of the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> became more comfortable and more sustainable. He regained consciousness. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>, having regained consciousness, said to the great caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>: "Where are you from, endowed with such knowledge and wisdom, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, wise, discerning, intelligent, of keen conduct, knowledgeable in all treatises, skilled in all sciences, proficient in all arts, understanding the speech of all beings, understanding gestures? Of what birth are you? Of what lineage? And for what reason have you come to this region uninhabited by humans?" Thus addressed, the caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s> replied: "Excellent, excellent, great caravan-leader."

body.text:
069.003. kāle 'smi mahāsarthavāhena jātikulagotrāgamanaprayojanaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ/
069.004. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghāya sārthavāhāya jātikulagotrāgamanaprayojanaṃ vistareṇārocayati sma, paraṃ cainaṃ vijñnāpayati -- sārvāhānubhāvādahaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ paśyeyam/
069.006. evamahaṃ syāt paripūrṇamanoratho nistīrṇadṛḍhapratijñnaḥ sarvasattvamanorathaparipūrakaḥ/
069.007. atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasyāśrutapūrvāṃ parahitārthamabhyudyatāṃ dṛḍhapratijñnāṃ śrutvā paramavismayajāto 'nimiṣadṛṣṭiḥ suciraṃ nirīkṣya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat -- taruṇaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca/
069.009. āścaryamamānuṣaparākramaṃ te paśyāmi, yo nāma bhavāñ jambudvīpādamanuṣyāvacaritaṃ parvatasamudranadyottaraṇaṃ kṛtvā ihāgataḥ, yatrāmanuṣyāḥ pralayaṃ gacchanti, prāgeva manuṣyāḥ/
069.011. devaṃ tadbhavantaṃ paśyāmi devānyatamaṃ vā manuṣyaveṣadhāriṇam/
069.012. na te kiṃciddustaramasādhyaṃ vā/
069.012. api tu ahaṃ mahāvyādhinā grasto mumūrṣuḥ/
069.012. bhavāṃścāyātaḥ/
069.013. api tu ko bhavato 'rthe parahitārthe 'bhyudyatasyātmaparityāgamapi na kuryāt? tena hi vatsa kṣipraṃ maṅgalapotaṃ samudānaya, saṃvaraṃ cāropaya, yadāvayoryātrāyanaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
069.014. evaṃ sārthavāheti supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghāya mahāsārthavāhāya pratiśrutya maṅgalapotaṃ samudānīya saṃvaraṃ cāropya yena magho mahāsārthavāhastenaopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
069.016. upasaṃkramya maghaṃ sārthavāhamidamavocat -- deva samudānīto maṅgalapotaḥ, saṃvaraṃ cāropitam, yasyedānīṃ mahāsārthavāhaḥ kālaṃ manyate/
069.017. atha magho mahāsārthavāho vadaradvīpamahāpattanagamanakṛtabuddhiḥ svajanabandhuvargaputradāramitrāmātyajñnātisālohitaiḥ sabhṛtyavargeṇa ca rohitakarājñnā ca nivāryamāṇo 'pi guṇavati phalake baddhvā āśu supriyasārthavāhasahāyo maṅgalapotamabhiruhya mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
069.020. atha magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ supriyasya mahāsārthavāhasya kathayati -- ahaṃ bāḍhaglāno na śakyāmi sthiyo gantum/
069.021. tadarhasi śayyāṃ kalpayitum yatrāhamapāśrito gamiṣyāmīti/
069.022. api tu asmin mahāsamudre yāvadevaṃvidhāni nimittāni bhavanti udakasya varṇasaṃsthānāni ca mama nivedayitavyāni/
069.023. yathā anekāni yojanaśatāni gatvā adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāha ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyam/
069.024. dṛṣṭvā punarmaghāya sārthavahāyārocayati -- yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāḥ, ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyaṃ paśyāmi/
069.025. evamukte maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- naitanmahāsārthavāha ekapāṇḍaraṃ pānīyam/
069.026. api tu paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakena mahatsudhāparvatam yadidaṃ tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ ranñjitam/
069.027. yatraikaviṃśatidhātugotrāṇi, yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaiḍūryānyabhinirvartante, yadeke jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante/
069.029. idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya prathamanimittam/
069.029. punarapi gacchan paśyati supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ śastravarṇaṃ pānīyam/
069.030. dṛṣṭvā ca punarmaghāya sārthavāhāyārocayati -- yat khalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāh -- śastravarṇaṃ pānīyaṃ dṛśyate/
069.031. maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- naitacchastravaṇa pānīyam/
069.032. paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakeṇa mahacchastraparvatam/
069.032. tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ ranñjitam/
body.translated_text: At the [appointed] time, he was asked by the great caravan-leader about his birth, family, lineage, origin, and purpose. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> informed the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> in detail about his birth, family, lineage, origin, and purpose, and further petitioned him: "By the power of the caravan, may I see the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>. Thus may I become one whose wishes are fulfilled, whose firm vow is discharged, one who fulfills the wishes of all beings." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>, having heard the unprecedented firm vow of the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, undertaken for the benefit of others, was filled with supreme wonder and, gazing at the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> with unblinking eyes for a long time, said this: "You are young, sir, and you are devoted to <s>Dharma</s>. I see in you a marvelous, superhuman prowess, for you have come here from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, having crossed mountains, oceans, and rivers not traversed by humans — where even non-humans perish, let alone humans. I regard you as a god, or else as some deity wearing a human guise. Nothing is difficult or impossible for you. However, I am stricken with a great illness and am about to die. And you have arrived. But who, for the sake of one like you, striving for the benefit of others, would not even sacrifice himself? Therefore, my son, quickly prepare the auspicious vessel, hoist the sail, and let us set out on our voyage." "Yes, caravan-leader." The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having agreed to the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>, prepared the auspicious vessel, hoisted the sail, approached the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>, and having approached, said to the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>: "Lord, the auspicious vessel is prepared, the sail has been hoisted; let the great caravan-leader set out when he thinks the time is right." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>, having resolved to go to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, though dissuaded by his own people, relatives, sons, wives, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood-relations, as well as by his retinue and by King <s>Rohitaka</s>, nevertheless had himself bound to a sturdy plank and, swiftly, as companion to the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, boarded the auspicious vessel and descended into the great ocean. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> said to the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>: "I am gravely ill and cannot go standing. Therefore, please prepare a bed where I may recline while we travel." "Moreover, in this great ocean, as long as such-and-such signs appear — the colors and forms of the water — you must report them to me." Thus, having traveled many hundreds of <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw water of a uniform white color. Having seen it, he reported to the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>: "May the great caravan-leader know that I see water of a uniform white color." Thus addressed, the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> said: "That is not uniformly white water, great caravan-leader. Rather, do you see to the south a great chalk mountain? It is by its influence that the water is tinged. There are twenty-one mineral deposits, from which, when smelted, gold, silver, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) are produced, and where certain people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> take jewels and return. This is the first sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>." Traveling further, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw water the color of weapons. Having seen it, he reported to the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>: "May the great caravan-leader know — water the color of weapons is seen." The caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> said: "That is not weapon-colored water. Do you see to the south a great weapon mountain? It is by its influence that the water is tinged."

body.text:
070.001. <70>atrāpyanekāni dhātugotrāṇi, yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaidūryasphaṭikānyabhinirvartante, yadeke jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante/
070.002. idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya dvitīyaṃ nimittam/
070.003. evaṃ lohaparvatāstāmraparvatā rūpyaparvatāḥ suvarṇaparvatāḥ sphaṭikaparvatā vaidūryaparvatāḥ/
070.004. adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāho nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyam, antarjale ca dīpārciṣaḥ paśyati dīpyamānāḥ/
070.005. dṛṣṭvā ca punarmaghāya sārthavāhāyārocayati -- yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāh -- nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyaṃ dṛśyate, antarjale ca dīpārciṣo dīpyamānāḥ/
070.007. evemukte magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- naitanmahāsārthavāha nīlapītalohitāvadātaṃ pānīyam, nāpyete dīpā iva dīpyante/
070.008. paśyasi tvaṃ dakṣiṇakena catūratnamayaṃ parvatam/
070.009. tasyaitadanubhāvena pānīyaṃ ranñjitam/
070.009. ye 'pyete dīpā iva dīpyante, ete 'ntargatā auṣadhyo dīpyante/
070.010. atrāpyanekāni dhātugotrāṇi, yaṃ paktvā suvarṇarūpyavaidūryasphaṭikānyabhinirvartante, yatraike jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyā ratnānyādāya pratinivartante/
070.011. idaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya daśamaṃ nimittam/
070.012. api tu mahāsārthavāha iyantyevāhaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasya daśa nimittāni jāne gamanaṃ prati, ataḥ pareṇa na jāne/
070.013. evamukte supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- kadā badaradvīpamahāpattanasya gamanāyānto bhaviṣyati? evamukte maghaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- mayāpi supriya badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ kārtsyena na dṛṣṭam/
070.015. api tu mayā śrutaṃ paurāṇānāṃ mahāsārthavāhānāmantikājjīrṇānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ mahallakānām -- ito jalamapahāya paścimāṃ diśaṃ sthalena gamyate/
070.017. tena caivamabhihitam, maraṇāntikāścāsya vedanāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ/
070.017. tataḥ supriyāya mahāsārthavāhāya kathayati -- maraṇāntikā me vedanāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ/
070.018. etattvaṃ maṅgalapotaṃ tīramupanīya vetrapāśaṃ baddhvā maccharīre śarīrapūjāṃ kuruṣva/
070.019. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastaṃ maṅgalapotaṃ tīramupanīya vetrapāśaṃ badhnāti/
070.020. atrāntare magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ kālagataḥ/
070.021. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho maghaṃ sārthavāhaṃ kālagataṃ viditvā sthale utthāpya śarīre śarīrapūjaṃ kṛtvā cintayati -- maṅgalapotamāruhya yāsyāmīti/
070.022. sa ca poto vāyunā vetrapāśaṃ chittvā apahṛtaḥ/
070.023. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścatūratnamayasya parvatasya dakṣiṇena pārśvenāṭavyāṃ sthalena saṃprasthito mūlaphalāni bhakṣayamāṇaḥ/
070.024. anekāni yojanāni gatvā adrākṣīt ślakṣṇaṃ parvatamanupūrvapravaṇamanupūrvaprāgbhāram/
070.025. na śakyate 'bhiroḍhum/
070.025. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho madhunā pādau pralipyābhirūḍhaśca, avatīrṇaśca, anekāni yojanāni gatvā mūlaphalāhāro gataḥ/
070.027. sa tatra paśyati mahāntaṃ parvatamuccaṃ ca pragṛhītaṃ ca/
070.027. niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣamāṇo na labhate, na cāsya kaścinniḥsaraṇavyapadeṣṭā/
070.028. tataścintāparaḥ śayitaḥ/
070.028. tatra ca parvate nīlādo nāma yakṣaḥ prativasati/
070.029. sa saṃlakṣayati -- ayaṃ bodhisattvo lokahitārthamudyataḥ parikliśyate, yannvahamasya sāhāyyaṃ kalpayeyam/
070.030. idamanucintya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat -- ito mahāsārthavāha pūrveṇa yojanaṃ gatvā trīṇi parvataśṛṅgāṇyanupūrvaniṃnānyanupūrvapravaṇānyanupūrvaprāgbhārāṇi/
070.032. tatra tvayā vetraśiṭām(?) baddhvā atikramitavyam/
070.032. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ suptaprabuddho vetraśiṭām <71>baddhvā tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇyatikrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: Here too there are many mineral deposits, from which, when smelted, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), and crystal are produced, and where certain people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> take jewels and return. This is the second sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>. Likewise [he reported] iron mountains, copper mountains, silver mountains, gold mountains, crystal mountains, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> mountains. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw water of blue, yellow, red, and white colors, and beneath the water he saw flame-like lights blazing. Having seen them, he reported to the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s>: "May the great caravan-leader know — water of blue, yellow, red, and white colors is seen, and beneath the water flame-like lights are blazing." Thus addressed, the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> said: "That is not blue, yellow, red, and white water, great caravan-leader, nor are those lamps blazing as they appear. Do you see to the south a mountain made of four kinds of gems? It is by its influence that the water is tinged. And those that blaze like lamps — they are medicinal herbs glowing within the water. Here too there are many mineral deposits, from which, when smelted, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal are produced, and where certain people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> take jewels and return. This is the tenth sign of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>." "Moreover, great caravan-leader, these are only the ten signs of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> that I know regarding the journey; beyond this I do not know." Thus addressed, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> said: "When will the journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> come to an end?" Thus addressed, the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> said: "Even I, <s>Supriyo</s>, have not seen <s>Badaradvīpa</s> in its entirety. However, I have heard from ancient great caravan-leaders, aged, old, and elderly: 'From here, leaving the water, one proceeds westward by land.' Having said this, mortal pains arose in him. Then he said to the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>: "Mortal pains have arisen in me. Bring this auspicious vessel to the shore, fasten the bamboo cable, and perform the funeral rites for my body." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> brought that auspicious vessel to the shore and fastened the bamboo cable. In the meantime, the great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> passed away. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having learned that the caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> had passed away, carried him ashore and performed the funeral rites for his body, and then thought: "I shall board the auspicious vessel and set sail." But the vessel had been carried away by the wind, which had severed the bamboo cable. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, proceeding on foot by land along the southern side of the four-jeweled mountain, set out through the wilderness, eating roots and fruits. Having traveled many <s>yojanas</s>, he saw a smooth mountain with a gradual slope, gradually inclined. It could not be climbed. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having smeared his feet with honey, climbed up and descended, and having traveled many <s>yojanas</s> eating roots and fruits, he went on. There he saw a great mountain, lofty and towering. Searching for a way out, he could not find one, nor was there anyone to show him the way out. Then, consumed with anxiety, he lay down. On that mountain dwelt a <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit) named <s>Nīlāda</s>. He considered: "This <s>Bodhisattva</s>, striving for the welfare of the world, is in distress. Let me render him assistance." Having reflected thus, he said to the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>: "From here, great caravan-leader, traveling one <s>yojana</s> to the east, there are three mountain peaks, gradually descending, gradually sloping, gradually inclined. There you must bind a bamboo-strip [rope] and cross over." Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having awoken from sleep, bound a bamboo-strip and crossed over those mountain peaks.

body.text:
071.001. bhūyaḥ saṃprasthito 'drākṣīt supriyo mahāsāthavāhaḥ sphaṭikaparvataṃ ślakṣṇaṃ nirālambamagamyaṃ manuṣyamātrasya/
071.002. na cāsyopāyaṃ paśyati taṃ parvatamabhirohaṇāyeti viditvā cintāparo 'horātramavasthitaḥ/
071.003. tasmiṃśca parvate candraprabho nāma yakṣaḥ prativasati/
071.004. sa cintāparaṃ sārthavāhaṃ viditvā lokahitārthamabhyudyataṃ mahāyānasamprasthitaṃ prasannacittaṃ copetyāśvāsayati -- na khalu mahāsārthavahena viṣādaḥ karaṇīya iti/
071.005. pūrveṇa krośamātraṃ gatvā mahaccandanavanam/
071.006. tasmiṃśca candanavane mahatyaśmaśilā/
071.006. tāṃ vīryabalenotpāṭya guhāṃ drakṣyasi/
071.007. tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ prabhāsvarā nāmauṣadhī panñcaguṇopetā/
071.007. tayā gṛhītayā nāsya kāye śastraṃ kramiṣyati, amanuṣyāścāvatāraṃ na lapsyante, balaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca saṃjanayati, ālokaṃ ca karoti/
071.009. tenālokena drakṣyasi catūratnamayaṃ sopānam/
071.009. tena sopānena sphaṭikaparvatamatikramitavyam/
071.010. sphaṭikaparvatamatikrāntasya te prabhāsvarā auṣadhyantardhāsyati/
071.010. tatra te na śocitavyaṃ na kranditavyaṃ na paridevitavyam/
071.011. atha candraprabho yakṣaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ samanuśāsya tatraivāntarhitaḥ/
071.012. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścandraprabheṇa mahāyakṣeṇa samāśvāsya ādeśitamārgo yathoktena vidhinā sphaṭikaparvatamatikrāntaḥ/
071.013. atikrāntasya cāsya prabhāsvarā auṣadhyantarhitā/
071.014. bhūyaḥ saṃprasthito 'drākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sauvarṇaṃ mahānagaramārāmasampannaṃ puṣkariṇīsampannam/
071.015. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho nagaradvāraṃ gataḥ/
071.015. yāvadbaddhaṃ nagaraṃ paśyati/
071.016. dṛṣṭvā ca punarudyānaṃ gatvā cintayati -- yadyapyahaṃ nagaramadrākṣam, tadapi śūnyam/
071.017. kadā badaradvīpasya mahāpattanasyāgamanāyādhvā bhaviṣyatīti viditvā śayitaḥ/
071.017. atha sā pūrvadevatā supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ durmanasaṃ viditvā rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaya uṣasaṃkramya samāśvāsya utkarṣayati -- sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha, nistīrṇāni te mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi manuṣyāmanuṣyāgamyāni/
071.020. saṃprāpto 'si badaradvīpamahāpattanaṃ manuṣyāmanuṣyānavacaritaṃ maheśākhya puruṣādhyuṣitam/
071.021. kiṃ tarhi na sāmpratamapramādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
071.021. indriyāṇi ca gopayitavyāni cakṣurādīni, kāyagatā smṛtirbhāvayitavyā/
071.022. śvobhūte nagaradvāraṃ trikoṭayitavyam/
071.022. tataścatasraḥ kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prasādikāścāturyamādhuryasampannāḥ sārvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ paramarūpābhijātāḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā hasitaramitaparicāritanṛttagītavāditrakalāsvabhijñnāḥ/
071.025. tāstvāmatyarthamupalālayanti, evaṃ ca vakṣyanti -- etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ/
071.025. svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāha, asmākamasvāminīnāṃ svāmī bhava, apatikānāṃ patiralayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'trāṇānāṃ trāṇo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇamaparāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ/
071.027. imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni, prabhūtāni ca jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni, tadyathā -- maṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpamaśmagarbhamusāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ/
071.028. etāni ca te ratnāni/
071.030. tvaṃ cāsmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva/
071.031. tatra te tāsu mātṛsaṃjñnā upasthāpayitavyā, bhaginīsaṃjñnā duhitṛsaṃjñnā upasthāpayitavyā/
071.032. daśākuśalāḥ karmapathā vigarhitavyāḥ, daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ saṃvarṇayitavyāḥ/
071.032. subahvapi te <72>pralobhyamānena rāgasaṃjñnā notpādayitavyā/
body.translated_text: 071.001. Proceeding further, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw a crystal mountain — smooth, without handholds, inaccessible to a mere human. 071.002. Not seeing any means to climb that mountain, he remained absorbed in thought for a day and a night. 071.003. On that mountain dwelt a <s>yakṣa</s> (nature spirit) named <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moonlight). 071.004. He, knowing the caravan-leader to be absorbed in thought, risen for the welfare of the world, set forth on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), and of serene mind, approached and consoled him: 'The great caravan-leader should not despair!' 071.005.
