'Going one <s>krośa</s> (league) to the east, there is a great sandalwood forest. 071.006. In that sandalwood forest is a great stone slab. 071.006. Uprooting it by the force of vigor, you will see a cave. 071.007. In that cave is an herb named <s>Prabhāsvarā</s> (Radiant), endowed with five qualities. 071.007. When that is taken, no weapon will penetrate his body, non-human beings will find no entry, it generates strength and vigor, and it produces light. 071.009. By that light you will see a stairway made of four kinds of jewels. 071.009. By that stairway the crystal mountain is to be crossed. 071.010. Once you have crossed the crystal mountain, the <s>Prabhāsvarā</s> herb will disappear. 071.010. There you should not grieve, should not cry, should not lament.' 071.011. Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>, having instructed the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, vanished on the spot. 071.012. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, consoled by the great <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>, following the indicated path, crossed the crystal mountain by the method as described. 071.013. And when he had crossed, the <s>Prabhāsvarā</s> herb disappeared. 071.014. Proceeding further, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw a great golden city, endowed with gardens and endowed with lotus-ponds. 071.015. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> went to the city gate. 071.015. He saw that the city was locked. 071.016. Having seen this, going back to the park, he thought: 'Although I have seen the city, it too is empty.' 071.017. 'When will there be a path for reaching the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>?' — knowing this, he lay down. 071.017. Then that former deity, knowing the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> to be dejected, at the time of dawn's approach at the end of the night, drawing near at the break of dawn, consoled and encouraged him: 'Well done, well done, great caravan-leader! You have crossed great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses inaccessible to humans and non-humans. 071.020. You have arrived at the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, uninhabited by humans, presided over by the great deity named <s>Maheśākhya</s>. 071.021. But now, diligence must be applied! 071.021. The sense-faculties beginning with the eye must be guarded, and mindfulness directed to the body must be cultivated. 071.022. Tomorrow morning, you must knock three times at the city gate. 071.022. Then four <s>kinnarī</s> (celestial) maidens will come out — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with charm and sweetness, possessing all major and minor limbs, of supreme beauty and noble birth, adorned with all ornaments, skilled in the arts of laughter, sport, attendance, dance, song, and music. 071.025. They will caress you exceedingly, and will speak thus: "Let the great caravan-leader come! 071.025. Welcome, great caravan-leader! Be the lord of us who have no mistress, the husband of us who have no husband, the shelter of us who have no shelter, the island of us who have no island, the refuge of us who have no refuge, the protector of us who have no protector, the final resort of us who have no final resort! 071.027. Here are your food-houses, drink-houses, clothing-houses, bedchamber-houses, delightful gardens, and abundant jewels of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — namely: gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, cat's-eye, <s>musāragalva</s>, ruby, and right-spiraling [conches]. 071.028. These jewels are yours. 071.030. And sport, play, and enjoy yourself with us!" 071.031. There you must regard them with the perception of a mother, the perception of a sister, the perception of a daughter. 071.032. The ten unwholesome courses of action are to be censured; the ten wholesome courses of action are to be praised. 071.032. Even though greatly tempted, the perception of passion must not be aroused.'

body.text:
072.001. sacedutpādayiṣyasi tatraivānayena vyasanamāpatsyase/
072.002. sūpasthitasmṛtestava saphalaḥ śramo bhaviṣyati/
072.002. yadyapi te subhāṣitasyārghamaṇiṃ prayaccheyuḥ, tatastvayā nipuṇaṃ praṣṭavyāh -- asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko 'nubhāva iti/
072.003. evaṃ dvitīyaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptasyāṣṭau kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti, tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca/
072.005. tatrāpi te eṣānupūrvī karaṇīyā/
072.005. yāvaccaturthakinnaranagaraprāptasya te dvātriṃśat kinnarakanyā nirgamiṣyanti tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca darśanīyatarāśca prāsādikatarāścāpsarasah -- pratispardhinyaḥ/
072.007. śatasahasraśobhitā bhaviṣyanti/
072.007. tatrāpi te eṣaivānupūrvī karaṇīyā/
072.007. ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā//
body.translated_text: 072.001. 'If you do arouse it, right there you will meet with misfortune and calamity through that transgression. 072.002. If your mindfulness is well-established, your effort will be fruitful. 072.002. If they should offer you an invaluable gem for [your] good words, then you must ask them carefully: "Sisters, what is the power of this gem?" 072.003. Thus, upon arriving at the second <s>kinnara</s> city, eight <s>kinnarī</s> maidens will come out, even more beautiful than the previous ones. 072.005. There too, the same procedure is to be followed. 072.005. Until, upon arriving at the fourth <s>kinnara</s> city, thirty-two <s>kinnarī</s> maidens will come out, even more beautiful and lovely and pleasing than the previous ones — rivaling the <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs). 072.007. They will be adorned with a hundred thousand [ornaments]. 072.007. There too, the same procedure is to be followed.' 072.007. Having spoken thus, that deity vanished on the spot.

body.text:
072.009. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ pramuditamanāḥ sukhapratibuddhaḥ kālyamevo 'tthāya sauvarṇaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptaḥ/
072.010. dvāramūlamupasaṃkramya trikoṭayati/
072.010. tataḥ supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre catasraḥ kinnarakanyā nirgatā abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāścāturyamādhuryasampannāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ paramarūpābhijātā hasitaramitaparicāritanṛttagītavāditrakalāsvabhijñnāḥ/
072.013. tā evamāhuh -- etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ/
072.013. svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāha/
072.013. asmākamasvāminīnāṃ svāmī bhava, apatīnāṃ patiralayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇo 'trāṇānāṃ trāṇo 'parāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ/
072.015. imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni vanaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni ca/
072.016. jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni, tadyathāmaṇayo muktā vaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāh etāni ca/
072.018. tvaṃ cāsmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva/
072.018. atha supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ sūpasthitasmṛtiṃ tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ sarvāṅgairanuparigṛhya sauvarṇaṃ kinnaranagaraṃ praveśya prāsādamabhiropya prajñnapta evāsane niṣādayanti/
072.020. niṣaṇṇaḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho daśākuśalān karmapathān vigarhati, daśa kuśalān karmapathān saṃvarṇayati, subahvapi pralobhyamāno na śakyate skhalayitum/
072.022. tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti -- āścaryam yatredānīṃ daharaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca/
072.023. na ca kāmeṣu sajjase vā badhyase vā/
072.023. prabhūtaiśca ratnaiśca pravārayanti/
072.023. dharmadeśanāvarjitāśca ekaṃ saubhāsinikaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti/
072.024. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastasya ratnasya prabhāvānveṣī kathayati -- asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko 'nubhāva iti/
072.025. tāḥ kathayanti -- yatkhalu sārthavāha jānīyāh -- tadeva poṣadhe panñcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnāta upoṣadhoṣita idaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya yojanasahasraṃ sāmantakena yo yenārthī bhavati hiraṇyena vā suvarṇena vā annena vā vastreṇa vā pānena vā alaṃkāraviśeṣeṇa vā dvipādena vā catuṣpādena vā yānena vā vāhanena vā dhanena vā dhānyena vā, sa cittamutpādayatu, vācaṃ ca niścārayatu/
072.029. sahacittotpādād vāgniścāraṇena yathepsitāścopakaraṇaviśeṣā ākāśādavatariṣyanti/
072.030. ayamasya ratnasyānubhāvaḥ/
072.030. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya sauvarṇāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrāntaḥ/
072.032. adrākṣīt supriyo <73>mahāsārthavāho rūpyamayaṃ kinnaranagaramārāmasampannaṃ vanasampannaṃ puṣkariṇīsampannam/
body.translated_text: 072.009. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, with a delighted mind, having slept well, rising early in the morning, arrived at the golden <s>kinnara</s> city. 072.010. Approaching the gate, he knocked three times. 072.010. When the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> knocked three times at the gate, four <s>kinnarī</s> maidens came out — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with charm and sweetness, possessing all major and minor limbs, of supreme beauty and noble birth, skilled in the arts of laughter, sport, attendance, dance, song, and music. 072.013. They said thus: 'Let the great caravan-leader come! 072.013. Welcome, great caravan-leader! 072.013. Be the lord of us who have no mistress, the husband of us who have no husband, the shelter of us who have no shelter, the island of us who have no island, the refuge of us who have no refuge, the protector of us who have no protector, the final resort of us who have no final resort! 072.015. Here are your food-houses, drink-houses, clothing-houses, bedchamber-houses, delightful with gardens, delightful with forests, delightful with lotus-ponds. 072.016. Jewels of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — namely: gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, cat's-eye, <s>musāragalva</s>, ruby, and right-spiraling [conches] — these too [are yours]. 072.018. And sport, play, and enjoy yourself with us!' 072.018. Then the <s>kinnarī</s> maidens, embracing the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> with well-established mindfulness with all their limbs, led him into the golden <s>kinnara</s> city, ascended the palace, and seated him on a prepared seat. 072.020. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, seated, censured the ten unwholesome courses of action and praised the ten wholesome courses of action; even though greatly tempted, he could not be made to stumble. 072.022. The <s>kinnarī</s> maidens, pleased, said: 'How wonderful that one so young is also a lover of <s>Dharma</s>! 072.023. And you are not attached to or bound by sensual pleasures!' 072.023. And they offered him abundant jewels. 072.023. Won over by his <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, they gave him one wish-fulfilling gem (<s>saubhāsinika ratna</s>). 072.024. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, inquiring about the power of that gem, said: 'Sisters, what is the power of this gem?' 072.025. They said: 'Know this, caravan-leader — on the <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance day), on the fifteenth, having bathed one's head, having observed the fast, raising this jewel-gem upon a banner-pole, within a radius of a thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), whoever needs anything — whether gold, silver, food, clothing, drink, special ornaments, two-footed or four-footed animals, vehicles, conveyances, wealth, or grain — let him generate the thought and utter the words. 072.029. Simultaneously with the arising of the thought and the utterance of the words, the desired special provisions will descend from the sky. 072.030. Such is the power of this gem.' 072.030. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having instructed, guided, inspired, and delighted the <s>kinnarī</s> maidens with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>, having taken leave of them as a mother, sister, and daughter, departed from the golden <s>kinnara</s> city. 072.032. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> saw a silver <s>kinnara</s> city, endowed with gardens, forests, and lotus-ponds.

body.text:
073.001. tatrāpi supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre'ṣṭau kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ/
073.002. tā apyevamāhuh -- etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ/
073.003. svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāhāya/
073.003. asmākamasvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava, pūrvadyāvattābhirapi dharmadeśanāvarjitābhistadviśiṣṭataraṃ dvisāhasrayojanavarṣakaṃ maṇiratnamanupradattam/
073.004. tatrāpi supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kthayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya rūpyamayāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrānto yāvat tṛtīyaṃ vaiḍūryamayaṃ kinnaranagaramanuprāptaḥ/
073.007. tatrāpi supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trikoṭite dvāre ṣoḍaśa kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ, tāsāṃ pūrvikānāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca prāsādikatarāśca/
073.008. tā api dharmadeśanāvarjitāstata eva viśiṣṭataraṃ saubhāsinikaṃ trisāhasrayojanikaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti/
073.009. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhastasya ratnasya prabhāvānveṣī kathayati -- asya ratnasya bhaginyaḥ ko'nubhāva iti? kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti -- pūrvavat/
073.011. supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛbhaginīduhitṛvat pratisaṃmodya tṛtīyāt kinnaranagarāt pratiniṣkrāntaḥ/
073.013. adrākṣīt supriyo mahāsārthavāhaścaturthaṃ catūratnamayaṃ kinnaranagaramārāmodyānaprāsādadevakulapuṣkariṇītaḍāgasuvibhaktarathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakāntarāpaṇasuracitagandhojjvalaṃ nānāgītavāditayuvatimadhurasvaravajravaiḍūryaśātakumbhamayaprākāratoraṇopaśobhitam/
073.015. dvāraṃ trirākoṭayati/
073.015. tataḥ supriyeṇa sārthavāhena trirākoṭite dvāre dvātriṃśat kinnarakanyā nirgatāḥ, tāsāṃ pūrvikāṇāmantikādabhirūpatarāśca darśanīyatarāścāpsarasaḥpratispardhinyaḥ śatasahasraśobhitāḥ/
073.017. tā apyevamāhuh -- etu mahāsārthavāhaḥ/
073.018. svāgataṃ mahāsārthavāhāya/
073.018. asamākamasvāmikānāṃ svāmī bhava, apatīnāṃ patiralayanānāṃ layano 'dvīpānāṃ dvīpo 'śaraṇānāṃ śaraṇo 'trāṇānāṃ traṇo 'parāyaṇānāṃ parāyaṇaḥ/
073.020. imāni ca te 'nnagṛhāṇi pānagṛhāṇi vastragṛhāṇi śayanagṛhāṇyārāmaramaṇīyāni vanaramaṇīyāni puṣkariṇīramaṇīyāni/
073.021. prabhūtāni ca jāmbudvīpakāni ratnāni, tadyathā -- maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ/
073.023. etāni ca te vayaṃ ca/
073.023. asmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ krīḍasva ramasva paricārayasva/
073.023. tatrāpi supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ sūpasthitasmṛtistāḥ kinnarakanyā vividhairdharmapadavyanñjanaiḥ paritoṣayāmāsa/
073.025. tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ sarvāṅgairanuparigṛhya catūratnamayaṃ kinnaranagaramanupraveśya prāsādamabhiropya prajñnapta evāsane niṣādayanti/
073.026. niṣaṇṇaḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho daśākuśalān karmapathān vigarhati, daśa kuśalān karmapathān saṃvarṇayati, subahvapi pralobhyamāno na śakyate skhalayitum/
073.028. tuṣṭāśca tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ kathayanti -- āścaryam yatredānīṃ daharaśca bhavān dharmakāmaśca/
073.029. na ca kāmeṣu sajjase vā badhyase vā/
073.029. prabhūtaiśca ratnaiḥ pravārayanti/
073.030. tā api dharmadeśanāvarjitāḥ saubhāsinikaṃ jāmbudvīpapradhānamanarghyeyamūlyamanantaguṇaprabhāvaṃ badaradvīpamāpattane sarvasvabhūtaṃ ratnamanuprayacchanti/
073.031. evaṃ ca kathayanti -- idamasmākaṃ mahāsārthavāha maṇiratnaṃ badareṇa bhrātrā kinnararājñnā anupradattam, asmin badaradvīpamahāpattane <74>cihnabhūtamālakṣyabhūtaṃ maṇḍanabhūtaṃ ca/
body.translated_text: There too, when the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> knocked three times at the gate, eight <s>Kinnara</s> maidens came forth. They too spoke thus: "Let the great caravan-leader come! Welcome to the great caravan-leader! Be the lord of us who are without a lord." They too, having been won over by the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, gave him an even more excellent jewel-gem that could rain down over two thousand <s>yojanas</s>. There too, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, and having taken leave of them as if they were his mothers, sisters, and daughters, departed from the silver <s>Kinnara</s> city and arrived at the third <s>Kinnara</s> city, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). There too, when the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> knocked three times at the gate, sixteen <s>Kinnara</s> maidens came forth, more beautiful and pleasing than the previous ones. They too, having been won over by the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, offered an even more excellent <s>saubhāsinika</s> gem extending over three thousand <s>yojanas</s>. Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, seeking to know the power of the gem, asked: "Sisters, what is the potency of this gem?" The <s>Kinnara</s> maidens replied: "As before." The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, and having taken leave of them as if they were his mothers, sisters, and daughters, departed from the third <s>Kinnara</s> city. The great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> then beheld the fourth <s>Kinnara</s> city, made of four kinds of gems, adorned with gardens, parks, palaces, temples, lotus-ponds, tanks, well-divided streets, avenues, squares, and crossroads, with beautifully arranged bazaars, radiant with fragrance, resounding with various songs and music and the sweet voices of maidens, embellished with ramparts and gateways made of diamond, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and gold. He knocked three times at the gate. Then, when the caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> knocked three times, thirty-two <s>Kinnara</s> maidens came forth, more beautiful and lovely than the previous ones, rivaling the <s>Apsarases</s>, adorned with a hundred thousand splendors. They too spoke thus: "Let the great caravan-leader come! Welcome to the great caravan-leader! Be the lord of us who are without a lord, the husband of us who are without a husband, the shelter of us who are without shelter, the island of us who have no island, the refuge of us who have no refuge, the protector of us who have no protector, the resort of us who have no resort. Here are your food-halls, drink-halls, garment-halls, sleeping-halls, delightful gardens, delightful groves, and delightful lotus-ponds. And here are abundant gems of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, namely: <s>maṇis</s> (jewels), pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, silver, gold, cat's-eye, <s>musāragalva</s>, red-gems, and right-spiraling [conches]. All these and we ourselves [are yours]. Sport with us, delight with us, enjoy yourself with us!" There too, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, with well-established mindfulness, pleased those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens with various words and phrases of the <s>Dharma</s>. And those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens, delighted, embraced the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> with all their limbs, led him into the four-jeweled <s>Kinnara</s> city, conducted him up to a palace, and seated him on a prepared seat. Seated there, the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> denounced the ten unwholesome courses of action and praised the ten wholesome courses of action; even though greatly tempted, he could not be caused to stumble. Those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens, delighted, said: "How wonderful that you, young as you are, are devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>! You are neither attached to nor bound by sensual pleasures." And they offered him abundant gems. They too, having been won over by the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, offered the <s>saubhāsinika</s> gem — the foremost of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, of priceless value, of infinite power — the very essence of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, the great port. And they said: "This jewel-gem of ours, O great caravan-leader, was given by our brother <s>Badara</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s> king. In this great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, it serves as an emblem, a landmark, and an ornament."

body.text:
074.001. tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ kathayati -- asya ratnasya ko 'nubhāva iti? tāḥ kathayanti -- yatkhalu mahāsārthavāha jānīyāh -- idaṃ maṇiratnaṃ tadeva poṣadhoṣito dhvajāgre baddhvā āropya kṛtsne jambudvīpe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ karaṇīyam -- śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpanivāsinaḥ stīmanuṣyāḥ, yuṣmākam yo yenarthī upakaraṇaviśeṣeṇa hiraṇyena vā subarṇena vā ratnena vā annena vā pānena vā vastreṇa vā bhojanena vā alaṃkāraviśeṣeṇa vā dvipadena vā catuṣpadena vā vāhanena vā yānena vā dhanena vā dhānyena vā sa cittamutpādayatu, vacanaṃ ca niścārayatu/
074.007. sahacittotpādādvāgniścāraṇena ca yathepsitāścopakaraṇaviśeṣa asya ratnasyānubhāvādākāśādavatariṣyanti/
074.008. ayaṃ tu prativiśeṣah -- yāni cāsya lokasya bhavanti mahābhayāni, tadyathā -- rājato vā cairato vā agnito vā udako vā manuṣyato vā amiṣyato vā siṃhato vā vyāghrato vā dvīpatarakṣuto vā yakṣyarākṣasapretapiśācakumbhāṇḍapūtanakaṭapūtanato vā, ītayopadravo vā, upasargo vā, anāvṛṣṭirvā durbhikṣabhayāni vā, asminnucchrite ratnaviśeṣe ima īrayopadravā na bhaviṣyanti/
074.012. iryuktvā tāḥ kinnarakanyāḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsuh --- sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha, nistīrṇāni mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi/
074.013. pūritā te dṛḍhasupratijñā/
074.014. saphalīkṛtā te śraddhā/
074.014. te gopitānīndriyāṇi/
074.014. sādhitā badaradvīpamahāpattanayātrā/
074.015. adhigataṃ te sarvajanamanorathasampādakaṃ jambudvīpapradhānaṃ ratnaviśeṣam/
074.015. api tu yena tvaṃ pathenāgataḥ, amanuṣyāstāvat, pralayaṃ gaccheyuḥ prāgeva manuṣyāḥ/
074.016. anyadeva vayaṃ sanmārgaṃ vyapadekṣyāmaḥ kṣipraṃ vārāṇasīgamanāya/
074.017. tacchṛṇu, manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣyāmah -- itaḥ paścime digbhāge sapta pratānatikramya mahāparvata uccaḥ/
074.018. tasmin parvate lohitākṣo nāma rākṣasaḥ prativasati raudraḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ/
074.019. sa ca parvato 'manuṣyavacaritaḥ kṛṣṇamandhakāraṃ savisphuliṅgaṃ vāyuṃ mokṣayati/
074.020. tatra te etadeva ratnaṃ dhvajāgre 'varopayitvā gantavyam/
074.020. ratnaprabhāvācca te ītayo vilayaṃ gamiṣyanti/
074.021. mahāparvatamatikramya aparaparvataḥ/
074.021. tasmin parvate 'gnimukho nāgaḥ prativasati/
074.022. sa tava gandhamāghrāya sapta rātriṃdivasānyaśaniṃ pātayiṣyati/
074.022. tatra ratnaguhāṃ samanviṣya praveṣṭavyam/
074.023. saptarātrasya cātyayādduṣṭanāgaḥ svapiṣyati/
074.023. śayite diṣṭanāge parvatamadhiroḍhavyam/
074.023. tatra drakṣyasi samaṃ bhūmipradeśamakṛṣṭoptaṃ ca taṇḍulaphalaśālimakaṇakamatuṣaṃ śuciṃ niṣphuṭigandhikaṃ caturaṅgulaparyavanaddham/
074.025. yastamaṣṭamyāṃ panñcadaśyāṃ vā bālāho'śvarājaḥ paribhujya sukhī arogo balavān prīṇitendriyaḥ pūrvakāyamabhyunnamayyodānamudānayati -- kaḥ pāragāmī, kaḥ pāragāmī, kaṃ pāraṃ nayāmi, svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambudvīpamanuprāpayāmi, sa tvayopasaṃkramya idaṃ syādvacanīyam -- ahaṃ pāragāmī, māṃ pāraṃ naya, māṃ svastikṣemābhyāṃ vārāṇasīmanuprāpaya/
074.028. atha sa supriyo mahāsārthavāhastāḥ kinnarakanyā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya mātṛduhitṛvat pratisamodya yathoddiṣṭena mārgeṇa yathoktena vidhinā anupūrveṇa taṃ bhūmipradeśamanuprāptaḥ/
074.030. sa ca bālāho'śvarājaścarannevamāha -- kaḥ pāragāmī, kaḥ pāragāmī, kaṃ pāraṃ nayāmi, svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambudvīpamanuprāpayāmi? tataḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāno yena bālāho 'śvarājastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> asked: "What is the potency of this gem?" They replied: "Know this, O great caravan-leader: this jewel-gem, having observed the <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting day), is to be raised and fastened atop a banner-staff, and a bell-proclamation should be made throughout the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>: 'Hear, O inhabitants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, women and men! Whoever among you desires any particular provision — whether gold, silver, gems, food, drink, garments, meals, ornaments, bipeds, quadrupeds, vehicles, conveyances, wealth, or grain — let that person generate the intention and utter the word. With the mere arising of intention and utterance of the word, the desired provisions will descend from the sky by the power of this gem.' And there is this further distinction: whatever great terrors exist in this world — whether from kings, robbers, fire, water, humans, enemies, lions, tigers, leopards and bears, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>pūtanas</s>, <s>kaṭapūtanas</s>, or calamities, disturbances, misfortunes, droughts, or fears of famine — when this special gem is raised aloft, these calamities and disturbances will not occur." Having said this, those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens praised the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>: "Well done, well done, great caravan-leader! You have crossed the great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses. Your firm and noble vow has been fulfilled. Your faith has been made fruitful. Your senses have been well-guarded. The journey to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s> has been accomplished. You have obtained the special gem, the foremost of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, which fulfills the wishes of all people. However, the path by which you came — even non-human beings would perish on it, let alone humans. We shall point out a different, safe route for a swift return to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Listen and pay attention, we shall speak: From here, in the western direction, crossing seven extended great mountains, there is a high mountain. On that mountain dwells a <s>rākṣasa</s> (demon) named <s>Lohitākṣa</s> (Red-Eye), fierce and a taker of others' lives. That mountain, uninhabited by humans, releases a dark, spark-filled wind. There, you must proceed with this very gem raised atop a banner-staff. By the power of the gem, the calamities will be dispelled. Beyond the great mountain is another mountain. On that mountain dwells a <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Agnimukha</s> (Fire-Face). Smelling your scent, he will hurl thunderbolts for seven days and nights. There, you must seek a gem-cave and enter it. After the passage of seven nights, the wrathful <s>Nāga</s> will fall asleep. When the wicked <s>Nāga</s> is asleep, you must climb the mountain. There you will see a level tract of land, with unhusked, unplanted, naturally grown, pure rice — fragrant, four fingers in height, without chaff. On the eighth or fifteenth day, the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>, having grazed on it, being happy, healthy, strong, and with pleased senses, raising the front of his body, utters this call: 'Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over? Whom shall I carry across? I will bring [you] safely to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>!' You must approach him and say: 'I wish to cross over. Carry me across. Bring me safely to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>!' Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s>, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted those <s>Kinnara</s> maidens with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, and having taken leave of them as if they were his mothers and daughters, followed the indicated route and the prescribed method, and gradually arrived at that tract of land. And the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>, while grazing, spoke thus: 'Who wishes to cross over? Who wishes to cross over? Whom shall I carry across? I will bring [you] safely to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>!' Then the great caravan-leader <s>Supriyo</s> approached the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>.

body.text:
075.001. <74>upasaṃkramya ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bālāho 'śvarājastenānñjaliṃ praṇamya bālāhamaśvarājamidavocat -- ahaṃ pāragāmī, ahaṃ pāragāmī, naya mām/
075.003. svastikṣemābhyāṃ vārāṇasīmanuprāpaya/
075.003. evamukte bālāho 'śvarājaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocat -- na te mahāsārthavāha mama pṛṣṭhādhirūḍhena diśo nāvalokayitavyāḥ, nimīlitākṣeṇa te stheyam/
075.005. ityuktvā bālāho'śvarājaḥ pṛṣṭhamupanāmayati/
075.005. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāho bālāhasyāśvarājasya pṛṣṭhamadhiruhya yathānuśiṣṭo 'lpaiśca kṣaṇalavamuhūrtairvārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ/
075.006. sva uyhāne 'vataritaḥ/
075.007. avatīrya supriyo mahāsārthavāho bālāhāśvarājapṛṣṭhādbālāhāśvarājaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya pādābhivandanaṃ karoti/
075.008. tato bālāho 'śvarājaḥ supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsa -- sādhu sādhu mahāsārthavāha/
075.009. nistīrṇāni te mahāsamudraparvatanadīkāntārāṇi/
075.009. pūritā te dṛḍhapratijñnā/
075.010. saphalīkṛtaste 'dhvā/
075.010. gopitānīndrayāṇi/
075.010. sādhitā te badaradvīpamahāpattanayātrā/
075.010. adhigataste sarvajanamanorathasampādako jambudvīpasya pradhāno ratnaviśeṣaḥ/
075.011. evaṃ hi parahitārthamabhyudyatāḥ kurvanti sattvaviśeṣāḥ/
075.012. ityuktvā bālāho 'śvarājaḥ prakrāntaḥ/
075.012. athāciraprakrānte bālāhe 'śvarājani supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ svagṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
075.013. aśrauṣurvārāṇasīnivāsinaḥ paurā brahmadattaśca kāśirājah -- supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ pūrṇena varṣaśatena saṃsiddhayātraḥ pūrṇamanorathaḥ svagṛhamanuprāpta iti/
075.015. śrutvā ca punarbrahmadattaḥ kāśirāja ānanditaḥ/
075.015. pauravargaḥ supriyaṃ sārthavāhaṃ saṃrādhayāmāsa/
075.016. aśrauṣīt tat pūrvakaṃ caurasahasramanyaśca jano dhanārthī -- supriyo mahāsārthavāhaḥ saṃsiddhayātraḥ paripūrṇamanoratha āgata iti/
075.017. srutvā ca punarupasaṃkramya supriyaṃ mahāsārthavāhamidamavocan -- parikṣīṇadhanāḥ sma iti/
075.018. evamukte mahāsārthavāhastān sarvān maitreṇa cakṣuṣā vyavalokya vijñnāpayati -- gacchatu bhavantaḥ svakasvakeṣu vijiteṣu/
075.019. yo yenārthī upakaraṇaviśeṣeṇa bhavati, sa tasyārthe cittamutpādayatu, vācaṃ ca niścārayatu/
075.020. śrutvā ca punaḥ prakrāntaḥ/
075.020. atha supriyo mahāsārthavāhastadeva poṣadhe panñcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnāta upoṣadhoṣito yattatprathamalabdhaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya vācaṃ ca niścārayati, yojanasahasrasāmantakena yathepsitāni sattvānāmupakaraṇānyutpadyante, sahābhidhānacca yo yenārthī tasya tadvarṣaṃ bhavati/
075.023. tataḥ paripūrṇamanorathāste sattvāḥ/
075.024. taccaurasahasraṃ supriyeṇa mahāsārthavāhena daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Having approached, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king, he said this to <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king: "I wish to cross over, I wish to cross over -- lead me! Bring me safely and securely to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>." Thus addressed, <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king said this to <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader: "O great caravan-leader, while mounted on my back, you must not look in any direction; you must remain with your eyes closed." Having said this, <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king offered his back. Then <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader, having mounted the back of <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king, doing as instructed, in just a few moments reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. He descended in his own garden. Having descended from the back of <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king, <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader circumambulated <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king three times and bowed at his feet. Then <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king praised <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader: "Well done, well done, O great caravan-leader! You have crossed the great oceans, mountains, rivers, and wildernesses. You have fulfilled your firm resolve. Your journey has been made fruitful. Your senses have been guarded. You have accomplished the voyage to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>. You have obtained the chief and special jewel of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> that fulfills the wishes of all people. Thus indeed do exceptional beings who are devoted to the welfare of others act." Having said this, <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king departed. Soon after <s>Bālāha</s> the horse-king departed, <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader entered his own house. The citizens dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and <s>Brahmadatta</s> the king of <s>Kāśī</s> heard: "<s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader, having completed his journey over a full hundred years, with his wishes fulfilled, has returned to his own house." Having heard this, <s>Brahmadatta</s> the king of <s>Kāśī</s> was delighted. The citizenry praised the caravan-leader <s>Supriya</s>. The former thousand thieves and other people seeking wealth heard: "<s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader has arrived with his journey completed and his wishes fully fulfilled." Having heard this, they approached <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader and said: "We are depleted of wealth." Thus addressed, the great caravan-leader, looking upon them all with a gaze of loving-kindness, informed them: "Go, sirs, to your own respective domains. Whoever desires any particular provision, let him set his mind upon it and utter his wish." Having heard this, he departed. Then <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader, on that very <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day), the fifteenth, having bathed his head and observed the <s>upoṣadha</s> fast, raised upon the top of a banner that very first-obtained jewel-gem, and uttered the command: within a radius of a thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues), the desired provisions of all beings were produced, and with the mere utterance, whatever anyone desired, that rained down upon them. Thus those beings had their wishes fulfilled. Those thousand thieves were established by <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader in the ten wholesome courses of action.

body.text:
075.025. atrāntarāt kālagate brahmadatte kāśirājani paurāmātyaiḥ supriyo mahāsārthavāho rājābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ/
075.026. mahābhiṣiktena supriyeṇa mahārājñnā dvitīyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ dhvajāgre āropya pūrvavidhinā dvīyojanasahasrasāmantakena yathepsitāni sattvānāmupakaraṇānyutpadyantāmiti sahābhidhānācca yo yenārthī tasya tadvarṣati/
075.028. tṛtīyena maṇiratnena yathoktena vidhinā dhvajāgrocchritena yathepsitopakaraṇaviśeṣavarṣaṇāni saṃpannāni/
075.029. evaṃ triyojanasahasrasāmantakenopakaraṇaiḥ strīmanuṣyāḥ saṃtarpitāḥ/
075.030. tato 'nupūrveṇa jambudvīpaiśvaryabhūtena supriyeṇa mahārājñnā tadeva poṣadhe panñcadaśyāṃ śiraḥsnātenopoṣadhoṣitena kṛtsne jambudvīpe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā upakaraṇotpannābhilāṣiṇāṃ strīmanuṣyāṇāṃ jambudvīpanivāsinām yanmaṇiratnaṃ badaradvīpamahāpattanasarvasvabhūtam yathepsitam <76>sarvopakaraṇavarṣiṇaṃ dhvajāgre āropayāmāsa/
body.translated_text: In the meantime, when <s>Brahmadatta</s> the king of <s>Kāśī</s> had passed away, <s>Supriya</s> the great caravan-leader was consecrated as king by the citizens and ministers with a royal consecration. The great-anointed King <s>Supriya</s>, raising the second jewel-gem upon the top of a banner, by the same method as before, within a radius of two thousand <s>yojanas</s>, caused the desired provisions of beings to be produced, and with the mere utterance, whatever anyone desired, that rained down upon them. With the third jewel-gem, raised upon the banner-top according to the same method, the raining of desired special provisions was accomplished. Thus, within a radius of three thousand <s>yojanas</s>, men and women were satisfied with provisions. Then, in due course, King <s>Supriya</s>, having become sovereign of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, on that very <s>poṣadha</s> the fifteenth, having bathed his head and observed the <s>upoṣadha</s> fast, having made a bell-proclamation throughout the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, for the men and women dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> who desired provisions, raised upon the top of a banner that very jewel-gem which was the supreme treasure of the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, which rained all desired provisions.

body.text:
076.001. samanantaraṃ dhvajāgrāvaropite tasmiñ jambudvīpapradhānamaṇiratne kṛtsno jambudvīpanivāsī mahājanakāyo yathepsitairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ saṃtarpitaḥ/
076.003. upakaraṇasaṃtarpitaśca jambudvīpanivāsī janakāyaḥ supriyeṇa rājñnā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
076.004. tato jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ rājyaiśvaryādhipatye partiṣṭhāpya rājarṣibrahmacaryaṃ caritvā caturo brahmān vihārān bhāvayitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihārī brahmalokasabhāgatāyāṃ copapanno mahābrahmā saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: Immediately upon that chief jewel-gem of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> being raised upon the banner-top, the entire great multitude of people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was satisfied with desired special provisions. And the people dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, having been satisfied with provisions, were established by King <s>Supriya</s> in the ten wholesome courses of action. Then, having established his eldest prince in the sovereignty of the kingdom, having practiced the holy life of a royal sage (<s>rājarṣi</s>), and having cultivated the four <s>Brahma-vihāras</s> (divine abodes), having abandoned desire for sensual pleasures, dwelling extensively in those states, he was reborn in the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā) and became a Great <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text:
076.007. bhagavanāha -- kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau supriyo nāma mahāsārthavāhaḥ, ahameva tena kālena tena samayena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ vartitavān/
076.008. yattaccaurasahasram, etadeva bhikṣasahasram/
076.009. yā sā pūrvadevatā, kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddho bodhisattvabhūtaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena/
076.010. yaścāsau magho mahāsārthavāhaḥ, eṣa eva śāriputro bhukṣuḥ sa tena kā
lena tena samayena/
076.011. yaścāsau nīlādo nāma mahāyakṣaḥ, eṣa evānando bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena/
076.012. yaścāsau candraprabho yakṣaḥ, eṣa evāniruddho bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena/
076.012. yaścāsau lohitākṣo nāma mahāyakṣaḥ, sa eṣa eva devadattastena kalena tena samayena/
076.013. yaścāsau agnimukho nāma nāgaḥ, eṣa eva māraḥ pāpīyān sa tena kalena tena samayena/
076.014. yaścāsau bālāho 'śvarājaḥ, maitreyo boddhisattvastena kālena tena samayena/
076.015. tadā tāvanmayā bhikṣavo dṛḍhapratijñnena pratijñnāpūraṇārthaṃ saptavārāṃścaurasahasrāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ/
076.016. aparituṣṭāṃśca caurān viditvā dṛḍhapratijñnā kṛtā/
076.017. kṛtvā cānekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairbadaradvīpamahāpattanasya yātrāṃ sādhayitvā caurasahasrapramukhaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jambudvīpaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
076.019. idānīmapi mayā anekairduṣkaraśatasahasrairanuttaraṃ jñnānamadhigamya maitrāyatā karuṇayā saptakṛtvaścaurasahasrasakāśāt sārthaḥ paritrātaḥ/
076.020. aparituṣṭaṃ ca caurasahasraṃ viditvā yāvadāptaṃ dhanena saṃtarpayitvā atyantaniṣṭhe 'nuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ/
076.021. anekāni ca devamanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi yakṣarākṣasapretapiśācakumbhāṇḍapūtanakaṭapūtanakoṭiśatasahasrāṇi śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, O monks? That great caravan-leader named <s>Supriya</s> -- that was none other than myself at that time, in that era, practicing the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Those thousand thieves -- they are these very thousand monks. That former deity -- that was <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> when he was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> at that time. That great caravan-leader <s>Magha</s> -- he is this very monk <s>Śāriputra</s> at that time. That great <s>Yakṣa</s> named <s>Nīlāda</s> -- he is this very monk <s>Ānanda</s> at that time. That <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Candraprabha</s> -- he is this very monk <s>Aniruddha</s> at that time. That great <s>Yakṣa</s> named <s>Lohitākṣa</s> -- he is this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time. That <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Agnimukha</s> -- he is this very <s>Māra</s> the Evil One at that time. That horse-king <s>Bālāha</s> -- he was the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> at that time. At that time, O monks, with firm resolve, for the sake of fulfilling my vow, I rescued the caravan from the thousand thieves seven times. And knowing the thieves to be unsatisfied, I made a firm vow. Having made it, through hundreds of thousands of difficult austerities, having accomplished the voyage to the great port of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, having satisfied with wealth the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> beginning with the thousand thieves, I established them in the ten wholesome courses of action. Now too, having attained unsurpassed knowledge through hundreds of thousands of difficult austerities, with friendliness and compassion, I rescued the caravan from the thousand thieves seven times. And knowing the thousand thieves to be unsatisfied, having satisfied them with as much wealth as could be obtained, I have established them in the ultimate, unsurpassed <s>yogakṣema</s> (security from bondage), <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And hundreds of thousands of gods, humans, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Pūtanas</s>, and <s>Kaṭapūtanas</s>, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, have been established in the refuges and precepts."

body.text:
076.024. idamavocadbhagavān/
076.024. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Those monks, with uplifted minds, rejoiced in the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 076.025. iti śrīdivyāvadāne supriyāvadānamaṣṭamam//
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Supriyāvadāna</s> (Story of Supriya) is the eighth.

body.text: 077.001. div9 meNDhakagRhaptivibhūtiparicchedaḥ/
body.translated_text: The chapter on the wealth of the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>.

body.text:
077.002. śrāvastyāṃ nidānam/
077.002. tena khalu samayena bhadraṃkare nagare ṣaḍ janā mahāpuṇyāḥ prativasanti--meṇḍhako gṛhapatir meṇḍhakapatnī meṇḍhakaputro meṇḍhakasnuṣā meṇḍhakadāso meṇḍhakadāsī/
077.004. kathaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatirjñāto mahāpuṇyah? sa yadi riktakāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi paśyati, sahadarśanādeva pūryante/
077.005. evaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatirjñāto mahāpuṇyaḥ/
077.005. kathaṃ meṇḍhakapatnī? sā ekasyārthāya sthālikāṃ sādhayati, śatāni sahasrāṇi ca bhuñjate/
077.006. evaṃ meṇḍhakapatnī/
077.006. kathaṃ meṇḍhakaputrah? tasya pañcaśatiko nakulako kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati/
077.007. sa yadi śataṃ sahasraṃ vā parityajati, tadā pūrṇa eva tiṣṭhati, na parikṣīyate/
077.008. evaṃ meṇḍhakaputraḥ/
077.008. kathaṃ meṇḍhakasnuṣā? sā ekasyārthāya gandhaṃ saṃpādayati, śatasahasrasya paryāptirbhavati/
077.009. evaṃ meṇḍhakasnuṣā/
077.010. kathaṃ meṇḍhakadāsah? sa yadaikaṃ halasīraṃ kṛṣati, tadā sapta sīrāḥ kṛṣṭā bhavanti/
077.010. evaṃ meṇḍhakadāsaḥ/
077.010. kathaṃ meṇḍhakadāsī mahāpuṇyā? sā yadaikaṃ vastu rakṣati, tatsaptaguṇaṃ syāt/
077.011. yadā ekamātraṃ pratijāgarti, tadā sapta mātrāḥ saṃpadyante/
077.012. evaṃ maṇḍhakadāsī mahāpuṇyā//
body.translated_text: The setting is in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At that time, in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>, six persons of great merit dwelt -- the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant. How was the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> known to be of great merit? Whenever he looked at his empty treasuries and granaries, at the very moment of seeing them, they became full. Thus was the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> known to be of great merit. How about <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife? She would cook for one person, yet hundreds and thousands would eat from it. Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife. How about <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son? He had a purse of five hundred coins tied at his waist. If he gave away a hundred or a thousand, it would remain full, never becoming depleted. Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son. How about <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law? She would prepare perfume for one person, yet it would suffice for a hundred thousand. Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law. How about <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant? Whenever he ploughed with one ploughshare, seven furrows would be ploughed. Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant. How about <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant, of great merit? Whenever she guarded one thing, it would become sevenfold. Whenever she kept watch once, seven watches would be accomplished. Thus was <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant, of great merit.

body.text:
077.013. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgavipratihīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānāmaṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātrestrirdivasasya ṣaṭkṛtvo rātriṃdivasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ
vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate--ko hīyate, ko vardhate, kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ, kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ, ko 'pāyaniṃnaḥ, ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ, ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ, kamahamapāyamārgādvyutthāpya svargaphale mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanupradadyām,
kamāryadhanavirahitamāryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayāmi, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam, kasya pakvāni vimocayeyam, kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣurviśodhayeyam/
077.025. apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ/
077.026. na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet//1//
body.translated_text:
077.013. It is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — who are of great compassion, who have crossed the four floods, who are well-established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have long practiced the four means of gathering [disciples], who are free from the five hindrances, who have transcended the five destinies, who are endowed with the six limbs, who have fulfilled the six <s>Pāramitās</s>, who are adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, who are guides of the eightfold path, who are skilled in the nine successive attainments, who are mighty with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who are distinguished by sovereignty over a thousand — [that] three times during the night and three times during the day, six times in a day-and-night, they survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, and the vision of knowledge arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who has fallen into hardship, distress, and straits? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who leans toward the lower realms? Whom shall I raise up from the path of the lower realms and establish in the fruit of heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, shall I extend the hand of deliverance? Whom, deprived of the noble treasures, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the noble treasures? For whom shall I plant roots of merit not yet planted? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened? For whom, whose eyes are covered with the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I purify the vision with the collyrium-stick of knowledge?'
077.025. 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its bounds,
077.026. but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the [appointed] time for those who are his calves to be trained.' // 1 //

body.text:
077.027. sarvajñasaṃtānanivāsinī hi
077.028. kāruṇyadhenurmṛgayatyakhinnā/
077.029. vaineyavatsān bhavadurganaṣṭān
077.030. vatsān praṇaṣṭāniva vatsalā gauḥ//2//
body.translated_text:
077.027. 'The cow of compassion, dwelling in the continuum of the Omniscient,
077.028. searches tirelessly
077.029. for the trainable calves lost in the fortress of existence,
077.030. like a loving cow for her lost calves.' // 2 //

body.text:
077.031. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ meṇḍhako gṛhapatiḥ saparivāro bhadraṃkare nagare prativasati/
077.032. tasya vaineyakālaṃ pakvamiva gaṇḍaṃ śastrābhinipātamavekṣate/
077.032. yannvahaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikām <78>careyam/
body.translated_text:
077.031. The Blessed One reflected: 'This householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, together with his retinue, dwells in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.
077.032. The time for his training awaits the application of the instrument, like a ripe boil [awaiting the surgeon's lance].
077.032. Let me go on a teaching tour through the <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> countries.'

body.text:
078.001. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha tvamānanda, bhikṣūṇāmārocaya--tathāgato bhikṣavo bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
078.002. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum, sa cīvarakāṇi pratigṛhṇātu iti/
078.003. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati--tathāgata āyuṣmanto bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
078.005. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ bhadraṃkareṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritum, sa cīvarakāṇi pratigṛhṇātu iti/
078.006. evamāyuṣmanniti te bhiṣava āyuṣmata ānandasya pratiśrutya pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchanti//
body.translated_text:
078.001. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the monks: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, monks, will go on a teaching tour through the <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> countries.
078.002. Whoever among you is willing to go on a teaching tour through the <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> countries with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robes."'
078.003. 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One and announced to the monks: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, Venerable Ones, will go on a teaching tour through the <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> countries.
078.005. Whoever among you is willing to go on a teaching tour through the <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> countries with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robes.'
078.006. 'Yes, Venerable One,' those monks replied to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and followed close behind, one after another.

body.text:
078.008. atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāraḥ, vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛtaḥ, siṃha iva daṃṣṭragaṇaparivāraḥ, haṃsarāja iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, suparṇa iva pakṣigaṇaparivṛtaḥ, vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ, koṭṭarāja iva mantriygaṇaparivṛtaḥ,
cakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ, candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ, sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛtaḥ, dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, vemacittirivāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, brahmeva brahmakāyikaparivṛtah,
stimita iva jalanidhiḥ, sajala iva jalanidhiḥ, vimada iva gajapatiḥ, sudāntairindriyairasaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇairaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājatagātro daśabhirbalaiścaturbhirvaiśāradyaistribhiḥ smṛtyupasthānairmahākaruṇayā ca/
078.019. evamanekaguṇagaṇasamanvāgato buddho bhagavāñ janapadacārikayā bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
078.020. yadā bhagavatā śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitam, nirbhartsitā ānanditā devamanuṣyāḥ, toṣitāni sajjanahṛdayāni, tadā bhagnaprabhāvāstīrthyāḥ pratyantān saṃśritāḥ/
078.022. tataḥ kecidbhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ gatvā avasthitāḥ/
078.023. taiḥ śrutaṃ śramaṇa gautama āgacchatīti/
078.023. śrutvā ca punarvyathitāste parasparaṃ kathayanti--pūrvaṃ tāvadvayaṃ śramaṇena gautamena madhyadeśānnirvāsitāḥ/
078.024. sa yadīhāgamiṣyati, niyatamito 'pi nirvāsayiṣyati/
078.025. tadupāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyamiti/
078.025. te kulopakaraṇaśālā upasaṃkramya kathayanti--dharmalābho dharmalābhaḥ/
078.026. te kathayanti--kimidam? avalokitā gamiṣyāmaḥ/
078.026. kasyārthāya? dṛṣṭā asmābhiryuṣmākaṃ saṃpattiḥ, yāvadvipattiṃ na paśyāmaḥ/
078.027. āryakāḥ, asmākaṃ vipattirbhaviṣyati/
078.028. bhavantaḥ, śramaṇo gautamaḥ kṣurāśaniṃ pātayannanekā aputrikā apatikāśca kurvannāgacchati/
078.029. āryāḥ, yadyevam, yasminneva kāle sthātavyaṃ tasminneva kāle 'smākaṃ parityāgas triyate/
078.030. tiṣṭhata, na gantavyam/
078.030. te kathayanti--kiṃ vayaṃ na tiṣṭhāmah? na yūyamasmākaṃ śroṣyatha/
078.030. āryāḥ kathayata, śroṣyāmaḥ/
078.031. te kathayanti--bhadraṃkarasāmantakena sarvajanakāyamudvāsya bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ pravāsayata/
078.032. śādvalāni kṛṃṣata/
078.032. sthaṇḍilāni pātayata/
078.032. puṣpaphalavṛkṣaṃ chedayata/
078.032. panīyāni <79>viṣeṇa dūṣayata/
body.translated_text:
078.008. Then the Blessed One — tamed, with a tamed retinue; tranquil, with a tranquil retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; at ease, with a retinue at ease; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with a retinue of <s>Arhats</s>; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring confidence, with a retinue inspiring confidence — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle, like a lion surrounded by a troop of fanged beasts, like a king of geese surrounded by a flock of geese, like a <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa) surrounded by a flock of birds, like a teacher surrounded by a company of students, like a skilled physician surrounded by a group of patients, like a hero surrounded by a band of warriors, like a guide surrounded by a group of travelers, like a caravan-leader surrounded by a company of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by the townsfolk, like a fortress-king surrounded by a company of ministers, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>, like <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Vemacitri</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by the host of the Thirty-Three, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [gods] — like a still ocean, like a full ocean, like a lordly elephant free of rut, with well-controlled senses moving in his gait without disturbance, his body resplendent with the thirty-two marks of a great being and the eighty minor characteristics, endowed with the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the three applications of mindfulness, and great compassion —
078.019. thus endowed with a multitude of many virtues, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, set out on a teaching tour to the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.
078.020. When the Blessed One had displayed the great miraculous display at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and had humbled and delighted gods and humans, and the hearts of good people were satisfied, then the non-Buddhist ascetics, their prestige broken, took refuge in the border regions.
078.022. Some of them went to the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> and settled there.
078.023. They heard: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is coming.'
078.023. Hearing this, they became anxious and said to one another: 'Previously we were driven out of the central lands by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.
078.024. If he comes here, he will surely drive us out from here too.
078.025. A stratagem must be devised.'
078.025. They approached the family supporters' hall and said: 'It is a gain of <s>Dharma</s>! A gain of <s>Dharma</s>!'
078.026. They said: 'What is this?' 'Look upon us; we are leaving.'
078.026. 'For what reason?' 'We have seen your prosperity; we do not wish to see your downfall.
078.027. Noble ones, there will be downfall for us.'
078.028. 'Sirs, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is coming, hurling his razor-thunderbolt, making many women sonless and husbandless.'
078.029. 'Noble ones, if that is so, at the very time when you should stand firm, our abandonment is being carried out.'
078.030. 'Stay; do not go.'
078.030. They said: 'Why would we not stay? But you will not listen to us.'
078.030. 'Noble ones, tell us; we shall listen.'
078.031. They said: 'Drive out all the people from the vicinity of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> and expel them from <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> city.
078.032. Plow up the meadows.
078.032. Demolish the resting-places.
078.032. Cut down the flowering and fruit trees.
078.032. Poison the drinking waters.'

body.text:
079.001. te kathayanti--āryāḥ, tiṣṭhata, sarvamanutiṣṭhāma iti/
079.001. te 'vasthitāḥ/
079.001. tatastairbhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakena sarvo janakāya udvāsya bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaraṃ pravāsitaḥ, śādvalāni kṛṣṭāni, sthaṇḍilāni pātitāni, puṣpaphalavṛkṣāśchinnāḥ, pānīyāni viṣadūṣitāni/
079.003. tataḥ śakro devendraḥ saṃlakṣayati--na mama pratirūpam yadahaṃ bhagavato 'satkāramadhyupekṣeyam/
079.004. yena nāma bhagavatā tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairanekair duṣkaraśatasahasraiḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūryānuttarajñānamadhigatam, sa nāma bhagavān sarvalokaprativiśiṣṭaḥ sarvavādavijayī śūnye janapade cārikaṃ cariṣyati/
079.007. yannvahaṃ bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya sukhasparśārthāya autsukyamāpadyeyamiti/
079.007. tena vātabalāhakānāṃ devaputrāṇāmājñā dattā--gacchata bhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakena, viṣapānīyāni śoṣayata iti/
079.009. varṣabalāhakānāṃ devaputrāṇāmājñā dattā--āṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasyāpūryateti/
079.009. cāturmahārājikā devā uktāh--yūyaṃ bhadraṃkarāṇāṃ janapadānāṃ vāsayateti/
079.010. tato vātabalāhakairdevaputrairviṣadūṣitāni pānīyāni {śoṣitāni}, varṣabalāhakaistānyeva kūpodapānavāpīsarastaḍāgānyaṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasya pūritāni/
079.012. cāturmahārājikairdevairbhadraṃkaranagarasāmantakaṃ sarvamāvāsitam/
079.012. janapadā ṛddhāḥ sphītāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
079.013. tīrthyair nagarajanakāyasametairavacarakāḥ preṣitāh--gatvā paśyata kīdṛśā janapadā iti/
079.014. te gatāḥ paśyantyatiśayena janapadān ṛddhān sphītān/
079.014. tata āgatya kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, na kadācidasmābhirevamrūpā janapadā ṛddhāḥ sphītā dṛṣṭapūrvā iti/
079.015. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, vo yastāvadacetanān bhāvānanvāvartayati, sa yuṣmānnānvāvartayiṣyatīti? kuta etat? sarvathā avalokitā bhavantaḥ, apaścimaṃ vo darśanam, gacchāma iti/
079.017. te kathayanti--āryāḥ, tiṣṭhata, kim yuṣmākaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ karoti? so 'pi pravrajitaḥ, yūyamapi pravrajitā bhikṣācarāḥ/
079.019. kimasau yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣāṃ cariṣyatīti? tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--samayena tiṣṭhāmo yadi yūyaṃ kriyākāraṃ kuruta--na kenacicchramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitavyam/
079.020. ya upasaṃkrāmati, sa ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇo daṇḍya iti/
079.021. taiḥ pratijñātaṃ kriyākāraśca kṛtaḥ//
body.translated_text:
079.001. They said: 'Noble ones, stay; we shall carry out everything.'
079.001. They stayed.
079.001. Then by them, all the people from the vicinity of the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> were driven out and expelled from <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> city; the meadows were plowed up, the resting-places demolished, the flowering and fruit trees cut down, and the drinking waters poisoned.
079.003. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, reflected: 'It is not fitting for me to look on indifferently while the Blessed One is dishonored.
079.004. The Blessed One, who over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, through hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds, fulfilled the six <s>Pāramitās</s> and attained unsurpassed knowledge — that Blessed One, pre-eminent in all the world, victorious over all disputants, will wander in an empty country?
079.007. Let me exert myself for the comfort of the Blessed One together with his community of disciples.'
079.007. He gave an order to the wind-cloud gods: 'Go to the vicinity of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> city and dry up the poisoned waters.'
079.009. He gave an order to the rain-cloud gods: 'Fill [the wells] with water possessing the eight qualities.'
079.009. The gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven were told: 'You, settle the regions of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.'
079.010. Then the wind-cloud gods dried up the poisoned waters; the rain-cloud gods filled those very wells, ponds, tanks, lakes, and reservoirs with water possessing the eight qualities.
079.012. The <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods settled the entire vicinity of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> city.
079.012. The regions became prosperous and thriving.
079.013. The non-Buddhist ascetics, together with the townsfolk, sent scouts: 'Go and see what the countryside looks like.'
079.014. They went and saw that the regions were exceedingly prosperous and thriving.
079.014. They came back and said: 'Sirs, never before have we seen such prosperous and thriving regions.'
079.015. The non-Buddhist ascetics said: 'Sirs, he who can command even inanimate things — will he not command you? How could it be otherwise? In any case, look upon us, sirs; this is your last sight of us. We are leaving.'
079.017. They said: 'Noble ones, stay! What does the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> do to you? He too is a renunciant, and you too are renunciants living on alms.
079.019. Will he beg for alms from you?' The non-Buddhist ascetics said: 'We shall stay on a condition, if you make an agreement: No one shall approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> for an audience.
079.020. Whoever approaches him shall be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.'
079.021. They agreed, and the agreement was made.

body.text:
079.022. tato {bhagavān} janapadacārikāṃ caran bhadraṃkaraṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ/
079.022. bhadraṃkare nagare viharati dakṣiṇāyatane/
079.023. ten khalu samayena kapilavastuno brāhmaṇadārikā bhadraṃkare nagare pariṇītā/
079.024. tayā prākārasthayā bhagavānandhakāre dṛṣṭaḥ/
079.024. sā saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ bhagavāñ śākyakulanandanaḥ śākyakulādrājyamapahāya pravrajitaḥ/
079.025. sa idānīmandhakāre tiṣṭhati/
079.025. yadyatra sopānaṃ syāt, ahaṃ pradīpamādāyāvatareyamiti/
079.026. tato bhagavatā tasyāścetasā cittamājñāya sopānaṃ nirmitam/
079.027. tato hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā pradīpamādāya sopānenāvatīrya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntā/
079.027. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ purastāt pradīpaṃ sthāpayitvā pādau śirasā vanditvā niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
079.028. tato bhagavatā tasyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī catruāryasatyasamprativedhikī pūrvavadyāvaccharaṇagatāmabhiprasannāmiti/
079.030. atha bhagavāṃstāṃ dārikāmidamavocat--ehi tvaṃ dārike yena meṇḍhako gṛhapatistenopasaṃkrama, upasaṃkramyaivaṃ madvacanādārogyāpaya, evaṃ ca vada--gṛhapate, tvāmuddiśyāhamihāgataḥ, tvaṃ ca dvāraṃ baddhvā sthitaḥ/
079.032. yuktametadevamatitheḥ pratipattum yathā tvam <80>pratipanna iti? yadi kathayati--gaṇena kriyākāraḥ kṛta iti, vaktavyah--tava putrasya pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati/
body.translated_text:
079.022. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.
079.022. He dwelt in <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> city at the southern monastery.
079.023. At that time, a Brahmin girl from <s>Kapilavastu</s> had been married in the city of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s>.
079.024. Standing on the rampart, she saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the darkness.
079.024. She reflected: 'This <s>Bhagavān</s>, the joy of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, having renounced the kingship of the <s>Śākya</s> clan, has gone forth as a renunciant.
079.025. Now he stands in darkness.
079.025. If there were a stairway here, I would take a lamp and descend.'
079.026. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known with his mind the thought in her mind, magically created a stairway.
079.027. Then, delighted, joyful, and elated, she took a lamp and descended by the stairway and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
079.027. Having approached, she placed the lamp before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed her head at his feet, and sat down to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.
079.028. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known her disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, as before, until she became one who had gone to the refuges and was full of faith.
079.030. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the girl: 'Come, girl, approach the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, and having approached, convey my greetings of good health in my name, and say thus: "Householder, I have come here on your account, yet you have barred the door and remain standing.
079.032. Is it proper to treat a guest in the way you have treated him? If he says, 'The guild made a resolution,' you should say: 'Your son has a purse of five hundred tied at his waist.
080.001. If he spends a hundred or a thousand, it fills up again and is never exhausted.'"

body.text:
080.002. sa yadi śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā vyayīkaroti, pūryata eva, na parikṣīyate/
080.003. na śaknoṣi ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇaṃ dattvā āgantumiti? evaṃ bhadanteti sā dārikā bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya saṃprasthitā/
080.004. yathāparijñātaiva kenacideva meṇḍakasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gatā/
080.005. gatvā ca kathayati--gṛhapate bhagavāṃsta ārogyayati/
080.005. sa kathayati--vande buddhaṃ bhagavantam/
080.006. gṛhapate, bhagavānevamāha--tvāmevāhamuddiśyāgataḥ, tvaṃ ca dvāraṃ baddhvā avasthitaḥ/
080.007. yuktametadevamatitheḥ pratipattum yathā tvaṃ pratipanna iti? sa kathayati--dārike, gaṇena kriyākāraḥ kṛtah--na kenacicchramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ darśanāya upasaṃkramitavyam/
080.008. ya upasaṃkrāmati, sa gaṇena ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇo daṇḍya iti/
080.009. gṛhapate, bhagavān kathayati--tava putrasya pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāṃ baddhastiṣṭhati/
080.010. sa yadi śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā vyayīkaroti, pūryata eva, na parikṣīyate/
080.011. na śaknoṣi tvaṃ ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇaṃ datvā āgantumiti? sa saṃlakṣayati--na kaścidetajjānīte/
080.011. nūnaṃ sarvajñaḥ sa bhagavān/
080.012. gacchāmīti/
080.012. sa ṣaṣṭikārṣāpaṇān dvāre sthāpayitvā brāhmaṇadārikopadiṣṭena sopānenāvatīrya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
080.013. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
080.014. tato bhagavatā meṇḍhakasya gṛhapaterāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā yāvacchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
080.016. sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ kathayati--bhagavan, kimeṣo 'pi bhadraṃkaranagaranivāsī janakāya evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhīte? bhagavānāha--gṛhapate, tvāmāgamya bhūyasā sarva eva janakāyo lābhīte/
080.018. tato meṇḍhako gṛhapatirbhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
080.019. svagṛhaṃ gatvā nagaramadhye kārṣāpaṇānāṃ rāśiṃ vyavasthāpya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
080.021. yo draṣṭumicchati jinaṃ jitarāgadoṣaṃ nirbandhamapratisamaṃ karuṇāvadātam/
080.023. so 'niścareṇa hṛdayena suniścitena kṣipraṃ prayātu dhanamasya mayā pradeyam//3// iti//
body.translated_text:
080.002. If he spends a hundred or a thousand, it fills up again and is never exhausted.
080.003. Can you not come after paying sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>?' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the girl, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, set out.
080.004. She went, as if already knowing the way, somehow to the presence of the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>.
080.005. Having gone, she said: 'Householder, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends you greetings of good health.'
080.005. He said: 'I pay homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
080.006. 'Householder, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says thus: "I have come here on your account alone, yet you have barred the door and remain standing.
080.007. Is it proper to treat a guest in the way you have treated him?" He said: 'Girl, the guild made a resolution: No one shall approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> for an audience.
080.008. Whoever approaches him shall be fined sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> by the guild.'
080.009. 'Householder, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says: "Your son has a purse of five hundred tied at his waist.
080.010. If he spends a hundred or a thousand, it fills up again and is never exhausted.
080.011. Can you not come after paying sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>?" He reflected: 'No one else knows this.
080.011. Surely the <s>Bhagavān</s> is omniscient.
080.012. I shall go.'
080.012. He placed sixty <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> at the door and descended by the stairway shown by the Brahmin girl and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
080.013. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.
080.014. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character of the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
080.016. He, having seen the truth, said: 'Blessed One, will this townspeople of <s>Bhadraṃkara</s> also gain such excellent <s>Dharmas</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Householder, on your account, the greater part of the entire townspeople will gain them.'
080.018. Then the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
080.019. Having gone to his own house, he placed a heap of <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> in the middle of the city and spoke a verse:
080.021. 'Whoever wishes to see the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), who has conquered passion and hatred, who is incomparably steadfast, resplendent with compassion,
080.023. let him go quickly with a heart that is unwavering and resolute; the wealth for this shall be given by me.' // 3 // Thus.

body.text:
080.025. janakāyaḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, śreyaḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya darśanam? sa kathayati--śreyaḥ/
080.026. te kathayanti--yadyevam, gaṇenaivaṃ kriyākāraḥ kṛto gaṇa eva udghāṭayatu/
080.026. ko 'tra virodhah? te kriyākāramudghāṭya nirgantumārabdhāḥ/
080.027. tataḥ parasparaṃ saṃghaṭṭanena na śaknuvanti nirgantumiti vajrapāṇinā yakṣeṇa vineyajanānukampayā vajraḥ kṣiptaḥ/
080.028. prākārasya khaṇḍaḥ patitaḥ/
080.029. anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni, kānicit kutūhalajātāni, kānicit pūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni/
080.030. te gatvā bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purato niṣaṇṇāḥ/
080.031. yāvadbhagavataḥ sāmantakena parṣat saṃnipatitā/
080.031. atha baghavāṃstāṃ parṣadamabhyavagāhya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣadyānekasattvasaṃtānakuśalamūlasamāropikāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yām <81>śrutvā kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni/
body.translated_text:
080.025. The townspeople said: 'Householder, is it good to see the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' He said: 'It is good.'
080.026. They said: 'If so, since the guild made this resolution, let the guild itself revoke it.
080.026. What objection is there?' They revoked the resolution and began to go out.
080.027. Then, due to the mutual jostling, they could not get out, so <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> the <s>Yakṣa</s>, out of compassion for those to be guided, hurled his thunderbolt.
080.028. A section of the rampart collapsed.
080.029. Many hundreds of thousands of beings went out — some out of curiosity, some impelled by their former roots of merit.
080.030. Having gone and bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, they sat down before him.
080.031. In due course, an assembly gathered around the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
080.031. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having surveyed that assembly, sat down on the very seat prepared before the community of monks and delivered a <s>Dharma</s> teaching that planted roots of merit in the minds of many beings, upon hearing which some directly realized the fruit of stream-entry, and some took the refuges and precepts.

body.text:
081.002. bhagavato 'ci{taści}raṃ dharmaṃ deśayato bhojanakālo 'tikrāntaḥ/
081.002. meṇḍhako gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--bhagavan bhaktakṛtyaṃ kriyatāmiti/
081.003. bhagavānāha--gṛhapate, bhojanakālo 'tikrānta iti/
081.003. sa kathayati--bhagavan, kimakāle kalpate? bhagavānāha--dhṛtaguḍaśarkarāpānakāni ceti/
081.004. tato meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā śilpina āhūya uktāh--bhagavato 'kālakhādyakāni śīghraṃ sajjīkuruteti/
081.006. tairakālakāni sajjīkṛtāni/
081.006. tato meṇḍhakena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'kālakhādyakairakālapānakaiśca saṃtarpitaḥ/
081.007. tato bhagavān meṇḍhakaṃ gṛhapatiṃ saparivāraṃ satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ karvaṭanivāsinaṃ janakāyam yathābhavyatayā vinīya prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
081.002. While the <s>Bhagavān</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> for a long time, the mealtime passed.
081.002. The householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> said: 'Blessed One, let the meal be prepared.'
081.003. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Householder, the mealtime has passed.'
081.003. He said: 'Blessed One, what is permissible at an improper time?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Ghee, molasses, sugar, and beverages.'
081.004. Then the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> summoned the artisans and said: 'Quickly prepare untimely food for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
081.006. They prepared the untimely food.
081.006. Then the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> satisfied the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with untimely solid food and untimely beverages.
081.007. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having established the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> together with his retinue in the truths, and having guided the townspeople of the market-town according to their capacity for liberation, departed.

body.text:
081.009. idamavocadbhagavān/
081.009. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
081.009. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
081.009. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 081.010. iti śrīdivyāvadāne meṇḍhakagṛhapativibhūtiparicchedo navamaḥ//
body.translated_text: 081.010. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the chapter on the splendor of the householder <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, the ninth.

body.text: 082.001. div10 meṇḍhakāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 082.001. Chapter 10: The <s>Meṇḍhaka Avadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>).

body.text:
082.002. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta meṇḍhakena meṇḍhakapatnyā meṇḍhakaputreṇa meṇḍhakasnuṣayā meṇḍhakadāsena meṇḍhakadāsyā karma kṛtam yena ṣaḍabhijñātā mahāpuṇyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike satyāni dṛṣṭāni, bhagavāṃścaibhirārāgito na virāgita iti? bhagavānāha--ebhireva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
082.006. ebhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
082.007. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
082.010. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
082.011. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//1//
body.translated_text:
082.002. The monks, filled with doubt, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the dispeller of all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> was performed by <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>, <s>Meṇḍhaka's</s> wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka's</s> son, <s>Meṇḍhaka's</s> daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka's</s> male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka's</s> female servant, that they became possessors of the six superknowledges and of great merit, saw the truths in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> was pleased with them and not displeased?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By these very ones, monks, <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition.
082.006. By these, <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated.
082.007. Who else shall experience [their results]? Monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed ripen in the very <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) that have been appropriated, both wholesome and unwholesome.
082.010. <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons).
082.011. When the right combination and time are met, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // 1 //

body.text:
082.012. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskarogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannamakhilamakaṇṭakam/
082.014. ekaputramiva rājyaṃ pālayati/
082.015. tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ naimittikairdvādaśavarṣikā anāvṛṣṭirvyākṛtā/
082.016. trividhaṃ durbhikṣaṃ bhaviṣyati--cañcu śvetāsthi śalākāvṛtti ca/
082.016. tatra cañcu ucyate--samudgake tasmin manuṣyā bījāni prakṣipya anāgate sattvāpekṣayā sathāpayanti/
082.017. mṛtā nāma anena te bījakāyaṃ kariṣyantīti/
082.018. idaṃ samudgakaṃ baddhvā cañcu ucyate/
082.018. śvetāsthi nāma durbhikṣam--tasmin kāle manuṣyā asthīnyupasaṃhṛtya tāvat kvāthayanti, yāvat tānyasthīni śvetāni saṃvṛttānīti/
082.019. tatastatkvāthaṃ pibanti/
082.020. idaṃ śvetāsthi durbhikṣamityucayate/
082.020. śalākāvṛttir nāma--tasmin kāle manuṣyāḥ khalu bilebhyo dhānyaguḍakāni śalākayā ākṛṣya bahudakasthālyāṃ kvāthayitvā pibanti/
082.021. iyaṃ śalākāsambaddhatvācchalākāvṛttirityucyate/
082.022. tato rājñā brahmadattena vārāṇasyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--śṛṇvantu bhavanto vārāṇasīnivāsinaḥ paurāḥ/
082.023. naimittikairdvādaśavarṣikā anāvṛṣṭirvyākṛtā śalākāvṛtti durbhikṣaṃ cañcu śvetāsthi ca/
082.024. yeṣāṃ vo dvādaśavarṣikaṃ bhaktamasti, taiḥ sthātavyam/
082.025. yeṣāṃ nāsti, te yatheṣṭaṃ gacchantu/
082.025. vigatadurbhikṣabhayāḥ subhikṣe punarapyupāgamiṣyanti/
082.026. tasminśca samaye vārāṇasyāmanyatamo gṛhapatirāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaparivāraḥ/
082.027. tena koṣṭhāgārika āhūya uktah--bhoḥ puruṣa, bhaviṣyati me saparivārāṇāṃ me saparivārāṇāṃ dvādaśa varṣāṇi bhaktamiti? sa kathayati--ārya bhaviṣyatīti/
082.028. sa tatraivāvasthitaḥ/
082.028. samantarānubaddhaṃ caitat dubhikṣam/
082.029. tasya kośakoṣṭhāgārāḥ parikṣīṇāḥ/
082.029. sarvaśca parijanaḥ kālagataḥ/
082.029. ātmanā ṣaṣṭho vyavasthitaḥ/
082.030. tatastena gṛhapatinā kośakoṣṭhāgarāṇi śodhayitvā dhānyaprastha upasaṃhṛtaḥ/
082.031. so 'sya patnyā sthālyāṃ prakṣipya sādhitaḥ/
082.031. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
082.032. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho <83>janapadacārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ/
body.translated_text:
082.012. Once upon a time, O monks, in the past, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled over a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, free from strife, quarrels, disturbances, tumults, thieves, and diseases, abundant in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo — complete and untroubled.
082.014. He governed the kingdom as if it were his only son.
082.015. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the astrologers predicted a twelve-year drought.
082.016. There would be a threefold famine — <s>cañcu</s> (seed-hoarding), <s>śvetāsthi</s> (white-bone), and <s>śalākāvṛtti</s> (pin-subsistence).
082.016. Of these, <s>cañcu</s> is described thus: people place seeds in a casket and store them for the sake of future beings.
082.017. 'These are dead; by means of these, they will make a seed-body.'
082.018. This casket, being bound up, is called <s>cañcu</s>.
082.018. The <s>śvetāsthi</s> famine is as follows: at that time, people collect bones and boil them until those bones turn white.
082.019. Then they drink the broth.
082.020. This is called the <s>śvetāsthi</s> (white-bone) famine.
082.020. <s>Śalākāvṛtti</s> (pin-subsistence) is as follows: at that time, people extract grains of rice from rat-holes with a pin, boil them in a pot with much water, and drink it.
082.021. Because it is connected with a pin (<s>śalākā</s>), it is called <s>śalākāvṛtti</s>.
082.022. Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s> had a bell-proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Hear, O citizens and residents of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>!
082.023. The astrologers have predicted a twelve-year drought — <s>śalākāvṛtti</s> famine, <s>cañcu</s>, and <s>śvetāsthi</s>.
082.024. Those of you who have provisions for twelve years may remain.
082.025. Those who do not, let them go wherever they wish.
082.025. When the famine-fear has passed and prosperity returns, they may come back again.'
082.026. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain householder who was wealthy, of great riches, of great fortune, and with an extensive retinue.
082.027. He summoned the storehouse keeper and said: 'Good man, will there be provisions for me and my household for twelve years?' He replied: 'Yes, sir, there will be.'
082.028. So he remained there.
082.028. But the famine followed without interruption.
082.029. His storehouses and treasuries were exhausted.
082.029. All his household members had died.
082.029. He remained with only six persons including himself.
082.030. Then that householder, having swept the storehouses, gathered one <s>prastha</s> (measure) of grain.
082.031. His wife cooked it in a pot.
