082.031. When <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) appear — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, subsisting on food received at the outskirts, sole worthy recipients of offerings in the world.
082.032. Then a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

body.text:
083.001. sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vārāṇasīṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ/
083.002. sa ca gṛhapatirātmanā ṣaṣṭho 'vasthito bhoktum/
083.002. sa ca pratyekabuddho 'nupūrveṇa piṇḍapātamaṭaṃs tasya gṛhapatir niveśanamanuprāptaḥ/
083.003. sa tena gṛhapatinā dṛṣṭaścittaprāsādikaḥ kāyaprāsādikaśca/
083.004. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃlakṣayati--etadapyahaṃ parityajya niyataṃ prāṇairviyokṣye/
083.005. yannvahaṃ svapratyaṃśamasmai pravrajitāya dadyāmiti/
083.005. tena bhāryā abhihitā--bhadre, yo mama pratyaṃśastamahamasmai pravrajitāyānuprayacchāmīti/
083.006. sa saṃlakṣayati--mama svāmī na paribhuṅkte, kathamahaṃ paribhokṣya iti/
083.007. sā kathayati--āryaputra, ahamapi pratyaṃśamasmai prayacchāmi/
083.007. evaṃ putreṇa snuṣayā dāsena dāsyā ca vicārya svasvapratyaṃśāḥ parityaktāḥ/
083.008. tatastaiḥ sarvaiḥ saṃbhūya pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ/
083.009. kāyikī teṣāṃ mahātmanāṃ dharmadeśanā, na vācikī/
083.009. sa vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarāja upari vihāyasamudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ/
083.010. āśu pṛthagjanāvarjanakarī ṛddhiḥ/
083.011. te mūlanikṛttā iva drumāḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ/
083.012. gṛhapatiḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadi riktakāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi sahadarśanānme pūrṇāni syuh--evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
083.014. patnī praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekasyārthāya sthālīṃ paceyam, sā śatenāpi paribhujyeta, sahasreṇāpi, na parikṣayaṃ gacchet, yāvanmayā prayogo 'pratipraśrabdhaḥ, ityevaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhinī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
083.018. putraḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena pañcaśatiko nakulakaḥ kaṭyāmuparibaddhastiṣṭhet, yadi ca śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā tato vyayaṃ kuryāt, pūrṇa eva tiṣṭhet, mā parikṣayaṃ gacchet--evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāagayeyamiti/
083.022. snuṣā praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekasya gandham yojayeyam, śataṃ vā gandhaṃ ghrāsyati, taṃ na ca parikṣayaṃ gaccheyuryāvanmayā apratipraśrabdham--evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ labhinī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
083.025. dāsaḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekahalasīraṃ kṛṣeyam, sapta sīrāḥ kṛṣṭāḥ syuh--evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
083.028. dāsī praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhā--evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yadyekāṃ mātramārabheyam, sapta mātrāḥ saṃpadyeran--evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca labhinī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti/
083.030. taiścaivaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam/
083.031. sa ca mahātmā pratyekabuddhasteṣāmanukampayā ṛddhyā upari vihāyasā rājakulasyopariṣṭāt saṃprasthitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
083.001. In the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms.
083.002. The householder, with only six persons including himself, was seated to eat.
083.002. That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, going in due order for alms, arrived at the householder's dwelling.
083.003. He was seen by the householder, and inspired confidence by his appearance and bearing.
083.004. Having seen him, he reflected: 'Even if I give this up, I will surely die.
083.005. Let me give my own share to this renunciant.'
083.005. He said to his wife: 'Dear one, I shall give my own share to this renunciant.'
083.006. She reflected: 'If my husband does not eat, how shall I eat?'
083.007. She said: 'Noble husband, I too give my share to him.'
083.007. In the same way, the son, the daughter-in-law, the male servant, and the female servant each considered and relinquished their respective shares.
083.008. Then, all of them together provided the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> with alms-food.
083.009. The teaching of <s>Dharma</s> by those great beings is physical, not verbal.
083.009. Like the king of geese with wings spread, he rose up into the sky above and began to perform miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and flashing.
083.010. Swiftly does supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) win over ordinary people.
083.011. Like trees cut at the root, they fell at his feet and began to make aspirations.
083.012. The householder began to make his aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may my empty storehouses and treasuries become full at the very sight of them — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s> (teachings), and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.014. The wife began to make her aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may I cook a pot for the sake of one person, yet may it be enjoyed by a hundred, by a thousand, and never be exhausted for as long as I make the effort — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.018. The son began to make his aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may a five-hundred-piece purse (<s>nakulaka</s>) remain tied at my waist, and even if I spend a hundred or a thousand from it, may it remain full and never be exhausted — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.022. The daughter-in-law began to make her aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may I prepare fragrance for one person, yet may a hundred smell the fragrance, and may it never be exhausted for as long as I apply it — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.025. The male servant began to make his aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may I plow with a single plow, and seven furrows be plowed — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.028. The female servant began to make her aspiration: 'By the merit of this offering made to such a true and worthy recipient, may I begin one measure of grain, and seven measures be produced — and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I honor a Teacher even more distinguished than this, and may I never turn away from him.'
083.030. Thus they all made their aspirations.
083.031. That great <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, out of compassion for them, rose up into the sky by his supernatural power and set out over the royal palace.

body.text:
084.001. <84>tena khalu samayena rājā brahmadatta upariprāsādatalagatastiṣṭhati/
084.001. tasya ṛddhyā gacchato rājño brahmadattasyopari cchāyā nipatitā/
084.002. sa ūrdhvamukho nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ/
084.002. paśyati taṃ pratyekabuddham/
084.003. tasyaitadabhavat--kasyāpyanena mahātmanā ṛddhimahālāṅgalairdāridryamūlānyutpāṭitāni/
084.004. balavatī āśā/
084.004. tato 'sau gṛhapatiḥ kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi pratyavekṣitumārabdho yāvatpūrṇāni paśyati/
084.005. sa patnīmāmantrayate--mama tāvat praṇidhānaṃ pūrṇam, yuṣmākamapīdānīṃ paśyāma iti/
084.006. tato dāsyā dhānyānāmekāṃ mātrāmārabdhā parikarmayitum, sapta mātrāḥ saṃpannāḥ/
084.007. prātiveśyairanekaiśca prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ paribhuktam, tathaivāvasthitā/
084.008. tathaiva putrasya snuṣāyā dāsasya praṇidhiḥ siddhā/
084.009. tato gṛhapatinā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritaṃ vārāṇasyām--yo bhavanto 'nnenārthī, sa āgacchatu iti/
084.010. vārāṇasyāmuccaśabdho mahāśabdho jātaḥ/
084.010. rājñā śrutam/
084.010. kathayati--kimeṣa bhavanta uccaśabdo mahāśabda iti? amātyaiḥ samākhyātam--deva, amukena gṛhapatinā kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇi uddhāṭitānīti/
084.012. rājā tamāhūya kathayati--yadā eva lokaḥ kālagataḥ, tadā tvayā kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇyuddhāṭitānīti/
084.013. deva, kasya kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇyuddhāṭitāni? api tu adyaiva me bījamuptamadyaiva phaladāyakamiti/
084.014. rājā pṛcchati--yathā katham? sa etat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati/
084.015. rājā kathayati--gṛhapate, tvayā asau mahātmā piṇḍakena pratipāditah? deva mayaiva pratipāditaḥ/
084.016. so 'bhiprasanno gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
084.017. aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam/
084.018. yatroptaṃ bījamadyaiva adyaiva phaladāyakam//2// iti/
084.019. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau gṛhapatirgṛhapatipatnī gṛhapatiputro gṛhapatisnuṣā gṛhapatidāso gṛhapatidāsī, ayameva meṇḍhako gṛḥpatir meṇḍhakapatnī meṇḍhakaputro meṇḍhakasnuṣā meṇḍhakadāso meṇḍhakadāsī ca/
084.021. yadebhiḥ pratyekabuddhe kārān kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena ṣaḍ mahāpuṇyā jātāḥ, mamāntike dṛṣṭasatyāni/
084.022. ahaṃ caibhiḥ pratyekabuddhakoṭiśatasahasrebhyaḥ prativiśiṣṭaḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ/
084.023. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
084.025. tasmāttarhi evaṃ śikṣitavyam, yadekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
084.026. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text:
084.001. At that time, King <s>Brahmadatta</s> was standing on the upper terrace of the palace.
084.001. As the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> passed overhead by his supernatural power, his shadow fell upon King <s>Brahmadatta</s>.
084.002. He began to look upward.
084.002. He saw that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.
084.003. He thought: 'By this great being, with the great plow of supernatural power, someone's roots of poverty have been uprooted.'
084.004. His hope was strong.
084.004. Then that householder began to inspect his storehouses and treasuries, and found them full.
084.005. He called his wife and said: 'My aspiration has been fulfilled; now let us see about yours.'
084.006. Then the female servant began to prepare one measure of grain, and seven measures were produced.
084.007. Neighbors and many hundreds of thousands of beings ate from it, yet it remained the same.
084.008. Likewise, the aspirations of the son, the daughter-in-law, and the male servant were fulfilled.
084.009. Then the householder had a bell-proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Whoever among you needs food, let him come!'
084.010. A great and loud noise arose in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
084.010. The king heard it.
084.010. He asked: 'What is this great and loud noise?' The ministers reported: 'Your Majesty, such-and-such a householder has opened his storehouses and treasuries.'
084.012. The king summoned him and said: 'Just when the people were dying, you opened your storehouses and treasuries!'
084.013. 'Your Majesty, whose storehouses and treasuries have been opened? Rather, the seed I sowed today has borne fruit this very day.'
084.014. The king asked: 'How so?' He related the entire matter in detail.
084.015. The king said: 'Householder, was it you who provided that great being with alms-food?' 'Your Majesty, it was indeed I who provided it.'
084.016. Greatly pleased, he spoke a verse:
084.017. 'Oh, what a meritorious field, free from all faults!
084.018. Where a seed sown today bears fruit this very day!' // 2 //
084.019. What do you think, O monks? That householder, the householder's wife, the householder's son, the householder's daughter-in-law, the householder's male servant, and the householder's female servant — they are none other than <s>Meṇḍhaka</s> the householder, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s wife, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s son, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s daughter-in-law, <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s male servant, and <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>'s female servant.
084.021. Because they made offerings to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and made aspirations, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, six great meritorious ones were born, and they realized the truths in my presence.
084.022. And I, as a Teacher more distinguished than a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, have been honored by them, not turned away from.
084.023. Thus, O monks, the ripening of entirely dark <s>karmas</s> is entirely dark; the ripening of entirely bright <s>karmas</s> is entirely bright; the ripening of mixed <s>karmas</s> is mixed.
084.025. Therefore, you should train thus: abandoning entirely dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright <s>karmas</s>.
084.026. Thus, O monks, should you train.

body.text:
084.027. idamavocadbhagavān/
084.027. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
084.027. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
084.027. Those monks, delighted, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 084.028. iti śrīdivyāvadāne meṇḍhakāvadānaṃ daśamam//
body.translated_text: 084.028. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Meṇḍhaka Avadāna</s> (the Story of <s>Meṇḍhaka</s>), the tenth.

body.text: 085.001. div11 aśokavarNāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 085.001. Chapter 11: The <s>Aśokavarṇa Avadāna</s> (the Story of <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>).

body.text:
085.002. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
085.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairasurairyakṣairgauḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavāñ jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma markaṭasahasradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām/
085.006. tena khalu samayena vaiśālikā licchavaya idamevamrūpaṃ kriyākāramakārṣuh--pañcadaśyāṃ bhavantaḥ pakṣasya aṣṭamyāaṃ caturdaśyāṃ ca prāṇino hantavyā yatkāraṇameyurmanuṣyā māṃsamanveṣanta iti/
085.008. tena khalu samayena anyatamo goghātako mahāntaṃ vṛṣabhamādāya nagarānniṣkramati praghātayitum/
085.009. tamenaṃ mahājanakāyaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddho māṃsārthī kathayati--śīghramenaṃ vṛṣaṃ ghātaya, vayaṃ māṃsenārthina iti/
085.010. sa kathayati--evaṃ kariṣyāmi, kiṃ tu muhūrtamudīkṣadhvamiti/
085.011. tato vṛṣa īdṛśamanāryaṃ vaco duruktaṃ śrutvā bhītastrastaḥ saṃvignah āhṛṣṭaromakūpa itaścāmutaśca saṃbhrānto nirīkṣate, cintayati ca--ko māṃ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptamatrāṇamaśaraṇamiṣṭena jīvitenācchādayediti/
085.013. sa caivaṃ vihvalavadanastrāṇānveṣī tiṣṭhati/
085.014. bhagavāṃśca pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat/
085.015. athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakamam/
085.017. sahadarśanaiścāsya bhagavato 'ntike cittamabhiprasannam/
085.017. prasannacittaśca saṃlakṣayati--prāsādiko 'yaṃ sattvaviśeṣaḥ/
085.018. śakṣyatyeṣo mama prāṇaparitrāṇaṃ kartum/
085.019. yannvahamenamupasaṃkrameyamiti/
085.019. atha sa vṛṣo bhagavatyavekṣāvān pratibaddhacittah eṣo me śaraṇamiti sahasaiva tāni dṛḍhāni varatrakāṇi bandhanāni cchittvā pradhāvan yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
085.021. upasaṃkramyobhābhyāṃ jānubhyāṃ bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya pādau jihvayā nileḍhumārabdhaḥ/
085.022. sa cāsya raudrakarmā goghātakaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddha eva śastravyagrahastaḥ/
085.022. tato bhagavāṃstaṃ raudrakarmāṇaṃ goghātakamidamavocat--kuruṣva tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa anena govṛṣabheṇa sārdhaṃ sātmyam/
085.024. jīvitenācchādayeti/
085.024. sa kathayati--nāhaṃ bhadanta prabhavābhyenaṃ jīvitenācchādayitum/
085.024. tatkasya hetoh? mayā eṣa bahunā mūlyena krītaḥ/
085.025. putradāraṃ ca me bahu poṣitavyamiti/
085.025. bhagavānāha---yadi mūlyaṃ dīyate, pratimuñcasīti?/
085.026. sa kathayati--pratimokṣyāmi bhagavanniti/
085.026. atha bhagavāmllaukikacittamutpādayati--aho bata śakro devendrastrīṇi kārṣāpaṇasahasrāṇyādāyāgacchediti/
085.028. sahacittotpādādbhagavataḥ śakro devendraḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasratrayamādāya bhagavataḥ purastādasthāt/
085.029. atha bhagavāñ śakraṃ devendramidamavocat--anuprayaccha kauśika asya goghātakasya triguṇaṃ mūlyam/
085.030. adācchakro devendrastasya goghātakasya kārṣāpaṇatrayasahasraṃ vṛṣamūlyam/
085.030. atha goghātakaḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasrayaṃ vṛṣamūlyaṃ gṛhītvā hṛṣṭastuṣṭaḥ pramudito bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā taṃ govṛṣaṃ bandhanānmuktvā prakrāntaḥ/
085.032. śakro devendro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>—thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>—the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, known as one of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the <s>saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s> on the bank of the Markaṭa-sahasra, in the Gabled Hall. At that time, the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> had established this custom: on the fifteenth, the eighth, and the fourteenth days of the fortnight, living beings were to be slaughtered, because people would come seeking meat. At that time, a certain cattle-butcher, taking a great bull, went out from the city to slaughter it. A great crowd of people followed closely behind him, desiring meat, saying: "Quickly slaughter this bull! We want meat." He said: "I shall do so, but wait a moment." Then the bull, hearing such ignoble and harsh words, became frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, and looked about frantically in all directions, thinking: "Who will shelter me with the gift of life, when I have fallen into such distress, danger, and peril, without protection, without refuge?" And so he stood with a distressed face, seeking a protector. Now the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by a company of <s>bhikṣus</s> and preceded by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms. Then the bull saw the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being), his body resplendent with eighty secondary characteristics, ornamented with a fathom-wide aura, with radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, his mind became filled with faith. With a faithful mind he perceived: "This is a distinguished and gracious being. He will be able to grant me protection of life. Let me approach him." Then that bull, looking toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> with his mind fixed upon him, thinking "He is my refuge," suddenly broke through those strong leather straps and bonds, and ran swiftly to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was. Having approached, he fell on both knees at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and began licking his feet with his tongue. That cruel-working cattle-butcher followed closely behind, weapon in hand. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to that cruel-working cattle-butcher: "Good man, make peace with this bull. Shelter him with life." He said: "Venerable sir, I am not able to shelter him with life. Why is that? I purchased him for a great price, and I have a wife and children to feed." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "If the price is given, will you release him?" He said: "I will release him, <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated a worldly thought: "If only <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, would come bringing three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>." The moment the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated this thought, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, taking three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>: "Give to this cattle-butcher, <s>Kauśika</s>, triple the price." <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, gave to that cattle-butcher three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as the price of the bull. Then the cattle-butcher, having received the three thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as the bull's price, delighted, pleased, and overjoyed, bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, released the bull from his bonds, and departed. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet and vanished right there.

body.text:
086.001. <86>atha govṛṣo gatapratyāgataprāṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā bhagavatyabhiprasanno bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddho bhagavato mukhaṃ vyavalokayamāno 'sthāt/
086.002. atha bhagavān smitamakārṣīt/
086.003. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātāḥ puṣpaparāgapadmarāgavajravaiḍūryamuasāragalvārkalohitakādakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti, kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti/
086.006. yā adhastādgacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvamutpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaparyantān narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti, ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti/
086.008. tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante/
086.009. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, āhosvidanyatropapannā iti/
086.009. teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati/
086.010. teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃ bhavati--na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, nāpyanyatropapannā iti/
086.011. api tvayamapūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti/
086.012. te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhir gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti/
086.013. yā upariṣṭādgacchanti, tāścāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānabṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhaparyantān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyuddhoṣayanti/
086.017. gāthādvayaṃ bhāṣante--
086.018. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
086.019. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//1//
body.translated_text: Then the bull, his life-breath having departed and returned, with even greater faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, followed closely behind, and stood gazing at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> face. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> smiled. For it is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, manifest a smile, at that time rays of blue, yellow, red, and white—the colors of flower-pollen, ruby, diamond, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, <s>musāragalva</s>, sunstone, right-spiraling conch-shell, crystal, coral, gold, and silver—issue forth from their mouths: some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having reached the hells extending from <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, to <s>Mahāpadma</s>—in the hot hells they fall as coolness, in the cold hells they fall as warmth. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are relieved. They think: "Have we, friends, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical creation. Having seen that creation, they think: "Indeed we have not, friends, passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, and by his power our distinctive sufferings have been relieved." Having generated faith in the magical creation, and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> (action) to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among <s>devas</s> and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward, having reached the <s>devas</s> of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, up to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>—they proclaim: "Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!" They speak two verses: "Strive forth, go forth, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching! Crush the army of death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!"

body.text:
086.020. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
086.021. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//2// iti/
086.022. atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti/
086.023. tadyadi bhagavānatītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante/
086.024. anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastādantardhīyante/
086.024. narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale-ntardhīyante/
086.025. tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante/
086.025. pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante/
086.026. manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunorantardhīyante/
086.027. balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante/
086.027. cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante/
086.028. devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyāmantardhīyante/
086.029. śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante/
086.029. pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante/
086.030. anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante/
086.031. atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyāmantarhitāḥ//
body.translated_text: "For whoever shall dwell heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline), having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering." Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, followed closely behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (minor universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth among <s>devas</s>, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (the tuft between his brows). If he wishes to prophesy <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance). Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>ūrṇā</s>.

body.text:
086.032. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--
086.033. nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "A cluster of manifold rays, decorated with a thousand colors, has issued forth from within your mouth,

body.text: 087.001. <87>avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva//3//
body.translated_text: illuminating the directions on all sides, just as by the sun at its rising."

body.text:
087.003. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣite--
087.004. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
087.006. nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ//4//
body.translated_text: And he spoke a verse: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from birth, having abandoned wretchedness and pride, the supreme causes in the world, the <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors) who have vanquished their foes, do not display a smile white as conch and lotus-stalk without reason."

body.text:
087.008. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīra buddhyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
087.010. dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//5//
body.translated_text: "Having yourself realized at the proper time through wisdom, O steadfast <s>Śramaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Jinas</s>, for the listeners who are filled with longing, O bull among sages, with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, dispel the doubt that has arisen."

body.text:
087.012. nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ/
087.014. yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrā staṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ//6// iti//
body.translated_text: "Not without cause do the fully awakened protectors, firm as the salt-ocean mountain, display a smile. That for the sake of which the steadfast ones display a smile—those crowds of people wish to hear."

body.text:
087.016. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametat/
087.016. nāhetvapratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
087.017. dṛṣṭaste ānanda ayaṃ govṛṣah? dṛṣṭo bhadanta/
087.017. eṣa ānanda govṛṣastathāgatasyāntike prasannacittaḥ saptame divase kālaṃ kṛtvā cātrumahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.019. vaiśravaṇasya mahārājasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.019. tataścyutvā trāyastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.020. śakrasya devendrasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.020. tataścyutvā yāmeṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.020. yāmasya devasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.021. tataścyutvā tuṣiteṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.021. sa tuṣitasya devasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.022. tataścyutvā nirmāṇaratiṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.022. sunirmitasya devaputrasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.022. tataścyutvā parinirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣūpapatsyate/
087.023. vaśavaratino devaputrasya putro bhaviṣyati/
087.023. tadanayā saṃtatyā navanavatikalpasahasrāṇi vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati/
087.024. tataḥ kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu divyaṃ sukhamanubhūya paścime bhave paścime nikete samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe manuṣyatvaṃ pratilabhya rājā bhaviṣyati aśokavarṇo nāma cakravartī caturarṇavāntavijetā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ/
087.027. tasyemānyevamrūpāṇi sapta ratnāni bhaviṣyanti/
087.027. tadyathā--cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam/
087.028. pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇā parasainyapramardakānām/
087.029. imāmeva samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthivīmakhilāmakaṇṭakāmanutpīḍāmadaṇḍenāśastreṇa dharmyeṇa samayenābhinirjitya adhyāvatsyati/
087.031. so 'pareṇa samayena dānāni datvā cakravartirājyamapahāya keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi ...ṣamyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajya pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkariṣyati, aśokavarṇo nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati/
087.033. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--kiṃ bhadanta anena govṛṣeṇa karma kṛtam yena tiryagyonāvupapannaḥ, kiṃ karma kṛtam yena divyamānuṣasukhamanubhūya <88>pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigamiṣyati? bhagavānāha--anenaiva ānanda govṛṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: 'It is so, <s>Ānanda</s>, it is so. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, display a smile. Have you seen, <s>Ānanda</s>, this bull? Yes, Venerable Sir. This bull, <s>Ānanda</s>, with a mind of faith toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, on the seventh day will die and be reborn among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven. He will become the son of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the great king. Falling from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. He will become the son of <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods. Falling from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Yāma</s> gods. He will become the son of the god <s>Yāma</s>. Falling from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods. He will become the son of the god <s>Tuṣita</s>. Falling from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods. He will become the son of the divine son <s>Sunirmita</s>. Falling from there, he will be reborn among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods. He will become the son of the divine son <s>Vaśavartin</s>. By this continuity, for ninety-two thousand <s>kalpas</s> (eons), he will not fall into a lower realm. Then, having experienced divine happiness among the gods of the desire realm, in his last existence, last abode, last birth, last bodily form, having obtained human birth, he will become a king named <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), conqueror of the four seas, a righteous <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of righteousness), endowed with the seven treasures. His seven treasures will be of this kind, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the commander-treasure as the seventh. He will have a full thousand sons, heroes and warriors, of excellent form, crushers of enemy armies. He will conquer and dwell upon this entire great earth, bounded by the ocean, whole, without thorns, without oppression, without punishment, without weapons, by righteous means. Then, at a later time, having given gifts, having renounced his sovereignty as a <s>Cakravartin</s>, having shaved off his hair and beard, having put on the saffron robes... with perfect faith, having gone forth from home to homelessness, he will directly realize solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); he will become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joined palms, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> (deed) was done by this bull that he was born in an animal womb? What <s>karma</s> was done that, having experienced divine and human happiness, he will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>)?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By this very bull, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>karmas</s> were done and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably to bear fruit.'

body.text:
088.002. govṛṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
088.003. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na hyānanda karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāśubhāni ca/
088.006. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatairapi/
088.007. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//7//
body.translated_text: By the bull were <s>karmas</s> done and accumulated. Who else shall experience their results? For indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>karmas</s> that have been done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> that have been done ripen in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), both wholesome and unwholesome. <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (eons); having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.

body.text:
088.008. bhūtapūrvamānanda atīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
088.010. sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīmupaniśritya viharati, anyatamasmin vanaṣaṇḍe/
088.010. tasya nātidūre ṣaṣṭibhikṣavaḥ prativasantyāraṇyakāḥ piṇḍapātikāḥ/
088.011. sarve ca vītarāgā vigatadveṣā vigatamohā yāvat pañcamātrāṇi dhūrtakaśatāni tena tenāhiṇḍyamānāni taṃ pradeśamanuprāptāni/
088.013. teṣāmetadabhavat--ete hi pravrajitā mahātmānah īdṛśeṣu sthāneṣvabhiramante/
088.013. yadyeṣāṃ jīvitopacchedaṃ na kariṣyāmaḥ, na bhūya etasmin pradeśe svasthairvihartavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
088.014. yadyapyete mahātmānaḥ sarvasattvahitodayapravṛttā na pareṣāmārocayiṣyanti, tathāpyeṣāṃ pradhānapuruṣā upasaṃkramiṣyanti/
088.016. te 'smākaṃ rājñaḥ samarpayiṣyanti/
088.016. tatrāsmābhiścārakāvaruddhairmartavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
088.017. kathamatra pratipattavyamiti? ekastatraiva nirghṛṇahṛdayastyaktaparalokaḥ/
088.017. sa kathayati--aghātayitvā etān kutaḥ kṣema iti? taiste jīvitādvyaparopitāḥ/
088.018. te caitatkarma kṛtvā pāpakamakuśalamekanavatikalpānapāyeṣūpapannāḥ/
088.019. yadbhūyasā tu narakeṣu tiryagyonau upapannāśca santo nityaṃ śastreṇa praghātitāḥ/
088.020. tatra yo 'sau caurasteṣāṃ samādāpakaḥ, sa evāyaṃ govṛṣaḥ/
088.020. tasya karmaṇo vipākena iyantaṃ kālaṃ na kadācit sugatau upapannaḥ/
088.021. yatpunaridānīṃ mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena divyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukhamanubhūya pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigamiṣyati/
088.023. evaṃ hi ānanda tathāgatānāṃ cittaprasādo 'pyacintyavipākaḥ, kiṃ punaḥ praṇidhānam/
088.024. tasmāttarhi ānanda evaṃ śikṣitavyam yatstokastokaṃ muhūrtamuhūrtamantato 'cchaṭāsaṃghātamātramapi tathāgatamākārataḥ samanusmariṣyāmītyevaṃ te ānanda śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a perfectly awakened one named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone one), a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, in a certain forest grove. Not far from him, sixty monks lived — forest-dwellers and alms-round practitioners. All were free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion. Meanwhile, as many as five hundred rogues, wandering here and there, arrived at that place. They thought: 'These renunciants, great souls, delight in such places. If we do not put an end to their lives, we shall never again be able to dwell at ease in this place. Although these great souls, devoted to the welfare of all beings, will not report us to others, nevertheless their chief followers will approach them. They will hand us over to the king. There, caught by the guards, we shall have to die. What is to be done here?' One among them was of a merciless heart, one who had cast away regard for the next world. He said: 'Without killing them, how can there be safety?' So they put them to death. And having committed this deed, that evil, unwholesome act, for ninety-one thousand <s>kalpas</s> they were reborn in the lower realms. For the most part they were born in hells and in animal wombs, and were constantly slain by weapons. There, the one who was the ringleader among the thieves who incited them — he is this very bull. As the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for this long a time he has never once been reborn in a fortunate destination. But now, having generated faith in his mind toward me, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, having experienced divine and human happiness, he will attain solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>). Thus indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>, even the generation of faith toward a <s>Tathāgata</s> bears inconceivable fruit — how much more so a formal aspiration! Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should train yourself thus: 'Little by little, moment by moment, even for the duration of a finger-snap, I shall recollect the <s>Tathāgata</s> in his true form.' Thus should you train yourself, <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text:
088.026. athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyānandyānumodya bhikṣūṇāṃ purastādgāthā bhāṣate--
088.027. aho nāthasya kāruṇyaṃ sarvajñasya hitaiṣiṇaḥ/
088.028. sukṛtenaiva vātsalyam yasyedṛśamahodbhutam//8//
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having rejoiced and approved of the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke verses before the monks: 'Oh, the compassion of the Protector, the Omniscient One who seeks the welfare of all!'

body.text:
088.029. āpanno hi paraṃ kṛcchraṃ govṛṣo yena mocitaḥ/
088.030. vyākṛtaśca bhave divye pratyekaśca jino hyasau//9// iti//
body.translated_text: 'Such wonderful affection through merit alone toward this bull who had reached the utmost distress, by whom he was liberated; and he was prophesied for divine existence and as a solitary victor (<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>).' Thus.

body.text:
088.031. idamavocadbhagavān/
088.031. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: This was spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at his words.

body.text: 088.032. iti śrīdivyāvadāne 'śokavarṇāvadānamekādaśamam//
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Aśokavarṇāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Aśokavarṇa</s>), the eleventh.

body.text: 089.001. div12 prātihāryasūtram/
body.translated_text: Chapter 12: The <s>Prātihāryasūtra</s> (The Miracle Discourse).

body.text: 089.002. sa bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrairdhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhairdevair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍaiḥ kinnarairmahoragairiti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bagavāñ jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho divyānāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ ca bhagavānanupalipto viharati padmapatramivāmbhasā//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground), honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known as one of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines for the sick, together with his community of disciples, lived untouched by worldly things, as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.

body.text:
089.007. tena khalu samayena rājagṛhe nagare ṣaṭ pūrṇādyāḥ śāstāro 'sarvajñāḥ sarvajñamāninaḥ prativasanti sma/
089.008. tadyathā--pūrṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ, maskarī gośālīputraḥ, saṃjayī vairaṭṭīputraḥ, ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ, kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ, nirgrantho jñātiputraḥ/
089.009. atha ṣaṇṇāṃ pūrṇādīnāṃ tīrthyānāṃ kutūhalaśālāyāṃ saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃrūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ -- yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran--yadā śramaṇo gautamo loke 'nutpannaḥ, tadā vayaṃ satkṛtāścābhūvan gurukṛtāśca mānitāśca pūjitāśca rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ naigamānāṃ jānapadānāṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānām/
089.013. lābhīnaścābhūvaṃścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām/
089.014. yadā tu śramaṇo gautamo loke utpannaḥ, tadā śramaṇo gautamaḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājñāṃ rājamātrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ janapadānāṃ dhanināṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānām/
089.015. lābhī ca śramaṇo gautamaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghaścīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām/
089.017. asmākaṃ ca lābhasatkāraḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ samucchinnaḥ/
089.017. vayaṃ sma ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ/
089.018. śramaṇo 'pi gautamo riddhimāñ jñāvādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
089.018. arhati jñāvādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
089.019. yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautamo 'nuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ dve/
089.020. dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ catvāri/
089.020. catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayamaṣṭau/
089.021. aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa/
089.021. ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tattriguṇaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ/
089.023. upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu, vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ/
089.024. tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
089.024. atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat--asakṛdasakṛnmayā śramaṇasya gautamasya prākrāntam, na ca kadācidavatāro labdhaḥ/
089.026. yannvahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ prahareyam/
089.026. iti viditvā pūraṇavadātmānamabhinirmāya upari vihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā maskariṇaṃ gośālīputramāmantrayate--yatkhalu maskariñ jānīyāh--ahaṃ riddhimāñ jñānavādī, śramaṇo gautamo riddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ parijānīte/
089.029. arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
089.030. yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, ahaṃ dve/
089.031. dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ catvāri/
089.031. catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahamaṣṭau/
089.031. aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ ṣoḍaśa/
089.032. ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo <90>gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ taddviguṇamuttaraṃ manuṣyadharmaṃ riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ/
body.translated_text:
089.007. At that time, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, six teachers headed by <s>Pūraṇa</s> — not omniscient yet thinking themselves omniscient — were dwelling.
089.008. Namely: <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Saṃjayī Vairaṭṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s>.
089.009. Then the six <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretical teachers) headed by <s>Pūraṇa</s>, gathered and assembled in their debating hall, had this kind of conversation among themselves: 'As you venerable ones may know — when the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> had not arisen in the world, we were honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, Brahmins, householders, townsfolk, countryfolk, guild-masters, and caravan-leaders.
089.013. We were recipients of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines and provisions for the sick.
089.014. But when the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> arose in the world, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> became honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, Brahmins, householders, countryfolk, the wealthy, guild-masters, and caravan-leaders.
089.015. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> together with his community of disciples became the recipient of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines and provisions for the sick.
089.017. Our gains and honor have been completely cut off.
089.017. We are possessors of supernatural power and proclaimers of knowledge.
089.018. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> too declares himself to be a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge.
089.018. It is fitting that one proclaimer of knowledge should display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another proclaimer of knowledge.
089.019. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, we shall display two.
089.020. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we shall display four.
089.020. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we shall display eight.
089.021. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we shall display sixteen.
089.021. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we shall display thirty-two — and so on, whatever miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, we shall display double and triple that.
089.023. Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come halfway, and we too shall go halfway.
089.024. There let our contest of the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> take place.'
089.024. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One had this thought: 'Again and again I have striven against the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, but never have I found an opening.
089.026. Let me now incite the <s>tīrthyas</s>.'
089.026. Knowing this, he magically created a form like <s>Pūraṇa</s>, rose up into the sky, performed miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and flashing, and addressed <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>: 'As you, <s>Maskarī</s>, should know — I am a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> declares himself to be a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge.
089.029. It is fitting that one proclaimer of knowledge should display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another proclaimer of knowledge.
089.030. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, I shall display two.
089.031. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, I shall display four.
089.031. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, I shall display eight.
089.031. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, I shall display sixteen.
089.032. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, I shall display thirty-two — and so on, whatever miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, we shall display double that miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text:
090.002. upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu, ahamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmi/
090.003. tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
090.004. atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat--asakṛdasakṛnmayā śramaṇasya gautamasya parākrāntam, na ca kadācidavatāro labdhaḥ/
090.005. yannvahaṃ tīrthyānāṃ prahareyam/
090.005. iti viditvā maskarivadātmānamabhinirmāya upari vihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavidyotanavarṣaṇaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā saṃjayinaṃ vairaṭṭīputramāmantrayate--yatkhalu saṃjayiñ jānīyāh--ahaṃ riddhimāñ jñānavādī, śramaṇo gautamo riddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
090.008. arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
090.009. yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, ahaṃ dve/
090.010. dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ catvāri/
090.010. catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahamaṣṭau/
090.011. aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ ṣoḍaśa/
090.011. ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ, ahaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, ahaṃ taddviguṇamuttaraṃ manuṣyadharmaprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi/
090.013. upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu, ahamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmi/
090.014. tatra me bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
090.015. evamanyonyaṃ sarve viheṭhitāḥ/
090.015. ekaika evamāha--riddherlābhī nāhamiti//
body.translated_text:
090.002. 'Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come halfway, and I too shall go halfway.
090.003. There let our contest of the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> take place.'
090.004. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One had this thought: 'Again and again I have striven against the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, but never have I found an opening.
090.005. Let me now incite the <s>tīrthyas</s>.'
090.005. Knowing this, he magically created a form like <s>Maskarī</s>, rose up into the sky, performed miracles of blazing, burning, flashing, and raining, and addressed <s>Saṃjayī Vairaṭṭīputra</s>: 'As you, <s>Saṃjayī</s>, should know — I am a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> declares himself to be a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge.
090.008. It is fitting that one proclaimer of knowledge should display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another proclaimer of knowledge.
090.009. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, I shall display two.
090.010. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, I shall display four.
090.010. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, I shall display eight.
090.011. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, I shall display sixteen.
090.011. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, I shall display thirty-two — and so on, whatever miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, I shall display double that miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
090.013. Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come halfway, and I too shall go halfway.
090.014. There let my contest of the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> take place.'
090.015. In the same way, all of them were mutually deceived.
090.015. Each one said: 'I am not a possessor of supernatural power.'

body.text:
090.016. pūraṇādyāḥ ṣaṭ śāstāraḥ sarvajñajñānino yena rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastenopasaṃkrāman/
090.017. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāramidamavocan--yatkhalu deva jānīyāh--vayam ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ/
090.018. śramaṇo 'pi gautamo riddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
090.018. arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
090.019. yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ dve/
090.020. dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ catvāri/
090.021. catvāri śramaṇo gautama, vayamaṣṭau/
090.021. aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa/
090.021. ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tatriguṇaṃ riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ/
090.023. upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu, vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ/
090.024. tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
090.025. evamukte rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastīrthyānidamavocat--yūyamapi śavā bhūtvā bhagavatā sārdhaṃ riddhiṃ prārabhadhve? atha pūraṇādyāḥ ṣaṭ śāstāro 'sarvajñāḥ sarvajñānajñānino 'rdhamārge rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ vijñāpayanti--vayaṃ smo deva riddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ/
090.028. śramaṇo 'pi gautamo riddhimāñ jñānavādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
090.029. arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
090.030. yāvat tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
090.031. evamukte rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastāṃstīrthikaparivrājakānidamavocat--yadyevaṃ trirapyetamarthaṃ vijñāpayiṣyatha, nirviṣayān vaḥ kariṣyāmi/
090.032. atha tīrthyānāmetadabhavat--ayaṃ rājā <91>māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya śrāvakaḥ/
body.translated_text:
090.016. The six teachers headed by <s>Pūraṇa</s>, who were not omniscient yet thought themselves omniscient, approached King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>.
090.017. Having approached, they said this to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>: 'As Your Majesty should know — we are possessors of supernatural power and proclaimers of knowledge.
090.018. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> too declares himself to be a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge.
090.018. It is fitting that one proclaimer of knowledge should display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another proclaimer of knowledge.
090.019. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, we shall display two.
090.020. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we shall display four.
090.021. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we shall display eight.
090.021. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we shall display sixteen.
090.021. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we shall display thirty-two — and so on, whatever miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays, we shall display double and triple that miracle of supernatural power.
090.023. Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come halfway, and we too shall go halfway.
090.024. There let our contest of the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> take place.'
090.025. When this was said, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> said this to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'Even dead men would you challenge the <s>Bhagavān</s> to a contest of supernatural power?' Then the six teachers headed by <s>Pūraṇa</s>, who were not omniscient yet thought themselves omniscient, appealed to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> halfway through the conversation: 'We, Your Majesty, are possessors of supernatural power and proclaimers of knowledge.
090.028. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> too declares himself to be a possessor of supernatural power and a proclaimer of knowledge.
090.029. It is fitting that one proclaimer of knowledge should display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another proclaimer of knowledge.
090.030. Up to: There let our contest of the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> with the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> take place.'
090.031. When this was said, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> said this to those <s>tīrthya</s> wanderers: 'If you bring up this matter even a third time, I shall banish you from my realm.'
090.032. Then the <s>tīrthyas</s> had this thought: 'This King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> is a disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.'

body.text:
091.001. bimbisārastiṣṭhatu/
091.001. rājā prasenajit kauśalo madhyasthaḥ/
091.002. yadā śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrāvastīṃ gamiṣyati, tatra vayaṃ gatvā śramaṇaṃ gautamamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihārye āhvayiṣyāmaḥ/
091.003. ityuktvā prakrāntāḥ//
body.translated_text:
091.001. 'Let <s>Bimbisāra</s> be.
091.001. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> is neutral.
091.002. When the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> goes to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, we shall go there and challenge the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> to the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.'
091.003. Having said this, they departed.

body.text:
091.004. atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro 'nyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa kṣipram/
091.005. bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojaya, yatrāhamadhiruhya bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi paryupāsanāyai/
091.006. evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājño māgadhasya śreṇyasya bimbisārasya pratiśrutya kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā yena rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
091.007. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāramidamavocat--yuktaṃ devasya bhadraṃ yānaṃ yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyata iti/
091.008. atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhadraṃ yānamabhiruhya rājagṛhānniryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya/
091.010. tasya yāvatī yānasya bhūmistāvadyānena gatvā yānādavatīrya padbhyāmevārāmaṃ prāvikṣat/
091.011. antarā rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavantamadrākṣīt/
091.012. tadantarā pañca kakudānyapanīya tadyathā--uṣṇīṣaṃ chatraṃ khaḍgamaṇiṃ vālavyajanaṃ citre copānahau, sa pañca kakudānyapanīya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
091.013. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
091.014. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ viditvā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
091.015. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
091.016. atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavantamabhyānandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
091.004. Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> addressed a certain man: 'Go quickly, good man.
091.005. Harness a fine chariot, so that I may mount it and approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience and attendance.'
091.006. 'So be it, Your Majesty,' the man, having assented to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, quickly harnessed the fine chariot and approached King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>.
091.007. Having approached, he said this to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>: 'Your Majesty's fine chariot is harnessed; may Your Majesty do what he considers timely.'
091.008. Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, mounting the fine chariot, set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience and attendance.
091.010. Having gone by chariot as far as the ground was suitable for a chariot, he descended from the chariot and entered the monastery on foot.
091.011. On the way, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
091.012. In the interval, he removed the five insignia of royalty, namely: the turban, the parasol, the sword-jewel, the yak-tail fan, and the ornate sandals. Having removed the five insignia of royalty, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
091.013. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side.
091.014. Knowing that King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> was seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
091.015. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
091.016. Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and departed from the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
091.019. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--kutra pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām? devatā bhagavata ārocayanti--śrutapūrvaṃ bhadanta pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti/
091.021. bhagavato jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate--śrāvastyāṃ pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti/
091.022. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha tvamānanda, bhikṣūṇāmārocaya/
091.023. tathāgataḥ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
091.024. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cartum, sa cīvarakāṇi dhāvatu sīvyatu rañjayatu/
091.025. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati--bhagavānāyuṣmantaḥ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
091.026. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritum, sa cīvarāṇi dhāvatu sīvyatu rañjayatu iti/
091.027. te bhikṣava āyuṣmata ānandasya pratyaśrauṣuḥ/
091.028. atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gaja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭṭagaṇaparivṛto rājahaṃsa iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto<92> deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva pauragaṇaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaścakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaścandra iva
nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto vemacitra ivāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmeva
brahmakāyikagaṇaparivṛtaḥ stimiva iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntairindriyairasaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro 'nekairāveṇikairbuddhadharmairmahatā bhikṣusaṃghena ca puraskṛto yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text:
091.019. Then the Blessed One thought: 'Where did the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> display the great miracle for the benefit of living beings?' The deities reported to the Blessed One: 'It has been heard, Venerable Sir, that the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> displayed the great miracle for the benefit of living beings.'
091.021. The knowledge-vision of the Blessed One arose: 'At <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> displayed the great miracle for the benefit of living beings.'
091.022. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, announce to the monks.
091.023. The <s>Tathāgata</s> will go on a wandering tour through the <s>Kośala</s> countries.
091.024. Whoever among you is willing to go on a wandering tour with the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Kośala</s> countries, let him wash, sew, and dye his robes.'
091.025. 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One and announced to the monks: 'The Blessed One, Venerable Ones, will go on a wandering tour through the <s>Kośala</s> countries.
091.026. Whoever among you is willing to go on a wandering tour with the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Kośala</s> countries, let him wash, sew, and dye his robes.'
091.027. Those monks assented to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
091.028. Then the Blessed One — tamed, with a tamed retinue; tranquil, with a tranquil retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; at ease, with a retinue at ease; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with a retinue of <s>Arhats</s>; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring confidence, with a retinue inspiring confidence — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle, like an elephant surrounded by young elephants, like a lion surrounded by a troop of fanged beasts, like a king of geese surrounded by a flock of geese, like a <s>Suparṇī</s> (Garuḍa) surrounded by a flock of birds, like a learned man surrounded by a group of disciples, like a skilled physician surrounded by a group of patients, like a hero surrounded by a band of warriors, like a guide surrounded by a group of travelers, like a caravan-leader surrounded by a company of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by the townsfolk, like a fortress-king surrounded by a company of ministers, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>, like <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Vemacitri</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by a host of the Thirty-Three, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods — like a still ocean, like a rain-cloud full of water, like a rutless elephant, with well-tamed faculties and an undisturbed deportment, with a great assembly of monks at the fore, and endowed with many special qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, he set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text: 092.007. anekaiśca devatāśatasahasrairanugamyamāno 'nupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme//
body.translated_text: 092.007. Accompanied by many hundreds of thousands of deities, wandering in due order, he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> he dwelt in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

body.text:
092.010. aśrauṣustīrthyāḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ śrāvastīṃ gata iti/
092.010. śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastīṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
092.011. te śrāvastīṃ gatvā rājānaṃ prasenajitkauśalamidamavocan--yatkhalu deva jānīthāh--vayam ṛddhimanto jñānavādinaḥ/
092.012. śramaṇo gautamo ṛddhimāñ jñāvādītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
092.013. arhati jñānavādī jñānavādinā sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
092.013. yadyekaṃ śramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ dve/
092.014. dve śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ catvāri/
092.015. catvāri śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayamaṣṭau/
092.015. aṣṭau śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ ṣoḍaśa/
092.015. ṣoḍaśa śramaṇo gautamaḥ, vayaṃ dvātriṃśaditi yāvacchramaṇo gautama uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati, vayaṃ taddviguṇaṃ tattriguṇamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmaḥ/
092.017. upārdhaṃ mārgaṃ śramaṇo gautama āgacchatu, vayamapyupārdhaṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ/
092.018. tatrāsmākaṃ bhavatu śramaṇena gautamena sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
092.019. evamukte rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--āgamayantu tāvadbhavanto yāvadahaṃ bhagavantamavalokayāmi/
092.020. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nyatamaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa/
092.021. kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojaya/
092.022. ahamabhiruhya adyaiva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramiṣyāmi paryupāsanāyai/
092.022. evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya kṣipraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā yena rājā prasenajit kauśalastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
092.024. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat--yuktaṃ devasya bhadraṃ yānaṃ yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyate/
092.025. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhadraṃ yānamabhiruhya śrāvastyā niryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya upasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya/
092.027. tasya yāvatī yānasya bhūmistāvadyānena gatvā yānādavatārya pādābhyāmeva ārāmaṃ praviśya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
092.028. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
092.029. ekānte niṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat--ime bhadanta tīrthyā bhagavantamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryeṇāhvayante/
092.030. vidarśayatu bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām/
092.031. nirbhartsayatu bhagavāṃstīrthyān/
092.031. nandayatu devamanuṣyān/
092.031. toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi/
092.032. evamukte bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat--nāhaṃ mahārāja <93>evaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi evam yūyaṃ bhikṣava āgatāgatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayateti/
body.translated_text:
092.010. The <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics) heard: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.'
092.010. Having heard this, they set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
092.011. Having gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, they said this to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'May Your Majesty know this — we possess supernatural powers and claim to be knowers of truth.
092.012. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> also claims to possess supernatural power and to be a knower of truth.
092.013. It is fitting that one who claims to be a knower of truth should display the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) in the higher human <s>dharma</s> against another such claimant.
092.013. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays one miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, we shall display two.
092.014. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays two, we shall display four.
092.015. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays four, we shall display eight.
092.015. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays eight, we shall display sixteen.
092.015. If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays sixteen, we shall display thirty-two — and so on: whatever the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays as a miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>, we shall display double that, triple that.
092.017. Let the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> come halfway along the road, and we too shall go halfway.
092.018. There let there be a contest between us and the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> in the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.'
092.019. When this was said, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'Wait, Sirs, while I consult the Blessed One.'
092.020. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> addressed a certain man: 'Go, good man.
092.021. Quickly harness a fine chariot.
092.022. I shall mount it and go this very day to see and attend upon the Blessed One.'
092.022. 'So be it, Your Majesty,' that man assented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, quickly harnessed a fine chariot, and approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>.
092.024. Having approached, he said to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'Your Majesty's fine chariot is ready; let Your Majesty proceed at whatever time he thinks fit.'
092.025. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, mounting the fine chariot, departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to approach the Blessed One for an audience and attendance.
092.027. Having gone by chariot as far as the ground permitted, he descended from the chariot and entered the park on foot, and approached the Blessed One.
092.028. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
092.029. Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, these <s>tīrthyas</s> challenge the Blessed One to a miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
092.030. May the Blessed One display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> for the benefit of living beings.
092.031. May the Blessed One rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>.
092.031. May he gladden the gods and humans.
092.031. May he delight the hearts and minds of good people.'
092.032. When this was said, the Blessed One said to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'I do not, O great king, teach the <s>dharma</s> to my disciples thus: "You monks, go and display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who come to you."'

body.text:
093.002. api tu ahamevaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi--praticchannakalyāṇā bhikṣavo viharata vivṛtapāpā iti/
093.003. dvirapi trirapi rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat--vidarśayatu bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām/
093.004. nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān/
093.005. nandayatu bhagavān devamanuṣyān/
093.005. toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi/
093.005. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jīvatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyamāṇānām yāpayatām yaduta daśāvaśyakariṇīyāni bhavanti/
093.007. na tāvadbuddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvānti yāvanna buddho buddhaṃ vyākaroti, yāvanna dvitīyena sattvenāparivartyamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditaṃ bhavati, sarvabuddhavaineyā vinītā bhavanti, tribhāga āyuṣa utsṛṣṭo bhavati, sīmābandhaḥ kṛto bhavati, śrāvakayugamagratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ bhavati, sāṃkāśye nagare devatāvataraṇaṃ vidarśitaṃ bhavati, anavatapte mahāsarasi śrāvakaiḥ sārdhaṃ pūrvikā karmaplotirvyākṛtā bhavati, mātāpitarau satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau bhavataḥ, śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ bhavati/
093.012. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--avaśyakaraṇīyametattathāgateneti viditvā rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate--gaccha tvaṃ mahārāja/
093.013. itaḥ saptame divase tathāgato mahājanapratyakṣamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati hitāya prāṇinām/
093.014. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantamidamavocat--yadi bhagavānanujānīyāt, ahaṃ bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ kārayeyam/
093.016. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--katarasmin pradeśe pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇināmiti? devatā bhagavata ārocayanti--antarā bhadanta śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarāt pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhermahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām/
093.019. bhagavato 'pi jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate--antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarāt pūrvakaiḥ samyaksambuddhairmahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ hitāya prāṇinām/
093.020. adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
093.021. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavantamidamavocat--katamasmin bhadanta pradeśe prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ kārayāmi? antarā ca mahārāja śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanam/
093.023. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
093.002. 'Rather, I teach the <s>dharma</s> to my disciples thus: "Monks, dwell with your virtues hidden and your faults exposed."'
093.003. A second and a third time, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> for the benefit of living beings.
093.004. May he rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>.
093.005. May the Blessed One gladden the gods and humans.
093.005. May he delight the hearts and minds of good people.'
093.005. It is the nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, while living, abiding, maintaining, and continuing, that there are ten things that must be done.
093.007. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, do not attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final nirvāṇa) until: a <s>Buddha</s> has prophesied [the future of] another <s>Buddha</s>; a second being has generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>), the irreversible aspiration; all those to be trained by the <s>Buddha</s> have been trained; two-thirds of the lifespan have been relinquished; the boundary-delimitation (<s>sīmābandha</s>) has been established; the foremost pair of disciples has been designated; the descent from the gods at <s>Sāṃkāśya</s> city has been displayed; the former account of <s>karmic</s> deeds has been proclaimed with the disciples at Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>; the mother and father have been established in the truths; and the great miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s> has been displayed.
093.012. Then the Blessed One thought: 'This is something the <s>Tathāgata</s> must necessarily do.' Knowing this, he addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'Go, O great king.
093.013. On the seventh day from today, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s> before a great multitude of people, for the benefit of living beings.'
093.014. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the Blessed One: 'If the Blessed One permits, I shall have a miracle pavilion (<s>prātihāryamaṇḍapa</s>) constructed for the Blessed One.'
093.016. Then the Blessed One thought: 'In which place did the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> display the great miracle for the benefit of living beings?' The deities reported to the Blessed One: 'Between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, Venerable Sir — in the area between them, the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> displayed the great miracle for the benefit of living beings.'
093.019. The knowledge-vision of the Blessed One also arose: 'Between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, in the area between them, the former perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksambuddhas</s> displayed the great miracle for the benefit of living beings.'
093.020. The Blessed One consented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> by silence.
