093.021. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, having understood the Blessed One's consent by his silence, said to the Blessed One: 'In which place, Venerable Sir, shall I have the miracle pavilion constructed?' 'Between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, O great king.'
093.023. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, having rejoiced and approved of the Blessed One's words, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from the Blessed One's presence.

body.text:
093.026. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran--itaḥ saptame divase bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyati/
093.027. atha tīrthyānāmetadabhavat--kiṃ punaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ saptabhirdivasairanadhigatamadhigamiṣyati, atha vā niṣpalāyiṣyati, atha vā pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmah? teṣāmetadabhavat--na hyeva śramaṇo gautamo niṣpalāyiṣyati, nāpyanadhigatamadhigamiṣyati/
093.030. nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ/
093.031. vayamapi tāvat pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ/
093.031. iti viditvā raktākṣo nāma parivrājaka indrajālābhijñaḥ sa āhūtaḥ/
093.032. raktākṣasya parivrajakasyaitat prakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayanti, evaṃ cāhuh--<94>yatkhalu raktākṣa jānīyāh--śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhiriddhyā āhūtaḥ/
body.translated_text:
093.026. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'Know this, Sirs — on the seventh day from today, the Blessed One will display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.'
093.027. Then the <s>tīrthyas</s> thought: 'Will the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> attain in seven days something he has not yet attained? Or will he flee? Or does he wish to seek allies?' They thought: 'Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will not flee, nor will he attain something not yet attained.
093.030. Certainly the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek allies.
093.031. We too shall seek allies.'
093.031. Knowing this, a wandering ascetic named <s>Raktākṣa</s>, skilled in magic and illusion, was summoned.
093.032. They related the entire matter in detail to the wandering ascetic <s>Raktākṣa</s>, and said thus: 'Know this, <s>Raktākṣa</s> — the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us through supernatural power.'

body.text:
094.001. sa kathayati--itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti/
094.001. nūnaṃ śramaṇo gatamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ/
094.003. tvamapi tāvat sabrahmacāriṇāṃ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kuruṣva/
094.003. tena tatheti pratijñātam/
094.003. atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakāstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
094.004. upasaṃkramya nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakānāmetatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati, evaṃ cāha--yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran--śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhiriddhyā āhūtaḥ/
094.006. sa kathayati--itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśāyiṣyāmīti/
094.007. nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ/
094.008. bhavadbhirapi brahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam/
094.008. saptame divase yuṣmābhirbahiḥ śrāvastyā nirgantavyam/
094.009. taistatheti pratijñātam/
094.009. athānyatamasmin parvate pañcamātrāṇi ṛṣiśatāni prativasanti/
094.010. atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena te ṛṣayastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
094.011. upasaṃkramya teṣāmetatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati, evaṃ cāha--yatkhalu bhavanto jānīran--śramaṇo gautama ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ/
094.012. sa kathayati--itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti/
094.013. nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ/
094.013. bhavadbhirapi sabrahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam/
094.014. saptame divase yuṣmābhiḥ śrāvastīmāgantavyam/
094.014. taistatheti pratijñātam/
094.015. tena khalu samayena subhadro nāma parivrājakaḥ pañcābhijñaḥ/
094.015. tasya kuśinagaryāmāvasatho 'navatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ/
094.016. atha raktākṣaḥ parivrājako yena subhadraḥ parivrājakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
094.017. upasaṃkramya etatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati, evaṃ cāha--yatkhalu subhadra jānīyāh--śramaṇo gautamo 'smābhih ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ/
094.018. sa kathayati--itaḥ saptame divase uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmīti/
094.019. nūnaṃ śramaṇo gautamaḥ pakṣaparyeṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ/
094.019. tvayā sabrahmacāriṇāṃ sāhāyyaṃ karaṇīyam/
094.020. saptame divase tvayā śrāvastīmāgantavyam/
094.020. subhadreṇābhihitam--na śobhanaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kṛtam yadyuṣmābhiḥ śramaṇo gautamo riddhyā āhūtaḥ/
094.021. tatkasya hetoh? mama tāvat kuśinagaryāmāvāso 'navatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ/
094.022. śramaṇasya gautamasya śāriputro nāma śiṣyastasya cundo nāma śrāmaṇerakastasyāpi tatraivānavatapte mahāsarasi divā vihāraḥ/
094.024. na tathānavataptakāyikā devatā api kārān kartavyān manyante yathā tasya/
094.025. eko 'yaṃ samayaḥ/
094.025. ihāhaṃ kuśinagarīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā piṇḍapātamādāya anavataptaṃ mahāsarasaṃ gacchāmi/
094.026. tasya mamānavataptakāyikā devatā anavataptānmahāsarasaḥ pānīyamuddhṛtya ekānte na prayacchati/
094.027. cundaḥ śramaṇoddeśaḥ pāṃśukūlānyādāyānavataptaṃ mahāsaro gacchati/
094.027. tasyānavataptakāyikā devatā pāṃśukūlāni dhāvayitvā tena pānīyenātmānaṃ siñcati/
094.028. yasya tāvadvayaṃ śiṣyapratiśiṣyakayāpi na tulyāḥ, sa yuṣmābhiruttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryeṇāhūtaḥ/
094.029. na śobhanaṃ bhavadbhiḥ kṛtam yacchramaṇo gautamo riddhiprātihāryeṇāhūtaḥ/
094.030. evamahaṃ jāne yathā maharddhikaḥ śramaṇo gautamo mahānubhāva iti/
094.031. raktakṣeṇābhihitam--tvaṃ tāvaccramaṇasya gautamasya pakṣaṃ vadasi/
094.032. tvayā tāvanna gantavyam/
094.032. subhadreṇābhihitam--naiva gamiṣyāmīti//
body.translated_text: He said: 'On the seventh day from now, I shall display the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) in the higher human dharma.' Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek allies. You too should seek allies among your fellow practitioners. He agreed, saying: 'So be it.' Then <s>Raktākṣa</s> the wanderer approached the various non-Buddhist ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, mendicants, and wanderers. Having approached, he informed them of this matter in detail, and said: 'May the venerable ones know this — the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us through supernatural power. He says: "On the seventh day from now, I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma." Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek allies. You too, fellow practitioners, must render assistance. On the seventh day, you must go outside <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' They agreed, saying: 'So be it.' Now, on a certain mountain, about five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) were dwelling. Then <s>Raktākṣa</s> the wanderer approached those <s>ṛṣis</s>. Having approached, he informed them of this matter in detail, and said: 'May the venerable ones know this — the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged through supernatural power. He says: "On the seventh day from now, I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma." Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek allies. You too, fellow practitioners, must render assistance. On the seventh day, you must come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' They agreed, saying: 'So be it.' At that time, there was a wanderer named <s>Subhadra</s>, possessing the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). His dwelling was at <s>Kuśinagara</s>, and his daytime retreat was at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>. Then <s>Raktākṣa</s> the wanderer approached the wanderer <s>Subhadra</s>. Having approached, he informed him of this matter in detail, and said: 'May <s>Subhadra</s> know this — the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us through supernatural power. He says: "On the seventh day from now, I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma." Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> wishes to seek allies. You, fellow practitioner, must render assistance. On the seventh day, you must come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' <s>Subhadra</s> replied: 'What you have done is not good — that you have challenged the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> through supernatural power. Why? My dwelling is at <s>Kuśinagara</s> and my daytime retreat is at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has a disciple named <s>Śāriputra</s>, whose novice is named <s>Cunda</s>, and even he has his daytime retreat at that very great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>. The <s>Anavatapta</s> deities do not even think it fit to perform services for me as they do for him. This is one case. Here I go to <s>Kuśinagara</s> for alms, and taking my alms-food, I go to the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>. The <s>Anavatapta</s> deities do not even offer me drinking water drawn from the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s> and set aside. But when <s>Cunda</s> the novice takes his rag-robes and goes to the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, the <s>Anavatapta</s> deities wash his rag-robes and sprinkle themselves with that water. We are not even equal to his disciple's disciple, and yet you have challenged him through the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma! What you have done is not good, that you have challenged the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> through the miracle of supernatural power. I know well that the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is of great supernatural power and great might.' <s>Raktākṣa</s> replied: 'You are speaking on behalf of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. You need not come.' <s>Subhadra</s> replied: 'Indeed, I shall not come.'

body.text:
095.001. <95>atha rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya kālo nāṃnā bhrātā abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ/
095.002. sa rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya niveśanadvāreṇābhiniṣkrāmati/
095.003. anyatamayā cāvaruddhikayā prāsādatalagatayā rājakumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā sragdāmaṃ kṣiptam/
095.004. tat tasyopari nipatitam/
095.004. mitrārimadhyamo lokaḥ/
095.004. tai rājñe niveditam--yatkhalu deva jānīthāḥ--kālena devasyāntaḥpuraṃ prārthitam/
095.005. rājā prasenajit kauśalaścaṇḍo rabhasaḥ kakarśaḥ/
095.006. tenāparīkṣya pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā--gacchantu bhavantaḥ/
095.006. śīghraṃ kālasya hastapādāṃś chindantu/
095.007. evaṃ deveti pauruṣeyai rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya kālasya vīthīmadhye hastapādāśchinnāḥ/
095.008. sa ārtasvaraṃ krandate, duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ devanāṃ vedayate/
095.008. kālaṃ rājakumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā mahājanakāyo vikroṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
095.009. pūraṇādāyaśca nirgranthāstaṃ pradeśamanuprāptāḥ/
095.010. kālasya jñātibhirabhihitam--etamāryāḥ kālaṃ rājakumāraṃ satyābhiyācanayā yathāpaurāṇaṃ kurudhvamiti/
095.011. pūraṇenābhihitam--eṣa śramaṇasya gautamasya śrāvakaḥ/
095.011. śramaṇadharmeṇa gautamo yathāpaurāṇaṃ kariṣyati/
095.012. atha kālasya rājakumārasyaitadabhavat--kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaṃ māṃ bhagavān na samanvāharatīti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
095.014. imāmavasthāṃ mama lokanātho na vetti saṃbādhagatasya kasmāt/
095.016. namo 'stu tasmai vigatajvarāya sarveṣu bhūteṣvanukampakāya//1//
body.translated_text: Now, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had a brother named <s>Kāla</s>, who was handsome, good-looking, pleasing, faithful, virtuous, and of noble disposition. He was leaving through the gate of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>'s palace. A certain courtesan, standing on the upper floor of the palace, upon seeing the prince, threw down a garland. It fell upon him. The world has friends, enemies, and neutrals. They reported to the king: 'May the lord know this — <s>Kāla</s> has aspired to the lord's inner quarters.' King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> was fierce, violent, and harsh. Without investigation, he gave an order to his servants: 'Go, sirs! Quickly cut off <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet.' 'So be it, lord,' the servants of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> assented, and cut off <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet in the middle of the street. He cried out in agony, experiencing painful, intense, sharp, bitter, and disagreeable bodily sensations. Seeing the prince <s>Kāla</s>, a great crowd of people began to wail. <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the other <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain monks) arrived at that place. <s>Kāla</s>'s kinsmen said: 'Noble sirs, perform the ancient restoration for this prince <s>Kāla</s> by the truth-invocation.' <s>Pūraṇa</s> replied: 'This one is a disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. Let <s>Gautama</s> perform the ancient restoration by his ascetic dharma.' Then the prince <s>Kāla</s> thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> does not attend to me when I have reached this dire straits of danger and distress.' Knowing this, he spoke a verse: 'Why does the Protector of the World not see this state of mine, who am in such a strait? Homage to that One free from fever, who has compassion for all beings!'

body.text:
095.018. asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
095.018. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma--gaccha tvamānanda saṃghāṭimādāya anyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena kālo rājabhrātā tenopasaṃkrāma/
095.020. upasaṃkramya kālasya rājakumārasya hastapādān yathāsthāne sthāpayitvā evaṃ vada--ye kecit sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā bahupadā vā arūpiṇo vā rūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino vā nāsaṃjñinaḥ, tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhasteṣāṃ sattvānāmagra ākhyāyate/
095.023. ye kecid dharmā asaṃskṛtā vā saṃskṛtā vā, virāgo dharmasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ/
095.025. anena satyena satyavākyena tava śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ syāt/
095.025. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya saṃghāṭīmādāyānyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścācchramaṇena yena rājabhrātā kālastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
095.027. upasaṃkramya kālasya rājakumārasya hastapādān yathāsthāne sthāpayitvā evamāha--ye kecit sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuṣpadā vā bahupadā vā yāvannaivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñinaḥ, tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhasteṣāṃ sattvānāmagra ākhyātaḥ/
095.029. ye keciddharmāḥ saṃkṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā, virāgo dharmasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ/
095.030. ye kecit saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā parṣado vā, tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghasteṣāmagra ākhyātaḥ/
095.031. anena satyena satyavākyena tava śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ bhavatu/
095.032. sahābhidhānāt kālasya rājakumārasya śarīram yathāpaurāṇaṃ saṃvṛttam, <96>yathāpi tatra buddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena/
body.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are of unfailing memory. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, take the outer robe and, accompanied by a monk as an attendant, approach <s>Kāla</s>, the king's brother. Having approached, place Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet back in their proper positions, and speak thus: "Whatever beings there are — footless, two-footed, four-footed, many-footed, or formless, or with form, or with perception, or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, is declared the foremost among those beings. Whatever <s>dharmas</s> there are, whether conditioned or unconditioned, dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is declared the foremost among them. By this truth, by this true statement, may your body be restored to its former state."' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and taking the outer robe, accompanied by a monk as an attendant, approached <s>Kāla</s>, the king's brother. Having approached, he placed Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s hands and feet back in their proper positions and said: 'Whatever beings there are — footless, two-footed, four-footed, many-footed, up to those neither with perception nor without perception — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one, is declared the foremost among those beings. Whatever <s>dharmas</s> there are, whether conditioned or unconditioned, dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is declared the foremost among them. Whatever communities, groups, guilds, or assemblies there are, the community of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples is declared the foremost among them. By this truth, by this true statement, may your body be restored to its former state.' The moment these words were spoken, Prince <s>Kāla</s>'s body was restored to its former state — both through the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and through the power of the deities.

body.text:
096.001. kālena kumāreṇa tenaiva saṃvegena anāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ṛddhiścāpi nirhṛtā/
096.002. tena bhagavata ārāmo niryātitaḥ/
096.002. sa bhagavata upasthānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
096.003. yatrāsya śarīraṃ gaṇḍagaṇḍaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya gaṇḍaka ārāmika iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
096.004. atha rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sa pravāritaḥ/
096.004. kālenābhihitam--na mama tvayā prayojanam/
096.005. bhagavata evopasthānaṃ kariṣyāmīti//
body.translated_text: By Prince <s>Kāla</s>, through that very spiritual urgency, the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) was directly realized, and supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) was also attained. He dedicated a park to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He began to attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Since his body had been made into a mass of wounds, he came to be known as <s>Gaṇḍaka</s> (the Wounded One), the park-keeper. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> offered him all manner of provisions. <s>Kāla</s> replied: 'I have no need of you. I shall attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone.'

body.text:
096.006. rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena antarā ca śrāvastīmantarā ca jetavanamatrāntarādbhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ kāritaḥ śatasahasrahastah .... caturṇāṃ maṇḍapo vitataḥ/
096.007. bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptam/
096.008. anyatīrthikaśrāvakairapi pūrṇādīnāṃ nirgranthānāṃ pratyekapratyekamaṇḍapaḥ kāritaḥ/
096.009. rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena saptame divase yāvajjetavanaṃ yāvacca bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapo 'ntarāt sarvo 'sau pradeśo 'pagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalyo vyavasthitaḥ/
096.010. dhūpacūrṇāndhakāraḥ kṛtaḥ/
096.011. chatradhvajapatākāgandhodakapariṣikto nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇo ramaṇīyaḥ/
096.011. antarāntarā ca puṣpamaṇḍapāḥ sajjīkṛtāḥ//
body.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had a miracle pavilion (<s>prātihāryamaṇḍapa</s>) constructed for the <s>Bhagavān</s> between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Jetavana</s>, one hundred thousand hands [in measure]... a pavilion spread out for the four [directions]. A lion-seat was prepared for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The disciples of the other <s>tīrthyas</s> also had separate pavilions constructed for <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the other <s>Nirgranthas</s>, each one separately. On the seventh day, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had the entire area between <s>Jetavana</s> and the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle pavilion cleared of stones, pebbles, and rubble. It was made dark with incense-powder. It was sprinkled with water of fragrances, strewn with canopies, banners, flags, and various flowers, made delightful. At intervals, flower pavilions were prepared.

body.text:
096.013. atha bhagavān saptame divase pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
096.014. śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratiśrāmya bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ pratisaṃlayanāya/
096.015. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo 'nekaśataparivāro 'nekasahasraparivāro 'nekaśatasahasraparivāro yena bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
096.017. upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
096.017. tīrthyā api mahājanakāyaparivṛtā yena maṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
096.018. upasaṃkramya pratyekapratyekasminnāsane niṣaṇṇāḥ/
096.019. niṣadya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocan--yatkhalu deva jānīyāh--ete vayamāgatāḥ/
096.020. kutra etarhi śramaṇo gautamah? tena bhavanto muhūrtamāgamayata/
096.020. eṣa idānīṃ bhagavānadhigamiṣyati/
096.021. atha rājā prasenajit kauśala uttaraṃ māṇavamāmantrayate--ehi tvamuttara, yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāma/
096.023. upasaṃkramyāsmākaṃ vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛccha, alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca anavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca/
096.024. evaṃ ca vada--rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśala evamāha--ime bhadanta tīrthyā āgatā yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyate/
096.025. evaṃ devetyuttaro māṇavo rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya pratiśrutya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
096.026. upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
096.027. ekāntaniṣaṇṇa uttaro māṇavo bhagavantamidamavocat--rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśalo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandate, alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchati alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātraṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca anavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca/
096.030. sukhī bhavatu māṇava rājā prasenajit kauśalastvaṃ ca/
096.030. rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśala evamāha--ime bhadanta tīrthyā āgatā yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate/
096.031. evamukte bhagavānuttaraṃ māṇavamidamavocat--māṇava eṣo 'hamadyāgacchāmi/
096.032. bhagavatā tathādhiṣṭhito yathottaro <97>māṇavastat evoparivihāyasā prakrāntaḥ, yena rājā prasenajit kauśalastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text:
096.013. Then the Blessed One, on the seventh day, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.
096.014. Having gone for alms in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having finished his meal, having returned from the alms-round after eating, having put away his bowl and robe, having washed his feet outside the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), he entered the <s>vihāra</s> for seclusion.
096.015. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, accompanied by many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, approached the miracle pavilion (<s>prātihāryamaṇḍapa</s>) of the Blessed One.
096.017. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared for him.
096.017. The <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics) too, surrounded by a great multitude of people, approached the pavilion.
096.018. Having approached, they sat down each on their own separate seats.
096.019. Having sat down, they said to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'May your Majesty know — we have arrived.
096.020. Where is the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> now?' 'Good sirs, wait a moment.
096.020. The Blessed One will arrive presently.'
096.021. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> addressed the young man <s>Uttara</s>: 'Come, <s>Uttara</s>, approach the Blessed One.
096.023. Having approached, bow your head at the feet of the Blessed One on our behalf, and inquire about his health — whether he has few ailments, few afflictions, is light in rising, has ease of living, strength, comfort, blamelessness, and pleasant abiding.
096.024. And say thus: "King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, Venerable Sir, says this — these <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics) have arrived, Venerable Sir; may the Blessed One come when he thinks it is time."'
096.025. 'So be it, your Majesty,' the young man <s>Uttara</s>, having assented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, approached the Blessed One.
096.026. Having approached, he exchanged various greetings and pleasantries with the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
096.027. Seated to one side, the young man <s>Uttara</s> said to the Blessed One: 'King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, Venerable Sir, bows his head at the feet of the Blessed One and inquires about his health — whether he has few ailments, few afflictions, is light in rising, has ease of living, strength, comfort, blamelessness, and pleasant abiding.'
096.030. 'May King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> be happy, young man, and may you as well.'
096.030. 'King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, Venerable Sir, says this — these <s>tīrthyas</s> have arrived, Venerable Sir; may the Blessed One come when he thinks it is time.'
096.031. When this was said, the Blessed One said to the young man <s>Uttara</s>: 'Young man, I am coming right now.'
096.032. The Blessed One so empowered it that the young man <s>Uttara</s> <97>departed through the air above the <s>vihāra</s> and approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>.

body.text:
097.002. adrākṣīdrājā prasenajit kauśala uttaraṃ māṇavakamupari vihāyasā āgacchatam/
097.002. dṛṣṭvā ca punastīrthyānidamavocat--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
097.003. yūyamapi vidarśayata/
097.004. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ/
097.004. kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kenaitad vidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena? atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte 'rgaḍacchidreṇārciṣo nirgatya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍape nipatitāḥ, sarvaśca prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ prajvalitaḥ/
097.007. adrākṣustīrthyā bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ prajvalitam, dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocan--eṣa idānīṃ mahārāja śramaṇasya gautamasya prātihāryamaṇḍapaḥ prajvalitaḥ/
097.009. gaccha idānīṃ nirvāpaya/
097.009. atha so 'gniraspṛṣṭa eva vāriṇā sarvaprātihāryamaṇḍapamadagdhvā svayameva nirvṛto yathāpi tadbuddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena/
097.010. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
097.012. yūyamapi vidarśayata/
097.012. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ/
097.013. kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena? bhagavatā kanakamarīcikāvabhāsā utsṛṣṭāḥ, yena sarvaloka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt/
097.014. adrākṣīdrājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sarvalokamudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭam/
097.015. dṛṣṭvā ca punastīrthyānāmantrayate--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
097.016. yūyamapi vidarśayata/
097.016. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ/
097.017. kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena? bhagavatā kanakamarīcikāvabhāsā utsṛṣṭā yena sarvaloka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt/
097.019. adrākṣīdrājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sarvalokamudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭam/
097.019. dṛṣṭvā ca punastīrthyānāmantrayate--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
097.020. yūyamapi vidarśayata/
097.021. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--mahājanakāyo 'tra mahārāja saṃnipatitaḥ/
097.021. kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena vā gautamena? gaṇḍakenārāmikenottarakauravād dvīpāt karṇikāravṛkṣamādāya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapasyāgrataḥ sthāpitaḥ/
097.023. ratnakenāpyārāmikena gandhamādanādaśokavṛkṣamānīya bhagavataḥ prātihāryamaṇḍapasya pṛṣṭhataḥ sthāpitaḥ/
097.024. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
097.025. yūyamapi vidarśayata/
097.026. tīrthyāḥ kathayanti--mahājanakāyo 'tra saṃnipatitaḥ/
097.026. kiṃ tvaṃ jñāsyasi kena etadvidarśitamasmābhirvā śramaṇena gautamena? bhagavatā sābhisaṃskāreṇa pṛthivyāṃ pādau nyastau/
097.028. mahāpṛthivīcālaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
097.028. ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturiyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ kampati prakampati saṃprakampati/
097.029. calati saṃcalati saṃpracalati/
097.029. vyathati saṃvyathati saṃpravyathati/
097.030. pūrvāvanamati paścimonnamati/
097.030. {pūrvonnamati paścimāvanamati/}
097.031. dakṣiṇonnamati uttarāvanamati/
097.031. uttaronnamati dakṣiṇāvanamati/
097.031. madhye unnamati ante 'vanamati/
097.032. madhye 'vanamati ante unnamati/
097.032. imau sūryacandramasau bhāsatastapato virocataḥ/
body.translated_text:
097.002. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> saw the young man <s>Uttara</s> coming through the air above.
097.002. Having seen him, he said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'The Blessed One has displayed the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
097.003. Now you too should display yours.'
097.004. The <s>tīrthyas</s> said: 'A great multitude has gathered here, O great king.
097.004. How will you know whether this was displayed by us or by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' Then the Blessed One entered into a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of such a kind that, with his mind concentrated, flames burst forth through a lattice opening and fell upon the Blessed One's miracle pavilion, and the entire miracle pavilion was set ablaze.
097.007. The <s>tīrthyas</s> saw the Blessed One's miracle pavilion ablaze, and having seen it, said to <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'Now, O great king, the miracle pavilion of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is ablaze.
097.009. Go now and extinguish it.'
097.009. Then that fire, untouched by water, having left the entire miracle pavilion unburned, went out by itself — such was the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and the power of the deities.
097.010. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'The Blessed One has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
097.012. Now you too should display yours.'
097.012. The <s>tīrthyas</s> said: 'A great multitude has gathered here, O great king.
097.013. How will you know whether this was displayed by us or by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' The Blessed One sent forth rays of golden light, by which the entire world was filled with a magnificent radiance.
097.014. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> saw the entire world filled with magnificent radiance.
097.015. Having seen it, he addressed the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'The Blessed One has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
097.016. Now you too should display yours.'
097.016. The <s>tīrthyas</s> said: 'A great multitude has gathered here, O great king.
097.017. How will you know whether this was displayed by us or by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' The Blessed One sent forth rays of golden light by which the entire world was filled with a magnificent radiance.
097.019. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> saw the entire world filled with magnificent radiance.
097.019. Having seen it, he addressed the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'The Blessed One has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
097.020. Now you too should display yours.'
097.021. The <s>tīrthyas</s> said: 'A great multitude has gathered here, O great king.
097.021. How will you know whether this was displayed by us or by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' By the park-keeper <s>Gaṇḍaka</s>, a <s>karṇikāra</s> tree was brought from the <s>Uttarakuru</s> continent and placed before the Blessed One's miracle pavilion.
097.023. By the park-keeper <s>Ratnaka</s> too, an <s>aśoka</s> tree was brought from <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain and placed behind the Blessed One's miracle pavilion.
097.024. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: 'The Blessed One has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human <s>dharma</s>.
097.025. Now you too should display yours.'
097.026. The <s>tīrthyas</s> said: 'A great multitude has gathered here.
097.026. How will you know whether this was displayed by us or by the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>?' The Blessed One deliberately placed his feet on the earth.
097.028. A great earthquake occurred.
097.028. This great earth of the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system trembled, shook, and quaked in six ways.
097.029. It moved, swayed, and convulsed.
097.029. It dipped in the east and rose in the west.
097.030. It rose in the east and dipped in the west.
097.031. It rose in the south and dipped in the north.
097.031. It rose in the north and dipped in the south.
097.031. It rose in the middle and dipped at the edges.
097.032. It dipped in the middle and rose at the edges.
097.032. And the sun and moon shone, blazed, and radiated brilliantly.

body.text:
098.001. <98>vicitrāṇi ca āścaryādbhutāni prādurbhūtāni/
098.001. gaganatalasthā devatā bhagavata upariṣṭāddivyānyutpalāni kṣipanti padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkānyagarucūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni tamālapatrāṇi, divyāni māndārakāṇi puṣpāṇi kṣipanti, divyāni ca vāditrāṇi saṃpravādayanti, cailavikṣepaṃ cākārṣuḥ//
body.translated_text:
098.001. <98>Various wondrous and marvelous signs appeared.
098.001. The deities stationed in the sky above the Blessed One rained down divine blue lotuses, lotuses, water-lilies, white lotuses, <s>aguru</s> (aloe) powder, sandalwood powder, <s>tagara</s> (valerian) powder, and <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay leaves); they rained down divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers, played divine musical instruments, and waved their garments.

body.text:
098.005. atha teṣām ṛṣīṇāmetadabhavat--kimarthaṃ mahāpṛthivīcālaḥ saṃvṛtta iti/
098.005. teṣāmetadabhavat--nūnamasmākaṃ sabrahmacāribhiḥ śramaṇo gautamo riddhyā āhūto bhaviṣyatīti viditvā pañca ṛṣiśatāni śrāvastīṃ saṃprasthitāni/
098.007. teṣāmāgacchatāṃ bhagavatā ekāyano mārgo 'dhiṣṭhitaḥ/
098.008. adrākṣuste ṛṣayo bhagavantaṃ dūrādeva dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ mūrtimantamiva dharmaṃ havyāvasiktamiva hutavahaṃ kāñcanabhājanasthamiva pradīpaṃ jaṅgamamiva suvarṇaparvataṃ nānāratnavicitramiva suvarṇarūpaṃ sphuṭapaṭumahāvimalaviśuddhabuddhiṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam/
098.010. dṛṣṭvā ca punar na tathā dvādaśavarṣe 'bhyastaśamatho yogācārasya cittasya kalyatāṃ janayati, aputrasya vā putraḥ pratilambho daridrasya vā nidhidarśanaṃ rājyābhinandino vā rājyābhiṣeko yathā tatprathamatapūrvabuddhāropitakuśalamūlānāṃ tatprathamato buddhadarśanam/
098.013. atha te ṛṣayo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
098.014. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte sthitāḥ/
098.014. ekāntasthitāste ṛṣayo bhagavantamidamavocan--labhemahi vayaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
098.016. carema vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike pravrajya brahmacaryam/
098.016. te bhagavatā brāhmeṇa svareṇāhūtāḥ--eta bhikṣavaścarata brahmacaryam/
098.017. sahābhidhānānmuṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtāḥ pātrakaravyagrahastāḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśravo varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣorīryāpathenāvasthitāḥ/
098.019. ehīti coktāśca tathāgatena muṇḍāśca saṃghāṭiparītadehāḥ/
098.021. satya(dyaḥ) praśāntendriyā eva tasthurevaṃ sthitā buddhamanorathena//2//
body.translated_text:
098.005. Then those <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) thought: 'For what purpose has this great earthquake occurred?'
098.005. They thought: 'Surely the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> must have been invited by our fellow <s>brahmacārins</s> (spiritual companions) through supernatural power.' Knowing this, five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
098.007. As they were approaching, the Blessed One created a single path for them.
098.008. Those <s>ṛṣis</s> saw the Blessed One from afar, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being — like <s>Dharma</s> embodied in form, like a sacrificial fire anointed with oblations, like a lamp placed in a golden vessel, like a moving mountain of gold, like a golden form adorned with various jewels, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, with a radiant, keen, great, stainless, and perfectly pure wisdom.
098.010. Having seen him, they [felt] — not so much does twelve years' practice of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) in <s>yogācāra</s> (meditative discipline) bring felicity to the mind, nor the gaining of a son by one who is childless, nor the sight of a treasure by one who is destitute, nor a royal consecration by one who delights in sovereignty, as does the first sight of a <s>Buddha</s> for those in whom roots of merit were planted by a <s>Buddha</s> encountered for the first time.
098.013. Then those <s>ṛṣis</s> approached the Blessed One.
098.014. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
098.014. Standing to one side, those <s>ṛṣis</s> said to the Blessed One: 'May we, Venerable Sir, obtain the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of monks in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>?
098.016. May we practice the holy life in the presence of the Blessed One?'
098.016. They were summoned by the Blessed One with his <s>Brāhma</s> (divine) voice: 'Come, monks, practice the holy life.'
098.017. With that very utterance, they became tonsured, clad in monastic robes, holding bowls in their hands, with hair and beard as if shaven for seven days, standing in the deportment of monks ordained for a hundred years.
098.019. And those who were called 'Come!' by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured, their bodies clad in robes,
098.021. stood that very day with tranquil faculties — thus established by the <s>Buddha's</s> wish. //2//

body.text:
098.023. atha bhagavān divyamānuṣyeṇa pūjāsatkāreṇa satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rhannarhatparivāro saptabhiśca nikāyaiḥ saṃpuraskṛto mahatā ca janaughena yena prātihāryamaṇḍapastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
098.025. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
098.025. bhagavataḥ kāyādraśmayo nirgatya sarvaṃ prātihāryamaṇḍapaṃ suvarṇavarṇāvabhāsaṃ kṛtavatyaḥ/
098.026. atha lūhasudatto gṛhapatirutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu/
098.028. ahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi/
098.029. nirbhartsayiṣyāmi tīrthyān/
098.029. saha dharmeṇa nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān/
098.030. toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi/
098.030. na tvaṃ gṛhapate ebhih ṛddhyā āhūtaḥ, api tvahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ riddhyā āhūtaḥ/
098.031. ahamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi/
098.032. sthānametadvidyate yattīrthyā evaṃ vadeyuḥ--nāsti śramaṇasya gautamasyottare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam<99>/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with divine and human offerings and homage, surrounded by <s>Arhats</s> and accompanied by the seven communities, and by a great multitude of people, approached the miracle pavilion (<s>prātihāryamaṇḍapa</s>). Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks). From the body of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rays of light emanated, making the entire miracle pavilion radiant with a golden hue. Then the householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> be of little concern. I shall display the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>) in the higher human dharma against the <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics). I shall rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>. I shall gladden the gods and humans in accordance with the Dharma. I shall delight the hearts and minds of good people." "You, householder, were not challenged by them through supernatural power; rather, I was challenged by the <s>tīrthyas</s> through supernatural power. I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma. There is indeed the possibility that the <s>tīrthyas</s> might say thus: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has no miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma—

body.text:
099.001. śrāvakasyaiṣā gṛhiṇo 'vadātavasanasya ṛddhiriti/
099.001. niṣīda tvaṃ gṛhapate yathāsvake āsane/
099.002. niṣaṇṇo lūhasudatto gṛhapatiryathāsvake āsane/
099.002. yathā lūhasudatto gṛhapatirevaṃ kālo rājabhrātā, rambhaka ārāmikaḥ, ṛddhilamātā upāsikā śramaṇoddeśikā, cundaḥ śramaṇoddeśaḥ, utpalavarṇā bhikṣuṇī/
099.004. athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu/
099.005. ahaṃ tīrthyaiḥ sārdhamuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi/
099.006. tīrthyān nigṛhṇiṣyāmi/
099.006. saha dharmeṇa nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān/
099.007. toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanagṛhṛdayamanāṃsi/
099.007. pratibalastvaṃ maudgalyāyana tīrthyān sahadharmeṇa nigṛhītum/
099.008. api tu na tvaṃ tīrthyair riddhyā āhūtaḥ/
099.008. ahameṣāmuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayiṣyāmi hitāya prāṇinām/
099.009. nirbhartsayiṣyāmi tīrthyān/
099.009. nandayiṣyāmi devamanuṣyān/
099.010. toṣayiṣyāmi sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi/
099.010. niṣīda tvaṃ maudgalyāyana yathāsvake āsane/
099.011. niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yathāsvake āsane/
099.011. tatra bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate--ko mahārāja tathāgatamadhyeṣate uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām? atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat--ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavantamadhyeṣe uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitum/
099.015. bhagavānuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam {vidarśayatu} hitāya prāṇinām/
099.016. nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān/
099.017. nandayatu devamanuṣyān/
099.017. toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi/
099.017. atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte svasminnāsane 'ntarhitaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya caturvidhamīryāpathaṃ kalpayati tadyathā--caṃkramyate tiṣṭhati niṣīdati śayyāṃ kalpayati/
099.020. tejodhātumapi saṃpadyate/
099.020. tejodhātusamāpannasya buddhasya bhagavato vividhānyarcīṃṣi kāyānniścaranti tadyathā nīlapītāni lohitānyavadātāni mañjiṣṭhāni sphaṭikavarṇāni/
099.021. anekānyapi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayati/
099.022. adhaḥkāyaṃ prajvālayati, uparimāt kāyācchītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante/
099.023. yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśi evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśīti caturdiśaṃ caturvidham ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśya tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
099.024. niṣadya bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamidamavocat--iyaṃ mahārāja tathāgatasya sarvaśrāvakasādhāraṇā ṛddhiḥ/
099.026. tatra bhagavān dvirapi rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamāmantrayate--ko mahārāja tathāgatamadhyeṣate 'sādhāraṇāyām ṛddhyāmuttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām? atha rājā prasenajit kauśala utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavantamadhyeṣe 'sādhāraṇāyām ṛddhyāmuttare manuṣyadharme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ hitāya prāṇinām/
099.030. nirbhartsayatu tīrthyān/
099.031. nandayatu devamanuṣyān/
099.031. toṣayatu sajjanahṛdayamanāṃsi//
body.translated_text: this is the supernatural power of a disciple, a householder, a white-robed layperson.' Sit down, householder, on your own seat." The householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s> sat down on his own seat. Just as with the householder <s>Lūhasudatta</s>, so too with <s>Kāla</s> the king's brother, <s>Rambhaka</s> the park-keeper, <s>Ṛddhilamātā</s> the lay woman novice, <s>Cunda</s> the male novice, and <s>Utpalavarṇā</s> the nun. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> be of little concern. I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma against the <s>tīrthyas</s>. I shall subdue the <s>tīrthyas</s>. I shall gladden the gods and humans in accordance with the Dharma. I shall delight the hearts and minds of good people." "You are indeed capable, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, of subduing the <s>tīrthyas</s> in accordance with the Dharma. However, you were not challenged by the <s>tīrthyas</s> through supernatural power. I shall display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma for the benefit of living beings. I shall rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>. I shall gladden the gods and humans. I shall delight the hearts and minds of good people. Sit down, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, on your own seat." The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> sat down on his own seat. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: "Who, O great king, requests the <s>Tathāgata</s> to display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma for the benefit of living beings?" Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "I, Venerable Sir, request the <s>Bhagavān</s> to display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> display the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma for the benefit of living beings. May he rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>. May he gladden the gods and humans. May he delight the hearts and minds of good people." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered into a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of such a kind that, with his mind concentrated, he vanished from his own seat and rose up into the sky in the eastern direction, manifesting the four modes of deportment, namely: walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. He also attained the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>). From the body of the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> who had attained the fire element, various rays emanated—blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He displayed many other miracles as well. He set the lower part of his body ablaze, while from the upper part of his body cool streams of water flowed. Just as in the eastern direction, so too in the southern direction—thus he displayed the fourfold miracle of supernatural power in all four directions. Having withdrawn those supernatural transformations, he sat down on the very seat that had been prepared. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: "This, O great king, is the supernatural power that the <s>Tathāgata</s> shares in common with all disciples." There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> a second time: "Who, O great king, requests the <s>Tathāgata</s> to display the miracle of supernatural power in the uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇā</s>) supernatural ability, in the higher human dharma, for the benefit of living beings?" Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "I, Venerable Sir, request the <s>Bhagavān</s> to display the miracle of supernatural power in the uncommon supernatural ability, in the higher human dharma, for the benefit of living beings. May he rebuke the <s>tīrthyas</s>. May he gladden the gods and humans. May he delight the hearts and minds of good people."

body.text:
099.032. bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam/
099.032. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatām yadi laukikaṃ cittamutpādayanti, antaśaḥ kuntapipīliko 'pi prāṇī bhagavatah cetasi cittamājānanti/
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly (<s>laukika</s>) thought. It is the nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, that when they produce a worldly thought, even a tiny ant-like creature can know the thought in the mind of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
100.001. <100>atha lokottaracittamutpādayanti, tatrāgatirbhavati pratyekabuddhānāmapi, kaḥ punarvādaḥ śrāvakāṇām? atha śakrabrahmādīnāṃ devānāmetadabhavat--kimarthaṃ bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam? teṣāmetadabhavat--śrāvastyāṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitukāmo hitāya prāṇinām/
100.004. atha śakrabrahmādayo devā anekāni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi bhagavataścetasā cittamājñāya tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃkuñcitaṃ vā bāhuṃ prasārayet, prasāritaṃ vā saṃkuñcayet, evameva śakrabrahmādayo devā anekāni ca devatāśatasahasrāṇi ca devaloke 'ntarhitāni, bhagavataḥ puratastasthuḥ/
100.006. atha brahmādayo devā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇāḥ/
100.008. śakrādayo devā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīktya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇāḥ/
100.009. nandopanandābhyāṃ nāgarājābhyāṃ bhagavata upanāmitaṃ nirmitaṃ sahasrapatraṃ śakaṭacakramātraṃ sarvasauvarṇaṃ ratnadaṇḍaṃ padmam/
100.010. bhagavāṃśca padmakarṇikāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya/
100.011. padmasyopari padmaṃ nirmitam/
100.012. tatrāpi bhagavān paryaṅkaniṣaṇṇaḥ/
100.012. evamagrataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvataḥ/
100.012. evaṃ bhagavatā buddhapiṇḍī nirmitā yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanamupādāya buddhā bhagavanto parṣannirmitam(?)/
100.013. kecidbuddhanirmāṇāścaṃkramyante, kecit tiṣṭhanti, kecinniṣīdanti, kecicchāyāṃ kalpayanti, tejodhātumapi samāpadyante, jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kurvanti/
100.015. anye praśnān pṛcchanti, anye visarjayanti/
100.016. gāthādvayaṃ bhāṣante--
100.017. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
100.018. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//3//
body.translated_text: But when they produce a supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>) thought, even <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) cannot reach it—how much less the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples)! Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods had this thought: "For what purpose has the <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought?" They thought: "He wishes to display the great miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s> for the benefit of living beings." Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods, along with many hundreds of thousands of deities, having known the thought in the mind of the <s>Bhagavān</s>—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—in the same way, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods, along with many hundreds of thousands of deities, vanished from the divine realm and stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat down on the right side. <s>Śakra</s> and the other gods circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat down on the left side. The <s>Nāga</s> kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> offered to the <s>Bhagavān</s> a magically created thousand-petaled lotus, the size of a cart wheel, entirely golden, with a jeweled stalk. The <s>Bhagavān</s> sat on the pericarp of the lotus, crossing his legs, holding his body erect, establishing mindfulness before him. Above that lotus, another lotus was magically created. There too the <s>Bhagavān</s> sat cross-legged. Thus in front, behind, and on the sides. In this way the <s>Bhagavān</s> created a mass of <s>Buddhas</s> reaching up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven, Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> with an assembly magically created. Some of the magically created <s>Buddhas</s> were walking, some standing, some sitting, some lying down; they also entered the fire element, performing miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and flashing. Others asked questions, others answered. They spoke a pair of verses: "Strive forth, go forth, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching! Shake off the army of Death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut!"

body.text:
100.019. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
100.020. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//4//
body.translated_text: "Whoever in this Dharma and Vinaya shall live heedfully, having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering."

body.text: 100.021. bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā sarvaloko 'nāvṛtamadrākṣīdbuddhāvataṃsakaṃ yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanamupādāya antato bāladārakā api, yathāpi tadbuddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> had so empowered it that the entire world saw without obstruction the garland of <s>Buddhas</s> reaching up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven—even small children—such was the power of the <s>Buddha</s> and the power of the deities.

body.text:
100.024. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--tāvat pratigṛhṇīta bhikṣavo 'nupūrve sthitāyā buddhapiṇḍyā nimittam/
100.025. ekapade 'ntardhāsyanti/
100.025. yāvadekapade 'ntarhitā/
100.025. atha bhagavāṃstam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāraṃ pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
100.026. niṣadya bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
100.028. tāvadavabhāsate kṛmiryāvannodayate divākaraḥ/
100.029. virocana udgate tu vairavyārto(?) bhavati na cāvabhāsate//5//
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: "Behold, monks, take note of the form of the mass of <s>Buddhas</s> standing in sequence. In a single step, they will vanish." Whereupon in a single step they vanished. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having withdrawn that supernatural transformation, sat down on the very seat that had been prepared. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that time spoke this verse: "A glowworm shines only so long as the sun has not risen; but when the radiant sun has risen, it is distressed and shines no more."

body.text:
100.030. tāvadavabhāsitamāsa tārkikairyāvannoditavāṃstathāgataḥ/
100.031. saṃbuddhāvabhāsite tu loke na tārkiko bhāsate na cāsya śrāvakaḥ//6//
body.translated_text: "The logicians shone only so long as the <s>Tathāgata</s> had not arisen; but when the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) illuminates the world, neither the logician shines nor his disciple."

body.text:
100.032. atha rājā prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatā uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
100.033. yūyamapi vidarśayadhvam/
100.033. evamukte tīrthyāstūṣṇīṃbhūtā yāvat <101>prayāṇaparamāḥ sthitāḥ/
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma. Now you too should display yours." When this was said, the <s>tīrthyas</s> remained silent, intent only on departing.

body.text:
101.001. dvirapi prasenajit kauśalastīrthyānidamavocat--vidarśitaṃ bhagavatā uttare manuṣyadharme riddhiprātihāryam/
101.002. yūyamapi vidarśayadhvam/
101.002. evamukte tīrthyā anyonyaṃ vighaṭṭayanta evāhuḥ--tvamuttiṣṭha tvamuttiṣṭheti/
101.003. na kaścidapyuttiṣṭhati//
body.translated_text: A second time, <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>tīrthyas</s>: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> has displayed the miracle of supernatural power in the higher human dharma. Now you too should display yours." When this was said, the <s>tīrthyas</s>, pushing each other, said: "You get up! You get up!" But not a single one got up.

body.text:
101.004. tena khalu punaḥ samayena pāñciko mahāsenāpatistasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃnipatitaḥ/
101.005. atha pāñcikasya yakṣasenāpateretadabhavat--ciramapi te ime mohapuruṣā bhagavantaṃ viheṭhayiṣyanti bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ceti viditvā tumulaṃ vātavarṣaṃ saṃjanayya mahāntamutsṛṣṭavān/
101.006. tumulena vātavarṣeṇa tīrthyāṇāṃ maṇḍapā adarśanapathe kṣiptāḥ/
101.007. tīrthyā hyaśanivarṣeṇa bādhyamānā diśo digbhyo vicalanti/
101.008. anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇyativarṣeṇa bādhyamānāni yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
101.009. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāni/
101.009. bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā tasyāṃ parṣadyekavāribindur na patitaḥ/
101.010. ekāntaniṣaṇṇānyanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇyudānamudānayanti--aho buddhaḥ, aho dharmaḥ, aho saṃghaḥ/
101.011. aho dharmasya svākhyātatā/
101.012. pāñcikena yakṣasenāpatinā tīrthyā abhihitāh--ete yūyaṃ mohapuruṣā bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchadhvaṃ dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
101.013. te niṣpalāyamānāḥ kathayanti--ete vayaṃ parvataṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ, vṛkṣāṇāṃ kuḍyānāmārāmāṇāṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ//
body.translated_text:
101.004. At that time, <s>Pāñcika</s>, the great general, was also seated in that assembly.
101.005. Then <s>Pāñcika</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s> general, thought: 'These deluded men will harass the Blessed One and the community of monks for a long time.' Knowing this, he generated a tumultuous storm of wind and rain and unleashed a great one.
101.006. By the tumultuous storm of wind and rain, the pavilions of the heretics were hurled out of sight.
101.007. The heretics, assailed by the thunderbolt rain, scattered in all directions.
101.008. Many hundreds of thousands of beings, afflicted by the excessive rain, approached the Blessed One.
101.009. Having approached and bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
101.009. The Blessed One made such a resolution that not a single drop of water fell in that assembly.
101.010. The many hundreds of thousands of beings, seated to one side, uttered exclamations of wonder: 'Oh, the <s>Buddha</s>! Oh, the <s>Dharma</s>! Oh, the <s>Saṃgha</s>!'
101.011. 'Oh, the excellence of the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>!'
101.012. <s>Pāñcika</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s> general, addressed the heretics: 'You deluded men! Take refuge in the Blessed One, in the <s>Dharma</s>, and in the community of monks!'
101.013. Fleeing, they said: 'We take refuge in mountains, we take refuge in trees, walls, and gardens!'

body.text:
101.015. atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
101.016. bahavaḥ śaraṇam yānti parvatāṃśca vanāni ca/
101.017. ārāmāṃścaityavṛkṣāṃśca manuṣyā bhayatarjitāḥ//6//
body.translated_text:
101.015. Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke a verse:
101.016. 'Many take refuge in mountains and forests,
101.017. in gardens and sacred trees — humans terrified by fear.'

body.text:
101.018. na hyetaccharaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naitaccharaṇamuttamam/
101.019. naitaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhāt pramucyate//7//
body.translated_text:
101.018. 'This is not the best refuge, this is not the supreme refuge;
101.019. By taking this refuge, one is not freed from all suffering.'

body.text:
101.020. yastu buddhaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gataḥ/
101.021. āryasatyāni catvāri paśyati prajñayā yadā//8//
body.translated_text:
101.020. 'But one who has taken refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>,
101.021. when one sees with wisdom the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāri āryasatyāni</s>) —'

body.text:
101.022. duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasamutpannaṃ nirodhaṃ samatikramam/
101.023. āryaṃ cāṣṭāṅgikaṃ mārgaṃ kṣemaṃ nirvāṇagāminām//9//
body.translated_text:
101.022. 'Suffering, the origin of suffering, cessation, and the transcendence,
101.023. the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgika mārga</s>), the secure path leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> —'

body.text:
101.024. eta{dvai} śaraṇaṃ śreṣṭhametaccharaṇamuttamam/
101.025. etaccharaṇamāgamya sarvaduḥkhātpramucyate//10//
body.translated_text:
101.024. 'This indeed is the best refuge, this is the supreme refuge;
101.025. By taking this refuge, one is freed from all suffering.'

body.text:
101.026. atha pūraṇasyaitadabhavat--śramaṇo gautamo madīyāñ śrāvakānanvāvartayiṣyati/
101.026. iti viditvā niṣpalāyan kathayati--aham yuṣmākaṃ śāsanasarvasvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi/
101.027. yāvad dṛṣṭigatān grāhayitumārabdhaḥ/
101.028. yaduta antavāmllokaḥ, anantaḥ, antavāṃścānantavāṃśca, naivāntavānnānantavān, sa jīvastaccharīramanyo jīvo 'nyaccharīramiti/
101.029. te kalahajātā viharanti bhaṇḍanajātā vigṛhītā vivādamāpannāḥ/
101.030. pūraṇo 'pi bhīto niṣpalāyitumārabdhaḥ/
101.030. sa niṣpalāyan paṇḍakena pratimārge dṛṣṭaḥ/
101.031. paṇḍako dṛṣṭvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text:
101.026. Then <s>Pūraṇa</s> thought: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will win over my disciples.'
101.026. Knowing this, he fled saying: 'I shall tell you the essence of all teachings!'
101.027. He then began to make them grasp his wrong views.
101.028. Namely: 'The world has an end; it is endless; it has an end and is endless; it neither has an end nor is endless; the soul is the same as the body; the soul is different from the body.'
101.029. They dwelt quarreling, disputing, arguing, and engaged in conflict.
101.030. <s>Pūraṇa</s> too, frightened, began to flee.
101.030. While fleeing, he was seen on the road by a eunuch.
101.031. The eunuch, seeing him, spoke a verse:

body.text:
102.001. <102>kutastvamāgacchasi muktapāṇi rathakārameṣa iva nikṛttaśṛṅgaḥ/
102.003. dharmaṃ hyabhijñāya jinapraśastamāhiṇḍase kolikagardabho yathā//11//
body.translated_text:
102.001. 'From where do you come, empty-handed, like a ram of the wheelwright with horns cut off?
102.003. Having known the <s>Dharma</s> praised by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), you wander about like a donkey of <s>Kolika</s>!'

body.text:
102.005. pūraṇaḥ prāha--
102.006. gamanāya me samayaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ kāyasya me balavīryam {na?} kiṃcit/
102.008. spṛṣṭāśca bhāvāḥ sukhaduḥkhate me anāvṛtaṃ jñānamihārhatām//12//
body.translated_text:
102.005. <s>Pūraṇa</s> replied:
102.006. 'The time for my departure has arrived; my body has no strength or vigor.
102.008. Feelings of pleasure and pain have been experienced by me; uncovered is the knowledge of the <s>Arhats</s> here.'

body.text:
102.010. dūrāpagato 'smi .... paratimirāpanudaśca tṛṣaṃ patati/
102.012. ācakṣva me dūṣika etamarthaṃ śītodakā kutra sā puṣkiriṇī//13//
body.translated_text:
102.010. 'I have gone far... and the dispeller of the darkness of others thirsts and falls.
102.012. Tell me, you wretch, this matter — where is that pool of cool water?'

body.text:
102.014. napuṃsakaḥ prāha--
102.015. eṣā khalu śītā puṣkiriṇī nalinī ca virājati toyadhārā/
102.017. śramaṇādhama hīnāsatpuruṣa tvamimāṃ nanu paśyasi puṣkariṇīm//14//
body.translated_text:
102.014. The eunuch replied:
102.015. 'Here indeed is a cool pool, and a lotus pond shines with streams of water.
102.017. O lowest of ascetics, vile and wicked man, do you not see this pool?'

body.text:
102.019. purāṇaḥ prāha--
102.020. na tvaṃ naro nāpi ca nārikā tvaṃ śmaśrūṇi ca te nāsti na ca stanau tava/
102.022. bhinnasvaro 'si na ca cakravākah evaṃ bhavān vātahato nirucyate//15//
body.translated_text:
102.019. <s>Pūraṇa</s> replied:
102.020. 'You are not a man, nor are you a woman; you have no beard, nor do you have breasts.
102.022. Your voice is broken, yet you are not a <s>cakravāka</s> bird; thus you are called one struck by the wind.'

body.text:
102.024. atha pūraṇo nirgrantho vālukāghaṭaṃ kaṇṭhe baddhvā śītikāyāṃ puṣkiriṇyāṃ patitaḥ/
102.024. sa tatraiva kālagataḥ//
body.translated_text:
102.024. Then <s>Pūraṇa</s> the <s>Nirgrantha</s>, having tied a pot of sand around his neck, plunged into the cool pool.
102.024. There he died.

body.text:
102.026. atha te nirgranthāḥ pūraṇaṃ mṛgayamāṇāḥ pratimārge gaṇikāṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛcchanti--bhadre, kaṃcit tvamadrākṣīrgacchantamiha pūraṇaṃ dharmaśāṭapraticchannaṃ kaṭacchavratabhojanam? gaṇikā prāha--
102.028. āpāyiko nairayiko muktahastāvacārakaḥ/
102.029. śvetābhyāṃ pāṇipādābhyāmeṣa dhvaṃsati pūraṇaḥ//16//
body.translated_text:
102.026. Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s>, searching for <s>Pūraṇa</s>, saw a courtesan on the road and asked: 'Good woman, did you see <s>Pūraṇa</s> passing by here, concealed in a dharma-cloth, eating with a ladle as his vow?' The courtesan replied:
102.028. 'Destined for the lower realms, bound for hell, with hands free and wandering,
102.029. with pale hands and feet, this <s>Pūraṇa</s> falls to ruin.'

body.text:
102.030. bhadre maivaṃ vocastvaṃ naitattava subhāṣitam/
102.031. dharmaśāṭapraticchanno dharmaṃ saṃcarate (saṃśrayate?) muniḥ//17//
body.translated_text:
102.030. 'Good woman, do not speak thus; this is not well spoken by you.
102.031. Concealed in a dharma-cloth, the sage resorts to the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text:
102.032. gaṇikā prāha--
102.033. kathaṃ sa buddhimān bhavati puruṣo vyañjanānvitaḥ/
102.034. lokasya paśyato yo 'yaṃ grāme carati nagnakaḥ//18//
body.translated_text:
102.032. The courtesan replied:
102.033. 'How can that man be wise, endowed with the marks of a man,
102.034. who walks naked in the village while the world looks on?'

body.text:
103.001. <103>yasyāyamīdṛśo dharmaḥ purastāllambate daśā/
103.002. tasya vai śravaṇau rājā kṣurapreṇāvakṛntatu//19//
body.translated_text:
103.001. 'One whose <s>dharma</s> is such that his condition hangs before him —
103.002. let the king cut off his ears with a razor!'

body.text:
103.003. atha te nirgranthā yena śītikā puṣkiriṇī tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
103.003. adrākṣuste nirgranthāḥ pūraṇaṃ kāśyapaṃ puṣkiriṇyāṃ mṛtam/
103.004. kālagataṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ puṣkiriṇyā uddhṛtya ekānte chorayitvā prakrāntāḥ//
body.translated_text:
103.003. Then those <s>Nirgranthas</s> approached the cool pool.
103.003. They saw <s>Pūraṇa</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> dead in the pool.
103.004. Seeing him dead, they pulled him out of the pool, abandoned him to one side, and departed.

body.text:
103.006. bhagavatā buddhanirmāṇo nirmito dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgato muṇḍaḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ/
103.007. dharmatā khalu buddhā bhagavanto nirmitena sārdhaṃ niścayaṃ kurvanti/
103.007. yaṃ khalu śrāvako nirmitamabhinirmimīte, yadi śrāvako bhāṣate, nirmito 'pi bhāṣate/
103.008. śrāvake tūṣṇībhūte nirmito 'pi tūṣṇībhavati/
103.010. ekasya bhāṣamāṇasya sarve bhāṣanti nirmitāḥ/
103.011. ekasya tūṣṇībhūtasya sarve tūṣṇībhavanti te//20//
body.translated_text:
103.006. The Blessed One created a <s>Buddha</s>-emanation endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, tonsured and clad in a monastic robe.
103.007. It is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, to make a determination together with the emanation.
103.007. When a disciple creates an emanation — if the disciple speaks, the emanation also speaks.
103.008. When the disciple is silent, the emanation is also silent.
103.010. When one speaks, all the emanations speak;
103.011. when one is silent, all are silent.

body.text:
103.012. bhagavān nirmitaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchati, bhagavān vyākaroti/
103.012. eṣā hi dharmatā tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksambuddhānām//
body.translated_text:
103.012. The Blessed One asked the emanation a question; the Blessed One answered.
103.012. For such is the nature of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones.

body.text:
103.014. bhagavatā tasya mahājanakāyasya tathā abhiprasannasya āśayaṃ cānuśayaṃ ca dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhakī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yathā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni kaiściduṣma(?)gatānyadhigatāni mūrdhānaḥ kṣāntayo laukikā agradharmāḥ/
103.017. kaiścitsrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalamanāgāmiphalam/
103.017. kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
103.018. kaiścicchrāvakamahābodhau bījānyavaropitāni/
103.018. kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau bījānyavaropitāni/
103.019. yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā/
103.020. atha bhagavāṃstāṃ parṣadaṃ buddhaniṃnāṃ dharmapravaṇāṃ saṃghaprāgbhārāṃ vyavasthāpyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ//

103.022. dhanyāste puruṣā loke ye buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ/
103.023. nirvṛtiṃ te gamiṣyanti buddhakārakṛtau janāḥ//21//
body.translated_text:
103.022. 'Blessed are those people in the world who have taken refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>;
103.023. they shall go to liberation (<s>Nirvṛti</s>), those people who have served the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text:
103.024. ye 'lpānapi jine kārān kariṣyanti vināyake /
103.025. vicitraṃ svargamāgamya te lapsyante 'mṛtaṃ padam//22//
body.translated_text:
103.024. 'Those who will render even small services to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), the Guide,
103.025. having attained the marvelous heavenly realm, they shall obtain the immortal state.'

body.text:
103.026. idamavocadbhagavān/
103.027. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
103.026. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
103.027. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 103.028. iti śrrīdivyāvadāne prātihāryasūtraṃ dvādaśamam//
body.translated_text: 103.028. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Prātihārya Sūtra</s> (the Miracle Discourse), the twelfth.

body.text: 104.001. div13 svāgatāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 104.001. Chapter 13: The <s>Svāgata Avadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Svāgata</s>).

body.text:
104.002. buddho bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
104.002. tena khalu punaḥ samayena śiśumāragirau bodho nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhāno mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
104.004. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
104.005. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
104.005. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
104.006. sā upariprāsādatalagatā ayantritopacārā dhāryate, kālartukaiścopakaraṇairanuvidhīyate, vaidyaprajñaptaiścāhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyaistiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitairāhāraiḥ/
104.008. hārārdhahārabhūṣitagātrā apsareva nandanavanacāriṇī mañcānmañcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭhamanavatarantī adharimāṃ bhūmim/
104.010. na cāsyāḥ kiṃcidamanojñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya/
104.010. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
104.011. dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prādādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā/
104.012. tasyāstrīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasān vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā varṇasaṃsthānaviśeṣānurūpaṃ nāmadheyaṃ vyapasthāpitam/
104.013. sā dhātryaṅkagatā unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā saripimaṇḍenānyaiśca cottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
104.014. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam/
104.015. yadā mahatī saṃvṛttā, tadā rūpiṇī yauvanānurūpayā ācāravihāraceṣṭayā devakanyeva tadgṛhamavabhāsamānā sugṛtsambandhibāndhavānāmantarjanasya ca prītimutpādayati/
104.016. tasyāstādṛśīṃ vibhūtiṃ śrutvā nānādeśanivāsrājaputrā amātyaputrā gṛhapatiputrā dhaninaḥ śreṣṭhiputrāḥ sārthavāhaputrāśca bhāryārtham yācanakān preṣayanti/
104.018. yathā yathā cāsau prāthyate, tathā tathā bodho gṛhapatiḥ sutarāṃ prītimutpādayati/
104.019. saṃlakṣayati--mayā eṣā na kasyacidrūpeṇa deyā, na śilpena, nāpyādhipatyena, kiṃ tu yo mama kulaśīlena vā dhanena vā sadṛśo bhavati, tasya mayā dātavyeti/
104.020. sa caivaṃ cintayati//
body.translated_text:
104.002. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
104.002. At that time, in <s>Śiśumāragiri</s>, there lived a householder named <s>Bodha</s>, who was wealthy, possessing great riches and great fortune, with extensive and vast property, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s wealth.
104.004. He had brought a wife from a family of equal standing.
104.005. He enjoyed himself, delighted, and amused himself with her.
104.005. In time, while he was enjoying, delighting, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant.
104.006. She was kept on the upper terrace of the mansion, attended without restraint, provided with seasonal provisions, and given food prescribed by physicians — not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, free from bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent extremes.
104.008. Her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>Apsaras</s> wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, she did not descend from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the lower floor.
104.010. Nor was any unpleasant sound heard by her — all for the sake of the ripening of the embryo.
104.010. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth.
104.011. A girl was born — beautiful, lovely, radiant, endowed with all limbs and features.
104.012. For her, the birth celebration was performed elaborately for three weeks, twenty-one days, and a name was given befitting her complexion and form.
104.013. Held in the lap of a nurse, she was raised and nourished with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions.
104.014. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.
104.015. When she had grown up, with a beauty and conduct befitting her youth, like a divine maiden she illuminated that household, generating delight among kin, relatives, and the household members.
104.016. Having heard of her such splendor, princes, sons of ministers, sons of householders, wealthy men, sons of merchants, and sons of caravan leaders from various lands sent suitors seeking her hand in marriage.
104.018. The more she was sought, the more the householder <s>Bodha</s> was exceedingly pleased.
104.019. He considered: 'I shall not give her to anyone for beauty alone, nor for skill, nor for power alone. Rather, I shall give her to one who is equal to me in family, character, or wealth.'
104.020. And so he reflected.

body.text:
104.021. anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā śrutam yathā śiśumāragirau bodho gṛhapatistasya duhitā evaṃ rūpayauvanasamuditā, sā nānādeśanivāsināṃ rājāmātyagṛhapatidhanināṃ śreṣṭhisārthavāhaputrāṇāmarthāya prārthyata iti/
104.023. śrutvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--ahamapi tāvat tāṃ putrasyārthāya prārthayāmi/
104.024. kadācid bodho gṛhapatirdadyāditi viditvā tasyā yācanakāḥ preṣitāḥ/
104.024. bodhena gṛhapatinā anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ samudācāradhanasampadaṃ ca vicārya dattā/
104.025. anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā mahatā śrīsamudayena putrasya pariṇītā/
104.026. yāvat punarapi bodhasya gṛhapateḥ patnyā sārdhaṃ krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
104.027. yameva divasamāpannasattvā saṃvṛttā, tameva divasaṃ bodhasya gṛhapateranekānyanarthaśatāni prādurbhūtāni/
104.028. tena naimittikā āhūya pṛṣṭāh--bhavantaḥ, paśyata kasya prabhāvānmamānarthaśatāni prādurbhūtāni/
104.029. naimittikā vicāryaikamatenāhuh--gṛhapate, ya eṣa tava patnyāḥ kukṣimavakrāntaḥ, asyaiṣa prabhāvaḥ/
104.030. tadasya parityāgaḥ kriyatām/
104.031. iti śrutvā bodho gṛhapatiḥ paraṃ viṣādamāpannaḥ/
104.031. kathayati--bhavantaḥ, svāgataṃ na parityakṣyāmīti/
104.032. naimittāḥ svastītyuktvā prakrāntāḥ/
104.032. atha bodho gṛhapatirviyogasaṃjanitadaurmanasyo 'pi<105> lokāpavādabhayādabhyupekṣyāvasthitaḥ/
body.translated_text:
104.021. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard that in <s>Śiśumāragiri</s>, the householder <s>Bodha</s> had a daughter endowed with such beauty and youth, and that she was being sought by princes, sons of ministers, householders, wealthy men, guild-masters, and sons of caravan-leaders from various lands.
104.023. Having heard this, he thought: 'I too shall seek her for my son.'
104.024. Thinking that perhaps the householder <s>Bodha</s> might give her, he sent suitors to ask for her.
104.024. The householder <s>Bodha</s>, having considered the conduct, wealth, and prosperity of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, gave her.
104.025. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> married her to his son with great pomp and splendor.
104.026. In due course, while the householder <s>Bodha</s> was again enjoying, delighting, and amusing himself with his wife, his wife became pregnant.
104.027. On the very day she became pregnant, hundreds of misfortunes arose for the householder <s>Bodha</s>.
104.028. He summoned diviners and asked them: 'Sirs, look and see — by whose influence have these hundreds of misfortunes arisen for me?'
104.029. The diviners, having deliberated, said unanimously: 'Householder, the one who has descended into your wife's womb — this is his influence.
104.030. Therefore, let him be abandoned.'
104.031. Hearing this, the householder <s>Bodha</s> was overcome with extreme dejection.
104.031. He said: 'Sirs, I shall not abandon <s>Svāgata</s> (the welcome one).'
104.032. The diviners said 'So be it' and departed.
104.032. Then the householder <s>Bodha</s>, though afflicted with grief born of separation, endured the situation out of fear of public censure.

body.text:
105.001. yathā yathāsau garbho vṛddhiṃ gacchati, tathā tathā bodhasya gṛhapateruttarottarātiśayenānarthaśatānyutpadyante/
105.002. sa saṃlakṣayati--ka etāni śṛṇoti? udyānaṃ gatvā tiṣṭhāmīti viditvā tena pauruṣeyā uktāh--yadi me kaścinmahānanartha utpadyate, sa śrāvayitavyo nānya ityuktvā udyānaṃ gatvā avasthito yāvadasyāsau patnī prasūtā/
105.005. dārako jātaḥ/
105.005. anyatamaḥ puruṣastvaritaṃ tvaritaṃ bodhasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
105.005. tenāsau dūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ/
105.006. sa saṃlakṣayati--yathāyaṃ tvaritatvaritamāgacchati, nūnaṃ mahānanarthaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
105.007. iti viditvā sasambhramaḥ pṛcchati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ tvaritvaritamāgacchasīti? sa kathayati--gṛhapte, diṣṭyā vardhase, putraste jāta iti/
105.008. sa kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, yadyapi me putro 'narhaśatānyutpādya jātaḥ, tathāpi svāgatamasyeti/
105.009. tadanantarameva dvitīyapuruṣastathaiva tvaritatvaritamaśruparyākulekṣaṇo bodhasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
105.010. so 'pi tenānarthatayā sasambhrameṇa pṛṣṭah--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ tvaritatvaritamāgacchasīti? sa bāṣpoparudhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ karuṇādīnavilambitākṣaraṃ kathayati--gṛhapate, gṛhe 'gnirutthitaḥ/
105.012. sarvaṃ svāpateyaṃ dagdhamiti/
105.012. sa muhurmuhuranarthaśravaṇadṛḍhīkṛtacittasaṃtatiḥ kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, prāptavyametat/
105.013. alaṃ viṣādena, tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭheti/
105.014. atha tasya jñātayo lokadharmānuvṛttyā avajñāpūrvakena nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayitumārabdhāh--kiṃ bhavatu dāraksya nāmeti/
105.015. tatraike kathayanti--yatkulasadṛśaṃ tatkriyatāmiti/
105.015. apare kathayanti--yena bodhasya gṛhapateḥ kukṣigatenaivānekadhanasamuditaṃ gṛhaṃ nidhanamupanītam, tasya kīdṛśaṃ kulasadṛśaṃ nāma vyavasthāpyate? api tu ayaṃ pitrā jātamātraḥ svāgatavādena samudācaritaḥ, tasmādasya svāgata iti nāma bhavatu iti/
105.018. tasya svāgata iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
105.018. yathā yathā svāgato vṛddhimupayāti, tathā tathā bodhasya gṛhapaterdhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyāstanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti/
105.020. yāvadapareṇa samayena bodho gṛhapatiḥ kālagataḥ/
105.021. sāpyasya patnī kālagatā/
105.021. tadgṛhaṃ pratisaṃskṛtaṃ punaragninā dagdham/
105.022. ye 'pyasya pauruṣeyāḥ paṇyamādāya deśāntaragatā mahāsamudram yāvattīrṇāḥ, tataḥ keṣāṃcidyānapātraṃ vipannam, keṣāṃcit paṇyamapaṇyījātam, kecit tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannāḥ, keṣāṃcit kāntāramadhyagatānāṃ caurairdravyamapahṛtam, keṣāṃcinnagarasamīpamanuprāptānāṃ śaulkikaśaulkikairdravyaṃ vicārayadbhiḥ sāro gṛhītaḥ, keṣāṃcit pattanamanuprāptānāṃ rājñā viniyuktairdoṣamutpādya sarvasvamapahṛtam/
105.026. kecidbodhasya gṛhapateḥ prāṇaviyogaṃ śrutvā tatraiva avasthitāḥ/
105.027. jñātīnāmapi kecit kālagatāḥ, kecinniṣpalāyitāḥ, kecit tatraivāvasthitāḥ svāgatasya vācamapi na prayacchanti/
105.028. dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyā api kecit kālagatāḥ, kecinniṣpalāyitāḥ, kecidanyāśrayeṇa tatraivāvasthitāḥ santaḥ svāgatasya nāmāpi na gṛhṇanti/
105.030. kiṃ tu bodhasyaikā purāṇavṛddhā dāsī kṛtajñatayā svāgatasyopasthānaṃ kurvantī tiṣṭhati/
105.031. tayā sa lipyakṣaracāryasyākṣarāṇi śikṣayitumupanyastaḥ/
105.031. sā saṃlakṣayati--bodhasya gṛhapatergṛhamanekadhanasamuditaṃ vistīrṇasvajanabandhuvargaṃ prabhūtadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyam<106> paryādānaṃ gatam/
body.translated_text:
105.001. As the embryo grew, so too did hundreds of misfortunes arise for the householder <s>Bodha</s>, each surpassing the last.
105.002. He reflected: 'Who listens to all this? I shall go to the garden and stay there.' Knowing this, he told his servants: 'If some great misfortune befalls me, that alone should be reported to me, and nothing else.' Having said this, he went to the garden and stayed there. In due course, his wife gave birth.
105.005. A boy was born.
105.005. One of the men went hurrying to the presence of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.
105.005. He was seen by him from afar.
105.006. He reflected: 'The way this one comes hurrying, surely a great misfortune has occurred.'
105.007. Knowing this, he asked anxiously: 'Good man, why do you come in such haste?' He said: 'Householder, congratulations! A son has been born to you!'
105.008. He said: 'Good man, although my son has been born bringing hundreds of misfortunes, still — welcome (<s>svāgata</s>) to him.'
105.009. Immediately after, a second man came in the same hurrying manner, his eyes brimming with tears, to the presence of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.
105.010. He too was anxiously asked by the one expecting misfortune: 'Good man, why do you come in such haste?' He, his throat choked with tears, his voice faltering with sorrow, said in drawn-out, pity-filled syllables: 'Householder, a fire has broken out in the house.
105.012. All the property has been burned.'
105.012. He, his mind strengthened by repeatedly hearing of misfortunes, said: 'Good man, this was to be expected.
105.013. Enough of dejection; be silent.'
105.014. Then his relatives, following worldly custom, began to assign a name with contempt: 'What shall the boy's name be?'
105.015. Some said: 'Let it be befitting the family.'
105.015. Others said: 'The one by whose very presence in the womb the household of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, rich with abundant wealth, was brought to ruin — what kind of name befitting the family can be given to him?
