Rather, this one was greeted at birth by his father with the word "welcome" (<s>svāgata</s>); therefore let his name be <s>Svāgata</s>.'
105.018. Thus the name <s>Svāgata</s> was given to him.
105.018. As <s>Svāgata</s> grew up, so too did the wealth, grain, gold, silver, female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants of the householder <s>Bodha</s> diminish, waste away, and come to exhaustion.
105.020. In time, the householder <s>Bodha</s> passed away.
105.021. His wife too passed away.
105.021. Their house, once repaired, was again burned by fire.
105.022. Those servants who had taken merchandise and gone abroad or descended into the great ocean — of some, their vessels were wrecked; of some, the merchandise became worthless; some there met with calamity through misfortune; of some traveling through the wilderness, their goods were plundered by robbers; of some who reached near a city, the essence was seized by tax-collectors examining their goods; of some who reached the port, the king's officers manufactured charges and confiscated everything.
105.026. Some, hearing of the death of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, remained right there.
105.027. Of the relatives too, some passed away, some fled, some remained right there but would not even give <s>Svāgata</s> a word.
105.028. Of the female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants too, some passed away, some fled, some remained right there depending on others and would not even acknowledge <s>Svāgata</s>'s name.
105.030. However, one old servant woman of <s>Bodha</s>, out of gratitude, continued to attend upon <s>Svāgata</s>.
105.031. By her, he was sent to a writing master to learn his letters.
105.031. She reflected: 'The household of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, rich with abundant wealth, with an extensive circle of relatives and kinsmen, with numerous female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants, has come to exhaustion.'

body.text:
106.001. svāgato 'haṃ cāvasthitāḥ/
106.001. tajjijñāsyāmi tāvat kasyāpuṇyenāyamupaplavaḥ, kiṃ svāgatasya āhosvinmameti/
106.002. tayā svāgatasya nāṃnā sthālyāṃ taṇḍulān prakṣipya bhaktārtham yojitā vinaṣṭāḥ/
106.003. tata ātmano nāṃnā tathaiva yojitāḥ, śobhanaṃ bhaktaṃ saṃpannam/
106.004. sā saṃlakṣayati--asau mandabhāgyaḥ/
106.004. etamāgamya bodhasya gṛhapatergṛhamanekadhanasamuditaṃ vistīrṇasvajanabandhuvargaṃ prabhūtadāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam/
106.006. ahaṃ punar na yāsyāmīti/
106.006. kṛtaḥ sthāsyāmīti? atra prāptakālaṃ sarvathā yāvat prāṇaviyogo na bhavati tāvanniṣpalāyeyem/
106.007. iti viditvā yattatra kiṃcit sāramasti, tamādāya niṣpalāyitā/
106.008. tasmiñ śūnye gṛhe śvānaḥ praviśya kalahaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ/
106.008. yāvadanyatamo dhūrtapuruṣastena pradeśenātikrāmati/
106.009. sa śvānakalahaṃ śrutvā saṃlakṣayati--bodhasya gṛhapatergṛhe śvānaḥ kaliṃ kurvanti/
106.010. kiṃ tadanyaṃ bhavet? paśyāmi tāvaditi/
106.010. sa tatra praviṣṭo yāvat paśyati śūnyam/
106.011. so 'pi tasmādyat kiṃciccheṣāvaśeṣamasti, tamādāya prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
106.001. '<s>Svāgata</s> and I alone remain.
106.001. Let me find out whose demerit has caused this calamity — is it <s>Svāgata</s>'s or mine?'
106.002. By her, rice was thrown into a pot in <s>Svāgata</s>'s name and prepared for cooking — it was ruined.
106.003. Then in the same way, rice was prepared in her own name — excellent food was produced.
106.004. She reflected: 'That one is ill-fortuned.
106.004. On his account, the household of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, rich with abundant wealth, with an extensive circle of relatives and kinsmen, with numerous female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants, has wasted away and come to exhaustion.
106.006. And I — shall I not go?
106.006. Shall I stay? The right time has come for this; by all means, before my life is lost, I should flee.'
106.007. Knowing this, she took whatever of value was there and fled.
106.008. In that empty house, dogs entered and began to fight.
106.008. Meanwhile, a certain rogue was passing by that area.
106.009. Hearing the dogs fighting, he reflected: 'Dogs are fighting in the house of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.
106.010. What could be the matter? Let me see.'
106.010. He entered and saw that it was empty.
106.011. He too took whatever small remnants remained and departed.

body.text:
106.012. tataḥ svāgato bhojanavelāṃ jñātvā lekhaśālāyāḥ svagṛhamāgato bhoktumiti yāvat paśyati śūnyam/
106.013. sa bhoktukāmāvarjitasaṃtatih(?) kṣudhāsaṃjanitadaurmanasyaḥ śabdāpayitumārabdhah--amba ambeti/
106.014. na kaścidvacanaṃ dadāti/
106.014. sa tadgṛhamatiścāmutaśca vyavalokya nairāśyamāpanno niṣkrāntaḥ/
106.015. tasya gṛhasya nātidūre 'nyagṛham/
106.015. tasmin svāgatasya jñātastiṣṭhanti/
106.015. sa teṣāṃ sakāśaṃ gato yāvattatra kaliḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
106.016. te kalahaṃ kṛtvā vyupaśāntāḥ parasparaṃ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, pūrvamasmākamanyonyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sneho bhavati, idānīṃ tu dveṣaḥ/
106.017. paśyadhvaṃ kaścidanya āgataḥ syāditi/
106.018. te samanveṣitumārabdhā yāvat paśyanti svāgatam/
106.018. tatraike kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, svāgataḥ praviṣṭa iti/
106.019. apare kathayanti--nāyaṃ svāgatāḥ, kiṃ tu durāgataḥ, imamāgamyāsmākaṃ kaliḥ prādurbhūta iti/
106.020. sa tairgrīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā niṣkāsito 'nyatra gataḥ/
106.021. tasmādapi niṣkāsito yāvat kroḍamallānāṃ madhye praviṣṭaḥ/
106.021. te yatra yatra bhaikṣārthikāḥ praviśanti, tatra nirbhartsyante niṣkāsyante ca/
106.022. te nairāśyamāpannā riktahastakā riktamallakāḥ śūnyadevakulamaṇḍapavṛkṣamūlānyāgatāḥ/
106.023. te 'nyonyaṃ pṛcchanti--bhavantaḥ, vayaṃ pūrve yatra yatra gacchāmastataḥ pūrṇahastāḥ pūrṇamallakā āgacchāmaḥ/
106.024. idānīṃ ko yogo yena vayaṃ riktahastakā riktamallakā nairāśyamāpannā ihāgatā iti? tatraike kathayanti--nūnaṃ ko 'pi mandabhāgyo 'smākaṃ madhye praviṣṭo yena vayaṃ riktahastā riktamallakā ihāgatā iti/
106.027. apare kathayanti--gatametat/
106.027. dvidhā bhūtvā praviśāma iti/
106.027. te parasmin divase dvidhā praviṣṭāḥ/
106.028. tatra yeṣāṃ madhye svāgataste tathaiva nirbhartsitā niṣkāsitāśca nairāśyamāpannā riktahastā riktamallāśca yathānilayamāgatāḥ/
106.029. te tvanye pūrṇahastā pūrṇamallakā āgatāḥ/
106.030. ye te riktahastakā riktapātrā āgatāste bhūyo dvidhā bhūtvā praviṣṭāḥ/
106.030. tatra teṣāmapi yeṣāṃ madhye svāgataste tathaiva riktahastā riktamallakāścāgatāḥ/
106.031. te bhūyo dvidhā bhūtā evam yāvat svāgatakroḍamallakau praviṣṭau riktahastau riktamallakau āgatau/
106.032. te tvanye pūrṇahastāh <107>pūrṇamallakā āgatāḥ/
body.translated_text:
106.012. Then <s>Svāgata</s>, knowing it was mealtime, came home from the writing school to eat, and found the house empty.
106.013. He, hungry and wanting to eat, his mental continuity disturbed, afflicted with grief born of hunger, began to call out: 'Mother! Mother!'
106.014. No one answered.
106.014. He, looking here and there through the house, overcome with despair, went out.
106.015. Not far from his house was another house.
106.015. In that house lived some of <s>Svāgata</s>'s relatives.
106.015. He went to them, but immediately a quarrel broke out there.
106.016. After quarreling and then calming down, they said to one another: 'Sirs, formerly when we saw each other we had affection; now there is hatred.
106.017. Look — has someone else come in?'
106.018. They began to search and found <s>Svāgata</s>.
106.018. Some said: 'Sirs, <s>Svāgata</s> has come in.'
106.019. Others said: 'This is not <s>Svāgata</s> ("well-come"), but rather <s>Durāgata</s> ("ill-come"); on his account our quarrel broke out.'
106.020. He was seized by the neck and thrown out, and went elsewhere.
106.021. Thrown out from there too, he eventually joined a group of bowl-beggars.
106.021. Wherever those alms-seekers went in, they were rebuked and thrown out.
106.022. They, overcome with despair, empty-handed and with empty bowls, came to empty temple porches, pavilions, and tree-roots.
106.023. They asked one another: 'Sirs, formerly wherever we went, we came back with full hands and full bowls.
106.024. What is the reason that now we have come here empty-handed, with empty bowls, overcome with despair?' Some said: 'Surely some ill-fortuned one has joined our group, on account of whom we have come here empty-handed with empty bowls.'
106.027. Others said: 'Enough of this.
106.027. Let us split into two groups and go in.'
106.027. The next day they went in divided into two groups.
106.028. Those in whose group <s>Svāgata</s> was — they were similarly rebuked, thrown out, overcome with despair, and came back empty-handed with empty bowls.
106.029. But the others came back with full hands and full bowls.
106.030. Those who had come back empty-handed with empty bowls again divided into two groups and went in.
106.030. Of those too, the group in which <s>Svāgata</s> was — they similarly came back empty-handed with empty bowls.
106.031. They divided again and again until at last <s>Svāgata</s> and one bowl-beggar went in together, and they came back empty-handed with empty bowls.
106.032. But the others came back with full hands and full bowls.

body.text:
107.001. tataste kroḍamallakāḥ sarve saṃbhūya saṃkalpaṃ kartumārabdhāh--bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ mandabhāgyo 'smākaṃ madhye praviṣṭho yena vayaṃ riktahastā rikmallakāścāgatāḥ/
107.002. niṣkāsayāma enamiti/
107.003. sa taiḥ prabhūtān prahārān dattvā śirasi ca mallakaṃ bhaṅktvā niṣkāsitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
107.001. Then all the bowl-beggars gathered together and began to make a decision: 'Sirs, this ill-fortuned one has joined our group, on account of whom we have come back empty-handed with empty bowls.
107.002. Let us throw him out.'
107.003. They gave him many blows, broke his bowl on his head, and threw him out.

body.text:
107.004. atrāntare yāvacchrāvasteyo vaṇijo bodhasya gṛhapatervayasyaḥ paṇyamādāya śiśumāragirimanuprāptaḥ/
107.005. tena svāgato mallakena hastagatena pīṭhīṃ gato mukhabimbakena pratyabhijñāta uktaśca--putra tvaṃ bodhagṛhapateḥ putra iti? sa kathayati--tāta, ahaṃ tasya putro durāgata iti/
107.006. sa muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīṃ sthitvā aśruparyākulekṣaṇaḥ kathayati--putra, tau tava mātāpitarau kālagatau? te jñātayah? sa āha--teṣāmapi kecit kālagatāḥ kecidihaiva tiṣṭhanto vācamapi na prayacchanti/
107.008. te dāsīdāskarmakarapauruṣeyāh? teṣāmapi kecit kālagatāḥ, kecinniṣpalāyitāḥ, kecidihaivānyānāśrityāvasthitā vācamapi na prayacchanti/
107.010. yadavaśiṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ tadapi kiṃcidagninā dagdham/
107.011. ye vaṇikpauruṣeyāḥ paṇyaṃ gṛhītvā dhanārthino deśāntaraṃ mahāsamudraṃ cāvatīrṇāḥ, tatrāpi keṣāṃcit paṇyamapaṇyībhūtam, kecit tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannāḥ, keṣāṃcit kāntāramadhyagatānāṃ taskairadravyamapahṛtam, keṣāṃcinnagarasamīpamanuprāptānāṃ śaulkikaśaulkikairdravyaṃ vicārayadbhiḥ sāro gṛhītaḥ, keṣāṃcit pattanamanuprāptānāṃ rājño viniyuktairdoṣamutpādya sarvasvamapahṛtam/
107.015. kecit tasya prāṇaviyogaṃ śrutvā tatraivāvasthitāḥ/
107.015. sa dīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca niśvasya kathayati--putra śrāvastīṃ kiṃ na gacchasi? tāta, kiṃ tatragatasya bhaviṣyati? putra, tatrānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ, tasya putreṇa tava bhaginī pariṇītā/
107.017. sā tava yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyatīti/
107.017. sa kathayati--tāta, yadyevaṃ gacchāmīti/
107.018. tena tasya dvau kārṣāpaṇau dattau, uktaśca--putra, ābhyāṃ tāvadātmānaṃ saṃdhāraya, yāvadahaṃ paṇyaṃ visarjayāmi/
107.019. mayā sārdhaṃ gamiṣyasi/
107.019. tena tau kārṣāpaṇau khustavastrānte baddhvā sthāpitau, karmavipākena vismṛtau/
107.020. tathaivāsau kutaścit kiṃcidārāgayati kiṃcinnārāgāyati/
107.021. kṣudhayā pīḍyamāno 'vasthitaḥ/
107.021. yāvadasau vaṇik paṇyaṃ visarjayitvā pratipaṇyamādāya svāgataṃ vaismṛtya saṃprasthitaḥ/
107.022. svāgato 'pi tena sārdhaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
107.023. yāvat te sārthakāḥ kaliṃ kartumārabdhāḥ, balīvardā yoddhumārabdhāḥ/
107.023. sārthikāḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, pratyavekṣata sārtham/
107.024. mā asau durāgato 'trāgataḥ syāditi/
107.024. taiḥ pratyavekṣamāṇairasau dṛṣṭaḥ/
107.024. te taṃ khaṭucapeṭādibhistāḍayitvā ardhacandrakāreṇa grīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā niṣkāsitumārabdhāḥ/
107.025. sa niṣkāsitaḥ/
107.026. niṣkramyamāṇo vikroṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
107.026. sārthavāhastaṃ kolāhalaśabdaṃ śrutvā nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ, yāvat paśyati taṃ niṣkāsyamānam/
107.027. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, mā enaṃ niṣkāsayata, mamaiṣa vayasyaputro bhavatīti/
107.028. te kathayanti--sārthavāha, yamāgamya bodhasya gṛhapateranekadhanasamuditaṃ sasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavaṃ gṛhaṃ vinaṣṭam, kathaṃ tena sārdhaṃ gacchāmah? sarvathā tvaṃ sārthasya svāmī/
107.029. yadyeṣa gacchati, vayaṃ na gacchāma iti/
107.030. sārthavāhastaṃ kathayati--putra, mahājanavirodho 'tra bhavati/
107.030. sārthakāḥ kṣubhitāḥ/
107.031. tvaṃ paścādvāsoddhātikayā gaccha, ahaṃ tavārthe āhāraṃ sthāpayāmīti/
107.031. sa mātāpitṛviyogapratispardhinā pūrvakarmāparādhaprabhāveṇa duḥkhadaurmanasyena saṃtāpitamanāḥ sāśrukaṇṭhastūṣṇīmavasthitaḥ/
body.translated_text:
107.004. In the meantime, a merchant from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a friend of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, arrived at <s>Śiśumāragiri</s> carrying merchandise.
107.005. <s>Svāgata</s>, holding his bowl, went to a bench, and was recognized by his facial features. He was asked: 'Son, are you the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s>?' He replied: 'Sir, I am his son, <s>Durāgata</s> (ill-fated one).'
107.006. The merchant stood silent for a moment, his eyes filled with tears, and said: 'Son, have your parents passed away?' 'And those relatives?' He replied: 'Of them too, some have passed away, some remain right here but will not even give a word.'
107.008. 'And the female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants?' 'Of them too, some have passed away, some have fled, some remain right here depending on others and will not even give a word.'
107.010. 'Whatever wealth remained, some was burned by fire.'
107.011. 'Those merchant-servants who took merchandise and went abroad or descended into the great ocean seeking wealth — of some the merchandise became worthless, some there met with calamity through misfortune, of some traveling through the wilderness, their goods were plundered by robbers, of some who reached near a city, the essence was seized by tax-collectors examining their goods, of some who reached the port, the king's officers manufactured charges and confiscated everything.'
107.015. 'Some, hearing of his death, remained right there.' He sighed deeply and warmly and said: 'Son, will you not go to <s>Śrāvastī</s>?' 'Sir, what will happen if I go there?' 'Son, there is the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>; his son has married your sister.
107.017. She will provide for your livelihood.' He said: 'Sir, if so, I shall go.'
107.018. The merchant gave him two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins) and said: 'Son, sustain yourself with these until I sell my merchandise.
107.019. You shall go with me.' He tied those two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> in the corner of his tattered garment, but through the workings of <s>karma</s>, he forgot them.
107.020. Thus he managed to get some food from somewhere, and sometimes did not.
107.021. Afflicted by hunger, he remained there. Then that merchant, having sold his merchandise and taken return goods, set out having forgotten <s>Svāgata</s>.
107.022. <s>Svāgata</s> also set out following him.
107.023. Then the caravan members began to quarrel, the bullocks began to fight. The caravan members said: 'Sirs, inspect the caravan.
107.024. Lest that ill-fated one has come here.' Looking around, they spotted him. They struck him with slaps, cuffs, and the like, seized him by the neck with a half-moon grip, and began to expel him.
107.025. He was expelled.
107.026. As he was being cast out, he began to cry aloud. The caravan leader, hearing that commotion, began to look, and saw him being expelled.
107.027. He said: 'Sirs, do not expel him; he is the son of my friend.' 
107.028. They replied: 'Caravan leader, on account of whom the house of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, rich with abundant wealth and full of friends, relatives, and kinsmen, was destroyed — how can we travel with him? In any case, you are the master of the caravan.
107.029. If he goes, we shall not go.'
107.030. The caravan leader said to him: 'Son, there is great opposition from the people here. The caravan members are agitated.
107.031. You go behind, following the trail of ox-dung; I shall set aside food for you.' He, tormented by the grief of separation from his parents, rivaled by the power of former misdeeds, his mind afflicted with sorrow and dejection, his throat choked with tears, stood in silence.

body.text:
108.001. <108>sārthaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
108.001. so 'pi vāsoddhātikayā gantumārabdhaḥ/
108.001. sa sārthavāhastasyāhāraṃ patrapuṭake baddhvā kiṃcidbhūmau pāṃśunā praticchādya sthāpayati, kiṃcidvṛkṣaśākhāpatrairavacchādya/
108.002. tatra yaṃ bhūmau sthāpayati, sa śṛgālairanyaiścatuṣpādaurbhakṣyate/
108.003. yaṃ vṛkṣaśākhāsu, sa pakṣibhiḥ śākhāmṛgaiśca bhakṣyate/
108.004. tataḥ kiṃcidārāgayati kiṃcinnārāgayati/
108.004. asthānamanavakāśo yaccaramabhavikaḥ sattvo 'samprāpte viśeṣādhigame so 'ntarā kālaṃ kuryāt/
108.005. sa kṛcchreṇa śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
108.005. bahiḥ śrāvastyāmudapānopakaṇṭhake viśrāntaḥ/
108.006. yāvat tasya bhaginyāḥ santikā preṣyadārikā udakārthinī kumbhamādāya gatā/
108.007. sa tayā mukhabimbakena pratyabhijñātaḥ/
108.007. sā ciraṃ nirīkṣya hīnadīnavadanā kathayati--dāraka, tvaṃ bodhasya gṛhapateḥ śuśumāragirīyakasya putra iti? sa kathayati--evaṃ māṃ bhaginījanaḥ saṃjānīta iti/
108.009. sā aśruparyākulekṣaṇā bāṣpoparudhyamānakaṇṭhā urasi prahāraṃ dattvā karuṇādīnavilambitākṣaraṃ praṣṭumārabdhā/
108.010. tau tava mātāpitarau kālagatau? kālagatau/
108.011. te jñātayah? sa kathayati--teṣāmapi kecit kālagatāḥ, kecinniṣpalāyitāḥ, kecit tatraiva tiṣṭhanto vācamapi na prayacchanti/
108.012. te dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyāh? teṣāmapi kecit kālagatāḥ, kecinniṣpalāyitāḥ, kecit tatraivānyānāśrityāvasthitā vācamapi na prayacchanti/
108.014. yadapi dhanajātaṃ tadapi kiṃcidagninā dagdham, kiṃcidanyapauruṣeyā gṛhītvā dhanārthino deśāntaraṃ mahāsamudraṃ cāvatīrṇāḥ/
108.015. tatrāpi keṣāṃcidyānapātraṃ vipannam, keṣāṃcit paṇyamapaṇyībhūtam, kecit tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannāḥ, keṣāṃcit kāntāramadhyagatānāṃ taskarairdravyamapahṛtam, keṣāṃcinnagarasamīpamanuprāptānāṃ śaulkikaśaulkikairdravyaṃ vicārayadbhiḥ sāro gṛhītaḥ, keṣāṃcit pattanamanuprāptānāṃ rājaniyuktairdoṣamutpādya sarvasvamapahṛtam, kecittasya prāṇaviyogaṃ śrutvā tatraivāvasthitāḥ/
108.019. sā dīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca niśvasya kathayati--ihaiva tiṣṭha yāvatte bhaginyāḥ kathayāmīti/
108.020. tayā gatvā tasyāḥ prayacchannaṃ kathitam/
108.020. kīdṛśena paṇyeneti? sā kathayati--kuto 'sya paṇyam? daṇḍamasya haste mallakaśceti/
108.021. tayā tasyārthaṃ mahārhāṇi vastrāṇi dattāni/
108.021. kārṣāpaṇāṃśca dattvā uktā ca--sa vaktavyo yadi te bhāgineyo vā bhāgineyikā vā upasaṃkrāmati, tasyaiva kārṣāpaṇān dadyāḥ/
108.023. mā jñātīnāṃ pratarkyo bhaviṣyatīti/
108.023. sā vastrāṇyādāya kārṣāpaṇāṃśca tasya sakāśaṃ gatā kathayati--imāni te vastrāṇi kārṣāpaṇāśca bhaginyā preṣitāni, kathayati ca--yadi te bhāgineyo vā bhāgineyikā vā upasaṃkrāmati, tasyaitatkārṣāpaṇān dadyāḥ/
108.025. mā jñātīnāṃ pratarkyo bhaviṣyasi/
108.026. sa kathayati--śobhanameva bhavati/
108.026. ityuktvā tūṣṇīmavasthitaḥ/
108.027. dārikā prakrāntā/
108.027. sa saṃlakṣayati--anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirvistīrṇasvajanaparivāraḥ/
108.027. asmākamapi pitā vistīrṇaparivāraḥ/
108.028. teṣāmamekaikaśo vārtāṃ pratyavekṣate/
108.028. bhaginyā ciramālāpo bhaviṣyati/
108.029. sa ca mārgapariśramakhinnena kṣudhārtena na śakyate kartum/
108.029. purobhakṣikāṃ tāvat karomi/
108.030. tṛptaḥ sukhālāpam udyānaṃ gatvā śayitaḥ/
108.031. ācaritaṃ śrāvastyāmudyānamoṣakāḥ puruṣāḥ pratidinamanvāhiṇḍyante/
108.032. te yadi suptaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyanti, pādena ghaṭṭayanti/
108.032. sa yadi prativibudhyate<109>, tamevaṃ vadanti--bhoḥ puruṣa, na tvayā śrutam yathā śrāvastyāmudyānamoṣakāḥ puruṣāḥ pratidinamanvāhiṇḍyante? te yadi suptaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyanti, vadanti--uttiṣṭha gaccheti/
body.translated_text:
108.001. The caravan set out. He too began to follow by the trail of ox-dung. The caravan leader would tie food in leaf-cups, concealing some on the ground under dust and some under tree branches and leaves.
108.002. What was placed on the ground was eaten by jackals and other four-footed animals.
108.003. What was on the tree branches was eaten by birds and tree-dwelling animals.
108.004. Thus he sometimes got food and sometimes did not. It is impossible and inconceivable that a being in his final existence should die before attaining special realization.
108.005. With great difficulty he reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He rested outside <s>Śrāvastī</s> near a well.
108.006. Then a servant girl from his sister's household went with a pitcher seeking water.
108.007. She recognized him by his facial features. After gazing at him for a long time, her face downcast and sorrowful, she said: 'Boy, are you the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s> of <s>Śiśumāragiri</s>?' He replied: 'Yes, my sister's people should know me.'
108.009. With eyes filled with tears, her throat choked with sobs, striking her chest, she began to ask in a voice drawn out with pity and sorrow:
108.010. 'Have your parents passed away?' 'They have passed away.'
108.011. 'And those relatives?' He replied: 'Of them too, some have passed away, some have fled, some remain right there and will not even give a word.'
108.012. 'And the female servants, male servants, workers, and attendants?' 'Of them too, some have passed away, some have fled, some remain right there depending on others and will not even give a word.'
108.014. 'And the wealth?' 'Some was burned by fire; some was taken by other servants who went abroad or descended into the great ocean seeking wealth.
108.015. Of some, their vessels were wrecked; of some, the merchandise became worthless; some there met with calamity through misfortune; of some traveling through the wilderness, their goods were plundered by robbers; of some who reached near a city, the essence was seized by tax-collectors examining their goods; of some who reached the port, the king's officers manufactured charges and confiscated everything; some, hearing of his death, remained right there.'
108.019. She sighed deeply and warmly and said: 'Stay right here while I tell your sister.' 
108.020. She went and told her privately. 'With what kind of merchandise?' She replied: 'Where would he get merchandise? He has a staff in his hand and a bowl.'
108.021. The sister gave expensive garments for him, and giving <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), said: 'Tell him — if your nephew or niece comes to you, give these <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> to them.
108.023. Lest it become a matter of suspicion among the relatives.' She took the garments and <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> and went to him, saying: 'These garments and <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> are sent by your sister, and she says — if your nephew or niece comes to you, give these <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> to them.
108.025. Lest you become a matter of suspicion among the relatives.'
108.026. He replied: 'That is well.' Having said this, he remained in silence.
108.027. The girl departed. He reflected: 'The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> has an extensive retinue of his own people.
108.027. Our father too had an extensive retinue.
108.028. He looks after the affairs of each of them one by one. There will be a long conversation with my sister.
108.029. And that cannot be managed by one exhausted from the journey's fatigue and afflicted by hunger.
108.029. Let me eat something first.'
108.030. Satiated, he went to a park for a comfortable rest and fell asleep.
108.031. It was customary in <s>Śrāvastī</s> that park-thieves — men — roamed about daily.
108.032. If they saw a sleeping man, they would nudge him with their foot. If he woke up, they would say to him: 'Fellow, have you not heard that in <s>Śrāvastī</s> park-thieves roam about daily? If they see a sleeping man, they say — get up and go.'

body.text:
109.002. yadi na prativibudhyate, muṣitvā gacchanti/
109.003. taiḥ pādena ghaṭṭito na prativibudhyate/
109.003. muṣitvā prakrāntāḥ/
109.003. sa vigatamadyamadaḥ pratibuddho yāvat paśyati tānyevānantakāni(?) prāvṛtyāvasthitaḥ/
109.004. tato 'sya bhaginī saṃlakṣayati--aticirayatyasau/
109.005. nūnamatra kāraṇena bhavitavyamiti/
109.005. tasyāsau dārikā punaḥ preṣitā--dārike gaccha, cirayatyasau, paśya kimarthaṃ nāgacchatīti/
109.006. sā gatā yāvat paśyati muṣitakaṃ tenaiva veṣeṇāvasthitam/
109.007. sā tvaritatvaritaṃ gatā tasyāḥ kathayati--ārye, muṣitastenaiva veṣeṇa tiṣṭhatīti/
109.008. sā saṃlakṣayati--yamāgamya bodhasya gṛhapateranekadhanasamuditaṃ sasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavaṃ gṛhaṃ vinaṣṭam, yadi tamiha praveśayāmi, sthānametadvidyate yanmayāpi śvaśuragṛhamanayena vyasanamāpatsyate/
109.010. nāsāviha praveśayitavyaḥ/
109.010. iti viditvā tayāpyupekṣitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
109.002. If he does not wake up, they rob him and leave.
109.003. They nudged him with their foot, but he did not wake up. They robbed him and departed.
109.003. Awakened from his intoxication of exhaustion, he saw that only those same endless(?/worthless?) things remained, and he stood wrapped in them.
109.004. Then his sister reflected: 'He is taking very long.
109.005. There must be some reason for this.'
109.005. That same girl was sent again: 'Girl, go; he is taking long; see why he is not coming.'
109.006. She went and saw him robbed, standing in the same condition.
109.007. She went hurriedly and told her: 'Noble lady, he has been robbed and stands in the same state.'
109.008. She reflected: 'On account of whom the house of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, rich with abundant wealth and full of friends, relatives, and kinsmen, was destroyed — if I bring him in here, it is quite possible that my father-in-law's house too will meet with calamity through misfortune.
109.010. He must not be brought in here.'
109.010. Having decided thus, he was abandoned by her as well.

body.text:
109.011. tasyāpi pūrvakarmāparādhādvismṛtam/
109.011. sa kroḍamallakānāṃ madhye praviṣṭaḥ/
109.011. te yatra yatra bhaikṣārthinaḥ praviśanti, tatra tatra nirbhatsyante ca niṣkāsyante ca/
109.012. nairāśyamāpannā riktahastā riktamallakāḥ śūnyadevakulamaṇḍapavṛkṣamūlānyāgatāḥ/
109.013. te 'nyonyaṃ pṛcchanti--bhavantaḥ, vayaṃ pūrvam yatra yatra gacchāmastataḥ pūrṇahastāḥ pūrṇamallakā gacchāmaḥ/
109.014. idānīṃ ko yogo yena vayaṃ riktahastā riktamallakā nairāśyamāpannā ihāgatā iti? tatraike kathayanti--nūnaṃ ko 'pi mandabhāgyo 'smākaṃ madhye praviṣṭo yena vayaṃ riktahastā riktamallakā ihāgatā iti/
109.016. apare kathayanti--dvidhā bhūtvā praviśāma iti/
109.017. te 'parasmin divase dvidhā bhūtvā praviṣṭāḥ/
109.017. tatra yeṣāṃ madhye svāgataḥ, te tathaiva nirbhartsitā niṣkāsitāśca nairāśyamāpannā riktahastā riktamallakāścāgatāḥ/
109.018. te tvanye pūrṇahastāḥ pūrṇamallakā āgatā/
109.019. ye riktahastā riktamallakā āgatāḥ, te bhūyo dvidhā bhūtvā praviṣṭāḥ/
109.020. teṣāmapi yeṣāṃ madhye svāgataḥ, te tathaiva riktahastā riktamallakāścāgatāḥ/
109.020. te bhūyo dvidhā bhūtā evam yāvat svāgato 'nyaśca kroḍamallakaḥ praviṣṭaḥ/
109.021. tau riktahastau riktamallakau āgatau, te tvanye pūrṇahastāḥ pūrṇamallakā āgatāḥ/
109.022. te kroḍamallakāḥ sarve saṃbhūya saṃjalpaṃ kartumārabdhāh--bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ mandabhāgyasattvo 'smākaṃ madhye praviṣṭo yena vayaṃ riktahastā riktamallakāścāgatāḥ/
109.024. niṣkāsayāma enamiti/
109.024. sa taiḥ prabhūtān prahārān dattvā śirasi ca mallakaṃ bhaṅktvā niṣkāsitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
109.011. On account of his former misdeeds, he too forgot [about his sister].
109.011. He entered among the beggars with broken bowls.
109.011. Wherever those alms-seekers entered, they were scolded and driven out.
109.012. Having fallen into despair, empty-handed and with empty bowls, they came to deserted temple halls, pavilions, and the bases of trees.
109.013. They asked one another: 'Good people, previously wherever we went, we would go away with full hands and full bowls.
109.014. What is the reason now that we have come here empty-handed, with empty bowls, fallen into despair?' Thereupon some said: 'Surely some ill-fated person has entered among us, on account of whom we have come here empty-handed and with empty bowls.'
109.016. Others said: 'Let us divide into two groups and enter.'
109.017. The next day they divided into two groups and entered.
109.017. Of those, in whose group <s>Svāgata</s> was, they were scolded and driven out just the same, and came back having fallen into despair, empty-handed and with empty bowls.
109.018. But the others came back with full hands and full bowls.
109.019. Those who came back empty-handed and with empty bowls divided again into two and entered.
109.020. Of those too, in whose group <s>Svāgata</s> was, they came back empty-handed and with empty bowls just the same.
109.020. They divided again into two, and so on until <s>Svāgata</s> and one other beggar with a broken bowl entered.
109.021. Those two came back empty-handed with empty bowls, while the others came back with full hands and full bowls.
109.022. All those beggars with broken bowls gathered together and began to confer: 'Good people, this ill-fated creature has entered among us, on account of whom we have come back empty-handed and with empty bowls.
109.024. Let us drive him out!'
109.024. They gave him many blows, broke his bowl on his head, and drove him out.

body.text:
109.025. atrāntare 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ/
109.026. tena dauvārikāṇāmājñā dattā--na tāvat kasyacit kroḍamallakasya praveśo dātavyo yāvadbuddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktam/
109.027. paścāt tān bhojayiṣyāmīti/
109.027. kroḍamallakā ye tasya gṛhaṃ pratiśaraṇabhūtāste sarve saṃnipatitāḥ praveṣṭumārabdhāḥ/
109.028. dauvārikeṇa virodhitāḥ/
109.029. kathayanti--bhoḥ puruṣa, asmākameva nāṃnā ayaṃ gṛhapatiḥ prajñāyate anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiriti/
109.030. tat kimidamiti kṛtvā asmān vidhārayasīti? sa kathayati--gṛhapatinā ājñādattā--na tāvat kasyacit kroḍamallakasya praveśo dātavyo yāvadbuddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhuktam/
109.032. paścāt tān bhojayiṣyāmīti/
109.032. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, na kadācidvayaṃ vidhāryamāṇāh<110>/
body.translated_text:
109.025. In the meantime, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had invited the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks) headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal in his private quarters.
109.026. He had given orders to the doorkeepers: 'No beggar with a broken bowl is to be admitted until the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has eaten.
109.027. Afterwards I shall feed them.'
109.027. The beggars with broken bowls, for whom his house was a refuge, all gathered and tried to enter.
109.028. They were stopped by the doorkeeper.
109.029. They said: 'Good man, it is by our very name that this householder is known as <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> ("giver of food to the destitute")!
109.030. On what account then do you obstruct us?' He said: 'The householder has given an order — no beggar with a broken bowl is to be admitted until the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has eaten.
109.032. Afterwards he shall feed them.'
109.032. They said: 'Good people, never before have we been obstructed. <110>

body.text:
110.001. taṃ paśyata mā atrāryā durāgata āgato bhavediti/
110.001. te samanveṣṭitumārabdhā yāvat paśyantyekasmin pradeśe nilīyāvasthitam/
110.002. tatastaiḥ kolāhalaśabdaḥ kṛtah--ayaṃ bhavantaḥ sa durāgato nilīnastiṣṭhatīti/
110.003. sa taiḥ prabhūtān prahārān datvā niṣkāsitastīvreṇa ca paryavasthānena śirasi mallakena prahāro dattaḥ/
110.004. tasya śiro bhagnam/
110.004. sa nivartya vipralapitumārabdhaḥ/
110.005. tatastairhastapādeṣu gṛhītvā saṃkārakūṭe kṣiptah--durāgata atra tiṣṭheti/
110.005. sa rudhireṇa pragharatā tasmin saṃkārakūṭe 'vasthitaḥ/
110.006. yāvadbhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yenānāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
110.008. adrākṣīdbhagavān svāgataṃ paruṣarūkṣāṅgulidīrghakeśaṃ rajasāvacūrṇitagātraṃ kṛśamalpasthānaṃ malinajīrṇavāsonivasitaṃ śirasā bhagnena rudhireṇa pragharatā anyaiśca vraṇaiścākīrṇaiḥ, makṣikābhirupadrutaiḥ saṃkārakūṭe nipatitam/
body.translated_text:
110.001. Look around, lest that noble <s>Durāgata</s> (ill-fated one) has come here.'
110.001. They began to search and found him crouching and hiding in one spot.
110.002. Then they raised a commotion: 'Good people, here that <s>Durāgata</s> is crouching and hiding!'
110.003. They gave him many blows and drove him out, and in their fierce rage struck him on the head with a bowl.
110.004. His head was cracked open.
110.004. He turned back and began to babble deliriously.
110.005. Then they seized him by the hands and feet and threw him on a rubbish heap, saying: '<s>Durāgata</s>, stay here!'
110.005. He lay on that rubbish heap, bleeding profusely.
110.006. Meanwhile, the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks and accompanied by the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>, approached the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
110.008. The Blessed One saw <s>Svāgata</s> — with rough, coarse fingers and long hair, his body covered with dust, emaciated, with barely any flesh, clothed in dirty, worn-out garments, his head cracked open, blood flowing profusely, covered with other wounds infested by flies — lying on the rubbish heap.

body.text:
110.010. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--tṛpyata bhikṣavaḥ sarvabhavopapattibhyaḥ/
110.011. tṛpyata sarvabhavopapattyupakaraṇebhyaḥ, yatra nāma caramabhavikasya sattvasyeyamavasthā/
110.011. tatra bhagavāṃs taṃ svāgatamāmantrayate--ākāṅkṣase vatsa pātraśeṣam? bhagavan/
110.012. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--svāgatasya te ānanda pātraśeṣaḥ sthāpayitavyamiti/
110.013. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt//
body.translated_text:
110.010. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'Be sated, monks, with all forms of existence and rebirth.
110.011. Be sated with all the requisites of existence and rebirth — for such is the condition of a being in his final existence.'
110.011. There the Blessed One addressed <s>Svāgata</s>: 'Do you desire, son, the <s>pātraśeṣa</s> (food remaining in the bowl)?' 'Yes, Blessed One.'
110.012. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Ānanda</s>, you must set aside <s>pātraśeṣa</s> (food remaining in the bowl) for <s>Svāgata</s>.'
110.013. 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One.

body.text:
110.015. atha bhagavān yenānāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapaterbhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
110.015. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
110.016. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
110.019. āyuṣmata ānandasya tatpātraśeṣaṃ svāgatāya vismṛtam/
110.019. asaṃmoṣadharmāṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
110.020. bhagavatā utthāpitam/
110.020. āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pātraṃ gṛhītumārabdho yāvat paśyati tatra pātraśeṣaṃ na saṃsthāpitam/
110.021. dṛṣṭvā ca smṛtirutpannā/
110.021. sa dharmatattvo vacasā(?) atha roditumārabdhaḥ/
110.022. bhagavānāha--kasmāt tvamānanda rodiṣīti/
110.022. sa kathayati--na mayā bhadanta bhagavataḥ kadācidājñā pratyūḍhapūrveti/
110.023. kiṃ kṛtam? svāgatasya pātraśeṣaṃ na sthāpitamiti/
110.024. bhagavānāha--na tvayā ānanda mamājñā pratismṛtā, api tu svāgatasyaiva tāni karmāṇi labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayānyoghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyabhāvīni yena tava vismṛtam/
110.026. alaṃ viṣādena/
110.026. gaccha, taṃ śabdāpayeti/
110.026. sa gatvā śabdāpayitumārabdhaḥ/
110.026. anekaiḥ prativacanaṃ dattam/
110.027. svāgatasya tadapi vismṛtam yadbhagavatā pratijñātam--tava pātraśeṣaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmīti/
110.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--ko 'pyayaṃ puṇyakarmā bhagavatā trailokyaguruṇā samanvāhṛtaḥ śabdata iti/
110.028. āyuṣmatā ānandena gatvā bhagavata ārocitam/
110.029. bhagavan svāgata ityuktvā anekaiḥ prativacanaṃ dattam/
110.030. na jāne kaṃ śabdāpayāmīti/
110.030. bhagavānāha--gaccha ānanda, gatvā kathaya--yo bodhasya gṛhapateḥ śuśumāragirīyasya putraḥ svāgataḥ, sa āgacchatu iti/
110.031. āyuṣmatā ānandena gatvoccaiḥ śabdairuktah--yo bodhasya gṛhapateḥ śuśumāragirīyakasya putraḥ svāgataḥ, sa āgacchatu iti/
110.032. tena putur nāmaśravaṇādātmano nāma smṛtam/
110.032. sa śanairdaṇḍaviṣṭambhanayogādutthāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text:
110.015. Then the Blessed One approached the meal-offering at the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s house.
110.015. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>.
110.016. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having ascertained that the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, served them with his own hands with choice food, both hard and soft, until they were satisfied and had eaten their fill; and knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl set aside, he took a lower seat and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.
110.019. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> forgot to set aside the <s>pātraśeṣa</s> for <s>Svāgata</s>.
110.019. <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are of the nature of unfailing memory.
110.020. The Blessed One reminded him.
110.020. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> began to take up the Blessed One's bowl and then noticed that no <s>pātraśeṣa</s> had been set aside in it.
110.021. Seeing this, the memory arose in him.
110.021. Moved by that realization, he began to weep.
110.022. The Blessed One said: 'Why do you weep, <s>Ānanda</s>?'
110.022. He said: 'Venerable Sir, never before have I failed to carry out the Blessed One's instruction.'
110.023. 'What happened?' 'The <s>pātraśeṣa</s> for <s>Svāgata</s> was not set aside.'
110.024. The Blessed One said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, it is not that you failed to remember my instruction; rather, <s>Svāgata</s>'s own <s>karmas</s> (deeds) have gathered their requisite conditions, their causes have ripened, they have arrived like a torrent, and they are inevitable — that is why you forgot.
110.026. Do not be distressed.
110.026. Go and call him.'
110.026. He went and began to call for him.
110.026. Many people answered back.
110.027. <s>Svāgata</s> too had forgotten that the Blessed One had promised: 'I shall set aside <s>pātraśeṣa</s> for you.'
110.028. He thought: 'Whoever this meritorious being may be, sought out by the Blessed One, the Teacher of the Three Worlds — that person is being called.'
110.028. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> went and reported to the Blessed One:
110.029. 'Blessed One, when I called out "<s>Svāgata</s>," many people answered back.
110.030. I do not know whom to call.'
110.030. The Blessed One said: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and having gone, say: "He who is the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s> of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, <s>Svāgata</s> — let him come."'
110.031. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> went and called out loudly: 'He who is the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s> of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, <s>Svāgata</s> — let him come!'
110.032. Upon hearing his father's name, he remembered his own name.
110.032. He rose slowly, supporting himself with a staff, and spoke a verse:

body.text:
111.001. <111>bhraṣṭaḥ svāgataśabdo 'yaṃ kutaḥ punarihāgataḥ/
111.002. nūnaṃśreyaso nāśaḥ śreyasaśca samudbhavaḥ//1//
body.translated_text:
111.001. <111>'This word "<s>Svāgata</s>" (Well-Come) was lost — from where has it come here again?
111.002. Surely there is a destruction of fortune and also an arising of fortune!' //1//

body.text:
111.003. teṣāṃ sarvajña nātho 'si ye hi tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ/
111.004. teṣāṃ svāgatamāryāṇām ye ca te śāsane ratāḥ//2//
body.translated_text:
111.003. 'You are the protector of all, O Omniscient One, who have taken refuge in you;
111.004. "Well-come" (<s>svāgata</s>) it is for those noble ones who delight in your teaching.' //2//

body.text:
111.005. ahaṃ tu bhāgyarahitaḥ sarvabandhuvivarjitaḥ/
111.006. śocyaḥ kaṣṭāṃ daśāṃ prāptaḥ śokaśalyasamarpitaḥ//3// iti/
111.007. athāyuṣmānānandastamādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
111.007. upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat--ayaṃ bhadanta svāgata iti/
111.008. sa bhagavatā kṣudhāsaṃjanitadaurmanasyaḥ samāśvāsitaḥ, uktaśca--putra, imaṃ pātraśeṣaṃ paribhuṅkṣveti/
111.009. sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--yadyapyahaṃ bhagavatā trailokyaguruṇā daivāt samanvāhṛtaḥ, tadapi stokaḥ pātraśeṣaḥ sthāpitaḥ/
111.010. kimatra bhokṣya iti/
111.011. bhagavāṃstasya cetasā cittamājñāya kathayati--vatsa, yadi tvaṃ sumerumātraiḥ piṇḍaiḥ samudrasadṛśena kuṣkiṇā paribhokṣyase, tathāpyavyayaṃ tanna parikṣayaṃ gamiṣyati, yāvattṛptaḥ paribhuṅkṣva yathāsukhamiti/
111.013. tena tāvad bhuktam yāvat tṛpta iti/
111.013. tatsaṃtarpitendriyo bhagavato mukhaṃ vyavalokayitumārabdhaḥ/
111.014. bhagavānāha--vatsa svāgata, tṛpto 'si? tṛpto 'smi bhagavan/
111.014. vatsa, yadyevamapaścimaṃ kavalaṃ gṛhāṇa, antardhāsyatyeṣa pātra iti/
111.015. tenāpaścimakavalo gṛhītaḥ, so 'ntarhitaḥ/
111.015. bhagavān dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ/
111.016. caramabhavikaḥ sa sattvo bhagavantaṃ pṛṣṭataḥ pṛṣṭataḥ samanubaddhaḥ/
111.017. yāvadbhagavān vihāraṃ gatvā purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
111.017. so 'pi bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
111.018. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--puṣpāṇāmenaṃ preṣayāmi, karmāpanayo 'sya kartavya/
111.019. iti viditvā svāgatamāmantrayate--vatsa sbāgata, santi te kārṣāpaṇāh? na santi bhagavan/
111.020. vatsa svāgata, vastrāntaṃ nirīkṣasva/
111.020. vastrāntaṃ nirīkṣitumārabdho yāvat paśyati dvau kārṣāpaṇau/
111.021. sa kathayati--bhagavan, dvau kārṣāpaṇau/
111.021. vatsa gaccha, gaṇḍakasyārāmikasya sakāśānnīlotpalāni gṛhītvā āgaccheti/
111.022. svāgatastasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
111.022. sa taṃ dūrādeva dṛṣṭvā paryavasthitaḥ/
111.023. sa saṃlakṣayati--āgato 'yaṃ dūrāgataḥ/
111.023. niyataṃ mamānartho bhavati/
111.023. iti viditvā saparuṣaṃ kathayati--durāgata, kimarthaṃ rvamihāgacchasīti/
111.024. sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
111.025. nīlotpalairasti kāryaṃ me tathānyair nāpi paṅkajaiḥ/
111.026. munīndrasya tu dūto 'haṃ sarvajñasya yaśasvinaḥ//4//
body.translated_text:
"But I am devoid of fortune, bereft of all kinsmen,
pitiable, having reached a wretched state, pierced by the arrow of grief." // 3 //
Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> took him and approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: 'This, Venerable Sir, is <s>Svāgata</s>.'
The Blessed One consoled him, afflicted as he was by distress born of hunger, and said: 'Son, eat this <s>pātraśeṣa</s> (food remaining in the bowl).'
Seeing it, he reflected: 'Although I have been, by good fortune, attended to by the Blessed One, the Teacher of the Three Worlds, still only a small amount of <s>pātraśeṣa</s> (leftover food) has been set aside.
What shall I eat here?'
The Blessed One, knowing his mind with his own mind, said: 'Son, even if you were to eat with morsels the size of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and a belly like the ocean, still it would remain inexhaustible and would not come to an end; eat as much as you wish, at your ease.'
He ate until he was satisfied.
With his senses restored by that nourishment, he began to gaze upon the face of the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said: 'Son <s>Svāgata</s>, are you satisfied?' 'I am satisfied, Blessed One.'
'Son, if so, take the last morsel; this bowl will disappear.'
He took the last morsel, and it vanished.
The Blessed One, having given the teaching of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (merit-dedication), departed.
That being, who was in his final existence, followed closely behind the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having gone to the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), sat upon the seat prepared for him before the assembly of monks.
He too, having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, sat to one side.
The Blessed One reflected: 'I shall send him to [the garden of] <s>Puṣpa</s> (flowers); the removal of his <s>karma</s> (karmic obstruction) must be accomplished.'
Knowing this, he addressed <s>Svāgata</s>: 'Son <s>Svāgata</s>, do you have any <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins)?' 'No, Blessed One.'
'Son <s>Svāgata</s>, look at the hem of your garment.'
He began to examine the hem of his garment and saw two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins).
He said: 'Blessed One, there are two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.'
'Son, go to the gardener <s>Gaṇḍaka</s>, obtain blue lotuses, and return.'
<s>Svāgata</s> went to him.
Seeing him from afar, [<s>Gaṇḍaka</s>] became agitated.
He reflected: 'This ill-fated one has come.
Surely misfortune will befall me.'
Knowing this, he spoke harshly: 'Ill-fated one, why have you come here?'
He spoke a verse:
'I have need of blue lotuses and no other water-lilies;
I am the messenger of the Lord of Sages, the Omniscient and Glorious One.' // 4 //

body.text:
111.027. ityuktvā pratinivartitumārabdhaḥ/
111.027. so 'pi gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
111.028. ehyehi yadi dūto 'si tasya śāntātmano muneḥ/
111.029. pūjyaḥ sa naradevānāṃ pūjyaḥ pūjyatamairapi//5//
body.translated_text:
Having spoken thus, he began to turn back.
Then he too spoke a verse:
'Come, come, if you are indeed the messenger of that peaceful-souled Sage;
He is worthy of worship by gods and men, worthy of worship even by the most venerable.' // 5 //

body.text:
111.030. ityuktvā sa kathayati--buddhadūtastvam? buddhadūtaḥ/
111.030. kimarthamāgatah? puṣpārtham/
111.030. yadi buddhadūtastvam, gṛhāṇa yathepsitam/
111.031. nīlotpalānāṃ bhāramādāya bhagavataḥ sakāśamāgataḥ/
body.translated_text:
Having spoken thus, he said: 'Are you the <s>Buddha's</s> messenger?' 'I am the <s>Buddha's</s> messenger.'
'For what purpose have you come?' 'For flowers.'
'If you are the <s>Buddha's</s> messenger, take as many as you wish.'
He took a load of blue lotuses and came to the presence of the Blessed One.

body.text:
112.001. <112>bhagavānāha--vatsa, bhikṣūṇāṃ cāraya/
112.001. sa bhikṣūṇāṃ cārayitumārabdhaḥ/
112.001. bhikṣavo na pratigṛhṇanti/
112.002. bhagavānāha--gṛhṇīdhvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaugandham/
112.002. cakṣurbhyāṃ karmāpanayo 'sya kartavya iti/
112.003. bhikṣubhirgṛhītāni/
112.003. gṛhītvā puṣpitāni/
112.003. tenāpūrvaṃ nīlakṛtsnamutpāditaṃ pūrvam/
112.003. sa vṛddhānte sthitvā tāni puṣpāṇi dṛṣṭvā sutarāṃ nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ/
112.004. tasya tannīlakṛtsnamāmukhībhūtam/
112.005. tatastaṃ bhagavānāha--vatsa, kiṃ na pravrajasīti? sa kathayati--pravrajāmi bhagavanniti/
112.005. bhagavatā pravrajita upasampādito manasikāraśca dattaḥ/
112.006. tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idameva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
112.008. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhaḥ/
112.010. sendropendrāṇāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
112.011. so 'rhattvaṃ prāpto vimuktisukhapratisaṃvedī tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
112.012. upāyapāśairvīreṇa baddhvāhaṃ tattvadarśinā/
112.013. kāruṇyāduddhṛto duḥkhājjīrṇaḥ paṅkādiva dvipaḥ//6//
body.translated_text:
The Blessed One said: 'Son, distribute them among the monks.'
He began to distribute them to the monks.
The monks would not accept them.
The Blessed One said: 'Accept them, monks; they are entirely fragrant.
The removal of <s>karma</s> (karmic obstruction) for his eyes must be accomplished.'
The monks accepted them.
Having accepted them, they bloomed.
By him, the <s>nīlakṛtsna</s> (blue totality meditation) was first produced, something never before achieved.
Standing at the far end, having seen those flowers, he began to gaze upon them intently.
That <s>nīlakṛtsna</s> (blue totality meditation) became manifest before him.
Then the Blessed One said to him: 'Son, why do you not go forth into homelessness?' He replied: 'I shall go forth, Blessed One.'
By the Blessed One he was given the going-forth, the full ordination, and instruction for contemplation.
Striving, exerting, and applying himself diligently, having understood this five-spoked wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) to be unstable, having overcome all the courses of <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) through their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and destruction, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).
He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in all three realms, equal-minded toward a clod of earth and gold, with a mind as impartial as the sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood paste, one whose egg-shell of ignorance was split open by knowledge, who had attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvits</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor.
He became worthy of worship, reverence, and salutation even by <s>Indra</s> and the lesser <s>Indras</s>.
Having attained <s>Arhattva</s>, experiencing the bliss of liberation, at that moment he spoke a verse:
'Bound by the snares of skillful means by the Hero who sees the truth,
out of compassion I have been pulled from suffering, like an aged elephant from the mire.' // 6 //

body.text:
112.014. svāgato 'hamabhūvaṃ prāktataḥ paścāddurāgataḥ/
112.015. āgato 'smi purā nātha śrutvā vākyaṃ tavottamam//7//
body.translated_text:
'I was formerly "<s>Svāgata</s>" (Well-Come), then afterwards "<s>Durāgata</s>" (Ill-Come);
Now I have truly arrived, O Lord, having heard your supreme word.' // 7 //

body.text:
112.016. sāmprataṃ svāgato vyaktam {saṃvṛtto na durāgatah}/
112.017. sāmprataṃ kāñcanaṃ dehaṃ dhārayāmi nirāśravam//8//
body.translated_text:
'Now I am clearly "<s>Svāgata</s>" (Well-Come), {no longer "<s>Durāgata</s>" (Ill-Come)};
Now I bear a golden body, free from all taints.' // 8 //

body.text:
112.018. ratnāni pratilebhe hi svargaṃ mokṣaṃ ca kāṅkṣatām/
112.019. śreṣṭhā kalyāṇamitrāṇāṃ sadā sevā hitaiṣiṇām//9// iti/
112.020. yadā āyuṣmān svāgataḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitaḥ, tadā sāmantakena śabdo visṛtah--śramaṇena gautamenāsau durāgataḥ kroḍamallakaḥ pravrajitaḥ/
112.021. tīrthyaiḥ śrutam/
112.021. te 'vadhyāyanti kṣipanti vivādayanti--śramaṇo bhavanto gautama evamāha--sāmantaprāsādikaṃ me śāsanamiti/
112.023. atra kiṃ sāmantaprāsādikamityasya yatredānīṃ durāgataprabhṛtayo 'pi kroḍamallakāḥ pravrajantīti? atrāntare nāsti kiṃcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāmajñātamadṛṣṭamaviditamavijñātam/
112.024. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--sumeruprakhyo mahāśrāvake mahājanakāyaḥ prasādaṃ pravedayate/
112.025. tadguṇodbhāvanamasya kartavyam, kutra kartavyam? yatraiva patitaḥ/
112.026. iti jñātvā ānandamāmantrayate sma--gaccha ānanda bhikṣūṇāmārocaya--tathāgato bhikṣavo bhargeṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
112.027. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ bhargeṣu cārikāṃ cartum, sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu iti/
112.028. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati--bhagavānāyuṣmanto bhargeṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ cariṣyati/
112.029. yo yuṣmākamutsahate bhagavatā sārdhaṃ bhargeṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritum, sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu iti/
112.031. atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikah <113>prasādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gaja iva kalabhaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭṛgaṇaparivṛto haṃsarāja iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva pauragaṇaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaścakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaścandra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ
sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpakṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto vemacitrīvāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmeva
brahmakāyikagaṇaparivṛtaḥ stimati iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapariḥ sudāntendriyairasaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'śītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātro vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtamūrtiḥ sūryasahasrātirekaprabho jaṅgama iva ratnaparvataḥ samantato bhadrako daśabhirbalaiścaturbhir vaiśāradyaistribhirāveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānairmahākaruṇayā ca samanvāgata ājñātakauṇḍinyabāṣpamahānāmāniruddhaśāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapānandaraivataprabhṛtibhirmahāśrāvakaiḥ parivṛto 'nyena ca mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena yena śuśumāragiristenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text:
'Indeed, one who desires heaven and liberation obtains jewels;
The greatest [treasure] is the constant attendance upon spiritual friends who seek one's welfare.' // 9 //
When the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> went forth into homelessness in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, the word spread throughout the region: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has given the going-forth to that ill-fated beggar-monk <s>Durāgata</s>.'
The <s>tīrthyas</s> (heterodox teachers) heard this.
They disparaged, reviled, and argued: 'Sirs, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> says thus: "My teaching inspires faith in the surrounding regions."
What is faith-inspiring about this, when now even ill-fated beggars like <s>Durāgata</s> are going forth?'
Meanwhile, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unlearned, or unrecognized by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>.
The Blessed One reflected: 'The great multitude will generate faith in a great disciple as mighty as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.
His virtues must be made manifest. Where should this be done? Right where he fell.'
Knowing this, he addressed <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the monks: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, monks, will go on a wandering tour through the <s>Bharga</s> countries.
Whoever among you is willing to go on a wandering tour with the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the <s>Bharga</s> countries, let him take up his robes."'
'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One and announced to the monks: 'The Blessed One, Venerable Ones, will go on a wandering tour through the <s>Bharga</s> countries.
Whoever among you is willing to go on a wandering tour with the Blessed One through the <s>Bharga</s> countries, let him take up his robes.'
Then the Blessed One — tamed, with a tamed retinue; tranquil, with a tranquil retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; at ease, with a retinue at ease; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with a retinue of <s>Arhats</s>; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; serene, with a serene retinue — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cows, like an elephant surrounded by young elephants, like a lion surrounded by a pride of predators, like a king of geese surrounded by a flock of geese, like a <s>Suparṇī</s> (Garuḍa) surrounded by a flock of birds, like a learned man surrounded by a group of disciples, like a skilled physician surrounded by a group of patients, like a hero surrounded by a band of warriors, like a guide surrounded by a group of travelers, like a caravan leader surrounded by a group of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by a group of citizens, like a feudal king surrounded by a group of ministers, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>, like <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Vemacitri</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by a host of the Thirty-three gods, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods — like a still ocean, like a rain-cloud full of water, like a rutless elephant, with well-tamed faculties and an undisturbed deportment, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, his body resplendent with eighty minor marks, his form adorned with a fathom-wide halo, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious in every direction, endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three special mindfulness-foundations, and great compassion — surrounded by <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Bāṣpa</s>, <s>Mahānāma</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and other great disciples, and by another great assembly of monks, he approached <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>.

body.text:
113.013. anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śuśumāragirimanuprāptaḥ/
113.014. śuśumāragirau viharati bhīṣaṇikāvane mṛgadāve/
113.014. aśrauṣuḥ śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayah--bhagavān bhargeṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śuśumāragirimanuprāptaḥ śuśumāragirau viharati bhīṣaṇikāvane mṛgadāva iti/
113.016. śrutvā ca punaḥ saṃghāt saṃghaṃ pūgātpūgaṃ saṃgamya śuśumāragirer niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
113.017. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
113.018. śuśumāragirīyakān brāhamaṇagṛhapatīn dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
113.019. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
113.020. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocan--adhivāsayatvasmākaṃ bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
113.022. adhivāsayati bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena/
113.023. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ/
113.025. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayastāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanakāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayanti--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
113.028. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
113.030. upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
113.030. śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayanti saṃpravārayanti/
113.032. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena <114>bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
body.translated_text: Wandering on his teaching tour in due order, he arrived at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>. He dwelt at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, in the <s>Bhīṣaṇikāvana</s> (Terrifying Forest), in the deer park. The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> heard: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a teaching tour through the <s>Bharga</s> countries, has arrived at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> and is dwelling at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, in the <s>Bhīṣaṇikāvana</s>, in the deer park.' Having heard this, assembling from group to group, from guild to guild, coming out of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. He instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal from us tomorrow in our house, together with the community of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> by his silence. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent by his silence, having rejoiced and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and departed from his presence. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent hard and soft foods, having risen early in the morning, prepared the seats, set out water-pitchers, and sent a messenger to the <s>Bhagavān</s> to announce the time: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come at whatever time he sees fit.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by the assembly of monks and accompanied by the community of monks, approached the place where the meal had been prepared for the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>. Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared. The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with their own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent hard and soft foods. Having in many ways served and satisfied them with pure and excellent hard and soft foods with their own hands, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating and had washed his hands and put away his bowl, they took lower seats and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
114.002. atha bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
114.004. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.

body.text:
114.005. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavantamidamavocat--bhagavatā bhadanta nānādeśeṣu nānādhiṣṭhāneṣu te te duṣṭanāgā duṣṭayakṣāśca vinītāḥ/
114.006. ayaṃ bhadanta aśvatīrthiko nāgo 'smākamavairāṇāṃ vairī asapatnānāṃ sapatno 'drugdhānāṃ drugdhaḥ/
114.007. nityamasmākaṃ jātāni jātāni śasyāni vināśayati, strīpuruṣadārakadārikāgomahiṣānajaiḍakāṃśca/
114.008. aho bata bhagavāṃstaṃ vinayedanukampāmupādāyeti/
114.009. adhivāsayati bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām/
114.010. tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati/
114.010. atha bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsya utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
114.011. atha bhagavān vihāraṃ gatvā purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
114.012. niṣadya bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha ānanda, bhikṣūṇāmevamārocaya, śalākāṃ cāraya--yo yuṣmākamutsahate aśvatīrthikaṃ nāgaṃ vinetum, sa śalākāṃ gṛhṇātu iti/
114.014. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣusaṃghasyārocayitvā buddhapramukhe bhikṣusaṃghe śalākāṃ cārayitumārabdhaḥ/
114.015. bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā/
114.015. sthavirā bhikṣavaḥ samanvāhartuṃ saṃvṛttāh--kimarthaṃ bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā iti? paśyantyāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya guṇodbhāvanāṃ kartukāmaḥ/
114.017. tairapi na gṛhītā/
114.017. āyuṣmān svāgataḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttah--kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā śalākā na gṛhītā sthavirasthaviraiśca bhikṣubhiriti? paśyati mama guṇodbhāvanāṃ kartukāmaḥ/
114.019. tacchāsturmanorathaṃ pūrayāmi, gṛhṇāmi śalākāmiti/
114.019. tenārdhāsanaṃ muktvā gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya śalākā gṛhītā/
114.020. jānakāḥ pṛcchakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
114.021. pṛcchati buddho bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandam--katareṇānanda bhikṣuṇā śalākā gṛhīteti? sa kathayati--svāgatena bhadanteti/
114.022. bhagavānāha--gaccha ānanda, svāgataṃ bhikṣumevaṃ vada--duṣṭanāgo 'sau, kāyendriyaṃ te rakṣitavyamiti/
114.023. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
114.024. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat--āyuṣman svāgata, bhagavānevamāha--duṣṭanāgo 'sau, kāyendriyaṃ te rakṣitavyamiti/
114.025. sa kathayati--āyuṣmannānanda akopyā śāsturājñā/
114.026. api tu yādṛśo 'śvatīrthiko nāgaḥ, īdṛśānāṃ nāgānāmikṣuveṇunaḍavadyadi pūrṇo jambudvīpaḥ syāt, tathāpi me te romāpi neñjayituṃ samarthāḥ syuḥ, prāgevāśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ kāyendriyasyoparodhaṃ kariṣyatīti/
114.028. āyuṣmānānanda ārogyamityuktvā prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, Venerable Sir, has tamed various wicked <s>Nāgas</s> and wicked <s>Yakṣas</s> in various lands and various places. Here, Venerable Sir, there is a <s>Nāga</s> called <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> who is hostile to us who are without enmity, an adversary to us who are without adversaries, harmful to us who are without malice. He constantly destroys our crops as they grow, as well as our women, men, boys, girls, cows, buffaloes, and goats and sheep. Oh, if only the <s>Bhagavān</s> would tame him, out of compassion!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>. He consented by his silence. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having consented to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> by his silence, rose from his seat and departed. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having gone to the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery), sat down on the seat prepared for him before the community of monks. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, announce to the monks and have the lots distributed — whoever among you is able to tame the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> <s>Nāga</s>, let him take the lot.' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having announced to the community of monks, began to distribute the lots among the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> did not take the lot. The elder monks reflected: 'Why did the <s>Bhagavān</s> not take the lot?' They saw: he wishes to display the virtues of the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>. They too did not take it. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> reflected: 'Why did the <s>Bhagavān</s> not take the lot, nor the elder monks?' He saw: he wishes to display my virtues. 'I shall fulfill the Teacher's wish; I shall take the lot.' Rising from half his seat, extending his arm like the trunk of an elephant, he took the lot. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, know yet still ask. The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> asked the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'By which monk was the lot taken, <s>Ānanda</s>?' He said: 'By <s>Svāgata</s>, Venerable Sir.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and tell the monk <s>Svāgata</s> thus: "That <s>Nāga</s> is wicked; you must protect your bodily faculty."' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and approached the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>. Having approached, he said to the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: 'Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says thus: "That <s>Nāga</s> is wicked; you must protect your bodily faculty."' He replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the Teacher's command is inviolable. Moreover, even if <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were filled with <s>Nāgas</s> like the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> <s>Nāga</s>, as densely as sugarcane, bamboo, or reeds, they would still not be able to stir even a single hair of mine — how much less will the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> <s>Nāga</s> be able to cause harm to my bodily faculty!' The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said 'Good health to you' and departed.

body.text:
114.029. athāyuṣmān svāgatastasyā eva rātreratyayātpūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śuśumāragiriṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
114.030. śuśumāragiriṃ piṇḍāya caritvā yenāśvatīrthikasya nāgasya bhavanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
114.031. adrākṣīdaśvatīrthiko nāga āyuṣmantaṃ svāgataṃ dūrādeva/
114.031. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kimanene śramaṇakena mama mṛtipravṛttir yena me bhavanamāgacchatīti? punaḥ saṃlakṣayati--<115>āganturayam, āgacchatu tāvaditi/
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, at the end of that very night, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, entered <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> for alms. Having gone for alms in <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, he approached the abode of the <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> <s>Nāga</s>. The <s>Aśvatīrthika</s> <s>Nāga</s> saw the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> from afar. Having seen him, he considered: 'What can this petty ascetic do to bring about my death, that he comes to my abode?' Then he reconsidered: 'He is a visitor; let him come.'

body.text:
115.001. athāyuṣmān svāgatastasya hradaṃ gatvā pātracīvaramekāntamupasaṃkṣipya pādau prakṣālya hastau nirmādya pānīyaṃ parisrāvya jīrṇaparṇakāni samudānīya niṣadya bhaktakṛtyaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
115.003. aśvatīrthikena nāgenāsāvatithiriti kṛtvādhyupekṣitaḥ/
115.003. āyuṣmān svāgataḥ saṃlakṣayati--nāsaṃkṣobhitā duṣṭanāgā damathamāgacchanti/
115.004. saṃkṣobhayāmyenamiti/
115.004. tena pātraṃ pakṣālya tatpātrodakaṃ tasmin hrade prakṣiptam/
115.005. sa saṃkṣubdhaḥ/
115.005. sa saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ mayā śramaṇa āgacchannadhyupekṣitaḥ, bhuñjāno 'pyupekṣitaḥ, anena mama bhavane ucchiṣṭodakaṃ choritam/
115.007. nāmāvaśeṣamenaṃ karomīti tīvreṇa paryavasthānena paryavasthitaḥ/
115.007. uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya āyuṣmataḥ svāgatasyopari cakrakaṇapaparaśubhindipālādīni praharaṇāni kṣeptumārabdhaḥ/
115.008. āyuṣmān svāgato maitrīsamāpannaḥ/
115.009. tānyasya divyānyutpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandārakāṇi puṣpāṇi bhūtvā kāye nipatanti/
115.010. aśvatīrthiko nāgo 'ṅgāravarṣamutsraṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
115.010. tadapi divyāni puṣpāṇi māndārakāṇi bhūtvā kāye nipatitumārabdham/
115.011. aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ pāṃsu varṣitumārabdhaḥ/
115.012. tadapi divyānyagurucūrṇāni tamālapatracūrṇāni bhūtvā nipatitumārabdham/
115.013. aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ krodhaparyavasthānānubhāvāddhūmayitumārabdhaḥ/
115.013. āyuṣmānapi svāgata ṛddhyanubhāvāddhūmayitumārabdhaḥ/
115.014. aśvatīrthiko nāgaḥ krodhaparyavasthānānubhāvāt prajvalitaḥ/
115.015. āyuṣmānapi svāgatastejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ/
115.015. iti tatrāśvatīrthikasya nāgasya krodhasyānubhāvenāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya ṛddhyanubhāvena mahānavabhāsaḥ prādurbhūto yaṃ dṛṣṭvā śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ saṃbhrāntāh itaścāmutaśca nirīkṣitumārabdhāḥ/
115.017. kathayanti--eṣa bhavanto bhagavānaśvatīrthikaṃ nāgaṃ vinayati, āgacchata paśyāma iti/
115.018. anekāni prāṇaśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni/
115.019. bhikṣavo 'pi tamudārāvabhāsaṃ tatrasthā eva nirīkṣitumārabdhāḥ/
115.019. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāmabhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānām yaduta svāgato bhikṣuriti/
115.021. yadāśvatīrthiko nāgo vigatamadadarpaḥ kṣīṇapraharaṇaśca saṃvṛttaḥ, tadā niṣpalāyitumārabdhaḥ/
115.022. āyuṣmatā svāgatena samantato 'gnir nirmitaḥ/
115.022. aśvatīrthako nāgo yām yāṃ diśaṃ gacchati, tāṃ tāṃ diśamādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ saṃprajvalitāmekajvālībhūtāṃ paśyati/
115.023. sa itaścāmutaśca nairmāṇikenāgninā paryākulīkṛto 'trāṇaḥ sarvamaśāntaṃ paśyati nānyatrāyuṣmata eva svāgatasya samīpaṃ śāntaṃ śītibhūtam/
115.025. sa yenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
115.025. upasaṃkramya āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat--ahaṃ bhadanta svāgata/
115.026. kiṃ māṃ viheṭhayasīti? sa kathayati--jarādharmā nāhaṃ tvāṃ viheṭhayāmi, api tu tvameva māṃ viheṭhayasi/
115.027. yadi mayā evaṃvidhā guṇagaṇā nādhigatā abhaviṣyan, adyāhaṃ tvayā nāmāvaśeṣaḥ kṛto 'bhaviṣyamiti/
115.028. sa kathayati--bhadanta svāgata, ājñāpayatu, kiṃ mayā karaṇīyam? bhadramukha, bhagavato 'ntikaṃ gatvā śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhāṇeti/
115.030. sa kathayati--bhadanta svāgata, śobhanam, evaṃ karomīti/
115.030. athāyuṣmān svāgato 'śvatīrthanāgamādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
115.031. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
115.032. ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān svāgato bhagavantamidamavocat--ayaṃ so 'śvatīrthiko<116> nāga iti/
body.translated_text:
115.001. Then the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, having gone to that <s>Nāga's</s> lake, set aside his bowl and robe in a secluded place, washed his feet, cleaned his hands, strained his drinking water, gathered old leaves, sat down, and began to take his meal.
115.003. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, regarding him as an uninvited guest, ignored him.
115.003. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> reflected: 'Wicked <s>Nāgas</s> do not come to taming unless they are provoked.
115.004. I shall provoke him.'
115.004. He washed his bowl and cast the bowl-water into that lake.
115.005. The <s>Nāga</s> was provoked.
115.005. He reflected: 'This ascetic — when he arrived, I ignored him; while he was eating, I also ignored him; yet he has thrown his leftover water in my dwelling.
115.007. I shall annihilate him!' Seized by intense fury,
115.007. he rose up into the sky above the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> and began to hurl weapons — discuses, maces, axes, javelins, and the like.
115.008. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> entered the attainment of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).
115.009. Those weapons became divine flowers — blue lotuses, lotuses, water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandāra</s> flowers — and fell upon his body.
115.010. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s> began to rain down embers.
115.010. Those too became divine <s>māndāra</s> flowers and began to fall upon his body.
115.011. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s> began to rain down dust.
115.012. That too became divine <s>aguru</s> (aloe) powder and <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay leaf) powder and began to fall.
115.013. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, through the power of his rage, began to emit smoke.
115.013. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> also, through the power of his <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural ability), began to emit smoke.
115.014. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, through the power of his rage, burst into flames.
115.015. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> also entered the <s>tejodhātu</s> (fire element meditation).
115.015. Thus, through the power of the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga's</s> rage and the power of the Venerable <s>Svāgata's</s> <s>ṛddhi</s>, a great radiance appeared, and seeing it, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> became alarmed and began looking about in all directions.
115.017. They said: 'Sirs, the Blessed One is taming the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>! Come, let us watch!'
115.018. Many hundreds of thousands of beings came forth.
115.019. The monks too, standing right there, began to look at that magnificent radiance.
115.019. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'This, O monks, is the foremost among my monk-disciples who repeatedly enters the <s>tejodhātu</s> (fire element meditation), namely the monk <s>Svāgata</s>.'
115.021. When the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, his pride and arrogance gone and his weapons exhausted, began to flee,
115.022. the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> created fire on all sides.
115.022. The <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, in whichever direction he went, saw that direction blazing, burning, flaming, and become a single mass of fire.
115.023. Thus bewildered on all sides by the magically created fire, without refuge, seeing everything unquiet, he found only the vicinity of the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> himself to be peaceful and cool.
115.025. He approached the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.
115.025. Having approached, he said to the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: 'I surrender, Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.
115.026. Why do you torment me?' He replied: 'It is the law of nature, <s>Nāga</s>; I do not torment you, but rather you torment me.
115.027. Had I not attained such a multitude of virtues, I would have been annihilated by you today.'
115.028. The <s>Nāga</s> said: 'Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, command me; what should I do?' 'Good sir, go to the Blessed One and take the refuges and precepts (<s>śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni</s>).'
115.030. He said: 'Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, excellent; I shall do so.'
115.030. Then the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, taking the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, approached the Blessed One.
115.031. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
115.032. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> said to the Blessed One: 'This is that <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>.'

body.text:
116.001. tatra bhagavānaśvatīrthikaṃ nāgamāmantrayate--tvaṃ tāvadbhadramukha, pūrvakeṇa duścaritena pratyavarāyāṃ tiryagyonau upapannaḥ/
116.002. sa tvametarhi hataprahataniviṣṭaḥ paraprāṇaharaḥ paraprāṇoparodhena jīvikāṃ kalpayasi/
116.003. itaścyutasya te kā gatirbhaviṣyati, kā upapattiḥ, ko 'bhisamparāyah? iti/
116.004. sa kathayati--bhagavan, ājñāpaya, kiṃ mayā karaṇīyamiti/
116.005. bhagavānāha--mamāntikāccharaṇaśikṣāpadāni gṛhāṇa, śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmabhayamanuprayaccheti/
116.006. sa kathayati--eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi, śikṣāpadāni ca gṛhṇāmi, adyāgreṇa ca śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmabhayamanuprayacchāmīti/
116.008. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ prabhūtamabhisāraṃ gṛhītvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
116.009. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
116.009. ekāntaniṣaṇṇāḥ śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavantamidamavocat--bhagavatā bhadanta aśvatīrthiko nāgo vinītah? bhagavānāha--na mayā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'śvatīrthako nāgo vinītaḥ, api tu svāgatena bhikṣuṇā/
116.012. katamena bhadanta? ihanivāsinaiva bodhasya gṛhapateḥ putreṇa/
116.012. saṃpattikāmo loko vipattipratikūlaḥ/
116.013. tatraike kathayanti--asmākamasau bhrātuḥ putro bhavati/
116.013. apare kathayanti--asmākaṃ bhagineya iti/
116.014. apare kathayanti--asmākaṃ vayasyaputra iti/
116.014. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapataya utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocan--adhivāsayatvasmākaṃ bhagavān bhadantasvāgatamāgamya bhaktaṃ saptāhena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti/
116.017. adhivāsayati bhagavāñ śuśumāragirīyakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena/
116.018. atha śuśumāragirīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ//
body.translated_text:
116.001. There the Blessed One addressed the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>: 'You, good sir, by your former misconduct, were born in the lower realm of animals.
116.002. And now you persist in violence and destruction, taking the lives of others and sustaining your livelihood by harming the life-force of others.
116.003. When you pass away from here, what will be your destiny, what your rebirth, what your future state?'
116.004. He replied: 'Blessed One, command me; what should I do?'
116.005. The Blessed One said: 'Take the refuges and precepts from me, and grant safety to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>.'
116.006. He replied: 'I take refuge in the Blessed One, and I accept the precepts; from this day forward, I grant safety to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>.'
116.008. Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, taking abundant offerings, approached the Blessed One.
116.009. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
116.009. Seated to one side, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Has the Blessed One tamed the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, Venerable Sir?' The Blessed One said: 'It was not I, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, who tamed the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>, but rather the monk <s>Svāgata</s>.'
116.012. 'Which one, Venerable Sir?' 'The one who dwells right here — the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.'
116.012. The world delights in success and dislikes failure.
