116.013. Some there said: 'He is our brother's son.'
116.013. Others said: 'He is our nephew.'
116.014. Others said: 'He is our friend's son.'
116.014. Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said: 'May the Blessed One consent to accept, on behalf of the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, a meal for seven days together with the community of monks.'
116.017. The Blessed One consented to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> by silence.
116.018. Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s>, having understood the Blessed One's consent by his silence, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and departed from his presence.

body.text:
116.020. śuśumāragirau anyatamo brāhmaṇa ahituṇḍiko bodhasya gṛhapatervayasyaḥ/
116.020. so 'śvatīrthikasya nāgasya bhayānniṣpalāyya śrāvastīṃ gataḥ/
116.021. sa rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena hastimadhyasyopari viśvāsikaḥ sthāpitaḥ/
116.022. sa kenacideva karaṇīyena śuśumāragirimanuprāptaḥ/
116.022. tena śrutam yathā svāgatena bhikṣuṇā bodhasya gṛhapateḥ putreṇāśvatīrthiko nāgo vinīta iti/
116.023. śrutvā ca punaryenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
116.024. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
116.025. sa brāhmaṇa āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me āryasvāgata śvo 'ntargṛhe bhakteneti/
116.026. āyuṣmāan svāgataḥ kathayati--brāhmaṇa, māmāgamya śuśumāragirīyakairbrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhirbuddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho bhaktena saptāhenopanimantritaḥ/
116.027. nāhamadhivāsayāmi/
116.028. brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati--ārya, yadi sāmprataṃ nādhivāsayasi, yadā śrāvastīgato bhavasi, tadā mama gṛhe tatprathamataḥ piṇḍapātaḥ paribhoktavya iti/
116.029. kathayati--evamastu iti/
116.029. brāhmaṇaḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ/
116.030. atha bhagavān yathābhiramyaṃ śuśumāragirau vihṛtya yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
116.031. anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
116.031. śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
116.032. aśrauṣīdanāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavān bhargeṣu janapadacārikām<117> carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ, ihaiva viharatyasmākamevārāma iti/
body.translated_text:
116.020. In <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> snake-charmer, a friend of the householder <s>Bodha</s>.
116.020. He had fled from the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s> out of fear and gone to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
116.021. He had been placed by King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> as a trusted overseer over the elephant stables.
116.022. He arrived at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> on some business.
116.022. There he heard that the monk <s>Svāgata</s>, the son of the householder <s>Bodha</s>, had tamed the <s>Aśvatīrthika Nāga</s>.
116.023. Having heard this, he approached the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>.
116.024. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> and sat down to one side.
116.025. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said to the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: 'May the noble <s>Svāgata</s> consent to accept a meal at my home tomorrow.'
116.026. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> replied: 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, on my account, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> have invited the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks) headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal for seven days.
116.027. I cannot consent.'
116.028. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'Noble one, if you cannot consent now, then when you go to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, please take your first alms-meal at my house.'
116.029. He said: 'So be it.'
116.029. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having paid his respects at his feet, departed.
116.030. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at <s>Śuśumāragiri</s> as long as he wished, set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
116.031. Wandering in due order, he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
116.031. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> he dwelt in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
116.032. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard that the Blessed One, having wandered through the <s>Bharga</s> countries, had arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s> and was dwelling right there in their own park.

body.text:
117.001. śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastyā niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
117.002. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
117.003. ekāntaniṣaṇṇamanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
117.004. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
117.005. anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti/
117.007. adhivāsayati bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena/
117.008. athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatirbhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
117.010. aśrauṣīt sa brāhmaṇo bhagavān bhargeṣu janapadacārikāṃ carannihānuprāpta ihaiva viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāma iti/
117.011. śrutvā ca punaryenāyuṣmān svāgatastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
117.011. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me āryaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhakteneti/
117.012. adhivāsayatyāyuṣmān svāgatastasya brāhmaṇasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
117.013. atha sa brāhmaṇa āyuṣmantaḥ svāgatasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
117.014. athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
117.017. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yenānāthapiṇḍadasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
117.018. tenāpi brāhmaṇenāyuṣmataḥ svāgatasya praṇīta āhāraḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ/
117.019. āyuṣmānapi svāgataḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya yena tasya brāhmaṇasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
117.020. upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
117.021. ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān svāgatastena brāhmaṇena praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ/
117.021. sa brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--āryeṇa svāgatena praṇīta āhāraḥ paribhuktaḥ, no jarayiṣyati, pānakamasmai prayacchāmi/
117.023. iti viditvā āyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamidamavocat--ārya, praṇītaste āhāraḥ paribhuktaḥ/
117.024. pānakaṃ piba/
117.024. pānaṃ jarayiṣyatīti/
117.024. sa kathayati--śobhanam/
117.024. evaṃ karomīti/
117.024. tena pānakaṃ sajjīkṛtya hastimadādaṅguliḥ prakṣiptā/
117.025. asamanvāhṛtyārhatāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate/
117.025. āyuṣmatā svāgatena tatpānakaṃ pītam/
117.026. tato dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ śrāvastīvīthīṃ kiliñjacchannām/
117.027. sa tāmatikrānta ātapena spṛṣṭo madyakṣiptaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ/
117.027. asaṃmoṣadharmaṇo buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
117.028. bhagavatā suparṇikā kuṭir nirmitā--maitaṃ kaścid dṛṣṭvā śāsane 'prasādaṃ pravedayiṣyatīti/
117.029. anāthapiṇḍadaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena svahastena saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
117.030. anekaparyāyeṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
117.032. atha bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā <118>saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: Having heard this, he departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat down to one side. The <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow in my house, together with the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks)." The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> by his silence. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having understood the <s>Bhagavān's</s> consent through his silence, having rejoiced in and approved the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> feet, departed from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence. That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Bharga</s> countries, had arrived here and was dwelling right here in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Having heard this, he approached the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "May the noble one consent to accept a meal from me tomorrow in my house." The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> consented to that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by his silence. Then that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having understood the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>'s consent through his silence, rose from his seat and departed. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food both hard and soft, rising early in the morning, having arranged seats and set out water vessels, announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: "It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come at whatever time he sees fit." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by a company of monks and preceded by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, approached the dwelling of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too had prepared excellent food for the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> also, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, approached the dwelling of that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> was served excellent food by that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> thought: "The noble <s>Svāgata</s> has eaten excellent food; it will not digest easily. I shall give him a drink." Having thought thus, he said this to the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>: "Noble one, you have eaten excellent food. Drink this beverage. The drink will aid digestion." He replied: "Very well. I shall do so." The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> prepared the drink and dropped in a finger's measure of <s>hastimada</s> (elephant intoxicant, a type of liquor). Without careful reflection, the knowledge and vision of an <s>Arhat</s> does not operate. The Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> drank that beverage. Then, having given instructions for the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (merit-dedication), he departed along the main street of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, which was covered with reed mats. Having passed beyond them, struck by the sun's heat and overcome by the liquor, he fell to the ground. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are of unfailing mindfulness. The <s>Bhagavān</s> created a <s>suparṇikā</s> (vine-like shelter) with his power, thinking: "Let no one see him and lose faith in the teaching." <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, seeing the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> comfortably seated, served them with his own hands with pure and excellent food, satisfying and regaling them. Having in many ways satisfied and regaled them with his own hands, and knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl removed, he took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text:
118.001. anupūrveṇa tatpradeśanuprāptaḥ/
118.002. atha bhagavāṃstān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--ayaṃ sa bhikṣavaḥ svāgato bhikṣuryenāśvatrīrthiko nāgastāvaccaṇḍo vinītaḥ/
118.003. kimidānīmeṣa śakto durbhuktasyāpi viṣamapanetum? no bhadanta iti/
118.004. bhikṣavaḥ, ime cānye cādīnavā madyapāne/
118.004. tasmānna bhikṣuṇā madyaṃ pātavyaṃ dātavyaṃ vā/
118.005. atha bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ svāgataṃ madyavaśāt suptamutthāpyedamavocat--svāgata, kimidam? asamanvāhāro bhagavan, asamanvāhāraḥ sugata/
118.006. tato bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ svāgatamādāya vihāraṃ gatvā purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
118.007. niṣadya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--māṃ bho bhikṣavaḥ śāstāramuddiśya bhavadbhirmadyamapeyamadeyamantataḥ kuśāgreṇāpi//
body.translated_text: Gradually he arrived at that place. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, withdrawing those displays of supernatural power, addressed the monks: "This, O monks, is that <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Svāgata</s> by whom the <s>Nāga</s> at <s>Aśvatrīrthika</s>, so exceedingly fierce, was subdued. Is he now capable of removing even an ill-eaten morsel?" "No, Venerable Sir." "Monks, these and other dangers lie in drinking liquor. Therefore a <s>bhikṣu</s> must neither drink nor give liquor." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> roused the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s>, who had fallen asleep from the effects of the liquor, and said: "<s>Svāgata</s>, what is this?" "It was without mindful reflection, <s>Bhagavān</s>; without mindful reflection, <s>Sugata</s>." Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> with him, went to the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) and sat down on the seat prepared before the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>. Having sat down, he addressed the monks: "Henceforth, O monks, designating me as your teacher, you must not drink liquor, nor give it — not even so much as the tip of a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass."

body.text:
118.009. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā svāgatena karma kṛtam yenāḍhye kule mahādhane mahābhoge jātah? kiṃ karma kṛtam yena kroḍamallako jātaḥ, durāgata iti ca saṃjñā saṃvṛttā? kiṃ karma kṛtam yena bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāṃ cāgratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭah? bhagavānāha--svāgatenaiva bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyabhāvīni/
118.014. svāgatena karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
118.015. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tu upātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
118.018. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
118.019. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//10//
body.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What <s>karma</s> (action), Venerable Sir, did the Venerable <s>Svāgata</s> perform that he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions? What <s>karma</s> did he perform that he was born a <s>kroḍamallaka</s> (stunted dwarf), and came to bear the name <s>Durāgata</s> (Ill-arrived)? What <s>karma</s> did he perform that, having gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching, he realized <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and was declared foremost among those who attain the <s>tejodhātu-samāpatti</s> (mastery of the fire element)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: "It was <s>Svāgata</s> the monk himself, O monks, who performed and accumulated those <s>karmas</s>, whose conditions have matured and whose requisite causes have ripened, which stand present like a flood and whose fruition is inevitable. <s>Svāgata</s> performed and accumulated those <s>karmas</s>. Who else would experience their results? Monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated — whether wholesome or unwholesome — ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); when the right conjunction and time are reached, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings."

body.text:
118.020. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
118.021. so 'pareṇa samayena suhṛtsambandhibāndhavaparivṛto 'ntarjanaparivṛtaścodyānabhūmiṃ nirgataḥ/
118.022. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
118.023. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
118.024. so 'dhvapariśramāddhātuvaiṣamyāśca glānaḥ piṇḍārthī tadudyānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
118.025. sa gṛhapatistaṃ dṛṣṭvā paryavasthitaḥ/
118.025. tena pauruṣeyāṇāmājñā dattā--bhavantaḥ, niṣkāsayatainaṃ pravrajitamiti/
118.026. teṣāṃ na kaścidutsahate niṣkāsayitum/
118.027. tena gṛhapatinā bhūyasā paryavasthitena sa mahātmāa svayameva grīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā niṣkāsitaḥ, uktaśca--kroḍamallakānāṃ madhye prativaseti/
118.028. sa durbalaprāṇo bhūmau nipatitaḥ/
118.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--hato 'yaṃ tapasvī gṛhapatirupahataśca/
118.029. abhyuddhāro 'sya kartavyaḥ/
118.029. iti viditvā uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ/
118.030. āśu pṛthagjanasya riddhirāvarjanakarī/
118.031. sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--avatarāvatara mahādakṣiṇīya, mama duścaritapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayaccheti/
118.032. sa tasyānugrahārthamavatīrṇaḥ/
118.032. tena tasya <119>pūjāsatkāraṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye 'pakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, mā asya karmaṇo bhāgī syām/
body.translated_text: "In the past, O monks, in a certain small town, there dwelt a householder who was wealthy, of great riches, great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) in wealth. On a certain occasion, surrounded by friends, kinsmen, and relatives, and attended by his household, he went out to a pleasure garden. In the absence of <s>Buddhas</s> arising in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, fond of secluded lodgings and meals, sole worthy recipients of offerings in the world. Now a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at that small town. He, weary from the journey and ill from an imbalance of bodily humors, entered that garden seeking alms. That householder, seeing him, was overcome with hostility. He gave an order to his servants: 'Sirs, throw this wandering mendicant out!' None of them dared to throw him out. Then that householder, overcome with even greater hostility, himself seized that great-souled one by the neck and threw him out, saying: 'Go dwell among the <s>kroḍamallakas</s> (stunted dwarfs)!' The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, weakened, fell to the ground. He then reflected: 'Alas, this wretched householder is ruined and destroyed. I must bring about his deliverance.' Having resolved thus, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> rose up into the sky and began to perform miraculous feats of blazing, burning, raining, and flashing. Swiftly, supernatural power turns the heart of a common person. That householder, like a tree cut at the root, fell at his feet and said: 'Descend, descend, O great worthy recipient of gifts! Extend to me your hand to lift me out, as I am sunk in the mire of my evil conduct!' The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> descended out of compassion for him. The householder, having performed worship and honor for him, made a vow: 'Whatever harm I have done to such a truly worthy recipient of gifts — may I not bear the fruit of that deed!

body.text: 119.002. yattūpakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyam, evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti//
body.translated_text: But as for the service I have rendered, by this root of merit may I be born in a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions, may I obtain such excellent <s>Dharmas</s> (teachings), and may I find a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and may I be drawn toward him, never turning away from him.'"

body.text:
119.005. bhagavānāha--kiṃ kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau gṛhapatireva, asau svāgato bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena/
119.006. yadanena pratyekabuddhe kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, tenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ/
119.007. yadapakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, tena pañcajanmaśatāni kroḍamallako jātaḥ/
119.007. yāvadetarhyapi caramabhaviko 'pi tatkroḍamallaka eva jātaḥ/
119.008. yatpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
119.009. ahamanena pratyekabuddhakoṭiśatasahasrebhyaḥ prativiśiṣṭataraḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ/
119.010. bhūyo 'pi kāśyape bhagavati samyaksambuddhe pravrajito babhūva/
119.011. yasya bhikṣorantike pravrajitaḥ, sa bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ/
119.012. tatrānena yāvadāyurbrahmacaryaṃ cāritam, na ca kaścidguṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ/
119.013. sa maraṇasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā bhagavati kāśyape samyaksambuddhe 'nuttare dakṣiṇīye yādavāyurbrahmacaryaṃ caritam, na ca kaścidguṇaguṇo 'dhigataḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenottaro māṇavo vyākṛtah--bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti, tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuryām/
119.017. yathā mām upādhyāyo bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ, evaṃ māmapi sa bhagavāñ śākyamuniḥ śākyādhirājo 'bhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagraṃ nirdiśediti/
119.019. tatpraṇidhānavaśādetarhi tathāgatenābhīkṣṇaṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpadyamānānāmagro nirdiṣṭaḥ/
119.020. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
119.022. tasmāttarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmaṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
119.023. ityevaṃ bho bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text:
119.005. The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was that householder — he is none other than the monk <s>Svāgata</s> at that time, in that era.
119.006. Because he rendered service to a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great fortune.
119.007. Because he committed an offense, he was born as a beggar with a broken bowl for five hundred lifetimes.
119.007. Even now, in his final existence, he was born as that very beggar with a broken bowl.
119.008. Because he made an aspiration, he has gone forth in my teaching and, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).
119.009. By him, I — the Teacher, who am more distinguished than a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — have been gratified, not displeased.
119.010. Furthermore, he also went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
119.011. The monk under whom he went forth was designated by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, as the foremost among those who repeatedly enter the <s>tejodhātu</s> (fire element meditation).
119.012. There he practiced the holy life for his entire lifespan, yet did not attain any collection of virtues.
119.013. At the time of death, he began to make an aspiration: "Inasmuch as I have practiced the holy life for my entire lifespan under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the unsurpassed field of merit, yet have not attained any collection of virtues — by this root of merit, may I, in the teaching of the one who was prophesied by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, as the young man <s>Uttara</s> — 'You, young man, shall become among people with a lifespan of a hundred years a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>' — may I go forth in his teaching and, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, directly realize <s>Arhattva</s>.
119.017. Just as my preceptor was designated by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, as the foremost among those who repeatedly enter the <s>tejodhātu</s>, so too may that Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Supreme Lord of the <s>Śākyas</s>, designate me as the foremost among those who repeatedly enter the <s>tejodhātu</s>."
119.019. By the power of that aspiration, he has now been designated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as the foremost among those who repeatedly enter the <s>tejodhātu</s>.
119.020. Thus, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for deeds that are entirely bright, the result is entirely bright; for deeds that are mixed, the result is mixed.
119.022. Therefore, monks, having abandoned entirely dark and mixed deeds, you should devote yourselves only to entirely bright deeds.
119.023. Thus, monks, should you train.'

body.text:
119.024. ityavocadbhagavān/
119.024. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
119.024. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
119.024. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 119.025. iti śrīdivyāvadāne svāgāvadānaṃ nāma trayodaśamam//
body.translated_text: 119.025. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Svāgatāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Svāgata</s>), the thirteenth.

body.text: 120.001. div14 sūkarikāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 120.001. Chapter 14: The <s>Sūkarikāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Sow).

body.text:
120.002. dharmatā khalu cyavanadharmaṇo devaputraysa pañca pūrvanimittāni prādurbhavanti--akliṣṭāni vāsāṃsi kliśyanti, amlānāni mālyāni mlāyanti, daurgandhaṃ kāyena niṣkrāmati, ubhābhyāṃ kakṣābhyāṃ svedaḥ prādurbhavanti, cyavanadharmā devaputraḥ sva āsane dhṛtiṃ na labhate/
120.003. athānyatamaścyavanadharmā devaputraḥ pṛthivyāmāvartate, saṃparivartyaivaṃ cāha--hā mandākinī, hā puṣkariṇī, hā vāpī, hā caitraratha, hā pāruṣyaka, hā nandanavana, hā miśrakāvana, hā pāriyātraka, hā puṇḍukambalaśilā, hā devasabhā, hā sudarśana, iti karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevate sma/
120.007. adrākṣīcchakro devānāmindrastaṃ devaputramatyarthaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartantaṃ parivartantam/
120.008. dṛṣṭvā punaryena sa devaputrastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
120.009. upasaṃkramya taṃ devaputramidamavocat--hā kasmāt tvaṃ mārṣa atyarthaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartase, saṃparivartase, karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevase--hā mandākinī, hā puṣkiriṇī, hā vāpī, hā caitraratha, hā pāruṣyaka, hā nandanavana, hā miśrakāvana, hā pāriyātraka, hā pāṇḍukambalaśilā, hā devasabhā, hā sudarśana iti karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevase? evamukte devaputraḥ śakraṃ devānāmindramidamavocat--eṣo 'haṃ kauśika divyaṃ sukhamanubhūya itaḥ saptame divase rājagṛhe nagare sūkaryāḥ kukṣau upapatsyāmi/
120.014. tatra mayā bahūni varṣāṇyuccāraprasrāvaḥ paribhoktavya iti/
120.014. atha śakro devānāmindraḥ kāruṇyatayā taṃ devaputramidamavocat--ehi tvaṃ mārṣa, buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha dvipadānāmagryam, dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha virāgāṇāmagryam, saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha gaṇānāmagryamiti/
120.016. atha sa devaputrastiryagyonyupapattibhayabhīto maraṇabhayabhītaśca śakraṃ devānāmindramidamavocat--eṣo 'haṃ kauśika buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam, dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam, saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam/
120.019. atha sa devaputrastriśaraṇaparigṛhīto bhūtvā cyutaḥ kālagatastuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ//
body.translated_text:
120.002. It is the nature of a celestial being (<s>devaputra</s>) subject to death that five premonitory signs appear — his unwithered garments become soiled, his unfaded garlands wilt, a foul odor emanates from his body, sweat appears from both armpits, and a celestial being subject to death finds no composure on his own seat.
120.003. Then a certain celestial being subject to death was rolling on the ground, and turning over, he cried out thus: 'Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>! Alas, <s>Vāpī</s>! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandana</s> grove! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, <s>Puṇḍukambala</s> stone! Alas, <s>Devasabhā</s>! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!' — thus he lamented most pitifully.
120.007. <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, saw that celestial being rolling and turning on the ground in extreme distress.
120.008. Having seen him, he approached that celestial being.
120.009. Having approached, he said to that celestial being: 'Alas, why do you, good sir, roll and turn on the ground in such extreme distress, lamenting most pitifully — "Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>! Alas, <s>Vāpī</s>! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandana</s> grove! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, <s>Pāṇḍukambala</s> stone! Alas, <s>Devasabhā</s>! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!"?' When this was said, the celestial being said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: 'After having enjoyed divine happiness, on the seventh day from now I shall be reborn in the womb of a sow in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
120.014. There I shall have to consume excrement and urine for many years.'
120.014. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, out of compassion said to that celestial being: 'Come, good sir, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds; take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among those free from passion; take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among assemblies.'
120.016. Then that celestial being, terrified by the fear of rebirth in the animal realm and terrified by the fear of death, said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: 'I take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds; I take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among those free from passion; I take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among assemblies.'
120.019. Then that celestial being, having taken the Three Refuges, died, passed away, and was reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods.

body.text:
120.021. dharmatā khalu adhastāddevānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate nordhvam/
120.021. atha śakro devānāmindrastaṃ devaputramavalokayati--kimasau devaputraḥ sūkarikāyāḥ kukṣau upapanno na veti/
120.022. yāvat paśyati--nopapannastiryakpreteṣu/
120.023. narakeṣūpapanna iti paśyati/
120.023. nopapannaḥ/
120.023. manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupapanna iti paśyati/
120.024. nopapannaḥ/
120.024. cāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśāṃścāvalokayitumārabdhaḥ/
120.025. tatrāpi nādrākṣīt/
120.025. atha śakro devānāmindraḥ kutūhalajāto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
120.026. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
120.026. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ śakro devānāmindro bhagavantamidamavocat--ihāhaṃ bhadanta adrākṣamanyatamaṃ devaputraṃ cyavanadharmāṇaṃ pṛthivyāmāvartamānaṃ karuṇakaruṇaṃ ca paridevamānam--hā mandākini, hā puṣkiriṇi, hā vāpi, hā caitraratha, hā pāruṣyaka, hā nandanavana, hā miśrakāvana, hā pāriyātraka, hā pāṇḍukambalāśilā, hā devasabhā, hā sudarśana iti/
120.029. tamenamevaṃ vadāmi--kasmāt tvaṃ mārṣa atyarthaṃ śocasi paridevase krandasi urasi tāḍayasi saṃmohāpadyasa iti? sa evamāha--eṣo 'haṃ kauśika divyaṃ sukhamapahāya itaḥ saptame divase rājagṛhe nagare sūkarikāyāḥ kukṣau upapatsyāmi/
120.031. tatra mayā <121>bahūni varṣāṇi uccāraprasrāvaḥ paribhoktavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
body.translated_text:
120.021. It is the nature that the knowledge and vision of lower gods extends downward, not upward.
120.021. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, looked for that celestial being — 'Has that celestial being been reborn in the womb of a sow or not?'
120.022. He looked and saw — he had not been reborn among animals or hungry ghosts.
120.023. 'He has been reborn in the hells,' he thought. He looked — he had not.
120.023. 'He has been reborn in the realm of humans,' he thought.
120.024. He had not.
120.024. He began to look among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
120.025. He did not see him there either.
120.025. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, filled with curiosity, approached the Blessed One.
120.026. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
120.026. Seated to one side, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, said to the Blessed One: 'Here, Venerable Sir, I saw a certain celestial being subject to death, rolling on the ground and lamenting most pitifully — "Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>! Alas, <s>Vāpī</s>! Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s>! Alas, <s>Pāruṣyaka</s>! Alas, <s>Nandana</s> grove! Alas, <s>Miśrakāvana</s>! Alas, <s>Pāriyātraka</s>! Alas, <s>Pāṇḍukambala</s> stone! Alas, <s>Devasabhā</s>! Alas, <s>Sudarśana</s>!"
120.029. I said to him: "Why do you, good sir, grieve and lament so extremely, crying and beating your breast, falling into confusion?" He said: "After having abandoned divine happiness, on the seventh day from now I shall be reborn in the womb of a sow in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
120.031. There I shall have to consume excrement and urine <121>for many years."

body.text:
121.001. tamenamevaṃ vadāmi--ehi tvaṃ mārṣa buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha dvipadānāmagryam, dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha virāgāṇāmagryam, saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha gaṇānāmagryamiti/
121.003. sa evamāha--eṣo 'haṃ kauśika buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dvipadānāmagryam, dharmaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi virāgāṇāmagryam, saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi gaṇānāmagryam/
121.004. ityuktvā sa devaputraḥ kālagataḥ/
121.005. kutrāsau bhadanta devaputra upapannah? bhagavānāha--tuṣitā nāma kauśika devāḥ sarvakāmasamṛddhayaḥ/
121.006. tatrāsau modate devo gatveha śaraṇatrayam/
121.006. atha śakro devānāmindra āttamānāstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
121.008. ye buddhaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.009. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//1//
body.translated_text:
121.001. I said to him: "Come, good sir, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds; take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among those free from passion; take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among assemblies."
121.003. He said: "I take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds; I take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s>, the foremost among those free from passion; I take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the foremost among assemblies."
121.004. Having said this, that celestial being died.
121.005. Where, Venerable Sir, has that celestial being been reborn?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Kauśika</s>, there are gods called <s>Tuṣita</s>, rich in the fulfillment of all desires.
121.006. There that celestial being rejoices, having gone to the Three Refuges here.'
121.006. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, delighted, at that moment spoke this verse:
121.008. 'Those who take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s> do not go to an evil rebirth;
121.009. Having left behind human bodies, they assume divine bodies.' //1//

body.text:
121.010. ye dharmaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.011. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//2//
body.translated_text:
121.010. 'Those who take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s> do not go to an evil rebirth;
121.011. Having left behind human bodies, they assume divine bodies.' //2//

body.text:
121.012. ye saṃghaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.013. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//3//
body.translated_text:
121.012. 'Those who take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s> do not go to an evil rebirth;
121.013. Having left behind human bodies, they assume divine bodies.' //3//

body.text:
121.014. atha bhagavāñ śakrasya devānāmindrasya bhāṣitamanusaṃvarṇayannevamāha--evametat kauśika, evametat/
121.016. ye buddhaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.017. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//4//

121.018. ye dharmaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.019. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//5//
body.translated_text:
121.018. 'Those who take refuge in the <s>Dharma</s> do not go to an evil rebirth;
121.019. Having left behind human bodies, they assume divine bodies.' //5//

body.text:
121.020. ye saṃghaṃ śaraṇam yānti na te gacchanti durgatim/
121.021. prahāya mānuṣān kāyān divyān kāyānupāsate//6//
body.translated_text:
121.020. 'Those who take refuge in the <s>Saṃgha</s> do not go to an evil rebirth;
121.021. Having left behind human bodies, they assume divine bodies.' //6//

body.text: 121.022. atha śakro devānāmindro bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya prāñjalikṛtasampuṭo bhagavantaṃ namasyamānastatraivāntarhitaḥ//
body.translated_text: 121.022. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, having approved and rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and with palms joined in respect, paying homage to the Blessed One, vanished right there.

body.text:
121.024. idamavocadbhagavān/
121.024. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo 'bhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
121.024. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
121.024. Delighted, those monks rejoiced.

body.text: 121.025. iti śrīdivyāvadāne sūkarikāvadānaṃ caturdaśamam//
body.translated_text: 121.025. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Sūkarikāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Sow), the fourteenth.

body.text: 122.001. div15 cakravartivyākṛtāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 122.001. Chapter 15: The <s>Cakravartivyākṛtāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Prophecy of the Universal Monarch).

body.text:
122.002. buddho bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
122.002. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jīvatāṃ dhriyamāṇānām yāpayatāṃ keśanakhastūpā bhavanti/
122.002. yadā buddhā bhagavantaḥ pratisamlīnā bhavanti, tadā bhikṣavaḥ keśanakhastūpe pujāṃ kṛtvā kecit puṇḍāya praviśanti, keciddhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisukhānyanubhavanti/
122.005. tena khalu samayena buddho bhagavāṃs tathāgatamākārataḥ samanusmaraṃścittamabhiprasādayati--ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārithaḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavāniti/
122.009. atha bhagavān sāyāhṇe pratisamlayanādvyutthāya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
122.010. adrākṣīdbhagavāṃstaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśanakhastūpe sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya cittamabhiprasādayantam/
122.011. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--paśyata yūyaṃ bhikṣava etaṃ bhikṣuṃ keśanakhastūpe sarvaśarīreṇa praṇipatya cittamabhiprasādayantam? evaṃ bhadanta/
122.012. anena bhikṣuṇā yāvatī bhūmirākrāntā adho 'śītiyojanasahasrāṇi yāvat kāñcanacakramityatrāntarā yāvatyo vālukāstāvantyanena bhikṣuṇā cakravartirājyasahasrāṇi paribhoktavyāni/
122.014. atha teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāmetadabhavat--puruṣamātrāyām yāvadgartāyāṃ na śakyate vālukā gaṇayitum, kṛtaḥ punaraśītiyojanasahasrāṇi yāvat kāñcanacakramiti/
122.016. kaḥ śakyate iyatkālaṃ saṃsāre saṃsaritumiti/
122.016. atha te bhikṣavo na bhūyaḥ keśanakhastūpe kārāṃ kartumārabdhāḥ/
122.017. atha bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ cetasā cittamājñāya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--anavarāgro bhikṣavaḥ saṃsāro 'vidyānīvaraṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ tuṣṇāsamyojanānāṃ tṛṣṇārgalabaddhānāṃ dīrghamadhvānaṃ saṃdhāvatāṃ saṃsaratām/
122.019. pūrvā koṭtir na prajñāyate duḥkhasya/
122.020. āyuṣmānupālī buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papraccha--yaduktaṃ bhagavatā asya bhikṣoriyatpuṇyaskandha iti, kutra bhadanta iyatpuṇyaskandhastanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gamiṣyati? nāhamupālinn ito bahiḥ samanupaśyāmyeva kṣatiṃ copahatiṃ ca yathā sabrahmacārī sabrahmacāriṇo 'ntike/
122.023. tatropālinn imāni mahānti kuśalamūlāni tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti/
122.023. tasmāttarhi te upālinn evaṃ śikṣitavyam, yaddagdhasthūṇāyā api cittaṃ na pradūṣayiṣyāmaḥ, prāgeva savijñānake kāye//
body.translated_text:
122.002. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
122.002. It is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, that while they are alive and abiding, there are <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary shrines) of hair and nails.
122.002. When the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, pass into final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the monks, having worshipped at the hair-and-nail <s>stūpas</s>, some enter into merit, and some experience the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment).
122.005. At that time, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, recollecting the <s>Tathāgata</s> in his essential nature, generated faith of mind: 'Such indeed is the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
122.009. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the evening, having risen from seclusion, sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.
122.010. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw that monk prostrating with his entire body before the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>, generating faith of mind.
122.011. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'Do you see, monks, this monk prostrating with his entire body before the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>, generating faith of mind?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.'
122.012. 'By this monk, however much ground was covered — down eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) to the golden wheel — however many grains of sand there are in between, that many thousands of <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) kingdoms shall be enjoyed by this monk.
122.014. Then those monks had this thought: 'In a pit the height of a man, the grains of sand cannot be counted — how much less in eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> down to the golden wheel!
122.016. Who could wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) for such a long time?'
122.016. Then those monks ceased to pay respect at the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>.
122.017. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing with his mind the thoughts in the minds of those monks, addressed the monks: 'Beginningless, monks, is <s>saṃsāra</s> for beings hindered by ignorance, fettered by craving, bound by the bolt of thirst, running and wandering for a long time.
122.019. The prior limit of suffering is not discernible.
122.020. The Venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has spoken of such a mass of merit for this monk — where, Venerable Sir, will such a mass of merit diminish, waste away, and come to exhaustion?' 'I do not see, <s>Upāli</s>, any diminution or destruction coming from outside, as from one fellow in the spiritual life toward another.
122.023. But, <s>Upāli</s>, these great roots of merit diminish, waste away, and come to exhaustion right here [among companions].
122.023. Therefore, <s>Upāli</s>, you should train thus: "We shall not corrupt our minds even toward a burnt pillar, how much less toward a sentient body."'

body.text:
122.026. idamavocadbhagavān/
122.026. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo 'bhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
122.026. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
122.026. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 122.027. iti śrīdivyāvadāne anyatamabhikṣuścakravartivyākṛtaḥ pañcadaśamam//
body.translated_text: 122.027. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, a certain monk is predicted to become a <s>Cakravartin</s> — the fifteenth.

body.text: 123.001. div16 śukapotakāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 123.001. Chapter 16: The <s>Śukapotaka Avadāna</s> (The Story of the Parrot Chicks).

body.text:
123.002. śrāvastyāṃ nidānam/
123.002. tena khalu samayena anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhaptinā dvau śukaśāvakau pratilabdhau/
123.003. tena niveśanaṃ nītvā ālāpitau poṣitau saṃvardhitau mānuṣālāpaṃ ca śikṣāpitau/
123.004. tayoścāyuṣmānānando 'bhīkṣṇamāgatya caturāryasatyasamprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ karoti--yaduta idaṃ duḥkham, ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ, ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ, iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi/
123.005. sthavirasthavirā api bhikṣavo 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamupasaṃkrāmanti śāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapānandaraivataprabhṛtayaḥ/
123.007. teṣāṃ kālānukālamupasaṃkrāmatāṃ tābhyāṃ śukaśāvakābhyāṃ nāmāni parijñātāni/
123.008. yāvadapareṇa samayenāyuṣmāñ śāriputro 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamanuprāptaḥ/
123.011. adrāṣṭāṃ tau śukaśāvakau āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram/
123.009. dṛṣṭvā antarjanamāmantrayatah--eṣa bhadantaḥ sthaviraḥ śāriputra āgacchati, āsanamasya prajñāpayateti/
123.010. evamāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ kāśyapaṃ raivatamāyuṣmantamānandaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayatah--eṣo 'smākamācāryānanda āgacchati, āsanamasya prajñāpayateti/
123.012. yāvadapareṇa samayena bhagavānanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśanamanuprāptaḥ/
123.012. adrāṣṭāṃ tau śukaśāvakau bhagavantaṃ dūrādevāgacchantaṃ prāsādikaṃ prasādanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ parameṇa cittamatyupaśamena samanvāgataṃ suvarṇayūpamiva śriyā jvalantam/
123.014. dṛṣṭvā ca punastvaritatvaritamantarjanamāmantrayatah--eṣa bhadanto bhagavānāgacchati, āsanamasya prajñāpayateti hṛṣṭamadhurasvareṇa nikūjataḥ/
123.016. atha bhagavāṃstayoranugrahārthaṃ praviśya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
123.016. niṣadya bhagavatā śukaśāvakau caturāryasatyasamprativedhikayā dharmadeśanayā śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitau/
123.018. atha bhagavāñ śukaśāvakau antarjanaṃ ca dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
123.019. tau cāntarjanasya viharataḥ pramādavihāriṇau biḍālena prāṇinā gṛhītau/
123.020. vihvalavadanau cchidyamāneṣu marmasu mucyamāneṣu saṃdhiṣu namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāyetyuktvā kālagatau cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapannau//
body.translated_text:
123.002. The setting is <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
123.002. At that time, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had obtained two young parrots.
123.003. He brought them to his residence, tamed them, reared them, raised them, and taught them human speech.
123.004. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> would frequently come and give them a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths: 'This is suffering, this is the origin of suffering, this is the cessation of suffering, this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'
123.005. Senior monks too would visit the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> — <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and others.
123.007. As they visited from time to time, the two young parrots learned their names.
123.008. In due course, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> arrived at the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
123.011. The two young parrots saw the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.
123.009. Having seen him, they called to the household members: 'The Venerable Elder <s>Śāriputra</s> is coming; prepare a seat for him.'
123.010. Similarly, upon seeing the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, they said: 'Our teacher <s>Ānanda</s> is coming; prepare a seat for him.'
123.012. In due course, the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
123.012. The two young parrots saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> coming from afar — pleasing to behold, inspiring faith, with senses at peace, with mind at peace, endowed with supreme tranquility of mind, blazing with glory like a golden pillar.
123.014. Having seen him, they quickly called to the household members: 'The Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s> is coming; prepare a seat for him,' chirping in joyful, sweet tones.
123.016. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the sake of their benefit, entered and sat down on the seat prepared for him.
123.016. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> established the two young parrots in the refuges and precepts through a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths.
123.018. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened the young parrots and the household members with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.
123.019. The two, dwelling among the household members, living heedlessly, were seized by a cat.
123.020. With distressed faces, as their vital points were pierced and their joints torn apart, they uttered 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>' and died, and were reborn among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven.

body.text:
123.022. atha bhagavānanyatamasmin pradeśe smitamakārṣīt/
123.022. adrākṣīdāyuṣmānānando bhagavantaṃ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvantam/
123.023. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhagavantamidamavocat--nāhetupratyayaṃ bhadanta tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
123.024. ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāviṣkaraṇe? evametadānanda, evametat/
123.025. nāhetupratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
123.026. dṛṣṭau tvayā ānanda tau śukaśāvakau? dṛṣṭau bhadanta/
123.026. tau ānanda śukaśāvakau mama samanantaraprakrāntasya biḍālena prāṇinā jīvitād vyaparopitau/
123.027. tau buddhadharmasaṃghāvalambanayā smṛtyā kālagatau cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapannau//
body.translated_text:
123.022. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at a certain spot, smiled.
123.022. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> smiling.
123.023. Having seen this, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Not without cause or condition, Venerable Sir, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, smile.
123.024. What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of the smile?' 'Just so, <s>Ānanda</s>, just so.
123.025. Not without cause or condition do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, smile.
123.026. Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, those two young parrots?' 'I saw them, Venerable Sir.'
123.026. 'Those two young parrots, <s>Ānanda</s>, immediately after I departed, were killed by a cat.
123.027. They, with mindfulness based on the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, died and were reborn among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven.'

body.text:
123.029. atha saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣan/
123.030. aśrauṣuḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya pracaranto 'nāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśane śukaśāvakau--namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāyeti biḍālena prāṇinā vyaparopitau<124> iti/
body.translated_text:
123.029. Then a number of monks, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.
123.030. The monks, while going for alms in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, heard that in the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, the two young parrots, having uttered 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>,' had been killed by a cat.

body.text:
124.001. śrutvā ca punaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyāḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntāḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisāmayya pādau prakṣālya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
124.002. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
124.003. ekāntaniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavo bhagavantamidamavocan--iha vayaṃ bhadanta saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavad yāvadanāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveśane dvau śukaśāvakau--namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāyeti kurvāṇau biḍālena prāṇinā jīvitādvyaparopitau iti/
124.006. tayorbhadanta kā gatiḥ, kopapattiḥ, ko 'bhisamparāyah? bhagavānāha--tau bhikṣavaḥ śukaśāvakau tasya śaraṇagamanasya vipākena ṣaṭtriṃśatkṛtvaścāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣūpapatsyete, ṣaṭtriṃśatkṛtvastrāyastriṃśeṣu, yāmeṣu, tuṣiteṣu, nirmāṇaratiṣu, paranirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣūpapastyete/
124.009 tatastāvat ṣaṭsu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu sattvā vyapasaṃsṛtya paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe manuṣyapratilābhaṃ labdhvā pratyekāṃ bodhimabhisambhotsyete, dharmaśca sudharmaśca pratyekabuddhau bhaviṣyataḥ/
124.011. evaṃ hi bhikṣavo mahāphalaṃ dharmaśravaṇaṃ mahānuśaṃsakam, kaḥ punarvādo dharmadeśanā dharmābhisamayo vā/
124.012. tasmāttarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam yanno dharmaśravaṇābhiratā bhaviṣyāmaḥ/
124.013. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text:
124.001. Having heard this, and having completed their alms-round in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, after the meal, having returned from the alms-round and having put away their bowls and robes, washed their feet, they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
124.002. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side.
124.003. Seated to one side, the monks said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, Venerable Sir, we monks, as before, up to: in the residence of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, the two young parrots, while uttering "Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, homage to the <s>Dharma</s>, homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>," were killed by a cat.
124.006. What, Venerable Sir, is their destination, what is their rebirth, what is their future state?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those two young parrots, monks, by the ripening of that going to the refuges, will be reborn thirty-six times among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven, thirty-six times among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, among the <s>Yāma</s> gods, among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, and among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods.
124.009. Then, having transmigrated through the six classes of desire-realm gods, in their final existence, their final abode, their final obtaining of a self, having obtained a human birth, they will attain solitary enlightenment (<s>Pratyekabodhī</s>). They shall become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> named <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Sudharma</s>.
124.011. Thus indeed, monks, hearing the <s>Dharma</s> is of great fruit and great benefit — how much more so teaching the <s>Dharma</s> or realizing the <s>Dharma</s>!
124.012. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall be devoted to hearing the <s>Dharma</s>."
124.013. Thus, monks, should you train.'

body.text:
124.014. idamavocadbhagavān/
124.014. ātamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
124.014. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
124.014. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 124.015. iti śrīdivyāvadāne śukapotakāvadānaṃ ṣoḍaśam//
body.translated_text: 124.015. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Śukapotaka Avadāna</s> (The Story of the Parrot Chicks), the sixteenth.

body.text: 125.001. div17 māndhātāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 125.001. Chapter 17: The <s>Māndhāta Avadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Māndhāta</s>).

body.text:
125.002. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
125.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām/
125.003. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
125.004. vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamayya yena cāpālacaityaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
125.005. upasaṃkramyānyatamaṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya/
125.006. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--ramaṇīyā ānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiścāpālacaityaṃ saptāmrakam {bahupatrakam} gautamanyagrodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhurānikṣepanaṃ mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam/
125.008. citro jambudvīpaḥ, madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām/
125.008. yasya kasyacidānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, ākāṅkṣan sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
125.010. tathāgatasya ānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ/
125.011. ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
125.011. evamukte āyuṣmānānandastūṣṇīm/
125.012. dvirapi trirapi bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--ramaṇīyā ānanda vaiśālī vṛjibhūmiścāpālaṃ caityaṃ saptāmrakaṃ bahupatrakaṃ gautamanyagrodhaḥ śālavanaṃ dhuranikṣepanaṃ mallānāṃ makuṭabandhanaṃ caityam/
125.014. citro jambudvīpaḥ, madhuraṃ jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām/
125.014. yasya kasyacidānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, ākāṅkṣan sa kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
125.016. tathāgatasya ānanda catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ/
125.016. ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
125.017. dvirapi trirapi āyuṣmānānandastūṣṇīm/
125.017. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--sphūṭo 'bhavadānando bhikṣurmāreṇa pāpīyasā yatredānīm yāvat trirapi audārike avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkriyamāṇe na śaknoti tannimittamājñātum yathāpi tataḥ sphuṭo māreṇa pāpīyasā/
125.020. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha tvamānanda, anyataravṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya vihara, mā ubhāvapi ākīrṇavihāriṇau bhaviṣyāvaḥ/
125.021. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagvataḥ pratiśrutya anyatamavṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya/
125.022. sa māraḥ pāpīyān yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
125.023. uapsaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat--parinirvātu bhagavān/
125.023. parinirvāṇakālasmayaḥ sugatasya/
125.024. kasmāt tvaṃ pāpīyann evaṃ vadasi--parinirvātu bhagavān, parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya? eko 'yaṃ bhadanta samayah--bhagavānurubilvāyāṃ viharati nadyā nairañjanāyāstīre bodhimūle 'cirābhisambuddhaḥ/
125.026. so 'ham yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
125.026. upasaṃkramya bhagavantamevaṃ vadāmi--parinirvātu bhagavān, parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya/
125.027. bhagavānevamāha--na tāvat pāpīyan parinirvāsyāmi, yāvanna me śrāvakāḥ piṇḍatā bhaviṣyanti vyaktā vinītā viśāradāḥ, alamutpannotpannānāṃ parapravādināṃ sahadharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ, alaṃ svasya vādasya paryavadāpayitāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā uapāsikāḥ/
125.030. vaistārikaṃ ca te brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyanti bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksamprakāśitam/
125.031. etarhi bhadanta bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā vyaktā vinītā viśāradā alamutpannotpannānāṃ parapravāditāṃ sahadharmeṇa <126>nigrahītāraḥ, svasya vādasya paryavadāpayitāro bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikāḥ/
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, on the bank of the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robes, entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms. Having gone for alms in <s>Vaiśālī</s>, having finished his meal and returned from the alms-round, having put away his bowl and robes, he approached the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine. Having approached, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his daytime retreat. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Delightful, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>; delightful is the <s>Vṛji</s> land, the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, the <s>Saptāmraka</s>, the <s>Bahupatraka</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> Banyan, the <s>Śāla</s> grove, the Yoke-dropping place, and the Crown-binding shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>. Colorful is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, sweet is the life of humans. Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and frequently practiced the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipādas</s>), he, if he so wished, could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> (eon) or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and frequently practiced the four bases of supernatural power. If he so wished, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.' When this was said, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> remained silent. A second time and a third time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Delightful, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Vaiśālī</s>; delightful is the <s>Vṛji</s> land, the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, the <s>Saptāmraka</s>, the <s>Bahupatraka</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> Banyan, the <s>Śāla</s> grove, the Yoke-dropping place, and the Crown-binding shrine of the <s>Mallas</s>. Colorful is <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, sweet is the life of humans. Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and frequently practiced the four bases of supernatural power, he, if he so wished, could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, has cultivated, developed, and frequently practiced the four bases of supernatural power. If he so wished, the <s>Tathāgata</s> could remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.' A second time and a third time, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> remained silent. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'The monk <s>Ānanda</s> has been bewitched by <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, since now, even when such an obvious and manifest sign has been displayed three times, he is unable to understand the sign — so thoroughly has he been bewitched by <s>Māra</s> the Evil One.' There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, sit at the foot of another tree for your daytime retreat. Let us not both be dwellers in a crowded place.' 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down at the foot of another tree for his daytime retreat. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>! It is time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.' 'Why do you, Evil One, speak thus — "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>; it is time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>"?' 'There was a time, Venerable Sir, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Uruvilva</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, shortly after his full awakening. I approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, I said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>; it is time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "I shall not yet pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, Evil One, until my disciples become learned, skilled, trained, and confident, capable of refuting the doctrines of opponents with the counter-dharma, capable of establishing their own doctrine — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen. And until their holy life is practiced widely, extensively, and fully proclaimed to gods and humans." Now, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples are learned, skilled, trained, and confident, capable of refuting the doctrines of opponents with the counter-dharma, capable of establishing their own doctrine — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.'

body.text:
126.002. vaistārikaṃ ca te brahmacaryaṃ bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksamprakāśitam/
126.003. tasmādahamevaṃ vadāmi--parinirvātu bhagavān, parinirvāṇakālasamayaḥ sugatasya/
126.004. alpotsukastvaṃ pāpīyan bhava/
126.004. nicirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasya trayāṇāṃ varṣikāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayānnirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati/
126.005. atha mārasya pāpīyasa etadabhavat--parinirvāsyate bata śramaṇo gautamaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'And their holy life is practiced widely, extensively, and fully proclaimed to gods and humans. Therefore I say: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>; it is time for the <s>Sugata</s>'s final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>."' 'Be unconcerned, Evil One. Before long, at the end of three months of the rainy season, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>).' Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One thought: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will indeed pass into final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>!'

body.text: 126.006. iti viditvā hṛṣṭastuṣṭaḥ pramudita udagraḥ prītisaumanasyajātastatraivāntarhitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Knowing this, delighted, joyful, elated, uplifted, filled with gladness and satisfaction, he vanished right there.

body.text:
126.007. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--kastathāgatasya saṃmukhaṃ vaineyah? supriyo gandharvarājā subhadraśca parivrājakaḥ/
126.008. tayostrayāṇāṃ varṣikāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayādindriyaparipāko bhaviṣyati sukhādhiṣṭhānaṃ vā/
126.009. śakyaṃ śrāvakavaineyastathāgatena vinayituṃ na tu tathāgatavaineyaḥ śrāvakeṇa//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Who is to be personally trained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>? <s>Supriyo</s>, the king of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Subhadra</s> the wanderer. At the end of three months of the rainy season, the maturation of their faculties or the conducive conditions will come about. A being trainable by the disciples can be trained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, but a being trainable by the <s>Tathāgata</s> cannot be trained by a disciple.'

body.text:
126.010. atha bhagavata etadabhavat--yannvahaṃ tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyeyam yathā samāhite citte jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārānutsṛjeyam/
126.011. atha bhagavāṃstadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārānutsraṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
126.012. samanantarādhiṣṭhiteṣu jīvitasaṃskāreṣu mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūdulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ/
126.013. antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti/
126.014. samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu ṣaṇnimittāni prādurbhūtānipuṣpavṛkṣaḥ śīrṇāḥ, ratnavṛkṣāḥ śīrṇāḥ, ābharaṇavṛkṣāḥ śīrṇāḥ, bhavanasahasrāṇi prakampitāni, sumeruśṛṅgāni viśīrṇāni, daivatāni vāditrabhāṇḍāni parāhatāni/
126.016. atha bhagavāṃstasmāt samādhervyutthāya tasyā velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
126.018. tulyamatulyaṃ ca saṃbhavaṃ bavasaṃskāramapotsṛjanmuniḥ/
126.019. adhyātmarataḥ samāhito hyabhinitkośamivāṇḍasambhavaḥ//1//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Let me now enter into such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that, with my mind concentrated, having sustained the life-formations, I shall release the lifespan-formations.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered into such a <s>samādhi</s> that, with his mind concentrated, having sustained the life-formations, he began to release the lifespan-formations. The moment the life-formations were sustained, a great earthquake occurred, meteors fell, and the directions blazed. In the sky, divine drums resounded. The moment the lifespan-formations were released, among the gods of the desire realm, six signs appeared: the flower-trees withered, the jewel-trees withered, the ornament-trees withered, thousands of palaces trembled, the peaks of <s>Sumeru</s> crumbled, and the divine musical instruments were struck without being played. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen from that <s>samādhi</s>, at that moment spoke a verse: 'The sage, releasing the formation of becoming, both equal and unequal in origin, inwardly delighted and concentrated, broke through the shell like one born from an egg.'

body.text:
126.020. samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣu ṣaṭ kāmāvacarā devāḥ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā bhagavato 'ntikaṃ prakrāntā darśanāya vandanāya/
126.021. bhagavatā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yadanekairdevatāśatasahasraiḥ satyāni dṛṣṭāni, dṛṣṭasatyāḥ svabhavanamanuprāptāḥ/
126.022. samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāreṣvanekāni parvatakandaragiriguhābhyo 'nekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇyāgatāni/
126.023. te bhagavatā 'eta bhikṣavaścarata brahmacaryam' pravrajitāḥ/
126.024. tairyojayadbhirghaṭadbhiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
126.024. samanantarotsṛṣṭeṣvāyuḥsaṃskāroṣvanekā nāgayakṣagandharvakinnaramahoragā bhagavataḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntā bhagavato darśanāya/
126.026. bhagavatā teṣāmevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā yadanekair nāgayakṣagandharvakinnarairmahoragaiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni yāvat svabhavanamanuprāptāḥ//
body.translated_text: The moment the lifespan-formations were released, the six desire-realm gods, having made preparations, set out to see and pay homage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that many hundreds of thousands of deities realized the truths; having realized the truths, they returned to their own abodes. The moment the lifespan-formations were released, from many mountain caves, gorges, and grottoes, many hundreds of thousands of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) came. They were ordained by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the words 'Come, monks, practice the holy life.' Striving and exerting themselves, through the abandonment of all afflictions, they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. The moment the lifespan-formations were released, many <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> to see him. The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave them such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that many <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> took the refuges and precepts, and then returned to their own abodes.

body.text:
126.028. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ sāyāhṇe 'bhisamlayanādvyutthāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
126.028. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthād/
126.029. ekāntasthita āyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--ko bhadanta hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya? aṣṭau ime ānanda aṣṭau pratyayā mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
126.031. katame 'ṣṭau? iyamānanda mahāpṛthivī apsu pratiṣṭhitā, āpo vāyau pratiṣṭhitāḥ, vāyurākāśe pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
126.032. bhavatyānanda samayo yadākāśe yadākāśe viṣamā <127>vāyavo vānti, āpaḥ kṣobhayanti, āpaḥ kṣubdhāḥ pṛthivīṃ cālayanti/
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, in the evening, having emerged from his meditative seclusion, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition, of the great earthquake?' 'There are, <s>Ānanda</s>, eight causes, eight conditions, of a great earthquake. What are the eight? This, <s>Ānanda</s>, great earth rests upon water, water rests upon wind, wind rests upon space. There comes a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, when uneven winds blow in space, and they agitate the waters; the agitated waters cause the earth to quake.'

body.text:
127.001. ayamānanda prathamo hetuḥ prathamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.002. punaraparamānanda bhikṣurmaharddhiko bhavati mahānubhāvaḥ/
127.003. sa ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ pṛthivīṃ cālayati/
127.004. devatā maharddhikā bhavati mahānubhāvā/
127.004. sāpi parittāṃ pṛthivīsaṃjñāmadhitiṣṭhati apramāṇāṃ cāpsaṃjñam/
127.005. sāpyākāṅkṣamāṇā pṛthivīṃ cālayati/
127.005. ayaṃ dvitīyo heturdvitīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.006. punaraparamānanda/
127.006. yasmin samaye bodhisattvastuṣitāddevanikāyāccyuttvā mātuḥ kukṣimavakrāmati, atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati, sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati/
127.008. yā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatrāmū sūryācandramasau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
127.010. tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ, te tayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānante--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
127.012. ayamānanda tṛtīyo hetustṛtīyaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.013. punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo mātuḥ kukṣer niṣkrāmati, atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati/
127.014. yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
127.016. tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ, te tayā ābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
127.018. ayamānanda caturtho hetuścaturthaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.019. punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye bodhisattvo 'nuttaraṃ jñānamadhigacchati, atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati, sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati/
127.020. yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā pi tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
127.023. tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ, te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
127.024. ayamānanda pañcamo hetuḥ pañcamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.025. punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye tathāgatastriparivartadvādaśākāraṃ dharmacakraṃ parivartayati, atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati, sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati/
127.027. yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
127.029. tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ, te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
127.031. ayamānanda ṣaṣṭho hetuḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
127.032. punaraparamānanda yasmin samaye tathāgato jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya <128>āyuḥsaṃskāranutsṛjati, atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati ulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ, antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti, sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo bhavati/
body.translated_text:
127.001. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the first cause, the first condition for a great earthquake.
127.002. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, a monk may be one of great supernatural power and great might.
127.003. He, if he so wishes, causes the earth to quake.
127.004. A deity may be one of great supernatural power and great might.
127.004. She too resolves upon a limited perception of earth and an unlimited perception of water.
127.005. She too, if she so wishes, causes the earth to quake.
127.005. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the second cause, the second condition for a great earthquake.
127.006. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>,
127.006. at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, falling from the <s>Tuṣita</s> host of gods, descends into his mother's womb — at that time a great earthquake occurs, and this entire world is suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.008. Even those inter-cosmic voids of the world, blind darkness and obscure gloom, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, are suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.010. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
127.012. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the third cause, the third condition for a great earthquake.
127.013. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> emerges from his mother's womb — at that time a great earthquake occurs, and this entire world is suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.014. Even those inter-cosmic voids of the world, blind darkness and obscure gloom, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, are suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.016. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
127.018. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the fourth cause, the fourth condition for a great earthquake.
127.019. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains unsurpassed knowledge — at that time a great earthquake occurs, and this entire world is suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.020. Even those inter-cosmic voids of the world, blind darkness and obscure gloom, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, are suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.023. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
127.024. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the fifth cause, the fifth condition for a great earthquake.
127.025. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s> sets in motion the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) with its three turnings and twelve aspects — at that time a great earthquake occurs, and this entire world is suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.027. Even those inter-cosmic voids of the world, blind darkness and obscure gloom, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, are suffused with a magnificent radiance.
127.029. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
127.031. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the sixth cause, the sixth condition for a great earthquake.
127.032. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, at the time when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having maintained the life-force, relinquishes the life-formations — at that time a great earthquake occurs, meteors fall, the directions blaze, divine drums resound in the sky, and this entire world is suffused with a magnificent radiance.

body.text:
128.003. yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhāstamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayāa ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
128.005. tatra ye sattvā upapannāḥ, te tayābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
128.006. ayamānanda saptamo hetuḥ saptamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya/
128.007. punaraparamānanda nacirasyedānīṃ tathāgatasya nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati/
128.008. atha tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo bhavati ulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ, antarikṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinandanti, sarvaścāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena yatremau sūryacandramasau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā bhavanti/
128.012. tatra ye sattvā, upapannāḥ, te tayā ābhayā anyonyaṃ sattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjānanti--anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannāḥ, anye 'pīha bhavantaḥ sattvā upapannā iti/
128.014. ayamānanda aṣṭamo heturaṣṭamaḥ pratyayo mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya//
body.translated_text:
128.003. Even those inter-cosmic voids of the world, blind darkness and obscure gloom, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, are suffused with a magnificent radiance.
128.005. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
128.006. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the seventh cause, the seventh condition for a great earthquake.
128.007. Furthermore, <s>Ānanda</s>, before long the <s>Tathāgata</s> will attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder of clinging.
128.008. At that time a great earthquake will occur, meteors will fall, the directions will blaze, divine drums will resound in the sky, and this entire world will be suffused with a magnificent radiance, where even the sun and moon, so mighty and so powerful, cannot reach with their light — even those, at that time, will be suffused with a magnificent radiance.
128.012. Those beings who have been reborn there, by that radiance, seeing one another, will become aware: 'Other beings too have been reborn here; other beings too have been reborn here.'
128.014. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the eighth cause, the eighth condition for a great earthquake.

body.text:
