128.015. athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--yathā khalvahaṃ bhadanta bhagavatā bhāsitasyārthamājānāmi, ihaiva bhagavatā jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuhasaṃskārā utsṛṣṭā bhaviṣyanti/
128.017. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametat/
128.017. etarhi ānanda tathāgatena jīvitasaṃskārānadhiṣṭhāya āyuḥsaṃskārā utsṛṣṭāḥ/
128.018. saṃmukhaṃ me bhadanta bhagavato 'ntikācchrutaṃ saṃmukhamudgṛhītam--yasya kasyaciccatvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhat, kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
128.020. bhagavatā bhadanta catvāra ṛddhipādā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ/
128.021. ākāṅkṣamāṇastathāgataḥ kalpaṃ vā tiṣṭhet kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
128.021. tiṣṭhatu bhagavān kalpam, tiṣṭhatu sugataḥ kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā/
128.022. tavaivānanda aparādhastavaiva duṣkṛtam yastvaṃ tathāyatasya yāvat trirapyaudāre avabhāsanimitte prāviṣkṛte na śaknoṣi tannimittaṃ pratiśrāvayitum, api tataḥ sphuṭo māreṇa pāpīyasā/
128.024. kimanyasya ānanda bhāṣeta tathāgatastāṃ vācam yā syād dvidhā? no bhadanta/
128.025. sādhu sādhu ānanda, asthānametadānanda anavakāśo yat tathāgatastāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣeta yā syāddvidhā/
128.026. gaccha tvamānanda, yāvanto bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti, tān sarvānupasthānaśālāyāṃ saṃnipātaya/
128.027. evaṃ bhadanta/
128.027. āyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yāvanto bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti, tān sarvānupasthānaśālāyāṃ saṃnipātya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
128.029. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt/
128.030. ekāntasthita āyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--yāvanto bhadanta bhikṣavaścāpālaṃ caityamupaniśritya viharanti, sarve te upasthānaśālāyāṃ niṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ, yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate/
128.032. atha bhagavān yenopasthānaśālā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text:
128.015. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'As I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, Venerable Sir, it is right here that the Blessed One, having maintained the life-force, has relinquished the life-formations.'
128.017. The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.
128.017. Now, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has, having maintained the life-force, relinquished the life-formations.'
128.018. 'I have heard directly from the Blessed One, Venerable Sir, received directly: "Whoever has cultivated, developed, and made much of the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the <s>Tathāgata</s>, if he so wishes, may remain for a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>."
128.020. The Blessed One, Venerable Sir, has cultivated, developed, and made much of the four bases of supernatural power.
128.021. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, if he so wishes, may remain for a <s>kalpa</s> or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>.
128.021. May the Blessed One remain for a <s>kalpa</s>! May the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone) remain for the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>!'
128.022. 'This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is your own fault, your own misdeed, that when the <s>Tathāgata</s> made clear and manifest the splendid, radiant sign three times, you were unable to respond to that sign — being covered over by <s>Māra</s> the Evil One.
128.024. Would the <s>Tathāgata</s> speak a word that would be false, <s>Ānanda</s>?' 'No, Venerable Sir.'
128.025. 'Good, good, <s>Ānanda</s>. It is impossible and inconceivable, <s>Ānanda</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> would speak a word that would be false.'
128.026. 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and summon to the assembly hall all the monks who dwell in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine.'
128.027. 'So be it, Venerable Sir.'
128.027. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, summoned to the assembly hall all the monks who dwelt in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, and then approached the Blessed One.
128.029. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
128.030. Standing to one side, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'All the monks who dwell in the vicinity of the <s>Cāpāla</s> shrine, Venerable Sir, have assembled and gathered in the assembly hall. May the Blessed One proceed at whatever time he thinks fit.'
128.032. Then the Blessed One approached the assembly hall.

body.text:
129.001. <129>upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat/
129.001. niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--anityā bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā adhruvā anāśvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇo yāvadalameva bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārān saṃskaritumalam/
129.003. viramantu tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ/
129.003. etarhi vā me 'tyayādye te dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya, saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya, te bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpya tathā tathā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā grāhayitavyā yathaiva tatra brahmacaryaṃ virasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksamprakāśitam/
129.006. etarhi bhikṣavo dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya, saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya, ye bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpay tathā tathā dhārayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathaitadbrahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksamprakāśitam/
129.009. yaduta catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāni, āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ/
129.011. ime te bhikṣavo dharmā dṛṣṭadharmahitāya saṃvartante dṛṣṭadharmasukhāya, saṃparāyahitāya saṃparāyasukhāya, bhikṣubhirudgṛhya paryavāpya tathā tathā dhārayitavyā grāhayitavyā vācayitavyā yathaitadbrahmacaryaṃ cirasthitikaṃ syādbahujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtam yāvaddevamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksamprakāśitam/
129.013. āgamaya ānanda yena kuśigrāmakam/
129.014. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt/
129.014. bhagavān vaiśālīvanamabhisaran dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitena vyavalokayati/
129.015. athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--nāhetvapratyayaṃ bhadanta tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā dakṣiṇena nāgāvalokitamavalokayanti/
129.017. ko bhadanta hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayo nāgāvalokitasya? evametadānanda, evametat/
129.018. nāhetvapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā dakṣiṇena sarvakāyena nāgāvalokitena vyavalokayanti/
129.019. idamānanda tathāgatasyāpaścimaṃ vaiśālīdarśanam/
129.019. na bhūya ānanda tathāgato vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati/
129.020. parinirvāṇāya gamiṣyati mallānāmupavartanam yamakaśālavanam/
129.021. athānyataro bhikṣustasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
129.022. idamapaścimakaṃ nātha vaiśālyāstava darśanam/
129.023. na bhūyaḥ sugato buddho vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati//2//
body.translated_text:
129.001. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.
129.001. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Impermanent, O monks, are all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — unstable, unreliable, subject to change. Enough, monks, of producing any more conditioned things! Enough!
129.003. Therefore, monks, you should desist.
129.003. After my passing, those teachings (<s>dharmas</s>) which conduce to well-being in this very life and to happiness in this very life, which conduce to well-being in future lives and to happiness in future lives — those teachings should be learned, comprehended, retained, recited, and taught to others by the monks, so that this holy life may be long-lasting, widely spread, and fully proclaimed to gods and humans.
129.006. Now, monks, those teachings which conduce to well-being in this very life and to happiness in this very life, which conduce to well-being in future lives and to happiness in future lives — those should be learned, comprehended, retained, taught, and recited by the monks, so that this holy life may be long-lasting, widely spread, and fully proclaimed to gods and humans.
129.009. Namely: the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>).
129.011. These, monks, are the teachings which conduce to well-being in this very life and to happiness in this very life, which conduce to well-being in future lives and to happiness in future lives. They should be learned, comprehended, retained, taught, and recited by the monks, so that this holy life may be long-lasting, widely spread, and fully proclaimed to gods and humans.'
129.013. 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Kuśigrāmaka</s>.'
129.014. 'So be it, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One.
129.014. The Blessed One, while heading toward the forest of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, looked back at it with his whole body, turning like an elephant.
129.015. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Not without cause or condition, Venerable Sir, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, look back with the whole body, turning like an elephant.
129.017. What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the condition for looking back like an elephant?' 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.
129.018. Not without cause or condition do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, look back with the whole body, turning like an elephant.
129.019. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> last sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.
129.019. No more, <s>Ānanda</s>, will the <s>Tathāgata</s> come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.
129.020. He will proceed to his <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, to the <s>Mallas'</s> <s>Upavartana</s>, the twin <s>Śāla</s> grove.'
129.021. Then a certain monk, at that moment, spoke a verse:
129.022. 'This is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> last sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, O Protector;
129.023. No more will the <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.' // 2 //

body.text:
129.024. nirvāṇāya gamiṣyati mallānāmupavartanam yamakaśālavanam/
129.024. yadā ha bhagavatā vāg bhāṣitā idamapaścimakaṃ vaiśālyā darśanam, tadā anekābhirvaiśālīvananivāsinībhirdevatairaśrupātaḥ kṛtaḥ/
129.026. sthavirānandaḥ kathayati--na bhagavannameghenaiva varṣāsu pravṛṣṭah? bhagavānāha--vaiśālivananivāsinībhirdaivatairmama viyogādaśrupātaḥ kṛtaḥ/
129.027. tā api devatā(?) vaiśālyāṃ śabdo niścāritah--bhagavān parinirvāṇāya gacchati, na bhūyo bhagavān vaiśālīmāgamiṣyati/
129.029. devatānāṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā anekāni vaiśālikāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi bhagavatsakāśamupasaṃkrāntāni/
129.030. bhagavatā teṣāmāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā evaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yathā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni/
129.031. kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ kaiścit sakṛdāgamiphalaṃ kaiścidanāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam/
129.032. kaiścit pravrajitvā arhattvaṃ prāptam/
129.032. kaiścicchrāvakabodhau<130> cittamutpāditam/
body.translated_text:
129.024. 'He will proceed to his <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, to the <s>Mallas'</s> <s>Upavartana</s>, the twin <s>Śāla</s> grove.'
129.024. When the Blessed One spoke the words 'This is the last sight of <s>Vaiśālī</s>,' then many forest-dwelling deities of <s>Vaiśālī</s> shed tears.
129.026. The Elder <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Is it not raining when the rains have not come, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'The forest-dwelling deities of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, out of grief at separation from me, have shed tears.'
129.027. Those deities too spread the word in <s>Vaiśālī</s>: 'The Blessed One is going to his <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>; no more will the Blessed One come to <s>Vaiśālī</s>.'
129.029. Having heard the sound of the deities, many hundreds of thousands of beings of <s>Vaiśālī</s> approached the Blessed One.
129.030. The Blessed One, knowing their dispositions, tendencies, natures, and characters, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> that many hundreds of thousands of beings took the refuges and precepts.
129.031. Some attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>), some the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), some the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>).
129.032. Some, having gone forth, attained <s>Arhatship</s>.
129.032. Some generated the aspiration for the enlightenment of a disciple (<s>śrāvakabodhi</s>).

body.text:
130.001. kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam/
130.001. kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditam/
130.002. kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni/
130.002. yadbhūyasā sā parṣadbuddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā/
130.003. sthavirānandaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhagavantamidamavocat--paśya bhadanta yāvat tvam/
130.004. bhagavatā parinirvāṇāya prasthitenānekāni devatāśatasahasrāṇi satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni/
130.005. anekābhyaḥ parvatakandaragiriguhābhyo 'nekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇyāgatāni/
130.006. bhagavatā ete bhikṣavaḥ pravrajitāḥ/
130.006. tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhirvyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
130.007. anekairdevanāgayakṣagandharvakinnaramahoragaiḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni/
130.008. anekāni vaiśālakāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi srotāapattiphale pratiṣṭhāpitāni/
130.009. kecit sakṛdāgamiphale, kecidanāgāmiphale, kecit pravrājitaḥ/
130.010. pravrajitvā arhattvaṃ prāptam/
130.010. keciccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ/
130.010. atra ānanda kimāścaryaṃ mayā etarhi sarvajñena sarvākārajñenānuttarajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena astatṛṣṇena nirupādānena sarvāhaṃkāramamakārāsmimānābhiniveśānuśayaprahīṇena evaṃvidhaṃ vaineyakāryaṃ kṛtam/
130.012. yanmayā atīte 'pyadhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmeṇa yanmayā maraṇāntikayā vedanayā spṛṣṭena evaṃvidhā parikarmakathā kṛtā, yadanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi gṛhāśramamapahāya, ṛṣayaḥ pravrajitvā catvāro brahmavihārān bhāvayitvā kalpavṛndaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokasabhāgatāyāmupapannāḥ/
130.016. tacchruṇu--
130.017. bhūtapūrvamānanda upoṣadho nāma rājā babhūva/
130.017. upoṣadhasya rājño mūrdhni piṭṭako jāto mṛduḥ sumṛduḥ, tadyathā tūlapicurvā karpāsapicurvā/
130.018. na kaṃcidābādhaṃ janayati/
130.018. pakvaḥ sphuṭitaḥ/
130.019. kumāro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ/
130.019. upoṣadhasya rājñaḥ ṣaṣṭistrīsahasrāṇi/
130.020. sarvāsāṃ stanāḥ prasṛtāḥ/
130.020. ekaikā kathayati--māṃ dhaya māṃ dhaya/
130.020. mūrdhato jāto mūrdhāta iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
130.021. māṃ dhaya māṃ dhaya māndhāta iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
130.021. anye kathayanti--kecinmādhāta iti saṃjānīte/
130.022. māndhātasya kumārasya kumārakrīḍāyāṃ krīḍataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
130.023. yauvarājye pratiṣṭhitasya ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
130.023. māndhātā janapadān gataḥ/
130.023. janapadān gatasya pitā glānībhūtaḥ/
130.024. sa mūlapatragaṇḍapuṣpabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva/
130.024. tatastairamātyaiḥ saṃdeśo visarjitah--pitā te glānībhūtaḥ/
130.025. āgacchatu/
130.025. devarājyaṃ pratīccha/
130.025. tasyānāgacchatas tasyānāgacchataḥ pitā kālagataḥ/
130.026. tairamātyaiḥ punaḥ saṃdeśo visarjitah--pitā te kāladharmaṇā samyuktaḥ/
130.026. āgaccha, devarājyaṃ pratīcchasva/
130.027. tato 'sau saṃlakṣayati--yadi mama pitā kālagataḥ, kiṃ bhūyo 'haṃ gacchāmīti? tato bhūyaḥ saṃdeśo 'bhyāgataḥ/
130.028. āgaccha, devarājyaṃ pratīccha/
130.028. sa kathayati--yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate, ihaiva rājyābhiṣeka āgacchatu/
130.029. tataste amātyaiḥ kathayanti--ratnaśilayā deva prayojanaṃ bhavati/
130.030. tasya ca divaukaso nāma yakṣaḥ purojavaḥ/
130.030. tena ratnaśilā ānītā/
130.031. yadā ratnaśilā ānītā, tataste amātyā bhūyaḥ kathayanti--deva śrīparyaṅkenātra prayojanaṃ bhavati/
130.032. tatastenaiva divaukasena śrīparyaṅka ānītaḥ/
130.032. tataste amātyā bhūyaḥ kathayanti--<131>devādhiṣṭhānamadhye 'bhiṣekaḥ kriyate/
body.translated_text:
130.001. Some generated the aspiration for solitary enlightenment (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>).
130.001. Some generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>).
130.002. Some took the refuges and precepts.
130.002. For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
130.003. The Elder <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, said to the Blessed One: 'See, Venerable Sir, how much you have accomplished!
130.004. As the Blessed One set out for <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, many hundreds of thousands of deities have been established in the truths.
130.005. From many mountain caves, gorges, and grottoes, many hundreds of thousands of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) have come.
130.006. By the Blessed One, these monks have been ordained.
130.006. By them, striving and exerting themselves, through the abandonment of all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), <s>Arhatship</s> has been directly realized.
130.007. Many gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> have taken the refuges and precepts.
130.008. Many hundreds of thousands of beings of <s>Vaiśālī</s> have been established in the fruit of stream-entry.
130.009. Some in the fruit of once-returning, some in the fruit of non-returning; some have gone forth.
130.010. Having gone forth, they have attained <s>Arhatship</s>.
130.010. Some have been established in the refuges and precepts.
130.010. Herein, <s>Ānanda</s>, what is so wondrous? That I, the Omniscient One, the Knower of All Modes, having attained mastery over unsurpassed knowledge, free from thirst, without clinging, having abandoned all self-view, possessiveness, pride of 'I am,' and latent tendencies — that I should have accomplished such a task of training beings?
130.012. That even in the past, when I was still endowed with passion, with hatred, with delusion, not freed from birth, aging, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and distress — even then, when I was touched by the pain of death, I performed such preparatory deeds that many hundreds of thousands of beings, having abandoned the household life, went forth as <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages); having gone forth, they cultivated the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings), and having relinquished hosts of worldly <s>kalpas</s>, dwelling much in those states, they were reborn in the company of <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
130.016. Hear then —
130.017. Once upon a time, <s>Ānanda</s>, there was a king named <s>Upoṣadha</s>.
130.017. On the head of King <s>Upoṣadha</s>, a boil appeared — soft, very soft, like cotton fiber or a ball of cotton.
130.018. It caused no pain.
130.018. When ripe, it burst open.
130.019. A prince was born — handsome, good-looking, attractive, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being.
130.019. King <s>Upoṣadha</s> had sixty thousand queens.
130.020. All their breasts began to lactate.
130.020. Each one said: 'Suckle me! Suckle me!'
130.020. Since he was born from the head, the name <s>Mūrdhāta</s> ('head-born') was given.
130.021. Since they cried 'Suckle me! Suckle me!' (<s>māṃ dhaya</s>), the name <s>Māndhāta</s> was given.
130.021. Others say some knew him as <s>Mādhāta</s>.
130.022. While the prince <s>Māndhāta</s> was playing children's games, six wheel-jewels appeared.
130.023. When he was installed as crown prince, six more wheel-jewels appeared.
130.023. <s>Māndhāta</s> went to the provinces.
130.023. While he was in the provinces, his father fell ill.
130.024. Despite being treated with medicines of roots, leaves, compresses, and flowers, he only worsened.
130.024. Then the ministers sent a message: 'Your father has fallen ill.
130.025. Come.
130.025. Accept the kingdom.'
130.025. While he did not come, while he did not come, his father died.
130.026. The ministers sent another message: 'Your father has met his natural end.
130.026. Come, accept the kingdom.'
130.027. Then he reflected: 'If my father has died, why should I go any further?' Then yet another message arrived:
130.028. 'Come, accept the kingdom.'
130.028. He said: 'If the kingdom shall come to me by right, let the royal consecration come here itself.'
130.029. Then the ministers said: 'Your Majesty, the jewel-seat is needed.'
130.030. He had a <s>Yakṣa</s> servant named <s>Divaukasa</s> who was swift.
130.030. By him, the jewel-seat was brought.
130.031. When the jewel-seat was brought, the ministers then said: 'Your Majesty, the throne of glory (<s>śrīparyaṅka</s>) is needed here.'
130.032. Then by that very <s>Divaukasa</s>, the throne of glory was brought.
130.032. Then the ministers said further: 'Your Majesty, the consecration is performed in the midst of the royal domain.'

body.text:
131.001. sa kathayati--yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate, ihaivādhiṣṭhānamāgacchatu/
131.002. tato 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ svayameva tatpradeśaṃ gatam/
131.002. svayamāgataṃ svayamāgataṃ sāketasāketamiti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
131.003. paścāt te 'mātyā bhaṭabalāgranaigamajanapadāścābhiṣekaṃ gṛhītvā āgatāḥ/
131.004. te kathayanti--abhiṣekaṃ deva pratīcchasva/
131.004. sa kathayati--mama manuṣyāḥ paṭṭaṃ bandhiṣyanti? yadi dharmeṇa rājyaṃ prāpsyate, amanuṣyāḥ paṭṭaṃ bandhantu/
131.005. tato 'manuṣyaiḥ paṭṭo baddhaḥ/
131.005. tasya sapta ratnāni prādurbhūtāni, tadyathā--cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnameva saptamam/
131.007. pūrṇaṃ cāsya sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarupiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
131.008. vaiśālīsāmantakena ramaṇīyaṃ vanakhaṇḍam/
131.008. tatra pañca ṛṣiśatāni pañcābhijñāni dhyāyanti/
131.009. tatra vanakhaṇḍe prabhūtāḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāśca prativasanti/
131.009. śabdakaṇṭakāni ca dhyānāni/
131.010. te ca pakṣiṇo 'vatīryamāṇā avatīryamāṇāḥ śabdaṃ kurvanti/
131.010. durmukho nāma ṛṣiḥ/
131.010. sa kupitaḥ/
131.011. tenoktam--bakānāṃ pakṣāṇi śīryantām/
131.011. yadā teṣām ṛṣikopena pakṣāṇi śīrṇāni, tataste pādoddhārakeṇa prasthitāḥ/
131.012. sa ca rājā janapadānanusaṃsārya paśyati pādoddhārakeṇa gacchataḥ/
131.013. yataste 'mātyāḥ pṛṣṭāh--kasmāt pādoddhārakeṇa gacchanti? paścāt te 'mātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, śabdakaṇṭakāni dhyānānīti eteṣām ṛṣikopena pakṣāṇi śīrṇāni/
131.014. tato rājñā abhihitam--evaṃvidhā api ṛṣayo bhavanti, yeṣāṃ sattvānāmantike nāstyanukampā? tato rājñā amātyāḥ saṃdiṣṭāh--gacchantu bhavantaḥ, ṛṣīṇāmevaṃ vadantu--tatra gacchata yatrāhaṃ na vasayā(sā?)mīti/
131.017. yatastairamātyaih ṛṣayo 'bhihitāḥ/
131.017. rājā samādiśati--na mama rājye vastavyam/
131.018. gacchantu bhavanto yatrāhaṃ na vasayā(sā?)mīti/
131.018. tataste saṃlakṣayanti--eṣo 'yaṃ caturdvīpeśvaraḥ/
131.019. gacchāmo vayaṃ sumeruparikhaṇḍam/
131.019. te tatra gatvā avasthitāḥ//
body.translated_text:
131.001. He said: 'If the kingship will come to me by righteousness, let the throne come here of its own accord.'
131.002. Then the throne went of its own accord to that very place.
131.002. 'It has come by itself, it has come by itself' — thus the name <s>Sāketa</s> ('come by itself') arose.
131.003. Afterwards, those ministers, soldiers, army chiefs, townsfolk, and countryfolk came bearing the consecration.
131.004. They said: 'Accept the consecration, Your Majesty.'
131.004. He said: 'Shall humans tie the royal diadem upon me? If the kingship is to come by righteousness, let non-humans tie the diadem.'
131.005. Then non-humans tied the diadem.
131.005. The seven treasures appeared for him, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the counselor-treasure, the wife-treasure, and the householder-treasure as the seventh.
131.007. He had a full thousand sons — heroic, valiant, of noble form, crushers of enemy armies.
131.008. Near <s>Vaiśālī</s> there was a delightful forest grove.
131.008. There five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) possessing the five superknowledges meditated.
131.009. In that forest grove dwelt many birds and deer.
131.009. And <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) are disturbed by sound.
131.010. Those birds, as they descended again and again, made noise.
131.010. There was a sage named <s>Durmukha</s> ('Foul-Mouth').
131.010. He became angry.
131.011. He said: 'Let the wings of the cranes fall off!'
131.011. When their wings had fallen off by the sage's wrath, they set out walking on foot.
131.012. The king, touring the countryside, saw them walking on foot.
131.013. He asked the ministers: 'Why are they walking on foot?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, <s>dhyānas</s> are disturbed by sound — their wings have fallen off by the sage's wrath.'
131.014. Then the king said: 'Are there even such sages who have no compassion for living beings?' Then the king instructed his ministers: 'Go, sirs, and say this to the sages — "Go to a place where I do not dwell."'
131.017. The ministers conveyed this to the sages.
131.017. 'The king commands: "You must not dwell in my kingdom.
131.018. Go, sirs, to a place where I do not dwell."'
131.018. They reflected: 'This one is lord of the four continents.
131.019. Let us go to the slopes of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.'
131.019. They went there and settled.

body.text:
131.020. rājño mūrdhātasyāmātyāścintakāstulakā upaparīṣakāḥ/
131.020. cintayitvā tulayitvopaparīkṣya pṛthak pṛthagutkāḥ śilpasthānakarmasthānāni māpayitum/
131.021. cintakā ime tulakā upaparīkṣakā iti mantrajā mantrajā iti saṃjñā/
131.022. tairārabdhāni karṣaṇakarmāṇi kartum/
131.022. yataḥ sa rājā paśyati janapadānanusaṃsāryākṛṣyān karmāntān kurvataḥ/
131.023. yato rājñā abhihitam--kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti? tatastairamātyai rājā abhihitah--ete deva manuṣyāḥ śāsyādīni kṛṣanti, tato oṣadhayo bhaviṣyanti/
131.025. yataśca sa rājā kathayati--mama rājye manuṣyāḥ kṛṣiṣyanti? tatastenoktam--aptāviṃśatibījajātīnāṃ devo varṣatu/
131.026. sahacittotpādādeva rājño mūrdhātasya saptāviṃśatibījajātirdevo vṛṣṭaḥ/
131.027. rājñā mūrdhātena janapadāḥ pṛṣṭāh--kasyaitāni puṇyāni? tairabhihitam--devasya cāsmākaṃ ca/
131.028. yataste manuṣyāḥ karpāsavātānārabdhā māpayitum, bhūyo 'pi ca rājñā mūrdhātena janapadānanusaṃsārya tena pṛṣṭāḥ/
131.029. tato rājñā abhihitam--kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti? tairamātyairabhihitam--deva, manuṣyāḥ karpāsavātān māpayanti/
131.030. paścāt rājñā abhihitam--kasyārthe? tairamātyairabhihitam--deva, vastrāṇāmarhe/
131.031. tato rājñā tenoktam--mama rājye manuṣyāḥ karpāsavātān māpayiṣyantīti karpāsameva devo varṣatu/
131.032. sahacittotpādādeva<132> rājño mūrdhātasya karpāsāneva devo vṛṣṭaḥ/
body.translated_text:
131.020. King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> ministers were thinkers, weighers, and examiners.
131.020. Having thought, weighed, and examined, they separately devised various crafts and industries.
131.021. 'These are thinkers, weighers, and examiners' — thus the designation 'born of counsel' (<s>mantrajā</s>) arose.
131.022. They began to perform plowing work.
131.022. The king, touring the countryside, saw them performing agricultural work.
131.023. The king said: 'What are these people doing?' The ministers told the king: 'Your Majesty, these people are plowing crops and such; from this, plants will grow.'
131.025. The king said: 'In my kingdom, people shall plow? Let the sky rain down the twenty-seven kinds of seeds!'
131.026. With the very arising of King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> thought, the sky rained down the twenty-seven kinds of seeds.
131.027. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> asked the countryfolk: 'Whose are these merits?' They replied: 'Your Majesty's and ours.'
131.028. Then those people began to prepare cotton plantations. Again, King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, touring the countryside, asked them.
131.029. The king said: 'What are these people doing?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, the people are preparing cotton plantations.'
131.030. Then the king said: 'For what purpose?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, for the sake of garments.'
131.031. Then the king said: 'In my kingdom, people shall prepare cotton plantations? Let the sky rain down cotton itself!'
131.032. With the very arising of King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> thought, the sky rained down cotton.

body.text:
132.001. sa ca rājā janapadān pṛcchati/
132.001. kasyaitāni puṇyāni? te kathayanti--devasya cāsmākaṃ ca/
132.002. paścāt tena janena tatkarpāsaṃ kartitumārabdham/
132.003. sa rājā kathayati--kimete manuṣyāḥ karvanti? tairamātyairabhihitam--deva sūtreṇa prayojanam/
132.004. tato rājñā abhihitam--mama rājye manuṣyāḥ kartiṣyanti? sūtrameva devo varṣatu/
132.004. sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasya sūtrameva devo vṛṣṭaḥ/
132.005. sa ca rājā kathayati--kasyaitāni puṇyāni? yataste kathayanti--devasya cāsmākaṃ ca/
132.006. yatastairanupūrveṇa vastrāṇyārabdhāni vāpayitum/
132.006. sa rājā kathayati--kimete manuṣyāḥ kurvanti? tairamātyairabhihitam--deva, vastrāṇi vāpayanti, vastraiḥ prayojanam/
132.008. yato rājā saṃlakṣayati--mama rājye manuṣyā vastrāṇi vāpayiṣyante? vastrāṇyeva devo varṣatu/
132.009. sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasya vastrāṇyeva devo vṛṣṭaḥ/
132.009. sa rājā kathayati--kasyaitāni puṇyāni? te kathayanti--devasya cāsmākaṃ ca/
132.010. yataḥ sa rājā saṃlakṣayati--manuṣyā mama puṇyānāṃ prabhāvaṃ na jānanti/
132.011. atha rājño māndhātasyaitadabhavat/
132.011. asti me jambudvīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca/
132.012. santi me sapta ratnāni, tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam/
132.014. pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
132.015. aho bata me 'ntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patet, ekakārṣāpaṇo 'pi bahir na nipatet/
132.015. sahacittotpādādeva rājño māndhātasyāntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ vṛṣṭam/
132.016. ekakārṣāpaṇo 'pi bahir na nipatito yathāpi tanmaharddhikasya sattvasya mahānubhāvasya kṛtapuṇyasya kṛtakuśalasya svakaṃ puṇyaphalaṃ pratyanubhavataḥ/
132.018. yataḥ sa rājā kathayati--kasyaitāni puṇyāni? te kathayanti--devasya cāsmākaṃ ca/
132.019. yato rājā sa rājā kathayati--kṣuṇṇā bhavanto yadi yuṣmābhiḥ pūrvamevābhihitamabhaviṣyaddevasya puṇyānīti, mayā sakalaṃ jambudvīpaṃ ratnairabhivṛṣṭamabhaviṣyat/
132.020. api tu yo yuṣmākaṃ ratnairarthī, sa yāvadīpsitāni ratnāni gṛhṇātu//
body.translated_text:
132.001. The king asked the countryfolk.
132.001. 'Whose are these merits?' They said: 'Your Majesty's and ours.'
132.002. Then those people began to spin that cotton into thread.
132.003. The king said: 'What are these people doing?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, there is a need for thread.'
132.004. Then the king said: 'In my kingdom, people shall spin? Let the sky rain down thread itself!'
132.004. With the very arising of King <s>Māndhāta's</s> thought, the sky rained down thread.
132.005. The king said: 'Whose are these merits?' They replied: 'Your Majesty's and ours.'
132.006. Then in due course they began to weave garments.
132.006. The king said: 'What are these people doing?' The ministers replied: 'Your Majesty, they are weaving garments; there is a need for garments.'
132.008. The king reflected: 'In my kingdom, people shall weave garments? Let the sky rain down garments themselves!'
132.009. With the very arising of King <s>Māndhāta's</s> thought, the sky rained down garments.
132.009. The king said: 'Whose are these merits?' They replied: 'Your Majesty's and ours.'
132.010. Then the king reflected: 'The people do not know the power of my merits.'
132.011. Then King <s>Māndhāta</s> thought:
132.011. 'My <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is prosperous, flourishing, secure, with abundant food, and teeming with a great multitude of people.
132.012. I have the seven treasures, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the householder-treasure, the wife-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh.
132.014. I have a full thousand sons — heroic, valiant, of noble form, crushers of enemy armies.
132.015. Oh, if only a rain of gold would fall in my inner palace for seven days, with not even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> falling outside!'
132.015. With the very arising of King <s>Māndhāta's</s> thought, a rain of gold fell in his inner palace for seven days.
132.016. Not even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> fell outside — such is the personal fruit of merit experienced by a being of great supernatural power, great might, who has performed meritorious deeds and performed wholesome deeds.
132.018. The king said: 'Whose are these merits?' They replied: 'Your Majesty's and ours.'
132.019. Then the king said: 'You have offended, sirs! If you had said from the beginning "They are Your Majesty's merits," I would have rained down jewels over the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
132.020. However, whoever among you desires jewels, let him take as many as he wishes.'

body.text:
132.022. tasya tatra mūrdhātasya rājño mahārājyaṃ kārayataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
132.022. rājño mūrdhātasya divaukaso yakṣaḥ purojavaḥ/
132.023. sa rājñā mūrdhātenoktah--asti kiṃcidanyadvīpe nājñāpitam yadvayamājñāpayema? yataḥ paścāddivaukasenābhihitah--asti deva pūrvavideho nāma dvīpaḥ, ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaḥ/
132.025. svayaṃ nu devo gatvā tamapyājñāpayet/
132.025. atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat--asti me jambudvīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca/
132.027. asti me sapta ratnāni tadyathā cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam/
132.028. pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
132.029. vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam/
132.029. śrūyate atha khalu pūrvavideho nāma dvīpaḥ/
132.030. yannvahaṃ tamapi gatvā samanuśāseyam/
132.030. sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhāta uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ/
132.031. agamadrājā māndhātaḥ pūrvavidehadvīpam/
132.032. pratyaṣṭhādrājā māndhātā pūrvavidehadvīpe/
132.032. samanuviṣṭavān <133>rājā mūrdhātaḥ pūrvavidehaṃ dvīpam/
body.translated_text:
132.022. While King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was thus ruling a great kingdom there, six wheels fell [from heaven].
132.022. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> had a <s>Yakṣa</s> named <s>Divaukasa</s> ('Sky-dweller') as his vanguard.
132.023. The king said to him: 'Is there any other continent not yet under my command that I should bring under my command?' Then <s>Divaukasa</s> replied: 'There is, Your Majesty — the continent called <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, prosperous, flourishing, secure, with abundant food, and teeming with a great multitude of people.
132.025. Your Majesty might go there himself and bring it under his command.'
132.025. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> thought: 'My <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is prosperous, flourishing, secure, with abundant food, and teeming with a great multitude of people.
132.027. I have the seven treasures, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the wife-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh.
132.028. I have a full thousand sons — heroic, valiant, of noble form, crushers of enemy armies.
132.029. A rain of gold has fallen in my inner palace for seven days.
132.029. And now I hear there is a continent called <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.
132.030. Let me go and govern it also.'
132.030. With the very arising of his thought, King <s>Māndhāta</s> rose up into the sky, together with eighteen <s>koṭis</s> (one hundred and eighty million) of soldiers and warriors, surrounded by a thousand sons, with the seven treasures as his vanguard.
132.031. King <s>Māndhāta</s> went to the continent of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.
132.032. King <s>Māndhāta</s> established himself in <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.
132.032. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> governed the continent of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>.

body.text:
133.001. tasya tatra samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
133.001. bhūyaḥ sa rājā divaukasam yakṣamāmantrayati--asti divaukasaṃ kiṃcidanyadvīpe nājñāpitam? divaukasa āha--asti deva aparagodānīyaṃ nāma dvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
133.004. yannu devastamapi gatvā samanuśāset/
133.004. atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat--asti me jambudīpa ṛddhaśca sphītaśca kṣemaśca subhikṣaśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaśca/
133.005. santi ca me sapta ratnāni/
133.005. pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
133.006. vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam yathāpi tanmaharddhikasya sattvasya mahānubhāvasya kṛtakuśalasya svapuṇyaphalaṃ pratyanubhavataḥ/
133.008. śrūyate aparagodānīyaṃ nāma dvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
133.009. yannvahaṃ tamapi gatvā samanuśāseyam/
133.009. sahacittopādādeva rājā māndhātā uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ/
133.011. agamadrājā māndhātā aparagodānīyaṃ dvīpam/
133.011. anuśāsti rājā māndhātā aparagodānīyam/
133.012. tasya samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
133.012. yataḥ sa rājā māndhātā divaukasam yakṣaṃ pṛcchati--asti kaścidanyadvīpo nājñāpitah? āgato 'smi pūrvān/
133.013. asti deva uttarakurur nāma dvīpaḥ/
133.014. kiṃ cāpi te manuṣyā amamā aparigrahāḥ/
133.014. yannu devo gatvā svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāset/
133.015. atha rājño māndhātasyaitadabhavat--asti me jambudvīpam ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
133.016. santi me sapta ratnāni/
133.016. pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
133.017. vṛṣṭameva saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam/
133.018. śrūyate uttarakurur nāma dvīpaḥ/
133.018. kiṃcāpi te manuṣyā amamā aparigrahāḥ/
133.018. yannvahaṃ tatrāpi gatvā svaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāseyam/
133.019. sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhātā sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ saptaratnapurojava uparivihāyasenābhyudgataḥ/
133.020. adrākṣidrājā māndhātaḥ sumerupārśvenānuyāyaṃś citropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān/
133.021. dṛṣṭvā ca punardivaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate sma--kimetaddivaukasa citropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān/
133.022. ete deva uttarakauravāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ kalpadūṣyavṛkṣāḥ, yata uttarakauravā manuṣyāḥ kalpadūṣyāṇi prāvṛṇvanti/
133.024. devo 'pyatraiva gatvā kalpadūṣyāni prāvarītu/
133.024. śrutvā ca punā rājā māndhātā amātyānāmantrayate--paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaścitropacitrān vṛkṣānāpīḍakajātān? evaṃ deva/
133.026. ete grāmaṇya uttarakauravāṇāṃ mānuṣyāṇāṃ kalpadūṣyavṛkṣā yata uttarakauravā manuṣyāḥ kalpadūṣyāṇi prāvaranti/
133.027. yūyamapyatra gatvā kalpadūṣyayugāni prāvaradhvam/
133.027. adrākṣīdrājā māndhātā sumerupārśvenānuyāyañ śvetaśvetaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam? etaddeva uttarakauravakāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāmakṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśālim yata uttarakauravakā manuṣyā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ paribhuñjanti/
133.030. devo 'pyatra gatvā akṛṣṭoptaṃ taṇḍulaphalaśāliṃ paribhuñjatu/
133.031. agamadrājā māndhātā uttarakurudvīpam/
133.032. pratyaṣṭādrājā māndhātā uttarakurau dvīpe/
133.032. samanuśāsti rājā māndhātā uttarakurau dvīpe svakam <134>bhaṭabalāgram/
body.translated_text:
133.001. As he was governing there, six <s>cakras</s> (wheels/discuses) fell.
133.001. Again, that king addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'Is there, <s>Divaukasa</s>, any other continent that has not been governed?' <s>Divaukasa</s> said: 'There is, Your Majesty, a continent called <s>Aparagodānīya</s> — prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
133.004. May Your Majesty go there and govern it.'
133.004. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> thought: 'I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
133.005. I have the Seven Treasures.
133.005. My full thousand sons are heroes, valiant, of excellent form, and crushers of enemy armies.
133.006. For seven days, gold rained in my inner palace — as befits a being of great power and great might, meritorious, experiencing the fruit of his own merit.
133.008. I have heard that the continent called <s>Aparagodānīya</s> is prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
133.009. Let me go there and govern it.'
133.009. With the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s> rose up into the sky, together with eighteen <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of elite soldiers, surrounded by a thousand sons, with the Seven Treasures leading the way.
133.011. King <s>Māndhātā</s> went to the continent of <s>Aparagodānīya</s>.
133.011. King <s>Māndhātā</s> governs <s>Aparagodānīya</s>.
133.012. As he was governing there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
133.012. Whereupon King <s>Māndhātā</s> asks the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'Is there any other continent that has not been governed? I have come from the east.'
133.013. 'There is, Your Majesty, a continent called <s>Uttarakuru</s>.
133.014. But the people there are without possessiveness and without attachment.
133.014. May Your Majesty go there and govern his own elite soldiers.'
133.015. Then King <s>Māndhātā</s> thought: 'I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
133.016. I have the Seven Treasures.
133.016. My full thousand sons are heroes, valiant, of excellent form, and crushers of enemy armies.
133.017. For seven days, gold rained in my inner palace.
133.018. I have heard that the continent called <s>Uttarakuru</s> exists.
133.018. And the people there are without possessiveness and without attachment.
133.018. Let me go there and govern my own elite soldiers.'
133.019. With the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s>, together with eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of elite soldiers, surrounded by a thousand sons, with the Seven Treasures leading the way, rose up into the sky.
133.020. King <s>Māndhātā</s> saw, while traveling along the side of <s>Sumeru</s>, marvelously colorful trees growing in rows.
133.021. Having seen them, he addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'What are these, <s>Divaukasa</s> — these marvelously colorful trees growing in rows?'
133.022. 'These, Your Majesty, are the wish-fulfilling garment trees of the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, from which the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s> take <s>kalpa</s>-garments (garments of the cosmic age) to wear.
133.024. May Your Majesty also go there and put on <s>kalpa</s>-garments.'
133.024. Having heard this, King <s>Māndhātā</s> addressed his ministers: 'Do you see, ministers, these marvelously colorful trees growing in rows?' 'Yes, Your Majesty.'
133.026. 'These, ministers, are the wish-fulfilling garment trees of the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, from which the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s> take <s>kalpa</s>-garments to wear.
133.027. You too should go there and put on pairs of <s>kalpa</s>-garments.'
133.027. King <s>Māndhātā</s> saw, while traveling along the side of <s>Sumeru</s>, a white-white tract of earth. 'This, Your Majesty, is the self-grown rice of the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, bearing grain without cultivation, from which the people of <s>Uttarakuru</s> eat self-grown rice bearing grain without cultivation.
133.030. May Your Majesty also go there and eat the self-grown rice bearing grain without cultivation.'
133.031. King <s>Māndhātā</s> went to the continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.
133.032. King <s>Māndhātā</s> halted at the continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.
133.032. King <s>Māndhātā</s> governs his own <134>elite soldiers at the continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s>.

body.text:
134.001. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.001. atha rājā māndhātā divaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate--asti kiṃcidanyadvīpamanājñāpitamiti? nāsti deva/
134.002. śrūyante devāstrāyastriṃśā dīrghāyuṣo varṇavantaḥ sukhabahulā ucceṣu vimāneṣu cirasthitikāḥ/
134.003. yannu devo devāṃstrāyastriṃśān darśanāyopasaṃkramet/
134.004. atha rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavat--asti me jambudvīpam, ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
134.005. asti me sapta ratnāni/
134.006. pūrṇaṃ ca me sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
134.006. vṛṣṭaṃ me saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣam/
134.007. samanuśiṣṭo me aparagodānīyo dvīpaḥ/
134.008. samanuśiṣṭaṃ me uttarakurudvīpe svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgram/
134.008. śrūyante devāstrāyaṃstriśā dīrghāyuṣo varṇavantaḥ sukhabahulā ucceṣu vimāneṣu cirasthitikāḥ/
134.009. yannvahaṃ devāṃstrāyāstriṃśān darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam/
134.010. sahacittotpādādeva rājā māndhātā uparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ sārdhamaṣṭādaśabhirbhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ saptaratnapurojavaḥ putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ/
134.011. sumeruḥ parvatarājā saptakāñcanaparvataparivṛtaḥ/
134.012. atha rājā nimiṃdhare parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.012. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.013. nimiṃdharāt parvatāt vinatake parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.013. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.014. vinatakāt parvatādaśvakarṇagirau parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.015. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.015. aśvakarṇagirerapi parvatāt sudarśane parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.016. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.017. sudarśanāt parvatāt khadirake parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.017. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.018. khadirakāt parvatādīṣādhāre parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.018. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.019. īṣāadhārāt parvatādyugaṃdhare parvate pratyaṣṭhāt kāñcanamaye/
134.020. tasya tatra svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ samanuśāsataḥ ṣaṭ cakrāścyutāḥ/
134.021. yugaṃdharāt parvatāduparivihāyasamabhyudgataḥ/
134.021. tatra sumerupariṣaṇḍāyāṃ pañca ṛṣiśatāni dhyāpayanti/
134.021. taiḥ sa rājā dṛṣṭa āgacchan/
134.022. te kathayanti--ayamasau bhavantaḥ kalirājā āgacchati/
134.022. tatra durmukho nāma ṛṣiḥ/
134.023. tena gṛhyodakasyāñjaliḥ kṣiptaḥ/
134.023. viṣkambhitaṃ bhaṭabalāgram/
134.023. tasya cāgrataḥ pariṇāyakaratnamanuyāti/
134.024. tena ṛṣayo 'bhihitāh--
134.025. gacchatha brāhmaṇyako 'yaṃ naitat sarvatra sidhyati/
134.026. mūrdhātā nṛpatirhyeṣo naite vaiśālikā bakāḥ//3//
body.translated_text:
134.001. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.001. Then King <s>Māndhātā</s> addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'Is there any other continent that has not been governed?' 'There is not, Your Majesty.'
134.002. 'I have heard that the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods are long-lived, beautiful, rich in happiness, and dwell for a long time in lofty palaces.
134.003. Let me go and visit the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.'
134.004. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> thought: 'I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
134.005. I have the Seven Treasures.
134.006. My full thousand sons are heroes, valiant, of excellent form, and crushers of enemy armies.
134.006. For seven days, gold rained in my inner palace.
134.007. The continent of <s>Aparagodānīya</s> has been governed by me.
134.008. My own elite soldiers at the continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s> have been governed by me.
134.008. I have heard that the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are long-lived, beautiful, rich in happiness, and dwell for a long time in lofty palaces.
134.009. Let me go and visit the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.'
134.010. With the very arising of that thought, King <s>Māndhātā</s> rose up into the sky, together with eighteen <s>koṭis</s> of elite soldiers, with the Seven Treasures leading the way, surrounded by a thousand sons.
134.011. <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, is encircled by seven golden mountains.
134.012. Then the king halted on <s>Nimiṃdhara</s>, the golden mountain.
134.012. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.013. From <s>Nimiṃdhara</s> mountain he halted on <s>Vinataka</s>, the golden mountain.
134.013. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.014. From <s>Vinataka</s> mountain he halted on <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s>, the golden mountain.
134.015. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.015. From <s>Aśvakarṇagiri</s> mountain he halted on <s>Sudarśana</s>, the golden mountain.
134.016. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.017. From <s>Sudarśana</s> mountain he halted on <s>Khadiraka</s>, the golden mountain.
134.017. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.018. From <s>Khadiraka</s> mountain he halted on <s>Īṣādhāra</s>, the golden mountain.
134.018. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.019. From <s>Īṣādhāra</s> mountain he halted on <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>, the golden mountain.
134.020. As he was governing his own elite soldiers there, six <s>cakras</s> fell.
134.021. From <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> mountain he rose up into the sky.
134.021. There, on the plateau of <s>Sumeru</s>, five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) were seated in meditation.
134.021. They saw that king approaching.
134.022. They said: 'Good sirs, that king of strife is approaching.'
134.022. Among them was a <s>ṛṣi</s> named <s>Durmukha</s>.
134.023. He cast a handful of water.
134.023. The elite army was brought to a halt.
134.023. Before him, the <s>Pariṇāyakaratna</s> (the Jewel Minister) was following.
134.024. He addressed the <s>ṛṣis</s>:
134.025. 'Go away, this man is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; this does not work everywhere.
134.026. This is King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>; these are not the cranes of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.' //3//

body.text:
134.027. atha rājā tasmiñ śāsane 'bhyāgataḥ kathayati--kenaitadviṣkambhitaṃ bhaṭabalāgram? tenoktam--ṛṣibhirdeva taṃ bhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam/
134.028. paścād rājñā abhihitam--kimeṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ sarvaṃ priyamiti? pariṇāyakaratnenoktam--jaṭā ṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣṭāḥ/
134.029. tato rājñā abhihitam--ṛṣīṇāṃ jaṭāḥ śīryantām, mama ca bhaṭabalāgraṃ vihāyasā gacchatu/
134.030. teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ jaṭāḥ śīrṇāḥ, rājñaśca mūrdhātasya bhaṭabalāgraṃ vihāyasena prasthitam/
134.031. sumeruḥ parvatarājā aśītiyojanasahasrāṇyadhastāt kāñcanamayyāṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhito 'śītiyojanasahasrāṇyudakādabhyudgata<135> ūrdhvamadhaśca ṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasraṃ pārśvaṃ pārśvamaṣītiyojanasahasarāṇi tadbhavati samantaparikṣepeṇa viṃśatyadhikāni trīṇi yojanaśatasahasrāṇi/
body.translated_text:
134.027. Then the king, arriving at that obstructed place, said: 'Who has halted the elite army?' He was told: 'The <s>ṛṣis</s>, Your Majesty, have halted that elite army.'
134.028. Then the king said: 'What is dear to these <s>ṛṣis</s> above all else?' The <s>Pariṇāyakaratna</s> (Jewel Minister) said: 'Their matted locks are the most prized possession of all <s>ṛṣis</s>.'
134.029. Then the king said: 'Let the matted locks of the <s>ṛṣis</s> fall off, and let my elite army proceed through the sky.'
134.030. The matted locks of those <s>ṛṣis</s> fell off, and King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>'s elite army proceeded through the sky.
134.031. <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, extends eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) below, established on a golden base, and eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> above the water <135>— above and below a total of one hundred and sixty thousand <s>yojanas</s>, eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> on each side, making a total circumference of three hundred and twenty thousand <s>yojanas</s>.

body.text:
135.002. abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaścatūratnamayaḥ/
135.003. tasya mūrdhni devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma nagaram/
135.003. devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ pañca rakṣāḥ sthāpitāh--udakaniśritā nāgāḥ, karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ, mālādhārā devāḥ, sadāmattā devāḥ, catvāraśca mahārājānaḥ/
135.005. tasya rājño mūrdhātasyodakaniśritair nāgairbalakāyo viṣkambhitaḥ/
135.006. rājā ca mūrdhātastatsthānamāgataḥ/
135.006. tenoktam--kenaitadbhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam? te kathayanti--deva, udakaniśritair nāgaiḥ/
135.007. rājā kathayati--tiryañco mama yudhyanti? tena hyudakaniśritā eva me nāgāḥ purojavā bhavantu/
135.008. tataste nāgā rājño mūrdhātasyāgrato 'nuyāyino jātāḥ/
135.009. teṣāṃ nāgānāmanusamyāyatāṃ karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ saṃprāptāḥ/
135.009. yato nāgaistaiḥ karoṭapāṇibhirdevaiḥ sārdhaṃ miśribhāvaṃ gatvā punastadbalāgraṃ stambhitam/
135.010. rājñā mūrdhātenoktam--kenaitadbhaṭabalāgraṃ stambhitam? te kathayanti--deva, ete karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ/
135.011. etairbhaṭabalāgraṃ stambhitam/
135.012. rājā mūdhātaḥ kathayati--ete 'pyeva me karoṭapāṇayo devāḥ purojavā bhavantu/
135.012. yataste 'grataḥ pradhāvitāḥ/
135.013. paścāt teṣāṃ nāgaiḥ sārdhaṃ dhāvatāṃ mālādhārā devāḥ saṃprāptāḥ/
135.013. mālādhārairdevaiste pṛṣṭāh--kiṃ bhavanto dhāvatah? te kathayanti--eṣa manuṣyarājā āgacchati/
135.014. yatastaiḥ smabhūya nāgairdevaiśca punastadbalāgraṃ stambhitam/
135.015. rājā ca māndhātastatsthānamanuprāptaḥ/
135.015. tenoktam--kimetadbhavantah? te kathayanti--deva, mālādhārairdevaiḥ/
135.016. rājā kathayati--mālādhārā devāḥ purojavā me bhavantu/
135.017. yato mālādhārā devāstair nāgairdevaiśca sārdhaṃ mūrdhātasyāgrataḥ pradhāvitāḥ/
135.018. teṣāṃ dhāvatāṃ sadāmattakā devāḥ saṃprāptāḥ/
135.018. sadāmattairdevaiḥ pṛṣṭāh--kiṃ bhavanto dhāvatah? tair nāgaiḥ karoṭapāṇyādibhiśca devairabhihitāh--eṣa manuṣyarājā āgacchati/
135.019. yato bhūyaḥ sadāmattairdevaiḥ karoṭapāṇyādibhiśca devair nāgaiḥ sārdhaṃ miśrībhāvaṃ kṛtvā bhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam/
135.020. rājā ca mūrdhātastatsthānamanuprāptaḥ/
135.021. tenoktam--kimetadbhaṭabalāgraṃ viṣkambhitam? te kathayanti--ete deva sadāmattā devāḥ/

135.023. teṣāṃ dhāvatāṃ cātrumahārājikā devāḥ saṃprāptāḥ/

135.032. devo 'pyatra gatvā divyaih <136>pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūtas trīḍatu ramatāṃ paricārayatu/
body.translated_text: He was handsome, good-looking, pleasing, and made of the four [precious] substances. On its summit was the city named <s>Sudarśana</s> of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods had five guards stationed: the water-dwelling <s>Nāgas</s>, the skull-handed gods (<s>Karoṭapāṇi</s>), the garland-bearing gods (<s>Mālādhāra</s>), the ever-intoxicated gods (<s>Sadāmatta</s>), and the Four Great Kings. The army vanguard of King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was blocked by the water-dwelling <s>Nāgas</s>. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> arrived at that place. He said: 'By whom has this front of the warrior host been blocked?' They replied: 'By the water-dwelling <s>Nāgas</s>, O lord.' The king said: 'Animals fight against me? Then let those very water-dwelling <s>Nāgas</s> become my vanguard.' So those <s>Nāgas</s> became the advance guard marching before King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>. As those <s>Nāgas</s> were marching along, the skull-handed gods arrived. The <s>Nāgas</s>, having joined together with the skull-handed gods, again blocked the army vanguard. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said: 'By whom has this front of the warrior host been blocked?' They replied: 'By these skull-handed gods, O lord. They have blocked the army vanguard.' King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said: 'Let these very skull-handed gods also become my vanguard.' So they ran ahead of him. Afterwards, as they ran along with the <s>Nāgas</s>, the garland-bearing gods arrived. The garland-bearing gods asked them: 'Why are you running, sirs?' They replied: 'A human king is coming.' So those, having joined together — the <s>Nāgas</s> and gods — again blocked the army vanguard. King <s>Māndhāta</s> arrived at that place. He said: 'What is this, sirs?' They replied: 'By the garland-bearing gods, O lord.' The king said: 'Let the garland-bearing gods also become my vanguard.' So the garland-bearing gods, together with the <s>Nāgas</s> and gods, ran ahead of <s>Mūrdhāta</s>. As they ran, the ever-intoxicated gods arrived. The ever-intoxicated gods asked: 'Why are you running, sirs?' The <s>Nāgas</s> and the skull-handed and other gods replied: 'A human king is coming.' So the ever-intoxicated gods, together with the skull-handed and other gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, having joined together, blocked the army vanguard. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> arrived at that place. He said: 'By whom has this army vanguard been blocked?' They replied: 'By these ever-intoxicated gods, O lord.' The king said: 'Let the ever-intoxicated gods also become my vanguard.' So the ever-intoxicated gods, together with the other gods and <s>Nāgas</s>, ran ahead. As they ran, the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods arrived. They said: 'Why are you running, sirs?' The <s>Nāgas</s> and other gods who were the advance guard replied: 'A human king is coming.' The Four Great Kings reflected: 'This is a being of great merit and great power. It is not possible to oppose him.' Then those Four Great Kings informed the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: 'Sirs, the human king <s>Mūrdhāta</s> is coming.' The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods reflected: 'This is a being of great merit and great power. He must not be opposed. Let us go forth to welcome him with gifts of honor.' So the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods went forth to welcome him with gifts of honor. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, while ascending the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, saw a dark blue line of forest, rising high like a bank of clouds. Having seen it, he addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> attendant <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'What is this, <s>Divaukasa</s>, this dark blue line of forest rising high like a bank of clouds?' 'This, O lord, is the <s>Pārijātaka</s> <s>Kovidāra</s> tree of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, under which the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods sport, delight, and enjoy themselves for four months of the rainy season, endowed with the five strands of divine sensual pleasure. May the lord too go there and, endowed with the five strands of divine sensual pleasure, sport, delight, and enjoy himself.'

136.001. śrutvā ca punā rājā mūrdhāto 'mātyānāmantrayate--paśyatha yūyaṃ nīlanīlāṃ vanarājiṃ megharājimivonnatām? evaṃ deva/

136.007. dṛṣṭvā ca punardivaukasam yakṣamāmantrayate--kimetaddivaukasa śvetaśvetamabhrakūṭamivonnatam? eṣā deva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudharmā nāma devasabhā, yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścatvāraśca mahārājānaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cārthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca cintayanti tulayanti upaparīkṣyanti/
136.010. devo 'pyatra gamiṣyatu/
136.010. śrutvā ca punaramātyānāmantrayate--paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ śvetaśvetamabhrakūṭamivonnatam? evaṃ deva/
136.011. eṣā trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudharmā nāma devasabhā yatra devāstrāyastriṃśāścatvāraśca mahārājānaḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ saṃnipatitā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cārthaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca cintayanti tulayanti upaparīkṣyanti/

136.014. devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma nagaramardhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇyāyāmena ardhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇi vistareṇa samantataḥ parikṣepeṇa daśayojanasahasrāṇi saptabhiḥ kāñcanamayaiḥ prākāraiḥ parikṣiptam/
136.016. te prākārā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanānyucchrayeṇa/
136.016. teṣu prākāreṣu caturvidhāḥ ṣo(kho)ḍakā māpitāḥ suvarṇamayā rūpyamayā vaiḍūryamayā sphaṭikamayāḥ/
136.018. ūrdhvī ekā nibaddhā saṃkramaṇakā/
136.018. sudarśananagare 'bhyantare bhūmibhāgo 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaścitraḥ sucitra ekaikacitradhātuśatena mṛduḥ sumṛdus tadyathā tulapicurvā/

136.022. dvāre dvāre pañcaśatāni nīlavāsasām yakṣāṇāṃ sthāpitāni saṃnaddhāni santi citrakalāpāni yāvadeva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmārakṣaṇārthamatyarthaṃ śobhanārtham/
136.024. sudarśanasya nagarasya vīthyah ardhatṛtīyāni yojanasahasrāṇyāyāmena vistareṇa dvādaśa yojanānyabhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāḥ kanakavālukāstīrṇāścandanavāripariṣiktā hemajālāvanaddhāḥ/

136.026. tā puṣkariṇyaścaturvidhairiṣṭakaiścitāḥ suvarṇamayai rūpyamayaiḥ sphaṭikamayairvaiḍūryamayaiḥ/

136.030. sāmantake vividhāḥ puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛkṣāḥ sujātāḥ susaṃsthitā āpīḍakajātāḥ, tadyathā dakṣeṇa mālākāreṇa vā mālākārāntevāsinā vā mālā vā agrasthitāvataṃsakāni vā suracitāni/
136.032. vividhaiḥ sthalajaiḥ śakunakairvalgusvarairmanojñasvaraih <137>kāmarūpibhirabhinikūjitāḥ/
body.translated_text: Having heard this, King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> addressed his ministers: 'Do you see this dark blue line of forest rising high like a bank of clouds?' 'Yes, O lord.' 'This is the <s>Pārijātaka</s> <s>Kovidāra</s> tree of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, under which the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods sport, delight, and enjoy themselves for four months of the rainy season, endowed with the five strands of divine sensual pleasure. You too, good sirs, go there and, endowed with the five strands of divine sensual pleasure, sport, delight, and enjoy yourselves.' King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>, while ascending the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, saw a pure white mass rising high like a peak of clouds. Having seen it, he addressed the <s>Yakṣa</s> attendant <s>Divaukasa</s>: 'What is this, <s>Divaukasa</s>, this pure white mass rising high like a peak of clouds?' 'This, O lord, is the divine assembly hall named <s>Sudharmā</s> of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and the Four Great Kings, having assembled and gathered, deliberate, weigh, and examine matters concerning both gods and humans. May the lord too go there.' Having heard this, he addressed his ministers: 'Do you see, good sirs, this pure white mass rising high like a peak of clouds?' 'Yes, O lord.' 'This is the divine assembly hall named <s>Sudharmā</s> of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, where the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and the Four Great Kings, having assembled and gathered, deliberate, weigh, and examine matters concerning both gods and humans. You too, good sirs, shall go there.' The city named <s>Sudarśana</s> of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods is two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length, two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in width, and ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in circumference, surrounded by seven golden ramparts. Those ramparts are two and a half <s>yojanas</s> in height. In those ramparts, four kinds of archways are constructed — of gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and crystal. Above is a single stairway bridge. Inside the city of <s>Sudarśana</s>, the ground is handsome, good-looking, pleasing, variegated and beautifully painted with hundreds of different pigments, soft and extremely soft, like cotton wool or cotton fiber. When a foot is set down, it sinks; when a foot is lifted, it rises. It is strewn knee-deep with divine <s>mandāra</s> flowers. By contact with the wind, the old flowers are blown away and new flowers spread forth. In the city of <s>Sudarśana</s> there are nine hundred and ninety-nine gates. At each gate, five hundred blue-clad <s>Yakṣas</s> are stationed, armed, with quivers of many colors — solely for the protection of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and for great adornment. The streets of the city of <s>Sudarśana</s> are two and a half thousand <s>yojanas</s> in length and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in width, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, strewn with golden sand, sprinkled with sandalwood water, covered with golden nets. On all sides, various lotus ponds have been constructed. Those lotus ponds are lined with four kinds of bricks — of gold, silver, crystal, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>. The railing has crystal needles, balustrades, and platforms. The crystal [railing] has <s>vaiḍūrya</s> needles, balustrades, and platforms. Those lotus ponds are filled with cool water, with water sweet as honey, covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, night-lotuses, and white lotuses, resounding with various aquatic birds of sweet and delightful voices, of wondrous forms. On all sides, various flowering and fruiting trees grow, well-grown, well-formed, growing in rows — as if arranged by a skillful garland-maker or his apprentice, like garlands or head-ornaments beautifully fashioned. They resound with various land-birds of sweet and delightful voices, of wondrous forms.

137.014. tatra devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmāsanāni prajñaptāni, yatra pṛthak dvātriṃśatīnāmupendrāṇāmāsanāni, trayastriṃśatimaṃ śakrasya devānāmindrasya/

137.032. paścādrājā mūrdhāto nirgatastasmādevanagarāt <138>teṣāṃ devānāmasurairbhagnakānāṃ svaṃ ca kāyaṃ saṃnahya/
body.translated_text:
137.001. In the city of <s>Sudarśana</s> there are four kinds of wish-fulfilling garment trees — blue, yellow, red, and white.
137.002. From the wish-fulfilling garment trees come four kinds of cloth-wrappings.
137.002. From those cloth-wrappings come four kinds of wish-fulfilling garments — blue, yellow, red, and white.
137.003. Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, with the very arising of the thought it appears in their hand.
137.004. There are four kinds of ornament trees — ornaments for the hands, for the feet, concealed ornaments, and displayed ornaments.
137.005. Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, with the very arising of the thought it appears in their hand.
137.006. There are four kinds of musical instrument trees — flutes, vines, and melodious ones.
137.006. Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, with the very arising of the thought it appears in their hand.
137.007. There are also four kinds of ambrosia — blue, yellow, red, and white.
137.008. Whatever a god or divine maiden desires, with the very arising of the thought it appears in their hand.
137.008. Honey, <s>Mādhava</s> wine, <s>Kādambarī</s> liquor, and <s>Pāripāna</s> drink.
137.009. There are houses, gabled mansions, terraced buildings, palaces, resting places, viewing galleries, and promenades.
137.010. Adorned by troupes of celestial women, attended by thousands of <s>Apsarases</s>, resounding with the sound of musical instruments, provided with food and drink —
137.010. there the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods play, delight, and enjoy themselves, experiencing the fruit of their own merit.
137.011. The <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods is three hundred <s>yojanas</s> in length, three hundred <s>yojanas</s> in breadth, nine hundred <s>yojanas</s> in circumference, beautiful, pleasing, lovely, made of crystal, rising four and a half <s>yojanas</s> above the city.
137.014. There the seats of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are prepared — separate seats for the thirty-two sub-<s>Indras</s>, and the thirty-third for <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods.
137.015. At the very end among those gods, a seat was prepared for King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.
137.016. Afterwards, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods came forth bearing welcome-offerings for King <s>M��rdhāta</s>.
137.017. Those beings renowned for the greatness of their merit entered in due order; the rest remained standing outside.
137.017. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> reflected: 'Of these prepared seats, the one at the very end — that shall be mine.'
137.019. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> thought: 'Oh, if only <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, would invite me to share his half-seat!'
137.020. With the very arising of his thought, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, gave half his seat to King <s>Māndhāta</s>.
137.021. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> entered upon the half-seat of <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods.
137.021. When King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, were seated on the same seat, there was no difference whatever between them — neither in height or girth, nor in the excellence of complexion, nor in the modulation of voice — except only that <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, did not blink.
137.024. While King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> dwelt among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, thirty-six wheels fell [from heaven].
137.024. And there a war between gods and <s>Asuras</s> took place.
137.025. When the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated, they would bar the gates of the <s>Asura</s> city.
137.025. When the five guardians of the gods were defeated,
137.026. they too would bar the gates of the city of the gods.
137.026. Thus, among those gods and <s>Asuras</s>, a state of mutual alarm arose.
137.027. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods: 'What is this? Why are you gods so extremely alarmed?' The <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods said: 'Our five guardians have been broken by these <s>Asuras</s>, and therefore we have barred the gates.'
137.029. King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said: 'My men! Let them bring the bow.'
137.029. The bow was brought to him.
137.030. He then took the bow and twanged the bowstring.
137.030. The sound of that bowstring
137.031. was heard by the <s>Asuras</s>.
137.031. Having heard it, the <s>Asuras</s> said: 'Whose is this sound of the bowstring?' They heard: 'This is the sound of King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> bowstring.'
137.032. Having heard that sound, they were struck with amazement.
137.032. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> went forth from that divine city, and having armored his own body for those gods whose guardians had been broken by the <s>Asuras</s>,

body.text:
138.001. dharmatā ca punareṣāṃ devāsurāṇām yudhyatāṃ rathā vaihāyasena tiṣṭhanti/
138.002. teṣāmanyonyaṃ na kasyacidadhiko vā hīno vā/
138.002. rājño mūrdhātasya sarveṣāmapyasurāṇāṃ vaihāyasamabhyudgamyoparisthitaḥ/
138.003. paścāt te 'surāḥ kathayanti--ka eṣo 'smākamuparivihāyasamabhyudgatah? yatastaiḥ śrutam--manuṣyarājā eṣa mūrdhāto nāma/
138.004. paścāt te saṃlakṣayanti--puṇyavipākamaheśākhyo 'yaṃ sattvo yasyāsmākamuparivaihāyasaṃ ratho gacchati/
138.005. jitā bhagnāḥ parājitāḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtā āsurīṃ purīṃ praviṣṭāḥ/
138.006. paścādrājā mūrdhātaḥ kathayati--kasya jayah? yato 'mātyāḥ kathayanti devasya jayaḥ/
138.007. sa rājā saṃlakṣayati--ahameva devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sakāśādabhyadhikaḥ/
138.008. tasya rājño mūrdhātasyaitadabhavati--etadasti me jambudvīpaḥ, asti me sapta ratnāni, asti me sahasraṃ putrāṇām, vṛṣṭaṃ me 'ntaḥpure saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣam, samanuśiṣṭaṃ me pūrvahideham, samanuśiṣṭaṃ me 'paragodānīyaṃ dvīpam, samanuśiṣṭaṃ me uttarakuruṣu svakaṃ bhaṭabalāgram, adhiṣṭhitaṃ me 'sti devāṃstrāyastriṃśān, praviṣṭo 'smi sudharmāṃ devasabhām, dattaṃ me śakreṇa devendreṇārdhasanam/
138.012. aho batāhaṃ śakraṃ devānāmindramasmāt sthānāccyāvayitvā svayameva devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayeyam/
138.013. sahacittotpādādrājā mūrdhātastasmāt ṛddhitaḥ paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpeṣu pratyaṣṭhāt/
138.014. svaramābādhaṃ spṛṣṭavān/
138.014. pragāḍhāṃ devānāṃ maraṇāntikīm/
138.014. atha rājño mūrdhātasyāmātyagaṇamahāmātyā rājyakartāro mantrasahajīvino yena rājā mūrdhātastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
138.016. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ mūrdhātamidamavocan--bhaviṣyanti khalu devasyātyayāt paścimā janapadāh? paripṛṣṭavantah--rājñā mūrdhātena maraṇasamaye kiṃ vyākṛtam? saced vo grāmṇyo mamātyayāt kaścidupasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet--kiṃ bhavanto rājñā mūrdhātena maraṇasamaye vyākṛtam, teṣāmidaṃ syādvacanīyām--rājā bhavanto mūrdhāto ratnaiḥ samanvāgato 'bhūt/
138.019. catasṛbhiśca mānuṣikābhī ṛddhibhiścaturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayitvā devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍhaḥ/
138.021. atṛpta eva pañcānāṃ kāmaguṇānāṃ kālagataḥ/
138.022. na kārṣāpaṇavarṣeṇa tṛptiḥ kāmeṣu vidyate/
138.023. alpāsvādān bahuduḥkhān kāmān vijñāya piṇḍataḥ//4//
body.translated_text:
138.001. It is the nature that when those gods and <s>Asuras</s> are fighting, their chariots stand in the sky.
138.002. Neither side is superior or inferior to the other.
138.002. King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> [chariot] rose above all the <s>Asuras</s> in the sky and stood above them.
138.003. The <s>Asuras</s> said: 'Who is this that has risen above us in the sky?' They heard: 'This is a human king named <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.'
138.004. Then they reflected: 'This being is renowned for the greatness of his merit-fruition, whose chariot goes above us in the sky.'
138.005. They were conquered, broken, defeated, and put to rout; they entered the <s>Asura</s> city.
138.006. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> said: 'Whose is the victory?' The ministers said: 'The victory is Your Majesty's.'
138.007. The king reflected: 'I am indeed superior even to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.'
138.008. Then King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> thought: 'I have <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; I have the seven treasures; I have a thousand sons; a rain of gold fell in my inner palace for seven days; I have governed <s>Pūrvavideha</s>; I have governed <s>Aparagodānīya</s>; I have established my own army in <s>Uttarakuru</s>; I have ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods; I have entered the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall; <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, has given me half his seat.
138.012. Oh, if only I could dislodge <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, from his position and myself exercise sovereign rule over both gods and humans!'
138.013. With the very arising of that thought, King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> fell from that supernatural power and landed on <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
138.014. His body was afflicted by illness —
138.014. a severe, death-dealing divine affliction.
138.014. Then the ministers, great ministers, royal administrators, and counselors who shared King <s>Mūrdhāta's</s> life approached King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.
138.016. Having approached, they said this to King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>: 'After Your Majesty's passing, will there be final instructions for the people of the realm?' They asked: 'What has King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> declared at the time of death?' 'If any villager should come to you after my passing and ask: "What did King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> declare at the time of death?" — to them this should be said: "Sirs, King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was endowed with treasures.
138.019. Having exercised sovereign rule over the four continents with four kinds of human supernatural powers, he ascended to the <s>Trāyastri���śa</s> gods.
138.021. Yet unsatisfied in the five strands of sensual pleasure, he died.
138.022. Not even by a rain of <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> is there satisfaction in sensual pleasures.
138.023. Know that sensual pleasures are of little sweetness and of much suffering!"' // 4 //

body.text:
138.024. api divyeṣu kāmeṣu ratiṃ naivādhigacchati/
138.025. tṛṣṇākṣaye rato bhavati samyaksambuddhaśrāvakaḥ//5//
body.translated_text:
138.024. 'Even in divine pleasures one finds no delight;
138.025. The disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One delights in the destruction of craving.' // 5 //

body.text:
138.026. parvato 'pi suvarṇasya samo himavatā bhavet/
138.027. nālamekasya tadvittamiti vidvān samācaret//6//
body.translated_text:
138.026. 'Even if there were a mountain of gold equal to the <s>Himavat</s>,
138.027. it would not suffice for the wealth of one person — knowing this, let the wise man conduct himself accordingly.' // 6 //

body.text:
138.028. yaḥ prekṣati duḥkhamitonidānaṃ kāmeṣu jātu sa kathaṃ ramate/
138.030. loke hi śalyamupādhiṃ viditvā tasyaiva dhīro vinayāya śikṣet//7//
body.translated_text:
138.028. 'He who sees that suffering has its source here in sensual desires — how can he ever delight in sensual pleasures?
138.030. Having known attachment to be a thorn in the world, the wise man should train himself in its removal.' // 7 //

body.text:
139.001. <139>yadā ca punastena janakāyena śrutaṃ rājā mūrdhāto glāno maraṇāvasthita iti, tataste 'mātyā janapadāścānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi rājānaṃ mūrdhātamupasaṃkramya darśanāya/
139.002. yatastena rājñā tasya janasya tāvadevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā--kāmeṣvādīnavakathā gṛhāśramapadasyādīnavo bhāṣitaḥ, tathā kāmo jugupsito yathā anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi ṛṣīṇāmantike pravrajya gṛhāśramapadānyapahāya vanaṃ saṃśritāḥ, ṛṣibhiḥ pravrajitvā catvāri brahmavihārān bhāvayitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ prahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokasabhāgatāyāmupapannāḥ/
139.006. yāvacca jambudvīpe yāvacca pūrvavidehe dvīpe yāvaccāparagodānīye dvīpe yāvaccottarakuruṣu yāvacca saptasu kāñcanamayeṣu parvateṣu yāvacca devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍaḥ, atrāntare caturdaśottaraṃ śakraśataṃ cyutam/
139.009. śakrasya bhikṣavo devānāmindrasyāyuṣaḥ prāmāṇam yanmanuṣyāṇāṃ varṣamekaṃ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmekarātriṃdivasam/
139.011ṭena rātriṃdivasena triṃśadrātrakena māsena dvādaśamāsena saṃvatsareṇa divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmāyuṣaḥ pramāṇam/
139.012. tadbhavati mānuṣikayā gaṇanayā tisro varṣalakṣāḥ ṣaṣṭiśca varṣasahasrāṇi//
body.translated_text:
139.001. When the people heard that King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> was ill and at the point of death, those ministers, countryfolk, and many hundreds of thousands of beings approached King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> for a final audience.
139.002. Then the king gave the people a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> of this kind — a discourse on the dangers of sensual pleasures, the danger of the household state. He so reviled sensual pleasures that many hundreds of thousands of beings went forth as renunciants in the company of the sages, abandoning the household state and taking to the forest; and having gone forth under the sages, they cultivated the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), abandoned desire for sensual pleasures, dwelt in those states abundantly, and were reborn in the company of <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
139.006. During the time he reigned over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, <s>Uttarakuru</s>, the seven golden mountains, and having ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods — in that interval, one hundred and fourteen <s>Śakras</s> passed away.
139.009. Monks, the measure of the lifespan of <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, is this: one human year equals one day and night of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
139.011. By such days and nights, thirty nights make a month, twelve months make a year, and a thousand divine years is the measure of the lifespan of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
139.012. That equals, by human reckoning, three hundred thousand and sixty thousand years.

body.text:
139.014. yasminnānanda samaye rājā mūrdhāto devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍhaḥ, evaṃvidhaṃ cittamutpāditam--aho bata me śakro devānāmindro 'rdhāsanenopanimantrayate, kāśyapo bhikṣustena kālena tena samayena śakro devānāmindro babhūva/
139.016. yasmin khalvānanda samaye rājño mūrdhātasyaivaṃvidhaṃ cittamutpannam--yannvahaṃ śakraṃ devānāmindramasmāt sthānāccyāvayitvā svayameva devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayeyam, kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddhastena kālena tena samayena śakro devānāmindro babhūva/
139.019. maheśākhye sattve cittaṃ pradūṣitam, tasmādṛddheḥ paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpe pratyaṣṭhāt, kharamābādhaṃ spṛṣṭavān, prāgāḍhāṃ vedanāṃ maraṇāntikīm/
139.020. yo 'sau rājā mūrdhātaḥ, ahamevānanda tena kālena tena samayena/
139.021. tatra tāvanmayā ānanda sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohena aparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmeṇa maraṇakālasamaye tāvadevaṃvidhā parikathā kṛtā yadanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi gṛhāśramamapahāya ṛṣibhyaḥ pravrajitvā kāmeṣu kāmacchandaṃ vyapahāya tadbahulavihāriṇo brahmalokamupapāditāḥ/
139.024. idānīṃ sarvajñenānuttarajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena nirvāṇāya saṃprasthitena tāvadevaṃvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yadanekāni devatā śatasahasrāṇi satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāni/
139.026. anekāni ṛṣiśatasahasrāṇi etabhikṣava iti pravrajitāni/
139.027. tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhirvyāyacchadbhiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ prāptam/
139.027. anekadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu vyavasthāpitāḥ/
139.028. anekāni vaiśālikāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi yeṣāṃ kecitsrotāpattiphale vyavasthāpitāḥ, kecit sakṛdāgāmiphale, kecidanāgāmiphale, kaiścit pravrajitvā^rhattvaṃ prāptam, kaiścit śrāvakabodhau, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpāditāni, kaiściccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni//

140.001. <140>bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kāni bhadanta karmāṇi kṛtāni rājñā mūrdhātena yeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākena sahacittotpādādeva saptāhamantaḥpure hiraṇyavarṣaṃ vṛṣṭam? bhagavānāha--
140.004. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani sarvābhibhūr nāma tathāgato 'rhaṃl loke utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
140.006. tena khalu samayena anyataraḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'cirapratiṣṭhitaḥ/
140.006. tatra viṣaye dharmatā--yā aciroḍhā dārikā bhartari pravahaṇakena pratipradīyate, sā catūratnamayaiḥ puṣpairavakīrya baddhakā svāmine pradīyate/
140.008. sā ca bhartāramādāya svagṛhaṃ gacchati/
140.008. sa ca śreṣṭhidārakaścatūratnamayāni puṣpāṇi pratigṛhya yānamadhiruhya śvaśuragṛhamanuprasthitaḥ/
140.009. tasya gacchato 'bhimukhaṃ sarvābhibhūḥ samyaksambuddho janapadeṣu caryāṃ carannanupūrveṇābhyāgataḥ/
140.010. taṃ dṛṣṭvā dvātriṃśallakṣaṇālaṃkṛtamasecanakadarśanamatīva prasāda utpannaḥ/
140.011. yato 'sau prasādīkṛtacetā yānādavatīrya taṃ bhagavantaṃ taiścatūratnamayaiḥ puṣpairavakiriti/
140.012. tāni sarvābhibhuvā samyaksambuddhenādhiṣṭhitāni tathā yathā śakaṭacakramātrāṇyabhinirvṛttāni/
140.013. tāni vitānaṃ baddhvā gacchato 'nugacchanti, tiṣṭhatastiṣṭhanti/
140.013. sa prasādajāto gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
140.015. anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ/
