140.017. tīrṇaśca tārayeyaṃ mahājanaughān atāritā ye pūrvakairjinendraiḥ//8//
body.translated_text:
140.001. <140>The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> perform, by the ripening of which gold rained for seven days in his inner palace with the very arising of that thought?' The Blessed One said:
140.004. 'Long ago, monks, in a past era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, named <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.
140.006. At that time, a certain guild-master's son had just been married.
140.006. It was the custom in that land that a newly-wed girl was given to her husband in a wedding carriage, strewn with flowers made of four kinds of jewels, and bound with garlands was given to her lord.
140.008. She, taking her husband, went to her own house.
140.008. And that guild-master's son, having received the flowers made of four kinds of jewels, mounted a vehicle and set out for his father-in-law's house.
140.009. As he was going, the Perfectly Enlightened One <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, wandering on a teaching tour through the provinces, came approaching him face to face.
140.010. Seeing him, adorned with the thirty-two marks, of irresistibly beautiful appearance, an exceedingly great faith arose in him.
140.011. With faith-inspired mind, he descended from his vehicle and scattered those flowers made of four kinds of jewels upon the Blessed One.
140.012. Those flowers were so empowered by the Perfectly Enlightened One <s>Sarvābhibhū</s> that they became as large as cart-wheels.
140.013. They, having formed a canopy, followed him as he walked and stood still when he stood still.
140.013. He, filled with faith, spoke a verse:
140.015. "By this great and lofty gift, may I become a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Self-Arisen One;
140.017. and having crossed over, may I ferry across the great floods of beings who were not ferried across by the former Lords of Victors." //8//

body.text:
140.019. sarvābhibhūrme bhagavān maharṣiravakīrṇaḥ puṣpaiḥ sumanoramaiśca/
140.021. praṇidhiśca me tatra kṛtā udārā ākāṅkṣatā vā idamagrabodhim//9//
body.translated_text:
140.019. 'The Blessed One <s>Sarvābhibhū</s>, the Great Sage, was scattered upon by me with beautiful and lovely flowers;
140.021. and a noble aspiration was made there by me, desiring this supreme awakening.' //9//

body.text:
140.023. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākato me prāpta hi me bodhiḥ śivā anuttarā/
140.025. vṛṣṭaṃ ca saptāhahiraṇyavarṣaṃ mūrdhātasya rājño mahābalasya//10//
body.translated_text:
140.023. 'By the ripening of that very deed, I have attained this auspicious, unsurpassed awakening;
140.025. and gold rained for seven days upon King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> of great power.' //10//

body.text: 140.027. tasyaiva karmaṇo vipākato me nagaramapi sauvarṇakāñcanaṃ babhūva mahāsudarśanasya ramaṇīyā kuśāvatī nāma purī babhūva//
body.translated_text:
140.027. 'By the ripening of that very deed, the city too became of gold,
and the beautiful city named <s>Kuśāvatī</s> of King <s>Mahāsudarśana</s> came into being.' //

body.text: 140.029. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kīdṛśaṃ bhadanta rājñā mūrdhātena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena caturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritam, devāṃstrāyastriṃśānadhirūḍhah? bhagavānāha--
body.translated_text: 140.029. The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What kind of deed, Venerable Sir, did King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> perform, by the ripening of which he exercised sovereign lordship and dominion in the four continents and ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods?' The Blessed One said:

body.text:
141.001. <141>bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vipaśyī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho loke utpannaḥ/
141.002. atha sa vipaśyī samyaksabuddho janapadeṣu caryāṃ caramāṇo 'nupūrveṇa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ/
141.003. atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bandhumatīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśāt/
141.004. tatrānyataraścautkariko nāma vaṇik/
141.004. bhagavantaṃ vipaśyinamasecanakadarśanarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā adhikaḥ prasāda utpannaḥ/
141.005. prasādajātena tasya mudgānāṃ muṣṭiṃ gṛhītvā pātre prakṣiptā/
141.006. tato mudgāścatvāraḥ pātre patitāḥ, ekaḥ kaṇṭakamāhatya bhūmau patitaḥ/
141.006. avaśiṣṭaṃ naivaṃ saṃprāptaṃ pātram, asamprāptā eva bhūmau patitāḥ/
141.007. tato vaṇik prasādajātaḥ praṇidhiṃ karoti--
141.009. anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ/
141.011. tīrṇaśca tārayeyaṃ mahājanaughān na tāritā ye pūrvakairjinendraiḥ//11/
141.013. bhagavānāha--yo 'sau otkariko vaṇik, ahameva tena kālena tena samayena/
141.013. yanmayā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya prasādajātena mudgānāṃ muṣṭiḥ pātre pakṣiptā, tasmāccatvāro mudgāḥ pātre patitā avaśiṣṭā bhūmau patitāḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena caturṣu dvīpeṣu rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritam/
141.016. yaścāsau mudgaḥ pātrakaṇṭakamāhatya bhūmau patitaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena trāyastriṃśān devānadhirūḍaḥ/
141.017. sacedbhikṣavaḥ sa mudgaḥ pātre patito 'bhaviṣyanna bhūmau, sthāanametadvidyate yaddeveṣu ca manuṣyeṣu ca rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritamabhaviṣyat/
141.018. yo 'sau otkariko vaṇik tena kālena tena samayena, sa eṣa rājā mūrdhātaḥ/
141.019. yo mūrdhāto rājā, ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena/
141.020. yasmādevaṃ buddhe bhagavati mahākāruṇike kārāḥ kṛtā atyarthaṃ mahāphalā bhavanti mahānuśaṃśā mahādyutayo mahāvaistārikā iti, tasmādbhavabodhiḥ/
141.021. kiṃ karaṇīyam? buddhe dharme saṃghe kārāḥ karaṇīyāḥ samyakpraṇidhānāni ca karaṇīyānīti//
body.translated_text:
141.001. <141>'Long ago, monks, in a past era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Vipaśyin</s>.
141.002. Then the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, wandering on a teaching tour through the provinces, arrived in due course at the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>.
141.003. Then the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Bandhumatī</s> for alms.
141.004. There was a certain peddler named <s>Cautkarika</s>.
141.004. Seeing the Blessed One <s>Vipaśyin</s>, of irresistibly beautiful appearance, an exceptional faith arose in him.
141.005. With faith, he took a handful of mung beans and threw them into the bowl.
141.006. Of those, four mung beans fell into the bowl, one struck the rim of the bowl and fell to the ground.
141.006. The rest neither reached the bowl nor the ground, but fell to the earth without reaching it.
141.007. Then the peddler, filled with faith, made an aspiration:
141.009. "By this great and lofty gift, may I become a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Self-Arisen One;
141.011. and having crossed over, may I ferry across the great floods of beings who were not ferried across by the former Lords of Victors." //11//
141.013. The Blessed One said: 'He who was that peddler <s>Cautkarika</s> — I myself was he at that time, in that era.
141.013. Because I, filled with faith, threw a handful of mung beans into the bowl of the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, and four mung beans fell into the bowl while the rest fell to the ground — by the ripening of that deed, sovereign lordship and dominion was exercised in the four continents.
141.016. And the one mung bean that struck the rim of the bowl and fell to the ground — by the ripening of that deed, he ascended to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
141.017. If, monks, that mung bean had fallen into the bowl and not onto the ground, it is possible that sovereign lordship and dominion over both gods and humans would have been exercised.
141.018. He who was that peddler <s>Cautkarika</s> at that time, in that era — he is this King <s>Mūrdhāta</s>.
141.019. He who was King <s>Mūrdhāta</s> — I myself was he at that time, in that era.
141.020. Since services rendered to a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, who is greatly compassionate, are of exceedingly great fruit, great benefit, great splendor, and great extent — therefore, awakening arises.
141.021. What should be done? Services should be rendered to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and right aspirations should be made.'

body.text:
141.023. idamavocadbhagavān/
141.023. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
141.023. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
141.023. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 141.024. iti śrīdivyāvadāne māndhātāvadānaṃ saptadaśamam//
body.translated_text: 141.024. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Māndhātāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Māndhātā</s>), the seventeenth.

body.text: 142.001. div18 dharmarucyavadānam/
body.translated_text: 142.001. Chapter 18: The <s>Dharmarucyavadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Dharmaruci</s>).

body.text:
142.003. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
142.003. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
142.004. tena khalu samayena pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya anupūrveṇa grāmanigamapallīpattanarājadhānīṣu cañcūryamāṇāni mahāsamudrataṭamanuprāptāni/
142.005. tair nipuṇataḥ sāmudram yānapātraṃ pratipāditam/
142.006. yato vaṇijastaṃ mahāsamudraṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃbhinnamanaso na prasahante samavataritum/
142.007. paścāttervaṇigbhiḥ karṇadhāra uktah--uddhoṣaya naḥ puruṣo mahāsamudrasya bhūtaṃ varṇam/
142.008. yato varṇadhāra uddhoṣayituṃ pravṛttah--śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, santyasmin mahāsamudre evaṃvidhāni ratnāni, tadyathā--maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilā pravālo rajataṃ jātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartāḥ/
142.010. ya icchati evamrūpai ratnairātmānaṃ samyaksukhena prīṇayituṃ mātāpitarau putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ mitrāmātyajñātisālohitam, kālena ca kālaṃ dakṣiṇīyebhyaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitumūrdhvagāminīṃ saubhāgyakarīṃ sukhavipākāmāyatyāṃ svargasaṃvartanīm, so 'smin mahāsamudre avataratu dhanahetoḥ/
142.014. evamukte ca punaḥ sarva eva sattvāḥ saṃpattikāmā vipattipratikūlāstaṃ śrutvā tasmin mahāsamudre vyavasitāḥ samavataritum/
142.015. yatastadvahanamatiprabhūtairmanuṣyairatibhāreṇa ca ākrāntatvāt tatraivāvasīdati/
142.016. tataḥ karṇadhāreṇoktam--asahyaṃ vahanam/
142.016. yato vaṇijaḥ kathayanti--kasyedānīṃ vakṣyāmo vahanāt pratyavatarasveti/
142.017. tairvaṇigbhiḥ karṇadhārasyoktam--mahāsamudrasya bhūtaṃ varṇamudghoṣayata/
142.018. tataḥ sa udghoṣayituṃ pravṛttah--śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, santyasmin mahāsamudre imāni evamrūpāṇi mahānti mahābhayāni, tadyathā timibhayaṃ timiṃgilabhayamūrmibhayaṃ kūrmabhayaṃ sthale utsīdanabhayaṃ jale saṃsīdanabhayamantarjalagatānāṃ parvatānāmāghaṭṭanabhayaṃ kālikāvātabhayam/
142.021. caurā api āgacchanti nīlavāsaso dhanahāriṇaḥ/
142.021. yena cātmano jīvitaparityāgo vyavāsthito mātāpitarau putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ mitrāmātyajñātisālohitaṃ citraṃ ca jambudvīpaṃ parityaktum, sa mahāsamudramavataratu/
142.023. alpāḥ śūrā bahavaḥ kātarāḥ/
142.023. taṃ śrutvā tathodghuṣya tu tasmādyānapātrādavatīrṇā bahavaḥ, kecidavaśiṣṭāḥ/
142.024. tatastairvaṇigbhirvahanasyaikaṃ varatraṃ chinnam/
142.025. paścād dvau trayo yāvadanupūrveṇa sarve varatrāśchinnāḥ/
142.025. tāsu cchinnāsu tadvahanaṃ mahākarṇadhārasampreritaṃ gagane mahāvātasamprerito megha iva balavadvāyusampreritaṃ kṣiprameva saṃprasthitam/
142.027. yāvadratnadvīpamanuprāptaḥ/
142.027. sa taṃ pradeśamanuprāptānāṃ karṇadhāraḥ kathayati--santyasmin ratnadvīpe kācamaṇayo ratnasadṛśāḥ, te bhavadbhirupaparīkṣyopaparīkṣya gṛhītavyāḥ/
142.028. mā vaḥ paścājjambudvīpagatānāṃ tāpyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
142.029. tatraiva ca kroñcakumārikā nāma striyo bhavanti/
142.029. tāḥ puruṣaṃ labdhvā tathopalāṃstāḍayanti, yathā atraivānayena vyasanamāpadyate/
142.030. atraiva ca madanīyāni phalāni bhavanti/
142.031. tāni yo bhakṣayati, sa sapta rātriṃdivasān suptastiṣṭhati/
142.031. asminneva ca ratnadvīpe saptāhāt pareṇa amanuṣyā na sahante, tāvadvidhān viparītān vāyūnutpādayanti yairvahanamapahriyate yathāpi tadakṛtakāryāṇām/
142.033. tāni bhavadbhirlabdhāni na bhakṣayitavyāni/
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, about five hundred merchants, having gathered their merchandise, traveling in due order through villages, towns, hamlets, market-cities, and royal capitals, arrived at the shore of the great ocean. They had a sea-going vessel carefully prepared. But the merchants, seeing that great ocean, became faint-hearted and could not bring themselves to descend into it. Then those merchants said to the helmsman: 'Announce to us, good man, the true description of the great ocean.' So the helmsman began to announce: 'Hear, O people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! In this great ocean there are such jewels as these, namely: gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch, stone, coral, silver, gold, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (cat's eye), <s>musāragalva</s> (agate), ruby, and right-spiraling conch shells. Whoever wishes to delight himself in true happiness with such jewels, and to delight his mother and father, sons and wife, female servants, male servants, workers, attendants, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen, and from time to time to make offerings to worthy recipients — <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — offerings that lead upward, that bring good fortune, that have a pleasant result, that lead to heaven in the future — let him descend into this great ocean for the sake of wealth.' When this was said, all beings, desiring prosperity and averse to misfortune, having heard this, resolved to descend into that great ocean. Because that vessel was overloaded with too many people and too heavy a burden, it began to sink right there. Then the helmsman said: 'The vessel cannot bear it.' The merchants said: 'To whom shall we now say — get off the vessel?' Those merchants said to the helmsman: 'Announce the true description of the great ocean.' Then he began to announce: 'Hear, O people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! In this great ocean there are such great and terrible dangers as these, namely: the danger of the <s>timi</s> (whale), the danger of the <s>timiṃgila</s> (whale-swallower), the danger of waves, the danger of turtles, the danger of running aground on land, the danger of sinking in water, the danger of collision with submerged mountains, and the danger of the <s>kālikā</s> storm winds. Pirates too come, blue-clad robbers of wealth. Whoever has resolved to give up his own life, to abandon mother and father, sons and wife, female servants, male servants, workers, attendants, friends, ministers, relatives, kinsmen, and colorful <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — let him descend into the great ocean. Few are the brave; many are the cowards.' Having heard and understood this announcement, many descended from the vessel, while some remained. Then those merchants cut one mooring rope of the vessel. Then two, three, and gradually all the mooring ropes were cut. When they were cut, that vessel, propelled by the great helmsman, like a cloud in the sky propelled by a great wind, driven swiftly by a powerful wind, set out. It arrived at the Jewel Island. The helmsman said to those who had arrived at that place: 'In this Jewel Island there are glass gems resembling precious stones; you must examine them carefully before taking them. Lest you suffer regret when you have returned to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. And here there are also women called <s>Kroñcakumārikās</s> (crane-maidens). They, having obtained a man, strike him with stones in such a way that he meets with ruin right here. Here too there are intoxicating fruits. Whoever eats them sleeps for seven nights and days. Moreover, on this very Jewel Island, after seven days, the non-human beings cannot tolerate [the visitors]; they produce such contrary winds that the vessel is carried away, leaving those who have not completed their task. Those fruits must not be eaten by you.'

body.text:
143.001. <143>tacchrutvā vaṇijo 'vahitamanaso 'pramādenāvasthitāḥ/
143.001. prāpya ca taṃ ratnadvīpaṃ prayatnamāsthāya ratnānveṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā anupūrveṇopaparīkṣya ratnānāṃ tadvahanaṃ pūritaṃ tadyathā yavānāṃ vā yavasasyānāṃ vā mudgānāṃ vā bhāṣāṇāṃ vā/
143.003. vahanaṃ pūryitvā te 'nukūlaṃ jambudvīpābhimukhena vāyunā saṃprasthitāḥ/
143.004. mahāsamudre ca tribhiḥ skandhaiḥ prāṇinaḥ saṃmiśritāḥ/
143.004. prathame yojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ, dvistriyojanaśatikā ātmabhāvaḥ/
143.005. dvitīye skandhe 'ṣṭayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvā navadaśayāvaccaturdaśayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ/
143.006. tṛtīye skandhe pañcadaśayojanaśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ, ṣoḍaśayojanaśatikā yāvadekaviṃśatikā ātmabhāvāḥ/
143.007. tatra ca mahāsamudre tā matsyajātayaḥ parasparānyonyabhakṣaṇaparāḥ/
143.008. ye prathamāyāṃ bhūmau avasthitāḥ, te dvitīyabhūmisthairbhakṣyante/
143.008. ye dvitīyabhūmisthāḥ, te tṛtīyabhūmisthairbhakṣyante/
143.009. tatra timiṃgilo nāma matsyāstṛtīyādudakaskandadhādabhyudgamya uparimandakaskandhamādāya carati/
143.010. sa yasyāṃ velāyāṃ mukhamāvṛṇoti, tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāsamudrāt pānīyaṃ mahatā vegenākṣiptaṃ mukhadvāram yato dhāvati/
143.011. tenaivodakaskandhenākṣiptā matsyakacchapavallabhakaśuśumāramakarādyā matsyajātayo mukhadvāreṇodare patanti/
143.012. tasyaivaṃ carata ātmabhāvācchira evaṃ lakṣyate dūrata eva, tadyathā--parvato nabhaḥpramāṇaḥ/
143.013. akṣīṇi cāsya durata eva saṃlakṣyante nabhasīvādityau/
143.014. yatastairvaṇigbhirdūrata evopadhāritam/
143.014. tanmahārṇavarūpamupadhārya cintayituṃ pravṛttāh--kimetadbhavanta ādityadvayasyodayanam? teṣāmevaṃ cintayatāṃ tadvahanaṃ tasya mukhadvāram yato vegenopahartumārabdham/
143.016. teṣāṃ vahanaṃ vegenāpahriyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā ādotuadvayotpādanaṃ ca saṃlakṣya saṃvega utpannah--kiṃ bhavanto yat tacchrūyate saptādityāḥ kalpasaṃvartanyāṃ samudāgamiṣyantīti, tadevedānīṃ proditāḥ syuḥ/
143.018. yataḥ karṇadhāreṇa teṣāṃ vimarśajātānāmuktam--yat tadbhavantaḥ śrūyate timitimiṃgila iti, timitimiṃgilabhayamidam/
143.019. tat paśyantu bhavantaḥ/
143.020. pānīyādabhyudgataparvatavadālokyate etattasya śiraḥ/
143.020. paśyatha caiṣā tasya parā dantamālā/
143.022. paśyatha etau dūrata eva sūryavadavalokyete etau akṣitārakau/
143.022. punasasau karṇadhāro vaṇijāṃ kathayati--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ, nāsmākamidānīṃ jīvitopāyaḥ kaścidyena vayamasmādbhayāt mucyema/
143.024. sarvoṣāmevāsmākaṃ maraṇaṃ pratyupasthitam/
143.024. tadidānīṃ bhavadbhiḥ kiṃ karaṇīyam? yasya vo yasmin deve bhaktiḥ sa tamāyācatu/
143.025. yadi tenāpi tāvadāyācanena kāciddevatā asmākamasmānmahābhayādvimoṣkaṇaṃ kuryāt/
143.026. na cānyo 'sti kaścidupāyo jīvitasya/
143.027. yatastairvaṇigbhirmaraṇabhayabhītaiḥ śivavaruṇakuberamahendropendrādayo devā jīvitaparitrāṇārthamāyācitumārabdhāḥ/
143.028. naiva ca teṣāmāyācatāṃ tasmānmaraṇabhayāt jīvitaparitrāṇaviśeṣaḥ kaścit/
143.029. tathaiva tadvahanaṃ salilavegāt bhikṣiptaṃ timiṃgilamukhadvāram yato 'pahriyate/
143.029. tatra copāsako 'bhirūḍhaḥ/
143.030. tenoktam--bhavantaḥ, nāsmākamasmānmaraṇabhayānmokṣaḥ kaścit/
143.030. sarvairevāsmābhirmartavyam/
143.031. kiṃ tu sarva evaikaraveṇa namo buddhāyeti vadāmaḥ/
143.031. sati maraṇe buddhāvalambanayā smṛtyā kālaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ/
143.032. sugatigamanaṃ bhaviṣyati/
143.032. yatastairvaṇigbhirekaraveṇa namo buddhāyeti <144>praṇāmaḥ kṛtaḥ sarvaireva/
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the merchants remained vigilant and heedful. Having reached that Jewel Island and making effort in searching for jewels, carefully examining them in due order, they filled that vessel with jewels — as one might fill it with barley, barley grains, mung beans, or chickpeas. Having filled the vessel, they set out with a favorable wind heading toward <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. In the great ocean, there are beings mixed in three strata. In the first, beings have bodily forms one to two or three hundred <s>yojanas</s> in size. In the second stratum, beings have bodily forms eight hundred <s>yojanas</s> in size, nine, ten, up to fourteen hundred <s>yojanas</s>. In the third stratum, beings have bodily forms fifteen hundred <s>yojanas</s> in size, sixteen hundred, up to twenty-one hundred <s>yojanas</s>. In that great ocean, those fish species devour each other. Those stationed in the first level are devoured by those of the second level. Those of the second level are devoured by those of the third level. There, the <s>timiṃgila</s> (whale-swallower) fish, rising from the third water-stratum, takes the upper water-stratum and moves about. At the time when it opens its mouth, water from the great ocean is drawn in with great force and rushes toward its mouth-entrance. By that very current of water, fish, turtles, <s>vallabhakas</s>, crocodiles, <s>makaras</s>, and other fish species are drawn into its stomach through its mouth. As it moves about in this way, its head can be seen from a distance — like a mountain reaching to the sky. Its eyes too can be seen from a distance — like two suns in the sky. Those merchants, having perceived it from afar, and having observed that appearance of the great ocean, began to wonder: 'What is this, sirs — the rising of two suns?' While they were thinking thus, their vessel began to be carried with great speed toward its mouth-entrance. Seeing their vessel being swept away with great speed and perceiving the appearance of two suns, a sense of urgency arose: 'Sirs, what we hear about — that seven suns will arise at the time of cosmic dissolution — could it be that they have now risen?' Then the helmsman, seeing their bewilderment, said: 'What you have heard about, sirs — the <s>timi</s> and <s>timiṃgila</s> — this is the danger of the <s>timiṃgila</s>. Look, sirs! That which appears like a mountain rising from the water — that is its head. See that row of teeth beyond it. See those two that appear from a distance like suns — those are its eyeballs.' The helmsman further said to the merchants: 'Listen, sirs! We now have no means of saving our lives by which we might escape from this danger. Death stands before all of us. What then should you do? Whoever among you has devotion to any god, let him pray to that god. If by such a prayer some deity might deliver us from this great danger — otherwise, there is no other means for our lives.' Then those merchants, terrified by the fear of death, began to pray to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and other gods for the protection of their lives. But even as they prayed, no relief from that mortal danger came to protect their lives. Just so, that vessel, swept by the water current, was being carried toward the mouth-entrance of the <s>timiṃgila</s>. Now, a lay follower (<s>upāsaka</s>) had boarded [the vessel]. He said: 'Sirs, there is no deliverance for us from this mortal danger. All of us must die. But let all of us, with one voice, say: "Homage to the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Namo Buddhāya</s>)!" If we must die, we shall die with mindfulness fixed upon the <s>Buddha</s>. There will be a fortunate rebirth.' Then all those merchants, with one voice, uttered the salutation: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Namo Buddhāya</s>)!'

body.text:
144.001. bhagavatā ca jetavanasthena sa vādaḥ śruto divyena śrotreṇa viśuddhena atikrāntamānuṣeṇa/
144.002. śrutvā ca punarbhagavatā sa nādastathā adhiṣṭhito yathā tena timiṃgilena śrutam/
144.003. tasya taṃ namo buddhāyeti rāvaṃ śrutvā manaso 'marṣa utpanno viklavībhūtaśca--buddho bata loka utpannaḥ/
144.004. na mama pratirūpaṃ syāt yadahaṃ buddhasya bhagavato nāmodghoṣaṃ śrutvā āhāramāhareyam/
144.005. sa cintayituṃ pravṛttah--yadyahamidanīṃ sahasaiva mukhadvāraṃ pidhāsyāmi, salilavegapratyāhatasya vahanasya vināśo bhaviṣyati, eteṣāṃ cānekānāṃ jīvitavināśaḥ/
144.006. yannvahaṃ mṛdunopakrameṇa svairaṃ svairaṃ mukhadvāraṃ saṃpidadhyām/
144.007. tatastena timiṃgilenātmīyaṃ mukhadvāraṃ mṛdunopakrameṇa svairaṃ svairaṃ pihitam/
144.008. paścāt tadvahanaṃ tasmānmahāgrāhamukhādvinirmuktamanuguṇaṃ vāyumāsādya tīramanuprāptam/
144.009. atha te vaṇijastīramāsādya tadbhāṇḍaṃ śakaṭoṣṭragogardabhādibhiḥ purayitvā anupūrveṇa grāmanigamapallīpattanādiṣu cañcūryamāṇāḥ śrāvastīmanuprāptāḥ/
144.010. te tatra gatvā saṃlakṣayanti--dharmataiṣā yasya nāṃnā vahanaṃ saṃsiddhayānapātramāgacchati, tasyaiva tāni ratnāni gamyāni bhavanti/
144.012. yannu vayametāni ratnāni buddhasya bhagavato dadyāmaḥ/
144.012. te tāni ratnāni saṃgṛhya bhagavataḥ sakāśamupagatāḥ/
144.013. anupūrveṇa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavataḥ kathayanti--bhagavan, asmākaṃ samudre yānapātreṇāvatīrṇānāṃ timiṃgilagrāheṇa tasmin yānapāre 'pahriyamāṇe jīvitavināśe pratyupasthite bhagavataḥ smaraṇaparāyaṇānāṃ nāmagrahaṇaṃ tasmāt mahāgrāhamukhādvinirmuktam, tato vayaṃ bhagavan saṃsiddhayānapārāḥ kṣemasvastinā ihāgatāḥ/
144.016. dharmatā caiṣā yasya nāṃnā vahanaṃ saṃsiddhayānapātrā āgacchanti, tasya tadgamyaṃ bhavati/
144.017. tadvayaṃ bhagavato nāmagrahaṇena maraṇabhayādūttīrṇāḥ/
144.018. tadasmākametāni ratnāni bhagavān gṛhṇātu/
144.018. bhagavānāha--yena mayendrāya(?) balabodhyaṅgaratnānyadhigatāni, kiṃ tathāgatasya bhūyaḥ prākṛtaratnaiḥ karaṇīyam? yadi cecchata asmacchāsane vatsāḥ pravrajitum, āgacchatha/
144.020. yataste saṃlakṣayanti vaṇijah--yadasmākaṃ kiṃcit jīvitam, tatsarvaṃ buddhasya bhagavatastejasā/
144.021. yadvayametāni ratnāni tyaktvā bhagavato 'ntike pravrajema iti/
144.022. paścāt te tāni ratnāni mātāpitṛbhyaḥ putradāradāsīdāsakarmakaramitrāmātyajñātisālohitebhyo yathānyāyataḥ saṃvibhajya pravrajitāḥ/
144.023. pravrajya tairyujyadbhirghaṭadbhirvyāyacchadbhiryāvadarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam//
body.translated_text:
144.001. The Blessed One, residing at <s>Jetavana</s>, heard that cry with his divine ear, purified and surpassing the human.
144.002. Having heard it, the Blessed One empowered that sound so that it was heard by the <s>timiṃgila</s> (whale-monster).
144.003. Having heard that cry 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!', remorse arose in his mind and he became agitated: 'Alas! A <s>Buddha</s> has appeared in the world!
144.004. It would not be fitting for me, having heard the proclamation of the name of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, to take food.'
144.005. He began to consider: 'If I close my mouth-entrance suddenly now, the vessel, driven back by the force of the water, will be destroyed, and many of these beings will perish.
144.006. Let me rather, by gentle means, slowly and gradually close my mouth-entrance.'
144.007. Then that <s>timiṃgila</s>, by gentle means, slowly and gradually closed its mouth-entrance.
144.008. Afterwards, that vessel, released from the mouth of that great sea-monster, caught a favorable wind and reached the shore.
144.009. Then those merchants, having reached the shore, loaded their merchandise onto carts, camels, oxen, donkeys, and the like, and traveling in due order through villages, towns, hamlets, and ports, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
144.010. Having gone there, they reflected: 'It is the natural law that the jewels belonging to a successfully completed voyage belong to the one by whose name the vessel arrived safely.
144.012. Let us give these jewels to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
144.012. They gathered those jewels and approached the Blessed One.
144.013. In due order, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and said: 'Blessed One, when we had descended into the ocean with our vessel, and the <s>timiṃgila</s> sea-monster was carrying our vessel away, and the destruction of our lives was imminent — we who had the recollection of the Blessed One as our refuge, by the invocation of his name, were released from the mouth of that great sea-monster. Thus, Blessed One, having completed our voyage safely, we have come here in safety and well-being.
144.016. It is the natural law that the cargo of a vessel which arrives with a successful voyage belongs to the one by whose name it came.
144.017. We have been saved from the fear of death by invoking the name of the Blessed One.
144.018. May the Blessed One accept these jewels from us.'
144.018. The Blessed One said: 'I have already attained the jewels of the powers and the factors of enlightenment (<s>balabodhyaṅgaratnāni</s>); what use has the <s>Tathāgata</s> for ordinary jewels? But if you wish, dear ones, to go forth in my teaching, come.'
144.020. Then those merchants reflected: 'Whatever life we have, all of it is due to the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
144.021. Let us give up these jewels and go forth in the presence of the Blessed One.'
144.022. Afterwards, they distributed those jewels appropriately among their mothers, fathers, sons, wives, female servants, male servants, workers, attendants, friends, ministers, relatives, and kinfolk, and went forth.
144.023. Having gone forth, striving, exerting, and applying themselves, they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

body.text:
144.024. yato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kīdṛśāni karmāṇi bhagavan, ebhirvaṇigbhiḥ kṛtānyupacitāni, yeṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākena bhagavānārāgito na virāgitah? bhagavānāha--
144.027. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāśyapaḥ samyaksambuddho loka utpanno 'bhūt/
144.027. tasya ca śāsane eta eva ca pravrajitā abhūvan/
144.028. tatra pravrajya ca na kaścit tadrūpo guṇagaṇo 'dhigato nānyatra sabrahmacāriṇāmuddiṣṭamadhītaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ ca/
144.029. maraṇakālasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavantah--yadasmābhiḥ kāśyapaṃ samyaksambuddhamāsādyoddiṣṭamadhītaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ ca, na kaścit guṇagaṇo 'dhigato 'sti, asya karmaṇo vipākena vayam yo 'sau anāgato 'dhvani kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena śākyamuninarmā samyaksambuddho vyākṛtaḥ, taṃ vayamārāgayemo na virāgayemaḥ//
body.translated_text:
144.024. Then the monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What kind of deeds, Blessed One, were done and accumulated by these merchants, by the ripening of which deeds the Blessed One was gratified and not displeased?' The Blessed One said:
144.027. 'Once upon a time, monks, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, had appeared in the world.
144.027. These very ones had gone forth in his teaching.
144.028. Having gone forth there, no such collection of virtues was attained by them, other than what was directed, studied, and recited by their fellow practitioners of the holy life.
144.029. At the time of death, they made an aspiration: "Since we, having encountered <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, received instruction, studied, and recited, yet have attained no collection of virtues — by the ripening of this deed, may we in the future, in the teaching of him whom <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, prophesied as the future <s>Samyaksambuddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> — may we gratify him and not displease him."'

body.text:
145.001. <145>bhagavānāha--kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāni tāni pañcabhikṣuśatānyatīte 'dhvanyāsan kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajitāni, etāvantyetāni pañcabhikṣuśatāni/
145.002. tadā caiṣāmindriyāṇi paripācitāni, etarhi arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
145.003. yaścāsau mahāsamudre timistimiṃgilo nāma matsyo buddhaśabdaṃ śrutvā anāhāratāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ, sa svabhāvenaiva tīkṣṇāgnitayā kṣudduḥkhasyāsahatvāccyutaḥ kālagataḥ/
145.005. tena śrāvastyāṃ ṣaṭkarmanirate brāhmaṇakule pratisaṃghirgṛhītaḥ/
145.006. tasya taccharīraṃ kalevaraṃ mahāsamudre utplutam/
145.006. nāgaiśca tasya svabhavanasamīpasthasya gandhamasahadbhiranyato vikṣiptam/
145.007. yatra ca vikṣiptaṃ tatrāpi samīpe nāgasyaiva bhavanam/
145.008. tenāpi gandhamasahatā anyataḥ kṣiptam/
145.008. evaṃ kṣiptena pāramparyeṇa tat kalevaraṃ mahāsamudrataṭaṃ samudānītam/
145.009. yato 'nantaraṃ smudravelayotsārya sthale prakṣiptam/
145.009. taccānekaiḥ kākagṛdhraśvaśṛgālaśvāpadādyaiḥ pakṣibhistatsamucchritaiśca kṛmibhirbhakṣyamāṇamasthikaraṅkajīrṇamāsaṃ śvetaṃ śvetaṃ vyavasthitam/
145.011. asyāṃ ca śrāvastyāṃ tasya brāhmaṇasya yadā patnī antarvartinī saṃvṛttā, tadeva tasyā garbhotpādādatīva kṣudduḥkhena pīḍyamānayā gṛhasvāmyabhihitah--āryaputra, kṣuddukhenātīva bādhye/
145.013. tasyā evaṃ vadantyā gṛhasvāminoktam--bhadre, yadasmadgṛhe 'nnapānaṃ tatsarvamabhyavaharasva/
145.014. tayā abhyavahartumārabdham/
145.014. sā ca tadannapānaṃ sarvamabhyavahṛtya naiva tṛptimupayāti/
145.015. punarapi gṛhasvāmin vijñāpayati--āryaputra, naiva tṛptimupagacchāmi/
145.015. yatastena tiraḥprātiveśyasuhṛtsvajanādibhyo 'ntikadannapānamanviṣya tasyā anupradattam/
145.016. sā tamapyavahṛtya naiva tṛptiṃ gacchati/
145.017. bhūyo gṛhasvāminaḥ kathayati--āryaputra, naiva tṛptimupagacchāmi/
145.017. yato 'sau brāhmaṇaḥ saṃvignamanāḥ khedamāpannaḥ/
145.018. kimetadbhavantaḥ syāt--asyāḥ sattvamudare utpannam yasyotpādānnaiva tṛptimupayāti? yataḥ sa brāhmaṇo naimittakānāṃ darśayitvā saṃśayanirṇayanārthaṃ vaidyādīn bhūtatantravidaśca--paśyantu bhavantaḥ, iyaṃ brāhmaṇī kiṃ mahatā rogeṇābhibhūtā syādatha bhūtagrahāviṣṭā syādanyadvā syādrūpaṃ maraṇaliṅgamanenopasaṃkrameṇa pratyupasthitā syāt/
145.021. taiḥ śrutvā tathāvidha upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ/
145.022. tasyā brāhmaṇyāste indriyāṇāmanyathātvamupalakṣayanti/
145.022. yadā asyā indriyāṇāmanyathātvaṃ nopalakṣayanti, tadā tairvaidyanaimittakabhūtatantravidbhiścikitsakaiḥ sā brāhmaṇīparyanuyuktā--kasmāt kālādārabhya tavaivaṃvidhā dīptāgnitā samutpannā? tayā abhihitam--garbhalambhasamakālameva sa evaṃvidha upakramaḥ kṛtaḥ/
145.025. yato naimittakavaidyacikitsakairabhihitam--nāsyāḥ kaścidanyastadrūpo rogo nāpi bhūtagrahāveśo bādhākara utpannaḥ/
145.027. asyaivaiṣā garbhasyānubhāvenaivaṃvidhā dīptāgnitā/
145.027. yato 'sau brāhmaṇa upalabdhavṛttāntaḥ svasthībhūtaḥ/
145.028. sāpi brāhmaṇī naiva kadācidannapānasya tṛptā/
145.028. anupūrveṇa samakālameva putro jātaḥ/
145.029. tasya dārakasya jātamātrasya sā brāhmaṇī vinītakṣudduḥkhā saṃvṛttā/
145.029. sa dārako jātamātra eva atyarthaṃ bubhukṣayopapīḍyate/
145.030. tasya bubhukṣayā pīḍyamānasya mātā stanaṃ dātuṃ pravṛttā/
145.031. sa ca dārakaḥ stanaṃ pītvāpi sarvaṃ naiva tṛptimupayāti/
145.031. paścāt tena brāhmaṇena tayā ca brāhmaṇyā tiraskṛtaprātiveśyasvajanayuvatyaścābhyarthya stanaṃ tasya dārakasya dāpayituṃ pravṛttāḥ/
body.translated_text:
145.001. The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? Those five hundred monks of the past who had gone forth in the teaching of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One — they are these very five hundred monks.
145.002. At that time their faculties were ripened, and now they have directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.
145.003. As for that fish in the great ocean, the <s>timi-timiṃgila</s>, having heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, he resolved upon abstinence from food, but by its very nature, due to the sharpness of its digestive fire and the inability to endure the suffering of hunger, it fell and died.
145.005. It took rebirth in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> family in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, devoted to the six duties.
145.006. Its body, the carcass, floated up in the great ocean.
145.006. The <s>Nāgas</s>, unable to bear the stench of it near their dwellings, cast it elsewhere.
145.007. Where it was cast, there too was a <s>Nāga's</s> dwelling nearby.
145.008. That one too, unable to bear the stench, cast it elsewhere.
145.008. Thus, cast about in succession, that carcass was brought to the shore of the great ocean.
145.009. From there, thrown onto the dry land by the ocean waves,
145.009. it was eaten by many crows, vultures, dogs, jackals, wild animals, and birds, as well as worms that crawled on it, until it became a skeleton — dried, white and bleached.
145.011. Meanwhile, in this <s>Śrāvastī</s>, when the wife of that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> became pregnant, from the very moment of conception she was tormented by an extreme hunger-pain and said to her husband: 'Noble husband, I am sorely afflicted by hunger-pain.'
145.013. When she spoke thus, the husband said: 'Dear one, eat whatever food and drink there is in our house.'
145.014. She began to eat.
145.014. Having consumed all the food and drink, she was still not satisfied.
145.015. Again she informed the husband: 'Noble husband, I am still not satisfied.'
145.015. Then he sought food and drink from neighbors, friends, and relatives and gave it to her.
145.016. Having consumed that too, she was still not satisfied.
145.017. Again she told the husband: 'Noble husband, I am still not satisfied.'
145.017. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, his mind alarmed, fell into distress.
145.018. 'Could this be, Sirs — that a being has been born in her womb by whose birth she cannot find satisfaction?' Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having shown her to soothsayers, physicians, and exorcists skilled in spirit-lore for the purpose of resolving his doubt — 'Look, Sirs, is this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman overcome by some great disease, or is she possessed by some spirit, or is there some other form of death or mortal sign that has approached her?'
145.021. Having heard this, they performed an appropriate examination.
145.022. They observed any alteration in that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman's faculties.
145.022. When they observed no alteration of her faculties, the physicians, soothsayers, and exorcists questioned the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman: 'From what time did this blazing digestive fire arise in you?' She said: 'From the very time of conception itself, this condition arose.'
145.025. Then the soothsayers, physicians, and exorcists said: 'There is no other disease affecting her, nor has any harmful spirit-possession arisen.
145.027. This blazing digestive fire is by the very influence of her fetus.'
145.027. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having understood the situation, became composed.
145.028. Yet that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman was never satisfied with food and drink.
145.028. In due course, a son was born.
145.029. The moment that boy was born, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman's hunger-pain ceased.
145.029. The boy, from the very moment of birth, was extremely tormented by hunger.
145.030. As he was tormented by hunger, the mother began to give him the breast.
145.031. But the boy, even having drunk the breast-milk, was still not satisfied.
145.031. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman began soliciting their neighbors, relatives, and young women to give their breasts to the boy.

body.text:
146.001. <146>sa ca dārakaḥ sarvāsāmapi stanaṃ pītvā naiva tṛptimabhyupagacchate/
146.001. paścāt tena brāhmaṇena tayārthe chagalikā kṛtvā/
146.002. sa dārakastasyā api cchagalikāyāḥ kṣīraṃ pītvā janikāyāśca stanaṃ naiva tṛpyate/
146.003. tatra kālena kālaṃ bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaśca piṇḍapātaṃ praviṣya parikathāṃ kurvanti/
146.004. sa dārakastāṃ parikathāṃ śrutvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ na roditi, avahitaśrotrastūṣṇībhūtvā tāṃ dharmaśravaṇakathāṃ śṛṇoti/
146.005. pratyavāsṛteṣu bhikṣubhikṣuṇīṣu ca punaḥ pipāsāduḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedayamāno rohituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
146.006. taiḥ saṃlakṣitam--dharme vatsāya ruciriti/
146.006. tasya dharmarucīti nāma pratiṣṭhāpitam/
146.007. sa ca dārako 'nupūrveṇa māsārdharmāsādīnāmatyayādbhuñjāno naiva kadācidannapānasya tṛpyati/
146.008. yadā ca viśiṣṭe vasasi sthitaḥ, tadā tasya mātāpitṛbhyāṃ bhakṣabhājanaṃ dattam/
146.009. gaccha vatsa, idaṃ te bhaikṣabhājanam/
146.009. gṛhītvā śrāvastyāṃ bhikṣāṃ paryaṭitvā āhārakṛtyaṃ kuru/
146.010. yataḥ sa dārako bhaikṣabhājanaṃ gṛhītvā śrāvastyāṃ bhaikṣaṃ paryaṭati/
146.010. paryaṭanneva ca bhuktvā bhuktvā atṛpyamāna eva gṛhamāgacchati/
146.011. yato 'sau saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ mayā karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena na kadācit vitṛpyamāna āhāramārāgayāmi? sa viṣaṇṇacetāścintayituṃ pravṛttah--kiṃ tāvadagnipraveśaṃ karomi, uta jalapraveśamatha taṭaprapātaṃ karomi? sa evaṃ cintayā sthitaḥ/
146.014. upāsakenopalakṣitaḥ/
146.014. tasya tenoktam--kiṃ cintāpara evaṃ tiṣṭhasi? gaccha tvam/
146.015. mahāntaṃ buddhaśāsanaṃ maharddhikaṃ mahānubhāvam/
146.015. tatra pravraja/
146.015. tatra ca tvaṃ pravrajitaḥ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃcayaṃ kariṣyasi/
146.016. akuśalāśca te dharmā ye 'sminnapi janmani saṃcitā bhaviṣyanti, te tanvībhaviṣyanti/
146.017. yadi tāvadguṇagaṇānadhigamiṣyasi, paryatīkṛtaste saṃsāro bhaviṣyati/
146.018. atha sa mahātmā upāsakena codito jetavanaṃ gataḥ/
146.018. jetavanaṃ gatvā tatra bhikṣūn pāṭhasvādhyāyamanasikārodyuktān dṛṣṭvā atīva prasādajātaḥ/
146.019. bhikṣumupasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadati--arya, pravrajitumicchāmi/
146.020. yato bhikṣubhiruktah--mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñāto 'si? sa kathayati--nāhaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñātaḥ/
146.021. tairuktah--gaccha vatsa, mātāpitṛbhyāmanujñāṃ mārgasva/
146.021. yataḥ sa mātāpitṛbhyāṃ sakāśādanujñāṃ mārgituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
146.022. sa mātāpitṛbhyāmabhihitah--gaccha vatsa, yathābhipretaṃ kuru/
146.023. sa labdhānujño bhikṣusakāśaṃ gataḥ/
146.023. paścādbhikṣuṇā pravrājitaḥ/
146.024. tatra ca bhikṣūṇāṃ kadācit piṇḍapāto bhavati, kadācit nimantraṇaṃ bhavati/
146.024. sa ca yasmin divase piṇḍapāto bhavati, tatropādhyāyenocyate--vatsa, kiṃ tṛpto 'si uta na? sa upādhyāyasya kathayati--nāsti tṛptiḥ/
146.026. yata upādhyāyenāsya saṃlakṣitah--taruṇavayasā pravrajito dīptāgnitayā na tṛptimupayāti/
146.027. sa ātmīyādapi piṇḍapatāt tasya saṃvibhāgaṃ prārabdhaḥ kartum/
146.028. punaśca pṛcchati--vatsa, kimidānīṃ tṛpto 'si? atha sa tamupādhyāyaṃ vadati--na tṛpto 'smi/
146.029. yata upādhyāyastaṃ śrutvā sapremān bhikṣūnanyāṃśca sārdhavihāriṇaḥ prārabdho vaktum/
146.030. yataḥ samānopādhyāyaiḥ samānācāryairanyaiśca sapremakairbhikṣubhirupasaṃhāra ārabdhaḥ kartum/
146.031. teṣāmantikāllabhamāno naiva tṛptimupayāti/
146.031. yadā ca nimantraṇaṃ bhavati, tadāpi te tathaiva tasyopasaṃhāraṃ kurvanti/
146.032. dānapatirapi viditvā yadyadadhikaṃ tattadasmai datvā āgacchati/
body.translated_text: That boy, even after drinking from the breasts of all of them, did not reach satiation. Afterwards, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> procured a she-goat for his sake. That boy, even after drinking the milk of that she-goat and his mother's breast, was never satisfied. Then, from time to time, <s>bhikṣus</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> would enter for their alms-round and engage in religious discourse. That boy, upon hearing that discourse, at that time did not cry; with attentive ears he became silent and listened to that teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. When the <s>bhikṣus</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> departed, he again began to cry, experiencing the suffering of thirst. They observed: "The child delights in the <s>Dharma</s>." So they established his name as <s>Dharmaruci</s> (Delighting in Dharma). That boy, gradually, over the passing of months and half-months, though eating, was never at any time satisfied with food and drink. When he was old enough to stand on his own, his parents gave him a begging bowl. "Go, child, here is your begging bowl. Having gone begging through <s>Śrāvastī</s>, take care of your need for food." Then that boy, taking the begging bowl, went begging through <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Even while wandering about, eating and eating, still unsatisfied, he would come home. Then he reflected: "What <s>karma</s> have I done, by the ripening of which I never find satisfaction no matter how much food I consume?" He, with a despondent mind, began to think: "Shall I enter fire, or enter water, or throw myself from a cliff?" As he stood thus absorbed in thought, he was noticed by an <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee). That one said to him: "Why do you stand so absorbed in worry? Go! The teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> is great, of great supernatural power, of great majesty. Go forth there. Having gone forth there, you will accumulate wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And whatever unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> you may have accumulated even in this birth, they will become diminished. If indeed you attain the collection of virtues, <s>saṃsāra</s> will be brought to an end for you." Then that noble soul, urged by the <s>upāsaka</s>, went to <s>Jetavana</s>. Having gone to <s>Jetavana</s>, seeing the <s>bhikṣus</s> there engaged in recitation, study, and meditation, he was filled with exceeding faith. Approaching a <s>bhikṣu</s>, he spoke thus: "Venerable one, I wish to go forth." The <s>bhikṣus</s> asked: "Have you been given permission by your parents?" He replied: "I have not been given permission by my parents." They said: "Go, child, seek permission from your parents." Then he set out to seek permission from his parents. His parents said to him: "Go, child, do as you wish." Having obtained permission, he went to the <s>bhikṣus</s>. Afterwards, he was ordained by a <s>bhikṣu</s>. There, sometimes the <s>bhikṣus</s> received alms-food, sometimes invitations to meals. On the day when there was alms-food, his preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) would ask: "Child, are you satisfied or not?" He would tell his preceptor: "There is no satisfaction." Then the preceptor observed: "Having gone forth at a young age, due to his blazing digestive fire he does not reach satiation." He began to share with him from his own alms-food as well. And again he asked: "Child, are you now satisfied?" Then he said to that preceptor: "I am not satisfied." Then the preceptor, having heard this, with affection began to speak to other <s>bhikṣus</s> and co-residents. Then those who shared the same preceptor, the same teacher, and other affectionate <s>bhikṣus</s> began to contribute to his support. Even receiving from them, he did not reach satiation. And when there was an invitation to a meal, they likewise made contributions for him. The patron of the donation (<s>dānapati</s>), also learning of this, would give him whatever extra there was and depart.

body.text:
147.001. <147>atha pānakaṃ bhavati tadapi tathaiva yadadhikaṃ bhavati tattasyānupradīyate/
147.001. tasya ca yataḥ pravrajitasya na kadācidannapānena kukṣiḥ pūṇaḥ/
147.002. tena khalu samayena anyatamena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgha upanimantritaḥ/
147.003. bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamantargṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya/
147.004. dharmarucirvihāre upadhivāriko vyavasthāpitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then when there was a beverage, likewise whatever extra there was, that was given to him. For since his going forth, his belly was never filled with food and drink. At that time, a certain householder invited the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken up his bowl and robes, entered the inner quarters of the house. <s>Dharmaruci</s> was appointed as the monastery attendant (<s>upadhivārika</s>).

body.text:
147.005. tatra ca śrāvastyāmanyatamo gṛhapatiḥ prativasati/
147.005. tena caivamupalabdham yo 'saṃviditameva buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayati sa sahasaiva bhogairabhyudgacchati/
147.006. yatastena pañcamātrāṇāṃ bhikṣuśatānāmāhāraḥ samudānītaḥ/
147.007. sa tasyāhārasya śakaṭaṃ pūrayitvā praṇītapraṇītasya śucinaḥ sārdhaṃ sarvarūpairmitrasvajanasahāyo buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti vihāraṃ nirgataḥ/
147.009. sa paśyati tasmiñ jetavane bhikṣava eva na santi/
147.009. tena tatrānvāhiṇḍatā upadhivāriko dharmaruṣirdṛṣṭaḥ/
147.010. tasya tena gṛhapatinoktam--ārya, kva gatā bhikṣavah? sa kathayati--antargṛhe upanimantritāḥ praviṣṭāḥ/
147.011. sa gṛhapatistacchutvā durmanā vyavasthitah--kaṣṭam, evamasmākaṃ viphalaḥ pariśramo jātaḥ/
147.012. saṃcintya ca tasya dharmaruceḥ kathayati--ārya, bhakṣa tvamapi tāvat/
147.012. sa kathayati--yadi te mahātman parityaktaṃ bhavati/
147.013. tatastena gṛhapatinā saṃlakṣayitvā yenāhāreṇaikasya bhikṣoḥ paryāptaṃ bhavati, tāvadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ gṛhītvā taṃ dharmaruciṃ pariveṣayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
147.014. tena dharmarucinā bhoktumārabdhaṃ tanniravaśiṣṭam/
147.015. naiva tṛptaḥ/
147.015. gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakSayati--nāyaṃ tṛptaḥ/
147.016. tena ucyate--ārya, punarbhokṣyase? sa kathayati--mahātman, yadi te parityaktam/
147.016. tatastena gṛhapatinā bhūyastasmāt śakaṭādyena bhikṣudvayasyāhāreṇa paryāptaṃ syāt, tāvadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ gṛhītvā bhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
147.018. yato dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ/
147.018. gṛhaptinā bhūyaḥ saṃlakṣitam--nāyaṃ tṛptaḥ/
147.019. tenoktam--ārya, punarbhokṣyase? sa kathayati--mahātman, yadi te parityaktam/
147.020. yatastasmācchakaṭādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā trayāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ paryāptaṃ syāditi punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
147.021. sa dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ/
147.021. pṛṣṭah--ārya, punarbhokṣyase? sa kathayati--yadi te parityaktam/
147.022. yataḥ sa gṛhapatistasmādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā yena caturṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ paryāptaṃ syāditi punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
147.023. sa dharmarucistadapi bhuktvā naiva tṛptaḥ/
147.023. pṛṣṭah--ārya, punarbhokṣyase? bhūyaḥ sa kathayati--yadi te parityaktam/
147.024. yataḥ punastasmācchakaṭādyena pañcabhikṣūṇāmannapānaistṛptiḥ syāt, tāvadgṛhītvā punarbhojayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
147.025. tadapi cābhyavahṛtam/
147.025. naiva tṛptaḥ/
147.026. vistareṇa yāvaddaśānāṃ bhikṣūṇāmannapānena paryāptaṃ syāt, tāvad bhuktvā naiva tṛpyate/
147.026. yatastena saṃlakṣitam--nāyaṃ manuṣyo manuṣyavikāraḥ/
147.027. yataḥ śrūyate pañcabhir nīlavāsaso yakṣaśatairjetavanamaśūnyamiti teṣāṃ bhaviṣyatyeva anyatamaḥ/
147.028. iti saṃcintya garbharūpāṇi gṛhe 'nupraveśayituṃ pravṛttah--gacchatha yūyaṃ śīghraṃ gṛhameva, ahamevaiko yadi jīvāmi mriye veti/
147.029. sa gṛhajanaṃ visarjya maraṇabhayabhītastasmāt śakaṭādannapānaṃ gṛhītvā pariveṣayitumārabdhaḥ/
147.030. sa ca svairaṃ bhuñjati/
147.031. gṛhapatinā uktam--ārya, tvaritatvaritaṃ pratīcchasva/
147.031. yatastena dharmarucinā kṣipraṃ pratigṛhītvā bhiktumārabdham/
147.032. sa gṛhapatistvaritatvaritaṃ pariveṣayitvā niravaśeṣatastadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ dattvā <148>dakṣiṇādeśanāmapi bhayagṛhīto 'śrutvā tvaritatvaritaṃ vandāmyāryeti pṛṣṭhamanavalokayamāno nagaraṃ prasthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: Now in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there dwelt a certain householder. He had learned the following: "Whoever feeds the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> without prior arrangement, he suddenly rises in prosperity." Therefore he prepared food for five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s>. Having filled a cart with that food, most excellent and pure, together with all manner of provisions, accompanied by friends and kinsmen, he set out for the monastery thinking, "I shall feed the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>." He saw that in that <s>Jetavana</s> there were no <s>bhikṣus</s> at all. Wandering about there, he saw <s>Dharmaruci</s>, the monastery attendant. That householder said to him: "Venerable one, where have the <s>bhikṣus</s> gone?" He replied: "They have been invited to a household and have entered there." The householder, hearing that, stood dejected: "Alas, thus our effort has been in vain!" After reflecting, he said to <s>Dharmaruci</s>: "Venerable one, at least you should eat." He replied: "If it is relinquished by you, great soul." Then that householder, having considered, took from the cart enough food and drink as would suffice for one <s>bhikṣu</s>, and began to serve <s>Dharmaruci</s>. <s>Dharmaruci</s> began to eat; he consumed it all without remainder. He was not satisfied. The householder observed: "This one is not satisfied." He said: "Venerable one, will you eat again?" He replied: "Great soul, if it is relinquished by you." Then that householder took from the cart food and drink sufficient for two <s>bhikṣus</s> and began to feed him. <s>Dharmaruci</s> ate that too and was not satisfied. The householder again observed: "This one is not satisfied." He said: "Venerable one, will you eat again?" He replied: "Great soul, if it is relinquished by you." Then he took from that cart food and drink sufficient for three <s>bhikṣus</s> and began to feed him again. <s>Dharmaruci</s> ate that too and was not satisfied. Asked: "Venerable one, will you eat again?" He replied: "If it is relinquished by you." Then that householder took food and drink sufficient for four <s>bhikṣus</s> and began to feed him again. <s>Dharmaruci</s> ate that too and was not satisfied. Asked: "Venerable one, will you eat again?" Again he replied: "If it is relinquished by you." Then again he took from that cart food and drink by which five <s>bhikṣus</s> would be satiated, and began to feed him again. That too was consumed. He was not satisfied. In brief, he ate food and drink sufficient for ten <s>bhikṣus</s> and was still not satisfied. Then the householder thought: "This is no human being but a supernatural creature. For it is heard that <s>Jetavana</s> is never empty, being inhabited by five hundred <s>yakṣas</s> wearing blue garments; this must be one of them." Thinking thus, he began to send those of his household inside: "Go, all of you, quickly to the house! I alone shall see whether I live or die." Having sent away his household, terrified by the fear of death, he took food and drink from that cart and began to serve it. And <s>Dharmaruci</s> ate at his leisure. The householder said: "Venerable one, accept it quickly, quickly!" Then <s>Dharmaruci</s>, receiving it swiftly, began to eat. That householder, having served it hurriedly, having given all the food and drink of the cart without remainder — seized by fear, without even hearing the dedication of merit (<s>dakṣiṇādeśanā</s>), saying hurriedly "I salute you, venerable one," set out for the city without looking back.

body.text:
148.002. tasmānnagarāt piṇḍapātanirhārako bhikṣu tasyaiva piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā gataḥ/
148.003. tena tadapi bhuktam/
148.003. tasya dharmarucer na kadācidyato jātasya kuṣkiṃ pūrṇaḥ/
148.003. taddivasaṃ cāsya tenāhāreṇa tṛptirjātā/
148.004. tasya ca gṛhapater nagaraṃ praviśato 'bhimukhaṃ bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaḥ saṃprāptaḥ/
148.005. sa gṛhapatirbhagavataḥ kathayati--bhagavan, ahaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamuddiśya pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāṃ tṛptitaḥ śakaṭamannapānasya pūrayitvā jetavanaṃ gato buddhapramyukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti/
148.007. na ca me tatra bhikṣavo labdhāḥ/
148.007. eko me bhikṣurdṛṣṭaḥ/
148.007. tena samākhyātaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamantargṛham upanimantraṇaṃ praviṣṭam/
148.008. tasya mamaivaṃ cittamutpannam--eṣo 'pi tāvadeko bhuṅktāmiti/
148.009. yatastasya mamānupūrveṇa sarvaṃ tadannapānaṃ śakaṭaṃ dattam/
148.009. tena sarvaṃ nipuṇato 'bhyavahṛtam/
148.010. kiṃ bhagavan manuṣyo 'tha vā amanuṣyah? bhagavatābhihitam--gṛhapate, bhikṣuḥ sa dharmarucir nāṃnā/
148.011. prāmodyamutpādaya, adya sa tvadīyenānnapānnena tṛpto 'rhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati//
body.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> who brought alms-food from that city had taken his alms-food and gone. He ate that also. For <s>Dharmaruci</s>, from the time he was born, his belly had never been full. But on that day, by that food, satisfaction arose in him. And as that householder was entering the city, coming toward him the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s>, arrived. That householder said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, intending to feed the <s>saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, I filled a cart with food and drink sufficient to satisfy five hundred <s>bhikṣus</s> and went to <s>Jetavana</s>, thinking 'I shall feed the <s>saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.' But I did not find the <s>bhikṣus</s> there. I saw one <s>bhikṣu</s>. He informed me that the <s>saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> had entered a household upon invitation. Then this thought arose in me: 'Let at least this one eat.' Thereupon I gradually gave him all the food and drink of the entire cart. He consumed everything thoroughly. Is he, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a human being or a non-human?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: "Householder, that <s>bhikṣu</s> is named <s>Dharmaruci</s>. Generate joy! Today, satiated by your food and drink, he will realize <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship)."

body.text:
148.012. atha bhagavāñ jetavanamabhyāgataḥ/
148.012. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--ko 'sau dānapatirbhaviṣyati yo 'sau dharmaruceretāvatā āhāreṇa pratidivasam yogodvahanaṃ kariṣyati? yato 'sya bhagavatā abhihitam--dṛṣṭastvayā dharmaruce mahāsamudraḥ/
148.014. sa kathayati--no bhagavan/
148.014. yato bhagavānāha--gṛhāṇa madīyaṃ cīvarakarṇikam, paścāt te 'haṃ mahāsamudraṃ darśayāmi/
148.015. yato dharmarucinā bhagavataścīvarakarṇiko 'valambitaḥ, paścādbhagavān vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājaḥ sahacittotpādāt ṛddhyā dharmaruciṃ gṛhītvā samudrataṭamanuprāptaḥ/
148.017. yasmiṃścāsya sthāne timitimiṃgilabhūtasyāsthaśakalā tiṣṭhati, tatra nītvā sthāpitaḥ/
148.018. uktaṃ cāsya--gaccha vatsa, manasikāraṃ cintaya/
148.018. yato 'sau dhramarucistāṃ samīkṣitumārabdhaḥ/
148.019. kimetat kāṣṭhaṃ syādathāsthiśakalā, atha phalakinī syāt/
148.020. sa tasmād vyaktimalabhamānaḥ paryantamanveṣituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
148.020. vyaktiṃ copalabdham/
148.020. sa itaścāmutaśca tasyā anupārśvanaṃ tāṃ paryeṣamāṇaḥ śramamupagataḥ/
148.021. na cāsya paryantamāsādayati/
148.022. tasyaitadabhavat--nāhamasya vyaktiṃ jñāsyāmi kimetaditi, na ca paryantamāsādayiṣye/
148.022. gacchāmi, asminnarthe bhagavantameva pṛcchāmi/
148.023. yato 'sau bhagavato 'ntikaṃ gatvā bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati--kiṃ tadbhagavan? nāhaṃ tasya vyaktimupalabhāmi/
148.024. yato 'sya bhagavānāha--vatsa, asthiśakalaiṣā/
148.025. sa kathayati--bhagavan, evaṃvidho 'sau sattvo yasyedṛśī asthiśakalā? bhagavatoktam--tṛpyasva dharmaruce bhavebhyaḥ, tṛpyasva bhavopakaraṇebhyaḥ/
148.026. tavaiṣā asthiśakalā/
148.026. dharmarucistaṃ śrutvā bhagavadvaco vyākulitacetāḥ kathayati--mamaiṣedṛśī asthiśakalā? tasyoktam--eṣā dharmaruce tavāsthiśakalā/
148.028. tathāvidhamupaśrutya atīva saṃvignaḥ/
148.028. yato 'sya bhagavatā avavādo dattah--dharmaruce, idaṃ cedaṃ manasikuru/
148.029. ityuktvā bhagavān vitatapakṣa iva rājahaṃsa ṛddhyā jetavanamanuprāptaḥ/
148.030. atha dharmarucinā cintayatā manasikāramanutiṣṭhatā uṣmagatānyutpāditāni murdhānaḥ kṣāntayo laukikā agradharmā darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgaḥ/
148.031. srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptam/
148.032. sakṛdāgamiphalamanāgamiphalamarhattvaṃ prāptam/
148.032. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana <149>ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto 'nunayapratighaprahīṇo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukho vāsīcandanakalpaḥ/
body.translated_text:
148.012. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> returned to <s>Jetavana</s>.
148.012. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'Who will be the patron who will support <s>Dharmaruci</s> in his daily practice of yoga with such provisions of food?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him: 'Have you seen the great ocean, <s>Dharmaruci</s>?'
148.014. He said: 'No, Blessed One.'
148.014. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Hold on to the corner of my robe, and I shall show you the great ocean.'
148.015. When <s>Dharmaruci</s> had grasped the corner of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> robe, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, like a royal goose with outstretched wings, with the very arising of his thought, by supernatural power took <s>Dharmaruci</s> and reached the shore of the ocean.
148.017. He brought him to the place where his bone fragment lay from his former existence as a <s>Timitimiṃgila</s> (great sea-monster), and set him down there.
148.018. He said to him: 'Go, son, and contemplate with attention.'
148.018. Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> began to examine it.
148.019. 'What is this — is it a piece of wood, or a bone fragment, or a plank?'
148.020. Unable to discern its nature, he set out to find its extent.
148.020. He discerned its nature.
148.020. Going this way and that along its sides, searching for its end, he became exhausted.
148.021. Yet he could not reach its end.
148.022. He thought: 'I shall not be able to determine what this is, nor shall I find its end.
148.022. Let me go and ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this matter.'
148.023. He went to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and asked: 'What is that, Blessed One? I cannot discern its nature.'
148.024. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him: 'Son, this is a bone fragment.'
148.025. He said: 'Blessed One, what kind of being had such a bone fragment?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Be sated, <s>Dharmaruci</s>, with existences; be sated with the requisites of existence.
148.026. This is your own bone fragment.'
148.026. <s>Dharmaruci</s>, hearing the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, his mind agitated, said: 'Is this enormous bone fragment mine?' He was told: 'This is your bone fragment, <s>Dharmaruci</s>.'
148.028. Hearing such a thing, he was extremely shaken with spiritual urgency.
148.028. The <s>Bhagavān</s> then gave him instruction: '<s>Dharmaruci</s>, attend to this and that with mindfulness.'
148.029. Having spoken thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, like a royal goose, by supernatural power returned to <s>Jetavana</s>.
148.030. Then <s>Dharmaruci</s>, reflecting and applying mindful attention, generated the warmth, summit, patience, and supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s>, the path of seeing and the path of cultivation.
148.031. He attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
148.032. He attained the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).
148.032. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in all three realms, equal-minded toward a clod of earth and gold, with a mind as impartial as the sky and the palm of the hand, with attraction and aversion abandoned, whose egg-shell of ignorance was split open by knowledge, who had attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvits</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor, like a razor and sandalwood paste.

body.text:
149.002. sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
149.003. samanvāhartumātmanaḥ pūrvajātiṃ pravṛttah--kuto hyahaṃ cyutaḥ, kutropapanna iti/
149.014. yataḥ paśyati anekāni jātiśatāni narakatiryakpretacyutaścopapannaśca/
149.014. tasyaitadabhavat--yadahaṃ bhagavatā na samanvāhṛto 'bhaviṣyam, anāgatāsvapi jātiṣu upasṛto 'bhaviṣyam/
149.005. yataḥ saṃlakṣayati--anāgatāpyātmano jātisaṃtatir nirantaramanuparataprabandhena narakapretopapattiḥ/
149.006. sa evaṃ saṃlakṣya duṣkarakārako bata me bhagavān/
149.007. yadi ca bhagavatā mamaivaikasyārthe 'nuttarā samyaksambodhiradhigatā syāt, tanmahaddhi upakṛtaṃ syāt, prāgevānekeṣāṃ sattvasahasrāṇāmapāyagatigamanamapanayati/
149.009. tato 'sau dharmarucirṛddhyā jetavanamanuprāpto bhagavantaṃ darśanāya/
149.009. tena khalu samayena bhagavānanekaśatāyā bhikṣuparṣadaḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt/
149.010. dharmaṃ deśayati/
149.010. athāsau dharmaruciryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
149.011. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte nyaṣīdat/
149.012. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo bhagavatā abhihitah--cirasya dharmaruce? dharmaricirāha--cirasya bhagavan/
149.013. bhagavānāha--sucirasya dharmaruce? dharmarucirāha--sucirasya bhagavan/
149.013. bhagavānāha--suciracirasya dhramaruce? dharmarucirasya bhagavan//
body.translated_text:
149.002. He became worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and the sub-<s>Indras</s>.
149.003. He set about recollecting his former births: 'From where did I pass away, and where was I reborn?'
149.014. He saw that for many hundreds of births he had passed away from and been reborn in the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts.
149.014. He thought: 'If I had not been guided by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, I would have been caught in future births as well.'
149.005. He reflected: 'The unbroken, unceasing stream of my future births too would have continued as rebirths in hells and among hungry ghosts.'
149.006. Having reflected thus, he thought: 'Truly, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done what is difficult to do for me.
149.007. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> had attained unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment for the sake of me alone, even that would have been a great service — how much more so when he removes the passage to woeful destinies for many thousands of beings!'
149.009. Then <s>Dharmaruci</s>, by supernatural power, reached <s>Jetavana</s> for an audience with the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
149.009. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seated before a congregation of several hundred monks,
149.010. teaching the <s>Dharma</s>.
149.010. Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
149.011. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side.
149.012. Seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him: 'It has been a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>?' <s>Dharmaruci</s> replied: 'A long time, Blessed One.'
149.013. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>?' <s>Dharmaruci</s> replied: 'A very long time, Blessed One.'
149.013. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A very, very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>?' <s>Dharmaruci</s> replied: 'A very, very long time, Blessed One.'

body.text:
149.015. yato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--bhagavan dharmarucirihaiva śrāvastyāṃ jāto 'sminneva jetavane pravrajito na kutaścidāgato na kutracidgataḥ/
149.017. ihaiva tiṣṭhan bhagavatā dharmarucirevamucyate--cirasya dharmaruce, sucirasya dharmaruce, suciracirasya dharmaruce/
149.018. kiṃ saṃdhāya bhagavān kathayati? evamukte bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--na bhikṣavaḥ pratyutpannaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi/
149.019. atītaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi/
149.019. atītaṃ saṃdhāya mayaivamuktam/
149.019. icchatha bhikṣavo 'sya dharmaruceḥ pūrvikāṃ karmaplotimārabhya dhārmikathāṃ śrotum? etasya bhagavan kālaḥ, etasya sugata samayo yadbhagavān dharmarucimārabhya bhikṣūṇāṃ dhārmikathāṃ kuryāt/
149.021. bhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti//
body.translated_text:
149.015. Then the monks, filled with doubt, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the dispeller of all doubts: 'Blessed One, <s>Dharmaruci</s> was born right here in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, went forth right here in <s>Jetavana</s>, has not come from anywhere nor gone anywhere.
149.017. Standing right here, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says to <s>Dharmaruci</s>: "It has been a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; a very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; a very, very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>."
149.018. With what meaning does the <s>Bhagavān</s> say this?' When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Monks, I do not say this referring to the present.
149.019. I say this referring to the past.
149.019. Referring to the past, I have spoken thus.
149.019. Do you wish, monks, to hear the previous <s>karma</s> story concerning this <s>Dharmaruci</s>, a <s>Dharma</s> discourse?' 'This is the time, Blessed One; this is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>, for the <s>Bhagavān</s> to give a <s>Dharma</s> discourse concerning <s>Dharmaruci</s> to the monks.
149.021. Having heard it from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the monks will retain it.'

body.text:
149.023. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani prathame 'saṃkhyeye kṣemaṃkaro nāma tathāgato loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān/
149.025. sa ca kṣemāvatīṃ rājadhānīmupaniśritya viharati/
149.025. tasyāṃ ca kṣemāvatyāṃ kṣemo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati/
149.026. tasyāṃ ca kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanyatamo vaṇikśreṣṭhī prativasati/
149.027. tenāsau kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ traimāsān sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena sarvopakaraṇairupasthitaḥ/
149.028. yato 'sau śreṣṭhī saṃlakṣayati--gacchāmi mahāsamudram/
149.028. bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya tasmācca ratnānyānīya saṃghe pañcavārṣikaṃ kariṣyāmīti/
149.029. evaṃ saṃcintya bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīya grāmanigamapallīpattanarājadhānīṣvanupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇaḥ samudramanuprāptaḥ/
149.030. ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā sāmudreṇa yānapātreṇa mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
149.031. asya tasmin mahāsamudre 'vatīrṇasya kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalambuddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ/
149.032. tasya parinirvṛtasya vaśino bhikṣavah <150>parinirvṛtāḥ/
body.translated_text:
149.023. In the past, monks, long ago, in the first incalculable <s>kalpa</s> (eon), a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> ('Maker of Safety') arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
149.025. He dwelt near the royal capital called <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>.
149.025. In that <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>, a king named <s>Kṣema</s> ruled the kingdom.
149.026. In that royal capital of <s>Kṣemāvatī</s> there lived a certain chief merchant.
149.027. He had served the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> together with the community of monks for sixty three-month periods with all requisites.
149.028. Then that merchant reflected: 'I shall go to the great ocean.
149.028. Having assembled merchandise, I shall bring back jewels from there, and shall hold a quinquennial festival for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'
149.029. Having decided thus, he assembled his merchandise and, traveling in due order through villages, towns, hamlets, ports, and royal capitals, arrived at the ocean.
149.030. He announced the departure with the sounding of a bell and descended into the great ocean in a seagoing vessel.
149.031. While he had descended into the great ocean, the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, having completed all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without residue.
149.032. After his passing, his faithful monks also passed into final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text:
150.001. saptāhaparinirvṛtasya śāsanamantarhitam/
150.001. sa ca śreṣṭhī saṃsiddhayānapātreṇa devatāmānuṣyaparigṛhītena tasmānmahāsamudrāt tīrṇaḥ/
150.002. uttīrya ca taṃ bhāṇḍaṃ śakaṭairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiśca cotkṣipya anupūrveṇa saṃprasthitaḥ/
150.003. sa ca panthānaṃ gacchan prātipathikān pṛcchati--kiṃ bhavanto jānīdhvaṃ kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ pravṛttih? tairuktam--jānīmaḥ/
150.004. sa kathayati--asti kaścit kṣemāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ kṣemaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddhah? te kathayanti--parinirvṛtaḥ sa bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ/
150.006. sa ca tacchrutvā paraṃ khedamupagataḥ/
150.006. saṃmūrchitaśca bhūmau patitaḥ/
150.007. tasmācca jalābhiṣekeṇa pratyāgataprāṇo jīvita utthāya bhūyaḥ pṛcchati--kiṃ bhavanto jānīdhvaṃ śrāvakā api tāvattasya bhagavatastiṣṭhanti? tairuktah--te 'pi vaśino bhikṣavaḥ parinirvṛtāḥ/
150.009. saptāhaparinirvṛtasya ca buddhasya bhagavataḥ kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya kṣemeṇa rājñā caityamalpeśākhyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
150.010. tena ca gatvā śreṣṭhinā janapadāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ/
150.010. asti bhavantastasya bhagavato buddhasya kiṃcit stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
150.011. tairuktam--asti, kṣemeṇa rājñā alpeśākhyaṃ caityaṃ pratiṣṭhapitam/
150.012. tasya etadabhavat--etaṃ mayā suvarṇaṃ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksambuddham uddiśyānītam/
150.013. sa ca parinirvṛtaḥ/
150.013. yannvahametenaiva suvarṇena tasyaiva bhagavataścaityaṃ maheśākhyataraṃ kārayeyam/
150.014. evaṃ vicintya kṣemaṃ rājānaṃ vijñāpayati--mahārāja, idaṃ mayā suvarṇaṃ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksambuddhamuddiśyānītam/
150.015. sa ca bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ/
150.015. idānīṃ mahārāja yadi tvamanujānīyāt, ahametenaiva suvarṇenaitat tasya bhagavataścaityaṃ maheśākhyataraṃ kārayeyam/
150.016. sa rājñā abhihitah--yathābhipretaṃ kuru/
150.017. tato brāhmaṇā nagaraṃ prati nivāsinaḥ saṃbhūya sarve tasya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayanti--bho mahāśreṣṭhin, yadā kṣemaṃkaro buddho loke 'nutpanna āsīt, tadā vayaṃ lokasya dakṣiṇīyā āsan/
150.019. yadā tūtpannaḥ, tadā dakṣiṇīyo jātaḥ/
150.019. idānīṃ tu tasya parinirvṛtasya vayameva dakṣiṇīyāḥ/
150.020. etat suvarṇamasmākaṃ gamyam/
150.020. sa teṣāṃ kathayati--nāham yuṣmākametat suvarṇaṃ dāsyāmi/
150.021. te kathayanti--yadyasmākaṃ na dāsyasi, na vayaṃ tava kāmakāraṃ dāsyāmaḥ/
150.022. te brāhmaṇā bahavaḥ, śreṣṭhī cālpaparivāraḥ/
150.022. teṣāṃ tathā vyutpadyatāṃ na lebhe taccaityam yathepsitaṃ tena suvarṇena kārayitum/
150.023. atha sa śreṣṭhī rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--mahārāja, taccaityaṃ na labhe brāhmaṇānāṃ sakāśādyathābhipretaṃ kārayitum/
150.024. yato 'sya rājñā svapuruṣo dattaḥ sahasrayodhī/
150.025. evaṃ ca rājñā svapuruṣa ājñaptah--yadyasya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ stūpamabhisaṃskurvataḥ kaścidapanayaṃ karoti, sa tvayā mahatā daṇḍena śāsayitavyaḥ/
150.026. evaṃ deveti sahasrayodhī puruṣo rājñaḥ pratiśrutya nirgataḥ/
150.027. nirgamya ca tān brāhmaṇānevaṃ vadati--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ, ahaṃ rājñāsya mahāśreṣṭhinaḥ svapuruṣo dattah--yadyasya stūpamabhisaṃskurvataḥ kaścidvighātaṃ kuryāt, sa tvayā mahatā daṇḍena śāsayitavya iti/
150.029. yadi yūyamatra kiṃcid vighnaṃ kariṣyatha, ahaṃ vo mahatā daṇḍenānuśāsayiṣyāmi/
150.030. te brāhmaṇāḥ sahasrayodhinaḥ puruṣasyaivaṃ śrutvā bhītāḥ/
150.030. yatastena mahāśreṣṭhinā saṃcintya yathaitat suvarṇaṃ tatraiva garbhasaṃsthaṃ syāt tathā kartavyamiti tasya stūpasya sarvaireva caturbhiḥ pārśvaiḥ pratikaṇṭhukayā catvāri sopānāni ārabdhāni kārayitum/
150.032. yāvadanupūrveṇa<151> prathamā meḍhī tato 'nupūrveṇa dvitīyā tatastṛtīyā meḍhī yāvadanupūrveṇāṇḍam/
body.translated_text:
150.001. Seven days after the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, the teaching disappeared.
150.001. And that merchant, with a successfully completed vessel guided by deities and humans, crossed over from that great ocean.
150.002. Having crossed, he loaded those goods onto carts, camels, oxen, and donkeys, and set out in due course.
150.003. As he was traveling along the road, he asked those coming from the opposite direction: 'Do you know, sirs, what is happening in the royal capital <s>Kṣemavatī</s>?' They said: 'We know.'
150.004. He asks: 'Is there still in the royal capital <s>Kṣemavatī</s> a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>?' They say: 'That Blessed One <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.'
150.006. Hearing that, he was overcome with extreme grief.
150.006. He fainted and fell to the ground.
150.007. Revived by a sprinkling of water, he rose up alive and asked again: 'Do you know, sirs, whether at least the disciples of that Blessed One still remain?' They said: 'Those accomplished monks too have passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.'
150.009. Seven days after the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) called <s>Alpeśākhya</s> ('Of Small Renown') was established by King <s>Kṣema</s>.
150.010. The merchant, having gone there, asked the country-folk:
150.010. 'Has any <s>stūpa</s> been established for that Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, sirs?'
150.011. They said: 'Yes, a <s>caitya</s> called <s>Alpeśākhya</s> has been established by King <s>Kṣema</s>.'
150.012. This thought occurred to him: 'This gold was brought by me dedicated to the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>.
150.013. He has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.
150.013. What if I, with this very gold, were to have a <s>caitya</s> of great renown made for that very Blessed One?'
150.014. Having thus reflected, he petitions King <s>Kṣema</s>: 'Great King, this gold was brought by me dedicated to the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>.
150.015. That Blessed One has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.
150.015. Now, Great King, if you would permit it, I would have a <s>caitya</s> of greater renown made for that Blessed One with this very gold.'
150.016. The king said to him: 'Do as you wish.'
150.017. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> dwelling in the city, having assembled together, all went to that great merchant and said: 'O great merchant, when the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> had not yet arisen in the world, we were the ones worthy of offerings from the people.
150.019. When he arose, he became the one worthy of offerings.
150.019. Now that he has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, we alone are the ones worthy of offerings.
150.020. This gold should come to us.'
150.020. He said to them: 'I will not give you this gold.'
150.021. They said: 'If you will not give it to us, we will not grant you free passage.'
150.022. Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were many, and the merchant had but a small retinue.
150.022. Due to their opposition, he was unable to have that <s>caitya</s> made as he wished with that gold.
150.023. Then the merchant, going to the king, said: 'Great King, I am unable to have that <s>caitya</s> made as I wish because of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.'
150.024. Thereupon the king gave him his own man, a warrior of a thousand battles.
150.025. And the king instructed his man thus: 'If anyone creates an obstruction for this great merchant as he constructs the <s>stūpa</s>, he is to be punished by you with a great penalty.'
150.026. 'Yes, Your Majesty' — the warrior of a thousand battles assented to the king and went forth.
150.027. Having gone forth, he said to those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>: 'Listen, sirs: I have been given by the king as this great merchant's own man — if anyone creates an obstruction for him as he constructs the <s>stūpa</s>, he is to be punished by me with a great penalty.
150.029. If you create any obstruction here, I will discipline you with a great penalty.'
150.030. Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, hearing the warrior of a thousand battles, were frightened.
150.030. Then that great merchant, having planned that this gold should be incorporated into the very core of the structure, began to have four staircases constructed on all four sides of that <s>stūpa</s>, with a surrounding parapet.
150.032. Gradually, <151> the first terrace, then in due course the second, then the third terrace, and so on up to the dome.

body.text:
151.001. tathāvidhaṃ ca stūpasyāṇḍaṃ kṛtam yatra sā yūpayaṣṭirabhyantare pratipāditā/
151.002. paścāt tasyātinavāṇḍasyopari harmikā kṛtā/
151.003. anupūrveṇa yaṣṭyāropaṇaṃ kṛtam/
151.003. varṣasthāle mahāmaṇiratnāni tānyāropitāni/
151.004. tatra ca kriyamāṇe sahasrayodhinaḥ puruṣasyaivamutpannam--nātra kaścididānīṃ prahariṣyati/
151.005. viśvastamanāḥ kenacitkāryeṇa janapadeṣu gataḥ/
151.005. tena ca mahāśreṣṭhinā tasya stūpasya caturbhiḥ pārśvaiścatvāro dvārakoṣṭhakā māpitāḥ, caturbhiḥ pārśvaiścatvāri mahācaityāni kāritāni, tadyathā jātirabhisambodhirdharmacakrapravartanaṃ parinirvāṇam/
151.007. tacca stūpāṅgaṇaṃ ratnaśilābhiścitam/
151.008. catvāraścopāṅgāścaturdiśaṃ māpitāḥ/
151.008. puṣkariṇyaścaturdiśamanupārśvena māpitāḥ/
151.008. tatra ca vividhāni jalajāni mālyāni ropitāni tadyathā utpalaṃ padmaṃ kumudaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sugandhikaṃ mṛdugandhikam/
151.010. vividhāni ca puṣkariṇītīreṣu sthalajāni mālyāni ropitāni, tadyathā atimuktakaṃ campakapāṭalāvārṣikāmallikāsumanāyūthikā dhātuṣkārī/
151.012. sarvartukālikāḥ puṣpaphalāḥ stūpapūjārtham/
151.012. sthāvarā vṛttiḥ prajñaptāḥ/
151.012. stūpadāsā dattāḥ/
151.013. śaṅkhapaṭahavādyāni tūryāṇi dattāni/
151.013. ye tasmiṃścaitye gandhairdhūpairmālyaiśca cūrṇaiḥ kārāḥ kurvanti/
151.014. tasmāccādhiṣṭhānādviṣayāccāgamya janapadā gandhairmālyairdhūpaiścūrṇaistasmiṃścaitye kāraṃ kurvanti/
151.014. yadi ca dakṣiṇo vāyurvāti, dakṣiṇena vāyunā sarvapuṣpajātīnāṃ gandhena taccaityamaṅgaṇaṃ cāsya sphuṭaṃ bhavatyanubhāvitam/
151.016. evaṃ paścimena vāyunā, anupūrveṇāpi ca vāyunā/
151.016. vāyatā vāyatā taccaityāṅgaṇaṃ ca tena vividhena gandhamālyena sphuṭaṃ bhavatyanubhāvitam/
151.017. tasmiṃśca stūpe sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭite sahasrayodhī abhyāgataḥ/
151.018. sa taṃ stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvajātakṛtaniṣṭhitaṃ kathayati--asmiṃścaitye kārāṃ kṛtvā kimavāpyate? yato 'sau śreṣṭhī buddhodāharaṇaṃ pravṛttaḥ kartum--evaṃ tribhirasaṃkhyeyairvīryeṇa vyāyamatā anuttarā bodhiravāpyate/
151.020. sa taṃ śrutvā viṣādamāpanno hīnotsāhatayā kathayati--nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ samudānayitum/
151.021. tato 'sau śreṣṭhī pratyekabuddhodāharaṇaṃ pravṛttaḥ kartum--evaṃ sahasrayodhī tasyāpi varṇodāharaṇaṃ śrutvā viṣaṇṇacetāḥ kathayati--etāmapyahaṃ pratyekabodhiṃ na śaktaḥ samudānayitum/
151.023. tataḥ sa mahāśreṣṭhī śrāvakavarṇodāharaṇaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--asminnapi tāvat praṇidhatsva cittam/
151.024. yataḥ sahasrayodhyāha--tvayā punarmahāśreṣṭhin katamasyāṃ bodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam? tena mahāśreṣṭhinoktam--anuttarasyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam/
151.026. sahasrayodhyāha--yadi tvayā anuttarasyāṃ bodhau cittamutpāditam, ahaṃ tavaiva śrāvakaḥ syām/
151.027. tvayāhaṃ samanvāhartavyaḥ/
151.027. yato 'sya śreṣṭhī āhabahukilbiṣakārī bata bhavān/
151.028. kiṃ tu loke yadā tvaṃ buddhotpādaśabdaṃ śrutvā smṛtiṃ pratilabhethāḥ/
151.029. sa ca śreṣṭhī taṃ caityaṃ kṛtvā nirīkṣya pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ karoti--
