151.030. anena dānena mahadgatena buddho bhaveyaṃ sugataḥ svayambhūḥ/
151.032. tīrṇo 'haṃ tārayeyaṃ janaughānatāritā ye paurvakairjinendraiḥ//1//
body.translated_text:
151.001. And such a dome of the <s>stūpa</s> was made that the central pillar was accommodated within its interior.
151.002. Afterward, upon the top of that newly-made dome, a <s>harmikā</s> (railing enclosure) was constructed.
151.003. Gradually, the mounting of the pillar was completed.
151.003. Great jewel-gems were placed upon the rain-collector.
151.004. While this was being done, the warrior of a thousand battles thought: 'No one will attack now.'
151.005. With a trusting mind, he went to the provinces on some business.
151.005. And that great merchant had four gate-chambers constructed on the four sides of that <s>stūpa</s>, and on the four sides four great <s>caityas</s> were made depicting the four events: birth, enlightenment, the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, and <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.
151.007. The courtyard of the <s>stūpa</s> was paved with jeweled slabs.
151.008. Four subsidiary shrines were constructed in the four directions.
151.008. Lotus ponds were laid out on the sides in the four directions.
151.008. There, various aquatic flowers were planted, namely <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily), <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus), <s>sugandhika</s> (fragrant lotus), and <s>mṛdugandhika</s> (soft-scented lotus).
151.010. And various land-growing flowers were planted on the banks of the ponds, namely <s>atimukta</s> (jasmine), <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭala</s>, <s>vārṣika</s>, <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), <s>sumanā</s>, <s>yūthikā</s> (jasmine), and <s>dhātuṣkārī</s>.
151.012. Flowers and fruits of all seasons were dedicated for the worship of the <s>stūpa</s>.
151.012. A permanent endowment was established.
151.012. Servants for the <s>stūpa</s> were assigned.
151.013. Conch-shells, drums, and musical instruments were provided.
151.013. Those who perform worship at that <s>caitya</s> with perfumes, incense, garlands, and powders;
151.014. and from that district and from surrounding regions, country-folk came and performed worship at that <s>caitya</s> with perfumes, garlands, incense, and powders.
151.014. And when a southern wind blew, by the southern wind the fragrance of all kinds of flowers pervaded and perfumed the entire courtyard of that <s>caitya</s>.
151.016. Likewise by the western wind, and gradually by every wind.
151.016. As the winds blew, the <s>caitya</s> courtyard was pervaded and perfumed by that varied fragrance of flowers.
151.017. When the <s>stūpa</s>, fully completed in every respect, was finished, the warrior of a thousand battles returned.
151.018. Seeing that <s>stūpa</s> fully completed in every respect, he said: 'What is gained by performing worship at this <s>caitya</s>?' Then the merchant began to give an account of the <s>Buddha</s>: 'Thus, by striving with effort through three incalculable aeons, unsurpassed awakening is attained.'
151.020. Hearing that, he became despondent and, with diminished enthusiasm, said: 'I will not be able to accomplish unsurpassed perfect awakening.'
151.021. Then that merchant began to give an account of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> — likewise the warrior of a thousand battles, having heard the praise and account of that too, said with a disheartened mind: 'I am not able to accomplish even solitary awakening.'
151.023. Then the great merchant, having given an account praising the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple), said: 'Then at least set your mind upon this.'
151.024. The warrior of a thousand battles said: 'But you, great merchant, in which awakening have you made your aspiration?' The great merchant said: 'I have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed awakening.'
151.026. The warrior of a thousand battles said: 'If you have generated the aspiration for unsurpassed awakening, I shall be your disciple.
151.027. You must look after me.'
151.027. The merchant said to him: 'Alas, sir, you are one who has done many misdeeds.
151.028. But when in this world you hear the word of a <s>Buddha</s>'s arising, may you then regain mindfulness.'
151.029. Then the merchant, having made that <s>caitya</s>, gazed upon it, fell at its feet, and made an aspiration:
151.030. 'By this great and lofty gift, may I become a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Self-Arisen One;
151.032. having crossed over, may I ferry across the great floods of beings who were not ferried across by the former Lords of Victors.' //1//

body.text:
152.001. <152>bhagavānāha--yo 'sau atīte 'dhvani śreṣṭhī abhūt, ahameva sa tasmin samaye bodhisattvacaryāṃ vartāmi/
152.002. yo 'sau sahasrayodhī, eṣa eva dharmarucistena kālena tena samayena/
152.003. idaṃ mama prathame 'saṃkhyeye etasya dharmarucerdarśanam/
152.003. tatsaṃdhāya kathayāmi--cirasya dharmaruce/
152.004. yato dharmarucirājñāyāha--cirasya bhagavan//
body.translated_text:
152.001. <152>The Blessed One said: 'He who was that merchant in the past — I myself was he at that time, practicing the conduct of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
152.002. He who was the warrior of a thousand battles — he is this very <s>Dharmaruci</s>, at that time, in that era.
152.003. This was my first encounter with this <s>Dharmaruci</s> in the first incalculable aeon.
152.003. With reference to that I say: "After a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>!"
152.004. Then <s>Dharmaruci</s> understood and said: "After a long time, Blessed One!"'

body.text:
152.005. dvitīye dīpaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddho loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasamyaksambuddhaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān/
152.006. atha dīpamakaraḥ samyaksambuddho janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran dvīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ/
152.007. dvīpāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ dvīpo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
152.009. tatra dīpena rājñā dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ/
152.010. tasya ca dīpasya rājño vāsavo nāma sāmantarājo 'bhūt/
152.010. tena tasya dūto 'nupreṣitah--āgaccha, iha mayā dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ/
152.011. tasya pūjāṃ kariṣyāma iti/
152.012. tadā ca vāsavena rājñā dvādaśavarṣāṇi yajñamiṣṭvā yajñāvasāne rājñā pañca mahāpradānāni vyavasthāpitāni, tadyathā--sauvarṇakaṃ daṇḍakamaṇḍalu, sauvarṇā sapātrī, catūratnamayī śayyā, pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni, kanyā ca sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā/
152.014. tena khalu samayena anyeṣu janapadeṣu dvau māṇavakau prativasataḥ/
152.015. tābhyāṃ copadhyāyasakāśādvedādhyayanaṃ kṛtam/
152.016. dharmatā ācāryasyācāryadhanamupādhyāyasyopādhyāyadhanaṃ pradeyamiti jñātvā cintayataḥ/
152.017. tābhyāṃ ca śrutaṃ vāsavena rājñā pañca mahāpradānāni yajñāvasāne samudānītāni, yo brāhmaṇaḥ svādhyāyasampanno bhaviṣyati sa lapsyatīti/
152.018. tayoretadabhavat--gacchavastatra, taṃ pradānaṃ pratigṛhṇīvaḥ/
152.019. ko 'smākaṃ tatra bahuśrutatamo vā svādhyāyatamo bhaviṣyatīti saṃcintya yena vāsavasya rājño mahānagaraṃ tena saṃprasthitau/
152.020. tasya ca rājño devatayā ārocitam/
152.020. yau etau dvau māṇavakau āgacchataḥ sumatiśca matiśca, anayordvayoḥ sumateretatpradānaṃ dada/
152.021. yadevaṃ dvau māṇakakau āgacchataḥ sumitaśca matiśca, anayordvayoḥ sumateretatpradānaṃ dada/
152.021.yadevaṃ mahārāja tvayā dvādaśa varṣāṇi yajña iṣṭaḥ, asmāt puṇyaphalānmahattamapadasya sumatermāṇavakasya mahāpradānaṃ dāsyasi/
152.023. sa rājā saṃlakṣayati--nūnametau mahātmānau yeṣāmāmarthāya devatā apyārocayanti/
152.024. yato 'sau rājā paśyati māṇavakau dūrata evāgacchantau agrasanamībhiruhyavasthitau/
152.025. yato rājā vāsavastyau sumatiṃ māṇavaṃ pṛcchati--bhavān sumati? tenoktam--aham/
152.028. yato rājā vāsavaḥ sumatiṃ māṇavamagrāsane bhojayitvā pañca pradānāni prayacchati/
152.029. sumatirmāṇavaścatvāri mahāpradānāni gṛhṇāti daṇḍakamaṇḍaluprabhṛtīni, ekaṃ kanyāpradānaṃ na pratigṛhṇāti/
152.030. sa kathayati--ahaṃ brahmacārī/
152.030. yataḥ sā kanyā sumatiṃ māṇavaṃ prāsādikamabhirūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā lubdhā snehotpannā, taṃ sumatiṃ māṇavamevamāha--pratigṛhṇa māṃ brāhmaṇa/
152.032. sa kathayati--na śakyaṃ pratigṛhītum/
152.032. yataḥ sā kanyā rājñā pradānabuddhyā parityaktā <153>na punargṛhītā, sumatināpi māṇavenāpratigṛhyamāṇā rājño dīpasya dīpāvatīṃ nagarīṃ gatā/
body.translated_text: In the second [age], a perfectly awakened one named <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, wandering on a teaching tour through the countries, arrived at the royal capital <s>Dvīpāvatī</s>. In the royal capital <s>Dvīpāvatī</s>, a king named <s>Dvīpa</s> was ruling — the kingdom was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. There, King <s>Dvīpa</s> invited <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, for a formal entry into the city with elaborate preparations. King <s>Dvīpa</s> had a vassal king named <s>Vāsava</s>. He sent a messenger to him: 'Come; I have invited <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, for a formal entry into the city with elaborate preparations. We shall make offerings to him.' At that time, King <s>Vāsava</s>, having performed a sacrifice for twelve years, at the conclusion of the sacrifice had arranged five great gifts, namely: a golden staff and water-pot, a golden vessel with its tray, a couch made of the four precious substances, five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), and a maiden adorned with all ornaments. At that time, in other countries, two young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> students were dwelling. They had studied the <s>Vedas</s> under their preceptor. Knowing that it is the custom to give the teacher's fee to the teacher and the preceptor's fee to the preceptor, they reflected. They heard that King <s>Vāsava</s> had prepared five great gifts at the conclusion of his sacrifice, and that whichever <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would be accomplished in recitation would receive them. They thought: 'Let us go there and receive that gift.' Thinking — 'Which of us will be the most learned or the most accomplished in recitation?' — they set out for the great city of King <s>Vāsava</s>. A deity informed the king: 'These two young men are coming — <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Mati</s>. Of these two, give the gift to <s>Sumati</s>. If so, O great king, since you have performed the sacrifice for twelve years, from the meritorious fruit thereof you shall give the great gift to the young man <s>Sumati</s>, who is destined for the highest attainment.' The king reflected: 'Surely these are great souls, for whose sake even the deities give notice.' Then the king saw the two young men coming from afar, who stood upon their foremost seats. King <s>Vāsava</s> asked the young man <s>Sumati</s>: 'Are you <s>Sumati</s>?' He replied: 'I am.' Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, having fed <s>Sumati</s> the young man in the foremost seat, offered him the five gifts. <s>Sumati</s> the young man accepted four of the great gifts — the staff, water-pot, and so forth — but did not accept the one gift of the maiden. He said: 'I am a celibate.' Thereupon, that maiden, having seen the handsome and pleasing young man <s>Sumati</s>, became infatuated and enamored, and said to <s>Sumati</s> the young man: 'Accept me, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' He replied: 'It is not possible for me to accept you.' Because that maiden had been given away by the king as a gift and was not taken back, and was also not accepted by <s>Sumati</s> the young man, she went to the city of <s>Dvīpāvatī</s> of King <s>Dvīpa</s>.

body.text:
153.002. sā tatra gatvā tadātmīyamalaṃkāraṃ śarīrādavatārya mālākārāyānuprayacchati--asyālaṃkārasya mūlyaṃ me pratidivasaṃ devasyārthe nīlotpalāni dadasva/
153.003. sā tenopakrameṇa tadalaṃkārikaṃ suvarṇaṃ datvā devaśuśraūṣikā saṃvṛttā/
153.004. sa ca māṇavakaḥ sumatistāni catvāri mahāpradānāni gṛhya upādhyāyasakāśaṃ gataḥ/
153.005. gatvā copādhyāyāya tāni catvāri mahāpradānānyanuprayacchati/
153.006. tebhyaścopādhyāyastrīṇi pratigṛhṇāti, kārṣāpaṇānāṃ tu pañca śatāni tasyaiva sumaterdadāti/
153.006. sa ca sumatistasyāmeva rātrau daśa svapnānadrākṣīt--mahāsamudraṃ pibāmi, vaihāyasena gacchāmi, imau candrādityau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau pāṇinā āmārṣṭi parimārṣṭi, rājño rathe yojayāmi ṛṣīn, śvetān hastinaḥ, haṃsān, siṃhān, mahāśailaṃ parvatāniti/
153.009. sa tān dṛṣṭvā pratibuddhaḥ/
153.010. pratibuddhasyaitadabhavat--ka eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ mama vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyati? tatra pañcābhijña ṛṣir nātidūre prativasati/
153.011. atha sumatirmāṇavaḥ saṃśayanirṇayanārtham ṛṣeḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
153.012. sumatistasya ṛṣeḥ pratisaṃmodanaṃ kṛtvā svapnānākhyāyāha--kuruṣva me eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ nirṇayam/
153.013. sa ṛṣirāha--nāhameṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyāmi/
153.013. gaccha dīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīm/
153.013. tatra dīpena rājñā dīpaṃkaro nāma samyaksambuddhaḥ sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ/
153.014. sa eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ kariṣyati/
153.015. atha vāsavo rājā tasya dīpasya rājñaḥ pratiśrutya aśītyamātyasahasraparivṛto dīpāvatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptaḥ/
153.016. tena ca dīpena rājñā saptamāddivasāddīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśaṃ kariṣyāmīti sarvaviṣayādhiṣṭhānāñca sarvapuṣpāṇāṃ saṃgrahaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
153.018. tatra ca yasmin divase rājñā dīpena tasya dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya sābhisaṃskāreṇa nagarapraveśa ārabdhaḥ kartum, tasminneva divase sumatirapi tatraivāgataḥ/
153.020. tatra rājñā sarvapuṣpāṇāṃ saṃgrahaḥ kāritaḥ/
153.020. sā ca devopasthāyikā dārikā mālākārasakāśaṃ gatā--prayaccha me nīlotpalāni, devārcanaṃ kariṣyāmīti/
153.022. mālākāra āha--adya rājñā sarvapuṣpāṇi gṛhītāni dīpaṃkaranagarapraveśasyārthe/
153.022. sā kathayati--gacchata, punarapi tatra puṣkiriṇyām yadi matpuṇyair nīlotpalapadmamanuddhṛtamāsādyeta/
153.023. tatra puṣkiriṇyāṃ sumateḥ puṇyānubhāvāt sapta nīlapadmāni prādurbhūtāni/
153.024. yataḥ sa mālākāro gataḥ, sa tāni paśyati/
153.025. dṛṣṭvā ca dārikayā mālākārasyoktam--uddharaitāni padmāni/
153.025. mālākāraḥ kathayati--nāhamuddhariṣyāmi/
153.026. rājakulānmamopālambho bhaviṣyati/
153.026. yataḥ sā kathayati--na/
153.027. tvayā sarvapuṣpāṇyuddhṛtya rājñaḥ pūrvaṃ dattānyeva/
153.027. mālākāra āha--datāni/
153.027. yataḥ sā dārikā kathayati--madīyaiḥ puṇyairetāni prādurbhūtāni, prayacchoddhṛtāni mama/
153.028. mālākāraḥ kathayati--kathametāni praveśakāni bhaviṣyantyasaṃviditaṃ rājakulasya? dārikā āha--uddharatu bhavān/
153.030. ahamudakakumbhe prakṣiptaṃ praveśayiṣyāmi/
153.030. tena mālākāreṇaivaṃ śrutvā tasyā dārikayāstānyuddhṛtya anupradattāni/
153.031. sā tāni gṛhītvā udakakumbhe prakṣipya tatkumbhamudakasya pūrayitvā adhiṣṭhānaṃ gatā prasthitā/
153.032. sa ca sumatistatsthānamanusamprāptaḥ/
153.032. tasyaitadabhavat--kathamahaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam <154>dṛṣṭvā na pūjayāmi? sa mālākāragṛhāṇyanvāhiṇḍati sarvapuṣpānveṣaṇaparaḥ, na ca kiṃcidekapuṣpamāsādayati/
body.translated_text: Having gone there, she removed her own ornaments from her body and gave them to a garland-maker, saying: 'With the value of these ornaments, give me blue lotuses daily for the worship of the god.' By that arrangement, having given the gold from her ornaments, she became a temple attendant. The young man <s>Sumati</s>, having taken those four great gifts, went to his preceptor. Having gone, he offered the four great gifts to his preceptor. The preceptor accepted three of them, but gave the five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> back to <s>Sumati</s> himself. That very night, <s>Sumati</s> saw ten dreams: 'I am drinking the great ocean; I am traveling through the sky; I am wiping and polishing these sun and moon, of such great power and great might, with my hand; I am yoking <s>ṛṣis</s> to the king's chariot; white elephants, geese, lions, a great mountain of rock.' Having seen these, he awoke. Upon awakening, he thought: 'Who will interpret these dreams for me?' There, not far away, dwelt a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) possessing the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Then <s>Sumati</s> the young man went to the <s>ṛṣi</s> to have his doubts resolved. <s>Sumati</s>, having exchanged greetings with the <s>ṛṣi</s>, recounted his dreams and said: 'Please interpret these dreams for me.' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'I shall not interpret these dreams. Go to the royal capital <s>Dvīpāvatī</s>. There, King <s>Dvīpa</s> has invited <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, for a formal entry into the city with elaborate preparations. He will interpret these dreams.' Then King <s>Vāsava</s>, having assented to King <s>Dvīpa</s>, surrounded by eighty thousand ministers, arrived at the royal capital <s>Dvīpāvatī</s>. King <s>Dvīpa</s> had begun to collect all the flowers from all the territories and dominions from the seventh day onward, intending: 'I shall conduct the formal entry of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, with elaborate preparations.' On the very day when King <s>Dvīpa</s> began to conduct the formal city-entry of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the perfectly awakened one, on that very day <s>Sumati</s> also arrived there. The king had ordered the collection of all flowers. That girl, the temple attendant, went to the garland-maker: 'Give me blue lotuses; I shall perform the worship of the god.' The garland-maker said: 'Today all the flowers have been taken by the king for the city-entry of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>.' She said: 'Go again; perhaps in that lotus-pond, by my merit, some blue lotuses or lotuses may be found still unplucked.' In that lotus-pond, by the power of <s>Sumati</s>'s merit, seven blue lotuses had appeared. The garland-maker went there and saw them. Having seen them, the girl said to the garland-maker: 'Pick up those lotuses.' The garland-maker said: 'I shall not pick them up. There will be a rebuke from the royal court.' She said: 'No. You have already picked all the flowers and given them to the king previously.' The garland-maker said: 'That is so.' The girl said: 'These have appeared by my merit; give them to me once picked.' The garland-maker said: 'How will these be allowed in without the knowledge of the royal court?' The girl said: 'Pick them up, sir. I shall bring them in hidden inside a water-pot.' The garland-maker, having heard this, picked them up and gave them to the girl. She, having taken them, put them in a water-pot, filled it with water, and set out for the sanctuary. <s>Sumati</s> too arrived at that very place. He thought: 'How can I see the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> and not make an offering?' He wandered through the garland-makers' shops, searching everywhere for flowers, but could not find even a single flower.

body.text:
154.002. paścādbāhyenādhiṣṭhānānnirgamya ārāmeṇārāmaṃ puṣpāṇi paryeṣamāṇaḥ paryaṭati, na caikapuṣpamāsādayati/
154.003. atha paryaṭamānastadudyānaṃ saṃprāptaḥ/
154.003. sā ca dārikā tasmādudyānāt tasya sumatermāṇavasyābhimukhamāgatā/
154.004. yataḥ puṇyānubhāvena tāni nīlapadmāni tasmādudakakumbhādabhyudgatāni/
154.005. yatastāni sumatirdṛṣṭvā tasyā dārikāyāḥ kathayati--prayaccha mamaitāni padmāni/
154.006. matsakāśādeṣāṃ niṣkrayaṃ pañcakārṣāpaṇaśataṃ gṛhāṇa/
154.006. sā dārikā tasya sumateḥ kathayati--tadā necchasi māṃ pratigṛhītum/
154.007. idānīṃ māṃ padmāni yācase/
154.007. nāhaṃ dāsyāmi/
154.008. evamuktvā taṃ sumatiṃ māṇavamuvāca--kimebhiḥ kariṣyasi? sumatirāha--buddhaṃ bhagavantamarcayiṣyāmi/
154.009. paścāddārikā kathayati--kiṃ mama kārṣāpaṇaiḥ kṛtyam? evamahaṃ buddhāya dāsye, yadi tvameṣāṃ padmānāṃ pradānaphalena mamāpi jātyāṃ jātyāṃ patnīmicchasi, asya dānasya pradānakāle yadyevaṃ praṇidhānaṃ karoṣi--jātyāṃ jātyāṃ mama bhāryā syāditi/
154.011. sumatirāha--vayaṃ dānābhiratāḥ svagarbharūpaparityāgaṃ svamāṃsaparityāgaṃ ca kurmaḥ/
154.012. tataḥ sā dārikā sumateḥ kathayati--tvamevaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kuru, paścādyenābhyarthīyase, tasya māmanuprayacchethāḥ/
154.013. evamukte tayā dārikayā tasya sumateḥ pañca padmānyanupradattāni, ātmanā dve gṛhīte/
154.014. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
154.015. praṇidhām yatra kuryāstvaṃ buddhamāsādya nāyakam/
154.016. tatra te 'haṃ bhavet patnī nityaṃ sahadharmacāriṇī//2//
body.translated_text: Afterwards, going outside the sanctuary, he wandered from garden to garden searching for flowers, but could not find even a single flower. Then, while wandering, he arrived at that park. That girl was coming from that very park, facing the young man <s>Sumati</s>. Then, by the power of merit, those blue lotuses rose up from the water-pot. <s>Sumati</s>, having seen them, said to the girl: 'Give me those lotuses. Take from me the price of five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> for them.' The girl said to <s>Sumati</s>: 'Then you did not wish to accept me, and now you ask me for lotuses? I shall not give them.' Having said this, she asked the young man <s>Sumati</s>: 'What will you do with them?' <s>Sumati</s> said: 'I shall worship the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the girl said: 'What use do I have for <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>? I shall give them to the <s>Buddha</s> on this condition: if, at the time of offering these lotuses, you make this aspiration with the merit of giving them — "In life after life, may she be my wife" — and if you wish me to be your wife in life after life, then I shall give them.' <s>Sumati</s> said: 'We who delight in giving make renunciation even of our own bodies and our own flesh.' Then the girl said to <s>Sumati</s>: 'Make this aspiration, and then whenever you are requested, hand me over to whomever asks.' Having said this, the girl gave <s>Sumati</s> five lotuses and kept two for herself. She spoke a verse: 'Wherever you make your aspiration, having encountered the <s>Buddha</s>, the Guide, there may I be your wife, always your companion in the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text:
154.017. tena rājñā tatra sarvamapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ kāritamucchritadhvajapatākātoraṇamāmuktapaṭṭadāmaṃ gandhodakacūrṇapariṣiktam/
154.018. nagaradvārādārabhya yāvacca vihāro yāvacca nagarametadantaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ kāritamucchritadhvajapatākatoraṇamāmuktapaṭṭadāma gandhodakacūrṇapariṣiktam/
154.020. sa ca rājā śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ gṛhītvā dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya pratyudgataḥ/
154.021. evamevāmātyāḥ/
154.021. evameva vāsavo rājā amātyaiḥ saha pratyudgataḥ/
154.021. dīpo rājā bhagavato buddhasya pādayor nipatya vijñāpayati--bhagavan, adhiṣṭhānaṃ praviśa/
154.022. yataḥ sa bhagavān bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto 'dhiṣṭhānapraveśābhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
154.023. sa ca rājā dīpaḥ śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya dhārayati/
154.024. tathaivāmātyāḥ, vāsavo rājā amātyasahāyaḥ/
154.024. bhagavatā ṛddhyā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā ekaikaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ahaṃ bhagavataśchatraṃ dhārayāmīti/
154.025. atha bhagavāṃstathāvidhayā śobhayā janamadhyamanuprāptaḥ/
154.026. tatra bhagavatā sābhisaṃskāra indrakīle pādo vyavasthāpitaḥ/
154.027. yadaiva bhagavatā indrakīle pādo vyavathāpitaḥ, tadaiva samanantarakālaṃ pṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitā--calitā pracalitā saṃpracalitā, vedhitā pravedhitā saṃpravethitā/
154.028. dharmatā ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatām yadendrakīle sābhisaṃskāreṇa pādau vyavasthāpayanti, citrāṇyāścaryaṇyadbhutadharmāḥ prādurbhavanti--unmattāḥ svacittaṃ pratilabhante, andhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante, badhirāḥ śrotraśravaṇasamarthā bhavanti, mūkāḥ pravyāharaṇasamarthā bhavanti, paṅgavo gamanasamarthā bhavanti, mūḍhā garbhiṇīnāṃ strīṇāṃ garbhā anulomībhavanti, hiḍinigaḍabaddhānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ bandhanāni <155>śithilībhavanti, janmajanmavairānubaddhāstadanantaraṃ maitracittatāṃ pratilabhante, vatsā dāmāni cchittvā mātṛbhiḥ saṃgacchanti, krośanti, aśvā hreṣante, ṛṣabhā garjanti, śukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakā
madhuraṃ nikūjanti, aneritāni vāditrabhāṇḍāni madhuraśabdān niścārayanti, peḍākṛtā alaṃkārā madhuraśabdānniścaranti, unnatāḥ pṛthivīpradeśā avanamanti, avanatāśconnamanti, apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālāstiṣṭhanti, antarikṣāddevatā
divyānyutpalāni kṣipanti, padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkānyagurucūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni tamālapatrāṇi divyāni mandāravāṇi puṣpāṇi kṣipanti, pūrvo digbhāga unnamati paścimo 'vanamati, paścima unnamati pūrvo 'vanamati, dikṣiṇa unnamatyuttaro 'vanamati, uttara unnamati dakṣiṇo 'vanamati, madhya unnamatyanto 'vanamati, anta unnamati madhyo 'vanamati/
body.translated_text:
154.017. By that king, that entire area was made free of stones, gravel, and potsherds, with lofty banners, flags, and arched gateways erected, with silk garlands hung, and sprinkled with perfumed water and fragrant powders.
154.018. From the city gate extending as far as the monastery and as far as the city — that entire intervening space was made free of stones, gravel, and potsherds, with lofty banners, flags, and arched gateways erected, with silk garlands hung, and sprinkled with perfumed water and fragrant powders.
154.020. That king, taking a hundred-ribbed parasol, went forth to welcome <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
154.021. Likewise the ministers.
154.021. Likewise King <s>Vāsava</s> went forth with his ministers to welcome him.
154.021. King <s>Dīpa</s>, falling at the feet of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, requested: 'Blessed One, enter the royal residence.'
154.022. Thereupon the Blessed One, preceded by the community of monks, set out heading toward the entrance of the royal residence.
154.023. King <s>Dīpa</s> held the hundred-ribbed parasol over <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
154.024. Likewise the ministers, and King <s>Vāsava</s> with his ministers.
154.024. The Blessed One so empowered it by his supernatural power that each one perceived: 'It is I who hold the parasol over the Blessed One.'
154.025. Then the Blessed One, with such splendor, arrived in the midst of the people.
154.026. There, the Blessed One deliberately placed his foot on the threshold-peg (<s>indrakīla</s>).
154.027. The very moment the Blessed One placed his foot on the threshold-peg, at that very instant the earth trembled with a sixfold quaking — it shook, shook greatly, and shook exceedingly; it trembled, trembled greatly, and trembled exceedingly.
154.028. For it is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, that when they deliberately place their feet on the threshold-peg, marvelous, wondrous, and extraordinary phenomena manifest — the mad regain their minds, the blind regain their sight, the deaf become able to hear, the mute become able to speak, the lame become able to walk, the confused fetuses of pregnant women become properly positioned, the bonds of beings bound in fetters and chains become loosened, those harboring enmity from life to life thereupon attain a mind of loving-kindness, calves break their tethers and reunite with their mothers, they cry out, horses neigh, bulls bellow, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds sing sweetly, unplayed musical instruments emit sweet sounds, ornaments kept in boxes emit sweet sounds, elevated areas of the earth subside and depressed areas rise up, they become free of stones, gravel, and potsherds, from the sky the deities cast down divine blue lotuses, lotuses, night-lotuses, white lotuses, aloe powder, sandalwood powder, <s>tagara</s> powder, <s>tamāla</s> leaves, and divine <s>mandāra</s> flowers, the eastern quarter rises and the western subsides, the western rises and the eastern subsides, the southern rises and the northern subsides, the northern rises and the southern subsides, the center rises and the edges subside, the edges rise and the center subsides.

body.text:
155.009. tatra ca dīpāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi puṣpairdhūpairgandhaiśca kārāṃ kurvanti/
155.010. te 'pi ca sumatiśca dārikā ca yena dīpaṃkaraḥ samyaksambuddhastenānugacchanti padmāni gṛhya/
155.011. te ca tatra mahājanakāyena pūjārthaṃ saṃparivṛtasya bhagavata upaśleṣaṃ na labhante/
155.012. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--bahutaraṃ sumatirmāṇavo 'smānmahājanakāyāt puṇyaprasavaṃ kariṣyati iti/
155.013. matvā mahatīṃ tumulāṃ vātavṛṣṭimabhinirmiṇoti/
155.014. yatastena janakāyenāvakāśo dattaḥ/
155.014. labdhāvakāśaśca sumatirmāṇavo bhagavantamasecanakadarśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā atīva prasādajātaḥ/
155.015. prasādajātena ca tāni pañca padmāni bhagavataḥ kṣiptāni/
155.016. tāni ca bhagavatā dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena tathā adhiṣṭhitāni, yathā śakaṭīcakramātrāṇi vitānaṃ buddhvā vyavasthitāni/
155.017. gacchato 'nugacchanti, tiṣṭhato 'nutiṣṭhanti/
155.018. tathā dṛṣṭvā tayā dārikayā prasādajātayā dvau padmau bhagavataḥ kṣiptau/
155.018. tau cāpi bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitau yathā śakaṭīcakramātrau karṇasamīpe vitānaṃ baddhvā vyavasthitau/
155.019. tatra ca pradeśe tumulena vātavarṣeṇa kardamo jātaḥ/
155.020. paścāt sumatirmāṇavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakardamaṃ pṛthivīpradeśamupagataḥ/
155.021. tasmin sakardame pṛthivīpradeśe jātaṃ saṃtīrya bhagavato bhagavataḥ purato gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
155.022. yadi buddho bhaviṣyāmi bodhāya buddhavodhana/
155.023. ākramiṣyasi me padbhyāṃ jaṭāṃ janmajarāntakām//3//
body.translated_text:
155.009. There in the royal capital of <s>Dīpāvatī</s>, many hundreds of thousands of beings made offerings with flowers, incense, and perfumes.
155.010. And both <s>Sumati</s> and the maiden followed <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, carrying lotuses.
155.011. But there, because of the great crowd of people surrounding the Blessed One for worship, they could not get close to him.
155.012. The Blessed One perceived: 'The young man <s>Sumati</s> will produce a far greater store of merit from this great crowd of people.'
155.013. Having considered this, he conjured a great, tumultuous storm of wind and rain.
155.014. Thereupon that crowd of people gave way.
155.014. Having gained an opening, the young man <s>Sumati</s>, seeing the Blessed One of irresistibly beautiful appearance, was filled with an exceedingly great faith.
155.015. Filled with faith, he cast those five lotuses toward the Blessed One.
155.016. Those lotuses were so empowered by the Blessed One <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, that they became as large as cart-wheels and, having formed a canopy, remained suspended.
155.017. When he walked, they followed; when he stood still, they stood still.
155.018. Seeing this, the maiden, filled with faith, cast two lotuses toward the Blessed One.
155.018. Those two were likewise empowered by the Blessed One so that, becoming as large as cart-wheels, they remained suspended near his ears, having formed a canopy.
155.019. In that area, a muddy pool had formed from the tumultuous wind and rain.
155.020. Then the young man <s>Sumati</s> approached the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> at the muddy stretch of ground.
155.021. Having assessed that muddy stretch of ground, he recited a verse before the Blessed One:
155.022. 'If I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, O Awakener of <s>Buddhas</s>, for the sake of awakening,
155.023. may you tread upon my matted locks with your feet — the destroyer of birth and old age.' //3//

body.text:
155.024. tatastena dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena samyaksambuddhena tasya sumatermāṇavasya jaṭāsu pādau vyavasthāpitau/
155.025. tasya ca sumateḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubuddha eva matirmāṇavastiṣṭhati/
155.025. tena kupitenābhihitaṃ bhagavato dīpaṃkarasya--paśya tāvadbhoḥ, anena dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhenāsya sumatermāṇavasya tiraścām yathā padbhyāṃ jaṭā avaṣṭabdhāḥ/
155.027. paścāt dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena sumatirmāṇavo vyākṛtah--bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ nṛbhavādvimukto mukto vimurlokahitāya śāstā/
155.030. śākyātmajaḥ śākyamunīti nāṃnā trilokasāro jagataḥ pradīpaḥ//4//
body.translated_text:
155.024. Then <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, placed his feet upon the matted locks of the young man <s>Sumati</s>.
155.025. Behind <s>Sumati</s>, the young man <s>Mati</s> stood as one who had also understood.
155.025. He, angered, said to the Blessed One <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>: 'Look here, sir! By this <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the matted locks of this young man <s>Sumati</s> have been trodden upon with his feet as if they were an animal's!'
155.027. Then <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, prophesied concerning the young man <s>Sumati</s>: 'You shall become, released from human existence, a liberated Teacher for the welfare of the world;
155.030. a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, known by the name <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the essence of the three worlds, the lamp of beings.' //4//

body.text:
156.001. <156>yadā ca sa sumatirmāṇavo dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena vyākṛtaḥ, tatsamakālameva vaihāyasaṃ saptatālānabhyudgataḥ/
156.002. tāścāsya jaṭāḥ śīrṇāḥ, anyāḥ praviśiṣṭatarā jaṭāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ/
156.003. sa vaihāyasastho mahatā janakāyena dṛṣṭaḥ/
156.003. dṛṣṭvā ca praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam--yadā anenānuttarajñānamadhigataṃ tadāsya vayaṃ śrāvakā bhavema/
156.004. sāpi ca dārikā praṇidhānaṃ karoti--
156.005. praṇidhānam yatra kuryāstvaṃ buddhamāsādya nāyakam/
156.006. tatra te 'haṃ bhavetpatnī nityaṃ sahadharmacāriṇī//5//
body.translated_text:
156.001. When the young man <s>Sumati</s> was prophesied by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, at that very moment he rose up into the sky to the height of seven palm trees.
156.002. Those matted locks of his fell away, and other, more excellent matted locks appeared.
156.003. He was seen in the sky by a great crowd of people.
156.003. Having seen him, they made an aspiration: 'When he attains unsurpassed knowledge, may we become his disciples.'
156.004. That maiden too made an aspiration:
156.005. 'Wherever you make your aspiration, having encountered the <s>Buddha</s>, the Guide,
156.006. there may I be your wife, ever your companion in the holy life.' //5//

body.text:
156.007. yadā bhavasi saṃbuddho loke jyeṣṭhavināyakaḥ/
156.008. śrāvikā te bhaviṣyāmi tasmin kāla upasthite//6//
body.translated_text:
156.007. 'When you become a Perfectly Enlightened One, the foremost guide in the world,
156.008. I shall become your female disciple when that time has arrived.' //6//

body.text:
156.009. khagasthaṃ māṇavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrāṇi śatāni ca/
156.010. śrāvakatvaṃ prārthayante sarve tatra hyanāgate//7//
body.translated_text:
156.009. 'Having seen the young man standing in the sky, hundreds and thousands
156.010. aspired for discipleship — all of them, there in the future.' //7//

body.text:
156.011. yadā bhavasi saṃbuddho loke jyeṣṭhavināyakaḥ/
156.012. śrāvakāste bhaviṣyāmastasmin kāle hyupasthite//8//
body.translated_text:
156.011. 'When you become a Perfectly Enlightened One, the foremost guide in the world,
156.012. we shall become your disciples when that time has arrived.' //8//

body.text:
156.013. yadā ca sumatirmāṇavo dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena vyākṛtaḥ, tadāsya dīpena rājñā jaṭā gṛhītāḥ/
156.014. vāsavo rājā kathayati--mamaitā jaṭā anuprayaccha/
156.014. tatastasya dīpena rājñā anupradattāḥ/
156.015. tena gṛhītvā gaṇitāh aśītirvālasahasrāṇi/
156.015. tasya rājño 'mātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, asmākamekaikaṃ vālamanuprayaccha/
156.016. vayameṣāṃ caityāni kariṣyāmaḥ/
156.016. tena rājñā teṣāṃ bhṛtyānāmekaiko vālo dattaḥ/
156.017. tairamātyaiḥ svake vijite gatvā caityāni pratiṣṭhāpitāni/
156.017. yadā sumatirmāṇavo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambuddhau vyākṛtaḥ, tadā dīpena rājñā vāsavena ca rājñā tairanekaiśca naigamajānapadaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārito 'nāgataguṇāvekṣatayā/
156.019. tataḥ sa matirmāṇava ucyate--ahamanuttarasyāṃ samyaksambodhau vyākṛtah--tvayā kutra cittamutpāditam? sa kathayati--kṣato 'haṃ sumate māṇava/
156.021. sa kathayati--kathaṃ kṛtvā kṣato 'si? tataḥ sa kathayati--yadā tava dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena padbhyāṃ jaṭā avaṣṭabdhāḥ, tadā kupitena vāg niścāritā--dīpaṃkareṇa samyaksambuddhena śrotriyasya jaṭā tiraścām yathā padbhyāmavaṣṭabdhāḥ/
156.023. yatastasya sumatiḥ kathayati--āgacchasva, buddhasya bhagavato 'ntike pravrajāvaḥ/
156.024. tatastau sumatirmatiśca dīpaṃkarasya samyaksambuddhasya pravacane pravrajitau/
156.025. sumatinā ca pravrajya trīpi piṭakānyadhītāni, dharmeṇa parṣat saṃgṛhītā/
156.026. sa ca sumatirmāṇavaścyutaḥ kālagatastuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ/
156.026. matirmāṇavaścyutaḥ kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ//
body.translated_text:
156.013. When the young man <s>Sumati</s> was prophesied by <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, his matted locks were taken by King <s>Dīpa</s>.
156.014. King <s>Vāsava</s> said: 'Give me those matted locks.'
156.014. Then King <s>Dīpa</s> gave them to him.
156.015. He took them and counted them — eighty thousand hairs.
156.015. The ministers of that king said: 'Your Majesty, give us one hair each.
156.016. We shall make shrines (<s>caityas</s>) for them.'
156.016. That king gave one hair to each of his attendants.
156.017. Those ministers, having gone to their own domains, established shrines.
156.017. When the young man <s>Sumati</s> was prophesied for unsurpassed perfect awakening, then by King <s>Dīpa</s>, King <s>Vāsava</s>, and those many townspeople and countryfolk, he was invited with all requisites, in anticipation of his future virtues.
156.019. Then the young man <s>Mati</s> was asked: 'I have been prophesied for unsurpassed perfect awakening — where have you generated your aspiration?' He said: 'I am vexed, O <s>Sumati</s>, young man.'
156.021. He said: 'How are you vexed?' Then he said: 'When <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, trod upon your matted locks with his feet, in anger I uttered the words: "<s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has trodden upon the matted locks of a Vedic scholar with his feet as though they were an animal's!"'
156.023. Thereupon <s>Sumati</s> said to him: 'Come, let us go forth in the presence of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
156.024. Then both <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Mati</s> went forth in the teaching of <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
156.025. <s>Sumati</s>, having gone forth, mastered the three <s>Piṭakas</s> (collections of scriptures) and gathered a congregation through the <s>Dharma</s>.
156.026. That young man <s>Sumati</s>, having died and departed, was reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods.
156.026. The young man <s>Mati</s>, having died and departed, was reborn in the hells.

body.text:
156.028. bhagavānāha--yo 'sau vāsavo rājābhūt tena kālena tena samayena, sa rājā bimbisāraḥ/
156.029. yāni tānyaśītiramātyasahasrāṇi tena kālena tena samayena, tānyetarhyaśītirdevatāsahasrāṇi/
156.030. yo 'sau dīpāvatīyako janakāyaḥ, yāsau dārikā, eṣaiva sā yaśodharā/
156.030. yo 'sau sumatiḥ, ahameva tasmin samaye bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ vartāmi/
156.031. yo 'sau matiḥ, eṣa eva sa dharmaruciḥ/
body.translated_text:
156.028. The Blessed One said: 'He who was King <s>Vāsava</s> at that time, in that era — he is King <s>Bimbisāra</s>.
156.029. Those eighty thousand ministers at that time, in that era — they are now the eighty thousand deities.
156.030. He who was that populace of <s>Dīpāvatī</s>, and that maiden — she is this very <s>Yaśodharā</s>.
156.030. He who was <s>Sumati</s> — I myself at that time was engaged in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> career.
156.031. He who was <s>Mati</s> — he is this very <s>Dharmaruci</s>.

body.text: 157.001. <157>etaddvitīye 'saṃkhyeye asya ca dharmarucermama ca darśanam yadahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi--cirasya dharmaruce, sucirassya dharmaruce//
body.translated_text: 157.001. This was in the second incalculable age (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) — this encounter between <s>Dharmaruci</s> and myself. It is with reference to this that I say: 'Long indeed, <s>Dharmaruci</s>! Very long indeed, <s>Dharmaruci</s>!'

body.text:
157.003. tasmādapyārvāk tṛtīye 'saṃkhyeye krakucchando nāma samyaksambuddho loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
157.005. tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāmanyataro mahāśreṣṭhī prativasati/
157.005. tena ca sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
157.006. sa ca kalatrasahāyaḥ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
157.006. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ/
157.007. sa ca gṛhapatiḥ śrāddhaḥ/
157.007. tasya cārhan bhikṣuḥ kulāvavādako 'sti/
157.007. sa ca gṛhapatistāṃ patnīmevamāha--jāto 'smākam ṛṇadharo dhanaharaḥ/
157.008. gacchāmyahamidānīṃ bhadre vaṇigdharmāṇāṃ deśāntaraṃ bhāṇḍamādāya/
157.009. sa ca vaṇiglokenāvṛto dūrataraṃ gato bhāṇḍamādāya/
157.009. yato 'sya na bhūyaściramapyāgacchati/
157.010. sa ca dārakaḥ kālāntareṇa mahān saṃvṛtto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ/
157.011. tato 'sau mātaraṃ pṛcchati--amba, kimasmākaṃ kulārthāgataṃ karma? sā kathayati--vatsa, pitā tava āpaṇaṃ vāhayannāsīt/
157.012. tataḥ sa dāraka āpaṇamārabdho vāhayitum/
157.012. sā ca mātā asya kleśairbādhyamānā cintayituṃ pravṛttā--ka upāyaḥ syāt yadahaṃ kleśān vinodayeyam, na ca me kaścijjānīyāt? tayā saṃcintyaivamadhyavasitam--evameva putrakāmahetostathā paricarāmi, yathā anenaiva me sārdhaṃ rogavinodakaṃ bhavati, naiva svajanasya śaṅkā bhaviṣyati/
157.016. tatastayā vṛddhayuvatī āhūya bhojayitvā dvis triḥ paścānnavena paṭenācchāditā/
157.016. tasyāḥ sā vṛddhā kathayati--kena kāryeṇaiva mamānuprasādādinā upakrameṇānupravṛttiṃ karoṣi? sā tasyā vṛddhāyā viśvastā bhūtvā evamāha--amba, śṛṇu vijñāpyam/
157.018. kleśairatīva bādhye, priyatāṃ mamotpādya manuṣyānveṣaṇaṃ kuru, yo 'bhyantara eva syānna ca śaṅkanīyo janasya/
157.019. vṛddhā kathayati--neha gṛhe tathāvidho manuṣyaḥ saṃvidyate, nāpi praṇayavān kaścit praviśati, yo janasyāśaṅkanīyo bhavet/
157.021. katamaḥ sa manuṣyo bhaviṣyati yasyāhaṃ vakṣyāmi? tataḥ sā vaṇikpatnī tasyā vṛddhāyāḥ kathayati--yadyanyo manuṣya evaṃvidhopakramayukto nāsti, eṣa eva me putro bhavati, naiṣa lokasya śaṅkanīyo bhaviṣyati/
157.023. tasyāstayā vṛddhayā abhihitam--kathaṃ nu putreṇa sārdhaṃ ratikrīḍāṃ gamiṣyasi? yuktaṃ syādanyena manuṣyeṇa sārdhaṃ ratikrīḍāmanubhavitum/
157.024. tataḥ sā vaṇikpatnī kathayati--yadyanyo 'bhyantaro manuṣyo na saṃvidyate, bhavatu eṣa eva me putraḥ/
157.025. tayā vṛddhayā abhihitam--yathepsitaṃ kuru/
157.026. tataḥ sā vṛddhayuvatī tasya vaṇijaḥ putrasyaivāgamya pṛcchati--vatsa, taruṇo 'si rūpavāṃśca/
157.027. kiṃ pratiṣṭhito 'syārthena? tena tasyā abhihitam--kimetat? tataḥ sā vṛddhā kathayati--bhavānevamabhirūpaśca yuvā ca asmin vayasi taruṇayuvatyā sārdhaṃ śobhethāḥ krīḍan raman paricārayan/ kimeva kāmabhogaparihīnastiṣṭhasi? vaṇigdārakastaṃ śrutvā lajjāvyapatrāpyasamlīnacetāstasyā vṛddhāyāstadvacanaṃ nādhivāsayati/
157.030. tataḥ sā vṛddhā evaṃ dvirapi trirapi tasya dārakasya kathayati--taruṇayuvatistavārthe kleśairbādhyate/
157.031. sa vaṇigdārako dvirapi trirapyucyamānastasyā vṛddhāyāḥ kathayati--amba, kiṃ tasyāstaruṇayuvatyāḥ saṃnimitte kiṃcidabhihitam? tatah <158>sā vṛddhā kathayati--uktaṃ tasyā mayā tannimittam/
body.translated_text:
157.003. Earlier still, in the third incalculable <s>kalpa</s> (eon), a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
157.005. In that royal capital there lived a certain great chief merchant.
157.005. He had brought a wife from a family of equal standing.
157.006. He enjoyed himself, delighted, and amused himself with his wife.
157.006. While he was enjoying, delighting, and amusing himself, a son was born to him.
157.007. That householder was a man of faith.
157.007. He had an <s>Arhat</s> monk as his family advisor.
157.007. That householder said to his wife: 'A debt-bearer and wealth-consumer has been born to us.
157.008. I shall now go abroad, dear, taking merchandise in the manner of merchants.'
157.009. He went far away with a group of merchants, taking his merchandise.
157.009. He did not return for a long time.
157.010. In time, the boy grew up — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing to behold.
157.011. He asked his mother: 'Mother, what was the family occupation?' She said: 'Son, your father used to run a shop.'
157.012. Then the boy began to run the shop.
157.012. Meanwhile, the mother, afflicted by sensual desires, began to think: 'What means would there be for me to relieve my passions, without anyone knowing?' Having reflected, she decided thus: 'Under the very pretext of desire for a son, I shall arrange things in such a way that the remedy for my affliction will be with him, and the relatives will have no suspicion.'
157.016. Then she summoned an old woman, fed her, and two or three times afterwards covered her with new cloth.
157.016. The old woman said to her: 'For what purpose are you showing me such kindness and attention?' Having gained the old woman's trust, she said: 'Mother, hear my request.
157.018. I am exceedingly afflicted by desires. Generating affection for me, search for a man who would be within the household and not suspicious to people.'
157.019. The old woman said: 'There is no such man available in this house, nor does any intimate acquaintance enter who would be above suspicion to people.
157.021. Who would this man be to whom I would speak?' Then the merchant's wife said to the old woman: 'If no other man suitable for this purpose exists, there is my own son — he will not be suspicious to people.'
157.023. The old woman said to her: 'How can you engage in sexual pleasure with your son? It would be proper to experience pleasure with another man.'
157.024. Then the merchant's wife said: 'If no other man within the household is available, let it be my own son.'
157.025. The old woman said: 'Do as you wish.'
157.026. Then the old woman went to the merchant's son and asked: 'Son, you are young and handsome.
157.027. Are you established with regard to sensual enjoyments?' He said to her: 'What is this?' Then the old woman said: 'You, being so handsome and young, would look splendid at this age playing, delighting, and enjoying yourself with a young woman. Why do you remain deprived of sensual pleasures?' The merchant's son, hearing this, his mind overcome with shame and modesty, did not accept the old woman's proposal.
157.030. Then the old woman said to the boy again a second and third time: 'A young woman is afflicted by desires on your account.'
157.031. The merchant's son, being told a second and third time, said to the old woman: 'Mother, has something been said on behalf of that young woman?' Then the old woman said: 'I spoke to her on that account.'

body.text:
158.001. tayā mama nimitte na pratijñātam/
158.001. sā ca dārikā hīvyapatrāpyagṛhītā na kiṃcidvakṣyati/
158.002. na ca śarīramāvṛtaṃ kariṣyati/
158.002. na tvayā tasyā vā anveṣaṇe yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
158.003. tatastena vaṇigdārakeṇa tasyā vṛddhāyā abhihitam--kutrāsmākaṃ saṃgataṃ bhaviṣyati? tayā abhihitam--madīye gṛhe/
158.004. tenoktam--kutrāvakāśe tava gṛham? tato 'sya tayā vṛddhayā gṛhaṃ vyapadiṣṭam/
158.005. sā ca vṛddhā tasyā vaṇikpatnyāḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--icchāpitaḥ sa vo 'yaṃ dārakaḥ/
158.006. sā kathayati--kutrāvakāśe saṃgataṃ bhaviṣyati? madīye gṛhe/
158.007. sa ca dārakaḥ kāryāṇi kṛtvā gataḥ/
158.007. anupūrveṇa bhuktvā tasyā mātuḥ kathayati--gacchāmyaham/
158.008. vayasyagṛhe svapsye/
158.008. tato 'sya mātrāpyanujñātam--gaccha/
158.008. sa dārako labdhānujñastasyā vṛddhāyā gṛhaṃ gataḥ/
158.009. tasya dārakasya tasmin gṛhe gatasya ratikrīḍākālamāgamayamānasya tiṣṭhato niśikālamapratyabhijñātam/
158.010. rūpe kāle sā mātā asya vaṇigdārakasya tasminneva gṛhe ratikrīḍāmanubhavanārthaṃ tatraiva gatā/
158.011. gatvā ca tasmin gṛhe vikālamavyaktiṃ vibhāvyamāne rūpākṛtau nirgūḍhenopacārakrameṇa ratikrīḍāṃ putreṇa sārdhamanubhavituṃ pravṛttā pāpakenāsaddharmeṇa/
158.013. sā ca parikṣīṇāyāṃ rātrau anubhūtaratikrīḍā satamondhakāre kālāyāmeva rajanyāmavibhāvyamānarūpākṛtau svagṛhaṃ gacchati/
158.014. sa cāpi vaṇigdārako ratikrīḍāmanubhūya prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ bhāṇḍāvāriṃ gatvā kuṭumbakāryāṇi karoti/
158.015. evaṃ dvirapi trirapi/
158.015. tatra vṛddhāyā gṛhe ratikrīḍāmanubhavaṃśca cirakālamevaṃ vartamānena ratikrīḍākrameṇa tasya dārakasya sā mātā cintayituṃ pravṛttā--kiyatkālamabyadgṛhamahamevamavibhāvyamānarūpā ratikrīḍāmanubhaviṣyāmi? yannvahamasyaitat ratikrīḍākramaṃ tathāvidhaṃ krameṇa saṃvedayeyam, yathā ihaiva gṛhe ratikrīḍā bhavet/
158.019. iti saṃcintya tatraiva vṛddhāgṛhe gatvā ratikrīḍāṃ putreṇa sārdhamanubhūya rajanyāḥ kṣaye satamondhakārakāle tasya dārakasyoparimaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ nivasyātmanīyāṃ ca śirottarapaṭṭikāṃ tyaktvā svagṛhaṃ gatā/
158.021. sa ca dārakaḥ prabhāakāle tāṃ paṭṭikāṃ śirasi mañcasyāvatiṣṭhantīṃ saṃpaśyati/
158.022. ātmīyāmevopariprāvaraṇapotrīmalabhamānastatraiva tāṃ paṭṭikāṃ saṃlakṣya tyaktvā bhāṇḍāvārīṃ gatvā yugalamanyaṃ prāvṛtya svagṛhaṃ gataḥ/
158.023. tatra ca gataḥ saṃpaśyati tamevātmīyaṃ pravaraṇaṃ tasyā mātuḥ śirasi prāvṛtam/
158.024. dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ mātaraṃ pṛcchati--amba, kuto 'yaṃ śirasi prāvaraṇo 'bhyāgatah? yatastayā abhihitam--adyāpyahaṃ tavāmbā? evaṃ cirakālaṃ tava mayā sārdhaṃ kāmān paribhuñjato 'dyāpyahaṃ tava saivāmbā? yataḥ sa vaṇigdārakastathāvidhaṃ mātṛvacanamupaśrutya saṃmūḍho vihvalacetā bhūmau nipatitaḥ/
158.027. tatastayā sa mātrā ghaṭajalapariṣekeṇāvasiktaḥ/
158.027. sa jalapariṣekāvasikto dārakaścireṇa kālena pratyāgataprāṇastayā mātrā samāśvāsyate--kimevaṃ khedamupāgatastvam? asmadīyaṃ vacanamupaśrutya dhīramanā bhavasva/
158.029. na te viṣādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
158.029. sa dārakastasyāḥ kathayati--kathamahaṃ khedaṃ na kariṣyāmi saṃmohaṃ vā, yena mayā evaṃvidhaṃ pāpakaṃ karma kṛtam? tataḥ sa tayābhihitah--na te manaḥśūkaṃsdminnarthe utpādayitavyam/
158.031. panthāsamo mātṛgrāmaḥ/
158.031. yenaivaṃ hi yathā pitā gacchati, putro 'pi tenaiva gacchati/
158.032. na cāsau panthā putrasyānugacchato doṣakārako <159>bhavati, evameva mātṛgrāmaḥ/
body.translated_text:
158.001. 'She did not make a commitment on my account.
158.001. But that girl, being seized by shame and modesty, will not say anything.
158.002. Nor will she conceal her body.
158.002. You need not make any effort in seeking her.'
158.003. Then the merchant's son said to the old woman: 'Where will our meeting take place?' She said: 'At my house.'
158.004. He said: 'Where is your house?' Then the old woman indicated her house to him.
158.005. The old woman went to the merchant's wife and said: 'That boy of yours has been persuaded.'
158.006. She said: 'Where will the meeting take place?' 'At my house.'
158.007. The boy, having finished his work, went.
158.007. In due course, after eating, he said to his mother: 'I am going.
158.008. I shall sleep at a friend's house.'
158.008. His mother gave permission: 'Go.'
158.008. The boy, having received permission, went to the old woman's house.
158.009. While the boy was waiting in that house for the time of the amorous encounter, he did not recognize the time of night.
158.010. At the right time, the mother of the merchant's son went to that very house to experience sexual pleasure.
158.011. Having gone, in that house, in the darkness when form and appearance could not be discerned, she proceeded to experience sexual pleasure with her son through concealed conduct, by the wicked and unrighteous deed.
158.013. When the night had passed, having experienced the pleasure, she went home in the dense darkness of night while form and appearance could not be discerned.
158.014. The merchant's son too, having experienced the pleasure, went at dawn to the shop to attend to business.
158.015. Thus it happened a second and a third time.
158.015. While he was experiencing pleasure at the old woman's house for a long time in this way, the mother began to think: 'How long will I experience this pleasure at another's house with my form unrecognized? Let me gradually make him aware of this arrangement, so that the pleasure can take place in my own house.'
158.019. Having decided thus, she went to the old woman's house, experienced pleasure with her son, and at the end of the night, in the dense darkness, put her son's upper garment on herself and left her own head-cloth behind, and went home.
158.021. The boy, at dawn, saw that cloth on the headboard of the bed.
158.022. Not finding his own upper garment, he noticed that cloth there, left it, went to the shop, wrapped himself in another pair of garments, and went home.
158.023. Having gone there, he saw that very upper garment of his wrapped around his mother's head.
158.024. Having seen this, he asked his mother: 'Mother, where did this garment on your head come from?' She said: 'Am I still your mother? For such a long time you have been enjoying sensual pleasures with me, and am I still that very mother of yours?'
158.024. The merchant's son, hearing such words from his mother, was stupefied, his mind bewildered, and he fell to the ground.
158.027. His mother revived him by sprinkling him with water from a pot.
158.027. Revived by the sprinkling of water after a long time, the boy was consoled by his mother: 'Why have you become so distressed? Having heard my words, be firm-minded.
158.029. You must not be dejected.'
158.029. The boy said to her: 'How can I not be distressed or bewildered, when I have committed such a wicked deed?' Then she said to him: 'You should not feel remorse in this matter.
158.031. Womankind is like a road.
158.031. Just as the father travels by a road, the son also travels by it.
158.032. And that road does not cause fault to the son who follows — so it is with womankind.'

body.text:
159.001. tīryasamo 'pi ca mātṛgrāmaḥ/
159.001. yatraiva hi tīrye pitā snāti, putro 'pi tasmin snāti, na ca tīryaṃ putrasya snāyato doṣakārakaṃ bhavati/
159.002. evameva mātṛgrāmaḥ/
159.002. api ca pratyanteṣu janapadeṣu dharmataivaiṣā yasyāmeva pitā asaddharmeṇābhigacchati, tāmeva putro 'pyadhigacchati/
159.004. evamasau vaṇigdārako mātrā bahuvidhairanunayavacanairvinītaśokastayā mātrā tasmin pātake 'saddharme punaḥ punaratīva saṃjātarāgaḥ pravṛttaḥ/
159.005. tena ca śreṣṭhinā gṛhe lekhyo 'nupreṣitaḥ/
159.005. bhadre, dhīrorjitamahotsāhā bhavasva/
159.006. ahamapi lekhānupadamevāgamiṣye/
159.006. sā vaṇikpatnī tathāvidhaṃ lekhārthaṃ śrutvā vaimanasyajātā cintayituṃ pravṛttā--mahāntaṃ kālaṃ mama tasyāgamanamudīkṣamāṇāyāḥ/
159.007. tadā nāgataḥ/
159.008. idānīṃ mayā evaṃvidhenopakrameṇa putraṃ ca paricaritvā sa cāgamiṣyati/
159.008. ka upāyaḥ syāt yadahaṃ tamihāsamprāptameva jīvitāt vyaparopayeyam? iti saṃcintya taṃ putramāhūya kathayati--pitrā te lekhyo 'nupreṣitah āgamiṣyatīti/
159.010. jājase 'smābhiridānīṃ kiṃ karaṇīyamiti? gacchasva, pitaramasamprāptameva ghātaya/
159.011. sa kathayati--kathamahaṃ pitaraṃ ghātayiṣye? yadā asau na prasahate pitṛvadhaṃ kartum, tadā tayā mātrā bhūyo 'nuvṛttivacanairabhihitah--tasyānuvṛttivacanairucyamānasya kāmeṣu saṃraktasyādhyavasāyo jātaḥ pitṛvadhaṃ prati/
159.013. kāmān khalu pratisevato na hi kiṃcit pāpakaṃ karmākaraṇīyamiti vadāmi/
159.014. tatastenoktam--kenopāyena ghātayāmi? tayā abhihitam--ahamevopāyaṃ saṃvidhāsye/
159.015. ityuktvā viṣamādāya samitāyāṃ miśrayitvā maṇḍilakān paktvā anye 'pi ca nirviṣāḥ paktāḥ/
159.016. yatastaṃ dārakamāhūya kathayati--gacchasva/
159.017. amī saviṣā maṇḍilakā nirviṣāśca/
159.017. gṛhya pitṛsakāśaṃ gatvā ca tasya viśvastasyaikatra bhuñjata etān saviṣān maṇḍilakān prayacchasva, ātmanā ca nirviṣān bhakṣaya/
159.018. tataḥ sa dārakastena lekhavāhikamanuṣyeṇa sārdhaṃ tān maṇḍilakān gṛhya gataḥ pitṛsakāśam/
159.019. āgamya pitā asya atīva taṃ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā abhirūpaprāsādikaṃ maheśākhyaṃ prāmodyaṃ prāptaḥ/
159.020. sahyāsahyaṃ pṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ vaṇijāmākhyāti--ayaṃ bhavanto 'smākaṃ putraḥ/
159.021. yadā tena dārakeṇa saṃlakṣitaṃ sarvatra ahamanena pitrā pratisaṃvedita iti, tatastaṃ pitaramāha--tāta, ambayā maṇḍilakāḥ praheṇakamanupreṣitam/
159.023. tattātaḥ paribhuñjatu/
159.023. paścāttena pitrā sārdhamekaphalāyāṃ bhuñjatā tasya pituḥ saviṣā maṇḍilakā dattāḥ, ātmanā nirviṣāḥ prabhakṣitāḥ/
159.024. yato 'sya pitā tān saviṣān maṇḍilakān bhakṣayitvā bhṛtaḥ/
159.025. tasya ca pituḥ kāladharmaṇā yuktasya ca dārako na kenacit pāpakaṃ karma kurvāṇo 'bhiśaṅkito vā pratisaṃvedito vā/
159.026. paścāttairiṣṭasnigdhasuhṛdbhirvaṇigbhiḥ śocayitvā yattattu kiṃcittasya vaṇijo bhaṇḍamāsīddhiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ vā, tattasya dārakasya dattam/
159.028. sa dārakastaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ gṛhya svagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
159.029. tasya ca gatasya svagṛhaṃ sā mātā pracchannāsaddharmeṇa taṃ putraṃ paricaramāṇā ratiṃ nādhigacchati, anabhiratarūpā ca taṃ putraṃ vadati--kiyatkālaṃ vayamevaṃ pracchannena krameṇa ratikrīḍāmanubhaviṣyāmah? yannu vayamasmāddeśādanyadeśāntaraṃ gatvā prakāśakrameṇa niḥśaṅkā bhūtvā jāyāpatīti vikhyātadharmāṇaḥ sukhaṃ prativasema/
159.032. tatastau gṛhaṃ tyaktvā <160>mitrasvajanasambandhivargānapahāya purāṇadāsīdāsakarmakarāṃstyaktvā yāvadarthajātaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ca gṛhya anyaviṣayāntaraṃ gatau/
body.translated_text:
159.001. And womankind is like a ford.
159.001. For wherever a father bathes at a ford, the son also bathes there, and the ford does not become a cause of fault for the bathing son.
159.002. Just so is womankind.
159.002. Moreover, in the borderland provinces, it is the very nature of things that the very woman whom the father approaches through immoral conduct, the son also approaches.
159.004. Thus that merchant's son, his grief removed by his mother through various kinds of cajoling words, was made to engage again and again with excessive passion in that sinful, immoral practice by that mother.
159.005. Meanwhile, the merchant sent a letter to his home:
159.005. 'Dear one, be steadfast, brave, and of great enthusiasm.
159.006. I too shall come following immediately upon this letter.'
159.006. That merchant's wife, hearing the purport of such a letter, became distressed and began to think: 'For a long time I have been watching for his arrival.
159.007. He did not come then.
159.008. Now, having attended to my son by such a stratagem, he will come.
159.008. What means might there be by which I could deprive him of life even before he arrives here?' Having thus reflected, she called her son and said: 'Your father has sent a letter saying he will come.
159.010. You know what we must do now. Go — kill your father before he arrives.'
159.011. He said: 'How can I kill my father?' When he could not bring himself to commit patricide, then that mother addressed him again with cajoling words — and as those cajoling words were spoken to him, passionate as he was for sensual pleasures, the resolve arose in him toward patricide.
159.013. For I say that for one who indulges in sensual pleasures, there is no evil deed that cannot be done.
159.014. Then he said: 'By what means shall I kill him?' She said: 'I myself will arrange the means.'
159.015. Having said this, she took poison, mixed it into a flour mixture, and baked poisoned cakes; and others, non-poisoned, were also baked.
159.016. Then, calling that boy, she said: 'Go.
159.017. These are the poisoned cakes and these the non-poisoned ones.
159.017. Take them, go to your father, and when he trusts you and you eat together from one plate, give him these poisoned cakes, and eat the non-poisoned ones yourself.'
159.018. Then that boy, together with the man carrying the letter, took those cakes and went to his father.
159.019. Upon his arrival, the father, seeing his son — handsome, attractive, and of great renown — was exceedingly delighted.
159.020. Having asked after his wellbeing, he announced to all the other merchants: 'This, sirs, is our son.'
159.021. When the boy perceived that 'I have been introduced by this father everywhere,' then he said to his father: 'Father, mother has sent cakes as a gift.
159.023. Please eat them, father.'
159.023. Then, as they ate together from one plate, the son gave the poisoned cakes to his father and ate the non-poisoned ones himself.
159.024. And his father, having eaten those poisoned cakes, died.
159.025. When his father had met his end, no one suspected or identified the boy as having done an evil deed.
159.026. Afterward, those dear and affectionate merchant friends, having mourned, gave whatever merchandise, gold, or silver that belonged to that merchant to that boy.
159.028. The boy, taking his father's merchandise, gold, and silver, arrived at his own home.
159.029. When he had returned home, that mother, secretly attending to her son through immoral conduct, found no satisfaction, and with a discontented appearance she said to her son: 'For how long shall we experience this secret pleasure of lovemaking? Let us leave this country and go to another region, where we may live openly, without fear, publicly known as husband and wife, and dwell in happiness.'
159.032. Then the two of them abandoned their home, <160> leaving behind friends, relatives, and kinsmen, abandoning their old servants, slaves, and workers, and taking whatever wealth, gold, and silver they had, went to another region.

body.text:
160.002. tatra gatvā janapadeṣu vikhyāpayamānau jāyāpatikamiti ratikrīḍāmanubhavamānau vyavasthitau/
160.003. yāvadarhan bhikṣuḥ kenacit kālāntareṇa janapadacārikāṃ caraṃs tamadhiṣṭhānamanuprāptaḥ/
160.004. tena tatra piṇḍapātamanvāhiṇḍatā vīthyāṃ niṣadya ayaṃ vaṇigdharmaṇā saṃvyavahāramāṇaḥ sa dārako dṛṣṭaḥ/
160.005. dṛṣṭvā cārogyayitvā cābhibhāṣyoktah--mātuste kuśalam? sa ca dārakastamarhantaṃ tathā abhivadamānamupaśrutya saṃbhinnacetāḥ svena duścaritena karmaṇā śaṅkitamanāścintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
160.007. sa vicintya mātṛsakāśaṃ gatvā saṃvedayati--yatirabhyāgataḥ, yo 'sau asmadgṛhamupasaṃkrāmati, eṣa sa ihādhiṣṭhāne pratisaṃvedayiṣyati eṣā asya dārakasya māteti/
160.009. vayaṃ cehaṃ jāyāpatikamiti khyātau/
160.009. kathameṣa śakyaṃ ghātayitum? tatastayoḥ saṃcintya taṃ gṛhamenamupanimantrayitvā bhuñjānaṃ ghātayāmaḥ/
160.010. tatastayorevaṃ saṃcintya so 'rhan bhikṣurantargṛhamupanimantrayitvā bhojayitumārabdhaḥ/
160.011. sa dārako gūḍhaśastro bhūtvā arhantaṃ bhojayituṃ mātrā saha nirjanaṃ gṛhaṃ kṛtvā sa cārhadbhikṣubhuktvā tasmādgṛhādviśrabdhacārakrameṇa pratinirgataḥ/
160.013. tatastena jīvitād vyaparopayati/
160.014. kāmāśca lavaṇodakasadṛśāḥ/
160.014. yathā yathā sevyanti, tathā tathā tṛṣṇā vṛddhimupayāti/
160.015. tasya dārakasya sā mātā taṃ putramasaddharmeṇānuvartamānā tasminnevādhiṣṭhāne śreṣṭhiputreṇa sārdhaṃ pracchannakāmā asaddharmeṣu saktacittā jātā/
160.016. tasya dārakasya tathāvidha upakramaḥ pratisaṃviditaḥ/
160.017. tasya dārakasya tathāvidha upakramaḥ pratisaṃviditaḥ/
160.017. tatastena tasya māturuktam--amba nivartasvedṛśāddoṣāt/
160.018. sā ca tasmiñ śreṣṭhiputre saṃraktacittā dvirapi trirapyucyamānā na nirvartate/
160.018. tatastena niṣkoṣamāsiṃ kṛtvā sā mātā jīvitādvyaparopitā/
160.019. yadā tasya trīṇyānantaryāṇi paripūrṇāni, tadā devatābhirjanapadeṣvārocitam--pāpa eṣa pitṛghātako 'rhaddhātako mātṛghātakaśca/
160.021. trīṇyanenānantaryāṇi narakakarmasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
160.021. tatastenādhiṣṭhānajanena tacchrutvā tadadhiṣṭhānānnirvāsitaḥ/
160.022. sa yadā nirvāsitastasmādadhiṣṭhānāt tadā cintayituṃ pravṛttah--asti cāsya buddhaśāsane kaścidevānunayah? evaṃ manasi kṛtam--gacchāmi, idānīṃ pravrajāmīti/
160.024. sa ca vihāraṃ gatvā bhikṣusakāśamupasaṃkramya evaṃ kathayati--ārya, pravrajeyam/
160.025. tatastena bhikṣuṇā uktam--mā tāvat pitṛghātako 'si? tena bhikṣurabhihitah--asti mayā ghātitaḥ pitā/
160.026. tataḥ punaḥ pṛṣṭah--mā tāvanmātṛghātako 'si? tenoktam--ārya, ghātitā mayā mātā/
160.027. sa bhūyaḥ pṛṣṭah--mā tāvadarhadvadhaste kṛtah? tataḥ sa kathayati--arhannapi ghātitaḥ/
160.028. tatastena bhikṣuṇā abhihitah--ekaikena eṣāṃ karmāṇāmācaraṇānna pravrajyārho bhavasi, prāgeva samastānām/
160.029. gaccha vatsa, nāhaṃ pravrājayiṣye/
160.030. tataḥ sa puruṣo 'nyasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati--ārya pravrajeyam/
160.031. tatastenāpi bhikṣuṇā anupūrveṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ/
160.031. tataḥ paścādanyasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
160.032. tamapi tathaiva pravrajyāmāyācate/
160.032. tenāpi tathā anupūrvakrameṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ/
160.032. sa yadā <161>dvirapi trirapi pravrajyāmāyācamāno 'pi bhikṣubhir na pravrājitaḥ, tadā amarṣajātaścintayituṃ pravṛttah--yā api sarvasādhāraṇā pravrajyā, tāmahamapyāyācanna labhāmi/
body.translated_text:
160.002. Having gone there, they established themselves in the provinces, publicly declaring themselves husband and wife, and enjoying their pleasures together.
160.003. In the course of time, a monk who was an <s>Arhat</s>, wandering on a tour of the provinces, arrived at that settlement.
160.004. As he was going about collecting alms there, he saw that boy sitting in a street conducting business in the manner of a merchant.
160.005. Having seen him, he greeted him and said: 'Is your mother well?' And that boy, hearing the <s>Arhat</s> address him thus, became alarmed in mind and, fearful due to his own misconduct, began to think.
160.007. Having reflected, he went to his mother and informed her: 'An ascetic has arrived, the one who used to visit our house — he will reveal here in this settlement that "This is that boy's mother."
160.009. And we are known here as husband and wife.
160.009. How can he be killed?' Then the two of them planned: 'Let us invite him into the house and kill him while he eats.'
160.010. Having thus planned, they invited that <s>Arhat</s> monk into the inner house and began to feed him.
160.011. The boy, with a hidden weapon, having made the house empty of other people together with his mother, proceeded to feed the <s>Arhat</s>; and that <s>Arhat</s> monk, having eaten, went out from that house with a trusting gait.
160.013. Then he was deprived of life by the boy.
160.014. Sensual desires are like salt water.
160.014. The more they are indulged, the more thirst increases.
160.015. That boy's mother, continuing in immoral conduct with her son, at that very settlement became secretly desirous of a merchant's son, her mind attached to immoral practices.
160.016. That boy became aware of such a scheme.
160.017. That boy became aware of such a scheme.
160.017. Then he said to his mother: 'Mother, turn back from such a fault.'
160.018. But she, with her mind enamored of that merchant's son, though told twice and thrice, did not desist.
160.018. Then, drawing his sword from its sheath, he deprived his mother of life.
160.019. When his three <s>ānantarya</s> crimes (deeds of immediate retribution) were complete, the deities announced throughout the provinces: 'This evil one is a patricide, a killer of an <s>Arhat</s>, and a matricide.
160.021. Three <s>ānantarya</s> deeds leading to hell have been performed and accumulated by him.'
160.021. Then the people of that settlement, hearing this, banished him from that place.
160.022. When he was banished from that settlement, he began to think: 'Is there perhaps any refuge for me in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>?' Having thus reflected, he thought: 'I shall go; I shall now go forth into the monastic order.'
160.024. He went to a monastery and, approaching a monk, said: 'Venerable sir, I wish to go forth.'
160.025. Then that monk said: 'You are not a patricide, are you?' He said to the monk: 'I have killed my father.'
160.026. Then he was asked again: 'You are not a matricide, are you?' He said: 'Venerable sir, I have killed my mother.'
160.027. He was asked further: 'You have not killed an <s>Arhat</s>, have you?' Then he said: 'I have killed an <s>Arhat</s> as well.'
160.028. Then that monk said: 'By the commission of even one of these deeds you are unworthy of ordination, let alone all of them together.
160.029. Go, my child; I will not ordain you.'
160.030. Then that man approached another monk and said: 'Venerable sir, I wish to go forth.'
160.031. By that monk too, having been questioned in due order, he was refused.
160.031. Then afterward he went to yet another monk.
160.032. He entreated him too for ordination in the same way.
160.032. By him too, having been questioned in due order, he was refused.
160.032. When, <161> even after entreating twice and thrice, he was not ordained by the monks, then, filled with resentment, he began to think: 'Even the ordination that is open to all, I cannot obtain even upon requesting it.'

body.text:
161.002. tatastena tasmin vihāre śayitānāṃ bhikṣūṇāmagnirdattaḥ/
161.003. tasmin vihāre 'gniṃ datvā anyatra vihāraṃ gataḥ/
161.003. tatrāpi gatvā bhikṣūṇāmupasaṃkramya pravrajyāmāyācate/
161.004. tairapi tathaivānupūrveṇa pṛṣṭvā pratyākhyātaḥ/
161.004. tatrāpi tena tathaiva pratihatacetasā agnirdattaḥ/
161.005. tatrāpi vihāre bahavo bhikṣavaḥ śaikṣāśaikṣāśca dagdhāḥ/
161.006. evaṃ tasyānekān vihārān dahataḥ sarvatra śabdo visṛtah--evaṃvidhaścaivaṃvidhaśca pāpakarmakārī puruṣo bhikṣubhyaḥ pravrajyāmalabhan vihārān bhikṣūṃśca dahatīti/
161.007. sa ca puruṣo 'nyavihāraṃ prasthitaḥ/
161.008. tatra ca vihāre bodhisattvajātīyo bhikṣuḥ prativasati tṛpitaḥ/
161.008. tena śrutaṃ sa evaṃ duṣkarakarmakārī puruṣa ihāgacchatīti/
161.009. yataḥ sa bhikṣustasya puruṣasyāsamprāptasyaiva tasmin vihāre pratyudgataḥ/
161.010. sa taṃ puruṣaṃ sametya kathayati--bhadramukha, kimetat? yato 'sya puruṣeṇoktam--ārya, pravrajyāṃ na labhāmi/
161.011. tatastena bhikṣuṇām uktam--āgaccha vatsa, ahaṃ te pravrājayāmīti/
161.012. paścāt tena bhikṣuṇā tasya puruṣasya śiro muṇḍāpayitvā kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi dattāni/
161.013. paścāt sa puruṣaḥ kathayati--ārya, śikṣāpadāni me 'nuprayaccha/
161.013. tatastena bhikṣuṇā uktah--kiṃ te śikṣāpadaiḥ prayojanam? evaṃ sarvakālaṃ vadasva--namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya, namaḥ saṃghāyeti/
161.015. paścāt sa bhikṣustasya puruṣasya dharmadeśanāmārabdhaḥ kartum--tvamevaṃvidhaścaivaṃvidhaśca pāpakarmakārī sattvo yadi kadācidbuddhaśabdaṃ śṛṇoṣi, smṛtiṃ pratilabhethāḥ/
161.016. athāsau tripiṭo bhikṣuścyutaḥ kālagato deveṣupapannaḥ/
161.017. sa cāpi puruṣaścyutaḥ kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then he set fire to the monastery while the monks were sleeping in it. Having set fire to that monastery, he went to another monastery. Having gone there too, he approached the monks and begged for ordination. By them as well, having been questioned in the same manner in due order, he was refused. There too, with a resentful heart, he set fire in the same way. In that monastery too, many monks — both learners and those beyond learning — were burned. Thus, as he burned many monasteries, word spread everywhere: 'Such-and-such an evildoing man, not having obtained ordination from the monks, is burning monasteries and monks.' That man set out for yet another monastery. In that monastery dwelt a monk of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage, a learned one. He heard that this man, a doer of terrible deeds, was coming there. Thereupon, that monk went out to meet that man even before he arrived at the monastery. That monk, having met the man, said: 'Good sir, what is this about?' The man replied: 'Venerable one, I cannot obtain ordination.' Then that monk said to them: 'Come, dear one, I shall ordain you.' Afterwards, that monk had the man's head shaved and gave him saffron-colored robes. Then the man said: 'Venerable one, give me the precepts of training.' The monk replied: 'What need have you of precepts? Just say this at all times: <s>Namo Buddhāya</s> (Homage to the Buddha), <s>Namo Dharmāya</s> (Homage to the Dharma), <s>Namaḥ Saṃghāya</s> (Homage to the Saṃgha).' Afterwards, that monk began to give the man a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>: 'You are such-and-such an evildoing being. If ever you hear the word "Buddha," you should regain mindfulness.' Then that learned monk passed away and was reborn among the gods. And that man too passed away and was reborn in the hells.

body.text:
161.018. yato bhagavānāha--kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavah? yo 'sau atīte 'dhvani bhikṣus tripiṭah āsa, ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena/
161.019. yo 'sau pāpakarmakārī sattvo mātāpitrarhaddhātakaḥ, eṣa eva dharmaruciḥ/
161.020. idaṃ mama tṛtīye 'saṃkhyeye 'sya dharmarucerdarśanam/
161.020. tadahaṃ saṃdhāya kathayāmi--cirasya dharmaruce, sucirasya dharmaruce, suciracirasya dharmaruce/
161.021. yāvacca mayā bhikṣavastribhirasaṃkhyeyaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiranyaiśca duṣkaraśatasahasrairanuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ samudānītā, tāvadanena dharmarucinā yadbhūyasā narakatiryakṣu kṣipitam//
body.translated_text: Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was that learned monk in the past — I myself was he at that time, in that era. He who was that evildoing being, a killer of his mother and father and of <s>Arhats</s> — he is none other than this <s>Dharmaruci</s>. This is my third encounter with this <s>Dharmaruci</s> in the third incalculable age. It is with this in mind that I say: "After a long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after a very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>; after a very, very long time, <s>Dharmaruci</s>." And insofar as, monks, throughout three incalculable ages, through the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections) and other hundreds of thousands of difficult practices, unsurpassed perfect awakening was brought to fruition by me — for that entire time, this <s>Dharmaruci</s> was for the most part cast into the hells and the animal realms.'

body.text: 161.024. idamavocadbhagavān/ āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 161.025. dharmarucyavadānamaṣṭādaśam//
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmarucyavadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Dharmaruci</s>), the eighteenth.

body.text:
162.001. div19 jyotiṣkāvadānam/
162.002. buddho bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe/
162.002. rājagṛhe nagare subhadro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ/
162.003. so 'tyarthaṃ nirgrantheṣvabhiprasannaḥ/
162.003. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
162.004. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
162.004. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
162.005. bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
162.006. rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caran yena subhadrasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
162.007. adrākṣīt subhadro gṛhapatirbhagavantaṃ dūrādeva/
162.007. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ patnīmādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
162.008. upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat--bhagavan, iyaṃ me patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
162.009. kiṃ janayiṣyatīti/
162.009. bhagavānāha--gṛhapate, putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati/
162.011. tena bhagavataḥ śucinaḥ praṇītasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya pātrapūro dattaḥ/
162.012. bhagavānārogya ityuktvā piṇḍapātamādāya prakrāntaḥ/
162.012. tasya nātidūre bhūrikastiṣṭhati/
162.013. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadapyasmākamekaṃ bhikṣakulam, tadapi śramaṇo gautamo 'nvāvartayati/
162.013. gacchāmi, paśyāmi kiṃ śramaṇena gautamena vyākṛtamiti/
162.014. sa tatra gatvā kathayati--gṛhapate, śramaṇo gautama āgata āsīt? āgataḥ/
162.015. kiṃ tena vyākṛtam? ārya, mayā tasya patnī darśitā--kiṃ janayiṣyati? sa kathayati--putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
162.017. sa bhūriko gaṇitre kṛtāvī śvetavarṇāṃ gṛhītvā gaṇayitumārabdhah--paśyati yathā bhagavatā vyākṛtaṃ tatsarvaṃ tathaiva/
162.019. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi anusaṃvarṇyiṣyāmyaham, gṛhapatirbhūyasyā mātrayā śramaṇasya gautamasyābhipraśaṃsyati/
162.020. tadatra kiṃcid saṃvarṇayitavyaṃ kiṃcit vivarṇayitavyamiti viditvā hastau saṃparivartayati, mukhaṃ ca vibhaṇḍayati/
162.021. subhadro gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--ārya, kiṃ hastausamparivartayasi mukhaṃ ca vibhaṇḍayasīti? sa kathayati--gṛhapate, atra kiṃcit satyaṃ kiṃcinmṛṣā/
162.023. ārya, kiṃ satyaṃ kiṃ vā mṛṣā? gṛhapate, yadanenoktaṃ putraṃ janayiṣyatīti, idaṃ satyaṃ kathayati/
162.024. kulamuddyotayiṣyatītīdamapi satyam/
162.024. agrajyotiriti saṃjñā/
162.024. mandabhāgyaḥ sa sattvo jātamātra evāgninā kulaṃ dhakṣyati/
162.025. yat kathayati--divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti, idaṃ mṛṣā/
162.026. gehapate, asti kaścit tvayā dṛṣṭo manuṣyabhūto divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhavan? yatkathayati--mama śāsane pravrajiṣyatīti, idaṃ satyam/
162.027. yadā asya na bhaktaṃ na vastram, tadā niścayena śramaṇasya gautamasyāntike pravrajiṣyati/
162.028. sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti, idaṃ mṛṣā/
162.029. śramaṇasyaiva tāvadgautamasya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ nāsti, prāgevāsya bhaviṣyatīti/
162.029. subhadro viṣādamāpannaḥ kathayati--ārya, atra mayā kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti? bhūrikaḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, vayaṃ pravrajitāḥ śamānuśikṣāḥ/
162.031. tvameva jānīṣe/
162.031. iyuktvā prakrāntaḥ/
162.031. subhadraḥ saṃlakṣayati--sarvathā parityājyo 'sau iti viditvā sa bhaiṣajyaṃ dātumārabdhaḥ/
162.032. caramabhaviko 'sau <163>sattvaḥ/
body.translated_text: Chapter 19: The <s>Jyotiṣkāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Jyotiṣka</s>). The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground). In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> there lived a householder named <s>Subhadra</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions. He was exceedingly devoted to the <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain ascetics). He had brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Walking through <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, he approached the residence of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>. The householder <s>Subhadra</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen him, he took his wife and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, this wife of mine has become pregnant. What will she give birth to?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Householder, she will give birth to a son. He will illuminate the family, will experience both divine and human glory, and having gone forth in my teaching, will realize <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).' Then he gave the <s>Bhagavān</s> a bowl-full of pure and excellent food, both hard and soft. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having said 'Good health,' took the alms-food and departed. Not far from there stood <s>Bhūrika</s> (a <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetic). He reflected: 'Even the one alms-family that belongs to us, the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> steals away. Let me go and see what the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> has prophesied.' He went there and said: 'Householder, did the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> come?' 'He did.' 'What did he prophesy?' 'Venerable one, I showed him my wife — "What will she give birth to?" He said: "She will give birth to a son; he will illuminate the family, will experience both divine and human glory, and having gone forth in my teaching, will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions."' That <s>Bhūrika</s>, skilled in reckoning, took a white [calculating stone] and began to calculate — he saw that everything prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s> was exactly so. He reflected: 'If I confirm it, the householder will praise the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> all the more.' So, knowing that some of it should be confirmed and some should be disparaged, he turned his hands back and forth and contorted his face. The householder <s>Subhadra</s> said: 'Venerable one, why are you turning your hands and contorting your face?' He replied: 'Householder, herein some is true and some is false.' 'Venerable one, what is true and what is false?' 'Householder, what he said — "She will give birth to a son" — this he speaks truly. "He will illuminate the family" — this too is true. The name will be <s>Agrajyoti</s> ("First-Light"). But that being is unfortunate — as soon as he is born, he will burn the family with fire. What he says — "He will experience divine and human glory" — this is false. Householder, have you ever seen any human being experiencing divine and human glory? What he says — "He will go forth in my teaching" — this is true. When he has no food and no clothing, then surely he will go forth under the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>. "He will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions" — this is false.
