Even the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> himself has not realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions — how much less will this one attain it!' <s>Subhadra</s>, having become despondent, said: 'Venerable one, what should I do about this?' <s>Bhūrika</s> said: 'Householder, we are renunciants, practitioners of tranquility. You yourself must decide.' Having said this, he departed. <s>Subhadra</s> reflected: 'By all means, that one must be abandoned.' Having decided thus, he began to administer medicine [to cause an abortion]. That being was in its final existence.

163.004. prātiveśyaiḥ śrutam/
163.004. te tvaritatvaritaṃ gatāḥ pṛcchanti--bhavantaḥ, kimiyaṃ gṛhapatipatnī virauti? subhadraḥ kathayati--kukṣimatyeṣā/
163.006. nūnamasyāḥ prasavakāla iti/
163.006. te prakrāntaḥ/
163.006. subhadraḥ saṃlakṣayati--na śakyamasyā atropasaṃkramaṃ kartum/
163.007. araṇyaṃ nayāmīti/
163.007. sā tenāraṇyaṃ nītvā tathopakrāntā yathā kālagatā/
163.007. sa tāṃ pracchannaṃ gṛhamānīya suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānāṃ prātiveśakānāṃ ca kathayati--bhavantaḥ, patnī me kālagateti/
163.009. te vikroṣṭamārabdhāḥ/
163.009. sā tairvikrośadbhir nīlapītalohitāvadātairvastraiḥ śibikāmalaṃkṛtya śītavanaṃ śmaśānamabhinirhṛtā/
163.010. nirgranthaiḥ śrutam--te hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditāśchatrapatākā ucchrayitvā rājagṛhasya nagarasya rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭake upāhiṇḍamānā ārocayanti--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ/

163.014. sā ca kālagatā śītavanaśmaśānamabhinirhṛtā/
163.014. yasya tāvadvṛkṣamūlameva nāsti, kutastasya śākhāpatraphalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atrāntare kiṃcidbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāmajñātamadṛṣṭamaviditamavijñātam/
163.016. dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttānāmekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānām {catur}ṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśāradyaviśāradānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāmasaṃhatavihāriṇāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānāmaṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ
daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trirdivasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate--ko hīyate, ko vardhate, kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ, kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ, kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptaḥ, ko 'pāyaniṃnaḥ, ko 'pāyapravaṇah,
ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ, kamahamapāyāduddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamūlānyavaropayeyam, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam, kasya paripakkāni vimocayeyam/
163.026. āha ca--
163.027. apyevātikramedvelāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ/
163.028. na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velāmatikramet//1//iti/
163.029. atha bhagavānanyatarasmin pradeśe smitamakārṣīt/
163.029. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti, kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti/
163.031. yā adhastādgacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhavamutpalaṃ padma <164>mahāpadmaṃ narakaṃ gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti/

163.001. 'Perhaps this might serve as medicine for him.'
163.001. He began to press her left flank.
163.001. The fetus moved to the right flank.
163.002. <s>Subhadra</s> began to press the right flank.
163.002. The fetus moved to the left flank.
163.002. It is impossible and inconceivable that a being in its final existence would be cut off and die prematurely before the destruction of the defilements is reached.
163.004. That householder's wife, being squeezed in the womb, began to cry out.
163.004. The neighbors heard it.
163.004. They came in haste and asked: 'Sirs, why is this householder's wife crying out?' <s>Subhadra</s> said: 'She is with child.
163.006. Surely it is her time of delivery.'
163.006. They departed.
163.006. <s>Subhadra</s> reflected: 'It is not possible to dispose of her here.
163.007. I shall take her to the forest.'
163.007. He took her to the forest and so treated her that she died.
163.007. He brought her back to the house secretly and told his friends, relatives, kinsmen, and neighbors: 'Sirs, my wife has died.'
163.009. They began to weep.
163.009. She, by those who were weeping, was adorned with blue, yellow, red, and white garments on a litter and carried out to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground.
163.010. The <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jain ascetics) heard this. Delighted, pleased, and overjoyed, they raised parasols and banners and, parading through the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, proclaimed: 'Hear, good sirs!
163.012. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> prophesied concerning the wife of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>: "She will bear a son, will illuminate the family, will experience divine and human glory, and having gone forth in my teaching, will directly realize <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all defilements."
163.014. She has died and been carried out to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground.
163.014. When there is not even a root of a tree, how can there be branches, leaves, and fruits?' Meanwhile, nothing is unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, or unrealized by <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones.
163.016. For it is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), long practiced in the four means of gathering disciples, well-established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, confident in the four kinds of fearlessness, having abandoned the five limbs [of sensual desire], having transcended the five destinies, endowed with six limbs, having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), abiding in non-attachment, adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, guides on the Noble Eightfold Path, skilled in the nine successive attainments, empowered by the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, surpassing the lords of a thousand [worlds] — three times by night and three times by day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world, and knowledge-vision arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into adversity? Who has fallen into hardship, distress, and adversity? Who is headed for the lower realms? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is falling toward the lower realms? Whom may I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and in liberation? For whom may I plant wholesome roots not yet planted? For whom may I ripen those already planted? For whom may I liberate those already ripened?'
163.026. And it is said:
163.027. 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its shore,
163.028. but never would the <s>Buddha</s> transgress the occasion of beings to be trained.' //1//
163.029. Then the Blessed One, at a certain place, produced a smile.
163.029. For it is the nature that when <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward.
163.031. Those that go downward descend to the <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> hells — and in the hot hells they fall down cooled,

164.002. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, āhosvidanyatropapannā iti/
164.003. teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati/
164.003. teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃ bhavati--na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, nāpyanyatropapannāḥ/
164.004. api tvayamapūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ, asyānubhāvādasmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti/
164.005. te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya tannarakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti/
164.007. yā upariṣṭāgacchanti, tāścāturmahārājakāyikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśām yāmāṃstuṣitānnirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrāhmaṇaḥ parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhān devān gatvā duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyuddhoṣayanti/
164.011. gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante--
164.012. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
164.013. dhūnīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//2//
body.translated_text:
164.001. whereby the particular torments of those beings are allayed.
164.002. They think: 'Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?'
164.003. For the purpose of generating faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation.
164.003. Having seen the emanation, they think: 'We have certainly not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.
164.004. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, by whose power our particular torments have been allayed.'
164.005. They, having generated faith in the emanation, exhaust the karma to be experienced in those hells, and take rebirth among gods and humans where they become vessels for the truths.
164.007. Those rays that go upward ascend to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim: 'Suffering! Emptiness! Non-self!'
164.011. And they recite two verses:
164.012. 'Strive! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching!
164.013. Shake off the army of Death, as an elephant shakes a reed hut.' //2//

body.text:
164.014. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
164.015. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//3//
body.translated_text:
164.014. 'Whoever shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline),
164.015. having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall make an end of suffering.' //3//

164.016. atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti/
164.017. bhagavata āsye 'ntarhitāḥ/
164.017. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--
164.018. nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ/
164.020. avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva//4//
body.translated_text:
164.016. Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, circled back and followed behind the Blessed One.
164.017. They disappeared into the mouth of the Blessed One.
164.017. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:
164.018. 'From within your mouth has issued forth a cluster of rays, of a thousand hues and varied colors;
164.020. by which the directions all around are illuminated, as by the sun when it rises.' //4//

body.text:
164.022. gāthāśca bhāṣate--
164.023. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
164.026. nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ//5//
body.translated_text:
164.022. And he spoke verses:
164.023. 'The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, having abandoned meanness, pride, and intoxication, the supreme cause for beings in the world,
164.026. do not display a smile — conch-white and lotus-bright — the Victors, conquerors of foes, without reason.' //5//

body.text:
164.028. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīra buddhyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
164.030. dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//6//
body.translated_text:
164.028. 'Having yourself realized at that very time, O Steadfast One, through your own wisdom, O ascetic, foremost of sages,
164.030. dispel the doubt that has arisen for the listeners who are eager to hear, with your firm, excellent, and auspicious words, O Bull among Sages.' //6//

body.text:
165.001. <165>nākasmāllavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāḥ/
165.003. yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti nāthāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ//7//iti/
165.005. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametat/
165.005. nāhetupratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
165.006. gaccha ānanda, bhikṣūṇāmārocaya--tathāgato bhikṣavaḥ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantukāmaḥ/
165.007. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantum, sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu/
165.008. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhikṣūṇāmārocayati--tathāgata āyuṣmantaḥ śmaśānacārikāṃ gantukāmaḥ/
165.009. yo yuṣmākamutsahate tathāgatena sārdhaṃ śmaśānacārikaṃ gantum, sa cīvarakāṇi gṛhṇātu/
165.010. evamāyuṣmanniti te bhikṣavaḥ sarve saṃśrutya bhagavatsakāśamupagatāḥ/
165.011. atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvāstaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhannarhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gajarāja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭagaṇaparivṛto haṃsarāja iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suparṇīva parikṣagaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaścakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaścandra iva
nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto brahmeva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntairindrayairasaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro dvātriṃśatā
mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'śītyā cānuvyañjanairvirājitagātro vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtamūrtiḥ sūryasahasrātirekaprabho jaṅgama iva ratnaparvataḥ samantato bhadrako daśabhirbalaiścaturbhirvaiśāradyaistribhirāveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānairmahākaruṇayā ca samanvāgata ājñātakauṇḍinyāśvajidbāṣpamahānāmabhadrikaśāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapayaśaḥpūrṇaprabhṛtimahāśrāvakaiḥ parivṛto 'nyena ca mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena anekaiśca prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ śītavanaṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
165.026. aṣṭādaśānuśaṃsā buddhacārikāyāmityanekāni devatāśatasahasrāṇi bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhāni/
165.027. śītavanānuguṇāśca vāyavo vāyitumārabdhāḥ//
body.translated_text:
165.001. 'Not without cause, like the ocean and the king of mountains in steadfastness, do the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddhas</s>, the steadfast ones, display a smile.
165.003. For whose sake the Protectors display a smile — that is what those multitudes of people desire to hear.' //7//
165.005. The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.
165.005. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, display a smile.
165.006. Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and announce to the monks: "The <s>Tathāgata</s>, monks, wishes to go on a charnel-ground excursion."
165.007. Whoever among you is willing to go on a charnel-ground excursion with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robes.'
165.008. 'So be it, Venerable Sir.' The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, announced to the monks: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, Venerable Ones, wishes to go on a charnel-ground excursion.
165.009. Whoever among you is willing to go on a charnel-ground excursion with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him take his robes.'
165.010. 'So be it, Venerable Sir.' Those monks, having all assented, approached the Blessed One.
165.011. Then the Blessed One — tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; reassured, with a reassured retinue; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with an <s>Arhat</s> retinue; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring confidence, with a retinue inspiring confidence — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cows, like an elephant-king surrounded by a herd of young elephants, like a lion surrounded by a pack of predators, like a king of geese surrounded by a flock of geese, like a <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa) surrounded by a flock of birds, like a learned one surrounded by a company of students, like a skilled physician surrounded by a company of the sick, like a warrior surrounded by a company of soldiers, like a guide surrounded by a company of travelers, like a caravan-leader surrounded by a company of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by the townsfolk, like a petty king surrounded by a company of ministers, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods — like a calm ocean, like a rain-bearing cloud, like a rut-free elephant-lord, with senses well-tamed, his conduct and deportment unperturbed, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being and the eighty minor marks, his body radiant with an aura of a <s>vyāma</s>'s breadth, his radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a walking mountain of jewels, splendid on all sides — endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three special qualities, the foundations of mindfulness, and great compassion, accompanied by the Elders <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Aśvajit</s>, <s>Bāṣpa</s>, <s>Mahānāma</s>, <s>Bhadrika</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Yaśas</s>, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and other great disciples, surrounded by another great community of monks and by many hundreds of thousands of beings, set out for the <s>Śītavana</s> great charnel ground.
165.026. There are eighteen benefits of a <s>Buddha's</s> excursion — thus many hundreds of thousands of deities followed behind the Blessed One.
165.027. And winds began to blow in the direction of the <s>Śītavana</s>.

body.text:
165.028. rājagṛhāt dvau bāladārakau brāhmaṇadārakaḥ kṣatriyadārakaśca bahir nirgatya krīḍataḥ/
165.029. tayoḥ kṣatriyadārako 'vagāḍhaśrāddho brāhmaṇadārako na tathā/
165.029. sa brāhmaṇadārakaḥ kṣatriyadārakasya kathayati--vayasya, bhagavatā subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ patnī vyākṛtā--putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
165.032. sā ca mṛtā kālagatā śītavanaṃ śmaśānaṃ nirhṛtā--mā haiva bhagavatā bhāṣitaṃ vitathaṃ syāditi/
165.033. sa kṣatriyadārako gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
166.001. <166>sacandratāraṃ prapatedihāmbaraṃ mahī saśailā savanā nabho vrajet/
166.003. mahodadhīnāmudakaṃ kṣayaṃ vrajenmaharṣayaḥ syūr na mṛṣābhidhāyinaḥ//8//iti
166.005. sa ca brāhmaṇadārakaḥ kathayati--vayasya, yadyevam, gacchāmaḥ śītavanaṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ paśyāmah? vayasya, gacchāmaḥ/
166.006. tau smprasthitau/
166.006. bhagavāṃśca rājagṛhānnirgataḥ/
166.006. adrākṣīt sa kṣatriyadārako bhagavantaṃ dūrādeva/
166.007. dṛṣṭvā ca punargāthāṃ bhāṣate--
166.008. anuddhato vigatakutūhalo muniryathā vrajatyeṣa janaughasaṃvṛtaḥ/
166.010. niḥsaṃśayaṃ paragaṇavādimardano nadasyate mṛgapatinādamuttamam//9//
body.translated_text:
165.028. Two young boys from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy and a <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy, went outside to play.
165.029. Of the two, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy was deeply faithful, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy was not so.
165.029. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy said to the <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy: 'Friend, the Blessed One predicted of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>'s wife: "She will bear a son, she will illuminate the family, she will experience both divine and human prosperity, and having gone forth in my teaching, she will realize <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)."
165.032. But she has died, passed away, and been carried out to the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cold Grove) charnel ground — surely the Blessed One's words could not be false!'
165.033. The <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy spoke a verse:
166.001. <166>'The sky with its moon and stars might fall down here; the earth with its mountains and forests might fly up to the heavens;
166.003. The waters of the great oceans might be exhausted — but the Great Sages would never speak falsely.' //8//
166.005. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> boy said: 'Friend, if that is so, shall we go to the <s>Śītavana</s> great charnel ground and see?' 'Friend, let us go.'
166.006. The two set out.
166.006. And the Blessed One had departed from <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
166.006. The <s>Kṣatriya</s> boy saw the Blessed One from afar.
166.007. Having seen him, he again spoke a verse:
166.008. 'The way this sage walks, unagitated, free from curiosity, surrounded by a crowd of people —
166.010. Without doubt, this crusher of opposing schools' doctrines will roar the supreme roar of the lion.' //9//

body.text:
166.012. yathā hyamī śītavanonmukhotsukāḥ pravānti vātā himapaṅkaśītalāḥ/
166.014. prayānti nūnaṃ bahavo divaukaso nirīkṣituṃ śākyamunervikurvitam//10//iti/
166.016. rājñā bimbisāreṇa śrutam--bhagavatā subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ patnī vyākṛtā--putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati/
166.018. sā ca mṛtā kālagatā śītavanaṃ śmaśānamabhinirhṛtā/
166.018. bhagavāṃśca saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śītavanaṃ saṃprasthita iti/
166.019. śrutvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--na bhagavān nirarthakaṃ śītavanaṃ gacchati/
166.020. nūnaṃ bhagavān subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ patnīmāgamya mahadvineyakāryaṃ kartukāmo bhaviṣyati/
166.021. paśyāmīti/
166.021. so 'pyantaḥpurakumārāmātyapaurajānapadaparivṛto rājagṛhānnirgantumārabdhaḥ/
166.022. adrākṣīt sa kṣatriyakumārako rājānaṃ māgadhaśreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dūrādeva/
166.022. dṛṣṭvā ca punargāthāṃ bhāṣate--
166.024. yathā hi śreṇyo magadhādhipo hyayaṃ viniryayau rājagṛhāt sabāndhavaḥ/
166.026. pravartate me hṛdi niścitā matirmahājanasyābhyudayo bhaviṣyati//11//iti/
166.028. janakāyena bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vivaramanupradattam/
166.028. bhagavān smitonmukho mahājanamadhyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
166.029. nirgrantha bhagavantaṃ smitonmukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayanti--yathā śramaṇo gautamaḥ smitonmukho mahājanamadhyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ, nūnamayaṃ bodhisattvo na kālagataḥ/
166.030. taiḥ subhadro gṛhapatiruktah--gṛhapate, nanvayaṃ sattvo mandabhāgyo na kālagata iti/
166.031. sa kathayati--ārya yadyevam, <167>kathamatra pratipattavyamiti? te kathayanti--gṛhapate, vayaṃ śamāttaśikṣāḥ, tvameva jñāsyasīti/
body.translated_text:
166.012. 'Just as these winds blow toward the <s>Śītavana</s>, eager and cold with frost and mud,
166.014. Surely many celestial beings are coming to witness the miraculous display of <s>Śākyamuni</s>.' //10//
166.016. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> had heard: 'The Blessed One predicted of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>'s wife: "She will bear a son, she will illuminate the family, she will experience both divine and human prosperity, and having gone forth in my teaching, she will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>."
166.018. But she has died, passed away, and been carried out to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground.
166.018. And the Blessed One together with the community of disciples has set out for the <s>Śītavana</s>.'
166.019. Having heard this, he thought: 'The Blessed One does not go to the <s>Śītavana</s> without purpose.
166.020. Surely the Blessed One, having arrived at the householder <s>Subhadra</s>'s wife, will wish to accomplish a great work of training those to be trained.
166.021. Let me go and see.'
166.021. He too, surrounded by his inner court, princes, ministers, and city and country folk, set out from <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
166.022. The <s>Kṣatriya</s> prince saw King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> from afar.
166.022. Having seen him, he again spoke a verse:
166.024. 'Just as <s>Śreṇya</s>, lord of <s>Magadha</s>, has come forth from <s>Rājagṛha</s> together with his kinsmen,
166.026. A firm conviction arises in my heart: there will be a great upliftment of the multitude.' //11//
166.028. The crowd of people, seeing the Blessed One, made way for him.
166.028. The Blessed One, with a smiling countenance, entered into the midst of the great assembly.
166.029. The <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain) ascetics, seeing the Blessed One with a smiling countenance, observed: 'Just as the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has entered the midst of the great assembly with a smiling face, surely this being is not dead.'
166.030. They said to the householder <s>Subhadra</s>: 'Householder, surely this unlucky being has not died?'
166.031. He said: 'Venerable sirs, if that is so, <167> what should be done about it?' They said: 'Householder, we are those whose practices have been perfected through tranquility; you yourself will know.'

body.text:
167.002. sa tāṃ patnīṃ citāyāmāropya dhmāpayitumārabdhaḥ/
167.002. tasyāḥ sarvaḥ kāyo dagdhaḥ sthāpayitvā kukṣisāmantakam/
167.003. tathāsau kukṣiḥ sphuṭitaḥ, padmaṃ prādurbhūtam/
167.003. tasya coparipadmakarṇikāyāṃ kumāro niṣaṇṇo 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ/
167.004. taṃ dṛṣṭvā anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi paraṃ vismayamupagatāni/
167.005. nirgranthā nipātamadamānā naca(naṣṭa?)prabhāvāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
167.006. tatra bhagavān subhadraṃ gṛhapatimāmantrayate--gṛhapate, gṛhāṇa kumāram/
167.006. sa nirgranthānāṃ mukhamavalokitumārabdhaḥ/
167.007. te kathayanti--gṛhapate, yadi prajvalitāmetāṃ citāṃ pravekṣyasi, sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyasīti/
167.008. sa na pratigṛhṇāti/
167.008. tatra bhagavāñ jīvakaṃ kumārabhūtamāmantrayate--gṛhāṇa jīvaka kumārakamiti/
167.009. sa saṃlakṣayati--asthānamanavakāśo bhagavān māmasthāne niyokṣyati/
167.010. gṛhṇāmīti/
167.010. tena nirviśaṅkena citāṃ vigāhya gṛhītaḥ/
167.011. vigāhatastasya jinājñayā citāṃ pratigṛhṇataścāgnigataṃ kumārakam/
167.013. jinaprabhāvānmahato hutāśanaḥ kṣaṇena jāto himapaṅkaśītalaḥ//12//
body.translated_text:
167.002. He placed his wife on the pyre and began to cremate her.
167.002. Her entire body was burned, except for the area around the womb.
167.003. And thus her womb burst open, and a lotus appeared.
167.003. Upon it, seated on the lotus receptacle, was a boy — handsome, beautiful, and pleasing to behold.
167.004. Seeing him, many hundreds of thousands of beings were filled with supreme wonder.
167.005. The <s>Nirgrantha</s> ascetics were confounded, having lost their influence.
167.006. Then the Blessed One addressed the householder <s>Subhadra</s>: 'Householder, take the boy.'
167.006. He began to look toward the faces of the <s>Nirgrantha</s>s.
167.007. They said: 'Householder, if you enter this blazing pyre, you will be completely destroyed.'
167.008. He did not accept the child.
167.008. Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhūta</s>: 'Take the boy, <s>Jīvaka</s>.'
167.009. He reflected: 'It is impossible that the Blessed One would employ me in an improper task.
167.010. I shall take him.'
167.010. Without hesitation, he plunged into the pyre and took the child.
167.011. As he plunged into the pyre at the Victor's command and received the fire-engulfed boy,
167.013. By the power of the Victor, the great fire in an instant became cold as frost and mud. //12//

body.text:
167.015. tato jīvakaṃ kumārabhūtamidamavocat--jīvaka, māsi kṣata upahato veti? sa kathayati--rājakule 'haṃ bhadanta jāto rājakule vṛddhaḥ/
167.016. nābhijānāmi gośīrṣacandanasyāpīdṛśaṃ śaityam yadbhagavatā adhiṣṭhitāyāścitāyāḥ/
167.017. tatra bhagavān subhadraṃ gṛhapatimāmantrayate--gṛhāṇedānīṃ gṛhapate kumāramiti/
167.018. sa mithyādarśanavihataḥ/
167.018. tathāpi na saṃpratipadyate/
167.018. nirgranthānāmeva mukhaṃ vyavalokayati/
167.019. te kathayanti--gṛhapate, ayaṃ sattvo 'tīva mandabhāgyo yo hi nāma sarvabhakṣeṇāpyagninā na dagdhaḥ/
167.020. kiṃ bahunā? yadyevaṃ gṛhaṃ praveśayasi, nīyatām/
167.020. te gṛhamutsādayad bhaviṣyasi, tvaṃ ca prāṇairviyujyasa iti/
167.021. nāsti ātmasamaṃ premeti/
167.021. tenāsau na pratigṛhītaḥ/
167.022. tatra bhagavān rājānaṃ bimbisāramāmantayate--gṛhāṇa mahārāja kumāramiti/
167.022. tena sasambhrameṇa hastau prasārya gṛhītaḥ/
167.023. tataḥ samantato nirīkṣya kathayati--bhagavan, kiṃ bhavatu asya dārakasya jyotiṣka iti nāmeti/
167.025. tasya jyotiṣka iti nāṃdheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
167.025. tato bhagavatā tasya janakāyasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā bahubhiḥ sattvaśatairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ/
167.027. kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam, kaiścidanāgāmiphalam, kaicit sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiściduṣmagatāni kuśalamūlānyutpāditāni, kaiścinmūrdhānaḥ, kaiścit mṛdumadhyāḥ kṣāntayaḥ, kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau, kaiściccharaṇagamanāni, kaiścicchikṣāpadāni/
167.031. yadbhūyasā sā parṣadbuddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā/
167.032. jyotiṣko dārako rājñā bimbisāreṇa aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradatto <168>dvābhyāsaṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhāgtrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām/
body.translated_text:
167.015. Then the Blessed One said to <s>Jīvaka Kumārabhūta</s>: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, are you cut, wounded, or injured?' He said: 'Venerable Sir, I was born in the royal household and raised in the royal household.
167.016. I have never known such coolness even from <s>gośīrṣa</s> (ox-head) sandalwood as that of the pyre blessed by the Blessed One.'
167.017. Then the Blessed One addressed the householder <s>Subhadra</s>: 'Take the boy now, householder.'
167.018. He, corrupted by wrong views,
167.018. still did not comply.
167.018. He kept looking toward the faces of the <s>Nirgrantha</s>s.
167.019. They said: 'Householder, this being is exceedingly unlucky, for even the all-consuming fire did not burn him.
167.020. What more need be said? If you bring him into the house, he will destroy the household and you yourself will lose your life.'
167.021. 'There is no love equal to love of self' — therefore the child was not accepted by him.
167.022. Then the Blessed One addressed King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Take the boy, Great King.'
167.022. He eagerly stretched out his hands and took the child.
167.023. Then, looking around on all sides, the king said: 'Blessed One, let his name be <s>Jyotiṣka</s> ("Radiant").'
167.025. And the name <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was established for him.
167.025. Then the Blessed One, knowing the dispositions, latent tendencies, natures, and constitutions of that crowd of people, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of beings attained a great distinction.
167.027. By some, the fruit of stream-entry was realized; by some, the fruit of once-returning; by some, the fruit of non-returning; by some, <s>Arhattva</s> was realized through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>; by some, wholesome roots in the category of warmth were generated; by some, the summit; by some, the gentle and middling forbearances; by some, the mind was directed toward the awakening of a disciple; by some toward solitary awakening; by some toward unsurpassed perfect awakening; by some the refuges were taken; by some the precepts.
167.031. For the most part, that assembly remained inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
167.032. The boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was entrusted by King <s>Bimbisāra</s> to eight nurses: <168> two nurses for carrying, two wet-nurses, two nurses for bathing, and two nurses for playing.

body.text:
168.002. so 'ṣṭhābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
168.003. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam//
body.translated_text:
168.002. Raised by those eight nurses, he grew, nourished with milk, curds, fresh butter, clarified butter, cream of clarified butter, and other choice and excellent provisions.
168.003. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. //

body.text:
168.004. tasya mātulaḥ paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gataḥ/
168.004. tena śrutam yathā mama bhaginī sattvavatī saṃvṛttā/
168.005. sā bhagavatā vyākṛtā--putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyoyiṣyati, divyāmānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
168.006. sa paṇyaṃ visarjayitvā pratipaṇyamādāya rājagṛhamāgataḥ/
168.007. tena śrutam yathā sā asmākaṃ bhaginī kālagateti/
168.008. śrutvā ca punaḥ saṃlakṣayati--bhagavatā asau vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyāṃ mānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
168.010. mā haiva tabhagavato bhāṣitaṃ vitathaṃ syāt/
168.010. tena tiraḥprātiveśyāḥ pṛṣṭāh--śrutaṃ mayā asmākaṃ bhaginī sattvavatī saṃvṛttā/
168.011. sā bhagavatā vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati, kulamuddyotayiṣyati, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyati, mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
168.013. śrutvā vayaṃ parituṣṭāḥ/
168.013. sā ca śrūyate mṛtā kālagateti/
168.014. mā haiva bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ vitathaṃ syāditi/
168.014. te gāthāṃ bhāṣante--
168.015. sacandratāraṃ prapatedihāmbaraṃ mahī saśailā savanā nabho vrajet/
168.017. mahodadhīnāmudakaṃ kṣayaṃ vrajenmaharṣayaḥ syūr na mṛṣābhidhāyinaḥ//13//
body.translated_text:
168.004. His maternal uncle, having taken merchandise, had gone to another country.
168.004. He heard that his sister had become pregnant.
168.005. 'She was predicted by the Blessed One: "She will bear a son, she will illuminate the family, she will experience both divine and human prosperity, and having gone forth in my teaching, she will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>."'
168.006. Having sold the merchandise and taken the return goods, he came to <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
168.007. He heard that 'our sister has passed away.'
168.008. Hearing this, he reflected: 'The Blessed One predicted of her: "She will bear a son, she will illuminate the family, she will experience both divine and human prosperity, and having gone forth in my teaching, she will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>."
168.010. Surely the Blessed One's words could not be false.'
168.010. He asked the neighbors across the street: 'I heard that our sister had become pregnant.
168.011. She was predicted by the Blessed One: "She will bear a son, she will illuminate the family, she will experience both divine and human prosperity, and having gone forth in my teaching, she will realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>."
168.013. Hearing that, we were delighted.
168.013. But we hear that she has died, passed away.
168.014. Surely the Blessed One's words could not be false.'
168.014. They spoke a verse:
168.015. 'The sky with its moon and stars might fall down here; the earth with its mountains and forests might fly up to the heavens;
168.017. The waters of the great oceans might be exhausted — but the Great Sages would never speak falsely.' //13//

body.text:
168.019. na bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ vitatham/
168.019. kathaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ vitathaṃ bhaviṣyati? kiṃ tu tena svāmināpi asau tathā tathā upakrāntā, yathā kālagatā/
168.020. sa dārako maharddhiko mahānubhāvaḥ/
168.021. agninā na dagdhaḥ/
168.021. adyāpi rājakule saṃvardhata iti/
168.021. sa subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--na yuktaṃ gṛhapate tvayā kṛtam/
168.022. kiṃ kṛtam? asmākaṃ sattvavatī bhaginī tvayā nirgranthavigrāhitena tathā tathā upakrāntā, yathā kālagatā/
168.023. sa dārako maharddhiko mahānubhāvaḥ/
168.023. agnināpi na dagdhaḥ/
168.024. adyāpi rājakule saṃvardhate/
168.024. tadgatametat/
168.024. yadi tāvatkumārabhānayasi, ityevaṃ kuśalam/
168.025. no cedvayaṃ tvāṃ jñātimadhyādutkṣipāmaḥ/
168.025. salokānām {sālohitānām?} saṃkāraṃ pātayāmaḥ, rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu cāvaraṇaṃ niścārayāmah--asmākaṃ bhaginī subhadreṇa gṛhapatinā praghātitā/
168.027. strīghātako 'yam/
168.027. na kenacidābhāṣitavyamiti/
168.027. rājakule ca te 'narthaṃ kārayāma iti/
168.028. sa śrutvā vyathitaḥ/
168.028. yathaiṣa paribhāṣate, nūnamevaṃ karomīti viditvā rājñaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--deva, mama jñātaya evaṃ paribhāṣante--yadi tāvat kumāramānayasītyevaṃ kuśalam, no cedānayasi, vayaṃ tvāṃ jñātimadhyādutkṣipāmaḥ, saṃkāraṃ pātayāmaḥ, rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu cāvaraṇaṃ niścārayāmah--asmākaṃ bhaginī subhadreṇa gṛhapatinā praghātitā/
168.032. strīghātako 'yam/
168.032. na kenacidābhāṣitavyamiti/
168.032. rājakule ca te 'narthaṃ kārayāma iti/
body.translated_text:
168.019. The word of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is not false.
168.019. How could the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s> be false? But that boy was so mistreated by his own master that he died.
168.020. That boy is of great supernatural power and great might.
168.021. He was not burned by fire.
168.021. Even now he is growing up in the royal palace.
168.021. He went to the householder <s>Subhadra</s> and said: 'What you have done, householder, is not right.'
168.022. 'What have I done?' 'Our sister <s>Sattvavatī</s> was so mistreated by you, who were led astray by the <s>Nirgrantha</s> (Jain ascetic), that she died.
168.023. That boy is of great supernatural power and great might.
168.023. He was not even burned by fire.
168.024. Even now he is growing up in the royal palace.
168.024. Let that matter pass.
168.024. If you bring back the boy, then all is well.
168.025. If you do not, we shall expel you from the midst of the kinsmen.
168.025. We shall cast you onto the refuse-heap before the relatives {blood-relations?}, and in the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections we shall proclaim: "Our sister was killed by the householder <s>Subhadra</s>.
168.027. He is a murderer of women.
168.027. No one should speak to him."
168.027. And we shall cause trouble for you at the royal court.'
168.028. Hearing this, he was distressed.
168.028. Knowing that 'he will certainly do as he threatens,' he fell at the feet of the king and said: 'Your Majesty, my relatives are threatening me thus: "If you bring back the boy, then all is well. If you do not bring him, we shall expel you from the midst of the kinsmen, cast you onto the refuse-heap, and in the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections we shall proclaim: Our sister was killed by the householder <s>Subhadra</s>.
168.032. He is a murderer of women.
168.032. No one should speak to him.
168.032. And we shall cause trouble for you at the royal court."'

body.text:
169.001. <169>tadarhasi jyotiṣkaṃ kumāraṃ dātumiti/
169.001. rājā kathayati--gṛhapate, na mayā tvatsakāśāt jyotiṣkaḥ kumāro gṛhītaḥ, kiṃ tu bhagavatā mama nyastaḥ/
169.002. yadi tvaṃ kumāreṇārthī, bhagavatsakāśaṃ gaccheti/
169.002. sa bhagavatsakāśaṃ gataḥ/
169.003. pādayor nipatya kathayati--bhagavan, mama jñātaya evaṃ paribhāṣante--yadi tāvat kumāramānayasītyevaṃ kuśalam/
169.004. no cedānayasi, vayaṃ tvāṃ jñātimadhyādutkṣipāmaḥ, saṃkāraṃ pātayāmaḥ, rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu cāvaraṇaṃ niścārayāmaḥ/
169.005. asmākaṃ bhaginī subhadreṇa gṛhapatinā praghātitā/
169.006. strīghātako 'yam/
169.006. na kenacidābhāṣitavya iti/
169.006. rājakule cānarthaṃ kārayāma iti/
169.007. tadarhasi jyotiṣkaṃ kumāraṃ dāpayitumiti/
169.007. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--yadi subhadro jyotiṣkaṃ kumāraṃ na labhate, sthānametadvidyate yaduṣṇaṃ rudhiraṃ chardayitvā kālaṃ kariṣyati/
169.008. iti viditvā āyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha ānanda, rājānaṃ bimbisāraṃ madvacanenārogyaya, evaṃ ca vada--anuprayaccha mahārāja subhadrasya gṛhapaterjyotiṣkaṃ kumāram/
169.010. yadi subhadro gṛhapatirjyotiṣkaṃ kumāraṃ na labhate, sthānametadvidyate yaduṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ chardayitvā kālaṃ kariṣyatīti/
169.012. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yena rājā bimbisārastenopasaṃskrāntaḥ/
169.013. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ bimbisārametadavocat--bhagavāṃste mahārāja ārogyayati, kathayati ca--anuprayaccha mahārāja subhadrasya gṛhapaterjyotiṣkaṃ kumāram/
169.014. yadi subhadro gṛhapatirjyotiṣkaṃ kumāraṃ na labhate, sthānametadvidyate yat subhadro gṛhapatiruṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ chardayitvā kālaṃ kariṣye/
169.016. rājā kathayati--vande bhadantānanda buddhaṃ bhagavantam/
169.016. yathā bhagavānājñāpayati tathā kariṣye/
169.017. ārogyamityuktā āyuṣmānānandaḥ prakrāntaḥ/
169.017. rājā bimbisāraḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, mayā ayaṃ kumāraḥ saṃvardhitaḥ/
169.018. priyaśca me manāpaśca/
169.018. samayato 'haṃ muñcāmi, yadi māṃ divase divase triṣkālaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmatīti/
169.019. sa kathayati--deva upasaṃkramiṣyati/
169.020. ko 'nya upasaṃkramitavya iti? sa rājñā sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaṃ kṛtvā hastiskandha āropya visarjitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
169.001. 'Therefore, please give the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s>.'
169.001. The king said: 'Householder, I did not take the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> from you; rather, the <s>Bhagavān</s> entrusted him to me.
169.002. If you want the boy, go to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
169.002. He went to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
169.003. Falling at his feet, he said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, my relatives are threatening me thus: "If you bring back the boy, then all is well.
169.004. If you do not bring him, we shall expel you from the midst of the kinsmen, cast you onto the refuse-heap, and in the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections we shall proclaim:
169.005. Our sister was killed by the householder <s>Subhadra</s>.
169.006. He is a murderer of women.
169.006. No one should speak to him.
169.006. And we shall cause trouble for you at the royal court."
169.007. Therefore, please have the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> returned to me.'
169.007. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'If <s>Subhadra</s> does not obtain the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, it is possible that he will vomit hot blood and die.'
169.008. Having realized this, he addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, convey my greetings to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, and say thus: "Return the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> to the householder <s>Subhadra</s>, O great king.
169.010. If the householder <s>Subhadra</s> does not obtain the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, it is possible that he will vomit hot blood and die."'
169.012. 'Yes, Venerable Sir' — the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approached King <s>Bimbisāra</s>.
169.013. Having approached, he said this to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> conveys his greetings to you, O great king, and says: "Return the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> to the householder <s>Subhadra</s>, O great king.
169.014. If the householder <s>Subhadra</s> does not obtain the boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, it is possible that the householder <s>Subhadra</s> will vomit hot blood and die."'
169.016. The king said: 'I pay homage, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
169.016. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> commands, so shall I do.'
169.017. Having conveyed the greetings, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> departed.
169.017. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said: 'Householder, I have raised this boy.
169.018. He is dear and pleasing to me.
169.018. I release him on this condition: that he comes to visit me three times daily.'
169.019. He said: 'Your Majesty, he will come.
169.020. Who else should he visit?' Then the king, having adorned the boy with all ornaments, mounted him on an elephant's back and sent him off.

body.text:
169.022. ācaritametallokasya--na tāvat putrasya nāma prajñāyate yāvat pitā jīvati/
169.022. yāvadapareṇa samayena subhadro gṛhapatiḥ kālagataḥ/
169.023. jyotiṣkaḥ kumāraḥ svagṛhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
169.023. sa buddhe 'bhiprasanno dharme saṃghe 'bhiprasannaḥ/
169.024. buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gato dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ/
169.024. tena yasmin pradeśe tena subhadreṇa patnī āghātitā, tasmin pradeśe vihāraṃ kārayitvā sarvāpakaraṇasampūrṇaścāturdiśāryabhikṣusaṃghāya niryātitaḥ/
169.026. tathā sthavirairapi sūtrānta upanibaddham--bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati mṛditakukṣike dāva iti//
body.translated_text:
169.022. It is the custom of the world that a son's name does not become known as long as the father lives.
169.022. In the course of time, the householder <s>Subhadra</s> died.
169.023. The boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was established in his own household.
169.023. He was devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and devoted to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
169.024. He took refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, and took refuge in the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
169.024. At the very place where <s>Subhadra</s> had his wife killed, he had a <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) built, and, having furnished it with all requisites, he donated it to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks of the four directions.
169.026. Thus the elders also incorporated it into a <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourse): 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Mṛditakukṣika</s> grove.'

body.text:
169.028. subhadrasya gṛhapateḥ pauruṣeyā ye paṇyamādāya deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ, taiḥ śrutam--subhadro gṛhapatiḥ kālagataḥ/
169.029. jyotiṣkaḥ kumāraḥ svagṛhe pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
169.029. sa buddhe 'bhiprasanno dharme saṃghe 'bhiprasanno buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gato dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gata iti/
169.030. teṣāṃ ca gośīrṣacananamayaṃ pātraṃ saṃpannam/
169.031. taistadratnānāṃ pūrayitvā jyotiṣkasya gṛhapateḥ prābhṛtamanupreṣitam/
169.031. tena taddīrghe stambhe āropya sthāpitam/
169.032. ghaṇḍāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--nedaṃ kenacit viṣṭayā vā <170>śītayā vā karkaṭakena vā gṛhītavyam/
body.translated_text:
169.028. The servants of the householder <s>Subhadra</s>, who had gone abroad with merchandise, heard that the householder <s>Subhadra</s> had died.
169.029. The boy <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was established in his own household.
169.029. He was devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, had taken refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, and had taken refuge in the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
169.030. They had acquired a bowl made of <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood (ox-head sandalwood).
169.031. They filled it with jewels and sent it as a gift for the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s>.
169.031. He placed it atop a tall pillar.
169.032. A bell-proclamation was made: 'No one is to take this by means of a ladder, or a pole, or a hook.

body.text:
170.001. ya etacchramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā maharddhiko vā mahānubhāvah ṛddhyā gṛhṇāti, tasyedam yathāsukhamiti/
170.002. tīrthyāḥ kalyamevotthāya tīrthyasparśanaṃ gacchanti/
170.003. taistad dṛṣṭam/
170.003. dṛṣṭvā ca punarjyotiṣkasya gṛhapateḥ kathayanti--gṛhapate, kimetaditi? tena teṣāṃ vistareṇārocitam/
170.004. te kathayanti--gṛhapate, tvaṃ śramaṇaśākyaputreṣvabhiprasannaḥ/
170.005. te evaṃ grahīṣyantītyuktvā prakrāntāḥ/
170.005. yāvat sthavirasthavirā bhikṣavo rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭāḥ/
170.006. tairdṛṣṭvā tairapi jyotiṣko gṛhapatiḥ pṛṣṭah--kimetaditi? tena tathaiva vistareṇa samākhyātam/
170.007. te kathayanti--gṛhapate, kiṃ pātramātrasyārthāyātmānaṃ saṃprakāśayāmah? uktaṃ bhagavatā--pracchannakalyāṇairvo bhikṣavo vihartavyaṃ dhūtapāpairityuktvā prakrāntāḥ/
170.008. yāvadāyuṣmān daśabalaḥ kāśyapastamanuprāptaḥ/
170.009. sa pṛcchati--gṛhapate, kimetaditi? tena yathāvṛttamārocitam/
170.010. āyuṣmān daśabalakāśyapaḥ saṃlakṣayati--yena mayā anādikālopacitaṃ kleśagaṇaṃ vāntaṃ tyaktaṃ charditaṃ pratinisṛṣṭam, taṃ māṃ gṛhapatistīrthikasādhāraṇayā ṛddhyā āhvayati/
170.012. tadasya manorathaṃ pūrayāmīti/
170.012. tena gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya tatpātraṃ gṛhītam/
170.012. sa tadgṛhītvā vihāraṃ gato bhikṣubhirucyate--sthavira, kutastava gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ pātramiti? tena yathāvṛttamārocitam/
170.014. bhikṣavaḥ kathayanti--sthavira, kalpate tava pātramātrasyārthāya ṛddhiṃ vidarśayitumiti? kathayati--āyuṣmantaḥ, kalpatu vā mā vā/
170.015. kṛtamidānīm/
170.015. kiṃ kriyatāmiti? etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti/
170.016. bhagavānāha--na bhikṣuṇā āgārikasya purastāt ṛddhirvidarśayitavyā/
170.017. darśayati, sātisāro bhavati/
170.017. api tu catvāri pātrāṇi suvarṇamayaṃ rūpyamayaṃ varḍūryamayaṃ sphaṭikamayam/
170.018. aparāṇyapi catvāri pātrāṇi rītimayaṃ tāmramayaṃ kaṃsamayamabhramayaṃ ca/
170.019. tatra yāni pūrvakāṇi catvāri pātrāṇi, etānyanupasthāpitāni nopasthāpayitavyāni, upasthāpitāni visarjayitavyāni/
170.020. yāni paścimāni catvāri pātrāṇi, etānyanupasthāpitāni nopasthāpayitavyāni, uapsthāpitāni tu bhaiṣajyaśaravaparibhogena paribhoktavyāni/
170.022. api tvadhīṣṭāni te dve pātre āyasaṃ mṛṇmayam/
170.022. yāvadapareṇa samayena jyotiṣkasya gṛhapaterdivyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā/
170.023. antarā ca rājagṛhamantarā ca campāmatrāntare śulkaśālā/
170.024. tasyāṃ śulkaśālikaḥ kālagataḥ/
170.024. sa vyālayakṣeṣūpapannaḥ/
170.024. tena putrāṇāṃ svapnadarśanaṃ dattam--yaḥ kaścit paṇyamaśulkayitvā gamiṣyati, sā ghaṇṭā tāvadviraviṣyati yāvadasau nivartya śulkaṃ dāpayitavyamiti (yiṣyatīti?)/
170.027. taistaṃ svapnaṃ saṃbandhibāndhavānāṃ nivedya divasatithimuhūrtena tasmin pradeśe yakṣasthānaṃ kāritam/
170.028. tatra ca ghaṇṭā baddhvā lambitā//
body.translated_text:
170.001. Whichever <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or being of great supernatural power and great might takes it by supernatural power, it shall be his to enjoy as he pleases.'
170.002. The <s>tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist sectarians), rising early in the morning, go to the <s>tīrthya</s> bathing-place.
170.003. They saw it.
170.003. Having seen it, they said to the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: 'Householder, what is this?' He told them the matter in detail.
170.004. They said: 'Householder, you are devoted to the <s>śramaṇas</s>, the followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son.
170.005. They will take it' — and having said this, they departed.
170.005. Then the elder monks entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms.
170.006. Having seen it, they too asked the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: 'What is this?' He told them the matter in detail in the same way.
170.007. They said: 'Householder, shall we display ourselves for the sake of a mere bowl? The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "You monks should live with your virtues concealed and your faults exposed"' — and having said this, they departed.
170.008. Then the Venerable <s>Daśabala Kāśyapa</s> arrived after them.
170.009. He asked: 'Householder, what is this?' He told him the matter as it had occurred.
170.010. The Venerable <s>Daśabala Kāśyapa</s> reflected: 'I have vomited, discarded, expelled, and cast away the mass of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) accumulated since beginningless time, and this householder challenges me with a display of supernatural power shared in common with the <s>tīrthyas</s>.
170.012. Let me fulfill his heart's desire.'
170.012. Extending his arm, resembling an elephant's trunk, he took that bowl.
170.012. Having taken it, he went to the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery). The monks said to him: 'Elder, from where did you get this bowl of <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood?' He told them the matter as it had occurred.
170.014. The monks said: 'Elder, is it proper for you to display supernatural power for the sake of a mere bowl?' He said: 'Venerable ones, whether it is proper or not,
170.015. what is done is done.
170.015. What should be done now?' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
170.016. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A monk must not display supernatural power before householders.
170.017. One who displays it commits a <s>sātisāra</s> (transgression with residue).
170.017. Furthermore, there are four kinds of bowls: made of gold, made of silver, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and made of crystal.
170.018. And there are four other kinds of bowls: made of <s>rīti</s> (brass), made of copper, made of <s>kaṃsa</s> (bell-metal), and made of mica.
170.019. Of these, the first four kinds of bowls — those that have not been set up should not be set up, and those that have been set up should be discarded.
170.020. The latter four kinds of bowls — those that have not been set up should not be set up, but those that have been set up may be used with the function of a medicine vessel.
170.022. Moreover, two kinds of bowls are prescribed for you: iron and earthenware.'
170.022. In the course of time, both divine and human prosperity arose for the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s>.
170.023. Between <s>Rājagṛha</s> and <s>Campā</s>, there was a toll-station.
170.024. At that toll-station, the toll-collector died.
170.024. He was reborn among the <s>vyāla-yakṣas</s> (fierce <s>yakṣas</s>).
170.024. He gave a dream-vision to his sons: 'Whoever passes without paying the toll, that bell will ring until that person is turned back and made to pay the toll.'
170.027. They, having reported that dream to their relatives and kinsmen, on the day and hour established a <s>yakṣa</s>-shrine at that place.
170.028. There they tied and hung a bell.

body.text:
170.030. campāyāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ/
170.030. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
170.030. sā brāhmaṇī saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ brāhmaṇo yaistairupāyairdhanopārjanaṃ karoti/
170.031. ahaṃ bhakṣayāmi/
170.031. na mama pratirūpam yadahamakarmikā tiṣṭheyamiti/
170.032. tayā vīthīṃ gatvā karpāsaḥ krītaḥ/
170.032. taṃ parikarmayitvā ślakṣṇam <171>sūtraṃ kartitam/
body.translated_text:
170.030. In <s>Campā</s> there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
170.030. He had brought a wife from a family of equal standing.
170.030. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman thought: 'This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> earns wealth by various means.
170.031. I consume it.
170.031. It is not fitting that I should remain idle.'
170.032. She went to the marketplace and bought cotton.
170.032. Having processed it, she spun fine thread.

body.text:
171.001. śobhanena kuvindena kārṣāpaṇasahasramūlyā yamalī vāyitā/
171.001. tayā brāhmaṇa uktah--brāhmaṇa, asyā yamalyāḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasraṃ mūlyam/
171.002. gṛhītvā vīthīṃ gaccha/
171.002. yadi kaścit yācati, kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa dātavyā, no cedapattanaṃ ghoṣayitvā anyatra gantavyamiti/
171.003. sa tāṃ gṛhītvā vīthīṃ gataḥ/
171.004. na kaścit kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa gṛhaṇāti/
171.004. so 'pattanaṃ ghoṣayitvā tām yamalīṃ chatradaṇḍe prakṣipya sārthena sārdhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ saṃprasthito yāvadanupūrveṇa śulkaśālāmanuprāptaḥ/
171.006. śulkāśālikena sārthaḥ śulkitaḥ/
171.006. sa śulkaṃ dattvā saṃprasthitaḥ/
171.006. ghaṇṭā raṭitumārabdhā/
171.007. śailkikāḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, yatheyaṃ ghaṇṭā raṇati, nūnaṃ sārtho na nipuṇaṃ śulkitaḥ/
171.008. bhūyaḥ śulkayāma iti/
171.008. tairasau sārthaḥ punaḥ pratinivartya śulkitaḥ/
171.008. nāsti kiṃcidaśulkitam/
171.009. ghaṇṭā raṭatyeva/
171.009. tairasau sārtho bhūyaḥ pratinivartya pratyavekṣitaḥ/
171.009. nāstyevakiṃcit/
171.010. sārthikā avadhyātumārabdhāh--kim yūyamasamān bhūṣitukāmā yena bhūyo bhūyaḥ pratinivartayadhvamiti? tairasau dvidhā kṛtvā muktaḥ/
171.011. yeṣāṃ madhye sa brāhmaṇo nāsti, te 'tikrāntāḥ/
171.012. anyeṣāṃ gacchatāṃ sā ghaṇṭā tathaiva raṭitumārabdhā/
171.012. taiste punaḥ pratyavekṣitāḥ/
171.013. evaṃ tāvat dvidhākṛtāḥ, yāvat sa caiko brāhmaṇo 'vasthita iti/
171.013. sa tairgṛhītaḥ/
171.014. sa kathayati--pratyavekṣata yadi mama kiṃcidastīti/
171.014. taiḥ sarvataḥ pratyavekṣya muktaḥ/
171.014. sā ghaṇṭā raṭatyeva/
171.015. tairasau brāhmaṇaḥ pratinivartyoktah--bho brāhmaṇa kathaya, naiva śulkaṃ dāpayāmaḥ/
171.016. kiṃ tu devasyaiva sānnidhyaṃ jñātaṃ bhavatīti/
171.016. kathayati--satyaṃ na dāpayatha? na dāpayāmaḥ/
171.017. tena cchatradaṇḍādapanīya sā yamalī darśitā/
171.017. te paraṃ vismayamāpannāh--bhavantaḥ, īdṛśamapi devasya sānnidhyamiti/
171.018. taistat ekaṃ vastramuddhāṭya devaḥ prāvṛtaḥ/
171.018. brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati--yūyaṃ kathayatha śulkaṃ na dāpayāma iti/
171.019. idānīṃ sarvasvamapaharatha iti/
171.019. te kathayanti--brāhmaṇa, nāsmābhirgṛhītam/
171.020. api devasyaitat sānnidhyamiti kṛtvā asmābhiḥ prāvṛtaḥ/
171.020. gṛhītvā gaccheti/
171.021. sa taṃ punargṛhītvā punaśchatranāḍikāyāṃ prakṣipya prakrāntaḥ/
171.021. anupūrveṇa rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
171.022. sa vīthyāṃ prasāryāvasthitaḥ/
171.022. tatrāpi tāṃ na kaścit kārṣāpaṇasahasreṇa yācate/
171.023. sa rājagṛhamapyapattanaṃ ghoṣayitumārabdhaḥ/
171.023. jyotiṣkaśca kumāro rājakulānniṣkramya hastiskandhābhirūḍho vīthīmadhyena svagṛhaṃ gacchati/
171.024. tena śrutam/
171.024. sa taiḥ śabditaḥ/
171.025. jyotiṣkeṇoktah--bho brāhmaṇa, kimarthaṃ tvam apattanaṃ ghoṣayasi? gṛhapate, asyā yamalyāḥ kārṣāpaṇasahasraṃ mūlyam/
171.026. na ca kaścidyācata iti/
171.027. sa kathayati--ānaya, paśyāmaḥ/
171.027. tenopadarśitā/
171.027. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--astyetadeva/
171.028. kiṃ tu atraikaṃ vastraṃ paribhuktakam/
171.028. ekamaparibhuktakam/
171.028. yadaparibhuktam, asya pañcakārṣāpaṇaśatāni mūlyam/
171.029. yattu paribhuktakam, asyārdhatṛtīyāni/
171.029. brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati--kimetadevaṃ bhaviṣyati? jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--brāhmaṇa, tava pratyakṣīkaromi/
171.030. paśyeti/
171.030. tenāsau aparibhukta uparivihāyasā kṣiptaḥ/
171.031. vitānaṃ kṛtvā avasthitaḥ/
171.031. paribhuktaḥ kṣiptaḥ/
171.031. kṣiptamātraka eva patitaḥ/
171.032. brāhmaṇo dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ/
171.032. kathayati--gṛhapate, maharddhikastvam <172>mahānubhāva iti/
body.translated_text:
171.001. A pair of garments worth a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> was woven by a skilled weaver.
171.001. She said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the price of this pair of garments is a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
171.002. Take it and go to the market street.
171.002. If anyone asks, it should be given for a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>; if not, you should announce that you are leaving and go elsewhere.'
171.003. He took it and went to the market street.
171.004. No one would purchase it for a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
171.004. Having announced his departure, he placed that pair of garments on his parasol-staff and, together with a caravan, set out for <s>Rājagṛha</s>, until in due course he arrived at the customs house.
171.006. The customs officer levied the toll on the caravan.
171.006. Having paid the toll, the caravan set out.
171.006. The bell began to ring.
171.007. The toll-collectors said: 'Sirs, the way this bell is ringing, surely the caravan has not been properly assessed.
171.008. Let us assess it again.'
171.008. They turned the caravan back and assessed it again.
171.008. There was nothing un-assessed.
171.009. The bell kept on ringing.
171.009. They turned the caravan back again and inspected it.
171.009. There was simply nothing.
171.010. The caravan merchants began to grumble: 'Do you want to annoy honest people by turning us back again and again?' They divided the caravan in two and released it.
171.011. Those among whom the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was not present passed through.
171.012. As the others were going, the bell began to ring just as before.
171.012. They inspected those again.
171.013. In this way they kept dividing them in half, until only that one <s>brāhmaṇa</s> remained.
171.013. He was seized by them.
171.014. He said: 'Look whether I have anything.'
171.014. They searched him thoroughly from all sides and released him.
171.014. The bell kept on ringing.
171.015. They turned the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> back and said: 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, tell us — we will not make you pay the toll.
171.016. But let the presence of the king's [property] be known.'
171.016. He said: 'Truly you will not make me pay?' 'We will not make you pay.'
171.017. He then removed the pair of garments from the parasol-staff and showed them.
171.017. They were struck with the utmost astonishment: 'Sirs, even such is the king's detection!'
171.018. They unfolded one garment and wrapped the deity's [image].
171.018. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'You said you would not make me pay the toll.
171.019. Now you are taking my entire property.'
171.019. They said: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, we have not taken it.
171.020. Rather, knowing it to be the king's detection, we have wrapped [the deity's image] with it.
171.020. Take it and go.'
171.021. He took it back, placed it again on the parasol-staff, and departed.
171.021. In due course he arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
171.022. He spread it out in the market street and stood waiting.
171.022. There too, no one would ask for it at a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
171.023. He began to announce his departure from <s>Rājagṛha</s> as well.
171.023. Now the young prince <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, coming out from the royal court, mounted on an elephant, was going through the middle of the market street to his own house.
171.024. He heard it.
171.024. He was hailed by them.
171.025. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, why are you announcing your departure?' 'Householder, the price of this pair of garments is a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
171.026. But no one will buy it.'
171.027. He said: 'Bring it, let me see.'
171.027. It was shown to him.
171.027. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'That is indeed the case.
171.028. But one garment of this pair has been used.
171.028. And one has not been used.
171.028. The unused one is worth five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
171.029. But the used one is worth two hundred and fifty.'
171.029. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'How can this be so?' <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall demonstrate it to you.
171.030. Watch.'
171.030. He threw the unused one up into the air.
171.031. It formed a canopy and remained suspended.
171.031. He threw the used one.
171.031. The moment it was thrown, it fell.
171.032. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having seen this, was struck with the utmost astonishment.
171.032. He said: 'Householder, you are one of great supernatural power and great might.'

body.text:
172.001. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--brāhmaṇa, punaḥ paśyainam yo 'sau aparibhuktaka iti, sa kaṇṭakavāṭasyopariṣṭāt kṣipto 'sajjamāno gataḥ/
172.002. so 'nyaḥ kṣiptaḥ kaṇṭake lagnaḥ/
172.002. sa brāhmaṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā abhiprasannaḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, maharddhikastvaṃ ṃhānubhāvaḥ/
172.003. yat tavābhipretaṃ tatprayaccheti/
172.004. sa kathayati--brāhmaṇa, atithistvam/
172.004. tavaiva pūjā kṛtā bhavati/
172.004. sahasrameva paryacchāmīti/
172.005. tena tasya kārṣāpaṇasahasraṃ dattam/
172.005. brāhmaṇastamādāya prakrāntaḥ/
172.005. jyotiṣkeṇa tato yaḥ paribhuktakaḥ sa dārakāya dattaḥ, aparibhuktakastu snānaśāṭakaḥ kṛtaḥ/
172.006. yāvadapareṇa samayena rājā bimbisāra upariprāsādatalagato 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtastiṣṭhati/
172.007. jyotiṣkasya sa snānaśāṭaka upari gṛhasyābhyavakāśe śoṣito vāyunā hriyamāṇo rājño bimbisārasyopari patitaḥ/
172.009. rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, rājārhamidaṃ vastram/
172.009. kuta etaditi?/
172.009. te kathayanti--deva, śrūyate rājño māndhātuḥ saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patitam/
172.010. devasyāpi vastravarṣaḥ patitumārabdham/
172.011. nacirāddhiraṇyavarṣaḥ patiṣyatīti/
172.011. rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, jyotiṣko gṛhapatirbhagavatā vyākṛto divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti/
172.012. idaṃ ca divyaṃ vastramākāśāt patitam/
172.013. sthāpayata/
172.013. tasyaivāgatasya dāsyāmīti/
172.013. te caivamālāpaṃ kurvanti, jyotiṣkaścāgataḥ/
172.014. rājā kathayati--kumāra, tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛto divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatīti/
172.014. mama cedaṃ divyaṃ vastramākāśāt patitam/
172.015. gṛhāṇeti/
172.015. tena hastaḥ prasāritaḥ/
172.015. deva ānaya, paśyāmīti/
172.016. sa nirīkṣitumārabdho yāvat paśyatyātmīyaṃ snānaśāṭakam/
172.016. sa vismṛtya kathayati--deva, madīyo 'yaṃ snānaśāṭako vāyunopakṣipta ihāgata iti/
172.017. kumāra, tava divyamānuṣyakī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā? deva, prādurbhūtā/
172.018. kumāra, yadyevam, kimarthaṃ na nimantrayasi? deva, nimantrito bhava/
172.019. gaccha, bhaktaṃ sajjīkuru/
172.019. deva, yasya divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā, kiṃ tena sajjīkartavyam? nanu sajjīkṛtameva, gaccheti/
172.020. sa jyotiṣkasya gṛhaṃ gataḥ/
172.020. rājā bāhyaṃ parijanaṃ dṛṣṭvā indriyāṇyutkṣipati/
172.021. deva, kimarthamindriyāṇyutkṣipasi/
172.021. sa kathayati--kumāra, vadhūjano 'yamiti kṛtvā/
172.022. deva nāyaṃ vadhūjanaḥ, bāhyo 'yaṃ parijanaḥ/
172.022. sa paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ/
172.022. punarmadhyaṃ janaṃ dṛṣṭvā indriyāṇyutkṣiptumārabdhaḥ/
172.023. tathaiva pṛcchati/
172.023. rājā api tathaiva kathayati/
172.023. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--deva, ayamapi na vadhūjanaḥ, kiṃ tu madhyo 'yaṃ janaḥ/
172.024. sa bhūyasyā mātrayā paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ/
172.024. tasya madhyamāyāṃ dvāraśālāyāṃ maṇibhūmiruparacitā/
172.025. tasyāṃ matsyā udakapūrṇāyāmiva yantrayogoparibhramanto dṛśyante/
172.026. rājā praveṣṭukāmo vāpīti kṛtvopānahau moktumārabdhaḥ/
172.026. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--deva kasyārthe upānahau apanayasīti? sa kathayati--kumāra, pānīyamuttarttavyamiti/
172.027. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--deva nedaṃ pānīyam, maṇibhūmireṣā/
172.028. sa kathayati--kumāra, ime matsyā upari bhramantaḥ paśyanti/
172.029. deva yantrayogenaite paribhramanti/
172.029. sa na śraddhatte/
172.029. tenāṅgulimudrā kṣiptā/
172.029. sā raṇaraṇāśabdena bhūmau patitā/
172.030. tato vismayamāpannaḥ praviśya siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
172.030. vadhūjanaḥ pādābhivandana upasaṃkrāntaḥ/
172.031. tāsāmaśrupāto jātaḥ/
172.031. rājā kathayati--kumāra, kasmādayaṃ vadhūjano roditi? deva nāyaṃ roditi, kiṃ tu devasya kāṣṭhadhūmena vastrāṇi dhūpitāni, tena <173>āsāmaśrupato jāta iti/
body.translated_text:
172.001. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, look again at the unused one' — it was thrown over a thorn fence and passed through without catching.
172.002. The other one was thrown and caught on the thorns.
172.002. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, even more greatly impressed, said: 'Householder, you are of great supernatural power and great might.
172.003. Give whatever price you wish.'
172.004. He said: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, you are a guest.
172.004. The honor is yours.
172.004. I shall give you the full thousand.'
172.005. He gave him a thousand <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
172.005. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> took them and departed.
172.005. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> then gave the used one to a servant boy, and kept the unused one as a bathing cloth.
172.006. Some time later, King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, standing on an upper terrace of his palace surrounded by a company of ministers,
172.007. <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> bathing cloth, drying in the open space above his house, was carried by the wind and fell upon King <s>Bimbisāra</s>.
172.009. The king said: 'Sirs, this is a garment fit for a king.
172.009. Where did it come from?'
172.009. They said: 'Your Majesty, it is heard that gold rained for seven days upon King <s>Māndhāta</s>.
172.010. A rain of garments has begun to fall upon Your Majesty as well.
172.011. Before long, a rain of gold will fall.'
172.011. The king said: 'Sirs, the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was prophesied by the Blessed One: "He will experience divine and human glory."
172.012. This divine garment has fallen from the sky.
172.013. Set it aside.
172.013. I shall give it to him when he comes.'
172.013. While they were still talking thus, <s>Jyotiṣka</s> arrived.
172.014. The king said: 'Young man, you were prophesied by the Blessed One: "He will experience divine and human glory."
172.014. This divine garment has fallen to me from the sky.
172.015. Take it.'
172.015. He stretched out his hand.
172.015. 'Your Majesty, bring it here, let me see.'
172.016. He began to examine it, and then he saw that it was his own bathing cloth.
172.016. Forgetting himself, he said: 'Your Majesty, this is my bathing cloth, blown here by the wind.'
172.017. 'Young man, has your divine and human glory manifested?' 'It has manifested, Your Majesty.'
172.018. 'Young man, if so, why do you not invite me?' 'Your Majesty, consider yourself invited.'
172.019. 'Go, prepare a meal.'
172.019. 'Your Majesty, for one whose divine and human glory has manifested, what need is there to prepare? Is it not already prepared? Go.'
172.020. He went to <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> house.
172.020. The king, seeing the outer attendants, raised his eyes in wonder.
172.021. 'Your Majesty, why do you raise your eyes?'
172.021. He said: 'Young man, because these are women of the household.'
172.022. 'Your Majesty, these are not women of the household; these are the outer attendants.'
172.022. He was struck with the utmost astonishment.
172.022. Then, seeing the middle attendants, he again began to raise his eyes in wonder.
172.023. He asked in the same way.
172.023. The king said the same thing.
172.023. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'Your Majesty, these too are not the women of the household, but rather the middle attendants.'
172.024. He was even more greatly astonished.
172.024. In the middle entrance-hall, a jewel floor was inlaid.
172.025. In it, fish were seen revolving on top as if in a pool filled with water, by means of a mechanical device.
172.026. The king, wishing to enter, thinking it was a pond, began to remove his sandals.
172.026. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'Your Majesty, why are you removing your sandals?' He said: 'Young man, to cross the water.'
172.027. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'Your Majesty, this is not water; it is a jewel floor.'
172.028. He said: 'Young man, I see these fish revolving on top.'
172.029. 'Your Majesty, they revolve by means of a mechanical device.'
172.029. He did not believe it.
172.029. He threw his signet ring.
172.029. It fell on the floor with a clattering sound.
172.030. Thereupon, astonished, he entered and sat down on the lion-throne.
172.030. The women of the household came forward to pay their respects at his feet.
172.031. Tears fell from their eyes.
172.031. The king said: 'Young man, why are these women weeping?' 'Your Majesty, they are not weeping. Rather, Your Majesty's garments have been perfumed with wood smoke, and from that their tears have arisen.'

body.text:
173.001. rājā tatra divyamānuṣyā śriyā upacaryamāṇaḥ pramatto na niṣkrāṃti/
173.002. rājakṛtyāni rājakariṇīyāni parihātumārabdhāni/
173.002. amātyairajātaśatruḥ kumāro 'bhibhūtah--kumāra, devo jyotiṣkasya gṛhaṃ praviśya pramattaḥ/
173.003. gaccha, nivedayeti/
173.003. tena gatvā uktah--deva, kimatra praviśyāvasthitah? amātyāḥ kathayanti--rājakṛtyāni rājakaraṇīyāni parihīyanta iti/
173.005. sa kathayati--kumāra, na śaknoṣi tvamekaṃ divasaṃ rājyaṃ kārayitum? kiṃ devo jānīte--mamaiko divasaḥ praviṣṭasaya? adya devasya saptamo divaso vartate/
173.006. rājā jyotiṣkasya mukhaṃ nirīkṣya kathayati--kumāra satyam? deva satyam/
173.007. saptam eva divaso vartate/
173.007. kumāra, kathaṃ rātrijñāyate divaso vā? deva, puṣpāṇāṃ saṃkocavikāsānmaṇīnāṃ jvalanājvalanayogācchakunīnāṃ ca kūjanākūjanāt/
173.009. santi tāni puṣpāṇi yāni rātrau vikasanti, divā mlāyanti? santi yāni divā vikasanti rātrau mlāyanti? santi te maṇayo ye rātrau jvālanti, na divā? santi ye divā jvalanti, na rātrau? santi te śakunayo ye rātrau kūjanti, na divā? santi ye divā kūjñati, na rātrau? rājā vismayamāpannaḥ kathayati--kumāra, avitathavādī bhagavān/
173.013. yathā tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtastathaiva nānyathetyuktvā jyotiṣkagṛhāt niṣkrāntaḥ/
173.014. ajātaśatrukumāreṇa jyotiṣkasantako maṇirapahṛtya dārakasya haste dattaḥ/
173.014. ten yata eva gṛhītastatraiva gatvāvasthitaḥ/
173.015. ajātaśatruḥ kathayati--dāraka, ānaya taṃ maṇiṃ paśyāmīti/
173.015. sa muṣṭhiṃ vighāṭya kathayati--kumāra, na jāne kutra gata iti/
173.016. sa taṃ tāḍayitumārabdhaḥ/
173.016. jyotiṣkaḥ kathayati--kumāra, kimarthamenaṃ tāḍayasi? ghapate, ahaṃ cauraḥ, eṣa mahācauraḥ/
173.017. mayā tvadīyo maṇirapahṛtaḥ, so 'pyanenāpahṛta iti/
173.018. sa kathayati--kumāra, na tvayā apahṛto nāpyanena, api tu yata eva tvayā gṛhītastatraiva gatvā avasthitaḥ/
173.019. api tu kumāra, svakaṃ te gṛham/
173.020. yāvadbhirmaṇibhiranyena vā prayojanaṃ tāvadgṛhāṇa yathāsukhamiti/
173.020. sa pratibhinnakaḥ saṃlakṣayate--yadā pituratyayādrājā bhaviṣyāmi, tadā grahīṣyāmīti/
173.021. yadā ajātaśatruṇā devadattavigrāhitena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, svayameva ca paṭṭaṃ baddhvā pratitiṣṭhitaḥ, tadā tena jyotiṣko 'bhihitah--gṛhapate, tvaṃ mama bhrātā bhavasi/
173.023. gṛhaṃ bhājayāma iti/
173.024. sa saṃlakṣayati--yena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ praghātitaḥ, sa māṃ marṣayatīti kuta etat? nūnamayaṃ madgṛhamāgacchatu, kāmaṃ prayacchāmīti viditvā kathayati--deva, vibhaktameva, kimatra vibhaktavyam? madīyaṃ gṛhamāgaccha, ahaṃ tvadīyaṃ gṛhamāgacchāmīti/
173.026. ajātaśatruḥ kathayati--śobhanam/
173.027. evaṃ kuru/
173.027. sa tasya gṛhaṃ gataḥ/
173.027. jyotiṣko 'pyajātaśatrorgṛhaṃ gataḥ/
173.028. sā śrīstasmādgṛhādantarhitā, yatra jyotiṣkastatraiva gatā/
173.028. evam yāvat saptavārānantarhitā prādurbhūtā ca/
173.029. ajātaśatruḥ saṃlakṣayate--evamapi mayā na śakitaṃ jyotiṣkasya maṇīnapahartum/
173.030. anyadupāyaṃ karomi/
173.030. tena dhūrtapuruṣāḥ prayuktāh--gacchata, jyotiṣkasya gṛhānmaṇīnapaharateti/
173.031. te hi śīṭākarkaṭakaprayogenābhiroḍhumārabdhāḥ/
173.031. te 'ntaḥpurikayā upariprāsādatalagatayā dṛṣṭāḥ/
173.032. tayā dhūrtadhūrtakā iti nādo muktaḥ/
173.032. jyotiṣkeṇa śrutam/
173.032. tenāśayato vāgniścāritā--tiṣṭhantu <174>dhūrtakā iti/
body.translated_text: The king, being served there with divine and human glory, became heedless and would not come out. The royal duties and royal obligations began to be neglected. The ministers informed Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Prince, the king has entered <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> house and become heedless. Go and inform him.' He went and said: 'Your Majesty, why have you entered and remained here? The ministers say that royal duties and royal obligations are being neglected.' The king said: 'Prince, can you not manage the kingdom for a single day? Does the king know — that I have been inside for one day? Today is the king's seventh day.' The king, looking at <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> face, said: 'Prince, is this true?' 'Your Majesty, it is true. It is indeed the seventh day.' 'Prince, how does one distinguish night from day?' 'Your Majesty, by the closing and opening of flowers, by the blazing and non-blazing of gems, and by the singing and not-singing of birds.' 'Are there flowers that bloom at night and wilt by day? Are there those that bloom by day and wilt at night? Are there gems that blaze at night but not by day? Are there those that blaze by day but not at night? Are there birds that sing at night but not by day? Are there those that sing by day but not at night?' The king, filled with wonder, said: 'Prince, the <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks truly. Just as you were prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, so it is and not otherwise.' Having said this, he left <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> house. Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s> stole one of <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> gems and placed it in the boy's hand. But it went back to the very place from which it had been taken. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Boy, bring me that gem so I can see it.' The boy, opening his fist, said: 'Prince, I do not know where it has gone.' He began to beat the boy. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'Prince, why do you beat him? Householder, I am a thief, but this one is a great thief! I stole your gem, and he in turn stole it.' <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said: 'Prince, it was neither stolen by you nor by him; rather, it went back to the very place from which you took it. But, Prince, this is your own home. Take as many gems as you need, or whatever else you require, at your pleasure.' That resentful one reflected: 'When my father has passed away and I become king, then I shall take them.' When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, incited by <s>Devadatta</s>, had his righteous father, the righteous king, put to death, and himself, having bound the royal diadem, was installed as king, he then said to <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: 'Householder, you are my brother. Let us divide the estate.' <s>Jyotiṣka</s> reflected: 'He who had his righteous father, the righteous king, killed — will he spare me? There is no chance of that. Surely he is coming to my house; I shall give him whatever he desires.' Having decided thus, he said: 'Your Majesty, it has already been divided; what is there to divide further? My house is yours — come to it. I shall come to yours.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Excellent. Do so.' He went to <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> house. <s>Jyotiṣka</s> too went to <s>Ajātaśatru's</s> house. But the glory vanished from that house and went to wherever <s>Jyotiṣka</s> was. Thus, up to seven times, it vanished and reappeared. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> reflected: 'Even by this means I have been unable to seize <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> gems. I shall devise another stratagem.' He dispatched crafty men: 'Go and steal the gems from <s>Jyotiṣka's</s> house.' They began to scale the walls using ladders and grappling hooks. They were seen by a woman of the inner quarters who was on the upper terrace of the palace. She cried out: 'Thieves! Thieves!' <s>Jyotiṣka</s> heard this. From his bed, he uttered a command of power: 'Let those thieves stay where they are!'

body.text:
174.001. teṣām yo yatrābhirūḍhaḥ sa tatraivāsthito yāvat prabhātā rajanī saṃvṛttā/
174.002. mahājanakāyena dṛṣṭāḥ/
174.002. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, anena kalirājena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Whoever had climbed up to whatever point remained stuck right there until dawn broke. A great crowd of people saw them. They said: 'Good people, this wicked king had his righteous father, the righteous king, put to death.'

body.text:
174.003. idānīṃ gṛhāṇyapi moṣayati/
174.003. tatkiṃ na me moṣiṣyata iti? purakṣobho jātaḥ/
174.004. ajātaśatruṇā jyotiṣkasay dūto 'nupreṣitah--muñcata mamāyaṃ khalīkāra saṃlakṣayate--yena nāma pitā jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, sa māṃ na praghātayitṣyatīti kuta etat? sarvathā ahaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtah--mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarthattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyatīti/
174.008. gacchāmi, pravrajāmīti/
174.008. tena sarvaṃ ghanajātaṃ dīnānāthakṛpaṇebhyo dattam/
174.008. adhanāḥ sadhanā vyavasthāpitāḥ/
174.009. atha jyotiṣko gṛhapatiḥ suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānavalokya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
174.010. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
174.010. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo jyotiṣko gṛhapatirbhagavantamidamavocat--labheyāhāṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
174.012. careyamahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryamiti/
174.012. sa bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitah--ehi bhikṣo, cara brahmacaryamiti/
174.013. bhagavato vācāvasānameva muṇḍaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
174.014. saṃghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ pātrakaravyagrahastaḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśrurvarṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣurīryāpathenāvasthitaḥ/
174.016. ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaśca saṃghāṭiparītadehaḥ/
174.018. sadyaḥ praśāntendriya eva tasthāvupasthito buddhamanorathena//14//
body.translated_text: 'And now he robs even houses. Will he not rob mine too?' An uproar arose in the city. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> sent a messenger to <s>Jyotiṣka</s>: 'Release them.' <s>Jyotiṣka</s> reflected: 'He who had his own father put to death — will he not have me killed? There is no chance of that. Certainly I have been prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Having gone forth in my teaching, he will realize <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all afflictions." Let me go and go forth.' He gave away all his accumulated wealth to the destitute, the helpless, and the wretched. He established those without wealth as people of means. Then the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s>, having looked upon his friends, relatives, and kinsmen, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Jyotiṣka</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, receive the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' He was addressed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the 'Come, monk' ordination: 'Come, monk, practice the holy life.' With the very end of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> utterance, he became tonsured, clad in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (monastic robe), with bowl and water-pot in hand, with hair and beard as if shaved seven days ago, standing with the deportment of a monk who had been ordained for a hundred years.
