'Come!' — thus addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured and with body wrapped in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, he stood at once with senses perfectly calmed, attended by the aspiration of the <s>Buddha</s>. //14//

body.text:
174.020. tasya bhagavatā avavādo dattaḥ/
174.020. tenodyacchamānena vyāyacchamānena idameva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatyasarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
174.023. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhaḥ/
174.024. sendropeṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: He was given instruction by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-knotted wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, and having struck down all the courses of <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) by recognizing their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in all three realms, equal-minded toward a clod of earth and gold, with a mind as impartial as the sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood paste, whose egg-shell of ignorance was split open by knowledge, who had attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvits</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. He became worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and the sub-<s>Indras</s>.

body.text:
174.025. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā jyotiṣkeṇa karma kṛtam yena citāmāropitaḥ, divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā, bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtamiti? bhagavānāha--jyotiṣkeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasaṃhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayānyoghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
174.028. jyotiṣkeṇa karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
174.029. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ kārmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
body.translated_text: The monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, did the Venerable <s>Jyotiṣka</s> perform, by the ripening of which he was placed on the funeral pyre, divine and human glory manifested for him, and having gone forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Monks, it is the deeds done and accumulated by <s>Jyotiṣka</s> himself, whose consequences have converged, whose conditions have matured, that stand present like a flood, whose fruition is inevitable. The deeds were done and accumulated by <s>Jyotiṣka</s> himself. Who else shall experience them? Monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen in the earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, deeds done and accumulated ripen in the very <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) that have been appropriated — whether wholesome or unwholesome.

body.text:
175.001. <175>na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
175.002. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//15//
body.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (eons). When the right conjunction and the right time arrive, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. //15//

body.text:
175.003. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣava ekanavatikalpe vipaśyī nāma śāstā loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
175.005. dvāṣaṣṭibhikṣusahasraparivāro janapadacārikāṃ caran bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīmanuprāpto bandhumatyāṃ viharati sma bandhumatīyake dāve/
175.006. tena khalu samayena bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ bandhumān nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannam/
175.008. dhārmiko dharmarājā dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
175.009. tasyānaṅgaṇo nāma gṛhapatirāḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
175.010. sa saṃlakṣayate--bahuśo mayā vipaśyī samyaksambuddho 'ntargṛhe upanimantraya bhojitaḥ/
175.011. na tu kadācit traimāsīṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritaḥ/
175.012. yannvahaṃ vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ traimāsīṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayeyam/
175.012. iti viditvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
175.013. upasaṃkramya vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
175.014. ekāntaniṣaṇṇamanaṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ vipaśyī samyakasmbuddho dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
175.015. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
175.016. athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃs traimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti/
175.019. adhivāsayati vipaśyī samyaksambuddho 'naṅgaṇasya gṛhapatestūṣṇīmbhāvena/
175.019. athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirbhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
175.021. aśrauṣīdbandhumān rājā--vipaśyī samyaksambuddho dvāṣaṣṭibhikṣusahasraparivāro janapadacārikāṃ caran bandhumatīmanuprāpto bandhumatyāṃ viharati bandhumatīye dāve iti/
175.023. śrutvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--bahuśo mayā bhagavānantargṛhe upanimantrya bhojitaḥ/
175.023. na tu kadācit traimāsīṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritaḥ/
175.024. yannvahaṃ vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayeyam/
175.025. iti viditvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
175.025. upasaṃkramya vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
175.026. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ bandhumantaṃ rājānaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
175.027. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
175.028. atha bandhumān rājā utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastenāñjaliṃ praṇamya vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃstraimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
175.031. upanimantrito 'smi mahārāja tvatprathamato 'naṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā/
175.031. adhivāsayatu bhagavān, ahaṃ tathā kariṣye yathā anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirājñāsyati/
175.032. sacet te mahārāja anaṅgaṇo <176>gṛhapatiranujānīte, evaṃ te 'hamadhivāsayāmi/
body.translated_text:
175.003. Long ago, monks, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), a Teacher named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.
175.005. Accompanied by sixty-two thousand monks, wandering on a teaching tour through the provinces, he arrived at the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> and dwelt in the <s>Bandhumatīya</s> grove at <s>Bandhumatī</s>.
175.006. At that time, in the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>, a king named <s>Bandhumān</s> was ruling the kingdom — prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, teeming with many people, with quarrels, conflicts, disputes, and disturbances pacified, free from thieves and disease, and rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo.
175.008. A righteous king, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, he governed the kingdom through <s>Dharma</s>.
175.009. His householder named <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> was wealthy, of great riches, great resources, with vast and extensive possessions, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth.
175.010. He reflected: 'Many times have I invited the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> into my inner house and fed him.
175.011. But never once have I provided for the three-month retreat with all requisites.
175.012. What if I were to provide the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> with all requisites for the three-month retreat?'
175.012. Having thus resolved, he approached the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>.
175.013. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, he sat down to one side.
175.014. The Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
175.015. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
175.016. Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, said: 'May the Blessed One accept from me for the three-month retreat robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of monks.'
175.019. The Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> accepted the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>'s invitation through silence.
175.019. Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, understanding the Blessed One's acceptance through silence, bowed his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, rose from his seat, and departed.
175.021. King <s>Bandhumān</s> heard: 'The Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, accompanied by sixty-two thousand monks, wandering on a teaching tour through the provinces, has arrived at <s>Bandhumatī</s> and is dwelling in the <s>Bandhumatīya</s> grove.'
175.023. Hearing this, he thought: 'Many times have I invited the Blessed One into my inner house and fed him.
175.023. But never once have I provided for the three-month retreat with all requisites.
175.024. What if I were to provide the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> with all requisites?'
175.025. Having thus resolved, he approached the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>.
175.025. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, he sat down to one side.
175.026. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted King <s>Bandhumān</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
175.027. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
175.028. Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, said: 'May the Blessed One accept from me for the three-month retreat robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of monks.'
175.031. 'I have already been invited, Great King, before you, by the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>.'
175.031. 'May the Blessed One accept; I will act in such a way that the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> will agree.'
175.032. 'If, Great King, the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> <176> permits you, then I accept from you.'

body.text:
176.001. atha bandhumān rājā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrānto yena svaṃ nirveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
176.003. bandhumān rājā anaṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dūtena prakrośyedamavocat--yatkhalu gṛhapate jānīyāt--ahaṃ tvatprathamato vipaśyinaṃ samyakasmbuddhaṃ bhojayāmi, tataḥ paścāt tavāpi na duṣkaraṃ bhaviṣyati vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ bhojayitumiti/
176.005. sa kathayati--deva, mayā vipaśyī samyaksambuddhastvatprathamata upanimantritaḥ/
176.006. ahameva bhojayāmi/
176.006. rājā kathayati--gṛhapate, yadyapyevam, tathāpi tvaṃ mama viṣayanivāsī/
176.007. nārhāmyahaṃ tvatprathamato bhojayitum? deva, yadyapyahaṃ tava viṣayanivāsī, tathāpi yena pūrvanimantritaḥ sa eva bhojayati/
176.008. nātra devasya nirbandho yuktaḥ/
176.008. na te gṛhapate kāmakāraṃ dadāmi/
176.009. api tu yo bhaktottarikayā jeṣyati, so 'vaśiṣṭaṃ kālaṃ bhojayiṣyati/
176.010. tathā bhavatu ityanaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ pratyaśrauṣīt/
176.010. tathā anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāyodakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate/
176.012. atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto yenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapaterbhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
176.014. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
176.015. athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
176.016. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
176.018. atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddho 'naṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
176.020. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya prakrāntaḥ/
176.020. evaṃ bandhumatā rājñā bhojitaḥ/
176.021. eṣa eva grantho vistareṇa kartavyaḥ/
176.021. ma kvacidbhakrottarikayā parājayati/
176.022. tato bandhumān rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ/
176.022. amātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, kasmāt tvaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparastiṣṭhasīti? sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kathamahaṃ na cintāparastiṣṭhāmi yo 'haṃ mama viṣayanivāsinaṃ kuṭumbinaṃ na śaknomi bhaktottarikayā parājayitum? te kathayanti, deva, tasya gṛhapateḥ kāṣṭhaṃ nāsti/
176.025. kāṣṭhavikrayo vidhāryatāmīti/
176.026. rājñā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam/
176.026. bhavantaḥ, na kenacit madviṣayanivāsinā kāṣṭhaṃ vikretavyam/
176.027. yo vikrīṇīte, tena madviṣaye na vastavyamiti/
176.027. anaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirgandhakāṣṭhairbhaktaṃ sādhayitumārabdhaḥ/
176.028. sugandhatailena ca vastrāṇi tīmayitvā khādyakānyullāḍayitum/
176.028. surabhiṇā gandhena sarvā bandhumatī nagarī sphuṭā saṃvṛttā/
176.029. bandhumān rājā pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, kuta eṣa manojñagandha iti? tairvistareṇa samākhyātam/
176.030. sa kathayati--ahamapyevaṃ karomi/
176.030. kiṃ mama vibhavo nāstīti? amātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, kasyārthe evaṃ kriyate? ayaṃ gṛhapatiraputro nacirāt kālaṃ kariṣyati/
176.032. devasyaiva sarvaṃ santasvāpateyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
176.032. kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñāsyatāmiti<177>/
body.translated_text:
176.001. Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, having bowed his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, rose from his seat and departed to his own palace.
176.003. King <s>Bandhumān</s> sent a messenger to the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> and said: 'Know this, householder — let me feed the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> before you, and then afterward it will not be difficult for you either to feed the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>.'
176.005. He said: 'Your Majesty, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> was invited by me before you.
176.006. I shall be the one to feed him.'
176.006. The king said: 'Householder, even so, you are still a resident of my domain.
176.007. Am I not entitled to feed him before you?' 'Your Majesty, even though I am a resident of your domain, still the one who invited first is the one who feeds.
176.008. Your Majesty's insistence is not appropriate here.'
176.008. 'I do not grant you free leave in this, householder.
176.009. Rather, whoever wins by the superiority of the food offering, he shall feed for the remaining time.'
176.010. 'So be it' — the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> assented.
176.010. And so the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food both hard and soft, arose early, set out water-vessels, and announced the time to the Blessed One through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the food is ready. May the Blessed One now come at his convenience.'
176.012. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by the community of monks, approached the food-offering place of the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>.
176.014. Having approached, he sat down on a seat prepared at the head of the community of monks.
176.015. Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, seeing the community of monks with the <s>Buddha</s> at its head comfortably seated, served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent food both hard and soft.
176.016. Having in many ways served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent food, and knowing the Blessed One had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl set aside, he took a lower seat and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.
176.018. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
176.020. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he departed.
176.020. Likewise, King <s>Bandhumān</s> fed him.
176.021. This same narrative should be expanded in full detail.
176.021. But nowhere was the householder defeated in the superiority of food offerings.
176.022. Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, placing his cheek on his hand, remained absorbed in thought.
176.022. The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, why do you stand with your cheek on your hand, absorbed in thought?' He said: 'Sirs, how can I not be absorbed in thought, when I am unable to defeat a householder residing in my own domain in the superiority of food offerings?' They said: 'Your Majesty, that householder has no firewood.
176.025. Let a ban on the sale of firewood be decreed.'
176.026. The king had a proclamation made by bell:
176.026. 'Sirs, no one residing in my domain shall sell firewood.
176.027. Whoever sells it shall not dwell in my domain.'
176.027. The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> began to prepare the food with fragrant woods.
176.028. And having soaked cloths in fragrant oil, he used them to stir-fry the delicacies.
176.028. The entire city of <s>Bandhumatī</s> was pervaded with a delightful fragrance.
176.029. King <s>Bandhumān</s> asked: 'Sirs, where does this pleasant fragrance come from?' They told him in full detail.
176.030. He said: 'I too shall do the same.
176.030. Do I not have the resources?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, for what purpose is this being done? This householder is without a son and will soon die.
176.032. All his property and wealth will belong to Your Majesty.
176.032. Let the ban on firewood sales be lifted.' <177>

body.text:
177.001. tena kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñātaḥ/
177.001. anaṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā śrutam--rājñā kāṣṭhavikrayo 'nujñāta iti/
177.002. tena cittaṃ pradūṣya kharā vāg niścārita--tāvanme bhaktakāṣṭhamasti, yenāham enaṃ sahāmātyaṃ citāmāropya dhmāpayāmīti/
177.003. rājā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ/
177.004. amātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, kimarthaṃ kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparistiṣṭhasīti? tena vistareṇa samākhyātam/
177.005. te kathayanti--deva, alaṃ viṣādena/
177.005. vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmo yathā devaścānaṅgaṇaṃ gṛhapatiṃ parājayatīti/
177.006. tairaparasmin divase bandhumatī rājadhānī apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalyā vyavasthāpitā candanavāripariṣiktā surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibanddhā āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpā ucchritadhvajapatākā nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇā nandanavanodyānasadṛśā/
body.translated_text:
177.001. He lifted the ban on firewood sales.
177.001. The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> heard that the king had lifted the ban on firewood sales.
177.002. With a corrupted mind, he uttered a harsh word: 'I have enough firewood for the food-offerings that I could place him together with his ministers on a pyre and cremate them.'
177.003. The king, placing his cheek on his hand, remained absorbed in thought.
177.004. The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, why do you stand with your cheek on your hand, absorbed in thought?' He told them in full detail.
177.005. They said: 'Your Majesty, enough of despondency.
177.005. We shall act in such a way that Your Majesty defeats the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>.'
177.006. On the following day, they had the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s> cleared of stones, gravel, and refuse, sprinkled with sandalwood-water, festooned with vessels of fragrant incense, adorned with released streamers and garlands of silk, raised with banners and flags, strewn with various flowers — made to resemble the <s>Nandana</s>-grove paradise.

body.text:
177.008. tatpratispardhaśobhāvibhūṣito maṇḍavāṭaḥ kāritaḥ/
177.009. tasmin nānāratnavibhūṣitāsanavasanasampannaśobhāsanaprajñaptiḥ kāritā/
177.010. mṛduviśadasurabhigandhasampanno vividhabhaktavyañjanasahito divyasudhāmanojñasaṃkāśasrailokyaguroranurūpa āhāra upasamanvāhṛtaḥ/
177.011. tato bandhumān rājā dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ/
177.012. tato vismayāvarjitacittasaṃtatirvipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya dūtena kālamārocayati--samaye bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
177.014. atha vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena bandhumato rājño bhaktābhisārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
177.016. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
177.017. bandhumato rājño maṅgalyābhiṣeko hastināgo vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya śataśalākaṃ chatramupari mūrdhno dhārayati, avaśiṣṭā hastināhā bhikṣūṇām/
177.018. bandhumato rājño 'gramahiṣī vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sauvarṇena maṇivālavyajanena vījayati, avaśiṣṭā antaḥpurikā avaśiṣṭānāṃ bhikṣūṇām/
177.020. anaṅgaṇena gṛhapatinā avacarakaḥ puruṣaḥ preṣitah--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, paśya kīdṛśenāhāreṇa bandhumān rājā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayatīti/
177.021. sa gatastāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāvarjitamanāstatraivāvasthitaḥ/
177.022. evaṃ dvitīyaḥ, tṛtīyaḥ preṣitaḥ/
177.023. so 'pi tatraiva gatvā avasthitaḥ/
177.023. tato 'naṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ svayameva gataḥ/
177.023. so 'pi tāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ viṣādamāpannaḥ saṃlakṣayati--śakyamanyat saṃpādayitum/
177.024. kiṃ tu hastināmantaḥpurasya ca kuto mama vibhavah? iti viditvā niveśanaṃ gato dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--bhoḥ puruṣa, yadi kaścidyācanaka āgacchati, sa yat prārthayate taddātavyam, no tu praveśaḥ/
177.026. ityuktvā śokāgāraṃ praviśya avasthitaḥ/
177.027. śakrasya devendrasyādhastāt jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate/
177.027. sa saṃlakṣayati--ye kecilloke dakṣiṇīyāḥ, vipaśyī samyaksambuddhasteṣāmagraḥ, dānapatīnāmapyanaṅgaṇo gṛhapatiḥ/
177.029. sāhāyyamasya kalpayitavyam/
177.029. iti viditvā kauśiko brāhmaṇaveṣamabhinirmāya yenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
177.030. upasaṃkramya dauvārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, anaṅgaṇasya gṛhapateḥ kathaya--kauśikagotro brāhmaṇo dvāre tiṣṭhati bhavantaṃ draṣṭukāma iti/
177.031. sa kathayati--brāhmaṇa, gṛhapatinā ahaṃ sthāpitah--yaḥ kaścid yācanaka āgacchati, sa yat prāthayate<178>, taddātavyaṃ na tu praveśa iti/
body.translated_text: A pavilion was constructed, adorned with the splendor of that competition. In it, a seating arrangement was prepared, furnished with seats decorated with various jewels and endowed with beautiful coverings. Food was brought forth — soft, pure, and endowed with fragrant aromas, accompanied by various dishes and condiments, resembling divine ambrosia, delightful, and befitting the Guru of the Three Worlds. Then King <s>Bandhuman</s>, having seen it, was struck with the utmost amazement. Then, his mind-stream overcome with wonder, he announced the time to the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> through a messenger: "It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> come at whatever time he sees fit." Then the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded by a company of <s>bhikṣus</s> and attended by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, approached the place where King <s>Bandhuman</s>'s meal-offering was prepared. Having approached, he sat down on a seat arranged at the head of the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>. King <s>Bandhuman</s>'s ceremonial elephant held a hundred-ribbed parasol over the head of the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, while the remaining elephants held parasols for the <s>bhikṣus</s>. King <s>Bandhuman</s>'s chief queen fanned the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> with a golden fan set with gems and coral, while the remaining ladies of the inner palace fanned the remaining <s>bhikṣus</s>. The householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> sent a servant: "Go, good man, and see with what kind of food King <s>Bandhuman</s> is feeding the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>." He went, and having seen that splendor, his mind overcome with wonder, he remained standing right there. Thus a second and a third man were sent. He too, having gone there, remained standing. Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> went himself. He too, having seen that splendor, was overcome with the utmost despair and reflected: "It is possible to arrange other things, but where do I have the resources for elephants and ladies of the inner palace?" Having realized this, he went to his residence and addressed the doorkeeper: "Good man, if any petitioner comes, give him whatever he asks for, but do not let him enter." Having said this, he entered the chamber of sorrow and remained there. Now, the knowledge-and-vision of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, arose from below. He reflected: "Of all those in the world who are worthy of offerings, the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> is foremost among them, and among donors, the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> is foremost. Assistance must be rendered to him." Having realized this, <s>Kauśika</s> assumed the guise of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and approached the residence of the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>. Having approached, he addressed the doorkeeper: "Go, good man, and tell the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Kauśika</s> lineage stands at the door, wishing to see you.'" He replied: "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the householder has instructed me: 'Whoever comes as a petitioner, give him whatever he asks for, but do not let him enter.'"

body.text:
178.001. yena te prayojanaṃ tadgṛhītvā gaccha/
178.001. kiṃ te gṛhapatinā dṛṣṭeneti? sa kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, na mama kenacit prayojanam/
178.002. ahaṃ gṛhapatimeva draṣṭukāmaḥ/
178.003. gaccheti/
178.003. tenānaṅgaṇasya gṛhapatergatvā niveditam--ārya, kauśikasagotro brāhmaṇo dvāre tiṣṭhati āryaṃ draṣṭukāma iti/
178.004. sa kathayati--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, yena taysa prayojanaṃ tat prayaccha--kiṃ tenātra praviṣṭeneti? sa kathayati--ārya, ukto mayā evaṃ kathayati--nāhaṃ kiṃcit prārthayāmi, api tu gṛhapatimeva draṣṭukāma iti/
178.006. sa kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa yadyevam, praveśaya/
178.006. sa tena praveśitaḥ/
178.007. brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati--kasmāt tvaṃ gṛhapate kare kapolaṃ cintāparastiṣṭhasīti? sa gṛhapatirgāthāṃ bhāṣate--
178.009. na tasya kathayecchokam yaḥ śokānna pramocayet/
178.010. tasmai tu kathayecchokam yaḥ śokātsampramocayet//16//iti/
178.011. śakraḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, kastava śokah? kathaya, ahaṃ te śokātpramocayāmīti/
178.011. tena vistareṇa samākhyātam/
178.012. atha śakro devendraḥ kauśikabrāhmaṇarūpamantardhāpy svarūpeṇa sthitvā kathayati--gṛhapate, viśvakarmā te devaputraḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpayiṣyatītyuktvā prakrāntaḥ/
178.013. atha śakro devendro devāṃstrāyastriṃśān gatvā viśvakarmāṇaṃ devaputramāmantrayate--gaccha, viśvakarman, anaṅgaṇasya gṛhapateḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpaya/
178.015. paraṃ bhadraṃ tava kauśiketi viśvakarmaṇā devaputreṇa śakrasya devendrasya pratiśrutya āgataḥ/
178.016. prativiśiṣṭatarā nagaraśobhā nirmitā, divyo maṇḍalavāṭo divyāsanaprajñaptirdivya āhāraḥ samanvāhṛtaḥ/
178.017. airāvaṇo nāgarājo vipaśyinaḥ samyaksambuddhasya śataśalākaṃ chatramupari mūrdhno dhārayati, avaśiṣṭā nāgā avaśiṣṭānāṃ bhikṣūṇām/
178.018. śacī devakanyā vipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ sauvarṇena maṇivālavyajanena vījayati, avaśiṣṭā apsaraso bhikṣūn/
178.019. bandhumatā rājñā avacarakaḥ puruṣaḥ preṣitah--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, kīdṛśenāhāreṇānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatir buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ tarpayatīti? sa puruṣastatra gatastāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraiva avasthitaḥ/
178.021. tenāmātyaḥ preṣitaḥ/
178.022. so 'pi tatraivāvasthitaḥ/
178.022. kumāraḥ preṣitaḥ/
178.022. so 'pi tatraivāsthitaḥ/
178.022. tato bandhumān rājā svayameva taddvāraṃ gatvā avasthitaḥ/
178.023. vipaśyī samyaksambuddhaḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, bandhumān rājā dṛṣṭasatyaḥ/
178.024. tasyāntike tvayā kharavākkarma niścāritam/
178.024. sa eva dvāre tiṣṭhati/
178.025. gaccha kṣamayeti/
178.025. tenāsau nirgatya kṣamita uktaśca--mahārāja, praviśa svahastena pariveṣaṇaṃ kuru/
178.026. sa praviṣṭaḥ/
178.026. paśyati divyā vibhūtim/
178.026. dṛṣṭvā ca paraṃ vismayamāpannaḥ kathayati--gṛhapate, tvamevaiko 'rhasi dine dine buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayituṃ na vayaṃtī/
178.027. athānaṅgaṇo gṛhapatirvipaśyinaṃ samyaksambuddhamanayā vibhūtyā traimāsyaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kārā kṛtā, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyam, divyamānuṣīṃ śriyaṃ pratyanubhaveyam, evaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām, evaṃvidhameva śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti//
body.translated_text: "Take whatever you need and go. What need have you to see the householder?" He replied: "Good man, I have no need of anything. I wish only to see the householder. Go." He went and informed the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>: "Noble sir, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the <s>Kauśika</s> lineage stands at the door, wishing to see the noble sir." He replied: "Go, good man, give him whatever he needs — what purpose is there in his entering here?" He said: "Noble sir, I told him thus, but he says: 'I do not ask for anything; I only wish to see the householder.'" He replied: "Good man, if that is so, let him enter." He was admitted. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said: "Why, O householder, do you stand with your cheek resting on your hand, absorbed in worry?" The householder spoke this verse: "One should not tell one's sorrow to him who cannot free one from sorrow; one should tell one's sorrow only to him who can truly free one from sorrow." <s>Śakra</s> said: "Householder, what is your sorrow? Tell me, and I shall free you from it." He told him everything in detail. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, caused the form of the <s>Kauśika</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to disappear and, standing in his own form, said: "Householder, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Viśvakarman</s> shall render you assistance." Having said this, he departed. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, went to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and addressed the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Viśvakarman</s>: "Go, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, and render assistance to the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>." "Very well, O <s>Kauśika</s>," replied the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Viśvakarman</s> to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, and he came. He created a city-splendor even more excellent than before — a divine pavilion, a divine seating arrangement, and divine food was brought forth. <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, king of the <s>Nāgas</s>, held a hundred-ribbed parasol over the head of the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, while the remaining <s>Nāgas</s> held parasols for the remaining <s>bhikṣus</s>. <s>Śacī</s>, the divine maiden, fanned the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> with a golden fan set with gems and coral, while the remaining <s>Apsarases</s> fanned the <s>bhikṣus</s>. King <s>Bandhuman</s> sent a servant: "Go, good man — with what kind of food is the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> satisfying the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>?" That man went there, and having seen that splendor, he remained standing right there. Then a minister was sent. He too remained standing right there. A prince was sent. He too remained standing right there. Then King <s>Bandhuman</s> himself went and stood at that gate. The Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> said: "Householder, King <s>Bandhuman</s> has seen the truth. In his presence you have uttered harsh speech. He himself stands at the door. Go and ask his forgiveness." <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> went out and asked forgiveness, and said: "Great King, please enter and serve with your own hands." He entered. He beheld the divine splendor. Having seen it, he was struck with the utmost amazement and said: "Householder, you alone are worthy to feed the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> day after day — not we." Then the householder <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s>, having satisfied the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> with this splendor and with excellent food for three months, fell at his feet and began to make a vow: "By whatever merit I have rendered service to such a true and worthy recipient, by this root of virtue may I be born in a wealthy family of great riches and great fortune; may I enjoy both divine and human prosperity; may I attain such <s>dharmas</s>; may I please such a Teacher and never displease him."

body.text:
179.001. <179>kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau anaṅgaṇo nāma gṛhapatiḥ, eṣa evāsau jyotiṣkaḥ kulaputrastena kālena tena samayena/
179.002. yadanena bandhumato rājño dṛṣṭasatyasyāntike kharā vāgniścāritā, tasya karmaṇo vipākena pañcaśatāni samātṛkaścitāyāmāropya dhmāpitaḥ/
179.003. yāvadetarhi api citāmāropya dhmāpitaḥ/
179.004. yadvipaśyini tathāgate kārāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ/
179.005. divyamānuṣī śrīḥ prādurbhūtā/
179.005. mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
179.006. ahamanena vipaśyinā samyaksambuddhena sārdhaṃ samajavaḥ samabalaḥ samadhuraḥ samasāmānyaprāptaḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ/
179.007. iti hi bhikṣavah ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
179.009. tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
179.010. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who was the householder named <s>Anaṅgaṇa</s> — that was none other than this young man <s>Jyotiṣka</s> at that time, on that occasion. Because he uttered harsh speech in the presence of King <s>Bandhuman</s>, who had seen the truth, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was placed upon the funeral pyre and set ablaze five hundred times. And even now he was placed upon the pyre and set ablaze. Because he rendered service to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s> and made a vow, as the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great fortune. Divine and human prosperity manifested for him. Having gone forth in my teaching, he realized <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). I, together with the Fully Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, am equal in swiftness, equal in strength, equal in steadfastness, and equally attained in common qualities — a Teacher who was pleased and not displeased. Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for <s>karmas</s> that are entirely dark, the ripening is entirely dark; for those that are entirely bright, entirely bright; and for those that are mixed, mixed. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, having abandoned entirely dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, effort should be directed only toward entirely bright <s>karmas</s>. Thus should you train yourselves, O <s>bhikṣus</s>."

body.text:
179.011. idamavocadbhagavān/
179.011. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 179.012. iti divyāvadāne jyotiṣkāvadānamūnaviṃśatimam//
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Jyotiṣkāvadāna</s> (Story of <s>Jyotiṣka</s>), the nineteenth.

body.text: 180.001. div20 kanakavarṇāvadānam/
body.translated_text: The twentieth story in the <s>Divyāvadāna</s>: the <s>Kanakavarṇāvadāna</s> (Story of <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>).

body.text:
180.001. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
180.001. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ/
180.002. satkṛto bhagavān gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito bhikṣubhirbhikṣuṇībhirupāsakairupāsikābhī rājabhī rājamātrair nānātīrthikaśramaṇabrāhamaṇacarakaparibrājakairdevair nāgairyakṣairasurairgaruḍairgandharvaiḥ kinnarairmahorahaiḥ/
180.004. lābhī bhagavān prabhūtānāṃ praṇītānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ divyānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca/
180.007. taiśca bhagavānanupaliptaḥ padmamiva vāriṇā/
180.007. bhagavataścāyamevamrūpo digvidikṣu udārakalyāṇakīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgatah--ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
180.009. sa imaṃ sadevakaṃ lokaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇīṃ prajāṃ sadevamānuṣīṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayamabhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya pravedayate/
180.011. sa dharmaṃ deśayati ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye paryavasāne kalyāṇam/
180.012. svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati/
180.013. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--sacedbhikṣavaḥ sattvā jānīyurdānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam, apīdānīm yo 'sau apaścimaḥ kavalaścarama ālopaḥ, tato 'pyadatvā asaṃvibhajya na paribhuñjīran, sacellabheran dakṣiṇīyaṃ pratigrāhakam/
180.016. na caiṣāmutpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhet/
180.017. yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānante dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam, tasmāddhetoradattvā asaṃvibhajya paribhujyante āgṛhīteṃś cetasā/
180.019. utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati/
180.020. tatkasya hetoh?
180.021. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani rājābhūt kanakavarṇo nāma abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paramayā suvarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
180.022. rājā bhikṣavaḥ kanakavarṇa āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ/
180.023. prabhūtasattvasvāpateyaḥ prabhūvittopakaraṇaḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpaḥ prabhūtahastyaśvagaveḍakaḥ paripūṇakośakoṣṭhāgāraḥ/
180.024. rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya khalu bhikṣavaḥ kanakāvatī nāma rājadhānī babhūva pūrveṇa paścimena ca dvādaśa yojayānyāmena, dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca sapta yojanāni ca vistāreṇa/
180.026. ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca ramaṇīyā ca/
180.027. rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāśītir nagarasahasrāṇyabhūvan/
180.028. aṣṭādaśa kulakoṭī ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāṇi subhikṣāṇyākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi/
180.029. saptapañcāśadgrāmakoṭya ṛddhāḥ sphītāḥ kṣemāḥ subhikṣā ramaṇīyā mahājanākīrṇamanuṣyāḥ/
180.030. ṣaṣṭiḥ karvaṭasahasrāṇyabhūvann ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāṇi subhikṣāṇyākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi/
180.031. rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāṣṭādaśāmātyasahasrāṇyabhūvan/
180.031. viṃśatistrīsahasrāṇyantaḥpuramabhūt/
180.032. rājā bhikṣavaḥ kanakavarṇo dhārmiko babhūva/
180.032. dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati//
body.translated_text:
180.001. Thus have I heard.
180.001. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great community of monks — twelve hundred and fifty monks.
180.002. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped by monks, nuns, male lay-followers, female lay-followers, kings, royal ministers, various non-Buddhist <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wanderers, and itinerants, by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>.
180.004. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was a recipient of abundant and excellent robes, alms-food, bedding, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick — both divine and human.
180.007. Yet the <s>Bhagavān</s> was untouched by these, like a lotus by water.
180.007. And this noble, auspicious fame and renown of the <s>Bhagavān</s> had spread in all directions and intermediate directions: 'He is indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
180.009. He makes known to this world with its gods, with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, to this generation with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods and humans, that which he has himself directly known, realized, and attained in this very life.
180.011. He teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, which is good at the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end.
180.012. He proclaims the holy life that is good in meaning, good in expression, complete, fulfilled, pure, and perfectly clear.
180.013. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'If, monks, beings knew the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts, they would not eat even their last morsel, their final bite of food, without giving and sharing — if they could find a worthy recipient.
180.016. Nor would the arisen stain of miserliness persist in overcoming their minds.
180.017. But since, monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the fruit and ripening of sharing gifts, therefore they consume without giving and without sharing, with minds seized by greed.
180.019. And the arisen stain of miserliness persists in overcoming their minds.
180.020. What is the reason for this?
180.021. Long ago, monks, in a past era, there was a king named <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> (Golden-Complexioned) — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with supreme golden beauty.
180.022. King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, monks, was wealthy, of great riches and great possessions,
180.023. with abundant livestock and property, abundant equipment and resources, abundant wealth, grain, gold, silver, gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch, stone, coral, silver, and gold, abundant elephants, horses, cattle, and sheep, with full treasuries and granaries.
180.024. King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, monks, had a royal capital named <s>Kanakāvatī</s> — twelve <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in length from east to west, and seven <s>yojanas</s> in width from south to north.
180.026. It was prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, and delightful.
180.027. King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had eighty thousand cities,
180.028. eighteen <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of noble families — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people.
180.029. Fifty-seven <s>koṭis</s> of villages — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, and teeming with many people.
180.030. Sixty thousand market-towns — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people.
180.031. King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> had eighteen thousand ministers.
180.031. His inner palace had twenty thousand women.
180.032. King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, monks, was righteous.
180.032. He governed the kingdom according to the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text:
181.001. <181>athāpareṇa samayena rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya ekākino rahogatasya pratisamlīnasya evaṃ cetasi cetaḥparivitarkamudapādi--yannvahaṃ sarvavaṇijo 'śulkānagulmān muñceyam/
181.002. sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyānakārānagulmān muñceyamiti/
181.003. atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapariṣadyānāmantrayate--adyāgreṇa vo grāmaṇyaḥ sarvavaṇijo 'śulkān muñcāmi, sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyānakārānaśulkān muñcāmi/
181.005. tasyānenopāyena bahūni varṣāṇi rājyaṃ kārayato 'pareṇa samayena nakṣatraṃ viṣamībhūtam, dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na varṣati/
181.006. atha brāhmaṇā lakṣaṇajñā naimittikā bhūmyantarikṣamantrakuśalā nakṣatraśukragrahacariteṣu tat saṃlakṣayitvā yena rājā kanakavarṇaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
181.008. apasaṃkramya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamidamavocan--yatkhalu devo jānīyāt--nakṣatraṃ viṣamībhūtam, dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na varṣiṣyati/
181.009. atha rājā kanakavarṇa idamevamrūpaṃ nirghoṣaṃ śrutvā aśrūṇi pravartayati--aho bata me jāmbudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, aho bata me jambudvīpah ṛddhaḥ sphītaḥ kṣemaḥ subhikṣo ramaṇīyo bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyo nacirādeva śūnyo bhaviṣyati rahitamanuṣyaḥ/
181.012. atha rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya muhūrtaṃ śocitvā etadabhavat--ya ime āḍhyā mahādhanā mahābhogāḥ, te śakṣyanti yāpayitum/
181.013. ya ime daridrā alpadhanā alpānnapānabhogāḥ, te katham yāpayiṣyanti? tasyaitadabhavat--yannvahaṃ jambudvīpādannādyaṃ saṃhareyam, sarvajāmbudvīpān sattvān gaṇayeyam/
181.015. atha gaṇayitvā māpayeyam, māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ kārayeyam/
181.016. ekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ kārayitvā sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ pratyarpayeyamiti/
181.017. atha kanakavarṇo rājā gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyānāmantrayate--gacchata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ, sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ saṃhṛtya gaṇayata, gaṇayitvā māpayata, māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekaṃ koṣṭhāgāraṃ sthāpayata/
181.019. paraṃ deveti gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pratiśrutya sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ gaṇayanti, gaṇayitvā māpayanti, māpayitvā sarvadrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sthāpayanti/
body.translated_text:
181.001. Then, at another time, when King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was alone, in seclusion, in meditative retreat, this thought arose in his mind:
181.002. 'Let me release all merchants from tolls and customs-posts. Let me release all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from taxes and customs-posts.'
181.003. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, great ministers, counselors, and chamberlains: 'From today onward, good sirs, I release all merchants from tolls, and I release all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from taxes and tolls.'
181.005. While he had been governing the kingdom in this manner for many years, at another time the stars became unfavorable, and for twelve years the rains did not fall.
181.006. Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who were experts in signs, omens, earth, sky, and spells, and skilled in the movements of stars, planets, and celestial bodies, having observed this, approached King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.
181.008. Having approached, they said this to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: 'May the lord know — the stars have become unfavorable; for twelve years the rains will not fall.'
181.009. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, hearing this kind of proclamation, shed tears: 'Alas, my people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! Alas, my <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, delightful, and teeming with many people — will before long become empty and devoid of people!'
181.012. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, after grieving for a moment, thought: 'Those who are wealthy, of great riches and great possessions — they will be able to survive.
181.013. Those who are poor, of little wealth and little food, drink, and provisions — how will they survive?' This thought occurred to him: 'Let me collect all the food from <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and count all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
181.015. Then, having counted, let me measure it; having measured, let me have one granary established in every village, city, town, market-town, and royal capital.
181.016. Having established one granary, let me distribute equal rations of food to all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.'
181.017. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, great ministers, counselors, and chamberlains: 'Go, good sirs, collect all the food from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, count it, having counted it measure it, having measured it establish one granary in every village, city, town, market-town, and royal capital.'
181.019. 'Yes, Your Majesty' — the accountants, great ministers, counselors, and chamberlains, having assented to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, collected all the food from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, counted it, having counted it measured it, having measured it stored it in one granary in every village, city, town, market-town, and royal capital.

body.text:
181.021. ekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sthāpayitvā yena rājā kanakavarṇaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
181.022. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamidamavocat--yat khalu deva jānīyāh--sarvagrāmanagaranigamakarvaṭarājadhānīṣvannādyaṃ saṃhṛtam, saṃhṛtya gaṇitam, gaṇayitvā māpitam, māpayitvā sarvagrāmanagaranigamarājadhānīṣvekasmin koṣṭhāgāre sathāpitam yasyedānīṃ devaḥ kālaṃ manyate/
181.025. atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ saṃkhyāgaṇakalipikapauruṣeyānāmantrayitvā etadavocat--gacchata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ, sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān gaṇayata, gaṇayitvā grāmaṇyaḥ sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ prayacchata/
181.027. paraṃ deveti saṃkhyāgaṇakalipikapauruṣeyā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pratiśrutya sarvajāmbudvīpakān manuṣyān gaṇayanti, saṃgaṇya rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamādau kṛtvā sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ samaṃ bhaktaṃ prajñapayanti/
181.030. te yāpayantyekādaśavarṣāṇi, dvādaśavarṣaṃ na yāpayanti/
181.030. nirgato dvādaśasya varṣasyaiko māso yāvadbahavaḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikā jighatsitāḥ pipāsitāḥ kālaṃ kurvanti/
181.031. ten khalu punaḥ samayena sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇamanyatra rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā//
body.translated_text:
181.021. Having stored it in one granary, they approached King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.
181.022. Having approached, they said this to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: 'May the lord know — the food has been collected from every village, city, town, market-town, and royal capital; having been collected, it has been counted; having been counted, it has been measured; having been measured, it has been stored in one granary in every village, city, town, and royal capital. Now let the lord determine the proper time.'
181.025. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, having summoned the accountants, calculators, scribes, and servants, said this: 'Go, good sirs, count all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; having counted them, good sirs, distribute equal rations of food to all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.'
181.027. 'Yes, Your Majesty' — the accountants, calculators, scribes, and servants, having assented to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, counted all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; having counted them, beginning with King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> himself, they established equal rations of food for all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
181.030. They survived for eleven years, but could not survive the twelfth.
181.030. When one month of the twelfth year had passed, many women, men, boys, and girls, starving and thirsting, died.
181.031. At that time, all the food in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was exhausted, except for one measure of grain belonging to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> that remained.

body.text:
182.001. <182>tena khalu samayena anyatamaścatvāriṃśatkalpasamprasthito bodhisattva imāṃ sahālokadhātumanuprāpto babhūva/
182.002. adrākṣīd bodhisattvo 'nyatarasmin banaṣaṇḍe putraṃ mātrā sārdhaṃ vipratipadyamanam/
182.003. dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--kliśyanti bateme sattvāḥ, saṃkliśyanti bateme sattvāḥ, yatra hi nāma asyāmeva nava māsān kukṣau uṣitvā, asyā eva stanau pītvā, atraiva kālaṃ kariṣyati iti/
182.005. alaṃ me īdṛśaiḥ sattvairadhārmikairadharmarāgaraktairmithyādṛṣṭakairviṣamalobhābhibhūtairamātṛrajñaiśrāmaṇyaraibrāhmaṇyairakule jyeṣṭhāpacāyakaiḥ/
182.006. ka utsahata īdṛśānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya bodhisattvacaryāṃ caritum? yannvahaṃ svake kārye pratipadyeyam/
182.007. atha bohisattvo yenānyataradvṛkṣamūlaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
182.008. upasaṃkramya tasmin vṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇaḥ/
182.008. paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya pañcasūpādānaskandheṣūdayavyayānudarśī viharati yadutedaṃ rūpam, ayaṃ rūpasamudayaḥ, ayaṃ rūpasyāstaṃgamaḥ, iyaṃ vedanā, iyaṃ saṃjñā, ime saṃkrārāḥ, idaṃ vijñānam, ayaṃ vijñānasamudayaḥ, ayaṃ vijñānasyāstaṃgama iti/
182.011. sa evaṃ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣūdayavyayānudarśī viharannacirādeva yatkiṃcit samudayadharmakaṃ tat sarvaṃ nirodhadharmakamiti viditvā tatraiva pratyekāṃ bodhimadhigatavān/
182.013. atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho yathāprāptānavalokya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
182.014. saṃsevamānasya bhavanti snehāḥ snehānvayaṃ saṃbhavatīha duḥkham/
182.016. ādīnavaṃ snehagataṃ viditvā ekaścaret khaṅgaviṣāṇakalpaḥ//1//iti/
182.018. atha tasya bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhasyaitadabhavat--bahūnāṃ me sattvānāmarthāya duṣkarāṇi cīrṇāni, na ca kasyacit sattvasya hitaṃ kṛtam/
182.019. kamadyāhamanukampeyam, kasyāhamadya piṇḍapātamāhṛtya paribhuñjīya? atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa sarvāvantamimaṃ jambudvīpaṃ samantādanuvilokayannadrākṣīt sa bhagavān pratyekabuddhaḥ sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇam, anyatra rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā/
182.022. tasyaitadabhavat--yannvahaṃ rājānaṃ kanakavarṇamanukampeyam/
182.023. yannvahaṃ rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya niveśanāt piṇḍapātamahṛtya paribhuñjīya/
182.024. atha bhagavān pratyekabuddhastat eva ṛddhyā vihāyasamabhyudgamya dṛśyatā kāyena śakuniriva ṛddhyā yena kanakāvatī rājadhānī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
182.025. tena khalu samayena rājā kanakavarṇa upariprāsādatalagato 'bhūt pañcamātrairamātyasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ/
182.026. adrākṣīdanyatamo mahāmātrastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ dūrata evāgacchantam/
182.027. dṛṣṭvā ca punarmahāmātrānāmantrayate--paśyata paśyata grāmaṇyaḥ/
182.028. dūrata eva lohitapakṣaḥ śakunta ihāgacchati/
182.028. dvitīyo mahāmātra evamāha--naiṣa grāmaṇyo lohitapakṣaḥ śakuntaḥ, rākṣasa eva ojohāra ihāgacchati/
182.029. eṣo 'smākaṃ bhakṣayiṣyati/
182.030. atha rājā kanakavarṇa ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ mukhaṃ saṃparimārjya mahāmātrānāmantrayate--naiṣa grāmaṇyo lohitapakṣaḥ śakuntaḥ, na ca rākṣasa ojohāraḥ/
182.031. ṛṣireṣo 'smākamanukampayehāgacchati/
182.032. atha sa bhagavān pratyekabuddho rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya prāsāde pratyaṣṭhāt//
body.translated_text:
182.001. At that time, a certain <s>Bodhisattva</s> who had set out forty <s>kalpas</s> ago arrived in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system.
182.002. That <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw in a certain forest grove a son quarreling with his mother.
182.003. Having seen this, he thought: 'Alas, how these beings suffer, how they are tormented! For one who dwelt nine months in her very womb, who drank from her very breasts — he will cause her death right here.'
182.005. 'Enough of such beings for me — unrighteous, stained with unlawful passion, holding wrong views, overcome by crooked greed, ungrateful to their mothers, having no respect for ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, not honoring the elders of the family.
182.006. Who would undertake the <s>Bodhisattva</s> career for the sake of such beings? Let me rather attend to my own affair.'
182.007. Then that <s>Bodhisattva</s> approached the foot of a certain tree.
182.008. Having approached, he sat down at the foot of that tree.
182.008. Crossing his legs, holding his body erect, establishing mindfulness before him, he dwelt contemplating the arising and passing away in the five aggregates of clinging: 'This is form, this is the arising of form, this is the cessation of form; this is feeling, this is perception, these are formations, this is consciousness, this is the arising of consciousness, this is the cessation of consciousness.'
182.011. Thus dwelling, contemplating the arising and passing away in the five aggregates of clinging, before long he understood: 'Whatever is of the nature to arise, all that is of the nature to cease' — and right there he attained solitary awakening (<s>Pratyekabodhi</s>).
182.013. Then the Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, surveying what he had attained, spoke a verse at that time:
182.014. 'For one who associates, attachments arise; following upon attachment, suffering arises in this world.
182.016. Having seen the danger inherent in attachment, let one wander alone like the horn of a rhinoceros.' //1//
182.018. Then this thought occurred to that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>: 'I have performed austerities for the sake of many beings, yet I have not benefited even a single being.
182.019. Upon whom should I now have compassion? From whose dwelling should I today accept an alms-meal?' Then the Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, with his divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, surveying this entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> on all sides, saw that food had been exhausted throughout all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, except for one measure of cooked rice remaining with King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.
182.022. He thought: 'Let me have compassion on King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.
182.023. Let me accept an alms-meal from the dwelling of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.'
182.024. Then the Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, rising by supernatural power into the sky from that very place, with his body visible like a bird, flew through the sky to the royal capital of <s>Kanakāvatī</s>.
182.025. At that time, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> was standing on an upper terrace of his palace, surrounded by five thousand ministers.
182.026. A certain chief minister saw that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> approaching from afar.
182.027. Having seen him, he addressed the ministers: 'Look, look, good sirs!
182.028. From afar, a red-winged bird is coming here.'
182.028. A second minister said: 'That, good sirs, is not a red-winged bird — it is a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon), a devourer of vital essence, coming here.
182.029. He will devour us.'
182.030. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, wiping his face with both hands, addressed the ministers: 'This, good sirs, is not a red-winged bird, nor is it a <s>Rākṣasa</s> devourer of vital essence.
182.031. This is a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) coming here out of compassion for us.'
182.032. Then that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> alighted on the terrace of King <s>Kanakavarṇa's</s> palace.

body.text:
183.001. <183>atha rājā kanakavarṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhamutthāyāsanāt pratyudgamya pādau śirasā vanditvā prajñapta evāsane niṣīdayati/
183.002. atha rājā kanakavarṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyekabuddhamidamavocat--kimartham ṛṣe ihābhyāgamanam? bhojanārthaṃ mahārāja/
183.003. evamukte rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prārodīt/
183.004. aśrūṇi pravartayannevamāha--aho me dāridryam, aho dāridryam, yatra hi nāma jambudvīpaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayitvā ekasyāpi ṛṣerasamarthaḥ piṇḍapātaṃ pratipādayitum/
183.005. atha yā kanakāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmadhyuṣitā devatā, sā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya purastādgāthāṃ bhāṣate--
183.007. kiṃ duḥkhaṃ dāridryaṃ kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ tadeva dāridryam/
183.008. maraṇasamaṃ dāridryam//2//
body.translated_text:
183.001. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, rising from his seat, went out to welcome that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, paid homage at his feet with his head, and seated him on a prepared seat.
183.002. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> said to that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>: 'For what purpose, O sage, have you come here?' 'For a meal, Great King.'
183.003. When this was said, King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> wept.
183.004. Shedding tears, he said: 'Alas, my poverty! Alas, poverty! For even while exercising sovereignty and lordship over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, I am unable to provide even a single sage with an alms-meal!'
183.005. Then a deity dwelling in the royal capital of <s>Kanakāvatī</s> spoke a verse before King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>:
183.007. 'What is painful? Poverty. What is more painful? That very poverty.
183.008. Poverty is equal to death.' //2//

body.text:
183.009. atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ koṣṭhāgārikaṃ puruṣamāmantrayate--asti bhoḥ puruṣa, mama niveśane kiṃcidbhaktam, yadahamasya ṛṣeḥ pradāsyāmi? sa evamāha--yat khalu deva jānīyāh--sarvajambudvīpādannādyaṃ parikṣīṇam, anyatra devasyaikā mānikā bhaktasyāvaśiṣṭā/
183.011. atha rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaitadabhavat--sacet paribhuñje, jīviṣye/
183.012. atha na paribhokṣye, mariṣye/
183.012. tasyaitadabhavat--yadi paribhokṣye, yadi vā na paribhokṣye, avaśyaṃ mayā kālaḥ kartavyaḥ/
183.013. alaṃ me jīvitena/
183.013. kathaṃ nāmehedṛśa ṛṣiḥ śīlavān kalyāṇadharmā mama niveśane 'dya yathādhautena pātreṇa nirgamiṣyati? atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyān saṃnipātyaivamavocat--anumodata yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ, ayaṃ rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāpaścima odanātisargaḥ/
183.016. anena kuśalamūlena sarvajāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dāridryasamucchedaḥ syāt/
183.017. atha rājā kanakavarṇastasya maharṣestat pātraṃ gṛhītvā ekāṃ mānikāṃ bhaktasya pātre prakṣipya ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ pātraṃ gṛhītvā jānubhyāṃ nipatya tasya bhagavataḥ pratyekabuddhasya dakṣiṇe pāṇau pātraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati/
183.019. dharmatā punarbhagavatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ kāyikī dharmadeśanā na vācikī/
183.020. atha bhagavān pratyekabuddho rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyāntikāt piṇḍapātramādāya tat eva ṛddhyā uparivihāyasā prakrāntaḥ/
183.022. atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā tāvadanimiṣaṃ prekṣamāṇo 'sthāt, yāvaccakṣuṣpathādatikrānta iti/
183.023. atha rājā kanakavarṇo gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyānāmantrayate--gacchata grāmaṇyaḥ svakasvakāni niveśanāni/
183.024. mā ihaiva prāsāde jighatsāpipāsābhyāṃ sarva eva kālaṃ kariṣyatha/
183.025. ta evamāhuh--yadā devasya śrīsaubhāgyasampadāsīt, tadā vayaṃ devena sārdhaṃ krīḍatā ramatā kathaṃ punarvayamidānīṃ devaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye parityakṣyāma iti/
183.026. atha rājā kanakavarṇaḥ prārodīt/
183.027. aśrūṇi pravartayati/
183.027. aśrūṇi saṃparimārjya gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyānidamavocat--gacchata grāmaṇyo yathāsvakasvakāni niveśanāni/
183.028. mā ihaiva prāsāde jighatsāpipāsābhyāṃ sarva eva kālaṃ kariṣyatha/
183.029. evamuktā gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapāriṣadyāḥ prarudanto 'śrūṇi pravartayanto 'śrūṇi saṃparimārjya yena rājā kanakavarṇastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
183.030. upasaṃkramya rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasya pādau śirasā vanditvā añjaliṃ kṛtvā rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyaitadūcuh--kṣantavyaṃ te yadasmābhiḥ kiṃcidaparāddham/
183.032. adyāsmākaṃ devasyāpaścimaṃ darśanam//
body.translated_text:
183.009. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the granary keeper: 'Good man, is there any food at all in my dwelling that I might give to this sage?' He replied: 'May Your Majesty please know — all food throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s> has been exhausted; only one measure of cooked rice remains for Your Majesty.'
183.011. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> thought: 'If I eat it, I shall live.
183.012. If I do not eat it, I shall die.'
183.012. He thought further: 'Whether I eat it or do not eat it, I must certainly die.
183.013. Enough of life for me!
183.013. How can it be that such a sage, virtuous and of excellent character, should today leave my dwelling with his bowl as clean as when he entered?' Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, having summoned his accountants, chief ministers, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers, said this: 'Rejoice, good sirs! This is King <s>Kanakavarṇa's</s> last gift of food.
183.016. By this wholesome root, may the poverty of all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be eradicated.'
183.017. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, having taken that great sage's bowl, dropped the one measure of cooked rice into the bowl, and holding the bowl with both hands, kneeling on both knees, he placed the bowl in the right hand of that Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.
183.019. For it is the nature of Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> that their teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> is through bodily action, not through speech.
183.020. Then the Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, having accepted the alms-meal from King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, departed from that very place by supernatural power, rising into the sky.
183.022. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, with palms joined, stood gazing without blinking for as long as he had not passed beyond the range of his vision.
183.023. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> addressed the accountants, chief ministers, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers: 'Go, good sirs, each to your own dwellings.
183.024. Do not let all of us die right here on this terrace from hunger and thirst.'
183.025. They said: 'When Your Majesty had the fortune of glory and prosperity, we played, delighted, and enjoyed ourselves with Your Majesty. How then could we abandon Your Majesty now, in his final hour?'
183.026. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> wept.
183.027. He shed tears.
183.027. Wiping his tears, he said to the accountants, chief ministers, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers: 'Go, good sirs, each to your own dwellings.
183.028. Do not let all of us die right here on this terrace from hunger and thirst.'
183.029. When this was said, the accountants, chief ministers, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers, weeping, shedding tears, wiping their tears, approached King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>.
183.030. Having approached, they paid homage at the feet of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> with their heads, joined their palms, and said to King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>: 'May you forgive us for whatever offense we have committed.
183.032. Today is our last sight of Your Majesty.'

body.text:
184.001. <184>tadyathā tena bhagavatā pratyekabuddhena sa piṇḍapātraḥ paribhuktaḥ, atha tasminneva kṣaṇe samantāccatasṛṣu dikṣu catvāryabhrapaṭalāni vyutthitāni, śītalāśca vāyavo vātumārabdhāḥ, ye jambudvīpādaśuciṃ vyapanayanti, meghāśca pravarṣayantaḥ pāṃśūñ śamayanti/
184.003. atha tasminneva divase dvitīye 'rdhabhāge vividhasya khādanīyabhojanīyasya varṣaṃ pravarṣati/
184.004. idamevamrūpaṃ bhojanamodanasaktavaḥ kulmāṣamatsyamāṃsam, idamevamrūpaṃ khādanīyaṃ mūlakhādanīyaṃ skandhakhādanīyaṃ patrakhādanīyaṃ puṣpakhādanīyaṃ phalakhādanīyaṃ tilakhādanīyaṃ khaṇḍaśarkaraguḍakhādanīyaṃ piṣṭakhādanīyam/
184.006. atha rājā kanakavarṇo hṛṣṭatuṣṭah udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto gaṇakamahāmātrāmātyadauvārikapārṣadyānāmantrayate--paśyatha yūyaṃ grāmaṇyaḥ, adyaiva tasyaikapiṇḍapātadānasyāṅkuraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
184.009. phalamanyadbhaviṣyati//
body.translated_text:
184.001. Just as that alms-meal was consumed by the Blessed <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, at that very instant, from all four directions, four banks of clouds arose, and cool winds began to blow that carried away the impurities from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, and the clouds, raining, settled the dust.
184.003. Then on that very day, in the second half, a rain of various kinds of hard and soft food fell —
184.004. food of this kind: rice, barley-broth, rice-cakes, porridge; and hard food of this kind: root-food, stem-food, leaf-food, flower-food, fruit-food, sesame-food, sugar and molasses food, and flour-food.
184.006. Then King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, delighted, pleased, overjoyed, elated, uplifted, joyful, and filled with gladness and satisfaction, addressed the accountants, chief ministers, ministers, doorkeepers, and courtiers: 'See, good sirs! This very day, the sprout of that single alms-gift has appeared.
184.009. The fruit will be something else entirely.'

body.text:
184.010. atha dvitīye divase saptāhaṃ dhānyavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti, tadyathā--tilataṇḍulā mudgamāṣā yavā godhūmamasūrāḥ śālayaḥ/
184.011. saptāhaṃ sarpivarṣaṃ pravarṣanti, saptāhaṃ karpāsavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti, saptāhaṃ nānāvidhadūṣyavarṣaṃ pravarṣanti, saptāhaṃ saptaratnānāṃ varṣaṃ pravarṣanti, suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya/
184.013. sarvasya rājñaḥ kanakavarṇasyānubhāvena jāmbudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ dāridryasamucchedo babhūva//
body.translated_text:
184.010. Then on the second day, for seven days a rain of grain fell — namely: sesame, rice, mung beans, black beans, barley, wheat, lentils, and <s>śāli</s> rice.
184.011. For seven days a rain of ghee fell; for seven days a rain of cotton fell; for seven days a rain of various kinds of cloth fell; for seven days a rain of the seven precious substances fell — gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), crystal, red pearls, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (cat's eye), and <s>musāragalva</s> (agate).
184.013. All by the power of King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>, the poverty of the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was eradicated.

body.text:
184.015. syāt khalu bhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājā kanakavarṇo babhūva/
184.016. na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
184.016. ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājā kanakavarṇo babhūva/
184.017. tadanena bhikṣavaḥ paryāyeṇa veditavyam/
184.017. sacedbhikṣavaḥ sattvā jānīyurdānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam--apīdānīm yo 'sau apaścimakaḥ kavalaścarama ālopaḥ, tato 'pyadattvā asaṃvibhajya na paribhuñjīran, sacellabheran dakṣiṇīyaṃ pratigrāhakam/
184.019. na caiṣāmutpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati/
184.020. yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānate dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam--yathā ahaṃ jāne dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam, tasmātte 'dattvā asaṃvibhajya paribhuñjate āgṛhītena cetasā, utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādattaṃ tiṣṭhati/
184.024. na naśyate pūrvakṛtaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ na naśyate sevanaṃ piṇḍatānām/
184.026. na naśyate āryajaneṣu bhāṣitaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtajñeṣu na jātu naśyati//3//
body.translated_text: Perhaps, monks, you might have doubt or uncertainty: 'Someone else was King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> at that time, in that era.' It should not be viewed thus. I myself was King <s>Kanakavarṇa</s> at that time, in that era. By this method, monks, it should be understood: If, monks, beings knew the fruit of giving and the result and ripening of sharing gifts — even that very last morsel, that final mouthful, they would not consume without giving and without sharing, provided they could find a worthy recipient. Nor would the stain of miserliness arise and persist in their minds. But since, monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the result and ripening of sharing gifts — as I know the fruit of giving and the result and ripening of sharing gifts — therefore they consume without giving and without sharing, with a mind of grasping, and the stain of miserliness arises and persists in their minds. 'What was formerly done, whether wholesome or unwholesome, does not perish; nor does the serving of alms-food perish; nor does what is spoken among noble people perish; what is done for the grateful never perishes.' //3//

body.text:
184.028. sukṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ karma duṣkṛtaṃ vāpyaśobhanam/
184.029. asti caitasya vipāko avaśya dāsyate phalam//4//
body.translated_text: 'Whether a deed well done and beautiful, or a deed ill done and ugly — there is indeed a ripening of this; it will inevitably bear fruit.' //4//

body.text:
184.030. idamavocadbhagavān/
184.030. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikādevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayaḥ sarvāvatī ca parṣadbhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and the entire assembly rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 184.032. iti śrīdivyāvadāne kanakavarṇāvadānaṃ viṃśatimam/
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Kanakavarṇāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Kanakavarṇa</s>), the twentieth.

body.text: 185.001. div21 sahasodgatāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 21: The <s>Sahasodgatāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Sahasodgata</s>).

body.text:
185.002. buddho bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe/
185.002. ācaritamāyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya kālena kālaṃ narakacārikāṃ carituṃ tiryakcārikāṃ carituṃ pretacārikāṃ devacārikāṃ manuṣyacārikāṃ caritum/
185.004. sa yāni tāni nārakāṇāṃ sattvānāmutpāṭānupāṭanacchedanabhedanādīni duḥkhāni, tiraścāmanyonyabhakṣaṇādīni, pretānāṃ kṣuttṛṣādīni, devānāṃ cyavanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanādīni, manuṣyāṇāṃ paryeṣṭicyasanādīni duḥkhāni, tāni dṛṣṭvā jambudvīpamāgatya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāmārocayati/
185.007. yasya kasyacit sārdhaṃvihārī antevāsī vā anabhirato brahmacaryaṃ carati, sa tamādāya yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanastenopasaṃkrāmati, āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana enaṃ samyagavavadiṣyati, anuśāsiṣyatīti/
185.009. tamāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ samyagavavadati samyaganuśāsti/
185.010. evamaparamaparaṃ te āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena samyagavavāditāḥ samyaganuśiṣṭā abhiratā brahmacaryaṃ caranti, uttare ca viśeṣamadhigacchanti/
185.011. tena khalu samayenāuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaścatasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhirākīrṇo viharati bhikṣubhirbhikṣuṇībhirupāsakairupāsikābhiśca/
185.013. jānakāḥ pṛcchakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
185.013. pṛcchati buddho bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandam/
185.014. sa kathayati--ācaritaṃ bhadanta āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya kālena kālaṃ narakacārikāṃ carituṃ tiryakcarikāṃ pretacārikāṃ devacārikāṃ manuṣyacārikāṃ caritum/
185.015. sa yāni tāni nārakāṇāṃ sattvānāmutpāṭānupāṭanacchedanabhedanādīni duḥkhāni, tiryaścāmanyonyabhakṣaṇādīni, pretānāṃ kṣuttṛṣādīni, devānāṃ cyavanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanādīni, manuṣyāṇāṃ paryeṣṭivyasanādīni duḥkhāni, tāni dṛṣṭvā jambudvīpamāgatya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāmārocayati/
185.018. yasya kasyacit sārdhaṃvihārī antevāsī vā anabhirato brahmacaryaṃ carati, sa tamādāya yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanastenopasaṃkrāmati, āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana eva samyagavavadiṣyati samyaganuśāsiṣyatīti, tamāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ samyagavavadati samyaganuśāsti/
185.021. evamaparamaparaṃ te āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena samyagavavāditāḥ samyagavuśiṣṭā abhiratā brahmacaryaṃ caranti, uttare ca viśeṣamadhigacchanti/
185.023. ayaṃ bhadanta heturayaṃ pratyayo yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaścatasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhirākīrṇo viharati bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikābhiḥ/
185.024. na sarvatra ānanda maudgalyāyano bhikṣurbhaviṣyati maudgalyāyanasadṛśo vā/
185.025. tasmād dvārakoṣṭhake pañcagaṇḍakaṃ cakraṃ kārayitavyam/
185.026. uktaṃ bhagavatā dvārakoṣṭhake pañcagaṇḍakaṃ cakraṃ kārayitavyamiti/
185.026. bhikṣavo na jānate kīdṛśaṃ kārayitavyamiti/
185.027. bhagavānāha--pañca gatayaḥ kartavyā narakāstiryañcaḥ pretā devā manuṣyāśca/
185.028. tatrādhastāt narakāḥ kartavyāḥ, tiryañcaḥ pretāśca, upariṣṭāt devā manuṣyāśca/
185.029. catvāro dvīpāḥ kartavyāḥ pūrvavideho 'paragodānīya uttarakururjambudvīpaśca/
185.029. madhye rāgadveṣamohāḥ kartavyāḥ, rāgaḥ pārāvatākāreṇa, dveṣo bhujaṅgākāreṇa, mohaḥ sūkarākāreṇa/
185.030. buddhapratimāścaitannirvāṇamaṇḍalamupadarśayantyaḥ kartavyāḥ/
185.031. anupapādukāḥ sattvā ghaṭīyantraprayogeṇa cyavamānā upapadyamānāśca kartavyāḥ/
185.032. sāmantakena dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo 'nulomapratilomaḥ kartavyaḥ/
185.033. sarvamanityatayā grastaṃ kartavyam, gāthādvayaṃ ca lekhayitavyam--
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground). It was the practice of the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> to travel from time to time through the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, the divine realm, and the human realm. Whatever sufferings he saw — the tearing, rending, cutting, and splitting of beings in the hells; the mutual devouring of animals; the hunger and thirst of hungry ghosts; the falling, declining, scattering, and disintegrating of the gods; and the seeking and failing of humans — having seen these, he would return to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and announce them to the four assemblies. Whoever had a companion or pupil practicing the holy life without delight would bring that person to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, who would properly instruct and admonish him. Thus, one after another, those who were properly instructed and admonished by the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> practiced the holy life with delight and attained higher distinction. At that time, the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> dwelt surrounded by the four assemblies — monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are knowers who ask. The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> asked the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. He said: 'Venerable Sir, it is the practice of the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> to travel from time to time through the hells, the animal realm, the realm of hungry ghosts, the divine realm, and the human realm. Whatever sufferings he sees — the tearing, rending, cutting, and splitting of beings in the hells; the mutual devouring of animals; the hunger and thirst of hungry ghosts; the falling, declining, scattering, and disintegrating of the gods; and the seeking and failing of humans — having seen these, he returns to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and announces them to the four assemblies. Whoever has a companion or pupil practicing the holy life without delight brings that person to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, who properly instructs and admonishes him. Thus, one after another, those who are properly instructed and admonished by the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> practice the holy life with delight and attain higher distinction. This, Venerable Sir, is the reason and the cause why the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> dwells surrounded by the four assemblies of monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers.' 'Not everywhere, <s>Ānanda</s>, will there be a monk like <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> or one comparable to <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Therefore, a five-sectored wheel should be painted in the gate-chamber.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said that a five-sectored wheel should be painted in the gate-chamber. The monks did not know what kind should be painted. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Five destinies should be depicted: the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, gods, and humans. There, at the bottom, the hells should be depicted, with animals and hungry ghosts; above, gods and humans. The four continents should be depicted: <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, <s>Aparagodānīya</s>, <s>Uttarakuru</s>, and <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. In the center, passion, hatred, and delusion should be depicted — passion in the form of a pigeon, hatred in the form of a serpent, delusion in the form of a pig. Images of the <s>Buddha</s> should be made pointing toward the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> circle. Beings who are born spontaneously should be depicted as falling and being reborn by the mechanism of a water-wheel. Around the periphery, the twelve-linked chain of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) should be depicted, in both forward and reverse order. The whole should be depicted as seized by impermanence, and two verses should be inscribed—'

body.text:
186.001. <186>ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
186.002. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//1//
body.translated_text: 'Strive forth! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>! Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!' //1//

body.text:
186.003. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
186.004. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//2//iti/
186.005. uktaṃ bhagavatā dvārakoṣṭhake pañcagaṇḍakaṃ cakraṃ kārayitavyamiti bhikṣubhiḥ kāritam/
186.006. brāhmaṇagṛhapataya āgatya pṛcchanti--ārya, kimidaṃ likhitamiti? te kathayanti--bhadramukhāḥ, vayamapi na jānīma iti/
186.007. bhagavānāha--dvārakoṣṭhake bhikṣuruddeṣṭavyo ya āgatāgatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ darśayati/
186.008. uktaṃ bhagavatā bhikṣuruddeṣṭavya iti/
186.008. te aviśeṣeṇoddiśanti bālānapi mūḍhānapi avyaktānapi akuśalānapi/
186.009. te ātmanā na jānate, kutaḥ punarāgatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ darśayiṣyanti? bhagavānāha--pratibalo bhikṣuruddeṣṭavya iti//
body.translated_text: 'He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall make an end of suffering.' //2// The <s>Bhagavān</s> said that a five-sectored wheel should be painted in the gate-chamber, and the monks had it painted. <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders came and asked: 'Venerable ones, what is this that has been painted?'
