They replied: 'Good sirs, we ourselves do not know.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A monk should be appointed at the gate-chamber who shows it to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who come.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said that a monk should be appointed. They appointed indiscriminately — even the foolish, the confused, the inarticulate, and the unskilled. Those monks themselves did not understand it; how then would they explain it to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who came? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'A capable monk should be appointed.'

body.text:
186.011. rājagṛhe 'nyatamo gṛhapatiḥ prativasati/
186.011. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
186.012. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
186.012. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ/
186.013. tasya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasān vistareṇa jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā kulasadṛśaṃ nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
186.014. sa patnīmāmantrayate--bhadre, jāto 'smākam ṛṇaharo dhanaharaḥ/
186.014. tadgacchāmi, paṇyamādāya mahāsamudramavatarāmīti/
186.015. sā kathayati--āryaputra, evaṃ kuruṣveti/
186.015. sa suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānāmantrayitvā antarjanaṃ ca samāśvāsya mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyamādāya divasatithimuhūrtena mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
186.017. tatraiva ca nidhanamupayātaḥ/
186.017. tasya patnyā sa dārako jñātibalena hastabalena pālitaḥ poṣitaḥ saṃvardhito lipyāmupanyasto lipyakṣareṣu ca kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ/
186.018. sa vayaskareṇa sārdhaṃ veṇuvanaṃ gato vihāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ paśyati dvārakoṣṭhake pañcagaṇḍakaṃ cakramabhilikhitam/
186.019. sa pṛcchati--ārya, kimidamabhilikhitamiti? bhikṣuḥ kathayati--bhadramukha, etāḥ pañca gatayo narakāstiryañcaḥ pretā devā manuṣyāśca/
186.021. ārya, kimebhiḥ karma kṛtam yenaivaṃvidhāni duḥkhāni praryanubhavantīti? sa kathayati--ete prāṇātipātikā adattādāyikāḥ kāmamithyācārikā mṛṣāvādikāḥ paiśunikāḥ pāruṣikāḥ saṃbhinnapralāpikā abhidhyālavo vyāpannacittā mithyādṛṣṭikāḥ/
186.024. tadebhirete daśākuśalāḥ karmapathā atyarthamāsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, yena evaṃvidhāni duḥkhānyutpāṭānupāṭacchedanabhedanādīni pratyanubhavanti/
186.025. ārya, gatametat/
186.026. ebhiranyaiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena evaṃvidhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti? duḥkhānyanyonyabhakṣaṇādīni pratyanubhavanti/
186.028. ārya, etadapi gatam/
186.028. ebhiranyaiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena evaṃvidhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti? bhadramukha, ete 'pi matsariṇa āsan kuṭukuñcakā āgṛhītapariṣkārāḥ/
186.030. tattena mātsaryeṇāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena evaṃvidhāni duḥkhāni kṣuttṛṣādīni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti/
186.031. ārya, etadapi gatam/
186.031. ebhiranyaiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena evaṃvidhāni sukhāni pratyanubhavanti? bhadramukha, ete prāṇātipātāt prativiratā adattādānāt <187>kāmamithyācārānmṛṣāvādāt paiśunyāt pāruṣyāt saṃbhinnapralāpādanabhidhyāpannacittāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ/
body.translated_text: In <s>Rājagṛha</s> there dwelt a certain householder. He had brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, in the course of time a son was born to him. On the twenty-first day after the birth, having performed the birth celebration in full, a name befitting the family was given. He said to his wife: 'Dear one, an heir has been born to us, one who will repay our debts and bring wealth. So let me go, take merchandise, and descend into the great ocean.' She said: 'Noble husband, do so.' Having taken leave of his friends, relatives, and kinsmen, and having consoled the household, he took merchandise suitable for an ocean voyage and, on an auspicious day and hour, descended into the great ocean. Right there he met his death. His wife raised that boy with the support of relatives and by her own strength — she nourished him, brought him up, and had him placed in a writing school, where he became skilled in letters and script. He went with a companion to the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, entered the monastery, and saw the five-sectored wheel painted in the gate-chamber. He asked: 'Venerable one, what is this that has been painted?' The monk said: 'Good sir, these are the five destinies: the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, gods, and humans.' 'Venerable one, what deeds did these beings do that they experience such sufferings?' He said: 'These are killers of living beings, takers of what is not given, practitioners of sexual misconduct, speakers of falsehood, slanderers, speakers of harsh words, speakers of idle chatter, the covetous, the malicious, and holders of wrong views. By them, these ten unwholesome courses of action were exceedingly cultivated, developed, and made much of — by which they experience such sufferings as tearing, rending, cutting, and splitting.' 'Venerable one, that is understood. What deeds did these others do that they experience such sufferings?' 'They experience sufferings of mutual devouring.' 'Venerable one, that too is understood. What deeds did these others do that they experience such sufferings?' 'Good sir, these too were miserly, mean, with clenched possessions. By that miserliness, cultivated, developed, and made much of, they experience such sufferings as hunger, thirst, and the like.' 'Venerable one, that too is understood. What deeds did these others do that they experience such happiness?' 'Good sir, these abstained from killing living beings, from taking what is not given, from sexual misconduct, from false speech, from slander, from harsh speech, from idle chatter; they were free from covetousness, free from malice, and possessed right views.'

body.text:
187.002. tadebhirete daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā atyarthamāsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, yena evaṃvidhāni divyastrīlalitavimānodyānasukhāni pratyanubhavanti/
187.003. ārya, etadapi gatam/
187.004. ebhiranyaiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam yena sukhāni pratyanubhavanti? bhadramukha, ebhirapi daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāstanutarā mṛdutarāścāsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtāḥ, yena evaṃvidhāni hastyaśvarathānnapānaśayanāsanastrīlalitodyānasukhāni pratyanubhavanti/
187.006. ārya, āsāṃ pañcānāṃ gatīnām yā etāstisro gatayo narakāstiryañcaḥ pretāśca, etā mahyaṃ na rocante/
187.007. ye tu ete devā manuṣyāśca ete rocete/
187.008. tatkathamete daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ samādāya vartayitavyāh? bhadramukha, svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya saced dṛṣṭa eva dharme ājñāmārāgayiṣyasi, eṣa eva te 'nto duḥkhasya/
187.010. atha sāvaśeṣasamyojanaḥ kālaṃ kariṣyasi, deveṣūpapatsyase/
187.010. uktaṃ hi bhagavatā--pañcānuśaṃsān samanupaśyatā piṇḍatenālameva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum/
187.011. katamāni pañca? āveṇikā ime svārthā anuprāpto bhaviṣyāmīti saṃpaśyatā piṇḍatenālameva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum/
187.012. yeṣāmahaṃ dāsaḥ preṣyo nirdeśyo bhujiṣyo nayena kāmaṃgamaḥ, teṣāṃ pūjyaśca bhaviṣyāmi praśaṃsyaśceti saṃpaśyatā piṇḍatena alameva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum/
187.014. anuttaram yogakṣemaṃ nirvāṇamanuprāpsyāmīti saṃpaśyatā piṇḍatena alameva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum/
187.015. anuttaraṃ vā yogakṣemaṃ nirvāṇamanuprāpnuvato 'nāpattikasya sato deeveṣūpapattirbhaviṣyatīti saṃpaśyatā piṇḍatena alameva pravrajyādhimuktena bhavitum/
187.016. anekaparyāyeṇa pravrajyā varṇitā buddhaiśca buddhaśrāvakaiśca/
187.017. ārya, śobhanam/
187.017. kiṃ tatra pravrajyāyāṃ kriyate? bhadramukha, yāvajjīvaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caryate/
187.018. ārya, na śakyametat/
187.018. anyo 'sti upāyah? bhadramukha, asti, upāsako bhava/
187.019. ārya, kiṃ tatra kriyate? bhadraṃkha, yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇātipātāt prativiratiḥ saṃrakṣyā, adattādānāt kāmamithyācārāt surāmaireyamadyapramādasthānāt prativiratiḥ saṃrakṣyā/
187.021. ārya, etadapi na śakyate/
187.021. anyamupāyaṃ kathayeti/
187.021. bhadramukha, buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojaya/
187.022. ārya, kiyadbhiḥ kārṣāpaṇairbuddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho bhojyate? bhadramukha, pañcabhiḥ kārṣāpaṇaśataiḥ/
187.023. ārya, śakyametat/
187.023. sa tasya pādabhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ/
187.023. yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
187.024. upasaṃkramya mātaramidamavocat--amba, adyāhaṃ veṇuvanaṃ gataḥ/
187.024. tatra mayā dvārakoṣṭhake pañcagaṇḍakaṃ cakramabhilikhitaṃ dṛṣṭam/
187.025. tatra pañca gatayo narakāstiryañcaḥ pretā devā manuṣyāśca/
187.026. tatra nārakā utpāṭanupāṭanacchedabhedanādīni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti/
187.027. tiryañcaścānyonyabhakṣaṇādīni/
187.027. pretāḥ kṣuttṛṣādīni/
187.027. devā divyastrīlalitodyānavimānasukhāni pratyanubhavanti/
187.028. manuṣyā hastyaśvarathānnapānaśayanāsanastrīlalitodyānāni pratyanubhavanti/
187.028. āsāṃ mama tisro gatayo nābhipretāḥ, dve abhiprete/
187.029. tatkimicchasi tvaṃ māṃ deveṣūpapadyamānam? putra, sarvasattvānicchāmi deveṣūpapadyamānān prāgeva tvām/
187.030. amba, yadyevam, prayaccha pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni/
187.031. buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayāmi/
187.031. putra, mayā tvaṃ jñātibalena hastabalena cāpyāyitaḥ poṣitaḥ saṃvardhitaḥ/
187.032. kuto me pañcānāṃ kārṣāpaṇaśatānāṃ vibhavah? amba, yadi <188>nāsti, bhṛtikayā karma karomi/
body.translated_text:
187.002. 'By these ones, these ten wholesome paths of action were exceedingly cultivated, developed, and made abundant, by which they experience such pleasures of divine women, sport, celestial palaces, and gardens.'
187.003. 'Venerable sir, that too is understood.
187.004. What deed did these others perform, by which they experience pleasures?' 'Good sir, by these too the ten wholesome paths of action were cultivated, developed, and made abundant, but to a lesser and gentler degree, by which they experience such pleasures of elephants, horses, chariots, food, drink, lodging, women, sport, and gardens.'
187.006. 'Venerable sir, of these five destinies, the three destinies of the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts — these do not please me.
187.007. But those of the gods and humans — these please me.
187.008. How then should these ten wholesome paths of action be undertaken and practiced?' 'Good sir, having gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), if you attain perfect knowledge in this very life, this itself will be the end of your suffering.
187.010. But if you die with fetters remaining, you will be reborn among the gods.
187.010. For the Blessed One has said: "Seeing five benefits, it is enough to be inclined toward going forth even for a morsel of food."
187.011. What are the five? Seeing that "I shall attain these unique personal goals" — it is enough to be inclined toward going forth even for a morsel of food.
187.012. Seeing that "Those whose slave, servant, one to be commanded, one to be enjoyed, one to go at their will I am — I shall become worthy of their reverence and praise" — it is enough to be inclined toward going forth even for a morsel of food.
187.014. Seeing that "I shall attain the unsurpassed security from bondage, <s>Nirvāṇa</s>" — it is enough to be inclined toward going forth even for a morsel of food.
187.015. Seeing that "If I do not attain the unsurpassed security from bondage, <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, being without offense, there will be rebirth among the gods" — it is enough to be inclined toward going forth even for a morsel of food.
187.016. In many ways, going forth has been praised by <s>Buddhas</s> and disciples of <s>Buddhas</s>.'
187.017. 'Venerable sir, excellent.
187.017. What is done in that going forth?' 'Good sir, the holy life of celibacy is practiced for as long as one lives.'
187.018. 'Venerable sir, I am not able to do that.
187.018. Is there another way?' 'Good sir, there is — become a lay follower.'
187.019. 'Venerable sir, what is done therein?' 'Good sir, for as long as one lives, abstinence from taking life is to be maintained, abstinence from taking what is not given, from sexual misconduct, and from intoxicants which are the occasion for heedlessness is to be maintained.'
187.021. 'Venerable sir, that too I am not able to do.
187.021. Tell me another way.'
187.021. 'Good sir, feed the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'
187.022. 'Venerable sir, how many <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins) does it take to feed the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>?' 'Good sir, five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.'
187.023. 'Venerable sir, that I can do.'
187.023. Having paid obeisance at his feet, he departed.
187.023. He went to his own home.
187.024. Having approached, he said to his mother: 'Mother, today I went to the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove).
187.024. There I saw a wheel with five sections painted at the gate-chamber.
187.025. In it are five destinies: hells, animals, hungry ghosts, gods, and humans.
187.026. Among them, hell-beings experience sufferings such as tearing, ripping, cutting, and splitting.
187.027. Animals experience mutual devouring and the like.
187.027. Hungry ghosts experience hunger, thirst, and the like.
187.027. Gods experience divine pleasures of women, sport, gardens, and celestial palaces.
187.028. Humans experience elephants, horses, chariots, food, drink, lodging, women, sport, and gardens.
187.028. Of these, three destinies are not desired by me; two are desired.
187.029. So do you wish for me to be reborn among the gods?' 'Son, I wish for all beings to be reborn among the gods, how much more so for you.'
187.030. 'Mother, if so, give me five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
187.031. I will feed the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'
187.031. 'Son, I have raised, nourished, and brought you up by the strength of my relatives and the strength of my own hands.
187.032. Where do I have the resources for five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>?' 'Mother, if <188> you do not have them, I shall work for wages.'

body.text:
188.001. putra, tvaṃ sukumāraḥ/
188.001. na śakyasi bhṛtikayā karma kartum/
188.002. amba gacchāmi, śakyāmi/
188.002. putra, yadi śakyo 'si, gaccha/
188.002. sa tayā anujñāto bhṛtakavīthīṃ gatvā avasthitaḥ/
188.003. brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'nyān bhṛtakapuruṣān gṛhṇanti, taṃ na kaścit pṛcchati/
188.004. sa tatra divasamatināmya vikāle gṛhaṃ gataḥ/
188.004. sa mātrā pṛṣṭah--putra, kṛtaṃ te bhṛtikayā karma? amba, kiṃ karomi? na māṃ kaścit pṛcchati/
188.005. putra, na evaṃvidhā bhṛtakapuruṣā bhavanti/
188.005. putra, sphaṭitaparuṣā rūkṣakeśā malinavastranivasanāḥ/
188.006. yadyavaśyaṃ tvayā bhṛtikayā karma kartavyam, īdṛśaṃ veṣamāsthāya bhṛtakavīthīṃ gatvā tiṣṭha/
188.007. amba, śobhanam/
188.007. evaṃ karomi/
188.007. so 'parasmin divase tādṛśaṃ veṣamāsthāya bhṛtakavīthīṃ gatvā avasthitaḥ/
188.008. yāvadanyatarasya gṛhapatergṛhamuttiṣṭhate/
188.009. sa bhṛtakānāmarthe vīthīṃ gataḥ/
188.009. tena taṃ pratyākhyāya anye bhṛtakapuruṣā gṛhītāḥ/
188.010. sa kathayati--gṛhapate, ahamapi bhṛtikayā karma karomīti/
188.010. gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--putra, tvaṃ sukumāraḥ, na śakṣyasi bhṛtikayā karma kartum/
188.011. tāt, kiṃ tvaṃ pūrvaṃ bhṛtiṃ dadāsi, āhosvit paścāt?/
188.012. tāt, adya tātvat karma karomi/
188.012. yadi toṣayiṣyāmi, dāsyasi bhṛtimiti/
188.013. sa saṃlakṣayati--śobhanameṣa kathayati/
188.013. adya tāvat jijñāsyāmi yadi śakṣyati karma kartum, dāsyāmi/
188.014. na śakṣyati, na dāsyāmīti viditvā kathayati--putra āgaccha, gacchāma iti/
188.015. sa tena gṛhaṃ nītaḥ/
188.015. te 'nyabhṛtakāḥ śāṭhyena karma kurvanti/
188.015. sa tvaritatvaritaṃ karma karoti/
188.016. tāṃśca bhṛtakān samanuśāsti/
188.016. vayaṃ tāvat pūrvakeṇa duścaritena daridragṛheṣūpapannāḥ/
188.017. tadyadi śāṭhyena karma kariṣyāmaḥ, itaścyutānāṃ kā gatibhaviṣyati? te kathayanti--bhāgineya, tvaṃ navadāntaḥ/
188.018. sthānametadvidyate yadasmākaṃ pṛṣṭhato gamiṣyasi/
188.018. āgaccha paśyāmaḥ/
188.019. sa lokākhyāyikāyāṃ kuśalaḥ/
188.019. teṃs teṣāṃ tādṛśī lokākhyānakathā prastutā, yāṃ śrutvā te bhṛtakapuruṣā ākṣiptāḥ/
188.020. tasyātisvareṇa gacchato 'nupadaṃ gacchanti, mā lokākhyāyikāṃ na śroṣyāma iti/
188.021. tasmin divase tairbhṛtakapuruṣaistaddviguṇaṃ karma kṛtam/
188.022. so 'dhiṣṭhāyakapuruṣaṃ pṛcchati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ tvayā apare bhṛtakā gṛhītāh? ārya, na gṛhītāḥ/
188.023. atha kasmādadya dviguṇaṃ karma kṛtam? tena yathāvṛttamārocitam/
188.024. śrutvā gṛhapatistasya dārakasya dviguṇāṃ bhṛtiṃ dātumārabdhaḥ/
188.025. sa kathayati--tāt, kiṃ dvidaivasikāṃ bhṛtiṃ dadāsīti? sa kathayati--putra, na dvidaivasikāṃ dadāmi, api tu prasanno 'haṃ prasannādhikāraṃ karomīti/
188.026. sa kathayati--tāt, yadi tvaṃ mamābhiprasannaḥ, yāvat tava gṛhe karma kartavyaṃ tāvat tavaiva haste tiṣṭhatu/
188.028. putra evaṃ bhavatu/
188.028. yadā tasya gṛhapatestadgṛhaṃ parisamāptam, tadā asau dārako bhṛtiṃ gaṇayitumārabdho yāvat pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni na paripūryante/
188.029. sa roditumārabdhaḥ/
188.029. sa gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--putra, kiṃ rodiṣi? māsi mayā kiṃcit vyaṃsitaḥ/
188.030. tāt, mahātmā tvam, kiṃ māṃ vyaṃsayiṣyasi? api tu ahameva mandabhāgyaḥ/
188.031. mayā pañcānāṃ kārṣāpaṇaśatānāmarthāya bhṛtikayā karma prārabdhaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmi, tato deveṣūpapatsyāmīti/
188.032. tāni <189>na paripūrṇāni/
body.translated_text:
188.001. 'Son, you are delicate.
188.001. You will not be able to work for wages.'
188.002. 'Mother, I shall go; I am able.'
188.002. 'Son, if you are able, go.'
188.002. Permitted by her, he went to the hired-workers' street and stood there.
188.003. <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders hired other laborers, but no one asked him.
188.004. He spent the day there and went home in the evening.
188.004. His mother asked him: 'Son, did you do wage-work?' 'Mother, what can I do? No one asked me.'
188.005. 'Son, hired workers are not like this.
188.005. Son, they are rough-skinned, with unkempt hair, wearing dirty clothes.
188.006. If you must work for wages, adopt such an appearance and go stand at the hired-workers' street.'
188.007. 'Mother, very well.
188.007. I shall do so.'
188.007. The next day, he adopted such an appearance and went to the hired-workers' street and stood there.
188.008. Then a certain householder's house was being built.
188.009. He went to the street in search of laborers.
188.009. Having passed that boy over, he hired other laborers.
188.010. The boy said: 'Householder, I too will work for wages.'
188.010. The householder said: 'Son, you are delicate; you will not be able to do wage-work.'
188.011. 'Sir, will you pay the wages first, or afterward?'
188.012. 'Sir, let me first do the work today.
188.012. If I satisfy you, you will give the wages.'
188.013. He thought: 'This boy speaks well.
188.013. Today I shall test him — if he can do the work, I will pay him.
188.014. If he cannot, I will not.' Having thus resolved, he said: 'Son, come, let us go.'
188.015. He was taken to the house.
188.015. The other laborers worked deceitfully.
188.015. But he worked with great haste.
188.016. And he admonished those laborers:
188.016. 'We have been reborn in poor households because of our past misdeeds.
188.017. If we work deceitfully now, when we fall from here, what destiny will await us?' They said: 'Nephew, you are newly tamed.
188.018. It is quite possible that you will end up following behind us.
188.018. Come, let us see.'
188.019. He was skilled in popular tales.
188.019. He began to tell them such popular tales that, upon hearing them, those laborers were captivated.
188.020. As he walked swiftly, they followed right behind him, lest they miss the popular tales.
188.021. On that day, those laborers did double the work.
188.022. The overseer asked the foreman: 'Good man, did you hire additional laborers?' 'Sir, I did not.'
188.023. 'Then why has double the work been done today?' He told him what had happened.
188.024. Hearing this, the householder began to give double wages to that boy.
188.025. He said: 'Sir, are you giving me two days' wages?' He said: 'Son, I am not giving two days' wages; rather, I am pleased, and I am making a gift out of my pleasure.'
188.026. He said: 'Sir, if you are pleased with me, let whatever work needs to be done in your house remain in my hands for as long as it takes.'
188.028. 'Son, so be it.'
188.028. When that householder's building was finished, the boy began to count his wages, but five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> were not complete.
188.029. He began to weep.
188.029. The householder said: 'Son, why do you weep? Have I cheated you of something?'
188.030. 'Sir, you are a great-souled man; why would you cheat me? Rather, I myself am unlucky.
188.031. I began working for wages for the purpose of five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, to feed the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, and then be reborn among the gods.
188.032. Those <189> are not complete.'

body.text:
189.001. punarapi mayā anyatra bhṛtikayā karma kartavyamiti/
189.001. sa gṛhapatirbhūyasā mātrayā atiprasannaḥ/
189.002. sa kathayati--putra, yadyevam, ahaṃ pūrayāmi/
189.002. tāt, mā deveṣūpapatsye/
189.002. putra, abhiśraddadhāsi tvaṃ bhagavatah? tāt abhiśraddadhe/
189.003. putra gaccha, bhagavantaṃ pṛccha/
189.003. yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
189.004. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
189.004. sa gṛhapatiputro bhagavantamidamavocat--bhagavan, mayā pañcānāṃ kārṣāpaṇaśatānāmarthāya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmītyamukasya gṛhapaterbhṛtikayā karma kṛtam/
189.006. tāni mama na paripūrṇāni/
189.007. sa gṛhapatiḥ paripūrayati/
189.007. bhagavan kim? āha--vatsa gṛhāṇa, śrāddhaḥ sa gṛhapatiḥ/
189.007. bhagavan, mā deveṣu nopapatsye? vatsa upapatsyase, gṛhāṇa/
189.008. sa parituṣṭo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yena sa gṛhapatistenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
189.009. upasaṃkramya gṛhapaterantikāt pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni gṛhītvā mātuḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
189.010. kathayati--amba, etāni pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni/
189.011. bhaktaṃ sajjīkuru/
189.011. buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti/
189.011. sā kathayati--putra, na mama bhāṇḍopaskaro na śayanāsanam/
189.012. sa eva gṛhapatirvistīrṇabhāṇḍopaskaraḥ śrāddhaśca/
189.013. tameva gatvā prārthaya/
189.013. śaknotyasau saṃpādayitumiti/
189.013. sa tasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ śiraḥpraṇāmaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--tvayaiva etāni pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni dattāani/
189.014. asmākaṃ gṛhe na bhāṇḍopaskaro nāpi śayanāsanam/
189.015. tadarhasi mamānukampayā bhaktaṃ sajjīkartum/
189.015. ahamāgatya svahastena buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmīti/
189.016. gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati--mamedaṃ gṛhamacirotthitaṃ buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena paribhuktaṃ bhaviṣyati, pratijāgarmi/
189.017. iti viditvā kathayati--putra, śobhanam/
189.018. sthāpayitvā kārṣāpaṇān gaccha, śvo buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamupanimantraya/
189.018. ahamāhāraṃ sajjīkaromīti/
189.019. sa saṃjātasaumanasyaḥ śiraḥpraṇāmaṃ kṛtvā prakrānto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
189.020. upasaṃkramya vṛddhānte sthitvā kathayati--so 'haṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamupanimantrayāmīti/
189.021. adhivāsayati bhagavāṃstasya gṛhapatiputrasya tūṣṇībhāvena/
189.021. atha sa gṛhapatiputro bhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
189.001. 'Moreover, I must still do work elsewhere for hire.'
189.001. That householder was greatly delighted beyond measure.
189.002. He said: 'Son, if so, I shall make up the amount.
189.002. Father, will I not be reborn among the gods?'
189.002. 'Son, do you have faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 'Father, I do have faith.'
189.003. 'Son, go and ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
189.003. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
189.004. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side.
189.004. That householder's son said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, I have done work for hire for a certain householder for the purpose of five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, intending to feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of disciples.
189.006. Those have not been fully earned by me.
189.007. That householder is completing the amount.
189.007. <s>Bhagavān</s>, what should I do?' He said: 'My child, accept them; that householder is a man of faith.'
189.007. '<s>Bhagavān</s>, will I not fail to be reborn among the gods?' 'My child, you will be reborn; accept them.'
189.008. Satisfied, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and, departing from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence, approached that householder.
189.009. Having approached, he received five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> from the householder and went to his mother.
189.010. He said: 'Mother, here are five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
189.011. Prepare the food.
189.011. I shall feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'
189.011. She said: 'Son, I have no cooking utensils or furnishings, nor bedding or seats.
189.012. That very householder is well-equipped with utensils and is a man of faith.
189.013. Go to him and make the request.
189.013. He is able to arrange it.'
189.013. He went to the householder, bowed his head, and said: 'You yourself gave these five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>.
189.014. In our house there are no cooking utensils, nor any bedding or seats.
189.015. Therefore, please, out of compassion for me, prepare the food.
189.015. I shall come and with my own hands feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'
189.016. The householder reflected: 'My house, newly established, will be enjoyed by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. I am vigilant in this.'
189.017. Having realized this, he said: 'Son, excellent.
189.018. Leave the <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> and go; tomorrow invite the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.
189.018. I shall prepare the food.'
189.019. Overjoyed, he bowed his head and departed, and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
189.020. Having approached, standing to one side, he said: 'I hereby invite the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.'
189.021. The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the householder's son by his silence.
189.021. Then that householder's son, understanding the <s>Bhagavān's</s> consent by his silence, departed from the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence.

body.text:
189.023. tenāpi gṛhapatinā tāmeva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya gṛhaṃ saṃmārjitam/
189.024. sukumārī gomayakārṣī dattā, āsanaprajñaptiḥ kāritā, udakamaṇayaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ/
189.025. tenāpi gṛhapatiputreṇa gatvā bhagavata ārocitam--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti/
189.026. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena tasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
189.027. ṣaḍvargīyāḥ pṛcchanti--kenāayaṃ buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgha upanimantrita iti? apare kathayanti--amukena gṛhapatiputreṇeti/
189.029. te parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurvanti--nandopananda, bhṛtakapuruṣaḥ saḥ/
189.029. kimasau dāsyati? gacchāma kulopakagṛheṣu gatvā purobhaktakāṃ karma iti/
189.030. te kulopakagṛhāṇyupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
189.030. tairuktāh--ārya, purobhaktakāṃ kuruteti/
189.031. te kathayanti--evaṃ kurma iti/
189.031. taiḥ purobhaktakā kṛtā/
189.031. bhagavāṃstasya gṛhapater niveśane purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
189.032. ṣaḍvargīyā api purobhaktakāṃ kṛtvā <190>saṃghamadhye niṣaṇṇaḥ/
body.translated_text:
189.023. That householder, on that very night, having gathered pure and excellent food, both hard and soft, rose early in the morning; the house was swept and cleaned.
189.024. Soft cowdung was applied, seats were arranged, and water-jars were set in place.
189.025. That householder's son too, having gone, announced to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the food is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come when he deems it the proper time.'
189.026. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks and preceded by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, approached the residence of that householder.
189.027. The Group of Six monks asked: 'By whom has this <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> been invited?' Others said: 'By such-and-such a householder's son.'
189.029. They conferred with one another: '<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, he is a hired laborer.
189.029. What will he give? Let us go to the houses of our patron families and take a pre-meal snack.'
189.030. They approached the houses of their patron families.
189.030. They said to them: 'Venerable ones, prepare a pre-meal snack for us.'
189.031. They said: 'We shall do so.'
189.031. They prepared the pre-meal snack for them.
189.031. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the householder's residence, sat upon the seat prepared for him before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.
189.032. The Group of Six monks also, having eaten their pre-meal snack, sat down in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text:
190.001. atha sa gṛhapatipurtaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhijanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
190.002. satatapariveṣaṇaṃ kurvāṇaḥ paśyti ṣaḍvargīyān na satkṛtya parimuñjānān/
190.003. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhagavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ bhagavataḥ purastāt sthitvā kathayati--bhagavan, kaiścidatrāryakair na satkṛtya paribhuktamāhāram/
190.005. deveṣu nopapatsye iti? bhagavānāha--vatsa, śayanāsanaparibhogena tāvat tvaṃ deveṣūpapadyethāḥ prāgevānnapānaparibhogeneti/
190.006. atha bhagavāṃstaṃ gṛhapatiputraṃ ca dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
190.001. Then that householder's son, knowing that the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent food, both hard and soft.
190.002. While serving continuously, he noticed the Group of Six monks eating without respect or appreciation.
190.003. Having seen this, and knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished his meal and his bowl had been removed, he stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, certain noble ones here have eaten the food without showing respect.
190.005. Will I not be reborn among the gods?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'My child, by the merit of providing lodging and bedding alone you would be reborn among the gods — how much more so by providing food and drink.'
190.006. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and delighted that householder's son with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text:
190.008. atrāntare pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni mahāsamudrāt saṃsiddhayānapātrāṇni rājagṛhamanuprāptāni/
190.009. rājagṛhe ca parva pratyupasthitamiti na kiṃcit krayeṇāpi labhyate/
190.009. tatraiko vaṇigbhikṣugocarikaḥ/
190.010. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, āgamayata kasyādya gṛhe buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhaktam, tatrāvaśyaṃ kiṃcidutsadanadharmakaṃ bhavatīti/
190.011. te śravaṇaparamparayā cānveṣamāṇāstasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
190.012. kathayanti--gṛhapate, tavādya buddhapramukhena bhikṣusaṃghena bhukte iha parva pratyupasthitamiti na kiṃcit krayeṇāpi labhyate/
190.013. yadi kiṃcidutsadanadharmakamasti, mūlyena dīyatāmiti/
190.014. na mamaitadbhaktam, api tu tasyaitadgṛhapatiputrasya bhaktam/
190.014. enam yācadhvamiti/
190.014. te tasya sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayanti--gṛhapatiputra, dīyatāmasmākaṃ bhuktaśeṣam yadasti/
190.015. mūlyaṃ prayacchāma iti/
190.016. sa kathayati--nāhaṃ mūlyenānuprayacchāmi/
190.016. api tu evameva prayacchāmīti/
190.016. te tenānnapānena saṃtarpitā gṛhapatergatvā kathayanti--tasya te gṛhapate lābhāḥ sulabdhā yasya te niveśane buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'nnapānena saṃtarpitaḥ, imāni ca pañca vaṇikśatānīti/
190.018. sa kathayati--anena gṛhapatiputreṇa lābhāḥ sulabdhāḥ/
190.019. anena buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'nnapānena saṃtarpito na mayeti/
190.020. te pṛcchanti--katarasyāyaṃ gṛhapateḥ putrah? amukasya sārthavāhasya/
190.020. sārthavāhaḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, mamaiṣa vayasyaputro bhavati/
190.021. tasya pitā mahāsamudramavatīrṇo 'nayena vyasanamāpannaḥ/
190.021. śakyaṃ bahubhirekaḥ samuddhartum, na tveva ekena bahavaḥ/
190.022. tadayaṃ paṭakaṃ prajñapto yena vo yat parityaktam, so 'smin paṭake 'nuprayacchatviti/
190.023. te pūrvamevābhiprasannāḥ sārthavāhena ca protsāhitā iti tairyathāsambhāvyena maṇimuktādīni ratnāni dattāni/
190.024. mahān rāśiḥ saṃpannaḥ/
190.024. sārthavāhaḥ kathayati--putra, gṛhāṇeti/
190.025. sa kathayati--tāt, na mayā mūlyena dattamiti/
190.025. sārthavāhaḥ kathayati--putra, na vayaṃ tava mūlyaṃ prayachāmaḥ/
190.026. yadi ca mūlyaṃ gaṇyate, ekena ratnenedṛśānāṃ bhaktānāmanekāni śatāni saṃvidyante/
190.027. kiṃ tu vayaṃ tavābhiprasannāḥ prasannādhikāraṃ kurmaḥ, gṛhāṇeti/
190.027. sa kathayati--tāt, mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho bhojito deveṣūpapatsye iti/
190.028. tasmādavaśiṣṭam yuṣmabhyaṃ dattam/
190.029. yadi grahīṣyāmi, sthānametadvidyate yaddeveṣu nopapatsye? sārthavāhah--putra, abhiśraddadhāsi tvaṃ bhagavatah? tāt, abhiśraddadhe/
190.030. gaccha, bhagavantaṃ pṛccha/
190.030. sa yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
190.031. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
190.031. sa gṛhapatiputro bhagavantamidamavocat--bhagavan, mayā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā yadannapānamavaśiṣṭam <191>tadviṇijāṃ dattam/
body.translated_text:
190.008. Meanwhile, about five hundred merchants arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s> from the great ocean with their vessels successfully completed.
190.009. A festival was at hand in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and nothing at all could be obtained even for purchase.
190.009. Among them was a merchant who was familiar with the monks' alms-rounds.
190.010. He said: 'Sirs, wait. Let us find out at whose house today the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has eaten — there will certainly be some surplus food.'
190.011. Following word of mouth, they made inquiries and approached that householder.
190.012. They said: 'Householder, today the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has dined at your place, and here a festival is at hand, so nothing can be obtained even for purchase.
190.013. If there is any surplus food, give it to us for a price.'
190.014. 'This food is not mine; it belongs to that householder's son.
190.014. Ask him.'
190.014. They approached him and said: 'Householder's son, give us the leftover food.
190.015. We shall pay the price.'
190.016. He said: 'I shall not give it for a price.
190.016. Rather, I give it freely.'
190.016. They, having been satisfied with that food and drink, went to the householder and said: 'That is your good fortune, householder, well-gained — that in your residence the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has been satisfied with food and drink, and these five hundred merchants as well.'
190.018. He said: 'The good fortune belongs to that householder's son.
190.019. It was he who satisfied the <s>Saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with food and drink, not I.'
190.020. They asked: 'Whose son is this householder's son?' 'The son of such-and-such a caravan-leader.'
190.020. The caravan-leader said: 'Sirs, this boy is the son of my friend.
190.021. His father descended into the great ocean and met with misfortune through calamity.
190.021. Many can help one, but one cannot help many.
190.022. Therefore, let a cloth be spread out, and whatever each of you wishes to part with, let him place it upon this cloth.'
190.023. They, already favorably disposed and further encouraged by the caravan-leader, gave gems, pearls, and other jewels as was fitting.
190.024. A great heap was accumulated.
190.024. The caravan-leader said: 'Son, accept these.'
190.025. He said: 'Father, I did not give for a price.'
190.025. The caravan-leader said: 'Son, we are not paying you a price.
190.026. If a price were to be reckoned, for a single gem one could purchase many hundreds of such meals.
190.027. Rather, we are favorably disposed toward you and are making a devotional offering; accept them.'
190.027. He said: 'Father, I fed the <s>Saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> so that I would be reborn among the gods.
190.028. Therefore I gave the surplus to you.
190.029. If I accept, is it possible that I will not be reborn among the gods?' The caravan-leader said: 'Son, do you have faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 'Father, I do have faith.'
190.030. 'Go and ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
190.030. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
190.031. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side.
190.031. That householder's son said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, having fed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, whatever food and drink was left over I gave to the merchants.

body.text:
191.001. te mama prasannaḥ prasannādhikāraṃ kurvanti/
191.001. kiṃ kalpate tanmama grahītumāhosvinna kalpata iti? bhagavānāha--yadi prasannāḥ prasannādhikāraṃ kurvanti, gṛhāṇa/
191.002. bhagavan, mā deveṣu notpapatsye? bhagavānāha--vatsa, puṣpametat, phalamanyadbhaviṣyati/
191.003. tena bhagavadvacanābhisampratyayāt parituṣṭena gatvā ratnāni gṛhītāni//
body.translated_text:
191.001. They, being favorably disposed toward me, are making a devotional offering.
191.001. Is it proper for me to accept it, or is it not proper?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If they are favorably disposed and are making a devotional offering, accept it.'
191.002. '<s>Bhagavān</s>, will I not fail to be reborn among the gods?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'My child, this is the flower; the fruit will be something else.'
191.003. He, satisfied by faith in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words, went and accepted the jewels.

body.text:
191.005. atrāntare rājagṛhe 'putraḥ śreṣṭhī kālagataḥ/
191.005. tato rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ saṃnipatya saṃjalpaṃ kurvanti--bhavantaḥ, śreṣṭhī kālagataḥ/
191.006. kaṃ śreṣṭhinamabhiṣañcāma iti? tatraike kathayanti--yaḥ puṇyamaheśākhya iti/
191.007. apare kathayanti--kathamasmābhirjñātavyamiti? te kathayanti--nānāvarṇāni bījāni pakkakumbhe prakṣipāmaḥ, ya ekavarṇānyuddhariṣyati, taṃ śreṣṭhinamabhiṣiñcāma iti/
191.009. tair nānāvarṇāni bījāni pakkakumbhe prakṣiptāni/
191.009. ārocitaṃ ca--bhavantaḥ, ya ekavarṇāni bījāni etasmāt kumbhāduddharet, sa śreṣṭhyabhiṣicyate/
191.010. yasya vaḥ śreṣṭhitvamabhipretaṃ ca, uddharatu iti/
191.011. ta uddhartumārabdhāḥ/
191.011. sarvair nānāvarṇānyuddhṛtāni/
191.011. tena tu gṛhapatiputreṇaikavarṇānyuddhṛtāni\
191.012. paurajānapadāḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ/
191.012. sarva enaṃ śreṣṭhinamabhiṣiñcāmaḥ/
191.013. tatraike kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ bhṛtakapuruṣaḥ/
191.013. kathamenaṃ śreṣṭhinamabhiṣiñcāma iti? apare kathayanti--punarapi tāvat jijñāsāmaḥ/
191.014. tena yāvat trirapyekavarṇānyuddhṛtāni/
191.014. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, manuṣyakā apyasya sākṣepamanuprayacchanti/
191.015. āgacchata, enamevābhiṣiñcāma iti/
191.016. sa taiḥ śreṣṭhī abhiṣiktaḥ/
191.016. sa gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati--yadapyanena mama bhṛtikayā karma kṛtam, tathāpyayaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ sattvaḥ/
191.017. saṃgrahosya kartavya iti/
191.017. tena tasya sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā duhitā bhāryārthaṃ dattā/
191.018. tacca gṛham, prabhūtaṃ svāpateyam/
191.018. sahasaivaṃ bhogairabhyudgata iti tasya sahasodgato gṛhapatiḥ sahasodgato gṛhapatiriti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text:
191.005. Meanwhile, the childless guild-master of <s>Rājagṛha</s> died.
191.005. Then the citizens residing in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having assembled, deliberated: 'Sirs, the guild-master has died.
191.006. Whom shall we install as guild-master?' Some among them said: 'Whoever is renowned for the greatness of his merit.'
191.007. Others said: 'How shall we determine this?' They said: 'Let us place seeds of various colors in a baked pot; whoever draws out seeds of a single color, him we shall install as guild-master.'
191.009. They placed seeds of various colors in a baked pot.
191.009. And it was announced: 'Sirs, whoever draws out seeds of a single color from this pot shall be installed as guild-master.
191.010. Whoever among you desires the position of guild-master, let him draw.'
191.011. They began to draw.
191.011. All drew out seeds of mixed colors.
191.011. But that householder's son drew out seeds of a single color.
191.012. The townspeople and countryfolk said: 'Sirs, this one is renowned for the greatness of his merit.
191.012. Let us all install him as guild-master.'
191.013. Some among them said: 'Sirs, this man is a hired servant.
191.013. How can we install him as guild-master?' Others said: 'Let us test him once more.'
191.014. Three times he drew out seeds of a single color.
191.014. They said: 'Sirs, even the people themselves are giving evidence on his behalf.
191.015. Come, let us install this very one.'
191.016. He was installed by them as guild-master.
191.016. That householder reflected: 'Although he did work for me as a hired servant, nevertheless this being is renowned for the greatness of his merit.
191.017. He should be supported.'
191.017. He gave him his daughter, adorned with all ornaments, as a wife.
191.018. And the house, and abundant wealth.
191.018. Since he had suddenly risen to prosperity in this way, the designation 'Householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>' ('Suddenly Risen') became established for him.

body.text:
191.020. sa saṃlakṣayati--yā kācidasmākaṃ śrīsaubhāgyasampat, sarvāsau buddhaṃ bhagavantamāgamya/
191.021. yannvahaṃ punarapi buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamantargṛhe upanimantrya bhojayeyam/
191.021. iti viditvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
191.022. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
191.022. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ sahasodgataṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
191.024. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
191.025. atha sahasodgato gṛhapatirutthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu bhagavāñ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti/
191.026. adhivāsayati bhagavān sahasodgatasya gṛhapatestūṣṇībhāvena/
191.027. atha sahasodgato gṛhapatirbhagavatastūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
191.028. atha sahasodgato gṛhapatistāmeva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapyodakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti/
191.031. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto yena sahasodgatasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
191.032. upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya<192> prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
body.translated_text:
191.020. He reflected: 'Whatever fortune and prosperity we have, all of it is thanks to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
191.021. Let me again invite the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> into my inner house and feed them.'
191.021. Having decided thus, he approached the Blessed One.
191.022. Having approached, he paid homage at the feet of the Blessed One with his head and sat down to one side.
191.022. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>.
191.024. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
191.025. Then the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept a meal tomorrow in my inner house, together with the community of monks.'
191.026. The Blessed One assented to the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s> by his silence.
191.027. Then the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, having understood the Blessed One's assent through his silence, paid homage at the feet of the Blessed One with his head and departed from the Blessed One's presence.
191.028. Then the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent hard and soft food, and rising early in the morning, having arranged seats and set out water-vessels, announced the time to the Blessed One through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the Blessed One come at whatever time he thinks fit.'
191.031. Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by the community of monks, approached the dwelling of the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>.
191.032. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared before the community of monks.

body.text:
192.001. atha sahasodgato gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati/
192.002. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātraṃ nīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastāt niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
192.005. tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāyasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā sahasodgatena gṛhapatinā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
192.007. sa dṛṣṭasatyastrirudānamudānayati--idamasmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā neṣṭena na svajanabandhuvargeṇa na rājñā na devatābhir na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇairyadbhagavatā asmākaṃ kṛtam/
192.009. ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrasamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitānyapāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, smo devamanuṣyeṣu/
192.011. abhikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta abhikrāntaḥ/
192.011. eṣo 'haṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
192.012. upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetamabhiprasannamiti/
192.012. atha bhagavān sahasodgataṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
192.001. Then the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, having ascertained that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent hard and soft food.
192.002. Having in many ways with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent hard and soft food, and knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating, with his hands washed and his bowl set aside, he took a lower seat and sat down before the Blessed One for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.
192.005. The Blessed One, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that penetrates the Four Noble Truths, that upon hearing it, the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>, having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the self-existent body rising with its twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
192.007. He, having seen the truths, thrice uttered a solemn declaration: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, not by our father, not by loved ones, not by the clan of friends and relatives, not by the king, not by the gods, not by the departed ancestors, not by ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us.
192.009. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed over, the doors to the lower realms have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened. We have been established among gods and humans.
192.011. I am overcome, Venerable Sir, overcome!
192.011. I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks.
192.012. May you regard me as a lay follower, from this day forward, as long as life lasts, endowed with breath and faith.'
192.012. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

body.text:
192.015. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāaḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta sahasodgatena gṛhapatinā karma kṛtam yena bhṛtikayā karma kṛtam, yena sahasā bhogairabhivṛddhaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtamiti? bhagavānāha--sahasodgatenaiva bhikṣavo gṛhapatinā karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyabhāvīni/
192.018. sahasodgatena gṛhapatinā karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
192.019. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipaṣyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tu upātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
192.023. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
192.024. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//3//
body.translated_text:
192.015. The monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, was done by the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s> that he performed service as a hired laborer, then suddenly increased in wealth, and also attained the vision of the truths?' The Blessed One said: 'It was the householder <s>Sahasodgata</s> himself, monks, who performed and accumulated deeds whose requisite conditions had come together, whose causes had ripened, which stood ready like a flood, and which were of inevitable fruition.
192.018. The householder <s>Sahasodgata</s> performed and accumulated those deeds.
192.019. Who else would experience their result? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element — rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed and accumulated ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome.
192.023. Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);
192.024. having obtained the proper conjunction of conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.' //3//

body.text:
192.025. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatarasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
192.026. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
192.027. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
192.027. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
192.028. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
192.029. dārako jātaḥ/
192.029. tasya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasāni vistareṇa jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā kulasadṛśaṃ nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
192.030. sa unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttaḥ/
192.031. yāvadapareṇa samayena sa gṛhapatiḥ saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakonnāditam<193> vanakhaṇḍamantarjanasahāya udyānabhūmiṃ nirgataḥ/
body.translated_text:
192.025. In the past, monks, in a certain market-town there lived a householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with extensive and vast property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, comparable to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches.
192.026. He had brought a wife from a family of equal standing.
192.027. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her.
192.027. While he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, his wife became pregnant.
192.028. After the passing of eight or nine months, she gave birth.
192.029. A boy was born.
192.029. For him, the three sets of seven — twenty-one days — and, in detail, the birth-festival having been performed, a name befitting the family was established.
192.030. He was raised and nurtured, and grew to maturity.
192.031. Then, at another time, when the spring season had arrived and the trees were in bloom, that householder, with his inner household companions, went out to a garden resounding with geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds.

body.text:
193.001. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasyā/ yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
193.004. prāntaśayanāsanasevinaste na/
193.004. so 'praviśyaiva karvaṭakam yena tadudyānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
193.004. adrākṣīt sa gṛhapatistaṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ kāyaprāsādikaṃ ca śānteneryāpathenodyānaṃ praviśantam/
193.005. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prītiprāmodyajātastvaritatvaritaṃ pratyudgataḥ/
193.006. pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ākīrṇamidamudyānam/
193.007. anyatra gacche/
193.007. iti viditvā pratinivartitumārabdhaḥ/
193.007. sa gṛhapatiḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--ārya, kiṃ nivartase tvam? piṇḍakenārthī/
193.008. ahamapi puṇyena/
193.008. asminnevodyāne vihara, piṇḍakenāvighātaṃ karomīti/
193.009. parānugrahapravṛttāste mahātmānaḥ/
193.009. sa tasyānukampācittamupasthāpya tasminnevodyāne vihartumārabdhaḥ/
193.010. so 'pi tasya piṇḍakena yogodvahanaṃ kartuṃ pravṛttaḥ/
193.011. yāvadapareṇa samayena tasya gṛhapateranyatarakarvaṭake kiṃcit karaṇīyamutpannam/
193.011. sa patnīmāmantrayate--bhadre, mamāmuṣmin karvaṭake kiṃcit karaṇīyamutpannam/
193.012. tatrāhaṃ gacchāmi/
193.012. tvayā tasya mahātmanaḥ pravrajitasyānnapānenāvighātaḥ kartavyaḥ/
193.013. ityuktvā prakrāntaḥ/
193.013. aparasmin divase sā gṛhapatnī kālyamevotthāya tadarthamannapānaṃ sādhayitumārabdhā/
193.014. sā putreṇocyate--amba, kasyārthe 'nnapānaṃ sādhyata iti? sā kathayati--putra, yo 'sau udyāne śāntātma pravrajitastiṣṭhati, tasyārthe sādhyata iti/
193.016. sa ruṣitaḥ kathayati--amba, kimarthaṃ bhṛtikayā karma kṛtvā na bhuṅkta iti? sā kathayati--putra, mā evaṃ vocaḥ/
193.017. aniṣṭo 'sya karmaṇo vipāka iti/
193.018. sa nivāryamāṇo 'pi nāvatiṣṭhate/
193.018. yāvadasau gṛhapatirāgataḥ/
193.018. patnīmāmantrayate--bhadre, kṛtaste tasya piṇḍakenāvighātah? āryaputra kṛtaḥ/
193.019. kiṃ tu anena dārakeṇa tasyāntike kharāvāgniścāritā/
193.020. sa kathayati--bhadre, kiṃ kathayati? tayā vistareṇa samākhyātam/
193.020. sa saṃlakṣayati--kṣamo 'yaṃ tapasvī/
193.021. gacchāmi, taṃ mahātmānaṃ kṣamāpayāmi--mā atyantameva kṣato bhaviṣyati/
193.022. iti viditvā taṃ dārakamādāya yena pratyekabuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
193.022. adrākṣīt sa pratyekabuddhastaṃ gṛhapatimātmanā dvitīyamāgacchantam/
193.023. sa saṃlakṣayati--na kadācidayaṃ gṛhapatirātmanā dvitīyamāgacchati/
193.024. tat kimatra kāraṇamiti? asamanvāhṛtya śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate/
193.025. sa samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ/
193.025. ten samanvāhṛtya vijñātam/
193.025. kāyikī teṣāṃ mahātmanāṃ dharmadeśanā na vācikī/
193.026. sa tasyānukampārthaṃ vitatapakṣa hava haṃsarāja uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ/
193.027. āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhirāvarjanakarī/
193.028. sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ saputraḥ pādayor nipatitaḥ/
193.028. tataḥ sa dāraka āhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ kathayati--avatara avatara sadbhūtadakṣiṇīya, mama kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayaccheti/
193.030. sa tasyānukampārthamavatīrṇaḥ/
193.030. sa gṛhapatiputrastīvreṇāśayena pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye kharā vāgniścāritā, mā tasya karmaṇo bhāgī syām/
193.032. yattu idānīṃ cittamabhiprasāditam, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlenāḍhye mahādhane <194>mahābhoge kule jāyeyam, evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti//
body.translated_text: When <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, devoted to secluded lodgings and food, the sole field of merit for the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a tour through the countryside, arrived at that market-town. Being one who frequented secluded lodgings, without even entering the town he went to the garden. That householder saw the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, pleasing of body, entering the garden with a peaceful deportment. Having seen him, filled with joy and delight, he quickly went out to meet him. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> reflected: 'This garden is crowded. I should go elsewhere.' Having decided thus, he began to turn back. That householder, falling at his feet, said: 'Venerable one, why do you turn back? You need alms-food, and I need merit. Dwell right here in this garden; I shall provide you with alms-food without interruption.' Those great souls are inclined to help others. Having generated a mind of compassion for him, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> began to dwell right there in that garden. And the householder began to undertake the burden of providing him with alms-food. Then, at another time, some business arose for that householder in another market-town. He said to his wife: 'Dear one, some business has arisen for me in another market-town. I shall go there. You must provide the great renunciant with food and drink without interruption.' Having said this, he departed. On the next day, that householder's wife, rising early in the morning, began to prepare food and drink for that purpose. Her son said to her: 'Mother, for whose sake is food and drink being prepared?' She said: 'Son, it is being prepared for the sake of that peaceful renunciant who dwells in the garden.' He said angrily: 'Mother, why does he not work for wages and eat?' She said: 'Son, do not speak thus. The fruit of such a deed is undesirable.' Though restrained by her, he did not desist. Then that householder returned. He asked his wife: 'Dear one, have you provided him with alms-food without interruption?' 'Yes, noble husband, I have. But this boy has spoken harsh words to him.' He said: 'Dear one, what did he say?' She told him in full. He reflected: 'That ascetic is forbearing. Let me go and ask forgiveness of that great soul — lest the consequence be utterly harmful.' Having decided thus, he took the boy and approached the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> saw the householder coming in the company of a second person. He reflected: 'Never before has this householder come in the company of a second person. What is the reason for this?' Without investigation, the knowledge and vision of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> does not operate. He began to investigate. Having investigated, he understood. The teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> by those great souls is through the body, not through speech. Out of compassion for that boy, like a royal goose with wings outstretched, he rose up into the sky and began to perform miraculous feats of blazing, burning, raining, and illuminating. Quickly does the supernatural power of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> captivate an ordinary person. That boy, together with his father, fell at his feet like a tree severed at its root. Then, with hair standing on end, the boy said: 'Descend, descend, O true field of merit! Extend the hand of salvation to me, who am sunk in the mud of desire!' Out of compassion for him, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> descended. That householder's son, with intense devotion, falling at his feet, began to make an aspiration: 'Whatever harsh words I have uttered toward such a true field of merit — may I not share in the fruit of that deed! But now that my mind has been inspired with faith, by this root of merit may I be born in a wealthy, prosperous, affluent family; may I obtain such teachings as these; and may I revere a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and never turn away from him!'

body.text:
194.003. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavah? yo 'sau gṛhapatiputraḥ, eṣa evāsau sahasodgato gṛhapatiḥ/
194.004. yadanena pratyekabuddhasyāntike kharā vāgniścāritā, tena pañca janmaśatāni bhṛtakapuruṣo jātaḥ/
194.005. yāvadetarhyapi bhṛtikayā karma kṛtam/
194.005. yat punastasyaivāntike cittamabhiprasādya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tena sahasaiva bhogairabhivṛddhaḥ/
194.006. mamāntike satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam/
194.006. ahaṃ cānena pratyekabuddhakoṭiśatasahasrebhyaḥ prativiśiṣṭataraḥ śāstā ārāgito na virāgitaḥ/
194.007. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
194.009. tasmāttarhi ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
194.010. ityevaṃ vo bhikavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? He who was that householder's son — he is none other than this householder <s>Sahasodgata</s>. Because he spoke harsh words to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, he was born for five hundred lifetimes as a hired servant. And even now he has performed hired labor. But because he then inspired his mind with faith in that very <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and made an aspiration, he suddenly increased in wealth. He has attained the vision of truth in my presence. And I, a teacher more distinguished than hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, have been revered by him, not rejected. Thus, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for deeds that are entirely bright, the result is entirely bright; for deeds that are mixed, the result is mixed. Therefore, abandoning entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be applied solely to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.'

body.text:
194.010. (iyaṃ tāvadutpattir na tāvat buddho bhagavāñ śrāvakāṇāṃ vinaye śikṣāpadam/?)
194.012. idamavocadbhagavān/ āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: (This is the origin story, but the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> has not yet laid down a training rule for the disciples in the <s>Vinaya</s>.) Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 194.013. sahasodgatasya prakaraṇāvadānamekaviṃśatimam//
body.translated_text: The <s>Prakaraṇāvadāna</s> (Narrative Story) of <s>Sahasodgata</s>, the twenty-first.

body.text: 195.001. div22 candraprabhabodhisattvacaryāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 22: The <s>Candraprabhabodhisattvacaryāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>).

body.text:
195.002. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
195.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavān bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśābhirbhikṣuśataiḥ/
195.003. tatra bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--paśya bhadanta, yāvadāyuṣmantau śāriputramaudgalyāyanau tatprathamataraṃ nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtau, na tveva pitṛmaraṇamāgamitavantau/
195.005. atredānīṃ bhikṣavaḥ kimāścaryam yadetarhi śāriputramaudgalyāyanau bhikṣū vigatarāgau vigatadveṣau vigatamohau parimuktau jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaur nistṛṣṇau nirupādānau prahīṇasarvāhaṃkāramamakārāsmimānābhiniveśānuśayau tiṣṭhati buddhapramukhe bhikṣusaṃghe tatprathamataraṃ nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtau, na tveva pitṛmaraṇamāgamitavantau/
195.009. yattvatīte 'dhvani śāriputramaudgalyāyanau sarāgau sadveṣau samohāvaparimuktau jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsairmamāntike cittamabhiprasādya kālaṃ kṛtvā kāmadhātumatikramya brahmaloka upapannau, na tveva pitṛmaraṇamāgamitavantau, tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, with a great community of monks — twelve hundred and fifty monks. There, the monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> entered final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without residue ahead of all others, yet they did not await even their father's death.' 'Here, monks, what is wonderful about this? That now <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, monks free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, free from craving, free from clinging, who have abandoned all ego-making, mine-making, conceit, and latent tendencies, standing in a community of monks with the <s>Buddha</s> at their head, entered final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without residue ahead of all others, yet did not await even their father's death. But in the past, when <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> were still possessed of passion, hatred, and delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair — having inspired their minds with faith in me, they died, transcended the realm of desire, and were reborn in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, yet did not await even their father's death. Listen to that!'

body.text:
195.013. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvanyuttarāpathe bhadraśilā nāma nagarī rājadhānī abhūt, ṛddhā ca sphītā ca kṣemā ca subhikṣā ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca/
195.014. dvādaśayojanānyāyāmena dvādaśayojanāni vistareṇa caturasrā caturdvārā suvibhaktā uccaistoraṇagavākṣavātāyanavedikāpratimaṇḍitā nānāratnasampūrṇā susamṛddhasarvadravyavaṇigjananiketā pārthivāmātyagṛhapatiśreṣṭhirāṣṭrikanīti(?)maulidharāṇāmāvāso vīṇāveṇupaṇavasughoṣakavallarīmṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahaśaṅkhanirnāditā/
195.018. tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāmagurugandhāścandanagandhāścūrṇagandhāḥ sarvakālikāśca kusumagandhā nānāvātasamīritā atiramaṇīyā vīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu vāyavo vāyanti sma/
195.019. hastyaśvarathapattibalakāyasampannā yugyayānopaśobhitā vistīrṇātiramaṇīyavīthīmahāpathā ucchritavicitradhvajapatākā toraṇagavākṣārdhacandrāvanaddhā amarālaya iva śobhate/
195.021. utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāni surabhijalajakusumaparimaṇḍitāni svādusvacchaśītalajalaparipūrṇapuṣkiriṇītaḍāgodapānaprasravaṇopaśobhitā śālatālatamālasūtra(?)karṇikārāśokatilakapuṃnāganāgakeśaracampakabakulātimuktakapāṭalāpuṣpasaṃchannā kalaviṅkaśukaśārikākokilabarhigaṇajīvaṃjīvakonnāditavanaṣaṇḍodyānaparimaṇḍitā/
195.025. bhadraśilāyāṃ ca rājadhānyāmanyataraṃ maṇigarbhaṃ nāma rājodyānaṃ nānāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣaviṭapopaśobhitaṃ sodapānaṃ haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakaśakunimanojñaravanir nāditamatiramaṇīyam/
195.027. evaṃ suramaṇīyā bhadraśilā rājadhānī babhūva/
195.027. bhadraśilāyāṃ rājādhānyāṃ rājābhūccandraprabho nāma abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko divyacakṣuścaturbhāgacakravartī dhārmiko dharmarājā jambudvīpe rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kāritavān svayamprabhuḥ/
195.029. na khalu rājñaścandraprabhasya gacchato 'ndhakāraṃ bhavati, na ca maṇirvā pradīpo vā ulkā vā purastāt nīyate, api tu svakāt kāyāt rājñaścandraprabhasya prabhā niścaranti tadyathā candramaṇḍalādraśmayaḥ/
195.032. anena kāraṇena rājñaścandraprabhasya candraprabha iti saṃjñā babhūva//
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, in the northern region, there was a royal capital called <s>Bhadraśilā</s> — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with a great multitude of people. It was twelve <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in length and twelve <s>yojanas</s> in width, square, with four gates, well-arranged, adorned with lofty gateways, windows, ventilators, and balustrades, filled with various jewels, teeming with well-provisioned merchants' houses stocked with all goods, the abode of princes, ministers, householders, guild-masters, administrators, and crown-bearers, resounding with the sounds of <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), flutes, <s>paṇavas</s> (drums), <s>sughoṣakas</s> (trumpets), <s>vallarīs</s> (stringed instruments), <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (barrel drums), <s>bherīs</s> (war drums), <s>paṭahas</s> (kettledrums), and conch shells. In that royal capital, the fragrances of aloe, sandalwood, powders, and all-season blossoms, stirred by various winds, most delightful, blew through the streets, crossroads, and intersections. Endowed with armies of elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry, adorned with yoked vehicles, with broad and exceedingly delightful streets and highways, with lofty and variegated banners and flags, adorned with gateways, windows, and half-moon arches, it shone like the city of the gods. Adorned with <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily), and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) — with pools, ponds, wells, and springs full of sweet, clear, cool water, adorned with fragrant aquatic flowers — shaded with <s>śāla</s>, <s>tāla</s> (palm), <s>tamāla</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, <s>puṃnāga</s>, <s>nāgakeśara</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>atimukta</s> (jasmine), and <s>pāṭala</s> trees in bloom — adorned with groves and gardens resounding with <s>kalaviṅka</s> (cuckoos), parrots, mynas, <s>kokila</s> (Indian cuckoos), peacocks, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds. In the royal capital of <s>Bhadraśilā</s> there was a royal garden called <s>Maṇigarbha</s> ('Jewel-Womb'), adorned with various flowering and fruiting trees and shrubs, with springs, resounding with the delightful calls of geese, cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynas, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds — most charming. Such was the exceedingly beautiful royal capital of <s>Bhadraśilā</s>. In the royal capital of <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, there was a king named <s>Candraprabha</s> ('Moon-Light') — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, possessed of the divine eye, a quarter-<s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a righteous king ruling the <s>Dharma</s>, exercising sovereign rule and dominion over <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a lord in his own right. When King <s>Candraprabha</s> walked, there was no darkness; neither a gem, nor a lamp, nor a torch was carried before him. Rather, from King <s>Candraprabha's</s> own body, radiance streamed forth, just as rays stream from the disc of the moon. For this reason, the name <s>Candraprabha</s> ('Moon-Light') arose for the king.

body.text:
196.001. <196>tena khalu samayenāsmiñ jambudvīpe 'ṣḍaṣaṣṭinagarasahasrāṇi babhūvurbhadraśilārājadhānīprabhukhāni ṛddhāni sphītāni kṣemāṇi subhikṣāṇyākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāṇi/
196.002. apīdānīṃ jambudvīpakā akarā abhūvann aśulkā atarapaṇyāḥ/
196.003. kṛṣisampannāḥ saumyā janapadā babhūvuḥ/
196.003. kukkuṭasampātamātrāśca grāmanigamarāṣṭrarājadhānyo babhūvuḥ/
196.004. tena khalu samayena catuścatvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi jambudvīpe manuṣyāṇāmāyuṣaḥ pramāṇamabhūt/
196.005. rājā candraprabho bodhisattvo 'bhūt sarvaṃdadaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca/
196.006. mahati tyāge vartate/
196.006. tena bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ nirgatya bahirdhā nagarasya caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu catvāro catvāro mahāyajñavāṭā māpitāśchatradhvajayūpapatākātyucchritāḥ/
196.007. tataḥ suvarṇabherīḥ saṃtāḍya dānāni dīyante, puṇyāni kriyante, tadyathā--annamannārthibhyaḥ, pānaṃ pānārthibhyaḥ, svādyabhojyamālyavilepanavastraśayanāsanāpāśrayāvāsapradīpacchatrāṇi rathā ābharaṇānyalaṃkārāḥ, suvarṇapātryo rūpyacūrṇaparipūrṇāḥ, rūpyapātryaḥ suvarṇaparipūrṇāḥ, suvarṇaśṛṅgāśca gāvaḥ kāmadohinyaḥ/
196.011. kumārāḥ kumārikāśca sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāḥ kṛtvā pradānāni dīyante/
196.011. vastrāṇi nānāraṅgāni nānādeśasamucchritāni nānāvicitrāṇi, tasyathā--paṭṭāṃśukacīnakauśeyadhautapaṭṭavastrāṇyūrṇādukūlamayaśobhanavastrāṇyaparāntakaphalakaharyaṇikambalaratnasuvarṇaprāvarakākāśikāṃśukṣomakādyāḥ/
196.014. rājñā candraprabheṇa tāvantaṃ dānamanudattam, yena sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyā āḍhyā mahādhanā mahābhogāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
196.015. rājñā candraprabheṇa tāvanti hastyaśvarathacchatrāṇi pradānamanupradattāni, yathā asmiñ jambudvīpe ekamanuṣyo 'pi padbhyāṃ na gacchati/
196.016. sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyā hastipṛṣṭhaiśca caturaśvayuktaiśca rathairuparisuvarṇamayai rūpyamayaiścātapatrairudyānenodyānaṃ grāmeṇa grāmamanuvicaranti sma/
196.018. tato rājñaścandraprabhasyaitadabhavat--kiṃ punarme itvareṇa dānena pradattena? yannvaham yādṛśānyeva mama vastrālaṃkārāṇyābharaṇāni, tādṛśānyeva dānamanuprayaccheyam, yat sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyā rājakrīḍayā krīḍeyuḥ/
196.020. atha rājā candraprabho jambudvīpakebhyo manuṣyebhyo maulipaṭṭavastrālaṃkārābharaṇāṇyanuprayacchati, tadyathā--harṣakaṭakakeyūrāhārārdhahārādīn pradānamanuprayacchati sma/
196.022. rājñā candraprabheṇa tāvanti rājārhāṇi vastrāṇyalaṃkārāṇi maulayaḥ paṭṭāścānupradattāḥ, yena sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyā maulidharāḥ paṭṭadharāśca saṃvṛttāḥ/
196.023. yā rājñaścandraprabhasyākṛtistādṛśā eva sarve jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
196.024. tato rājñā candraprabheṇāṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu nagarasahasreṣu ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--sarve bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyā rājakrīḍayā, krīḍantu, yāvadahaṃ jīvāmīti/
196.026. atha jambudvīpakā manuṣyā rājñaścandraprabhasya ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇāṃ śrutvā sarva eva rājakrīḍayā krīḍitumārabdhāḥ/
196.027. vīṇāveṇupaṇavasughoṣakavallarībherīpaṭahamṛdaṅgatālaśaṅkhasahasraistūryaśabdaśataiśca vādyamānaiḥ keyūrahāramaṇimuktābharaṇakuṇḍaladharāḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitapramadāgaṇaparivṛtā rājaśriyamanubhavanti sma/
196.029. tena khalu samayena jambudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ rājalīlayā krīḍatām yaśca vīṇāveṇupaṇavasughoṣakavallarībherīmṛdaṅgapaṭahaśabdo yaścāṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tālavaṃśanirghoṣo yaścandraprabhasya caturṣu mahāyajñavāṭeṣu suvarṇabherīṇāṃ tāḍyamānānāṃ varṇamanojñaśabdo niścarati, tena sarvo jambudvīpo manojñaśabdanādito 'bhūt tadyathā devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmabhyantaraṃ devaputam <197>nṛttagītavāditaśabdena nirnāditam/
body.translated_text:
196.001. <196>At that time, in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, there were sixty-eight thousand cities, chief among them the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s> — prosperous, thriving, safe, abundant in food, and teeming with many people.
196.002. Moreover, the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> at that time were free from taxes, duties, and trade-levies.
196.003. The provinces were blessed with agriculture and peaceful.
196.003. Villages, market-towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals were so close as to be within a cock's flight of each other.
196.004. At that time, the measure of the lifespan of humans in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was forty-four thousand years.
196.005. King <s>Candraprabha</s> was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a giver of all, one who renounced everything, who renounced without attachment.
196.006. He engaged in great generosity.
196.006. He went forth from the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s> and had great sacrificial enclosures constructed at each of the four city gates outside the city, lofty with parasols, banners, sacrificial posts, and flags.
196.007. Then, striking golden drums, gifts were given and merit was made — namely: food to those desiring food, drink to those desiring drink, delicacies, meals, garlands, ointments, garments, bedding, lodgings, shelters, dwellings, lamps, parasols, chariots, ornaments, and adornments; golden vessels filled with silver dust; silver vessels filled with gold; gold-horned cows yielding milk at will.
196.011. Boys and girls, adorned with every ornament, were given as gifts.
196.011. Garments of various colors, from various lands, of various patterns — namely: silk, fine cloth, Chinese silk, <s>kauśeya</s> (silk), bleached silk garments, woolen cloths, beautiful <s>dukūla</s> (fine muslin) garments, <s>Aparāntaka</s> fabrics, board-textiles, <s>Haryaṇī</s> blankets, jeweled golden cloaks, <s>Ākāśika</s> cloth, <s>kṣoma</s> (linen), and others.
196.014. So much was given by King <s>Candraprabha</s> that all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became wealthy, of great riches and great resources.
196.015. So many elephants, horses, chariots, and parasols were given by King <s>Candraprabha</s> that not a single person in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> traveled on foot.
196.016. All the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> traveled from garden to garden and from village to village on elephant-backs and in four-horse chariots, with golden and silver parasols above.
196.018. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> thought: 'What use is this ordinary gift that I have given? Let me give such gifts of garments, ornaments, and adornments as are equal to my own, so that all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> may sport in royal splendor.'
196.020. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> gave to the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> crown-turbans, silken garments, ornaments, and adornments — namely: bracelets, armlets, <s>keyūras</s> (upper-arm ornaments), necklaces, half-necklaces, and the like.
196.022. So many kingly garments, ornaments, crowns, and silks were given by King <s>Candraprabha</s> that all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became crown-wearers and silk-wearers.
196.023. All the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became identical in appearance to King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
196.024. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> had a proclamation by bell made in the sixty-eight thousand cities: 'Let all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> sport in royal splendor for as long as I live.'
196.026. Then the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, hearing the bell-proclamation of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, all began to sport in royal splendor.
196.027. With <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), flutes, <s>paṇavas</s> (small drums), <s>sughoṣakas</s>, <s>vallarīs</s> (stringed instruments), kettledrums, tabors, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (drums), cymbals, and thousands of conch-shells, and with hundreds of instrumental sounds being played, wearing armlets, necklaces, jewels, pearls, ornaments, and earrings, surrounded by groups of women adorned with every ornament, they enjoyed royal splendor.
196.029. At that time, with the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> sporting in royal fashion, and with the sounds of <s>vīṇās</s>, flutes, <s>paṇavas</s>, <s>sughoṣakas</s>, <s>vallarīs</s>, kettledrums, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, tabors, and the sound of bamboo clappers in the sixty-eight thousand cities, and with the pleasant sounds of the golden drums being struck in <s>Candraprabha</s>'s four great sacrificial enclosures, the whole of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> resounded with delightful sounds, just as the inner realm of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods <197> resounds with the sounds of divine dance, song, and music.

body.text:
197.001. evameva tasmin kāle tasmin samaye sarvo jambudvīpavāsināṃ janakāyastena gītavāditaśabdena ekāntasukhasamarpito 'tyarthaṃ ramate/
197.002. tena khalu samayena bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ dvāsaptatirayutakoṭīśatāni manuṣyāṇāṃ prativasanti sma/
197.004. teṣāṃ rājā candraprabha ṛṣṭo babhūva priyo manāpaśca/
197.004. apīdānīṃ varṇākṛtiliṅgasthairyamasya nirīkṣamāṇā na tṛptimupayānti sma/
197.005. yasmiṃśca samaye rājā candraprabho mahāyajñavāṭaṃ gacchati, tasmin samaye prāṇikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyavalokayanti, evaṃ cāhuh--devagarbho batāyaṃ rājā candraptabha iha jamudvīpe rājyaṃ kārayati/
197.007. na khalu manuṣyā īdṛgvarṇasaṃsthānā yādṛśā devasya candraprabhasyeti/
197.008. rājā candraprabho yena yenāvalokayati, tena tena strīsahasrāṇyavalokayanti--dhanyāstāḥ striyo yāsāmeṣa bharteti/
197.009. tacca śuddhairmanobhir nānyathābhāvāt/
197.009. evaṃ darśanīyo rājā candraprabho babhūva/
197.010. candraprabhasya rājño 'rdhatrayodaśāmātyasahasrāṇi/
197.010. teṣāṃ dvau agrāmātyau mahācandro mahīdharaśca/
197.011. vyaktau paṇḍitau medhāvinau guṇaiśca sarvāmātyamaṇḍalaprativiśiṣṭau sarvādhikṛtau rājaparikarṣakau rājaparipālakau/
197.012. alpotsuko rājā sarvakarmānteṣu/
197.013. mahācandraścāgrāmātyo 'bhīkṣṇaṃ jambudvīpakān manuṣyān daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu niyojayati--imān bhavanto jambudvīpakā manuṣyā daśa kuśalān karmapathān samādāya vartatheti/
197.014. yādṛśī ca rājñaścakravartino 'vavādānuśāsanī, tādṛśī mahācandrasyāmātyasyāvavādānuśāsanī babhūva/
197.016. mahācandrasyāgrāmātyasya rājā candraprabha iṣṭaścābhūt priyaśca manāapaśca/
197.016. apīdānīṃ varṇākṛtiliṅgasaṃsthānamasya nirīkṣamāṇo na tṛptimupayāti//
body.translated_text:
197.001. Just so, at that time, in that era, the entire populace dwelling in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, given over to consummate happiness by those sounds of song and music, delighted exceedingly.
197.002. At that time, in the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, seventy-two billion and hundreds of millions of people were dwelling.
197.004. For them, King <s>Candraprabha</s> was beloved, dear, and pleasing.
197.004. Moreover, gazing upon his complexion, form, appearance, and bearing, they could not get enough.
197.005. And at whatever time King <s>Candraprabha</s> went to the great sacrificial enclosure, at that time billions upon billions of beings would gaze upon him and say: 'Surely this King <s>Candraprabha</s> is of divine birth, ruling the kingdom here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.
197.007. Humans are surely not of such complexion and stature as the divine <s>Candraprabha</s>.'
197.008. In whatever direction King <s>Candraprabha</s> looked, in that direction thousands of women would gaze: 'Fortunate are those women whose husband he is.'
