197.009. And this was with pure minds, without any impropriety.
197.009. So beautiful was King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
197.010. King <s>Candraprabha</s> had twelve and a half thousand ministers.
197.010. Of them, two were the chief ministers: <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s>.
197.011. They were learned, wise, intelligent, and distinguished in virtues above the entire council of ministers — they were placed in charge of everything, supporters of the king and protectors of the king.
197.012. The king had little concern for all administrative affairs.
197.013. The chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s> constantly exhorted the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> to the ten wholesome paths of action: 'May all you people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> undertake and practice these ten wholesome paths of action.'
197.014. And such was the instruction and admonition of the minister <s>Mahācandra</s> as is the instruction and admonition of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).
197.016. For the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>, King <s>Candraprabha</s> was beloved, dear, and pleasing.
197.016. Moreover, gazing upon his complexion, form, appearance, and bearing, he could not get enough.

body.text:
197.018. yāvadapareṇa samayena mahācandreṇāgrāmātyena svapno dṛṣṭah--rājñaścandraprabhasya dhūmavarṇaiḥ piśācairmaulirapanītaḥ/
197.019. prativibuddhasya cābhūdbhayam, abhūcchaṅkitatvam, abhūdromaharṣah--mā haiva devasya candraprabhasya śiroyācanaka āgacchet/
197.020. devaśca sarvaṃdadaḥ/
197.020. sarvaparityāge nāstyasya kiṃcidaparityaktaṃ dīnānāthakṛpaṇavanīpakayācanakebhya iti/
197.021. tasya buddhirutpannā--na mayā rājñaścandraprabhasya svapno nivedayitavyaḥ/
197.022. api tu ratnamayāni śirāṃsi kārayitvā koṣakoṣṭhāgāraṃ praveśya sthāpayitavyāni/
197.023. yadi nāma kaściddevasya śiroyācanaka āgacchet, tamenamebhī ratnamayaiḥ śirobhiḥ pralobhayiṣyāmi/
197.024. iti viditvā ratnamayāni śirāṃsi kārayitvā koṣakoṣṭhāgareṣu prakṣipya sthāpitavān/
197.025. apareṇa samayena mahīdhareṇāgrāmātyena svapno dṛṣṭah--sarvaratnamayaḥ potaścandraprabhasya kulasthaḥ śataśo viśīrṇaḥ/
197.026. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhītastrastaḥ saṃvignah--mā haiva rājñaścandraprabhasya rājyacyutirbhaviṣyati jīvitasya cāntarasya cāntarāya iti/
197.027. tena brāhmaṇā ye naimittikā vipaścikāścāhūya uktāh--bhavantaḥ, mayedṛśaḥ svapno dṛṣṭaḥ, nirdoṣaṃ kuruteti/
197.028. tatastairbrāhmaṇair naimittikairvipaścikaiśca samākhyātam--yādṛśo 'yaṃ tvayā svapno dṛṣṭaḥ, nacirādeva rājñaścandraprabhasya śiroyācanaka āgamiṣyati/
197.030. sa cāsyāmeva bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāmavatariṣyatīti/
197.030. tato mahīdharo 'grāmātyaḥ svapnanirdeśaṃ śrutvā kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitah--atikṣipraṃ rājñaścandraprabhasya maitrātmakasya kāruṇikasya sattvavatsalasyānityatābalaṃ pratyupasthitamiti/
197.032. athāpareṇa samayenārdhatrayodaśābhiramātyasahasraih<198> svapno dṛṣṭah--rājñaścandraprabhasya caturṣu yajñavāṭeṣu karoṭapāṇibhiryakṣaiścachatradhvajapatākāḥ pātitāḥ, suvarṇabheryaśca bhinnāḥ/
body.translated_text:
197.018. Then, on another occasion, the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s> had a dream: smoke-colored <s>piśācas</s> (demons) removed the crown of King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
197.019. Upon waking, he was afraid, he was anxious, his hair stood on end: 'Let it not be that someone comes to beg for the head of the lord <s>Candraprabha</s>!
197.020. The lord gives everything.
197.020. In his total renunciation, there is nothing that has not been given away to the destitute, helpless, wretched, forest-dwellers, and beggars.'
197.021. This thought arose in him: 'I must not inform King <s>Candraprabha</s> of this dream.
197.022. Rather, I should have jeweled heads made and place them in the treasury and storehouses.
197.023. If anyone comes to beg for the lord's head, I will entice him away with these jeweled heads.'
197.024. Having thus resolved, he had jeweled heads made and placed them in the treasuries and storehouses.
197.025. On another occasion, the chief minister <s>Mahīdhara</s> had a dream: the all-jeweled ship belonging to the family of <s>Candraprabha</s> was shattered into a hundred pieces.
197.026. Having seen this, he was frightened, terrified, and alarmed: 'Let it not be that King <s>Candraprabha</s> will lose his kingdom, or that there will be danger to his life!'
197.027. He summoned the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who were soothsayers and diviners and said: 'Sirs, I have had such a dream; please render it harmless.'
197.028. Then those <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> soothsayers and diviners told him: 'From this dream that you have had, it will not be long before someone comes to beg for King <s>Candraprabha</s>'s head.
197.030. And he will descend upon this very royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>.'
197.030. Then the chief minister <s>Mahīdhara</s>, hearing the interpretation of the dream, placed his cheek on his hand and remained absorbed in thought: 'All too soon has the power of impermanence arrived for King <s>Candraprabha</s>, who is of a loving nature, compassionate, and devoted to beings.'
197.032. Then, on another occasion, all twelve and a half thousand ministers <198> had a dream: in King <s>Candraprabha</s>'s four sacrificial enclosures, <s>Yakṣas</s> with bowl-shaped hands pulled down the parasols, banners, and flags, and broke the golden drums.

body.text:
198.002. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhītāstrastāḥ saṃvignāh--mā haiva rājñaścandraprabhasya mahāpṛthivīpālasya maitrātmakasya kāruṇikasya sattvavatsalasyānityatābalamāgacchet, mā haiva asmākaṃ devena sārdhaṃ nānābhāvo bhaviṣyati vinābhāvo viprayogaḥ, mā haiva atrāṇo 'paritrāṇo jambudvīpo bhaviṣyatīti/
198.005. rājñā candraprabheṇa śrutam/
198.005. tena śrutvā aṣṭaṣaṣṭinagarasahasreṣu ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--rājalīlayā bhavantaḥ sarve jambudvīpakā mānuṣyāḥ krīḍantu yāvadahaṃ jīvāmi/
198.007. kim yuṣmākaṃ māyopamaiḥ svapnopamaiścintitaih? rājñaścandraprabhasya ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ śrutvā sarva eva jambudvīpakā manuṣyā rājalīlayā krīḍitumārabdhāḥ, vīṇāvoṇupaṇavasughoṣakavallarībherīmṛdaṅgatālaśaṅkhasahasraistūryaśabdaśataiśca vādyamānaiḥ keyūrahāramaṇimuktābharaṇakuṇḍaladharāḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitapramadāgaṇaparivṛtāa rājaśriyamanubhavanti sma/
198.010. tena khalu samayena jambudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ rājakrīḍayā krīḍatām yaśca rājñaścandraprabhasya caturṣu mahāyajñavāṭeṣu suvarṇabherīṇāṃ tāḍyamānānāṃ valgurmanojñaḥ śabdo niścarati, tena sarvo jambudvīpo manojñaśabdanir nādito 'bhūt/
198.013. tadyathā devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāmanyataraṃ devapuraṃ nṛttagītavāditam, evameva tasmin kāle tasmin samaye sarvo jambudvīpanivāsī janakāyastena gītaśabdenaikāntasukhasamarpito 'tyarthaṃ ramate//
body.translated_text:
198.002. Having seen this, they were frightened, terrified, and filled with spiritual urgency: 'May the power of impermanence not come upon King <s>Candraprabha</s>, the great protector of the earth, who is of a benevolent nature, compassionate, and tender toward all beings! May there not be separation, parting, or estrangement between us and our lord! May <s>Jambudvīpa</s> not become unprotected and unguarded!'
198.005. King <s>Candraprabha</s> heard this.
198.005. Having heard, he had a bell-proclamation made in the sixty-eight thousand cities: 'Let all of you, people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, sport with royal splendor as long as I live.
198.007. What use are your thoughts, which are like illusions and dreams?' Having heard King <s>Candraprabha's</s> bell-proclamation, all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> began to sport with royal splendor — with the sound of <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), flutes, <s>paṇavas</s> (small drums), <s>sughoṣakas</s> (resonant drums), <s>vallarīs</s> (stringed instruments), <s>bherīs</s> (kettledrums), <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (tabor drums), cymbals, conches, and hundreds of thousands of instrumental sounds being played; wearing armlets, necklaces, ornaments of gems and pearls, earrings, adorned with all ornaments, surrounded by troupes of women, they experienced the splendor of royalty.
198.010. At that time, as the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> sported with royal amusement, from the golden kettledrums being struck at King <s>Candraprabha's</s> four great sacrificial enclosures, a sweet and delightful sound issued forth, and all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> resounded with that delightful sound.
198.013. Just as in a certain divine city of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods there is dance, song, and music, even so at that time all the inhabitants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, transported to absolute bliss by that sound of music, rejoiced exceedingly.

body.text:
198.016. tena khalu samayena gandhamādane parvate raudrākṣo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati sma indrajālavidhijñaḥ/
198.017. aśrauṣīdraudrākṣo brāhmaṇo bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ candraprabho nāma rājā sarvaṃdado 'smītyātmānaṃ pratijānīte/
198.018. yannvahaṃ gatvā śiro yāceyamiti/
198.018. tasyaitadabhavat--yadi tāvat sarvadado bhaviṣyati, mama śiro dāsyati/
198.019. api tu duṣkarametadasthānamanavakāśo yadevamiṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ manāpamuttamāṅgaṃ parityakṣyati yaduta śīrṣam, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate/
198.021. iti viditvā gandhamādanāt parvatādavatīrṇaḥ/
198.021. atha gandhamādananivāsinī devatā vikroṣṭumārabdhā--hā kaṣṭaṃ rajñaścandraprabhasya maitrātmakasya mahākāruṇikasya sattvavatsalasyānityatābalaṃ pratyupasthitamiti/
198.023. tena khalu samayena sarvajambudvīpa ākulākulaḥ, dhūmāndhakāraḥ, upakāpātāḥ, diśodāhāḥ, antarīkṣe devadundubhayo 'bhinadanti/
198.024. bhadraśilāyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ nātidūre pañcābhijño ṛṣiḥ praivasati viśvāmitro nāṃnā pañcaśataparivāro maitrātmakaḥ kāruṇikaḥ sattvavatsalaḥ/
198.026. atha sa ṛṣiḥ sarvajambudvīpamākulaṃ dṛṣṭvā māṇavakānāmantrayate--yatkhalu māṇavakā jānīta sarvajambudvīpa etarhyākulākulo dhūmāndhakāraḥ/
198.027. sūryācandramasau evamahānubhāvau na bhāsato na tapato na virocataḥ/
198.028. nūnaṃ kasyacinmahāpuruṣasya nirodho bhaviṣyati/
198.028. tathā hi--
198.029. rodanti kinnaragaṇā vanadevatāśca dhikkāramutsṛjanti devagaṇā pi na sthuḥ/
198.031. candro na bhāti na vibhāti sahasraraśmir naiva vādyavāditaravo 'pi niśāmyate 'tra//1//
body.translated_text:
198.016. At that time, on the <s>Gandhamādana</s> (Fragrant) mountain, there dwelt a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Raudrākṣa</s> (Fierce-Eyed), skilled in the arts of illusion.
198.017. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> heard: 'In the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, a king named <s>Candraprabha</s> declares himself to be an all-giver.'
198.018. 'Let me go and ask for his head.'
198.018. This thought occurred to him: 'If he is truly an all-giver, he will give me his head.
198.019. But this is difficult — it is unlikely and impossible that he would give up something so cherished, beloved, dear, and delightful as his own head; this cannot happen.'
198.021. Having thus reflected, he descended from the <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain.
198.021. Then a deity dwelling on <s>Gandhamādana</s> began to cry out: 'Alas, woe! The power of impermanence has come upon King <s>Candraprabha</s>, who is of a benevolent nature, greatly compassionate, and tender toward all beings!'
198.023. At that time, all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> was in turmoil — darkened with smoke, with meteors falling, with fires burning in the directions, and in the sky the celestial war-drums were thundering.
198.024. And in the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, not far away, there dwelt a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) named <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, possessing the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), attended by five hundred students, of a benevolent nature, compassionate, and tender toward all beings.
198.026. Then that <s>ṛṣi</s>, seeing all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in turmoil, addressed the students: 'Know, students, that at this very time all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is in turmoil, darkened with smoke.
198.027. The sun and moon, of such great power, do not shine, do not blaze, do not radiate.
198.028. Surely there will be the destruction of some great being.
198.028. For indeed:
198.029. The <s>Kinnaras</s> weep and the forest deities too; the hosts of gods utter cries of woe and do not stand firm.
198.031. The moon does not shine, nor does the thousand-rayed sun; not even the sound of musical instruments can be heard here.' //1//

body.text:
199.001. <199>ete hi pādapagaṇāḥ phalapuṣpanaddhā bhūmau patanti pavanairapi cālitāni/
199.003. saṃśrūyate dhvanirayaṃ ca yathātibhīmo vyakto bhaviṣyati pure vyasanaṃ mahāntam//2//
body.translated_text:
199.001. 'These multitudes of trees, laden with fruits and flowers, fall to the earth, shaken by the winds.
199.003. And this sound is heard, which is exceedingly terrible — clearly a great calamity will befall the city.' //2//

body.text:
199.005. ete bhadraśilānivāsaniratāḥ sarve saduḥkhā janā atyantapratiśokaśalyavihatāḥ praspandakaṇṭhānanāḥ/
199.007. etāścandranibhānanā yuvatayo rodanti veśmottame sarve ca prarudanti tīvrakaruṇāḥ santaḥ śmaśāne yathā//3//
body.translated_text:
199.005. 'These people who delight in dwelling at <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, all afflicted with grief, struck by the arrow of deep sorrow, with trembling throats and faces —
199.007. these young women with moon-like faces weep in the uppermost chambers, and all the good people weep with intense pity, as if in a cremation ground.' //3//

body.text:
199.009. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ puranivāsijanāḥ samagrāḥ saṃpiṇḍitaṃ manasi duḥkhamidaṃ vahanti/
199.011. utkrośatāmaniśamardhakṛtāgrahastairaiśvaryamapratisamaṃ niruṇaddhi vācam//4//
body.translated_text:
199.009. 'For what reason do all the people dwelling in the city bear this accumulated grief in their hearts?
199.011. As they cry out ceaselessly, with their arms half-raised in helplessness, their unequaled sovereignty restrains their speech.' //4//

body.text:
199.013. ete payodā vinadantyatoyā jalāśrayāḥ śokamamī vrajanti/
199.015. bhuvorivāmbhasi ca bālasamīraṇāstā vātāḥ pravānti ca kharā rajasā vimiśrāḥ//5//
body.translated_text:
199.013. 'These clouds thunder without water, these water-reservoirs go into mourning;
199.015. as if from the bowels of the earth, these breezes blow — harsh winds mixed with dust.' //5//

body.text:
199.017. aśivāni nimittāni pravaraṇi hi sāmpratam/
199.018. kṣemāṃ diśamato 'smākamito gantuṃ kṣamo bhavet//6//
body.translated_text:
199.017. 'Truly inauspicious omens are now arising.
199.018. From here it would be proper for us to go in a safe direction.' //6//

body.text:
199.019. api tu khalu māṇavakā rājñaścandraprabhasya caturṣu mahāyajñavāṭeṣu suvarṇabherīṇāṃ tāḍyamānānāṃ na bhūyo manojñaḥ svaro niścarati/
199.020. nūnaṃ bata bhadraśilāyāṃ mahānupadravo bhaviṣyatīti//
body.translated_text:
199.019. 'But indeed, students, from the golden kettledrums being struck at King <s>Candraprabha's</s> four great sacrificial enclosures, the delightful sound no longer issues forth.
199.020. Surely a great calamity will befall <s>Bhadraśilā</s>.'

body.text:
199.021. atha raudrakṣo brāhmaṇo bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāmanuprāptaḥ/
199.021. tato nagaravivāsinī devatā raudrākṣaṃ brahmaṇaṃ dūrādeva dṛṣṭvā yena rājā candraprabhāstenopasaṃkrāntā/
199.022. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ candraprabhamidamavocat--yatkhalu deva jānīyāh--adya devasya yācanaka āgamiṣyati hiṃsako viheṭhako 'vatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī/
199.024. sa devasya śiro yāciṣyatīti/
199.024. taddevena sattvānāmarthāyātmānaṃ paripālayitavyamiti/
199.025. atha rājā candraprabhaḥ śiroyācanakamupaśrutya pramuditamanā vismayotphalladṛṣṭirdevatāmuvāca--gaccha devate, yadyāgamiṣyati, ahamasya dīrghakālābhilaṣitaṃ manorathaṃ paripūrayiṣyamīti/
199.027. atha sā devatā rājñaścandraprabhasya idamevamrūpaṃ vyavasāyaṃ viditvā duḥkhinī durmanaskā vipratisāriṇī tatraivāntarhitā/
199.028. atha rājñaścandraprabhasyaitadabhavat--kimatrāścaryam yadahamannamannārthibhyo 'nuprayacchāmi, pānaṃ pānārthibhyo vastrahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktādīṃs tadarthibhyaḥ/
199.030. yannvaham yācanakebhyaḥ svaśarīramapi parityajeyamiti/
199.030. tato raudrākṣo brāhmaṇo dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa praviśan devatayā nivāritah--gaccha pāpabrāhmaṇa, mā praviśa/
199.031. kathamidānīṃ tvam <200>mohapuruṣa rājñaścandraprabhasya maitrātmakasya kāruṇikasya sattvavatsalasyānekaguṇasampannasya jambudvīpaparipālakasyādūṣiṇo 'napakāriṇaḥ śiraśchetsyasi? raudracitta pāpabrāhmaṇa, mā praviśeti/
body.translated_text:
199.021. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> arrived at the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>.
199.021. The deity dwelling in the city, seeing the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> from afar, approached King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
199.022. Having approached, she said this to King <s>Candraprabha</s>: 'May the lord know — today a petitioner will come to the lord, a harmful one, a troublemaker, one who watches for an opening, one who seeks a vulnerability.
199.024. He will ask for the lord's head.
199.024. Therefore, the lord should protect himself for the sake of all beings.'
199.025. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, hearing about the head-petitioner, with a joyful mind and eyes wide with wonder, said to the deity: 'Go, deity. If he comes, I shall fulfill his long-cherished desire.'
199.027. Then that deity, knowing the resolve of King <s>Candraprabha</s> to be of this nature, unhappy, distressed, and full of remorse, vanished right there.
199.028. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> thought: 'What is so remarkable about my giving food to those who seek food, drink to those who seek drink, clothing, gold, silver, gems, pearls, and the like to those who seek them?
199.030. Let me give even my own body to the petitioners.'
199.030. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>, entering through the southern gate of the city, was stopped by the deity: 'Go, wicked <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, do not enter!
199.031. How can you, deluded man, cut off the head of King <s>Candraprabha</s> — one who is of a benevolent nature, compassionate, tender toward all beings, endowed with many virtues, the protector of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, who has done you no harm and no wrong? Cruel-minded, wicked <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, do not enter!'

body.text:
200.003. yāvadetat prakaraṇaṃ rājñā candraprabheṇa śrutam--yācanako me nagaradvāre devatayā vidhāryate iti/
200.004. śrutvā ca punarmahācandramagrāmātyamāmantrayate--yatkhalu mahācandra jānīyāh--yācanako me nagaradvāri devatayā vidhāryate/
200.005. gaccha, śīghraṃ matsakāśamānayeti/
200.005. evaṃ deveti mahācandro 'grāmātyo rājñaścandraprabhasya pratiśrutya nagaradvāraṃ gatvā tāṃ devatāmuvāca--yatkhalu devate jānīyāh--praviśatveṣa brāhmaṇa, rājā candraprabha enamāhvāpayata iti/
200.007. tato nagaranivāsinī devatā mahācandramagrāmātyamidamavocat--yatkhalu mahācandra jānīyāh--eṣa brāhmaṇo raudracitto niṣkāruṇiko rājñaścandraprabhasya vināśārthaṃ bhadraśilāmanuprāptaḥ/
200.009. kimanena durātmanā praveśitena? eṣa mayā devate upāyaścintito yenāyaṃ brāhmaṇo na prabhaviṣyati devasya śiro grahītumiti/
200.011. atha mahācandro 'grāmātyo raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamādāya nagaraṃ praviśya ratnadharānājñāpayati--ānīyantāṃ bhavanto ratnamayāni śirāṃsi/
200.013. asmai brāhmaṇāya dāsyāmīti/
200.013. bhāṇḍāgārikai ratnamayānāṃ śīrṣāṇāṃ rājadvāre rāśiḥ kṛtaḥ/
200.014. mahācandreṇāgrāmātyena raudrākṣasya ratnamayāni śīrṣāṇyupadarśitāni--pratigṛhṇa tvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa prabhūtāni ratnamayāni śīrṣāṇi/
200.015. yāvadāptaṃ ca te hiraṇyasuvarṇamanuprayacchāmi, yena te putrapautrāṇāṃ jīvikā bhaviṣyati/
200.016. kiṃ te devasya śīrṣeṇa majjāśiṅghāṇakavasādipūrṇeneti? evamukte raudrākṣo brāhmaṇo mahācandramagrāmātyamidamavocat--na ratnamayairme śirobhiḥ prayojanam/
200.018. nāpi hiraṇyasuvarṇena/
200.018. api tvahamasya mahāpṛthivīpālasya sarvaṃdadasya sakāśamāgataḥ śiraso 'rthāya/
200.019. evamukte mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparau vyavasthitau--kimidānīṃ prāptakālamiti/
200.020. athaitadvṛttāntamupaśrutya rājā candraprabho mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau dūreṇa prakrośyaitadavocat--ānīyatāmeṣa matsamīpam/
200.021. ahamasyaivaṃ manorathaṃ pūrayiṣyāmīti/
200.022. evamukte mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau sāśrudurdinavadanau karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevamānau abhirudya devasya maitrātmakasya kāruṇikasya sattvavatsalāsyānekaguṇasamuditasya jñānakuśalasya divyacakṣuṣo 'nityatābalaṃ pratyupasthitam, adyāsmākaṃ devena sārdhaṃ nānābhāvo bhaviṣyati vinābhāvo viprayogo visamyogaḥ/
200.025. iti viditvā rājñaḥ pādayor nipatya ekānte niṣaṇṇau/
200.025. atha rājā candraprabhaḥ paramatyāgaprativiśiṣṭaṃ tyāgaṃ parityakukāmo dūrata eva taṃ brāhmaṇamāmantrayate--ehi tvaṃ brāhmaṇa, yacchatām yat prārthayase tadgṛhāṇeti/
200.027. atha raudrākṣo brāhmaṇo yena rājā candraprabhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
200.028. upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ candraprabhaṃ jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvā rājānaṃ candraprabhamidamavocat--
200.029. dharme sthito 'si vimale śubhabuddhisattva sarvajñatāmabhilaṣan hṛdayena sādho/
200.031. mahyaṃ śiraḥ sṛja mahākaruṇāgracetā mahyaṃ dadasva mama toṣakaro bhavādya//7//
body.translated_text:
200.003. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> heard about this matter — that his petitioner was being detained at the city gate by the deity.
200.004. Having heard, he addressed his chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>: 'Know, <s>Mahācandra</s>, that my petitioner is being detained at the city gate by the deity.
200.005. Go, bring him quickly to me.'
200.005. 'Yes, Your Majesty' — the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>, having assented to King <s>Candraprabha</s>, went to the city gate and said to that deity: 'Know, deity, let this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> enter; King <s>Candraprabha</s> has summoned him.'
200.007. Then the city-dwelling deity said this to the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>: 'Know, <s>Mahācandra</s>, this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is cruel-minded and merciless; he has come to <s>Bhadraśilā</s> for the purpose of destroying King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
200.009. What is to be gained by letting this evil one enter? I have devised a plan, deity, by which this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> will not be able to take the lord's head.'
200.011. Then the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>, taking the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>, entered the city and commanded the jewel-keepers: 'Bring jewel-encrusted heads.
200.013. I shall give them to this <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.'
200.013. The treasury-keepers piled up a heap of jewel-encrusted heads at the royal gate.
200.014. The chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s> showed the jewel-encrusted heads to <s>Raudrākṣa</s>: 'Accept, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, these abundant jewel-encrusted heads.
200.015. And I shall also give you as much gold and silver as will suffice, by which your sons and grandsons will have a livelihood.
200.016. What use is the lord's head to you, filled as it is with marrow, mucus, and fat?' When this was said, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> said this to the chief minister <s>Mahācandra</s>: 'I have no use for jewel-encrusted heads.
200.018. Nor for gold and silver.
200.018. Rather, I have come to this great protector of the earth, this all-giver, for the purpose of obtaining his head.'
200.019. When this was said, the chief ministers <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s>, resting their cheeks on their hands, stood absorbed in thought: 'What is to be done now?'
200.020. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, having heard of this matter, calling out to the chief ministers <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s> from a distance, said: 'Bring him to me.
200.021. I shall fulfill his desire.'
200.022. When this was said, the chief ministers <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s>, with tearful faces like a rainy day, lamenting pitifully, crying aloud — 'The power of impermanence has come upon our lord, who is of a benevolent nature, compassionate, tender toward all beings, endowed with many virtues, skilled in knowledge, possessed of the divine eye.
200.025. Today there will be separation, parting, estrangement, and disunion between us and our lord' — knowing this, they fell at the king's feet and sat to one side.
200.025. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, wishing to relinquish his gift that was supreme in renunciation, addressed that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> from afar: 'Come, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Let it be given; take what you desire.'
200.027. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> approached King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
200.028. Having approached, he congratulated King <s>Candraprabha</s> with victory and long life, and said this to King <s>Candraprabha</s>:
200.029. 'You stand in the stainless <s>Dharma</s>, O being of auspicious wisdom, desiring omniscience with your heart, O virtuous one;
200.031. Grant me your head, O foremost in great compassion — give it to me, and be my joy-giver today!' //7//

body.text:
201.001. <201>atha rājā candraprabho brāhmaṇasyāntikādidamevamrūpaṃ vākpravyāhāraṃ śrutvā pramuditamanāḥ prītivisphāritākṣo raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamuvāca--hantedaṃ brāhmaṇa śiro 'vighnataḥ sādhu pragṛhyatāmuttamāṅgamiti/
201.003. āha ca--
201.004. priyo yathā yadyapi caikaputrakastathāpi me kharpamidaṃ gṛhāṇa/
201.006. tvaccintitānāṃ phalamastu śīghraṃ śiraḥpradānāddhi labheya bodhim//8//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, having heard this manner of speech from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with a joyful mind and eyes wide with delight, said to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>: "Come, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, take this head without hindrance; please accept my <s>uttamāṅga</s> (head)." And he said: "Even as dear as an only son, still, take this skull of mine. May the fruit of your wishes come swiftly; by the gift of my head, may I attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)."

body.text:
201.008. ityuktvā svayameva svaśiraso maulimapanītavān/
201.008. yadā ca rājā candraprabheṇa śiraso maulirapanītaḥ, tatsamanantarameva sarveṣāṃ jambudvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ maulayaḥ patitāḥ/
201.010. bhadraśilāyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ caturdiśamulkāpātā diśodāhāśca prādurbhūtāḥ/
201.010. nagaradevatābhiśca śabdo niścāritah--asya rājñaścandraprabhasya pāpabrāhmaṇo śiraśchetsyatīti/
201.011. tacchrutvā mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau rājñaścandraprabhasyedamevamrūpaṃ śarīraparityāgaṃ viditvā sāśrudurdidavadanau rājñaścandraprabhasya pādau pariṣvajyāhatuh--dhanyāste puruṣā deva ya evamatyadbhutarūpadarśanaṃ vā drakṣyantīri/
201.014. tau abhimukhamudvīkṣyamāṇau rājani candraprabhe cittamabhiprasādya raudrākṣe ca brāhmaṇe maitryacittamutpādya nāvāṃ śakṣyāmo nirupamaguṇādhārāsya devasyānityatāṃ draṣṭumiti tasminneva muhūrte kālagatau/
201.016. kāmadhātumatikramya brāhmalokamupapannau/
201.016. rājñaścandraprabhasyedamevamrūpaṃ vyavasāyaṃ buddhvā tāṃ ca nagaranivāsinīnāṃ devatānāmārtadhvanimupaśrutya bhaumā yakṣā antarikṣacarāśca yakṣāḥ krinditumārabdhāh--hā kaṣṭamidānīṃ rājñaścandraprabhasya śarīranikṣepo bhaviṣyatīti//
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he himself removed the crown from his own head. And when King <s>Candraprabha</s> had removed the crown from his head, at that very instant the crowns of all the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> fell off. In the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, meteors fell in the four directions and the quarters blazed with fire. The city deities cried out: "A wicked <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will cut off the head of King <s>Candraprabha</s>!" Hearing this, <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s>, the chief ministers of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, learning of this manner of bodily self-sacrifice, with tearful, weeping faces, embracing the feet of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, said: "Blessed are those men, O Lord, who will witness such a wondrous sight!" Looking directly at King <s>Candraprabha</s>, having purified their minds toward him, and having generated a thought of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>, saying "We shall not be able to witness the impermanence of our Lord, the repository of incomparable virtues," at that very moment they passed away, transcended the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (realm of desire), and were reborn in <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Having understood this resolve of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, and hearing the anguished cries of the city-dwelling deities, the earthly <s>yakṣas</s> and the sky-roaming <s>yakṣas</s> began to wail: "Alas, how terrible! Now there will be the destruction of King <s>Candraprabha</s>'s body!"

body.text:
201.019. atrāntare ca rājakuladvāre 'nekāni praṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitānyabhūvan/
201.019. tato raudrākṣo brāhmaṇastaṃ mahājanakāyamavekṣya śiro grahītum/
201.021. yadi ca te śiraḥ parityaktam, ekāntaṃ gacchāva iti/
201.022. evamukte rājā candraprabho raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamavocat--evaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa kriyatām/
201.023. ṛddhyantāṃ tava saṃkalpāḥ, paripūryantāṃ manorathā iti/
201.023. atha rājā candraprabho rājā āsanādutthāya tīkṣaṇamasimādāya yena maṇiratnagarbhamudyānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
201.024. atha rājā candraprabhasya idamevamrūpaṃ vyavasāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhadraśilāyāṃ rājadhānyāmanekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi vikrośamānāni pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhāni/
201.026. so 'drākṣīdrājā candraprabho mahājanasaṃnipātaṃ vikrośāntam/
201.026. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ samāśvāsayannāha--apramādaḥ karaṇīyaḥ kuśaleṣu dharmoṣviti/
201.027. saṃkṣepeṇa dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtvā raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamādāya maṇiratnagarbhamudyānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
201.028. samanantarapraviṣṭasya rājñaścandraprabhasya maṇiratnagarbha udyāne bhadraśilāyāṃ chatrāṇi dhvajapatākāśca yena maṇiratnagarbhamudyānaṃ tenāvanāmitāḥ/
201.029. tato rājā candraprabho maṇiratnagarbhasyodyānasya dvāraṃ pidhāya taṃ taṃ raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamāmantrayate--pratigṛhyatāṃ brāhmaṇa mamottamāṅgamiti/
201.031. evamukte raudrākṣo brāhmaṇo rājānaṃ candraprabhamuvāca--nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi devasya śiraśchettumiti/
201.032. maṇiratnagarbhasya codyānasya madhye kurabakaḥ/
201.032. tatra sarvakālikaścampakavṛkṣo<202> jātaḥ/
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, at the gate of the royal palace, many hundreds of thousands of beings had gathered. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>, seeing that great multitude, said he would take the head: "If you have surrendered your head, let us go to a secluded place." Thus addressed, King <s>Candraprabha</s> said to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>: "So be it, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, let it be done. May your intentions be fulfilled, may your desires be satisfied." Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> rose from his throne, took a sharp sword, and proceeded to the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden. Seeing this resolve of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, many hundreds of thousands of beings in the royal capital <s>Bhadraśilā</s>, crying out, followed closely behind him. King <s>Candraprabha</s> saw the great assembly of people wailing. Having seen them, he consoled them, saying: "Diligence must be practiced in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>." Having briefly given a <s>Dharma</s> teaching, he took the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> and entered the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden. As soon as King <s>Candraprabha</s> entered the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden, in <s>Bhadraśilā</s> the parasols, banners, and flags all inclined toward the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, having closed the gate of the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden, addressed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>: "Accept my head, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>." Thus addressed, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s> said to King <s>Candraprabha</s>: "I am not able to cut off the Lord's head." In the middle of the <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden was a <s>kurabaka</s> tree. There, an ever-blooming <s>campaka</s> tree had grown.

body.text:
202.001. tato rājā candraprabhastīkṣṇamasiṃ gṛhītvā yena sarvakālikaścampakavṛkṣastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
202.002. atha yā devatāstasminnudyāne 'dhyavasitāḥ, tā rājñaścandraprabhasyedamevamrūpaṃ svaśarīraparityāgaṃ viditvā vikroṣṭumārabdhāḥ/
202.003. evaṃ cāhuh--kathamidānīṃ tvaṃ pāpabrāhmaṇa rājñaścandraprabhasyādūṣiṇo 'napakāriṇo mahājanavatsalasyānekaguṇasampannasya śiraśchetsyasīti? tato rājā candraprabha udyānadevatā nivārayati--mā devatā mama śiroyācanakasyāntarāyaṃ kuruta/
202.006. tatkasya hetoh? bhūtapūrvaṃ devatā mamottamāṅgam yācanakasya devatāyā antarāyaḥ kṛtaḥ/
202.007. tayā devatayā bahu apuṇyaṃ prasūtam/
202.007. tatkasya detoh? yadi tayā devatayā antarāyo na kṛto 'bhaviṣyat, mayā laghu laghvevānuttarajñānamadhigatamabhaviṣyat/
202.008. ataśca tvāmahamevaṃ bravīmi--mā me tvamuttamāṅgayācanakasyāntarāyaṃ kuruṣveti/
202.009. asminneva te maṇiratnagarbha udyāne mayā sahasraśaḥ śiraḥparityāgaḥ kṛtaḥ, na ca me kenacidantarāyaḥ kṛtaḥ/
202.010. tasmāt tvaṃ devate mamottamāṅgayācanakasyāntarāyaṃ mā kuru/
202.011. eṣa eva devate sa pṛṣṭhībhūto maitreyo yo vyāghryā ātmānaṃ parityajya catvāriṃśatkalpasamprasthito maitreyo bodhisattva ekena śiraḥparityāgenāvapṛṣṭhīkṛtaḥ/
202.013. atha sā devatā rājñaścandraprabhasya maharddhitāmavetya tasmin rājani paraṃ prasādaṃ pravedayantī tūṣṇīmavasthitā/
202.014. atha rājā candraprabhaḥ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ, ye daśādikṣu sthitā devatāsuragaruḍagandharvakinnarā adhyuṣitāḥ, ihāhamudyāne tyāgaṃ kariṣyāmi, asmiṃs tyāgaṃ svaśiraḥparityāgam yena cāhaṃ satyena svaśiraḥ parityajāmi, na rājyārthāya na svargārthāya na bhogārthāya na śakratvāya na brahmatvāya na cakravartivijayāya nānyatra kathamahamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambuddhya adāntān sattvān damayeyam, aśāntāñ śamayeyam, atīrṇāṃstārayeyam, amuktān mocayeyam, anāśvastānāśvāsayeyam, aparinirvṛtān parinirvāpayeyam/
202.020. anena satyena satyavacanena saphalaḥ pariśramaḥ syāt, parinirvṛtāsya ca sarṣapaphalapramāṇadhātavo bhaveyuḥ, asya ca maṇiratnagarbhasyodyānasya madhye mahān stūpaḥ syāt sarvastūpaprativiśiṣṭaḥ/
202.022. ye ca sattvāḥ śāntakāyā mahācaityaṃ vanditukāmā gaccheyuḥ, te taṃ sarvastūpaprativiśiṣṭaṃ dhātuparaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśrāntā bhaveyuḥ/
202.023. parinirvṛtasyāpi mama caityeṣu, janakāyā āgatya kārāṃ kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyāṇā bhaveyuriti/
202.024. evaṃ samyak praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā tasmiṃścampakavṛkṣe śikhāṃ baddhvā raudrākṣaṃ brāhmaṇamuvāca--āgaccha mahābrāhmaṇa, pratigṛhyatām/
202.026. mā me vighnaṃ kuruṣveti/
202.027. tato rājā candraprabha ātmanaḥ kāyasya sthāma ca balaṃ ca saṃjanya tasmiṃśca brāhmaṇe karuṇāsahagataṃ maitracittamutpādya śiraśichattvā raudrākṣāya brāhmaṇāya niryātitavān/
202.028. kālaṃ ca kṛtvā atikramya brahmalokaṃ praṇītatvācchubhakṛtsne devanikāye upapannaḥ/
202.029. samanantaraparityakte rājñā candraprabheṇa śirasi ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātus triḥ kampitaḥ saṃkampitaḥ saṃprakampitaḥ, calitaḥ saṃcalitaḥ saṃpracalitaḥ, vyadhitaḥ pravyādhitaḥ saṃpravyādhitaḥ/
202.031. gaganatalasthāśca devatā divyānyutpalāni kṣeptumārabdhāḥ, padmāni kumudāni puṇḍarīkānyagarucūrṇāni tagaracūrṇāni candanacūrṇāni tamālapatrāṇi divyāni <203>māndāravāṇi puṣpāṇi, divyāni ca vādyāni pravādayitmārabdhāḥ, cailavikṣepāṃśca cākarṣuḥ/
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, taking the sharp sword, approached the ever-blooming <s>campaka</s> tree. The deities who dwelt in that garden, learning of this manner of King <s>Candraprabha</s>'s self-sacrifice of his own body, began to cry out. And they said: "How can you, wicked <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, cut off the head of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, who is blameless, who has done no harm, who is compassionate to all people, and who is endowed with countless virtues?" Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> restrained the garden deities: "Do not, O deities, create an obstacle to the one who requests my head. For what reason? In the past, a deity created an obstacle for one requesting my head. That deity produced much <s>apuṇya</s> (demerit). For what reason? If that deity had not created the obstacle, I would have quickly, very quickly attained supreme knowledge. Therefore I say to you: do not create an obstacle for the one who requests my head. In this very <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden, I have sacrificed my head a thousand times, and no one has created an obstacle for me. Therefore, O deity, do not create an obstacle for the one who requests my head. This very thing, O deity, caused <s>Maitreya</s> to fall behind — he who sacrificed himself to the tigress and had set out forty <s>kalpas</s> ahead; <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> was surpassed by a single act of head-sacrifice." Then that deity, recognizing the great spiritual power of King <s>Candraprabha</s>, experiencing supreme faith in that king, remained silent. Then King <s>Candraprabha</s> began to make his solemn vow: "Let those hear who dwell in the ten directions — <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s> — here in this garden I shall make the sacrifice, this sacrifice of my own head. By this truth with which I sacrifice my own head: it is not for the sake of kingship, not for the sake of heaven, not for the sake of enjoyments, not for <s>Śakra</s>-hood, not for <s>Brahma</s>-hood, not for the victory of a <s>cakravartin</s>, but solely that, having attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), I may tame the untamed beings, pacify the unpeaceful, ferry across those who have not crossed, liberate the unliberated, console the unconsoled, and bring to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. By this truth, by this truthful speech, may my toil bear fruit; and when I have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, may my relics become the size of mustard seeds, and in the middle of this <s>Maṇiratnagarbha</s> garden may there be a great <s>stūpa</s>, the most excellent of all <s>stūpas</s>. And may those beings of peaceful body who come wishing to honor the great <s>caitya</s>, seeing that most excellent of all <s>stūpas</s>, supreme in relics, find rest. And even after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, may the people who come to my <s>caityas</s> and make offerings be destined for heaven and liberation." Having thus made his solemn vow, he tied his hair to that <s>campaka</s> tree and said to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>: "Come, great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, accept it. Do not create an obstacle for me." Then King <s>Candraprabha</s>, generating strength and power in his own body, and producing a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) accompanied by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) toward that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, cut off his head and presented it to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>. And having died, transcending <s>Brahmaloka</s>, due to the excellence of his merit, he was reborn in the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Wholly Beautiful) divine abode. At the very moment King <s>Candraprabha</s> sacrificed his head, this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (three-thousandfold great-thousandfold world-system) trembled, shook, and quaked; moved, shifted, and swayed; shuddered, convulsed, and was violently agitated. The deities stationed in the sky began to cast divine <s>utpalas</s> (blue lotuses), <s>padmas</s> (lotuses), <s>kumudas</s> (white water-lilies), <s>puṇḍarīkas</s> (white lotuses), <s>agaru</s> (aloe) powder, <s>tagara</s> (fragrant bark) powder, <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) powder, <s>tamālapatras</s> (bay leaves), and divine <s>Māndārava</s> flowers; they began to play divine instruments and waved their garments.

body.text:
203.002. tato raudrākṣo brāhmaṇaḥ śirograhāyodyānānnirgataḥ/
203.002. athāsminnantare 'nekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair nādo muktah--hā kaṣṭam/
203.003. praghātito devaḥ sarvajanamanorathaparipūraka iti/
203.003. tata ekatyāḥ pṛthivyāmāvartante parivartante, eke bāhubhiḥ prakrośanti, kāścit prakīrṇakeśyo rudanti/
203.004. anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni/
203.005. tata ekatyāstasminneva pradeśe sthitvā dhyānānyutpādya tatraiva kālaṃ kṛtvā śubhakṛtsne devanikāye upapannā rājñaścandraprabhasya sabhāgatāyām/
203.006. apare dhyānānyutpādya tatraiva kālaṃ kṛtvā bhāsvare devanikāye upapannāḥ/
203.007. apare prathamadhyānamutpādya kālaṃ kṛtvā brahmalokasabhāgatāyāmupapannāḥ/
203.008. aparaiḥ saṃnipātya rājñaścandraprabhasya śarīraṃ sarvagandhakāṣṭhaiścitāṃ citvā, dhmāpitāni ca asthīni sauvarṇakumbhe prakṣipya, caturmahāpathe śarīrastūpaḥ pratiṣṭāpitaḥ/
203.010. chatradhvajapatākāścāropitāḥ/
203.010. gandhairmālyairdhūpairdīpaiḥ puṣpaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā candraprabhe rājani svacittamabhiprasādya kālagatāḥ ṣaṭsu devanikāyeṣu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣūpapannāḥ/
203.012. yaiśca tatra kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, sarve te svargamokṣaparāyaṇāḥ saṃvṛttā iti//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Raudrākṣa</s>, having taken the head, departed from the garden. At that moment, a cry was raised by many hundreds of thousands of beings: "Alas, how terrible! The Lord, the fulfiller of all people's desires, has been slain!" Then some rolled upon the ground, some struck their arms and cried out, and some women wept with their hair disheveled. Many hundreds of thousands of beings had gathered. Then some, standing at that very spot, generated the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), died right there, and were reborn in the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Wholly Beautiful) divine abode, in the same company as King <s>Candraprabha</s>. Others generated the <s>dhyānas</s>, died right there, and were reborn in the <s>Bhāsvara</s> (Radiant) divine abode. Others generated the first <s>dhyāna</s>, died, and were reborn in the company of <s>Brahmaloka</s>. Others gathered together, built a funeral pyre for King <s>Candraprabha</s>'s body with all manner of fragrant woods, placed the cremated bones in a golden urn, and at the crossroads of four great roads established a <s>śarīra-stūpa</s> (reliquary shrine). Parasols, banners, and flags were raised. Having made offerings with perfumes, garlands, incense, lamps, and flowers, purifying their minds toward King <s>Candraprabha</s>, they passed away and were reborn among the gods of the six <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire-realm) divine abodes. And all those who made offerings there became destined for heaven and liberation.

body.text:
203.013. syātkhalu yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā anyā sā tena kālena samayenottarāpathe bhadraśilā nāma rājadhānyabhūditi/
203.014. na khalu evaṃ draṣṭvyam/
203.014. tatkasya hetoh? eṣaiva sā takṣaśilā tena kālena tena samayena bhadraśilā nāma rājadhānī babhūva/
203.015. syātkhalu yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayenottarāpathe bhadraśilā nāma rājadhānyabhūditi/
203.014. na khalu evaṃ draṣṭavyam/
203.014. tatkasya hetoh? eṣaiva sā takṣaśilā tena kālena tena samayena bhadraśilā nāma rājadhānī babhūva/
203.015. syātkhalu yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣuvaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena candraprabho nāma rājābhūditi/
203.017. na khalu evaṃ draṣṭavyam/
203.017. tatkasya hetoh? ahameva tena kālena tena samayena rājā candraprabho babhūva/
203.018. syātkhalu yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena raudrākṣo nāma brāhmaṇo 'bhūditi/
203.019. na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
203.019. tatkasya hetoh? eṣa eva sa tena kālena tena samayena devadatto babhūva/
203.020. syātkhalu yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyau tau tena samayena mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau babhūvaturiti/
203.020. na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
203.022. tatkasya hetoh? etāveva mahācandramahīdharau agrāmātyau śāriputramaudgalyāyanau babhūvatuḥ/
203.023. tadāpyetau tatprathamataḥ kālagatau, na tveva putṛmaraṇamārāgitavantau iti//
body.translated_text:
203.013. 'Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt or uncertainty, thinking: "That royal capital in the northern region named Bhadraśilā at that time was someone else's."
203.014. It should not be seen thus.
203.014. Why? That very <s>Takṣaśilā</s> was at that time the royal capital named <s>Bhadraśilā</s>.
203.015. Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt or uncertainty, thinking: "That royal capital in the northern region named Bhadraśilā at that time was someone else's."
203.014. It should not be seen thus.
203.014. Why? That very <s>Takṣaśilā</s> was at that time the royal capital named <s>Bhadraśilā</s>.
203.015. Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt or uncertainty, thinking: "That King <s>Candraprabha</s> at that time was someone else."
203.017. It should not be seen thus.
203.017. Why? I myself at that time was King <s>Candraprabha</s>.
203.018. Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt or uncertainty, thinking: "That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Raudrākṣa</s> at that time was someone else."
203.019. It should not be seen thus.
203.019. Why? He at that time was none other than <s>Devadatta</s>.
203.020. Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt or uncertainty, thinking: "Those two chief ministers <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s> at that time were others."
203.020. It should not be seen thus.
203.022. Why? Those two chief ministers <s>Mahācandra</s> and <s>Mahīdhara</s> were none other than <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.
203.023. Even then, these two died first, and yet they did not indulge in grief over the death of a son.'

body.text:
203.024. idamavocadbhagavān/
203.024. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo 'nye ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
203.024. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
203.024. Delighted, those monks and the other gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 203.026. candraprabhabodhisattvacaryāvadānaṃ nāma dvāviṃśatimam/
body.translated_text: 203.026. This is the twenty-second: the <s>Candraprabhabodhisattvacaryāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Bodhisattva Conduct of <s>Candraprabha</s>).

body.text: after this, ṃss. add:
body.translated_text: After this, the manuscripts add:

body.text:
tathā ca candraprabhabhūpatirbhūte
maṇikanakarajatavaiḍrruyendranīlādidraviṇavasanayānabhojanālāṃkāragrāmanagaranigamaviṣayarājyādayo
rājyarathasutakalatramāṃsarudhirakaracaraṇaśirokṣigrīvādisarvaparityāgamantareṇa
durgatijananamaraṇajarākaracaraṇakaraṇavikalatāpriyaviyogāditaraduḥkhopanipātabhayābhihatajanaparitrāṇakaraṇasamarthā
sakalabhuvanādhipatyābhiṣekamahatī gāthādhunī guṇasamṛddhir na
śakyate 'dhigantumiti
kāruṇyādaśeṣajagadduḥkhopaśamakṛtaniścayah
praṇatasakalasāmantacūḍāmaṇimayūkhāvicchuritapādapīṭhah
turagagajarathavastrālaṃkārādiparityāgena
parīpūritaniravaśeṣajāmbūdvīpakajanamanorathah
sakalajanamanonayanahārī śiraḥ parityaktavān/
kathamityevamanuśrūyate iti//
body.translated_text: And so, when <s>Candraprabha</s> was king, without the renunciation of all — jewels, gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, sapphire, and other wealth, garments, vehicles, food, ornaments, villages, cities, towns, territories, kingdoms, royal chariots, sons, wives, flesh, blood, hands, feet, head, eyes, neck, and all else — it is impossible to attain the great consecration of sovereignty over all worlds, the great river of verses, the fullness of virtues, which is capable of rescuing people afflicted by the terrors of miserable birth, death, old age, mutilation of hands and feet, crippling, separation from loved ones, and the onslaught of other sufferings. Therefore, out of compassion, having resolved to alleviate the suffering of the entire world without remainder, with the rays of the crest-jewels of all bowing vassal kings illuminating his footstool, having fulfilled the wishes of all the people of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> by the renunciation of horses, elephants, chariots, garments, ornaments, and the like, captivating the minds and eyes of all people — he gave up his head. Thus it is traditionally heard.

body.text: 204.001. div23 saṅgharakSitāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 204.001. Chapter 23: The <s>Saṅgharakṣitāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>).

body.text:
204.002. kiṃ mahāllenādhigatam? ekottarikā/
204.002. ayaṃ tāvat khustikayā ekottarikayā dharmaṃ deśayati--amī bhikṣavo dharmakathikā yuṃktamutkamuktapratibhānāḥ/
204.003. kasmānnaitānadhyeṣayasi? sa tairabhihitah--mahalla, kiṃ tvayā adhigatam? sa kathayati--ekottarikā/
204.004. te kathayanti--tvaṃ tāvanmahalla khustikayā ekottarikayā dharmaṃ deśayasi/
204.005. amī bhikṣavastṛpitā dharmakathikā yuktamuktapratibhānāḥ/
204.006. kasmānnaitānadhyeṣayasi? sa kathayati--āryāḥ, yūyaṃ kasyārthe na deśayata? kimahaṃ nivārayāmīti? te kathayanti--nandopananda, prativadatyeṣo 'smākaṃ mahallaḥ/
204.007. kuruta asyotkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma/
204.008. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi me utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kariṣyanti, nāgabhavane 'pyahamavakāśaṃ na lapsye/
204.009. sa teṣāṃ śayitakānāṃ taṃ vihāramantarhāpayitvā mahāsamudraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
204.009. te vālukāsthale śayitakāstiṣṭhanti/
204.010. nandopananda, uttiṣṭha siṃhāsanaṃ prajñāpaya, dharmaṃ deśayāmaḥ/
204.010. te kathayanti--ko 'pyasau devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā bhagavatyabhiprasanno buddhe dharme saṃghe kārān kurvan, so 'smābhirviheṭhitaḥ/
204.012. etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti/
204.012. bhagavānāha--yo 'sau bhikṣavo nirmito yadi ṣaḍvargikairbhikṣubhir na viheṭhito 'bhaviṣyat, yāvacchāsanakoṭimuddhāṭako buddhe dharme saṃghe kārānakariṣyat/
204.014. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--yaḥ kaścidādīnavo bhikṣavaḥ, anadhīṣṭo dharmaṃ deśayati, tasmānna bhikṣuṇā^nadhīṣṭena dharmo deśayitavyaḥ/
204.015. bhikṣuranadhīṣṭo dharmaṃ deśayati, sātisāro bhavati/
204.016. anāpattayastanmukhikayā nirgatā bhavanti//
body.translated_text:
204.002. 'What has the elder attained?' '<s>Ekottarikā</s> (the Numerical Discourses).'
204.002. 'This one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> with a mere smattering of the <s>Ekottarikā</s> — while these monks are <s>Dharma</s>-preachers of ready, fluent eloquence.
204.003. Why do you not invite them?' They said to him: 'Elder, what have you attained?' He said: 'The <s>Ekottarikā</s>.'
204.004. They said: 'You, elder, teach the <s>Dharma</s> with a mere smattering of the <s>Ekottarikā</s>.
204.005. These monks are accomplished <s>Dharma</s>-preachers of ready, fluent eloquence.
204.006. Why do you not invite them?' He said: 'Noble ones, why do you yourselves not teach? Am I preventing you?' They said: '<s>Nandopananda</s>, this elder talks back to us.
204.007. Let us perform the act of suspension against him.'
204.008. He reflected: 'If they perform the act of suspension against me, I will find no refuge even in the <s>Nāga</s> realm.'
204.009. While they were sleeping, he caused that monastery to vanish and entered the great ocean.
204.009. They found themselves lying on a sand-bank.
204.010. '<s>Nandopananda</s>, get up, set up the lion-throne — let us teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'
204.010. They said: 'Some god or <s>Nāga</s> or <s>Yakṣa</s>, devoted to the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, performing services — we have harassed him.'
204.012. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.
204.012. The Blessed One said: 'O monks, if that created being had not been harassed by the group-of-six monks, he would have performed services to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> until the end of the teaching.'
204.014. The Blessed One reflected: 'Monks, there is this danger — one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> without being invited. Therefore, a monk should not teach the <s>Dharma</s> without being invited.
204.015. A monk who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> without being invited commits an offense.
204.016. Those who go out face-to-face are not at fault.'

body.text:
204.017. śrāvastyāṃ buddharakṣito nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ/
204.017. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
204.018. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍate ramate paricārayati/
204.018. tasya krīḍato ramataḥ paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
204.019. āyuṣmāñ śāriputro vaineyāpekṣayā tatkulamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
204.020. tena sa gṛhapatiḥ sapatnīkaḥ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadeṣu pratikṣṭhāpitaḥ/
204.020. apareṇa samayena sā tasya patnī āpannasattvā savṛttā/
204.021. āyuṣmāñ śāriputrastasya ca vaineyakālaṃ jñātvā ekākyeva tat kulamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
204.022. sa gṛhapatiḥ kathayati--nāstyāryaśāriputrasya kaścit paścācchramaṇah? sa kathayati--gṛhapate, kimasmākaṃ kāśadhānādvā kuśadhānādvā paścācchramaṇā bhavanti? api tu ye bhavadvidhānāṃ sakāśāllabhyante, asmākaṃ te paścācchramaṇā bhavanti/
204.025. buddharakṣito gṛhapatih--ārya, mama patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
204.025. yadi putraṃ janayiṣyati, tamahamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmi/
204.026. sa kathayati--gṛhapate, aupayikam//
body.translated_text:
204.017. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there dwelt a householder named <s>Buddharakṣita</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions.
204.017. He took a wife from an equal family.
204.018. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her.
204.018. While he was sporting, delighting, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant.
204.019. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, out of regard for those to be guided, visited that household.
204.020. He established that householder and his wife in the refuges and the training rules.
204.020. On another occasion, his wife became pregnant.
204.021. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, knowing the time for their guidance, visited that household alone.
204.022. The householder said: 'Does the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> have no attendant monk?' He replied: 'Householder, do our attendant monks come from grass-sheds or reed-sheds? Rather, those obtained from the likes of you become our attendant monks.'
204.025. The householder <s>Buddharakṣita</s> said: 'Noble sir, my wife is pregnant.
204.025. If she bears a son, I shall give him to the noble one as an attendant monk.'
204.026. He said: 'Householder, that is fitting.'

body.text:
204.027. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām {atyayāt} prasūtā/
204.027. dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāsaḥ/
204.029. tasya jñātayaḥ saṃgamya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasāni vistareṇa jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpayanti--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma? ayaṃ dārako buddharakṣitasya gṛhapateḥ putraḥ/
204.031. bhavatu dārakasya saṃgharakṣito nāma/
204.031. yasminneva divase saṃgharakṣito jātaḥ, tasminneva divase pañcānāṃ vaṇikśatānāṃ pañca putraśatāni jātāni/
204.032. teṣāmapi kulasadṛśāni <205>nāmadheyāni vyavasthāpitāni/
body.translated_text:
204.027. After eight or nine months, she gave birth.
204.027. A boy was born — handsome, beautiful, pleasing, fair, golden-complexioned, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, joined brows, and a prominent nose.
204.029. His relatives gathered, and for three periods of seven — twenty-one days — they celebrated his birth festival in grand style and established his name: 'What shall be the boy's name? This boy is the son of the householder <s>Buddharakṣita</s>.
204.031. Let the boy's name be <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>.'
204.031. On the very day <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> was born, five hundred sons were born to five hundred merchant families.
204.032. Names befitting their families were established for them as well.

body.text:
205.001. saṃgharakṣito dāraka unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
205.002. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam/
205.003. yadā mahān samṛttaḥ, tadā āyuṣmāñ śāriputrastasya vaineyakālaṃ jñātvā ekākyeva tatkulamupasaṃkramya nimittamupadarśayitumārabdhaḥ/
205.004. buddharakṣitena gṛhapatinā saṃgharakṣito 'bhihitah--putra, ajāta eva tvaṃ mayā āryaśāriputrasya paścācchramaṇo datta iti/
205.006. caramabhavikaḥ sa āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa pravrājita upasampādita āgamacatuṣṭayaṃ ca grāhitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
205.001. The boy <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> was raised and nourished with milk, curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other specially prepared provisions.
205.002. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.
205.003. When he had grown up, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, knowing the time for his guidance, visited that household alone and began to show signs.
205.004. The householder <s>Buddharakṣita</s> said to <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>: 'Son, even before you were born, I gave you to the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> as an attendant monk.'
205.006. He was one in his last existence. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> ordained him, gave him full ordination, and taught him the four <s>Āgamas</s>.

body.text:
205.007. athāpareṇa samayena tāni pañca vaṇikśatāni mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānīya mahāsamudramavatartukāmāni kathayanti--kiṃcidvayaṃ bhavanta āryakamavatārayāma yo 'smākaṃ mahāsaudramadhyagatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati/
205.009. te kathayati--bhavantaḥ, ayamasmākamāryasaṃgharakṣito vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanakaḥ/
205.010. etamevāvatārayāmaḥ/
205.010. te tasya sakāśamupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
205.010. ārya saṃgharakṣita, tvamasmākaṃ vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanakaḥ/
205.011. vayaṃ ca mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
205.012. tvamapyasmābhiḥ sārdhamavatara, samudramadhyagatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyasi/
205.012. sa kathayati--nāhaṃ svādhīnaḥ/
205.013. upādhyāyamavalokayata/
205.013. te yenāyuṣmāñ śāriputrastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
205.013. upasaṃkramya kathayanti--ārya śāriputra, ayamasmākamāryasaṃgharakṣito vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanakaḥ/
205.014. vayaṃ mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
205.015. eṣo 'pyasmābhiḥ sārdhamavataratu, asmākaṃ mahāsamudramadhyagatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati/
205.016. sa kathayati--bhagavantamavalokayata/
205.016. te bhagavataḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
205.016. bhagavan, vayaṃ mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitāḥ/
205.017. ayamasmākamāryasaṃgharakṣito vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanakaḥ/
205.018. eṣo 'pyasmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ mahāsamudramavataratu/
205.018. asmākaṃ mahāsamudramadhyagatānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati/
205.019. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--astyeṣāṃ kānicit kuśalamūlāni? asti/
205.019. kasyāntike pratibuddhāni? saṃgharakṣitasya bhikṣoḥ/
205.020. tatra bhagavān saṃgharakṣitamāmantrayate--gaccha saṃgharakṣita, bhayabhairavasahiṣṇunā bhavitavyam/
205.021. adhivāsayatyāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito bhagavatastūṣṇībhāveṇa//
body.translated_text:
205.007. On another occasion, those five hundred merchants, having gathered merchandise suitable for an ocean voyage, wishing to set out to sea, said: 'Let us, sirs, take along some noble one who will teach us the <s>Dharma</s> when we are in the midst of the great ocean.'
205.009. They said: 'Sirs, this noble <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> is our companion, born on the same day, our childhood playmate.
205.010. Let us take him along.'
205.010. They approached him.
205.010. 'Noble <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>, you are our companion, born on the same day, our childhood playmate.
205.011. We are setting out for the great ocean.
205.012. Come down with us too; you will teach us the <s>Dharma</s> when we are in the midst of the ocean.'
205.012. He said: 'I am not my own master.
205.013. Consult my preceptor.'
205.013. They approached the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.
205.013. Approaching, they said: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, this noble <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> is our companion, born on the same day, our childhood playmate.
205.014. We are setting out for the great ocean.
205.015. Let him come down with us too; he will teach us the <s>Dharma</s> when we are in the midst of the great ocean.'
205.016. He said: 'Consult the Blessed One.'
205.016. They approached the Blessed One.
205.016. 'Blessed One, we are setting out for the great ocean.
205.017. This noble <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> is our companion, born on the same day, our childhood playmate.
205.018. Let him come down with us too into the great ocean.
205.018. He will teach us the <s>Dharma</s> when we are in the midst of the great ocean.'
205.019. The Blessed One reflected: 'Do these people have any roots of merit? They do.
205.019. Under whose guidance will they be awakened? Under the monk <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>.'
205.020. Then the Blessed One addressed <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>: 'Go, <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s>; you must be one who endures fear and terror.'
205.021. The Venerable <s>Saṅgharakṣita</s> assented to the Blessed One by silence.

body.text:
205.023. atha tāni pañca vaṇikśatāni kṛtakautukamaṅgalasvastyayanāni śakṭairbhārairmūḍhaiḥ piṭakairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiḥ prabhūtaṃ paṇyamāropya mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitāni/
205.025. te nipuṇataḥ samudrayānapātraṃ pratipadya mahāsamudramavatīrṇā dhanahārakāḥ/
205.026. teṣāṃ mahāsamudramadhyagatānāṃ nāgairvahanaṃ vidhāritam/
205.027. te devatāyācanaṃ kartumārabdhāh--yo 'smin mahāsamudre devo vā nāgo vā yakṣo vā prativasati, sa ācakṣatu kiṃ mṛgayatīti/
205.028. mahāsamudrācchabdo niścarati--āryasaṃgharakṣitamasmākamanuprayacchatheti/
205.029. te kathayati--āryasaṃgharakṣito 'smākaṃ vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanako bhadantaśāriputreṇānupradattako bhagavatānuparītakaḥ/
205.030. śreyo 'smākamanenaiva sārdhaṃ kālatriyā, na tvena vayaṃ saṃgharakṣitaṃ parityakṣyāmaḥ/
205.031. te mantrayante āyuṣmatā saṃgharakṣitena śrutāḥ/
205.032. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kiṃ kathayante? kathayanti--ārya saṃgharakṣita mahāsamudrācchabdo <206>niścaritah--āryasaṃgharakṣitamasmākamanuprayacchatheti/
body.translated_text:
205.023. Then those five hundred merchants, having performed auspicious rites, blessings, and benedictions, loaded abundant merchandise onto carts, pack-loads, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, and set out for the great ocean.
205.025. Having skillfully boarded the ocean-going vessel, those seekers of wealth descended into the great ocean.
205.026. When they had reached the middle of the great ocean, their vessel was held fast by <s>Nāgas</s>.
205.027. They began to make supplications to the deities: 'Whichever god, <s>Nāga</s>, or <s>Yakṣa</s> dwells in this great ocean, let him declare what he seeks.'
205.028. A voice issued from the great ocean: 'Hand over to us the noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.'
205.029. They said: 'The noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> is our companion, born together with us, our childhood playmate, entrusted to us by the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, and watched over by the Blessed One.
205.030. Better for us to die together with him — we shall not abandon <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.'
205.031. Their deliberations were heard by the venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.
205.032. He said: 'Sirs, what are you discussing?' They said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, a voice has issued from the great ocean <206>: "Hand over to us the noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>."'

body.text:
206.001. sa kathayati--kasmānnānuprayacchadhvam? te kathayanti--ārya, tvamasmākaṃ vayasyakaḥ sahajanmikaḥ sahapāṃśukrīḍanakaḥ/
206.002. bhadantaśāriputreṇānupradattako bhagavatānupradattakaḥ/
206.003. śreyo 'smākaṃ tvayaiva sārdhaṃ kālakriyā/
206.003. na tveva vayamārya saṃgharakṣita tvāṃ parityakṣyāmaḥ/
206.004. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ saṃlakṣayati--yaduktaṃ bhagavatā bhayabhairavasahiṣṇunā te bhavitavyamitīdaṃ tat/
206.005. sa pātracīvaraṃ gṛhītvā ātmānaṃ mahāsamudre prakṣeptumārabdhaḥ/
206.006. sa tairdṛṣṭaḥ/
206.006. te kathayanti--āryasaṃgharakṣita kiṃ karoṣi, āryasaṃgharakṣita kiṃ karoṣīti/
206.006. sa teṣa vikrośatāṃ mahāsamudre prapatitaḥ/
206.007. muktaṃ tadvahanam/
206.007. sa nāgairgṛhītvā nāgabhavanaṃ praveśitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
206.001. He said: 'Why do you not hand me over?' They said: 'Noble one, you are our companion, born together with us, our childhood playmate.
206.002. You were entrusted to us by the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and by the Blessed One.
206.003. Better for us to die together with you.
206.003. We shall never abandon you, noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.'
206.004. The venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> reflected: 'What was said by the Blessed One — "You must be one who endures fear and terror" — this is that very occasion.'
206.005. Taking his bowl and robe, he began to throw himself into the great ocean.
206.006. They saw him.
206.006. They cried: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, what are you doing? Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, what are you doing?'
206.006. While they were crying out, he plunged into the great ocean.
206.007. The vessel was released.
206.007. Seized by the <s>Nāgas</s>, he was brought into the <s>Nāga</s> realm.

body.text:
206.008. ārya saṃgharakṣita, iyaṃ vipaśyitaḥ samyaksambuddhasya gandhakuṭī/
206.008. iyaṃ śikhino viśvabhuvaḥ krakucchandasya kanakamuneḥ kāśyapasyeyaṃ bhagavato gandhakuṭī/
206.009. ārya saṃgharakṣita, bhagavataḥ sūtraṃ mātṛkā ca devamanuṣyeṣu pratiṣṭhitam/
206.010. vayaṃ nāgā vinipatitaśarīrāḥ/
206.010. aho bata, āryaḥ saṃghāṃ rakṣita ihāpyāgamacatuṣṭayaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet/
206.011. sa kathayati--evaṃ bhavatu/
206.011. tena trayo nāgkumārā utsāhitāḥ/
206.012. eko 'bhihitah--tvaṃ tāvat samyuktakamadhīṣva/
206.012. dvitīyo 'bhihitah--tvamapi madhyamam/
206.013. tṛtīyo 'bhihitah--tvamapi dīrghamamadhīṣva/
206.013. sa kathayati--ahamapi tāmevaikottarikāṃ vimṛṣṭarūpāṃ prajvālayāmi/
206.014. te 'dhyetumārabdhāḥ/
206.014. tatraikaścakṣuṣī nimīliyatvodveśaṃ gṛhṇāti, dvitīyaḥ pṛṣṭhatomukha uddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti, tṛtīyo dūrataḥ sthitvoddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti/
206.015. sa eva teṣāmekaḥ sagauravaḥ sapratīśa iti karaṇīyaiśca sarvatra pūrvaṃgamaḥ/
206.016. ārya uttiṣṭha, dantakāṣṭha, dantakāṣṭhaṃ visarjaya, bhagavato maṇḍalakamāmārjaya, caityābhivandanaṃ kuru, bhuṅkṣva, śayyāṃ kalpayeti/
206.017. sarvaistairāgamānyadhītāni/
206.018. sa kathayati--ārya, adhītānyebhirāgamāni/
206.018. kiṃ dhārayiṣyanti āhosvinnadhārayiṣyanti? sa kathayati--smṛtimattakā hyete dhārayiṣyanti, api tu doṣo 'styeṣām/
206.019. sa kathayati--ārya, ko doṣah? sarve hyete 'gauravā apratīśāḥ/
206.020. ekastāvaccakṣuṣī nimīlayitvodveśaṃ gṛhṇāti, dvitīyaḥ pṛṣṭatomukha uddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti, tṛtīyo dūrataḥ sthitvoddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti/
206.021. tvamevaikaḥ sagauravaḥ sapratīśa iti karaṇīyaiśca sarvatra pūrvaṃgamaḥ/
206.022. sa kathayati--ārya, na hyete 'gauravā apratīśāḥ/
206.023. yastāvadayaṃ cakṣuṣī nimīlayitvoddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti, ayaṃ dṛṣṭiviṣaḥ/
206.023. yo 'pyayaṃ pṛṣṣṭhatomukha uddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti, eṣo 'pi śvāsaviṣaḥ/
206.024. yo 'pyeṣa dūrataḥ sthitvoddeśaṃ gṛhṇāti, eṣo 'pi sparśaviṣaḥ/
206.025. ahameko daṃṣṭrāviṣaḥ/
206.025. sa bhīta utpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukaḥ kṛśāluko durbalako mlānako 'prāptakāyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
206.026. sa kathayati--ārya, kasmāt tvamutpāṇḍūtpāṇḍukaḥ kṛśāluko durbalako mlānako 'prāptakāyaḥ saṃvṛttah? sa kathayati--bhadramukha, amitramadhye 'haṃ vāsaṃ kalpayāmi/
206.028. sacet yuṣmākamanyatamo 'nyatamaṃ prakupyeta, māṃ nāmāvaśeṣaṃ kuryāt/
206.028. sa kathayati--āryāsya vayaṃ na praharāmaḥ/
206.029. api tu icchasi tvaṃ jambudvīpaṃ gantum? bhadramukha, icchāmi/
206.030. tacca vahanamāgatam/
206.030. sa tairutkṣiptaḥ//
body.translated_text:
206.008. 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, this is the perfumed chamber of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>.
206.008. This is of <s>Śikhin</s>; of <s>Viśvabhū</s>; of <s>Krakucchanda</s>; of <s>Kanakamuni</s>; of <s>Kāśyapa</s>; this is the perfumed chamber of the Blessed One.'
206.009. 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, the <s>sūtras</s> (discourses) and the <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrix of doctrines) of the Blessed One have been established among gods and humans.
206.010. We <s>Nāgas</s> are beings with fallen bodies.
206.010. Oh, if only the noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> would establish here as well the four collections of scriptures!'
206.011. He said: 'So be it.'
206.011. He then encouraged three young <s>Nāga</s> princes.
206.012. To one he said: 'You shall study the <s>Saṃyuktaka</s> (Connected Discourses).'
206.012. To the second he said: 'You shall study the <s>Madhyama</s> (Middle-length Discourses).'
206.013. To the third he said: 'You shall study the <s>Dīrgha</s> (Long Discourses).'
206.013. He said: 'And I shall polish and illuminate the <s>Ekottarika</s> (Numerical Discourses) myself.'
206.014. They began to study.
206.014. Among them, one closed his eyes while receiving instruction; the second turned his back while receiving instruction; the third stood far away while receiving instruction.
206.015. Only this one was respectful, attentive, and foremost in all duties.
206.016. 'Noble one, get up; here is a tooth-stick; discard the tooth-stick; sweep the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of the Blessed One; perform veneration of the <s>caitya</s>; eat; prepare the bed.'
206.017. By all of them the scriptural collections were studied.
206.018. He said: 'Noble one, the scriptural collections have been studied by them.
206.018. Will they retain them or will they not retain them?' He said: 'They are mindful beings; they will retain them. But there is a fault in them.'
206.019. He said: 'Noble one, what fault?' 'All of them are without reverence, without respect.
206.020. One closes his eyes while receiving instruction; the second turns his back while receiving instruction; the third stands far away while receiving instruction.
206.021. You alone are respectful, attentive, and foremost in all duties.'
206.022. He said: 'Noble one, they are not without reverence or without respect.
206.023. The one who closes his eyes while receiving instruction — he has poison in his gaze.
206.023. The one who turns his back while receiving instruction — he too has poison in his breath.
206.024. The one who stands far away while receiving instruction — he too has poison in his touch.
206.025. I alone have poison in my fangs.'
206.025. Hearing this, he became frightened, extremely pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and wasted in body.
206.026. He said: 'Noble one, why have you become so pale, emaciated, weak, withered, and wasted in body?' He said: 'Good sir, I am dwelling in the midst of enemies.
206.028. If any one of you were to become angry at any other, he would make an end of me as well.'
206.028. He said: 'Noble one, we will not harm you.
206.029. But do you wish to go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?' 'Good sir, I do.'
206.030. And the vessel arrived.
206.030. He was lifted up by them.

body.text:
206.031. viṇigbhirdṛṣṭaḥ/
206.031. te kathayanti--svāgatamāryasaṃgharakṣitāya/
206.031. sa kathayati--anumodantāṃ bhavantaḥ/
206.032. mayā nāgoṣvāgamacatuṣṭayaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
206.032. te kathayanti--ārya saṃgharakṣita, anumodayāmah<207>/
body.translated_text:
206.031. The merchants saw him.
206.031. They said: 'Welcome to the noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>!'
206.031. He said: 'May you all rejoice!
206.032. I have established the four collections of scriptures among the <s>Nāgas</s>.'
206.032. They said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, we rejoice.' <207>

body.text:
207.001. te taṃ vahane prakṣipya saṃprasthitāḥ/
207.001. te 'nupūrveṇa samudratīraṃ gatvā sarve te vaṇijaḥ śayitāḥ/
207.002. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito mahāsamudraṃ draṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
207.002.uktaṃ bhagavatā--pañcasecanakā darśanena/
207.004. hastināgaśca rājā ca sāgaraśca śiloccayaḥ/
207.005. asecanakā darśanena buddhaśca bhagavatāṃ varaḥ//1// iti/
207.006. ciraṃ mahāsamudraṃ paśyañ jāgaritaḥ/
207.006. so 'paścime yāme gaḍhanidrāvaṣṭabdhaḥ śayitaḥ/
207.007. te 'pi vaṇijaḥ sarātramevotthāya sthorāmllardayitvā saṃprasthitāḥ/
207.007. te kathayanti prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām--kutrāyaṃ saṃgharakṣitah? tatraika evamāhuh--purastādgacchati/
207.009. apara evamāhuh--pṛṣṭhata āgacchati/
207.009. te kathayanti--āryasaṃgharakṣito 'smābhiśchoritaḥ/
207.010. na śobhanamasmābhiḥ kṛtam/
207.010. pratinivartayāmaḥ/
207.010. āryasaṃgharakṣito bhavanto maharddhiko mahānubhāvo yaḥ samudramadhye na kālagataḥ/
207.011. sa idānīṃ kālaṃ kariṣyati? sthānametadvidyate yadasau agrata eva yāsyati/
207.012. āgacchata, gamiṣyāmaḥ/
207.012. te saṃprasthitāḥ//
body.translated_text:
207.001. They placed him on the vessel and set out.
207.001. They gradually reached the ocean shore, and all those merchants fell asleep.
207.002. The venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> began to gaze at the great ocean.
207.002. The Blessed One said: 'There are five things that are never tiresome to look at:
207.004. A great elephant, a king, the ocean, a mountain,
207.005. and a <s>Buddha</s>, the best of Blessed Ones — these are never tiresome to behold.' //1//
207.006. He stayed awake a long time gazing at the great ocean.
207.006. Then, in the last watch of the night, overcome by deep sleep, he lay down.
207.007. Those merchants, having risen early at dawn, loaded their pack-animals and set out.
207.007. At daybreak they said: 'Where is <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>?' Some said: 'He is walking ahead.'
207.009. Others said: 'He is coming from behind.'
207.009. They said: '<s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> has been left behind by us.
207.010. This is not a good thing we have done.
207.010. Let us turn back.'
207.010. 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, sirs, is of great supernatural power and great might — he who did not die in the middle of the ocean.
207.011. Will he die now? It is quite possible that he will travel ahead of us.
207.012. Come, let us go.'
207.012. They set out.

body.text:
207.013. āyuṣmānapi saṃgharakṣitaḥ sūryasyābhyudgamanasamaye sūryāṃśubhistāḍitaḥ pratibuddho yāvanna kiṃcitpaśyati/
207.014. prakrāntā vaṇijaḥ/
207.014. so 'pi panthalikāṃ gṛhītvā saṃprasthitaḥ/
207.014. yāvadanyatamasyāṃ sālāṭavyāṃ vihāraṃ paśyatyudgataṃ mañcapīṭhavedikājālavātāyanagavākṣaparimaṇḍitam, bhikṣūṃśca saṃprāvṛtān saṃpracchannāñ śānteneryāpathenāvasthitān/
207.016. sa teṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
207.016. sa tairuktah--svāgataṃ bhadantasaṃgharakṣitāya/
207.017. sa tairviśrāmitaḥ/
207.017. viśrāmayitvā vihāraṃ praveśito yāvat paśyati śobhanāṃ śayanāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtāṃ praṇītaṃ cāhāramupahṛtam/
207.018. sa tairuktah--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, mā tṛṣito 'si, mā bubhukṣito 'si? kathayati--āryāḥ, tṛṣito 'smi, bubhukṣito 'smi/
207.019. bhadanta saṃgharakṣita bhuṅkṣva/
207.020. sa kathayati--saṃghamadhye mokṣyāmi/
207.020. te kathayanti--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, muṅkṣva, ādīnavo 'tra bhaviṣyati/
207.021. tena muktam/
207.021. sa bhuktvā ekānte 'pakramyāvasthitaḥ/
207.021. yāvat teṣāṃ gaṇḍarākoṭitā/
207.022. te svakāsvakāni pātrāṇyādāya yathāgatya niṣaṇṇaḥ/
207.022. sa ca teṣāṃ vihāro 'ntarhitaḥ/
207.023. ayomudgatāḥ prādurbhūtam/
207.023. taistāvadayomudgaraiḥ parasparamārtasvaraṃ krandadbhiḥ śirāṃsi bhagnāni, yāvat kālādakālībhūtam/
207.024. tataḥ paścāt punarapi teṣāṃ vihāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, te ca bhikṣavaḥ śānteneryāpathenāvasthitāḥ/
207.025. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitasteṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
207.026. ke yūyamāyuṣmantaḥ, kena vā karmaṇā ihopapannāh? bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, duṣkuhakā jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ/
207.027. nābhiśraddadhāsyasi/
207.027. sa kathayati--ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī, kasmānnābhiśraddadhāsye? te kathayanti--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, vayaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvakā āsan/
207.028. tairasmākaṃ bhaktāgre raṇamutpāditam/
207.029. te vayaṃ bhaktāgre raṇamutpādayitvā iha pratyekanarakeṣūpapannāḥ/
207.0sthānametadvidyate yadasmābhiritaścyutair narakṛṣūpapattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
207.030. sādhu saṃgharakṣita, jambudvīpaṃ gatvā sabrahmacāriṇāmārocaya--mā āyuṣmantaḥ saṃghamadhye raṇamutpādayiṣyatha/
207.031. mā asyaivamrūpasya duḥkhadaurmanasyasya bhāgino bhaviṣyatha tadyathā śramaṇāḥ kāśyapīyāḥ//
body.translated_text:
207.013. The venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, at the time of sunrise, struck by the rays of the sun, awoke and saw nothing.
207.014. The merchants had departed.
207.014. He too, taking a path, set out.
207.014. Then, in a certain <s>śāla</s>-tree forest, he saw a monastery, elevated and adorned with platforms, benches, railings, lattice-work, wind-openings, and bull's-eye windows, and monks who were well-robed, well-covered, and dwelling with peaceful deportment.
207.016. He approached them.
207.016. They said: 'Welcome to the venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.'
207.017. They gave him rest.
207.017. Having refreshed him, they brought him into the monastery, where he saw a fine arrangement of bedding and seats, and excellent food was offered.
207.018. They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, are you not thirsty? Are you not hungry?' He said: 'Venerable sirs, I am thirsty and I am hungry.'
207.019. 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, eat.'
207.020. He said: 'I shall distribute it among the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'
207.020. They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, eat — there will be trouble here.'
207.021. He ate.
207.021. He withdrew and stood to one side.
207.021. Then their assembly bell was struck.
207.022. They each took their own bowls and sat down as they had come.
207.022. And their monastery vanished.
207.023. Iron hammers appeared.
207.023. With those iron hammers, crying out in agony, they smashed each other's heads until what had been a period of life became a period of death.
207.024. Then again afterward, their monastery reappeared, and those monks stood with peaceful deportment.
207.025. The venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> approached them.
207.026. 'Who are you, venerable sirs, and by what deed were you reborn here?' 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, the people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are wicked.
207.027. You will not believe it.'
207.027. He said: 'I am an eyewitness; why would I not believe?' They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, we were disciples of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
207.028. We raised a quarrel in the dining hall.
207.029. Having raised a quarrel in the dining hall, we have been reborn here in these private hells.
207.029. It is quite possible that, having fallen from here, we will be reborn in the great hells.
207.030. Please, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and tell our fellow practitioners: "Venerable sirs, do not raise quarrels within the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
207.031. Do not become partakers of such suffering and misery as the followers of <s>Kāśyapa</s>."'

body.text:
208.001. <208>sa saṃprasthitaḥ/
208.001. yāvat paśyati dvitīyaṃ vihāramudgataṃ mañcapīṭhavedikājālavātāyanaparikṣiptaṃ gavakṣaparimaṇḍitaṃ bhikṣūṃśca suprāvṛtān supraticchannāñ śāntāñ śānteryāpathe vyavasthitān/
208.003. teṣāmupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
208.003. sa tairuktah--svāgataṃ bhadantasaṃgharakṣitāya/
208.003. sa tairviśrāmitaḥ/
208.004. viśrāmayitvā vihāraṃ praveśito yāvat paśyati/
208.004. śobhanāṃ śayanāsanaprajñaptiḥ kṛtvā praṇītaṃ cāhāraṃ samanvāhṛtya sa tairuktah--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita muṅkṣva/
208.005. tena dṛṣṭādīnavena bhuktam/
208.005. muktvā ekānte 'pakramyāsthitaḥ/
208.006. teṣāṃ gaṇḍyākoṭitā/
208.006. te svakasvakāni pātrāṇyādāya yathāgatya niṣaṇṇāḥ/
208.007. sa ca vihāro 'ntarhitaḥ, tadannapānamayorasaṃ prādurbhūtam/
208.007. tairātasvaraṃ krandadbhistāvadayorasena parasparamātmā sikto yāvat kāladakālībhūtam/
208.008. tataḥ paścāt punarapi sa teṣāṃ vihāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
208.009. te ca bhikṣavaḥ punarapi śāntāḥ śānteryāpathenāvasthitāḥ/
208.009. sa teṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntah--ke yūyamāyuṣmantaḥ, kena vā karmaṇā ihopapannāh? duṣkuhakā bhadanta saṃgharakṣita jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, nābhiśraddaddhāsyanti/
208.011. sa kathayati--ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī, kasmānnābhiśraddadhāsye? te kathayanti--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, vayaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvakā āsan/
208.013. saṃghasya ca snehalābhe saṃpanne āgantukā bhikṣava āgatāḥ/
208.013. tairasmābhiranāryaparigṛhītairevaṃ cittamutpāditam--na tāvadbhojayiṣyāmo yāvadete āgantukā bhikṣavo na prakrāntā bhaviṣyantīti/
208.015. tairasmābhistattathaiva kṛtam/
208.015. saptāhikaṃ cākāladurdinaṃ prādurbhūtam/
208.015. tena tadannapānaṃ kledaṃ gatam/
208.016. vayaṃ śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātayitvā iha pratyekanarakeṣūpapannāḥ/
208.016. sthānametadvidyate yadasmābhiriha cyutair narakeṣūpapattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
208.017. sādhu bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, jambudvīpaṃ gatvā sabrahmacāriṇāmāraocaya--mā āyuṣmantaḥ śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātayiṣyatha, mā asya evamrūpasya duḥkhadaurmanasyasya bhāgino bhaviṣyatha, tadyathā brāhmaṇāḥ kāśyapīyāḥ//
body.translated_text:
208.001. He set out.
208.001. Presently he saw a second monastery risen up, surrounded by couches, benches, railings, lattices, and windows, adorned with round windows, and monks well-clothed, well-covered, calm, established in a calm deportment.
208.003. He approached them.
208.003. They said to him: 'Welcome to the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.'
208.003. They gave him rest.
208.004. Having rested him, they admitted him into the monastery, where he saw
208.004. a beautiful arrangement of bedding and seats, and excellent food had been brought.
208.004. They said to him: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, eat.'
208.005. Having seen the danger, he ate.
208.005. After eating, he withdrew and stood to one side.
208.006. Their bell was struck.
208.006. They took up their own bowls and sat down as they had come.
208.007. And that monastery vanished; in its place, a rain of molten iron appeared.
208.007. Screaming in agony, they were drenched by the molten iron, one upon another, until they died untimely deaths.
208.008. Then once again their monastery reappeared.
208.009. Those monks again stood calm, established in a calm deportment.
208.009. He approached them: 'Who are you, Venerable ones, and by what deed were you reborn here?' 'The people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are deceitful, Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> — they will not believe it.'
208.011. He said: 'I am an eyewitness; why would I not believe it?' They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, we were disciples of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
208.013. When an excellent offering of love had been made ready for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, visiting monks arrived.
