208.013. We, seized by ignoble impulses, generated this thought: "We shall not feed them until these visiting monks have departed."
208.015. And we acted accordingly.
208.015. An unseasonable storm arose for seven days,
208.015. and by it the food and drink were spoiled.
208.016. Having caused the destruction of what was given in faith, we were reborn here in individual hells.
208.016. It is possible that, passing away from here, we shall be reborn in the [great] hells.
208.017. Please, Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and tell your fellow practitioners in the holy life: "Do not, Venerable ones, cause the destruction of what is given in faith, lest you become sharers in suffering and misery of this kind, as happened to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Kāśyapīya</s> lineage."'

body.text:
208.020. sa saṃprasthito yāvat paśyati tṛtīyaṃ vihāramudgataṃ mañcapīṭhavidikājālavātāyanagavākṣaparimaṇḍitaṃ pūrvavadyāvadāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito saṃgharakṣito bhuktvā ekānte 'pakramyāvsthitaḥ/
208.021. gaṇḍyākoṭitā/
208.022. sa tena vihāra ādīptaḥ pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalita ekajvālībhūto dhmāyitumārabdhaḥ/
208.022. te 'pi tasminnārtasvaraṃ krandatastāvaddagdhā yāvat kālādakālībhūtam/
208.023. tataḥ paścāt punarapi teṣāṃ vihāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ, te ca bhikṣavaḥ śāntaśānteneryāpathenāvasthitāḥ/
208.024. sa teṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntah--ke yūyamāyuṣmantaḥ, kena vā karmaṇā ihopapannāh? duṣkuhakā bhadanta saṃgharakṣita jambudvīpakā manuṣyāḥ, nābhiśraddadhāsyasi/
208.026. sa kathayati--ahaṃ pratyakṣadarśī, kasmānnābhiśraddadhāsye? te kathayanti--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita vayaṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvakā āsan/
208.027. duḥśīlāste vayaṃ śīlavadbhirbhikṣubhir niṣkāsitāḥ/
208.028. tairasmābhirekaḥ śūnyavihāra āvāsitaḥ/
208.028. yāvat tatraikaḥ śīlavān bhikṣurāgataḥ/
208.029. asmākaṃ buddhirutpannā--tiṣṭhatu ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ/
208.029. ayamapyeko 'smākaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ śodhayiṣyati/
208.030. sa tatraiva sthito yāvat tasyānisaṅgena(?) punarapi bahavaḥ śīlavanto bhikṣava āgatāḥ/
208.031. te vayaṃ tatrāpi nirvāsitāḥ/
208.031. tairasmābhiramarṣajātaiḥ śuṣkāni kāṣṭhāni śuṣkāni tṛṇāni śuṣkāni gomayāni upasaṃhṛtya tasmin vihāro 'gnirdagdhaḥ/
208.032. tatra prabhūtāh <209>śaikṣāśaikṣāḥ pudgalā dagdhāḥ/
body.translated_text:
208.020. He set out. Presently he saw a third monastery risen up, surrounded by couches, benches, railings, lattices, windows, and round windows — as before, up to the point where the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, having eaten, withdrew and stood to one side.
208.021. The bell was struck.
208.022. That monastery caught fire, blazed up, burst into flames, became a single mass of fire, and began to smolder.
208.022. Those monks too, screaming in agony within it, were burned until they died untimely deaths.
208.023. Then once again their monastery reappeared, and those monks again stood calm, established in a calm deportment.
208.024. He approached them: 'Who are you, Venerable ones, and by what deed were you reborn here?' 'The people of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are deceitful, Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> — you will not believe it.'
208.026. He said: 'I am an eyewitness; why would I not believe it?' They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, we were disciples of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
208.027. We were of bad conduct, and we were expelled by virtuous monks.
208.028. They assigned us to live in an empty monastery.
208.028. Then a certain virtuous monk arrived there.
208.029. The thought arose in us: "Let this monk stay.
208.029. He too will purify our offerings."
208.030. He stayed there, and by his association many more virtuous monks arrived.
208.031. We were expelled from there as well.
208.031. Filled with resentment, we gathered dry wood, dry grass, and dry cow dung, and set fire to that monastery.
208.032. Many learners and adepts (<s>śaikṣa</s> and <s>aśaikṣa</s>) were burned therein.

body.text:
209.001. <209>te vayaṃ śaikṣāśaikṣān pudgalān dagdhvā iha pratyekanarakeṣūpapannāḥ/
209.002. sthānametadvidyate yadasmābhiriha cyutair narakeṣūpapattavyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
209.002. sādhu bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, jambudvīpaṃ gatvā sabrahmacāriṇāmārocaya--mā āyuṣmantaḥ sabrahmacāriṇāmantike praduṣṭacittamutpādayiṣyatha, mā asyaivamrūpasya duḥkhadaurmanasyasya bhagino bhavino bhaviṣyatha tadyathā śramaṇaḥ kāśyapīyāḥ//
body.translated_text:
209.001. Having burned those learners and adepts, we were reborn here in individual hells.
209.002. It is possible that, passing away from here, we shall be reborn in the [great] hells.
209.002. Please, Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and tell your fellow practitioners in the holy life: 'Do not, Venerable ones, generate a mind of hostility toward your fellow practitioners, lest you become sharers in suffering and misery of this kind, as happened to the ascetics of the <s>Kāśyapīya</s> lineage.'

body.text: 209.006. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ saṃprasthito yāvat sattvānadrakṣīt stambhākārān kuḍyākārān vṛkṣākārān patrākārān puṣpākārān phalākārān rajjvākārān saṃmārjanyākārānudūkhalākārān khaṭvākārān sthālikākārān//
body.translated_text: 209.006. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> set out. He saw beings in the shapes of pillars, walls, trees, leaves, flowers, fruits, ropes, brooms, mortars, bedsteads, and cooking pots.

body.text:
209.009. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito janapadān gataḥ/
209.009. anyatamasminnāśramapade pañcamātrāṇi ṛṣiśatāni prativasanti/
209.010. tairāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito dūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ/
209.010. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, kriyākāraṃ tāvat kurmah--bahubollakāḥ śramaṇāḥ śākyaputrīyā bhavanti/
209.011. nāsya kenacidvacanaṃ dātavyam/
209.012. te kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā avasthitāḥ/
209.012. āyuṣmāṃśca saṃgharakṣitasteṣāṃ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
209.013. upasaṃkramya pratiśrayam yācitumārabdhaḥ/
209.013. na kaścidvācamanuprayacchati/
209.013. tatraika ṛṣiḥ sa śukladharmaḥ/
209.014. kathayati--kim yuṣmākaṃ pratiśrayaṃ na dīyate? api tu yuṣmākaṃ doṣo 'sti/
209.014. bahubollakā yūyam/
209.015. samayenāhaṃ bhavataḥ pratiśrayaṃ dāsye, sacet kiṃcinna mantrayasi/
209.015. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--ṛṣe, evaṃ bhavatu/
209.016. tatraika ṛṣirjanapadacārikāṃ gataḥ/
209.016. tasya kuṭiḥ śūnyāvatiṣṭhati/
209.017. sa kathayati--asyāṃ kuṭikāyāṃ śāyyāṃ kalpaya/
209.017. āyuṣmatā saṃgharakṣitena sā kuṭikā siktā saṃmṛṣṭā saṃmārjitā sukumārīṃ gomayakāsiṃ cānupradattā/
209.018. tairdṛṣṭaḥ/
209.018. te kathayati--bhadanta, śucyapi mārjantyete śramaṇāḥ śākyaputrīyāḥ/
209.019. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito bahiḥ kuṭikāyāḥ pādau prakṣālya kuṭikāṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupashtāpya/
209.021. ya tasminnāśramapade devatā prativasati, sā rātryāḥ prathame yāme yenāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitastenopasaṃkrāntā/
209.022. upasaṃkramya kathayati--ārya saṃgharakṣita, dharmaṃ deśaya/
209.022. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--sukhitā tvam/
209.023. na paśyasi mayā triyākāreṇa pratiśrayaṃ labdham, kiṃ niṣkāsāpayitumicchasi? sā saṃlakṣayati--śrāntakāyo 'yam, svapitu/
209.024. madhyame yāme upasaṃkramiṣyāmi/
209.025. sā madhyame yāma upasaṃkrāntā/
209.025. upasaṃkramya kathayati--ārya saṃgharakṣita, dharmaṃ deśaya/
209.025. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--sukhitā tvam/
209.026. na paśyasi mayā kriyākāreṇa pratiśrayaṃ labdham? kiṃ niṣkāsāpayitumicchasi? sā saṃlakṣayati--śrāntakāyo 'yam, svapitu/
209.027. paścime yāme upasaṃkramiṣyāmi/
209.028. sā paścime yāme upasaṃkrāntā/
209.028. upasaṃkramya kathayati--ārya saṃgharakṣita, dharmaṃ deśaya/
209.029. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--sukhitā tvam/
209.029. na paśyasi mayā kriyākāreṇa pratiśrayaṃ labdham? kiṃ niṣkāsāpayitumicchasi? sā kathayati--ārya saṃgharakṣita, prabhātamidānīm/
209.031. sacinniṣkāsayiṣyanti, gamiṣyasi/
209.031. api tu nanūktaṃ bhagavatā bhayabhairavasahiṣṇunā te bhavitavyamiti/
209.032. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ saṃlakṣayati--śobhanaṃ kathayati--sacet sa niṣkāsayiṣyati, <210>gamiṣyāmi/
body.translated_text:
209.009. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> went to the countryside.
209.009. In a certain hermitage, about five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) were dwelling.
209.010. They saw the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> from afar.
209.010. They said: 'Sirs, let us first make an agreement — the <s>śramaṇas</s> who are followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son are very talkative.
209.011. Let no one give him a word.'
209.012. Having made this agreement, they stood firm.
209.012. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> approached them.
209.013. Having approached, he began to ask for lodging.
209.013. No one would give him a word.
209.013. There was one <s>ṛṣi</s> among them who was inclined toward wholesome qualities.
209.014. He said: 'Why do you not give him lodging? However, there is a fault in you all.
209.014. You are very talkative.
209.015. I shall give you lodging on the condition that you do not discourse on anything.'
209.015. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'O sage, so be it.'
209.016. There was one <s>ṛṣi</s> who had gone on a countryside tour.
209.016. His hut stood empty.
209.017. He said: 'Prepare your bed in this hut.'
209.017. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> sprinkled, cleaned, swept, and smeared the hut with fine cow-dung plaster.
209.018. They saw this.
209.018. They said: 'Venerable sir, these <s>śramaṇas</s> who are followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son even clean beautifully!'
209.019. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, having washed his feet outside the hut, entered the hut, sat down cross-legged, held his body erect, and established mindfulness before him.
209.021. The deity dwelling in that hermitage, in the first watch of the night, approached the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.
209.022. Having approached, she said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'
209.022. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'You are well off.
209.023. Do you not see that I obtained lodging only through a threefold agreement? Do you wish to get me expelled?' She reflected: 'He is weary in body; let him sleep.
209.024. I shall approach him in the middle watch.'
209.025. She approached in the middle watch.
209.025. Having approached, she said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'
209.025. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'You are well off.
209.026. Do you not see that I obtained lodging through an agreement? Do you wish to get me expelled?' She reflected: 'He is weary in body; let him sleep.
209.027. I shall approach him in the last watch.'
209.028. She approached in the last watch.
209.028. Having approached, she said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s>.'
209.029. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'You are well off.
209.029. Do you not see that I obtained lodging through an agreement? Do you wish to get me expelled?' She said: 'Noble <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, it is now dawn.
209.031. Even if they do expel you, you will simply leave.
209.031. Besides, was it not said by the Blessed One that one must be able to endure fears and terrors?'
209.032. The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> reflected: 'She speaks well — even if he does expel me, I shall leave.'

body.text:
210.001. sa saṃlakṣayati--brāhmaṇā hyete/
210.001. brāhmaṇapratisamyuktaṃ bhāṣayāmītyāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito brāhmaṇavargaṃ svādhyāyitumārabdhah--
210.003. na nagnacaryā na jaṭā na paṅko nānāśanaṃ sthaṇḍalaśāyikā vā/
210.005. na rajomalaṃ notkuṭukaprahāṇaṃ viśodhayenmohamaviśīrṇakāṅkṣam//2//
body.translated_text:
210.001. He reflected: 'These are <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
210.001. I shall recite something connected with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' And so the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> began to recite the <s>Brāhmaṇavarga</s> (Chapter on the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>):
210.003. 'Neither nakedness, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting, nor sleeping on the ground,
210.005. nor dust and filth, nor sitting in the squatting posture can purify a mortal who has not overcome doubt.' //2//

body.text:
210.007. alaṃkṛtaścāpi careta dharmaṃ dāntendrayaḥ śāntaḥ samyato brahmacārī/
210.009. sarveṣu bhūteṣu nidhāya daṇḍaṃ sa brāhmaṇaḥ sa śramaṇa sa bhikṣuḥ//3//
body.translated_text:
210.007. 'Even though adorned, if one practices the <s>Dharma</s> — calm, with senses tamed, restrained, living the holy life,
210.009. having laid down the rod toward all beings — he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, he is a <s>śramaṇa</s>, he is a <s>bhikṣu</s>.' //3//

body.text:
210.011. taiḥ śrutam/
210.011. te saṃlakṣayanti--brāhmaṇapratisamyuktam/
210.011. ityeka upasaṃkrānto dvitīyastṛtīyo yāvat sarve upasaṃkrāntāḥ/
210.012. tathā tayā devatayā adhiṣṭhitam, yathā parasparaṃ na paśyanti/
210.013. tataḥ paścādāyuṣmatā saṃgharakṣitena nagaropamaṃ sūtramupanikṣiptam/
210.013. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
210.014. yānīha bhūtāni samāgatāni sthitāni bhūmyāmathavāntarikṣe/
210.016. kurvantu maitrīṃ satataṃ prajāsu divā ca rātrau ca carantu dharmam//4// iti/
210.018. asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe sarvaistaiḥ sahasatyābhisamayādanāgāmiphalamanuprāptam/
210.019. ṛddhiścāpi nirhṛtā/
210.019. sarvaistaiḥ subhāṣitaṃ bhadantasaṃgharakṣitāyetyekanādo muktaḥ/
210.019. tayā devatayā ṛddhyabhisaṃskārāḥ pratiprasrabdhaḥ/
210.020. parasparaṃ draṣṭumārabdhāḥ/
210.020. te 'nyonyaṃ kathayanti--tvamapyāgatah?
210.021. āgato 'ham/
210.021. śobhanam/
210.021. te dṛṣṭasatyāḥ kathayanti--labhemo vayaṃ bhadanta saṃgharakṣita svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
210.022. caremo vayaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
210.022. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--kiṃ matsakāśe pravrajatha, āhosvidbhagavatah? te kathayanti--bhagavataḥ/
210.024. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ kathayati--yadyevam, āgacchatha, bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ gacchāmaḥ/
210.024. te kathayanti--bhadanta saṃgharakṣita, kimasmadīyayā ṛddhyā gacchāmaḥ, āhosvit tvadīyayā? āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ebhirmadīyenāvavādenaivaṃvidhā guṇagaṇā aghigatāḥ, ahaṃ laṅghanakopamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
210.027. sa kathayati--tiṣṭhantu tāvadbhavanto muhūrtam/
210.027. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito 'nyatamaṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhaṃ smṛtimupasthāpya/
210.028. uktaṃ bhagavatā--pañcānuśaṃsā bāhuśrutye/
210.029. dhātukuśalo bhavati, pratītyasamutpādakuśalo bhavati, sthānāsthānakuśalo bhavati, aparapratibaddhā cāsya bhavati avavādānuśāsanīti/
210.030. tenodyacchatā ghaṭatā vyāyacchatā sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
210.031. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgah <211>pūrvavadyāvanmānyaḥ pūjyaścābhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
body.translated_text: They heard it. They reflected: 'This pertains to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.' Thus one approached, a second, a third, until all of them had approached. That deity so empowered it that they could not see each other. Then the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> delivered the <s>Nagaropama Sūtra</s> (The Discourse on the Simile of the City). And he spoke a verse: 'Whatever beings have assembled here, standing on the earth or in the sky, may they always practice loving-kindness toward all creatures, and day and night may they practice the <s>Dharma</s>.' //4// While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, all of them, through the simultaneous realization of the truths, attained the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>). And supernatural power was also generated. All of them uttered a single cry: 'Well spoken, Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>!' That deity released the supernatural empowerment. They began to see each other. They said to one another: 'You too have come?' 'I have come.' 'Excellent!' Having seen the truths, they said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, may we receive the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May we practice the holy life in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'Do you wish to go forth under me or under the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' They said: 'Under the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said: 'If so, come, let us go to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, shall we go by our own supernatural power or by yours?' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> reflected: 'Through my instruction, they have attained such hosts of virtues, and I have remained like a stepping-stone.' He said: 'Wait a moment, good sirs.' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, having taken a seat at the foot of a certain tree, sat cross-legged, made his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said there are five benefits of great learning: one becomes skilled in the elements, skilled in dependent origination, skilled in what is possible and what is not possible, and one's instruction and admonishment become unrestricted. Striving, exerting, and applying himself, he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in all three realms — as before, up to — worthy of worship, honor, and salutation.

body.text:
211.001. te āyuṣmatā saṃgharakṣitenābhihitāh--bhavantaḥ, gṛhṇīdhvaṃ madīyaṃ cīvarakarṇikam, yāsyāmaḥ/
211.002. āyuṣmataḥ saṃgharakṣitasya cīvarakarṇike lagnāḥ/
211.003. athāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājastata eva ṛddhyā uparivihāyasā prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: They were addressed by the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>: 'Good sirs, take hold of the corner of my robe; we shall go.' They clung to the corner of the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita's</s> robe. Then the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, like a royal goose with outstretched wings, departed from that very place, traveling through the sky by supernatural power.

body.text:
211.004. yāvat tāni pañca vaṇikśatāni bhāṇḍaṃ pratisāmayanti/
211.004. teṣāmupari cchāyā nipatitā/
211.005. sa tairdṛṣṭaḥ/
211.005. te kathayanti--ārya saṃgharakṣita, āgatastvam? āgato 'ham/
211.005. kutra gacchasi? sa kathayati--imāni pañca kulaputraśatānyākāṅkṣanti svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
211.007. te kathayanti--ārya saṃgharakṣita, vayamapi pravrajiṣyāmaḥ/
211.007. avārasva yāvadbhāṇḍaṃ pratisāmayāma iti/
211.008. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito 'vatīrṇaḥ/
211.008. tairbhāṇḍaṃ pratisāmitam/
211.008. athāyuṣmān saṃgharakṣitastat kulaputrasahasramādāya yena bhagavāṃstenoasaṃkrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, those five hundred merchants were arranging their merchandise. His shadow fell upon them from above. He was seen by them. They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, have you come?' 'I have come.' 'Where are you going?' He said: 'These five hundred sons of good families wish to receive the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of monks in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' They said: 'Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, we too shall go forth. Wait while we arrange our merchandise.' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> descended. They arranged their merchandise. Then the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, taking that thousand sons of good families, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
211.010. tena khalu samayena bhagavānanekaśatāyā bhikṣuparṣadaḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati/
211.011. adrākṣīdbhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ saṃgharakṣitaṃ dūrādeva/
211.011. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣa bhikṣuvaḥ saṃgharakṣito bhikṣuḥ saprābhṛta āgacchati/
211.012. nāsti tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhaṃ prābhṛtam yathā vaineyaprābhṛtam/
211.013. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
211.013. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
211.014. ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito bhagavantamidamavocat--idaṃ bhadanta kulaputrasahasramākāṅkṣati svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
211.016. taṃ bhagavān pravrājayati upasampādayatyanukāmpāmupādāya/
211.016. te bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitāh--eta bhikṣuvaścarata brahmacaryam/
211.017. bhagavato vācāvasāne muṇḍāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtāḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśravaḥ pātrakarakavyagrahastā varṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣorīryāpathenāvasthitāḥ//
body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seated before a congregation of several hundred monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'That monk <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, monks, is coming bearing a gift. There is no gift for the <s>Tathāgata</s> such as the gift of those to be trained.' The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, this thousand sons of good families wishes to receive the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of monks in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> ordain and fully admit them, out of compassion.' They were addressed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the 'Come, monks' ordination: 'Come, monks, practice the holy life.' With the very end of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> utterance, they became tonsured, clad in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (monastic robe), with hair and beard as if shaved seven days ago, with bowl and water-pot in hand, standing with the deportment of monks who had been ordained for a hundred years.

body.text:
211.020. ehīti caoktā hi tathāgatena muṇḍāśca saṃghāṭiparītadehāḥ/
211.022. sadyaḥ praśāntendriyā eva tasthurevaṃ sthitā buddhamanorathena//5//
body.translated_text: 'Come!' — thus addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured and with bodies wrapped in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, they stood at once with senses perfectly calmed — thus established by the aspiration of the <s>Buddha</s>. //5//

body.text:
211.024. bhagavatā teṣāmavavādo dattaḥ/
211.024. tairudyacchamānairghaṭamānairvyāyacchadbhiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
211.025. arhantaḥ saṃvṛttāstraidhātukavītarāgāḥ pūrvavadyāvat pūjyāśca abhivādyāśca saṃvṛttāḥ//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave them instruction. Striving, exerting, and applying themselves, they directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). They became <s>Arhats</s>, free from passion in all three realms — as before, up to — worthy of worship, honor, and salutation.

body.text:
211.027. āyuṣmān saṃgharakṣito buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati--ihāhaṃ bhadanta sattvānadrākṣaṃ kuḍyākārān stambhākārān vṛkṣākārān patrākārān puṣpākārān phalākārāan rajjvākārān saṃmārjanyākārān khaṭvākārānudūkhalākārān sthālikākārān/
211.029. madhye 'vacchinnaṃ tantunā dhāryamāṇaṃ gacchati/
211.030. kasya karmaṇo vipākena? bhagavānāha--yāṃstvaṃ saṃgharakṣita sattvānadrākṣīḥ kuḍyākārāṃste kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvakā āsan/
211.031. taiḥ sāṃghikaṃ kuḍyaṃ śleṣmāṇā siṃhāṇakena <212>vināśitam/
body.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, here I have seen beings in the shape of walls, in the shape of pillars, in the shape of trees, in the shape of leaves, in the shape of flowers, in the shape of fruits, in the shape of ropes, in the shape of brooms, in the shape of beds, in the shape of mortars, and in the shape of cooking pots. One being, cut in half in the middle, goes about held together by a thread. By the ripening of what deed is this?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Those beings you saw in the shape of walls, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, were disciples of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. They had damaged the communal wall with phlegm and nasal mucus.

body.text:
212.001. te tasya karmaṇo vipākena kuḍyākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
212.001. yathā kuṭyākārāḥ, evaṃ stambhākārāḥ sattvāḥ/
212.002. yān saṃgharakṣita sattvānādrākṣīrvṛkṣākārāṃste kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvakā āsan/
212.003. taiḥ sāṃghikāḥ puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛkṣāḥ paudgalikaparibhogena bhuktāḥ/
212.004. te tasya karmaṇo vipākena vṛkṣākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
212.004. yathā vṛkṣākārāḥ, evaṃ patrākārāaḥ phalākārāḥ puṣpākārāḥ/
212.005. yaṃ tvaṃ saṃgharakṣita sattvamadrākṣī rajjvākāram, sa kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvaka āsīt/
212.006. tena saṃghikā rajjuḥ paudgalikaparibhogena paribhuktā/
212.007. sa tasy karmaṇo saṃgharakṣita sattvamadrākṣīstapvākāram (?) kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvaka āsīt śrāmaṇerakaḥ/
212.009. so 'pareṇa samayena pānakavāramuddiṣṭastadvārakaṃ nirmādayati/
212.010. āgantukāśca bhikṣuva āgatāḥ/
212.010. sa taiḥ pṛṣṭah--śrāmaṇeraka, kiṃ saṃghasya pānakaṃ bhaviṣyati? sa kathayati--nāstīti/
212.011. te nirāśībhūtāḥ prakrāntāḥ/
212.011. saṃghasya ca pānakaṃ saṃpannam/
212.011. sa tasya karmaṇo vipākena tapvākāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
212.012. yaṃ tvaṃ saṃgharakṣita sattvamadrākṣīrudūkhalākāram, sa kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śrāvaka āsīt/
212.013. tasya pātrakarma pratyupasthitam/
212.013. tatraikaḥ śrāmaṇerako 'rhan/
212.014. sa tenoktah--śrāmaṇeraka, dadasva me khalastokaṃ kuṭṭayitvā/
212.014. sa kathayati--sthavira, tiṣṭha tāvanmuhūrtam/
212.015. vyagro 'ham/
212.015. paścāddāsyāmīti/
212.015. so 'marṣajātaḥ kathayati--śrāmaṇeraka, yadi rocate, tvāmevāhamasminn udūkhale prakṣipya kuṭṭaye prāgeva khalastokam/
212.016. yattadarhato 'ntike kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam, sa tasya karmaṇo vipākena udūkhalākāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
212.017. yāṃstvaṃ saṃgharakṣita sattvānadrākṣīḥ sthālyākārāṃste kāśyapasya samyaksambbuddhasya kalpikārakā āsan/
212.018. te bhikṣūṇāṃ bhaiṣajyāni kvāthayamānāḥ sthālikāṃ bhañjate/
212.019. teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ vighāto bhavati/
212.019. te tasya karmaṇo vipākena sthālyākārāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
212.020. yaṃ tvaṃ saṃgharakṣita sattvamadrākṣīrmadhye chinnastantunā dhāryamāṇo gacchati, sa kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya pravacane pravrajita āsīllābhagrāhikaḥ/
212.021. tena yadvārṣikaṃ lābhaṃ tad dhaimantikaṃ pariṇāmitam, yaddhaimantikaṃ tadvārṣikam/
212.022. tasya karmaṇo vipākena madhye chinnastantunā dhāryamāṇo gacchati//
body.translated_text: By the ripening of that deed, they became wall-shaped beings. Just as they became wall-shaped, so too with the pillar-shaped beings. Those beings you saw in the shape of trees, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, were disciples of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. They had consumed communal flowering trees and fruit trees for personal use. By the ripening of that deed, they became tree-shaped beings. Just as they became tree-shaped, so too with the leaf-shaped, fruit-shaped, and flower-shaped beings. The being you saw in the shape of a rope, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, was a disciple of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He had used the communal rope for personal use. By the ripening of that deed — The being you saw in the shape of a pot (?), <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, was a disciple of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One — a novice. At another time, when it was his turn to prepare drinks, he was preparing the beverages. Then visiting monks arrived. They asked him: 'Novice, will there be a drink for the <s>Saṃgha</s>?' He said: 'There is none.' They departed without hope. But the drink for the <s>Saṃgha</s> was ready. By the ripening of that deed, he became a pot-shaped being. The being you saw in the shape of a mortar, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, was a disciple of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. His duty of pounding grain had come up. There was a novice who was an <s>Arhat</s>. He said to him: 'Novice, give me some pounded grain.' The novice said: 'Elder, wait a moment. I am busy. I shall give it later.' The elder, filled with anger, said: 'Novice, if it pleases you, I shall throw you into this mortar and pound you, let alone the grain!' Because he uttered harsh speech toward an <s>Arhat</s>, by the ripening of that deed he became a mortar-shaped being. Those beings you saw in the shape of cooking pots, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, were kitchen-workers of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. While boiling medicines for the monks, they would break the pots, causing distress to the monks. By the ripening of that deed, they became pot-shaped beings. The being you saw, <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, who was cut in half in the middle and went about held together by a thread — he had gone forth in the teaching of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and was a seizer of gain. He converted what was meant for the rainy season to winter use, and what was meant for winter to rainy-season use. By the ripening of that deed, he goes about cut in half in the middle, held together by a thread.

body.text: 212.024. saṃgharakṣitāvadānaṃ trayoviṃśatimam//
body.translated_text: The <s>Saṃgharakṣitāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>), the twenty-third.

body.text: 213.001. div24 nāgakumārāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 24: The <s>Nāgakumārāvadāna</s> (The Story of the <s>Nāga</s> Prince).

body.text:
213.002. bhikṣuvaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kuto bhadanta tena nāgakumāreṇa tatprathamataḥ śraddhā pratilabdhā? bhagavānāha--bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣuvo 'sminneva bhadrakalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma śāstā lokam utpannastathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān/
213.005. sa evaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati--etāni bhikṣavo 'raṇyāni śūnyāgārāṇi parvatakandaragiriguhāpalālapuñjābhyavakāśaśmaśānavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanāni dhyāyata/
213.006. bhikṣavo mā pramādata/
213.007. mā paścādvipratisāriṇo bhūta/
213.007. idamasmākamanuśāsanam/
213.007. tatra kecidbhikṣavaḥ sumerupariṣaṇḍāyāṃ gatvā dhyāyanti, kecinmandākinyāḥ puṣkariṇyāstīre, kecidanavatapte mahāsarasi, kecit saptasu kāñcanamayeṣu parvateṣu, kecit tāsu tāsu grāmanigamarājarāṣṭradhānīṣu gatvā dhyāyanti//
body.translated_text:
213.002. The monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'From where, Venerable Sir, did that <s>Nāga</s> prince first obtain faith?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Long ago, monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (eon), when the lifespan of beings was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed One, the Tamer of Men, the Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.
213.005. He taught the <s>Dharma</s> to his disciples thus: "These, monks, are the forests, the empty dwellings, the mountain gorges, mountain caves, heaps of straw, open spaces, charnel grounds, forest glades — secluded lodgings. Meditate!
213.006. Monks, do not be heedless!
213.007. Do not later become remorseful.
213.007. This is our instruction."
213.007. Among them, some monks went to the slopes of <s>Sumeru</s> to meditate, some to the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s> lotus-pond, some at the great lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, some on the seven golden mountains, some went to various villages, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals to meditate.

body.text:
213.011. anyatamaśca cirajātako nāgakumāraḥ suparṇinā pakṣirājena sumerupariṣaṇḍāyāmupariṣṭādapahriyate/
213.012. yāvat tena bhikṣavo dhyānādhyayanayogamanasikārayuktā viharanto dṛṣṭāḥ/
213.012. dṛṣṭvā cāsya cittamabhiprasannam/
213.013. prasādajātaḥ saṃlakṣayati--muktā hyete āryakā evaṃvidhād duḥkhāt/
213.014. cyutaḥ kālagato vārāṇasyāṃ ṣaṭkarmanirate brāhmaṇakule jātaḥ/
213.014. unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttaḥ/
213.015. so 'pareṇa samayena kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajitaḥ/
213.015. tenodyatā ghaṭatā vyāyacchatā sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
213.016. arhan saṃvṛttaḥ pūrvavadyāvanmānyaśca pūjyaścābhivandyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
213.017. sa saṃlakṣayati--kuto 'haṃ cyutah? tiryakṣu/
213.017. kutropapannaH? manuṣyeṣu/
213.017. kutra mama mātāpitarau? yāvat paśyati nāgabhavane rudantau tiṣṭhataḥ/
213.018. sa tatra gataḥ/
213.018. gatvā pṛcchitumārabdhah--amba tāta kasyārthe ruditah? tau kathayatah--ārya, sucirajātako 'smākaṃ nāgakumāraḥ suparṇinā pakṣirājenāpahṛtaḥ/
213.020. sa kathayati--ahamevāsau/
213.020. ārya, tādṛśaḥ sa duṣṭānāgo yadvayaṃ sugatigamanamapi na saṃbhāvayāmaḥ, prāgevedṛśānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati/
213.021. tena tau smāritau/
213.021. pādayor nipatya kathayatah--ārya, evaṃvidhāstvayā guṇagaṇā adhigatāḥ/
213.022. ārya tvaṃ piṇḍakenārthī, vayaṃ puṇyenārthikāḥ/
213.023. ihaiva tvamāgamya divase divase bhaktakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā gaccha/
213.023. sa nāgabhavane divyāṃ sudhāṃ paribhuktvā āgacchati/
213.024. tasya śrāmaṇerakaḥ sārdhavihārī/
213.024. sa bhikṣubhiruktah--śrāmaṇeraka, ayaṃ te upādhyāyaḥ kutra bhuktvā āgacchati? sa kathayati--nāhaṃ jāne/
213.025. te kathayanti--nāgabhavane divyāṃ sudhāṃ paribhujya pāribhujyāgacchati/
213.026. tvaṃ kasyārthe na gacchati? sa kathayati--ayaṃ maharddhiko mahānubhāvo yena gacchati/
213.027. kathamahaṃ gacchāmi? te kathayanti--yadā ayam ṛddhyā gacchati, tadā tvamasya cīvarakarṇikaṃ gṛhāṇa/
213.028. sa kathayati--mā pateyam/
213.028. te kathayanti--bhadramukha, yadi sumeruḥ parvatarājā cīvarakarṇikamavalambate, nāsau patet, prāgeva tvaṃ patiṣyasīti/
213.030. yo yasmin sthāne 'ntardhāsyati, tena tatra nimittamudgṛhītam/
213.030. sa tatpradeśaṃ pūrvameva gatvā avasthitaḥ/
213.031. sa cāntardhāsyatīti tena cīvarakarṇikaṃ gṛhītam/
213.031. tau upari vihāyasā <214>prakrāntau yāvat tau nāgairdṛṣṭau/
body.translated_text:
213.011. A certain long-born <s>Nāga</s> prince was being carried off from the slopes of <s>Sumeru</s> by the <s>Suparṇin</s> (divine eagle), the king of birds.
213.012. Then he saw the monks dwelling there engaged in the practice of meditation, study, yoga, and mindful attention.
213.012. Seeing them, his mind became filled with faith.
213.013. Having become faithful, he reflected: 'These noble ones are indeed freed from this kind of suffering.'
213.014. Having passed away, he died and was reborn in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> family devoted to the six duties.
213.014. He was raised, nourished, and grew up.
213.015. At another time, he went forth in the teaching of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
213.015. Striving, exerting, and applying himself, he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).
213.016. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, as before... worthy of worship, honor, and salutation.
213.017. He reflected: 'From where did I pass away? From the animal realm.
213.017. Where was I reborn? Among humans.
213.017. Where are my parents?' He saw them standing and weeping in the <s>Nāga</s> abode.
213.018. He went there.
213.018. Having gone, he began to ask: 'Mother, father, for what reason have you wept?' They said: 'Noble one, our long-born <s>Nāga</s> prince was carried off by the <s>Suparṇin</s>, the king of birds.'
213.020. He said: 'I am that very one.'
213.020. 'Noble one, he was such a wicked <s>Nāga</s> that we did not even consider it possible for him to go to a good destination, let alone that he would obtain such qualities.'
213.021. Then he reminded them.
213.021. Falling at his feet, they said: 'Noble one, you have attained such a collection of virtues.
213.022. Noble one, you are in need of alms-food, and we are in need of merit.
213.023. Come here every day, perform the meal-duty, and then go.'
213.023. He would eat the divine ambrosia in the <s>Nāga</s> abode and then come.
213.024. He had a fellow-resident novice.
213.024. He was asked by the monks: 'Novice, where does your preceptor go to eat and return?' He said: 'I do not know.'
213.025. They said: 'He eats divine ambrosia in the <s>Nāga</s> abode and returns.
213.026. Why do you not go?' He said: 'He is of great supernatural power and might, and so he goes.
213.027. How can I go?' They said: 'When he goes by supernatural power, you should grab the corner of his robe.'
213.028. He said: 'I might fall.'
213.028. They said: 'Dear friend, if even <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, were to hang from the corner of his robe, it would not fall — how much less will you fall?'
213.030. He observed the sign of the place where his preceptor would vanish.
213.030. He went to that spot beforehand and waited.
213.031. As his preceptor was about to vanish, the novice grabbed the corner of his robe.
213.031. The two flew through the sky, and the <s>Nāgas</s> saw them.

body.text:
214.001. tayordve te āsanaprajñaptikṛtau/
214.001. dvau maṇḍalakau āmārjitau/
214.001. sa saṃlakṣayati--kasyārthe 'yamapara āsanaḥ prajñaptah? sa pratinivartya paśyati yāvat śrāmaṇerakam/
214.003. sa kathayati--bhadramukha, tvamapyāgatah? upādyāya, āgato 'ham/
214.003. śobhanam/
214.003. nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--ayamāryo maharddhiko mahānubhāvaḥ/
214.004. śakyate divyāṃ sudhāṃ kārayitum/
214.004. ayamanyo na śakyate/
214.005. taistasya divyā sudhā dattā, tasyāpi prākṛta āhāraḥ/
214.005. sa tasya pātragrāhakaḥ/
214.005. tena tasya pātraṃ gṛhītam yāvat tatraikā odanamijya(?) vatiṣṭhate/
214.006. sā tenāsye prakṣiptā yāvaddivyamāsvādanam/
214.007. sa saṃlakṣayati--īdṛśā api matsariṇo nāgāḥ/
214.007. ekadhye niṣaṇṇayorasya divyā sudhā dattā, mamāpi prākṛta āhāraḥ/
214.008. sa praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā bhagavati kāśyape samyaksambuddhe 'nuttare mahādakṣiṇīye brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇam, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlenaitaṃ nāgamasmādbhavanāccyāvayitvā atraivopapadyeyamiti/
214.010. tasya dṛṣṭa eva dharme ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ jalaṃ syanditumārabdham/
214.011. nāgasyāpi śirortirbādhitumārabdhā/
214.011. sa kathayati--ārya, anena śrāmaṇerakenāśobhanacittamutpāditam/
214.012. pratinivartāpayatu enam/
214.012. sa kathayati--bhadramukha, apāyā hyete, nivartaya cittam/
214.013. sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
214.014. pravaṇībhūutamidaṃ cittaṃ na śaknomi nivārayitum/
214.015. ihasthasyaiva me bhadanta pāṇibhyāṃ syandate jalam//1//
body.translated_text:
214.001. For the two of them, two seats were prepared.
214.001. Two circular areas were swept.
214.001. The elder reflected: 'For what purpose has this other seat been prepared?' He turned back and saw — the novice.
214.003. He said: 'Dear friend, you too have come?' 'Preceptor, I have come.'
214.003. 'Very well.'
214.003. The <s>Nāgas</s> reflected: 'This noble one is of great supernatural power and might.
214.004. Divine ambrosia can be prepared for him.
214.004. But for this other one, it cannot.'
214.005. They gave him divine ambrosia, but gave the novice ordinary food.
214.005. The novice was the bowl-carrier for his preceptor.
214.005. He had taken his preceptor's bowl, and one grain of rice remained stuck in it.
214.006. He put it into his own mouth — and tasted the divine flavor.
214.007. He reflected: 'These <s>Nāgas</s> are indeed miserly.
214.007. Though seated together, to him they gave divine ambrosia, but to me only ordinary food.'
214.008. He began to make a vow: 'By the merit of my holy life lived under <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the supreme and unsurpassed field of merit — by this wholesome root, may I cause this <s>Nāga</s> to fall from this abode and may I myself be reborn here.'
214.010. In that very life, water began to flow from both his hands.
214.011. The <s>Nāga's</s> head too began to ache.
214.011. He said: 'Noble one, this novice has generated an unwholesome thought.
214.012. Make him turn back.'
214.012. The elder said: 'Dear friend, these are the lower realms of existence; turn back your thought.'
214.013. He spoke a verse:
214.014. 'This mind has become inclined downward; I am unable to restrain it.
214.015. Even as I stand here, Venerable Sir, water flows from my hands.' //1//

body.text:
214.016. sa taṃ nāgaṃ tasmādbhavanāccyāvayitvā tatraivopapannaḥ/
214.016. tatra bhikṣavastena nāgakumāreṇa tatprathamataḥ śraddhā pratilabdhā//
body.translated_text:
214.016. He caused that <s>Nāga</s> to fall from that abode and was himself reborn there.
214.016. There, monks, that <s>Nāga</s> prince first obtained faith.

body.text: 214.018. iti śrīdivyāvadāne nāgakumārāvadānam//
body.translated_text: 214.018. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Nāgakumārāvadāna</s> (The Story of the <s>Nāga</s> Prince).

body.text: 215.001. div25 sa gharakSitāvadānam (2)/
body.translated_text: 215.001. Chapter 25: The <s>Saṃgharakṣitāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>) (2).

body.text:
215.002. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā saṃgharakṣitena karma kṛtam, yasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhye mahābhoge kule jāto bhagavato 'ntike pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam? evaṃ taṃ ca vaineyakāryaṃ kṛtam? bhagavānāha--saṃgharakṣitenaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāni kṛtāni upacitāni pūrvavat/
215.005. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'sminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ nāma śāstā pūrvavat/
215.006. tasyāyaṃ śāsane pravrajita āsīdvaiyāvṛtyakaraḥ/
215.007. asya tatra pañca sārdhaṃvihāriśatāni/
215.007. yadbhūyasā ekakarvaṭanivāsī janakāyaḥ, asyaivābhiprasannaḥ/
215.008. anena tatra yāvadāyuḥparyantaṃ brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇam, na kaścidguṇo 'dhigataḥ/
215.009. apareṇa samayena glānībhūtaḥ/
215.009. mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva/
215.010. maraṇasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--yanmayā kāśyape bhagavati samyaksambuddhe 'nuttare mahādakṣiṇīye yāvadāyurbrahmacaryaṃ cīrṇam, na kāścidguṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksambuddhenottaro nāma māṇavo varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāmavaśyabhāgīyakasya bhāvyatāyāṃ buddho, vyākṛtaḥ, tasya śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuryām/
215.014. tataḥ paścāt sārdhaṃvihāriṇa upasaṃkrāntāḥ/
215.014. te kathayanti--upādhyāya, asti kiṃcit tvayā guṇagaṇamadhigatam? sa kathayati--nāsti/
215.015. kiṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam? idaṃ cedaṃ ca/
215.016. te kathayanti--vayamapyupādhyāyameva kalyāṇamitramāgamya tasyaiva bhagavato 'ntike sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuryuḥ/
215.017. karvaṭanivāsinā janakāyena śrutaṃ glāna āryaka iti/
215.018. te 'pyupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
215.018. asti kiṃcidāryeṇa guṇagaṇamadhigatam? nāsti/
215.019. kiṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam? idaṃ cedaṃ ca/
215.019. te kathayanti--vayamapyāryameva kalyāṇamitramāgamya tasyaiva bhagavato 'ntike sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkuryuḥ//
body.translated_text:
215.002. The monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, was done by the Venerable <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>, by the ripening of which deed he was born in a wealthy and prosperous family, and having gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> presence, directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>? And how was that work of training those to be trained accomplished?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s> himself, monks, were the deeds done and accumulated,' as before.
215.005. 'Long ago, monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of beings was twenty thousand years,' a teacher arose, as before.
215.006. 'In his teaching, this one had gone forth as a <s>vaiyāvṛtyakara</s> (attendant serving the community).
215.007. He had five hundred fellow-residents there.
215.007. The people of a certain market-town were for the most part devoted to him.
215.008. He lived the holy life there for his entire lifespan, but did not attain any spiritual quality.
215.009. At another time he fell ill.
215.009. Though attended with medicines of roots, tubers, leaves, flowers, and fruits, he only declined.
215.010. At the time of death, he began to make a vow: "By the merit of my holy life lived for the entire lifespan under <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Blessed One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the supreme and unsurpassed field of merit — though I have not attained any collection of virtues — by this wholesome root, may I, in the teaching of that one whom the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as the young man <s>Uttara</s> who, when the lifespan is a hundred years, will certainly become a <s>Buddha</s> — may I go forth in his teaching and directly realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>."
215.014. Then his fellow-residents approached.
215.014. They said: "Preceptor, have you attained any collection of virtues?" He said: "No."
215.015. "What vow have you made?" "Such-and-such."
215.016. They said: "We too, relying on our preceptor as a spiritual friend, would directly realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> in the presence of that very <s>Bhagavān</s>."
215.017. The people of the market-town heard: "The noble one is ill."
215.018. They too approached.
215.018. "Has the noble one attained any collection of virtues?" "No."
215.019. "What vow have you made?" "Such-and-such."
215.019. They said: "We too, relying on the noble one as a spiritual friend, would directly realize <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> in the presence of that very <s>Bhagavān</s>."'

body.text:
215.021. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavah? yo 'sau vaiyāvṛtyakaraḥ, eṣa evāsau saṃgharakṣito bhikṣuḥ/
215.022. yāni tāni pañca sārdhaṃvihāriśatāni, etānyeva tāni pañcabhikṣuśatāni/
215.022. yo 'sau karvaṭanivāsī janakāyaḥ, etānyeva tāni pañca vaṇikśatāni/
215.023. yadanena tara dharmavaiyāvṛtyaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule upapannaḥ/
215.024. yat tanmaraṇasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena mamāntike pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtamevaṃ ca vaineyakāryaṃ kṛtam//
body.translated_text:
215.021. 'What do you think, monks? He who was that attendant — he is this very monk <s>Saṃgharakṣita</s>.
215.022. Those who were the five hundred fellow-residents — they are these very five hundred monks.
215.022. Those who were the people of the market-town — they are these very five hundred merchants.
215.023. Because he performed service to the <s>Dharma</s> there, by the ripening of that deed he was born in a wealthy, prosperous, and affluent family.
215.024. Because he made that vow at the time of death, by the ripening of that deed he went forth in my presence, directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, and thus accomplished the work of training those to be trained.'

body.text: 215.027. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākah...pūrvavat//
body.translated_text: 215.027. 'Thus, monks, the ripening of exclusively dark deeds is exclusively dark... as before.'

body.text: 216.001. div26 pāṃśupradānāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 216.001. Chapter 26: The <s>Pāṃśupradānāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Gift of Dust).

body.text:
216.002. yo 'sau svamāṃsatanubhiryajanāni kṛtvā tāvacciraṃ karuṇayā jagato hitāya/
216.003. tasya śramasya saphalīkaraṇāya santaḥ saṃmārjitaṃ śṛṇuta sāmpratabhāṣyamāṇam//1//
body.translated_text:
216.002. 'He who for so long, out of compassion, performed sacrifices with his own flesh and body for the welfare of the world —
216.003. to bring the fruit of that exertion, O good ones, hear what is now being spoken about the sweeping.' //1//

body.text:
216.006. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
216.006. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharatīti sūtraṃ vaktavyam/
216.007. atra tāvadbhagavattathāgatavadanāṃmodharavivarapratyudgatavacanasaratsaliladhārāsampātāpanītarāgadveṣamohamadamānamāyāśāṭhyapaṅkapaṭalānāṃ śabdanyāyāditarkaśāstrārthāvalokanotpannaprajñāpradīpaprotsāritakuśāstradarśanāndhakārāṇāṃ saṃsāratṛṣṇāchedipravarasaddharmapayaḥpānaśauṇḍānāṃ gurūṇāṃ saṃnidhau sarvāvavādakaṃ mahātmānamatimāharddhikaṃ sthaviropaguptamārabhya kāṃcideva vibuddhajanamanaḥprasādakarīṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ samanusmariṣyāmaḥ/
216.012. tatra tāvadgurubhiravahitaśrotrairbhavitavyam//
body.translated_text:
216.006. Thus have I heard.
216.006. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> — the <s>sūtra</s> should be recited in full.
216.007. Here, in the presence of the Gurus — those whose stains of passion, hatred, delusion, pride, conceit, deceit, and guile have been washed away by the streaming flood of autumnal speech issuing forth from the opening of the mouth of the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>; those whose lamps of wisdom, arisen from contemplating the meaning of the sciences of grammar, logic, and other treatises, have driven away the darkness of wrong views; those who are passionate drinkers of the excellent water of the true <s>Dharma</s> that cuts through the thirst of <s>saṃsāra</s> — we shall call to mind a certain <s>Dharma</s>-discourse that inspires faith in the minds of awakened people, concerning the great-souled Elder <s>Upagupta</s> of supreme supernatural power, the foremost of all instructors.
216.012. Here, the Gurus should listen with attentive ears.

body.text:
216.013. evamanuśrūyate--yadā bhagavān parinirvāṇakālasamaye palālanāgaṃ vinīya kumbhakārīṃ caṇḍālīṃ gopālīṃ ca, teṣāṃ mathurāmanuprāptaḥ, tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma--asyāmānanda mathurāyāṃ mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya gupto nāma gāndhiko bhaviṣyati/
216.015. tasya putro bhaviṣyatyupagupto nāma alakṣaṇako buddho yo mama varṣaśatapatinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ bhavi(kari)ṣyati/
216.017. tasyāvavādena bahavo bhikṣavaḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti/
216.017. te 'ṣṭādaśahastāmāyāmena dvādaśahastāṃ vistāreṇa caturaṅgalamātrābhiḥ śaṇakābhiḥ pūjayiṣyanti/
216.018. eṣo 'gro me ānanda śrāvakāṇāṃ bhaviṣyatyavavādakānām yaduta upagupto bhikṣuḥ/
216.019. paśyasi tvamānanda dūrata eva nīlanīlāmbararājim? evaṃ bhadanta/
216.020. eṣa ānanda rurumuṇḍo nāma parvataḥ/
216.020. atra varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya śāṇakavāsī nāma bhikṣurbhaviṣyati/
216.021. so 'tra rurumuṇḍaparvate vihāraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati, upaguptaṃ ca pravrājayiṣyati/
216.022. mathurāyāmānanda naṭo bhaṭaśca dvau bhrātarau śreṣṭhinau bhaviṣyataḥ/
216.023. tasya naṭabhaṭiketi saṃjñā bhaviṣyati/
216.024. etadagraṃ me ānanda bhaviṣyati śamathānukūlānāṃ śayyāsanānām yadidaṃ naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatanam/
216.025. athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--āścaryaṃ bhadanta yadīdṛśamāyuṣmānupagupto bahujanahitaṃ kariṣyati/
216.026. bhagavānāha--na ānanda etarhi, yathā atīte 'pyadhvani tena vinipatitaśarīreṇāpyatraiva urumuṇḍaparvate trayaḥ pārśvāḥ/
216.027. ekatra pradeśe pañca pratyekabuddhaśatāni prativasanti/
216.028. dvitīye pañcaṛṣiśatāni/
216.028. tṛtīye pañcamarkaṭaśatāni/
216.028. tatra yo 'sau pañcānāṃ markaṭaśatānām yūthapatiḥ, sa tam yūthamapahāya yatra pārśve pañca pratyekabuddhaśatāni prativasanti, tatra gataḥ/
216.030. tasya tān pratyekabuddhān dṛṣṭvā prasādo jātaḥ/
216.030. sa teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ śīrṇaparṇāni mūlaphalāni copanāmayati/
216.031. yadā ca te paryaṅkenopaviṣṭā bhavanti, sa vṛddhānte praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā yāvannavāntaṃ gatvā paryaṅkenopaviśati, yāvat te pratyekabuddhāḥ parinirvṛtāḥ/
body.translated_text:
216.013. Thus it is heard by tradition: When the Blessed One, at the time approaching <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, having tamed the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Palāla</s>, the potter-woman, the <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, and the cow-herder woman, arrived at <s>Mathurā</s>, there the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Ānanda</s>, in this <s>Mathurā</s>, a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a perfume-merchant named <s>Gupta</s>.
216.015. His son will be named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks — he who, a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, will carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s work.
216.017. By his instruction, many monks, through the abandonment of all afflictions, will directly realize <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship).
216.017. They will honor him with hemp-cloth pieces measuring eighteen cubits in length, twelve cubits in width, and four finger-breadths in size.
216.018. This one, <s>Ānanda</s>, will be the foremost of my disciples among instructors — namely, the monk <s>Upagupta</s>.
216.019. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that dark-blue line of ridges in the distance?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.'
216.020. 'That, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mountain called <s>Urumuṇḍa</s>.
216.020. There, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a monk named <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> (Wearer of Hemp).
216.021. He will establish a monastery on that <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain and will ordain <s>Upagupta</s>.
216.022. In <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, there will be two brothers, guild-masters named <s>Naṭa</s> and <s>Bhaṭa</s>.
216.023. The designation "<s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>" will become established for it.
216.024. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, will be the foremost among my lodgings conducive to <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) — namely, the forest retreat of <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.'
216.025. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the Venerable <s>Upagupta</s> will accomplish such benefit for the many.'
216.026. The Blessed One said: 'Not only now, <s>Ānanda</s>, but even in the past, with a body that had fallen away, on this very <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, there were three slopes.
216.027. On one slope, five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> dwelt.
216.028. On the second, five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages).
216.028. On the third, five hundred monkeys.
216.028. There, the leader of the troop of five hundred monkeys, having left his troop, went to the slope where the five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> dwelt.
216.030. Upon seeing those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, faith arose in him.
216.030. He offered them fallen leaves, roots, and fruits.
216.031. And when they sat cross-legged, he, having bowed at the far end, went to the near end and sat cross-legged, until those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text:
217.001. <217>sa teṣāṃ śīrṇaparṇāni mūlaphalāni copanāmayati, te na pratigṛhṇanti/
217.001. sa teṣāṃ cīvarakarṇikānyākarṣayati, pādau gṛhṇāti/
217.002. yāvat sa markaṭaścintayati--niyatamete kālagatā bhaviṣyanti/
217.003. tataḥ sa markaṭaḥ śocitvā paridevitvā ca dvitīyaṃ pārśvaṃ gato yatra pañca ṛṣiśatāni prativasanti/
217.004. te ca ṛṣayaḥ kecit kaṇḍakāpāśrayāḥ, kecidbhasmāpāśrayāḥ, kecidūrdhvahastāḥ, kecit pañcātapāvasthitāḥ/
217.005. sa teṣāṃ teṣāmīryāpathān vikopayitumārabdhaḥ/
217.005. ye kaṇḍakāpāśrayāsteṣāṃ kaṇḍakānuddharati/
217.006. bhasmāpāśrayāṇāṃ bhasma vidhunoti/
217.006. ūrdhvahastānāmadho hastaṃ pātayati/
217.007. pāñcātapāvasthitānāmagnimavakirati/
217.007. yadā ca tairīryāpatho vikopito bhavati, tadā sa teṣāmagrataḥ paryaṅkaṃ badhnāti/
217.008. yāvat tairṛṣibhirācāryāya niveditam/
217.008. tenāpi coktam--paryaṅkena tāvanniṣīdatha, yāvat tāni pañca ṛṣiśatāni paryaṅkenopaviṣṭāni/
217.009. te 'nācāryakā anupadeśakāḥ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣān dharmānāmukhīkṛtya pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkṛtavantaḥ/
217.011. atha teṣāṃ pratyekabuddhānāmetadabhavat--yat kiṃcidasmābhiḥ śreyo 'vāptam, tatsarvamimaṃ markaṭamāgamya/
217.012. tairyāvat sa markaṭaḥ phalamūlaiḥ paripālitaḥ, kālagatasya ca taccharīraṃ gandhakāṣṭhairdhmāpitam//
body.translated_text:
217.001. He offered them fallen leaves, roots, and fruits, but they did not accept.
217.001. He tugged at the corners of their robes and grasped their feet.
217.002. Then that monkey reflected: 'Surely they must have passed away.'
217.003. Then that monkey, having grieved and lamented, went to the second slope where the five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> dwelt.
217.004. Among those <s>ṛṣis</s>, some practiced the thorn-bed austerity, some the ash-bed, some held their arms upraised, and some stood in the five-fire posture.
217.005. He began to disrupt the deportment of each of them.
217.005. Those who practiced the thorn-bed — he pulled out their thorns.
217.006. Those on the ash-bed — he scattered their ashes.
217.006. Those with upraised arms — he pulled their arms down.
217.007. Those standing in the five-fire posture — he scattered their fire.
217.007. And whenever their deportment was disrupted, he sat cross-legged before them.
217.008. At length, this was reported to their teacher.
217.008. He too said: 'Sit cross-legged, then.' And so the five hundred <s>ṛṣis</s> sat cross-legged.
217.009. They, without a teacher and without instruction, directing their minds toward the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>), directly realized <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).
217.011. Then this thought occurred to those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>: 'Whatever benefit we have obtained — all of it came about because of this monkey.'
217.012. They nurtured that monkey with fruits and roots for as long as he lived, and when he died, they cremated his body with fragrant wood.

body.text:
217.014. tatkiṃ manyase ānanda? yo 'sau pañcānāṃ markaṭaśatānām yūthapatiḥ, sa eṣa upaguptaḥ/
217.015. tadāpi tena vinipatitaśarīreṇāpyatraivorumuṇḍe parvate bahujanahitaṃ kṛtam/
217.015. anāgate 'pyadhvani varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama atraivorumuṇḍe parvate bahujanahitaṃ kariṣyati/
217.016. tacca yathaivaṃ tathopadarśayiṣyāmah--yadā sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinā urumuṇḍe parvate vihāraḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ, samanvāharati--kimasau gāndhika utpannaḥ, athādyāpi notpadyate iti? paśyatyutpannam/
217.018. sa yāvat samanvāharati--yo 'sau tasya putra upagupto nāṃnā alakṣa.ṅko buddho nirdiṣṭaḥ, yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti, kimasau utpanno 'dyāpi notpadyate? tena yāvadupāyena gupto gāndhiko bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasāditaḥ/
217.021. sa yadā abhiprasannastadā sthaviraḥ saṃbahulairbhikṣubhiḥ sārdhamekadivasaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
217.022. aparasminnahanyātmadvitīyaḥ/
217.022. anyasminnahanyekākī/
217.023. yāvadgupto gandhikaḥ sthaviraṃ śāṇakavāsinamekākinaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati--na khalu āryasya kaścit paścāccchramaṇah? sthavira uvāca--jarādharmāṇāṃ kuto 'smākaṃ paścācchramaṇo bhavati? yadi kecit śraddhāpurogena pravrajanti, te 'smākaṃ paścācchramaṇā bhavanti/
217.025. gupto gāndhika uvāca--ārya, ahaṃ tāvadgṛhavāse parigṛddho viṣayābhirataśca/
217.026. na mayā śakyaṃ pravrajitum/
217.026. api tu yo 'smākaṃ putro bhavati, taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ/
217.027. sthavira uvāca--vatsa, evamastu/
217.027. api tu dṛḍhapratijñāṃ smarethāstvamiti/
217.028. yāvadguptasya gāndhikasya putro jātaḥ/
217.028. tasyāśvagupta iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
217.029. sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamadhigamyovāca--vatsa, tvayā pratijñātam--yo 'smākaṃ putro bhaviṣyati, taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ/
217.031. anujānīhi, pravrajayiṣyāmīti/
217.031. gāndhika uvāca--ārya, ayamasmākamekaputraḥ/
217.031. marṣaya naḥ/
217.032. yo 'smākaṃ dvitīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati, taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ/
217.032. yāvat sthavirah <218>śāṇakavāsī samanvāharati--kimayaṃ sa upaguptah? paśyati neti/
body.translated_text:
217.014. 'What do you think, <s>Ānanda</s>? He who was the leader of those five hundred monkeys — he is this very <s>Upagupta</s>.
217.015. Even then, with a body that had fallen away, on this very <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, he accomplished great benefit for the many.
217.015. In the future as well, a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, on this very <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, he will accomplish great benefit for the many.'
217.016. And we shall show how that came about: When the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> had established a monastery on <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, he inquired: 'Has that perfume-merchant been born yet, or has he still not been born?' He saw that he had been born.
217.018. Then he inquired: 'He whose son, named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks, has been declared — he who, a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, will carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s work — has he been born, or has he still not been born?' Then, by skillful means, the Elder caused the perfume-merchant <s>Gupta</s> to be inspired with faith in the teaching of the Blessed One.
217.021. When he was inspired with faith, the Elder, together with a number of monks, entered his house one day.
217.022. On another day, he came accompanied by just one other.
217.022. On yet another day, he came alone.
217.023. Then the perfume-merchant <s>Gupta</s>, seeing the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> alone, said: 'Does the Noble one truly have no attendant monk?' The Elder said: 'How can those of us who are subject to old age have an attendant? If anyone goes forth out of faith, he becomes our attendant.'
217.025. The perfume-merchant <s>Gupta</s> said: 'Noble one, I myself am attached to household life and delighting in sense pleasures.
217.026. I am not able to go forth.
217.026. However, whichever son is born to us, him we shall give to the Noble one as an attendant.'
217.027. The Elder said: 'My child, so be it.
217.027. But remember this firm promise of yours.'
217.028. In time, a son was born to the perfume-merchant <s>Gupta</s>.
217.028. He was given the name <s>Aśvagupta</s>.
217.029. When he had grown up, the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> went to the perfume-merchant <s>Gupta</s> and said: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever son is born to us, him we shall give to the Noble one as an attendant."
217.031. Give your permission; I shall ordain him.'
217.031. The perfume-merchant said: 'Noble one, this is our only son.
217.031. Have patience with us.
217.032. Whichever second son is born to us, him we shall give to the Noble one as an attendant.'
217.032. Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> inquired: 'Is this one <s>Upagupta</s>?' He saw that he was not.

body.text:
218.001. tena sthavireṇābhihitah--evamastu iti/
218.002. tasya yāvaddvitīyaḥ putro jātaḥ/
218.002. tasya dhanagupta iti nāma kṛtam/
218.002. so 'pi yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ, tadā sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamuvāca--vatsa, tvayā pratijñātam--yo 'smākaṃ putro bhaviṣyati, taṃ vayamāryasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dāsyāmaḥ/
218.004. ayaṃ ca te putro jātaḥ/
218.005. anujānīhi, pravrajayiṣyāmīti/
218.005. gāndhika uvāca--ārya marṣaya, eko 'smākaṃ dravyaṃ saṃśayiṣyati, sa āryasya dattaḥ/
218.007. yāvat sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī samanvāharati--kimayaṃ sa upaguptah? paśyati neti/
218.008. tataḥ sthavira uvāca--evamastu iti/
218.008. yāvadguptasya gāndhikasya tṛtīyaḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prasādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇamasamprāptaśca divyavarṇam/
218.009. tasya vistareṇa jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā upagupta iti nāma kṛtam/
218.010. so 'pi yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ, yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamabhigamyovāca--vatsa, tvayā pratijñātam--yo 'smākaṃ tṛtīyaḥ putro bhaviṣyati, bayamāryasya dāsyāmaḥ paścācchramaṇārthe/
218.012. ayaṃ te tṛtīyaḥ putra utpannaḥ/
218.013. anujānīhi, pravrājayiṣyāmīti/
218.013. gupto gāndhika uvāca--ārya, samayataḥ/
218.013. yadā lābho 'nucchedo bhaviṣyatīti, tadā anujñāsyāmi/
218.014. yadā tena samayaḥ kṛtaḥ, tadā māreṇa sarvāvatī mathurā gandhāviṣṭā/
218.015. te sarve upaguptasakāśādgandhān krīṇanti/
218.015. sa prabhūtāni dāsyati/
218.015. yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ gataḥ/
218.016. upaguptaśca gandhāpaṇe sthitaḥ/
218.016. sa dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karoti, gandhān vikrīṇīte/
218.017. sa sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinā abhihitah--vatsa, kīdṛśāste cittacetasikāḥ pravartante kliṣṭā vā akliṣṭā veti? upagupta uvāca--ārya, naiva jānāmi kīdṛśāḥ kliṣṭāścittacetasikāḥ, kīdṛśā akliṣṭā iti/
218.019. sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī uvāca--vatsa, yadi kevalaṃ cittaṃ parijñātuṃ na śakyasi, pratipakṣaṃ mocayitum/
218.020. tena tasya kṛṣṇikapaṭṭikā dattā pāṇḍurikā ca/
218.021. yadi kliṣṭaṃ cittamutpadyate, kṛṣṇikāṃ paṭṭikāṃ sthāpaya/
218.021. athākliṣṭaṃ cittamutpadyate, pāṇḍurāṃ paṭṭikāṃ sthāpaya/
218.022. śubhāṃ manasi kuru, buddhānusmṛtiṃ ca bhāvayasveti tenāsya vyapadiṣṭam/
218.023. tasya yāvadārabdhā ākliṣṭāścittacetasikāḥ pravartitum, sa dvau bhāgau kṛṣṇikānāṃ sthāpayati, ekaṃ pāṇḍurikāṇām/
218.024. yāvadardhaṃ kuṣṇikānāṃ sthāpayati ardhaṃ pāṇḍurikāṇām/
218.025. yāvat dvau bhāgau pāṇḍurikāṇāṃ sthāpayati, ekaṃ kṛṣṇikānām/
218.025. yāvadanupūrveṇa sarvāṇyeva śuklāni cittānyutpadyante, sa pāṇḍurikāṇāmeva paṭṭikāṃ sthāpayati/
218.026. dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karoti//
body.translated_text:
218.001. The Elder said: 'So be it.'
218.002. In due course, a second son was born to him.
218.002. He was named <s>Dhanagupta</s>.
218.002. When he too had grown up, the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> said to <s>Gupta</s> the perfumer: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever son is born to us, we shall give him to the venerable one for renunciation."
218.004. And this son has been born to you.
218.005. Give your permission; I shall ordain him.'
218.005. The perfumer said: 'Venerable sir, please be patient. One of our sons will inherit the property — he has been given to the venerable one.
218.007. Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> examined: 'Is this one that <s>Upagupta</s>?' He saw that he was not.
218.008. Then the Elder said: 'So be it.'
218.008. In due course, a third son was born to <s>Gupta</s> the perfumer — handsome, beautiful, pleasing, surpassing the human complexion yet not having attained the divine complexion.
218.009. For him, with elaborate birth celebrations, the name <s>Upagupta</s> was given.
218.010. When he too had grown up, the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> approached <s>Gupta</s> the perfumer and said: 'My child, you promised: "Whichever is our third son, we shall give him to the venerable one for renunciation."
218.012. This third son of yours has been born.
218.013. Give your permission; I shall ordain him.'
218.013. <s>Gupta</s> the perfumer said: 'Venerable sir, on condition:
218.013. when there is no interruption in profits, then I shall give permission.'
218.014. When this condition was made, <s>Māra</s> filled all of <s>Mathurā</s> with the scent of perfumes.
218.015. Everyone bought their perfumes from <s>Upagupta</s>.
218.015. He was giving away large quantities.
218.015. Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> went to <s>Upagupta</s>.
218.016. <s>Upagupta</s> was standing in the perfume shop.
218.016. He was conducting business righteously, selling perfumes.
218.017. The Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> said to him: 'My child, what kind of mental states and mental factors arise in you — afflicted or unafflicted?' <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'Venerable sir, I do not even know what afflicted mental states and mental factors are, or what unafflicted ones are.'
218.019. The Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsin</s> said: 'My child, if you are not able to fully comprehend the mind alone, then apply the antidote.
218.020. He gave him a black tablet and a white tablet.
218.021. When an afflicted mental state arises, place a black tablet.
218.021. When an unafflicted mental state arises, place a white tablet.
218.022. Cultivate what is wholesome, and develop mindfulness of the <s>Buddha</s>' — thus he instructed him.
218.023. As unafflicted mental states began to arise in him, at first he placed two portions of black and one of white.
218.024. Then he placed half black and half white.
218.025. Then he placed two portions of white and one of black.
218.025. Until eventually, as only pure mental states arose, he placed only white tablets.
218.026. He conducted business righteously.

body.text:
218.028. mathurāyāṃ vāsavadattā nāma gaṇikā/
218.028. tasyā dāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ gatvā gandhān krīṇāti/
218.029. so vāsavadattayā cocyate--dārike, muṣyate sa gāndhikastvayā/
218.029. bahūn gandhānānayasīti/
218.030. dārikovāca--āryaduhite, upagupto gāndhikadārako rūpasampannaścāturyamādhuryasampannaśca dharmeṇa vyavahāraṃ karori/
218.031. śrutvā ca vāsavadattāyā upaguptasakāśe sānurāgaṃ cittamutpannam/
218.031. tayā yāvaddāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ preṣitā--tvatsakāśamāgamiṣyāmi/
218.032. icchāmi tvayā sārdhaṃ ratimanubhavitum/
218.032. yāvaddāsyā <219>upagutasya niveditam/
body.translated_text:
218.028. In <s>Mathurā</s>, there was a courtesan named <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.
218.028. Her maidservant went to <s>Upagupta</s> and bought perfumes.
218.029. <s>Vāsavadattā</s> teased her: 'Girl, you are being cheated by that perfumer.
218.029. You bring back too many perfumes.'
218.030. The maidservant said: 'Noble daughter, <s>Upagupta</s>, the perfumer's son, is endowed with beauty, charm, and sweetness, and conducts business righteously.'
218.031. Hearing this, a passionate desire arose in <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s mind toward <s>Upagupta</s>.
218.031. She sent the maidservant to <s>Upagupta</s>: 'I shall come to you.
218.032. I desire to enjoy pleasure with you.'
218.032. The maidservant <219> reported this to <s>Upagupta</s>.

body.text:
219.001. upagupta uvāca akālaste bhagini maddarśanāyeti/
219.001. vāsavadattā pañcabhiḥ purāṇaśataiḥ paricārayate/
219.002. tasyā buddhirutpannā--niyataṃ pañca purāṇaśatāni notsahate dātum/
219.002. tayā yāvaddāsī upaguptasakāśaṃ preṣitā--na mamāryaputrasakāśāt kārṣāpaṇenāpi prayojanam/
219.003. kevalamāryaputreṇa saha ratimanubhaveyam/
219.004. dāsyā tathā niveditam/
219.004. upagupta uvāca--akālaste bhagini maddarśanāyeti/
219.005. yāvadanyataraḥ śreṣṭhiputro vāsavadattāyāḥ sakāśaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
219.005. anyataraśca sārthavāha uttarāpathāt pañcaśatamaśvapaṇyaṃ gṛhītvā mathurāmanuprāptaḥ/
219.006. tenābhihitam--katarā veśyā sarvapradhānā? tena śrutam--vāsavadatteti/
219.007. sa pañca puraṇaśatāni gṛhītvā bahūṃśca prābhṛtān vāsavadattāyāḥ sakāśāmabhigataḥ/
219.008. tato vāsavadattayā lobhākṛṣṭena taṃ śreṣṭhiputraṃ praghātayitvā^vaskare prakṣipya sārthavāhena saha ratimanubhutā/
219.009. yāvat sa śreṣṭhiputro bandhubhiravaskarāduddhṛtya(tah)/
219.009. rājño niveditam/
219.010. tato rājñā abhihitam--gacchantu bhavantaḥ, vāsavadattāṃ hastapādau karṇanāsaṃ ca cchittvā śmaśāne chorayantu/
219.011. yāvat tairvāsavadattā hastapādau karṇanāsaṃ ca cchittvā śmaśāne choritā/
219.012. yāvadupaguptena śrutam--vāsavadattā hastapādau karṇanāsaṃ ca cchittvā śmaśāne choritā/
219.013. tasya buddhirutpannā--pūrvaṃ tayā mama viṣayanimittaṃ darśanamākāṅkṣitam/
219.013. idānīṃ tu tasyā hastapādau karṇanāsaṃ ca vikārtitau, idānīṃ tu tasyā darśanakāla iti/
219.014. āha ca--
219.015. yadā praśastāmbarasaṃvṛtāṅgī abhūdvicitrābharaṇairvibhūṣitā/
219.017. mokṣārthināṃ janmaparānmukhānāṃ śreyastadāsyāstu na darśanaṃ syāt//2//
body.translated_text:
219.001. <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'It is not the time for you, sister, to see me.'
219.001. <s>Vāsavadattā</s> charged five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> (ancient coins) for her services.
219.002. She thought: 'Surely he cannot afford to give five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>.'
219.002. She sent the maidservant to <s>Upagupta</s>: 'I have no need of money from the noble son.
219.003. I wish only to enjoy pleasure with the noble son.'
219.004. The maidservant reported this accordingly.
219.004. <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'It is not the time for you, sister, to see me.'
219.005. Meanwhile, a certain merchant's son had entered <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s house.
219.005. And a certain caravan-leader, having brought five hundred horses as merchandise from the northern region, arrived at <s>Mathurā</s>.
219.006. He asked: 'Which courtesan is the foremost of all?' He was told: '<s>Vāsavadattā</s>.'
219.007. Taking five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> and many gifts, he went to <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s house.
219.008. Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, drawn by greed, had that merchant's son murdered and thrown into the refuse heap, and enjoyed herself with the caravan-leader.
219.009. The merchant's son was recovered from the refuse heap by his relatives.
219.009. The matter was reported to the king.
219.010. Then the king ordered: 'Go, sirs, cut off <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s hands, feet, ears, and nose, and abandon her in the charnel ground.'
219.011. They cut off <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s hands, feet, ears, and nose and abandoned her in the charnel ground.
219.012. <s>Upagupta</s> heard: '<s>Vāsavadattā</s> has had her hands, feet, ears, and nose cut off and been abandoned in the charnel ground.'
219.013. This thought arose in him: 'Previously she desired to see me because of her attachment to sense objects.
219.013. Now her hands, feet, ears, and nose have been severed — now is the time to see her.'
219.014. And he said:
219.015. 'When she was adorned with excellent garments covering her limbs and adorned with variegated ornaments,
219.017. for those seeking liberation, those averse to rebirth — then, seeing her would not have been for their welfare.' //2//

body.text:
219.019. idānīṃ tu tasyāḥ kāle 'yaṃ draṣṭuṃ gatamānarāgaharṣāyāḥ/
219.020. niśitāsivikṣatāyāḥ svabhāvaniyatasya rūpasya//3//
body.translated_text:
219.019. 'Now, however, he has gone to see her at the proper time, her whose passion and delight have departed,
219.020. who has been cut by sharp swords — to see the true nature of form.' //3//

body.text:
219.021. yāvadekena dārakenopasthāyakena cchatramādāya praśānteneryāpathena śmaśānamanuprāptaḥ/
219.022. tasyāśca preṣikā pūrvaguṇānurāgāt samīpe 'vasthitā kākādīn nivārayati/
219.022. tayā ca vāsavadattāyā niveditam--āryaduhitaḥ, yasya tvayā ahaṃ sakāśaṃ punaḥ punaranupreṣitā, ayaṃ sa upagupto 'bhyagataḥ/
219.024. niyatameṣa kāmarāgārta āgato bhaviṣyati/
219.024. śrutvā ca vāsavadattā kathayati--
219.026. pranaṣṭaśobhāṃ duḥkhārtāṃ bhūmau rudhirapiñjarām/
219.027. māṃ dṛṣṭvā kathametasya kāmarāgo bhaviṣyati//4//
body.translated_text:
219.021. With a single attendant boy carrying a parasol, with peaceful deportment, he arrived at the charnel ground.
219.022. Her maidservant, out of affection for her former qualities, stood nearby, warding off crows and the like.
219.022. She informed <s>Vāsavadattā</s>: 'Noble daughter, the one to whom you sent me again and again — this <s>Upagupta</s> has arrived.
219.024. Surely he has come afflicted with desire.'
219.024. Hearing this, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> said:
219.026. 'My beauty is destroyed, I am racked with pain, I lie on the ground stained with blood;
219.027. seeing me thus, how could desire arise in him?' //4//

body.text:
219.028. tataḥ preṣikāmuvāca--yau hastapādau karṇanāsaṃ ca maccharīrādvikartitau, tau śleṣayeti/
219.029. tayā yāvat śleṣayitvā paṭṭakena pracchāditā/
219.029. upaguptaścāgatya vāsavadattāyā agrataḥ sthitaḥ/
219.029. tato vāsavadattā upaguptamagrataḥ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati--āryaputra, yadā maccharīraṃ svasthabhūtaṃ viṣayaratyanukūlaṃ tadā mayā āryaputrasya punaḥ punardūtī visarjitā/
219.031. āryaputreṇābhihitam--
body.translated_text:
219.028. Then she said to the maidservant: 'Reattach my severed hands, feet, ears, and nose to my body.'
219.029. She reattached them and covered her with a cloth.
219.029. <s>Upagupta</s> came and stood before <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.
219.029. Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, seeing <s>Upagupta</s> standing before her, said: 'Noble son, when my body was healthy and fit for sensual pleasure, I sent a messenger to the noble son again and again.
219.031. The noble son said:

body.text:
220.001. <220>akālaste bhagini māṃ darśanāyeti/
220.001. idānīṃ mama hastapādau karṇanāsau ca vikartitau, svarudhirakardama evāvasthitā/
220.002. idānīṃ kimāgato 'si? āha ca--
220.003. idam yadā paṅkajagarbhakomalaṃ mahārhavastrābharaṇairvibhūṣitam/
220.005. babhūva gātraṃ mama darśanakṣamaṃ tadā na dṛṣṭo 'si mayālpabhāgyayā//5//
body.translated_text:
220.001. <220>"It is not the time for you, sister, to see me."
220.001. Now my hands, feet, ears, and nose have been severed; I remain standing in my own mud of blood.
220.002. Why have you come now?'
220.002. And she said:
220.003. 'When this body of mine was soft as a lotus bud, adorned with costly garments and ornaments,
220.005. it was fit to be seen — but then I, the unlucky one, did not see you.' //5//

body.text:
220.007. etarhi kiṃ draṣṭumihāgato 'si yadā śarīraṃ mama darśanākṣamam/
220.009. nivṛttalīlāratiharṣavismayaṃ bhayāvahaṃ śoṇitapaṅkalepanam//6//
body.translated_text:
220.007. 'Now for what purpose have you come to see me, when my body is unfit to be seen,
220.009. when play, pleasure, delight, and wonder have departed, and it is fearsome, smeared with blood and mud?' //6//

body.text:
220.011. upagupta uvāca--
220.012. nāhaṃ bhagini kāmārtaḥ saṃnidhāvāgatastava/
220.013. kāmānāmaśubhānāṃ tu svabhāvaṃ draṣṭumāgataḥ//7//
body.translated_text:
220.011. <s>Upagupta</s> said:
220.012. 'I have not come to you afflicted with desire, sister.
220.013. I have come to see the true nature of impure sensual desires.' //7//

body.text:
220.014. pracchāditā vastravibhūṣaṇādyairbāhyairvicitrairmadanānukūlaiḥ/
220.016. nirīkṣyamāṇā api yatnavadbhir nāpyatra dṛṣṭāsi bhavedyathāvat//8//
body.translated_text:
220.014. 'Covered with garments, ornaments, and other external adornments, variegated and conducive to passion,
220.016. even when examined by those who look with care, you were never truly seen as you really are.' //8//

body.text:
220.018. idaṃ tu rūpaṃ tava dṛśyametat sthitaṃ svabhāve racanādviyuktam/
220.020. te 'paṇḍitāste ca vigarhaṇīyā ye prākṛte 'smin kuṇape ramante//9//
body.translated_text:
220.018. 'But this form of yours now visible, standing in its own nature, stripped of embellishment —
220.020. those are foolish and those are reprehensible who delight in this common heap of bones.' //9//

body.text:
220.022. tvacāvanaddhe rudhirāvasakte carmāvṛte māṃsaghanāvalipte/
220.024. śirāsahasraiśca vṛte samantāt ko nāma rajyeta itaḥ śarīre//10//
body.translated_text:
220.022. 'Wrapped in skin, steeped in blood, covered in hide, thickly coated with flesh,
220.024. surrounded on all sides by thousands of veins — who indeed would be enamored of this body?' //10//

body.text:
220.026. api ca bhagini/
220.027. bahirbhadrāṇi rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā bālo 'bhirajyate/
220.028. abhyantaraviduṣṭāni jñātvā dhīro virajyate//11//

220.029. avakṛṣṭāvakṛṣṭasya kuṇapasya hyamedhyatā/
220.030. medhyāḥ kāmopasaṃhārāḥ kāminaḥ śubhasaṃjñinaḥ//12//
body.translated_text:
220.029. 'The impurity of the debased body, degraded and degraded further, is vile;
220.030. yet those who follow sensual desires, perceiving them as beautiful, consider sensual attractions as pure.' //12//

body.text:
221.001. <221>iha hi--
221.002. daurgandhyaṃ prativāryate bahuvidhairgandhairamedhyākarairvaikṛtyaṃ bahirādhriyeta vividhairvastrādibhirbhūṣaṇaiḥ/
221.004. svedakledamalādayo 'pyaśucayastānnirharatyambhasā yenāmedhyakaraṅkametadaśubhaṃ kāmātmabhiḥ sevyate//13//

221.006. saṃbuddhasya tu ye vacaḥ suvacasaḥ śṛṇvanti kurvantyapi te kāmāñ śramaśokaduḥkhajananān sadbhiḥ sadā garhitān/
221.008. tyaktvā kāmanimittamuktamanasaḥ śānte vane nirgatāḥ pāram yānti bhavārṇavasya mahataḥ saṃśritya mārgaplavam//14//
body.translated_text:
221.006. 'But those who hear and practice the well-spoken words of the Perfectly Awakened One, having abandoned sensual desires — those generators of toil, grief, and suffering, always condemned by the good —
221.008. with minds freed from the cause of desire, having gone forth to the peaceful forest, they cross to the far shore of the great ocean of existence, having resorted to the raft of the Path.' //14//

body.text:
221.010. śrutvā vāsavadattā saṃsārādudvignā/
221.010. buddhaguṇānusmaraṇāccāvarjitahṛdayovāca--
221.011. evametattathā sarvam yathā vadasi paṇḍita/
221.012. me tvāṃ sādhuṃ samāsādya buddhasya vacanaṃ śrutam//15//
body.translated_text:
221.010. Hearing this, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> became disillusioned with <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth).
221.010. With her heart won over through the remembrance of the <s>Buddha</s>'s virtues, she said:
221.011. 'It is exactly so, all is just as you say, O wise one.
221.012. Having encountered you, a virtuous one, I have heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.' //15//

body.text:
221.013. yāvadupaguptena vāsavadattāyā anupūrvikāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyāni saṃprakāśitāni/
221.014. upaguptaśca vāsavadattāyāḥ śarīrasvabhāvamavagamya kāmadhātuvairāgyaṃ gataḥ/
221.014. tenātmīyayā dharmadeśanayā sahasatyābhisamayādanāgāmiphalaṃ vāsavadattayā ca srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptam/
221.015. tato vāsavadattā dṛṣṭasatyā upaguptaṃ saṃrāgayantyuvāca--
221.017. tavānubhāvātpihitaḥ sughoro hyapāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ/
221.019. apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaśca mayopalabdhaḥ//16//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upagupta</s>, having given <s>Vāsavadattā</s> a graduated discourse, revealed the truths to her. <s>Upagupta</s>, having contemplated the true nature of <s>Vāsavadattā's</s> body, attained dispassion toward the realm of desire. Through his own teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, he attained the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) through the simultaneous realization of the truths, and <s>Vāsavadattā</s> attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
