Then <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, having seen the truths, spoke to <s>Upagupta</s> with affection: 'By your power, the terrible path to the lower realms, full of many faults, has been closed; the meritorious path to heaven has been opened, and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.' //16//

body.text:
221.021. api ca/
221.021. eṣāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharma ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ cetyāha--
221.023. eṣā vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ vibuddhanavakamalavimaladhavalanetram/
221.024. tamamarabudhajanamahitaṃ jinaṃ virāgaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca//17// iti//
body.translated_text: Moreover, she said: 'I go for refuge to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and to the <s>Dharma</s> and the community of monks' — 'I go for refuge to the one whose eyes are pure, white, like newly-opened lotuses, the awakened one, honored by gods, wise beings, and humans, the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), the passionless one, and to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' //17//

body.text:
221.025. yāvadupagupto vāsavadattāṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya prakrāntaḥ/
221.025. aciraprakrānte copagupte vāsavadattā kālagatā deveṣūpapannā/
221.026. devataiśca mathurāyāmārocitam--vāsavadattayā upaguptasakāśāddharmadeśanāṃ śrutvā āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni, deveṣūpapanneti/
221.027. śrutvā ca mathurāvāsatavyena janakāyena vāsavadattāyāḥ śarīre pūjā kṛtā//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upagupta</s>, having edified <s>Vāsavadattā</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, departed. Shortly after <s>Upagupta's</s> departure, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> died and was reborn among the gods. And the deities announced in <s>Mathurā</s>: '<s>Vāsavadattā</s>, having heard the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> from <s>Upagupta</s>, has seen the Noble Truths and has been reborn among the gods.' Having heard this, the people dwelling in <s>Mathurā</s> performed worship upon the body of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.

body.text:
221.029. yāvat sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamabhigamyovāca--anujānīhi upaguptaṃ pravrājayiṣyāmīti/
221.030. gupto gāndhika uvāca--ārya, eṣa samayaḥ/
221.030. yadā na lābho na cchedo bhaviṣyati, tadā anujñāsyāmīti/
221.031. yāvat sthaviraśāṇakavāsinā ṛddhyā tathā adhiṣṭhitam yathā <222>
body.translated_text: Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> went to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-merchant and said: 'Give your permission; I shall ordain <s>Upagupta</s>.' <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-merchant said: 'Venerable one, this is the arrangement: when there is neither profit nor loss [in business], then I shall give permission.' Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> so empowered it by his supernatural power that—

body.text:
222.001. na lābho na cchedaḥ/
222.001. tato gupto gāndhiko gaṇayati, tulayati, māpayati, paśyati--na lābho na cchedaḥ/
222.002. tataḥ sthaviraḥ śāṇakavāsī guptaṃ gāndhikamuvāca--ayaṃ hi bhagavatā buddhena nirdiṣṭo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti/
222.003. anujānīhi, pravrājayiṣyāmīti/
222.003. yāvadguptena gāndhikenābhyanujñātaḥ/
222.004. tataḥ sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinā upagupto naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatanaṃ nītaḥ, upasampāditaśca/
222.005. jñapticaturthaṃ ca karma vyavasitam/
222.005. upaguptena ca sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
222.006. tataḥ sthavireṇa śāṇakavāsinābhihitam--vatsa upagupta, tvaṃ bhagavatā nirdiṣṭo vaiṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mamopagupto nāma bhikṣurbhaviṣyatyalakṣaṇako buddhaḥ, yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyatīti/
222.008. eṣo 'gro me ānanda śrāvakāṇāmavavādakānām yaduta upagupto bhikṣuḥ/
222.009. idānīṃ vatsa śāsanahitaṃ kuruṣveti/
222.009. upagupta uvāca--evamastu iti/
222.010. tataḥ sa dharmaśravaṇe 'dhīṣṭaḥ/
222.010. mathurāyāṃ ca śabdo visṛtah--upagupto nāmālakṣaṇako buddho 'dya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyatīti/
222.011. śrutvā cānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi nirgatāni/
222.011. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samāpadyāvalokayati--kathaṃ tathāgatena pariṣaṇṇā? paśyati cārdhacandrākāreṇa parṣadavasthitā/
222.013. yāvadavalokayati--kathaṃ tathāgatena dharmadeśanā kṛtā? paśyati pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasamprakāśanā kṛtā/
222.014. so 'pi pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasamprakāśanāṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
222.015. māreṇa ca tasyāṃ parṣadi muktāhāravarṣamutsṛṣṭam, vaineyānāṃ manāṃsi vyākulīkṛtāni, ekenāpi satyadarśanaṃ na kṛtam/
222.016. yāvat sthaviropagupto vyavalokayati--kenāyaṃ vyākṣepaḥ kṛtah? paśyati māreṇa/
222.017. yāvaddvitīye divase bahutarako janakāyo nirgataḥ/
222.017. upagupto dharmaṃ deśayati, muktāhāraṃ ca varṣopavarṣitamiti/
222.018. yāvat dvitīye 'pi divase sthaviropaguptena pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyasamprakāśanāyāmārabdhāyāṃ māreṇa cāsyāṃ parṣadi suvarṇavarṣamutsṛṣṭam, vaineyānāṃ manāṃsi saṃlakṣobhitāni, ekenāpi satyadarśanaṃ na kṛtam/
222.020. yāvat sthaviropagupto vyavalokayati--kenāyaṃ vyākṣepaḥ kṛtah? paśyati māreṇa pāpīyaseti/
222.021. yāvat tṛtīye śivase bahutarako janakāyo nirgataḥ/
222.022. upagupto dharmaṃ deśayati, muktāvarṣaṃ suvarṇavarṣaṃ ca patatīti/
222.023. yāvat tṛtīye 'pi divase sthaviropaguptaḥ pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyā nyārabdhaḥ saṃprakāśayitum/
222.024. māreṇa ca nātidūre nāṭakamārabdham/
222.024. divyāni ca vādyāni saṃpravāditāni, divyāścāpsaraso nāṭayituṃ pravṛttāḥ/
222.025. yāvadvītarāgo janakāyo divyāni rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā divyāṃśca śabdāñ śrutvā māreṇākṛṣṭaḥ/
222.026. ato māreṇopaguptasya parṣadākṛṣṭā/
222.026. praītimanasā māreṇa sthaviropaguptasya śirasi mālā buddhā/
222.027. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samanvāharitumārabdhah--ko 'yam? paśyati māraḥ/
222.028. tasya buddhirutpannā--ayaṃ māro bhagavacchāsane mahāntaṃ vyākṣepaṃ karoti/
222.029. kimarthamayaṃ bhagavatā na vinītah? paśyati mamāyaṃ vineyaḥ/
222.029. tasya ca vinayāt sattvānugrahādahaṃ bhagavatā alakṣaṇako buddho nirdiṣṭaḥ/
222.030. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ samanvāharati--kimasya vinayakāla upasthita āhosvinneti? paśyati--vinayakāla upasthitaḥ/
222.031. tataḥ sthaviropaguptena trayaḥ kuṇapā gṛhītāh--ahikṛṇapaṃ kurkurakuṇapaṃ manuṣyakuṇapam/
222.032. ṛddhyā ca <223>puṣpamālāmabhinirmāya mārasakāśamabhigataḥ/
body.translated_text: there was neither profit nor loss. Then <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-merchant counted, weighed, and measured, and found: there was neither profit nor loss. Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> said to <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-merchant: 'This one was designated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>: "A hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, he shall carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>." Give your permission; I shall ordain him.' Then <s>Gupta</s> the perfume-merchant gave his permission. The Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> took <s>Upagupta</s> to the <s>Naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatana</s> (the Forest Hermitage of the Actor's Ward) and gave him full ordination. The formal act with the fourth announcement was completed. And <s>Upagupta</s> directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Then the Elder <s>Śāṇakavāsī</s> said: 'Son <s>Upagupta</s>, you were designated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "A hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a monk named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks, who shall carry out the work of the <s>Buddha</s>." The Blessed One said: "This one, <s>Ānanda</s>, is foremost among my disciples who give instruction — namely, the monk <s>Upagupta</s>." Now, son, perform the work that benefits the teaching.' <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'So be it.' Then he applied himself to the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. And word spread in <s>Mathurā</s>: 'The one named <s>Upagupta</s>, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> today.' Having heard this, many hundreds of thousands of beings came forth. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, entering meditation, examined: 'How did the <s>Tathāgata</s> seat his assembly?' He saw that the assembly was arranged in a semicircle. Then he examined: 'How did the <s>Tathāgata</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>?' He saw that, having first given an account of past deeds, the revelation of the truths was made. He too, having first given an account of past deeds, began the revelation of the truths. But <s>Māra</s> released a shower of pearl necklaces upon that assembly, agitating the minds of those to be trained, and not a single one attained the vision of truth. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> examined: 'By whom has this disturbance been caused?' He saw: by <s>Māra</s>. On the second day, an even greater crowd came forth, hearing that <s>Upagupta</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> and that showers of pearl necklaces were falling. On the second day too, when the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having given an account of past deeds, had begun the revelation of the truths, <s>Māra</s> released a shower of gold upon that assembly, agitating the minds of those to be trained, and not a single one attained the vision of truth. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> examined: 'By whom has this disturbance been caused?' He saw: by <s>Māra</s>, the Evil One. On the third day, an even greater crowd came forth, hearing that <s>Upagupta</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> and that showers of pearls and gold were falling. On the third day too, when the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having given an account of past deeds, began to reveal the truths, <s>Māra</s> arranged a dramatic performance nearby. Divine musical instruments were played, and divine <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) began to dance. Those beings, not yet free from passion, seeing the divine forms and hearing the divine sounds, were drawn away by <s>Māra</s>. Thus <s>Māra</s> drew away <s>Upagupta's</s> assembly. With a delighted mind, <s>Māra</s> bound a garland on the Elder <s>Upagupta's</s> head. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> began to investigate: 'Who is this?' He saw: <s>Māra</s>. The thought arose in him: 'This <s>Māra</s> creates great obstruction to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Why was he not tamed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' He saw: 'He is to be tamed by me. And it is for the sake of taming him and benefiting beings that I was designated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks.' The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> investigated: 'Has the time for his taming arrived or not?' He saw: the time for his taming had arrived. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> took three carcasses — a snake carcass, a dog carcass, and a human carcass. Having conjured a flower garland by supernatural power, he went to <s>Māra</s>.

body.text:
223.001. dṛṣṭvā ca mārasya prītirutpannā--upagupto 'pi mayā ākṛṣṭa iti/
223.002. tato māreṇa svaśarīramupanāmitam/
223.002. sthaviropaguptaḥ svayameva badhnāti/
223.002. tataḥ sthaviropaguptenāhikuṇapaṃ mārasya baddham, kurkurakuṇapaṃ grīvāyām, karṇavasaktaṃ manuṣyakuṇapaṃ ca/
223.004. tataḥ samālabhyovāca--
223.005. bhikṣujanapratikūlā mālā baddhā yathaiva me bhavatā/
223.006. kāmijanapratikūlaṃ tava kuṇapamidaṃ mayā baddham//18//
body.translated_text: Seeing him, <s>Māra</s> was delighted: '<s>Upagupta</s> too has been won over by me.' Then <s>Māra</s> offered his own body. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> himself bound them — he bound the snake carcass on <s>Māra</s>, the dog carcass on his neck, and the human carcass hung from his ear. Then, touching them, he spoke: 'Just as a garland disagreeable to monks was bound upon me by you, so this carcass, disagreeable to pleasure-seekers, has been bound upon you by me.' //18//

body.text:
223.007. yatte balaṃ bhavati tatpratidarśayasva buddhātmajena hi sahādya samāgato 'si/
223.009. udvṛttamapyanilabhinnataraṃgavakraṃ vyāvartane malayakukṣiṣu sāgarāmbhaḥ//19//
body.translated_text: 'Show whatever power you possess — for today you have encountered a son of the <s>Buddha</s>. Even the waters of the ocean, though vast and wild with waves broken by the wind, turn back at the slopes of <s>Malaya</s>.' //19//

body.text:
223.011. atha mārastaṃ kuṇapamapanetumārabdhaḥ/
223.011. paramapi ca svayamanupraviśya pipīlika ivādrirājamapanayituṃ na śaśāka/
223.012. asamartho vaihāyasamutpatyovāca--
223.013. yadi moktuṃ na śakyāmi kaṇṭhāt śvakuṇapaṃ svayam/
223.014. anye devāpi mokṣyante matto 'bhyadhikatejasaḥ//20//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> began to try to remove that carcass. But even entering into his utmost effort, he could not remove it — like an ant trying to move the king of mountains. Unable to do so, he flew up into the sky and said: 'If I myself cannot free this dog carcass from my neck, other gods of greater power than mine will free me.' //20//

body.text:
223.015. sthavira uvāca--
223.016. brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ śatakratuṃ vā dīptaṃ vā praviśa hutāśamarṇavaṃ vā/
223.018. na kledaṃ na ca pariśoṣaṇaṃ na bhedaṃ kaṇṭhasthaṃ kuṇapamidaṃ tu yāsyatīha//21//
body.translated_text: The Elder said: 'Go for refuge to <s>Brahmā</s>, or to <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), or enter the blazing fire, or the ocean — this carcass on your neck will not dissolve, nor dry up, nor break apart here.' //21//

body.text:
223.020. samahendrarudropendradraviṇeśvarayamavaruṇakuberavāsavadīnāṃ devānāmabhigamya akṛtārtha eva brahmāṇamabhigataḥ/
223.021. tena coktah--marṣaya vatsa,
223.022. śiṣyeṇa daśabalasya svayamṛddhyā kṛtāntamaryādā/
223.023. kastāṃ bhettuṃ śakto velāṃ varuṇālayasyeva//22//
body.translated_text: Having gone to the gods — <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, the Lord of Wealth, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and others — without accomplishing his goal, he went to <s>Brahmā</s>. And <s>Brahmā</s> said: 'Be patient, my son. The disciple of the Ten-Powered One has himself established a boundary by his supernatural power. Who can break it — as one cannot break the boundary of the ocean?' //22//

body.text:
223.024. api padmanālasūtraiebaddhvā himavantamuccharet kaścit/
223.025. na tu tava kaṇṭhāsaktaṃ śvakuṇapamidamuddhareyamaham//23//
body.translated_text: 'Even if someone were to bind <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas) with lotus-stalk fibers and lift it up, I could not remove this dog carcass fixed to your neck.' //23//

body.text:
223.026. kāmaṃ mamāpi mahadasti balaṃ tathāpi nāhaṃ tathāgatasutasya balena tulyaḥ/
223.028. tejasvināṃ na khalu na jvalane 'sti kiṃ tu nāsau dyutirhutavahe ravimaṇḍale yā//24//
body.translated_text: 'Indeed, great is my power too; yet I am not equal in power to the son of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The luminous ones indeed have splendor in fire, but that radiance in the fire is not the same as that of the sun's disc.' //24//

body.text:
224.001. <224>māro 'bravīt--kimidānīmājñāpayasi? kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmīti? brahmābravīt--
224.002. śaghrīṃ tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja yaṃ sametya bhraṣṭo hi yaḥ kṣititale bhavatīha janturuttiṣṭhati kṣitimasāvavalambya bhūyaḥ//25//
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said: 'What do you command now? To whom shall I go for refuge?' <s>Brahmā</s> said: 'Go quickly for refuge to that very one, approaching whom — for the being who has fallen to the ground rises again by leaning on the earth itself.' //25//

body.text:
224.006. atha mārastathāgataśiṣyasāmarthyamupalabhya cintayāmāsa--
224.007. brahmaṇā pūjyate yasya śiṣyāṇāmapi śāsanam/
224.008. tasya buddhasya sāmarthya pramātuṃ ko nu śaknuyāt//26//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, having perceived the power of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> disciple, reflected: 'Whose disciple's authority is honored even by <s>Brahmā</s> — who could measure the power of that <s>Buddha</s>?' //26//

body.text:
224.009. kartukāmo 'bhaviṣyatkāṃ śiṣṭiṃ sa mama suvrataḥ/
224.010. yāṃ nākariṣyatkṣāntyā tu tenāhamanurakṣitaḥ//27//
body.translated_text: 'What discipline would that holy one of good vows have wished to impose upon me — yet he did not do so out of patience, and by that I was protected.' //27//

body.text:
224.011. kiṃ bahunā?
224.012. adyāvaimi munermahākaruṇatāṃ tasyātimaitryātmanaḥ sarvopadravavipramuktamanasaścāmīkarādridyuteḥ/
224.014. mohāndhena hi tatra tatra sa mayā taistair nayaiḥ kheditastenāhaṃ ca tathāpi nāma balinā naivāpriyaṃ śrāvitaḥ//28//
body.translated_text: 'What more need be said? Today I understand the great compassion of that Sage, whose nature is supreme loving-kindness, whose mind is free from all afflictions, whose radiance is like a mountain of gold. Blinded by delusion, here and there I troubled him by various stratagems — and yet that mighty one never uttered a single harsh word to me.' //28//

body.text:
224.016. atha kāmadhātvadhipatirmāro nāstyanyā gatiranyatropaguptakādeveti jñātvā sarvamutsṛjya sthaviropaguptasamīpamupetya pādayor nipatyovāca--bhadanta, kimaviditametadbhadantasya yathā bodhimūlamupādāya mayā bhagavato vipriyaśatāni kṛtāni? kutah?
224.019. śālāyāṃ brāhmaṇagrāme māmāsādya sa gautamaḥ/
224.020. bhaktacchedamapi prāpya nākārṣānmama vipriyam//29//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>, the lord of the realm of desire, knowing 'there is no other refuge except <s>Upagupta</s>,' abandoned everything and went to the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>. Falling at his feet, he said: 'Venerable Sir, is it not known to you, Venerable Sir, how many hundreds of offenses I committed against the <s>Bhagavān</s>, beginning from the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree? How so? In the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> village of <s>Śālā</s>, that <s>Gautama</s>, having encountered me and even having his food cut off, did no unkindness to me.' //29//

body.text:
224.021. gaurbhūtvā sarpavat sthitvā kṛtvā śākaṭikākṛtim/
224.022. sa mayāyāsito nātho na cāhaṃ tena hiṃsitaḥ//30//
body.translated_text: 'Having become a cow, having stood as a serpent, having taken the form of a cart-driver — the Lord was tormented by me, yet I was not harmed by him.' //30//

body.text:
224.023. tvayā punarahaṃ vīra tyaktvā (tu) sahajāṃ dāyām/
224.024. sadevāsuramadhyeṣu lokeṣvadya viḍambitaḥ//31//
body.translated_text: 'But by you, O hero, abandoning your innate compassion, I have been humiliated today in the worlds of gods and <s>Asuras</s>.' //31//

body.text:
224.025. sthaviro 'bravīt--pāpīyan, kathamaparīkṣyaiva tathāgatamāhātmyeṣyu śrāvakamupasaṃharasi--
224.026. kiṃ sarṣapeṇa samatāṃ nayasīha meruṃ khadyotakena raviṃ maṇḍalinā samudram/
224.028. anyā hi sā daśabalasya kṛpā prajāsu na śrāvakasya hi mahākaruṇāsti saumya//32//
body.translated_text:
224.025. The elder said: 'Evil One, how can you, without examination, compare a disciple to the greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?'
224.026. 'Do you here equate a mustard seed with <s>Meru</s>, a firefly with the sun, a puddle with the ocean?
224.028. Different indeed is the compassion of the Ten-Powered One toward beings — a disciple does not possess the great compassion, gentle one.' //32//

body.text:
224.030. api ca--
224.031. yadarthena bhagavatā sāparodho 'pi marṣitaḥ/
224.032. idaṃ tat kāraṇaṃ sākṣādasmābhirupalakṣitam//33//
body.translated_text:
224.030. 'Moreover:
224.031. For a certain purpose, even an offense was forgiven by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
224.032. This very reason has been directly observed by us.' //33//

body.text:
225.001. <225>māra uvāca--
225.002. brūhi brūhi śrīmatastasya bhāvaṃ saṅgaṃ chettuṃ kṣāntiguptavratasya/
225.004. yo 'sau mohānnityamāyāsito me tenāhaṃ ca prekṣito maitryeṇaiva//34//
body.translated_text:
225.001. <s>Māra</s> said:
225.002. 'Tell, tell me the nature of that glorious one, whose vow is guarded by patience, in order to cut my attachment —
225.004. he whom I, out of delusion, constantly tormented, yet he always regarded me with loving-kindness alone.' //34//

body.text:
225.006. sthavira uvāca--śṛṇu saumya, tvaṃ hi bhagavatyasakṛdasakṛdavaskhalitaḥ/
225.006. na ca buddhāvropitānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanyat prakṣālanamanyatra tathāgataprasādādeva/
225.008. tadetatkāraṇaṃ tena paśyatā dīrghadarśinā/
225.009. tvaṃ nāpriyamiha proktaḥ priyāṇyeva tu lambhitaḥ//35//
body.translated_text:
225.006. The elder said: 'Listen, gentle one. You have repeatedly and again stumbled against the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
225.006. And there is no other means of cleansing the unwholesome states heaped upon a <s>Buddha</s> than faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s> itself.
225.008. This very reason was seen by that far-seeing one.
225.009. You were never spoken to harshly; only kind things were given to you.' //35//

body.text:
225.010. nyāyenānena bhaktistava hṛdi janitā tenāgramatinā svalpāpi hyatra bhaktirbhavati matimatāṃ nirvāṇaphaladā/
225.012. saṃkṣepādyatkṛtaṃ te vṛjinamiha mune mohāndhamanasā sarvaṃ prakṣālitaṃ tattava hṛdayagataiḥ śraddhāmbuvisaraiḥ//36//
body.translated_text:
225.010. 'By this very principle, devotion was generated in your heart by that foremost of minds; for even a little devotion here yields the fruit of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> for the wise.
225.012. In brief, whatever sins were committed by you here, O sage, with a mind blinded by delusion — all that has been washed away by the streams of the waters of faith flowing from your heart.' //36//

body.text:
225.014. atha māraḥ kadambapuṣpavadāhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ sarvāṅgena praṇipatyovāca--
225.015. sthāne mayā bahuvidhaṃ parikhedito 'sau prāk siddhitaśca bhuvi siddhamanorathena/
225.017. sarvaṃ ca marṣitamṛṣipravareṇa tena putrāparādha iva sānunayena pitrā//37//
body.translated_text:
225.014. Then <s>Māra</s>, his hair-pores bristling with joy like a <s>kadamba</s> flower, bowed with his whole body and said:
225.015. 'Rightly was he tormented by me in many ways before, and that one with fulfilled desires achieved perfection on earth.
225.017. And all was forgiven by that supreme sage, as a father affectionately forgives the offense of a son.' //37//

body.text:
225.019. sa buddhaprasādāpyāyitamanāḥ suciraṃ buddhaguṇānanusmṛtya sthavirasya padayor nipatyovāca--
225.020. anugraho paraḥ kṛtastvayā niveśitam yanmayi buddhagauravam/
225.022. idaṃ tu kaṇṭhavyavalambi maitryā maharṣikopābharaṇaṃ visarjaya//38//
body.translated_text:
225.019. He, with his mind nourished by faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, having for a long time recollected the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, fell at the elder's feet and said:
225.020. 'The supreme kindness has been done by you — you have established in me reverence for the <s>Buddha</s>.
225.022. But this ornament of the Great Sage's anger hanging at my throat — release it with loving-kindness.' //38//

body.text:
225.024. sthavira uvāca--samayato vimokṣyāmīti/
225.024. māra uvāca--kaḥ samaya iti? sthavira uvāca--adyaprabhṛti bhikṣavo na viheṭhayitavyā iti/
225.025. māro 'bravīt--na viheṭhayiṣye/
225.025. kamaparamājñāpayasīti? sthavira uvāca--evaṃ tāvacchāsanakāryaṃ prati mamājñā/
225.026. svakāryaṃ prati vijñāpayiṣyāmi bhavantam/
225.027. tato māraḥ sasambhrama uvāca--prasīda sthavira, kimājñāpayasi? sthaviro 'bravīt--svayamavagacchasi--yadahaṃ varṣaśataparinirvṛte bhagavati pravrajitaḥ, taddharmakāyo mayā tasya dṛṣṭaḥ/
225.029. trailokyanāthasya kāñcanādrinibhastasya na dṛṣṭo rūpakāyo me/
body.translated_text:
225.024. The elder said: 'On a condition I shall release you.' <s>Māra</s> said: 'What condition?' The elder said: 'From today onward, you must not harass the monks.'
225.025. <s>Māra</s> said: 'I shall not harass them.
225.025. What else do you command?' The elder said: 'With regard to the business of the teaching, thus far goes my command.
225.026. With regard to my own personal matter, I shall make a request of you.'
225.027. Then <s>Māra</s> said eagerly: 'Be pleased, elder; what do you command?' The elder said: 'You yourself know — I went forth when a hundred years had passed since the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>; I have seen his <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of the <s>Dharma</s>).
225.029. But the <s>Rūpakāya</s> (physical body) of the Protector of the Three Worlds, radiant like a golden mountain — that I have not seen.

body.text:
226.001. <226>tadanu tvamanugrahamapratimimiha vidarśaya buddhavigraham/
226.003, priyamadhikamato hi nāstiṃ me daśabalarūpakutūhalo hyāham//39//
body.translated_text:
226.001. 'Therefore, show me here the form of the <s>Buddha</s> — that incomparable favor;
226.003. for there is nothing dearer to me than this, for I am filled with curiosity about the form of the Ten-Powered One.' //39//

body.text:
226.005. māra uvāca--tena hi mamāpi samayaḥ śrūyatām/
226.006. sahasā tamihodvīkṣya buddhanepathyadhāriṇam/
226.007. na praṇāmastvayā kāryaḥ sarvajñaguṇagauravāt//40//
body.translated_text:
226.005. <s>Māra</s> said: 'Then hear my condition as well.
226.006. Having suddenly looked up here at me, wearing the <s>Buddha's</s> guise,
226.007. you must not make a prostration, out of reverence for the qualities of the Omniscient One.' //40//

body.text:
226.008. buddhānusmṛtipeśalena manasā pūjām yadi tvaṃ mayi svalpāmapyupadarśayiṣyasi vibho dagdho bhaviṣyāmyaham/
226.010. kā śaktirmama vītarāgavihitāṃ soḍhuṃ praṇāmakriyāṃ hastanyāsamivodvahanti na gajasyairaṇḍavṛkṣāṅkurāḥ//41//
body.translated_text:
226.008. 'If with a mind devoted to recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, you display even the slightest worship toward me, O Lord, I shall be burned.
226.010. What power do I have to endure the act of prostration performed by one free from passion? Castor-oil seedlings cannot bear the weight of an elephant's foot placed upon them.' //41//

body.text:
226.012. sthaviro 'pyāha--evamastu/
226.012. na bhavantaṃ praṇamiṣyāmīti/
226.012. māro 'bravīt--tena hi muhūrtamāgamaya, yāvadahaṃ vanagahanamanupraviśya--
226.014. śūraṃ vañcayituṃ purā vyavasitenottaptahemaprabhaṃ bauddhaṃ rūpamacintyabuddhivibhavādāsīnmayā yatkṛtam/
226.016. kṛtvā rūpamahaṃ tadeva nayanaprahlādikaṃ dehināmeṣo 'pyarkamayūkhajālamamalaṃ bhāmaṇḍalenākṣipan//42//
body.translated_text:
226.012. The elder also said: 'So be it.
226.012. I shall not bow to you.'
226.012. <s>Māra</s> said: 'Then wait a moment while I enter the depths of the forest —
226.014. Just as once, in order to deceive the hero, I created out of inconceivable intellectual power the <s>Buddha's</s> form, radiant like heated gold —
226.016. making that very form, which is a delight to the eyes of beings, I too shall cast forth a web of sun-like rays with my halo of light.' //42//

body.text:
226.018. atha sthavirah evamastu ityuktvā taṃ kuṇapamapanīya tathāgatarūpadarśanotsuko 'vasthitaḥ/
226.019. māraśca vanagahanamanupraviśya buddharūpaṃ kṛtvā naṭa iva suruciranepathyastasmādvanagahanādārabdho nikṣramitum/
226.020. vakṣyate hi--
226.021. tathāgataṃ vapurathottamalakṣaṇāḍhyamādarśayannayanaśāntikaraṃ narāṇām/
226.023. pratyagraraṅgamiva citrapaṭaṃ mahārhamuddhāṭayan vanamasau tadalaṃcakāra//43///
body.translated_text:
226.018. Then the elder, having said 'So be it,' removed that corpse, and stood eagerly awaiting the vision of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> form.
226.019. <s>Māra</s>, entering the depths of the forest, assumed the <s>Buddha's</s> form, and like an actor in splendid costume, began to emerge from that forest depth.
226.020. And it shall be said:
226.021. 'Displaying the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, rich in supreme marks, which brings peace to the eyes of humans,
226.023. like unrolling a priceless painting-cloth of fresh colors, he adorned the forest with that.' //43//

body.text:
226.025. atha vyāmaprabhāmaṇḍalamaṇḍitamasecanakadarśanaṃ bhagavato rūpamabhinirmāya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthaviraśāradvatīputraṃ vāmapārśve sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanaṃ pṛṣṭhataścāyuṣmantamānandaṃ buddhapātravyagrahastaṃ sthaviramahākaśyapāniruddhasubhūtipramṛtīnāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ rūpāṇyabhinirmāya ardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśatairardhacandreṇānuparivṛtaṃ buddhaveṣamādarśayitvā māraḥ sthaviropaguptasyāntikamājagāma/
226.029. sthaviropaguptasya ca bhagavato rūpamidamīdṛśamiti prāmodyamutpannam/
226.029. sa pramuditamanāstvaritamāsanādutthāya nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca--
body.translated_text:
226.025. Then, having manifested the <s>Bhagavān's</s> form — adorned with the halo of light extending a <s>vyāma</s>'s length, of indescribably beautiful appearance — with the elder <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>) on the right side, the elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> on the left, and the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> behind holding the <s>Buddha's</s> bowl, having also manifested the forms of the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, and other great disciples, surrounded in a half-moon formation by twelve hundred and fifty monks — having displayed the <s>Buddha's</s> appearance, <s>Māra</s> came before the elder <s>Upagupta</s>.
226.029. And in the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, seeing the form of the <s>Bhagavān</s> — 'so this is what it was like!' — rapture arose.
226.029. He, with a rapturous mind, hastily rising from his seat, gazing, said:

body.text:
227.001. <227>dhigastu tāṃ niṣkaruṇāmanityatāṃ bhinatti rūpāṇi yadīdṛśānyapi/
227.003. śarīramīdṛkkila tanmahāmuneranityatāṃ prāpya vināśamāgatam//44//
body.translated_text:
227.001. 'Shame upon that merciless impermanence, which shatters even such forms as these!
227.003. That such a body as this, belonging to the Great Sage, having met with impermanence, has come to destruction!' //44//

body.text:
227.005. sa buddhāvalambanayā smṛtyā tathāpyāsaktamanāḥ saṃvṛtto yathā buddhaṃ bhagavantamahaṃ paśyāmīti vyaktamupāgataḥ/
227.006. sa padmamukulapratimamañjaliṃ kṛtvovāca--aho rūpaśobhā bhagavataḥ/
227.007. kiṃ bahunā?
227.008. vaktreṇābhibhavatyayaṃ hi kamalaṃ nīlotpalaṃ cakṣuṣā kāntyā puṣpavanaṃ ghanaṃ priyatayā candraṃ samāptadyutim/
227.010. gāmbhīryeṇa mahodadhiṃ sthiratayā meruṃ raviṃ tejasā gatyā siṃhamavekṣitena vṛṣabhaṃ varṇena cāmīkaram//45//
body.translated_text:
227.005. He, through the mindfulness anchored in the <s>Buddha</s>, became so absorbed that it was as though he clearly perceived: 'I am seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
227.006. He, making a lotus-bud-like <s>añjali</s> (gesture of reverence), said: 'Ah, the beauty of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> form!
227.007. What more need be said?
227.008. He surpasses the lotus with his face, the blue lotus with his eyes, the flower-garden with his radiance, the full-orbed moon with his loveliness,
227.010. the great ocean with his depth, <s>Meru</s> with his steadfastness, the sun with his splendor, the lion with his gait, the bull with his gaze, and gold with his complexion.' //45//

body.text:
227.012. sa bhūyasyā mātrayā harṣaṇāpūryamāṇahṛdayo vyāpinā svareṇovāca--
227.013. aho bhāvaviśuddhānāṃ karmaṇo madhuraṃ phalam/
227.014. karmaṇedaṃ kṛtaṃ rūpaṃ naiśvaryeṇa yadṛcchayā//46//
body.translated_text:
227.012. He, with his heart filled to overflowing with ever-greater delight, said in a resonant voice:
227.013. 'Ah, the sweet fruit of deeds performed with purity of intention!
227.014. This form was created by <s>karma</s> — not by sovereignty, not by chance.' //46//

body.text:
227.015. yattatkalpasahasrakoṭiniyutairvākkāyacittodbhavaṃ dānakṣāntisamādhibuddhiniyamaistenārhatā śodhitam/
227.017. tenedaṃ jananetrakāntamamalaṃ rūpaṃ samutthāpitam yaṃ dṛṣṭvā ripurapyabhipramuditaḥ syātkiṃ punarmadvidhaḥ//47//
body.translated_text:
227.015. 'That which was purified through myriads of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (eons) — through merit of speech, body, and mind, through giving, patience, meditation, wisdom, and discipline — by that <s>Arhatship</s> it was refined.
227.017. By that this stainless form was produced, a delight to the eyes of the world — seeing which, even an enemy would be overjoyed, how much more so one like me!' //47//

body.text:
227.019. saṃbuddhālambanaiḥ saṃjñāṃ vismṛtya buddhasaṃjñāmadhiṣṭhāya mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa mārasya pādayor nipatitaḥ/
227.020. atha māraḥ sasambhramo 'bravīt--evaṃ taṃ bhadanta nārhasi samayaṃ vyatikramitum/
227.021. sthavira uvāca--kaḥ samaya iti? māra uvāca--nanu pratijñātaṃ bhadantena--nāhaṃ bhavantaṃ praṇamiṣyāmīti/
227.022. tataḥ sthaviropaguptaḥ pṛthivītalādutthāya sagadgadakaṇṭho 'bravīt--pāpīyan,
227.024. na khalu na viditaṃ me yasya vādipradhāno jalavihata ivāgnir nirvṛtiṃ saṃprayātaḥ/
227.026. api tu nayanakāntāmākṛtiṃ tasya dṛṣṭvā tamṛṣimabhinato 'haṃ tvāṃ tu nābhyarcayāmi//48//
body.translated_text:
227.019. Forgetting his awareness of the <s>Saṃbuddha</s>-convention, establishing in himself the perception of the <s>Buddha</s>, like a tree cut at the root he fell with his whole body at <s>Māra's</s> feet.
227.020. Then <s>Māra</s>, alarmed, said: 'Venerable Sir, you should not thus transgress the agreement.'
227.021. The elder said: 'What agreement?' <s>Māra</s> said: 'Did you not promise, Venerable Sir, "I shall not bow to you"?'
227.022. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, rising from the ground, with a voice choked with emotion, said: 'Evil One,
227.024. It is not indeed unknown to me that the one foremost among teachers, like fire extinguished by water, has gone to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>;
227.026. but seeing that form of the sage, delightful to the eyes, I bowed to that sage — I do not worship you.' //48//

body.text:
227.028. māra uvāca--kathamihāhaṃ nārcito bhavāmi, yadevaṃ māṃ praṇamasīti/
227.028. sthaviro 'bravīt--śrūyatām, yathā tvaṃ naiva mayā abhyarcito bhavasi, na ca mayā samayātikramaḥ kṛta iti/
body.translated_text:
227.028. <s>Māra</s> said: 'How am I not worshipped, when you bow to me like this?'
227.028. The elder said: 'Listen, how you are indeed not worshipped by me, nor has the agreement been transgressed by me.'

body.text:
228.001. <228>mṛṇmayeṣu pratikṛtiṣvamarāṇām yathā janaḥ/
228.002. mṛtasaṃjñāmanādṛtya namatyamarasaṃjñayā//49//
body.translated_text:
228.001. 'Just as people, in the case of clay images of the gods,
228.002. disregarding the perception of clay, bow with the perception of a god —' //49//

body.text:
228.003. tathāhaṃ tvāmihodvīkṣya lokanāthavapurdharam/
228.004. mārasaṃjñāmanādṛtya nataḥ sugatasaṃjñayā//50//
body.translated_text:
228.003. 'so I, looking up at you here, bearing the form of the Protector of the World,
228.004. disregarding the perception of <s>Māra</s>, bowed with the perception of the <s>Sugata</s>.' //50//

body.text:
228.005. atha māro buddhaveṣamantardhāpayitvā sthaviropaguptamabhyarcya prakrāntaḥ/
228.005. yāvaccaturthe divase māraḥ svayameva mathurāyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣitumārabdhah--yo yuṣmākaṃ svargāpavargasukhaṃ prārthayate, sa sthaviroaguptasakāśāddharmaṃ śṛṇotu, yaiśca yuṣmābhistathāgato na dṛṣṭaste sthaviropaguptaṃ paśyantu iti/
228.008. āha ca--
228.009. utsṛjya dāridryamanarthamūlam yaḥ sphītaśobhāṃ śriyamicchatīha/
228.011. svargāpavargāya ca yasya vāñchā sa śraddhayā dharmamataḥ śṛṇotu//51//
body.translated_text:
228.005. Then <s>Māra</s>, having made the <s>Buddha's</s> guise disappear, paid homage to the elder <s>Upagupta</s> and departed.
228.005. Then, on the fourth day, <s>Māra</s> himself began making a bell-proclamation in <s>Mathurā</s>: 'Whoever among you desires the happiness of heaven and liberation, let him hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the elder <s>Upagupta</s>. And whoever among you has not seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, let him see the elder <s>Upagupta</s>.'
228.008. And he said:
228.009. 'Casting away poverty, the root of calamity — whoever here desires prosperity and splendid fortune,
228.011. and whoever has the wish for heaven and liberation — let him hear the <s>Dharma</s> from here with faith.' //51//

body.text:
228.013. dṛṣṭo na yairvā dvipadapradhānaḥ śāstā mahākāruṇikaḥ svayambhūḥ/
228.015. te śāstṛkalpaṃ sthaviropaguptaṃ paśyantu bhāsvatribhavapradīpam//52//
body.translated_text:
228.013. 'And those who have not seen the foremost of bipeds, the Teacher, the Greatly Compassionate, the Self-Arisen —
228.015. let them see the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, equal to the Teacher, a radiant lamp of the three worlds.' //52//

body.text:
228.017. yāvanmathurāyāṃ śabdo visṛtah--sthaviropaguptena māro vinīta iti/
228.017. śrutvā ca yadbhūyasā mathurāvāstavyo janakāyaḥ sthaviropaguptasakāśaṃ nirgataḥ/
228.018. tataḥ sthaviropagupto 'nekeṣu brāhamaṇaśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu siṃha iva nirbhīḥ siṃhāsanamabhirūḍhaḥ/
228.019. vakṣyati ca--
228.020. māṃ prati na te śakyaṃ siṃhāsanamaviduṣā samabhiroḍhum/
228.021. yaḥ sa siṃhāsanastho mṛga iva sa hi yāti saṃkocam//53//
body.translated_text:
228.017. Then the word spread in <s>Mathurā</s>: 'The elder <s>Upagupta</s> has tamed <s>Māra</s>.'
228.017. And hearing this, the greater part of the people dwelling in <s>Mathurā</s> went forth to the elder <s>Upagupta</s>.
228.018. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, when many hundreds of thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had assembled, fearless like a lion, ascended the lion's seat.
228.019. And it shall be said:
228.020. 'It is not possible for an ignorant person to ascend the lion's seat before me.
228.021. Whoever sits on the lion's seat without being qualified shrinks like an animal.' //53//

body.text:
228.022. siṃha iva yastu nirbhīr ninadati pravarāridarpanāśārtham/
228.023. siṃhāsanamabhiroḍhuṃ sa kathikasiṃho bhavati yogyaḥ//54//
body.translated_text:
228.022. 'But he who, fearless like a lion, roars for the destruction of the pride of foremost adversaries —
228.023. that lion among speakers is worthy of ascending the lion's seat.' //54//

body.text:
228.024. yāvat sthaviropaguptena pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā satyāni saṃprakāśitāni/
228.025. śrutvā cānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmokṣabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlānyākṣiptāni/
228.025. kaiścidanāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam, kaiścit srotāapattiphalam, yāvadaṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi pravrajitāni/
228.027. sarvaiśca yujyamānairyāvadarhattvaṃ prāpram//
body.translated_text:
228.024. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having first given a preliminary discourse, illuminated the truths.
228.025. And hearing this, many hundreds of thousands of beings planted wholesome roots leading to liberation.
228.025. By some, the fruit of non-returning was attained; by some, the fruit of once-returning; by some, the fruit of stream-entry; and eighteen thousand went forth as renunciants.
228.027. And all of them, striving, attained <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).

body.text:
228.028. tatra corumuṇḍaparvate guhā aṣṭadaśahastā dairdhyeṇa dvādaśahastā vistāreṇa/
228.028. yadā te kṛtakaraṇīyāḥ saṃvṛttāstadā sthaviropaguptenābhihitam--yo madīyenāvavādena sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyati, tena caturaṅgulamātrā śalākā guhāyāṃ prakṣeptavyā/
228.030. yāvadekasmin divase daśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ śalākāḥ prakṣiptāḥ/
228.031. tasya yāvadāsamudrāyām {pṛthivyām} śabdo visṛtah--mathurāyāmupaguptanāmā<229> avavādakānāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā/
body.translated_text:
228.028. There, on <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, was a cave eighteen cubits in length and twelve cubits in width.
228.028. When those monks had accomplished their task, the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> declared: 'Whoever, by my instruction, directly realizes <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship) through the abandonment of all afflictions, he shall cast a tally-stick of four finger-breadths into the cave.'
228.030. On a single day, ten thousand <s>Arhats</s> cast their tally-sticks.
228.031. His fame spread as far as the ocean-bounded earth: 'In <s>Mathurā</s>, one named <s>Upagupta</s> has been declared by the Blessed One as the foremost of instructors.'

body.text: 229.001. tadyathā hi vinītakāmadhātvīśvare dvitīyaśāstṛkalpe mahātmani sthaviropagupte suramanujamahoragāsuragaruḍayakṣagandharvavidyādharārcitapādayugme pūrvabuddhakṣotrāvaropitakuśalabījasaṃtatīnāmanekeṣāṃ sattvaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saddharmasalilavarṣadhārānipātena mokṣāṅkurānabhivardhayannurumuṇḍe śaile//
body.translated_text: 229.001. Just so, with the great-souled Elder <s>Upagupta</s> — who was like a second Teacher, the tamer of beings to be tamed, the lord of the realm of desire, whose pair of feet was worshipped by gods, humans, <s>Mahoragas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Vidyādharas</s> — nurturing the sprouts of liberation with a downpour of the rain-streams of the excellent true <s>Dharma</s> for the many hundreds of thousands of beings whose seeds of wholesome roots had been sown in the field of former <s>Buddhas</s>, on <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain.

body.text:
229.005. kāryānurodhāt praṇatasakalasāmantacūḍāmaṇimayūkhodbhāsitapādapīṭhasyāśokasya rājñaḥ pūrvaṃ pāṃśupradānaṃ samanusmariṣyāmaḥ/
229.006. ityevamanuśrūyate--
229.007. bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalindakanivāpe/
229.007. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
229.009. vakṣyati ca--
229.010. kanakācalasaṃnibhāgradeho dviradendrapratimaḥ salīlagāmī/
229.012. pāripūrṇaśaśāṅkasaumyavaktro bhagavān bhikṣugaṇairvṛto jagāma//55//
body.translated_text:
229.005. As the occasion demands, we shall first recall the gift of dirt by King <s>Aśoka</s>, whose footstool was illuminated by the rays of the crest-jewels of all the neighboring kings bowing before him.
229.006. Thus it is heard by tradition:
229.007. The Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground).
229.007. Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks and preceded by the community of monks, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms.
229.009. And it shall be said:
229.010. 'With a body like the peak of a golden mountain, walking with the graceful gait of the lord of elephants,
229.012. with a face as gentle as the full moon, the Blessed One went forth surrounded by companies of monks.' //55//

body.text:
229.014. yāvadbhagavatā sābhisaṃskāraṃ nagaradvāre pādaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
229.014. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ sābhisaṃskāraṃ nagaradvāramindrakīle pādau vyavasthāpayanti, tadā citrāṇyadbhutāni prādurbhavanti/
229.016. andhāścakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante/
229.016. badhirāḥ śrotragrahaṇasamarthā bhavanti/
229.017. paṅgavo gamanasamarthā bhavanti/
229.016. haḍinigaḍacārakāvabaddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ bandhanāni śithilībhavanti/
229.018. janmajanmavairānubaddhāḥ sattvāstadanantaraṃ maitracitratāṃ labhante/
229.018. vatsā dāmāni cchittvā mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ samāgacchanti/
229.019. hastinas trośanti, aśvā heṣante, ṛṣabhā garjanti, śukaśārikakokilajīvaṃjīvakabarhiṇo madhurān {śabdān} nikūjanti/
229.020. peḍāgatā alaṃkārā madhuraśabdaṃ niścārayanti/
229.021. aparāhatāni ca vāditrabhāṇḍāni madhuraṃ śabdaṃ niścārayanti/
229.021. unnatonnatāḥ pṛthivīpradeśā avanamanti/
229.022. avanatāśconnamanti, apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālāścāvatiṣṭhante/
229.022. iyaṃ ca tasmin samaye pṛthivī ṣaḍanikāraṃ prakampate/
229.023. tadyathā--pūrvo digbhāga unnamati paścimo 'vanamati, anto 'vanamati madhya unnamati, calitaḥ pracalito vedhitaḥ pravedhitaḥ/
229.024. itīme cānye cādbhutadharmāḥ prādurbhavanti bhagavato nagarapraveśe/
229.025. vakṣyati ca--
229.026. lavaṇajalanivāsinī tato vā nagaranigamamaṇḍitā saśailā/
229.028. municaraṇanipīḍitā ca bhūmī pavanabalābhihateva yāvapātram//56//
body.translated_text:
229.014. Then the Blessed One, with deliberate intention, placed his foot at the city gate.
229.014. For it is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, with deliberate intention place their feet at the city gate upon the threshold-stone (<s>indrakīla</s>), wondrous and marvelous things occur:
229.016. The blind regain their sight.
229.016. The deaf become able to hear.
229.017. The lame become able to walk.
229.016. The fetters, chains, and shackles of bound beings become loosened.
229.018. Beings bound by enmity through birth after birth at once attain a state of friendliness.
229.018. Calves, breaking their tethers, come together with their mothers.
229.019. Elephants trumpet, horses neigh, bulls bellow; parrots, mynas, cuckoos, <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds, and peacocks warble sweet sounds.
229.020. Ornaments kept in cases emit sweet sounds.
229.021. Unstruck musical instruments emit sweet sounds.
229.021. High and uneven places on the earth subside,
229.022. and low places rise up, becoming free of stones, gravel, and potsherds.
229.022. And at that time, this earth quakes in six ways:
229.023. namely — the eastern quarter rises and the western subsides, the sides subside and the center rises; it trembles, shakes, quivers, and quakes.
229.024. These and other wondrous phenomena occur at the Blessed One's entry into a city.
229.025. And it shall be said:
229.026. 'The earth — whether inhabited by ocean-dwellers, or adorned with cities, towns, and mountains —
229.028. pressed by the foot of the Sage, became like a winnowing basket struck by the force of the wind.' //56//

body.text:
229.030. atha buddhapraveśakālaniyataiḥ prātihāryairāvarhjitāḥ strīmanuṣyāstannagaramanilabalacalitabhinnavīcītaraṅgakṣubhitamiva mahāsamudraṃ vimuktoccanādaṃ babhūva/
229.031. na hi buddhapraveśatulyaṃ nāma jagatyadbhutamupalabhyate/
229.032. purapraveśasamaye hi bhagavataścitrāṇyadbhutāni dṛśyante/
229.032. vakṣyati ca--
body.translated_text:
229.030. Then the women and men, inspired by the miraculous signs that invariably attend a <s>Buddha</s>'s entry, burst into unrestrained cries, and the city became like the great ocean agitated by waves and billows stirred by the force of the wind.
229.031. For there is no marvel in the world equal to the entry of a <s>Buddha</s>.
229.032. Indeed, at the time of the Blessed One's entry into a city, wondrous and marvelous things are seen.
229.032. And it shall be said:

body.text:
230.001. <230>niṃnā connamate natāvanamate buddhānubhāvānmahī sthāṇuḥ śarkarakaṇḍakavyapagato nirdoṣatām yāti ca/
230.002. andhā mūkajaḍendriyāśca puruṣā vyaktendriyāstatkṣaṇaṃ saṃvādyantyanighaṭṭitāśca nagare nandanti tūryakhanāḥ//57//
body.translated_text:
230.001. 'By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the earth — where low, it rises; where raised, it subsides; stumps, gravel, and thorns vanish and it becomes flawless.
230.002. The blind, the mute, and those with dull senses become clear-sensed in that instant; unstruck instruments in the city resound and bring delight.' //57//

body.text:
230.005. sarvaṃ ca tannagaraṃ sūryasahasrātirekayā kanakamarīcivarṇayā buddhaprabhayā sphuṭaṃ babhūva/
230.006. āha ca--
230.007. sūryaprabhāmavabhartsya hi tasya bhābhirvyāptaṃ jagatsakalameva sakānanastham/
230.009. saṃprāpya ca pravaradharmakathābhirāmo lokaṃ surāsuranaraṃ hi samuktabhāvam//58//
body.translated_text:
230.005. And that entire city was flooded with the golden-rayed radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>, surpassing the brilliance of a thousand suns.
230.006. And it is said:
230.007. 'Outshining the radiance of the sun with his splendor, the world entire — with its forests and groves — was pervaded.
230.009. Arriving with delight in the excellent teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, he set free the world of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans.' //58//

body.text:
230.011. yāvadbhagavān rājamārgaṃ pratipannaḥ/
230.011. tatra dvau bāladārakau/
230.011. eko 'grakulikaputro dvitīyaḥ kulikaputraśca pāṃśvāgārais trīḍataḥ/
230.012. ekasya jayo nāma, dvitīyasya vijayaḥ/
230.012. tābhyāṃ bhagavān dṛṣṭo dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīrah asecanakadarśanaśca/
230.013. yāvajjayena dārakena saktuṃ dāsyāmīti pāṃśvañjalirbhagavataḥ pātre prakṣiptaḥ, vijayena ca kṛtāñjalinābhyanumoditam/
230.015. vakṣyati ca--
230.016. dṛṣṭvā mahākāruṇikaṃ svayambhavaṃ vyāmaprabhoddyotitasarvagātram/
230.018. dhīreṇa vaktreṇa kṛtaprasādaḥ pāṃśuṃ dadau jātijarāntakāya//59//
body.translated_text:
230.011. Then the Blessed One proceeded along the royal highway.
230.011. There, two young boys —
230.011. one the son of the chief guild-master, the second the son of a guild-master — were playing at building houses of dirt.
230.012. The name of one was <s>Jaya</s>, of the second <s>Vijaya</s>.
230.012. They beheld the Blessed One, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, lovely beyond compare.
230.013. Then the boy <s>Jaya</s>, thinking 'I shall give barley flour,' cast a handful of dirt into the Blessed One's bowl, and <s>Vijaya</s>, with palms joined, expressed his approval.
230.015. And it shall be said:
230.016. 'Seeing the Great Compassionate One, the Self-Born, his entire body radiant with the light of a fathom-wide aura,
230.018. with a steadfast face filled with faith, he gave the dirt to the Ender of Birth and Old Age.' //59//

body.text:
230.020. sa bhagavate pratipādayitvā praṇidhānaṃ kartumārabdhah--anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena ekacchatrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ rājā syām, atraiva ca buddhe kārāṃ kuryāmiti/
230.022. tato munistasya niśābhya bhāvaṃ bālasya samyakpraṇidhiṃ ca buddhvā/
230.024. iṣṭaṃ phalaṃ kṣṛtravaśena dṛṣṭvā jagrāha pāṃśuṃ karuṇāyamānaḥ//60//
body.translated_text:
230.020. Having offered it to the Blessed One, he began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I become king over the earth under a single parasol, and may I render service to the <s>Buddha</s> in this very place.'
230.022. 'Then the Sage, discerning the boy's inner disposition and understanding his righteous aspiration,
230.024. foreseeing the desired fruit through the power of the field, accepted the dirt with compassion.' //60//

body.text:
230.026. tena yāvadrājyavipākyaṃ kuśalamākṣiptam/
230.026. tato bhavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam/
230.026. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ vidarśayanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātamañjiṣṭhasphaṭikarajatavarṇā arciṣo mukhānniścaranti/
230.028. kecidūrdhvato gacchanti, kecidadhastādgacchanti/
230.029. ye 'dho gacchanti, te saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīciparyanteṣu gatvā ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣṇībhūtvā nipatanti, ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti/
230.031. tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante/
230.031. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--kiṃ nu <231>bhavanto vayamitaścyutāḥ, āhosvidanyatropapannā iti, yenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhāḥ/
body.translated_text:
230.026. By that act, <s>karma</s> projecting a royal destiny was set in motion.
230.026. Then the Blessed One displayed a smile.
230.026. For it is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that time rays of blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, crystal, and silver color issue forth from their mouths.
230.028. Some go upward, some go downward.
230.029. Those that go downward pass through the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, down to <s>Avīci</s> — and in the cold hells they fall as warmth, in the hot hells they fall as coolness.
230.031. By this, the particular torments of those beings are alleviated.
230.031. They think: 'Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere, that our particular torments have been alleviated?'

body.text:
231.002. teṣāṃ bhagavān prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ nirmitaṃ visarjayati/
231.002. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--na vayamitaścyutāḥ, nāpyanyatropapannāḥ/
231.003. api tvayamapūrvadarśanah {sattvah}/
231.003. asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti/
231.004. te nirmite cittāni prasādayitvā narakavedanīyāni karmāṇi kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti/
231.005. ye ūrddhvato gacchanti, te cāturmahārājikān devāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitānnirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmān parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānabṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhaparyanteṣu deveṣu gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyuddhoṣayanti/
231.009. gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante--
231.010. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
231.011. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//61//
body.translated_text:
231.002. For the sake of generating faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a magical creation.
231.002. They think: 'We have not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.
231.003. Rather, this is a being never seen before.
231.003. By his power, our particular torments have been alleviated.'
231.004. Having generated faith in the magical creation, they exhaust the <s>karmas</s> leading to hell-experience and take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths.
231.005. Those rays that go upward pass through the realms of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, up to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, and among the gods they proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!'
231.009. And they speak two verses:
231.010. 'Strive forth! Go forth! Apply yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!
231.011. Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!' //61//

body.text:
231.012. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
231.013. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//62//
body.translated_text:
231.012. 'He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,
231.013. having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall make an end of suffering.' //62//

body.text:
231.014. atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantamevānugacchanti/
231.015. yadi bhagavānatītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante/
231.015. anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purato 'ntardhīyante/
231.016. narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante/
231.016. tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyāmantardhīyante/
231.017. pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante/
231.018. manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānuno 'ntardhīyante/
231.018. balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante/
231.019. cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante/
231.020. devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyāmantardhīyante/
231.020. śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante/
231.021. pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyāmantardhīyante/
231.022. anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante/
231.022. atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato vāme karatale 'ntarhitāḥ/
231.023. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo gāthāṃ bhāsate--
231.025. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhā jagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
231.027. nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitaṃ vidarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ//36//
body.translated_text:
231.014. Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, returned and followed the Blessed One.
231.015. If the Blessed One intends to prophesy a past deed, they vanish behind him.
231.015. If he intends to prophesy a future event, they vanish in front of him.
231.016. If he intends to prophesy rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet.
231.016. If he intends to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels.
231.017. If he intends to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe.
231.018. If he intends to prophesy rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees.
231.018. If he intends to prophesy the sovereignty of a lesser universal monarch, they vanish in his left palm.
231.019. If he intends to prophesy the sovereignty of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm.
231.020. If he intends to prophesy rebirth among the gods, they vanish at his navel.
231.020. If he intends to prophesy <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening, they vanish at his mouth.
231.021. If he intends to prophesy <s>Pratyeka</s> awakening, they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows).
231.022. If he intends to prophesy supreme perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).
231.022. Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, vanished in the Blessed One's left palm.
231.023. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, spoke a verse:
231.025. 'The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, with pride and arrogance abandoned, supreme causes of benefit in the world,
231.027. do not without reason display a smile as white as conch, lotus-stalk — the Victorious Ones, conquerors of foes!' //36//

body.text:
231.029. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
231.031. dhīrābhirmunivṛṣa vāgbhiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//64//
body.translated_text:
231.029. 'Having understood the occasion yourself by your own wisdom, O Hero, O Bull among Sages, O <s>Jinendra</s>,
231.031. with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, dispel the doubt that has arisen in your listeners who are eager to know!' //64//

body.text:
232.001. meghastanitanirghoṣa govṛṣendranibhekṣaṇa/
232.002. phalaṃ pāṃśupradānasya vyākuruṣva narottam//65//
body.translated_text:
232.001. 'O Supreme of Men, whose voice is like the rumbling of thunderclouds, whose gaze is like that of the lord of bulls,
232.002. prophesy the fruit of the gift of dirt!' //65//

body.text:
232.003. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda evametadānanda/
232.003. nāhetvapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti/
232.004. api tu sahetu sapratyayaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti/
232.005. paśyasi tvamānanda dārakam yena tathāgatasya pātre pāṃśvañjaliḥ prakṣiptah? evaṃ bhadanta/
232.006. ayamānanda dārako 'nena kuśalamūlena varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya pāṭaliputre nagare aśoko nāṃnā rājā bhaviṣyati caturbhāgacakravartī dhārmiko dharmarājā, yo me śarīradhātūn vaistārikān kariṣyati/
232.008. caturaśītiṃ dharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati/
232.009. bahujanahitāya pratipatsyata iti/
232.009. āha ca--
232.010. astaṃgate mayi bhaviṣyati ekarājā yo 'sau hyaśoka iti nāma viśālakīrtiḥ/
232.012. maddhātugarbhaparimaṇḍitajambukhaṇḍametatkariṣyati narāmarapūjitānām//66//
body.translated_text:
232.003. The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is, <s>Ānanda</s>.
232.003. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, do not display a smile without cause and condition.
232.004. Rather, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile with cause and condition.
232.005. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that boy who threw a handful of dust into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bowl?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.'
232.006. 'This boy, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this wholesome root, a hundred years after the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, will become a king named <s>Aśoka</s> in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> — a ruler of a quarter of the world, a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king — who will distribute my bodily relics widely.
232.008. He will establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharma</s>-shrines.
232.009. He will act for the welfare of the many.'
232.009. And he said:
232.010. 'When I have passed away, there will be a sole king, he who is <s>Aśoka</s> by name, of vast renown;
232.012. he will make this <s>Jambu</s>-continent adorned with the womb of my relics, worshipped by humans and gods.' //66//

body.text:
232.014. ayamasya deyadharmo yattathāgatasya pāṃśvañjaliḥ pātre pakṣiptaḥ/
232.014. yāvadbhagavatā teṣāṃ sarva āyuṣmate ānandāya dattāḥ/
232.015. gomayena miśrayitvā yatra caṃkrame tathāgataścaṃkramyate, tatra gomayakārṣīṃ prayacchati/
232.016. yāvadāyuṣmatā ānandena teṣāṃ sagomayena miśrayitvā yatra caṃkramati bhagavān, tatra gomayakārṣī dattā//
body.translated_text:
232.014. This was his gift of merit: that a handful of dust was thrown into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s bowl.
232.014. All of those were given by the Blessed One to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
232.015. Mixing them with cow-dung and applying cow-dung plaster where the <s>Tathāgata</s> walks on the walking-path.
232.016. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having mixed those with cow-dung, applied cow-dung plaster where the Blessed One walks.

body.text:
232.018. tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājagṛhe bimbisāro rājā rājyaṃ kārayati/
232.018. rājño bimbisārasya ajātaśatruḥ putraḥ/
232.019. ajātaśatrorudāyī/
232.019. udāyibhadrasya muṇḍaḥ/
232.019. muṇḍasya kākavarṇī/
232.020. kākavarṇinaḥ sahalī/
232.020. sahalinastulakucī/
232.020. tulakucermahāmaṇḍalaḥ/
232.020. mahāmaṇḍalasya prasenajit/
232.021. prasenajito nandaḥ/
232.021. nandasya bindusāraḥ/
232.021. pāṭaliputre nagare biṃdusāro nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati/
232.022. bindusārasya rājñaḥ putro jātaḥ/
232.022. tasya susīma iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
232.023. tena ca samayena campāyāṃ nagaryāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ/
232.023. tasya duhitā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇī/
232.024. sā naimittikairvyākṛtā--āsyā dārikāyā rājā bhartā bhaviṣyati/
232.025. dve putraratne janayiṣyati, ekaścaturbhāgacakravartī bhaviṣyati/
232.025. dvitīyaḥ pravrajitvā siddhavrato bhaviṣyati/
232.026. śrutvā ca brāhamaṇasya romaharṣo jātaḥ/
232.026. saṃpattikāmo lokaḥ/
232.026. sa tāṃ duhitaraṃ grahāya pāṭaliputraṃ gataḥ/
232.027. tena sā sarvālaṃkārairvibhūṣayitvā rājño bindusārasya bhāryārthamanupradattā--iyaṃ hi devakanyā dhanyā praśastā ceti/
232.028. yāvad rājñā bindusāreṇāntaḥpuraṃ praveśitā/
232.029. antaḥpurikāṇāṃ buddhirutpannā--iyamabhirūpā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇī/
232.029. yadi rājā anayā sārdhaṃ paricārayiṣyati, asmākaṃ bhūyaścakṣuḥsampreṣaṇamapi na kariṣyati/
232.030. tābhiḥ sā nāpitākarma śikṣāpitā/
232.031. sā rājñaḥ kṛśaśmaśruṃ prasādhayati yāvat suśikṣitā saṃvṛttā/
232.031. yadā <233>ārabhate rājñaḥ keśaśmaśrum, tadā rājā śete/
body.translated_text:
232.018. At that time, in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was ruling the kingdom.
232.018. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s son was <s>Ajātaśatru</s>.
232.019. <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s son was <s>Udāyin</s>.
232.019. <s>Udāyibhadra</s>'s son was <s>Muṇḍa</s>.
232.019. <s>Muṇḍa</s>'s son was <s>Kākavarṇin</s>.
232.020. <s>Kākavarṇin</s>'s son was <s>Sahalin</s>.
232.020. <s>Sahalin</s>'s son was <s>Tulakuci</s>.
232.020. <s>Tulakuci</s>'s son was <s>Mahāmaṇḍala</s>.
232.020. <s>Mahāmaṇḍala</s>'s son was <s>Prasenajit</s>.
232.021. <s>Prasenajit</s>'s son was <s>Nanda</s>.
232.021. <s>Nanda</s>'s son was <s>Bindusāra</s>.
232.021. In the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a king named <s>Bindusāra</s> was ruling the kingdom.
232.022. A son was born to King <s>Bindusāra</s>.
232.022. He was given the name <s>Susīma</s>.
232.023. At that time, in the city of <s>Campā</s>, there was a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
232.023. A daughter was born to him — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, the fairest in the land.
232.024. Soothsayers predicted of her: 'A king will be this girl's husband.
232.025. She will bear two jewel-sons: one will be a ruler of a quarter of the world.
232.025. The second, having gone forth, will become one of perfected vows.'
232.026. Hearing this, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s hair stood on end with excitement.
232.026. The world desires good fortune.
232.026. Taking his daughter, he went to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
232.027. Having adorned her with all ornaments, he offered her to King <s>Bindusāra</s> as a wife: 'This is indeed a divine maiden, fortunate and praiseworthy.'
232.028. She was admitted by King <s>Bindusāra</s> into the inner palace.
232.029. The women of the inner palace thought: 'She is beautiful, pleasing, the fairest in the land.
232.029. If the king consorts with her, he will not so much as cast a glance at us.'
232.030. They taught her the barber's craft.
232.031. She would trim the king's beard until she became highly skilled.
232.031. When <233> she began to work on the king's hair and beard, the king would fall asleep.

body.text:
233.001. yāvat rājñā prītena vareṇa pravāritā--kiṃ tvaṃ varamicchasīti? tayā abhihitam--devena me saha samāgamaḥ syāt/
233.002. rājā āha--tvaṃ nāpinī, ahaṃ rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ/
233.003. kathaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ samāgamo bhaviṣyati? sā kathayati--deva nāhaṃ nāpinī, api tu brāhmaṇasyāhaṃ duhitā/
233.004. tena devasya patnyarthaṃ dattā/
233.005. rājā kathayati--kena tvaṃ nāpitakarma śikṣāpitā? sā kathayati--antaḥpurikābhiḥ/
233.005. rājā āha--na bhūyastvayā nāpitakarma kartavyam/
233.006. yāvadrājñā agramahiṣī sthāpitā/
233.006. tayā sārdhaṃ trīḍati ramate paricārayati/
233.007. sā āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
233.007. yāvadaṣṭānāṃ navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
233.008. tasyāḥ putro jātaḥ/
233.008. tasya vistareṇa jātimahaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ kumārasya bhavatu nāma? sā kathayati--asya dārakasya aśokāsmi saṃvṛttā/
233.009. tasya aśoka iti nāma kṛtam/
233.010. yāvaddvitīyaḥ putro jātaḥ/
233.010. tasya vigataśoka iti nāma kṛtam/
233.011. aśoko duḥsparśagātraḥ/
233.011. rājño bindusārasyānabhipretaḥ/
233.011. atha rājā bindusāraha kumāraṃ parīkṣitukāmaḥ piṅgalavatsājīvaṃ parivrājakamāmantrayate--upādhyāya, kumārāṃstāvatparīkṣāmah--kaḥ śakyate śakyate mamātyayādrājyaṃ kārayitum? piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ kathayati--tena hi deva kumārānādāya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ nirgaccha, parīkṣāmaḥ/
233.014. yāvadrājā kumārānādāya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ nirgataḥ/
233.015. yāvadaśokaḥ kumāro mātrā cocyate--vatsa, rājā kumārān parīkṣitukāmaḥ suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ gataḥ, tvamapi tatra gaccheti/
233.016. aśokaḥ kathayati--rājño 'hamanabhipreto darśanenāpi, kimahaṃ tatra gāmiṣyāmi? sā kathayati--tathāpi gaccheti/
233.018. aśoka uvāca--āhāraṃ preṣaya/
233.018. yāvadaśokaḥ pāṭaliputrānnirgacchati, rādhaguptena cāgrāmātyaputreṇoktah--aśoka, kva gamiṣyasīti? aśokaḥ kathayati--rājā adya suvarṇamaṇḍape udyāne kumārān parīkṣayati/
233.020. tatra rājño mahallako hastināgastiṣṭhati/
233.020. yāvadaśokastasmin mahallake 'bhiruhya suvarṇamaṇḍapamudyānaṃ gatvā kumārāṇāṃ madhye 'tra pṛthivyāṃ prastīrya niṣasāda/
233.022. yāvat kumārāṇāmāhāra upanāmitaḥ/
233.022. aśokasyāpi śālyodanaṃ dadhisamiśraṃ mṛdbhājane preṣitam/
233.023. tato rājñā bindusāreṇa piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājako 'bhihitah--upādhyāya, parīkṣa kumārān--kaḥ śakyate mamātyayādrājyaṃ kartumiti? paśyati piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ, cintayati ca--aśoko rājā bhaviṣyati/
233.025. ayaṃ ca rājño nābhipretaḥ/
233.025. yadi kathayiṣyāmi aśoko rājā bhaviṣyatīti, nāsti me jīvitam/
233.026. sa kathayati--deva abhedena vyākariṣyāmi/
233.027. rājā āha--abhedena vyākuruṣva/
233.027. āha--yasya yānaṃ śobhanaṃ sa rājā bhaviṣyati/
233.027. teṣāmekaikasya buddhirutpannā--mama yānaṃ śobhanam/
233.028. āha rājā bhaviṣyāmi/
233.028. aśokaścintayati--ahaṃ hastiskandhenāgataḥ/
233.029. mama yānaṃ śobhanam, ahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmīti/
233.029. rājā āha--bhūyastāvadupādhyāya parīkṣasva/
233.030. piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakaḥ kathayati--deva, yasyāsanamagram, sa rājā bhaviṣyati/
233.031. teṣāmekaikasya buddhirutpannā--mamāsanamagram/
233.031. aśokaścintayati--mama pṛthivyāsanam, ahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi/
233.032. evaṃ bhājanaṃ bhojanaṃ pānam/
233.032. vistareṇa kumārān parīkṣya praviṣṭaḥ/
body.translated_text:
233.001. Once, the king, pleased, offered her a boon: 'What boon do you wish?' She said: 'May I have union with Your Majesty.'
233.002. The king said: 'You are a barber woman; I am a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, an anointed sovereign.
233.003. How can there be union with me?' She said: 'Your Majesty, I am not a barber woman; I am the daughter of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
233.004. He gave me to Your Majesty as a wife.'
233.005. The king said: 'Who taught you the barber's craft?' She said: 'The women of the inner palace.'
233.005. The king said: 'You shall no longer perform the barber's craft.'
233.006. She was established as the chief queen.
233.006. He sported, delighted, and consorted with her.
233.007. She became pregnant.
233.007. At the end of eight or nine months, she gave birth.
233.008. A son was born to her.
233.008. With elaborate birth celebrations, they asked: 'What shall be the prince's name?' She said: 'When this boy was born, I became without sorrow (<s>a-śoka</s>).'
233.009. He was given the name <s>Aśoka</s>.
233.010. In due course, a second son was born.
233.010. He was given the name <s>Vigataśoka</s> ('Free from Sorrow').
233.011. <s>Aśoka</s> had rough skin.
233.011. He was not favored by King <s>Bindusāra</s>.
233.011. Then King <s>Bindusāra</s>, wishing to test his princes, addressed the wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>: 'Teacher, let us examine the princes — who is capable of ruling the kingdom after me?' The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> said: 'Then, Your Majesty, take the princes and go out to the Golden Pavilion garden; we shall examine them.'
233.014. The king took the princes and went out to the Golden Pavilion garden.
233.015. Prince <s>Aśoka</s> was told by his mother: 'Child, the king wishes to test the princes and has gone to the Golden Pavilion garden; you too should go there.'
233.016. <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'The king does not even wish to see me; why should I go there?' She said: 'Go nonetheless.'
233.018. <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'Send me food.'
233.018. As <s>Aśoka</s> was leaving <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, <s>Rādhagupta</s>, the son of the chief minister, said: '<s>Aśoka</s>, where will you go?' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'The king is testing the princes today at the Golden Pavilion garden.'
233.020. There stood the king's old state elephant.
233.020. <s>Aśoka</s> mounted that old elephant and went to the Golden Pavilion garden, where, in the midst of the princes, he spread himself out on the bare earth and sat down.
233.022. Food was served to the princes.
233.022. To <s>Aśoka</s> as well, rice with curds was sent in an earthen vessel.
233.023. Then King <s>Bindusāra</s> said to the wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>: 'Teacher, examine the princes — who is capable of ruling the kingdom after me?' The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> looked and thought: '<s>Aśoka</s> will become king.
233.025. But he is not favored by the king.
233.025. If I say "<s>Aśoka</s> will become king," my life will be in danger.'
233.026. He said: 'Your Majesty, I shall make a prediction by means of riddles.'
233.027. The king said: 'Make your prediction by riddles.'
233.027. He said: 'He whose vehicle is the finest — he will become king.'
233.027. Each of them thought: 'My vehicle is the finest.
233.028. I shall become king.'
233.028. <s>Aśoka</s> thought: 'I came on an elephant's back.
233.029. My vehicle is the finest; I shall become king.'
233.029. The king said: 'Teacher, examine them further.'
233.030. The wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s> said: 'Your Majesty, he whose seat is foremost — he will become king.'
233.031. Each of them thought: 'My seat is foremost.'
233.031. <s>Aśoka</s> thought: 'My seat is the earth itself; I shall become king.'
233.032. Likewise for vessel, food, and drink.
233.032. Having examined the princes in detail, the king returned.

body.text:
234.001. <234>yāvadaśoko mātrocyate--ko vyākṛto rājā bhaviṣyatīti? aśokaḥ kathayati--abhedena vyākṛtam--yasya yānamagramāsanaṃ pānaṃ bhājanaṃ ceti, sa rājā bhaviṣyatīti/
234.002. yathā paśyami--ahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi/
234.003. mama hastiskandham yānaṃ pṛthivī āsanaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ bhājanaṃ śālyodanaṃ dadhivyañjanaṃ pānīyaṃ pānamiti//
body.translated_text:
234.001. <234><s>Aśoka</s> was asked by his mother: 'Who was predicted to become king?' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'It was predicted by riddles: "He whose vehicle, seat, drink, and vessel is foremost — he will become king."
234.002. As I see it, I shall become king.
234.003. My vehicle was the elephant's back, my seat was the earth, my vessel was earthenware, my food was rice with curds, and my drink was water.'

body.text:
234.005. tataḥ piṅgalavatsājīvaḥ parivrājakah aśoko rājā bhaviṣyatīti tasya mātaramārabdhaḥ sevitum/
234.006. yāvat tayocyate--upādhyāya, kataraḥ kumāro rājño bindusārasyātyayādrājā bhaviṣyatīti? āha--aśokaḥ/
234.007. tayocyate--kadācit tvāṃ rājā nirbandhena pṛcchet/
234.007. gaccha tvam/
234.008. pratyantaṃ samāśraya/
234.008. yadā śṛṇoṣi aśoko rājā saṃvṛttāḥ, tadā āgantavyam/
234.008. yāvat sa pratyanteṣu janapadeṣu saṃśritaḥ//
body.translated_text:
234.005. Then the wandering ascetic <s>Piṅgalavatsājīva</s>, knowing that <s>Aśoka</s> would become king, began to attend upon his mother.
234.006. She asked him: 'Teacher, which prince will become king after King <s>Bindusāra</s>?' He said: '<s>Aśoka</s>.'
234.007. She said: 'Perhaps the king will one day press you with insistence.
234.007. Go.
234.008. Retire to the borderlands.
234.008. When you hear that <s>Aśoka</s> has become king, then come back.'
234.008. He retired to the borderland provinces.

body.text:
234.010. atha rājño bindusārasya takṣaśilā nāma nagaraṃ viruddham/
234.010. tatra rājñā bindusāreṇa aśoko visarjitah--gaccha kumāra, takṣaśilānagaraṃ saṃnāhaya/
234.011. caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ dattam, yānaṃ praharaṇaṃ ca pratiṣiddham/
234.012. yāvadaśokaḥ kumāraḥ pāṭaliputrānnirgacchan bhṛtyairvijñaptah--kumāra, naivāsmākaṃ sainyapraharaṇam--kena vayaṃ kam yudhyāmah? tatah aśokenābhihitam--yadi nāma rājyavipākyaṃ kuśalamasti, sainyaṃ praharaṇaṃ ca prādurbhavatu/
234.014. evamukte kumāreṇa pṛthivyāmavakāśo dattaḥ/
234.015. devatābhiḥ sainyapraharaṇāni copanītāni/
234.015. yāvat kumāraścaturaṅgena balakāyena takṣaśilāṃ gataḥ/
234.016. śrutvā takṣaśilānivāsinaḥ paurā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārge śobhāṃ kṛtvā pūrṇaghaṭamādāya pratyudgatāḥ/
234.017. pratyudgamya ca kathayanti--na vayaṃ kumārasya viruddhāḥ, nāpi rājño bindusārasya, api tu duṣṭāmātyā asmākaṃ paribhavaṃ kurvanti/
234.018. mahatā ca satkāreṇa takṣaśilāṃ praveśitaḥ/
234.019. evaṃ vistareṇāśokaḥ khaśarājyaṃ praveśitaḥ/
234.019. tasya dvau mahānagnau saṃśritau/
234.019. tena tau vṛttyā saṃvibhaktau tasyāgrataḥ parvatān saṃchindantau saṃprasthitau/
234.020. devatābhiścoktam--aśokaścaturbhāgacakravartī bhaviṣyati, na kenacidvirodhitavyamiti/
234.021. vistareṇa yāvadāsamudrā pṛthivī ājñāpitā//
body.translated_text:
234.010. Then a city called <s>Takṣaśilā</s> rebelled against King <s>Bindusāra</s>.
234.010. King <s>Bindusāra</s> dispatched <s>Aśoka</s> there: 'Go, prince, subdue the city of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>.'
234.011. A fourfold army was given to him, but vehicles and weapons were withheld.
234.012. As Prince <s>Aśoka</s> was leaving <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, his servants reported: 'Prince, we have neither a military force nor weapons — with what shall we fight, and whom?' Then <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'If there is wholesome merit ripening into kingship, let an army and weapons appear.'
234.014. When the prince said this, the earth opened up.
234.015. Deities brought forth an army and weapons.
234.015. The prince went to <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with a fourfold army.
234.016. Hearing of his arrival, the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> decorated the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>, and came forth to meet him bearing full water-pots.
234.017. Having come forth, they said: 'We are not in rebellion against the prince, nor against King <s>Bindusāra</s>; rather, it is the corrupt ministers who oppress us.'
234.018. He was received into <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with great honor.
234.019. Thus, in full detail, <s>Aśoka</s> was installed in the <s>Khaśa</s> kingdom.
234.019. Two great <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) had taken refuge with him.
234.019. He assigned them a livelihood, and they went forth ahead of him, splitting mountains.
234.020. And the deities proclaimed: '<s>Aśoka</s> will become a ruler of a quarter of the world; no one should oppose him.'
234.021. Thus, in full detail, the earth up to the ocean was brought under his authority.

body.text:
234.023. yāvat susīmaḥ kumāra udyānāt pāṭaliputraṃ praviśati/
234.023. rājño bindusārasyāgrāmātyaḥ khallāṭakaḥ pāṭaliputrānnirgacchati/
234.024. tasya susīmena kumāreṇa trīḍābhiprāyatayā khaṭakā pātitā/
234.025. yāvadamātyaścintayati--idānīṃ khaṭakāṃ nipātayati/
234.025. yadā rājā bhaviṣyati, tadā śastraṃ pātayiṣyati/
234.026. tathā kariṣyāmi yathā rājaiva na bhaviṣyati/
234.026. tena pañcāmātyaśatāni bhinnāni/
234.027. aśokaścaturbhāgacakravartī nirdiṣṭa eva, rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaḥ/
234.027. takṣśilāśca virodhitāḥ/
234.028. yāvadrājñā susīmaḥ kumārastakṣaśilāmanupreṣitaḥ/
234.028. na ca śakyate saṃnāmayitum/
234.028. bindusāraśca rājā glānībhūtaḥ/
234.029. tenābhihitam--susīmaṃ kumāramānayatha, rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti/
234.029. aśokaṃ takṣaśilāṃ praveśayatha/
234.030. yāvadamātyairaśokaḥ kumāro haridrayā pralipto lakṣāṃ ca lohapātre kvāthayitvā kvathitena rasena lohapātrāṇi mrakṣayitvā chorayanti--aśokaḥ kumāro glānībhūta iti/
234.032. yadā bindusāraḥ svalpāvaśeṣaprāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, tadā amātyairaśokaḥ kumāraḥ sarvālaṃkārairbhūṣayitvā<235> rājño bindusārasyopanītah--imaṃ tāvadrājye pratiṣṭhāpaya/
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Susīma</s> enters <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> from the garden. <s>Khallāṭaka</s>, the chief minister of King <s>Bindusāra</s>, is leaving <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Prince <s>Susīma</s>, in a playful mood, knocked off his turban-clasp. The minister thought: "Now he knocks off my clasp; when he becomes king, he will strike with a weapon. I shall act so that he never becomes king." He won over five hundred ministers, saying: "<s>Aśoka</s> has been prophesied as a ruler of a quarter of the world — we shall establish him in the kingdom." And the people of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> had revolted. The king sent prince <s>Susīma</s> to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, but the revolt could not be subdued. And King <s>Bindusāra</s> fell ill. He said: "Bring prince <s>Susīma</s> back; I shall establish him in the kingdom. Send <s>Aśoka</s> to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>." Then the ministers smeared prince <s>Aśoka</s> with turmeric, boiled lac in iron vessels, smeared the iron vessels with the boiled liquid, and sent word that prince <s>Aśoka</s> had fallen ill. When <s>Bindusāra</s> had only a little life remaining, the ministers adorned prince <s>Aśoka</s> with all ornaments and brought him before King <s>Bindusāra</s>, saying: "Establish this one in the kingdom for now."

body.text:
235.001. yadā susīma āgato bhaviṣyati, tadā taṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmaḥ/
235.002. tato rājā ruṣitaḥ/
235.002. aśokena cābhihitam--yadi mama dharmeṇa rājyaṃ bhavati, devatā mama paṭṭaṃ bandhantu/
235.003. yāvaddevatābhiḥ paṭṭo baddhaḥ/
235.003. taṃ dṛṣṭvā bindusārasya rājña uṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ mukhādāgatam yāvatkālagataḥ/
235.004. yadā aśoko rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ, tasyordhvam yojanam yakṣāḥ śṛṇvanti, adho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ/
235.005. tena rādhagupto 'grāmātyaḥ sthāpitaḥ/
235.006. susīmenāpi śrutam--bindusāro rājā kālagataḥ, aśoko rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
235.006. iti śrutvā ca ruṣito 'bhyāgataḥ/
235.007. tvaritaṃ ca tasmāddeśādāgataḥ/
235.007. aśokenāpi pāṭaliputre nagare ekasmin dvāre eko nagnaḥ sthāpitaḥ, dvitīye dvitīyaḥ, tṛtīye rādhaguptaḥ, pūrvadvāre svayameva rājā aśoko 'vasthitaḥ/
235.009. rādhaguptena ca pūrvasmin dvāre yantramayo hastī sthāpitaḥ/
235.009. aśokasya ca pratimāṃ parikhāṃ khanayitvā khadirāṅgāraiśca pūrayitvā tṛṇenācchādya pāṃśunākīrṇā/
235.010. susīmaścābhihitah--yadi śakyase 'śokaṃ ghātayituṃ rājeti(?)/
235.011. sa yāvatpūrvadvāraṃ gatah--aśokena saha yotsyāmīti/
235.012. aṅgārapūrṇāyāṃ parikhāyāṃ patitaḥ/
235.012. tatraiva cānayena vyasanamāpannaḥ/
235.012. yadā ca susīmaḥ praghātitaḥ, tasyāpi mahānagno bhadrāyudho nāṃnā anekasahasraparivāraḥ, sa bhagavacchāsane pravrajito 'rhan saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: "When <s>Susīma</s> arrives, we shall establish him in the kingdom." At that the king grew angry. And <s>Aśoka</s> declared: "If the kingdom is mine by right, let the gods bind the royal fillet upon me." Thereupon the gods bound the fillet. Seeing this, hot blood came from King <s>Bindusāra</s>'s mouth, and he passed away. When <s>Aśoka</s> was established in the kingdom, the <s>yakṣas</s> heard him for a <s>yojana</s> above, and the <s>nāgas</s> for a <s>yojana</s> below. He appointed <s>Rādhagupta</s> as chief minister. <s>Susīma</s> too heard that King <s>Bindusāra</s> had passed away and <s>Aśoka</s> had been established in the kingdom. Hearing this, he came in anger, arriving swiftly from that region. <s>Aśoka</s> stationed one naked ascetic at one gate of the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a second at the second gate, <s>Rādhagupta</s> at the third, and at the eastern gate King <s>Aśoka</s> himself stood. <s>Rādhagupta</s> placed a mechanical elephant at the eastern gate. He had a moat dug before <s>Aśoka</s>'s position, filled it with <s>khadira</s>-charcoal embers, covered it with grass, and scattered dust over it. <s>Susīma</s> was told: "If you can slay <s>Aśoka</s>, you shall be king." He went to the eastern gate, thinking: "I shall fight with <s>Aśoka</s>." He fell into the moat filled with embers, and there he met his destruction by that stratagem.
