When <s>Susīma</s> was slain, his great naked ascetic named <s>Bhadrāyudha</s>, who had a retinue of many thousands, went forth into the Blessed One's teaching and became an <s>Arhat</s>.

body.text:
235.014. yadā aśoko rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ sa tairamātyairavajñayā dṛśyate/
235.014. tenāmātyānāmabhihitam--bhavantaḥ, puṣpavṛkṣān phalavṛkṣāṃśca cchittvā kaṇṭakavṛkṣān paripālayatha/
235.015. amātyā āhuh--devena kutra dṛṣṭam? api tu kaṇṭakavṛkṣāṃś chittvā puṣpavṛkṣān phalavṛkṣāṃśca paripālayitavyam/
235.017. tairyāvat trirapi rājña ājñā pratikūlitā, tato rājñā ruṣitena asiṃ niṣkośaṃ kṛtvā pañcānāmamātyaśatānāṃ śiraṃsi cchinnāni/
235.018. yāvadrājā aśoko 'pareṇa samayenāntaḥpuraparivṛto vasantakālasamaye puṣpitaphaliteṣu pādapeṣu pūrvanagarasyodyānaṃ gataḥ/
235.019. tatra ca paribhramatā aśokavṛkṣaḥ supuṣpito dṛṣṭaḥ/
235.020. tato rājño mamāpi sahanāmā ityanunayo jātaḥ/
235.020. sa ca rājā aśoko duḥsparśagātraḥ/
235.021. tā yuvatayastaṃ necchanti spraṣṭum/
235.021. yāvadrājā śayitaḥ, tasyāntaḥpureṇa roṣeṇa tasmādaśokavṛkṣāt puṣpāṇi śākhāśca cchinnāḥ/
235.022. yāvadrājñā pratibuddhena so 'śokavṛkṣo dṛṣṭaḥ, pṛṣṭaśca--kena tacchinnam? te kathayanti--deva, antaḥpurikābhiriti/
235.023. śrutvā ca rājñā amarṣajātena pañca strīśatāni kiṭikaiḥ saṃveṣṭya dagdhāni/
235.024. tasyemānyaśubhānyālokya caṇḍo rājā caṇḍāśoka iti vyavasthāpitaḥ/
235.025. yāvadrādhaguptenāgrāmātyenābhihitah--deva, na sadṛśaṃ svayamevedṛśamakāryaṃ kartum/
235.026. api tu devasya vadhyaghātakāḥ puruṣāḥ sthāpayitavyāḥ, ye devasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ śodhayiṣyanti/
235.027. yāvadrājñā rājapuruṣāḥ prayuktāh--vadhyaghātaṃ me mārgadhveti/
235.028. yāvat tatra nātidūre pūrvatapādamūle karvaṭakam/
235.028. tatra tantravāyaḥ prativasati/
235.028. tasya putro jātaḥ/
235.028. girika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
235.029. caṇḍo duṣṭātmā mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ca paribhāṣate, dārakadārikāśca tāḍayati, pipīlikān makṣikān mūṣikān matsyāṃśca jālena baḍiśena praghātayati/
235.031. caṇḍo dārakastasya caṇḍagirika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
235.031. yāvadrājapuruṣairdṛṣṭaḥ pāpe karmaṇi pravṛttaḥ/
235.032. sa tairabhihitah--śakyase rājño 'śokasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ kartum? sa <236>āha--kṛtsnasya jambudvīpasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ sādhayiṣyāmīti/
body.translated_text: When <s>Aśoka</s> was established in the kingdom, those ministers regarded him with contempt. He said to the ministers: "Sirs, you cut down the flower trees and fruit trees and tend the thorn trees." The ministers replied: "Where has Your Majesty seen such a thing? Rather, one should cut down the thorn trees and tend the flower trees and fruit trees." When they had defied the king's command three times, the enraged king drew his sword from its sheath and cut off the heads of five hundred ministers. On another occasion, King <s>Aśoka</s>, surrounded by his harem, went to the garden of the eastern city during the spring season, when the trees were in flower and fruit. While wandering there, he saw a beautifully blossoming <s>aśoka</s> tree. Then the king felt a tender affection, thinking: "This tree shares my name." Now King <s>Aśoka</s> had a rough-skinned body, and those young women did not wish to touch him. When the king fell asleep, his harem women, out of spite, cut the flowers and branches from that <s>aśoka</s> tree. When the king awoke and saw that <s>aśoka</s> tree, he asked: "Who cut it?" They told him: "Your Majesty, the harem women did it." Hearing this, the king, filled with fury, had five hundred women wrapped in bark and burned. Seeing these wicked deeds of his, the cruel king was given the name <s>Caṇḍāśoka</s> (Aśoka the Fierce). Then chief minister <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: "Your Majesty, it is not fitting to do such terrible deeds yourself. Rather, Your Majesty should appoint executioners who will carry out the punishments for Your Majesty." The king dispatched royal agents: "Find me an executioner." Not far from there, at the foot of the eastern mountain, was a small town. A weaver lived there, and a son was born to him. He was given the name <s>Girika</s>. He was cruel and evil-natured — he abused his mother and father, beat the boys and girls, and killed ants, flies, rats, and fish with nets and hooks. The cruel boy was given the name <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> (Fierce Girika). The royal agents saw him engaged in sinful deeds. They said to him: "Can you carry out King <s>Aśoka</s>'s executions?" He replied: "I shall carry out the executions for the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>!"

body.text:
236.001. yāvadrājño niveditam/
236.001. rājñā abhihitam--ānīyatāmiti/
236.002. sa ca rājapuruṣairabhihitah--āgaccha, rājā tvāmāhvayatīti/
236.003. tenābhihitam--āgamayata, yāvadahaṃ mātapitarau avalokayāmīti/
236.003. yāvanmātāpitarau uvāca--amba tāta, anujānīdhvam/
236.004. yāsyāmyahaṃ rājño 'śokasya vadhyakaraṇīyaṃ sādhayitum/
236.004. tābhyāṃ ca sa nivāritaḥ/
236.005. tena tau jīvitādvyaparopitau/
236.005. evam yāvadrājapuruṣairabhihitah--kimarthaṃ cireṇābhyāgato 'si? tena caitatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocitam/
236.006. sa tairyāvadrājño 'śokasyopanāmitaḥ/
236.007. tena rājño 'bhihitam--mamārthāya gṛhaṃ kārayasveti/
236.007. yāvadrājñā gṛhaṃ kārapitaṃ paramaśobhanaṃ dvāramātraramaṇīyam/
236.008. tasya ramaṇīyakaṃ bandhanamiti saṃjñā vyavasthāpitā/
236.008. sa āha--deva, varaṃ me prayaccha, yastatra praviśettasya na bhūyo nirgama iti/
236.009. yāvadrājñābhihitam--evamastu iti/
236.011. tataḥ sa caṇḍagirikaḥ kurkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ/
236.011. bhikṣuśca bālapaṇḍitaḥ sūtraṃ paṭhati/
236.012. sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ/
236.012. yāvannarakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmau ādīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālibhūtāyāmuttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena viṣkambhakena mukhadvāraṃ viṣkambhya ayoguḍānādīptān pradīptān saṃprajvalitānekajvālībhūtānāsye prakṣipānti, ye teṣāṃ sattvānāmoṣṭhau api dahanti, jahvāmapi kaṇṭhamapi kaṇṭhamapi hṛdayamapi hṛdayasāmantamapi antrāṇyantraguṇānapi dagdhvā adhaḥ pragharati/
236.016. evaṃ duḥkhā hi bhikṣavo nārakāḥ sattvā narakeṣūpapannāḥ/
236.017. yāvannarakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmau ādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālibhūtāyāmuttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena viṣkambhakena mukhadvāraṃ viṣkambhya kvathitaṃ tāmramāsye prakṣipanti, yatteṣāṃ sattvānāmoṣṭhāvapi dahati, jihvāmapi tālvapi kaṇṭhamapi kaṇṭhanālamapi, antrāṇyantraguṇānapi dagdhvā adhaḥ pragharati/
236.020. evaṃ duḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ/
236.020. santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannā yānnarakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmau ādīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyāmavānmukhān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena sūtreṇādīptena saṃprajvalitenaikajvālībhūtenāskphāṭya ayomayena kuṭhāreṇādīptena saṃpradīptena saṃprajvalitenaikajvālībhūtena takṣaṇuvanti saṃtakṣṇuvanti saṃpratakṣṇuvanti aṣṭāṃśamapi ṣaḍaṃśamapi ṣaḍaṃśamapi caturasnamapi vṛttamapi maṇḍalamapi unnatamapi avanatamapi śāntamapi viśāntamapi takṣṇuvanti/
236.025. evaṃ duḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ/
236.025. santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannā yānnarakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmau ādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvalībhūtāyāmavanmukhān pratiṣṭhāpya ayomayena ayomayena sūtreṇādīptena pradīptena saṃprajvalitenaikajvālībhūtenāsphāṭya ayomayyāṃ bhūmyāmāadīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvālībhūtāyāṃ takṣṇuvanti saṃtakṣṇuvanti saṃparitakṣṇuvanti, aṣṭāṃśamapi ṣaḍaṃśamapi caturasnamapi maṇḍalamapi unnatamapi avanatamapi śāntamapi viśāntamapi takṣṇuvanti/
236.030. evaṃ duḥkhā hi bhikṣavo narakāḥ/
236.031. santi sattvā narakeṣūpapannā yānnarakapālā gṛhītvā ayomayyāṃ bhūmāvādīptāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ saṃprajvalitāyāmekajvalībhūtāyāmuttānakān pratiṣṭhāpya pañcaviṣaṭabandhanāṃ kāraṇāṃ kārayanti, ubhayorhastayorāyasau<237> kīlau trāmanti, ubhayoḥ pādayorāyase kīle trāmanti, madhye hṛdayasyāyasaṃ kīlaṃ krāmanti/
237.002. {evam} suduḥkhā hi bhiṣavo narakāḥ/
237.002. evaṃ pañca vedanā iti kurute sadṛśāśca kāraṇāḥ sattvānāmārabdhāḥ kārayitum//
body.translated_text: This was reported to the king. The king said: "Bring him." The royal agents told him: "Come, the king summons you." He replied: "Wait while I take leave of my mother and father." He said to his parents: "Mother, father, give me your permission. I shall go to carry out King <s>Aśoka</s>'s executions." But they both tried to dissuade him. So he deprived them both of their lives. Then the royal agents asked: "Why have you taken so long to come?" And he told them the whole matter in detail. They brought him before King <s>Aśoka</s>. He said to the king: "Have a house built for my purpose." The king had a supremely splendid house built, pleasing only at its entrance. It was given the designation "The Delightful Prison." He said: "Your Majesty, grant me a boon — whoever enters there shall never come out again." The king said: "So be it." Then that <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock's Monastery), where a <s>bhikṣu</s> was reciting the <s>Bālapaṇḍita Sūtra</s> (Discourse on the Fool and the Wise): "Beings are reborn in the hells. The hell-wardens seize them, lay them on their backs upon an iron ground that is blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, prop open their mouths with an iron gag, and cast into their mouths iron balls that are blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame — these burn their lips, burn their tongues, burn their throats, burn their hearts, burn the region around the heart, burn their entrails and intestinal membranes, and pass out below. So painful indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the hells for beings reborn there. The hell-wardens seize them, lay them on their backs upon an iron ground that is blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, prop open their mouths with an iron gag, and pour boiling copper into their mouths — this burns their lips, their tongues, their palates, their throats, their gullets, their entrails and intestinal membranes, and passes out below. So painful indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the hells. There are beings reborn in the hells whom the hell-wardens seize and lay face-down upon an iron ground that is blazing, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, mark them with a blazing, fiercely ablaze, single-flamed iron cord, and hew them with a blazing, fiercely burning, fiercely ablaze, single-flamed iron axe — they hew and chop and carve them into octagonal, hexagonal, square, round, circular, convex, concave, even, and smooth shapes. So painful indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the hells. There are beings reborn in the hells whom the hell-wardens seize and lay face-down upon an iron ground that is blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, mark them with a blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, single-flamed iron cord, and upon the iron ground that is blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, they hew and chop and carve them into octagonal, hexagonal, square, circular, convex, concave, even, and smooth shapes. So painful indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the hells. There are beings reborn in the hells whom the hell-wardens seize and lay on their backs upon an iron ground that is blazing, burning, fiercely ablaze, become a single mass of flame, and inflict the torture of the five-fold staking — they drive iron stakes into both hands, drive iron stakes into both feet, and drive an iron stake into the middle of the heart. So exceedingly painful indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, are the hells. Thus he experiences the five agonies, and such punishments are devised to be inflicted upon beings."

body.text:
237.004. yāvat śrāvastyāmanyatamaḥ sārthavāhaḥ patnyā saha mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
237.004. tasya sā patnī mahāsamudre prasūtā/
237.005. dārako jātaḥ/
237.005. tasya samudra iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
237.005. yāvadvistareṇa dvādaśabhirvarṣairmahāsamudrāduttīrṇaḥ/
237.006. sa ca sārthavāhaḥ pañcabhirdhūrtaśatairmuṣitaḥ/
237.006. sārthavāhaḥ sa praghātitaḥ/
237.007. sa ca samudraḥ sārthavāhaputro bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ/
237.007. sa janapadacārikāṃ caran pāṭaliputramanuprāptaḥ/
237.008. sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya pāṭaliputraṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ/
237.009. so 'nabhijñatayā ca ramaṇīyakaṃ bhavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
237.009. tacca dvāramātraramaṇīyamabhyantaraṃ narakabhavanasadṛśaṃ pratibhayam/
237.010. dṛṣṭvā ca punar nirgantukāmaścaṇḍairikenāvalokitaḥ/
237.010. gṛhītvā coktah--iha te nidhanabhupagantavyamiti/
237.011. vistareṇa kāryam/
237.011. tato bhikṣuḥ śokārto bāṣpakaṇṭaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
237.012. tenocyate--kimidaṃ bāladāraka iva rudasīti? sa bhikṣuḥ prāha--
237.013. na śarīravināśaṃ hi śocāmi sarvaśaḥ/
237.014. mokṣadharmāntarāyaṃ tu śocāmi bhṛśamātmanaḥ//67//
body.translated_text: Now, a certain caravan-leader from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, together with his wife, had descended into the great ocean. His wife gave birth on the great ocean. A boy was born. He was given the name <s>Samudra</s> ('Ocean'). After twelve years, in full detail, he crossed back from the great ocean. That caravan-leader was robbed by five hundred scoundrels. The caravan-leader was slain. That <s>Samudra</s>, the caravan-leader's son, went forth in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. Wandering on a tour through the countryside, he arrived at <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. In the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he entered <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> for alms. Unknowingly, he entered a charming-looking building. But it was charming only at the entrance — inside, it was like a hell-realm, terrifying. Having seen it, as he wished to leave, he was noticed by <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> (the fierce one). Having seized him, he said: 'You must meet your death here.' The details should be elaborated. Then the monk, stricken with sorrow, became choked with tears. He was told: 'Why do you weep like a young child?' The monk said: 'It is not the destruction of my body that I grieve for in every way; rather, I deeply grieve for the obstruction of my own liberation from <s>Dharma</s>.' //67//

body.text:
237.015. durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ pravrajyāṃ ca sukhodayām/
237.016. śākyasiṃhaṃ ca śāstāraṃ punastyakṣyāmi durmatiḥ//68//
body.translated_text: 'Having obtained this rare human birth and the going-forth that gives rise to happiness, and having the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> as my teacher — fool that I am, I shall lose them again.' //68//

body.text:
237.017. tenocyate--dattavaro 'haṃ nṛpatinā/
237.017. dhīro bhava/
237.017. nāsti te mokṣa iti/
237.017. tataḥ sakaruṇairvacanaistaṃ bhikṣuḥ kramam yācati sma māsam yāvat/
237.018. saptarātramanujñātaḥ/
237.018. sa khalu maraṇabhayodvignahṛdayaḥ saptarātreṇa me na bhavitavyamiti vyāyatamatiḥ saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: He was told: 'I have been granted a boon by the king. Be brave. There is no escape for you.' Then the monk, with compassionate words, begged him for a reprieve of up to a month. He was granted seven nights. With a heart agitated by the fear of death, knowing 'in seven nights I shall no longer exist,' he became intensely resolute in his determination.

body.text:
237.020. atha saptame divase 'śokasya rājño 'ntaḥpurikāṃ kumāreṇa saha saṃraktāṃ nirīkṣamāṇāṃ saṃlapantīṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sahadarśanādeva ruṣitena rājñā tau dvāvapi taṃ cārakamanupreṣitau/
237.021. tatra musalairayodroṇyāmasthyavaśeṣau kṛtau/
237.022. tato bhikṣustau dṛṣṭvā saṃvignaḥ prāha--
237.023. aho kāruṇikaḥ śāstā samyagāha mahāmuniḥ/
237.024. phenapiṇḍopamaṃ rūpamasāramanavasthitam//69//
body.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, King <s>Aśoka</s>, seeing a woman of the inner palace gazing at the prince with passion and conversing with him, became enraged at the very sight and dispatched both of them to that prison. There, they were reduced to nothing but bones by iron pestles in an iron trough. Then the monk, having seen them, was deeply moved and said: 'Ah, how compassionate was the Teacher! The Great Sage spoke rightly: form is like a lump of foam — without substance, without stability.' //69//

body.text:
237.025. kva tadvadanakāntitvaṃ gātraśobhā kva sā gatā/
237.026. dhigastvayaṃ saṃsāro ramante yatra bāliśāḥ//70//
body.translated_text: 'Where has that beauty of the face gone? Where has that grace of the limbs gone? Shame on this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), in which fools delight!' //70//

body.text:
237.027. idamālambanaṃ prāptaṃ cārake vasatā mayā/
237.028. yamāśritya tariṣyāmi pāramadya bhavodadheḥ//71//
body.translated_text: 'Having obtained this support while dwelling in this prison, relying upon it I shall today cross to the far shore of the ocean of existence.' //71//

body.text:
237.029. tena tāṃ rajanīṃ kṛtsnāam yujyatā buddhaśāsane/
237.030. sarvasamyojanaṃ chittvā prāptamarhattvamuttamam//72//
body.translated_text: By him, that entire night, applying himself to the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching, having cut through all fetters, the supreme <s>Arhattva</s> (state of an Arhat) was attained. //72//

body.text:
238.001. <238>tatastasmin najanīkṣaye sa bhikṣuścaṇḍagirikenocyate--bhikṣo, nirgatā rātriḥ/
238.001. udita ādityaḥ/
238.002. kāraṇākālastaveti/
238.002. tato bhikṣurāha--dīrghāyuḥ, mamāpi nirgatā rātriḥ, udita ādityaḥ/
238.003. parānugrahakāla iti/
238.003. yatheṣṭaṃ vartatāmiti/
238.003. caṇḍagirikaḥ prāha--nāvagacchāmi/
238.004. vistīryatāṃ vacanametaditi/
238.004. tato bhikṣurāha--
238.005. mamāpi hṛdayāddhorā nirgatā mohaśarvatī/
238.006. pañcāvaraṇasaṃchannā kleśataskarasevitā//73//
body.translated_text: Then, at the end of that night, the monk was told by <s>Caṇḍagirika</s>: 'Monk, the night has passed. The sun has risen. The time of your execution has come.' Then the monk said: 'Long-lived one, my night too has passed, and my sun has risen. Now is the time for benefiting others. Let things proceed as you wish.' <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> said: 'I do not understand. Explain these words fully.' Then the monk said: 'For me too, the terrible night of delusion, infested by the wolves of the five hindrances, beset by the thieves of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), has passed from my heart.' //73//

body.text:
238.007. udito jñānasūryaśca manonabhasi me śubhaḥ/
238.008. prabhayā yasya paśyāmi trailokyamiha tattvataḥ//74//
body.translated_text: 'And the sun of knowledge has risen, auspicious, in the sky of my mind — by whose radiance I see the three worlds here in their true nature.' //74//

body.text:
238.009. parānugrahakālo me śāsturvṛttānuvarinaḥ/
238.010. idaṃ śarīraṃ dīrghāyuryatheṣṭaṃ triyatāmiti//75//
body.translated_text: 'Now is the time for me to benefit others, following the way of the Teacher. This body, O long-lived one, may be dealt with as you wish.' //75//

body.text:
238.011. tatastena nirghṛṇena dāruṇahṛdayena paralokanirapekṣeṇa roṣāviṣṭena bahūdakāyāṃ sthālyāṃ nararudhiravasāmūtrapurīṣasaṃkulāyāṃ mahālohyāṃ prakṣiptaḥ/
238.012. prabhūtendhanaiścāgniḥ prajvālitaḥ/
238.012. sa ca bahunāpīndhanakṣayena na saṃtapyate/
238.013. tataḥ prajvālayitum (prārabdhaḥ/) yadā tadāpi na prajvalati, tato vicārya tāṃ lohīm, paśyati taṃ bhikṣuṃ pādmasyopari paryaṅkenopaviṣṭam/
238.014. dṛṣṭvā ca tato rājñe nivedayāmāsa/
238.015. atha rājani samāgate prāṇisahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu sa bhikṣurvaineyakālamavekṣamāṇah--
238.015. riddhiṃ samutpādya sa tanmuhūrtaṃ lohyanatarasthaḥ salilārdragātraḥ/
238.018. nirīkṣamāṇasya janasya madhye nabhastalaṃ haṃsa ivotpapāt//76//
body.translated_text: Then that merciless one, of cruel heart, heedless of the next world, seized by anger, threw him into a large iron cauldron filled with copious water, human blood, fat, urine, and excrement. A great fire was kindled with abundant fuel. But even with all the fuel exhausted, the monk did not burn. Then, attempting to make it blaze, when even then it would not ignite, he examined the cauldron and saw the monk seated cross-legged upon a lotus. Having seen this, he reported it to the king. Then, when the king arrived and thousands of beings had gathered, that monk, observing the time for training those to be trained — at that moment, standing within the cauldron, his body moist with water, before the eyes of the watching crowd, like a goose he flew up into the sky. //76//

body.text:
238.020. vicitrāṇi ca pratihāryāṇi darśayitumārabdhaḥ/
238.020. vakṣyati hi--
238.021. ardhena gātreṇa vavarṣa toyamardhena jajvāla hutāśanaśca/
238.023. varṣañ jvalaṃścaiva rarāja yaḥ khe dīptaucadhiprasravaṇeva śailaḥ//77//
body.translated_text: He began to display various miraculous feats. For it is said: 'With one half of his body he rained water, and with the other half he blazed with fire; raining and blazing, he shone in the sky like a mountain with a burning peak and a flowing waterfall.' //77//

body.text:
238.025. tamudgataṃ vyoṃni naśāmya rājā kṛtāñjalirvismayaphullavaktraḥ/
238.027. udvīkamāṇastamuvāca dhīraṃ kautūhalātkiṃcidahaṃ vivakṣuḥ//78//
body.translated_text: 'Seeing him risen into the sky, the king, with palms joined, his face expanded with wonder, gazing up at that steadfast one, wishing to say something, spoke with curiosity:' //78//

body.text:
238.029. manuṣyatulyaṃ tava saumya rūpam ṛddhiprabhāvastu narānatītya/
238.031. na niścayaṃ tena vibho vrajāmi ko nāma bhāvastava śuddhabhāva//79//
body.translated_text: 'Your form, O gentle one, is like that of a human, yet your supernatural power surpasses humans. Therefore, O Mighty One, I cannot arrive at certainty — what is your nature, O one of pure nature?' //79//

body.text:
239.001. <239>tatsāmprataṃ brūhi mamedamartham yathā prajānāmi tava prabhāvam/
239.003. jñātvā ca te dharmaguṇaprabhāvān yathābalaṃ śiṣyavadācareyam//80//
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, tell me this matter now, so that I may know your power; and having understood the power of your virtues in the <s>Dharma</s>, may I practice as a disciple to the best of my ability.' //80//

body.text:
239.005. tato bhikṣuḥ pravacanaparigrāhako 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati, bhagavaddhātuṃ ca vistarīṃ kariṣyati, mahājanahitārthaṃ ca pratipatsyata iti matvā svaguṇamudbhāvayaṃstamuvāca--
239.007. ahaṃ mahākāruṇikasya rājan prahīṇasarvāśravabandhanasya/
239.009. buddhasya putro vadatāṃ varasya dharmānvayaḥ sarvabhaveṣvasaktaḥ//81//
body.translated_text: Then the monk, thinking 'This one will become a supporter of the teaching; he will distribute the <s>Bhagavān's</s> relics widely and will act for the benefit of many people,' revealing his own virtues, said to him: 'I am, O king, a son of the Greatly Compassionate One who has destroyed all bonds of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) — of the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost of speakers — a follower of the <s>Dharma</s>, unattached to all forms of existence.' //81//

body.text:
239.011. dāntena dāntaḥ puruṣarṣabheṇa śāntiṃ gatenāpi śamaṃ praṇītaḥ/
239.003. muktena saṃsāramahābhayebhyo nirmokṣito 'haṃ bhavabandhanebhyaḥ//82//
body.translated_text: 'Tamed by the tamer, the bull among men, brought to peace by the one who has gone to peace, freed from the great terrors of <s>saṃsāra</s> by the one who is liberated — I have been released from the bonds of existence.' //82//

body.text:
239.015. api ca/
239.015. mahārāja, tvaṃ bhagavatā vyākṛtah--varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama pāṭaliputre nagare 'śoko nāma rājā bhaviṣyati caturbhāgacakravartī dharmarājaḥ, yo me śarīradhātūn vaistārikān kariṣyati, caturaśītiṃ dharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati/
239.017. idaṃ ca devena narakasadṛśaṃ sthānameva sthāpitam yatra prāṇisahasrāṇi nipātyante/
239.018. tadarhasi deva sarvasattvebhyo 'bhayapradānaṃ dātum, bhagavataśca manorathaṃ paripūrayitum/
239.019. āha ca--
239.020. tasmānnarendra abhayaṃ prayaccha sattveṣu kāruṇyapurojaveṣu/
239.022. nāthasya saṃpūrya manorathaṃ ca vistārikān dharmadharān kuruṣva//83//
body.translated_text: Moreover: 'Great King, you were prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "A hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, there will be a king named <s>Aśoka</s>, a quarter-<s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a righteous king, who will distribute my bodily relics widely and will establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> <s>stūpas</s>." And yet the king has established this very hell-like place where thousands of beings are cast down. Therefore, may Your Majesty grant the gift of safety to all beings and fulfill the aspiration of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' And he said: 'Therefore, O king of men, grant safety to all beings, with compassion as your foremost motivation; and fulfilling the aspiration of the Protector, establish the bearers of the <s>Dharma</s> widely.' //83//

body.text:
239.024. atha sa rājā buddhe samupajātaprasādaḥ kṛtakarasampuṭastaṃ bhikṣuṃ kṣamayannuvāca--
239.025. daśabalasuta kṣantumarhasīmaṃ ca tavādya deśayāmi/
239.027. śaraṇamṛṣimupaimi taṃ ca buddhaṃ gaṇavaramāryaniveditaṃ ca dharmam//84//
body.translated_text: Then that king, with faith arisen toward the <s>Buddha</s>, with palms joined, begging forgiveness of the monk, said: 'O son of the Ten-Powered One, please forgive this; and today I declare before you — I go for refuge to that <s>Buddha</s>, the Sage, and to the supreme <s>Saṃgha</s> and to the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed by the Noble Ones.' //84//

body.text:
239.029. api ca--
239.030. karomi caiṣa vyavasāyamadya taṃ tadgauravattātpravaṇaprasādāt/
body.translated_text: Moreover: 'And I make this resolve today, out of reverence for him, with my faith inclined—'

body.text: 240.001. <240>gāṃ maṇḍayiṣyāmi janendracaityairhaṃsāṃśaśaṅkhendubalākakalpaiḥ//85//
body.translated_text: 'I shall adorn the earth with shrines to the Lord of Men, beautiful as swans, moon, stars, and herons.' //85//

body.text:
240.003. yāvat sa bhikṣustadeva ṛddhyā prakrāntaḥ/
240.003. atha rājā ārabdho niṣkrāmitum/
240.004. tataścaṇḍagirikaḥ kṛtāñjaliruvāca--deva, labdhavaro 'ham/
240.004. naikasya vinirgama iti/
240.004. rājā āha--mā tāvanmamāpīcchasi ghātayitum/
240.005. sa uvāca--evameva/
240.005. rājā āha--ko 'smākaṃ prathamataraṃ praviṣṭah? caṇḍagirika uvāca--aham/
240.006. tato rājñā abhihitam/
240.006. ko 'treti? yāvadvadhyaghātairgṛhītaḥ/
240.007. gṛhītvā ca yantragṛhaṃ praveśitaḥ/
240.007. praveśayitvā dagdhaḥ/
240.007. tacca ramaṇīyakaṃ bandhanamapanītaṃ sarvasattvebhyaścābhayapradānamanupradattam/
240.008. tato rājā bhagavaccharīradhātuṃ vistarīṣyāmīti caturaṅgena balakāyena gatvā ajātaśatrupratiṣṭhāpitaṃ droṇastūpamutpāṭya śarīradhātuṃ gṛhītavān/
240.010. yatroddhāraṇaṃ ca vistareṇa kṛtvā dhātupratyaṃśaṃ datvā stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya evaṃ dvitīyaṃ stūpaṃ vitareṇa bhaktimato yāvatsaptadroṇādgrahāya stūpāṃśca pratiṣṭhāpya rāmagrāmaṃ gataḥ/
240.011. tato rājā nāgair nāgabhavanamavatāritaḥ, vijñaptaśca--vayamasyātraiva pūjāṃ kariṣyāma iti/
240.012. yāvadrājñā abhyanujñātam/
240.013. tato nāgarājā punarapi nāgabhavanāduttāritaḥ/
240.013. vakṣyati hi--
240.014. rāmagrāme tvaṣṭamaṃ stūpamadya nāgāstatkālaṃ bhaktimanto rarakṣuḥ/
240.016. dhātūnyetasmānnopalebhe sa rājā śraddhābhū(?) rājā cintayati yastvetatkṛtvā jagāma//86//
body.translated_text: Then that monk departed by supernatural power. And the king began to go out. Then <s>Caṇḍagirika</s>, with palms joined, said: 'Your Majesty, I have been granted a boon: no one shall leave alive.' The king said: 'Surely you do not wish to have me killed too?' He said: 'Even so.' The king said: 'Who among us entered first?' <s>Caṇḍagirika</s> said: 'I did.' Then the king commanded. 'Who is here?' — whereupon he was seized by the executioners. Having been seized, he was thrown into the device-house. Having been thrown in, he was burned. That charming-looking prison was demolished, and the gift of safety was granted to all beings. Then the king, resolving 'I shall distribute the <s>Bhagavān's</s> bodily relics widely,' went with his fourfold army and, having uprooted the <s>Droṇa-stūpa</s> established by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, took the bodily relics. Having performed the extraction in full detail, and distributing a portion of the relics and establishing a <s>stūpa</s>, he similarly went to a second <s>stūpa</s>, and in detail with devotion, having taken relics from all seven <s>Droṇa-stūpas</s> and establishing <s>stūpas</s>, he went to <s>Rāmagrāma</s>. There the king was taken down into the <s>Nāga</s> realm by the <s>Nāgas</s>, who implored: 'We shall perform worship of them right here.' The king gave his assent. Then the <s>Nāga</s> king brought him back up from the <s>Nāga</s> realm. For it is said: 'At <s>Rāmagrāma</s>, the eighth <s>stūpa</s>, the devoted <s>Nāgas</s> at that time protected the relics; that king did not obtain relics from it. The faithful king departed, wondering who had built it.' //86//

body.text:
240.018. yāvadrājā caturaśītikaraṇḍasahasraṃ kārayitvā sauvarṇarūpyasphaṭikavaiḍūryamayānāṃ teṣu dhātavaḥ prakṣiptaḥ/
240.019. evaṃ vistareṇa caturaśītikumbhasahasraṃ paṭṭasahasraṃ ca yakṣāṇāṃ haste datvā visarjitam--āsamudrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyameṣu nagareṣu yatra koṭiḥ paripūryate, tatra dharmarājikāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitavyam//
body.translated_text: Then the king had eighty-four thousand caskets made — of gold, silver, crystal, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) — and the relics were placed in them. In the same manner, in full detail, eighty-four thousand urns and an equal number of silk wrappings were given into the hands of <s>Yakṣas</s> and dispatched: 'Throughout the earth as far as the ocean, in cities high, low, and middling, wherever the population reaches a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), there a <s>Dharmarājikā</s> <s>stūpa</s> should be established.'

body.text:
240.022. tasmin samaye takṣaśilāyāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatkoṭayaḥ/
240.022. tairabhihitam--ṣaṭtriṃśatkaraṇḍakānanuprayaccheti/
240.023. rājā cintayati--na yadi vaistārikā dhātavo bhaviṣyanti/
240.023. upāyajño rājā/
240.024. tenābhihitam--pañcatriṃśatkoṭayaḥ śodhayitavyāḥ/
240.024. vistareṇa yāvadrājñā abhihitam--yatrādhikatarā bhavanti, yatra ca nyūnatarāḥ, tatra na dātavyam//
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Takṣaśilā</s> had thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> of people. They said: 'Give us thirty-six caskets.' The king reflected: 'If the relics are to be distributed widely, this will not do.' The king was skilled in stratagems. He said: 'Thirty-five <s>koṭis</s> must be verified.' In full detail, the king declared: 'Wherever there are more, and wherever there are fewer, there it shall not be given.'

body.text:
240.026. yāvadrājā kurkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā sthavirayaśasamabhigamyovāca--ayaṃ me manorathah--ekasmin divase ekasminmuhūrte caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayeyamiti/
240.027. sthavireṇābhihitam--evamastu/
240.028. ahaṃ tasmin samaye pāṇinā sūryamaṇḍalaṃ praticchādayiṣyāmīti/
240.028. yāvat tasmin divase sthavirayaśasā pāṇinā sūryamaṇḍalaṃ praticchāditam/
240.029. ekasmin divase ekamuhūrte caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
240.030. vakṣyati ca--
body.translated_text:
240.026. Then the king, having gone to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Grove Monastery) and approached the elder <s>Yaśas</s>, said: 'This is my wish — that in a single day, in a single hour, I should establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> (Dharma-King shrines).'
240.027. The elder said: 'So be it.
240.028. At that time, I shall cover the disc of the sun with my hand.'
240.028. Then, on that day, the elder <s>Yaśas</s> covered the disc of the sun with his hand.
240.029. In a single day, in a single hour, eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> were established.
240.030. And it shall be said:

body.text:
241.001. <241>tābhyaḥ saptabhyaḥ pūrvikābhyaḥ kṛtibhyo dhātuṃ tasya ṛṣeḥ sa hyupādāya mauryaḥ/
241.003. cakre stūpānāṃ śāradābhraprabhānāṃ loke sāśīti śāsadahnā sahasram//87//
body.translated_text:
241.001. 'From those seven earlier works, having taken the relics of that sage, that <s>Maurya</s>
241.003. made in the world, in a single day, a thousand and eighty <s>stūpas</s> radiant like autumn clouds.' //87//

body.text:
241.005. yāvacca rājñā aśokena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam, dhārmiko dharmarājā saṃvṛttaḥ/
241.006. tasya dharmāśoka iti saṃjñā jātā/
241.006. vakṣyati ca--
241.007. āryamauryaśrīḥ sa prajānāṃ hitārthaṃ kṛtsnaṃ stūpān kārayāmāsa lokam/
241.009. caṇḍāśokatvaṃ prāpya pūrvaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dharmāśokatvaṃ karmaṇā tena lebhe//88//
body.translated_text:
241.005. When King <s>Aśoka</s> had established the eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s>, he became a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king.
241.006. He came to be known as <s>Dharmāśoka</s> ('Aśoka of the <s>Dharma</s>').
241.006. And it shall be said:
241.007. 'That noble <s>Maurya</s> glory, for the welfare of his subjects, had <s>stūpas</s> constructed throughout the entire world.
241.009. Having first been <s>Caṇḍāśoka</s> ('Aśoka the Fierce') on earth, he obtained the title <s>Dharmāśoka</s> by that deed.' //88//

body.text: 241.011. pāṃśupradānāvadānaṃ ṣaḍviṃśatimam//
body.translated_text: 241.011. The <s>Pāṃśupradānāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Gift of Dust), the twenty-sixth.

body.text: 242.001. div27 kuṇālāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 242.001. Chapter 27: The <s>Kuṇālāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Kuṇāla</s>).

body.text:
242.002. sa idānīmacirajātaprasādo buddhaśāsane yatra śākyaputrīyān dadarśa ākīrṇe rahasi vā, tatra śirasā pādayor nipatya vandate sma/
242.003. tasya ca yaśo nāmāmātyaḥ paramaśrāddho bhagavati/
242.004. sa taṃ rājānamuvāca--deva, nārhasi sarvavarṇapravrajitānāṃ praṇipātaṃ kartum/
242.004. santi hi śākyaśrāmaṇerakāścaturbhyo varṇebhyaḥ pravrajitā iti/
242.005. tasya rājā na kiṃcidavocat/
242.005. atha sa rājā kenacit kālāntareṇa sarvasacivānuvāca--vividhānāṃ prāṇināṃ śirobhiḥ karyam/
242.007. tattvamamukasya prāṇinaḥ śīrṣamānaya, tvamamukasyeti/
242.007. yaśāmātyaḥ punarājñaptah--tvaṃ mānuṣaṃ śīrṣamānayeti/
242.008. samānīteṣu ca śiraḥsu abhihitāh--gacchata, imāni śiraṃsi mūlyena vikrīṇīdhvamiti/
242.009. atha sarvaśirāṃsi vikrītāni/
242.009. tadeva mānuṣyaṃ śiro na kaścijjagrāha/
242.009. tato rājñābhihitah--vināpi mūlyena kasmaicidetacchiro dehītai/
242.010. na cāsyaṃ kaścit pratigrāhako babhūva/
242.011. tato yaśāmātyastasyaḥ śirasaḥ pratigrāhakamanāsādya savrīḍo rājānamupetyedamarthamuvāca--
242.013. gogardabhorabhramṛgadvijānāṃ mūlyairgṛhītāni śirāṃsi pumbhiḥ/
242.015. śirastvidaṃ mānuṣamapraśastaṃ na gṛhyate mūlyamṛte 'pi rājan//1//
body.translated_text:
242.002. He (<s>Aśoka</s>), having now recently obtained faith in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching, wherever he saw followers of the <s>Śākya</s> son — whether in a crowd or in private — would bow his head at their feet in salutation.
242.003. He had a minister named <s>Yaśas</s>, who was supremely devoted to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
242.004. He said to the king: 'Your Majesty, you should not make prostrations to renunciants of all castes.
242.004. For the <s>Śākya</s> <s>śramaṇas</s> include those who have gone forth from all four castes.'
242.005. The king said nothing to him.
242.005. Then the king, after some time, said to all his ministers: 'I need the heads of various creatures.
242.007. You bring the head of such-and-such a creature, and you bring the head of such-and-such.'
242.007. But to the minister <s>Yaśas</s> he commanded: 'You bring a human head.'
242.008. When the heads had been brought, he said: 'Go and sell these heads for a price.'
242.009. All the heads were sold.
242.009. But the human head — no one would take it.
242.009. Then the king said: 'Give this head to someone even without a price.'
242.010. Yet no one would accept it.
242.011. Then the minister <s>Yaśas</s>, unable to find a buyer for that head, came back to the king ashamed and reported the matter:
242.013. 'The heads of cows, donkeys, rams, deer, and birds were taken by people for a price;
242.015. but this human head, being inauspicious, is not taken even without a price, O king.' //1//

body.text:
242.017. atha sa rājā tamamātyamuvāca--kimidamitīdaṃ mānuṣaśiro na kaścidgṛhṇātīti? amātya uvāca--jugupsitatvāditi/
242.018. rājābravīt--kimetadeva śiro jugupsitamāhosvit sarvamānuṣaśirāṃsīti? amātya uvāca--sarvamānuṣaśirāṃsīti/
242.019. rājābravīt--kimidaṃ madīyamapi śiro jugupsitamiti? sa ca bhayānnecchati tasmādbhūtārthamabhidhātum/
242.020. sa rājñābhihitah--amātyaḥ, satyamucyatamiti/
242.021. sa uvāca--evamiti/
242.021. tataḥ sa rājā tamamātyaṃ pratijñāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya pratyādiśannimamarthamuvāca--haṃ bhoḥ, rūpaiśvaryajanitamadavismita, yuktamidaṃ bhavataḥ, yasmāt tvaṃ bhikṣucaraṇapraṇāmaṃ māaṃ vicchandayitumicchasi?
242.024. vināpi mūlyairvijugupsitatvāt pratigrahītā bhuvi yasya nāsti/
242.026. śirastadāsādya mameha puṇyam yadyarjitaṃ kiṃ viparītamatra//2//
body.translated_text:
242.017. Then the king said to that minister: 'What is this? Why does no one take this human head?' The minister said: 'Because it is repulsive.'
242.018. The king said: 'Is this head alone repulsive, or are all human heads repulsive?' The minister said: 'All human heads are repulsive.'
242.019. The king said: 'Is this head of mine too repulsive?' But the minister, out of fear, did not wish to state the truth.
242.020. The king said to him: 'Minister, speak the truth.'
242.021. He said: 'It is so.'
242.021. Then the king, having established the minister in his promise, addressed him with this retort: 'Well then, sir, you who are astonished by the pride born of beauty and sovereignty — is it fitting for you to try to dissuade me from bowing at the feet of monks?
242.024. Since there is no one on earth who would accept it, even without a price, because of its repulsiveness —
242.026. having recognized this about my head, what merit have I acquired here? What is wrong in this?' //2//

body.text:
242.028. jātiṃ bhavān paśyati śākyabhikṣuṣvantargatāṃsteṣu guṇānna ceti/
242.030. ato bhavāñ jātimadāvalepādātmānamanyāṃśca hinasti mohāt//3//
body.translated_text:
242.028. 'You see the caste within the <s>Śākya</s> monks, but you do not see the virtues within them.
242.030. Therefore, out of the intoxication and arrogance of caste, you harm yourself and others through delusion.' //3//

body.text:
243.001. <243>āvāhakāle 'tha vivāhakāle jāteḥ parīkṣā na tu dharmakāle/
243.003. dharmakriyāyā hi guṇā nimittā guṇāśca jātiṃ na vicārayanti//4//
body.translated_text:
243.001. 'At the time of betrothal or at the time of marriage, caste is examined — but not at the time of practicing the <s>Dharma</s>.
243.003. For virtues are the basis of <s>Dharma</s> practice, and virtues do not inquire about caste.' //4//

body.text:
243.005. yadyucchakulīnagatā doṣā garhāṃ prayānti loke 'smin/
243.006. kathamiva nīcajanagatā guṇā na satkāramarhanti//5//
body.translated_text:
243.005. 'If faults residing in those of high birth are condemned in this world,
243.006. how then should virtues residing in those of low birth not deserve respect?' //5//

body.text:
243.007. cittavaśena hi puṃsāṃ kalevaraṃ nindyate 'tha satkriyate/
243.008. śākyaśramaṇamanāṃsi ca śuddhānyarcyānyataḥ śākyāḥ//6//
body.translated_text:
243.007. 'By the mind's disposition is a person's body censured or honored.
243.008. Since the minds of the <s>Śākya</s> <s>śramaṇas</s> are pure, the <s>Śākyas</s> are therefore worthy of worship.' //6//

body.text:
243.009. yadi guṇaparivarjito dvijātiḥ patita iti prathito 'pi yātyavajñām/
243.011. na tu nidhanakulodgato 'pi jantuḥ śubhaguṇayukta iti praṇamya pūjyaḥ//7//
body.translated_text:
243.009. 'Even a twice-born, if devoid of virtues, though renowned as "fallen," goes to disgrace;
243.011. but a being born of a lowly family, if endowed with auspicious virtues, is to be honored with a bow.' //7//

body.text:
243.013. api ca/
243.014. kiṃ te kāruṇikasya śākyavṛṣabhasyaitadvaco na śrutaṃ prājñaiḥ sāramasārakebhya iha yannṛbhyo grahītuṃ kṣamam/
243.016. tasyānanyathavādino yadi ca tāmājñāṃ cikīrṣāmyahaṃ vyāhantuṃ ca bhavān yadi prayatate naitat suhṛllakṣaṇam//8//
body.translated_text:
243.013. 'Moreover:
243.014. Have you not heard this saying of the compassionate Bull of the <s>Śākyas</s> — that the wise should take the essence from the essential and non-essential among people?
243.016. If I wish to carry out the command of that one whose word is never false, and you strive to obstruct me, that is not the mark of a friend.' //8//

body.text:
243.018. ikṣukṣodavadujijñato bhuvi yadā kāyo mama svapsyati pratyutthānanamaskṛtāñjalipuṭakleśakriyāsvakṣamaḥ/
243.020. kāyenāhamanena kiṃ nu kuśalaṃ śakṣyāmi kartuṃ tadā tasmānnāryamataḥ śmaśānanidhanāt sāraṃ grahītuṃ mayā//9//
body.translated_text:
243.018. 'When this body of mine, crushed like sugarcane, shall lie on the ground, unable to rise, bow, join palms, or perform the exertions of removing defilements —
243.020. what wholesome deed shall I then be able to do with this body? Therefore, the essence must be extracted by me from this body before its cremation-ground end, according to the noble teaching.' //9//

body.text:
243.022. bhavanādiva pradīptānnimajjamānādivāpsu ratnanidheḥ/
243.023. kāyādvidhānanidhanādye sāraṃ nādhigacchanti//10//
body.translated_text:
243.022. 'As from a burning house, or as from a treasure-chest sinking in water —
243.023. those who do not extract the essence from this body destined for destruction are lost.' //10//

body.text:
243.024. te sāramapaśyantaḥ sārāsāreṣvakovidā prājñāḥ/
243.025. te maraṇamakaravadanapraveśasamaye viṣīdanti//11//
body.translated_text:
243.024. 'They who do not see the essence, unskilled in discerning the essential from the non-essential — though called wise —
243.025. they despair at the moment of entering the jaws of the crocodile of death.' //11//

body.text:
243.026. dadhidhṛtanavanītakṣīratakropayogādvaramapahṛtasāro maṇḍakumbho 'vabhagnaḥ/
243.028. na bhavati bahu śocyam yadvadevaṃ śarīre sucaritahṛtasāre naiti śoko 'ntakāle//12//
body.translated_text:
243.026. 'Just as a curd-pot from which the essence has been extracted — its butter, ghee, fresh butter, and milk having been used up — is broken and not much lamented;
243.028. so too, when the essence has been extracted from the body through good conduct, grief does not come at the time of death.' //12//

body.text:
244.001. <244>sucaritavimukhānāṃ garvitānām yadā tu prasabhamiha hi mṛtyuḥ kāyakumbhaṃ bhinatti/
244.003. dahati hṛdayameṣāṃ śokavahnistadānīṃ dadhighaṭa iva bhagne sarvaśo 'prāptasāre//13//
body.translated_text:
244.001. 'But when death forcibly shatters the body-pot of those who are averse to good conduct and puffed up with pride,
244.003. then the fire of grief burns their hearts — like a curd-pot broken without its essence having been extracted.' //13//

body.text:
244.005. kartuṃ vighnamato na me 'rhati bhavān kāyapraṇāmaṃ prati śreṣṭho 'smītyaparīkṣako hi gaṇayan mohāndhakārāvṛtaḥ/
244.007. kāyam yastu parīkṣate daśabalavyāhāradīpairbudho nāsau pārthivabhṛtyayorviṣamatāṃ kāyasya saṃpaśyati//14//
body.translated_text:
244.005. 'Therefore, you should not obstruct my bodily prostrations. For one who, enveloped in the darkness of delusion, reckons without examination "I am superior" —
244.007. but one who is wise and examines the body by the lamp of the Ten-Powered One's words does not see inequality of body between a king and his servant.' //14//

body.text:
244.009. tvagmāṃsāsthiśirāyakṛtprabhṛtayo bhāvā hi tulyā nṛṇāmāhāryaistu vibhūṣaṇairadhikatā kāyasya niṣpadyate/
244.011. etatsāramiheṣyate tu yadimaṃ niśritya kāyādhamaṃ pratyutthānanamaskṛtādikuśalaṃ prājñaiḥ samutthāpyate//15// iti/
244.013. athāśoko rājā^hirodakasikatāpiṇḍairaṇḍakāṣṭhebhyo 'pi asārataratvaṃ kāyasyāvetya praṇāmādibhyaḥ samutthasya phalasya bahukalpaśaḥ sthāpayitvā sumeruvanmahāpṛthivībhyaḥ samutthasya phalasya bahukalpaśaḥ sthāpayitvā sumeruvanmahāpṛthivībhyaḥ sārataratāmavekṣya bhagavataḥ stūpavandanāyāmātmānamalaṃkartukāmo 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ kurkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā tatra vṛddhānte sthitvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca--asti--
244.018. kaścidanyo 'pi nirdiṣṭo dvitīyaḥ sarvadarśanā/
244.019. yathāhaṃ tena nirdiṣṭaḥ pāṃśudānena dhīmatā//16//
body.translated_text:
244.009. 'Skin, flesh, bone, veins, liver, and other constituents are indeed the same in all humans; superiority of the body is produced by external ornaments and adornments.
244.011. This is regarded here as the essence: that, depending on this lowly body, the wise generate the merit of rising, bowing, and other wholesome acts.' //15//
244.013. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having understood the body to be even more insubstantial than bubbles, sand-banks, castor-oil trees — and having seen that the fruit arising from prostrations and other acts persists for many <s>kalpas</s>, and is more substantial than <s>Sumeru</s> and the great earth — wishing to adorn himself for the worship of the <s>Bhagav��n's</s> <s>stūpa</s>, surrounded by a retinue of ministers, went to the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>. Standing to one side there, with palms joined, he said: 'Is there —
244.018. any other pointed out, a second one, by the All-Seeing One,
244.019. just as I was pointed out by that Wise One through the gift of dust?' //16//

body.text:
244.020. tatra yaśo nāṃnā saṃghasthavira uvāca--asti mahārāja/
244.020. yadā bhagavataḥ parinirvāṇakālasamaye tadā apalālaṃ nāgaṃ damayitvā kumbhakālaṃ caṇḍālīgopālīṃ ca nāgaṃ mathurāmanuprāptaḥ, tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--asyāmānanda mathutāyāṃ varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya gupto nāṃnā gāndhiko bhaviṣyati/
244.023. tasya putro bhaviṣyatyupagupto nāṃnā avavādakānāmagro 'lakṣaṇako buddhaḥ, yo mama varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyati/
244.024. paśyasi tvamānanda dūrata eva nīlanīlāmbararājim? evaṃ bhadanta/
244.025. eṣa ānanda urumuṇḍo nāma parvataḥ/
244.025. atra varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya naṭabhaṭikā nāmāraṇyāyatanaṃ bhaviṣyati/
244.026. etadagraṃ me ānanda bhaviṣyati śamathānukūlānāṃ śayyāsanānām yaduta naṭabhaṭikā nāmāraṇyāyatanam/
244.027. āha ca--
244.028. avavādakānāṃ pravara upagupto mahāyaśāḥ/
244.029. vyākṛto lokanāthena buddhakāryaṃ kariṣyati//17//
body.translated_text:
244.020. There the <s>Saṃgha</s>-elder named <s>Yaśas</s> said: 'There is, O great king.
244.020. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> was approaching the time of his <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, having tamed the <s>Nāga</s> <s>Apalāla</s>, <s>Kumbhakāla</s>, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, and <s>Gopālī</s>, he arrived at <s>Mathurā</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "In this <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a perfumer named <s>Gupta</s>.
244.023. His son will be <s>Upagupta</s>, foremost among instructors, a <s>Buddha</s> without the marks, who will carry out the <s>Buddha's</s> work a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.
244.024. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, from a distance, that dark blue line of forest?" "Yes, Venerable Sir."
244.025. "This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the mountain called <s>Urumuṇḍa</s>.
244.025. There, a hundred years after the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there will be a forest hermitage called <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.
244.026. This, <s>Ānanda</s>, will be the foremost of my lodgings conducive to tranquility — namely, the forest hermitage called <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>."
244.027. And he said:
244.028. '<s>Upagupta</s>, the foremost among instructors, of great renown,
244.029. was prophesied by the Protector of the World to carry out the <s>Buddha's</s> work.' //17//

body.text:
224.030. rājā āha--kiṃ punaḥ sa śuddhasattva utpannaḥ, athādyāpi notpadyata iti? sthavira uvāca--utpannaḥ sa mahātmā/
244.031. urumuṇḍe parvate jitakleśo 'rhadgaṇaiḥ parivṛtastiṣṭhati lokānukampārtham/
244.032. api ca deva--
body.translated_text:
244.030. The king said: 'Has that pure being already been born, or has he not yet been born?' The elder said: 'That great being has been born.
244.031. On <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain, having conquered the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he abides surrounded by hosts of <s>Arhats</s> for the benefit of the world.
244.032. Moreover, Your Majesty:'

body.text:
245.001. <245>sarvajñalīlo hi sa śuddhasattvo dharmaṃ praṇītaṃ vadate gaṇāgre/
245.003. devāsurendroragamānuṣāṃśca sahasraśo mokṣapuraṃ praṇetā//18//
body.translated_text:
245.001. 'That pure being, possessing the grace of the Omniscient One, teaches the excellent <s>Dharma</s> before the assembly,
245.003. and leads by the thousands gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Indras</s>, <s>Uragas</s> (serpents), and humans to the city of liberation.' //18//

body.text:
245.005. tena khalu samayena āyuṣmānupagupto 'ṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ parivṛto naṭabhaṭikāraṇyāyatane prativasati/
245.006. śrutvā ca rājā amātyagaṇānāhūya kathayati--
245.007. saṃnāhyatāṃ hastirathāśvakāyaḥ śīghraṃ prayāsyāmyurumuṇḍaśailam/
245.009. drakṣyāmi sarvāśravavipramuktaṃ sākṣādarhantaṃ hyupaguptaṃ nāma//19//
body.translated_text:
245.005. At that time, the Venerable <s>Upagupta</s>, surrounded by eighteen thousand <s>Arhats</s>, was dwelling in the forest hermitage of <s>Naṭabhaṭikā</s>.
245.006. Having heard this, the king, summoning his retinue of ministers, said:
245.007. 'Let the army of elephants, chariots, and horses be prepared! I shall set out swiftly for <s>Urumuṇḍa</s> mountain.
245.009. I shall see face to face the <s>Arhat</s> named <s>Upagupta</s>, freed from all the outflows.' //19//

body.text:
245.011. tato 'mātyairabhihitah--deva dūtaḥ preṣayitavyo viṣayanivāsī, sa devasya svayamevāgamiṣyati/
245.012. rājā āha--nāsau asmākamarhatyabhigantum, kiṃ tu vayamevārhāmastasyābhigantum/
245.013. api ca--
245.014. manye vajramayaṃ tasya dehaṃ śailopamādhikam/
245.015. śāstṛtulyopaguptasya yo hyājñāmākṣipennaraḥ//20//
body.translated_text:
245.011. Then the ministers said: 'Your Majesty, a messenger should be sent, one who resides in the territory; he himself will come to the lord.'
245.012. The king said: 'He does not deserve that we summon him to us; rather, we ourselves deserve to go to him.
245.013. Moreover:
245.014. I consider his body to be made of diamond, harder than a mountain.
245.015. For whoever would disregard the command of <s>Upagupta</s>, who is equal to the Teacher —' //20//

body.text:
245.016. yāvadrājñā sthaviropaguptasya sakāśaṃ dūto na preṣitaḥ sthaviradarśanāyāgamiṣyāmīti/
245.017. sthaviropaguptaścintayati--yadi rājā āgamiṣyati, mahājanakāyasya pīḍā bhaviṣyati gocarasya ca/
245.018. tataḥ sthavireṇābhihitam--svayamevābhigamiṣyāmīti/
245.018. tato rājñā sthaviropaguptasyārthe nauyānenāgamiṣyatīti yāvacca mathurām yāvacca pāṭaliputramantarānnausaṃkramo 'vasthāpitaḥ/
245.019. atha sthaviropagupto rājño 'śokasyānugrahārthamaṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasraiḥ parivṛto nāvamabhiruhya pāṭaliputramanuprāptaḥ/
245.021. tato rājapuruṣai rājño 'śokasya niveditam--deva, diṣṭyā vardhasva/
245.022. anugrahārthaṃ tava sopaguptaścitteśvaraḥ śāsanakarṇadhāraḥ/
245.024. puraskṛtastīrṇabhavaughapāraiḥ sārdhaṃ samabhyāgata eṣa padmyām//21//
body.translated_text:
245.016. Then the king sent a messenger to the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, saying: 'I shall come to see the Elder.'
245.017. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> reflected: 'If the king comes, there will be disturbance to the great multitude and to the alms-gathering.'
245.018. Then the Elder declared: 'I shall go to him myself.'
245.018. Then the king, for the sake of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s journey — since he would come by boat — established a chain of ferry-stations between <s>Mathurā</s> and <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
245.019. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, for the benefit of King <s>Aśoka</s>, surrounded by eighteen thousand <s>Arhats</s>, boarded a boat and arrived at <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
245.021. Then the king's men informed King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'Sire, may you prosper!
245.022. For your benefit, <s>Upagupta</s> the master of minds, the helmsman of the teaching,
245.024. accompanied by those who have crossed beyond the flood of existence, has come by river-boat.' //21//

body.text:
245.026. śrutvā ca rājñā prītamanasā śatasahasramūlyo muktāhāraḥ svaśarīrādapanīya priyākhyāyino dattaḥ/
245.027. ghāṇṭikaṃ cāhūya kathayati--ghuṣyantāṃ pāṭaliputre ghaṇṭāḥ/
245.027. sthaviropaguptasyāgamanaṃ nivedyatām/
245.028. vaktavyam--
245.029. utsṛjya dāridryamanarthamūlam yaḥ sphītaśobhāṃ śriyamicchatīha/
245.031. svargāpavargāya ca hetubhūtaṃ sa paśyatāṃ kāruṇikopaguptam//22//
body.translated_text:
245.026. Having heard this, the king, with a delighted mind, removed from his own body a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand and gave it to the bearer of the glad tidings.
245.027. He summoned the bell-ringer and said: 'Let bells be rung throughout <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
245.027. Let the arrival of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> be announced.
245.028. Say:
245.029. He who wishes to cast off poverty, the root of misfortune, and desires resplendent prosperity here,
245.031. as well as a cause for heaven and liberation — let him behold the compassionate <s>Upagupta</s>!' //22//

body.text:
246.001. <246>yebhir na dṛṣṭo dvipadapradhānaḥ śāstā mahākāruṇikaḥ svayambhūḥ/
246.003. te śāstṛkalpaṃ sthaviropaguptaṃ paśyantyudāraṃ tribhavapradīpam//23//
body.translated_text:
246.001. 'Those who have not seen the foremost among bipeds, the Teacher, the Great Compassionate One, the Self-Born —
246.003. let them behold the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, like unto the Teacher, the illustrious lamp of the three worlds!' //23//

body.text:
246.005. yāvadrājñā pāṭalipurre ghaṇṭāṃ ghoṣayitvā nagaraśobhāṃ ca kārayitvā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanāni gatvā sarvavādyena sarvapuṣpagandhamālyena sarvapauraiḥ sarvāmātyaiḥ saha sthaviropaguptaṃ pratyudgataḥ/
246.007. dadarśa rājā sthaviropaguptaṃ dūrata evāṣṭādaśabhirarhatsahasrairardhacandreṇopaguptam/
246.008. yadantaraṃ ca rājā sthaviropaguptamadrākṣīt, tadantaraṃ hastiskandhādavatīrya padmyāṃ nadītīramabhigamya ekaṃ pādaṃ nadītīre sthāpya dvitīyaṃ nauphalake sthaviropaguptaṃ sarvāṅgenānuparigṛhya nau{saṃkramād} uttāritavān/
246.010. uttārya ca mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇopaguptasya pādayor nipatito mukhatuṇḍakena ca pādau anuparimārjya utthāya dvau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivītale nikṣipya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthaviropaguptaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca--
246.013. yadā mayā śatrugaṇānnihatya prāptā samudrābharaṇā saśailā/
246.015. ekātapatrā pṛthivī tadā me prītir na sā yā sthaviraṃ nirīkṣya//24//
body.translated_text:
246.005. Then the king, having had bells rung throughout <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> and the city adorned, traveled two and a half <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) and went out to meet the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> with all musicians, all flowers, perfumes, and garlands, all citizens, and all ministers.
246.007. The king beheld the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> from afar, encircled in a crescent formation by eighteen thousand <s>Arhats</s>.
246.008. The moment the king caught sight of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, he dismounted from the back of his elephant, came to the riverbank by the river-boat, planted one foot on the riverbank and the other on the deck of the boat, embraced the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> with his whole body, and brought him across from the ferry.
246.010. Having brought him across, like a tree cut at the root, he fell at <s>Upagupta</s>'s feet with his whole body, and with the tip of his mouth kissed his feet. Then rising, he placed both knees upon the ground, joined his palms, and gazing at the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, said:
246.013. 'When, having slain the hosts of enemies, I obtained the earth adorned with oceans and mountains,
246.015. under a single parasol — even that joy of mine was not equal to the joy of beholding the Elder.' //24//

body.text:
246.017. tvadvarśanānme dviguṇaḥ prasādaḥ saṃjāyate 'smin varaśāsanāgre/
246.019. tvadvarśanāccaiva pare 'pi śuddhyā dṛṣṭo mayādyāpratimaḥ svayambhūḥ//25//
body.translated_text:
246.017. 'At your sight, twofold faith arises in me toward this supreme and excellent teaching.
246.019. And through the purity of seeing you, I have today beheld the incomparable Self-Born One.' //25//

body.text:
246.021. api ca/
246.022. śāntiṃ gate kāruṇike jinendre tvaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kuruṣe triloke/
246.024. naṣṭe jaganmohanimīlitākṣe tvamarkavajjñānavabhāsakartā//26//
body.translated_text:
246.021. Moreover:
246.022. 'When the compassionate Lord of Conquerors attained peace, you carry out the <s>Buddha</s>'s work in the three worlds.
246.024. When the world is lost, its eyes closed by delusion, you, like the sun, illuminate it with the light of knowledge.' //26//

body.text:
246.026. tvaṃ śāstṛkalpo jagadekacakṣuravavādakānāṃ pravaraḥ śaraṇyam/
246.028. vibho mamājñāṃ vada śīghramadya kartāsmi vākyaṃ śuddhasattvā//27//
body.translated_text:
246.026. 'You are like the Teacher, the single eye of the world, the foremost of instructors, the refuge.
246.028. O powerful one, command me quickly today — I, whose nature is pure, shall carry out your word.' //27//

body.text:
247.001. <247>atha sthaviropagupto dakṣiṇena pāṇinā rājānaṃ śirasi parimārjayannuvāca--
247.002. apramādena saṃpādya rājyaiśvaryaṃ pravartatām/
247.003. durlabhaṃ trīṇi ratnāni nityaṃ pūjaya pārthiva//28//
body.translated_text:
247.001. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, stroking the king's head with his right hand, said:
247.002. 'Having accomplished the task with diligence, let royal sovereignty continue.
247.003. Rare are the Three Jewels — always worship them, O King!' //28//

body.text:
247.004. api ca mahārāja tena tena bhagavatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksambuddhena tava ca mama {ca} śāsanamupanyastaṃ sattvasārathivareṇa gaṇamadhye parīttaṃ paripālyam yatnato 'smābhiḥ/
247.005. rājā āha--sthavira, yathā ahaṃ nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā, tadevānuṣṭhīyate/
247.006. kṛtah?
247.007. stūpairvicitrairgiriśṛṅgakalpaiśchatradhvajaiścocchritaratnacitraiḥ/
247.009. saṃśobhitā me pṛthivī samantādvaistārikā dhātudharāḥ kṛtāśca//29//
body.translated_text:
247.004. 'Moreover, Great King, by that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, the supreme charioteer of beings, this teaching has been entrusted to both you and me — limited in its assembly, it must be carefully guarded by us.'
247.005. The king said: 'Elder, as I have been designated by the Blessed One, so I am carrying out that very charge.
247.006. What has been done?
247.007. With variegated <s>stūpas</s> resembling mountain peaks, with raised parasols, banners, and jewel-adorned pinnacles,
247.009. the earth has been beautified by me on all sides, and relic-bearing monuments have been erected throughout.' //29//

body.text:
247.011. api ca/
247.012. ātmā putraṃ gṛhaṃ dārān pṛthivī kośameva ca/
247.013. na kiṃcidaparityaktaṃ dharmarājasya śāsane//30//
body.translated_text:
247.011. Moreover:
247.012. 'Self, son, house, wife, the earth, and the treasury itself —
247.013. there is nothing that has not been given up for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>-King.' //30//

body.text:
247.014. sthaviropagupta āha--sādhu sādhu mahārāja, etadevānuṣṭheyam/
247.014. kṛtah?
247.015. ye sāramupajīvanti kāyādbhogaiśca jīvikām/
247.016. gate kāle na śocanti iṣṭam yānti surālayam//31//
body.translated_text:
247.014. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'Well done, well done, Great King! This is exactly what should be done.
247.014. What has been done?
247.015. Those who, while alive, enjoy the essence from their body and livelihood through their possessions —
247.016. when the time comes, they do not grieve; they go to the beloved abode of the gods.' //31//

body.text:
247.017. yāvadrājā mahatā śrīsamudayena sthaviropaguptaṃ rājakule praveśayitvā sarvāṅgenānuparigṛhya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayāmāsa/
247.018. sthaviropaguptasya śarīraṃ mṛdu sumṛdu, tadyathā tūlapicurvā karpāsapicurvā/
247.019. atha rājā sthaviropaguptasya śarīrasaṃsparśamavagamya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
247.020. mṛdūni te 'ṅgāni udārasattvā tūlopamāḥ kāśisamopamāśca/
247.022. ahaṃ tvadhanyaḥ kharakarkaśāṅgo niḥsparśagātraḥ paruṣāśrayaśca//32//
body.translated_text:
247.017. Then the king, with great pomp and splendor, led the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> into the royal palace, embraced him with his whole body, and seated him on a prepared seat.
247.018. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s body was soft, exceedingly soft — like a ball of cotton or a ball of kapok.
247.019. Then the king, perceiving the softness of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>'s body, said with palms joined:
247.020. 'Your limbs are soft, O noble being, like cotton, comparable to <s>Kāśī</s> silk.
247.022. But I am unfortunate — rough, coarse of body, without pleasing touch, of a harsh constitution.' //32//

body.text:
247.024. sthavira uvāca--
247.025. dānaṃ manāpaṃ suśubhaṃ praṇītaṃ dattaṃ mayā hyapratipudgalasya/
247.027. na pāṃśudānaṃ hi mayā pradattam yathā tvayādāyi tathāgatasya//33//
body.translated_text:
247.024. The Elder said:
247.025. 'A gift that was pleasing, beautiful, and excellent was given by me to the Incomparable One —
247.027. yet it was not a gift of dirt that I gave, as you gave to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' //33//

body.text:
247.029. rājā āha--sthavira,
247.030. bālabhāvādahaṃ pūrvaṃ kṣetraṃ prāpya hyanuttaram/
247.031. pāṃśūn ropitavāṃstatra phalam yasyedṛśaṃ mama//34//
body.translated_text:
247.029. The king said: 'Elder,
247.030. in my childish state of old, having encountered that unsurpassed field,
247.031. I sowed dirt therein — the fruit of which is such as this for me.' //34//

body.text:
248.001. <248>atha sthaviro rājānaṃ saṃharṣayannuvāca--mahārāja,
248.002. paśya kṣetrasya mahātmayaṃ pāṃśuryatra viruhyate/
248.003. rājaśrīryena te prāptā ādhipatyamanuttaram//35//
body.translated_text:
248.001. Then the Elder, delighting the king, said: 'Great King,
248.002. behold the greatness of the field in which even dirt takes root —
248.003. by which royal splendor and unsurpassed sovereignty have been obtained by you.' //35//

body.text:
248.004. śrutvā ca rājā vismayotkullanetro 'mātyānāhūyovāca--
248.005. balacakravartirājyaṃ prāptaṃ me pāṃśudānamātreṇa/
248.006. kena bhagavān bhavanto nārcayitavyaḥ prayatnena//36//
body.translated_text:
248.004. Having heard this, the king, his eyes wide with wonder, summoned his ministers and said:
248.005. 'The sovereignty of a lesser universal monarch was obtained by me merely through a gift of dirt.
248.006. For what reason, then, should the Blessed One not be worshipped with effort by all of you?' //36//

body.text:
248.007. atha rājā sthaviropaguptasya pādayor nipatyovāca--sthavira, ayaṃ me manoratho ye bhagavatā buddhena pradeśā adhyuṣitāstānarceyam, cihnāni ca kuryāṃ paścimasyāṃ janatāyāmanugrahārtham/
248.009. āha ca--ye buddhena bhagavatā pradeśā adhyuṣitāḥ, tānarcayannahaṃ gatvā cihnāni caiva kuryāṃ paścimāṃ janatāmanukampārtham/
248.010. sthavira uvāca--sādhu sādhu mahārāja, śobhanaste cittotpādaḥ/
248.011. ahaṃ pradarśayiṣyāmyadhunā/
248.012. ye tenādhyuṣitā deśāstānnamasye kṛtāñjaliḥ/
248.013. gatvā cihnāni teṣveva kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ//37//
body.translated_text:
248.007. Then the king, falling at the feet of the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, said: 'Elder, this is my heart's desire — to worship the places inhabited by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, and to erect markers there for the benefit of future generations.'
248.009. He said: 'I shall go and worship the places inhabited by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, and erect markers, out of compassion for future generations.'
248.010. The Elder said: 'Well done, well done, Great King! Your aspiration is excellent.
248.011. I shall show them to you now.
248.012. The regions inhabited by him — I shall salute them with palms joined.
248.013. Going there, I shall without doubt erect markers in those very places.' //37//

body.text:
248.014. atha rājā caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya gandhamālyapuṣpamādāya sthaviropaguptasahāyaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
248.015. atha sthaviropagupto rājānamaśokaṃ sarvaprathamena lumbinīvanaṃ praveśayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhiprasāryovāca--asmin mahārāja pradeśe bhagavāñ jātaḥ/
248.016. āha ca--
248.017. idaṃ hi prathamaṃ caityaṃ buddhasyottamacakṣuṣaḥ/
248.018. jātamātreha sa muniḥ prakrāntaḥ saptapadaṃ bhuvi//38//
body.translated_text:
248.014. Then the king, having marshaled his fourfold army and taken perfumes, garlands, and flowers, set out with the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> as his companion.
248.015. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, first of all, led King <s>Aśoka</s> to the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, and extending his right hand, said: 'In this place, Great King, the Blessed One was born.'
248.016. And he said:
248.017. 'This is the first <s>caitya</s> (sacred site) of the <s>Buddha</s>, the one of supreme vision.
248.018. Immediately upon being born here, the Sage took seven steps upon the earth.' //38//

body.text:
248.019. caturdiśamabalokya vācaṃ bhāṣitavān purā/
248.020. iyaṃ me paścimā jātirgarbhāvāsaśca paścimaḥ//39//
body.translated_text:
248.019. 'Having surveyed the four directions, he spoke these words of old:
248.020. "This is my last birth, and this is my last dwelling in a womb."' //39//

body.text:
248.021. atha rājā sarvaśarīreṇa tatra pādayor nipatya utthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ prarudannuvāca--
248.022. dhanyāste kṛtapuṇyai(ṇyā)śca yairdṛṣṭaḥ sa mahāmuniḥ/
248.023. prajātaḥ saṃśrutā yaiśca vācastasya manoramāḥ//40//
body.translated_text:
248.021. Then the king, falling there at the Elder's feet with his whole body, rising, and with palms joined, weeping, said:
248.022. 'Fortunate and meritorious are those by whom that Great Sage was seen,
248.023. by whom his birth was witnessed, and by whom his delightful words were heard!' //40//

body.text:
248.024. atha sthaviro rājñaḥ prasādavṛddhyarthamuvāca--mahārāja, kiṃ drakṣyasi tāṃ devatām?
248.025. yayā dṛṣṭaḥ prajāyansa vane 'smin vadatāṃ varaḥ/
248.026. tramamāṇaḥ padān sapta śrutā vāco yayā muneḥ//41//
body.translated_text:
248.024. Then the Elder, to increase the king's faith, said: 'Great King, would you like to see that deity?
248.025. By whom was seen the Best of Speakers being born in this grove,
248.026. taking his seven trembling steps, and by whom were the Sage's words heard?' //41//

body.text:
248.027. rājā āha--paraṃ sthavira drakṣyāmi/
248.027. atha sthaviropagupto yasya vṛkṣasya śākhamavalambya devī mahāmāyā prasūtā, tena dakṣiṇahastamabhiprasāryovāca--
248.029. naivāsikā yā ihāśokavṛkṣe saṃbuddhadarśinī yā devakanyā/
248.031. sākṣādasau darśayatu svadehaṃ rājño hyaśokasya {manah}prasādavṛddhyai//42//
body.translated_text:
248.027. The king said: 'I would very much like to see her, Elder.'
248.027. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, extending his right hand toward the branch of the tree on which Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s> had leaned while giving birth, said:
248.029. 'The tree-deity who dwells here by this <s>Aśoka</s> tree, who witnessed the Perfectly Awakened One —
248.031. let her show her own form, for the increase of faith in King <s>Aśoka</s>!' //42//

body.text:
249.001. <249>yāvat sā devatā svarūpeṇa sthaviropaguptasamīpe sthitvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca--sthavira, kimājñāpayasi? atha sthaviro rājānāmaśokamuvāca--mahārāja, iyaṃ sā devatā, yayā dṛṣṭo bhagavāñ jāyamānaḥ/
249.003. atha rājā kṛtāñjalistāṃ devatāmuvāca--
249.004. dṛṣṭastvayā lakṣaṇabhūṣitāṅgaḥ prajāyamānaḥ kamalāyatākṣaḥ/
249.006. śrutvāstvayā tasya nararṣabhasya vāco manojñāḥ prathamā vane 'smin//43//
body.translated_text:
249.001. Then that deity, standing in her own form near the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, said with palms joined: 'Elder, what do you command?' Then the Elder said to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'Great King, this is that deity by whom the Blessed One was seen at the moment of his birth.'
249.003. Then the king, with palms joined, said to that deity:
249.004. 'You saw him, his limbs adorned with the marks, being born, the Lotus-Eyed One.
249.006. You heard the delightful first words of that Bull among Men in this grove.' //43//

body.text:
249.008. devatā prāha--mayā hi dṛṣṭaḥ kanakāvadātaḥ prajāyamāno dvipadapradhānaḥ/
249.011. padāni sapta kramāṇa eva śrutā ca vācamapi tasya śāstuḥ//44//
body.translated_text:
249.008. The deity said: 'I saw him being born, the foremost among bipeds, radiant as gold.
249.011. Taking his seven steps, I also heard the words of that Teacher.' //44//

body.text:
249.013. rājā āha--kathaya devate, kīdṛśī bhagavato jāyamānasya śrīrbabhūveti/
249.013. devatā prāha--na śakyaṃ mayā vāgbhiḥ saṃprakāśayitum/
249.014. api tu saṃkṣepataḥ śṛṇu--
249.015. vinirmitābhā kanakāvadātā sendre triloke nayanābhirāmā/
249.017. sasāgarāntā ca mahī saśailā mahārṇavasthā iva nauścāla//45//
body.translated_text:
249.013. The king said: 'Tell me, O deity, what was the splendor of the Blessed One at the moment of his birth?'
249.013. The deity said: 'I am not able to convey it in words.
249.014. But hear in brief:
249.015. His radiance, like that of a magical creation, was golden-white and beautiful to behold in the three worlds including <s>Indra</s>.
249.017. And the earth, with its oceans and mountains, shook like a ship on the great sea.' //45//

body.text:
249.019. yāvadrājñā jātyāṃ śatasahasraṃ dattam/
249.019. caityaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya rājā prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
249.019. Then the king gave a hundred thousand coins at the birthplace.
249.019. Having erected a <s>caitya</s> (sacred monument), the king departed.

body.text:
249.020. atha sthaviropagupto rājānaṃ kapilavastu nivedayitvā dakṣiṇahastamabhiprasāryovāca--asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyopanāmitaḥ/
249.021. taṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇālaṃkṛtaśarīramasecanakadarśanaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā rājā sarvaśarīreṇa bodhisattvasya pādayor nipatitaḥ/
249.023. idaṃ mahārāja śākyavardhaṃ nāma devakulam/
249.023. atra bodhisattvo jātamātra upanīto devamarcayiṣyatīti/
249.024. sarvadevatāśca bodhisattvasya pādayor nipatitāḥ/
249.024. tato rājñā śuddhodanena bodhisattvo devatānāmapyayaṃ deva iti tena bodhisattvasya devātideva iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam/
249.025. asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo brāhmaṇānāṃ naimittikānāṃ vipaścikānāmupadarśitaḥ/
249.026. asmin pradeśe asitena ṛṣiṇā nirdiṣṭo buddho loke bhaviṣyatīti/
249.027. asmin pradeśe mahārāja mahāprajāpatyā saṃvardhitaḥ/
249.028. asmin pradeśe lipijñānaṃ śikṣāpitaḥ/
249.028. asmin pradeśe hastigrīvāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe śaradhanurgrahe tomaragrahe 'ṅkuśagrahe kulānurūpāsu vidyāsu pāragaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
249.030. iyaṃ bodhisattvasya vyāyāmaśālā babhūva/
249.030. asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvo devatāśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ ṣaṣṭibhiḥ strīsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ ratimanubhūtavān/
249.031. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo jīrṇāturamṛtasaṃdarśanodvigno vanaṃ saṃśritaḥ/
249.032. asmin pradeśe jambucchāyāyāṃ niṣadya viviktam <250>pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhamanāśravasadṛśaṃ prathamadhyānaṃ samāpannaḥ/
body.translated_text:
249.020. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having led the king to <s>Kapilavastu</s>, extended his right hand and said: 'In this place, Great King, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was presented to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.
249.021. Seeing his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man and his irresistibly beautiful appearance, the king fell at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet with his entire body.
249.023. This, Great King, is the temple called <s>Śākyavardhana</s>.
249.023. Here the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just after birth, was brought to worship the deity.
249.024. And all the deities fell at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet.
249.024. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, because even the deities called the <s>Bodhisattva</s> a god, gave the <s>Bodhisattva</s> the name <s>Devātideva</s> ('God above the Gods').
249.025. In this place, Great King, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was shown to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> soothsayers and diviners.
249.026. In this place, the sage <s>Asita</s> declared: "He will become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world."
249.027. In this place, Great King, he was raised by <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>.
249.028. In this place, he was taught the art of writing.
249.028. In this place, he became accomplished in skills befitting his lineage — riding on elephant-necks, on horseback, in chariots, in handling arrows, bows, lances, and goads.
249.030. This was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exercise hall.
249.030. In this place, Great King, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of deities, enjoyed pleasure together with sixty thousand women.
249.031. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, distressed by seeing old age, sickness, and death, retired to the forest.
249.032. In this place, seated in the shade of a <s>jambu</s> (rose-apple) tree, secluded <250> from unwholesome, unskillful states, he attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), accompanied by directed thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, accompanied by joy and happiness, resembling the influx-free state.

body.text:
250.002. atha pariṇate madhyāhne atikrānte bhaktakālasamaye bhaktakālasamaye anyeṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ chāyā prācīnaniṃnā prācīnapravaṇā prācīnaprāgbhārā, jamucchāyā bodhisattvasya kāyaṃ na jahāti/
250.003. dṛṣṭvā ca punā rājā śuddhodanaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa bodhisattvasya pādayor nipatitaḥ/
250.004. anena dvāreṇa bodhisattvo devatāśatasahasraiḥ parivṛto 'rdharāteḥ kapilavastuno nirgataḥ/
250.005. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena cchandakasyāśvamābharaṇāni ca datvā pratinivartitaḥ/
250.006. āha ca--
250.007. chandābharaṇānyaśvaṃ ca asmin pratinivartitaḥ/
250.008. nirupasthāyiko vīraḥ praviṣṭhaikastapovanam//46//
body.translated_text:
250.002. Then, as midday passed and the meal-time had gone by, the shadows of other trees stretched to the east, inclining, sloping, and leaning eastward, but the shade of the <s>jambu</s> tree did not leave the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body.
250.003. Seeing this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> again fell at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet with his entire body.
250.004. By this gate, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of deities, departed from <s>Kapilavastu</s> at midnight.
250.005. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> gave <s>Chandaka</s> his horse and ornaments and sent him back.
250.006. And he said:
250.007. '<s>Chandaka</s>, the ornaments, and the horse were sent back at this place;
250.008. the hero, without an attendant, entered the ascetic grove alone.' //46//

body.text:
250.009. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo lubdhakasakāśāt kāśikairvastraiḥ kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi grahāya pravrajitaḥ/
250.010. asmin pradeśe bhārgaveṇāśrameṇopanimantritaḥ/
250.010. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvo rājñā bimbisāreṇārgharājyenopanimantritaḥ/
250.011. asmin pradeśe ārāḍodrakamabhigataḥ/
250.011. āha ca--
250.012. udrakārāḍakā nāma ṛṣayo 'smiṃstapovane/
250.013. adhigatācāryasattvena puruṣendreṇa tāpitā//47//
body.translated_text:
250.009. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtained ochre-colored robes from a hunter in exchange for his <s>Kāśī</s> garments and went forth.
250.010. In this place, he was welcomed by <s>Bhārgava</s>'s hermitage.
250.010. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was invited by King <s>Bimbisāra</s> with the offer of half his kingdom.
250.011. In this place, he approached <s>Ārāḍa</s> and <s>Udraka</s>.
250.011. And he said:
250.012. 'The sages <s>Udraka</s> and <s>Ārāḍa</s> in this ascetic grove,
250.013. were approached by the lord of beings, the Bull of Men, and put to shame.' //47//

body.text:
250.014. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena ṣaḍvarṣāṇi duṣkaraṃ cīrṇam/
250.014. āha ca--
250.015. ṣaḍvarṣāṇi hi kaṭukaṃ tapastaptvā mahāmuniḥ/
250.016. nāyaṃ mārgo hyabhijñāya iti jñātvā samutsṛjet//48//
body.translated_text:
250.014. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practiced severe austerities for six years.
250.014. And he said:
250.015. 'Having performed bitter austerities for six years, the Great Sage,
250.016. knowing "This is not the path," abandoned them.' //48//

body.text:
250.017. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvena nandāyā nandabalāyāśca grāmikaduhitryoḥ sakāśāt ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ madhupāyasaṃ parimuktam/
250.018. āha ca--
250.019. asmin pradeśe nandāyā bhuktvā ca madhupāyasam/
250.020. bodhimūlaṃ mahāvīro jagāma vadatāṃ varaḥ//49//
body.translated_text:
250.017. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> received a sixteen-fold sweetened milk-rice from the village-girls <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>.
250.018. And he said:
250.019. 'In this place, having eaten the sweetened milk-rice of <s>Nandā</s>,
250.020. the great hero, the best of speakers, went to the Bodhi-tree.' //49//

body.text:
250.021. asmin pradeśe bodhisattvaḥ kālikena nāgarājena bodhisamūlamabhigacchan saṃstutaḥ/
250.022. āha ca--
250.023. kālikabhujagendreṇa saṃstuto vadatāṃ varaḥ/
250.024. prayāto 'nena mārgeṇa bodhimaṇḍe 'mṛtārthinaḥ//50//
body.translated_text:
250.021. In this place, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, going toward the root of the Bodhi-tree, was praised by the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Kālika</s>.
250.022. And he said:
250.023. 'Praised by the serpent-lord <s>Kālika</s>, the best of speakers,
250.024. went by this path to the Bodhi-throne, seeking the deathless.' //50//

body.text:
250.025. atha rājā sthavirasya pādayor nipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
250.026. api paśyema nāgendram yena dṛṣṭastathāgataḥ/
250.027. vrajāno 'nena mārgeṇa mattanāgendravikramaḥ//51//
body.translated_text:
250.025. Then the king fell at the Elder's feet and, with palms joined, said:
250.026. 'Might we see the serpent-lord by whom the <s>Tathāgata</s> was seen,
250.027. striding along this path with the gait of a majestic elephant-lord?' //51//

body.text:
250.028. atha kāliko nāgarājaḥ sthavirasamīpe sthitvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca--sthavira, kimājñāpayasīti/
250.029. atha sthaviro rājānamuvāca--ayaṃ sa mahārāja kāliko nāgarājā yena bhagavānanena mārgeṇa bodhimūlaṃ nirgacchan saṃstutaḥ/
250.030. atha rājā kṛtāñjaliḥ kālikaṃ nāgarājamuvāca--
body.translated_text:
250.028. Then the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Kālika</s>, standing near the Elder, said with joined palms: 'Elder, what do you command?'
250.029. Then the Elder said to the king: 'This, Great King, is that <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Kālika</s> by whom the Blessed One was praised as he went along this path to the root of the Bodhi-tree.'
250.030. Then the king, with joined palms, said to the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Kālika</s>:

body.text:
251.001. <251>dṛṣṭastvā jvalitakāñcanatulyavarṇaḥ śāstā mamāpratisamaḥ śaradenduvaktraḥ/
251.003. ākhyāhi me daśabalasya guṇaikadeśaṃ tatkīdṛśī vada bhavan sugate tadānīm//52//
body.translated_text:
251.001. <251>'You saw the Teacher, whose complexion was like blazing gold, incomparable, with a face like the autumn moon;
251.003. tell me even a fraction of the virtues of the Possessor of Ten Powers — tell me, sir, what was it like for you in the presence of the Well-Gone One at that time?' //52//

body.text:
251.005. kālika uvāca--na śakyaṃ vigbhiḥ saṃprakāśayitum/
251.005. api tu saṃkṣepaṃ śṛṇu--
251.006. caraṇatalaparāhatā saśailā avanistadā pracacāla ṣaṭvikāram/
251.008. ravikiraṇaprabhādhikā nṛloke sugataśaśidyutisaṃnibhā manojñā//53//
body.translated_text:
251.005. <s>Kālika</s> said: 'It cannot be fully expressed in words.
251.005. But hear in brief:
251.006. The earth with its mountains trembled with a sixfold quaking, struck by his footsteps;
251.008. the radiance of the Well-Gone One in the human world was like the moon-light, surpassing the rays of the sun, and delightful.' //53//

body.text:
251.010. yāvadrājā caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya prakrāntaḥ/
251.010. atha sthaviropagupto rājānaṃ bodhimūlamupanāmayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karamabhiprasāryovāca--asmin pradeśe mahārāja bodhisattvena mahāmaitrīsahāyena sakalaṃ mārabalaṃ jitvā anuttarā samyaksambodhirabhisambuddhā/
251.012. āha ca--
251.013. iha munivṛṣabheṇa bodhimūle namucibalaṃ vikṛtaṃ nirastamāśu/
251.015. idamamṛtamudāramagryabodhiṃ hyadhigatamapratipudgalena tena//54//
body.translated_text:
251.010. The king established a <s>caitya</s> and departed.
251.010. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, having led the king to the root of the Bodhi-tree, extended his right hand and said: 'In this place, Great King, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, accompanied by great loving-kindness, having conquered the entire army of <s>Māra</s>, awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening.'
251.012. And he said:
251.013. 'Here, at the root of the Bodhi-tree, by the Bull of Sages, the deformed army of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Māra</s>) was swiftly repelled;
251.015. this deathless, noble, supreme awakening was attained by that unequaled one.' //54//

body.text:
251.017. yāvadrājñā bodhau śatasahasraṃ dattam/
251.017. caityaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya rājā prakrāntaḥ/
251.017. atha sthaviropagupto rājānamaśokamuvāca--asmin pradeśe bhagavāṃś caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sakāśāccatvāri śailamayāni pātrāṇi grahāyaikaṃ pātramadhimuktam/
251.019. asmin pradeśe trapuṣabhillikayorvaṇijorapi piṇḍapātraḥ pratigṛhītaḥ/
251.020. asmin pradeśe bhagavān vāraṇasīmabhigacchannupagenājīvikena saṃstutaḥ/
