251.021. yāvat sthaviro rājānam ṛṣivadana(patana?)mupanīya dakṣiṇaṃ hastamabhiprasāryovāca--asmin pradeśe mahārāja bhagavatā triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dharmyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravarjitatam/
251.023. āha ca--
251.024. śubhaṃ dharmamayaṃ cakraṃ saṃsāravinivartaye/
251.025. asmin pradeśe nāthena pravarjitamanuttaram//55//
body.translated_text:
251.017. The king gave a hundred thousand at the Bodhi-tree.
251.017. Having established a <s>caitya</s>, the king departed.
251.017. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s> said to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'In this place, the Blessed One received four stone bowls from the Four Great Kings and combined them into one bowl.
251.019. In this place, the alms-bowl was accepted from the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>.
251.020. In this place, the Blessed One, going to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, was praised by the <s>Ājīvika</s> <s>Upaga</s>.
251.021. The Elder then led the king to <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> (the 'Sage's Face'), extended his right hand, and said: 'In this place, Great King, the Blessed One turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, with three turnings and twelve aspects.'
251.023. And he said:
251.024. 'The auspicious <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, for the turning back of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
251.025. was turned in this place by the Lord, the unsurpassed one.' //55//

body.text:
251.026. asmin pradeśe jaṭilasahasraṃ pravrajitam/
251.026. asmin pradeśe rājño bimbisārasya dharmaṃ deśitam/
251.027. rājñā ca bimbisāreṇa satyāni dṛṣṭāni, aśītibhiśca devatāsahasrairanekaiśca māgadhakairbrāhmaṇagṛhapatisahasraiḥ/
251.028. asmin pradeśe bhagavatā śakrasya devendrasya dharmo deśitaḥ, śakreṇa ca satyāni dṛṣṭānyaśītibhiśca devatāsahasraiḥ/
251.029. asmin pradeśe mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitam/
251.030. asmin pradeśe bhagavān deveṣu trāyastriṃśoṣu varṣā māturjanayitryā dharmam <252>deśayitvā devagaṇaparivṛto 'vatīrṇaḥ/
body.translated_text:
251.026. In this place, a thousand matted-hair ascetics were ordained.
251.026. In this place, the <s>Dharma</s> was taught to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>.
251.027. And King <s>Bimbisāra</s> saw the truths, together with eighty thousand deities and many thousands of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Magadha</s>.
251.028. In this place, the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and <s>Śakra</s> saw the truths together with eighty thousand deities.
251.029. In this place, the great miracle was displayed.
251.030. In this place, the Blessed One, having taught the <s>Dharma</s> to his mother among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods during the rains retreat, descended <252> surrounded by a host of gods.

body.text:
252.001. vistareṇa yāvat sthaviro rājānamaśokaṃ kuśinagarīmupanāmayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karatalamabhiprasāryovāca--asmin pradeśe mahārāja bhagavān sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinivṛtaḥ/
252.003. āha ca--
252.004. lokaṃ sadevamanujāsurayakṣanāgamakṣayyadharmavinaye matimān vinīya/
252.005. vaineyasattvavirahānupaśāntabuddhiḥ śāntiṃ gataḥ paramakāruṇiko maharṣiḥ//56//
body.translated_text:
252.001. In full detail, the Elder, having led King <s>Aśoka</s> to <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, extended his right palm and said: 'In this place, Great King, the Blessed One, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without residue.'
252.003. And he said:
252.004. 'Having trained the world of gods, humans, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>, the wise one, in the imperishable <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,
252.005. the great sage of supreme compassion, his mind at peace upon separation from the beings to be trained, entered into peace.' //56//

body.text:
252.008. śrutvā ca rājā mūrchitaḥ patitaḥ/
252.008. yāvajjalapariṣekaṃ kṛtvotthāpitaḥ/
252.008. atha rājā kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya parivirvāṇe śatasahasraṃ datvā caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya pādayor nipatyovāca--sthavira, ayaṃ me mano rathah--ye ca bhagavatā śrāvakā agratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ, teṣāṃ śarīrapūjāṃ kariṣyāmīti/
252.011. sthavira uvāca--sādhu sādhu mahārāja/
252.011. śobhanaste cittotpādaḥ/
252.011. sthaviro rājānamaśokaṃ jetavanaṃ praveśayitvā dakṣiṇaṃ karamabhiprasāryovāca--ayaṃ mahārāja sthaviraśāriputrasya stūpaḥ/
252.013. triyatāmasyārcanāmiti/
252.013. rājā āha--ke tasya tasya guṇā babhūvah? sthavira uvāca--sa hi dvitīyaśāstā dharmasenādhipatirdharmacakraparavartanaḥ prajñāvatāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā/
252.016. sarvalokasya yā prajñā sthāpayitvā tathāgatam/
252.017. śāriputrasya prajñāyāḥ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm//57//
body.translated_text:
252.008. Hearing this, the king fainted and fell.
252.008. He was revived by a sprinkling of water.
252.008. Then the king, having barely regained consciousness, gave a hundred thousand at the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> site, established a <s>caitya</s>, fell at the Elder's feet, and said: 'Elder, this is my heart's desire — I wish to worship the relics of those disciples whom the Blessed One designated as foremost.'
252.011. The Elder said: 'Excellent, excellent, Great King!
252.011. Noble is your aspiration.'
252.011. The Elder, having brought King <s>Aśoka</s> into the <s>Jetavana</s>, extended his right hand and said: 'This, Great King, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>.
252.013. Let worship be offered to him.'
252.013. The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'He was a second Teacher, the commander of the <s>Dharma</s>-army, one who turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel further, designated by the Blessed One as foremost among the wise.
252.016. All the wisdom in the world, setting aside the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
252.017. is not equal to a sixteenth part of the wisdom of <s>Śāriputra</s>.' //57//

body.text:
252.018. āha ca--
252.019. saddharmacakramatulam yajjinena pravartitam/
252.020. anuvṛttaṃ hi tattena śāriputreṇa dhīmatā//58//
body.translated_text:
252.018. And he said:
252.019. 'The incomparable <s>Dharma</s>-wheel which the Victor turned,
252.020. was followed and furthered by the wise <s>Śāriputra</s>.' //58//

body.text:
252.021. kastasya sādhu buddhānyaḥ puruṣaḥ śāradvatasyeha/
252.022. jñātvā guṇagaṇanidhiṃ vaktuṃ śaknoti niravaśeṣāt//59//
body.translated_text:
252.021. 'What other man besides the <s>Buddha</s> could do justice to this son of <s>Śāradvatī</s> here?
252.022. Knowing him to be a treasury of hosts of virtues, who could fully describe them?' //59//

body.text:
252.023. tato rājā prītamanāḥ sthaviraśāradvatīputrastūpe śatasahasraṃ datvā kṛtājñaliruvāca--
252.024. śāradvatīputramahaṃ bhaktyā vande vimuktabhavasaṅgam/
252.025. lokaprakāśakīrti jñānavatāmuttamaṃ vīram//60//
body.translated_text:
252.023. Then the king, with a delighted mind, gave a hundred thousand at the <s>stūpa</s> of the son of <s>Śāradvatī</s> and, with joined palms, said:
252.024. 'I worship with devotion the son of <s>Śāradvatī</s>, freed from the bonds of existence,
252.025. whose fame illumines the world, the supreme hero among the wise.' //60//

body.text:
252.026. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpamupadarśannuvāca--idaṃ mahārāja sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpam/
252.027. triyatāmasyārcanamiti/
252.027. rājā āha--ke tasya guṇā babhūvuriti? sthavira uvāca--sa hi ṛddhimatāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā, yena dakṣiṇena pādāṅguṣṭhena śakrasya devendrasya vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ prakampitaḥ, nandopanandau nāgarājānau vinītau/
252.030. āha ca--
body.translated_text:
252.026. Then the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said: 'This, Great King, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>.
252.027. Let worship be offered to him.'
252.027. The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The Elder said: 'He was designated by the Blessed One as foremost among those possessing supernatural powers — he who with his right big toe caused the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, to tremble, and who subdued the <s>Nāga</s>-kings <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>.'
252.030. And he said:

body.text:
253.001. <253>śakrasya yena bhavanaṃ pādāṅguṣṭhena kampitam/
253.002. pūjanīyaḥ prayatnena kolitaḥ sa dvijottam//61//
body.translated_text:
253.001. <253>'He by whom <s>Śakra</s>'s palace was shaken with his big toe —
253.002. that <s>Kaulita</s> (<s>Maudgalyāyana</s>), the supreme twice-born, is to be worshipped with effort.' //61//

body.text:
253.003. bhujageśvarau pratibhayau dāntau tau yanātidurgamau/
253.004. loke kastasya śuddhabuddheḥ pāraṃ gacchedguṇārṇavasya//62//
body.translated_text:
253.003. 'Those two fearsome lords of serpents were tamed by him, though they were extremely hard to approach.
253.004. In the world, who could reach the far shore of the ocean of virtues of that one whose mind is pure?' //62//

body.text:
253.005. yāvadrājā mahāmaudgalyāyanasya stūpe śatasahasraṃ datvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
253.006. ṛddhimatāmagro yo janmajarāśokaduḥkhanirmuktaḥ/
253.007. maudgalyāyanamahaṃ vande mūrdhnā praṇipatya vikhyātam//63//
body.translated_text:
253.005. Then the king, having given a hundred thousand at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, with palms joined, said:
253.006. 'Foremost among those of supernatural power, freed from birth, old age, grief, and suffering —
253.007. I bow my head and pay homage to the renowned <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.' //63//

body.text:
253.008. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthaviramahākāśyapasya stūpam..../
253.008. triyatāmasyārcanamiti/
253.008. rājā āha--ke tasya guṇā babhūvah? sthavira uvāca--sa hi mahātmā alpecchānāṃ saṃtuṣṭānāṃ dhutaguṇavāditāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā, ardhāsanenopanimantritaḥ, śvetacīvareṇācchāditaḥ, dīnāturagrāhakaḥ śāstanasaṃdhārakaśceti/
253.011. āha ca--
253.012. puṇyakṣetramudāraṃ cīnāturagrāhako nirāyāsaḥ/
253.013. sarvajñacīvaradharaḥ śāsanasaṃdhārako matimān//64//
body.translated_text:
253.008. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s> showed the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>...
253.008. 'Let there be worship of this one.'
253.008. The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The elder said: 'That great one was declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be foremost among those of few desires, contentment, and the practice of ascetic qualities (<s>dhūtaguṇas</s>). He was invited to share a half-seat, he was covered with a white robe, he was a helper of the destitute and afflicted, and a maintainer of the teaching.'
253.011. And he said:
253.012. 'A noble field of merit, a helper of the destitute and afflicted, free from toil;
253.013. wearing the robe of the Omniscient One, a maintainer of the teaching, possessed of wisdom.' //64//

body.text:
253.014. kastasya gurormanujo vaktuṃ śakto guṇānniravaśeṣān/
253.015. āsanavarasya sumatiryasya jano dattavānardham//65//
body.translated_text:
253.014. 'Who among humans is able to describe completely the virtues of that teacher,
253.015. the wise one to whom the supreme leader gave half of his seat?' //65//

body.text:
253.016. tato rājā aśokaḥ sthaviramahākāśyapasya stūpe datvā kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
253.017. parvataguhānilāyaṃ vairaparānmukhaṃ praśamayuktam/
253.018. saṃtoṣaguṇavivṛddhaṃ vande khalu kāśyapaṃ sthaviram//66//
body.translated_text:
253.016. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having made an offering at the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, with palms joined, said:
253.017. 'Dwelling in mountain caves, averse to hostility, endowed with tranquility,
253.018. abounding in the virtue of contentment — I bow indeed to the elder <s>Kāśyapa</s>.' //66//

body.text:
253.019. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthaviravatkulasya stūpaṃ darśayannuvāca--idaṃ mahārāja sthavirabatkulasya stūpam/
253.020. triyatāmarcanamiti/
253.020. rājā āha--ke tasya guṇā babhūvuriti? sthavira uvāca--sa mahātmā alpābādhānāmagro nirdiṣṭo bhagavatā/
253.021. api ca/
253.021. na tena kasyaciddvīpadikā gāthā śrāvatī/
253.022. rājā āha--dīyatāmatra kākaṇiḥ/
253.022. yāvadamātyairabhihitah--deva, kimarthaṃ tulyeṣvavasthiteṣvatra kākāṇī dīyata iti? rājā āha--śrūyatāmatrābhiprāyo mama--
253.024. ājñāpradīpena manogṛhasthaṃ hataṃ tamo yadyapi kṛtaṃ hi tena yathā kṛtaṃ sattvahitaṃ tadanyaiḥ//67//
body.translated_text:
253.019. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Bakkula</s>, said: 'This, O great king, is the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Bakkula</s>.
253.020. Let there be worship of him.'
253.020. The king said: 'What were his virtues?' The elder said: 'That great one was declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be foremost among those of few illnesses.
253.021. Moreover,
253.021. he never preached even a two-line verse to anyone.'
253.022. The king said: 'Let a <s>kākiṇī</s> (small copper coin) be given here.'
253.022. Then the ministers said: 'Your Majesty, why, among equals, is only a <s>kākiṇī</s> given here?' The king said: 'Listen to my reasoning here:
253.024. Though the darkness dwelling in the house of the mind was dispelled by the lamp of the teaching, the benefit done for beings by others was not done equally by him.' //67//

body.text:
253.028. sā pratyāhatā tasyaiva rājñaḥ pādamūle nipatitā/
253.028. yāvadamātyā vismitā ūcuh--aho tasya mahātmano 'lpecchatā babhūva/
253.029. anayāpyanarthī/
253.029. yāvat sthaviropaguptaḥ sthavirānandasya stūpamupadarśayannuvāca--idaṃ sthavirānandasya stūpam/
253.030. triyatāmasyārcanamiti/
253.030. rājā āha--ke tasya guṇā babhūvuriti/
253.031. sthavira uvāca--sa hi bhagavata upasthāyako babhuva, bahuśrutānāmagryaḥ pravacanagrāhakaśceti/
253.032. āha ca--
body.translated_text:
253.028. That coin, rebounding, fell back at the very feet of the king.
253.028. The ministers, astonished, said: 'Ah, how great was the contentment of that great one!
253.029. He wants nothing even from this.'
253.029. Then the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, showing the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>, said: 'This is the <s>stūpa</s> of the elder <s>Ānanda</s>.
253.030. Let there be worship of him.'
253.030. The king said: 'What were his virtues?'
253.031. The elder said: 'He was the attendant of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, foremost among the learned, and a custodian of the word.'
253.032. And he said:

body.text:
254.001. <254>munipatrarakṣaṇapaṭuḥ smṛtidhṛtimatiniścitaḥ śrutasamudraḥ/
254.002. vispaṣṭamadhuravacanaḥ suranaramahitaḥ sadānandaḥ//68//
body.translated_text:
254.001. 'Skilled in guarding the sage's bowl, possessed of mindfulness, retention, and firm resolve, an ocean of learning;
254.002. of clear and sweet speech, honored by gods and humans — always <s>Ānanda</s>.' //68//

body.text:
254.003. saṃbuddhacittakuśalaḥ sarvatra vicakṣaṇo guṇakaraṇḍaḥ/
254.004. jinasaṃstuto jitaraṇo suranaramahitaḥ sadānandaḥ//69//
body.translated_text:
254.003. 'Skilled in the mind of the Perfectly Enlightened One, discerning in all matters, a casket of virtues;
254.004. praised by the Victor, victorious in battle, honored by gods and humans — always <s>Ānanda</s>.' //69//

body.text:
254.005. yāvadrājñā tasya stūpe koṭirdattā/
254.005. yāvadamātyairabhihitah--kimarthamayaṃ deva sarveṣāṃ sakāśādadhikataraṃ pūjyate? rājā āha--śrūyatāmabhiprāyah--
254.007. yattaccharīraṃ vadatāṃ varasya dharmātmano dharmamayaṃ viśuddham/
254.009. taddhāritaṃ tena viśokanāṃnā tasmādviśeṣeṇa sa pūjanīyaḥ//70//
body.translated_text:
254.005. Then the king gave a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) at his <s>stūpa</s>.
254.005. The ministers said: 'Why, Your Majesty, is this one honored more than all the others?' The king said: 'Listen to the reasoning:
254.007. That body of the foremost among speakers, the <s>Dharma</s>-natured one — pure and made of <s>Dharma</s> —
254.009. was borne by that one named "Sorrowless" (<s>Viśoka</s>, i.e. <s>Ānanda</s>); therefore he is especially to be honored.' //70//

body.text:
254.011. dharmapradīpo jvalati prajāsu kleśāndhakārāntakaro yadadya/
254.013. tattatprabhāvātsugatendrasūnostasmādviśeṣeṇa sa pūjanīyaḥ//71//
body.translated_text:
254.011. 'That the lamp of the <s>Dharma</s> today blazes among beings, destroying the darkness of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) —
254.013. that is by the power of the son of the Lord of Sugatas; therefore he is especially to be honored.' //71//

body.text:
254.015. yadā samudraṃ salilaṃ samudre kurvīta kaścinna hi goṣpadena/
254.017. nāthena taddharmamavekṣya bhāvaṃ sūtrāntako 'yaṃ sthavire 'bhiṣiktaḥ//72//
body.translated_text:
254.015. 'Just as no one could make the water of the ocean into a cow's hoofprint —
254.017. having observed the nature of that <s>Dharma</s>, the Protector anointed this elder as the guardian of the <s>sūtrāntas</s> (discourses).' //72//

body.text:
254.019. atha rājā sthavirāṇāṃ stūpārcanaṃ kṛtvā sthaviropaguptasya pādayor nipatya prītimanā uvāca--
254.021. mānuṣyaṃ saphalīkṛtaṃ kratuśatairiṣṭena saṃprāpyate rājyaiśvaryaguṇaiścalaiśca vibhavaiḥ sāraṃ gṛhītaṃ param/
254.023. lokaṃ caityaśatairalaṃkṛtamidaṃ śvetābhrakūṭaprabhairasyādyāpratimasya śāsanamidaṃ kiṃ naḥ kṛtaṃ duṣkaram//73// iti/
254.025. yāvadrājā sthaviropaguptasya prāṇāmaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
254.019. Then the king, having performed worship at the <s>stūpas</s> of the elders, fell at the feet of the elder <s>Upagupta</s> and, with a joyful mind, said:
254.021. 'Human birth has been made fruitful; through hundreds of sacrifices performed, kingship is obtained. With the fleeting qualities of sovereignty and power, the supreme essence has been seized.
254.023. This world has been adorned with hundreds of <s>caityas</s> radiant like white cloud-peaks. For this unequaled teaching — what difficult thing have we done?' //73//
254.025. Then the king, having paid homage to the elder <s>Upagupta</s>, departed.

body.text:
254.026. yāvadrājñā aśokena jātau bodhau dharmacakre parinirvāṇe ekaikaśatasahasraṃ dattam, tasya bodhau viśeṣataḥ prasādo jātah--iha bhagavatānuttarā samyaksambodhirabhisambuddheti/
254.027. sa yāni viśeṣayuktāni ratnāni, tāni bodhiṃ preṣayati/
254.028. atha rājño 'śokasya tiṣyarakṣitā nāma agramahiṣī/
254.029. tasyā buddhirutpannā--ayaṃ rājā mayā sārdhaṃ ratimanubhavati, viśeṣayuktāṃśca(krāni ca) ratnāni bodhau preṣayati/
254.030. tayā mātaṅgī vyāharitā--śakyasi tvaṃ bodhiṃ mama sapatnīṃ praghātitum? tayābhihitam--śakṣyāmi, kiṃ tu kārṣāpaṇān dehīti/
254.031. yāvanmātaṅgyā bodhivṛkṣo mantraiḥ parijaptaḥ, sūtraṃ ca buddham/
254.032. yāvadbodhimṛkṣaḥ śuṣkitumārabdhaḥ/
254.032. tato rājapuruṣai rājñe niveditam--deva, bodhivṛkṣaḥ śuṣyata iti/
254.033. āha ca--
body.translated_text:
254.026. King <s>Aśoka</s> had given a hundred thousand each at the places of birth, enlightenment, the turning of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, and <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. He had developed a special faith in the place of enlightenment: 'It was here that the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.'
254.027. He sent his finest jewels to the <s>Bodhi</s> tree.
254.028. Now, King <s>Aśoka</s> had a chief queen named <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>.
254.029. She thought: 'This king enjoys his pleasures with me, yet sends his finest jewels to the <s>Bodhi</s> tree.'
254.030. She addressed a <s>Mātaṅgī</s> (sorceress): 'Can you destroy the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, my rival?' She said: 'I can, but give me <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins).'
254.031. Then the <s>Mātaṅgī</s>, having enchanted the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with spells, also bound a thread.
254.032. The <s>Bodhi</s> tree began to wither.
254.032. Then the king's men informed the king: 'Your Majesty, the <s>Bodhi</s> tree is withering.'
254.033. And they said:

body.text:
255.001. <255>yatropaviṣṭena tathāgatena kṛtsnaṃ jagadbuddhamidam yathāvat/
255.003. sarvajñatā cādhigatā narendra bodhidrumo 'sau nidhanaṃ prayāti//74//
body.translated_text:
255.001. 'The place where the <s>Tathāgata</s> sat and this entire world was properly awakened,
255.003. and omniscience was attained, O lord of men — that <s>Bodhi</s> tree is going to its destruction.' //74//

body.text:
255.005. śrutvā ca rājā mūrcchito bhūmau patitaḥ/
255.005. yāvajjalasekaṃ dattvotthāpitaḥ/
255.005. atha rājā kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya prarudannuvāca--
255.007. dṛṣṭvānvahaṃ taṃ drumarājamūlaṃ jānāmi dṛṣṭo 'dya mayā svayambhūḥ/
255.009. nāthadrume caiva gate praṇāśaṃ prāṇāḥ prayāsyanti mamāpi nāśam//59//
body.translated_text:
255.005. Hearing this, the king fainted and fell to the ground.
255.005. He was revived by sprinkling with water.
255.005. Then the king, somehow regaining consciousness, weeping, said:
255.007. 'Having gazed upon that base of the king of trees, I felt as though I have today seen the Self-Arisen One himself.
255.009. But if the tree of the Protector goes to destruction, my very life too will go to ruin.' //75//

body.text:
255.011. atha tiṣyarakṣitā rājānaṃ śokārtamavekṣyovāca--deva, yadi bodhir na bhaviṣyati, ahaṃ devasya ratimutpādayiṣyāmi/
255.012. rājā āha--na sā strī, api tu bodhivṛkṣaḥ saḥ/
255.012. tatra bhagavatā anuttarā samyaksambodhiradhigatā/
255.013. tiṣyarakṣitā mātaṅgīmuvāca--śakyasi tvaṃ bodhivṛkṣam yathāpaurāṇamavasthāpitum? mātaṅgī āha--yadi tāvat prāṇāntikāvaśiṣṭā bhaviṣyati, yathāpaurāṇamavasthāpayiṣyāmīti/
255.015. vistareṇa yāvatayā sūtraṃ muktvā vṛkṣasāmantena khanitvā divase kṣīrakumbhasahasreṇa pāyayati/
255.016. yāvadalpairahobhiryathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
255.016. tato rājapuruṣai rājñe niveditam--deva, diṣṭyā vardhasva, yathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
255.017. śrutvā ca prītamanā bodhivṛkṣaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca--
255.019. bimbisāraprabhṛtibhiḥ pārthivendrairdyutiṃdharaiḥ/
255.020. na kṛtaṃ tatkariṣyāmi satkāradvayamuttamam//76//
body.translated_text:
255.011. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, seeing the king afflicted with grief, said: 'Your Majesty, if the <s>Bodhi</s> tree ceases to exist, I shall produce pleasure for the lord.'
255.012. The king said: 'That is not a woman — it is the <s>Bodhi</s> tree.
255.012. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.'
255.013. <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> said to the <s>Mātaṅgī</s>: 'Can you restore the <s>Bodhi</s> tree to its former state?' The <s>Mātaṅgī</s> said: 'If it is still in a near-death but not yet dead state, I shall restore it to its former condition.'
255.015. In detail — she removed the thread, dug around the tree, and watered it daily with a thousand pots of milk.
255.016. Within a few days, it was restored to its former state.
255.016. Then the king's men informed the king: 'Your Majesty, rejoice! It has been restored to its former state.'
255.017. Hearing this, with a joyful mind, gazing at the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, he said:
255.019. 'What was not done by the lords of kings from <s>Bimbisāra</s> onward, those radiant ones —
255.020. that I shall do: the supreme twofold honor.' //76//

body.text:
255.021. bodhiṃ ca snāpayiṣyāmi kumbhairgandhodakākulaiḥ/
255.022. āryasaṃghasya ca kariṣyāmi satkāraṃ pañcavārṣikam//77//
body.translated_text:
255.021. 'I shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with pots full of fragrant water,
255.022. and I shall perform the quinquennial (<s>pañcavārṣika</s>) festival of honor for the noble <s>Saṃgha</s>.' //77//

body.text:
255.023. atha rājā sauvarṇarūpyavaiḍūryasphaṭikamayānāṃ kumbhānāṃ sahasraṃ gandhodakena pūrayitvā prabhūtaṃ cānnapānaṃ samudrānīya gandhamālyapuṣpasaṃcayaṃ kṛtvā snātvā āhatāni vāsāṃsi navāni dīrghadaśāni prāvṛtya aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatamupavāsamupoṣya dhūpakaṭacchukamādāya śaraṇatalamabhiruhya caturdiśamāyācitumārabdhah--ye bhagavato buddhasya śrāvakāste mamānugrahāyāgacchantu/
255.026. api ca--
255.027. samyaggatā ye sugatasya śiṣyāḥ śāntendriyā nirjitakāmadoṣāḥ/
255.029. saṃmānanārhā naradevapūjitā āyāntu te 'sminnanukampayā mama//78//
body.translated_text:
255.023. Then the king, having filled a thousand pots of gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and crystal with fragrant water, and having brought abundant food and drink, and having gathered perfumes, garlands, and flowers, and having bathed, and having put on fresh, new, long-fringed garments, and having observed the eightfold fast, taking an incense-ladle, ascending the terrace, he began to invite in the four directions: 'Let those who are disciples of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, come here out of kindness for me.'
255.026. Moreover:
255.027. 'Those disciples of the <s>Sugata</s> who have gone the right way, with senses at peace, who have conquered desire and hatred,
255.029. worthy of honor, worshipped by gods and humans — let them come here, out of compassion for me.' //78//

body.text:
256.001. <256>praśamadamaratā vibhuktasaṃgāḥ pravarasutāḥ sugatasya dharmarājñaḥ/
256.003. asurasuranarārcitāryavṛttāstviha madanugrahaṇātsamabhyupaintu//79//
body.translated_text:
256.001. 'Those who delight in tranquility and restraint, free from attachment, the noble sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-king,
256.003. worshipped by <s>Asuras</s>, gods, and humans, of noble conduct — let them come here for my benefit.' //79//

body.text:
256.005. vasanti kāśmīrapure suramye ye cāpi dhīrāstamasāvane 'smin/
256.007. mahāvane revatake raye 'ryā anugrahāryaṃ mama te 'bhyupeyuḥ//80//
body.translated_text:
256.005. 'Those who dwell in beautiful <s>Kāśmīra</s>, and those steadfast ones in the dark <s>Tamasa</s> forest,
256.007. those noble ones in <s>Mahāvana</s> and <s>Revataka</s> — let them come for my benefit.' //80//

body.text:
256.009. anavataptahṛde nivasanti ye girinadīṣu saparvatakandareṣu/
256.011. jinasutāḥ khalu dhyānaratāḥ sadā samudayāntviha te 'dya kṛpābalāḥ//81//
body.translated_text:
256.009. 'Those who dwell at Lake <s>Anavatapta</s>, in the mountain rivers with their caves and gorges,
256.011. the sons of the Victor, ever delighting in meditation — let them come today, impelled by compassion.' //81//

body.text:
256.013. śairīṣake ye pravare vimāne vasanti putrā vadatāṃ varasya/
256.015. anugrahārthaṃ mama te viśokā hyāyantu kāruṇyaniviṣṭabhāvāḥ//82//
body.translated_text:
256.013. 'Those who dwell in the excellent <s>Śairī��aka</s> mansion, sons of the foremost among speakers,
256.015. let those sorrowless ones come for my benefit, whose hearts are established in compassion.' //82//

body.text:
256.017. gandhamādanaśaile ca ye vasanti mahaujasaḥ/
256.018. ihāyāntu kāruṇyamutpādyopanimantritāḥ//83//
body.translated_text:
256.017. 'And those of great power who dwell on <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain —
256.018. let them come here, generating compassion, having been invited.' //83//

body.text:
256.019. evamukte ca rājñā trīṇi śatasahasrāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃnipatitāni/
256.019. tatraikaṃ śatasahasrāṇāmarhatāṃ śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca/
256.020. na kāścidvṛddhāsanamākramyate sma/
256.020. rājā āha--kimarthaṃ vṛddhāsanaṃ tannākramyate? tatra yaśo nāṃnā vṛddhaḥ ṣaḍabhijñaḥ/
256.022. sa uvāca--mahārāja, vṛddhasya tadāsanamiti/
256.022. rājā āha--asti sthavira tvatsakāśādanyo vṛddhatara iti? sthavira uvāca--asti mahārāja--
256.024. vadatāṃ vareṇa vaśinā nirdiṣṭaḥ siṃhanādināmagryaḥ/
256.025. piṇḍolabharadvājasyaitadagrāsanaṃ nṛpate//84//
body.translated_text:
256.019. When the king had spoken thus, three hundred thousand monks assembled.
256.019. Among them, one hundred thousand were <s>Arhats</s>, along with learners and ordinary good men.
256.020. No one ascended the elder's seat.
256.020. The king said: 'Why is the elder's seat not being occupied?' There was an elder named <s>Yaśas</s>, possessing the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges).
256.022. He said: 'Great king, that seat belongs to an elder.'
256.022. The king said: 'Elder, is there one more senior than you?' The elder said: 'There is, great king:
256.024. Declared by the foremost among speakers, the self-controlled one, to be foremost among those who roar the lion's roar —
256.025. this is the senior seat of <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, O lord of men.' //84//

body.text:
256.026. atha rājā kadambapuṣpavadāhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ kathayati--asti kaścidbuddhadarśī bhikṣurdhriyata iti? sthavira uāca--asti mahārāja piṇḍolabharadvājo nāṃnā buddhadarśī tiṣṭhata iti/
256.028. rājā kathayati--sthavira, śakyaḥ so 'smābhirdraṣṭumiti? sthavira uvāca--mahārāja, idānīṃ drakṣyasi/
256.029. ayaṃ tasyāgamanakāla iti/
256.029. atha rājā prītamanā uvāca--
body.translated_text:
256.026. Then the king, his hair-pores bristling with joy like a <s>kadamba</s> flower, said: 'Is there a monk still living who has seen the <s>Buddha</s>?' The elder said: 'There is, great king — <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> by name, one who has seen the <s>Buddha</s>, is still living.'
256.028. The king said: 'Elder, is it possible for us to see him?' The elder said: 'Great king, you shall see him now.
256.029. This is the time of his arrival.'
256.029. Then the king, with a joyful mind, said:

body.text:
257.001. <257>lābhaḥ paraḥ syādatulo mameha mahāsukhaścāyamanuttamaśca/
257.003. paśyāmyaham yattamudārasattvaṃ sākṣādbharadvājasagotranāmam//85//
body.translated_text:
257.001. 'This would be the supreme, incomparable, and most excellent happiness for me here —
257.003. that I should see that noble being face to face, the one named by the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> clan.' //85//

body.text:
257.005. tato rājā kṛtakarapuṭo gaganatalāvasaktadṛṣṭiravasthitaḥ/
257.005. atha sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājo 'nekairarhatsahasrairardhacandrākāreṇopagūḍho rājahaṃsa iva gaganatalādavatīrya vṛddhānte niṣasāda/
257.007. sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājaṃ dṛṣṭvā nānyanekāni bhikṣuśatasahasrāṇi pratyupasthitāni/
257.008. adrākṣīdrājā piṇḍolabharadvājaṃ śvetapalitaśirasaṃ pralambabhrūlalāṭaṃ nigūḍhākṣitārakaṃ pratyekabuddhāśrayam/
257.009. dṛṣṭvā ca rājā mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājasya pādayoḥ patitaḥ/
257.010. mukhatuṇḍakena ca pādāvanuparimārjya utthāya tau jānumaṇḍalau pṛthivītale pratiṣṭhāpya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvājaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ prarudannuvāca--
257.012. yadā mayā śatrugaṇānnihatya prāptā samudrābharaṇā saśailā/
257.014. ekātaputrā pṛthaivī tadā me prītir na yā me sthaviraṃ nirīkṣya//86//
body.translated_text: Then the king, with palms joined and eyes fixed upon the sky, stood waiting. Then the Elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, surrounded by many thousands of <s>Arhats</s> in a semicircular formation, descended from the sky like a royal goose and sat down at the far end. Upon seeing the Elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, many other hundreds of thousands of monks also appeared. The king saw <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> — white-haired with grey locks, with drooping eyebrows over his forehead, with eyes deep-set, having the bearing of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Having seen him, the king, like a tree severed at its root, fell at the feet of the Elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s> with his entire body. Wiping the Elder's feet with his lips, he rose, placed both kneecaps on the ground, and with palms joined, gazing at the Elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, wept and said: 'When I, having slain hosts of enemies, obtained this earth with its mountains and oceans, sovereign over all — the joy I felt then was not equal to what I feel now, gazing upon the Elder.' //86//

body.text:
257.016. tvaddarśanādbhavati/
257.016. dṛṣṭo 'dya tathāgataḥ/
257.016. karuṇālābhāt rvaddarśanācca dviguṇaprasādo mamotpannaḥ/
257.017. api ca sthavira dṛṣṭaste trailokyanātho gururme bhagavān buddha iti? tataḥ sthavirapiṇḍolabharadvāja ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ bhruvamunnāmya rājānamaśokam uvāca--
257.019. dṛṣṭo mayā hyasakṛdapratimo maharṣiḥ saṃtaptakāñcanasamopamatulyatejāḥ/
257.021. dvātriśallakṣaṇadharaḥ śaradinduvaktro brāhmasvarādhikaraṇo hyaraṇāvihārī//87//
body.translated_text: 'From seeing you, it is as if the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself has been seen today. From receiving your compassion and from seeing you, a twofold faith has arisen in me. Moreover, Elder, have you seen the Lord of the Three Worlds, my teacher, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>?' Then the Elder <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, lifting his eyebrows with both hands, said to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'I have seen, not once but many times, that incomparable Great Sage, of radiance equal to heated gold, bearing the thirty-two marks, with a face like the autumn moon, endowed with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, dwelling in the state of non-conflict.' //87//

body.text:
257.023. rājā āha--sthavira, kutra te bhagavān dṛṣṭaḥ, kathaṃ ceti? sthavira uvāca--yadā mahārāja bhagavān vijitamāraparivāraḥ pañcabhirarhacchataiḥ sārdhaṃ prathamato rājagṛhe varṣāmupagataḥ, ahaṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsam/
257.025. mayā sa dakṣiṇīyaḥ samyagdṛṣṭa iti/
257.025. āha ca--
257.026. vītarāgaiḥ parivṛto vītarāgao mahāmuniḥ/
257.027. yadā rājagṛhe varṣā uṣitaḥ sa tathāgataḥ//88//
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Elder, where did you see the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and how?' The Elder said: 'When, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s> and his retinue, together with five hundred <s>Arhats</s>, first spent the rains at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, I was there at that time. I rightly saw that worthy field of merit.' And he said: 'Surrounded by those free from passion, the Great Sage, himself free from passion, when that <s>Tathāgata</s> spent the rains at <s>Rājagṛha</s>—' //88//

body.text:
257.028. tatkālamāsaṃ tatrāhaṃ saṃbuddhasya tadantike/
257.029. yathā paśyasi māṃ sākṣādevaṃ dṛṣṭo mayā miniḥ//89//
body.translated_text: 'At that time I was there, in the presence of the Perfectly Awakened One. Just as you see me face to face, so too was the Sage seen by me.' //89//

body.text:
257.030. yadāpi mahārāja bhagavatā śrāvastyāṃ tīrthyān bijayārthaṃ vijayārthaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ kṛtam, buddhāvataṃsakam yāvadakaniṣṭhabhavanaṃ nirmitaṃ mahan, tatkālaṃ taitraivāhamāsam/
257.031. mayā tadbuddhavikrīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭamiti/
257.032. āha ca--
body.translated_text: 'When, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed the Great Miracle at <s>Śrāvastī</s> to defeat the heretics, and conjured the great <s>Buddhāvataṃsaka</s> (ornament of Buddhas) extending up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> realm, at that time I was right there. I witnessed that sport of the <s>Buddha</s>.' And he said:

body.text:
258.001. tīrthyā yadā bhagavatā kupathaprayātā ṛddhiprabhāvavidhinā khalu nirgṛhītāḥ/
258.003. vikrīḍitaṃ daśabalasya tadāṃ hyudāraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mayā tu nṛpa harṣakaraṃ prajānām//10//
body.translated_text: 'When the heretics, who had gone on the wrong path, were restrained by the <s>Bhagavān</s> through the method of supernatural power — that glorious sport of the Ten-Powered One, bringing delight to the people, was seen by me, O king.' //90//

body.text:
258.005. yadāpi mahārāja bhagavatā deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu varṣā uṣitvā māturjanayitryā dharmaṃ deśayitvā devagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sāṃkāśye nagare 'vatīrṇaḥ, ahaṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsam/ mayā sā devamanuṣyasampadā dṛṣṭā, utpalavarṇayā ca nirmitā cakravartisampadā iti/
258.007. āha ca--
258.008. yadāvatīrṇo vadatāṃ variṣṭho varṣāmuṣitvā khalu devaloke/
258.010. tatrāpyahaṃ saṃnihito babhūva dṛṣṭo mayāsau muniragrasattvaḥ//91//
body.translated_text: 'When, great king, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having spent the rains among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and having taught the <s>Dharma</s> to his mother, descended at the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>, surrounded by hosts of gods, I was there at that time. I witnessed that concourse of gods and humans, and the display of the <s>Cakravartin's</s> splendor conjured by <s>Utpalavarṇā</s>.' And he said: 'When the foremost of speakers descended, having spent the rains in the world of gods, there too I was present — I saw that Sage, the foremost being.' //91//

body.text:
258.012. yadā mahārāja sumāgadhayā anāthapiṇḍadaduhitryā upanimantritaḥ pañcabhirarhacchataiḥ sārdham ṛddhyā puṇḍravardhanaṃ gataḥ, tadāhaṃ parvataśailaṃ grahāya gaganatalamākramya puṇḍravardhanaṃ gataḥ/
258.014. tannimittaṃ ca me bhagavatā ājñākṣiptā--na tāvat te parinirvātavyam yāvaddharmo nāntarhita iti/
258.015. āha ca--
258.016. yadā jagāmarddhibalena nāyakaḥ sumāgadhayopanimantrito guruḥ/
258.018. tadā gṛhītvārdhabalena śailaṃ jagāma tūrṇaṃ khalu puṇḍravardhanam//92//
body.translated_text: 'When, great king, <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with five hundred <s>Arhats</s>, flew by supernatural power to <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s> — at that time I seized a mountain peak and, ascending to the sky, went to <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>. On that account, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave me an injunction: "You shall not enter final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> until the <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared."' And he said: 'When the Guide, invited by <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, went by supernatural power — at that time, having seized a mountain with half his strength, I quickly went to <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>.' //92//

body.text:
258.020. ājñā tadā śākyakuloditena dattā ca me kāruṇikena tena/
258.022. tāvanna te nirvṛtirabhyupeyā antarhito yāvadayaṃ na dharmaḥ//93//
body.translated_text: 'Then the command was given to me by that compassionate one born of the <s>Śākya</s> clan: "Let there be no final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> for you until this <s>Dharma</s> has disappeared."' //93//

body.text:
258.024. yadāpi mahārāja tvayā pūrvaṃ bālabhāvādbhagavato rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭasya saktuṃ dāsyāmīti pāṃśvañjalirbhagavataḥ pātre prakṣiptaḥ, rādhaguptena cānumoditam, tvaṃ na bhagavatā nirdiṣṭah--ayaṃ dārako varṣaśataparinirvṛtasya mama pāṭaliputre nagare aśoko nāma rājā bhaviṣyati caturbhāgacakravartī dhārmiko dharmarājā, yo me śarīradhātukaṃ vaistārikāṃ kariṣyati, caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyati, ahaṃ tatkālaṃ tatraivāsīt/
258.028. āha ca--
258.029. yadā pāṃśvañjalirdattastvayā buddhasya bhājane/
258.030. bālabhāvāt prasāditvā tatraivāhaṃ tadābhavam//94//
body.translated_text: 'When, great king, you yourself in your childhood, as the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, saying "I shall give him roasted grain," threw a handful of dirt into the <s>Bhagavān's</s> bowl, and <s>Rādhagupta</s> gave the rejoicing-utterance — the <s>Bhagavān</s> then designated you: "This boy, a hundred years after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, will be a king named <s>Aśoka</s>, a quarter-<s>Cakravartin</s>, a righteous king of the <s>Dharma</s>, who will distribute my bodily relics widely and will establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> <s>stūpas</s>" — I was right there at that time.' And he said: 'When you gave a handful of dirt into the <s>Buddha's</s> bowl, out of childlike faith, I was right there at that time.' //94//

body.text:
259.001. <259>rājā āha--sthavira, kutredānīmuṣyata iti? sthavira uvāca--
259.002. uttare sararājasya parvate gandhamādane/
259.003. vasāmi nṛpate tatra sārdhaṃ sabrahmacāribhiḥ//95//
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Elder, where do you dwell now?' The Elder said: 'To the north of Lake Anavatapta, on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>, there I dwell, O king, together with my fellow practitioners of the holy life.' //95//

body.text:
259.004. rājā āha--kiyantaḥ sthavirasya parivārāh? sthavira uvāca--
259.005. ṣaṣṭyarhantaḥ sahasrāṇi parivāro nṛṇāṃ vara/
259.006. vasāmi yairahaṃ sārdhaṃ nispṛhairjitakalmaṣaiḥ//96//
body.translated_text: The king said: 'How many are the Elder's attendants?' The Elder said: 'Sixty thousand <s>Arhats</s> are my retinue, O best of men — I dwell with them, desireless, their defilements conquered.' //96//

body.text:
259.007. api ca mahārāja, kimanena saṃdehena kṛtena? pariviṣyatāṃ bhikṣusaṃghaḥ/
259.007. bhuktavato bhikṣusaṃghasya pratisaṃmodanāṃ kariṣyāmi/
259.008. rājā āha--evamastu, yathā sthavira ājñāpayati/
259.009. kiṃ tu buddhasmṛtipratibodhito 'haṃ bodhisnapanaṃ tāvat kariṣyāmi/
259.009. samanantaraṃ ca manāpena cāhāreṇa bhikṣusaṃghamupasthāsyāmīti/
259.010. atha rājā sarvamitramuddhoṣakamāmantrayati--ahamāryasaṃghasya śatasahasraṃ dāsyāmi, kumbhasahasreṇa ca bodhiṃ snāpayiṣyāmi, mama nāṃnā dhuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti/
259.012. tatkālaṃ ca kuṇālasya nayanadvayamavipannamāsīt/
259.012. sa rājño dakṣiṇe pārśve sthitaḥ/
259.013. tenāṅgulidvayamutkṣiptam, na tu vāgbhāṣitā/
259.013. dviguṇaṃ tvahaṃ prasādayiṣyāmītyākārayati/
259.014. pāṇinā vardhitamātre ca kuṇālena sarvajanakāyena hāsyaṃ muktam/
259.014. tato rājā hāsyaṃ muktvā kathayati--aho rādhagupta, kenaitadvardhitamiti? rādhaguptaḥ kathayati--deva, bahavaḥ puṇyārthinaḥ prāṇinaḥ/
259.016. yaḥ puṇyārthī, tena vardhitamiti/
259.016. rājā āha--śatasahasratryaṃ dāsyāmītyāryasaṃghe kumbhasahasreṇa ca bodhiṃ snapayiṣyāmi, mama nāṃnā ghuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti/
259.017. yāvat kuṇālena catasro 'ṅgulya utkṣiptāḥ/
259.018. tato rājā ruṣitaḥ/
259.018. rādhaguptmuvāca--aho rādhagupta, ko 'yamasmābhiḥ sārdhaṃ pratidvandvayatyalokajñah? ruṣitaṃ ca rājānamavekṣya rādhagupto rājñaḥ pādayor nipatyovāca--deva, kasya śaktir narendreṇa sārdhaṃ vispardhituṃ bhavet? kuṇālo guṇavān, pitrā sārdhaṃ vikurvate/
259.021. atha rājā dakṣiṇena parivṛtya kuṇālamavalokyovāca--sthaviro 'ham/
259.021. kośaṃ sthāpayitvā rājyamantaḥpuramamātyagaṇamātmānaṃ ca kuṇālaṃ suvarṇarūpyasphaṭikavaiḍūryamayānāṃ pañcakumbhasahasrāṇi nānāgandhapūrṇāni kṣīracandanakuṅkumakarpūrvāsitrairmahābodhiṃ snapayiṣyāmi, puṣpaśatasahasrāṇi ca bodhipramukhe cāryasaṃghe dadāmi, mama nāṃnā ghuṣyatāṃ pañcavārṣikamiti/
259.024. āha ca--
259.025. rājyaṃ samṛddhaṃ saṃsthāpya kośamantaḥpurāṇi cāmātyagaṇaṃ ca sarvam/
259.027. dadāmi saṃghe guṇapātrabhūte ātmā kuṇālaṃ ca guṇopapannam//97//
body.translated_text: Moreover, he said: 'Great king, what is the use of this hesitation? Let the community of monks be served with food. When the community of monks has eaten, I shall give the thanksgiving address.' The king said: 'So be it, as the Elder commands. But first, aroused by the remembrance of the <s>Buddha</s>, I shall perform the bathing of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. And immediately after, I shall serve the community of monks with agreeable food.' Then the king addressed his announcer <s>Sarvamitra</s>: 'I shall give a hundred thousand to the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s> and shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with a thousand urns. Let a quinquennial festival be proclaimed in my name.' At that time, <s>Kuṇāla's</s> two eyes were still unimpaired. He stood at the king's right side. He held up two fingers, but spoke no word — indicating 'I shall give double.' When <s>Kuṇāla</s> merely raised his hand, the whole crowd burst into laughter. Then the king, having laughed, said: 'O <s>Rādhagupta</s>, who raised the bid?' <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: 'Your Majesty, many beings seek merit. Whoever seeks merit has raised it.' The king said: 'I shall give three hundred thousand to the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s> and shall bathe the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with a thousand urns. Let a quinquennial festival be proclaimed in my name.' Then <s>Kuṇāla</s> held up four fingers. The king became angry. He said to <s>Rādhagupta</s>: 'O <s>Rādhagupta</s>, who is this ignorant person competing with us?' Seeing the king's anger, <s>Rādhagupta</s> fell at the king's feet and said: 'Your Majesty, who has the power to compete with the lord of men? <s>Kuṇāla</s>, being virtuous, is simply playing with his father.' Then the king, turning to the right and looking at <s>Kuṇāla</s>, said: 'I am the Elder. Setting aside the treasury, the kingdom, the inner palace, the council of ministers, myself, and <s>Kuṇāla</s>, I shall bathe the great <s>Bodhi</s> tree with five thousand urns of gold, silver, crystal, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, filled with various perfumes — milk, sandalwood, saffron, camphor, and liquid scents — and I give hundreds of thousands of flowers before the <s>Bodhi</s> tree and to the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s>. Let a quinquennial festival be proclaimed in my name.' And he said: 'Having established the prosperous kingdom, the treasury, the inner palace, and the entire council of ministers — I give all to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the vessel of virtues, together with myself and the virtuous <s>Kuṇāla</s>.' //97//

body.text:
259.029. tato rājā piṇḍolabharadvājapramukhe bhikṣusaṃghe niryātayitvā bodhivṛkṣasya ca caturdiśaṃ vāraṃ baddhvā svayameva ca vāramabhiruhya caturbhiḥ kumbhasahasrairbodhisanapanaṃ kṛtavān/
259.030. kṛtamātre ca bodhisnapane bodhivṛkṣo yathāpaurāṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
259.031. vakṣyati hi--
body.translated_text: Then the king, having made offerings to the community of monks led by <s>Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja</s>, and having built a platform around the <s>Bodhi</s> tree on all four sides and himself ascending the platform, bathed the <s>Bodhi</s> tree with four thousand urns. The very moment the bathing of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree was completed, the <s>Bodhi</s> tree was restored to its former state. For it is said:

body.text:
260.001. <260>kṛtamātre nṛpatinā bodhisnapanamuttamam/
260.002. bodhivṛkṣastadā jāto haritpallavakomalaḥ//98//
body.translated_text: 'The very moment the supreme bathing of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree was performed by the king, the <s>Bodhi</s> tree at that time became green with soft, tender shoots.' //98//

body.text:
260.003. dṛṣṭvā haritapatrāḍhyaṃ pallavāṅkurakomalam/
260.004. rājā harṣaṃ paraṃ jagāma sāmātyagaṇanaigamaḥ//99//
body.translated_text: 'Seeing the tree rich with green leaves, tender with buds and shoots, the king, together with his council of ministers and citizens, attained the highest joy.' //99//

body.text:
260.005. atha rājā bodhisnapanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pariveṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
260.005. tatra yaśo nāṃnā sthaviraḥ/
260.006. tenābhihitam--mahārāja, mahānayaṃ paramadakṣiṇīya āryasaṃghaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ, tathā te pariveṣṭavyam yathā te kṣatir na syāditi/
260.007. tato rājā svahastena pariveṣaṇam yāvannavakāntaṃ gataḥ/
260.007. tatra dvau śrāmaṇerau saṃrañjanīyaṃ dharmaṃ samādāya vartataḥ/
260.008. ekenāpi saktavo dattāḥ, dvitīyenāpi saktavaḥ/
260.009. ekena khādyakāḥ, dvitīyenāpi khādyakā eva/
260.009. ekena modikāḥ, dvitīyenāpi modikāḥ/
260.009. tau dṛṣṭvā rājā hasitaḥ/
260.010. imau śrāmaṇerau bālakrīḍayā krīḍataḥ/
260.010. yāvadrājñā bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pariveṣya vṛddhāntamārūḍhaḥ/
260.011. sthavireṇa cānuyuktah--mā devena kutracidaprasādamutpādita iti/
260.011. rājā āha--na iti/
260.012. api tu asti dvau śrāmaṇerau bālakrīḍayā krīḍataḥ/
260.013. sthavira uvāca--alaṃ mahārāja, ubhau hi tau ubhayatobhāgavimuktau arhantau/
260.014. śrutvā ca rājñaḥ prītimanaso buddhirutpannā--tau śrāmaṇerau āgamya bhikṣusaṃghaṃ paṭenācchādayiṣyāmi/
260.015. tatastau śrāmaṇerau rājño 'bhiprāyamavagamya bhūyo 'nye 'smābhiḥ svaguṇā udbhavayitavyā iti, tayorekena kaṭāhakā upasthāpitā, dvitīyena raṅgaḥ samudānītaḥ/
260.017. rājñā dṛṣṭau śrāmaṇerakau/
260.017. kimidamārabdham? tayorabhihitam--devo 'smākamavagamya bhikṣusaṃghaṃ paṭenācchādayitukāmaḥ/
260.018. tān paṭān rañjayiṣyāmaḥ/
260.019. śrutvā ca rājño buddhirutpannā--mayā kevalaṃ cintitam, na tu vāgniścāritā/
260.019. paracittavādau etau mahātmānau/
260.020. tataḥ sarvaśarīreṇa pādayor nipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
260.021. mauryaḥ samṛtyaḥ sajanaḥ sapauraḥ sulabdhalābhārthasuyaṣṭayajñaḥ/
260.023. yasyedṛśaḥ sādhujane prasādaḥ kāle tathotsāhi kṛtaṃ ca dānam//100//
body.translated_text:
260.005. Then the king, having performed the bathing of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, began to serve food to the community of monks.
260.005. There was an elder named <s>Yaśas</s>.
260.006. He said: 'Great King, this noble <s>Saṃgha</s>, supreme among those worthy of offerings, has assembled — you should serve in such a way that no loss befalls you.'
260.007. Then the king, serving with his own hands, went all the way to the end of the line.
260.007. There sat two novices (<s>śrāmaṇeras</s>), engaged in a charming display of <s>Dharma</s>.
260.008. One had been given barley flour, and the second also barley flour.
260.009. One received sweets, and the second also sweets.
260.009. One received confections, and the second also confections.
260.009. Seeing them, the king laughed:
260.010. 'These two novices are playing a childish game!'
260.010. When the king had finished serving the community of monks, he went to the far end of the assembly.
260.011. The elder questioned him: 'Has Your Majesty not generated any displeasure anywhere?'
260.011. The king said: 'No.'
260.012. 'However, there were two novices playing a childish game.'
260.013. The elder said: 'Enough, Great King — both of them are <s>Arhats</s>, liberated in both ways.'
260.014. Having heard this, the king, delighted, thought: 'Because of those two novices, I shall cover the entire community of monks with cloth.'
260.015. Then those two novices, perceiving the king's intention, thought: 'We must manifest further virtues.' One of them produced dyeing vats, and the other brought dye.
260.017. The king saw the two novices.
260.017. 'What is this about?' They said: 'Your Majesty intends, because of us, to cover the community of monks with cloth.
260.018. We shall dye those cloths.'
260.019. Having heard this, the king thought: 'I merely thought it — I did not utter a word.
260.019. These great souls are readers of others' minds!'
260.020. Then, falling at their feet with his whole body, with palms joined, he said:
260.021. 'Fortunate is this <s>Maurya</s>, with his servants, his people, his citizens, who has gained good profit, whose sacrifice is well-performed,
260.023. whose faith in such holy persons is of this kind, and whose gift has been made at the right time and with such zeal.' //100//

body.text:
260.025. yāvadrājñā abhihitam--yuṣmākamāgamya tricīvareṇa bhikṣusaṃghamācchādayiṣyāmīti/
260.026. tato rājā aśokaḥ pañcavārṣike paryavasite sarvabhikṣūṃs tricīvareṇācchādya catvāri śatasahasrāṇi saṃghasyācchādanaṃ datvā pṛthivīmantaḥpuramamātyagaṇamātmānaṃ ca kuṇālaṃ ca niṣkrītavān/
260.028. bhūyasā bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitamiti//
body.translated_text:
260.025. Then the king declared: 'Because of you two, I shall cover the community of monks with triple robes.'
260.026. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, at the conclusion of the <s>Pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival), having covered all the monks with triple robes and given four hundred thousand coverings to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, ransomed the earth, the inner palace, the ministers, himself, and <s>Kuṇāla</s>.
260.028. Having obtained even greater faith in the Blessed One's teaching, he established the eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> monuments.

body.text:
260.029. yasminneva divase rājñā aśokena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam, tasminneva divase rājño 'śokasya padmāvatī nāṃnā devī prasūtā/
260.030. putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ/
260.031. nayanāni cāsya paramaśobhanāni/
260.031. yāvadrājño 'śokasya niveditam--deva, diṣṭyā vṛddhiḥ/
260.032. devasya putro jātaḥ/
260.032. śrutvā rājā āttamanāḥ kathayati--
body.translated_text:
260.029. On the very day that King <s>Aśoka</s> established the eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s>, on that very day the queen of King <s>Aśoka</s> named <s>Padmāvatī</s> gave birth.
260.030. A son was born — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing.
260.031. His eyes were exceedingly beautiful.
260.031. This was reported to King <s>Aśoka</s>: 'Sire, may you prosper!
260.032. A son has been born to Your Majesty.'
260.032. Having heard this, the king, overjoyed, said:

body.text:
261.001. <261>prītiḥ parā me vipulā hyavāptā mauryasya vaṃśasya parā vibhūtiḥ/
261.003. dharmeṇa rājyaṃ mama kurvato hi jāto dharmavivardhano 'stu//101//
body.translated_text:
261.001. 'Supreme and abundant joy has been obtained by me; supreme is the glory of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty.
261.003. As I rule the kingdom according to <s>Dharma</s>, may the one born be an increaser of the <s>Dharma</s>!' //101//

body.text:
261.005. tasya dharmavivardhana iti nāma kṛtam/
261.005. yāvat kumāro rājño 'śokasyopanāmitaḥ/
261.005. atha rājā kumāraṃ nirīkṣya prītamanāḥ kathayati--
261.007. sutasya me netravarāḥ supuṇyāḥ sujātanīlotpalasaṃnikāśāḥ/
261.009. alaṃkṛtaṃ śobhati yasya vaktraṃ saṃpūrṇacandrapratimaṃ vibhāti//102//
body.translated_text:
261.005. He was given the name <s>Dharmavivardhana</s> ('Increaser of the <s>Dharma</s>').
261.005. The prince was brought before King <s>Aśoka</s>.
261.005. Then the king, gazing at the prince, said with a delighted mind:
261.007. 'The excellent eyes of my son are supremely meritorious, resembling well-born blue lotuses.
261.009. Adorned, his face shines radiantly, like the likeness of the full moon.' //102//

body.text:
261.011. yāvadrājā amātyānuvāca--dṛṣṭāni bhavadbhiḥ kasyedṛśāni nayanāni? amātyā ūcuh--deva, manuṣyabhūtasya na dṛṣṭāni, api tu deva, asti himavati parvatarāje kuṇāle nāma pakṣī prativasati, tasya sadṛśāni nayanāni/
261.013. āha ca--
261.014. himendrarāje giriśailaśṛṅge pravālapuṣpaprasave jalāḍhye/
261.016. kuṇālanāṃneti nivāsapakṣī netrāṇi tenāsya samānyamūni//103//
body.translated_text:
261.011. Then the king said to his ministers: 'Have you seen anyone with eyes like these?' The ministers said: 'Sire, among humans we have not; however, Sire, on the king of mountains, the <s>Himavat</s>, there dwells a bird named <s>Kuṇāla</s>, and its eyes are similar.'
261.013. And it was said:
261.014. 'On the peak of the lord of <s>Himālaya</s>, that mountain rich in coral-flowers and waters,
261.016. dwells a bird named <s>Kuṇāla</s> — its eyes are equal to his.' //103//

body.text:
261.018. tato rājñā abhihitam--kuṇālaḥ pakṣī ānīyatāmīti/
261.018. tasyordhvato yojanam yakṣāḥ śṛṇvantyadho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ/
261.019. tato yakṣaistatkṣaṇena kuṇālaḥ pakṣī ānītaḥ/
261.019. atha rājā kuṇālasya netrāṇi suciraṃ nirīkṣya na kiṃcidviśeṣaṃ paśyati/
261.020. tato rājñābhihitam--kumārasya kuṇālasadṛśāni nayanāni/
261.021. bhavatu kumārasya kuṇāla iti nāma/
261.021. vakṣyati hi--
261.022. netrānurāgeṇa sa pārthivendraḥ sutaḥ kuṇāleti tadā babhāṣe/
261.024. tato 'sya nāma prathitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ tasyāryasattvasya nṛpātmajasya//104//
body.translated_text:
261.018. Then the king commanded: 'Let the <s>Kuṇāla</s> bird be brought.'
261.018. Above it for a <s>yojana</s> the <s>Yakṣas</s> hear, and below for a <s>yojana</s> the <s>Nāgas</s>.
261.019. So the <s>Yakṣas</s> brought the <s>Kuṇāla</s> bird in an instant.
261.019. Then the king, gazing at the eyes of the <s>Kuṇāla</s> for a long time, saw no difference.
261.020. Then the king declared: 'The prince has eyes like the <s>Kuṇāla</s> bird.
261.021. Let the prince's name be <s>Kuṇāla</s>.'
261.021. For it shall be said:
261.022. 'That lord of kings, out of love for his son's eyes, then named him <s>Kuṇāla</s>.
261.024. And that name became renowned throughout the earth — the name of that noble-natured prince.' //104//

body.text:
261.026. vistareṇa yāvat kumāro mahān saṃvṛttaḥ/
261.026. tasya kāñcanamālā nāma dārikā patnyarthe ānītā/
261.027. yāvadrājā aśokaḥ kuṇālena saha kurkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ/
261.027. tatra yaśo nāṃnā saṃghasthaviro 'rhan ṣaḍabhijñaḥ/
261.028. sa paśyati--kuṇālasya nacirānnayanavināśo bhaviṣyati/
261.028. tena rājño 'bhihitam--kimarthaṃ kuṇālaḥ svakarmaṇi na niyujyate? tato rājñā abhihitah--kuṇāla, saṃghasthaviro yadājñāpayati tatparipālayitavyam/
261.030. tataḥ kuṇālaḥ sthavirasya pādayor nipatya kathayati--sthavira, kimājñāpayasi? sthavira uvāca--cakṣuḥ kuṇāla anityamiti kuru/
261.031. āha--
body.translated_text:
261.026. In full detail, the prince grew to maturity.
261.026. A girl named <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> was brought as a wife for him.
261.027. Once, King <s>Aśoka</s> went with <s>Kuṇāla</s> to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery).
261.027. There was an elder of the <s>Saṃgha</s> named <s>Yaśas</s>, an <s>Arhat</s> endowed with the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges).
261.028. He foresaw: 'Before long, <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes will be destroyed.'
261.028. He said to the king: 'Why is <s>Kuṇāla</s> not appointed to his duties?' Then the king said: '<s>Kuṇāla</s>, whatever the elder of the <s>Saṃgha</s> commands, that must be observed.'
261.030. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, falling at the elder's feet, said: 'Elder, what do you command?' The elder said: '<s>Kuṇāla</s>, contemplate that the eye is impermanent.'
261.031. And he said:

body.text:
262.001. <262>cakṣuḥ kumāraṃ satataṃ parīkṣyaṃ calātmakaṃ duḥkhasahasrayuktam/
262.003. yatrānuraktā bahavaḥ pṛthagjanāḥ kurvanti karmāṇyahitāvahāni//105//
body.translated_text:
262.001. 'The eye, O prince, must be constantly examined — it is of a changing nature, conjoined with a thousand sufferings.
262.003. Attached to it, many ordinary persons perform deeds that lead to harm.' //105//

body.text:
262.005. sa ca tathā abhyāsaṃ karoti manasikāraprayuktaḥ/
262.005. ekābhirāmah ekāmirābhirāmaḥ praśamārāmaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
262.006. sa rājakule vivikte sthāne 'vasthitaścakṣurādīnyāyatanānyanityādibhirākāraiḥ parīkṣate/
262.006. tiṣyarakṣitā ca nāṃnā aśokasyāgramahiṣā taṃ pradeśamabhigatā/
262.007. sā taṃ kuṇālamekākinaṃ dṛṣṭvā nayanānurāgeṇa gātreṣu pariṣvajya kathayati--
262.009. dṛṣṭvā tavedaṃ nayanābhirāmaṃ śrīmadvapurnetrayugaṃ ca kāntam/
262.011. daṃdagyate me hṛdayaṃ samantāddāvāgninā prajvalateva kakṣam//106//
body.translated_text:
262.005. And he practiced accordingly, engaged in mental attention.
262.005. He became one delighting in solitude, delighting in non-attachment, and delighting in tranquility.
262.006. He, staying in a secluded place within the royal palace, examined the eye and other sense-bases with the aspects of impermanence and the like.
262.006. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, the chief queen of <s>Aśoka</s>, came to that place.
262.007. Seeing <s>Kuṇāla</s> alone, she embraced his limbs with amorous glances and said:
262.009. 'Having seen this body of yours, beautiful to the eyes, glorious, and with a pair of lovely eyes,
262.011. my heart is burning on all sides, like a thicket blazing with a forest fire.' //106//

body.text:
262.013. śrutvā kuṇāla ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ karṇau pidhāya kathayati--
262.014. vākyaṃ na yuktaṃ tava vaktumetat sūnoḥ purastājjananī mamāsi/
262.016. adharmarāgaṃ parivarjayasva apāyamārgasya hi eṣa hetuḥ//107//
body.translated_text:
262.013. Having heard this, <s>Kuṇāla</s>, covering both ears with his hands, said:
262.014. 'It is not proper for you to speak such words — you are my mother, standing before your son.
262.016. Abandon this unrighteous passion — for it is the cause of the path to the lower realms.' //107//

body.text:
262.018. tatastiṣyarakṣitā tatkālamalabhamānā kruddhā kathayati--
262.019. abhikāmāmabhigatām yattvaṃ necchasi māmiha/
262.020. nacirādeva durbuddhe sarvathā na bhaviṣyasi//108//
body.translated_text:
262.018. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, not obtaining her desire at that moment, said in anger:
262.019. 'Since you do not desire me, who have come to you filled with longing,
262.020. before long, you of evil mind, you shall altogether cease to exist!' //108//

body.text:
262.021. kuṇāla uvāca--
262.022. mama bhavatu maraṇaṃ mā tu sthitasya dharme viśuddhabhāvasya/
262.023. na tu jīvitena kāryaṃ sajjanadhikkṛtena mama//109//

262.024. svargasya dharmalopo yato bhavati jīvitena kiṃ tena/
262.025. mama maraṇahetunā vai budhaparibhūtena dhikkṛtena//110//
body.translated_text:
262.024. 'Since the <s>Dharma</s> that leads to heaven is lost thereby, what use is such a life?
262.025. And what use is this life of mine that would be the cause of death — despised and reviled by the wise?' //110//

body.text:
262.026. yāvat tiṣyarakṣitā kuṇālasya cchidrānveṣiṇī avasthitā/
262.026. rājño 'śokasyottarāpathe takṣaśilā nagaraṃ viruddham/
262.027. śrutvā ca rājā svayamevābhiprasthitaḥ/
262.027. tato 'mātyairabhihitah--deva, kumāraḥ preṣyatam/
262.028. sa saṃtāmayiṣyati/
262.028. atha rājā kuṇālamāhūya kathayati--vatsa kuṇāla, gamiṣyasi takṣaśilānagaraṃ saṃnāmayitum? kuṇāla uvāca--paraṃ deva gamiṣyāmi/
body.translated_text:
262.026. From then on, <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> stood watching for an opportunity to harm <s>Kuṇāla</s>.
262.026. The city of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> in the northern region had revolted against King <s>Aśoka</s>.
262.027. Having heard this, the king intended to go himself.
262.027. Then the ministers said: 'Sire, let the prince be sent.
262.028. He will pacify them.'
262.028. Then the king, summoning <s>Kuṇāla</s>, said: 'My son <s>Kuṇāla</s>, will you go to <s>Takṣaśilā</s> to subdue them?' <s>Kuṇāla</s> said: 'Certainly, Sire, I shall go.'

body.text:
263.001. <263>tato nṛpastasya niśāmya bhāvaṃ putrābhidhānasya manorathasya/
263.003. snehācca yogyaṃ manasā ca buddhvā ājñāpayāmāsa vidhāya yātrām//111//
body.translated_text:
263.001. 'Then the king, having perceived the disposition and the heart's desire of his son,
263.003. out of affection and having deemed it fitting in his mind, commanded him and arranged the expedition.' //111//

body.text:
263.005. atha rājā aśoko nagaraśobhāṃ mārgaśobhāṃ ca kṛtvā jīrṇāturakṛpaṇānāthāṃśca mārgādapanīya ekarathe 'bhiruhya kumāreṇa saha pāṭaliputrānnirgataḥ/
263.006. anuvrajitvā nivartamānaḥ kuṇālaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya nayanaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaḥ prarudannuvāca--
263.008. dhanyāni tasya cakṣūṃṣi cakṣuṣmantaśca te janāḥ/
263.009. satatam ye kumārasya drakṣyanti mukhapaṅkajam//112//
body.translated_text:
263.005. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having adorned the city and the road, and having removed the aged, the sick, the wretched, and the destitute from the road, mounting a single chariot with the prince, departed from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
263.006. Accompanying him part of the way and then turning back, he embraced <s>Kuṇāla</s> at the throat, and gazing into his eyes, weeping, said:
263.008. 'Blessed are those eyes, and blessed are those people
263.009. who will constantly behold the lotus-face of the prince.' //112//

body.text:
263.010. yāvannaimittiko brāhmaṇah--kumārasya nacirānnayanavināśo bhaviṣyati/
263.010. sa ca rājā aśokastasya nayaneṣvatyarthamanuṣaktaḥ/
263.011. dṛṣṭvā ca kathayati--
263.012. nṛpātmajasya nayane viśuddhe mahīpatiścāpyanuraktamasya/
263.014. śriyā vivṛddhe hi sukhānukūle paśyāmi netre 'dya vinaśyamāne//113//
body.translated_text:
263.010. Meanwhile, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> soothsayer said: 'Before long, the prince's eyes will be destroyed.'
263.010. And King <s>Aśoka</s> was exceedingly attached to those eyes.
263.011. Having seen this, he said:
263.012. 'The prince's eyes are pure, and the lord of the earth is deeply attached to them.
263.014. Though they are growing in beauty and favorable to happiness, I foresee those eyes now being destroyed.' //113//

body.text:
263.016. idaṃ puraṃ svargāmiva prahṛṣṭaṃ kumārasaṃdarśanajātaharṣam/
263.018. puraṃ vipanne nayane tu tasya bhaviṣyati śokaparītacetāḥ//114//
body.translated_text:
263.016. 'This city, rejoicing like heaven, filled with joy at the sight of the prince —
263.018. when his eyes are ruined, this city will be one whose hearts are overwhelmed with grief.' //114//

body.text:
263.020. anupūrveṇa takṣaśilāmanuprāptaḥ/
263.020. śrutvā ca takṣaśilāpaurā ardhatrikāṇi yojanāni mārgaśobhāṃ nagaraśobhāṃ ca kṛtvā pūrṇakumbhaiḥ pratyudgatāḥ/
263.021. vakṣyati ca--
263.022. śrutvā takṣaśilāpauro ratnapūrṇaghaṭādikān/
263.023. gṛhya pratyujjagāmāśu bahumānyo nṛpātmajam//115//
body.translated_text:
263.020. Gradually, he arrived at <s>Takṣaśilā</s>.
263.020. Having heard of his approach, the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, having adorned the road and city for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>, came out to meet him with full water-pots.
263.021. And it shall be said:
263.022. 'The citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, hearing the news, taking pots full of jewels and the like,
263.023. quickly went out to welcome the prince with great honor.' //115//

body.text:
263.024. pratyudgamya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--na vayaṃ kumārasya viruddhāḥ, na rājño 'śokasya, api tu duṣṭātmāno 'mātyā āgatyāsmākamapamānaṃ kurvanti/
263.025. yāvatkuṇālo mahatā saṃmānena takṣaśilāṃ praveśitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
263.024. Having come out to meet him, they said with palms joined: 'We are not hostile to the prince, nor to King <s>Aśoka</s>; rather, it is the wicked ministers who came and subjected us to humiliation.'
263.025. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s> was admitted into <s>Takṣaśilā</s> with great honor.

body.text:
263.027. rājñaścāśokasya mahān vyādhirutpannaḥ/
263.027. tasya mukhāduccāro nirgantmārabdhaḥ/
263.028. sarvaromakūpebhyaścāśuci pragharati/
263.028. na ca śakyate cikitsitum/
263.028. tato rājñā abhihitam--kuṇālamānayata, rājye pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti/
263.029. kiṃ mamedṛśena jīvitena prayojanam? śrutvā ca tiṣyarakṣitā cintayati--yadi kuṇālaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāsyati, nāsti mama jīvitam/
263.031. tayā abhihitam--ahaṃ te svasthaṃ kariṣyāmi/
263.031. kiṃ tu vaidyānāṃ praveśaḥ pratiṣidhyatām/
263.032. yāvadrājñā vaidyānāṃ praveśaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ/
263.032. tatastiṣyarakṣitayā vaidyānāmabhihitam--yadi kaścidīdṛśena<264> vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ strī vā puruṣo vā āgacchati, mama darśayitavyaḥ/
body.translated_text:
263.027. And a great illness arose in King <s>Aśoka</s>.
263.027. Excrement began to issue from his mouth.
263.028. And impurities oozed from every pore of his body.
263.028. He could not be cured.
263.028. Then the king said: 'Bring <s>Kuṇāla</s>; I shall install him in the kingdom.
263.029. What use is such a life to me?' Hearing this, <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> thought: 'If <s>Kuṇāla</s> is installed in the kingdom, my life is finished.'
263.031. She said: 'I will make you well.
263.031. But let the entry of physicians be forbidden.'
263.032. The king forbade the entry of physicians.
263.032. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> told the physicians: 'If anyone afflicted with such an illness <264>, whether woman or man, comes to you, bring them to me.'

body.text:
264.001. anyatamaścābhīrastādṛśenaiva vyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ/
264.002. tasya patnyā vaidyāya vyādhir niveditaḥ/
264.002. vaidyenābhihitam--sa evāgacchatu āturaḥ/
264.003. vyādhiṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaiṣajyamupadekṣyāmi/
264.003. yāvadābhīro vaidyasakāśāmabhigataḥ/
264.004. vaidyena ca tiṣyarakṣitāyāḥ samīpamupanītaḥ/
264.004. tatastiṣyarakṣitayā pratigupte pradeśe jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ/
264.005. jīvitād vyaparopya kukṣiṃ pāṭayitvā paśyati ca tasya pakvāśayasthāne antrāyāṃ kṛmirmahān prādurbhūtaḥ/
264.0sa yadyūrdhvaṃ gacchati tenāśucīni pragharati, athādho gacchati, adhaḥ pragharati/
264.007. yāvat tatra maricān peṣayitvā dattaṃ na ca mriyate/
264.007. evaṃ pippalī śṛṅgaveraṃ ca/
264.008. vistareṇa yāvat palāṇḍurdattaḥ/
264.008. spṛṣṭaśca mṛta uccāramārgeṇa nirgataḥ/
264.008. etacca prakaraṇaṃ tayā rajñe niveditam--deva pālāṇḍuṃ parimuṅkṣva, svāsthyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
264.009. rājā āha--devi, ahaṃ kṣatriyaḥ/
264.010. kathaṃ palāṇḍuṃ paribhakṣayāmi? devyuvāca--deva, paribhoktavyaṃ jīvitasyārthe, bhaiṣajyametat/
264.011. rājñā paribhuktam/
264.011. sa ca kṛmirmṛtam uccāramārgeṇa nirgataḥ/
264.011. svasthībhūtaśca rājā/
264.012. tena parituṣṭena tiṣyarakṣitā vareṇa pravāritā--kiṃ te varaṃ prayacchāmi? tayā abhihitam--saptāhaṃ devo rājyaṃ prayacchatu/
264.013. rājā āha--ahaṃ ko bhaviṣyāmi? devyuvāca--saptāhasyātyayāddeva eva rājā bhaviṣyati/
264.014. yāvadrājñā tiṣyarakṣitāyāḥ saptāhaṃ rājyaṃ dattam/
264.014. tasyā buddhirutpannā--idānīṃ mayā asya kuṇālasya vairaṃ niryātitavyam/
264.015. tayā kapaṭalekho likhitastakṣaśilakānāṃ paurāṇām--kuṇālasya nayanaṃ vināśayitavyamiti/
264.016. āha ca--
264.017. rājā hyaśoko balavān pracaṇḍa ājñāpayattakṣaśilājanaṃ hi/
264.019. uddhāryatāṃ locanamasya śatrormauryasya vaṃśasya kalaṅka eṣaḥ//116//
body.translated_text:
264.001. Now a certain cowherd was afflicted with that very same illness.
264.002. His wife reported the illness to a physician.
264.002. The physician said: 'Let the sick man himself come.
264.003. Having seen the illness, I will prescribe the medicine.'
264.003. The cowherd went to the physician.
264.004. The physician brought him to <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>.
264.004. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> killed him in a hidden place.
264.005. Having killed him and cut open his belly, she saw that in the area of the cooked-food pouch, a great worm had appeared in the intestines.
264.005. When it went upward, impurities oozed from above; when it went downward, they oozed from below.
264.007. Ground pepper was applied to it, but it did not die.
264.007. Likewise long pepper and ginger.
264.008. In full detail, until onion was applied.
264.008. Upon being touched by it, the worm died and came out through the excretory passage.
264.008. She then reported the matter to the king: 'Your Majesty, eat onion and you will be restored to health.'
264.009. The king said: 'Queen, I am a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
264.010. How can I eat onion?' The queen said: 'Your Majesty, it must be eaten for the sake of your life; it is a medicine.'
264.011. The king ate it.
264.011. And the worm died and came out through the excretory passage.
264.011. The king was restored to health.
264.012. Pleased, he offered <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> a boon: 'What boon shall I give you?' She said: 'May Your Majesty grant me the kingdom for seven days.'
264.013. The king said: 'What will I become?' The queen said: 'After the seven days, Your Majesty himself will be king again.'
264.014. The king granted <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> the kingdom for seven days.
264.014. She thought: 'Now I must take my revenge on this <s>Kuṇāla</s>.'
264.015. She wrote a forged letter to the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>: '<s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes are to be destroyed.'
264.016. And she said:
264.017. 'The powerful and fierce King <s>Aśoka</s> commands the people of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>:
264.019. Let the eyes of this enemy be torn out — he is a stain on the lineage of the <s>Mauryas</s>.' //116//

body.text:
264.021. rājño 'śoksya yatra kāryamāśu pariprāpyaṃ bhavati, dantamudrayā mudrayati/
264.021. yāvat tiṣyarakṣitā śayitasya rājñastaṃ lekhaṃ dantamudrayā mudrayiṣyāmīti rājñaḥ sakāśamabhigatā/
264.022. rājā ca bhītaḥ pratibuddhaḥ/
264.023. devī kathayati--kimidamiti? rājā kathayati--devi, svapnaṃ me 'śobhanaṃ dṛṣṭam/
264.024. paśyāmi dvau gṛdhrau kuṇālasya nayanamutpāṭayitumicchataḥ/
264.024. devī kathayati--svāsthyaṃ kumārasyeti/
264.025. evaṃ dvirapi rājā bhītaḥ pratibuddhaḥ kathayati--devi, svapno me na śobhano dṛṣṭa iti/
264.026. tiṣyarakṣitā kathayati--kīdṛśaḥ svapna iti/
264.026. rājā āha--paśyāmi kuṇālam--dīrghakeśanakhaśmaśruḥ puraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
264.027. devyāha--svāsthyaṃ kumārasyeti/
264.027. yāvat tiṣyarakṣitayā rājñaḥ śayitasya sa lekho dantamudrayā mudrayitvā takṣaśilāṃ preṣitaḥ/
264.028. yāvadrājñā śayitena svapne dṛṣṭaṃ dantā viśīrṇāḥ/
264.029. tato rājā tasyā eva rātreratyaye naimittikānāhūya kathayati--kīdṛśa eṣāṃ svapnānāṃ vipāka iti? naimittikāḥ kathayati--deva, ya īdṛśasvapnāni paśyati/
264.030. āha ca--
264.031. dantā yasya viśīryante svapnānte prapatanti ca/
264.032. cakṣurbhedaṃ ca putrasya putranāśaṃ ca paśyati//117//
body.translated_text:
264.021. Whatever matter of the king needed swift dispatch was sealed with his tooth-seal.
264.021. <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> went to the king while he was sleeping, intending to seal that letter with his tooth-seal.
264.022. The king woke up, frightened.
264.023. The queen said: 'What is it?' The king said: 'Queen, I have had an inauspicious dream.
264.024. I see two vultures wishing to tear out <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes.'
264.024. The queen said: 'The prince is well.'
264.025. Twice more the king woke up frightened, saying: 'Queen, I have had an inauspicious dream.'
264.026. <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> said: 'What kind of dream?' 
264.026. The king said: 'I see <s>Kuṇāla</s> — with long hair, nails, and beard — entering the city.'
264.027. The queen said: 'The prince is well.'
264.027. Then <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, while the king was sleeping, sealed that letter with his tooth-seal and sent it to <s>Takṣaśilā</s>.
264.028. While the king was sleeping, he saw in a dream that his teeth had crumbled.
264.029. Then the king, at the passing of that night, summoned the soothsayers and said: 'What is the fruit of these dreams?' The soothsayers said: 'Your Majesty, one who has such dreams —'
264.030. And they said:
264.031. 'He whose teeth crumble and fall in a dream,
264.032. sees the destruction of his son's eyes, and the loss of his son.' //117//

body.text:
265.001. <265>śrutvā ca aśokastvaritaṃmutthāyāsanāt kṛtañjaliścaturdiśaṃ devatām yācayitumārabdhaḥ/
265.002. āha ca--
265.003. yā devatā śāsturabhiprasannā dharme ca saṃghe ca gaṇapradhāne/
265.005. ye cāpi loke ṛṣayo variṣṭhā rakṣantu te 'smattanayaṃ kuṇālam//118//
body.translated_text:
265.001. <265>Hearing this, <s>Aśoka</s> hastily rose from his seat and, with joined palms, began to entreat the deities of the four directions.
265.002. And he said:
265.003. 'May those deities who are devoted to the Teacher, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, chief of communities,
265.005. and those sages who are most eminent in the world — may they protect our son <s>Kuṇāla</s>!' //118//

body.text:
265.007. sa ca lekho 'nupūrveṇa takṣaśilāmupanītaḥ/
265.007. atha takṣaśilāḥ paurajānapadā lekhadarśanāt kuṇālasya guṇavistaratuṣṭā notsahante tadaptiyaṃ niveditum/
265.008. ciraṃ vicārayitvā rājā duṣṭaśīlaḥ svaputrasya na marṣayati, prāgevāsmākaṃ marṣayati/
265.009. āha ca--
265.010. munivṛttasya śāntasya sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇaḥ/
265.011. yasya dveṣaḥ kumārasya kasyānyasya bhaviṣyati//119//
body.translated_text:
265.007. That letter gradually reached <s>Takṣaśilā</s>.
265.007. The citizens and country-folk of <s>Takṣaśilā</s>, upon reading the letter, being pleased with <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s many virtues, could not bring themselves to inform him.
265.008. After long deliberation they thought: 'The king is of cruel disposition — he shows no mercy even to his own son, much less to us.'
265.009. And they said:
265.010. 'Of this prince, who conducts himself like a sage, who is peaceful, who seeks the welfare of all beings —
265.011. if there is hatred toward him, for whom else will there not be?' //119//

body.text:
265.012. tairyāvatkuṇālasya niveditam, lekhaścopanītaḥ/
265.012. tataḥ kuṇālo vācayitvā kathayati--viśrabdham yathātmaprayojanaṃ kriyatāmiti/
265.013. yāvaccaṇḍālā upanītāh--kuṇālasya nayanamutpāṭayatheti/
265.014. te ca kṛtāñjalipuṭā ūcuh--notsāhayāmaḥ/
265.014. kṛtah?
265.015. yo hi candramasaḥ kāntiṃ mohādabhyuddharennaraḥ/
265.016. sa candrasadṛśādvaktrāttava netre samuddharet//120//
body.translated_text:
265.012. They finally informed <s>Kuṇāla</s> and showed him the letter.
265.012. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, having had it read, said: 'Do what is to be done with confidence, as the purpose requires.'
265.013. <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) were brought: 'Tear out <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes.'
265.014. They, with joined palms, said: 'We cannot bring ourselves to do it.'
265.014. And they said:
265.015. 'He who in delusion would remove the radiance of the moon,
265.016. he alone could remove the eyes from your face, which is like the moon.' //120//

body.text:
265.017. tataḥ kumāreṇa makuṭaṃ dattam/
265.017. anayā dakṣiṇayotpāṭayatheti/
265.017. tasya tu karmaṇo 'vaśyaṃ vipattavyam/
265.018. puruṣo hi vikṛtarūpo 'ṣṭādaśābhirdaurvarṇikaiḥ samanvāgato 'bhyāgataḥ/
265.018. sa kathayati--ahamutpāṭayiṣyāmīti/
265.019. yāvatkuṇālasya samīpaṃ nītaḥ/
265.019. tasmiṃśca samaye kuṇālasya sthavirāṇāṃ vacanamāmukhībhūtam/
265.020. sa tadvacanamanusmṛtyovāca--
265.021. imāṃ vipattiṃ vijñāya tairuktaṃ tattvavādibhiḥ/
265.022. paśyānityamidaṃ sarvaṃ nāsti kaścid dhruve sthitaḥ//121//
body.translated_text:
265.017. Then the prince gave them his crown.
265.017. 'With this payment, tear them out.'
265.017. But that deed was destined to ripen.
265.018. A man of deformed appearance, possessed of the eighteen marks of ugliness, arrived.
265.018. He said: 'I will tear them out.'
265.019. He was brought near <s>Kuṇāla</s>.
265.019. At that moment, the words of the Elders came to <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s mind.
265.020. Remembering those words, he said:
265.021. 'Knowing this misfortune, those speakers of truth said:
265.022. "Behold — all this is impermanent; no one stands on firm ground."' //121//

body.text:
265.023. kalyāṇamitrāste mahyaṃ sukhakāmā hitaiṣiṇaḥ/
265.024. yairayaṃ deśito dharmo vītakleśairmahātmabhiḥ//122//
body.translated_text:
265.023. 'They are my spiritual friends, those who desire my happiness and seek my welfare,
265.024. by whom this <s>Dharma</s> was taught — those great souls free from afflictions.' //122//

body.text:
265.025. anityatāṃ saṃparipaśyato me gurūpadeśānmanasi prakurvataḥ/
265.027. utpāṭane 'haṃ na bibhemi saumya netradvayasyāsthiratāṃ hi paśye//123//
body.translated_text:
265.025. 'As I contemplate impermanence and bring to mind the teacher's instruction,
265.027. I do not fear, gentle one, the tearing out of my two eyes — for I see their instability.' //123//

body.text:
265.029. utpāṭe vā na vā netre yathā vā manyate nṛpaḥ/
265.030. gṛhītasāraṃ cakṣurme hyanityādibhirāśrayaiḥ//124//
body.translated_text:
265.029. 'Whether the eyes are torn out or not, as the king wishes —
265.030. I have grasped the essence with my eye through the refuges of impermanence and the like.' //124//

body.text:
265.031. tataḥ kuṇālastaṃ puruṣamuvāca--tena hi bhoḥ puruṣa, ekaṃ tāvannayanamutpāṭya mama haste 'nuprayaccha/
265.032. yāvat sa puruṣaḥ kuṇālasya nayanamutpāṭayituṃ pravṛttaḥ/
265.032. tato 'nekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi vikroṣṭumārabdhāni--kaṣṭaṃ bhoḥ/
body.translated_text:
265.031. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s> said to that man: 'Then, good man, first tear out one eye and place it in my hand.'
265.032. The man began to tear out <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eye.
265.032. Then many hundreds of thousands of beings began to cry out: 'Alas, how terrible!'

body.text:
266.001. <266>eṣā hi nirmalā jyotsnā gaganātpatate śaśī/
266.002. puṇḍarīkavanāccāpi śrīmannutpaṭyate 'mbujam//125//
body.translated_text:
266.001. <266>'It is as if the stainless moonlight falls from the sky,
266.002. and from the lotus grove the splendid lotus is being plucked!' //125//

body.text:
266.003. teṣu prāṇiśatasahasreṣu rudatsu kuṇālasyaiva nayanamutpāṭya haste dattam/
266.003. tataḥ kuṇālastannayanaṃ gṛhyovāca--
266.005. rūpāṇi kasmānna nirīkṣase tvam yathāpurā prākṛta māṃsapiṇḍa/
266.007. te vañcitāste ca vigarhaṇīyā ātmeti ye tvāmabudhāḥ//126//
body.translated_text:
266.003. While those hundreds of thousands of beings wept, <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eye was torn out and placed in his hand.
266.003. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, taking that eye, said:
266.005. 'Why do you not perceive forms as before, O common lump of flesh?
266.007. Those are deceived and those are reprehensible who, deluded, regard you as the self.' //126//

body.text:
266.009. sāmagrajaṃ budbadasaṃnikāśaṃ sudurlabhaṃ nirviṣamasvatantram/
266.011. evaṃ pravīkṣanti sadāpramattā ye tvāṃ na te duḥkhamanuprayānti//127//
body.translated_text:
266.009. 'Arisen together, resembling a water-bubble, extremely hard to obtain, uneven, and not self-governing —
266.011. those who are always vigilant and examine thus do not follow after suffering.' //127//

body.text:
266.013. evamanuvicintayatā tena sarvabhāveṣvanityatām/
266.014. srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptaṃ janakāyasya paśyataḥ//128//
body.translated_text:
266.013. 'As he reflected thus on the impermanence of all phenomena,
266.014. the fruit of stream-entry was attained, while the assembled people watched.' //128//

body.text:
266.015. tataḥ kuṇālo dṛṣṭasatyastaṃ puruṣamuvāca--idānīṃ dvitīyaṃ viśrabdhaṃ nayanamutpāṭya haste datta/
266.016. atha kuṇālo māṃsacakṣuṣyuddhṛte prajñācakṣuṣi ca viśuddhe kathayati--
266.017. uddhṛtaṃ māṃsacakṣurme yadyapyetatsudurlabham/
266.018. prajñācakṣurviśuddhaṃ me pratilabdhamaninditam//129//
body.translated_text:
266.015. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, having seen the truths, said to that man: 'Now tear out the second eye with confidence and place it in my hand.'
266.016. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, when the fleshly eye had been removed and the eye of wisdom had been purified, said:
266.017. 'Though this fleshly eye of mine, so hard to obtain, has been removed,
266.018. the blameless eye of wisdom has been purified and attained by me.' //129//

body.text:
266.019. parityakto 'haṃ nṛpatinā yadyahaṃ putrasaṃjñayā/
266.020. dharmarājasya putratvamupeto 'smi mahātmanaḥ//130//
body.translated_text:
266.019. 'Though I have been abandoned by the king under the designation of "son,"
266.020. I have attained the sonship of the great-souled King of the <s>Dharma</s>.' //130//

body.text:
266.021. eśvaryādyadyahaṃ bhraṣṭaṃ śokaduḥkhanibandhanāt/
266.022. dharmaiśvaryamavāptaṃ me duḥkhaśokavināśanam//131//
body.translated_text:
266.021. 'Though I have fallen from sovereignty, the cause of grief and sorrow,
266.022. the sovereignty of the <s>Dharma</s>, which destroys sorrow and grief, has been attained by me.' //131//

body.text:
266.023. yāvatkuṇālena śrutam--nāyaṃ tātasyāśokasya karma, api tu tiṣyarakṣitāyā ayaṃ prayoga iti/
266.024. śrutvā ca kuṇālaḥ kathayati--
266.025. ciraṃ sukhaṃ caiva sā tiṣyanāṃnī āyurbalaṃ pālayate ca devī/
