266.027. saṃpreṣito 'yaṃ hi yayā prayogo yasyānubhāvena kṛtaḥ svakārtham//132//
body.translated_text:
266.023. When <s>Kuṇāla</s> heard: 'This was not the deed of father <s>Aśoka</s>, but a scheme of <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> —'
266.024. hearing this, <s>Kuṇāla</s> said:
266.025. 'May that queen named <s>Tiṣyā</s> live long in happiness, and may she protect her life-force and strength;
266.027. for this scheme was dispatched by her — and through its power, my own purpose has been accomplished.' //132//

body.text:
266.029. tataḥ kāñcanamālayā śrutam--kuṇālasya nayanānyutpāṭitānīti/
266.029. śrutvā ca bhartṛtayā kuṇālasamīpamupasaṃkramya parṣadamavagāhya kuṇālamuddhṛtanayanaṃ rudhirāvasiktagātraṃ dṛṣṭvā sūrcchitā bhūmau patitā/
266.031. yāvajjalasekaṃ kṛtvotthāpitā/
266.031. tataḥ kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya sasvaraṃ prarudantyuvāca--
body.translated_text:
266.029. Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s> heard: '<s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes have been torn out.'
266.029. Hearing this, as his wife she went to <s>Kuṇāla</s>, entering the assembly, and seeing <s>Kuṇāla</s> with his eyes torn out, his body stained with blood, she fainted and fell to the ground.
266.031. She was revived by a sprinkling of water.
266.031. Then, having barely regained consciousness, weeping aloud, she said:

body.text:
267.001. <267>netrāṇi kāntāni manoharāṇi ye māṃ nirīkṣañjanayanti tuṣṭim/
267.003. te me vipannā hyanirīkṣaṇīyāstyajanti me prāṇasamāḥ śarīram//133//
body.translated_text:
267.001. <267>'Those beautiful, captivating eyes that, gazing at me, gave rise to joy —
267.003. they have perished, no longer to be seen; they leave my body, which is as dear to me as life itself.' //133//

body.text:
267.005. tataḥ kuṇālo bhāryāmanunayannuvāca--alaṃ ruditena/
267.005. nārhasi śokamāśrayitum/
267.006. svayaṃkṛtānāmiha karmaṇāṃ phalamupasthitam/
267.006. āha ca--
267.007. karmātmakaṃ lokamidaṃ viditvā duḥkhātmakaṃ cāpi janaṃ hi matvā/
267.009. matvā ca lokaṃ priyaviprayogaṃ kartuṃ priye nārhasi bāṣpamokṣam//134//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, consoling his wife, said: "Enough of weeping! You should not give yourself over to grief. The fruit of deeds self-wrought has now arrived." And he spoke: "Knowing this world to be governed by <s>karma</s> (action), and considering people to be subject to suffering, and knowing the world to be full of separation from the beloved — O dear one, you should not shed tears." (134)

body.text:
267.011. tataḥ kuṇālo bhāryayā saha takṣaśilāyā niṣkāsitaḥ/
267.011. sa garbhādānamupādāya paramasukumāraśarīraḥ/
267.012. na kiṃcidutsahate karma kartum/
267.012. kevalaṃ vīṇāṃ vādayati, gāyati ca/
267.013. tato bhaikṣyaṃ labhate/
267.013. kuṇālaḥ patnyā saha bhuṅkte/
267.013. tataḥ kāñcanamālā yena mārgeṇa pāṭaliputrādānītā, tameva mārgamanusmarantī bhartṛdvitīyā pāṭaliputraṃ gatā/
267.014. yāvadaśokasya gṛhamārabdhā praveṣṭum/
267.015. dvārapālena ca nivāritau/
267.015. yāvadrājño 'śokasya yānaśālāyāmavasthitau/
267.016. tataḥ kuṇālo rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaye vīṇāṃ vādayitumārabdhaḥ/
267.016. yathā nayanānyutpāṭitāni, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam, tadanurūpaṃ hitaṃ ca gītaṃ prārabdham/
267.017. āha ca--
267.018. cakṣurādīni yaḥ prājñaḥ paśyatyāyatanāni ca/
267.019. jñānadīpena śuddhena sa saṃsārādvimucyate//135//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kuṇāla</s> was expelled from <s>Takṣaśilā</s> together with his wife. He, whose body was supremely delicate from birth, was unable to undertake any work. He only played the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) and sang, and from that he obtained alms. <s>Kuṇāla</s> ate together with his wife. Then <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, remembering the very road by which she had been brought from <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, went to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> accompanied by her husband. They began to enter the house of <s>Aśoka</s>, but were stopped by the gatekeeper. They then stayed in King <s>Aśoka</s>'s carriage-hall. Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, at the dawn-hour of the night, began to play the <s>vīṇā</s>. Just as his eyes had been torn out and he had realized the vision of truth, so he began a fitting and beneficial song. And he spoke: "The wise one who perceives the eyes and other <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) with the pure lamp of knowledge — he is liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence)." (135)

body.text:
267.020. yadi tava bhavaduḥkhapīḍitā bhavati doṣaviniśritā matiḥ/
267.022. sukhamiha ca yadīcchasi dhruvaṃ tvaritamihāyatanāni saṃtyajasva//136//
body.translated_text: "If your mind, afflicted by the suffering of existence, has resorted to defilement, and if you desire lasting happiness here, then swiftly abandon the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases)!" (136)

body.text:
267.024. tasya gītaśabdo rājñā aśokena śrutaḥ/
267.024. śrutvā ca rājā prītamanā uvāca--
267.025. gītaṃ kuṇālena mayi prasaktaṃ vīṇāsvaraṃ caiva śrutiścireṇa/
267.027. abhyāgato 'pīha gṛhaṃ nu kaṃcinna cecchati draṣṭumayaṃ kumāraḥ//137//
body.translated_text: The sound of his singing was heard by King <s>Aśoka</s>. Having heard it, the king, his heart delighted, said: "This singing directed at me is that of <s>Kuṇāla</s>, and this sound of the <s>vīṇā</s> is one I have heard long ago. Has someone perhaps come here to the house, yet this prince does not wish to see me?" (137)

body.text:
267.029. atha rājā aśoko 'nyatamapuruṣamāhūyovāca--puruṣa, lakṣyate--
267.030. na khalveṣa kiṃ gītasya kuṇālasadṛśo dhvaniḥ/
267.031. karmaṇyadhairyatāṃ caiva sūcayanniva lakṣyate//138//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, summoning a certain man, said: "Man, observe — is this not indeed a voice resembling <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s singing? It seems to indicate unsteadiness in action." (138)

body.text:
267.032. tadanenāsmi śabdena dhairyādākampito bhṛśam/
267.033. kalabhasyeva naṣṭasya pranaṣṭakalabhaḥ karī//139//
body.translated_text: "By this sound I have been greatly shaken from my composure, like an elephant that has lost its young calf, hearing a lost calf's cry." (139)

body.text:
268.001. <268>gaccha, kuṇālamānayasveti/
268.001. yāvat puruṣo yānaśālāṃ gataḥ/
268.001. paśyati kuṇālamuddhṛtanayanaṃ vātātapaparidagdhagātram/
268.002. apratyabhijñāya ca rājānamaśokamabhigamyovāca--deva, na hyeṣa kuṇālaḥ/
268.003. andhaka eṣa vanīpakaḥ patnyā saha devasya yānaśālāyamavasthitaḥ/
268.003. śrutvā ca rājā saṃvignaścintayāmāsa--yathā mayā svapnānyaśobhanāni dṛṣṭāni, niyataṃ kuṇālasya nayanāni vinaṣṭāni bhaviṣyanti/
268.005. āha ca--
268.006. svapnāntare nimittāni yathā dṛṣṭāni me purā/
268.007. niḥsaṃśayaṃ kuṇālasya netre vai nidhanaṃ gate//140//
body.translated_text: "Go, bring <s>Kuṇāla</s> here!" The man went to the carriage-hall. He saw <s>Kuṇāla</s> with his eyes torn out, his body scorched by wind and sun. Not recognizing him, he went to King <s>Aśoka</s> and said: "Lord, this is not <s>Kuṇāla</s>. This is a blind street-musician staying with his wife in Your Majesty's carriage-hall." Hearing this, the king, deeply agitated, reflected: "Just as I saw inauspicious dreams, surely <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes must have been destroyed." And he spoke: "The omens that I saw before in my dreams — without doubt, <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s eyes have indeed perished." (140)

body.text:
268.008. tato rājā prarudannuvāca--
268.009. śīghramānīyatāmeṣa matsamīpaṃ vanīpakam/
268.010. na hi me śāmyate cetaḥ sutavyasanacintayā//141//
body.translated_text: Then the king, weeping, said: "Quickly, bring this musician into my presence! For my heart finds no peace, tormented by the thought of my son's calamity." (141)

body.text:
268.011. yāvat puruṣo yānaśālāṃ gatvā kuṇālamuvāca--kasya tvaṃ putraḥ, kiṃ ca nāma? kuṇālaḥ prāha--
268.013. aśoko nāṃ rājāsau mauryāṇāṃ kulavardhanaḥ/
268.014. kṛtsneyaṃ pṛthivī yasya vaśe vartani kiṃkara//142//
body.translated_text: The man went to the carriage-hall and said to <s>Kuṇāla</s>: "Whose son are you, and what is your name?" <s>Kuṇāla</s> replied: "The king named <s>Aśoka</s>, increaser of the <s>Maurya</s> lineage — this entire earth is under his command and serves him." (142)

body.text:
268.015. tasya rājñastvahaṃ putraḥ kuṇāla iti viśrutaḥ/
268.016. dhārmikasya tu putro 'haṃ buddhasyādityabāndhavaḥ//143//
body.translated_text: "I am the son of that king, renowned as <s>Kuṇāla</s>. I am the son of the righteous one, a kinsman of the <s>Buddha</s>, the friend of the sun." (143)

body.text:
268.017. tataḥ kuṇālaḥ patnyā saha rājño 'śokasya samīpamānītaḥ/
268.017. atha rājā aśokah {paśyati} kuṇālamuddhṛtanayanaṃ vātātapaparidagdhagātraṃ rathyācolakasaṃghātapratyavareṇa vāsasā lakṣyālakṣyapracchāditakaupīnam/
268.019. sa tamapratyābhijñāya ākṛtimātrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā kathayati--tvaṃ kuṇāla iti? kuṇālaḥ prāha--evaṃ deva, kuṇālo 'smīti/
268.020. śrutvā mūrcchito bhūmau patitaḥ/
268.020. vakṣyati hi--
268.021. tataḥ kuṇālasya mukhaṃ nirīkṣya netroddhṛtaṃ śokaparītacetāḥ/
268.023. rājā hyaśokaḥ patito dharaṇyāṃ hā putraśokena hi dahyamānaḥ//144//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kuṇāla</s> was brought with his wife into the presence of King <s>Aśoka</s>. The king saw <s>Kuṇāla</s> with his eyes torn out, his body scorched by wind and sun, his loincloth barely covered by a garment made of rags gathered from the streets. Not recognizing him, seeing only a vague form, the king asked: "Are you <s>Kuṇāla</s>?" <s>Kuṇāla</s> replied: "Yes, Lord, I am <s>Kuṇāla</s>." Hearing this, the king fainted and fell to the ground. For it will be said: "Then, gazing upon the face of <s>Kuṇāla</s> with his eyes torn out, his heart overwhelmed with grief, King <s>Aśoka</s> fell upon the earth, burning with the sorrow of a father for his son." (144)

body.text:
268.025. yāvajjalapariṣekaṃ kṛtvā rājānamutthāpayitvā āsane niṣāditaḥ/
268.025. atha rājā kathaṃcit saṃjñāmupalabhya kuṇālamutsaṅge sthāpayāmāsa/
268.026. vakṣyati hi--
268.027. tato muhūrtaṃ nṛpa āśvasitvā kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya rasāśrukaṇṭhaḥ/
268.028. muhuḥ kuṇālasya mukhaṃ pramṛjya bahūni rājā vilalāpa tatra//145//
body.translated_text: They sprinkled water upon him and, raising the king, seated him upon his throne. Then the king, having somehow regained consciousness, placed <s>Kuṇāla</s> upon his lap. For it will be said: "Then, after a moment, the king, recovering his breath, embracing him around the neck, his throat choked with tears, repeatedly wiping the face of <s>Kuṇāla</s>, the king lamented greatly there." (145)

body.text: 268.030. netre kuṇālapratime vilokya sutaṃ kuṇāleti purā babhāṣe/
body.translated_text: "Seeing eyes resembling <s>Kuṇāla</s>'s, I formerly called my son '<s>Kuṇāla</s>.'"

body.text: 269.001. <269>tadasya netre nidhanaṃ gate te putraṃ kuṇāleti kathaṃ ca vakṣye//146//
body.translated_text: "Now that those eyes of his have perished, how shall I call my son '<s>Kuṇāla</s>'?" (146)

body.text:
269.003. āha ca--
269.004. kathaya kathaya sādhu putra tāvadvadanamidaṃ tava cārunetram/
269.006. gaganamiva vipannacandratāravyapagataśobhamanīkṣakaṃ kṛtaṃ te//147//
body.translated_text: And he spoke: "Tell me, tell me truly, my son — this face of yours that once had beautiful eyes, like the sky bereft of moon and stars, has been made devoid of beauty and sightless." (147)

body.text:
269.008. akaruṇahṛdayena tena tāta munisadṛśasya na sādhu sādhubuddheḥ/
269.010. naravaranayaneṣvavairavairaṃ prakṛtamidaṃ mama bhūri śokamūlam//148//
body.translated_text: "By that cruel-hearted one, my son, this was not good — done to one of pure mind, resembling a <s>muni</s> (sage). This causeless enmity against the eyes of the best of men is for me a vast root of grief." (148)

body.text:
269.012. vada suvadana kṣiprametadarthaṃ vrajati śarīramidaṃ purā vināśam/
269.014. tava nayanavināśaśokadagdhaṃ vanamiva nāgavimuktavajradagdham//149//
body.translated_text: "Tell me, fair-faced one, quickly the reason for this: this body of yours will soon go to destruction, scorched by grief at the loss of your eyes, like a forest burnt by the thunderbolt loosed by an elephant." (149)

body.text:
269.016. tataḥ kuṇālaḥ pitaraṃ praṇipatyovāca--
269.017. rājannatītaṃ khalu naiva śocyaṃ kiṃ na śrutaṃ te munivākyametat/
269.019. yatkarmabhiste 'pi jinā na muktāḥ pratyekabuddhāḥ sudṛḍhaistathaiva//250//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kuṇāla</s>, bowing to his father, said: "O king, what is past should surely not be grieved over. Have you not heard this saying of the <s>munis</s> (sages)? — That even the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) were not freed from their <s>karmas</s> (deeds), nor likewise the firmly resolute <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. (250)

body.text:
269.021. labdhāḥ phalasthāśca pṛthagjanāśca kṛtāni kāmānyaśubhāni dehinām/
269.023. svayaṃkṛtānāmiha karmāṇāṃ phalaṃ kathaṃ tu vakṣyāmi parairidaṃ kṛtam//151//
body.translated_text: "Those who have attained the fruit and ordinary worldlings alike — the inauspicious deeds done by embodied beings are theirs. The fruit of deeds done by oneself here — how then shall I say that this was done by others? (151)

body.text:
269.025. ahameva mahārāja kṛtāparādhaśca sāparādhaśca/
269.026. vinivartayāmi yo 'haṃ vinayāmi vipattijananāni//152//
body.translated_text: "It is I myself, great king, who am the wrongdoer and the offender. It is I who turn back and remove the causes that produce misfortune. (152)

body.text:
269.027. na śastravajrāgniviṣāṇi pannagāḥ kurvanti pīḍāṃ nabhaso 'vikāriṇaḥ/
269.029. śarīralakṣyeṇa dhṛtena pārthiva patanti duḥkhānyaśivāni dehinām//153//
body.translated_text: "Sword, thunderbolt, fire, poisons, and serpents cause no harm to those who are unchanging like the sky. But for embodied beings who bear the mark of a body, O king, inauspicious sufferings befall them. (153)

body.text:
269.031. atha rājā śokāgninā saṃtāpitahṛdaya uvāca--
269.032. kenoddhṛtāni nayanāni sutasya mahyaṃ ko jīvitaṃ sumadhuraṃ tyajituṃ vyavastaḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the king, his heart inflamed by the fire of grief, said: "By whom were the eyes of my son torn out? Who is resolved to abandon his own most sweet life?

body.text: 270.001. <270>śokānalo nipatito hṛdaye pracaṇḍah ācakṣva putra kasya harāmi daṇḍam//154//
body.translated_text: "The fierce fire of grief has fallen upon my heart. Tell me, son, upon whom shall I bring down punishment?" (154)

body.text:
270.003. yāvadrājñā aśokena śrutam--tiṣyarakṣitāyā ayaṃ prayoga iti/
270.003. śrutvā rājā tiṣyarakṣitāmāhūyovāca--
270.005. kathaṃ hi dhanye na nimajjase kṣitau cchindāmi śīrṣaṃ paraśuprahāraiḥ/
270.007. tyajāmyahaṃ tvāmatipāpakāriṇīmadharmayuktāṃ śriyamātmavāniva//155//
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> heard that this was the doing of <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, having heard it the king summoned <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> and said: "How is it, O fortunate one, that you do not sink into the earth? I shall split your head with blows of an axe. I cast you off, you supremely wicked, unrighteous one, as a self-possessed man casts off ill-gotten fortune." (155)

body.text:
270.009. tato rājā krodhāgninā prajvalitastiṣyarakṣitāṃ nirīkṣyovāca--
270.010. utpāṭya netre paripātayāmi gātraṃ kimasyā nakharaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ/
270.012. jīvantiśūlāmatha kārayāmi cchindāmi nāsāṃ krakacena vāsyāḥ//156//
body.translated_text: Then the king, blazing with the fire of wrath, gazing at <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s>, said: "I shall tear out her eyes and let them fall; what of her limbs with sharp claws? (156)

body.text:
270.014. kṣureṇa jihvāmatha kartayāmi viṣeṇa pūrṇāmatha ghātayiṣye/
270.016. sa ityevamādivadhaprayogaṃ bahuprakāraṃ hyavadannarendraḥ//157//
body.translated_text: "I shall impale her alive upon a stake, or cut off her nose with a saw, or shave her tongue with a razor, or kill her by filling her with poison." Thus and in many such ways did the king speak of methods of execution. (157)

body.text:
270.018. vijñāpayāmāsa guruṃ mahātmā/
270.020. anāryakarmā yadi tiṣyarakṣitā tvamāryakarmā bhava mā vadha striyam//158//
body.translated_text: The great-souled one made known to his elder father: "If <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> is one of ignoble deeds, do you be one of noble deeds — do not slay a woman. (158)

body.text:
270.022. phalaṃ hi maitryā sadṛśaṃ na vidyate prabhostitakṣā sugatena varṇitā/
270.024. punaḥ praṇasya pitaraṃ kumāraḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ sūnṛtavāgjagāda//159//
body.translated_text: "There is no fruit comparable to loving-kindness; forbearance is praised by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)." Then again, bowing to his father, the prince, with palms joined and gentle words, spoke: (159)

body.text:
270.026. rājanna me duḥkhamalo 'sti kaścittīvrāpalāre 'pi na manyutāpaḥ/
270.028. manaḥ prasannam yadi me jananyām yenoddhṛte me nayane svayaṃ hi/
270.030. tattena satyena mamāstu tāvannetradvayaṃ prāktanameva sadyaḥ//160//
body.translated_text: "O king, I have no taint of suffering, nor any anguish of resentment even at this grievous outrage. If my mind is serene toward my mother, by whom my own eyes were torn out — by that truth let my two eyes at once become as they were before." (160)

body.text:
270.032. ityuktamātre pūrvādhikapraśobhite netrayugme prādurbabhūvatuḥ/
270.032. yāvadrājñā aśokena tiṣyarakṣitā amarṣitena jatugṛhaṃ praveśayitvā dagdhā, takṣaśilāśca paurāḥ praghātitāḥ//
body.translated_text: No sooner was this spoken than the pair of eyes appeared, more radiant than before. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, enraged, having made <s>Tiṣyarakṣitā</s> enter a house of lac, burned her, and the citizens of <s>Takṣaśilā</s> were put to death.

body.text:
271.001. <271>bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaśayacchettāramāyuṣmantaṃ sthaviropaguptaṃ pṛcchanti--kiṃ kuṇālena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena nayanānyutpāṭitāni? sthavira uvāca--tena hyāyuṣmantaḥ śrūyatām--
271.003. bhūtapūrvamatīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāmanyatamo lubdhakaḥ/
271.004. sa himavantaṃ gatvā mṛgān praghātayati/
271.005. so 'pareṇa samayena himavantaṃ gataḥ/
271.005. tatra pāśanipatitānyekasyāṃ guhāyāṃ praviṣṭānyāsāditāni/
271.006. tena vāgurayā sarve gṛhītāḥ/
271.006. tasya buddhirutpannā--yadi praghātayiṣyāmi, māṃsaḥ kledaṃmupayāsyati/
271.007. tena pañcānāṃ mṛgaśatānāṃ nayanātyutpāṭitāni//
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), their doubts arisen, asked the venerable elder <s>Upagupta</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What <s>karma</s> (deed) did <s>Kuṇāla</s> perform, by the ripening of which deed his eyes were torn out?" The elder said: "Then, venerable ones, listen — In the past, in a former age, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain hunter. He went to the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas) and slew deer. At another time he went to the <s>Himavat</s>. There, fallen into snares, having entered a single cave, they were found. He caught them all with a net. This thought occurred to him: 'If I slay them, the flesh will become putrid.' So he tore out the eyes of five hundred deer.

body.text:
271.008. kiṃ manyadhvamāyuṣmantah? yo 'sau lubdhakaḥ, sa eṣa kuṇālaḥ/
271.008. yattatrānena bahūnāṃ mṛgaśatānāṃ nayanānyutpāṭitāni, tasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣaśatasahasrāṇi narakeṣu duḥkhamanubhūya tataḥ karmāvaśeṣeṇa pañca janmaśatāni tasya nayanānyutpāṭitāni//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, venerable ones? That hunter — he is this very <s>Kuṇāla</s>. Because he there tore out the eyes of many hundreds of deer, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> (deed), having experienced suffering in the hells for many hundreds of thousands of years, then by the remainder of that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births his eyes were torn out.

body.text:
271.011. kiṃ karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākenocce kule upapannaḥ, prasādikaśca saṃvṛttaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam?
271.013. tena hyāyucmantaḥ śrūyatām--bhūtapūrvamatīte 'dhvani catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ krakucchando nāma samyaksambuddho loka udapādi/
271.014. yadā krakucchandaḥ samyaksambuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya aśokena rājñā catūratnamayaṃ stūpaṃ kāritam/
271.016. yadā rājā aśokaḥ kālagataḥ, aśrāddho rājā rājyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ/
271.016. tāni ratnānyadattādāyikairhṛtāni/
271.017. pāṃśukāṣṭaṃ cāvaśiṣṭam/
271.017. atra janakāyo gatvā viśīrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā śocitumārabdhaḥ/
271.018. tasmiṃśca samaye 'nyatamaśca śreṣṭhiputraḥ/
271.018. tenokrah--kimarthaṃ rudyata iti? tairabhihitam--krakucchandasya samyaksambuddhasya stūpaṃ catūratnamayamāsīt, sa idānīṃ viśīrṇa iti/
271.020. tatastena ca tatra krakucchandasya samyaksambuddhasya kāyapramāṇikā pratimā babhūva viśīrṇā, sā abhisaṃskṛtā, samyakpraṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam--yādṛśaḥ krakucchandaḥ śāstā, īdṛśameva śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyamiti//
body.translated_text: "What <s>karma</s> (action) was performed by the ripening of which he was born into a high family, became handsome, and attained the vision of truth? Therefore, venerable ones, listen — in the past, long ago, when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, in the dispensation of the Blessed <s>Krakucchanda</s>, a merchant's son went forth as a renunciant. And he became an attendant of the Blessed <s>Krakucchanda</s>. But he did not attain any special realization. When the Blessed One had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final extinction) and a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary monument) had been erected, he adorned that <s>stūpa</s> and placed golden eyes upon it, and having abandoned the ten unwholesome courses of action and adopted the ten wholesome courses of action, he made this aspiration: 'May I, in the dispensation of whatever teacher shall arise in the world in the future, attain direct realization.'"

body.text:
271.023. kiṃ manyadhvamāyuṣmantah? yo 'sau śreṣṭhiputraḥ, sa eṣa kuṇālaḥ/
271.023. yatrānena krakucchandasya stūpamabhisaṃskṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākenoccakule upapannaḥ/
271.024. yatpratimā abhisaṃskṛtā, tena karmaṇo vipākena kuṇākaḥ prāsādikaḥ samṛttaḥ/
271.025. yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena kuṇālena śākyamuniḥ samyaksambuddhastādṛśa eva śāstā samārāgito na virāgitaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, venerable ones? That merchant's son — he is this very <s>Kuṇāla</s>. Because he adorned the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Krakucchanda</s>, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was born into a high family. Because he adorned the images, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he became handsome. Because he placed golden eyes upon it, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he became known for having eyes resembling those of the <s>kuṇāla</s> bird. Because he abandoned the ten unwholesome courses of action, adopted the ten wholesome courses of action, and made an aspiration, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was led by me to direct realization. Thus was the <s>karma</s> performed by <s>Kuṇāla</s>, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). By him, in the presence of a Blessed <s>Buddha</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), one robe worth ten million was offered, and in return for that gift, when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, he went forth as a renunciant in the dispensation of the Blessed <s>Krakucchanda</s>."

body.text: 271.028. iti śrīdivyāvadāne kuṇālāvadānaṃ saptaviṃśatimaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Kuṇālāvadāna</s>, the twenty-seventh, is completed.

body.text: 272.001. div28 vītaśokāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 28: The <s>Vītaśokāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Vītaśoka</s>).

body.text:
272.002. yadā rājñā aśokena bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā, tena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaṃ pañcavārṣikaṃ ca kṛtam/
272.003. trīṇi śatasahastāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojitāni yatraiko 'rhatāṃ dvau śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca/
272.004. (sa)samudrāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ janakāyā yadbhūyasā bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasannāḥ/
272.005. tasya bhrātā vītaśoko nāma tīrthyābhiprasannaḥ/
272.005. sa tīrthyairvigrāhitah--nāsti śramaṇaśākyaputrīyāṇāṃ mokṣa iti/
272.006. ete hi sukhābhiratāḥ parikhedabhīravaśceti/
272.007. yāvadrājñā aśokenocyate--vītaśoka, mā tvamanāyatane 'prasādamutpādaya, api tu buddhadharmasaṃghe prasādamutpādaya/
272.008. eṣa āyatanagataḥ prasāda iti/
272.008. atha rājā aśoko 'pareṇa samayena mṛgavadhāya nirgataḥ/
272.009. tatra vītaśokenāraṇye ṛṣirdṛṣṭaḥ pañcātapenāvasthitaḥ/
272.010. sa ca kaṣṭatapaḥ sārasaṃjñī/
272.010. tenābhigamya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā sa ṛṣiḥ pṛṣṭah--bhagavan, kiyaccitraṃ te ihāraṇye prativasatah? sa uvāca--dvādaśa varṣāṇīti/
272.011. vītaśokaḥ kathayati--kastavāhārah? sa ṛṣiruvāca--phalamūlāni/
272.012. kiṃ prāvaraṇam? darbhacīvarāṇi/
272.012. kā śayyā? tṛṇasaṃstaraṇam/
272.013. vītaśoka uvāca--bhagavan, kiṃ duḥkhaṃ bādhate? ṛṣiruvāca--ime mṛgā ṛtukāle saṃvasanti/
272.014. yadā mṛgānāṃ saṃvāso dṛṣṭo bhavati, tasmin samaye rāgeṇa paridahyāmi/
272.015. vītaśoka uvāca--asya kaṣṭena tapasā rāgo 'dyāpi na bādhyate, prāgeva śramaṇāḥ śākyaputrīyāḥ svāstīrṇāsanaśayanopasevinaḥ/
272.016. kuta eṣāṃ rāgaprahāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati? āha ca--
272.017. kaṣṭe 'smin vijane vane nivasatāṃ vāyvambumūlāśināṃ rāgo naiva jito yadīha ṛṣiṇā kālaprakarṣeṇa hi/
272.019. bhuktavānnaṃ sadhṛtaṃ prabhūtapiśitaṃ dadhyuttamālaṃkṛtaṃ śākyeṣvindriyanigraho yadi bhavedvindhyaḥ plavetsāgare//1//
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> had gained faith in the teaching of the Blessed One, he established eighty-four thousand <s>dharmarājikā</s> (dharma-shrines) and held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival). Three hundred thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) were fed, among whom one was an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one) dwelling in <s>Yaṣṭhivana</s> (Bamboo Grove). This King <s>Aśoka</s> felt a longing: 'Why does none of my own family go forth as a renunciant in the teaching of the Blessed One?' He had a brother named <s>Vītaśoka</s>, who was devoted to the heterodox <s>tīrthya</s> (non-Buddhist) ascetics. Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, go forth in the teaching of the Blessed One.' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, <s>Vītaśoka</s> will not go forth in the teaching of the Blessed One. He has no faith in the <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) who are sons of the <s>Śākya</s>.' Nevertheless, King <s>Aśoka</s> told <s>Vītaśoka</s>: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, go forth in the teaching of the Blessed One.' At that, he became agitated and angry. The king said: 'Sir, why are you angry? Just say that you will not go forth.' He replied: 'Death would be better for me than going forth among the <s>śramaṇas</s> who are sons of the <s>Śākya</s>.' Then he struck out with both fists. The king said: 'Stop, do not go forth for now.' Then the <s>tīrthyas</s> (heterodox teachers), having heard of the quarrel between the righteous King <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Vītaśoka</s>, said:

body.text:
272.021. sarvathā vañjito rājā aśoko yacchramaṇeṣu śākyaputrīyeṣu kārāṃ karoti/
272.021. etacca vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā upāyajño 'mātyānuvāca--ayaṃ vītaśokastīrthyābhiprasannaḥ/
272.022. upāyena bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasādayitavyaḥ/
272.023. amātyā āhuh--deva, kimājñāpayasi? rājā āha--yadā ahaṃ rājā alaṃkāraṃ mauliṃ paṭṭaṃ cāpanayitvā snānaśālāṃ praviṣṭo bhavāmi, tadā yūyaṃ vītaśokasyopāyena mauliṃ paṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā siṃhāsane niṣādayiṣyatha/
272.025. evamastu iti/
272.025. yāvadrājā rājālaṃkāraṃ mauliṃ paṭṭaṃ cāpanayitvā snānaśālāyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ, tato 'mātyairvītaśoka ucyate--rājño 'śokasyātyayāt tvaṃ rājā bhaviṣyasi/
272.027. imaṃ tāvadrājālaṃkāraṃ pravaramauliṃ paṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā siṃhāsane niṣīdayiṣyāmah--kiṃ śobhase na veti/
272.028. taistadābharaṇamauliṃ paṭṭaṃ ca baddhvā siṃhāsane niṣādito rājñaśca niveditam/
272.029. tato rājā aśoko vītaśokaṃ rājālaṃkāraṃ maulipaṭṭabaddhaṃ ca siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati--adhyāpyahaṃ jīvāmi/
272.030. tvaṃ rājā saṃvṛttaḥ/
272.030. tato rājñā abhihitam--ko 'tra? tato yāvadvadhyaghātakā nīlāmbaravasanāḥ pralambakeśā ghaṇṭāśabdapāṇayo rājñaḥ pādayor nipatyovāca--deva, kimājñāpayasi? rājā āha--vītaśoko mayā parityakta iti/
body.translated_text: "King <s>Aśoka</s> has been completely deceived, since he renders service to the <s>śramaṇas</s> who are sons of the <s>Śākya</s>." Having heard this speech, the king, skilled in stratagems, said to his ministers: 'This <s>Vītaśoka</s> is devoted to the <s>tīrthyas</s>. By a stratagem, cause him to go forth in the teaching of the Blessed One.' Then the ministers devised a plan: 'Let us show some pretext and install <s>Vītaśoka</s> on the throne.' Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said to <s>Vītaśoka</s>: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, while I go to a pleasure resort, you shall administer this kingdom. When I return from the pleasure resort, I shall resume rule.' Thus he was installed. Another time, one man among those ministers went to <s>Vītaśoka</s> and said: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> has dispatched agents with this order: "Whoever does not obey my command, his head shall be cut off."' Then <s>Vītaśoka</s>, terrified, said to him: 'If that is so, quickly assemble allies and provisions for me.' He replied: 'Do not fear. The one sent by the king — by that same king, Your Majesty, has been summoned back from the pleasure resort. The king invited you, Your Majesty, and went to the pleasure resort, but you do not enjoy the royal splendor, you do not watch the theatrical performances, you do not listen to the sweet voices of the women.'

body.text:
273.001. <273>yāvadvītaśoka ucyate--saśastrairvadhyaghātairasmābhiḥ parivṛto 'sīti/
273.001. tato 'mātyā rājñaḥ pādayor nipalyovāca--deva, marṣaya vītaśokam/
273.002. devasyaiṣa bhrātā/
273.002. tato rājñā abhihitam--saptāhamasya marṣayāmi/
273.003. bhrātā caiṣaḥ/
273.003. mama bhrātuḥ snehādasya saptāhaṃ rājyaṃ prayacchāmi/
273.003. yāvat tūryaśatāni saṃpravāditāni, jayaśabdaiścānanditam, prāṇiśatasahasraiścāñjaliḥ kṛtaḥ, strīśataiśca parivṛtaḥ/
273.005. vadhyaghātakāśca dvāri tiṣṭhanti/
273.005. divase gate vītaśokasyāgrataḥ sthitvā ārocayanti--nirgataṃ vītaśoka ekaṃ divasam/
273.006. ṣaḍahānyavaśiṣṭāni/
273.006. evaṃ dvitīye divase/
273.006. vistareṇa yāvatsaptāhadivase vītaśoko rājālaṃkāravibhūṣito rājño 'śokasya samīpamupanītaḥ/
273.007. tato rājñā aśokenābhihitam--vītaśoka, kañcitsugītaṃ sunṛtyaṃ suvāditamiti ? vītaśoka uvāca--na me dṛṣṭaṃ vā syācchrutaṃ veti/
273.009. āha ca--
273.010. yena śrutaṃ bhavedgītaṃ nṛtyaṃ cāpi nirīkṣitam/
273.011. rasāścāsvāditā yena sa bhūyāttava nirṇayam//2//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vītaśoka</s> was told: 'You are surrounded by armed executioners.' Then a minister fell at the king's feet and said: 'Your Majesty, forgive <s>Vītaśoka</s>. He is Your Majesty's brother.' Then King <s>Aśoka</s> granted him the kingdom for seven days. Gardens were appointed, and accompanied by a hundred jewel-like women, he watched various theatrical performances. The minister <s>Nirdharmaśaṅkha</s> said: 'Your Majesty, King <s>Aśoka</s> has returned and will have you killed.' When the seven days were complete, <s>Vītaśoka</s> was told: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> has arrived, and you are surrounded by executioners. The time of execution is at hand; the seven days are over.' <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: 'I have not performed any act of kingship.' Then the minister said: 'Your Majesty, how could you be expected to perform acts of kingship? In such a brief moment you enjoyed the royal splendor. Hundreds of musical instruments were played, the victory cry was given, hundreds of salutations with joined palms were offered, and you were attended by hundreds of women.' Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, did you enjoy the royal splendor?' 'No, Your Majesty, I did not enjoy the kingdom for seven days. I did not partake of anything at all.'

body.text:
273.012. rājā āha--vītaśoka, idaṃ mayā rājyaṃ saptāhaṃ tava dattam, tūryaśatāni saṃpravāditāni, jayaśabdaiścānanditam, añjaliśatāni pragṛhītāni, strīśataiśca paricīrṇaḥ/
273.013. kathaṃ tvaṃ kathayasi--naiva me dṛṣṭaṃ na śrutamiti? vītaśoka uvāca--
273.015. na me dṛṣṭaṃ nṛtyaṃ na ca nṛpa śruto gītaninado na me gandhā ghrātā na khalu rasā me 'dya viditāḥ/
273.017. na me spṛṣṭaḥ sparśaḥ kanakamaṇihārāṅgajanitaḥ samūho nārīṇāṃ maraṇaparibaddhena manasā//3//
body.translated_text: The king said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, I gave you this kingdom for seven days; hundreds of musical instruments were played, it was celebrated with cries of victory, hundreds of salutations were offered, and you were attended by hundreds of women. How can you say "I did not partake"? How is it that this kingdom was given to you for seven days, and yet you did not partake?' <s>Vītaśoka</s> replied: 'The shadow does not remain under the control of men who lack courage. And surrounded by executioners, what royal splendor is there for me?' (verse 2)

body.text:
273.019. striyo nṛttaṃ gītaṃ bhavaśayanānyāsanavidhirvayo rūpaṃ lakṣmīrbahuvividharatnā ca vasudhā/
273.021. nirānandā śūnyā mama nṛpa varaśayyā gatasukhā sthitān dṛṣṭvā dvāre vadhakapuruṣānnīlavasanān//4//
body.translated_text: Women, dance, song, excellent couches and seats, youth, beauty, prosperity, and an earth rich with many varied gems — all were joyless, empty; the excellent bed was devoid of pleasure for me, O king, when I saw the executioners standing at the door in dark garments. (verse 3)

body.text:
273.023. śrutvā ghaṇṭāravaṃ ghoraṃ nīlāmbaradharasya hi/
273.024. bhayaṃ me maraṇājjātaṃ pārthivendra sudāruṇam//5//
body.translated_text: Having heard the terrible sound of the bell of the one wearing dark garments, fear of death arose in me, O lord of the earth, most dreadful. (verse 5)

body.text:
273.025. mṛtyuśalyaparīto 'haṃ nāśrauṣīdgītamuttamam/
273.026. nādrākṣaṃ nṛpate nṛttaṃ na ca bhoktuṃ manaḥspṛhā//6//
body.translated_text: Pierced by the dart of death, I did not hear the finest song, nor did I see the dance, O king, nor did my mind desire to eat. (verse 6)

body.text:
273.027. mṛtyujvaragṛhītasya na me svapno 'pi vidyate/
273.028. kṛtsnā me rajanī yātā mṛtyumevānucintayan//7//
body.translated_text: For one seized by the fever of death, there is not even sleep. My entire night passed in contemplating nothing but death. (verse 7)

body.text:
273.029. rājā āha--vītaśoka, mā tāvat tavaikajanmikasya maraṇabhayāttava rājaśriyaṃ prāpya harṣo notpannaḥ/
273.030. kiṃ punarbhikṣavo janmaśatamaraṇabhayabhītāḥ sarvāṇyupapattyāyatanāni duḥkhānyanusṛtāni paśyanti/
273.031. narake tāvaccharīrasaṃtāpakṛtamagnidāhaduḥkhaṃ ca, tiryakṣu anyonyabhakṣaṇaparitrāsaduḥkham, preteṣu kṣuttarṣaduḥkham, paryeṣṭisamudācāraduḥkhaṃ manuṣyeṣu, cyavanapatanabhraṃśaduḥkham<274> deveṣu/
body.translated_text: The king said: '<s>Vītaśoka</s>, do not be so — you, fearing death in just this one lifetime, having attained royal splendor, felt no joy. How much more so the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), who, frightened by the fear of death across hundreds of births, contemplating all the realms of rebirth as suffering, fulfill the accumulations for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Just as those executioners in dark garments, bells in hand, follow after the condemned, so too do those forms of death — birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — follow beings through hundreds of births. By these five sufferings, the entire triple world is beset.'

body.text:
274.001. ebhiḥ pañcabhirduḥkhaistrailokyamanuṣaktam/
274.001. śārīramānasairduḥkhairutpīḍitā vadhakabhūtān skandhān paśyanti, śūnyagrāmabhūtānyāyatanāni, cauribhūtāni viṣayāṇi, kṛtsnaṃ ca traidhātukamanityatāgninā pradīptaṃ paśyanti/
274.003. teṣāṃ rāgāḥ kathamutpadyate? āha ca--
274.004. mā tāvadekajanmikasya maraṇabhayāttava na jāyate harṣaḥ/
274.005. manasi viṣayairmanojñaiḥ satataṃ khalu paśyamānasya//8//
body.translated_text: By these five sufferings, the entire triple world is beset. Afflicted by physical and mental sufferings, they see the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) as murderers, the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) as empty villages, the sense objects as thieves, and the entire triple realm as unvanquished yet without delight, without refuge, without shelter, without a lamp, without protection. And he spoke: 'Good sir, forgive the <s>bhikṣus</s>, for they are frightened of death, just like you. Constantly pursued by the fear of death, they find no satisfaction even in food.' (verse 8)

body.text:
274.006. kiṃ punarjanmaśatānāṃ maraṇabhayamanāgataṃ vicintayatām/
274.007. manasi bhaviṣyati harṣo bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojanādyeṣu //9//
body.translated_text: How much less, for those who contemplate the future fear of death across hundreds of births, will there be joy in the <s>bhikṣus</s>' minds regarding food and other things? (verse 9)

body.text:
274.008. teṣāṃ tu vastraśayanāsanabhojanādi mokṣo 'bhiyuktamanasāṃ janayeta saṅgam/
274.010. paśyanti ye vadhakaśatrunibhaṃ śarīramādīptaveśmasadṛśāṃśca bhavānanityān //10//
body.translated_text: For those whose minds are devoted to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), would clothing, bedding, seats, and food generate attachment — they who see the body as resembling a murderous enemy, and impermanent existences as similar to a house on fire? (verse 10)

body.text:
274.012. kathaṃ ca teṣāṃ na bhavedvimokṣo mokṣārthināṃ janmaparānmukhānām/
274.014. yeṣāṃ manaḥ sarvasukhāśrayeṣu vyāvartate padmadalādivāmbhaḥ//11//
body.translated_text: And how could liberation not come to those who seek <s>mokṣa</s>, who have turned away from rebirth, whose minds turn away from all bases of pleasure, like water from a lotus petal? (verse 11)

body.text:
274.016. yadā vītaśoko rājñā aśokenopāyena bhagavacchāsane 'bhiprasāditaḥ, sa kṛtakarapuṭa uvāca--deva, eṣo 'haṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksambuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ceti/
āha ca--
274.019. eṣa vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ vibuddhanavakamalavimalanibhanetram/
274.020. budhavibudhamanujamahitaṃ jinaṃ virāgaṃ ca saṃghaṃ ca//12//iti/
274.021. atha rājā aśoko vītaśokaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajyovāca--na tvaṃ mayā parityaktaḥ, api tu buddhaśāsanābhiprasādārthaṃ tava mayā eṣa upāyaḥ pradarśitaḥ/
274.022. tato vītaśoko gandhapuṣpamālyādivāditrasamudayena bhagavataścaityānarcayati, saddharmaṃ ca śṛṇoti, saṃghe ca kārāṃ kurute/
274.024. sa kurkuṭārāmaṃ gataḥ/
274.024. tatra yaśo nāṃ sthaviro 'rhan ṣaḍabhijñaḥ/
274.024. sa tasya purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
274.025. sthaviraśca tamavalolayitumārabdhaḥ/
274.025. sa paśyati vītaśokamupacitahetukaṃ caramabhavikam/
274.026. tenaivāśrayenārhattvaṃ prāptavyam/
274.026. tena tasya pravrajyāyā varṇo bhāṣitaḥ/
274.027. tasya śrutvā spṛhā jātā--pravrajeyaṃ bhagavacchāsane/
274.027. tata utthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ sthavitamuvāca--labheyāhaṃ svakhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
274.028. careyamahaṃ bhavato 'ntike brahmacaryam/
274.029. sthavira uvāca--vatsa, rājānamaśokamanujñāpayasveti/
274.029. tato vītaśoko yena rājā aśokastenopasaṃkramya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--deva, anujānīhi mām/
274.030. pravrajiṣyāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikām/
274.031. āha ca--
body.translated_text: When <s>Vītaśoka</s> was brought to faith in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) through a stratagem by King <s>Aśoka</s>, he, with palms joined together, said: "Your Majesty, I go to that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s> (Teaching), and to the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (Community of Monks)." And he said: "I go for refuge to the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), whose eyes are pure like fresh lotuses of awakening, who is honored by the wise, the gods, and humans, who is free from passion, and to the <s>Saṃgha</s> (Community)." (12) Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, embracing <s>Vītaśoka</s> around the neck, said: "You were not abandoned by me; rather, this stratagem was shown to you by me for the purpose of bringing you to faith in the Buddha's teaching." Thereupon <s>Vītaśoka</s> worshipped the <s>caityas</s> (shrines) of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with an assembly of incense, flowers, garlands, and musical instruments, listened to the <s>Saddharma</s> (True Teaching), and rendered service to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. He went to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery). There was an elder named <s>Yaśas</s>, an <s>Arhat</s> possessed of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges). He sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The elder began to examine him. He saw that <s>Vītaśoka</s> had accumulated the requisite causes and was in his final existence. With that very bodily support he was to attain <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship). Therefore he spoke to him of the merits of going forth. Having heard this, a longing arose in him: "Let me go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." Then, rising and joining his palms, he said to the elder: "May I obtain the going forth, the <s>upasaṃpadā</s> (full ordination), and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharmavinaya</s> (Teaching and Discipline). Let me practice the <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life) in your presence." The elder said: "My son, obtain permission from King <s>Aśoka</s>." Then <s>Vītaśoka</s> approached King <s>Aśoka</s> and, with palms joined, said: "Your Majesty, grant me permission. I shall go forth from the household life into homelessness in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharmavinaya</s>, with complete faith." And he said:

body.text:
275.001. <275>udbhrānto 'smi niraṅkuśo rājā iva vyāvartito vibhramāt tvadbuddhiprabhavāṅkuśena vidhivadbuddhopadeśairaham/
275.001. ekaṃ tvamarhasi me varaṃ pradarśituṃ tvaṃ pārthivānāṃ pate lokālokavarasya śāsanavare liṅgaṃ śibhaṃ dhārayet//13//
body.translated_text: "I was a maddened elephant without a goad, but I have been turned back from delusion by the goad born of your wisdom, fittingly, through the teachings of the <s>Buddha</s>. You should grant me this one boon, O lord of kings: let me wear the auspicious mark of the supreme teaching of the best of the world-illuminators." (13)

body.text:
275.005. śrutvā ca rājā sāśrukaṇṭho vītaśokaṃ kaṇṭhe pariṣvajyovāca--vītaśoka, alamanena vyavasāyena/
275.006. pravrajya khalu vaivarṇikābhyupagatāvasaḥ, pāṃśukūlaṃ pravaraṇaṃ parijanojjñitam, āhāro bhaiṣyaṃ parakule, śayanāsanaṃ vṛkṣamūle tṛṇasaṃstaraḥ parṇasaṃstaraḥ, vyābādhe khalvapi bhaiṣajyamasulabhaṃ pūtimūtraṃ ca bhojanam/
275.008. tvaṃ ca sukumāraḥ śītoṣṇakṣutpipāsānāṃ duḥkhānāmasahiṣṇuḥ/
275.009. prasīda, nivartaya mānasam/
275.009. vītaśoka uvāca--deva,
275.010. naiva hi jāne taṃ nūnaṃ viṣayatṛṣito 'nāyāsavihataḥ pravrajyāṃ prāptukāmo na ripuhṛtabalo naivārthakṛpaṇaḥ/
275.012. duḥkhārtaṃ mṛtyuneṣṭaṃ vyasanaparigataṃ dṛṣṭvā jagadidaṃ panthānaṃ janmabhīruḥ śivamabhayamahaṃ gantuṃ vyavasitaḥ//14//
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, his throat choked with tears, embraced <s>Vītaśoka</s> around the neck and said: "<s>Vītaśoka</s>, enough of this resolve! Having gone forth, you will live in a state of discolored garments, wearing rags discarded by others as your robe, eating alms-food in others' houses, sleeping at the foot of trees on a bed of grass or leaves, and when ill, medicine is hard to obtain, and fermented urine is your sustenance. You are delicate, unable to endure the sufferings of cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. Please, turn your mind from this." <s>Vītaśoka</s> said: "Your Majesty, surely he does not know that one who is not afflicted by thirst for sense pleasures, not struck down without effort, who desires to attain the going forth, is not one whose power has been seized by enemies, nor one wretched for wealth. Seeing this world afflicted by suffering, seized by death, beset by calamities, I, fearing birth, am resolved to go on the auspicious, fearless path." (14)

body.text:
275.014. śrutvā ca rājā aśokaḥ satvaraṃ praruditumārabdhaḥ/
275.014. atha vītaśoko rājānamanunayannuvāca--deva,
275.016. saṃsāradolāmabhiruhya lolam yadā nipāto niyataḥ prajānām/
275.018. kimarthamāgacchati vikriyā te sarveṇa sarvasya yadā viyogaḥ//15//
body.translated_text: Having heard this, King <s>Aśoka</s> immediately began to weep. Then <s>Vītaśoka</s>, consoling the king, said: "Your Majesty, when beings who have mounted the swinging swing of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) are destined to fall, why does this distress come upon you, when for everyone there is separation from everything?" (15)

body.text:
275.020. rājā āha--vītaśoka, bhaikṣe tāvadabhyāsaḥ kriyatām/
275.020. rājakule vṛkṣavāṭikāyāṃ tasya tṛṇasaṃstaraḥ saṃstṛtaḥ, bhojanaṃ cāsya dattam/
275.021. so 'ntaḥpuraṃ paryaṭati, mahārhaṃ cāhāraṃ na labhate/
275.022. tato rājñā antaḥpurikā abhihitā--pravrajitasārūpyamasyāhāramanuprayacchateti/
275.022. tena yāvadabhidūṣitā pūtikulmāṣā labdhāḥ/
275.023. tāṃśca paribhoktumārabdhaḥ/
275.023. dṛṣṭvā rājñā aśokena nivāritaḥ/
275.024. tasya buddhirutpannā--yadīha pravrajiṣyāmi, ākīrṇo bhaviṣyāmi/
275.025. tato videheṣu janapadeṣu gatvā pravrajitaḥ/
275.026. tatastena yujyatā yāvadarhattvaṃ prāptam/
275.026. athāyuṣmato vītaśokasyārhattvaṃ prāptasya vimuktiprītisukhasaṃvedina etadabhavat--asti khalu me--pūrvaṃ rājño 'śokasya gṛhadvāramanuprāptaḥ/
275.028. tato dauvārikamuvāca--gaccha, rājño 'śokasya nivedaya--vītaśoko dvāri tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti/
275.029. tato dauvāriko rājānamaśokamabhigamyovāca--deva, diṣṭyā vṛddhiḥ/
275.030. vītaśoko 'bhyāgato dvāri tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ/
275.030. tato rājñā abhihitam--gaccha, śīghraṃ praveśayeti/
275.031. yāvadvītaśoko rājakulaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
275.031. dṛṣṭvā ca rajā aśokaḥ saṃhāsanādutthāya mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇāyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokaṃ nirīkṣamānaḥ prarudannuvāca--
body.translated_text: The king said: "<s>Vītaśoka</s>, first let the practice of begging be undertaken." In the royal grounds, in the garden, a bed of grass was spread for him, and food was given to him. He wandered within the inner palace, yet did not receive fine food. Then the king instructed the women of the inner palace: "Give him food befitting one who has gone forth." Thereupon he received spoiled, foul-smelling barley porridge. He began to eat it. Seeing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> stopped him. This thought arose in him: "If I go forth here, I will be encumbered." Therefore, having gone to the <s>Videha</s> country, he went forth. Then, while striving, he attained <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship). Then the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, having attained <s>Arhattva</s>, experiencing the bliss and joy of liberation, thought: "I indeed have — formerly I arrived at the gate of King <s>Aśoka</s>'s residence." Then he said to the doorkeeper: "Go, announce to King <s>Aśoka</s>: '<s>Vītaśoka</s> stands at the door, wishing to see His Majesty.'" The doorkeeper, approaching King <s>Aśoka</s>, said: "Your Majesty, good fortune and prosperity! <s>Vītaśoka</s> has come and stands at the door, wishing to see Your Majesty." Then the king commanded: "Go, let him enter quickly." Thereupon <s>Vītaśoka</s> entered the royal palace. Seeing him, King <s>Aśoka</s>, rising from his throne like a tree cut at the root, gazing at the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> with his entire body, said weeping:

body.text:
276.001. <276>bhūteṣu saṃsargagateṣu nityaṃ dṛṣṭvāpi māṃ naiti yathā vikāram/
276.003. vivekavegādhigatasya śaṅke prajñārasasyātirasasya tṛptaḥ//16//
body.translated_text: "Though you see me, one who is always attached to contact with living beings, you undergo no change of feeling; I think you are sated with the flavor of the supreme <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), having attained the force of detachment." (16)

body.text:
276.005. atha rājño 'śokasya rādhagupto nāmāgrāmātyaḥ/
276.005. sa paśyati--āyuṣmato vītaśokasya pāṃśukūlaṃ ca cīvaraṃ mṛṇmayaṃ pātram yāvadannaṃ bhaikṣyaṃ lūhapraṇītam/
276.006. dṛṣṭvā ca rājñaḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--deva, yathā ayamalpecchaḥ saṃtuṣṭaśca, niyatamayaṃ kṛtakaraṇīyo bhaviṣyati, prītirutpādyeta/
276.008. kṛtah?
276.009. bhaikṣānnabhojanam yasya pāṃśukūlaṃ ca cīvaram/
276.010. nivāso vṛkṣamūlaṃ ca tasyāniyataṃ katham//17//
body.translated_text: Now King <s>Aśoka</s> had a chief minister named <s>Rādhagupta</s>. He observed the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>'s rag-cloth robe, earthen bowl, and alms-food, plain and coarse. Seeing this, he fell at the king's feet and, with palms joined, said: "Your Majesty, since he is of few desires and content, surely he must have accomplished what was to be done; let joy arise! Is it accomplished? 'He whose food is alms, whose robe is rags, whose dwelling is the foot of a tree — how can he possibly be unsettled?'" (17)

body.text:
276.011. nirāśravam yasya mano viśālaṃ nirāmayaṃ copacitaṃ śarīram/
276.013. svacchandato jīvitasādhanaṃ ca nityotsavaṃ tasya manuṣyaloke//18//
body.translated_text: "He whose mind is vast and free from impurities, whose body is healthy and well-nourished, who sustains his life freely — for him it is an eternal festival in the human world." (18)

body.text:
276.015. śrutvā tato rājā prītamanā uvāca--
276.016. apahāya mauryavaṃśaṃ magadhapuraṃ sarvaratnanicayaṃ ca/
276.017. dṛṣṭvā vaṃśānivahaṃ prahīṇamadamānamohasārambham//19//
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king, his mind delighted, said: "Having left behind the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty, the city of <s>Magadha</s>, and the entire store of jewels, seeing the succession of dynasties, he has abandoned intoxication, pride, delusion, and aggression." (19)

body.text:
276.018. atyuddhṛtamiva manye yaśasā pūtaṃ puramiva mahaṃ ca/
276.019. pratipadyatāṃ tvayā daśabaladharaśāsanamudāreṇa//20//
body.translated_text: "I think the city and the dynasty have been supremely uplifted, purified by his fame. May the noble teaching of the Bearer of the Ten Powers be followed by you!" (20)

body.text:
276.020. atha rājā aśokaḥ sarvāṅgena parigṛhya prajñapta evāsane niṣādayāmāsa, praṇītena cāhāreṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati/
276.021. bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastamapanītapātramāyuṣmato vītaśokasya purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
276.022. athāyuṣmān vītaśoko rājānamaśokaṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayannuvāca--
276.024. apramādena saṃpādya rājyaiśvaryaṃ pravartatām/
276.025. durlabhā trīṇi ratnāni nityaṃ pūjaya pārthiva//21//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, embracing him with his whole body, seated him on a prepared seat and satisfied him with his own hands with fine food. Knowing that he had eaten, and that his hands were washed and his bowl removed, he sat down before the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, instructing King <s>Aśoka</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, said: "Exerting yourselves with diligence, let the rule of the kingdom proceed; the Three Jewels are rare — always worship them, O king." (21)

body.text: 276.026. sa yāvadharmyayā kathayā saṃharṣayitvā saṃprasthitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Having thus gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he set out on his way.

body.text:
276.027. atha rājā aśokaḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ pañcabhiramātyaśataiḥ parivṛto 'nekaiśca paurajanapadasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛta āyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokamanuvrajitumārabdhaḥ/
276.028. vakṣyati hi--
276.029. bhrātā jyeṣṭhena rājñā tu gauraveṇānugamyate/
276.030. pravrajyāyāḥ khalu ślādhyaṃ saṃdṛṣṭikamidaṃ phalam//22//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, with palms joined, surrounded by five hundred ministers and accompanied and preceded by many thousands of citizens and country-folk, began to follow after the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>. For it will be said: "The elder brother was followed by the king with great respect. This is the praiseworthy, visible fruit of going forth." (22)

body.text:
277.001. <277>tata āyuṣmān vītaśokaḥ svaguṇānudbhāvayan paśyataḥ sarvajanakāyasya ṛddhyā vaihāyasamutpatya prakrāntaḥ/
277.002. atha rājā aśokaḥ kṛtakarapuṭaḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto gaganatalāvasaktadṛṣṭirāyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokaṃ nirīkṣamāṇa uvāca--
277.004. svajanasnehaniḥsaṅgo vihaṃga iva gacchasi/
277.005. śrīrāganigadairbaddhānasmān pratyādiśānniva//23//
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, not displaying his own virtues, rose up into the sky by means of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) before the eyes of all the assembled people, and departed. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, with palms joined, surrounded and preceded by hundreds of thousands of living beings, his gaze fixed upon the vault of the sky, watching the Venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, said: "Free from attachment to the affection of kinsmen, you depart like a bird, as if rebuking us who are bound by the fetters of <s>śrī</s> (worldly glory) and <s>rāga</s> (passion)." (23)

body.text:
277.006. ātmāyattasya śāntasya mahaḥsaṃketacāriṇaḥ/
277.007. dhyānasya phalametacca rāgāndhairyanna dṛśyate//24//
body.translated_text: "This is the fruit of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) for one who is self-dependent, at peace, moving in the realm of great purpose, and it is not seen by those blinded by passion." (24)

body.text:
277.008. api ca/
277.009. ṛddhyā khalvavabhartsatāḥ paramayā śrīgarvitāste vayaṃ buddhyā khalvapi nāmitāḥ śirasitāḥ prajñābhimānodayam/
277.011. prāptārthena phalāndhabuddhimanasaḥ saṃvejitāste vayaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa sabāṣpadurdinamukhāḥ sthāne vimuktā vayam//25//
body.translated_text: "Moreover — Truly, by supreme <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) we who were proud of glory have been rebuked; truly by his wisdom too we who held conceit of intellect have had our heads bowed down. Having attained the goal, we whose minds were blind with the fruit, have been stirred to urgency; in brief, with tearful, downcast faces, we have been set free, fittingly so." (25)

body.text:
277.013. tatrāyuṣmān vītaśokaḥ pratyantimeṣu janapadeṣu śayyāsanāya nirgataḥ/
277.013. tasya ca mahān vyādhirutpannaḥ/
277.014. śrutvā ca rājñā aśokena bhaiṣajyamupasthāyikāśca visarjitāḥ/
277.014. tasya tena vyādhinā spṛṣṭasya śiraḥ khustamabhavat/
277.015. yadā ca vyādhirvigataḥ, tasya virūṭāni śirasi romāṇi/
277.016. tena vaidyopasthāyakāśca visarjitāḥ/
277.016. tasya ca gorasaprāya āhāro 'nusevyate/
277.016. sa ghoṣaṃ gatvā bhaikṣyaṃ paryaṭati/
277.017. tasmiṃśca samaye puṇḍravardhananagare nirgranthopāsakena buddhapratimā nirgranthasya pādayor nipātitā citrārpitā/
277.018. upāsakenāśokasya rājño niveditam/
277.018. śrutvā ca rājñā abhihitam--śīghramānīyatām/
277.019. tasyordhvam yojanam yakṣāḥ śṛṇvanti, adho yojanaṃ nāgāḥ/
277.019. yāvattaṃ tatkṣaṇena yakṣairupanītam/
277.020. dṛṣṭvā ca rājñā ruṣitenābhihitam--puṇḍravardhane sarve ājīvikāḥ praghātayitavyāḥ/
277.021. yāvadekadivase 'ṣṭādaśasahasrāṇyājīvikānāṃ praghātitāni/
277.021. tataḥ pāṭaliputre bhūyo 'nyena nirgranthopāsakena buddhapratimā nirgranthasya pādayor nipātitā citrārpitā/
277.022. śrutvā ca rājñā amarṣitena sa nirgranthopāsakaḥ sabandhuvargo gṛhaṃ praveśāyitvā agninā dagdhaḥ/
277.023. ājñaptaṃ ca--yo me nirgranthasya śiro dāsyati, tasya dīnāraṃ dāsyāmīti/
277.024. ghoṣitam/
277.024. sa cāyuṣmān vītaśoka ābhīrasya gṛhe rātriṃ vāsamupagataḥ/
277.025. tasya ca vyādhinā kliṣṭasya lūhāni cīvarāṇi, dīrghakeśanakhaśmaśruḥ/
277.026. ābhīryā buddhirutpannā--nirgrantho 'yamasmākaṃ gṛhe rātriṃ vāsamupagataḥ/
277.027. svāminamuvāca--āryaputra, saṃpanno 'yamasmākaṃ dīnāraḥ/
277.027. imaṃ nirgranthaṃ praghātayitvā śiro rājño 'śokasyopanāmayeyamiti/
277.028. tataḥ sa ābhīro 'siṃ niṣkoṣaṃ kṛtvā āyuṣmantaṃ vītaśokamabhigataḥ/
277.029. āyuṣmatā ca vītaśokena pūrvānte jñānaṃ kṣiptam/
277.029. paśyati svayaṃkṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalamidamupasthitam/
277.030. tataḥ karmapratiśaraṇo bhūtvā avasthitaḥ/
277.030. tena tathāsyābhīreṇa śiraśchinnam/
277.031. rājño 'śokasyopanītam--dīnāraṃ prayaccheti/
277.031. dṛṣṭvā ca rājñā aśokena parijñātam--viralāni cāsya śirasi romāṇi na vyaktimupagacchanti/
277.032. tato vaidyā upasthāyakā ānītāḥ/
277.032. tairdṛṣṭvā <278>abhihitam--deva, vītaśokasyaitacchiraḥ/
body.translated_text: There the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> went out to the border regions for lodging. And a great illness arose in him. Having heard this, King <s>Aśoka</s> sent medicines and attendants. Afflicted by that illness, his head became shaved. When the illness departed, the hairs on his head had grown back sparsely. He then dismissed the physicians and attendants. His diet consisted mostly of cow's milk. He went to a cowherd settlement and wandered about for alms. At that time, in the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, an image of the <s>Buddha</s> was cast down at the feet of a <s>Nirgrantha</s> and depicted thus by a <s>Nirgrantha</s> lay-devotee. A lay-follower reported this to King <s>Aśoka</s>. Having heard, the king commanded: "Let it be brought here at once!" Above him for one <s>yojana</s> (league) the <s>Yakṣas</s> hear, and below for one <s>yojana</s> the <s>Nāgas</s>. In that very instant it was brought by the <s>Yakṣas</s>. Having seen it, the enraged king declared: "In <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>, all <s>Ājīvikas</s> are to be slain!" In a single day, eighteen thousand <s>Ājīvikas</s> were slaughtered. Then in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, yet another <s>Nirgrantha</s> lay-devotee cast down an image of the <s>Buddha</s> at the feet of a <s>Nirgrantha</s> and depicted it thus. Having heard, the furious king had that <s>Nirgrantha</s> lay-devotee together with his kinsmen driven into a house and burned with fire. And he issued a decree: "Whoever brings me the head of a <s>Nirgrantha</s>, to him I shall give a <s>dīnāra</s> (gold coin)." This was proclaimed. Now the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> had come to the house of a cowherd for the night's lodging. Afflicted by illness, his robes were ragged, and his hair, nails, and beard had grown long. The cowherd's wife had the thought: "This <s>Nirgrantha</s> has come to our house for the night's lodging." She said to her husband: "Noble son, our <s>dīnāra</s> is secured! Let us slay this <s>Nirgrantha</s> and present his head to King <s>Aśoka</s>." Then that cowherd, drawing his sword from its sheath, approached the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>. The venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s> cast his knowledge into his former births. He saw that the fruit of his own past deeds had now arrived. Then, taking refuge in <s>karma</s> (the law of deeds), he remained still. The cowherd cut off his head in that manner. It was brought to King <s>Aśoka</s>: "Give the <s>dīnāra</s>." But King <s>Aśoka</s>, having seen it, recognized it — the sparse hairs on his head were unmistakable. Then the physicians and attendants were summoned. Having examined it, they declared: "Your Majesty, this is the head of <s>Vītaśoka</s>."

body.text:
278.001. śrutvā rājā mūrcchito bhūmau patitaḥ/
278.001. yāvajjalasekaṃ datvā sthāpitaḥ/
278.002. amātyaiścābhihitam--deva, vītarāgāṇāmapyatra pīḍā/
278.002. dīyatāṃ sarvasattveṣvabhayapradānam/
278.003. yāvadrājñā abhayapradānaṃ dattam--na bhūyaḥ kaścit praghātayitavyaḥ//
body.translated_text: Having heard this, the king fainted and fell to the ground. They revived him by sprinkling water upon him. The ministers said: "Your Majesty, even those free from passion feel anguish in such matters. Let a grant of safety be given to all beings." Thereupon the king issued a grant of fearlessness: "No one is to be slain henceforth!"

body.text: 278.004. tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāramāyuṣmantamupaguptaṃ pṛcchanti--kiṃ karma kṛtamāyuṣmatā vītaśokena yasya karmaṇo vipākena śastreṇa praghātitah? sthavira uvāca--tena hyāyuṣmantaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having doubts, asked the venerable <s>Upagupta</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What <s>karma</s> (deed) was done by the venerable <s>Vītaśoka</s>, by the ripening of which he was slain by a weapon?" The Elder said: "Listen then, venerable ones — he performed deeds previously in other births."

body.text:
278.006. śrūyatām--
278.007. bhutapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani anyatamo lubdho mṛgān praghātayitvā jīvikāṃ kalpayati/
278.008. aṭavyāmudapānam/
278.008. sa tatra lubdho gatvā pāśān yantrāṃśca sthāpayitvā mṛgān praghātayati/
278.009. asti buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante/
278.009. vistaraḥ/
278.009. anyataraḥ pratyekabuddhastasminnudapāne āhārakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā udapānāduttīrya vṛkṣamūle paryaṅkena niṣaṇṇaḥ/
278.010. tasya gandhena mṛgāstasminnudapāne nābhyāgatāḥ/
278.011. sa lubdha āgatya paśyati--neiva mṛgā udapānamabhyāgatāḥ/
278.012. padānusāreṇa ca taṃ pratyekabuddhamabhigataḥ/
278.012. dṛṣṭvā cāsya buddhirutpannā--anenaiṣa ādīnava utpāditaḥ/
278.013. tenāsiṃ niṣkoṣaṃ kṛtvā sa pratyekabuddhaḥ praghātitaḥ//
body.translated_text: "Listen — Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), in a past age, a certain hunter made his livelihood by slaughtering deer. In the forest there was a watering hole. That hunter, going there, set snares and traps and slaughtered the deer. When <s>Buddhas</s> do not arise in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) appear. The rest is told in detail. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, having taken his meal at that watering hole, climbed out and sat cross-legged at the foot of a tree. Because of his scent, the deer did not come to that watering hole. The hunter came and saw that no deer had come to the watering hole. Following the footprints, he approached that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Seeing him, this thought arose in him: 'This one has caused this misfortune.' Drawing his sword from its sheath, he slew that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>."

body.text:
278.014. kiṃ manyadhve āyuṣmantah? yo 'sau lubdhaḥ sa eṣa vītaśokaḥ/
278.014. yatrānena megāḥ praghātitāḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena mahān vyādhirutpannaḥ/
278.015. yatpratyekabuddhaḥ śastreṇa praghātitaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi narakeṣu duḥkhamanubhūya pañca janmaśatāni manuṣyeṣūpapannaḥ śastreṇa praghātitaḥ/
278.017. tatkarmāvaśeṣeṇaitarhi arhatprāpto 'pi śastreṇa praghātitaḥ//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, venerable ones? That hunter — he is this very <s>Vītaśoka</s>. Because he slaughtered the deer, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> (deed), a great illness arose in him. Because the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> was slain by a weapon, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, having suffered torment in the hells for many thousands of years, he was born among humans for five hundred lifetimes and was slain by a weapon each time. By the remainder of that very <s>karma</s>, even now, though he had attained <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat), he was slain by a weapon."

body.text:
278.018. kiṃ karma kṛtam yenoccakule upapannaḥ, arhattvaṃ ca prāptam? sthavira uvāca--kāśyape samyaksambuddhe pravrajito 'bhūt pradānaruciḥ/
278.019. tena dāyakadānapatayaḥ saṃghabhaktaṃ kārāpitāstarpaṇāni yavāgūpānāni nimantraṇakāni/
278.020. stūpeṣu ca cchatrāṇyavaropitāni, dhvajāḥ patākāḥ/
278.021. gandhamālyapuṣpavāditrasamudayena pūjāḥ kṛtāḥ/
278.021. tasya karmaṇo vipākenoccakule upapannaḥ/
278.022. yāvaddaśavarṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryaṃ caritvā samyakpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, tasya karmaṇo vipākenārhattvaṃ prāptamiti//
body.translated_text: "What <s>karma</s> (deed) did he perform by which he was born in a high family and attained <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship)?" The Elder said: "Under the perfectly enlightened <s>Kāśyapa Buddha</s>, he went forth as a renunciant and delighted in giving. He encouraged donors and benefactors to prepare communal meals for the <s>Saṅgha</s> (monastic community) — offerings of food, gruel-distributions, and feast-invitations. He placed parasols upon <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary shrines), along with banners and pennants. He performed worship with an abundance of incense, garlands, flowers, and music. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was born in a high family. Having practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate spiritual life) for ten thousand years and made a right aspiration, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he attained <s>Arhattva</s>."

body.text: 278.024. iti śrīdivyāvadāne vītaśokāvadānamaṣṭāviṃśatimam//
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Vītaśokāvadāna</s> (the legend of <s>Vītaśoka</s>), the twenty-eighth, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text: 279.001. div29 aśokāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 29: The <s>Aśokāvadāna</s> (the legend of <s>Aśoka</s>).

body.text:
279.002. yadā rājñā aśokena ardhāmalakadānena bhagavacchāsane śraddhā pratilabdhā, sa bhikṣūnuvāca--kena bhagavacchāsane prabhūtaṃ dānaṃ dattam? bhikṣava ūcuh--anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā/
279.004. rājā āha--kiyattena bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattam? bhikṣava ūcuh--koṭiśataṃ tena bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattam/
279.005. śrutvā ca rājā aśokaścintayati--tena gṛhapatinā bhūtvā koṭiśataṃ bhagavachāsane dānaṃ dattam/
279.006. tenābhihitam--ahamapi koṭiśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dāsyāmi/
279.007. tena yāvaccaturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam, sarvatra ca śatasahasrāṇi dattāni--jātau, bodhau, dharmacakre, parinirvāṇe ca, sarvatra śatasahasraṃ dattam/
279.008. pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtam/
279.009. tatra ca catvāri śatasahasrāṇi dattāni, trīṇi śatasahasrāṇi bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojitāni yatrekarmahatāṃ dvau śaikṣāṇāṃ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakānāṃ ca/
279.010. kośaṃ sthāpayitvā mahāpṛthivīmantaḥpurāmātyagaṇamātmānaṃ kuṇālaṃ ca āryasaṃghe niryātayitvā catvāri śatasahasrāṇi dattvā niṣkrītavān/
279.012. ṣaṇṇavatikoṭyo bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dattam/
279.012. sa yāvad glānībhūtaḥ/
279.012. atha rājā idānīṃ na bhaviṣyāmīti viklavībhūtaḥ/
279.013. tasya rādhagupto nāmāmātyo yena saha pāṃśudānaṃ dattam/
279.014. tadā sa rājānamaśokaṃ viklavībhūtamavekṣya pādayor nipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--
279.015. yacchatrusaṃghaiḥ prabalaiḥ sametya nodvīkṣitaṃ caṇḍadivākarābham/
279.017. padmānanaśrīśatasamprapītaṃ kasmāt sabāṣpaṃ tava deva vaktram//1//
body.translated_text: When King <s>Aśoka</s> had gained faith in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) through the gift of half a myrobalan fruit, he said to the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks): "Who has given the most abundant gifts to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>." The king said: "How much did he give to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "He gave one hundred <s>koṭis</s> (ten million each) to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." Having heard this, King <s>Aśoka</s> thought: "He, being merely a householder, gave one hundred <s>koṭis</s> to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." He declared: "I too shall give one hundred <s>koṭis</s> to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." He established eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s> (shrines of the King of Dharma), and at each he gave a hundred thousand — at the birth, the enlightenment, the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Law), and the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) — at each, a hundred thousand was given. He held the <s>Pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival). There four hundred thousand were given; three hundred thousand were spent feeding <s>bhikṣus</s>, among whom one portion went to those who had accomplished their task, two to learners, and the rest to virtuous ordinary persons. Setting aside only the treasury, the great earth, the inner palace, the ministers, himself, and <s>Kuṇāla</s>, he surrendered everything to the noble <s>Saṅgha</s> and, having given four hundred thousand, redeemed it all. Ninety-six <s>koṭis</s> had been given to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then he fell ill. The king, thinking "I shall not live much longer," became distressed. He had a minister named <s>Rādhagupta</s>, together with whom he had once made the gift of dirt. Then <s>Rādhagupta</s>, seeing King <s>Aśoka</s> in distress, fell at his feet and, with palms joined, said: "That face, fierce as the blazing sun, which was never gazed upon even by assembled hosts of powerful enemies, resplendent with the beauty of a hundred lotuses — why, O Lord, is your face now tearful?" (1)

body.text:
279.019. rājā āha--rādhagupta, nāhaṃ dravyavināśaṃ na rājyanāśanaṃ na cāśrayaviyogaṃ śocāmi, kiṃ tu śocāmi--āryairyadviprayukṣyāmi/
279.021. nāhaṃ punaḥ sarvaguṇopapannaṃ saṃghaṃ samakṣaṃ naradevapūjitam/
279.023. saṃpūjayiṣyāmi varānnapānairetaṃ vicintyāśruvimokṣaṇam//2//
body.translated_text: The king said: "<s>Rādhagupta</s>, I do not grieve over the loss of wealth, nor the loss of the kingdom, nor separation from loved ones. Rather, I grieve thus: I shall be parted from the Noble Ones. Never again shall I worship in person the <s>Saṅgha</s> (monastic community) endowed with all virtues, honored by kings of men, with excellent food and drink — contemplating this, my tears flow." (2)

body.text:
279.025. api ca rādhagupta, ayaṃ me manoratho babhūva--koṭiśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dānaṃ dāsyāmīti, sa ca me 'bhiprāyo na paripūrṇaḥ/
279.026. tato rājñā aśokena catvāraḥ koṭyaḥ paripūrayiṣyāmīti hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ kurkuṭārāmaṃ praṣayitumārabdhaḥ//
body.translated_text: "Moreover, <s>Rādhagupta</s>, this was my heart's desire: 'I shall give one hundred <s>koṭis</s> to the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' But that intention of mine has not been fulfilled." Thereupon King <s>Aśoka</s> began sending gold and silver to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery), thinking "I shall complete the remaining four <s>koṭis</s>."

body.text:
279.028. tasmiṃśca samaye kuṇālasya saṃpadir nāma putro yuvarājye pravartate/
279.028. tasyāmātyairabhihitam--kumāra, aśoko rājā svalpakālāvasthāyī/
279.029. idaṃ ca dravyaṃ kurkuṭārāmaṃ preṣyate/
279.029. kośabalinaśca rājānaḥ/
279.030. nivārayitavyaḥ/
279.030. yāvat kumāreṇa bhāṇḍāgārikaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ/
279.030. yadā rājño 'śokasyāpratiṣiddhā (tasya) suvarṇabhājane āhāramupanāmyate/
279.031. bhuktvā tāni suvarṇabhājanāni <280>kurkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayati/
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Saṃpadi</s> by name, the son of <s>Kuṇāla</s>, was installed as crown prince. His ministers said to him: "Prince, King <s>Aśoka</s> has but little time remaining. And this wealth is being sent to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s>. Kings are powerful through their treasuries. He must be restrained." Thereupon the prince forbade the treasurer. When King <s>Aśoka</s>'s direct orders could not be countermanded, his food was served to him in golden vessels. Having eaten, he would send those golden vessels to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s>.

body.text:
280.001. tasya suvarṇabhājanaṃ pratiṣiddham/
280.001. rūpyabhājane āhāramupanāmyate, tānyapi kurkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayati/
280.002. tato rūpyabhājanamapi pratiṣiddham, yāvallohabhājana āhāramupanāmyate/
280.003. tānyapi rājā aśokaḥ kurkuṭārāmaṃ preṣayati/
280.003. tasya yāvanmṛdbhājana āhāramupanāmyate/
280.004. tasmiṃśca samaye rājño 'śokasya ardhāmalakaṃ karāntaragatam/
280.004. atha rājā aśokaḥ saṃvigno 'mātyān paurāṃśca saṃnipātya kathayati--kaḥ sāmprataṃ pṛthivyāmīśvarah? tato 'mātya utthāyāsanādyena rājā aśokastenāñjaliṃ praṇamyovāca--deva, pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ/
280.006. atha rājā aśokaḥ sāśrudurdinanayanavadano 'mātyānuvāca--
280.008. dākṣiṇyādanṛtaṃ hi kiṃ kathayata bhraṣṭādhirājyā vayaṃ śeṣaṃ tvāmalakārdhamityavasitam yatra prabhutvaṃ mama/
280.010. eśvaryaṃ dhignāryamuddhatanadītoyapraveśopamaṃ martyendrasya mamāpi yatpratibhayaṃ dāridryamabhyāgatam//3//
body.translated_text: The golden vessels were forbidden to him. His food was then served in silver vessels, and he sent those too to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s>. Then the silver vessels were also forbidden, and his food was served in copper vessels. King <s>Aśoka</s> sent those too to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s>. Then his food was served in earthen vessels. At that time, King <s>Aśoka</s> had but half a myrobalan fruit remaining in his hand. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, deeply moved, summoned his ministers and citizens and said: "Who is now lord of the earth?" A minister rose from his seat, bowed with joined palms toward King <s>Aśoka</s>, and said: "Your Majesty is lord of the earth." Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, his eyes clouded with tears like a rainy sky, said to the ministers: "Why do you speak untruth out of courtesy? I have fallen from sovereign power; my dominion extends only to this half a myrobalan fruit — such is the extent of my authority. Shame on sovereignty, as fleeting as plunging into the waters of a swollen river! Even for me, lord among mortals, this fearful poverty has arrived." (3)

body.text: 280.012. athavā ko bhagavato vākyamanyathā kariṣyati? saṃpattayo hi sarvā vipattinidhanā iti pratijñātam yadavitathavādinā gautamena, na hi tadvisaṃvadati//
body.translated_text: "Moreover, who shall make the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) otherwise? For it has been declared by <s>Gautama</s> the speaker of truth that all prosperities end in ruin — and that does not prove false."

body.text:
280.014. pratiśiṣyate 'smanne cirādājñā mama yāvatī yathā manasā/
280.015. sādyaiva mahādriśilātalavihatanadīvat pratinivṛttā //4//
body.translated_text:
280.014. 'Before long, my command, great as it once was, will be reversed,
280.015. like a river thrown back from the rocky surface of a great mountain.' //4//

body.text:
280.016. ājñāpya vyavadhūtaḍimbaḍamarāmekātapatrāṃ mahīmutpāṭya pratigarvitānarigaṇānāśvāsya dīnāturān/
280.018. bhraṣṭasvāyatano na bhāti kṛpaṇaḥ saṃpratyaśoko nṛpah chinnāmlānaviśīrṇapatrakusumaḥ śuṣyatyaśoko yathā//5//
body.translated_text:
280.016. 'Having once commanded the earth under a single parasol, shaking off the tumultuous din of suppressed foes, and consoling the wretched and afflicted —
280.018. now, his own domains lost, the pitiable King <s>Aśoka</s> does not shine, just as an <s>Aśoka</s> tree withers, its leaves and flowers cut, wilted, and scattered.' //5//

body.text:
280.020. tato rājā aśokaḥ samīpo gataṃ puruṣamāhūyovāca--bhadramukha, pūrvaguṇānurāgādbhraṣṭaiśvaryasyāpi mama imaṃ tāvadapaścimaṃ vyāpāraṃ kuru/
280.021. idaṃ mamārdhāmalakaṃ grahāya kurkuṭārāmaṃ gatvā saṃghe niryātaya/
280.022. madvacanācca saṃghasya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā vaktavyam--jambudvīpaiśvaryasya rājña eṣa sāmprataṃ vibhava iti/
280.023. idaṃ tāvadapaścimaṃ dānaṃ tathā paribhoktavyam yathā me saṃghagatā dakṣiṇā vistīrṇā syāditi/
280.024. āha ca--
280.025. idaṃ pradānaṃ caramaṃ mamādya rājyaṃ ca taṃ caiva gataṃ svabhāvam/
280.027. ārogyavaidyoṣadhivarjitasya trātā na me 'styāryagaṇādbahirdhā//6//
body.translated_text:
280.020. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, summoning a man who had come near, said: 'Good man, out of love for my former virtues, even though I have lost my sovereignty, do me this one last service.
280.021. Take this half-<s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan) fruit and go to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s> (Cock Monastery) and present it to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
280.022. And having bowed at the feet of the <s>Saṃgha</s> on my behalf, say: "This is now the entire wealth of the lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."
280.023. "Let this last gift be enjoyed in such a way that my offering to the <s>Saṃgha</s> may become extensive."'
280.024. And he said:
280.025. 'This is my final gift today — the kingdom and all that went with it have passed away by their own nature.
280.027. For one lacking the physician and medicine of health, there is no protector for me outside the company of the noble ones.' //6//

body.text:
280.029. tatathā bhujyatām yena pradānaṃ mama paścimam/
280.030. yathā saṃghagatā me 'dya vistīrṇā dakṣiṇā bhavet//7//
body.translated_text:
280.029. 'Let it be so consumed that my last gift
280.030. may today become an extensive offering to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' //7//

body.text: 280.031. evaṃ deveti s puruṣo rājño 'śokasya pratiśrutya tadardhāmalakaṃ kurukuṭārāmaṃ gatvā vṛddhānte sthitvā kṛtāñjalistadardhāmalakaṃ saṃghe niryātayannuvāca--
body.translated_text: 280.031. 'So be it, Sire' — that man, having assented to King <s>Aśoka</s>, took the half-myrobalan, went to the <s>Kurkuṭārāma</s>, stood at the far end of the assembly, and with palms joined, presenting the half-myrobalan to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, said:

body.text:
281.001. <281>ekacchatrasamucchrayāṃ vasumatīmājñāpayan yaḥ purā lokaṃ tāpayati sma madhyadivasaprāpto divā bhāskaraḥ/
281.003. bhāgyacchidramavekṣya so 'dya nṛpatiḥ svaiḥ karmābhirvañcitaḥ saṃprāpte divasakṣaye raviriva bhraṣṭaprabhāvaḥ sthitaḥ//8//
body.translated_text:
281.001. 'He who formerly commanded the earth under a single parasol — like the mid-day sun scorching the world —
281.003. that king, now betrayed by his own <s>karmas</s>, having perceived the breach in his fortune, stands like the sun at the end of the day, his power gone.' //8//

body.text:
281.005. bhaktyavanatena śirasā praṇamya saṃghāya tena khalu dattamidamāmalakasyārdhaṃ lakṣmīcāpalyacihnitam/
281.006. tataḥ saṃghasthaviro bhikṣūnuvāca--bhadantā bhavantaḥ, śakyamidānīṃ saṃvegamutpādayitum/
281.007. kutah? evaṃ hyuktaṃ bhagavatā--paravipattiḥ saṃvejanīyaṃ sthānamiti/
281.007. kasyedānīṃ sahṛdayasya saṃvego notpadyate? kutah?
281.009. tyāgaśūro narendro 'sāvaśoko mauryakuñjaraḥ/
281.010. jambudvīpeśvaro bhūtvā jāto 'rdhāmalakeśvaraḥ//9//
body.translated_text:
281.005. 'With a head bowed in devotion, having saluted the <s>Saṃgha</s>, he has given this half of a myrobalan — a token of the fickleness of fortune.'
281.006. Then the elder of the <s>Saṃgha</s> addressed the monks: 'Venerable sirs, now indeed it is possible to generate a sense of urgency.
281.007. Why? For thus it was said by the Blessed One: "The misfortune of another is a cause for spiritual urgency."
281.007. Whose heart, if it has feeling, would not be stirred to urgency now? Why?
281.009. This <s>Aśoka</s>, the elephant of the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty, a hero of generosity among kings,
281.010. having been lord of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, has become lord of half a myrobalan.' //9//

body.text:
281.011. mṛtyaiḥ sa bhūmipatiradya hṛtādhikāro dānaṃ prayacchati kilāmalakārdhametat/
281.013. śrībhogāvistaramadairatigarvitānāṃ pratyādiśanniva manāṃsi pṛthagjanānām//10//
body.translated_text:
281.011. 'This lord of the earth, his authority now seized by death, gives as a gift, it seems, this mere half of a myrobalan —
281.013. as if rebuking the minds of ordinary people who are exceedingly proud with the intoxication of wealth, enjoyments, and power.' //10//

body.text:
281.015. yāvattadardhāmalakaṃ cūrṇayitvā yūṣe prakṣipya saṃghe cāritam/
281.015. tato rājā aśoko rādhaguptamuvāca--kathaya rādhagupta, kaḥ sāmprataṃ pṛthivyāmīśvarah? atha rādhagupto 'śokasya pādayor nipatya kṛtāñjaliruvāca--devaḥ pṛthivyāmīśvaraḥ/
281.017. atha rājā aśokaḥ kathaṃcidutthāya caturdiśamavalokya saṃghāya añjaliṃ kṛtvovāca--eṣa idānīṃ mahatkośaṃ sthāpayitvā imāṃ samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ bhagavacchrāvakasaṃghe niryātayāmi/
281.019. āha ca--
281.020. imāṃ samudrottamanīlakañcukāmanekaratnākarabhūṣitānanām/
281.022. dadāmyahaṃ bhūtadharāṃ samandarāṃ saṃghāya tasminnupabhujyate phalam//11//
body.translated_text:
281.015. Then the half-myrobalan was ground up, mixed into the broth, and distributed among the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
281.015. Then King <s>Aśoka</s> said to <s>Rādhagupta</s>: 'Tell me, <s>Rādhagupta</s>, who is now the lord of the earth?' Then <s>Rādhagupta</s>, falling at <s>Aśoka</s>'s feet with palms joined, said: 'Your Majesty is the lord of the earth.'
281.017. Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having somehow risen, surveyed the four directions, made <s>añjali</s> (salutation) to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and said: 'Now, having set aside the great treasury, I bestow this great earth bounded by the oceans upon the community of the Blessed One's disciples.'
281.019. And he said:
281.020. 'This earth, wearing the dark-blue garment of the ocean, her face adorned with many jewel-mines,
281.022. bearing all beings together with her caves — I give her to the <s>Saṃgha</s>; therein lies the fruit to be enjoyed.' //11//

body.text:
281.024. api ca/
281.025. dānenāhamanena nendrabhavanaṃ na brahmaloke phalaṃ kāṅkṣāmi drutavārivegacapalaṃ prāgeva rājaśriyam/
281.027. dānasyāsya phalaṃ tu bhaktimahato yanme 'sti tenāpnuyāṃ cittaiśvaryamahāryamāryamahitaṃ nāyāti yadvikriyām//12//
body.translated_text:
281.024. Moreover:
281.025. 'By this gift, I desire neither the palace of <s>Indra</s> nor the fruit of the <s>Brahma</s>-world, nor royal splendor, which is as fickle as the rush of flowing water.
281.027. Rather, by whatever devotion this gift of mine possesses, may I obtain that sovereignty of mind — noble, honored by the noble, inviolable — which admits of no change.' //12//

body.text:
281.029. yāvat patrābhilikhitaṃ kṛtvā dantamudrayā mudritam/
281.029. tato rājā mahāpṛthivīṃ saṃghe datvā kālagataḥ/
281.030. yāvadamātyair nīlapītābhiḥ śibikābhir nirhāritvā śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā rājānaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāma iti, yāvadrādhaguptenābhihitam/
281.031. rājñā aśokena mahāpṛthivī saṃghe niryātitā <282>iti/
body.translated_text:
281.029. He had it written on a leaf and sealed with a tooth-seal.
281.029. Then the king, having given the great earth to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, passed away.
