281.030. The ministers, having carried him out on blue and yellow biers, performed the funeral rites and were about to install a new king, when <s>Rādhagupta</s> announced:
281.031. 'King <s>Aśoka</s> bestowed the great earth upon the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'

body.text:
282.001. tato 'mātyairabhihitam--kimarthamiti? rādhagupta uvāca--eṣa rājño 'śokasya manorathe babhūva--koṭiśataṃ bhagavacchāsena dānaṃ dāsyāmīti/
282.002. tena ṣaṇṇavitikoṭyo dattā yāvadrājñyā pratiṣiddhā/
282.003. tadabhiprāyeṇa rājñā mahāpṛthivī saṃghe dattā/
282.003. yāvadamātyaiścatasraḥ koṭyo bhagavacchāsane dattvā pṛthivīṃ niṣkrīya saṃpadī rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
282.004. saṃpaderbṛhaspatiḥ putraḥ, bṛhaspatervṛṣasenaḥ, vṛṣasenasya puṣyadharmā, puṣyadharmaṇaḥ puṣyamitraḥ/
282.005. so 'mātyānāmantrayate--ka uapāyaḥ syādyadasmākaṃ nāma ciraṃ tiṣṭhet? nairabhihitam--devasya ca vaṃśādaśoko nāṃnā rājā babhūveti/
282.006. tena caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam/
282.007. yāvadbhagavacchāsanaṃ prāpyate, tāvattasya yaśaḥ sthāsyati/
282.008. devo 'pi caturaśītidharmarājikāsahasraṃ pratiṣṭhāpayatu/
282.008. rājā āha--maheśākhyo rājā aśoko babhūva/
282.009. anyaḥ kaścidupāya iti? tasya brāhmaṇapurohitaḥ pṛthagjano 'śrāddhaḥ/
282.010. tenābhihitam--deva, dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ nāma ciraṃ sthāsyati/
282.010. yāvadrājā puṣyamitraścaturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhayitvā bhagavacchāsanaṃ vināśayiṣyāmīti kukkuṭārāmaṃ nirgataḥ/
282.011. dvāre ca siṃhanādo muktaḥ/
282.012. yāvatsa rājā bhītaḥ pāṭaliputraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
282.012. evaṃ dvirapi trirapi/
282.012. yāvadbhikṣūṃśca saṃghamāhūya kathayati--bhagavacchāsanaṃ nāśāyiṣyāmīti/
282.013. kimicchatha stūpaṃ saṃghārāmān vā? bhikṣubhiḥ parigṛhītāḥ/
282.014. yāvatpuṣyamitro yāvat saṃghārāmaṃ bhikṣūṃśca praghātayan prasthitaḥ/
282.015. sa yāvacchākalamanuprāptaḥ/
282.015. tenābhihitam--yo me śramaṇaśiro dāsyati, tasyāhaṃ dīnāraśataṃ dāsyāmi/
282.016. dharmarājikāvārhadbuddhyā(?) śiro dātumārabdham/
282.016. śrutvā ca rājā arhatpraghātayitumārabdhaḥ/
282.017. sa ca nirodhaṃ samāpannaḥ/
282.017. tasya paropakarmo na kramate/
282.017. sa yatnamutsṛjya yāvatkoṣṭhakaṃ gataḥ/
282.018. daṃṣṭhrānivāsī yakṣaścintayati--idaṃ bhagavacchāsanaṃ vinaśyati/
282.018. ahaṃ ca śikṣāṃ dhārayāmi/
282.019. na mayā śakyaṃ kasyacidapriyaṃ kartum/
282.019. tasya duhitā kṛmiśena yakṣeṇa yācyate, na cānuprayacchati--tvaṃ pāpakarmakārīti/
282.020. yāvatsā duhitā tena kṛmiśasya dattā bhagavacchāsanaparitrāṇāryaṃ parigrahaparipālanārthaṃ ca/
282.021. puṣyamitrasya rājñaḥ pṛṣṭhato yakṣo mahān pramāṇe yūyam(?)/
282.022. tasyānubhāvātsa rājā na pratihanyate/
282.022. yāvaddaṃṣṭrānivāsī yakṣastaṃ puṣyamitrānubandhayakṣaṃ grahāya parvatacarye 'carat/
282.023. yāvaddakṣiṇā mahāsamudraṃ gataḥ/
282.023. kṛmiśena ca yakṣeṇa mahāntaṃ parvatamānayitvā puṣyamitro rājā sabalavāhano 'vaṣṭabdhaḥ/
282.024. tasya munihata iti saṃjñā vyavasthāpitā/
282.024. yadā puṣyamitro rājā praghātitastadā mauryavaṃśaḥ samucchinnaḥ//
body.translated_text:
282.001. Then the ministers said: 'For what purpose?' <s>Rādhagupta</s> said: 'This was King <s>Aśoka</s>'s heart's desire: "I shall give one hundred <s>koṭis</s> in donation to the Blessed One's teaching."
282.002. He had given ninety-six <s>koṭis</s> before the queen stopped him.
282.003. With that intention, the king gave the great earth to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'
282.003. Then the ministers, having given four <s>koṭis</s> to the Blessed One's teaching, ransomed the earth and installed <s>Saṃpadī</s> as king.
282.004. <s>Saṃpadī</s>'s son was <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s son was <s>Vṛṣasena</s>; <s>Vṛṣasena</s>'s son was <s>Puṣyadharma</s>; <s>Puṣyadharma</s>'s son was <s>Puṣyamitra</s>.
282.005. He consulted his ministers: 'What means is there by which our name might endure long?' They said: 'From Your Majesty's dynasty there was a king named <s>Aśoka</s>.
282.006. He established eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s>.
282.007. As long as the Blessed One's teaching endures, so long will his fame endure.
282.008. Let Your Majesty also establish eighty-four thousand <s>Dharmarājikā</s>.'
282.008. The king said: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> was a lord of great renown.
282.009. Is there any other means?' His <s>brāhmaṇa</s> chaplain, an ordinary person without faith,
282.010. said: 'Sire, by two causes a name endures long.'
282.010. Then King <s>Puṣyamitra</s>, marshaling his fourfold army, set out from the <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s> saying: 'I shall destroy the Blessed One's teaching.'
282.011. A lion's roar was uttered at the gate.
282.012. The king, frightened, returned to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>.
282.012. Thus a second and a third time.
282.012. Then, having summoned the monks and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, he said: 'I shall destroy the Blessed One's teaching.
282.013. What do you prefer — the <s>stūpas</s> or the monasteries?' The monks chose the monasteries.
282.014. Then <s>Puṣyamitra</s> set out, destroying monasteries and slaughtering monks.
282.015. He reached as far as <s>Śākala</s>.
282.015. He proclaimed: 'Whoever gives me the head of a <s>śramaṇa</s>, to him I shall give a hundred <s>dīnāras</s>.'
282.016. An <s>Arhat</s> of the <s>Dharmarājikā</s> began to offer his head.
282.016. Having heard this, the king began to slaughter <s>Arhats</s>.
282.017. But that <s>Arhat</s> had entered the attainment of cessation.
282.017. The king's weapon could not penetrate him.
282.017. He gave up his efforts and went to the treasury.
282.018. A <s>Yakṣa</s> named <s>Daṃṣṭrānivāsin</s> ('Fang-Dweller') reflected: 'This teaching of the Blessed One is being destroyed.
282.018. And I uphold the training.
282.019. I am unable to do harm to anyone.'
282.019. His daughter was sought in marriage by the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, but he would not give her — saying: 'You are a doer of evil deeds.'
282.020. But then he gave that daughter to <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, for the sake of protecting the Blessed One's teaching and guarding the dependents.
282.021. A great <s>Yakṣa</s> stood behind King <s>Puṣyamitra</s>.
282.022. By his power, the king could not be stopped.
282.022. Then the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Daṃṣṭrānivāsin</s>, having seized that <s>Yakṣa</s> who followed <s>Puṣyamitra</s>, wandered in a mountain range.
282.023. He went as far as the southern great ocean.
282.023. And the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, bringing a great mountain, crushed King <s>Puṣyamitra</s> together with his army and retinue.
282.024. The designation '<s>Munihata</s>' ('Killed by the Sage') was established for it.
282.024. When King <s>Puṣyamitra</s> was killed, the <s>Maurya</s> dynasty was extinguished.

body.text: 282.026. iti śrīdivyāvadāne aśokāvadānaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: 282.026. Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Aśokāvadāna</s> is concluded.

body.text: 283.001. div30 sudhanakumārāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 283.001. Chapter 30: The <s>Sudhanakumārāvadāna</s> (The Story of Prince <s>Sudhana</s>).

body.text: 283.002. punarapi mahārāja yanmayā anuttarasamyaksambodhiprāptaye dānāni dattāni, puṇyāni kṛtāni, vīryapāramitā ca pariripūtā, anuttarā samyaksambodhir nārādhitā, tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text: 283.002. 'Furthermore, Great King, hear about the gifts I gave, the merits I accumulated, and the perfection of vigor I fulfilled for the attainment of unsurpassed perfect awakening — and yet unsurpassed perfect awakening was not achieved.'

body.text:
283.003. bhūtapūrvaṃ mahāraja pañcālaviṣaye rājanau babhūvatuḥ, uttarapāñcālo dakṣiṇapāñcālaśca/
283.005. tatrottarapāñcālo mahādhano nāṃnā dastināpure rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca śāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍmarataskaradurbhikṣarogāpagataṃ śalīkṣugomahiṣīsampannam/
283.007. dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
283.007. tasmiṃśca nagare mahāhrada utpalakumudapuṇḍrīkasampanno haṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākopaśobhito ramaṇīyaḥ/
283.008. tatra ca hrade janmacitrako nāṃ nāgapotaḥ prativasati/
283.009. sa kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
283.010. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
283.010. śasyavatī vasumatī/
283.010. subhikṣānnapāno deśaḥ/
283.011. dānamānasatkāravāṃśca lokaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakopabhojyaḥ/
283.011. dakṣiṇapāñcālastu rājā adharmabhūyiṣṭhaścaṇḍo rabhasaḥ karkaśo 'dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati, nityaṃ daṇḍena ghātanadhāraṇabandhanahiḍinigaḍoparodhana rāṣṭranivāsināṃ trāsayati/
283.013. adharmabhūyiṣṭhatayā cāsya devo na kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhāramutsṛjati/
283.014. tato 'sau mahājanakāyaḥ saṃtrastaḥ svatrastaḥ svajīvitāpekṣayā rāṣṭraparityāgaṃ kṛtvā uttarapāñcālasyaiva rājño viṣayaṃ gatvā prativasati/
283.015. yāvadapareṇa samayena dakṣiṇapāñcālo rājā mṛgayāvyapadeśena janapadān vyavalokanāya nirgataḥ/
283.016. yāvat paśyati grāmanagarāṇi śūnyāni, udyānadevakulāni bhinnaprabhagnāni/
283.017. sa janakāyaḥ kva gata iti kathayati/
283.018. amātyāḥ kathayatnti--deva, uttarapāñcālasya rājño viṣayaṃ gataḥ/
283.018. kimartham? deva, abhayaṃ prayaccha, kathayāmaḥ/
283.019. dattaṃ bhavatu/
283.019. tataste kathayanti--deva, uttarapāñcālo rājā dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
283.020. tasya janapadā ṛddhāśca sphītāśca kṣemāśca subhikṣāśca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāśca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskaradurbhikṣarogāpagatāḥ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannāḥ/
283.022. dānamānasatkāravāṃśca lokaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇavanīpakopabhojyaḥ/
283.022. devastu caṇḍo rabhasaḥ karkaśo nityaṃ tāḍanaghātanadhāraṇabandhananigaḍoparodha(na) rāṣṭraṃ trāsayati/
283.023. yato 'sau janakāyaḥ saṃtrastaḥ saṃvegamāpanna uttarapāñcālasya rājño viṣayaṃ gataḥ/
283.024. dakṣiṇapāñcālo rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, ko 'sāvupāyaḥ syādenāsau janakāyaḥ punarāgatya eṣu grāmanagareṣu prativaset? amātyā āhuh--yadi deva uttarapāñcālavaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayasi, maitracitto 'nukampācittaśca rāṣṭraṃ pālayasi, nacirādasau janakāyaḥ punarāgatya eṣu grāmanagareṣu prativaset/
283.027. dakṣiṇapāñcālo rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yadyevam, ahamapyuttarapāñcālavaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayāmi, maitracitto hitacitto 'nukampācittaśca rāṣṭraṃ pālayāmi/
283.029. yūyaṃ tathā kuruta, yathā asau janakāyaḥ punarāgatya eṣu grāmanagareṣu prativasatīti/
283.030. amātyā āhuh--deva, aparo 'pi tatrānuśaṃso 'sti/
283.031. tasmin nagare mahāgrada utpalakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchanno haṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākopaśobhitah<284>/
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, great king, in the <s>Pañcāla</s> region there were two kings — <s>Uttarapāñcāla</s> (Northern <s>Pañcāla</s>) and <s>Dakṣiṇapāñcāla</s> (Southern <s>Pañcāla</s>). Of these, <s>Uttarapāñcāla</s>, named <s>Mahādhana</s> ('Great Wealth'), ruled the kingdom in <s>Hastināpura</s> — prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, free from strife, quarrels, tumult, disturbance, thieves, famine, and disease, abounding in rice, sugarcane, cows, and buffaloes. He was a righteous king, ruling the kingdom by the <s>Dharma</s>. In that city there was a great lake, covered with <s>utpala</s> (blue lotuses), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lilies), and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotuses), adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> (ruddy geese), and <s>cakravāka</s> (brahminy ducks) — most delightful. In that lake dwelt a young <s>Nāga</s> (serpent-deity) named <s>Janmacitraka</s> ('Wonderful-born'). He would release timely and proper rains. There was an exceedingly rich harvest of crops. The earth was rich with grain. The land had abundant food and drink. The people were generous, respectful, and hospitable, providing sustenance to <s>Śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and wandering beggars. The Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> king, however, was given to unrighteousness — fierce, violent, harsh, ruling the kingdom by injustice, constantly terrorizing the inhabitants of the realm with punishment, execution, seizing, imprisonment, fetters, and shackles. Because of his predominant unrighteousness, the sky-god did not release timely and proper rain for him. Therefore, that great multitude of people, frightened and alarmed, valuing their lives, abandoned the realm and went to dwell in the territory of the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king. At another time, the Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> king, under the pretext of hunting, went out to survey the countryside. He saw villages and cities deserted, gardens and temples broken and ruined. He said: 'Where has the populace gone?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, they have gone to the territory of the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king.' 'Why?' 'Your Majesty, grant us safety, and we shall tell you.' 'It is granted.' Then they said: 'Your Majesty, the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king rules by the <s>Dharma</s>. His provinces are prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, free from strife, quarrels, tumult, disturbance, thieves, famine, and disease, abounding in rice, sugarcane, cows, and buffaloes. The people are generous, respectful, and hospitable, providing sustenance to <s>Śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and wandering beggars. But Your Majesty is fierce, violent, harsh, constantly terrorizing the realm with beating, execution, seizing, imprisonment, fetters, and shackles. Therefore, that populace, frightened and alarmed, has gone to the territory of the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king.' The Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> king said: 'Good sirs, what stratagem could there be by which that populace would come back and dwell in these villages and cities?' The ministers said: 'If, Your Majesty, you rule the kingdom by the <s>Dharma</s> like the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king, with a mind of friendship, compassion, and benevolence protecting the realm, before long that populace will come back and dwell in these villages and cities.' The Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> king said: 'Good sirs, if that is so, I too shall rule the kingdom by the <s>Dharma</s> like the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king, with a mind of friendship, benevolence, and compassion protecting the realm. You must act in such a way that the populace comes back and dwells in these villages and cities.' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, there is yet another advantage there. In that city there is a great lake, covered with <s>utpala</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s>, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds.'

body.text:
284.001. tatra janmacitrako nāma nāgapotakaḥ prativasati/
284.001. sa kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhāramanuprayacchati/
284.002. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
284.002. teṃs tasya śasyavatī vasumatī, subhikṣānnapānaśca deśaḥ/
284.003. rājā āha--ko 'sau upāyaḥ syādyenāsau nāgapota ihānīyeta? amātyā āhuh--deva, vidyāmantradhāriṇḥ, tānānayeti/
284.004. te samanviṣyantām/
284.004. tato rājñā suvarṇapiṭakaṃ dhvajāgre baddhvā svavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--ya uttarapāñcālarājaviṣayājjanmacitrakaṃ nāma nāgapotakamānayati, tasyemaṃ suvarṇapiṭakaṃ dāsyāmi, mahatā ca satkāreṇa satkariṣyāmīti/
284.007. yāvadanyatamo 'hituṇḍiko 'mātyānāṃ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--mamedaṃ suvarṇapiṭakamanuprayacchata/
284.008. ahaṃ janmacitraṃ nāma nāgapitakamapahṛtyānayāmīti/
284.009. amātyāḥ kathayanti--eṣa gṛhāṇa/
284.009. sa kathayati--yo yuṣmākaṃ śraddhayitaḥ pratyayitaśca, tasya haste tiṣṭhatu/
284.010. ānīte janmacitre nāgapotake grahīṣyāmīti/
284.010. evaṃ kuruṣveti/
284.010. tato 'sau ahituṇḍikaḥ pratyayitasya puruṣasya haste suvarṇapiṭakaṃ sthāpayitvā hastināpuraṃ gataḥ/
284.012. tenāsau hradaḥ samantato vyavalokitaḥ/
284.012. nimittīkṛtah--asau jñmacitro nāgapotaka etasmin pradeśe tiṣṭhatīti/
284.013. tato balyupahāranimittaṃ punaḥ pratyāgataḥ/
284.013. amātyānāṃ kathayati--balyupahāramenaṃ prayacchata/
284.014. saptame divase taṃ nāgapotakamapahṛtya ānayāmīti/
284.014. sa cāhituṇḍikastena saṃlakṣitah--mamāsāvapaharaṇāyāgataḥ/
284.015. saptame divase māmapahariṣyati/
284.015. mātāpitṛviyogajaṃ me duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
284.016. kiṃ karomi, kiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadyeyamiti/
284.016. tasya hradasya nātidūre dvau lubdhakau prativasataḥ, sārako halakaḥ/
284.017. tau hradamāśritya jīvikāṃ kalpayataḥ/
284.017. ye sthalagatāḥ prāṇino mṛgaśarabhasūkarādayastaṃ hradamupasarpanti, tān praghātayataḥ, ye 'pi jalagatā matsyakacchapamaṇḍūkādayaḥ/
284.019. tatra sārakaḥ kālagataḥ, halako jīvati/
284.019. janmacitro nāgapotaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ko 'nyo 'sti mama śaraṇamṛte halakāt lubdhakāt? tato manuṣyaveṣamāsthāya halakasya lubdhakasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
284.021. gatvā kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ tvaṃ jānīṣe kasyānubhāvāddhanasya rājño janapadā ṛddhāśca sphītāśca subhikṣākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāśca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskaradurbhikṣarogāpagatāḥ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsampannā iti? sa kathayati--jāne sa rājā dhārmiko dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati, maitracitto hitacitto 'nukmpācittaśca rāṣṭraṃ pālayatīti/
284.025. asmin pradeśe janmacitrako nāma nāgapitakaḥ prativasati/
284.026. sa kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
284.027. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
284.027. śasyavatī vasumatī, subhikṣānnapānaśca deśa iti/
284.028. janmacitraḥ kathayati--taṃ nāgapotakamito viṣayādapaharet, tasya nāgapotakasya kiṃ syāt? na śobhanaṃ syāt, mātāpitṛviyogajaṃ duḥkhaṃ syādrājño rāṣṭrasya ca/
284.030. yo 'paharati, tasya kiṃ tvaṃ kuryāh? sa āha--jīvitādvyaparopayeyam/
284.030. jānīṣe tvaṃ kataro 'sau nāgapotaka iti? na jāne/
284.031. ahamevāsau nāgaḥ/
284.031. dakṣiṇapāñcālavaiṣayikenāhituṇḍikenāpahṛtya nīyeta/
284.032. sa balyupahāravidhānārthaṃ gataḥ/
284.032. saptame divase āgamiṣyati/
body.translated_text: In that lake dwelt a young <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Janmacitraka</s>. He would release timely and proper rains. There was an exceedingly rich harvest of crops. The earth was rich with grain, and the land had abundant food and drink. The king said: 'What stratagem could there be by which that young <s>Nāga</s> could be brought here?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, there are those who possess spells and <s>mantras</s>. Summon them.' 'Let them be sought out.' Then the king tied a golden basket to the top of a banner-pole and had an announcement by bell made throughout his domain: 'Whoever brings the young <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Janmacitraka</s> from the territory of the Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> king — to him I shall give this golden basket, and I shall honor him with great respect.' Then a certain snake-charmer went to the ministers and said: 'Give me this golden basket. I shall abduct and bring the young <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Janmacitraka</s>.' The ministers said: 'Here, take it.' He said: 'Let it remain in the hand of someone you trust and have confidence in. When <s>Janmacitraka</s> the young <s>Nāga</s> has been brought, I shall take it.' 'Do so.' Then that snake-charmer, having placed the golden basket in the hands of a trustworthy man, went to <s>Hastināpura</s>. He examined that lake from all sides. He identified: 'That young <s>Nāga</s> <s>Janmacitraka</s> dwells in this spot.' Then he went back again on the pretext of obtaining offerings. He said to the ministers: 'Provide me with offerings. On the seventh day, I shall abduct and bring that young <s>Nāga</s>.' And that <s>Nāga</s> observed the snake-charmer: 'This one has come to abduct me. On the seventh day he will abduct me. The suffering of separation from my parents will befall me.' 'What shall I do? To whom shall I go for refuge?' Not far from that lake dwelt two hunters, <s>Sāraka</s> and <s>Halaka</s>. They made their living from the lake. Whatever land creatures — deer, rabbits, boars, and the like — approached that lake, they killed them; and also whatever water creatures — fish, turtles, frogs, and the like. There, <s>Sāraka</s> had died, but <s>Halaka</s> was alive. The young <s>Nāga</s> <s>Janmacitraka</s> reflected: 'Who else is my refuge except the hunter <s>Halaka</s>?' Then, assuming human form, he went to the hunter <s>Halaka</s>. Having gone, he said: 'Good man, do you know by whose power the provinces of King <s>Mahādhana</s> are prosperous, thriving, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, free from strife, quarrels, tumult, disturbance, thieves, famine, and disease, abounding in rice, sugarcane, cows, and buffaloes?' He said: 'I know — that king is righteous, ruling the kingdom by the <s>Dharma</s>, with a mind of friendship, benevolence, and compassion protecting the realm.' 'In this spot dwells a young <s>Nāga</s> named <s>Janmacitraka</s>. He releases timely and proper rains. There is an exceedingly rich harvest of crops. The earth is rich with grain, and the land has abundant food and drink.' <s>Janmacitraka</s> said: 'If someone were to abduct that young <s>Nāga</s> from this territory, what would happen to him?' 'Nothing good — the suffering of separation from parents would befall the king and the realm.' 'What would you do to the one who abducts him?' He said: 'I would put him to death.' 'Do you know which one that young <s>Nāga</s> is?' 'I do not.' 'I am that very <s>Nāga</s>. A snake-charmer from the territory of the Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> king would abduct and carry me off. He has gone for the purpose of arranging offerings. On the seventh day he will return.'

body.text:
285.001. <285>āgatya asya hradasya catasṛṣu dikṣu khadiraśalākānnikhanya nānāraṅgaiḥ sūtrairveṣṭayitvā mantrānāvartayiṣyati/
285.002. tatra tvayā pracchanne saṃnikṛṣṭe sthātavyam/
285.002. yadā tenāyamevamrūpaḥ prayogaḥ kṛto bhavati, tadā hradamadhyāt kvathamānaṃ pānīyamutthāsyati ahaṃ cotthāsyāmi/
285.003. tadā tvayāsau ahituṇḍikaḥ śareṇa marmaṇi tāḍayitavyaḥ, āśu copasaṃkramya vaktavyah--mantrānupasaṃhara/
285.004. mā te utkṛttamūlaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ nipātayiṣyāmīti/
285.005. yadyasau mantrānanupasaṃhṛtya prāṇairviyokṣyate, mṛtaṃ te 'ham yāvajjīvaṃ mantrapāśabddhaḥ syāmiti/
285.006. lubdhakaḥ prāha--yadi tavaikasyaivaṃ guṇaḥ syāt, tathāpyahamevaṃ kuryām, prāgeva sarājakasya rāṣṭrasya/
285.007. gaccha, ahaṃ te trāteti/
285.008. tatastena nāgapotakena tasyaikapārśve guptasthānamupadarśitam/
285.008. yāvadasau lubdhakaḥ saptame divase pratigupte pradeśe ātmānaṃ gopayitvā avasthitaḥ/
285.009. sa cāhituṇḍika āgatya balyupahāraṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
285.010. tena catasṛṣu dikṣu catvāraḥ khadirakīlakā nikhātāḥ/
285.010. nānāraṅgaiḥ sūtrairveṣṭayitvā mantrā āvartitāḥ/
285.0tatastasmāt pānīyaṃ kvathitumārabdham/
285.011. lubdhakena ca śareṇa marmaṇi tāḍitaḥ/
285.012. niṣkośaṃ cāsiṃ kṛtvā abhihitah--tvamasmadviṣayanivāsinaṃ nāgapotamapaharasi/
285.013. mā te utkṛttamūlaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ nipātayāmīti/
285.013. tato 'hituṇḍikena duḥkhavedanābhibhūtena maraṇabhayabhītena mantrā vyāvartitāḥ/
285.014. tatsamanantaraṃ ca lubdhakena jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ/
285.015. tato nāgo mantrapāśavinirmukto hradādabhyudgamya lubdhakaṃ pariṣvaktavān, evaṃ cāha--tvaṃ me mātā, tvaṃ me pitā, yanmayā tvāmāgamya mātāpitṛviyogajaṃ duḥkhaṃ notpannam/
285.017. āgaccha, bhavanaṃ gacchāmaḥ/
285.017. tenāsau bhavanaṃ nītaḥ, nānāvidhena cānnapānena saṃtarpitaḥ, ratnāni copadarśitāni, mātāpitrośca niveditaḥ/
285.018. amba tāta--eṣa me suhṛccharaṇaṃ bāndhavaḥ/
285.019. asyānubhāvādyuṣmābhiḥ saha viyogo na jāta iti/
285.019. tābhyāmasau vareṇa pravārito vividhāni ca ratnāni dattāni/
285.020. sa tānyādāya tasmād hradād vyuthitaḥ/
285.020. tasya ca hradasya nātidūre puṣpaphalasalilasampanne nānāśakunikūjite ṛṣeragramāśramapadam/
285.021. tatra ca nāgapotakena sārdhaṃ vṛttakaṃ tatsarvaṃ vistareṇa samākhyātam/
285.022. tata ṛṣiḥ kathayati--kiṃ ratnaiḥ kiṃ vā te suvarṇena? tasya bhavane 'mogho nāṃ pāśastiṣṭhati, tam yācasva/
285.023. tato lubdhako 'moghapāśe saṃjātatṛṣṇah ṛṣivacanamupaśrutya punarapi nāgabhavanaṃ gataḥ/
285.024. yāvatpaśyati bhavanadvāre tamamoghapāśam/
285.025. tasyaitadabhavat--eṣa sa pāśo yo mayā prārthanīyaḥ/
285.025. iti viditvā nāgabhavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
285.025. tato janmacitreṇa nāgapotakena anyaiśca nāgaiḥ sasambhramaiḥ pratisaṃmodito ratnaiśca pravāritaḥ/
285.026. sa kathayati--alaṃ mama ratnaiḥ/
285.027. kiṃ tu etamamoghapāśaṃ prayacchatheti/
285.027. sa nāga āha--tavānena kiṃ prayojanam? yadā garutmatopadrutā bhavāmaḥ, tadā anenātmānaṃ rakṣāmaḥ/
285.028. lubdhaka āha--yuṣmākameṣa kadācit karhicit garutmatopadrutānāmupayogaṃ gacchati/
285.029. mama tu anena satatameva prayojanam/
285.030. yadasti kṛtamupakṛtaṃ ca, anuprayaccheti/
285.030. janmacitrasya nāgapotakasyaitadabhavat--mamānena bahūpakṛtam/
285.031. mātāpitarau avalokya dadāmīti/
285.031. ten mātāpitarau avalokya sa pāśo dattaḥ/
285.032. tato 'sau lubdhakaḥ pṛthivīlabdhaprakhyena sukhasaumanasyenāpyāyitamanā amoghapāśamādāya nāgabhavanādabhyudgamya svagṛhaṃ gataḥ//
body.translated_text:
285.001. 'Having come, he will drive <s>khadira</s> (acacia) stakes into the four directions of this lake, wrap them with threads of various colors, and recite <s>mantras</s>.
285.002. You must stand concealed and nearby there.
285.002. When he has performed this procedure of such a kind, then boiling water will rise up from the middle of the lake, and I too will rise up.
285.003. Then you must strike that snake charmer in a vital spot with an arrow, and quickly approaching, say: "Withdraw your <s>mantras</s>!
285.004. Otherwise I shall cut off your head at the root and cast it upon the ground."
285.005. If he dies without withdrawing the <s>mantras</s>, though dead, I would remain bound by the noose of <s>mantras</s> for as long as I live.'
285.006. The hunter said: 'Even if the benefit were for you alone, I would still do this — how much more so for the entire kingdom with its king!
285.007. Go, I am your protector.'
285.008. Then the young <s>Nāga</s> showed him a hidden place on one side.
285.008. On the seventh day, the hunter concealed himself in a secluded spot and stood ready.
285.009. The snake charmer came and began to make a sacrificial offering.
285.010. He drove four <s>khadira</s> stakes in the four directions.
285.010. Having wrapped them with threads of various colors, the <s>mantras</s> were recited.
285.010. Then the water from that lake began to boil.
285.011. And the hunter struck him in a vital spot with an arrow.
285.012. Drawing his sword from its sheath, he said: 'You are carrying off a young <s>Nāga</s> who dwells in our territory!
285.013. Otherwise I shall cut off your head at the root and cast it upon the ground.'
285.013. Then the snake charmer, overcome by painful sensations and frightened by the fear of death, withdrew the <s>mantras</s>.
285.014. And immediately thereafter, the hunter killed him.
285.015. Then the <s>Nāga</s>, freed from the noose of <s>mantras</s>, rose up from the lake and embraced the hunter, and said thus: 'You are my mother, you are my father, for by coming to you the suffering born of separation from my parents has not arisen.
285.017. Come, let us go to my dwelling.'
285.017. He was taken to the dwelling, satisfied with various kinds of food and drink, shown jewels, and introduced to the parents.
285.018. 'Mother, father — this is my friend, refuge, and kinsman.
285.019. By his power, separation from you has not occurred.'
285.019. By them he was offered a boon, and various jewels were given.
285.020. Taking those, he departed from that lake.
285.020. Not far from that lake, in a place abounding in flowers, fruits, and water, resonating with the songs of various birds, was the chief hermitage of a <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer).
285.021. There, together with the young <s>Nāga</s>, the entire episode was related in detail.
285.022. Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'What use are jewels? What use is gold to you? In his dwelling there is a noose named <s>Amogha</s> (Unfailing) — ask for that.'
285.023. Then the hunter, his desire aroused for the <s>Amoghapāśa</s> (Unfailing Noose), having heard the <s>ṛṣi's</s> words, went again to the <s>Nāga</s> dwelling.
285.024. He saw the <s>Amoghapāśa</s> at the entrance of the dwelling.
285.025. He thought: 'This is the noose that I should ask for.'
285.025. Having realized this, he entered the <s>Nāga</s> dwelling.
285.025. Then <s>Janmacitra</s>, the young <s>Nāga</s>, and the other <s>Nāgas</s> joyfully greeted him and offered him jewels.
285.026. He said: 'Enough of jewels for me.
285.027. Rather, give me this <s>Amoghapāśa</s>.'
285.027. The <s>Nāga</s> said: 'What use is this to you? When we are attacked by <s>Garuḍa</s>, we protect ourselves with this.'
285.028. The hunter said: 'For you, this is of use only occasionally, when attacked by <s>Garuḍa</s>.
285.029. But for me, there is constant use for it.
285.030. In return for what has been done and the service rendered, give it to me.'
285.030. The young <s>Nāga</s> <s>Janmacitra</s> thought: 'He has done me much service.
285.031. After consulting my parents, I will give it.'
285.031. Having consulted his parents, the noose was given.
285.032. Then that hunter, his mind filled with joy and delight as if he had obtained the earth, taking the <s>Amoghapāśa</s>, departed from the <s>Nāga</s> dwelling and went to his own home.

body.text:
286.001. <286>yāvadapareṇa samayena dhano rājā devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
286.001. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato na putro na duhitā/
286.002. sa kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitah--anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham/
286.003. na me putro na duhitā/
286.003. mamātyayātsvakulavaṃśacchede rāṣṭrāpahāraḥ sarvasantasvāpateyamaputramiti kṛtvā anyarājavidheyo bhaviṣyatīti/
286.004. sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavairucyate--deva, kimasi cintāparah? sa etatprakaraṇaṃ vistareṇārocayati/
286.006. te kathayati--devatārādhanaṃ kuru, putraste bhaviṣyatīti/
286.006. so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīnanyāṃśca devatāviśeṣānāyācate, tadyathā--ārāmadevatā vanadevatā catvaradevatā śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikāḥ/
286.008. sahajāḥ sahadharmikā nityāvubaddhā api devatā āyācate/
286.009. asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraśceti/
286.009. tacca neivam/
286.010. yadyevamabhaviṣyat, ekaikasya putrasahasramabhaviṣyat, tadyathā rājñaścakravartinaḥ/
286.010. api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvātputrā jāyante duhitaraśca/
286.011. katameṣāṃ trayāṇām? mātāpitarau raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau/
286.012. mātā cāsya kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī ca/
286.012. gandharvaḥ pratyupasthito bhavati/
286.013. eṣā trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvātputrā jāyante duhitaraśca/
286.013. sa caivamāyācanaparastiṣṭhati/
286.014. anyatamaśca bhadrakalpiko bodhisattvastasyāgramahiṣyā avakrāntaḥ/
286.015. pañcāveṇīyā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme/
286.015. katame pañca? raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti viraktaṃ jānāti/
286.016. kālaṃ jānāti kratuṃ jānāti/
286.016. garbhamavakrāntaṃ jānāti/
286.016. yasya sakāśādgarbhamavakrāmati tamapi jānāti/
286.017. dārakaṃ jānāti, dārikāṃ jānāti/
286.017. saceddārako bhavati, dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati/
286.018. saceddārikā bhavati, vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati/
286.018. sā āttamanāḥ svāminn ārocayati--diṣṭyā vardhasva āryaputra/
286.019. āpannasattvāsmi saṃvṛttā/
286.019. yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati, niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti/
286.020. so 'pyāttamanāttamanāḥ pūrvaṃ kāyamunnamayya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya udānamudānayati--apyevāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam/
286.022. jāto me syānnāvajātaḥ/
286.022. kṛtyāni me kurvīt/
286.022. pratibharet/
286.022. dāyādyaṃ me pratipadyeta/
286.023. kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt/
286.023. asmākaṃ cāpyatītakālagatānāmalpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāṃnā dakṣiṇāmādekṣyati--idaṃ tayoryatratatropapannayorgacchatoranugacchatu iti/
286.025. āpannasattvāṃ viditvā upariprāsādatalagatāmayantritāṃ dhārayati tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurkaṭukaṣāyavivarjitairāhāraiḥ/
286.026. hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīmapsarasamiva nandanavanacāriṇīṃ mañcānmañcaṃ pīṭhātpīṭhamanavatarantīmadharimāṃ bhūmim/
286.027. na cāsyāḥ kiṃcidamanojñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadeva garbhasya paripākāya/
286.028. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayātprasūtā/
286.029. dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaśchatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvistīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṇaḥ saṃgatabhrūstuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ/
286.030. tasya jātau ānandabheryastāḍitāḥ/
286.031. śrutvā rājā kathayati--kimetaditi/
286.031. antaḥpurikābhī rājñe niveditam--deva, diṣṭyā vardhasva/
286.032. putraste jāta iti/
286.032. tato rājñā taṃ sarvaṃ nagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallam <287>vyavasthitam, candanavārisiktamucchratadhvajapatākaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibuddhaṃ nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇaramaṇīyam/
body.translated_text:
286.001. At another time, King <s>Dhana</s> amused himself, sported, and enjoyed pleasures with his queen.
286.001. Though he amused himself, sported, and enjoyed pleasures, he had neither son nor daughter.
286.002. Resting his cheek on his hand, he stood absorbed in thought: 'My house is filled with abundant wealth.
286.003. I have neither son nor daughter.
286.003. After my death, with the cutting off of my family line, all property and possessions will be seized by the kingdom on the grounds that there is no son, and will come under the dominion of another king.'
286.004. The <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, relatives, and kinsmen said to him: 'Sire, why are you absorbed in thought?' He related the matter in full detail.
286.006. They said: 'Propitiate the deities; a son will be born to you.'
286.006. He, without a son but longing for one, prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), and other special deities, namely — garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, and those who accept offerings;
286.008. he also prayed to those deities who are born with one, co-dharmic, and ever-connected.
286.009. And there is this common saying in the world, that sons and daughters are born through the act of praying.
286.009. But this is not so.
286.010. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a <s>Cakravartin</s> king.
286.010. Rather, it is from the convergence of three conditions that sons and daughters are born.
286.011. Which three? The parents are passionate and have come together;
286.012. the mother is healthy and in her fertile period;
286.012. and a <s>gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) is present.
286.013. From the convergence of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born.
286.013. He continued to be devoted to prayer.
286.014. And a certain <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon) descended into his chief queen's womb.
286.015. There are five distinctive qualities in a certain wise-born woman.
286.015. Which five? She knows a man who is passionate; she knows one who is dispassionate.
286.016. She knows the time; she knows the capacity.
286.016. She knows when an embryo has descended.
286.016. She also knows from whom the embryo has descended.
286.017. She knows if it is a boy; she knows if it is a girl.
286.017. If it is a boy, it rests leaning toward the right side of the womb.
286.018. If it is a girl, it rests leaning toward the left side of the womb.
286.018. She, overjoyed, reported to her husband: 'May you prosper, noble husband!
286.019. I have become pregnant.
286.019. And since it rests leaning toward my right side, it will certainly be a boy.'
286.020. He too, overjoyed, stretching his body upward and extending his right arm, uttered an exclamation: 'May I see the face of a son long desired!
286.022. May he be born to me and not be still-born!
286.022. May he perform my duties!
286.022. May he provide for me!
286.022. May he receive my inheritance!
286.023. May my family line endure for a long time!
286.023. And having given gifts, whether small or great, and having made merit for those of us who have passed on, may he dedicate the offering in our name: "May this accompany those two, wherever they have been reborn and wherever they go."'
286.025. Having known her to be pregnant, he kept her on the upper floor of the palace, well cared for, fed with foods free from bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent tastes.
286.026. With her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like a celestial <s>Apsaras</s> wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> garden, she would not descend from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the ground below.
286.027. And she was not allowed to hear any unpleasant sound — all this was for the proper development of the embryo.
286.028. After the passing of eight or nine months, she gave birth.
286.029. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair, golden-complexioned, with a parasol-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a high nose, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, and endowed with all major and minor limbs.
286.030. At his birth, drums of joy were beaten.
286.031. Hearing this, the king said: 'What is this?'
286.031. The women of the inner palace informed the king: 'Sire, may you prosper!
286.032. A son has been born to you.'
286.032. Then the king had the entire city cleared of stones, gravel, and rubble, sprinkled with sandalwood water, with lofty banners and pennants raised, scent vessels of fragrant incense bound up, and strewn with various flowers, making it delightful.

body.text:
287.002. ājñā ca dattā--śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyo dānaṃ prayacchata, sarvabandhanamokṣaṃ ca kuruteti/
287.003. tasyaivaṃ trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatidivasān vistareṇa jātakarma karoti/
287.004. tasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitumārabdham--kiṃ bhavatu dāraksya nāmeti? amātyāḥ kathayanti--ayaṃ dārako dhanasya rājñaḥ putraḥ, bhavatu dārakasya sudhano nāmeti/
287.005. tasya sudhana iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavashtāpitam/
287.006. sudhano dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nudatto dvābhyāmaṃsadhātrībhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām/
287.007. so 'ṣṭābhirdhātrībhirunnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navatītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍairvā anyaiścottaptottaptairupakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ/
287.009. āśu vardhate hradasthamiva paṅkajam//
body.translated_text:
287.002. And the command was given: 'Give gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and travelers, and release all prisoners.'
287.003. Thus for three weeks — twenty-one days — he performed the birth celebrations in full detail.
287.004. Having performed the birth festival, they began to determine the name: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The ministers said: 'This boy is the son of King <s>Dhana</s>. Let the boy's name be <s>Sudhana</s> (Good Wealth).'
287.005. His name was established as <s>Sudhana</s>.
287.006. The boy <s>Sudhana</s> was given over to eight nurses — two wet-nurses, two milk-nurses, two nurses for cleaning, and two play-nurses.
287.007. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other specially prepared provisions.
287.009. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

body.text:
287.010. sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāmuddhāre nyāse nikṣepe vastuparīkṣāyāṃ kumāraparīkṣāyāṃ kumārikāparīkṣāyāṃ dāruparīkṣāyāṃ ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ vastraparīkṣāyām/
287.012. so 'ṣṭāsu parīkṣāsu ghaṭako vācakaḥ paṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
287.012. sa yāni tāni bhavanti rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryamanuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalamabhinirjityādhyāvasatāṃ pṛthagbhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni, tasyathā--hastigrīvāyāmaśvapṛṣṭhe rathe tsarau dhanuṣi apayāne niryāṇe 'ṅkuśagrahe pāśagrahe chedye bhedye muṣṭibandhe padabandhe dūravedhe śabdavedhe marmavedhe 'kṣuṇṇavedhe dṛḍhaprahāritāyām/
287.016. pañcasthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ/
287.017. tasya pitrā trīṇyantaḥpurāṇi vyavasthāpitāni jyeṣṭhaṃ madhyaṃ kanīyasam/
287.017. trīṇi vāsagṛhāṇi māpitāni, haimantikaṃ graiṣmikaṃ vārṣikam/
287.018. trīṇyudyānāni māpitāni, haimantikaṃ graiṣmikaṃ vārṣikam/
287.019. tataḥ sudhanakumāra upariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati//
body.translated_text:
287.010. When he had grown up, he was trained in writing, arithmetic, calculation, sealing, reckoning, depositing, safekeeping, evaluation of properties, evaluation of boys, evaluation of girls, evaluation of wood, evaluation of jewels, and evaluation of cloth.
287.012. He became expert, articulate, learned, and skilled in practice in all eight evaluations.
287.012. He mastered those various arts and crafts that belong to anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s> kings who have attained sovereignty over provinces and dwell having conquered the great circle of the earth — namely: riding on elephant-necks, on horseback, in chariots, in stealth, in archery, in retreat, in advance, in goad-wielding, in lasso-wielding, in cutting, in piercing, in fist-combat, in foot-combat, in long-distance striking, in sound-striking, in striking vital points, in unerring striking, and in delivering firm blows.
287.016. He became accomplished in the five positions.
287.017. His father established three inner courts for him: the senior, the middle, and the junior.
287.017. Three residential palaces were built: for winter, summer, and the rainy season.
287.018. Three gardens were laid out: for winter, summer, and the rainy season.
287.019. Then Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, ascending to the upper terrace of the palace, sported, delighted, and amused himself with music played without human musicians.

body.text:
287.021. yāvadapareṇa samayena halako lubdhako mṛgayāmanveṣamāṇastena tenānuvicarannanyatamaṃ parvatamanuprāptaḥ/
287.022. tasya ca parvatasyādhastādṛṣerāśramapadaṃ paśyati puṣpaphalasampannaṃ nānāpakṣigaṇavicāritam/
287.023. mahāntaṃ ca hradamutpalakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannaṃ haṃsakāraṇḍavacakravākopaśobhitam/
287.024. sa tamāśramapadaṃ paribhramitumārabdhaḥ/
287.024. yāvattam ṛṣiṃ paśyati dīrghakeśaśmaśrunakharomāṇaṃ vātāpakarṣitaśarīraṃ cīvaravalkaladhāriṇamanyatamavṛkṣamūlāśrayatṛṇakuṭikākṛtanilayam/
287.025. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kṛtāñjalipuṭaḥ papraccha--bhagavan, kiyacciramasmin pradeśe tava prativasatah? catvāriṃśadvarṣāṇi/
287.027. asti tvayā iyatā kālenāsmin pradeśe kaścidāścaryādbhutadharmo dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā? praśāntātmā ṛṣirmandaṃ mandamuvāca--bhadramukha, dṛṣṭaste 'yaṃ hradah? dṛṣṭo bhagavan/
287.029. eṣā brahmasabhā nāma puṣkiriṇī utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannā nānāpakṣigaṇaniṣevitā himarajatatuṣāragaurāmbusampūrṇā surabhikusumapūrṇatoyā/
287.030. asyāṃ puṣkiriṇyāṃ pañcadaśamyāṃ manoharā nāma drumasya kinnararājasya duhitā pañcakinnarīśataparivārā nānāvidhasnānodvartanairāgatya snāti/
287.032. snānakāle cāsyā madhuragītavāditaśabdena mṛgapakṣiṇo 'vahriyante/
body.translated_text:
287.021. Then, on another occasion, the hunter <s>Halaka</s>, wandering here and there in search of game, arrived at a certain mountain.
287.022. At the foot of that mountain, he saw the hermitage of a sage, abundant with flowers and fruits, frequented by flocks of various birds.
287.023. And a great lake covered with <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily), and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus), adorned with geese, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and <s>cakravāka</s> birds.
287.024. He began to wander about that hermitage.
287.024. Then he saw the sage — with long hair, beard, nails, and body-hair, his body emaciated by wind and sun, wearing bark-cloth garments, dwelling in a grass hut at the foot of a certain tree.
287.025. Having seen him and bowed at his feet, with joined palms he asked: 'Blessed one, how long have you dwelt in this place?' 'Forty years.'
287.027. 'Have you, in all this time, seen or heard anything wondrous or marvelous in this place?' The sage, serene of soul, said slowly and gently: 'Good sir, have you seen this lake?' 'I have, blessed one.'
287.029. 'This is the lotus pool called <s>Brahmasabhā</s>, covered with <s>utpalas</s>, lotuses, <s>kumudas</s>, and <s>puṇḍarīkas</s>, frequented by flocks of various birds, filled with waters white as snow, silver, and frost, and fragrant with blossoming flowers.
287.030. In this pool, on the fifteenth day of each fortnight, <s>Manoharā</s>, the daughter of the <s>Kinnara</s>-king <s>Druma</s>, accompanied by five hundred <s>Kinnarī</s> attendants, comes to bathe, with various ablutions and anointings.
287.032. And during her bathing, the sweet sound of her singing and music captivates the deer and birds.

body.text:
288.001. ahamapi taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā mahatā prītisaumanasyena saptāhamatināmayāmi/
288.001. etadāścaryaṃ bhadramukha mayā dṛṣṭamiti/
288.002. atha halakasya lubdhakasyaitadabhavat--śobhano 'yaṃ mayā amoghaḥ pāśo nāgāllabdho manoharāyāḥ kinnaryāḥ kṣepsyāmīti/
288.003. so 'pareṇa samayena pūrṇapañcadaśyāmamoghaṃ pāśamādāya hradatīrasamīpe puṣpaphalaviṭapagahanamāśritya avadhānatatparo 'vashtitaḥ/
288.004. yāvanmanoharā kinnarī pañcaśataparivāritā tādṛśyaiva vibhūtyā brahmasabhāṃ puṣkiriṇīmavatīrṇā snātum/
288.005. tatsamantaraṃ ca halakena lubdhakena amoghaḥ pāśaḥ kṣiptaḥ, yena manoharā kinnarī baddhā/
288.006. tayā amoghapāśaśritayā hrade mahāhatanādaḥ kṛto bhīṣaṇaśca śabdo niścāritaḥ, yaṃ śrutvā pariśiṣṭaḥ kinnarigaṇa itaścāmutaśca saṃbhrānto manoharāṃ nirīkṣitumārabdhaḥ/
288.008. paśyanti baddhām/
288.008. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhītā niṣpalāyitāḥ/
288.009. adrākṣītsa lubdhakastāṃ paramarūpadarśanīyām/
288.009. dṛṣṭvā ca punarupaśliṣṭo grahīṣyāmīti/
288.010. sā āha--hā hatāsmi, hā mandabhāgyā, mamodṛśīmavasthāmāptām/
288.011. mā naiṣīstvaṃ hi mā sprākṣīr naitattva suceṣṭitam/
288.012. rājabhogyā surūpāhaṃ na sādhu grahaṇaṃ tava//1// iti/
288.013. lubdhakaḥ prāha--yadi tvāṃ na gṛhṇāmi, niṣpalāyase/
288.013. sā kathayati--nāhaṃ niṣpalāye/
288.014. yadi na śraddadhāsi, imaṃ cūḍāmaṇiṃ gṛhāṇa/
288.014. asyānubhāvenāhamuparivihāyasā gacchāmīti/
288.015. lubdhakaḥ kathayati--kathaṃ jāne? tayā śirasthaścūḍāmaṇirdatta uktaśca--eṣa cūḍāmaṇiryasya haste, tasyāhaṃ vaśā bhavāmi/
288.016. tato lubdhakenāsau cūḍāmaṇirgṛhītaḥ, pāśabaddhāṃ caināṃ saṃprashtitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
288.001. I too, hearing that sound, pass seven days in great joy and delight.
288.001. This is the wonder, good sir, that I have seen.'
288.002. Then the hunter <s>Halaka</s> thought: 'This is excellent — I obtained this unfailing snare from a <s>Nāga</s>; I shall cast it upon the <s>Kinnarī</s> <s>Manoharā</s>.'
288.003. On another occasion, on the full-moon fifteenth day, taking the unfailing snare, he positioned himself near the lake shore, hidden among a thicket of flowering and fruiting branches, attentive and alert.
288.004. Then <s>Manoharā</s> the <s>Kinnarī</s>, accompanied by five hundred attendants, descended into the <s>Brahmasabhā</s> pool with that same splendor to bathe.
288.005. At that very moment, <s>Halaka</s> the hunter cast the unfailing snare, by which <s>Manoharā</s> the <s>Kinnarī</s> was bound.
288.006. Caught in the unfailing snare, she raised a great cry of anguish in the lake and uttered a terrifying sound; hearing it, the remaining company of <s>Kinnarīs</s>, bewildered this way and that, began to look for <s>Manoharā</s>.
288.008. They saw her bound.
288.008. Seeing her, they fled in terror.
288.009. The hunter saw that supremely beautiful creature.
288.009. Seeing her, he embraced her and was about to seize her.
288.010. She cried: 'Alas, I am doomed! Alas, I am unlucky, to have reached such a state!'
288.011. 'Do not take me away; do not touch me — this is not a fitting deed for you.
288.012. I am of beautiful form, fit to be enjoyed by a king; your seizure of me is not right.' //1//
288.013. The hunter said: 'If I do not seize you, you will fly away.'
288.013. She said: 'I will not fly away.
288.014. If you do not trust me, take this <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel).
288.014. It is by its power that I travel through the sky.'
288.015. The hunter said: 'How can I be sure?' She gave him the crest-jewel from her head and said: 'Whoever holds this crest-jewel, I am subject to his will.'
288.016. Then the hunter took that crest-jewel and set out, leading her bound with the snare.

body.text:
288.017. tena khalu samayena sudhanarājakumāro mṛgayānirgataḥ/
288.017. adrākṣītsa lubdhakaḥ sudhanaṃ rājakumāramabhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prāsādikam/
288.018. dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaitadabhavat--ayaṃ ca rājakumāraḥ, iyaṃ ca paramadarśanīyā/
288.019. yadyenāṃ drakṣyati, balādgrahīṣyati/
288.019. yannvahamenāṃ prābhṛtanyāyena svayamevopanayeyam/
288.020. tatastāṃ pāśabddhāmādāya yena rājakumārastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
288.020. upasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya kathayati--idaṃ mama devasya strīratnaṃ prābhṛtamānītam, pratigṛhyatāmiti/
288.021. adrākṣītsudhanakumāro manoharāṃ kinnarīmabhirūpāṃ darśanīyāṃ prāsādikāṃ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatāṃ sarvaguṇasamuditāmaṣṭādaśābhiḥ strīlakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtāṃ janapadakalyāṇāṃ kāñcanakalaśakūrmapīnonnatakaṭhinasahitasujātavṛttapragalbhamānastanīmabhinīlaraktāṃśukavisṛtāyatanavakamalasadṛśanayanāṃ subhruvamāyatatuṅganāsāṃ vidrūmamaṇiratnaviṃvaphalasaṃsthānasadṛśādharoṣṭhīṃ sudṛḍhaparipūrṇagaṇḍapārśvāmatyartharatikarakapolatilakānupūrvacaritāṃ saṃgatabhruvāravindavikacasadṛśaparipūrṇavimalaśaśivapuṣaṃ
pralambabāhuṃ gambhīrativalikasaṃtatamadhyāṃ stanabhārāvanāmyamānapūrvārdhāṃ rathāṅgasaṃsthitasujātajaghanāṃ kadalīgarbhasadṛśakarānupūrvāvasthitasujātakarabhoruṃ sunigūḍhasuracitasarvāṅgasundaraśirāṃ sahitamaṇipīḍāsamraktakaratalapraharṣanūpuravalayām
hārardhahāranirghoṣavimalaśitagatimāyatanīlasūkṣmakeśīṃ sacīvaraprabhraṣṭakāñcīguṇāṃ nūpurāvacchāditapādāṃ kṣāmodarīm/
288.030. tāṃ pratikīrṇahārāmuttaptajāmbūnadacārupūrṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā kumāraḥ sahasā papāta viddho dṛḍharāgaśareṇa/
288.031. tatra sa rāgavarāhadavadahanapataṅgasadṛśena jalacandracañcalavimalojjvalasvabhāvena durgrāhyatareṇa nadītaraṅgajñaṣamakarasurabhigamanena <289>garuḍapavanajavasamagatinā tūlaparivartanalaghutareṇa vānarāvasthitacapalodbhrāntatareṇa satatābhyāsakleśaniṣevaṇarāgasukhāsvādalobhena sarvakleśaviṣamadurgaprapātaniḥsaṅgena paramasalīlena cittena tadbhūtānugatayā ayoniśomanaskāradhanurvisṛtaiḥ samyogābhilaṣitaparamarahasyaśabdena kāmaśareṇa hṛdaye viddha/
body.translated_text:
288.017. At that time, the prince <s>Sudhana</s> had gone out hunting.
288.017. The hunter saw Prince <s>Sudhana</s> — handsome, beautiful, and pleasing.
288.018. Seeing him, he thought: 'Here is the prince, and here is this supremely beautiful creature.
288.019. If he sees her, he will take her by force.
288.019. Let me offer her to him as a tribute-gift on my own accord.'
288.020. Taking her, still bound, he approached the prince.
288.020. Approaching, he fell at his feet and said: 'This, my lord, is a jewel among women, brought as a tribute-gift — may it please you to accept her.'
288.021. Prince <s>Sudhana</s> beheld <s>Manoharā</s> the <s>Kinnarī</s> — beautiful, lovely, and pleasing, endowed with supremely auspicious complexion and fullness, possessing all virtues, adorned with the eighteen marks of feminine beauty, the fairest in the land — with golden-pitcher-shaped, tortoise-firm, elevated, firm, well-formed, round, proud breasts; with eyes like fresh blue-red lotuses with extended petals; with beautiful brows, a long and noble nose; with lower lip resembling the color of coral, ruby, and the <s>bimba</s> fruit; with firmly full cheeks and sides; with exceedingly delightful beauty-marks on the cheeks forming a graceful succession; with conjoined brows, a full and spotless face like a blooming lotus and the moon;
with long arms, a deep navel, a waist marked with fine lines, the front half bowing under the weight of her breasts; with well-formed hips like chariot-wheels; with forearms smooth as the core of a plantain, and well-formed beautiful thighs; with all limbs beautifully fashioned and veined; with gem-studded jewel ornaments, reddened palms, delightful anklets and bracelets;
necklaces and half-necklaces jingling, with a pure and steady gait, with long, fine, dark hair; with a loosened girdle-string from her garment, feet hidden by anklets, and a slender waist.
288.030. Seeing her, scattered necklaces and all, beautiful as refined <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, the prince suddenly fell, struck by the firm arrow of passion.
288.031. There, his mind — like a forest fire of passion, unstable as the moon reflected in water, more difficult to grasp than a fish or <s>makara</s> in river-waves, swift as <s>Garuḍa</s> or the wind, lighter than a turning cotton-flake, restless as a monkey, insatiably addicted to the taste of pleasure through constant habitual affliction, plunging without attachment through the impassable chasms of all afflictions, supremely playful — was struck in the heart by the arrow of desire, <289> released from the bow of improper attention, accompanied by the most secret sound of longing for union.

body.text:
289.004. āha ca--
289.005. dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ sudhana indusamānvaktrāṃ prāvṛḍaghanāntaraviniścariteva vidyuta/
289.007. tatsnehamanmathavilāsasamudbhavena sadyaḥ sa cetasi nu rāgaśareṇa viddhaḥ//2//
body.translated_text:
289.004. And he said:
289.005. 'Seeing her, <s>Sudhana</s>, with a face like the moon — like lightning flashing from within the rainy season's dense clouds —
289.007. was instantly struck in his heart by the arrow of passion, born of love, infatuation, and coquetry.' //2//

body.text:
289.009. sa tāmatimanoharāṃ gṛhītvā hastināpuraṃ gataḥ/
289.009. sa ca lubdhaḥ pañcagrāmavareṇācchāditaḥ/
289.010. tataḥ sudhano rājakumāro manoharayā rūpayauvanaguṇena sughanaḥ kumāronekaiścopacāraśataistathā apahṛto yathā muhūrtamapi tāṃ na jahāti/
289.011. yāvadapareṇa samayena jetavanāddvau brāhmaṇau abhyāgatau/
289.012. tatraiko rājānāṃ saṃśritaḥ, dvitīyaḥ sudhanaṃ kumāram/
289.012. yo rājānaṃ saṃśritaḥ, sa rājñā purohitaḥ sthāpito bhogaiśca saṃvibhaktaḥ/
289.013. yastu sudhanaṃ kumāram, sa bhogamātreṇa saṃvibhaktaḥ/
289.014. sa kathayati--yathā tava sahāyo brāhmaṇo mama pitrā paurohitye 'vasthāpitaḥ, evamahaṃ tvāmapi paurohitye sthāpayāmīti/
289.016. eṣa ca vṛttāntastena brāhmaṇena karṇaparamparayā śrutaḥ/
289.016. tasyaitadabhavat--ahaṃ tathā kariṣye, yathā kumāro rājyameva nāsādayiṣyati, kutastaṃ purohitaṃ sthāpayiṣyatīti? yāvadapareṇa samayena tasya rājño vijite 'nyatamaḥ kārvaṭikaḥ prativiruddhaḥ, tasya samucchittaye eko daṇḍaḥ preṣitaḥ/
289.019. sa hatavihatavidhvastaḥ pratyāgataḥ/
289.019. evam yāvatsapta, ye daṇḍāḥ preṣitāḥ, te 'pi hastavidhvastāḥ pratyāgatāḥ/
289.020. amātyai rājā vijñāpitaḥ sarvo 'sau āhūyatāmiti/
289.022. brāhmaṇa purohitaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ sa kumārasya vadhopāyakāla iti/
289.022. tena rājā vijñaptah--deva, naivamasau śakyaḥ saṃnāmayitum/
289.023. rājā kathayati--kiṃ mayā svayaṃ gantavyam? purohitaḥ kathayati--kimarthaṃ devaḥ svayaṃ gacchati? ayaṃ sudhanaḥ kumāro yuvā baladarpayuktaḥ/
289.025. eṣa daṇḍasahāyaḥ preṣyatāmiti/
289.025. rājā kathayati--evamastviti/
289.025. tato rājā kumāramāhūya kathayati--gaccha kumāra, daṇḍasahāyaḥ kārvaṭikaṃ saṃnāmaya/
289.026. evaṃ deveti sudhanaḥ kumāro rājñaḥ pratiśrutya antaḥpuraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
289.027. manoharādarśanāccāsya sarvaṃ vismṛtam/
289.027. punarapi rājñā abhihitah--punarapi taddarśanātsarvaṃ vismṛtam/
289.028. purohitena cābhihitah--deva, sudhanaḥ kumāro manoharayā atīva sakto na śakyate preṣayitum/
289.029. rājā kathayati--sādhanaṃ sajjaṃ kriyatām/
289.029. nirgataḥ kumāro 'ntaḥpurāt preṣayitavyo yathā manoharāyāḥ sakāśaṃ na prativasatīti/
289.030. evaṃ deveti amātyai rājñaḥ pratiśrutya balaugho hastyaśvarathapadātisampanno 'nakapraharaṇopakaraṇayuktaḥ sajjīkṛtaḥ/
289.032. tataḥ kumāro nirgatah uktah--gaccha kumāra, sajjo balaugha iti/
289.032. sa kathayati--deva, gamiṣyāmi <290>manoharāṃ dṛṣṭvā/
body.translated_text: Having taken that exceedingly captivating girl, he went to <s>Hastināpura</s>. And the hunter was rewarded with the gift of five choice villages. Then Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, enraptured by <s>Manoharā's</s> beauty, youth, and virtues, was so thoroughly captivated by hundreds of tender attentions that he would not leave her even for a moment. At another time, two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> arrived from <s>Jetavana</s>. Of these, one attached himself to the king, the other to Prince <s>Sudhana</s>. The one who attached himself to the king was appointed royal chaplain by the king and provided with a share of the wealth. The one who attached himself to Prince <s>Sudhana</s> was given only a portion of wealth. He said: 'Just as your companion, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, has been installed as chaplain by my father, so I shall install you as my chaplain.' This account was heard by that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> chaplain through word of mouth. He thought: 'I shall act in such a way that the prince will never attain the kingdom — how then would he install that man as chaplain?' At another time, a certain hill-chieftain in the king's domain revolted. One military expedition was sent to suppress him. It returned defeated, scattered, and destroyed. Thus up to seven expeditions were sent, and all returned defeated and destroyed. The ministers informed the king that a full call-to-arms was needed. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> chaplain reflected: 'This is the opportunity to contrive the prince's death.' He informed the king: 'Your Majesty, that rebel cannot be subdued thus.' The king said: 'Must I go myself?' The chaplain said: 'Why should Your Majesty go himself? This Prince <s>Sudhana</s> is young and full of the pride of strength. Let him be sent as commander of the army.' The king said: 'So be it.' Then the king, summoning the prince, said: 'Go, prince, and subdue the hill-chieftain as army commander.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' said Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having assented to the king, and he entered the inner palace. But upon seeing <s>Manoharā</s>, he forgot everything. Again the king commanded him — again upon seeing her, he forgot everything. The chaplain said: 'Your Majesty, Prince <s>Sudhana</s> is so attached to <s>Manoharā</s> that he cannot be sent.' The king said: 'Let the army be made ready. Once the prince has left the inner palace, he must be sent so that he does not return to <s>Manoharā's</s> presence.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' the ministers assented to the king. A great army was assembled, fully equipped with elephants, horses, chariots, infantry, and various weapons and implements. Then the prince came out and was told: 'Go, prince, the army is ready.' He said: 'Your Majesty, I shall go after seeing <s>Manoharā</s>.'

body.text:
290.001. rājā kathayati--kumāra na draṣṭavyā, kālo 'tivartate/
290.001. sa kathayati--tāvadyadi evam, mātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā gacchāmi/
290.002. gaccha kumāro avalokya jananīm/
290.002. sa manoharasantakaṃ cūḍāmaṇimādāya mātuḥsakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
290.003. pādayor nipatya kathayati--amba, ahaṃ kārvaṭikaṃ saṃnāmanāya gacchāmi/
290.005. duhitā śakrakalpasya kinnarendrasya māninī/
290.006. pālyā virahaśokārtā madvātsalyadhiyā//3//
body.translated_text: The king said: 'Prince, she must not be seen; the time is passing.' He said: 'If that is so, let me at least go after seeing my mother.' 'Go, prince, and look upon your mother.' He took a crest-jewel belonging to <s>Manoharā</s> and went to his mother. Falling at her feet, he said: 'Mother, I am going to subdue the hill-chieftain. The daughter of the <s>Kinnara</s> lord, proud as <s>Śakra's</s> own daughter — she must be protected, as she will be stricken with the grief of separation, through your motherly affection for me.' //3//

body.text:
290.007. ayaṃ cūḍāmaṇi suguptaṃ sthāpayitavyaḥ/
290.007. na kadācinmanoharāyā dātavyo 'nyatra prāṇaviyogāditi/
290.008. sa evaṃ mātaraṃ pitaraṃ saṃdiśya abhivādya ca nānāyodhabalaughatūryanir nāditaiḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
290.009. anupūrveṇa janapadānatikramya tasya kārvaṭikasya nātidūre 'nyataṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya vāsamupagataḥ/
290.010. tena khalu samayena vaiśravaṇo mahārājo 'nekayakṣaparivāro 'nekayakṣaśatasahasraparivāraḥ/
290.011. tena yakṣāṇām yakṣasamitiṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
290.011. tasya tena pathā gacchataḥ khagapathena yānamavasthitam/
290.012. tasyaitadabhavat--bahuśo 'hamanena pathā samatikrāntaḥ/
290.012. na ca me kadācidyānaṃ pratihatam/
290.013. ko 'tra heturyenedānīṃ pratihata iti? paśyati sudhanaṃ kumāram/
290.013. tasyaitadabhavat--ayaṃ bhadrakalpiko bodhisattvaḥ khedamāpatsyati yuddhāyābhiprasthitaḥ/
290.014. sāhāyyamasya karaṇīyam/
290.015. kārvaṭikaḥ saṃnāmayitavyaḥ/
290.015. na ca kasyacitprāṇinaḥ pīḍā karaṇīyeti viditvā pāñcikaṃ mahāyakṣasenāpatimāmantrayate--ehi tvaṃ pāñcika, sudhanasya kumārasya kārvaṭikamayuddhena saṃnāmaya/
290.017. na ca te kasyacitprāṇinaḥ pīḍā kartavyeti/
290.017. tatheti pāñcikena yakṣasenāpatinā vaiśravaṇasya mahārājasya pratiśrutya divyaścaturaṅgo balakāyo nirmitah--tālamātrapramāṇāḥ puruṣaḥ, parvatapramāṇā hastinaḥ, hastipramāṇā aśvāḥ/
290.019. tato nānāvidhakhaṅgamuśalatomarapāśacakraśaraparaśvadhādiśastraviśeṣeṇa nānāvāditrasaṃkṣobheṇa ca mahābhayamupadarśayan mahatā balaudhena pāñciko 'nuprāptaḥ/
290.021. hastyaśvarathanirghoṣānnānāvāditranidvanāt/
290.022. yakṣāṇāṃ svaprabhāvācca prākāraḥ prapapāta vai//4//
body.translated_text: 'This crest-jewel must be kept safely guarded. It must never be given to <s>Manoharā</s>, except at the point of her death.' Having thus instructed his mother and father and paid his respects, he set out amid the clamor of various instruments and the great mass of warriors, elephants, and horses. Traveling gradually through the provinces, he arrived not far from that hill-chieftain's territory and halted for the night at the foot of a certain tree. At that time, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King, was surrounded by a retinue of many <s>Yakṣas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>. He had set out for a <s>Yakṣa</s> assembly. As he was traveling by that path through the sky, his vehicle came to a halt. He thought: 'Many times have I passed this way. Never before has my vehicle been blocked. What is the reason it is blocked now?' He saw Prince <s>Sudhana</s>. He thought: 'This is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Fortunate Age who will meet with hardship, having set out for battle. He must be given assistance. The hill-chieftain must be subdued. But no living being must be harmed.' Having decided thus, he addressed <s>Pāñcika</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s> general: 'Come, <s>Pāñcika</s>, subdue the hill-chieftain for Prince <s>Sudhana</s> without battle. You must not harm any living being.' 'So be it,' said <s>Pāñcika</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s> general, having assented to the Great King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He conjured a divine fourfold army — men the height of palm trees, elephants the size of mountains, and horses the size of elephants. Then, displaying a great spectacle of terror with various swords, pestles, lances, nooses, discuses, arrows, battle-axes, and other special weapons, and with the tumult of various instruments, <s>Pāñcika</s> advanced with a great host of forces. 'From the thundering of elephants, horses, and chariots, from the roar of various instruments, and from the very radiance of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, the rampart crumbled and fell.' //4//

body.text:
290.023. tataste karvaṭanivāsinastaṃ balaughaṃ dṛṣṭvā tacca prākārapatanaṃ paraṃ viṣādamāpannāḥ papracchuh--kuta eṣa balaugha āgacchatīti? te kathayanti--śīghraṃ dvārāṇi muñcata/
290.024. eṣa pṛṣṭhataḥ kumāra āgacchati/
290.025. tasya ca balaugho yadi ciraṃ vidhārayiṣyatha, sarvathā na bhaviṣyatheti/
290.026. te kathayanti--
290.027. vyutpannā na vayaṃ rājño na kumārasya dhīmataḥ/
290.028. nṛpapauruṣakebhyo sma bhītāḥ saṃtrāsamāgatāḥ//5//
body.translated_text: Then the inhabitants of that hill-fort, seeing that army and the falling of the rampart, were overcome with extreme dismay and asked: 'Where is this army coming from?' They were told: 'Open the gates quickly! The prince is coming behind. If you withstand his army any longer, you will surely not survive.' They said: 'We have not revolted against the king, nor against the wise prince. We are frightened and terrified by the king's brutish men.' //5//

body.text:
290.029. tairdvārāṇi muktāni/
290.029. tata ucchritadhvajapatākāpūrṇakalaśā nānāvidhatūryanir nāditaiḥ sudhanaṃ kumāraṃ pratyudgatāḥ/
290.030. tena ca samāśvāsitāḥ, tadabhiprāyaśca rājabhaṭaḥ sthāpitaḥ/
290.030. nipakāśca nigṛhītāḥ/
290.031. karapratyāyāśca nibaddhāḥ/
290.031. tatastaṃ karvaṭakaṃ sphītīkṛtya sudhanakumārah <291>pratinivṛttaḥ/
body.translated_text: They opened the gates. Then, with raised banners and flags, full water-pots, and the sound of various instruments, they went out to welcome Prince <s>Sudhana</s>. He reassured them and stationed a royal officer in accordance with their wishes. The unruly were restrained. Tributes and taxes were fixed. Then, having made that hill-fort prosperous, Prince <s>Sudhana</s> turned back.

body.text:
291.001. dhanena ca rājñā tāmeva rātriṃ svapno dṛṣṭah--gṛdhreṇāgatya rājña udaraṃ sphoṭayitvā antrāṇyākṛṣya sarvaṃ tannagaramantrairveṣṭitam, sapta ratnāni gṛhaṃ praveśyamānāni dṛṣṭāni/
291.002. tato rājā bhītastrastaḥ saṃvigna āhṛṣṭaromakūpo laghukadhvevotthāya mahāśayane niṣadya kare kapokaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitah--mā haiva me atonidānaṃ rājyaccyutirbhaviṣyati, jīvitasya vā antarāya iti/
291.005. sa prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ svapnaṃ brāhmaṇāya purohitāya nivedayāmāsa/
291.005. sa saṃlakṣayati--yādṛśo devena svapno dṛṣṭaḥ, niyataṃ kumāreṇa karvaṭako nirjitaḥ/
291.006. vitathanirdeśaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
291.007. iti kṛtvā kathayati--deva, na śobhanaḥ svapnaḥ/
291.007. niyatamatonidānaṃ rājyāccyutirbhaviṣyati, jīvitasyāntarāya iti/
291.008. kevalaṃ tu atrāsti pratikāraḥ, sa ca brāhmaṇakamantreṣu dṛṣṭaḥ/
291.008. ko 'sau pratikārah? deva, udyāne puṣkariṇī puruṣapramāṇikā kartavyā/
291.009. tata sudhayā praleptavyā/
291.010. susaṃmṛṣṭāṃ kṛtvā kṣudramṛgāṇāṃ rudhireṇa pūrayitavyā/
291.010. tato devena snānaprayatena tāṃ puṣkariṇīmekena so 'ānenāvataritavyam, ekenāvatīrya dvitīyenottaritavyam, dvitīyenottīrya tṛtīyenāvataritavyam, tṛtīyenāvatīrya caturthenottaritavyam/
291.012. tataścaturbhirbrāhmaṇairvedavedāṅgapāragairdevasya pādayorjihvayā nirleḍhavyam, kinnaravasayā ca dhūpo deyaḥ/
291.013. evaṃ devo vidhūtapāpaściraṃ rājyaṃ pālayiṣyatīti/
291.014. rājā kathayati--sarvametacchakyam yadidaṃ kinnaramedamatīva durlabham/
291.014. purohitaḥ kathayati--deva, yadeva durlabhaṃ tadeva sulabham/
291.015. rājā kathayati--yathā katham? purohitaḥ kathayati--deva, nanviyaṃ manoharā kinnarī/
291.016. rājā kathayati--purohita, mā maivaṃ vada/
291.016. kumārasyātra prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ/
291.017. sa kathayati--nanu devena śrutam--
291.018. tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet/
291.019. grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet//6//
body.translated_text: That same night, the king had a dream — a vulture came and burst open the king's belly, pulled out his entrails, and the entire city was enveloped with intestines; and seven treasures were seen being brought into the palace. Then the king, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, rose quickly in the early hours, sat on his great bed, placed his cheek on his hand, and remained absorbed in worry: 'May it not be that from this, I shall lose my kingdom, or there be danger to my life!' At dawn, he reported the dream to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> chaplain. The chaplain reflected: 'From the dream the king has had, the prince has certainly conquered the hill-chieftain. A false interpretation must be given.' Having decided thus, he said: 'Your Majesty, the dream is not auspicious. Certainly from this cause, you shall lose your kingdom and your life will be in danger. However, there is a remedy, and it is found in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>mantras</s>.' 'What is that remedy?' 'Your Majesty, in the garden, a pool the depth of a man should be constructed. It should be plastered with white stucco. When smoothly polished, it should be filled with the blood of small animals. Then Your Majesty, having purified himself with a ritual bath, should descend into that pool by one stairway, and having descended, ascend by a second; having ascended by the second, descend by a third; having descended by the third, ascend by a fourth. Then four <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s> should lick Your Majesty's feet with their tongues, and incense should be offered with <s>Kinnara</s>-fat. Thus Your Majesty, having purified his sins, will rule the kingdom for a long time.' The king said: 'All of this is possible, but <s>Kinnara</s>-fat is exceedingly difficult to obtain.' The chaplain said: 'Your Majesty, what is difficult is precisely what is easy.' The king said: 'How so?' The chaplain said: 'Your Majesty, is not this <s>Manoharā</s> a <s>Kinnarī</s>?' The king said: 'Chaplain, do not say such a thing! The prince's very life rests in her.' He said: 'Has not Your Majesty heard? "One should sacrifice one for the sake of the family; sacrifice the family for the sake of the village; sacrifice the village for the sake of the country; sacrifice the whole earth for the sake of oneself."' //6//

body.text:
291.020. dṛḍhenāddhyātmanā(?) rājyaṃ kumārasyāsya dhīmataḥ/
291.021. śakṣyasi hyaparāṃ kartuṃ ghātayaināṃ manoharām//7// iti/
291.022. ātmābhinandino na kiṃcinna pratipadyanta iti tenādhivāsitam/
291.022. tato yathopadiṣṭaṃ purohitena kārayitumārabdham/
291.023. puṣkariṇī khātā sudhayopaliptā kṣudramṛgarudhiramupāvartāyitumārabdham/
291.024. sa ca prayogaḥ sudhanasyāntaḥpurajanenopalabdhaḥ/
291.024. tāḥ prītimanasaḥ saṃvṛttāh--vayaṃ rūpayauvanasampannāḥ/
291.025. idānīmasmākaṃ sudhanaḥ kumāraḥ paricārayiṣyatīti/
291.026. tāḥ pramuditā dṛṣṭvā manoharā pṛcchati--kim yūyamatīva praharṣitā iva? yāvadaparayā sa vṛttānto vistareṇa manoharāyā niveditaḥ/
291.027. tato manoharā saṃjātaduḥkhadaurmanasyā yena sudhanasya kumārasya jananī tenopasaṃkrāntā/
291.028. upasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya karuṇadīnavilambitairakṣarairetamarthaṃ nivedayāmāsa/
291.029. sā kathayati--yadyevaṃ svāgatamidaṃ kuru vicārayiṣyāmīti/
291.029. manoharayā āgamya punarapi samākhyātam/
291.030. tayā api vicāritam/
291.030. paśyati bhūtam/
291.030. tatastayā sa cūḍāmaṇirvastrāṇi ca manoharāyai dattāni, uktā ca--putrike, prāpte kāle āgantavyam/
291.031. evaṃ mamopālambho na bhavatīti/
291.032. tato rājā yathādiṣṭena krameṇa snānaprayato rudhirapūrṇāṃ puṣkiriṇimavatīryottīrṇah<292>/
292.001. tato 'sya brāhmaṇairjihvayā pādau nilīḍhau, avasthitah--ānīyatāṃ kinnarīti ca samādiṣṭam/
292.002. tatsamanantarameva manoharā gaganatalamutplutya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
292.003. sparśasaṃgamanaṃ mahyaṃ ramitaṃ ca me/
292.004. nāgīva bandhanānmuktā eṣā gacchāmi sāmpratam//8// iti/
292.005. rājñā dṛṣṭā vāyupathena gacchantī/
292.005. sa bhītaḥ purohitamāmantrayate--yadarthaṃ kṛto yatnaḥ, sa na saṃpannaḥ, manoharā kinnarī niṣpalāyiteti/
292.006. purohitaḥ kathayati--deva, siddhārtho 'pagatapāpo devaḥ sāmpratamiti/
292.007. tato manoharāyāḥ khagapathena gacchantyā etadabhavat--yadahametāmavasthāṃ prāptā, tattasya ṛṣerbyapadeśāt/
292.008. yadi tena nākhyātamabhaviṣyat, nāhaṃ grahaṇa gatā abhaviṣyat/
292.009. tena hi yasyāmi tāvadasyaiva ṛṣeḥ sakāśāmiti/
292.009. sā tasyāśramapadaṃ gatā/
292.009. pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā tam ṛṣimuvāca--maharṣe, tava vyapadeśādahaṃ grahaṇaṃ gatā, manuṣyasya saṃsparśaśca saṃprāptaḥ/
292.011. jīvitāntarāyaścaitatsaṃvṛttaḥ/
292.011. tadvijñāpayāmi--yadi yadā kadācitsudhanaḥ kumāra āgacchati māṃ samanveṣamāṇaḥ, tasyemāmaṅgulimudrāṃ dāturmahasi/
292.012. evaṃ ca vaktavyam--kumāra, viṣamāḥ panthāno durgamāḥ, khedamāpatsyase, nirvatasveti/
292.013. yadi nirvāyamāṇo na riṣṭhet, tasya mārgaṃ vyapadeṣṭumarhasi--kumāra, manoharayā samākhyātam--uttare digbhāge trayaḥ kālaparvatāḥ, tānatikramya apare trayaḥ, tānapyatikramya apare trayaḥ, tānatikramya himavān parvatarājaḥ, tasyottareṇotkalakaparvataḥ, tata utkūlako jalapatha ekadhārako vajrakaḥ kāmarūpī/
292.017. tatra khadirake parvate guhā, praveśa ekadhārake tu kīlakāḥ, vajrake pakṣirājena praveśaḥ/
292.018. ebhirupāyaiste parvatā atikramaṇīyāḥ, yantrāṇi ca bhuṅktavyāni/
292.019. ajavaktrameṇḍhakaḥ puruṣo rākṣasarūpī piṅgalāguhāyāṃ lālāsrotasā mahānajagaro vegena pradhāvati/
292.020. sa te vikrameṇa hantavyaḥ/
292.020. arāntaragatāṃ nābhīm yatra paśyettatra kiṭibhakaśca/
292.022. ayaṃ bhuktena bāṇena hantavyo mama kāraṇāt/
292.023. yatra paśyeddvau meṣau saṃghaṭṭantau parasparam/
292.024. tayoḥ śṛṅgamekaṃ bhaṅktvā mārgaṃ pratilapsyase//9//
body.translated_text:
291.020. 'Strengthen your inner resolve — the kingdom belongs to this wise prince.
291.021. You will be able to obtain another; have this charming one killed.' //7//
291.022. Those who are attached to self-gratification will stop at nothing — so the king consented.
291.022. Then what the chaplain had prescribed began to be carried out.
291.023. A pool was dug and plastered with lime; the blood of small animals was made to flow into it.
291.024. This scheme was discovered by the women of <s>Sudhana</s>'s inner palace.
291.024. They became delighted: 'We are endowed with beauty and youth.
291.025. Now Prince <s>Sudhana</s> will attend upon us!'
291.026. Seeing them joyful, <s>Manoharā</s> asked: 'Why are you all so excessively happy?' Then another woman reported the entire matter to <s>Manoharā</s> in detail.
291.027. Then <s>Manoharā</s>, overcome by grief and sorrow, approached the mother of Prince <s>Sudhana</s>.
291.028. Having approached, she fell at her feet and, with words faltering in piteous distress, reported the matter.
291.029. She said: 'If so, welcome — do as you please; I shall consider the matter.'
291.029. <s>Manoharā</s> came back and reported again.
291.030. She too investigated.
291.030. She found it to be true.
291.030. Then she gave to <s>Manoharā</s> her crest-jewel and garments, and said: 'Daughter, when the time comes, you must leave.
291.031. In this way, no blame will fall on me.'
291.032. Then the king, following the prescribed procedure, bathed himself in the pool filled with blood, emerged,
292.001. and his feet were licked with the tongues of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. He stood and commanded: 'Let the <s>Kinnarī</s> be brought.'
292.002. At that very moment, <s>Manoharā</s> leaped into the sky and spoke a verse:
292.003. 'I have had the touch and union;
292.004. like a she-elephant freed from her bonds, I now depart.' //8//
292.005. The king saw her going by the path of the wind.
292.005. Frightened, he addressed the chaplain: 'The purpose for which the effort was made has not been accomplished — the <s>Kinnarī</s> <s>Manoharā</s> has escaped!'
292.006. The chaplain said: 'Sire, Your Majesty has now accomplished his goal and is free from sin.'
292.007. Then, as <s>Manoharā</s> traveled by the sky-path, this occurred to her: 'That I reached this state was on account of that <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage).
292.008. If he had not revealed my whereabouts, I would not have been captured.
292.009. So let me first go to that very <s>ṛṣi</s>.'
292.009. She went to his hermitage.
292.009. Having bowed at his feet, she said to the <s>ṛṣi</s>: 'Great sage, through your revelation I was captured and came into contact with a human.
292.011. And this has become a threat to my life.
292.011. I make this request — if ever Prince <s>Sudhana</s> should come seeking me, please give him this signet ring.
292.012. And say to him: "Prince, the paths are treacherous and impassable; you will suffer hardship. Turn back."
292.013. If, while being dissuaded, he does not turn back, please show him the way: "Prince, <s>Manoharā</s> has described the route — in the northern direction there are three Black Mountains; beyond them, another three; beyond those, another three; beyond them is <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains; to its north is <s>Utkalaka</s> Mountain; then the <s>Utkūlaka</s> water-passage, the Single-Stream, the <s>Vajraka</s>, and the Shape-Shifter.
292.017. On <s>Khadiraka</s> Mountain there is a cave; entry to the Single-Stream is through pegs; entry to the <s>Vajraka</s> is through the king of birds.
292.018. By these means are the mountains to be crossed, and the mechanisms to be mastered.
292.019. A goat-faced ram-man in <s>Rākṣasa</s> form, and in the cave of <s>Piṅgalā</s> a great serpent rushes forth on a torrent of saliva.
292.020. He must be slain by valor.
292.020. Where one sees a navel in a gap without interval, there is a <s>kiṭibhaka</s> (insect-demon).
292.022. He must be killed with a spent arrow, for my sake.
292.023. Where one sees two rams butting each other,
292.024. by breaking one of their horns, you will find the path.' //9//

body.text:
292.025. āyasau puruśau dṛṣṭvā śastrapāṇī mahābhayau/
292.026. tayorekaṃ pādayitvā mārgaṃ pratilapsyase//10//
body.translated_text:
292.025. 'Seeing two iron men, armed and terrifying,
292.026. by felling one of them, you will find the path.' //10//

body.text:
292.027. saṃkocayantīṃ prasārayantīṃ rākṣasīmāyasaṃ mukham/
292.028. yadā paśyettatra kīlakaṃ lalāṭe tasyā nikhānayet//11//
body.translated_text:
292.027. 'A <s>Rākṣasī</s> with an iron mouth, contracting and expanding —
292.028. when you see her, drive a peg into her forehead.' //11//

body.text:
292.029. śūlāvartastadā kūpo vilaṅghyaste ṣaṣṭihastakaḥ/
292.030. haripiṅgalakeśākṣo dāruṇo yatra rākṣasaḥ//12//
body.translated_text:
292.029. 'Then there is the whirlpool of spears, a pit sixty hands deep,
292.030. where dwells a fearsome <s>Rākṣasa</s> with tawny-red hair and eyes.' //12//

body.text:
292.031. kārmukaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā hantavyaśca durāsadaḥ/
292.032. nadyaśca bahavastāryā nakragrahasamākulāḥ//13//
body.translated_text:
292.031. 'Having made a circle with the bow, the formidable one must be slain.
292.032. And there are many rivers to be crossed, swarming with crocodiles and sea-monsters.' //13//

body.text:
293.001. <293>raṅgā pataṅgā tapanī citrā rudantī hasantī āśīviṣā vetranadī ca/
293.002. raṅgāyāṃ rākṣasīkopaḥ pataṅgāyāmamanuṣyakāḥ/
293.003. tapantyāṃ grāhabahulatvaṃ citrāyāṃ kāmarūpiṇaḥ//14//

293.004. rudantyāṃ kinnarīceṭyo hasantyāṃ kinnarasnuṣā/
293.005. āśīviṣāyāṃ nānāvidhāḥ sarpā vetranadyāṃ tu śālmaliḥ//15//
body.translated_text:
293.004. 'In <s>Rudantī</s>, <s>Kinnarī</s> maidservants; in <s>Hasantī</s>, <s>Kinnara</s> daughters-in-law;
293.005. in <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, serpents of many kinds; and in the <s>Vetra</s> River, silk-cotton thorns.' //15//

body.text:
293.006. raṅgāyāṃ dhairyakaraṇaṃ pataṅgāyāṃ parākramaḥ/
293.007. tapantyāṃ grāhamukhabandhaṃ citrāyāṃ vividhagītam//16//
body.translated_text:
293.006. 'In <s>Raṅgā</s>, steadfastness is the means of crossing; in <s>Pataṅgā</s>, valor;
293.007. in <s>Tapanī</s>, binding the mouths of crocodiles; in <s>Citrā</s>, various songs.' //16//

body.text:
293.008. rudantyāṃ saumanasye samuttāram, hasantyāṃ tūṣṇībhāvayogena, aśīviṣāyāṃ sarpaviṣamantrayogena, vetranadyāṃ tīkṣṇaśastrasampātayogena samuttāraḥ/
293.009. nadīḥ samatikramya pañca yakṣaśatāni gulmakam/
293.010. taddhairyamāsthāya vidrābyam/
293.010. tato drumasya kinnararājasya bhavanamiti/
293.010. tato manoharā tam ṛṣimevamuktvā pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntā//
body.translated_text:
293.008. 'In <s>Rudantī</s>, the remedy is good cheer; in <s>Hasantī</s>, the practice of silence; in <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, the application of snake-venom spells; in the <s>Vetra</s> River, the remedy is the descent of sharp weapons.
293.009. After crossing the rivers, there are five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s> as an outpost.
293.010. They must be scattered by steadfastness.
293.010. Beyond that lies the palace of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.'" 
293.010. Having said this to the <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>Manoharā</s> bowed at his feet and departed.

body.text:
293.012. yāvatsudhanaḥ kumārastaṃ karvaṭakaṃ saṃnāmya gṛhītaprābhṛto hastināpuramanuprāptaḥ/
293.012. śrutvā ca rājā parāṃ prītimupagataḥ/
293.013. tataḥ kumāro mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya pituḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
293.013. praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā purastānniṣaṇṇaḥ/
293.014. rājñā paramayā saṃtoṣaṇayā saṃbhāṣitaḥ, uktaśca--kumāra, śivena tvamāgatah? deva, tava prasādātkarvaṭakaḥ saṃnāmitaḥ, nipakā gṛhītāḥ, cintakaḥ sthāpitaḥ/
293.015. ime tu karapratyayāḥ/
293.016. paṇyāgāraśca sthāpyatāmiti/
293.017. rājā kathayati--kumāra tiṣṭha, prābhṛtaṃ sahitā eva bhokṣyāmaḥ/
293.018. deva gacchāmi, ciraṃ dṛṣṭā me manoharā/
293.018. alaṃ kumāra adya gamanena/
293.018. tiṣṭha, śvo gāmiṣyasīti/
293.019. so 'navabudhyamāna evamāha--tāta, adyaiva mayā avaśyaṃ gantavyam/
293.019. rājā tūṣṇīmavasthitaḥ/
293.020. tataḥ kumāraḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ/
293.020. yāvatpaśyati śriyā varjitamantaḥpuradvāram/
293.020. sa cintāparaḥ praviśya manoharāṃ na paśyati/
293.021. itaścāmutaśca saṃbhrāntaḥ śūnyahṛdayaḥ śabdaṃ kartumārabdhah--manohare manohare iti/
293.022. yāvadantaḥpuraṃ saṃnipatitam/
293.022. tāḥ striyaḥ kṣepaṃ kartumārabdhāḥ/
293.022. viddho 'sau hṛdayaśalyena sutarāṃ praṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
293.023. tābhiryathābhūtaṃ samākhyātam/
