293.023. sa śokena saṃpramuhyate/
293.023. tāḥ striyaḥ kathayanti--deva, asminnantaḥpure tatpraviśiṣṭatarāḥ striyaḥ santi, kimarthaṃ śokaḥ kriyate? sa pitur nairguṇyamupaśrutya kṛtaghnatāṃ ca, mātuḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
293.025. pādayor nipatya kathayati--amba,
293.026. manoharāṃ na paśyāmi manorathaguṇairyutām/
293.027. sādhurūpasamāyuktā kva gatā me manoharā//17//
body.translated_text:
293.012. Meanwhile, Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having subdued the rebellious district and taken tribute, arrived at <s>Hastināpura</s>.
293.012. Having heard of his arrival, the king was supremely delighted.
293.013. Then the prince, having shaken off the fatigue of the journey, went to his father's presence.
293.013. Having bowed, he sat down before him.
293.014. The king addressed him with the highest satisfaction: 'Prince, have you arrived safely?' 'By Your Majesty's grace, the district has been pacified, the enemies captured, a watchman installed.
293.015. Here are the tribute-payments.
293.016. Let a revenue-office be established.'
293.017. The king said: 'Prince, wait — we shall enjoy the tribute together.'
293.018. 'Sire, I must go; it has been long since I have seen <s>Manoharā</s>.'
293.018. 'Enough, Prince — no going today.
293.018. Wait; you shall go tomorrow.'
293.019. But he, not understanding, insisted: 'Father, I must go this very day.'
293.019. The king stood in silence.
293.020. Then the prince went to his own residence.
293.020. He saw the gate of the inner palace bereft of splendor.
293.020. Filled with anxiety, he entered but did not see <s>Manoharā</s>.
293.021. Confused, looking here and there, with an empty heart, he began to call out: '<s>Manoharā</s>! <s>Manoharā</s>!'
293.022. The inner palace assembled.
293.022. The women began to taunt him.
293.022. Pierced by the arrow in his heart, he began to question them all the more.
293.023. They told him the truth.
293.023. He fainted from grief.
293.023. The women said: 'Lord, in this inner palace there are women even more distinguished than she — why do you grieve?' But he, having heard of his father's baseness and ingratitude, went to his mother's presence.
293.025. Falling at her feet, he said: 'Mother,
293.026. I do not see <s>Manoharā</s>, endowed with qualities that fulfill all desires.
293.027. Where has my <s>Manoharā</s> gone, she who was possessed of beautiful form?' //17//

body.text:
293.028. manasā saṃpradhāvāmi mano me saṃpramuhyate/
293.029. hṛdayaṃ dahyate caiva rahitasya tayā bhṛśam//18//
body.translated_text:
293.028. 'My mind races about, my mind grows bewildered.
293.029. My heart burns intensely, separated from her.' //18//

body.text: 293.030. manobhirāmā ca manoharā ca manonukūlā ca manoratiśca/
body.translated_text: 293.030. 'She who delights the mind, she who steals the heart, she who follows my every thought, she who is my heart's desire —

body.text:
294.001. <294>saṃtaptadeho 'smi manoharāṃ vinā kuto mamedaṃ vyasanaṃ samāgatam//19// iti/
294.003. sā kathayati--putra, kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasambādhaprāptā manohareti mayā pratimuktā/
294.003. amba, yathā katham? tayā yathāvṛttaṃ vistareṇa samākhyātam/
294.004. sa pitur nairguṇyamakṛtajñatāṃ ca jñātvā kathayati--kutra gatā katareṇa vā patheti? sā kathayati--
294.006. eṣo 'sau parvataśaila ṛṣisaṃghaniṣevitaḥ/
294.007. uṣito dharmarājena yatra yātā manoharā//20// iti/
294.008. sa manoharāviyogaduḥkhārtaḥ kṛcchraṃ vilalāpa, karuṇaṃ paridevate--
294.009. manoharāṃ na paśyāmi manorathaguṇairyutām/
294.010. sādhurūpasamāyuktā kva gatā me manoharā//21//
body.translated_text:
294.001. my body is aflame without <s>Manoharā</s>; from where has this calamity come upon me?' //19//
294.003. She said: 'Son, <s>Manoharā</s> was in dire distress and danger — so I released her.'
294.003. 'Mother, how so?' She told him the whole matter in detail.
294.004. Having learned of his father's baseness and ingratitude, he said: 'Where did she go, and by which path?' She said:
294.006. 'That mountain peak, frequented by communities of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages),
294.007. where the <s>Dharma</s>-king dwelt — that is where <s>Manoharā</s> has gone.' //20//
294.008. He, stricken with the sorrow of separation from <s>Manoharā</s>, grievously lamented, pitifully wailing:
294.009. 'I do not see <s>Manoharā</s>, endowed with qualities that fulfill all desires.
294.010. Where has my <s>Manoharā</s> gone, she who was possessed of beautiful form?' //21//

body.text:
294.011. manasā saṃpradhāvāmi mano me saṃpramuhyate/
294.012. hṛdayaṃ dahyate caiva rahitasya tayā bhṛśam//22//
body.translated_text:
294.011. 'My mind races about, my mind grows bewildered.
294.012. My heart burns intensely, separated from her.' //22//

body.text:
294.013. manobhirāmā ca manoharā ca manonukūlā ca manoratiśca/
294.015. saṃtaptadeho 'smi manoharāṃ vinā kuto mamedaṃ vyasanaṃ samāgatam//23// iti/
294.017. tato mātrā abhihitah--putra, santyasminnantaḥpure tadviśiṣṭatarāḥ striyaḥ/
294.017. kimarthaṃ śokas triyata iti? kumāraḥ kathayati--kuto me ratiranuprāpyatāmiti? sa tayā samāśvāsyamāno 'pi śokasaṃtāpasaṃtaptastasyāḥ pravṛttiṃ samanveṣamāṇa itaścāmutaśca paribhramitumārabdhaḥ/
294.019. tasya buddhirutpannā--yata eva labdhastameva tāvatpṛcchāmi/
294.020. sa halakasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ pṛcchati--manoharā kutastvayā labdheti? sa kathayati--amuṣmin pradeśe ṛṣiḥ prativasati/
294.021. tasyāśramapade brahmasabhā nāma puṣkiriṇī/
294.022. tasyāṃ snātumavatīrṇā ṛṣivyapadeśena labdheti/
294.022. sa saṃlakṣayati--ṛṣiridānīmabhigantavyaḥ, tasmātpravṛttirbhaviṣyatīti/
294.023. eṣa ca vṛttānto rājñā śrutah--manoharāviyogātkumāro 'tīva viklava iti/
294.024. tato rājñā abhihitah--kumāra, kimasi viklavah? idānīṃ tadviśiṣṭataramantaḥpuraṃ vyavasthāpayiṣyāmīti/
294.025. sa kathayati--tāta, na śakyaṃ mayā tāmanānīya antaḥpurasthena bhavitum/
294.026. sa rājñā bahvapyucyamāno na nivartate/
294.026. tato rājñā nagaraprākāraśṛṅgeṣvārakṣakāḥ puruṣāḥ sthāpitāḥ, yathā kumāro na niṣkāsatīti/
294.027. kumāraḥ kṛtsnāṃ rātriṃ jāgartukāmaḥ/
294.028. uktaṃ ca--pañceme rātryā alpaṃ svapanti bahu jāgārti/
294.028. katame pañca puruṣāh? striyāmavekṣya(pekṣā?)vān pratibaddhacittaḥ/
294.029. strīpuruṣa utkośaḥ, ṛṇī, caurasenāpatiḥ, bhikṣuścālabdhavīrya iti/
294.030. atha kumārasyaitadabhavat--yadi dvāreṇa yāsyāmi, rājā dvārapālakān rakṣakāṃśca daṇḍenotsādayiṣyati/
294.031. yannvahamarakṣitena pathā gaccheyamiti/
294.031. sa rātryā vyutthāya nīlotpalamālābaddhaśirā<295> yena rakṣiṇaḥ puruṣā na santi, tena tāṃ mālāṃ dhvaje baddhvā avatīrṇaḥ/
body.translated_text:
294.013. 'She who delights the mind, who captivates the heart, who is agreeable to the mind, and who is the pleasure of the mind —
294.015. my body is burning without <s>Manoharā</s>; from where has this calamity come upon me?' //23//
294.017. Then his mother said: 'Son, in this inner palace there are women even more distinguished than her.
294.017. Why do you grieve?' The prince said: 'From where can my pleasure be obtained?' Though consoled by her, still burning with the anguish of grief, searching for news of her, he began to wander hither and thither.
294.019. The thought occurred to him: 'I shall ask the very one from whom she was obtained.'
294.020. He went to <s>Halaka</s> and asked: 'Where did you obtain <s>Manoharā</s>?' He said: 'In such-and-such a place dwells a <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer).
294.021. At his hermitage there is a lotus pool named <s>Brahmasabhā</s>.
294.022. She had descended there to bathe, and was obtained on the pretext of the <s>ṛṣi</s>.'
294.022. He reflected: 'The <s>ṛṣi</s> must now be approached; from him there will be news.'
294.023. And this story was heard by the king: 'Because of separation from <s>Manoharā</s>, the prince is exceedingly distraught.'
294.024. Then the king said: 'Prince, why are you distraught? I shall now establish an inner court even more distinguished than her.'
294.025. He said: 'Father, it is not possible for me to remain in the inner palace without bringing her back.'
294.026. Though much persuaded by the king, he would not relent.
294.026. Then the king stationed guards on the turrets of the city walls, so that the prince would not go out.
294.027. The prince wished to stay awake the entire night.
294.028. And it is said: 'These five sleep little at night and stay much awake.
294.028. Which five persons? One whose mind is fixed upon a woman, with his heart attached;
294.029. a woman in love with a man; a debtor; a chief of thieves; and a monk who has not attained vigor.'
294.030. Then the prince thought: 'If I go through the gate, the king will punish the gatekeepers and guards with severe penalties.
294.031. Let me go by an unguarded path.'
294.031. Rising in the night, with a garland of blue lotuses tied around his head, he went where there were no guards, and tying that garland to a banner-pole, descended.

body.text:
295.001. candraścoditaḥ/
295.002. tato 'sau candramavekṣya manoharāvirahita evaṃ vilalāpa--
295.003. bhoḥ pūrṇacandra rajanīkara tārarāja tvaṃ rohiṇīnayanakānta susārthavāha/
295.005. kaccitpriyā mama manoharaṇaikadakṣā dṛṣṭā tvayā bhuvi manoharanāmadheyā//24// iti/
295.007. anubhūtapūrvaratimanusmarañ jagāma/
295.007. dadarśa mṛgīm/
295.007. tāmapyuvāca--
295.008. he tvaṃ kuraṅgi tṛṇavāripalāśabhakṣe svastyastu te cara sukhaṃ na mṛgārirasmi/
295.010. dīrghekṣaṇā mṛgavadhūkamanīyarūpā dṛṣṭā tvayā mama manoharanāmadheyā//25//
body.translated_text:
295.001. The moon had risen.
295.002. Then, gazing at the moon, separated from <s>Manoharā</s>, he lamented thus:
295.003. 'O full moon, maker of the night, king of stars, you who are dear to the eyes of <s>Rohiṇī</s>, good caravan-leader!
295.005. Has my beloved, skilled solely in captivating minds, named <s>Manoharā</s>, been seen by you anywhere on earth?' //24//
295.007. Remembering the pleasure he had formerly experienced, he journeyed on.
295.007. He saw a doe.
295.007. And he said to her too:
295.008. 'O you, doe, who feeds on grass, water, and leaves — may you be well! Roam happily; I am not an enemy of deer.
295.010. She of long eyes, of form as beautiful as a deer-bride — has she been seen by you, my <s>Manoharā</s> by name?' //25//

body.text:
295.012. sa tāmatikramya anyatamaṃ pradeśaṃ gato dadarśa vanaṃ nānāpuṣpaphalopaśobhitaṃ bhramarairupabhujyamānasāram/
295.013. tato 'nyatamaṃ bhramaramuvāca--
295.014. nīlāñjanācalasuvarṇa madhudvirepha vaṃśāntarāmburuhamadhyakṛtādhivāsa/
295.016. varṇādhimātrasadṛśāyatakeśahastā dṛṣṭā tvayā mama manoharanāmadheyā//26//
body.translated_text:
295.012. Passing beyond her, he went to another place and saw a forest adorned with various flowers and fruits, its essence being enjoyed by bees.
295.013. Then he said to one of the bees:
295.014. 'O bee of dark collyrium-mountain-gold hue, O honey-drinker who has made your dwelling in the midst of lotuses within bamboo groves!
295.016. She whose long tresses are like hands, equal in the excess of color — has she been seen by you, my <s>Manoharā</s> by name?' //26//

body.text:
295.018. tasmādapi pradeśādatikrāntaḥ paśyatyāśīviṣam/
295.018. dṛṣṭvā cāha--
295.019. bhoḥ kṛṣṇasarpa tanupallavalolajihva vaktrāntarotpatitadhūmakalāpavaktra/
295.021. rāgāgninā tava samo na viṣāgnirugro dṛṣṭā tvayā mama manoharanāmadheyā//27//
body.translated_text:
295.018. Passing beyond that place too, he sees a poisonous serpent.
295.018. Seeing it, he said:
295.019. 'O black serpent, with tongue flickering like a tender leaf-sprout, with mouth from which issues a mass of smoke-like vapors!
295.021. The fire of passion is not fiercer than your venom-fire — has she been seen by you, my <s>Manoharā</s> by name?' //27//

body.text:
295.023. tamapi pradeśaṃ samatikrānto dadarśāparaṃ kokilābhināditam/
295.023. dṛṣṭvā ca punastaṃ kokilamuvāca--
295.025. bhoḥ kokilottama vanāntaravṛkṣavāsin nārī manohara patatrigaṇasya rājan/
295.027. nīlotpalāmakasamāyatacārunetrā dṛṣṭā tvayā mama manoharanāmadheyā//28//
body.translated_text:
295.023. Passing beyond that place too, he saw another, resounding with cuckoos.
295.023. Seeing this, he again said to the cuckoo:
295.025. 'O best of cuckoos, dweller among trees of the forest-depths, O king of the flock of birds who captivate women's hearts!
295.027. She whose eyes are long and beautiful like blue lotuses and berries — has she been seen by you, my <s>Manoharā</s> by name?' //28//

body.text:
295.029. tamapi pradeśaṃ samatikrānto dadarśāśokavṛkṣaṃ sarvapariphullam/
295.030. maṅgalyanāmāntaranāmayukta sarvadrumāṇāmadhirājatulya/
body.translated_text:
295.029. Passing beyond that place too, he saw an <s>Aśoka</s> tree in full bloom.
295.030. 'O <s>Aśoka</s>, bearing a name associated with auspiciousness, equal to a king among all trees!

body.text: 296.001. <296>manoharāśoka vibhūrcchitaṃ mām eṣo 'ñjaliste kuru vītaśokam//29//
body.translated_text: 296.001. O <s>Manoharā</s>-<s>Aśoka</s>, make me, who am trembling, free from sorrow — this is my salutation to you.' //29//

body.text:
296.003. sa evaṃ viklavo 'nupūrveṇa tasya ṛṣerāśramapadamanuprāptaḥ/
296.003. sa tam ṛṣiṃ savinayaṃ praṇipatyovāca--
296.005. cīrājināmbaradhara kṣamayā viśiṣṭa mūlāṅkurāmalakabilvakapitthabhakta/
296.007. vande ṛṣe nataśirā vada me laghu tvaṃ dṛṣṭā tvayā mama manoharanāmadheyā//30//
body.translated_text:
296.003. He, thus distraught, gradually arrived at the hermitage of that <s>ṛṣi</s>.
296.003. He bowed reverently to the <s>ṛṣi</s> and said:
296.005. 'O you who wear bark-cloth and deer-skin garments, distinguished by patience, who eat roots, shoots, <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan), <s>bilva</s>, and <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple)!
296.007. I bow, O <s>ṛṣi</s>, with head bent — tell me quickly: has she been seen by you, my <s>Manoharā</s> by name?' //30//

body.text:
296.009. tataḥ sa ṛṣiḥ sudhanaṃ kumāraṃ svāgatavacanāsanadānakriyādipuraḥsaraḥ pratisaṃmodya uvāca--
296.011. dṛṣṭā sā paripūrṇacandravadanā nīlotpalābhāsvarā rūpeṇa priyadarśanā subadanā nīlañcatabhrūlatā/
296.013. tvaṃ svastho bhuvi bhujyatāṃ hi vividhaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ ca prabho pañcātsvasti gamiṣyasīti manasā nātrāsti me saṃśayaḥ//31//
body.translated_text:
296.009. Then that <s>ṛṣi</s>, having first greeted Prince <s>Sudhana</s> with welcoming words, the offering of a seat, and other courtesies, said:
296.011. 'She was seen — she of face like the full moon, radiant as a blue lotus, pleasing in form and appearance, with beautiful teeth, with brows like dark blue creepers.
296.013. Be at ease on earth — eat the various roots and fruits, O lord! In five days you shall go safely; of this I have no doubt in my mind.' //31//

body.text:
296.015. idaṃ hyavocadvacanaṃ ca subhrūḥ kumāra tṛṣṇā tvayi bādhate me/
296.017. mahacca duḥkhaṃ vasatāṃ vaneṣu yātāṃ ramāṃ drakṣyasi niṣcayena//32// iti/
296.019. iyaṃ ca tayā aṅgulimudrikā dattā/
296.019. kathayati ca-- kumāra, viṣamāḥ panthāno durgamāḥ/
296.020. khedamāpatsyase, nivartasveti/
296.020. yadi ca nivāryamāṇo na tiṣṭhet, tasya mārgamupadeṣṭumarhasi/
296.021. kumāra, idaṃ ca tayā samākhyātam--uttare digbhāge trayaḥ kālaparvatāḥ, tānatikramya apare trayaḥ, tānapyatikramya himavān parvatarājaḥ/
296.022. tatpradeśena tvayā imāni bhaiṣajyāni samudānetavyāni--tadyathā sūdayā nāmauṣadhistayā ghṛtaṃ paktvā pātavyam/
296.023. tena ca te na tṛṣā na bubhukṣā, smṛtibalaṃ ca vardhayati/
296.024. vānaraḥ samudānetavyaḥ, mantramadhyetavyam, saśaraṃ dhanurgrahītavyam, maṇayo 'vabhāsātmakāh agado viṣaghātako 'yaskīlāstrayo vīṇā ca/
296.026. himavataḥ parvarājasyottareṇotkīlakaḥ parvataḥ/
296.026. tataḥ kūlako jalapathaḥ khadiraka ekadhārako vajrakaḥ kāmarūpī/
296.027. utkīlaka erāvatako 'dhobāṇaḥ pramokṣaka ete parvatāḥ/
296.027. sarve te samatikramaṇīyāḥ/
296.028. tatra khadirake parvate guhā, praveśa ekadhārake tu kolakāḥ, vajrake pakṣirājena praveśaḥ/
296.029. ebhirupāyaiste sarve parvatāḥ samatikramaṇīyāḥ, yantrāṇi ca bhaṅktavyāni/
296.029. ajavaktro meṇḍhakaḥ puruṣo rākṣasīrūpī piṅgalāyāṃ guhāyāṃ lālāsrotasā mahatā ajagaro vegena pradhāvati/
296.031. sa te vikrameṇa hantavyaḥ/
296.031. arāntaragatāṃ nābhīm yatra paśyettatra kiṭibhakaśca/
body.translated_text:
296.015. 'And this did the fair-browed one say: "O prince, longing for you afflicts me.
296.017. Great is the suffering of those dwelling in the forests. You shall surely see the beauty who has departed."' //32//
296.019. And this finger-ring was given by her.
296.019. And she said: 'Prince, the paths are difficult and hard to traverse.
296.020. You will encounter hardship; turn back.'
296.020. But if, though warned, he does not stay, you should show him the way.
296.021. 'Prince, this is what she related: in the northern direction there are three Black Mountains; passing beyond those, there are three more; passing beyond those too is <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains.
296.022. In that region, you must gather these medicines — namely, cooking with the herb called <s>sūdayā</s>, you must drink the ghee prepared from it.
296.023. By this, you will feel neither thirst nor hunger, and it will increase your power of memory.
296.024. A monkey must be obtained, a <s>mantra</s> must be learned, a bow with arrows must be taken, gems that emit light, an antidote for poison, iron stakes, weapons, and a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute).
296.026. To the north of <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, is Mount <s>Utkīlaka</s>.
296.026. Beyond that are <s>Kūlaka</s>, the water-passage, <s>Khadiraka</s>, <s>Ekadhāraka</s>, <s>Vajraka</s>, and <s>Kāmarūpī</s>.
296.027. <s>Utkīlaka</s>, <s>Erāvataka</s>, <s>Adhobāṇa</s>, and <s>Pramokṣaka</s> — these are the mountains.
296.027. All of these must be crossed.
296.028. In <s>Khadiraka</s> mountain there is a cave; entry into <s>Ekadhāraka</s> is by means of wooden bowls; entry into <s>Vajraka</s> is by the king of birds.
296.029. By these means, all mountains must be crossed, and the mechanisms must be broken.
296.029. A goat-faced ram-man of <s>Rākṣasa</s> form, in the tawny cave, rushes forth with great speed like a python in a torrent of saliva.
296.031. He must be slain by your valor.
296.031. Where you see a navel in between — there is also a <s>kiṭibhaka</s> (creature).

body.text:
297.001. <297>ayaṃ muktena bāṇena hantavyo mama kāraṇāt/
297.002. yatra paśyeddvau meṣau saṃghaṭṭantau parasparam/
297.003. tayoḥ śṛṅgamekaṃ bhaṅktvā bhārgaṃ pratilapsyase//33//
body.translated_text:
297.001. 'This one must be killed with a released arrow, for my sake.
297.002. Where you see two rams butting each other,
297.003. break one of their horns, and you will obtain the passage.' //33//

body.text:
297.004. āyasau puruṣau dṛṣṭvā śastrapāṇī mahābhayau/
297.005. tayorekaṃ tāḍayitvā mārgaṃ pratilapsyase//34//
body.translated_text:
297.004. 'Seeing two iron men, wielding weapons, greatly fearsome,
297.005. strike one of them, and you will obtain the path.' //34//

body.text:
297.006. saṃkocayantīṃ prasārayantīṃ rākṣasīmāyasaṃ sukham/
297.007. yadā paśyettadā kīlaṃ lalāṭo tasyā nikhānayet//35//
body.translated_text:
297.006. 'When you see the iron <s>Rākṣasī</s>, contracting and expanding, at ease,
297.007. then drive the stake into her forehead.' //35//

body.text:
297.008. śūlāvartastadā kūpo vilaṅghyaste ṣaṣṭihastakaḥ/
297.009. haripiṅgalakeśākṣo dāruṇo yakṣarākṣasaḥ//36//
body.translated_text:
297.008. 'Then there is a well of whirlpool-spikes, sixty cubits deep, to be leapt over;
297.009. a fearsome <s>Yakṣa</s>-<s>Rākṣasa</s> with tawny-red hair and eyes.' //36//

body.text:
297.010. kārmukaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā hantavyaśca durāsadaḥ/
297.011. nadyaśca bahavastāryā nakragrahasamākulāḥ//37//
body.translated_text:
297.010. 'Making a circle with the bow, the formidable one must be slain.
297.011. And many rivers must be crossed, teeming with crocodiles and water-monsters.' //37//

body.text:
297.012. raṅgā pataṅgā tapanī citrā rudantī hasantī āśīviṣā vetranadī ca/
297.013. raṅgāyāṃ rākṣasīkopaḥ pataṅgāyāmamānuṣāḥ/
297.014. tapantyāṃ grāhabahutvaṃ citrāyāṃ kāmarūpiṇaḥ//38//

297.015. rudantyāṃ kinnarīceṭyo hasantyāṃ kinnarīsnuṣā/
297.016. āśīviṣāyāṃ nānāvidhāḥ sarpā vetranadyāṃ tu śālmaliḥ//39//
body.translated_text:
297.015. 'In <s>Rudantī</s>, <s>Kinnarī</s> maidservants; in <s>Hasantī</s>, <s>Kinnarī</s> daughters-in-law;
297.016. in <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, various kinds of serpents; and in the <s>Vetra</s> River, a silk-cotton tree.' //39//

body.text:
297.017. raṅgāyāṃ dhairyakaraṇaṃ pataṅgāyāṃ parākramaḥ/
297.018. tapantyāṃ grāhamukhabandhaścitrāyāṃ vividhaṃ gītam//40//
body.translated_text:
297.017. 'For <s>Raṅgā</s>, the remedy is steadfastness; for <s>Pataṅgā</s>, valor;
297.018. for <s>Tapanī</s>, binding the mouths of crocodiles; for <s>Citrā</s>, various songs.' //40//

body.text:
297.019. rudantyāṃ saumanasyena samuttāraḥ/
297.019. hasantyāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena, āśīviṣāyāṃ sarvaviṣamantraprayogeṇa samuttāraḥ, vetranadyāṃ tīkṣṇaśastrasampātayogena samuttāraḥ/
297.020. nadīmatikramya pañca yakṣaśatāni gulmakasthānam/
297.021. taddhairyamāsthāya vidrāvyam/
297.021. tato drumasya kinnararājasya bhavanamiti//
body.translated_text:
297.019. 'For <s>Rudantī</s>, crossing by maintaining good cheer;
297.019. for <s>Hasantī</s>, by silence; for <s>Āśīviṣā</s>, by the application of all-poison <s>mantras</s>; for the <s>Vetra</s> River, crossing by the device of sharp weapons.
297.020. Having crossed the river, there is a station of five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s>.
297.021. They must be routed by maintaining steadfastness.
297.021. Beyond that is the dwelling of <s>Druma</s>, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.'

body.text:
297.022. tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumāro yathopadiṣṭānauṣadhimantrāgadaprayogān samudānīya tasya ṛṣeḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ/
297.023. tatastena yathopadiṣṭāḥ sarve samudānītāḥ sthāpavitvā vānaram/
297.024. tatastānādāya punarapi tasya ṛṣeḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
297.024. uktaśca--alaṃ kumāra, kimanena vyavasāyena? kiṃ manoharayā? tvamekākī asahāyaḥ śirīrasaṃśayamavapsyasīti/
297.025. kumāraḥ prāha--maharṣe, avaśyamevāhaṃ prayāsyāmīti/
297.026. kutah?
297.027. candrasya khe vicarataḥ kva sahāyabhāvo daṃṣṭrābalena balinaśca mṛgādhipasya/
297.029. agneśca dāvadahane kva sahāyabhāvah asmadvidhasya ca sahāyabalena kiṃ syāt//41//
body.translated_text:
297.022. Then Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having gathered the prescribed medicines, <s>mantras</s>, antidotes, and provisions, bowed at the feet of the <s>ṛṣi</s> and set out.
297.023. He gathered all that had been prescribed, except the monkey.
297.024. Taking those, he went again to the <s>ṛṣi</s>.
297.024. He was told: 'Enough, prince — what is the use of this enterprise? What use is <s>Manoharā</s>? Alone and without companions, you will risk your life.'
297.025. The prince said: 'Great sage, I shall certainly set out.'
297.026. Why?
297.027. 'Where is the need for companions as the moon moves through the sky? Or of the powerful lion-king with the strength of his fangs?
297.029. Where is the need for companions of fire when burning the forest? What use would the strength of companions be to one such as me?' //41//

body.text: 298.001. <298>kiṃ bho mahārṇavajalaṃ na vigāhitavyaṃ kiṃ sarpadaṣṭa iti naiva cikitsanīyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 298.001. 'Why should the waters of the great ocean not be plunged into? Why should one bitten by a serpent not be treated?' //

body.text:
298.003. vīryaṃ bhajetsumahadūrjitasattvadṛṣṭam yatne kṛte yadi na siddhyati ko 'tra doṣaḥ//42// iti/
298.005. tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumāro manoharopadiṣṭena saṃprasthitaḥ/
298.005. anupūrveṇa parvatanadīguhāprapātādīni bhaiṣajyamantrāgadaprayogeṇa vinirjitya drumasya kinnararājasya bhavanasamīpaṃ gataḥ/
298.007. kumāro 'paśyannagaramadūraṃ śrīmadudyānopaśobhitaṃ nānāpuṣpaphalopetaṃ nānāvihagasevitaṃ taḍāgadīrghikāvāpikinnaraiḥ samupāvṛtam/
298.008. kinnarīstatra cāpaśyat pānīyārthamupagatāḥ/
298.008. tatastāḥ sudhanakumāreṇābhihitāh--kimanena bahunā pānīyena kriyata iti? tāḥ kathayanti--asti drumasya kinnararājasya duhitā manoharā nāma/
298.010. sā manuṣyahastagatā babhūva/
298.010. tasyāḥ sa manuṣyagandho naśyati/
298.011. sudhanaḥ kumāraḥ pṛcchati--kimete ghaṭāḥ samastāḥ sarve tasyā upari nipātyante, āhosvidanupūrveṇeti? tāḥ kathayanti--anupūrvyā/
298.012. sa saṃlakṣayati--śobhano 'yamupāyaḥ/
298.013. imāmaṅgulimudrāmekasmin ghaṭe prakṣipāmīti/
298.013. tenaikasyāḥ kinnaryā ghaṭe 'nālakṣitaṃ prakṣiptā/
298.014. sā ca kinnarī abhihitā--anena tvayā ghaṭena manoharā tatprathamataraṃ snāpayitavyā/
298.014. sā saṃlakṣayati--nūnamatra kāryeṇa bhavitavyam/
298.015. tatastayāsau ghaṭaḥ prathamataraṃ manoharāyā mūrdhni nipātito yāvadaṅgulimudrā utsaṅge nipatitā/
298.016. sā manoharayā pratyabhijñātā/
298.016. tataḥ kinnarīṃ pṛcchati--mā tatra kaścinmanuṣyo 'bhyāgatah? sā āha--ubhyāgtaḥ/
298.017. gaccha, enaṃ pracchannaṃ praveśaya/
298.018. tayā praveśitaḥ, sugupte pradeśe sthāpitaḥ/
298.018. tato manoharā pituḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--tāta, yadyasau sudhanaḥ kumāra āgacchet, yenāhaṃ hṛtā, tasya tvaṃ kiṃ kuryāh? sa kathayati--tamahaṃ khaṇḍaśataṃ kṛtvā catasṛṣu śikṣu kṣipeyam/
298.020. manuṣyo 'sau, kiṃ teneti/
298.020. manoharā kathayati--tāta, manuṣyabhūtasya kuta ihāgamanam? ahamevaṃ bravīmīti/
298.021. tato drumasya kinnararājasya paryavasthāno vigataḥ/
298.022. tato vigataparyavasthānaḥ kathayati--yadyasau kumāra āgacchet, tasyāhaṃ tvāṃ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāṃ prabhūtacitropakaraṇaiḥ kinnarīsahasraparivṛtāṃ bhāryārthaṃ dadyāmiti/
298.024. tato manoharayā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditayā sudhanaṃ kumāro divyālaṃkāravibhūṣito drumasya kinnararājasyopadarśitaḥ/
298.025. tato drumaḥ kinnnararājaḥ sudhanaṃ kumāraṃ dadarśa abhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prasādikaṃ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatam/
298.026. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paraṃ vismayamupagataḥ/
298.027. tatastasya jijñāsāṃ kartukāmena sauvarṇāḥ stambhā ucchritāḥ, sapta tālāḥ, sapta bheryaḥ, sapta sūkarāḥ/
298.028. āha ca--
298.029. tvayā kāntyā jitāstāvadete kinnaradārakāḥ/
298.030. saṃdarśitaprabhāvastu divyasambandhamarhasi//43//
body.translated_text:
298.003. 'One should exert heroic effort, with great firmness, courage, and insight; if, despite the effort, it does not succeed, what fault is there?' //42//
298.005. Then Prince <s>Sudhana</s> set out along the path indicated by <s>Manoharā</s>.
298.005. Gradually, by means of medicines, spells, and antidote-applications, he overcame mountains, rivers, caves, waterfalls, and the like, and reached the vicinity of the dwelling of <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king.
298.007. The prince saw, not far away, a city adorned with splendid gardens, furnished with various flowers and fruits, frequented by various birds, surrounded by lakes, long ponds, reservoirs, and <s>Kinnaras</s>.
298.008. He saw <s>Kinnarīs</s> there who had come to fetch water.
298.008. Prince <s>Sudhana</s> asked them: 'What is all this water for?' They said: 'There is a daughter of <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, named <s>Manoharā</s>.
298.010. She had fallen into the hands of a human.
298.010. The human scent on her must be removed.'
298.011. Prince <s>Sudhana</s> asked: 'Are all these jars poured over her at once, or one by one?' They said: 'One by one.'
298.012. He thought: 'This is an excellent stratagem.
298.013. I shall drop my signet ring into one of these jars.'
298.013. He secretly dropped it into one <s>Kinnarī</s>'s jar.
298.014. And he said to that <s>Kinnarī</s>: 'You must bathe <s>Manoharā</s> with your jar first, before the others.'
298.014. She thought: 'There must be some purpose in this.'
298.015. Then she poured that jar first upon <s>Manoharā</s>'s head, and the signet ring fell into her lap.
298.016. <s>Manoharā</s> recognized it.
298.016. She asked the <s>Kinnarī</s>: 'Has some human arrived there?' She said: 'He has.'
298.017. 'Go, bring him in secretly.'
298.018. She brought him in and placed him in a well-hidden spot.
298.018. Then <s>Manoharā</s>, falling at her father's feet, said: 'Father, if that Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, by whom I was taken, were to come here, what would you do to him?' He said: 'I would cut him into a hundred pieces and scatter them in the four directions.
298.020. He is a human — what of him?'
298.020. <s>Manoharā</s> said: 'Father, how could a human being come here? I was merely asking.'
298.021. Then the resentment of <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, subsided.
298.022. With his resentment gone, he said: 'If that prince were to come, I would give you to him as a wife, adorned with all ornaments, with abundant and splendid provisions, accompanied by a thousand <s>Kinnarīs</s>.'
298.024. Then <s>Manoharā</s>, joyful, delighted, and elated, presented Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, adorned with divine ornaments, to <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king.
298.025. Then <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, saw Prince <s>Sudhana</s> — handsome, beautiful, pleasing, endowed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness.
298.026. Seeing him, he was filled with supreme wonder.
298.027. Then, wishing to test him, golden pillars were erected — seven palm-trees, seven drums, and seven boars.
298.028. And he said:
298.029. 'By your beauty you have indeed conquered these <s>Kinnara</s> youths;
298.030. but now demonstrate your prowess — you are worthy of a divine alliance.' //43//

body.text:
298.031. atyāyataṃ śaravaṇaṃ kṛtvoddhṛtya śaraṃ kṣaṇāt/
298.032. vyuptamanyūnamuccitya punardehi tilāṭakam//44//
body.translated_text:
298.031. 'Uproot this exceedingly vast reed-grove, pluck out the reeds in an instant;
298.032. scatter sesame seeds on the cleared ground, then gather them again without loss and return them.' //44//

body.text:
299.001. <299>saṃdarśaya dhanurvede dṛṭalakṣādikauśalam/
299.002. tataḥ kīrtipatākeyaṃ tavāyattā manoharā//45//
body.translated_text:
299.001. <299>'Demonstrate your skill in archery, hitting firm targets and the like;
299.002. then this flag of fame and <s>Manoharā</s> will be yours.' //45//

body.text:
299.003. sudhanakumāro bodhisattvaḥ/
299.003. kuśalāśca bhavanti bodhisattvāsteṣu śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu/
299.004. devatāścaiṣāmautsukyamāpatsyante avighnabhāvāya/
299.004. tato bodhisattvo nṛttagītavīṇāpaṇavasughoṣakavallarīmṛdaṅgādinānāvidhena daivatopasaṃhṛtena vāditraviśeṣeṇa samantādāpūryamāṇe 'nekaiḥ kinnarasahasraiḥ pativṛtaḥ/
299.007. śatakratusamādiṣṭairyakṣaiḥ sūkararūpibhiḥ/
299.008. utpāṭite śaravane same vyuptaṃ tilāḍakam//46//
body.translated_text:
299.003. Prince <s>Sudhana</s> was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.
299.003. And <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are skilled in those arts and crafts.
299.004. And the deities were eager to ensure the absence of obstacles for them.
299.004. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by many thousands of <s>Kinnaras</s>, with a space all around filled with dancing, singing, <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, <s>sughoṣakas</s>, <s>vallarīs</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and various other divine instrumental music,
299.007. with <s>Yakṣas</s> in the form of boars, dispatched by <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>),
299.008. the reed-grove was uprooted and the ground leveled, and sesame seeds were scattered. //46//

body.text:
299.009. ekīkṛtaṃ samuccitya śakrasṛṣṭaiḥ pipīlakaiḥ/
299.010. kumāraḥ kinnarendrāya vismitāya nyavedayat//47//
body.translated_text:
299.009. The seeds were gathered into one, collected by ants sent by <s>Śakra</s>;
299.010. and the prince reported this to the astonished <s>Kinnara</s>-lord. //47//

body.text:
299.011. nīlotpaladalābhenāsinā gṛhītena paśyato drumasya kinnararājasya sauvarṇastambhasamīpaṃ gatvā tān stambhān kadalīcchedena khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ chettumārabdhaḥ/
299.012. tatastāṃs tilaśo 'vakīrya sapta tālān sapta bherīḥ sapta ca sūkarān bāṇena vidhya sumeruvadakampyo 'vasthitaḥ/
299.013. tato gaganatalasthābhirdevatābhiśca kinnaraśatasahasrairhāhākārakilikilāprakṣveḍoccair nādo muktaḥ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca kinnararājaḥ paraṃ vismayamupagataḥ/
299.015. tataḥ kinnarīsahasrasya manoharāsamānarūpasya madhye manoharāṃ sthāpayitvā sudhanaḥ kumāro 'bhihitah--ehi kumāra, pratyabhijānāsi manoharāmiti? tataḥ sudhanaḥ kumārastāṃ pratyabhijñāya gāthābhigītenoktavān--
299.018. yathā drumasya duhitā mameha tvaṃ manoharā/
299.019. śīghrametena satyena padaṃ vraja manohare//48//
body.translated_text:
299.011. With a sword having the luster of a blue lotus petal, he went, before the eyes of <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, to the golden pillars and began to cut them to pieces like slicing through plantain stalks.
299.012. Then, scattering them like sesame seeds, he pierced the seven palm-trees, seven drums, and seven boars with an arrow, and stood unshaken like <s>Sumeru</s>.
299.013. Then the deities stationed in the sky and hundreds of thousands of <s>Kinnaras</s> raised a great cry of 'Hā hā!', shrieks, and loud exclamations; seeing this, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king was filled with supreme wonder.
299.015. Then, placing <s>Manoharā</s> in the midst of a thousand <s>Kinnarīs</s> of equal beauty, Prince <s>Sudhana</s> was told: 'Come, prince, do you recognize <s>Manoharā</s>?' Prince <s>Sudhana</s>, having recognized her, spoke in verse:
299.018. 'Just as you, daughter of <s>Druma</s>, are my <s>Manoharā</s> here,
299.019. quickly by this truth, come forth, O <s>Manoharā</s>!' //48//

body.text:
299.020. tataḥ sā drutapadamabhikrāntā/
299.020. kinnarāḥ kathayanti--deva, ayaṃ sudhanaḥ kumāro balavīryaparākramasamanvito manoharāyāḥ pratirūpaḥ/
299.021. kimarthaṃ vipralabhya? dīyatāmasya manohareti/
299.022. tato drumaḥ kinnararājaḥ kinnaragaṇena saṃvarṇitaḥ sudhanaṃ kinnarābhimetena mahatā satkāreṇa puraskṛtya manoharāṃ divyālaṃkāravibhūṣitāṃ vāmena pāṇinā gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena sauvarṇabhṛṅgāraṃ sudhanaṃ kumāramabhihitah--kumāra, eṣā te manoharā kinnarīpativṛtā bhāryārthāya dattā/
299.024. aparicitā mānuṣāḥ, yathaināṃ na parityakṣasīti/
299.025. paraṃ tāteti sudhanaḥ kumāro drumasya kinnararājasya pratiśrutya kinnarabhavanastho manoharayā sārdhaṃ niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍate ramate paricārayati/
299.027. so 'pareṇa samayena svadeśamanusmṛtya mātāpitṛviyogajena duḥkhenātyāhato manoharāyā nivedayati--mātāpitṛviyogajaṃ me duḥkhaṃ bādhata iti/
299.028. tato manoharayā eṣa vṛttānto vistareṇa pitur niveditaḥ/
299.029. sa kathayati--gaccha kumāreṇa sārdham/
299.029. apakrāntayā te bhavitavyam/
299.029. vipralambhakā manuṣyāḥ/
299.030. tato drumeṇa kinnararājena prabhūtaṃ maṇimuktāsuvarṇādīn dattvā anupreṣitaḥ/
299.030. sa manoharayā sārdhamuparivihāyasā kinnarakhagapathena saṃprasthitaḥ/
299.031. anupūrveṇa hastināpuranagaramanuprāptah<300>/
body.translated_text:
299.020. Then she came forth with swift steps.
299.020. The <s>Kinnaras</s> said: 'Lord, this Prince <s>Sudhana</s> is endowed with strength, valor, and prowess — he is a fitting match for <s>Manoharā</s>.
299.021. Why deceive him? Give him <s>Manoharā</s>.'
299.022. Then <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, praised by the company of <s>Kinnaras</s>, honoring <s>Sudhana</s> with great respect among the <s>Kinnaras</s>, took <s>Manoharā</s>, adorned with divine ornaments, by the left hand, and with a golden pitcher in his right, said to Prince <s>Sudhana</s>: 'Prince, this <s>Manoharā</s> of mine, attended by <s>Kinnarīs</s>, is given to you as a wife.
299.024. Humans are unfamiliar — see that you do not abandon her.'
299.025. 'Very well, father' — Prince <s>Sudhana</s> assented to <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, and dwelling in the <s>Kinnara</s> realm, he sported, delighted, and amused himself with <s>Manoharā</s>, with music played without human musicians.
299.027. On another occasion, remembering his own country, afflicted with the sorrow of separation from his parents, he informed <s>Manoharā</s>: 'The sorrow of separation from my parents torments me.'
299.028. <s>Manoharā</s> reported the matter in detail to her father.
299.029. He said: 'Go with the prince.
299.029. You must depart.
299.029. Humans are deceivers.'
299.030. Then <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king, gave abundant jewels, pearls, gold, and the like, and sent them off.
299.030. He set out with <s>Manoharā</s> through the sky by the <s>Kinnara</s> bird-path.
299.031. Gradually he reached the city of <s>Hastināpura</s>. <300>

body.text:
300.001. tato hastināpuraṃ nagaraṃ nānāmanohareṇa surabhinā gandhaviśeṣeṇa sarvā digāmoditam/
300.002. śrutvā dhanena rājñā ānandabheryastāḍitāḥ, sarvaṃ ca tannagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ kāritam/
300.003. candanavāriṣiktamāmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpasamucchritadhvajapatākaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddhaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaramaṇīyam/
300.004. tataḥ kumāro 'nekanaravarasahasraparivṛto manoharayā sārdhaṃ hastināpuraṃ nagaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
300.005. tato mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya vividhāni ratnānyādāya pituḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
300.006. pitrā kaṇṭhe pariṣvaktaḥ/
300.006. pārśve rājāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
300.006. kinnaranagaragamanāgamanaṃ ca vistareṇa samākhyātam/
300.007. tato dhanena rājñā atibalavīryaparākrama iti viditvā rājyābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ/
300.008. sudhanaḥ kumāraḥ saṃlakṣayati--yanmama manoharayā sārdhaṃ samāgamaḥ saṃvṛtto rājyābhiṣekaścānuprāptaḥ, tatpūrvakṛtahetuviśeṣāt/
300.009. yannvahamidānīṃ dānāni dadyām, puṇyāni kuryāmiti/
300.010. tena hastināpure nagare dvādaśa varṣāṇi nirgaṭo yajña iṣṭaḥ//
body.translated_text:
300.001. Then the city of <s>Hastināpura</s> was pervaded in every direction with various enchanting and fragrant perfumes.
300.002. Hearing of the prince's arrival, King <s>Dhana</s> had the drums of joy beaten, and the entire city was cleared of stones, gravel, and refuse;
300.003. sprinkled with sandalwood-water, adorned with released silk streamers and garlands, raised with banners and flags, festooned with vessels of fragrant incense, and strewn with various flowers — made delightful.
300.004. Then the prince, surrounded by many thousands of excellent men, entered the city of <s>Hastināpura</s> together with <s>Manoharā</s>.
300.005. Having relieved the fatigue of travel and taking various jewels, he went to his father.
300.006. He was embraced at the neck by his father.
300.006. He sat on a royal seat beside him.
300.006. The entire story of going to and returning from the <s>Kinnara</s> city was told in detail.
300.007. Then King <s>Dhana</s>, knowing him to be of supreme strength, valor, and prowess, consecrated him with the royal consecration.
300.008. Prince <s>Sudhana</s> reflected: 'That I met with <s>Manoharā</s> and attained the royal consecration — all this is due to the special causes made in the past.
300.009. Let me now give gifts and make merit.'
300.010. He performed an unrestricted sacrifice in the city of <s>Hastināpura</s> for twelve years.

body.text:
300.011. syātkhalu te mahārāja anyaḥ sa tena kālena samayena sudhanaḥ kumāro veti? na khalvevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
300.012. api tvahameva tena kālena tena samayena bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ vartamānaḥ sudhano nāma rājā babhūva/
300.013. yanmayā manoharānimittaṃ balavīryaparākramo darśitaḥ, dvādaśa varṣāṇi nirargaṭo yajña iṣṭaḥ, na tena mayā anuttarā samyaksambodhiradhigatā, kiṃ tu taddānaṃ tacca vīryamanuttarāyāḥ samyaksamboderhetumātrakaṃ pratyayamātrakaṃ saṃbhāramātrakam//
body.translated_text:
300.011. 'Do you think, Great King, that Prince <s>Sudhana</s> at that time, in that era, was someone else? It should not be seen thus.
300.012. Rather, I myself at that time, in that era, while practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct, was the king named <s>Sudhana</s>.
300.013. Although I demonstrated strength, valor, and prowess for the sake of <s>Manoharā</s>, and performed an unrestricted sacrifice for twelve years, I did not thereby attain unsurpassed perfect awakening; rather, that generosity and that heroic effort were merely a cause, merely a condition, merely a requisite for unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text:
300.016. ityavocadbhagavān/
300.016. āttamanasaste ca sarve lokā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
300.016. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
300.016. Delighted, all those people rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 300.017. iti sudhanakumārāvadānaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: 300.017. Thus the <s>Sudhanakumārāvadāna</s> (The Story of Prince <s>Sudhana</s>) is concluded.

body.text: 301.001. div31 toyikāmahāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 301.001. Chapter 31: The <s>Toyikāmahāvadāna</s> (The Great Story of <s>Toyikā</s>).

body.text:
301.002. tatra bhagavbānāyuṣmantamāmantrayate--sma āgamaya ānanda yena śrāavastīti/
301.002. evaṃ bhadantetyāyucmānānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt/
301.003. atha bhagavān yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
301.004. yāvadanyatamasmin pradeśe brāhmaṇaśchinnabhakto halaṃ vāhayati, tasyārthāya dārikā peyāmādāya gatā/
301.005. bhagavāṃśca pradeśamanuprāptaḥ/
301.005. dadarśa sa brāhmaṇo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakcaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtamaśītyānuvyañjanairvirājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamamiva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam/
301.007. sahadarśanāccāsya bhagavati prasāda utpannaḥ/
301.008. na tathā dvādaśavarṣābhyastaḥ śamathaścattasya kalyatāṃ janayati, aputrasya vā putrapratilambhaḥ, daridrasya vā nidhidarśanam, rājyābhinandano vā rājyābhiṣekaḥ, yathopacitakuśalamūlasya sattvasya tatprathamato buddhadarśanam/
301.010. sa tāṃ peyāmādāya laghuladhveva yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
301.011. upasaṃkramya bhagavantametadavocat--iyaṃ bho gautama peyā/
301.011. yadyasti mamāntike 'nukampā, pibedbhagavān gautamaḥ peyāmiti/
301.012. tato bhagavatā brāhmaṇasya jīrṇakūpo darśitah--sacette brāhmaṇa parityaktā, asmiñ jīrṇakūpe prakṣipeti/
301.013. tena tasmiñ jīrṇakūpe prakṣiptā/
301.013. sa jīrṇakūpo vāpyāyamānaḥ peyāpūrṇaḥ, yathāpi tadbuddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena/
301.014. tato bhagavatā sa brāhmaṇo 'bhihitah--cāraya mahābrāhmaṇa peyāmiti/
301.015. sa cārayitumārabdhaḥ/
301.015. bhagavatā tathā adhiṣṭhitā yathā sarvasaṃghena pītā/
301.016. sa ca jīrṇakūpo vāpyāyamānastathaiva peyāpūrṇo 'vasthitaḥ/
301.017. tato 'sau brāhmaṇo bhūyasyā mātrayā abhiprasanno bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya/
301.018. tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāyasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, pūrvavadyāvadanādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
301.020. atikrānto 'haṃ bhadanta, atikrāntaḥ/
301.020. eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca/
301.021. upāsakaṃ ca māṃ dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatamabhiprasannam/
301.022. athāsau brāhmaṇo vaṇigiva labdhalābhaḥ śasyasampanna iva kṛṣīvalaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ sarvaroganirmukta ivāturo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyānandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yāvatkṣetraṃ gataḥ/
301.025. paśyati tasmin kṣetre sauvarṇān yavān saṃpannān/
301.025. dṛṣṭvā ca punarvismayotphullalocano gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
301.027. aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam/
301.028. adyaiva vāpitaṃ bījamadyaiva phaladāyakam//1//
body.translated_text:
301.002. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Śrāvastī</s>.'
301.002. 'Very well, Venerable Sir' — the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One.
301.003. Then the Blessed One set out on his wandering toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
301.004. In a certain place, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose food had been cut off was driving a plow; a girl had gone carrying gruel for him.
301.005. The Blessed One arrived at that place.
301.005. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, adorned with the radiance of a fathom-wide aura, of a brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jewel-mountain, auspicious in every way.
301.007. At the very moment of seeing him, faith arose in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> toward the Blessed One.
301.008. Not so powerfully does tranquility practiced for twelve years produce joy, nor the gaining of a son for one who is childless, nor the sight of a treasure for the destitute, nor the royal consecration for one who delights in kingship, as does the very first sight of the <s>Buddha</s> for a being whose wholesome roots have been accumulated.
301.010. Taking that gruel, he quickly approached the Blessed One.
301.011. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: 'O <s>Gautama</s>, here is gruel.
301.011. If you have compassion for me, may the Blessed <s>Gautama</s> drink the gruel.'
301.012. Then the Blessed One showed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> a ruined well: 'If you are willing to part with it, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, pour it into this ruined well.'
301.013. He poured it into the ruined well.
301.013. That ruined well filled up with gruel to the brim — such is the power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the power of the deities.
301.014. Then the Blessed One said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'Distribute the gruel, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.'
301.015. He began to distribute it.
301.015. The Blessed One so empowered it that the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> drank.
301.016. And the ruined well, filling up again, stood full of gruel as before.
301.017. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, with even greater faith, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.
301.018. The Blessed One, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that penetrates the Four Noble Truths — as before, up to — having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the self-existent body, accumulated since beginningless time, he directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
301.020. 'I have been saved, Venerable Sir, saved!
301.020. I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks.
301.021. Regard me as a lay follower, from this day forward, as long as life lasts, one who has gone for refuge, endowed with faith.'
301.022. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, like a merchant who has obtained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a warrior who has won a battle, like a sick man freed from all disease, having rejoiced in and approved the Blessed One's words, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with his head, departed from the Blessed One's presence, and went to his field.
301.025. He saw that in his field, golden barley had ripened.
301.025. Having seen it, with eyes wide in wonder, he spoke a verse:
301.027. 'Ah, what a meritorious field, free from all faults!
301.028. The seed sown this very day has yielded fruit this very day!' //1//

body.text:
301.029. tato 'sau brāhmaṇastvaritatvaritaṃ rājñaḥ sakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
301.029. upasaṃkramya jayenāyuṣā vardhayitvā rājānamuvāca--deva, mayā yavāḥ prakīrṇāḥ, te sauvarṇāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
301.030. tasyādhiṣṭhāyakena prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti/
301.031. rājñā adhiṣṭhāyako 'nupreṣitaḥ/
301.031. brāhmaṇena rāśīkṛtya bhājitaḥ/
301.031. rājabhāgaḥ svābhāvikā yavāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
301.032. adhiṣṭhāyakena rājñe niveditam/
301.032. rājñā samādiṣṭam--<302>punarbhājayateti/
body.translated_text:
301.029. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> hurriedly approached the king.
301.029. Having approached and having congratulated the king with wishes for victory and long life, he said: 'Sire, the barley I sowed has turned to gold.
301.030. Please send an overseer to validate this.'
301.031. The king sent an overseer.
301.031. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> had it heaped up and divided.
301.031. The king's share turned into ordinary barley.
301.032. The overseer reported this to the king.
301.032. The king commanded: 'Divide it again.'

body.text:
302.001. taiḥ punarbhājitam/
302.001. tathaiva rājabhāgaḥ svābhāvikā yavāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
302.001. evam yāvat saptakṛtvo bhājitam/
302.002. tathaiva/
302.002. rājā kutūhalajātaḥ svayameva paśyati--tathaiva/
302.003. tenāsau brāhmaṇo 'bhihitah--brāhmaṇa, tavaitatpuṇyanirjātam/
302.003. alaṃ rājabhāgena, yathābhipretaṃ tanmamānuprayaccheti/
302.004. tatastena brāhmaṇena parituṣṭena yaddattam, tatsauvarṇāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ//
body.translated_text:
302.001. They divided it again.
302.001. Once again, the king's share turned into ordinary barley.
302.001. Thus it was divided up to seven times.
302.002. Each time the same.
302.002. The king, overcome by curiosity, went to see for himself — and so it was.
302.003. He said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this has arisen from your merit.
302.003. Enough of the king's share; give me as much as you wish.'
302.004. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, pleased, gave whatever he offered — and it all turned to gold.

body.text:
302.005. tato bhagavān saṃprasthitaḥ/
302.005. yāvadanyatamasmin pradeśe pañcakārṣaśatānyutpāḍūtpāṇḍukāni sphuṭitapāṇipādāni śaṇaśāṭīnivāsitāni laṅgalāni vāhayanti/
302.006. te 'pi balīvardā baddhaiḥ prayoktraiḥ pratodayaṣṭibhiḥ kṣatavikṣatagātrā muhurmuhur niśvasanto vahanti/
302.007. tadṛśuste kārṣākā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ pūrvavadyāvadupacitakuśalamūlasattvasya tatprathamato buddhadarśanam/
302.009. tato yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
302.009. adrākṣīdbhagavāṃstān kārṣakān dūrādeva/
302.010. dṛṣṭvā ca punarvineyāpekṣayā mārgādapakramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
302.010. eta kārṣakā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekāntaniṣaṇṇāḥ/
302.011. tato bhagavatā teṣāṃ kārṣakāṇāmāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, pūrvavadyāvadanādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
302.014. te dṛṣṭasatyā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
302.014. praṇamayya bhagavantamidamavocat--deśaya bhadanta, svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
302.015. carema bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryamiti/
302.016. te bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā pravrājitāḥ pūrvavadyāvatte 'vasthitā buddhamanorathena/
302.017. teṣāṃ bhagavatā avavādo dattaḥ/
302.017. tairyujyamānaiḥ pūrvavadabhivādyāśca saṃvṛttāḥ/
302.017. te 'pi balīvardā yoktrāṇi varatrāṇi ca cchittvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
302.018. upasaṃkramya bhagavantaṃ sāmantakena anuparivāryāvasthitāḥ/
302.019. teṣāṃ bhagavatā tribhiḥ padārthairdharmo deśitaḥ pūrvavadyāvadyathā gaṅgāvatāre haṃsamatsyakūrmāṇām yāvad dṛṣṭasatyāḥ svarbhavanaṃ gatāḥ//
body.translated_text:
302.005. Then the Blessed One set out.
302.005. In a certain place, five hundred farmers — pale, with cracked hands and feet, dressed in hemp garments — were driving their plows.
302.006. Their oxen too, with yokes and straps fastened, their bodies wounded and gashed by goad-sticks, drew the plows with frequent sighs.
302.007. Those farmers beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man — as before, up to — the very first sight of the <s>Buddha</s> for a being whose wholesome roots have been accumulated.
302.009. They approached the Blessed One.
302.009. The Blessed One saw those farmers from afar.
302.010. Having seen them, out of regard for those to be trained, he left the road and sat down on a prepared seat before the community of monks.
302.010. Those farmers, having bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with their heads, sat down to one side.
302.011. Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character of those farmers, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that penetrates the Four Noble Truths — as before, up to — having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the self-existent body, accumulated since beginningless time, they directly realized the fruit of stream-entry.
302.014. Having seen the truths, they approached the Blessed One.
302.014. Bowing before the Blessed One, they said: 'Teach us, Venerable Sir; let us receive the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of monks in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.
302.015. Let us practice the holy life in the presence of the Blessed One.'
302.016. They were ordained by the Blessed One with the 'Come, monks' formula — as before — and they were established in the <s>Buddha</s>'s aspiration.
302.017. An instruction was given to them by the Blessed One.
302.017. Striving and exerting, as before, they became worshipful.
302.017. Those oxen too, breaking their yokes and straps, approached the Blessed One.
302.018. Having approached, they stood encircling the Blessed One all around.
302.019. To them the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> with three topics — as before, up to — just as geese, fish, and turtles at the descent into the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — they saw the truths and went to the heavenly realm.

body.text: 302.021. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ nu taiḥ kārṣakapūrvakairbhikṣubhiḥ karma kṛtam yena kārṣakāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, bhagavataśca śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam? tairbalīvardapūrvakairdevaputraiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtam, yana balīvardeṣūpapannāḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtamiti? bhagavānāha--ebhireva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pūrvavadyāvatphalanti khalu dehinām//
body.translated_text: 302.021. The monks, having had doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deed was done by those monks in their former lives as farmers that they became farmers, and then, having gone forth in the Blessed One's teaching, directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions? And what deed was done by those gods in their former lives as oxen that they were reborn as oxen, yet also attained the vision of the truths?' The Blessed One said: 'It was they themselves, monks, who performed and accumulated those deeds, whose conditions had come together — as before, up to — they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.text:
302.026. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'sminneva bhadrakalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma śāstā loka udapādi/
302.027. pūrvavat/
302.027. sa vārāṇasīnagarīmupaniśritya viharati ṛṣivadane(patane) mṛgadāve/
302.028. tasya śāsane etāni pañca karṣakaśatāni pravrajitānyabhūvan/
302.028. tatraibhir na paṭhitaṃ na svādhyāyitaṃ nāpi manasikāro vihitaḥ/
302.029. kiṃ tu śraddhādeyaṃ bhuktvā bhuktvā saṃgaṇikābhirataiḥ kausīdyenābhināmitam//
body.translated_text:
302.026. 'Once upon a time, monks, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, there arose in the world a Teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
302.027. As before.
302.027. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> (the Sage's Face), in the Deer Park.
302.028. In his teaching, these five hundred had gone forth as monks.
302.028. There they did not study, did not recite, and did not apply mental attention.
302.029. Rather, having consumed what was given in faith, they were given over to socializing and bent by laziness.'

body.text:
303.001. <303>kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāni tāni pañca bhikṣuśatāni, etānyeva tāni pañca karṣakaśatāni/
303.002. yo 'sau vihārasvāmī, sa evāsau gṛhapatiryasyaite kārṣahāḥ/
303.002. yadebhirvihārasvāmisantakaṃ śraddhādeyaṃ paribhujya na paṭhitaṃ na svādhyāyitaṃ nāpi manasikāro vihitaḥ, kiṃ tu saṃgaṇikābhirataiḥ kausīdyenābhināmitam, tena karmaṇā pañca janmaśatāni tasya vihārasvāminaḥ kārṣakāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
303.005. yāvadetarhyapi tasyaiva kārṣakā jātāḥ/
303.005. yadebhiḥ kāśayapasya samyaksambuddhāsya śāsane pravrajya brahmacaryaṃ caritam, tenaitarhi mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
303.007. te ca balīvardapūrviṇo devaputrāḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śāsane pravrajitā āsan/
303.008. tatraibhiḥ kṣudrānukṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni khaṇḍitāni/
303.008. tena karmaṇā balīvardeṣūpapannāḥ/
303.009. yanmamāntike cittamabhiprasāditam, tena deveṣūpapannāḥ/
303.009. yatkāśyape samyaksambuddhe brahmacaryaṃ vāsitam, tenedānīṃ devaputrabhūtaiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam/
303.010. iti bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, pūrvavadyāvadābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
303.011. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text:
303.001. 'What do you think, monks? Those five hundred monks — they are these very five hundred farmers.
303.002. He who was the monastery-owner is this very householder whose farmers they are.
303.002. Because they consumed what was given in faith belonging to the monastery-owner and did not study, did not recite, and did not apply mental attention, but rather, given to socializing, were bent by laziness — by that deed, for five hundred lifetimes they became that monastery-owner's farmers.
303.005. And even now they have been born as his farmers.
303.005. But because they went forth and practiced the holy life in the teaching of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, therefore now, having gone forth in my teaching, they have directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all afflictions.
303.007. And those gods who were formerly oxen — they had gone forth in the teaching of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>.
303.008. There they violated the minor and subsidiary training rules.
303.008. By that deed, they were reborn as oxen.
303.009. Because they generated faith in me, they were reborn among the gods.
303.009. Because they practiced the holy life under the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, now as gods they attained the vision of the truths.
303.010. Thus, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the ripening is entirely dark — as before, up to — exertion must be made.
303.011. Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.'

body.text:
303.013. tatra bhagavānāyucmantamāmantrayate sma--āgamaya ānanda yena toyikā/
303.013. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavato 'śrauṣīt/
303.014. bhagavāṃstoyikāmanuprāptaḥ/
303.014. tasmiṃśca pradeśe brāhmaṇo lāṅgalaṃ vāhayati/
303.015. athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātraṃ pūrvavadyāvatsamantato bhadrakam/
303.016. dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--yadi bhagavantaṃ gautamamupetya abhivādayiṣyāmi, karmaparihāṇirme bhaviṣyati/
303.017. atha nopetyābhivādayiṣyāmi, puṇyaparihāṇiḥ/
303.018. tatko 'sāvupāyaḥ syādyena me na karmaparihāṇi syānnāpi puṇyaparihāṇiriti? tasya buddhirutpannā--atrastha evābhivādanaṃ karomi/
303.019. evaṃ na karmaparihāṇirbhavati nāpi puṇyaparihāṇiriti/
303.020. tena yathāgṛhītayaiva pratodayaṣṭyā tatrasthenābhivādanaṃ kṛtam--abhivādaye buddhaṃ bhagavantam/
303.021. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--kṣaṇa ānanda eṣa brāhmaṇaḥ/
303.022. sacedasyaivaṃ samyakpratyātmajñānadarśanaṃ pravartate/
303.022. etasmin pradeśe kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopito 'shtisaṃghātastiṣṭhatīti/
303.023. athānenopasaṃkramya vandito bhaveyam/
303.023. evamanena dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ vandanā kṛtā bhavet/
303.024. tatkasya hetoh? asminn ānanda pradeśe kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopito 'sthisaṃghātastiṣṭhatīti/
303.025. athāyuṣmānānando laghulaghveva caturguṇamuttarāsaṅgaṃ prajñapya bhagavantamidamavocat--niṣīdatu bhagavān prajñapta evāsane/
303.027. evamayaṃ pṛthivīpradeśo dvābhyāṃ samyaksambuddhābhyāṃ paribhukto bhaviṣyati, yacca kāśyapena samyaksambuddhena, yaccaitarhi bhagavateti/
303.028. niṣaṇṇo bhagavān prajñapta evāsane/
303.028. niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātamavikopitaṃ draṣṭum? etasya bhagavan kālaḥ, etasya sugata samayo 'yam/
303.030. bhagavān bhikṣūṇāṃ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaṃ śarīrasaṃghātamupadarśayatu, dṛṣṭvā bhikṣavaścittamabhiprasādayiṣyanti/
303.032. bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam/
303.032. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavanto laukikam <304>
body.translated_text: There, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, let us go to <s>Toyikā</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at <s>Toyikā</s>. In that place, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was driving a plow. He saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being — as before, up to — beautiful on all sides. Having seen him, he reflected: 'If I approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Gautama</s> and salute him, my work will suffer. But if I do not approach and salute him, my merit will suffer. What stratagem could there be by which neither my work nor my merit suffers?' The thought arose in him: 'I shall make my salutation standing right here. Thus neither my work nor my merit will suffer.' Then, standing right there with goad-staff in hand just as he had been holding it, he made his salutation: 'I salute the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>!' There, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'A moment, <s>Ānanda</s> — this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>! If his own direct knowledge and insight were to operate, he would know that in this very spot stands the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Then, if he had approached and saluted me, he would have made salutation to two Perfectly Enlightened Ones. For what reason? Because in this very spot, <s>Ānanda</s>, stands the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, very quickly folding his upper robe fourfold, laid it out and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> be seated on this prepared seat. Thus this spot of earth will have been used by two Perfectly Enlightened Ones — both by <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and now by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> sat on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Do you wish, monks, to see the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One?' 'This is the time for it, Blessed One; this is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> show the monks the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having seen it, the monks will inspire their minds with faith.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought. For it is the nature that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, produce a worldly thought—

body.text:
304.001. <304>cittamutpādayanti, tasmin samaye kuntapipīlikādayo 'pi prāṇino bhagavataścetasā cittamājānanti/
304.002. nāgāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittamutpāditam? bhagavān kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghātamavikopitaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ/
304.003. tatastaiḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasyāvikopitaḥ śarīrasaṃghāta ucchrāpitaḥ/
304.004. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--gṛhṇīta bhikṣavo nimittam/
304.005. antardhāsyatīti/
304.005. antarhitaḥ//
body.translated_text: at that time, even the smallest creatures such as ants perceive the <s>Bhagavān's</s> thought with their minds. The <s>Nāgas</s> reflected: 'For what reason has the <s>Bhagavān</s> produced a worldly thought? The <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to see the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.' Then they raised up the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. There, the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Take note of the sign, monks. It will disappear.' It disappeared.

body.text:
304.006. rājñā prasenajitā śrutam--bhagavatā śrāvakāṇāṃ darśanāya avikopitaḥ kaśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śarīrasaṃghāta ucchrāpita iti/
304.007. śrutvā ca punaḥ kutūhalajātaḥ sārdhamantah--pureṇa kumārauramātyairbhaṭabalāgrair naigamajanapadaiśca draṣṭuṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
304.008. evaṃ virūḍhako 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ, ṛṣidattaḥ purāṇasthapatiḥ, viśākhā mṛgaramātā, anekāni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kutūhalajātāni draṣṭuṃ saṃprasthitāni pūrvakaiśca kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni/
304.010. yāvadasau antarhitaḥ/
304.011. taiḥ śrutam--antarhito 'sau bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya śīrarasaṃghāta iti/
304.012. śrutvā ca punasteṣāṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyamutpannam--vṛthā asmākamāgamanaṃ jātamiti//
body.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> heard: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has had the undisturbed bodily relic of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, raised up for the disciples to see.' Having heard this, filled with curiosity, together with the inner palace, princes, ministers, military commanders, citizens, and countryfolk, he set out to see it. Likewise <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, <s>Ṛṣidatta</s> the old master-builder, <s>Viśākhā</s> <s>Mṛgāramātā</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of beings, filled with curiosity and impelled by their former roots of merit, set out to see it. But it had already disappeared. They heard: 'The bodily relic of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has disappeared.' Having heard this, sorrow and dejection arose in them: 'Our coming has been in vain!'

body.text:
304.013. athānyatamena copāsakena sa pradeśaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtaḥ/
304.013. evaṃ cetasā cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--asmānme padāvihārāt kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃstasya mahājanakāyasyāvipratisārasaṃjananārthaṃ tasya copāsakasya cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣite--
304.016. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇaniṣkā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
304.018. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ padāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān//2//
body.translated_text: Then a certain lay follower circumambulated that spot and generated this thought: 'From this circumambulation of mine, how much merit will there be?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in order to generate freedom from regret in that great crowd, knowing the thought in that lay follower's mind with his own mind, spoke a verse: 'Hundreds of thousands of gold coins of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> (finest gold) are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, performs circumambulation at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //2//

body.text:
304.020. anyatamenāpyupāsakena tasmin pradeśe mṛttikāpiṇḍo dattaḥ/
304.020. evaṃ cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--padāvihārasya tāvadiyatpuṇyamākhyātaṃ bhagavatā/
304.021. asya tu mṛttikāpiṇḍasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃs tasyāpi cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
304.023. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇapiṇḍaṃ jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
304.025. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitta āropayenmettikapiṇḍamekam//3// iti/
304.028. tacchrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmṛtpiṇḍasamāropaṇaṃ kṛtam/
304.028. aparaistatra muktapuṣpāṇi kṣiptāni, evaṃ cittamabhisaṃskṛtam--padāvihārasya mṛttikāpiṇḍasya ceyatpuṇyamuktaṃ bhagavatā, asmākaṃ tu muktapuṣpāṇāṃ kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text: Yet another lay follower placed a lump of earth on that spot and generated this thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for circumambulation; but how much merit will there be for this lump of earth of mine?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his thought too, spoke a verse: 'Hundreds of thousands of heaps of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, places even a single lump of earth at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //3// Having heard this, many hundreds of thousands of beings placed lumps of earth. Others scattered loose flowers there and generated this thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for circumambulation and for lumps of earth; but how much merit will there be for our loose flowers?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts too, spoke a verse:

body.text:
305.001. <305>śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇamūḍhaṃ jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
305.003. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitta āropayenmuktakapuṣparāśim//4// iti/
305.005. aparaistatra mālāvihāraḥ kṛtaḥ, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--muktapuṣpāṇāṃ bhagavatā iyatpuṇyamuktam/
305.006. asmākaṃ mālāvihārasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
305.008. śatasahasrāṇi suvarṇavāhā jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
305.010. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto mālāvihāraṃ prakaroti vidvān//5// iti/
305.012. aparaistatra dīpamālā dattā, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--mālāvihārasya bhagavatā iyatpuṇyamuktam/
305.013. asmākaṃ pradīpadānasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
305.015. śataṃsahasrāṇi suvarṇakoṭyo jāmbūnadā nāsy bhavanti/
305.017. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacittaḥ pradīpadānaṃ prakaroti vidvān//6// iti/
305.019. aparaistatra gandhābhiṣeko dattaḥ, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--pradīpadānasya bhagavatā iyat puṇyamuktam/
305.020. asmākaṃ gandhābhiṣekasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
305.022. śatasahasrāṇi suvarṇāśayo jāmbūnadā nāsya samā bhavanti/
305.024. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitto gandhābhiṣekaṃ prakaroti vidvān//7// iti/
305.026. aparaistatra dhvajapatākāropaṇaṃ kṛtam, cittaṃ cābhisaṃskṛtam--padavihārasya mṛtpiṇḍadānasya, muktapuṣpāṇāṃ mālavihārasya pradīpadānasya gandhābhiṣekasya ca iyatpuṇyamuktaṃ bhagavatā, āsmākaṃ chatradhvajapatākāropaṇasya kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
body.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of loads of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, places a heap of loose flowers at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //4// Others made a garland-offering there and generated the thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for loose flowers; how much merit will there be for our garland-offering?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts too, spoke a verse: 'Hundreds of thousands of cartloads of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, makes a garland-offering at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //5// Others offered rows of lamps there and generated the thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for garland-offerings; how much merit will there be for our offering of lamps?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts too, spoke a verse: 'Hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, makes an offering of lamps at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //6// Others offered a perfume-anointing there and generated the thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for lamp-offering; how much merit will there be for our perfume-anointing?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts too, spoke a verse: 'Hundreds of thousands of treasuries of gold of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, makes a perfume-anointing at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //7// Others raised up parasols, banners, and flags there and generated the thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared such merit for circumambulation, lumps of earth, loose flowers, garland-offerings, lamp-offerings, and perfume-anointings; how much merit will there be for our raising of parasols, banners, and flags?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts, spoke a verse:

body.text:
306.001. <306>śatasahasrāṇi suvarṇaparvatā meroḥ samā nāsya bhavanti/
306.003. yo buddhacaityeṣu prasannacitta āropayecchatradhvajapatākam//8//
body.translated_text: 'Hundreds of thousands of golden mountains equal to <s>Meru</s> are not equal to this — the merit of the wise one who, with a faithful mind, raises up parasols, banners, and flags at a <s>Buddha</s>'s shrine.' //8//

body.text:
306.005. eṣāṃ hi dakṣiṇā proktā aprameye tathāgate/
306.006. samudrakalpe saṃbuddhe sārthavāhe anuttare//9// iti/
306.007. teṣāmetadabhavat--parinirvṛtasya tāvadbhagavataḥ pūjākaraṇādi yatpuṇyamuktaṃ bhagavatā, tiṣṭhataḥ kiyatpuṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
306.008. atha bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi cetasā cittamājñāya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
306.009. tiṣṭhantaṃ pūjayedyacca yaccāpi parinirvṛtam/
306.010. samaṃ cittaprasādena nāsti puṇyaviśeṣatā/
306.011. evaṃ hyacintiyā buddhā buddhadharmāpyacintiyā//10//
body.translated_text: 'The reward from offerings to such a <s>Tathāgata</s> is declared to be immeasurable — to a Perfectly Enlightened One who is ocean-like, a caravan-leader unsurpassed.' //9// Those people then thought: 'Such merit from making offerings to the <s>Bhagavān</s> who has entered final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s>; but how much merit will there be from offerings to one who is still living?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their thoughts too, spoke a verse: 'Whether one worships him while he is living or when he has entered final <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the merit is the same in the faith of the mind — there is no difference in merit. For <s>Buddhas</s> are indeed inconceivable, and the qualities of <s>Buddhas</s> are also inconceivable.' //10//

body.text:
306.012. acintiyaiḥ prasannānāmapratihatadharmacakrapravartinām/
306.013. samyaksambuddhānāṃ nālaṃ guṇapāramadhigantum//11// iti/
306.014. tato bhagavatā tasya mahājanakāyasya tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yām anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ/
306.015. kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiściduṣmagatāni pratilabdhāni, kaiścid mūrdhānaḥ, kaiścitsatyānulomaḥ kṣāntyaḥ, kaiścicchrotāapattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścitsakṛdāgāmiphalam, kaiścidanāgāmiphalam, kaiścitsarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
306.018. yadbhūyasā sā parṣadbuddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā/
306.019. sārdhaṃ tatra brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhistasmin pradeśe mahaḥ sthāpitah--toyikāmahastoyikāmaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text: 'For those who have faith in the inconceivable ones, the unobstructed turners of the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones — their virtues cannot be fully fathomed.' //11// Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> to that great crowd that many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great distinction. By some, minds were directed toward the awakening of a disciple; by some, toward solitary awakening; by some, the warmth stage was attained; by some, the summit; by some, the patience conforming to truth; by some, the fruit of stream-entry was directly realized; by some, the fruit of once-returning; by some, the fruit of non-returning; by some, <s>Arhattva</s> was directly realized through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>. For the most part, that assembly was established inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, disposed toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Together with the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders there, a great festival was established at that spot — and it came to be known as the 'Festival of <s>Toyikā</s>.'

body.text: 306.021. iti toyikāmahāvadānamekatriṃśattamam//
body.translated_text: Thus, the <s>Toyikāmahāvadāna</s> (The Great Story of <s>Toyikā</s>), the thirty-first.

body.text: 307.001. div32 rūpāvatyavadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 32: The <s>Rūpāvatyavadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Rūpāvatī</s>).

body.text:
307.002. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
307.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ/
307.003. satkṛto bhagavān gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito bhikṣubhibhikṇyupāsakopāsikai rājñā rājamātrair nānāvaṇikchramaṇabrāhmaṇaparivrājakanaigamajanapadair nāgairyakṣairgandharvairasuragatuḍakinnaramahoragaiḥ/
307.005. lābhī ca bhagavān prabhutānāṃ praṇītānāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ divyānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, taiśca bhagavānanupaliptaḥ padmamiva vāriṇā/
307.007. tena khalu punaḥ samayena ayameva bhagavato 'nurūpa udāraḥ kalyāṇakīrtiśabda śloko 'bhyudgatah--ityapi sa bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca buddho bhagavān/
307.010. sa imāṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ saśramaṇabrāhmaṇīṃ prajāṃ sadevamanuṣīṃ svayamabhijñāya sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya viharati/
307.011. sa dharmaṃ deśayatyādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇāṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam/
307.012. svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma/
307.013. tatra bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--evaṃ ca bhikṣavaḥ sattvā jānīyuh--dānaṃ dānaphalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca vipākam, apīdānīm yo 'sau caramaḥ kavalaḥ paścima ālopaḥ, tamapi nāsaṃvibhajya pariṣvātmanā vā paribhuñjīran, na cotpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭheyuḥ/
307.016. yasmāttarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānanti dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam yathāhaṃ jāne dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam, tasmātsattvā yo 'sau caramaḥ kavalaḥ paścima ālopaḥ, tamevādattvā imamasaṃvibhajya pareṣvātmanā vā paribhuñjate, utpannaṃ cauṣāṃ mātsaryamalaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati//
body.translated_text:
307.002. Thus have I heard.
307.002. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks, twelve hundred and fifty monks.
307.003. The Blessed One was honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped by monks, nuns, male and female lay-followers, by kings and royal ministers, by various merchants, ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, wandering mendicants, townspeople, and countryfolk, by <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>.
307.005. And the Blessed One was a recipient of abundant and excellent robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, both divine and human; yet the Blessed One was untouched by them, like a lotus by water.
307.007. And at that time, this fitting and exalted proclamation of glorious fame had arisen concerning the Blessed One: 'Such indeed is that Blessed One — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a Knower of the World, an Unsurpassed Charioteer of persons to be tamed, a Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.'
307.010. He dwells having directly known and realized for himself this world with its gods, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, with its ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, its people with gods and humans.
307.011. He teaches the <s>Dharma</s> that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good at the end.
307.012. He proclaims the holy life that is good in meaning, good in expression, complete, utterly perfect, pure, and cleansed.
307.013. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'If, O monks, beings knew — the gift, the fruit of giving, and the ripening of the reward of sharing — then even with their last morsel, their final mouthful, they would not consume it without sharing, either with the assembly or by themselves; nor would arisen stinginess of mind persist and dominate them.
307.016. But because, O monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the ripening of the reward of sharing, as I know the fruit of giving and the ripening of the reward of sharing, therefore beings consume even their last morsel, their final mouthful, without giving, without sharing, either with others or by themselves; and the arisen stain of stinginess persists and dominates their minds.'

body.text:
307.020. bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantamapṛcchan--āścaryaṃ bhadanta yāvacca bhagavata etarhi yācakāḥ priyāḥ/
307.021. na bhikṣava etarhi mama, yathā atīte 'pyadhvani yācanakāḥ priyāḥ/
307.022. taccrūyatām//
body.translated_text:
307.020. The monks, in whom all manner of doubts had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wondrous, Venerable Sir, how dear supplicants are to the Blessed One even now!'
307.021. 'Not only now, O monks, are supplicants dear to me; in the past as well, supplicants were dear to me.
307.022. Listen to this.'

body.text:
307.023. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvanyuttarāpatheṣu janapadeṣu utpalāvatī nāṃ nagarī rājadhānī babhūva ṛddhā ca sphaītā ca kṣemā ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyā ca/
307.024. athāpareṇa samayena utpalāvatyāṃ nagararājadhānyāṃ durbhikṣamabhūd durjīvaṃ durlabhapiṇḍaṃ nasukaramapatāne pragrahaṇe yāpayitum/
307.026. tena khalu samayenotpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ rūpāvatī nāma strī babhūva abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā śubhavarṇapuṣkalanayā samanvāgatā/
307.027. atha rūpāvatī strī svānniveśanānniṣkramya utpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ jaṅghāvihāramanukrāmati/
307.028. anyataradapavarakaṃ prāviśat/
