307.028. tasmin khalu samaye tasminnapavarake strī prasūtā, dārakaṃ prajātā abhirūpaṃ prāsādikaṃ śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatam/
307.030. taṃ sā strī kṣutkṣāmaparītā raikṣacittā dārakaṃ gṛhṇāti, icchati ca svāni putramāṃsāni bhikṣayitum/
307.031. tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpāvatī strī etadavovat--kimidaṃ bhagini kartukāmāsi? sā āha--jighatsitāsmi bhagini/
307.032. icchāmi svakāni putramāṃsāni <308>bhakṣayitum/
body.translated_text:
307.023. 'In the past, O monks, in a former age, in the countries of the northern region, there was a royal capital named <s>Utpalāvatī</s> — prosperous, flourishing, secure, and thronging with many people.
307.024. Then, at another time, in the royal capital <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, there arose a famine — life was hard, alms were scarce, and it was difficult to sustain oneself by gleaning or begging.
307.026. At that time, in the royal capital <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, there was a woman named <s>Rūpāvatī</s> — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness.
307.027. Then <s>Rūpāvatī</s>, going out from her own dwelling, was walking about on foot in the royal capital <s>Utpalāvatī</s>.
307.028. She entered a certain side-chamber.
307.028. At that time, in that side-chamber, a woman had given birth to a child — a boy, beautiful, pleasing, endowed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness.
307.030. That woman, overcome by hunger, with a cruel mind, seized the child and wished to eat her own son's flesh.
307.031. Seeing her, <s>Rūpāvatī</s> said: "What is this you intend to do, sister?" She replied: "I am starving, sister.
307.032. I wish to eat my own son's flesh."'

body.text:
308.001. rūpāvatī āha--tenabhagini niveśane kiṃcitsaṃvidyate 'nnaṃ vā pānaṃ vā bhojanaṃ vā svādanīyaṃ vā? durlabhaḥ putraśabdo lokasya/
308.002. na me bhagini kiṃcitsaṃvidyate niveśane annaṃ vā pānaṃ vā khādyaṃ vā bhojanaṃ vā svādanīyaṃ vā lehyaṃ vā/
308.003. durlabhaṃ jīvitaṃ lokasya/
308.004. rūpāvatyāha--tena hi bhagini muhūrtamāgamaya, yāvadahaṃ niveśanaṃ gatvā tavārthāya bhojanamānayiṣyāmi/
308.005. sā āha--yatkhalu bhagini jānīyāh--kukṣirme lupyati, pṛthivī me sphuṭati, hṛdayaṃ me dhūmāyati, diśo me na pratibhānti/
308.006. na tāvattvaṃ dvāraśālāyā nirgatā bhaviṣyasi yāvanme vāyava ākramiṣyanti/
308.007. yathā rūpāvatyā etadabhavat--yadi dārakaṃ gṛhītvā gamiṣyāmi, eṣā strī kṣutkṣāmaparītā kālaṃ kariṣyati/
308.008. atha dārakamapahāya yāsyāmi, niyataṃ dārakaṃ bhakṣayiṣyati/
308.009. yathākathaṃ punarmama kurvantyā dvayorjīvitalābhaḥ syāt? tasyā etadabhavat--anaparādhyāśayavati saṃsāre bahūni duḥkhānyanubhūtāni asakṛ nnarakeṣvasakṛttiryakṣvasakṛd yamaloke 'sakṛ nmanuṣyalokeṣu hastacchedāḥ pādacchedāḥ karṇacchedā karṇanāsācchedā aṅgapratyaṅgacchedāstathānyāni vividhāni bahūni duḥkhanyanubhūtāni/
308.012. ko mayā tenārtho 'nuprāpto yadā āhamātmanaḥ sthāmaṃ ca balaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca saṃjanayitvā imāṃ striyaṃ svena rudhireṇa māṃsena saṃtarpya imaṃ dārakaṃ parimocayeyam/
308.014. rūpāvatī pṛcchati--asti te bhagini niveśane śastram? sā strī āha--astīti/
308.015. tena hi yatra bhavati, tadupadarśaya/
308.015. sā taṃ pradeśamupadarśayāmāsa/
308.016. tato rūpāvatyā svayameva śastraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ gṛhītvā tau stanau cchittvā tāṃ striyaṃ svakena māṃsarudhireṇa saṃtarpayati sma/
308.017. saṃtarpya ca tāṃ striyametadavocat--yatkhalu bhagini jānīyāh--ayaṃ dārako mayā svakena māṃsarudhireṇa krītaḥ/
308.018. sāhaṃ tava nikṣepamanuprayacchāmi--mā bhūyo dārakaṃ bhakṣayiṣyasi, yāvadahaṃ niveśanaṃ gatvā tavārthāya bhojanamānayiṣyāmi/
308.019. sā āha--adya tāvan bhūyaḥ/
308.020. atha rūpāvatī strī rudhireṇoddharatā yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntā/
308.021. adrākṣīdrūpāvatyāḥ striyāḥ svāmī rūpāvatīm, strīṃ rudhireṇoddharatā pradharatā dūrata eva agacchantīm/
308.022. dṛṣṭvā ca punā rūpāvatīmetadavocat--kenedamevamrūpaṃ rūpāvati viprakāraṃ kṛtam? sautāṃ prakṛtiṃ vistareṇārocayati sma/
308.023. ārocayitvā etadavocat--prajñapaya āryaputra tasyā striyā bhaktam/
308.024. sa āha--prajñapaya āryaduhitastasyā bhaktam/
308.024. api tu satyavacanaṃ tāvatkariṣyāmi/
308.024. yenāryaduhitaḥ satyena satyavacanena ayamevamrūpa āścaryādbhuto dharmo na kadācid dṛṣṭo vā śruto vā, tena satyena satyavacanena ubhau tava stanau yathāpaurāṇau prādurbhavetām/
308.026. sahakṛtenāsminnevamrūpe satyavacane tasyā asminneva kṣaṇe ubhau stanau yathāpaurāṇau prādurbhūtau//
body.translated_text:
308.001. <s>Rūpāvatī</s> said: 'Then, sister, is there anything at all in your dwelling — food, drink, a meal, or something to eat? The name "son" is rare in this world.'
308.002. 'I have nothing at all in my dwelling, sister — no food, no drink, nothing to chew, no meal, nothing to eat, nothing to lick.
308.003. Life itself is scarce in this world.'
308.004. <s>Rūpāvatī</s> said: 'Then, sister, wait a moment while I go to my dwelling and bring food for you.'
308.005. She said: 'Know this, sister — my belly is collapsing, the earth is splitting beneath me, my heart is smoldering, the directions vanish before me.
308.006. You will not even have passed through the door before the winds of death seize me.'
308.007. Then <s>Rūpāvatī</s> thought: 'If I take the child and go, this woman, overcome by hunger, will die.
308.008. But if I leave the child and go, she will surely eat it.
308.009. How then can I act so that both may live?' She thought: 'In this beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, with its faultless and faulty intentions, many sufferings have been endured — again and again in the hells, again and again among animals, again and again in the world of <s>Yama</s>, again and again in the human world — hands cut off, feet cut off, ears cut off, ears and nose cut off, limbs and appendages cut off, and many other diverse sufferings endured.
308.012. What purpose was served by all that? Now let me, generating my own strength, power, and heroic effort, nourish this woman with my own blood and flesh and save this child.'
308.014. <s>Rūpāvatī</s> asked: 'Sister, is there a knife in your dwelling?' The woman said: 'There is.'
308.015. 'Then show me where it is.' She showed her the place.
308.016. Then <s>Rūpāvatī</s> herself took the sharp knife and cut off both her breasts, and with her own flesh and blood she nourished that woman.
308.017. Having nourished her, she said to that woman: 'Know this, sister — this child has been purchased by me with my own flesh and blood.
308.018. I now entrust him to your safekeeping — you must not eat the child again, while I go to my dwelling and bring food for you.'
308.019. She said: 'Enough for today.'
308.020. Then <s>Rūpāvatī</s>, dripping with blood, went toward her own dwelling.
308.021. <s>Rūpāvatī</s>'s husband saw <s>Rūpāvatī</s> approaching from afar, dripping and streaming with blood.
308.022. Seeing her, he said: 'Who has done such a thing to you, <s>Rūpāvatī</s>?' She told him the entire matter in detail.
308.023. Having told him, she said: 'Noble husband, prepare food for that woman.'
308.024. He said: 'Noble wife, prepare food for that woman. But first I shall make a declaration of truth.
308.024. By the truth of this truth-declaration, by which you, noble wife, performed this marvelous and astonishing deed never before seen or heard of — by that truth, by that truth-declaration, may both your breasts be restored as before.'
308.026. The moment this truth-declaration was made, at that very instant, both her breasts were restored as before.

body.text:
308.028. atha śakrasya devānāmindrasyaitadabhavat--atityāgo 'tityāgagauravatā yā rūpāvatyā striyā kṛtaḥ/
308.029. mā haiva sā rūpāvatī strī ataḥ śakrabhavanāccyāvayet/
308.029. yannvahamenāṃ mīmāṃseyam/
308.030. atha śakro devendra udārabrāhmaṇarūpamātmānamabhinirmāya sauvarṇadaṇḍakamaṇḍalumādāya suvarṇadaṇḍena maṇivālavyajanena vījyamānastadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃmiñjitaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayet prasāritaṃ saṃmiñjayet, evameva śakro devānāmindro deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣvantarhita utpalāvatyām <309>rājadhānyāṃ pratyasthāt/
body.translated_text:
308.028. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, thought: 'This is an extraordinary act of giving, an extraordinary weight of generosity, that <s>Rūpāvatī</s> has performed.
308.029. May this woman <s>Rūpāvatī</s> not cause me to fall from my <s>Śakra</s>-palace!
308.029. Let me test her.'
308.030. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, conjured himself into the form of a distinguished <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, took a golden staff and water-vessel, and fanned with a jeweled yak-tail whisk on a golden handle — just as a strong man might bend his outstretched arm or extend his bent arm — so <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, vanished from among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods and appeared in the royal capital <s>Utpalāvatī</s>.

body.text:
309.001. atha śakro devānāmindra utpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ bhaikṣyamanvāhiṇḍan yana rūpāvatyāḥ striyā niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkramya dvāri sthitvā bhaikṣyamutkrośate/
309.002. tato rūpāvatī strī bhaikṣamādāya yena sa brāhmaṇaveṣadharaḥ śakraḥ, tenopasaṃkramya bhaikṣamupanāmayate/
309.003. atha sa śakro devānāmindro rūpāvatīṃ striyametadvocat--satyaṃ te rūpāvari dārakasyārthāyobhau stanau parityaktau? sā āha--ārya brāhmaṇa satyam/
309.005. sa tāmāh--evaṃ te rūpāvatī ubhau stanau parityajāmīti parityajantyāḥ parityajya vā abhūccittasya vipratisārah? sā āha--na me ubhau stanau parityajantyā abhūccittasya vipratisāraḥ/
309.007. śakra aha--atra kaḥ śraddhāsyati? rūpāvatyāha--tena hi brāhmaṇa satyavacanaṃ kariṣyāmi/
309.008. yena satyena brahman satyavacanenobhau stanau parityajāmīti parityajantyāḥ parityajya vā nābhūccittasyānyathātvam, nābhūccittasya vipratisāraḥ, api ca brahman yena satyena mayā dārakasyārthāyobhau stanau parityaktau, na rājyārthaṃ na bhogārthaṃ na śakrārthaṃ na rājñāṃ cakravartināṃ viṣayārthaṃ nānyatrāhamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambudhya adāntān damayeyam, amuktān mocayeyam, anāśvastānāśvāsayeyam, aparinirvṛtān parinirvāpayeyam, tena satyena satyavacanena mama strīndriyamantardhāya puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhavet/
309.014. tasyāstasminneva kṣaṇe strīndriyamantarhitam, puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtam/
309.014. atha khalu śakro devendrastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātas tata eva ṛddhyā vaihāyasamabhyudgamyodānamudānayati--rūpāvatyāḥ strīndriyamantarhitam, puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtam/
309.016. rūpāvatyāḥ striyo rūpāvataḥ kumāra iti saṃjñā utpāditā//
body.translated_text:
309.001. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, went about begging for alms in the royal capital <s>Utpalāvatī</s>; approaching <s>Rūpāvatī</s>'s dwelling, he stood at the door and called out for alms.
309.002. Then <s>Rūpāvatī</s>, taking alms-food, approached <s>Śakra</s> who was disguised as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and offered him the alms.
309.003. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said to <s>Rūpāvatī</s>: 'Is it true, <s>Rūpāvatī</s>, that you gave up both your breasts for the sake of the child?' She said: 'Noble <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, it is true.'
309.005. He said to her: 'When you, <s>Rūpāvatī</s>, were giving up both your breasts — while giving them up, or after having given them up — was there any regret in your mind?' She said: 'While giving up both my breasts, there was no regret in my mind.'
309.007. <s>Śakra</s> said: 'Who will believe this?' <s>Rūpāvatī</s> said: 'Then, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall make a declaration of truth.
309.008. By the truth of this truth-declaration — that while giving up both my breasts, while giving them up, or after having given them up, there was no change of mind, no regret in my mind; and moreover, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, by the truth that I gave up both my breasts for the sake of the child — not for the sake of sovereignty, not for the sake of enjoyment, not for the sake of <s>Śakra</s>'s domain, not for the sake of the realm of universal monarchs, but for nothing other than that I, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, might tame the untamed, liberate the unliberated, comfort the uncomforted, and lead to <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> — by that truth, by that truth-declaration, may my female nature disappear and a male nature appear!'
309.014. At that very instant, her female nature disappeared and a male nature appeared.
309.014. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, pleased, elated, delighted, joyful, filled with gladness and delight, rising up into the sky by his supernatural power, proclaimed this exclamation: '<s>Rūpāvatī</s>'s female nature has disappeared and a male nature has appeared!'
309.016. For <s>Rūpāvatī</s> the woman, the designation 'Prince <s>Rūpāvata</s>' was established.

body.text:
309.018. athāpareṇa samayenopalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ nagaryāṃ rājā aputraḥ kālagataḥ/
309.018. tatra piṇḍatajātīyānāṃ mahāmātrāṇāmetadabhūt--yannu vayamutpalāvatyāṃ rāhadhānyāṃ rāhānaṃ sthāpayema/
309.020. teṣāmetadabhūt--nānyatra rūpāvatakumārātkṛtapuṇyātkṛtakuśalāt/
309.020. te rūpāvataṃ kumāramutpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ rājānaṃ sthāpayanti/
309.021. atha sa ṣaṣṭivarṣāṇi rājyaṃ kārayati/
309.021. dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā kālamakārṣīt/
309.022. kāyasya bhedāttasyāmevotpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanyatamasya śroṣṭhino gṛhapateragramahiṣyāḥ kukṣāvupapannaḥ/
309.023. sā pūrṇānāmaṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāddārakaṃ janayati abhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatam/
309.024. tasya jātamātrasya tādṛśī kāyātprabhā muktā, yayā prabhayā candrasya prabhā niṣprabhīkṛtā/
309.025. athānyatarā strī yena sa śreṣṭhī gṛhapatistenopasaṃkrāntā/
309.026. upasaṃkramya śreṣṭhinaṃ gṛhapatimetadavocat--yatkhalu gṛhapate jānīyāh--te dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ śubhayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
309.027. tasya jātamātrasya tādṛśī kāyātprabhā pramuktā, yayā candrasya prabhā niṣprabhīkṛtā/
309.028. atha sa śreṣṭhī gṛhapatistuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ prītasaumanasyajātas tasyā eva rātryā atyayādye jānanti brahmaṇā lakṣaṇyā naibhittikā vaipañcikā bhūmyantarikṣamantrakuśalā nakṣatraśukragrahacaritajñāḥ, sa tān saṃnipātya dārakamupadarśayati--yatkhalu brāhmaṇā jānīdhvam--ayamagramahiṣyā dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prasādikāḥ śubhayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
309.032. etasya jātamātrasya tādṛśī kāyātprabhā muktā, yayā candrasya prabhā niṣprabhīkṛtā/
309.033. tadasya brāhmaṇā dārakasya lakṣaṇāni prekṣya <310>nāma avasthāpayati/
body.translated_text: Then, at another time, in the royal capital city of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, the king died without a son. There, the ministers of the <s>piṇḍata</s> class had this thought: 'Let us install a king in the royal capital of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>.' They had this thought: 'There is none other than the prince <s>Rūpāvata</s>, who has made merit, who has made wholesome deeds.' They installed the prince <s>Rūpāvata</s> as king in the royal capital of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>. Then he ruled the kingdom for sixty years. Having ruled the kingdom righteously, he passed away. Upon the dissolution of his body, he was reborn in the womb of the chief queen of a certain <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-master) householder in that very royal capital of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>. She, after the completion of eight or nine full months, gave birth to a boy — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with an excellent complexion and beauty. At the very moment of his birth, such a radiance was emitted from his body that by that radiance the light of the moon was outshone. Then a certain woman approached that <s>śreṣṭhin</s> householder. Having approached, she said to the <s>śreṣṭhin</s> householder: 'May the householder please know — a boy has been born to you, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with an excellent complexion and beauty. At the very moment of his birth, such a radiance was emitted from his body that the light of the moon was outshone.' Then that <s>śreṣṭhin</s> householder, delighted, elated, overjoyed, filled with gladness and happiness, after the passing of that very night, summoned those who are learned in <s>Brahman</s>, skilled in reading marks, soothsayers, diviners, those skilled in the <s>mantras</s> of earth and sky, those who know the movements of the stars, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and the planets, and showed them the boy: 'May the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> please know — this boy has been born to the chief queen, handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with an excellent complexion and beauty. At the very moment of his birth, such a radiance was emitted from his body that the light of the moon was outshone. Therefore, let the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> examine the marks of this boy and bestow a name upon him.'

body.text:
310.001. tasye ta brāhmaṇā lakṣaṇanaimittikā vipañcikā bhūmyantarīkṣamantrakuśalā nakṣatraśukragrahacatiteṣu kovidā dārakamupagatāḥ/
310.002ṭe saṃlakṣya vadanti--te gṛhapate dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prasādikaḥ śubhayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgaraḥ/
310.003. asya jātamātrasya tādṛśī kāyātprabhā muktā yayā candraprabhā niṣprabhīkṛtā/
310.004. tadbhavatvasya candraprabha iti nāma/
310.005. atha śreṣṭhī gṛhapatistān brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā visarjya candraprabhasya dārakasya catasro dhātrīranuprayacchati aṅkadhātrī maladhātrī stanadhātrī karīḍāpaṇilā dhātrī/
310.006. aṅkadhātrītyucyate yā dārakamaṅkena parikarṣayati, aṅkapratyaṅgāni ca saṃsthāpayati/
310.007. maladhātrītyucyate yā dārakaṃ snāapayati, cīvarakānmalaṃ prapātayati/
310.008. stanyadhātryucyate yā dārakaṃ stanyaṃ pāyayati/
310.009. krūḍāpanikā dhātryucyate yāni tāni dārakāṇāṃ dakṣakāṇāṃ taruṇakānāṃ ktīḍāpanikāni bhavanti, yadyathā--akāyikā sakāyikā vitkoḍikā(?) syapeṭārikā vaṃśaghaṭikā saṃdhāvaṇikā hastivigrahā aśvavigrahā balīvardavigrahāḥ kathayanti dhanurgrahāḥ kāṇḍakaṭacchupūrakūrcabhaiṣajyasthavikāśca purataḥ patikṛṣyante/
310.012. sa ābhiścatasṛbhirunnīyate vardhyate mahatā śrīsaubhāgyena/
310.012. yadā candraprabho dārako 'ṣṭavarṣo jātyā saṃvṛttaḥ, tadainaṃ mātāpitarau susnātaṃ suviliptaṃ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaṃ kṛtvā saṃbahulairdārakaiḥ parivṛttaṃ lipiṃ prāpayante/
310.014. tena khalu samayena tasyāṃ lipiśālāyāṃ pañcamātrakadārakaśatāni lipiṃ śikṣanti/
310.015. atha candraprabho dārakastān dārakānetadavocat--etaddārakā vayaṃ sarve 'nuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambodhau cittamutpādayema/
310.016. te āhuh--kiṃ candraprabha bodhisattvena karaṇīyam? sa āha--ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrayitavyāḥ/
310.017. katamāḥ ṣaṭ? tadyathā--dānapāramitā śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā/
310.018. tadahaṃ dānaṃ dadāmi, yannvahaṃ tiryagyonigatebhyo 'pi dānaṃ dadyām/310.19. sa tīkṣṇaṃ śastramādāya madhusarpiśca yenānyataraṃ mahāśmaśānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
310.020. śastreṇātmanaḥ kāyaṃ kṣaṇitvā madhusarpiṣā mrakṣayitvā tasmin sa mahāśmaśāne ātmānaṃ vadhāyotsṛjati/
310.021. tena ca samayena tasmin mahāśmaśāne uccaṃgamaḥ pakṣī prativasati/
310.022. sa candraprabhasya dārakasyāṅge sthitvā dakṣiṇaṃ nayanaṃ gṛhītvā utpāṭayati, punarmuñcati/
310.023. dvirapi trirapi uccaṃgamaḥ prāṇī candraprabhasya dārakasya dakṣiṇaṃ nayanaṃ gṛhītvā utpāṭayitvā punarmuñcati/
310.024. atha candraprabho dāraka uccaṃgamaṃ pakṣiṇamidamavocat--kimidaṃ pakṣi mama nayanaṃ gṛhītvā utpāṭayitvā utpāṭayitvā punaḥ pramuñcasi? sa āha--na mama candraprabha kiṃcidevāmiṣye(?) yathā manuṣyākṣi/
310.026. taṃ manye candraprabha vārayiṣyasi? candraprabha āha--sacenmama pakṣī sahasrakṛtvo nayanaṃ gṛhītvā utpāṭayatu, punarmuñca (tu), na tvevāhaṃ vārayeyam/
310.028. ityuktvā tāvantaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ saṃnipatitāḥ/
310.028. yena candraprabho nirmāṃso 'sthiśakalīkṛtaḥ/
310.029. sa kālamakārṣīt/
310.029. tasyāmevotpalāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāmanyatarasya brāhmaṇamahāśālasyāgramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau upapannaḥ/
310.030. sā pūrṇānāṃ navānāṃ māsānāmatyayāddārakaṃ janayati, abhirūpaṃ darśanīyaṃ prāsādikāṃ śubhayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatam/
310.032. tasya mātāpitarau brāhmaprabha iti nāma sthāpitavantau/
310.033. yadā brāhmaprabho nāma māṇavako 'ṣṭavarṣajātīyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, tena sarve brāhmaṇakā <311>mantrā adhītāḥ/
body.translated_text: Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, skilled in reading marks and signs, diviners, those skilled in the <s>mantras</s> of earth and sky, learned in the movements of the stars, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), and the planets, approached the boy. Having examined him, they said: 'O householder, a boy has been born to you — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with an excellent complexion and beauty. At the very moment of his birth, such a radiance was emitted from his body that the light of the moon was outshone. Therefore, let his name be <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moon-radiance).' Then the <s>śreṣṭhin</s> householder, having fed and dismissed those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, appointed four nurses for the boy <s>Candraprabha</s>: a lap-nurse, a bathing-nurse, a breast-nurse, and a play-nurse. The one called the lap-nurse is she who carries the boy on her lap and sets his limbs and joints in proper position. The one called the bathing-nurse is she who bathes the boy and removes dirt from his garments. The one called the breast-nurse is she who gives the boy milk to drink. The one called the play-nurse — she provides those playthings that belong to boys, young and tender, such as: toy figures with and without bodies, toy carts, toy drums, bamboo rattles, racing games, toy elephants, toy horses, toy bulls, storytelling games, toy bows, arrows, toy ladles, toy brooms, toy medicine bags — these are drawn before him. He was raised and nourished by these four nurses with great prosperity and good fortune. When the boy <s>Candraprabha</s> had reached eight years of age, his parents had him well-bathed, well-anointed, adorned with all ornaments, and surrounded by many boys, and sent him to learn writing. At that time, in that writing school, some five hundred boys were learning to write. Then the boy <s>Candraprabha</s> said to those boys: 'Come, boys, let us all generate the aspiration for supreme, perfect <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).' They said: 'What is to be done by a <s>bodhisattva</s>, O <s>Candraprabha</s>?' He said: 'The six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) must be fulfilled. Which six? Namely: <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct), <s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīrya-pāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñā-pāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). I shall practice giving — let me give even to those born in animal realms.' Taking a sharp blade and honey mixed with ghee, he went to a certain great charnel ground. Having cut his own body with the blade and smeared it with honey and ghee, he offered himself up to be devoured in that great charnel ground. At that time, a bird called <s>uccaṃgama</s> (vulture) was dwelling in that great charnel ground. It alighted on the body of the boy <s>Candraprabha</s>, seized his right eye, plucked it out, then released it again. Twice, even three times, the <s>uccaṃgama</s> bird seized the right eye of the boy <s>Candraprabha</s>, plucked it out, and released it again. Then the boy <s>Candraprabha</s> said to the <s>uccaṃgama</s> bird: 'Why, O bird, do you seize my eye, pluck it out, and then release it again?' It said: 'There is nothing, O <s>Candraprabha</s>, that I relish as much as a human eye. Do you think, <s>Candraprabha</s>, that you will stop me?' <s>Candraprabha</s> said: 'Even if, O bird, you seize and pluck out my eye a thousand times and release it again, I would never stop you.' Having said this, that many birds gathered together, and <s>Candraprabha</s> was stripped of flesh and reduced to a heap of bones. He passed away. He was reborn in the womb of the chief queen of a certain great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder in that very royal capital of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>. She, after the completion of nine full months, gave birth to a boy — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with an excellent complexion and beauty. His parents bestowed upon him the name <s>Brahmaprabha</s> (Brahma-radiance). When the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> had reached eight years of age, he had studied all the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>mantras</s>.

body.text:
311.001. yadā brahmaprabho māṇavako dvādaśavarṣajātīyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, sa pañcamātrāṇi māṇavakāni svayameva mantrān vācayati/
311.002. yadā brahmaprabho māṇavakaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣo jātyā saṃvṛttaḥ, tadainaṃ mātāpitarau āhatuh--brahmaprabha, tavārthāya niveśanaṃ kariṣyāvaḥ/
311.003. sa āha--amba tāta, na tāvanmama niveśanena prayojanam/
311.004. tau āhatuh--kiṃ punastvaṃ brahmaprabha kariṣyasi? sa āha--icchāmyahaṃ sattvānāmarthāya tapastaptuṃ duṣkaraṃ caritum/
311.005. tau āhatuh--yasyedānīṃ brahmaprabha kālaṃ manyase/
311.006. brahmaprabhamāṇavako mātāpitroḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya utpalāvatyā rājadhānyā niṣkramya yenānyataradvanaṣaṇḍaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
311.007. tena khalu samayena tasmin vanaṣaṇḍe dvau brāhmaṇarṣī prativasataḥ/
311.008. apaśyatāṃ brāhmaṇarṣīṃ brahmaprabhaṃ māṇavakaṃ dūrata evāgacchantam/
311.009. dṛṣṭvā ca brahmaprabhaṃ māṇavakametadavocat--ehi brahmaprabha, svāgatam, mā śrānto 'si, mā klāntaḥ/
311.010. kimarthamidaṃ vanaṣaṇṭamabhyāgatah? sa āha--icchāmyahaṃ sarvasattvānāmarthāya tapastaptuṃ duṣkaraṃ caritum/
311.011. tau āhatuh--evamastu, bhavatu, ṛddhyantāṃ saṃkalpāḥ, paripūryantāṃ manorathāḥ//
body.translated_text: When the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> became twelve years of age, he himself taught the <s>mantras</s> to five young men. When the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> became sixteen years of age by birth, his mother and father said to him: "<s>Brahmaprabha</s>, we shall arrange a household for you." He said: "Mother, Father, I have no need yet of a household." The two said: "What then, <s>Brahmaprabha</s>, will you do?" He said: "I wish to practice <s>tapas</s> (austerities), hard to perform, for the benefit of beings." The two said: "Do now, <s>Brahmaprabha</s>, what you think is the time for." The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s>, having venerated the feet of his mother and father with his head and circumambulated them three times, departed from the royal capital of <s>Utpalāvatī</s> and approached a certain grove. At that time, in that grove there dwelt two <s>brāhmaṇa</s> seers (<s>brāhmaṇarṣis</s>). The two <s>brāhmaṇa</s> seers saw the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> coming from afar. And seeing him, they said this to the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s>: "Come, <s>Brahmaprabha</s>, welcome! May you not be weary, may you not be exhausted. For what purpose have you come to this grove?" He said: "I wish to practice <s>tapas</s> (austerities), hard to perform, for the benefit of all beings." The two said: "So be it, let it be; may your resolves prosper, may your aspirations be fulfilled."

body.text:
311.012. atha brahmaprabho māṇavako 'nyatarasmin pradeśe kuṭīṃ kārayitvā caṃkramaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sattvānāmarthāya tapastaptavān/
311.013. athāpareṇa samayena brahmaprabhasya kuṭyā nātidūre vyāghrī gurviṇī vāsamupagatā/
tāṃ brahmaprabho māṇavako 'drākṣīt/
311.014. tāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca yena punastau dvau brahmarṣī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
311.014. upasaṃkramya tau ca brahmarṣī etadavocat--yatkhalu ṛṣī jānītām--iha me kuṭyā nātidūre vyāghrī gurviṇī vāsamupagatā/
311.016. tasyāḥ ka utsahate bhaktaṃ dātum? tau āhatuh--āvāṃ tasyā bhaktaṃ dāsyāvaḥ/
311.017. athāpareṇa samayena vyāghrī prasūtā kṣutkṣāmaparītā icchati svakau potakau bhakṣayitum/
311.017. ekaṃ potakaṃ gṛhṇāti dvitīyaṃ muñcati, na bhakṣayati/
311.018. tāṃ brahmaprabho māṇavako 'paśyat/
311.018. dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena tau brahmarṣī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
311.019. upasaṃkramya punaryena tau dvau brahmarṣī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
311.020. upasaṃkramya dvau brahmarṣī etadavocat--yatkhalu brāhmaṇau jānītām--sā vyāghrī prasūtā kṣutkṣāmaparītā svakau potakau bhakṣayitumicchati/
311.021. ekaṃ potakaṃ gṛhītvā dvitīyaṃ muñcati na bhakṣayati/
311.022. tasyāḥ ka utsahate bhaktaṃ dātum? tau āhatuh--āvāṃ tasyā bhaktaṃ dāsyāvaḥ/
311.022. atha tau brahmarṣī yena sā vyāghrī tenopasaṃkrāntau/
311.023. apaśyatsā vyāghrī brahmarṣī dūrata evāgacchantau/
311.024. dṛṣṭvā ca kṣutkṣāmaparītā abhidravitukāmā/
311.024. tayoretadabhūt--ka utsahate tiryagyonigarasyārthāya jīvitaṃ parityaktumiti? tau tata eva ṛddhyā vaihāyasamabhinirgatau/
311.025. brahmaprabho māṇavako 'drākṣīt/
311.026. dṛṣṭvā ca punastau brahmarṣī etadavocat--nanu brāhmaṇau, yuvābhyāmetaduktam--āvāmasyā bhaktaṃ dāsyāva iti/
311.027. etatkhalu brāhmaṇau yuvayorbrāhmaṇajātyoḥ satyam? tau āhatuh--ka utsahate tiryagyonigatasyārthāya jīvitaṃ parityaktum? brahmaprabho māṇavaka āha--ahamutsahetiryagyonigatasyārthāya jīvitaṃ parityaktum/
311.029. atha sa brahmaprabho māṇavako yena sā vyāghrī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
311.030. tasyā vyāghryāḥ purata ātmānamavasṛjati sma/
311.030. brahmaprabho māṇavo bhaitrīvihārī babhūva/
311.031. sā taṃ na śaktābhidrotu(gdhu)m/
311.031. atha brahmaprabhasya māṇavasyaitadabhavat--iyaṃ mama vyāghrī sāvijñānakaṃ kāyaṃ na bhakṣayati/
311.032. sa itaścetaśca vilokitavān/
311.032. tatastīkṣṇaṃ ca veṇupeśīṃ tīkṣṇāṃ gṛhītvā idamevaṃ rūpaṃ satyavacanamakarot--samanvāharantu me ye 'smin vanaṣaṇḍe 'dhyuṣitā <312>udārā devā nāgā yakṣā asurā garuḍāḥ kinnarā mahoragāḥ, te 'pi sarve samanvāharantu/
body.translated_text: Then the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s>, having built a hut in a certain place and established a walking path, practiced <s>tapas</s> (austerities) for the benefit of beings. Then, at another time, a pregnant tigress came to dwell not far from <s>Brahmaprabha</s>'s hut. The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> saw her. Having seen her, he approached the two <s>brahmarṣis</s> (brahmin sages). Having approached, he said this to the two <s>brahmarṣis</s>: 'May the sages please know this — here, not far from my hut, a pregnant tigress has come to dwell. Who is willing to give her food?' The two said: 'We shall give food to her.' Then, at another time, the tigress, having given birth, overcome by hunger and emaciation, wished to devour her own two cubs. She seized one cub and released the other, but did not eat it. The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> saw her. Having seen her, he again approached the two <s>brahmarṣis</s>. Having approached, he said this to the two <s>brahmarṣis</s>: 'May the two <s>brāhmaṇas</s> please know this — that tigress, having given birth, overcome by hunger and emaciation, wishes to devour her own two cubs. Seizing one cub, she releases the other but does not eat it. Who is willing to give her food?' The two said: 'We shall give food to her.' Then the two <s>brahmarṣis</s> approached where that tigress was. The tigress saw the two <s>brahmarṣis</s> coming from afar. Having seen them, overcome by hunger and emaciation, she wished to rush at them. This thought occurred to them: 'Who is willing to give up one's life for the sake of a creature born in an animal womb?' The two then rose up into the sky by means of supernatural power and departed. The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> saw this. Having seen it, he again said this to the two <s>brahmarṣis</s>: 'Did not you two <s>brāhmaṇas</s> say this — "We shall give food to her"? Is this indeed the truth of you two, born as <s>brāhmaṇas</s>?' The two said: 'Who is willing to give up one's life for the sake of a creature born in an animal womb?' The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> said: 'I am willing to give up my life for the sake of a creature born in an animal womb.' Then the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> approached where that tigress was. He cast himself down before that tigress. The young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> had been abiding in <s>maitrī-vihāra</s> (the meditation of loving-kindness). She was unable to rush upon him. Then this thought occurred to the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s>: 'This tigress of mine does not eat my body while it is still conscious.' He looked here and there. Then, taking up a sharp sliver of bamboo, he made this declaration of truth: 'Let those noble <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> who dwell in this forest grove — let them all bear witness.'

body.text:
312.002. ayamahaṃ tyāgaṃ kariṣyāmi, atityāgaṃ tyāgātityāgaṃ svayaṃ galaparityāgam/
312.002. api tu yenāhaṃ satyena satyavacanena parityajāmi, na rājyārthaṃ na bhogārthaṃ na śakrāthaṃ na rājacakravartiviṣayārtham, anyatra kathamahamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhidhimabhisambudhya adāntān damayeyam, atirṇāṃs tārayeyam, amuktān mocayeyam, anāśvastānāśvāsayeyam, aparinirvṛtān parinirvāpayeyam, tena satyena satyavacanena mā me parityāgo niṣphalo bhūditi kṛtvā svayameva galaṃ chittvā tasyā vyāghryā purata upanikṣipati/
312.008. vyāghrīnakhāvalivilāsavilupyamānā vakṣaḥsthalī kṣaṇamalakṣyata vīkṣayārā(?)/
312.010. romāñcacarcitatanostuhināṃśuśubhrasattvā prakāśakiraṇāṅkurapūriteva//1//
body.translated_text: 'I shall make this sacrifice, a sacrifice beyond sacrifice, a self-offering of my own throat. Moreover, by whichever truth, by whichever declaration of truth I make this sacrifice — it is not for the sake of kingship, not for the sake of enjoyment, not for the sake of becoming <s>Śakra</s>, not for the sake of the dominion of a <s>rājacakravartin</s> (universal monarch), but rather: "How may I, having fully awakened to the unsurpassed <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect enlightenment), tame the untamed, ferry across those who have not crossed over, liberate those who are not liberated, comfort those who are not comforted, and bring to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) those who have not attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?" — by that truth, by that declaration of truth, may my sacrifice not be fruitless!' Having resolved thus, he himself cut his own throat and cast himself down before that tigress. His chest, being torn apart by the play of the tigress's claws, appeared for a moment as if beheld with a steady gaze, with hair standing on end over his body, radiant as the cool-rayed moon, as though filled with sprouts of rays manifesting his <s>sattva</s> (courage). (1)

body.text:
312.012ṭasyāmiṣāharaṇaśoṇitapānamattāṃ vyāghrīṃ sahasramavalokayataścakāra/
dīrghapravāsasamayākulitā muhūrtaṃ kaṇṭhāvalambanadhṛtiṃ nijajīvavṛttiḥ//2//
body.translated_text: He gazed a thousand times upon the tigress, intoxicated by drinking the blood as she carried away the flesh; for a moment, his life-breath, agitated as if by the anxiety of a long journey, held on clinging to his throat. (2)

body.text: 312.016. sahaparityakte khalu bhikṣavo brahmaprabheṇa māṇavena svake gale, ayaṃ rtisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ kampati saṃkampati saṃprakampati, calati saṃcalati, vedhati saṃvedhati saṃpravedhati, pūrvā digunnamati paścimā avanamati, paścimā digunnamati pūrvā digunnamati, dakṣiṇā digunnamati uttarā digavanamati, uttarā digunnamati dakṣiṇā digavanamati, madhyamunnamati, anto 'vanamati, anta unnamati, madhyamavanamati, sūryacandramasau na tapato na bhāsato na virājataḥ//
body.translated_text: At the very moment, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), when the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> sacrificed his own throat, this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s> (great trichiliocosm) trembled, shook, and shook violently; it quaked, quaked greatly; it vibrated, vibrated greatly, and vibrated most violently. The eastern direction rose up and the western direction sank down; the western direction rose up and the eastern direction sank down; the southern direction rose up and the northern direction sank down; the northern direction rose up and the southern direction sank down; the middle rose up and the edges sank down; the edges rose up and the middle sank down. The sun and moon neither burned, nor shone, nor radiated.

body.text:
312.021. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyā sā tena samayenottarāpatheṣu janapadeṣūtpalāvatīnāṃ nagarīrājadhānī babhūva/
312.022. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.022. puṣkalāvataṃ tena kālena tena samayenotpalāvataṃ nāma nagaraṃ rājadhānī babhūva/
312.023. syādbhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayenotpalāvate nagare rājadhānyāṃ rūpāvatī strī babhūva/
312.024. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.024. ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena rūpāvatī nāma strī babhūva/
312.025. syādbhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyā sā tena kālena tena samayenāpavarake strī prasūtā/
312.026. na caivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.026. candraprabhamāṇavikā tena kālena tena samayenāpavarake strī prasūtā/
312.027. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyastena kālena tena samayena dārako babhūva/
312.028. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.028. rāhulaḥ kumāraḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena dārako 'bhūt/
312.029. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena candraprabho nāma dārako babhūva/
312.030. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.030. ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena candraprabho nāma dārako babhūva/
312.031. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena pañcamātrāṇi dārakaśatānyabhūvan/
312.032. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
312.033. imāni tāni pañca etadbhadrikaśatāni tena kālena tena samayena pañcamātrāṇi dārakaśatāni <313>abhūvan/
body.translated_text: You might think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that the royal capital city of <s>Utpalāvatī</s> in the northern provinces at that time was a different place. But it should not be viewed thus. <s>Puṣkalāvata</s> was at that time known as the city called <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, the royal capital. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'She who at that time in the city of <s>Utpalāvatī</s>, the royal capital, was the woman <s>Rūpāvatī</s> — was she someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. I myself at that time was the woman named <s>Rūpāvatī</s>. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'She who at that time gave birth in the inner chamber — was she a different woman?' It should not be viewed thus. The maiden <s>Candraprabha</s> was the woman who at that time gave birth in the inner chamber. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'He who at that time was the boy — was he someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. Prince <s>Rāhula</s> was the boy at that time. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'He who at that time was the boy named <s>Candraprabha</s> — was he someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. I myself at that time was the boy named <s>Candraprabha</s>. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Those who at that time were the five hundred boys — were they others?' It should not be viewed thus. These very five hundred of the <s>Bhadrika</s> group were at that time the five hundred boys.

body.text:
313.001. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena tasmin mahāśmaśāne uccaṃgamo nāma pakṣī babhūva/
313.002. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
313.002. kauṇḍinyo bhikṣustena kālena tena samayenoñcaṃgamo nāma pakṣī babhūva/
313.003. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmaprabho nāma māṇavo 'bhūt/
313.004. na haivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
313.005. ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmaprabho nāma māṇavo 'bhūt/
313.005. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyau tau tena kālena tena samayena brahmaprabhasya māṇavasya mātāpitarau abhūtām/
313.007. na haivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
313.007. rājā śuddhodano māyādevī tena kālena tena samayena brahmaprabhasya māṇavasya mātāpitarau abhūvatām/
313.008. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vanamabhūt/
313.009. .... syādbhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyau tau tena kālena tena samayena dvau brahmarṣī abhūtām/
313.010. na haivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
313.010. maitreyo bodhisattvaḥ suprabhaśca buddhastena kālena tena samayena tasmin vanaṣaṇḍe dvau brahmarṣī abhūtām/
313.011. syādyuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaḥ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vyāghrī babhūva/
313.012. na haivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
313.012. kauṇḍinyo bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena dvau vyāghrapotau babhūvatuḥ/
313.015. na haivaṃ draṣavyam/
313.015. nando bhikṣū rāhulaśca tena kālena tena samayena vyāghrapotakau abhūtām/
313.016. tadā me bhikṣavaścatvāriṃśatkalpasamprasthito maitreyo bodhisattva ekena galaparityāgena paścānmukhīkṛtaḥ/
313.017. tadanena bhikṣavaḥ paryāyeṇa veditavyam/
313.017. evaṃ sacet sarve sattvā jānīyuh--dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca vipākam yathā ahaṃ jānābhi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca vipākam, yo 'sau caramaḥ kavalaḥ paścima ālopaḥ, tamāpi nādattvā nāsaṃvibhajyāpareṣvātmanā nopabhuñjīran, nāpyutpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhet/
313.020. yasmāttarhi bhikṣavaḥ sattvā na jānanti dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca vipākam, tasmātsattvā yo 'sau caramaḥ kavalaḥ paścima ālopaḥ, tamapyadattvā asaṃvibhajya apareṣāmātmanā paribhuñjate, utpannaścaiṣāṃ mātsaryamalaścittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati//
body.translated_text: You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'He who at that time in that great charnel ground was the bird named <s>Uccaṃgama</s> — was he someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> was at that time the bird named <s>Uccaṃgama</s>. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'He who at that time was the young man named <s>Brahmaprabha</s> — was he someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. I myself at that time was the young man named <s>Brahmaprabha</s>. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Those who at that time were the mother and father of the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s> — were they others?' It should not be viewed thus. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and <s>Māyādevī</s> were at that time the mother and father of the young man <s>Brahmaprabha</s>. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'He who at that time was the forest — was he someone else?' ... You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Those who at that time were the two <s>brahmarṣis</s> — were they others?' It should not be viewed thus. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and the Buddha <s>Suprabha</s> were at that time the two <s>brahmarṣis</s> in that forest grove. You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'She who at that time was the tigress — was she someone else?' It should not be viewed thus. The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> was at that time the tigress. The two tiger cubs — were they others? It should not be viewed thus. <s>Nanda</s> the <s>bhikṣu</s> and <s>Rāhula</s> were at that time the two tiger cubs. At that time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>Maitreya</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>, who had set forth forty <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) earlier, was surpassed by me through a single sacrifice of my throat. By this example, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, it should be understood: Thus, if all beings were to know the fruit of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts, just as I know the fruit of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts, they would not consume even the last morsel, the final mouthful, without giving it away, without sharing it with others; nor would the stain of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) arise and take hold of their minds. But since, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts, therefore beings consume even the last morsel, the final mouthful, without giving it away, without sharing it with others, and the stain of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) arises and takes hold of their minds.

body.text:
313.023. punākṛtaṃ na paśyati no śubhāśubhaṃ na sevitam/
313.024. na paśyati paṇḍite jane na nāśametyāryagaṇe//3//
body.translated_text: One does not see what was done in the past, nor what was good or evil that was practiced; one does not see destruction among the wise, nor among the assembly of the noble ones. (3)

body.text:
313.025. śubhāśubhaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛtajñeṣu na jātu naśyati/
313.026. sukṛtaṃ śobhanaṃ karma duṣkṛtaṃ cāpyaśobhanam/
313.027. ubhayasya vipāko 'sti hyavaśyaṃ dāsyate phalam//4//
body.translated_text: Good and evil deeds done among the grateful are never destroyed. Meritorious deeds are beautiful, and evil deeds are unbeautiful; of both there is a ripening — inevitably the fruit will be given. (4)

body.text:
313.028. idamavocadbhagavān/
313.028. āttamanaso bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇya upāsakā upāsikā devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāḥ sarvāvatī ca pariṣadbhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Blessed One). Delighted in mind, the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (laymen), <s>upāsikās</s> (laywomen), <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and the entire assembly rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: 313.030. rūpāvatyavadānaṃ dvātriṃśattamam//
body.translated_text: The <s>Rūpāvatyavadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Rūpāvatī</s>), the thirty-second.

body.text: 314.001. div33 śārdūlakarṇāvadānam/
body.translated_text: <s>Avadāna</s> 33: The <s>Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna</s> (The Legend of <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>).

body.text:
314.002. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
314.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
314.003. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ mahānagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
314.004. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyo yenānyatamamudapānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
314.005. tena khalu samayena tasminnudapāne prakṛtir nāma mātaṅgadārikā udakamuddharate sma/
314.006. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ prakṛtiṃ mātaṅgadārikāmetadavocat--dehi me bhagini pānīyam, pāsyāmi/
314.007. evamukte prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā āyuṣmantamānandamidamavocat--mātaṅgadārikāhamasmi bhadanta ānanda/
314.008. nāhaṃ te bhagini kulaṃ vā jātiṃ vā pṛcchāmi/
314.008. api tu sacette parityaktaṃ pānīyam, dehi, pāsyāmi/
314.009. atha prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā āyuṣmata ānandāaya pānīyamadāt/
314.010. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text:
314.002. Thus have I heard.
314.002. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
314.003. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.
314.004. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having wandered through <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms and having finished his meal, approached a certain well.
314.005. At that time, at that well, a <s>Mātaṅga</s> (outcaste) girl named <s>Prakṛti</s> was drawing water.
314.006. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl: 'Give me water, sister; I wish to drink.'
314.007. When this was said, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl said to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I am a <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.'
314.008. 'I do not ask you, sister, about your clan or your birth.
314.008. Rather, if you can spare the water, give it; I will drink.'
314.009. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl gave water to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
314.010. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having drunk the water, departed.

body.text:
314.011. atha prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā athāyuṣmata ānandasya śarīre mukhe svare ca sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca nimittamudgṛhītvā yoniśomanasikāreṇāviṣṭā saṃrāgacittamutpādayati sma--āryo me ānandaḥ svāmī syāditi/
314.013. mātā ca me mahāvidyādharī/
314.013. sā śakṣyatyāryamānandamānayitum/
314.013. atha prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā pānīyaghaṭamādāya yena caṇḍālagṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya pānīyaghaṭamekānte nikṣipya svāṃ jananīmidamavocat--yatkhalu evamamba jānīyāh--ānando nāma śramaṇo mahāśramaṇagautamasya śrāvaka upasthāyakaḥ/
314.016. tamahaṃ svāminamicchāmi/
314.016. śakṣyasi tamamba ānayitum? sā tāmavocat--śaktāhaṃ putri ānandamānayituṃ sthāpayitvā yo mṛtaḥ syādyo vā vītarāgaḥ/
314.018. api ca/
314.018. rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ śramaṇagautamamatīva sevate bhajate paryupāsane/
314.018. yadi jānīyāt, so 'yaṃ caṇḍālakulasyānarthāya pratipadyeta/
314.019. śramaṇaśca gautamo vītarāgaḥ śrūyate/
314.020. vītarāgasya {mantrāh} punaḥ sarvamantrānabhibhavanti/
314.020. evamuktā prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā mātaramidamavocat--sacedadamba śramaṇo gautamo vītarāgaḥ, tasyāntikācchramaṇamānandaṃ na pratilapsye, jīvitaṃ parityajeyam/
314.022. sacetpratilapsye, jīvāmi/
314.022. mā te putri jīvitaṃ parityajasi/
314.022. ānayāmi śramaṇamānandam//
body.translated_text:
314.011. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, having closely observed the body, face, and voice of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, well and truly grasping the signs, possessed by improper mental attention, generated a mind of passion: 'May the Noble <s>Ānanda</s> be my husband!'
314.013. 'My mother is a great sorceress.
314.013. She will be able to bring the Noble <s>Ānanda</s>.'
314.013. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, taking her water-pot, approached the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) house, set the water-pot down in a corner, and said this to her mother: 'Know this, Mother — there is a monk named <s>Ānanda</s>, a disciple and attendant of the great <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.
314.016. I desire him as my husband.
314.016. Can you, Mother, bring him?' She said to her: 'I am able to bring <s>Ānanda</s>, daughter — except one who is dead or one who is free from passion.
314.018. However,
314.018. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> greatly serves, honors, and attends upon the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.
314.018. If he were to learn of it, he would bring ruin upon the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> clan.
314.019. And the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> is said to be free from passion.
314.020. The <s>mantras</s> of one free from passion overpower all <s>mantras</s>.'
314.020. When this was said, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl said to her mother: 'If, Mother, the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> is free from passion and I cannot obtain the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Ānanda</s> from him, I shall give up my life.
314.022. But if I obtain him, I shall live.'
314.022. 'Do not give up your life, daughter.
314.022. I shall bring the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Ānanda</s>.'

body.text:
314.024. atha prakṛtermātaṅgadārikā mātā madhye gṛhāṅganasya gomayenopalepanaṃ kṛtvā vedīmālipya darbhān saṃstīrya agniṃ pajvālya aṣṭaśatamarkapuṣpāṇāṃ gṛhītvā mantrānāvartayamānā ekaikamarkapuṣpaṃ parijapya agnau pratikṣipati sma/
314.026. tatreyaṃ vidyā bhavati--
314.027. amale vimale kuṅkume sumane/
314.027. yena baddhāsi vidyut/
314.027. icchayā devo varṣati vidyotati garjati/
314.028. vismayaṃ mahārājasya samabhivardhayituṃ devebhyo manuṣyebhyo gandharvebhyaḥ śikhigrahā devā viśikhigrahā devā ānandasyāgamanāya saṃgamanāya kramaṇāya grāṇāya juhomi svāhā//
body.translated_text:
314.024. Then the mother of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, in the middle of the courtyard, smeared the ground with cow dung, built up an altar, spread <s>darbha</s> grass, kindled a fire, and taking eight hundred <s>arka</s> (milkweed) flowers, while reciting <s>mantras</s>, she consecrated each <s>arka</s> flower and cast it into the fire.
314.026. And this was the spell:
314.027. 'O Stainless, O Immaculate, O Saffron, O Fair-Minded!
314.027. By that which binds lightning,
314.027. by whose will the god rains, flashes, and thunders —
314.028. to increase the wonder of the great king, from the gods, from humans, from the <s>Gandharvas</s>, O Tuft-seizing gods, O Loose-tufted gods, for the coming, the meeting, the approaching, the grasping of <s>Ānanda</s> — I offer oblation! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text:
315.001. <315>athāyuṣmata ānandasya cittamakṣiptam/
315.001. sa vihārānniṣkramya yena caṇḍālagṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmati sma/
315.002. adrākṣīccaṇḍālī āyuṣmantamānandaṃ dūrādevāgacchantam/
315.002. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prakṛtiṃ duhitaramidamavocat--ayamasau putri śramaṇa ānanda āgacchati/
315.003. śayanaṃ prajñapaya/
315.004. atha prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā hṛṣṭatuṣṭā pramuditamanā āyuṣmata ānandasya śayyāṃ prajñapayati sma//
body.translated_text:
315.001. Then the mind of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was seized.
315.001. He left the monastery and began to go toward the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house.
315.002. The <s>Caṇḍālī</s> (outcaste woman) saw the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> coming from afar.
315.002. Having seen him, she said to her daughter <s>Prakṛti</s>: 'There, daughter, the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Ānanda</s> is coming.
315.003. Prepare the bed.'
315.004. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, joyful, pleased, and delighted in mind, prepared a bed for the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.

body.text:
315.005. athāyuṣmānāndo yena caṇḍālagṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
315.005. upasaṃkramya vedīmupaniśrityāsthāt/
315.005. ekāntasthitaḥ sa punarāyuṣmānāndaḥ prārodīt/
315.006. aśrūṇi pravartayamāna evamāha--vyasanaprāpto 'hamasmi/
315.007. na ca me bhagavān samanvāharati/
315.007. atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandaṃ samanvāharati sma/
315.008. samanvāhṛtya saṃbuddhamantraiścaṇḍālamantrān pratihanti sma/
315.008. tatreyaṃ vidyā--
315.009. sthitiracyutiḥ sunītiḥ/ svasti sarvaprāṇibhyaḥ//
body.translated_text:
315.005. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house.
315.005. Having approached, he stood leaning against the altar.
315.005. Standing alone, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> began to weep.
315.006. Shedding tears, he said: 'I have fallen into calamity!
315.007. And the Blessed One does not attend to me.'
315.007. But the Blessed One was attending to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
315.008. Having attended to him, he countered the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> spells with the spells of a Perfectly Awakened One.
315.008. And this was the spell:
315.009. '<s>Sthiti</s>, <s>Acyuti</s>, <s>Sunīti</s>! May all beings be well!'

body.text:
315.010. saraḥ prasannaṃ nirdeṣaṃ praśāntaṃ sarvato 'bhayam/
315.011. ītayo yatra śāmyanti bhayāni calitāni ca//1//
body.translated_text:
315.010. 'The lake is clear, faultless, tranquil, free from all fear;
315.011. where calamities are pacified and terrors are stilled.' //1//

body.text:
315.012. tadvai devā namasyanti sarvasiddhāśca yoginaḥ/
315.013. etena satyavākyena svastyānandāsya bhikṣave//2//
body.translated_text:
315.012. 'To that very one, the gods pay homage, and all accomplished <s>yogins</s>.
315.013. By this word of truth, may there be well-being for this monk <s>Ānanda</s>!' //2//

body.text: 315.014. athāyuṣmānāndaḥ pratihatacaṇḍālamantraścaṇḍālagṛhānniṣkramya yena svako vihārastenopasaṃkramitumārabdhaḥ//
body.translated_text: 315.014. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, his <s>Caṇḍāla</s> spell broken, left the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> house and began to go back to his own monastery.

body.text:
315.016. adrākṣītprakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā ānandamāyuṣmantaṃ pratigacchantam/
315.016. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ svāṃ jananīmidamavocat--ayamasau mātaḥ śramaṇa ānandaḥ pratigacchati/
315.017. tāmāha mātā--niyataṃ putri śramaṇena gautamena samanvāhṛto bhaviṣyati/
315.018. tena mama mantrāḥ pratihatā bhaviṣyanti/
315.018. prakṛtirāha--kiṃ punaramba balavattarāḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrā nāsmākam? tāmāha mātā--balavattarāḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrā nāsmākam/
315.020. ye putri mantrāḥ sarvalokasya prabhavanti, tān mantrāñ śramaṇo gautama ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ pratihanti/
315.021. na punarlokaḥ prabhavati śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrān pratihantum/
315.022. evaṃ balavattarāḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya mantrāḥ//
body.translated_text:
315.016. <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl saw the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> going back.
315.016. Having seen him, she said to her mother: 'Mother, the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Ānanda</s> is going back!'
315.017. Her mother said: 'Surely, daughter, he has been attended to by the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.
315.018. Therefore my spells must have been broken.'
315.018. <s>Prakṛti</s> said: 'But Mother, are the spells of the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> more powerful than ours?' Her mother said: 'The spells of the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> are more powerful; ours are not.
315.020. The spells, daughter, that prevail over the entire world — those spells the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>, if he wishes, can break.
315.021. But the world is not able to break the spells of the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.
315.022. Thus the spells of the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> are more powerful.'

body.text:
315.023. athāyuṣmānānando yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
315.023. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt/
315.024. ekāntasthitamāyuṣmantamānandaṃ bhagavānidamavocat--udgṛhṇa rvamānanda imāṃ ṣaḍakṣarīvidyām/
315.025. dhāraya vācaya paryavāpnuhi ātmano hitāya sukhāya bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāmupāsakānāmupāsikānāṃ hitāya sukhāya/
315.026. iyamānanda ṣaḍakṣarīvidyā ṣaḍbhiḥ samyaksambuddhairbhāṣitā, caturbhiśca mahārājaiḥ, śakreṇa devānāmindreṇa, brahmaṇā ca sahāpatinā/
315.027. mayā caitarhi śākyamuninā samyaksambuddhena bhāṣitā/
315.028. tvamapyetarhi ānanda tāṃ dhārasya vācaya paryavāpnuhi/
315.029. yaduta tadyathā--
315.030. aṇḍare pāṇḍare kāraṇḍe keyūre 'rcihaste kharagrīve bandhumati vīramati dhara vidha cilimile vilo:aya viṣāṇi loke/
315.031. viṣa cala cala/
315.031. golamati gaṇḍavile cilimile sātiniṃne yathāsaṃvibhakte golamati gaṇḍavilāyai svāhā//
body.translated_text:
315.023. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached the Blessed One.
315.023. Having approached, he bowed at the feet of the Blessed One with his head and stood to one side.
315.024. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> standing to one side: 'Learn, <s>Ānanda</s>, this Six-Syllable Spell.
315.025. Retain it, recite it, master it — for your own benefit and happiness, and for the benefit and happiness of monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers.
315.026. This Six-Syllable Spell, <s>Ānanda</s>, was spoken by six Perfectly Awakened Ones, by the four Great Kings, by <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, and by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>.
315.027. And it is now spoken by me, <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.
315.028. You too, <s>Ānanda</s>, should retain it, recite it, and master it.
315.029. Namely, thus:
315.030. <s>Aṇḍare Pāṇḍare Kāraṇḍe Keyūre Arcihaste Kharagrīve Bandhumati Vīramati Dhara Vidha Cilimile Vilokaya Viṣāṇi Loke</s>.
315.031. <s>Viṣa Cala Cala</s>.
315.031. <s>Golamati Gaṇḍavile Cilimile Sātiniṃne Yathāsaṃvibhakte Golamati Gaṇḍavilāyai Svāhā</s>.

body.text:
316.001. <316>yaḥ kaścidānanda ṣaḍakṣaryā vidyayā paritrāṇaṃ svastyayanaṃ kuryāt, sa yadi vadhārho bhavet, daṇḍena mucyate, daṇḍārhaḥ prahāreṇa, prahārārhaḥ, paribhāṣaṇayā, paribhāṣaṇārho romaharṣaṇena, romaharṣaṇārhaḥ punareva mucyate/
316.003. nāhamānanda taṃ samanupaśyāmi sadevaloke samāraloke sabrahmaloke saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ sadevamānuṣikāyāṃ sāsurāyām yastvanayā ṣaḍkṣaryā vidyayā rakṣāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ rakṣāsūtre bāhau baddhe svastyayane kṛte abhibhavituṃ śaknoti varjayitvā paurāṇaṃ karmavipākam//
body.translated_text:
316.001. 'Whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, should perform protection and blessing by means of the Six-Syllable Spell — if he were deserving of death, he would be freed with a beating; if deserving of a beating, with a reprimand; if deserving of a reprimand, with a rebuke; if deserving of a rebuke, with a hair-raising fright; if deserving of a hair-raising fright, he would simply be freed.
316.003. I do not see, <s>Ānanda</s>, in this world with its gods, its <s>Māras</s>, its <s>Brahmās</s>, in this generation with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods and humans, including <s>Asuras</s>, anyone who could overpower one for whom this Six-Syllable Spell has been used as protection, bound as a protective thread on the arm, and performed as a blessing — except through the ripening of former <s>karma</s>.'

body.text:
316.007. atha prakṛtirmāraṅgadārikā tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt śiraḥsnātā anāhatadūṣyaprāvṛtā muktāmālyābharaṇā yena śrāvastī nagarī tenopasaṃkramya nagaradvāre kapāṭamūle niśrityāsthādāyuṣmantamānandamāgamayamānā--niyatamanena mārgeṇa ānando ānando bhikṣurāgamiṣyatīti/
316.009. dadarśāyuṣmānānandaḥ prakṛtiṃ mātaṅgadārikāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhām/
316.010. dṛṣṭvā ca punarjehrīyamāṇarūpo 'pragalbhāyamānarūpo duḥkhī durmanāḥ śīghraṃ śīghraṃ śrāvastyā vinirgamya yena jetavanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
316.012. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt/
316.012. ekāntasthita āyucmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--iyaṃ me bhagavan prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā gacchantamanu gacchati, tiṣṭhantamanu tiṣṭhati/
316.014. yadyadeva kulaṃ pinṇḍāya praviśāmi, tasya tasyaiva dvāre tūṣṇībhūtā tiṣṭhati/
316.015. trāhi me bhagavan, trāhi me sugata/
316.015. evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamidamavocat--kiṃ te prakṛte mātaṅgadārike ānandena bhikṣuṇā? prakṛtirāha--svāminaṃ bhadanta ānandamicchāmi/
316.017. bhagavānāha--anujñātāsi prakṛte mātāpitṛbhyāmānandāya? anujñātāsmi bhagavan, anujñātāsmi sugata/
316.018. bhagavānāha--tena hi saṃmukhaṃ mamānujñāpaya tvam/
316.019. atha prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntā/
316.020. yena svakau mātāpitarau tenopasaṃkrāntā/
316.021. upasaṃkramya mātāpitroḥ pādāñ śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt/
316.021. ekāntasthitā svakau mātāpitarāvidamavocat--saṃmukhaṃ me amba tāta śramaṇasya gautamasya ānandāya utsṛjatam/
316.023. atha prakṛtermātaṅgadārikāyā mātāpitarau prakṛtimādāyā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntau/
316.024. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt/
316.025. ekāntasthitā bhagavantametadavocat--imau tau bhagavan mātāpitarāvāgatau/
316.026. atha bhagavān prakṛtermātaṅgadārikāyā mātāpitarāvidamavocat--anujñātā yuvābhyāṃ prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā ānandāyeti? tāvāhatuh--anujñātā bhagavan, anujñātā sugata/
316.028. tena hi yūyaṃ prakṛtimapahāya gacchata svagṛham/
316.028. atha prakṛtermātaṅgadārikāyā mātāpitarau bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavato 'ntikātprakrāntau//
body.translated_text:
316.007. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, at the passing of that very night, having bathed her head, wrapped in unworn cloth, wearing pearls, garlands, and ornaments, approached the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> and stood at the base of the city gate, waiting for the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Surely by this road the monk <s>Ānanda</s> will come.'
316.009. The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> saw <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl following close behind him.
316.010. Seeing her, feeling ashamed, lacking boldness, unhappy and dejected, he quickly departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and went to the <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's Grove).
316.012. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
316.012. Standing to one side, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'This <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, Blessed One, follows close behind me — when I walk, she walks after me; when I stand, she stands after me.
316.014. Whichever household I enter for alms, at the door of that very household she stands silently.
316.015. Save me, Blessed One! Save me, <s>Sugata</s>!'
316.015. Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'What do you want with the monk <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl?' <s>Prakṛti</s> said: 'I desire <s>Ānanda</s> as my husband, Venerable Sir.'
316.017. The Blessed One said: 'Have you been given permission by your parents to be with <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>?' 'I have been given permission, Blessed One; I have been given permission, <s>Sugata</s>.'
316.018. The Blessed One said: 'Then obtain permission from them directly in my presence.'
316.019. Then <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, having assented to the Blessed One, bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and departed from the Blessed One's presence.
316.020. She went to her own parents.
316.021. Having approached and bowed her head at the feet of her parents, she stood to one side.
316.021. Standing to one side, she said to her parents: 'Mother, father — release me to <s>Ānanda</s> directly in the presence of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.'
316.023. Then the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, taking <s>Prakṛti</s>, approached the Blessed One.
316.024. Having approached and bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they stood to one side.
316.025. Standing to one side, she said to the Blessed One: 'These, Blessed One, are the parents who have come.'
316.026. Then the Blessed One said to the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl: 'Have you given permission for <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl to be with <s>Ānanda</s>?' They said: 'Permission has been given, Blessed One; permission has been given, <s>Sugata</s>.'
316.028. 'Then you may leave <s>Prakṛti</s> here and go to your own home.'
316.028. Then the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, bowing their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulating the Blessed One three times, departed from the Blessed One's presence.

body.text: 316.031. atha prakṛtermātaṅgadārikāyā mātāpitarāvaciraprakrāntau viditvā bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅgadārikāmidamavocat--arthikāsi prakṛte ānandena bhikṣūṇā? prakṛtirāha--arthikāsmi bhagavan, <317>arthikāsmi sugata/
body.translated_text: 316.031. Then the Blessed One, knowing that the parents of <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl had departed not long ago, said this to <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl: 'Do you desire the monk <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>?' <s>Prakṛti</s> said: 'I desire him, Blessed One; I desire him, <s>Sugata</s>.'

body.text:
317.001. tena hi prakṛte ya ānandasya veṣaḥ, sa tvayā dhārayitavyaḥ/
317.001. sā āha--dhārayāmi bhagavan, dhārayāmi sugata/
317.002. pravrajayatu māṃ sugata, pravrajayatu māṃ bhagavān/
317.002. atha bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅgadārikāmidamavocat--ehi tvaṃ bhikṣuṇī, cara brahmacaryam/
317.003. evamukte prakṛtirmātaṅgadārikā bhagavatā muṇḍā kāṣāyapravṛtā/
317.004. atha bhagavān prakṛtiṃ mātaṅgadārikāmehibhikṣuṇīvādena pravrājayitvā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati sma, samādāpayati sma, smuttejayati sma, saṃpraharṣayati sma/
317.006. yeyaṃ kathā dīrgharātraṃ saṃsārasamāpannānāṃ pratikūlā śravaṇīyā, tadyathā--dānakathā śīlakathā svargakathā kāmeṣvādīnavaṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ bhayaṃ saṃkleśavyavadānam, bodhipakṣāṃstān dharmān bhagavān prakṛtyai bhikṣuṇyai saṃprakāśayati sma/
317.008. atha prakṛtirbhikṣuṇī bhagavatā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśitā samādāpitā samuttejitā saṃpraharṣitā hṛṣṭacittā kalyāṇacittāa muditacittā vinīvaraṇacittā ṛjucittākhilacittā bhavyā dharmadeśitamājñātum/
317.010. yadā ca bhagavāñ jñātaḥ prakṛtiṃ bhikṣuṇīṃ hṛṣṭacittāṃ kalyāṇacittāṃ muditacittāṃ vinīvaraṇacittāṃ bhavyāṃ pratibalāṃ sāmutkarṣikīṃ dharmadeśanāmājñātum, tadā yeyaṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhānāṃ caturāyasatyaprativedhikī dhrmadeśanā, yaduta duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārgaḥ, tāṃ bhagavān prakṛterbhikṣuṇyā vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma/
317.014. atha prakṛtirbhikṣuṇī tasminnevāsane niṣaṇṇā caturāyasatyānyabhijñātāsīt, duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgam/
317.015. tadyathā vastramapagatakālakaṃ rajanopagataṃ raṅgodake prakṣiptaṃ samyageva raṅgaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt, evameva prakṛtirbhikṣuṇī tasminnevāsane niṣaṇṇā caturāyasatyāni abhisamayati sma, tadyathā--duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgam//
body.translated_text:
317.001. 'Then, <s>Prakṛti</s>, you must adopt the same mode of life as <s>Ānanda</s>.'
317.001. She said: 'I will adopt it, Blessed One; I will adopt it, <s>Sugata</s>.
317.002. Let the <s>Sugata</s> ordain me; let the Blessed One ordain me.'
317.002. Then the Blessed One said to <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl: 'Come, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), practice the holy life.'
317.003. Thus addressed, <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl, by the Blessed One's word, became shaven-headed and clad in saffron robes.
317.004. Then the Blessed One, having ordained <s>Prakṛti</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> girl with the 'Come, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' formula, instructed, inspired, roused, and delighted her with a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.
317.006. That teaching which is disagreeable to hear for those long caught in <s>saṃsāra</s> — namely, a discourse on giving, a discourse on moral conduct, a discourse on heaven, the danger, degradation, and defilement in sensual pleasures, and purification — the Blessed One illuminated the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s> <s>dharmas</s>) for the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>.
317.008. Then the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, instructed, inspired, roused, and delighted by the Blessed One with a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, with a joyful mind, a wholesome mind, a delighted mind, a mind free from hindrances, a straightforward and honest mind, became capable of understanding the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.
317.010. And when the Blessed One knew that the nun <s>Prakṛti</s> was of joyful mind, wholesome mind, delighted mind, mind free from hindrances, capable and strong enough to understand the supreme teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, then that teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> which penetrates the Four Noble Truths, which is characteristic of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> — namely, suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path — that the Blessed One illuminated in full detail for the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>.
317.014. Then the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, seated in that very seat, directly realized the Four Noble Truths — suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.
317.015. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, when dipped in dye-water, would take the dye perfectly, even so the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, seated in that very seat, directly realized the Four Noble Truths — suffering, origin, cessation, and the path.

body.text:
317.018. atha praṛtirbhikṣuṇī dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadharmā viditadharmā akopyadharmā paryavasitadharmā adhigatārthalābhasaṃvṛttā tīrṇakāṅkṣāvicikitsā vigatakathaṃkathā vaiśāradyaprāptā aparapratyayā ananyaneyā śāstuḥ śāsane anudharmacāriṇī ājāneyamānā dharmeṣu bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirasā nipatya bhagavantamidamavocat--atyayo me bhagvan, atyayo me sugata/
317.021. yathā bālā yathā mūḍhā yathā avyaktā yathā akuśalā duṣṭrajñajātīyā, yāhamānandaṃ bhikṣuṃ svāmivādena samudācārṣam/
317.023. sāhaṃ bhadanta atyayamatyayataḥ paśyāmi/
317.023. atyayamatyayato dṛṣṭvā deśayāmi/
317.023. atyayamatyayata āviṣkaromi/
317.024. āyatyāṃ saṃvaramāpadye/
317.024. atastasyā mama bhagavann atyayamatyayato jānātu pratigṛhṇātu anukampāmupādāya/
317.025. bhagavānāha--āyatyāṃ saṃvarāya sthitvā tvaṃ prakṛte atyayamatyayato 'dhyāgamaḥ/
317.026. yathā bālā yathā mūḍhā yathā avyaktā yathā akuśalā duṣprajñajātīyā tvamānandaṃ bhikṣuṃ svāmivādena samudācarasīti/
317.027. yataśca tvaṃ prakṛte atyayaṃ jānāsi, atyayaṃ paśyasi, āyatyāṃ ca saṃvaramāpadyase, ahamapi te 'tyayamatyayato gṛhṇāmi/
317.028. vṛddhireva te prakṛte pratikāṅkṣitavyā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām, na hāniḥ/
317.029. atha prakṛtirbhikṣuṇī bhagavatābhinanditānuśiṣṭā ekā vyapakṛṣṭā apramattā ātāpinī smṛtimatī saṃprajānā prahitāni viviktāni viharati sma/
317.031. yadarthaṃ kuladuhitaraḥ keśānavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanāgārikāṃ pravrajanti, tadanuttarabrahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayamabhijñāya sākṣākṛtyopasampadya<318> pravedayate sma--kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryam, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyam, nāparamasmādbhavaṃ prajānāmīti//
body.translated_text:
317.018. Then the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, attained the <s>Dharma</s>, understood the <s>Dharma</s>, become unshakeable in the <s>Dharma</s>, fully penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, having obtained the attainment of the goal, having crossed beyond doubt and uncertainty, having gone beyond perplexity, having attained fearlessness, not dependent on others, not led by others, practicing in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> in the Teacher's teaching, of noble understanding in regard to the teachings — fell at the feet of the Blessed One with her head and said this to the Blessed One: 'Transgression has been committed by me, Blessed One; transgression has been committed by me, <s>Sugata</s>.
317.021. Foolish as I was, deluded, ignorant, unskillful, of poor wisdom, I addressed the monk <s>Ānanda</s> with the word "husband."
317.023. I, Venerable Sir, see the transgression as a transgression.
317.023. Seeing the transgression as a transgression, I confess it.
317.023. Seeing the transgression as a transgression, I make it manifest.
317.024. For the future, I undertake restraint.
317.024. Therefore, Blessed One, know my transgression as a transgression; accept it out of compassion.'
317.025. The Blessed One said: 'Standing firm in restraint for the future, you, <s>Prakṛti</s>, have acknowledged the transgression as a transgression.
317.026. Foolish as you were, deluded, ignorant, unskillful, of poor wisdom, you addressed the monk <s>Ānanda</s> with the word "husband."
317.027. Since you, <s>Prakṛti</s>, know the transgression, see the transgression, and undertake restraint for the future, I too accept your transgression as a transgression.
317.028. Only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected of you, <s>Prakṛti</s>, not decline.'
317.029. Then the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, approved and instructed by the Blessed One, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, mindful, and clearly comprehending, with exertion, in seclusion,
317.031. for that purpose for which well-born daughters, having shaved their hair and donned saffron robes, go forth in perfect faith from the household life to the homeless life — that supreme culmination of the holy life, in this very life, by her own direct knowledge, she realized, attained, and declared: 'Destroyed is birth; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been done; I know of no further existence beyond this.'

body.text:
318.002. aśrauṣuḥ śrāvasteyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayah--bhagavatā kila caṇḍāladārikā pravrājiteti/
318.004. śrutvā ca punaravadhyāyanti--kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāladārikā bhikṣūṇāṃ samyakcaryāṃ cariṣyati? bhikṣuṇīnāmupāsakānāmupāsikānāṃ samyakcaryāṃ cariṣyati? kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāladārikā brahmakṣatriyagṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu pravekṣyati?
318.007. aśrauṣīdrājā prasenajitkauśalah--bhagavatā caṇḍāladārikā pravrajiteti/
318.008. śrutvā ca punaravadhyāyati--kathaṃ hi nāma caṇḍāladārikā bhikṣūṇāṃ samyakcaryāṃ cariṣyati? bhikṣuṇīnāmupāsakānāmupādikānāṃ samyakcaryāṃ cariṣyati? kathaṃ brāhmaṇakṣatriyagṛhapatimahāśālakuleṣu pravekṣyati? vimṛśya ca bhadraṃ yānaṃ yojayitvā bhadraṃ yānamabhiruhya saṃbahulaiśca śrāvasteyairbrāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ śrāvastyā niryāti sma/
318.011. yena jetavanamanāthapiṇḍadasyārāmaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
318.012. tasya khalu yāvatī yānasya bhūmiḥ, tāvadyānena gatvāṃ sa yānādavatīrya pattikāyaparivṛtaḥ pattikāyapuraskṛtaḥ padbhyāmevārāmaṃ pravikṣat/
318.013. praviśya yena bhagavāṃstenopasṃkrāntaḥ/
318.014. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
318.014. te 'pi saṃbahulāḥ śrāvasteyakā brāhmaṇakṣatriyagṛhapatayo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
318.016. apyaikatyā bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃrañjanīṃ saṃmodinīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
318.017. apyaikatyā bhagavataḥ purataḥ svakasvakāni mātāpaitṛkāṇi nāmagotrāṇi nāmagotrāṇi anuśrāvya ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
318.018. apyaikatyā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ/
318.019. apyaikatyāstūṣṇīmbhūtā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ//
body.translated_text:
318.002. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s> heard: 'It is said that the Blessed One has ordained a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) girl.'
318.004. Having heard, they spoke disparagingly: 'How can a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> girl practice the proper conduct of monks? Of nuns? Of male and female lay followers? How can a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> girl enter the houses of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, householders, and great merchant families?'
318.007. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> heard: 'The Blessed One has ordained a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> girl.'
318.008. Having heard, he too spoke disparagingly: 'How can a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> girl practice the proper conduct of monks? Of nuns? Of male and female lay followers? How can she enter the houses of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, householders, and great merchant families?' Having deliberated, he had an excellent carriage yoked, mounted the excellent carriage, and accompanied by many <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, surrounded and attended by them, he departed from <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
318.011. He went to the <s>Jetavana</s>, <s>Anāthapiṇḍada's</s> park.
318.012. Having gone as far as the ground permitted for the carriage, he dismounted from the carriage and, surrounded and attended by his foot-escort, entered the park on foot.
318.013. Having entered, he approached the Blessed One.
318.014. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
318.014. Those many <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s> also bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
318.016. Some, having exchanged various pleasant and agreeable words face to face with the Blessed One, sat down to one side.
318.017. Some, having announced their own parental names and clans before the Blessed One, sat down to one side.
318.018. Some, having extended their joined palms toward the Blessed One, sat down to one side.
318.019. Some sat down to one side in silence.

body.text:
318.020. atha bhagavān rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalamārabhya teṣāṃ ca saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvasteyakānāṃ brāhmaṇakṣatriyagṛhapatīnāṃ cetasā cittamājñāya prakṛterbhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrvanivāsamārabhya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavastathāgatasya saṃmukhaṃ prakṛterbhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrvanivāsamārabhya dharmakathāṃ śrotum? bhikṣavo bhagavantamāhuh--etasya bhagavan kālaḥ, etasya sugata samayaḥ, yadbhagavān prakṛterbhikṣuṇyāḥ pūrvanivāsamārabhya dharmakathāṃ kathayet, yadbhagavataḥ śrutvā bhikṣavo dhārayiṣyanti/
318.025. bhagavānāha--tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta, bhāṣiṣye/
318.025. evaṃ sādhu bhagavanniti te bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ/
318.026. bhagavāṃstānidamavocat--
318.027. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani gaṅgātaṭe atimuktakadalīpāṭalakāmalakīvanagahanapradeśe tatra triśaṅkur nāma mātaṅgarājāḥ prativasati sma saṃbahulaiśca mātaṅgasahasraiḥ sārdham/
318.028. sa punaribhikṣavastriśaṅkurmātaṅgarājaḥ pūrvajanmādhītān vedān smanusmarati sma sāṅgopāṅgān sarahasyān sanighaṇṭakaiṭabhān sākṣaraprabhedānitihāsapañcamān, anyāni ca śāstrāṇi padako{śo?} vaiyākaraṇo lokāyate yajñamantre mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇe niṣṇāto niṣkāṅkṣaḥ/
318.031. bhāṣyaṃ ca yathādharmaṃ vedavratapadānyanuśrutaṃ ca bhāṣate sma/
318.032. tasya triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya śārdūlakarṇo nāma kumāro 'bhūdutpannaḥ/
<319>rūpataśca kulataśca śīlataśca guṇataśca sarvaguṇaiścopeto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known with his mind the thoughts in the minds of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> and of those many <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and householders of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, beginning with the former abode of the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>, addressed the monks: 'Do you wish, monks, to hear from the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face the Dharma-discourse beginning with the former abode of the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>?' The monks said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This is the time for it, <s>Bhagavān</s>; this is the occasion, <s>Sugata</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> deliver the Dharma-discourse beginning with the former abode of the nun <s>Prakṛti</s>. Having heard it from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the monks will retain it.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Then listen, monks, well and carefully, and pay attention; I shall speak.' 'Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>' — those monks listened attentively to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to them: 'Once upon a time, monks, in the past, on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in a region dense with <s>atimuktaka</s>, plantain, <s>pāṭala</s>, and <s>āmalakī</s> trees, there dwelt an elephant-king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>, together with many thousands of elephants. Now, monks, this elephant-king <s>Triśaṅku</s> remembered the <s>Vedas</s> studied in a former life — with their supplements and appendices, with their secrets, with their <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> glossaries, with their phonetic analysis, and with the <s>Itihāsas</s> as fifth; and other <s>śāstras</s> too — lexicography, grammar, <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialism), sacrificial <s>mantras</s>, and the marks of a great being — in all these he was accomplished and free from doubt. And he recited commentaries, Vedic observance-verses as prescribed, and what had been learned through tradition.
