To this elephant-king <s>Triśaṅku</s>, a prince named <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> was born — endowed in beauty, family, character, and virtues, possessed of all qualities, handsome, pleasing to look at, charming, and blessed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness.

body.text: 319.002. atha triśaṅkurmātaṅgarājaḥ śārdūlakarṇaṃ kumāraṃ pūrvajanmādhītān vedānadhyāpayati sma yaduta sāṅgopāṅgān sarahasyān sanighaṇṭakaiṭabhān sākṣaraprabhedānitihāsapañcamānm, anyāni ca śāstrāṇi, bhāṣyaṃ ca yathādharmaṃ vedavratapadāni//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, taught Prince <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> the <s>Vedas</s> studied in a former life — namely, with their supplements and appendices, with their secrets, with their <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> glossaries, with their phonetic analysis, and with the <s>Itihāsas</s> as fifth; and other <s>śāstras</s> too, as well as commentaries, Vedic observance-verses as prescribed.

body.text:
319.005. atha triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasyaitadabhavat--ayaṃ mama putraḥ śārdūlakarṇo nāma kumārah upeto rūpataśca kulataśca śīlataśca guṇataśca, sarvaguṇopetp^bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ, paramayā ca varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ/
319.007. cīrṇavrato 'dhītamantro vedapāragaḥ/
319.007. samayo 'yam yannvahamasya niveśanadharmaṃ kariṣye/
319.008. tatkuto nvahaṃ śārdūlakarṇasya putrasya śīlavatīṃ guṇavatīṃ rūpavatīṃ pratirūpāṃ prajāvatīṃ labheyamiti?
319.010. tasmin khalu samaye puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇa utkūṭaṃ nāma droṇamukhaṃ paribhuṅkte sma sasaptotsadaṃ stṛṇakāṣṭhodakaṃ dhānyasahagataṃ rājñāgnidattena brahmadeyaṃ dattam/
319.011. puṣkarasārī punarbrāhmaṇa upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ saṃśuddho gṛhiṇyāmanā {kule jātyāṃ vā} kṣipto jātivādena gotravādena yāvadāsaptamamātāmahapitāmaham/
319.013. yugapadupādhyāyo 'dhyāpako mantradharastrayāṇāṃ vedānāṃ pāragaḥ sāṅgopāṅgānāṃ sarahasyānāṃ sanighaṇṭakeiṭabhānāṃ sākṣaraprabhedānāmitihāsapañcamānāṃ padako{śo} vaiyākaraṇaḥ/
319.015. lokāyatayajñamantramahāpuruṣalakṣaṇeṣu pāragaḥ/
319.015. sphītamutkūṭaṃ nāma droṇamukhaṃ paribhuṅkte/
319.016. puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā bhūtā/
319.016. upetā rūpataśca kulataśca śīlataśca guṇataśca, sarvaguṇopetā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā paramayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā śīlavatī guṇavatī//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, thought: 'This son of mine, Prince <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>, is endowed in beauty, family, character, and virtues — possessed of all qualities, handsome, pleasing to look at, charming, and blessed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness. He has completed his vows, mastered the <s>mantras</s>, and reached the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>. It is time that I arrange his marriage. But from where shall I obtain for my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> a wife who is virtuous, endowed with good qualities, beautiful, fitting, and likely to bear children?' Now at that time, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> administered a district called <s>Utkūṭa</s>, a <s>droṇamukha</s> (township), together with its seven surrounding settlements, with its grass, wood, and water, along with its grain revenues — a royal <s>brahmadeya</s> (tax-free grant) given by King <s>Agnidatta</s>. This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> was pure on both mother's and father's side, neither he nor his wife reproached in family or birth by anyone alleging defective lineage, up to seven generations of maternal and paternal ancestors. He was simultaneously a teacher, an instructor, a bearer of <s>mantras</s>, one who had reached the far shore of three <s>Vedas</s> with their supplements and appendices, their secrets, their <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> glossaries, and their phonetic analysis, with the <s>Itihāsas</s> as fifth; a lexicographer, a grammarian, accomplished in <s>Lokāyata</s>, sacrificial <s>mantras</s>, and the marks of a great being. He administered the prosperous district of <s>Utkūṭa</s>. This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> had a daughter, a maiden named <s>Prakṛti</s> — endowed in beauty, family, character, and virtues, possessed of all qualities, beautiful, pleasing to look at, charming, blessed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness, virtuous, and of good qualities.

body.text:
319.019. atha triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasyaitadabhavat--astyuttarapūrveṇotkūṭo nāma droṇamukhaḥ/
319.019. tatra puṣkarasāro nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati/
319.020. upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛto yāvat traivedike pravacane vistareṇa/
319.021. sa cotkūṭaṃ droṇamukhaṃ paribhuṅkte sasaptotsadaṃ satṛṇakāṣṭhodakaṃ dhānyabhogaiḥ sahagataṃ rājñāgnidattena brahmadeyaṃ dattam/
319.022. tasya puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitā upetā rūpataśca kulataśca śīlataśca srvaguṇopetā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā paramayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā śīlavatī guṇavatī putrasya me śārdūlakarṇasya pratirūpā patnī bhaviṣyatīti/
319.025. atha triśaṅkurmātaṅgarāja etamevārthaṃ bahulaṃ rātrau cintayitvā vitarkya tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt pratyūṣakālasamaye srvaśvetaṃ vaḍavārathamabhiruhya mahatā śvapākagaṇena amātyagaṇena parivṛtaścaṇḍālanagarānniṣkramyottareṇa prāgacchadyenotkūṭaṃ droṇamukham/
319.027. atha triśaṅkurmātaṅgarāja utkūṭasyottarapūrveṇa sumanaskaṃ nāmodyānaṃ nānāvṛkṣasaṃchannaṃ nānāvṛkṣakusumitaṃ nānādvijanikūjitaṃ nandanamiva devānāṃ tadupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
319.029. upasaṃkramya brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇamāgamayamāno 'sthāt--brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī māṇavakān mantrān vācayitumihāgamiṣyatīti//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, thought: 'To the northeast is a district called <s>Utkūṭa</s>. There dwells a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, pure on both mother's and father's side — and so on in detail — up to accomplished in the threefold Vedic teaching. He administers the district of <s>Utkūṭa</s>, together with its seven surrounding settlements, with its grass, wood, and water, along with its grain revenues — a royal <s>brahmadeya</s> given by King <s>Agnidatta</s>. This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> has a daughter, a maiden named <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed in beauty, family, character, and virtues, possessed of all qualities, beautiful, pleasing to look at, charming, blessed with supreme auspicious complexion and fullness, virtuous, and of good qualities — she will be a fitting wife for my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>.' Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, having pondered and deliberated upon this very matter throughout the night, at the passing of that very night, at the dawn hour, mounting an all-white mare-drawn chariot, surrounded by a great company of <s>Śvapākas</s> (outcastes) and a company of ministers, set out from the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> settlement and headed northward toward the district of <s>Utkūṭa</s>. Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, arrived at a garden called <s>Sumanaska</s>, to the northeast of <s>Utkūṭa</s> — covered with various trees, blooming with various flowers, resounding with various birds, like <s>Nandana</s>, the garden of the gods — and having arrived there, stood waiting for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, thinking: 'The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> will come here to teach the students their <s>mantras</s>.'

body.text: 319.031. atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tasyā rva rātryā atyayāt srvaśvetaṃ vaḍavārathamabhiruhya śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ pañcamatrairmāṇavakaśataiḥ puraskṛta utkūṭānniryāti sma brāhmaṇān mantrān <320>vācayitum/
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, at the passing of that very night, mounting an all-white mare-drawn chariot, surrounded by his company of students, preceded by five hundred young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> pupils, set out from <s>Utkūṭa</s> to teach the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> students their <s>mantras</s>.

body.text:
320.001. adrākṣīttriśaṅkurmātaṅgarājo brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ sūryamivodayantaṃ tejasā, jvalantamiva hutavaham, yajñamiva brāhmaṇaparivṛtam, śakramiva devagaṇaparivṛtam, haimavantamivauṣadhibhiḥ, samudramiva ratnaiḥ, candramiva nakṣatraiḥ, vaiśravaṇamiva yakṣagaṇaiḥ, brahmāṇamiva devarṣigaṇaiḥ parivṛtaṃ śobhamānam/
320.004. dūrata evāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca enaṃ pratyudgamya yathādharmaṃ kṛtvedamavocat--haṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin, svāgatam, āyāhi/
320.005. kāryaṃ ca te vakṣyāmi, tacchrūyatām/
320.006. evamukte brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅgarājamidamavocat--na hi bhostriśaṅko śakyaṃ brāhmaṇena saha bhoḥkāraṃ kartum/
320.007. ahaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasāriñ śaknomi bhoḥkāraṃ kartum/
320.007. yacchakyaṃ me kartuṃ bhavati, naiva tacchakyaṃ te kartum/
320.008. api tu catvāro bhoḥ puṣkarasārin puruṣasya kāryamānambhāḥ pūrvasamārabdhā bhavanti yaduta ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vā ātmīyārthaṃ vā sarvabhūtasaṃgrahārthaṃ vā/
320.010. idaṃ cātra mahattaraṃ kāryam/
320.010. yatte vyākhyāsyāmi, tacchrūyatāam/
320.010. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaramutsṛja bhāryārthāya/
320.011. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase, tāvantaṃ dāsyāmi//
body.translated_text: <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, beheld the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> — like the sun rising in splendor, blazing like the sacrificial fire, like a sacrifice surrounded by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by hosts of gods, like the <s>Himālaya</s> with its herbs, like the ocean with its jewels, like the moon with its constellations, like <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> surrounded by hosts of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by hosts of divine sages — resplendent. Seeing him approaching from afar, he went out to meet him, and having greeted him properly, said: 'Ho, <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, welcome! Come. I shall tell you my business — hear it.' When thus addressed, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> said to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king: 'Indeed, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, it is not possible for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to exchange the greeting "Ho" with you.' 'I, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, am able to exchange the greeting "Ho." What I am able to do, you indeed are unable to do. But there are, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, four kinds of undertakings that a man may engage in: for his own sake, for the sake of others, for the sake of his own people, or for the welfare of all beings. And here the matter is of the greatest importance. Hear what I shall explain to you. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> as a wife to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>. Whatever bride-price you deem appropriate, I shall pay it.'

body.text:
320.013. idaṃ ca khalu punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya bhṛśaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī abhiṣiktaḥ kupitaścaṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanāḥ kopaṃ ca dveṣaṃ ca mrakṣaṃ ca tatpratyayātsaṃjanitvā lalāṭe triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā kaṇṭhaṃ dhamayitvā akṣiṇī parivartya nakulapiṅgalāṃ dṛṣṭimutpādya triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅgarājamidamavocat--dhig grāmyaviṣaya caṇḍāla, nedaṃ śvapākavacanam yuktam, yastvaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragaṃ hīnaścaṇḍālayonijo bhūtvā icchasyavamarditum/
320.017. bho durmate--
320.018. prakṛtiṃ tvaṃ na jānāsi ātmānaṃ cābhimanyase/
320.019. bālāgre sarṣapaṃ mā bhoḥ sthāpaya {mā} kleśamāgamaḥ/
320.020. mā prārthayāprārthanīyāṃ vāyuṃ pāśena bandhaya//3//
body.translated_text: Now, hearing this speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> became greatly agitated, angry, furious, and displeased. Having generated wrath, hatred, and hypocrisy on account of that, furrowing his brow into a triple-crested scowl, puffing up his throat, rolling his eyes, and casting a glance tawny as a mongoose's, he said to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king: 'Shame on you, village-dwelling <s>Caṇḍāla</s>! This is not a fitting speech for a <s>Śvapāka</s> (outcaste), that you, of low <s>Caṇḍāla</s> birth, should wish to humiliate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>! O fool — You do not know <s>Prakṛti</s>, yet you think highly of yourself. Do not place a mustard seed on the tip of a hair — do not invite trouble! Do not desire what is not to be desired — bind the wind with a noose!' //3//

body.text:
320.021. na hi cāmīkaraṃ mūḍha bhavedbhasma kadācana/
320.022. prakāśe vāndhakāre kiṃ viśeṣo nopalabhyate//4//
body.translated_text: 'Gold, O fool, never becomes ash. What difference is perceived between light and darkness?' //4//

body.text:
320.023. caṇḍālayonijastvaṃ hi dvijātiḥ punarapyaham/
320.024. hīnaḥ śreṣṭhena saṃbandhaṃ mūḍha prārthayase katham//5//
body.translated_text: 'You are born of <s>Caṇḍāla</s> womb, while I am of the twice-born; how, O fool, do you desire an alliance of the low with the noble?' //5//

body.text:
320.025. caṇḍālayonibhūtastvamahamasmi dvijātijaḥ/
320.026. na hi śreṣṭhaḥ prahīnena saṃbandhaṃ kartumicchati/
320.027. śreṣṭhāḥ śreṣṭhairhi saṃbandhaṃ kurvantīha dvijātayaḥ//6//
body.translated_text: 'You are born of <s>Caṇḍāla</s> origin, I am born of the twice-born. The noble does not wish to make an alliance with the low. For the noble make alliances with the noble, the twice-born among themselves.' //6//

body.text:
320.028. vidyayā ye tu saṃpannāḥ saṃśuddhāścaraṇena ca/
320.029. jātyā caivānabhikṣiptā mantraiḥ paramatāṃ gatāḥ//7//
body.translated_text: 'Those who are accomplished in learning, purified by conduct, unreproached in birth, and who have attained supremacy in <s>mantras</s>' //7//

body.text:
320.030. adhyāpakā mantradharāstriṣu vedeṣu pāragāḥ/
320.031. nighaṇṭakaiṭabhān vedān brāhmaṇā ye hyadhīyate/
320.032. taistādṛṣairhi saṃbandhaṃ kurvantīha dvijātayaḥ//8//
body.translated_text: 'Teachers, bearers of <s>mantras</s>, who have reached the far shore of the three <s>Vedas</s> — <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who study the <s>Vedas</s> with their <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> glossaries — with such ones do the twice-born make alliances here.' //8//

body.text:
321.001. <321>na hi śreṣṭho hi hīnena saṃbandhaṃ kartumicchati/
321.002. prārthayase 'prārthanīyāṃ vāyuṃ pāśena bandhitum/
321.003. yadasmābhiśca saṃbandhamiha tvaṃ kartumicchasi//9//
body.translated_text: 'The noble does not wish to make an alliance with the low. You desire what is not to be desired — to bind the wind with a noose — that you wish to make an alliance with us here.' //9//

body.text:
321.004. jugupsitaḥ sarvaloke kṛpaṇaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ/
321.005. gaccha tvaṃ vṛṣala kṣipraṃ kimasmānavamanyase//10//
body.translated_text: 'Despised by the whole world, wretched, lowest of men — go quickly, <s>Vṛṣala</s> (outcaste)! Why do you insult us?' //10//

body.text:
321.006. caṇḍālāḥ saha caṇḍālaiḥ pukkasāḥ saha pukkasaiḥ/
321.007. kurvantīhaiva saṃbandhaṃ jātibhirjātireva ca//11//
body.translated_text: '<s>Caṇḍālas</s> with <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Pukkasas</s> with <s>Pukkasas</s> — they make alliances here, each caste with its own caste.' //11//

body.text:
321.008. brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyaiḥ saha/
321.009. sārdhaṃ vaiśyāstathā vaiśyaiḥ śūdrāḥ śūdraistathā saha//12//
body.translated_text: '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> with <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s> likewise with <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Śūdras</s> with <s>Śūdras</s> likewise.' //12//

body.text:
321.010. sadṛśāḥ sadṛśaiḥ sārdhamāvahanti parasparam/
321.011. na hi kurvanti caṇḍālāḥ saṃbandhaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha//13//
body.translated_text: 'Equals marry equals among themselves. <s>Caṇḍālas</s> do not make alliances with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.' //13//

body.text:
321.012. sarvajātivihīno 'si sarvavarṇajugupsitaḥ/
321.013. kathaṃ hīnaśca śreṣṭhena saṃbandhaṃ kartumicchasi//14//
body.translated_text: 'You are devoid of all caste, despised by all classes. How does the low wish to make an alliance with the noble?' //14//

body.text:
321.014. idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya puṣkarasāriṇas triśaṅkurmātaṅgarāja idamavocat--
321.015. yathā bhasmani sauvarṇe viśeṣa upalabhyate/
321.016. brāhmaṇe vānyajātau vā na viśeṣo 'sti vai tathā//15//
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, said this: 'Just as a difference is perceived between gold and ash, so between a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and one of another caste, there is no such difference.' //15//

body.text:
321.017. yathā prakāśatamasorviśeṣa upalabhyate/
321.018. brāhmaṇe vānyajātau vā na viśeṣo 'sti vai tathā//16//
body.translated_text: 'Just as a difference is perceived between light and darkness, so between a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and one of another caste, there is no such difference.' //16//

body.text:
321.019. na hi brāhmaṇa ākāśānmaruto vā samutthitaḥ/
321.020. bhittvā vā pṛthivīṃ jāto jātavedā yathāraṇeḥ//17//
body.translated_text:
321.019. 'For the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is not arisen from the sky, nor from the wind,
321.020. nor born by splitting the earth — like fire from the fire-drill.' //17//

body.text:
321.021. brāhmaṇā yonito jātāścaṇḍālā api yonitaḥ/
321.022. śreṣṭhatve vṛṣalatve ca kiṃ vā paśyasi kāraṇam//18//
body.translated_text:
321.021. '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are born from a womb, and <s>Caṇḍālas</s> too are born from a womb.
321.022. In superiority and in inferiority, what cause do you see?' //18//

body.text:
321.023. brāhmaṇe 'pi mṛtotsṛṣṭo jugupsyo 'śucirucyate/
321.024. varṇāstathaiva cāpyanye kā nu tatra viśeṣatā//19//
body.translated_text:
321.023. 'Even among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, a dead body when cast out is called repulsive and impure.
321.024. And so too with the other castes — what distinction is there in this?' //19//

body.text:
321.025. yatkiṃcitpāpakaṃ karma kilbiṣaṃ kalireva ca/
321.026. sattvānāmupaghātāya brāhmaṇaistatprakāśitam//20//
body.translated_text:
321.025. 'Whatever sinful deed, whatever offense, whatever strife —
321.026. it is by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> that these have been proclaimed for the destruction of beings.' //20//

body.text:
321.027. iti karmāṇi caitāni prakāśitāni brāhmaṇaiḥ/
321.028. karmabhirdāruṇaiścāpi "puṇyo 'ham" bruvate dvijāḥ//21//
body.translated_text:
321.027. 'Thus these deeds have been proclaimed by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
321.028. and even through terrible deeds, the twice-born declare "I am meritorious."' //21//

body.text:
321.029. māṃsaṃ khāditukāmaistu brāhmaṇairupakalpitam/
321.030. mantrairhi prokṣitāḥ santaḥ svargaṃ gacchantyajaiḍakāḥ//22//
body.translated_text:
321.029. 'It was contrived by <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who desired to eat meat:
321.030. that goats and sheep, having been sprinkled with <s>mantras</s>, go to heaven.' //22//

body.text:
322.001. <322>yadeṣa mārgaḥ svagārya kasmānna brāhmaṇā hyamī/
322.002. ātmānamathavā bandhūnmantraiḥ saṃprokṣayanti vai//23//
body.translated_text:
322.001. 'If this is indeed the path to heaven, why do these <s>brāhmaṇas</s> not
322.002. sprinkle themselves or their kinsmen with <s>mantras</s>?' //23//

body.text:
322.003. mātaraṃ pitaraṃ caiva bhrātaraṃ bhaginīṃ tathā/
322.004. putra duhitaraṃ bhāryāṃ dvijā na prokṣayantyamī//24//
body.translated_text:
322.003. 'Their mother, their father, their brother, their sister,
322.004. their son, their daughter, their wife — these twice-born do not sprinkle them.' //24//

body.text:
322.005. mitraṃ jñātiṃ sakhīṃ vāpi ye vā viṣayavāsinaḥ/
322.006. prokṣitāste 'pi vā mantraiḥ sarve yāsyanti sadgatim//25//
body.translated_text:
322.005. 'A friend, a kinsman, a companion, or those dwelling in the realm —
322.006. if they too were sprinkled with <s>mantras</s>, all would go to a good destination.' //25//

body.text:
322.007. sarve yajñaiḥ samāhūtā gamiṣyanti satāṃ gatim/
322.008. paśubhiḥ kiṃ nu bho yaṣṭairātmānaṃ kiṃ na yakṣyase//26//
body.translated_text:
322.007. 'All, summoned by sacrifices, would go to the destination of the good.
322.008. What use are sacrificial animals? Why do you not sacrifice yourself?' //26//

body.text:
322.009. na prokṣaṇair na mantraiśca svargaṃ gacchantyajaiṭakāḥ/
322.010. na hyeṣa mārgaḥ svargāya mithyāprokṣaṇamucyate//27//
body.translated_text:
322.009. 'Not by sprinklings, not by <s>mantras</s> do goats and sheep go to heaven.
322.010. For this is not the path to heaven — the false sprinkling, it is said.' //27//

body.text:
322.011. brāhmaṇai raudracittaistu paryāyo hyeṣa cintitaḥ/
322.012. māṃsaṃ khāditukāmaistu prokṣaṇaṃ kalpitaṃ paśoḥ//28//
body.translated_text:
322.011. 'By <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of cruel hearts was this device devised —
322.012. the sprinkling of animals was contrived by those who desire to eat meat.' //28//

body.text:
322.013. anyaccāhaṃ pravakṣyāmi brāhmaṇairyat prakalpitam/
322.014. pātakā hi samākhyātā brāhmaṇeṣu caturvidhāḥ//29//
body.translated_text:
322.013. 'And I shall declare something else that has been contrived by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:
322.014. four kinds of grave sins have been declared among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' //29//

body.text:
322.015. suvarṇacauryaṃ madyaṃ gurudārābhimardanam/
322.016. brahmaghnatā ca catvāraḥ pātakā brāhmaṇeṣvamī//30//
body.translated_text:
322.015. 'Theft of gold, drinking liquor, violation of the teacher's wife,
322.016. and killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — these are the four grave sins among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.' //30//

body.text:
322.017. suvarṇaharaṇaṃ varjyaṃ steyamanyanna vidyate/
322.018. suvarṇam yo haredvipraḥ sa tenā^brāhmaṇo bhavet//31//
body.translated_text:
322.017. 'Stealing gold is forbidden, but other theft does not exist;
322.018. a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who steals gold — by that he becomes a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //31//

body.text:
322.019. surāpānaṃ na pātavyamannapānam yatheṣṭataḥ/
322.020. surāṃ tu yaḥ pibedvipraḥ sa tenābrāhmaṇo bhavet//32//
body.translated_text:
322.019. 'Liquor must not be drunk, but other food and drink may be taken at will;
322.020. but a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks liquor — by that he becomes a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //32//

body.text:
322.021. gurudārā na gantavyā anyadārā yatheṣṭataḥ/
322.022. gurudārāṃ tu yo gacchetsa tenābrāhmaṇo bhavet//33//
body.translated_text:
322.021. 'The teacher's wife must not be approached, but other women may be approached at will;
322.022. but a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who approaches the teacher's wife — by that he becomes a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //33//

body.text:
322.023. na hanyād brāhmaṇaṃ hyakaṃ hanyādanyānanekaśaḥ/
322.024. hanyāttu brāhmaṇam yo vai sa tenābrāhmaṇo bhavet//34//
body.translated_text:
322.023. 'One must not kill a single <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, but one may kill others repeatedly;
322.024. but he who kills a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — by that he becomes a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //34//

body.text:
322.025. ityete pātakā hyuktā brāhmaṇeṣu caturvidhāḥ/
322.026. bhavatyabrāhmaṇā yena tato 'nye 'pātakāḥ smṛtāḥ//35//
body.translated_text:
322.025. 'Thus these four kinds of grave sins among <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have been declared;
322.026. by which one becomes a non-<s>brāhmaṇa</s> — other than those, the rest are considered not sinful.' //35//

body.text:
322.027. kṛtvā caturṇāmekaikaṃ bhavedabrāhmaṇastu saḥ/
322.028. labhate na ca sāmīcīṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ samāgame/
322.029. āsanaṃ codakaṃ caiva vyutthānaṃ sa na cārhati//36//

322.030. tasy niḥsaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ patitasya tu/
322.031. vrataṃ vai sa samādāya punarbrāhmaṇatāṃ vrajet//37//
body.translated_text:
322.030. 'For one who has fallen, this escape has been devised by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:
322.031. by undertaking a vow, he may regain the status of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //37//

body.text:
323.001. <323>asau dvādaśavarṣāṇi dhārayitvā kharājinam/
323.002. khaṭvāṅgamucchritaṃ kṛtvā mṛtaśīrṣe ca bhijanam//38//
body.translated_text:
323.001. 'For twelve years, wearing an ass's hide,
323.002. bearing a raised skull-staff, and eating from a death's head —' //38//

body.text:
323.003. etadvrataṃ samādāya niścayena nirantaram/
323.004. pūrṇe dvādaśame varṣe punarbrāhmaṇatāṃ vrajet//39//
body.translated_text:
323.003. 'Having undertaken this vow with determination, without interruption,
323.004. at the completion of the twelfth year, he may regain the status of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' //39//

body.text:
323.005. iti niḥsaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇaistu tapasvibhiḥ/
323.006. kumārgagāmibhirmūḍhairaniḥsaraṇadarśābhiḥ//40//
body.translated_text:
323.005. 'Thus this escape was devised by the ascetic <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
323.006. deluded ones who tread the wrong path, who do not see that there is no escape.' //40//

body.text:
323.007. taditdaṃ brāhmaṇa te bravīmi--saṃjñāmātrakamidaṃ lokasya yadidamucyate brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
323.008. sarvamidamekameveti vijñāya putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ māṇavikāmanuprayaccha bhāryārthāya/
323.009. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvantamanupradāsyāmi//
body.translated_text:
323.007. 'And I say this to you, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: this is merely a designation of the world — what is called "<s>brāhmaṇa</s>" or "<s>kṣatriya</s>" or "<s>vaiśya</s>" or "<s>śūdra</s>."
323.008. Having understood that all this is one and the same, give <s>Prakṛti</s> the girl to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as a wife.
323.009. Whatever bride-price you deem appropriate, I shall pay that much.'

body.text:
323.010. idaṃ ca khalu punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī abhiṣaktaḥ kupitaścaṇḍībhūto 'nāttamanāḥ kopaṃ ca dveṣaṃ ca tatpratyayaṃ janayitvā lalāṭe triśikhāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ kṛtvā kaṇṭhaṃ dhamayitvā akṣiṇī parivartya nakulapiṅgalāṃ dṛṣṭimutpādya triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅgarājamidamavocat--
323.013. asamīkṣyaitattvayā hi kṛtā saṃjñeyamīdṛśī/
323.014. ekaiva jātirloke 'smin sāmānyā na pṛthagvidhā//41//
body.translated_text:
323.010. Having heard these words of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, offended, angry, furious, displeased, having generated wrath and hatred on that account, furrowing his brow into a triple ridge, puffing up his throat, rolling his eyes, producing a gaze tawny as a mongoose, said this to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king:
323.013. 'Without proper examination, you have made this kind of declaration —
323.014. that there is but one birth in this world, common and not of different kinds.' //41//

body.text:
323.015. kathaṃ śvapākajātīyo brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam/
323.016. nihīnayonijo bhūtvā vimarditumihecchasi//42//
body.translated_text:
323.015. 'How can one born of the dog-eater caste presume to trample upon a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has crossed to the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>,
323.016. having been born of a low womb?' //42//

body.text:
323.017. rājānaḥ khalu vṛṣala prati{vi}bhāgajñā bhavanti/
323.017. tadyathā deśadharme vā nagaradharme vā grāmadharme vā nigamadharme vā śulkadharme vā āvāhadharme vā vivāhadharme vā pūrvakarmasu vā/
323.019. catvāra ime vṛṣala varṇāḥ/
323.019. yaduta brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/
323.019. teṣāṃ vivāhadharmeṣu catasro bhāryā brāhmaṇasya bhavanti/
323.020. tadyathā brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/
323.020. tisraḥ kṣatriyasya bhāryā bhavanti/
323.021. kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/
323.021. vaiśyasya dve bhārye bhavataḥ/
323.021. vaiśyā śūdrī ceti/
323.022. śūdrasya tvekā bhāryā bhavati śūdrī eva/
323.022. evaṃ brāhmaṇasya vṛṣala catvāraḥ putrā bhavanti/
323.023. tadyathā brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdraśceti/
323.023. kṣatriyasya trayaḥ putrāḥ, kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/
323.024. vaiśyasy dvau putrau, vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/
323.024. śūdrasya tveka eva putro bhavati yaduta śūdra eva/
323.024. te brāhmaṇāḥ punarvṛṣala brāhmaṇaḥ putrāḥ/
323.025. aurasā mukhato jātāḥ/
323.025. urasto bāhutaḥ kṣatriyāḥ/
323.026. nābhito vaiśyāḥ/
323.026. padbhyāṃ śūdrāḥ/
323.026. brahmaṇāyaṃ khalu vṛṣala lokaḥ sarvabhūtāni nirmitāni/
323.027. tasya jyeṣṭhā vayaṃ putrāḥ kṣatriyāstadanantaram/
323.028. vaiśyāstṛtīyakā varṇāḥ śūdranāṃnā caturthakaḥ//43// iti//
body.translated_text:
323.017. '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, kings are indeed knowledgeable about distinctions —
323.017. such as the customs of the land, the customs of the city, the customs of the village, the customs of the market-town, the customs of tolls, the customs of bringing a bride, the customs of marriage, and in prior deeds.
323.019. There are, O lowly one, four castes —
323.019. namely, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>.
323.019. According to the customs of marriage, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has four wives —
323.020. namely, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> woman, a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>vaiśya</s> woman, and a <s>śūdra</s> woman.
323.020. A <s>kṣatriya</s> has three wives —
323.021. a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>vaiśya</s> woman, and a <s>śūdra</s> woman.
323.021. A <s>vaiśya</s> has two wives —
323.021. a <s>vaiśya</s> woman and a <s>śūdra</s> woman.
323.022. A <s>śūdra</s> has but one wife — a <s>śūdra</s> woman only.
323.022. Thus, O lowly one, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has four sons —
323.023. namely, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, and a <s>śūdra</s>.
323.023. A <s>kṣatriya</s> has three sons — a <s>kṣatriya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, and a <s>śūdra</s>.
323.024. A <s>vaiśya</s> has two sons — a <s>vaiśya</s> and a <s>śūdra</s>.
323.024. A <s>śūdra</s> has but one son — a <s>śūdra</s> only.
323.024. Those <s>brāhmaṇa</s> sons of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, O lowly one,
323.025. are legitimate, born from his mouth.
323.025. From his breast and arms, the <s>kṣatriyas</s>.
323.026. From his navel, the <s>vaiśyas</s>.
323.026. From his feet, the <s>śūdras</s>.
323.026. This world, O lowly one, along with all beings, was created by <s>Brahmā</s>.
323.027. We are his eldest sons, the <s>kṣatriyas</s> come next;
323.028. the <s>vaiśyas</s> are the third caste, and the fourth is called <s>śūdra</s>.' //43//

body.text:
323.029. sa tvaṃ vṛṣala caturthe 'pi varṇe na saṃdṛśase/
323.029. ahaṃ cāgre varṇe śreṣṭhe varṇe parame varṇe pravare varṇe/
323.030. paramārthaṃ ca samyogamākāṅkṣasi/
323.030. praṇaśya tvaṃ vṛṣala kṣipram/
323.030. mā cāsmākamavamaṃsthāḥ//
body.translated_text:
323.029. 'You, O lowly one, are not even to be reckoned among the fourth caste.
323.029. But I belong to the first caste, the best caste, the supreme caste, the most excellent caste.
323.030. And yet you desire an alliance with the highest?
323.030. Perish, you wretch, and quickly!
323.030. And do not insult us!'

body.text:
323.031. idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇasya puṣkarasāriṇastriśaṅkurmātaṅgarāja idamavocat--idamatra brāhmaṇa śṛṇu yad bravīmi/
323.032. brahmaṇāyaṃ lokaḥ, sarvabhūtāni nirmitāni/
body.translated_text:
323.031. Having heard these words of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king said this: 'Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, what I say in reply.
323.032. "This world was created by <s>Brahmā</s>, and all beings were fashioned by him."

body.text:
324.001. <324>tasya jyeṣṭho vayaṃ putrāḥ kṣatriyāstadanantaram/
324.002. vaiśyāstṛtīyakā varṇāḥ śūdranāṃnā catruthakaḥ//44// iti//
body.translated_text:
324.001. "We are his eldest sons, the <s>kṣatriyas</s> come next;
324.002. the <s>vaiśyas</s> are the third caste, and the fourth is called <s>śūdra</s>." //44//

body.text:
324.003. sapādajaṅghāḥ sanakhāḥ samāṃsāḥ sapārśvapaṛṣṭhāśca narā bhavanti/
324.005. ekāṃśato nāsti yato viśeṣo varṇāśca catvāra ito na santi//45//
body.translated_text:
324.003. 'Humans have heads, feet, and shins with nails, they have flesh, they have sides and backs.
324.005. From any single aspect there is no distinction — and therefore four castes do not exist.' //45//

body.text:
324.007. atho viśeṣaḥ pravaro 'sti kaścittad brūhi yaccānumatam yathā te/
324.009. atho viśeṣaḥ pravaro hi nāsti varṇāśca catvāra ito na santi//46//
body.translated_text:
324.007. 'Now if there is some distinction or superiority, declare it — whatever is acceptable to you.
324.009. But if there is no distinction or superiority, then four castes do not exist from this.' //46//

body.text:
324.011. yathā hi dārakā bālāḥ krīḍamānā mahāpathe/
324.012. pāṃśupuñjāni saṃpaṇḍya svayaṃ nāmāni kurvate//47//
body.translated_text:
324.011. 'Just as children playing on the highway
324.012. heap up mounds of dust and give them names of their own —' //47//

body.text:
324.013. idaṃ kṣīramidaṃ dadhi idaṃ māṃsamidaṃ ghṛtam/
324.014. na ca bālasya vacanātpāṃśavo 'nnaṃ bhavanti hi//48//
body.translated_text:
324.013. '"This is milk, this is curds, this is meat, this is ghee" —
324.014. but by a child's words, dust does not become food.' //48//

body.text:
324.015. varṇāstathaiva catvāro yathā brāhmaṇa bhāṣase/
324.016. pāṃśupuñjābhidhānena yogo '{yaḥ ko}pyeṣa na vidyate//49//
body.translated_text:
324.015. 'Likewise the four castes, as you, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, speak of them —
324.016. like the naming of dust-heaps, there is no real connection whatsoever.' //49//

body.text:
324.017. na keśena na karṇābhyāṃ na śīrṣeṇa na cakṣuṣā/
324.018. na mukhena na nāsayā na grīvayā na bāhunā//50//
body.translated_text:
324.017. 'Not by the hair, not by the ears, not by the head, not by the eyes,
324.018. not by the mouth, not by the nose, not by the neck, not by the arms —' //50//

body.text:
324.019. norasāpyatha pārśvābhyāṃ na pṛṣṭhenodareṇa ca/
324.020. norubhyāmatha jaṅghābhyāṃ pāṇipādanakhena ca//51//
body.translated_text:
324.019. 'not by the chest, nor by the sides, not by the back or belly,
324.020. not by the thighs, nor by the shins, not by the hands, feet, or nails —' //51//

body.text:
324.021. na svareṇa na varṇena na sarvāṃśair na maithunaiḥ/
324.022. nānāviśeṣaḥ sarveṣu manuṣyeṣu hi vidyate//52//
body.translated_text:
324.021. 'not by the voice, not by the complexion, not by all bodily parts, not by sexual intercourse —
324.022. no distinction whatever is found among all human beings.' //52//

body.text:
324.023. yathā hi jātiṣvanyāsu liṅgam yoniḥ pṛthak pṛthak/
324.024. sāmānyaṃ kāraṇaṃ tatra kiṃ vā jātiṣu manyase//53//
body.translated_text:
324.023. 'Just as in other species of creatures, the distinguishing mark and womb are different in each,
324.024. there the cause of commonality is clear — what then do you think regarding castes among humans?' //53//

body.text:
324.025. saśīrṣakāścātha narāsthiyuktāḥ sacarmakāḥ sendriyasodarāśca/
324.027. varṇā na yuktāścaturo 'bhidhātum//54//
body.translated_text:
324.025. 'Humans have heads, they are joined with bones, they have skin, they have sense-organs and stomachs;
324.027. it is not fitting to declare four castes.' //54//

body.text:
324.029. doṣo hyayaṃ cātra bhavedayukto yadyattvayā cābhihitaṃ nidāne/
324.031. śrutvā tu mattaḥ pratipadya saumya yaccātra manye śṛṇu codyamānam//55//
body.translated_text:
324.029. 'There would be a fault here, and it would be unjust, based on what you have stated at the outset;
324.031. but having heard from me and reflected, O gentle one, hear what I think is to be challenged.' //55//

body.text:
325.001. <325>yaccātra yuktaṃ viṣamaṃ samaṃ vā tatte pravakṣyāmi niyujyamānaḥ/
325.003. doṣo hi yaścāpi bhavedayukto vakṣyāmi te hyuttaratottaraṃ ca/
325.005. śrutvā tu mattaḥ pratipadya saumya karmādhipatyaprabhavā manuṣyāḥ//56//

325.007. anumānamapi te brāhmaṇa yadi pramāṇam, tatra yad bravīṣi--brahmā eka iti tasmātprajā api ekajātyā eva/
325.008. vayamapyekajātyā bhavāmaḥ/
325.008. yacca bravīṣi--brahmaṇāyaṃ lokaḥ sarvabhūtāni ca nirmitānīti/
325.009. sacette brāhmaṇa idaṃ pramaṇam, tadidaṃ te brāhmaṇa ayuktam yad bravīṣi catvāro varṇāh--brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrāśceti/
325.010. api tu brāhmaṇa mithyā mama vaco bhavet, yadi brāhmaṇa saṃvādena manuṣyajāter nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.011. yaduta śīrṣato vā mukhato vā karṇato vā nāsikāto vā bhrūto vā rūpato vā saṃsthānato vā varṇato vā ākārato vā yonito vā āhārato vā saṃbhavato vā nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text:
325.007. 'If inference is also valid evidence for you, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, then regarding what you say — "<s>Brahmā</s> is one" — therefore all creatures too are of one birth.
325.008. We too would be of one birth.
325.008. And as for what you say — "This world was created by <s>Brahmā</s>, and all beings were fashioned by him" —
325.009. if this is your evidence, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, then it is inconsistent for you to say there are four castes — <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>.
325.010. However, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, my words would be false if the differentiation of the human species could be perceived through any comparison —
325.011. whether through the head, mouth, ears, nose, brows, form, bodily structure, complexion, shape, womb, food, or origin — if any differentiation could be perceived.'

body.text:
325.014. tadyathāpi bhoḥ puṣkarasārin gavāśvagardabhoṣṭramṛgapakṣyajaiḍakānāmaṇḍajajarāyujasaṃsvedajaupapādukānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.015. yaduta pādato 'pi mukhato 'pi varṇato 'pi saṃsthānato 'pi āhārato 'pi yonisambhavato 'pi nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.016. na caivaṃ teṣāṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.017. tattasmātsarvamidamekamiti//
body.translated_text: Just as, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, among cows, horses, donkeys, camels, deer, birds, and sheep — whether egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, or spontaneously-born — diversity is perceived, namely in their feet, mouths, color, shape, diet, and mode of birth — diversity is perceived; but among those four <s>varṇas</s> (classes), no such diversity is perceived. Therefore, all this is one.

body.text:
325.018. api ca brāhmaṇa amīṣāṃ phalguvṛkṣāṇāmāmrātakajambukharjūrapanasadālāvanatindukamṛdvīkabījapūrakakapitthākṣoḍanārikelatiniśakarañjādīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.019. yaduta mūlataśca skandhataśca tvagbhāgataśca sārataśca patrataśca puṣpataśca phalataśca nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.020. na caivaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these soft-wood trees — <s>āmrātaka</s>, <s>jambu</s> (rose-apple), <s>kharjūra</s> (date-palm), <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit), <s>dālāvana</s>, <s>tinduka</s> (persimmon), <s>mṛdvīkā</s> (grape), <s>bījapūraka</s> (citron), <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple), <s>ākṣoḍa</s> (walnut), <s>nārikela</s> (coconut), <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and others — diversity is perceived, namely in root, trunk, bark, heartwood, leaf, flower, and fruit — diversity is perceived. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived.

body.text:
325.022. tadyathā brāhmaṇa amīṣāṃ sthalajānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ sāratamālanaktamālakarṇikārasaptaparṇaśirīṣakovidārasyandanacandanaśiṃśapairaṇḍakhadirādīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.023. yaduta mūlataśca skandhataśca tvagbhāgataśca gulmataśca sārataśca patrataśca phalataśca viśeṣa upalabhyate/
325.024. na caivaṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these land-growing trees — <s>sāra</s> (sal), <s>tamāla</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>kovidāra</s>, <s>syandana</s>, <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), <s>śiṃśapā</s>, <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor), <s>khadira</s> (acacia), and others — diversity is perceived, namely in root, trunk, bark, bush, heartwood, leaf, and fruit — a distinction is found. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived.

body.text:
325.026. tadyathā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin, amīṣāṃ kṣīravṛkṣāṇāmudumbaraplakṣāśvatthanayagrodhavalguketyevamādīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.027. yaduta mūlataśca skandhataśca tvagbhāgataśca sārataśca patrataśca puṣpataśca phalataśca nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.028. na tvena caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text: Just as, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, among these milk-sap trees — <s>udumbara</s> (fig), <s>plakṣa</s>, <s>aśvattha</s> (pipal), <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan), <s>valguka</s>, and such others — diversity is perceived, namely in root, trunk, bark, heartwood, leaf, flower, and fruit — diversity is perceived. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived.

body.text:
325.029. tadyathā puṣkarasārin, amīṣāmapi phalabhaiṣajyavṛkṣāṇāmāmalakīharītakīvibhītakīpharasakādīnāmanyāsāmapi vividhānāmoṣadhīnāṃ grāmajānāṃ pārvatīyānāṃ tṛṇavanaspatīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
325.031. yaduta mūlataśca skandhataśca gulmataśca sārataśca patrataśca puṣpataśca phalataśca nānākaraṇaṃ prajāyate/
325.032. na tveva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, even among these fruit-and-medicinal trees — <s>āmalakī</s> (myrobalan), <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>vibhītakī</s> (belleric myrobalan), <s>pharasaka</s>, and others, and also among various other herbs, whether village-grown or mountain-grown, grasses and forest trees — diversity is perceived, namely in root, trunk, bush, heartwood, leaf, flower, and fruit — diversity is perceived. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived.

body.text:
326.001. <326>tadyathā sthalajānāṃ puṣpavṛkṣāṇāmatimuktakacampakapāṭalānāṃ sumanāvārṣikādhanuṣkārikādīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
326.002. yaduta rūpato 'pi varṇato 'pi gandhato 'pi saṃsthānato 'pi nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
326.003. na tveva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate//
body.translated_text: Just as among land-growing flowering trees — <s>atimuktaka</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>pāṭala</s>, <s>sumanā</s> (jasmine), <s>vārṣikā</s>, <s>dhanuṣkārikā</s>, and others — diversity is perceived, namely in form, color, fragrance, and shape — diversity is perceived. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived.

body.text:
326.004. tadyathā brāhmaṇa amīṣāmapi jalajānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ padmotpalasaugandhakamṛdugandhikādīnāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
326.005. yaduta rūpataśca gandhataśca saṃsthānataśca varṇataśca nānākaraṇaṃ parjñāyate/
326.006. na tveva caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate/
326.006. tadyathā puṣkarasārinn amī brāhmaṇā iti kṣatriyā iti vaiśyā iti śūdrā iti/
326.007. tasmādekamevedaṃ sarvamiti//
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, even among these water-born flowers — <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>saugandhaka</s> (fragrant lotus), <s>mṛdugandhikā</s> (soft-scented lotus), and others — diversity is perceived, namely in form, fragrance, shape, and color — diversity is perceived. But among the four <s>varṇas</s>, no such diversity is perceived. Just as, <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, these are called <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, these <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, these <s>Vaiśyas</s>, these <s>Śūdras</s> — therefore all this is indeed one.

body.text:
326.008. apyanyatte pravakṣyāmi brāhmaṇaiḥ kalpitam yathā/
326.009. śiraḥ satāraṃ gaganamākāśamudaraṃ tathā//57//
body.translated_text: I shall tell you yet another thing, how it was devised by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>: 'The head is the star-bearing sky, and the belly is space.' //57//

body.text:
326.010. parvatāścāpyubhāvūrū pādau ca dharaṇītalam/
326.011. sūryācandramasau netre roma tṛṇavanaspatī//58//
body.translated_text: 'The mountains are the two thighs, and the feet are the surface of the earth; the sun and moon are the eyes, and the body-hair is the grasses and trees.' //58//

body.text:
326.012. aśrūṇyavocadvarṣāsya nadyaḥ prasrāvameva ca/
326.013. sāgarāścāpyamedhyaṃ vai evaṃ braṃhā prajāpatiḥ//59//
body.translated_text: 'The tears, they say, are the rains; the rivers are his streams; and the oceans are his impurities — thus <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Prajāpati</s>.' //59//

body.text:
326.014. parīkṣasva tvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ svalakṣaṇam/
326.014. yasmād brahmaṇo brāhmaṇā utpannāḥ, tasmātkṣatriyā api vaiśyā api śūdrā apyutpannāḥ//
body.translated_text: 'Examine for yourself the characteristics of <s>Brahmā</s>. Since from <s>Brahmā</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were born, from him the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> too were born, and the <s>Vaiśyas</s> too, and the <s>Śūdras</s> too.'

body.text:
326.016. evaṃ prasūtiryadi tattvataḥ syāttato hi syādvarṇakṛto viśeṣaḥ/
326.018. yadi brāhmaṇā brahmalokaṃ vrajeyustrayaśca varṇā na vrajeyuḥ svargam/
326.020. evaṃ bhavedvarṇakṛto viśeṣo na cenna catvāro bhavanti varṇāḥ//60//
body.translated_text: 'If this creation were truly so, then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s> (class). If the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> were to go to <s>Brahmaloka</s> and the three other classes were not to go to heaven, then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s>. But since that is not so, the four <s>varṇas</s> do not exist.' //60//

body.text:
326.022. yasmāddhi varṇaścaturtha evaṃ prayāti svargaṃ svakṛtena karmaṇā/
326.024. yatastapaścārṣamiha praśastaṃ tasmād dvijāter na viśeṣaṇaṃ syād//61//
body.translated_text: 'Since the fourth class also goes to heaven by its own deeds, and since austerity and the conduct of sages are praised here, therefore there should be no special distinction for the twice-born.' //61//

body.text:
326.026. yadi brāhmaṇaḥ syādihaika eva dvijihvaścatuḥśravaṇastathaiva/
326.028. caturviṣāṇo bahupād dviśīrṣa evaṃ kṛte varṇakṛto viśeṣaḥ//62//
body.translated_text: 'If a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> were the only one here with two tongues, four ears, four horns, many feet, and two heads, then there would be a distinction based on <s>varṇa</s>.' //62//

body.text:
327.001. <327>rāgaiśca nāma paraghātanaṃ ca evamprakāraṃ ca viheṭhanaṃ ca/
327.003. sattvasya vai karmaṇo dhvaṃsanaṃ ca etānyakalyāṇakṛtāni vipraiḥ//63//
body.translated_text: 'Passions, the killing of others, such forms of harassment, and the destruction of a being's deeds — these unwholesome acts are done by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> too.' //63//

body.text:
327.005. yuddhaṃ vivādaṃ kalahānyabhīkṣṇaṃ goprokṣaṇaṃ cintitaṃ brāhmaṇairhi/
327.007. atharvaṇaṃ karmaṇā trāsanaṃ ca etāni mantrāṇi kṛtāni vipraiḥ//64//
body.translated_text: 'War, quarrels, constant strife, the sacrifice of cattle — these were devised by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. <s>Atharvanic</s> rites and terrorizing through rituals — these <s>mantras</s> were composed by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.' //64//

body.text:
327.009. pāpecchatā bahujanavañcanaṃ ca śāṭhyaṃ ca dhauryaṃ ca tathaiva kalpam/
327.011. evaṃ pareṣāmahitaṃ vicintya kadā ca te svargamito vrajeyuḥ//65//
body.translated_text: 'Evil desires, the deception of multitudes, fraud, cruelty, and likewise scheming — having thus contrived harm to others, when would they ever go to heaven?' //65//

body.text:
327.013. ye brāhmaṇā ugratapā vinītā vratena śīlena sadā hyupetāḥ/
327.015. ahiṃsakā ye damasamyame ratāste brāhmaṇā brahmapuraṃ vrajanti//66//
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who practice intense austerity, who are disciplined, always endowed with vows and moral conduct, who are non-violent, who delight in self-control and restraint — those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> go to the abode of <s>Brahmā</s>.' //66//

body.text:
327.017. sahāsthimāṃsaḥ sanakhaḥ sacarmā duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ mūtrapurīṣamekam/
327.019. pañcendriyair nāsti yato viśeṣastasmānna vai varṇacatuṣka eṣaḥ//67//
body.translated_text: 'With the same bones, flesh, nails, skin — suffering and happiness, urine and feces are one; with the five sense-faculties there is no distinction — therefore this fourfold division of <s>varṇa</s> does not exist.' //67//

body.text:
327.021. tadyathā nāma brāhmaṇa kasyacitpuruṣasya catvāraḥ putrā bhaveyuḥ/
327.021. sa teṣāṃ nāmāni kuryāt--nandaka iti vā jīvaka iti vā aśoka iti vā śatāyuriti vā/
327.022. iṣṭāśca punarbho etasya puruṣasya putrā bhaveyuḥ/
327.023. tatra yo nandakaḥ sa nandet/
327.023. yo jīvakaḥ sa jīvet/
327.024. yo 'śokaḥ sa na śocet/
327.024. yaḥ śatāyuḥ sa varṣaśataṃ jīvet//
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, suppose a certain man had four sons. He would give them names — <s>Nandaka</s> ('Joy'), or <s>Jīvaka</s> ('Life'), or <s>Aśoka</s> ('Sorrowless'), or <s>Śatāyus</s> ('Hundred-years'). And suppose these sons were dear to that man. Would <s>Nandaka</s> therefore rejoice? Would <s>Jīvaka</s> therefore live? Would <s>Aśoka</s> therefore not grieve? Would <s>Śatāyus</s> therefore live a hundred years?

body.text:
327.025. nāmataḥ punarbrāhmaṇa teṣāṃ nānākaraṇaṃ prajñāyate na jātitaḥ/
327.025. tatkasya hetoh? iha khalu punarbrahmaṇa pitṛtaḥ putro jāyate/
327.026. tasmācca tatredaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati--
327.027. mātā bhastrā pituḥ putro yena jātaḥ sa eva saḥ/
327.028. yadyevaṃ bho vijānāsi na te (putrā) parabhūtāḥ kvacit//68//
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among these there is diversity perceived by name, not by birth. For what reason? Because, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a son is born from his father. Therefore, in this matter, the explanation is as follows: 'The mother is the bellows, the son is of the father — by whom he is born, he is that very one. If you understand this, Ho, then your sons are never inferior to anyone.' //68//

body.text:
327.029. parīkṣasva brāhmaṇa samyageva--ko 'tra brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdra iti/
327.030. sarve kāṇāśca kubjāśca sarve 'pasmāriṇo 'pi vā/
327.031. kilāsinaḥ kuṣṭhinaśca gaurāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ pṛthak pṛthak//69//
body.translated_text: Examine well, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — who here is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a <s>Śūdra</s>? 'All are one-eyed, hunchbacked, all are epileptic too; lepers and those with skin disease, fair and dark, each and every one' //69//

body.text: 328.001. <328>pratiṣṭhitāḥ//
body.translated_text: are established alike.

body.text:
328.002. samamajjānakhatvacapārścodaravaktrāḥ prajā hi tāḥ svakarmaṇā/
328.003. evaṃ gate brāhmaṇa naiva bhavati viśeṣaḥ ko jātikṛto viśeṣaḥ/
328.004. yasmānna jāterviśeṣaṇo 'sti tasmānna vai varṇacatuṣka eva//69//(a)
328.005. tasmātte brāhmaṇa bravīmi--saṃjñāmātramidaṃ lokasya yadidaṃ brāṃhaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā caṇḍāka iti vā/
328.006. ekamidaṃ sarvamidamekam/
328.006. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaramutsṛja bhāryārthāya/
328.007. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvantamanupradāsyāmi//
body.translated_text: 'With the same marrow, nails, skin, sides, belly, and mouth — people are distinguished by their own deeds. This being so, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, there is no distinction; what distinction is there based on birth? Since there is no distinction from birth, therefore this fourfold division of <s>varṇa</s> does not exist.' //69a// Therefore I tell you, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: this is merely a designation of the world — that one is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a <s>Śūdra</s>, or a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>. All this is one; all this is the same. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> as a wife to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>. Whatever bride-price you deem appropriate, I shall pay it.

body.text:
328.008. idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājāsya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī idamavocat--kiṃ punarbhavatā ṛgvedo 'dhītaḥ, yajurvedo 'dhītaḥ, sāmavedo 'dhītaḥ, arthavavedo 'dhītaḥ, āyurvedo 'dhītaḥ, kalpādhyāyo 'pi, adhyātmamapi, mṛgacakraṃ vā, nakṣatragaṇo vā, tithikramagaṇo vā tvayādhītah? karmacakraṃ vā tvayādhigatam? athavā aṅgavidyā vā vastravidyā vā śivāvidyā śakunividyā vā tvayādhītā? athavā rāhucaritaṃ vā śukracaritaṃ vā grahacaritaṃ tvayādhītam? athavā lokāyataṃ bhavatā bhāṣyapravacanaṃ vā pakṣādhyāyo vā nyāyo vā tvayādhītah?
328.014. evamukte triśaṅkurmātaṅgarājaḥ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ brāhmaṇametadavocat--etacca mayā brāhmaṇā adhītaṃ bhūyaścottaram/
328.015. bhūyaścottaram/
328.015. yadapi te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syāt--ahamasmi mantreṣu pāraṃ prāpta iti, tatra te brāhmaṇa saha dharmeṇānumānaṃ pravakṣyāmi/
328.016. na khalvevaṃ brāhmaṇa prāthamakalpikānāṃ sattvānāmetadabhavat--yaduta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
328.017. ekamidaṃ sarvamidamekam//
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> said this: 'But has your honor studied the <s>Ṛgveda</s>? The <s>Yajurveda</s>? The <s>Sāmaveda</s>? The <s>Atharvaveda</s>? The <s>Āyurveda</s>? The chapter on ritual practice? The science of the self? The animal-wheel? The science of constellations? The reckoning of lunar days? Have you mastered the wheel of action? Or have you studied the science of bodily marks, the science of cloth, the science of <s>Śiva</s>, the science of omens from birds? Or have you studied the movements of <s>Rāhu</s>, the movements of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), the movements of the planets? Or have you studied <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialism), commentarial exposition, the chapter on dialectics, or logic?' Thus addressed, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the elephant-king, said to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>: 'All that, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I have studied, and more besides. And more besides. And if, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, you should think thus — "I have reached the far shore of the <s>mantras</s>" — then, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall tell you an inference according to <s>Dharma</s>. It was not so, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, that among the primordial beings there was any such thing as "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>," "<s>Kṣatriya</s>," "<s>Vaiśya</s>," or "<s>Śūdra</s>." All this is one; all this is the same.'

body.text:
328.019. atha brāhmaṇa sattvānāmasadṛśānāṃ cobhayathā sadṛśānāṃ tato 'nye sattvāḥ śālikṣetrāṇi kelāyanti gopāyanti vāpayanti vā, te 'mī kṣatriyā iti saṃjñā udapādi/
328.020. athātra brāhmaṇa tadanyatamānāṃ sattvānāmetadabhavat--parigraho rogaḥ parigraho gaṇḍaḥ parigrahaḥ śalyaḥ/
328.021. yannu vayaṃ svaparigrahamapahāya araṇyāyatanaṃ gatvā tṛṇakāṣṭhaśākhāparṇapalāśakānupasaṃhṛtya tṛṇakuṭikāṃ vā parṇakuṭikāṃ vā kṛtvā praviśya dhyāyema iti/
328.023. atha te sattvāstaṃ parigrahamapahāyā araṇyāyatanaṃ gatvā tṛṇakāṣṭhaśākhāpatraparṇapālāśakaistṛṇakuṭiṃ vā parṇakuṭikāṃ vā kṛtvā tatraiva praviśya dhyāyanti sma/
328.025. te tatra sāyamāsanahetoḥ prāntavāṭikāṃ prātaraśanahetośca grāmaṃ piṇḍāya praviśanti sma//
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among those beings who were dissimilar in both respects and similar in both respects, some other beings cultivated rice-fields, guarded them, and sowed them. For those, the designation '<s>Kṣatriyas</s>' arose. Then, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, among certain other beings the following thought arose: 'Possession is a disease; possession is a boil; possession is a thorn. Let us now abandon our possessions, go to a forest hermitage, and having gathered grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage, having built a grass hut or a leaf hut, enter it and meditate.' Then those beings, having abandoned their possessions, went to a forest hermitage, and having gathered grass, wood, branches, leaves, and foliage, having built a grass hut or a leaf hut, entered it and meditated there. In the evening they went to the outskirts for their evening meal, and in the morning they entered the village for alms.

body.text:
328.027. atha teṣāṃ grāmavāsināṃ satvānāmetadabhavat--duṣkarakārakā bata bhoḥ sattvā ye svakaṃ parigrahamutsṛjya grāmanigamajanapadebhyo bahir nirgatāḥ/
328.028. teṣāṃ bahirmanaskā brāhmaṇā iti saṃjñā udapādi/
328.029. te ca punargrāmavāsinaḥ sattvāstānatīva satkurvanti sma/
328.029. teṣāṃ ca dātavyaṃ manyante sma//
body.translated_text: Then those village-dwelling beings thought: 'Truly remarkable are these beings who have given up their own possessions and gone forth from villages, towns, and districts!' For those who had turned their minds outward, the designation '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>' arose. Those village-dwelling beings honored them greatly and considered that gifts should be given to them.

body.text:
329.001. <329>atha etṣāmeva sattvānāmanyatame sattvāstāni dhyānānyasambhāvayanto grāmeṣvavatīrya mantrapadān svādhyāyanti sma/
329.002. tāṃste grāmanivāsina āhuh--na kevalamime sattvāḥ, ime 'dhyāpakāḥ, teṣāmadhyāpakā iti loke saṃjñā udapādi/
329.003. ayaṃ heturayaṃ pratyayo brāhmaṇānāṃ loke prādurbhāvāya//
body.translated_text: Then some of those very beings, unable to attain the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), descended to the villages and recited <s>mantra</s>-verses as their own study. Those village-dwellers said to them: 'These beings are not merely that — these are teachers.' For those, the designation 'teachers' arose in the world. This is the cause, this is the condition for the appearance of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world.

body.text:
329.005. athānyatame sattvā vivekakālapratisamyuktān kārmāntān vividhānarthapratisamyuktān kurvanti sma/
329.006. teṣāṃ vaiśyā iti saṃjñā udapādi//
body.translated_text:
329.005. Then certain beings engaged in various enterprises connected with the proper time for seclusion and various profitable activities.
329.006. For them the designation '<s>Vaiśyas</s>' arose.

body.text:
329.007. athānyatame sattvāḥ kṣudreṇa karmaṇā jīvikāṃ kalpayanti sma/
329.007. teṣāṃ śūdrā iti saṃjñā udapādi//
body.translated_text:
329.007. Then certain beings made their livelihood by menial work.
329.007. For them the designation '<s>Śūdras</s>' arose.

body.text:
329.009. bhūtapūrvaṃ brāhmaṇa anyatamaḥ sattvo vadhūmādāya rathamāruhya anyatamasminnaraṇyapradeśe gataḥ/
329.010. tatra ca ratho bhagnaḥ/
329.010. tasmānmātaṅgam {mā tvaṃ gāmah} iti saṃjñā udapādi//
body.translated_text:
329.009. In the past, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a certain being took his bride, mounted a chariot, and went to a certain forest region.
329.010. There the chariot broke down.
329.010. From this, the designation '<s>Mātaṅga</s>' (meaning 'Do not go!') arose.

body.text: 329.011. kṣetraṃ karṣanti ye teṣāṃ karṣakā iti saṃjñā pravṛttā//
body.translated_text: 329.011. Those who plough the fields — for them the designation 'cultivators' arose.

body.text: 329.012. bhāṣyeṇa ca parṣadaṃ rañjayati dharmeṇa śīlavratasamācāreṇa samyak, tasya rājā iti saṃjñābhūt//
body.translated_text: 329.012. One who by eloquence delights the assembly, and by <s>Dharma</s>, moral conduct, and proper observance rightfully — for him the designation 'king' arose.

body.text: 329.014. tato 'nye sattvā vāṇijyayā jīvikāṃ kalpayanti, teṣāṃ vaṇija iti saṃjñā udapādi//
body.translated_text: 329.014. Then other beings made their livelihood by trade; for them the designation 'merchants' arose.

body.text:
329.015. tataścānye sattvāḥ pravrajanti sma/
329.015. pravrajitvā parāñ jayanti kleśāñ jayantīti teṣāṃ pravrajitā iti loke saṃjñā udapādi//
body.translated_text:
329.015. Then other beings went forth into homelessness.
329.015. Having gone forth, they conquered the defilements, conquering others — for them the designation 'renunciants' arose in the world.

body.text:
329.017. api tu brāhmaṇa ekaiva saṃjñā loka udapādi/
329.017. tāṃ te pravakṣyāmi--
329.018. brahmā loke 'sminn imān vedān vācayati/
329.018. brahmā devānāṃ paramatāpasaḥ/
329.018. indrasya kauśikasya vedān vācayati sma/
329.019. indraḥ kauśiko 'raṇemi--gautamaṃ vedān vācayati/
329.019. araṇemi--gautamaḥ śvetaketuṃ vedān vācayati/
329.020. śvetaketuḥ śukaṃ paṇḍitaṃ vācayati/
329.020. śukaḥ paṇḍitaśca vedān vibhajati sma/
329.021. tadyathā puṣyo bahvṛcānāṃ paṅktiśchandogānāmekaviṃśatiradhvaryavaḥ/
329.022. kraturatharvāṇikānām/
329.022. ba ṛ??? cānāmete brāhmaṇa/
329.022. sarve te vyākhyāyante/
329.022. puṣya eko bhūtvā pañcaviṃśatidhā bhinnaḥ/
329.023. tadyathā śuklā valkalā māṇḍavyā iti/
329.023. tatra daśa śuklāḥ/
329.023. aṣṭau valkalāḥ/
329.024. sapta māṇḍavyāḥ/
329.024. itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa bahvṛcānāṃ śākhā/
329.024. puṣya eko bhūtvā pañcaviṃśatidhā bhinnaḥ//
body.translated_text:
329.017. Moreover, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a single designation arose in the world.
329.017. I shall declare it to you:
329.018. <s>Brahmā</s> taught these <s>Vedas</s> in this world.
329.018. <s>Brahmā</s> is the supreme ascetic among the gods.
329.018. He taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Indra Kauśika</s>.
329.019. <s>Indra Kauśika</s> taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Araṇemi-Gautama</s>.
329.019. <s>Araṇemi-Gautama</s> taught the <s>Vedas</s> to <s>Śvetaketu</s>.
329.020. <s>Śvetaketu</s> taught the wise <s>Śuka</s>.
329.020. And the wise <s>Śuka</s> distributed the <s>Vedas</s>.
329.021. Namely: <s>Puṣya</s> for the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (followers of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>), the <s>Paṅkti</s> for the <s>Chandogas</s> (followers of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>), twenty-one for the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (followers of the <s>Yajurveda</s>),
329.022. and <s>Kratu</s> for the followers of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.
329.022. All these, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of the <s>Bahvṛcas</s>,
329.022. all these are explained.
329.022. <s>Puṣya</s>, being one, was divided into twenty-five.
329.023. Namely: <s>Śuklā</s>, <s>Valkalā</s>, and <s>Māṇḍavyā</s>.
329.023. Of these, ten are <s>Śuklā</s>,
329.023. eight are <s>Valkalā</s>,
329.024. seven are <s>Māṇḍavyā</s>.
329.024. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Bahvṛcas</s>.
329.024. <s>Puṣya</s>, being one, was divided into twenty-five.

body.text:
329.026. anumānamapi brāhmaṇa pramāṇaṃ chandogānām/
329.026. brāhmaṇāḥ sarva ete chandogāḥ/
329.026. paṅktirityekā bhūtvā sāśītisahasradhā bhinnā/
329.027. tadyathā śīlavalkā araṇemikā laukākṣāḥ kauthumā brahmasamā mahāsamā mahāyāgikāḥ sātyamugrāḥ samantavedāḥ//
body.translated_text:
329.026. Inference too, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is authoritative regarding the <s>Chandogas</s>.
329.026. All these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are <s>Chandogas</s>.
329.026. The <s>Paṅkti</s>, being one, was divided into eighty thousand.
329.027. Namely: <s>Śīlavalkā</s>, <s>Araṇemikā</s>, <s>Laukākṣāḥ</s>, <s>Kauthumāḥ</s>, <s>Brahmasamāḥ</s>, <s>Mahāsamāḥ</s>, <s>Mahāyāgikāḥ</s>, <s>Sātyamugrāḥ</s>, and <s>Samantavedāḥ</s>.

body.text:
329.029. tatra śīlavalkā viṃśatiḥ/
329.029. araṇemikā viṃśatiḥ/
329.029. laukākṣāścatvāriṃśat/
329.029. kauthumānāṃ śatam/
329.030. brahmasamānāṃ śatam/
329.030. sātyamugrāṇāṃ śatam/
329.031. samantavedānāṃ śatam/
329.031. itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa cchandoganāṃ śākhā/
329.031. paṅktirityekā bhūtvā sāśītisahasradhā bhinnā//
body.translated_text:
329.029. Of these, the <s>Śīlavalkā</s> are twenty,
329.029. the <s>Araṇemikā</s> are twenty,
329.029. the <s>Laukākṣāḥ</s> are forty,
329.029. the <s>Kauthumāḥ</s> are a hundred,
329.030. the <s>Brahmasamāḥ</s> are a hundred,
329.030. the <s>Sātyamugrāḥ</s> are a hundred,
329.031. the <s>Samantavedāḥ</s> are a hundred.
329.031. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Chandogas</s>.
329.031. The <s>Paṅkti</s>, being one, was divided into eighty thousand.

body.text:
330.001. <330>anumānamapi pramāṇamadhvaryūṇām/
330.001. ete brāhmaṇā ekaviṃśatyadhvaryavo bhūtvā ekottaraśatadhā bhinnāḥ/
330.002. tadyathā kaṭhāḥ kaṇimā vājasaneyino jātukarṇāḥ praṣṭhapadā ṛṣayaḥ/
330.002. tatra daśa kaṭhāḥ/
330.003. daśa kaṇimāḥ/
330.003. ekādaśa vājasaneyinaḥ/
330.003. trayodaśa jātukarṇāḥ/
330.003. ṣoḍaśa ṣoṣṭhapadāḥ/
330.004. ekacatvāriṃśadṛṣayaḥ/
330.004. itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa adhvaryūṇāṃ śākhā/
330.004. ekaviṃśatyadhvaryavo bhūtvā ekottaraśatadhā bhinnāḥ//
body.translated_text:
330.001. Inference too is authoritative regarding the <s>Adhvaryus</s>.
330.001. These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the twenty-one <s>Adhvaryus</s>, were divided into one hundred and one.
330.002. Namely: <s>Kaṭhāḥ</s>, <s>Kaṇimāḥ</s>, <s>Vājasaneyinaḥ</s>, <s>Jātukarṇāḥ</s>, <s>Praṣṭhapadāḥ</s>, and <s>Ṛṣayaḥ</s>.
330.002. Of these, ten are <s>Kaṭhāḥ</s>,
330.003. ten are <s>Kaṇimāḥ</s>,
330.003. eleven are <s>Vājasaneyinaḥ</s>,
330.003. thirteen are <s>Jātukarṇāḥ</s>,
330.003. sixteen are <s>Praṣṭhapadāḥ</s>,
330.004. forty-one are <s>Ṛṣayaḥ</s>.
330.004. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Adhvaryus</s>.
330.004. The twenty-one <s>Adhvaryus</s> were divided into one hundred and one.

body.text:
330.006. anumānamapi brāhmaṇa pramāṇamatharvaṇikānām/
330.006. ete mantrāḥ sarve te 'tharvaṇikāḥ/
330.007. kratureko bhūtvā dvidhā bhinnaḥ/
330.007. caturdhā bhūtvā aṣṭadhā bhinnaḥ/
330.008. aṣṭadhā bhūtvā {nava}daśadhā bhinnaḥ/
330.008. itīyaṃ brahmaṇa arharvaṇikānāṃ śākhā/
330.008. kraturekaḥ ṣoḍaśottaradvādaśaśatadhā bhinnaḥ//
body.translated_text:
330.006. Inference too, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is authoritative regarding the followers of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.
330.006. All these mantras belong to the <s>Atharvaṇikas</s>.
330.007. <s>Kratu</s>, being one, was divided into two;
330.007. becoming four, was divided into eight;
330.008. becoming eight, was divided into nineteen.
330.008. This, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is the branch of the <s>Atharvaṇikas</s>.
330.008. <s>Kratu</s>, being one, was divided into twelve hundred and sixteen.

body.text:
330.010. anumānamapi brāhmaṇa pramāṇaṃ pratītya etāni dvādaśabhedaśatāni ṣoḍaśabhedāśca ye brāhmaṇaiḥ pauraṇaiḥ samyag dṛṣṭāḥ/
330.011. chandasi vā vyākaraṇe vā lokayate vā padamīmāṃsāyāṃ vā/
330.012. na caiṣāmūhāpohaḥ prajñāyate/
330.012. yaduta ekajātyo nāmeti viditvā bandhurbhavitumarhati/
330.012. tatte brāhmaṇa bravīmi--saṃjñāmātrakametallokasya yaduta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
330.014. ekamidaṃ sarvamidamekam/
330.014. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitamutsṛja bhāryārthāya/
330.015. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvantamanupradāsyāmi//
body.translated_text:
330.010. Inference too, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is authoritative: based on these twelve hundred divisions and sixteen subdivisions, which were correctly perceived by the ancient <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
330.011. whether in the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic metre), in grammar, in dialectics, or in the examination of words.
330.012. And no refutation or establishment of these is evident.
330.012. Knowing that they are of one birth, one should be willing to become a kinsman.
330.012. This I tell you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — this designation in the world is merely a label, namely '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' or '<s>Kṣatriya</s>' or '<s>Vaiśya</s>' or '<s>Śūdra</s>.'
330.014. All this is one; all this is the same.
330.014. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as a wife.
330.015. Whatever bride-price you think fitting, I shall pay.

body.text: 330.016. idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tūṣṇīmbhūto madgubhūtaḥ srastaskandho 'dhomukho niṣpratibhaḥ pradhyānaparo 'sthāt//
body.translated_text: 330.016. Having heard these words of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> stood silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downcast, without a reply, absorbed in thought.

body.text:
330.018. dadarśa triśaṅkurmātaṅgarājo brāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇaṃ tūṣṇīmbhūtaṃ madgubhūtaṃ srastaskandhamadhomukhaṃ niṣpratibhaṃ pradhyānaparaṃ sthitam/
330.019. dṛṣṭvā ca punaridamabravīt--yadapi te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syādasadṛśena saha saṃbandho bhaviṣyatīti/
330.020. na punastvayā brāhmaṇa evaṃ draṣṭavyam/
330.020. tatkasya hetoh? ye pramāṇaśrutiśīlaprajñādayo guṇā agryā lokasya te mama putrasya śārdūlakarṇasya saṃvidyante/
330.022. yadapi te brāhmaṇa evaṃ syāt--ye vājapeyam yajñam yajanti, aśvamedhaṃ puruṣamedhaṃ śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍam yajñam yajanti, sarve te kāyasya bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyanta iti/
330.024. na punarbrāhmaṇa tvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
330.024. tatkasya hetoh? vājapeyaṃ brāhmaṇa yajñam yajamānā aśvamedhaṃ puruṣamedhaṃ śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍam yajña ca yajamānā bahudhā mantrān pravartayantaḥ prāṇihiṃsāṃ ca pravartayanti/
330.026. tasmātte brāhmaṇa bravīmi--na hyeṣa mārgaḥ svargāya/
330.026. ahaṃ te brāhmaṇa mārgaṃ svargāya vyākhyāmi/
330.027. tacchṛṇu--
330.028. śīlaṃ rakṣeta medhāvī prārthayānaḥ sukhatrayam/
330.029. praśaṃsāṃ vittalābhaṃ ca pratya svarge ca modanam//70//
body.translated_text:
330.018. King <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> saw the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> standing silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downcast, without a reply, absorbed in thought.
330.019. Seeing him, he spoke again: 'Perhaps you think, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, that the alliance would be with one of unequal status.
330.020. But you should not see it thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
330.020. Why? Because those qualities that are foremost in the world — authority, learning, morality, and wisdom — these are found in my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>.
330.022. Perhaps you also think, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>: "Those who offer the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice, the human-sacrifice, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — all of them, at the breaking up of the body, are reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world, among the gods."
330.024. But you should not see it thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
330.024. Why? Because those who perform the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice, the human-sacrifice, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice, while reciting many mantras, also promote the killing of living beings.
330.026. Therefore I say to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — this is not the path to heaven.
330.026. I shall explain to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the path to heaven.
330.027. Listen:
330.028. 'The wise one should guard morality, aspiring to the threefold happiness —
330.029. praise, acquisition of wealth, and rejoicing in heaven.' //70//

body.text:
330.030. yairbrāhmaṇa itaḥ pūrvaṃ vājapeyo yajña iṣṭaḥ, yairaśvamedho yaiḥ puruṣamedho yaiḥ śāmyaprāśo yair nirargaḍo yajña iṣṭaḥ, parigṛhītastair nirargalaṃ ca kāmaiḥ kāmaḥ/
330.031. ito nākaḥ paryeṣyate/
330.031. ye <331>brāhmaṇa itaḥ paścādvājapeyam yajñam yakṣyanti, ye 'śvamedham ye śāmyaprāśaṃ nirargaḍam yajñam yakṣyanti, te nirarthakaṃ mahāvighātaṃ samyokṣyanti/
body.translated_text:
330.030. 'Those, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who in the past offered the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice, the human-sacrifice, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — they possessed the <s>Nirargala</s> and were embraced by desires.
330.031. From here, heaven was sought.
330.031. But those, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who hereafter will offer the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice, the horse-sacrifice, the <s>Śāmyaprāśa</s>, and the <s>Nirargaḍa</s> sacrifice — they will yoke themselves to a great calamity without purpose.'

body.text:
331.002. tasmātte brāhmaṇa bravīmi--ehi tvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ saṃbandham yojanayasva/
331.003. tatkasya hetoh? dharmeṇa hi caṇḍālā ajugupsanīyā bhavanti/
331.004. api ca/
331.005. śraddhā śīlaṃ tapastyāgaḥ śrutirjñānaṃ dayaiva ca//
body.translated_text:
331.002. 'Therefore I say to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — come, enter into alliance with me.
331.003. Why? Because by <s>Dharma</s>, even <s>Caṇḍālas</s> become not contemptible.
331.004. Moreover:
331.005. Faith, morality, austerity, generosity, learning, knowledge, and compassion —

body.text: 331.006. darśanaṃ sarvavedānāṃ svargavratapadāni vai//71//
body.translated_text: 331.006. insight into all the <s>Vedas</s> — these indeed are the steps to the vow of heaven.' //71//

body.text:
331.007. pramāṇamaṣṭaprakāraṃ svargāya/
331.008. tadebhiraṣṭābhiḥ prakārair dvargagamanamiṣyate/
331.008. ye prāyeṇa jānanti viśeṣeṇa khalvapyanekairvividhairyajñaiḥ/
331.008. aṣṭau cemā brāhmaṇa nirdiṣṭā mātṛtulyā bhaginyo loke pravartante/
331.009. tadyathā--aditirdevānāṃ mātā/
331.009. duturdānavānām/
331.009. manurmānavānām/
331.010. surabhiḥ saurabheyānām/
331.010. vinatā suparṇānām/
331.010. kadrunāgānām/
331.010. pṛthivī bhūtānāṃ mātā sarvabījānām/
331.011. marutāṃ mahāmaha/
331.011. mahākāśyapaṃ manasā vidanti ṛṣayaḥ//
body.translated_text:
331.007. 'Authority of eight kinds leads to heaven.
331.008. By these eight kinds, the path to heaven is desired.
331.008. Those who generally know, and especially through many diverse sacrifices —
331.008. and these eight, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, are declared to be the mothers and sisters who exist in the world as equals.
331.009. Namely: <s>Aditi</s> is the mother of the gods,
331.009. <s>Diti</s> is the mother of the <s>Dānavas</s>,
331.009. <s>Manu</s> is the mother of humans,
331.010. <s>Surabhi</s> is the mother of cattle,
331.010. <s>Vinatā</s> is the mother of <s>Suparṇas</s> (birds),
331.010. <s>Kadrū</s> is the mother of <s>Nāgas</s>,
331.010. the Earth is the mother of all beings and of all seeds,
331.011. and the great <s>Mahā</s> is the mother of the <s>Maruts</s>.
331.011. The sages know the great <s>Kāśyapa</s> by mind.'

body.text:
331.012. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin brāhmaṇānāṃ sapta gautrāṇi svākhyāsyāmi, tāni śrūyantām--tadyathā gautamā vātsyāḥ kautsāḥ kāśyapā vāsiṣṭhā māṇḍavyā ityetāni brāhmaṇa sapta gotrāṇi/
331.014. eṣāmekaikaṃ gotraṃ saptadhā bhinnam/
331.014. atra ye gautamāste kauthumāste gagarste bhāradvājāsta ārṣṭiṣeṇāste vaikhānasāste vajrapādāḥ/
331.015. tatra ye vātsyāsta ātreyāste maitreyāste bhārgavāste sāvarṇyāste bahujātāḥ/
331.016. tatra ye vātsyāsta ātreyāsta maitreyāste bhārgavāste sāvarṇyāste salīlāste bahujātāḥ/
331.016. tatra ye kautsāste maudgalyāyanāste gauṇāyanāste lāṅgalāste lagnāste daṇḍalagnāste somabhuvāh{vah}/
331.017. tatra ye kauśikāste kātyāyanāste darbhakātyāyanāste valkalinaste pakṣiṇaste laukākṣāste lohitāyanāh (lohityāyanāḥ/)/
331.018. tatra ye kāśyapāste maṇḍanāsta iṣṭāste śauṇḍāyanāste rocaneyāste 'napekṣāste 'gniveśyāḥ/
331.019. tatra ye kāśyapāste jātukarṇyāste dhānyāyanāste pārāśarāste vyāghranakhāste āṇḍāyanāsta aupamanyavāḥ/
331.021. tatra ye māṇḍavyāste bhāṇḍāyanāste dhomrāyaṇāste kātyāyanāste khalvavāahanāste sugandhārāyaṇāste kāpiṣṭhalāyanāḥ/
331.022. ityetāni brāhmaṇa evamekonapañcāśadgotrāṇi brāhmaṇaiḥ paurāṇaiḥ samyag dṛṣṭāni cchandasi vyākaraṇe padamīmāṃsāyām/
331.023. anyāni ca gotrāṇi vistarato mayā vācitāni/
331.024. tāni anyair na jñāyante//
body.translated_text:
331.012. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall correctly declare the seven <s>gotras</s> (lineages) of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; listen to them — namely: <s>Gautamāḥ</s>, <s>Vātsyāḥ</s>, <s>Kautsāḥ</s>, <s>Kāśyapāḥ</s>, <s>Vāsiṣṭhāḥ</s>, and <s>Māṇḍavyāḥ</s> — these, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, are the seven lineages.
331.014. Each of these lineages was divided into seven.
331.014. Among these: the <s>Gautamāḥ</s> include the <s>Kauthumāḥ</s>, the <s>Gagarāḥ</s>, the <s>Bhāradvājāḥ</s>, the <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇāḥ</s>, the <s>Vaikhānasāḥ</s>, and the <s>Vajrapādāḥ</s>.
331.015. Among these: the <s>Vātsyāḥ</s> include the <s>Ātreyāḥ</s>, the <s>Maitreyāḥ</s>, the <s>Bhārgavāḥ</s>, the <s>Sāvarṇyāḥ</s>, and the <s>Bahujātāḥ</s>.
331.016. Among these: the <s>Vātsyāḥ</s> include the <s>Ātreyāḥ</s>, the <s>Maitreyāḥ</s>, the <s>Bhārgavāḥ</s>, the <s>Sāvarṇyāḥ</s>, the <s>Salīlāḥ</s>, and the <s>Bahujātāḥ</s>.
331.016. Among these: the <s>Kautsāḥ</s> include the <s>Maudgalyāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Gauṇāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Lāṅgalāḥ</s>, the <s>Lagnāḥ</s>, the <s>Daṇḍalagnāḥ</s>, and the <s>Somabhuvāḥ</s>.
331.017. Among these: the <s>Kauśikāḥ</s> include the <s>Kātyāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Darbhakātyāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Valkalinaḥ</s>, the <s>Pakṣiṇāḥ</s>, the <s>Laukākṣāḥ</s>, and the <s>Lohitāyanāḥ</s>.
331.018. Among these: the <s>Kāśyapāḥ</s> include the <s>Maṇḍanāḥ</s>, the <s>Iṣṭāḥ</s>, the <s>Śauṇḍāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Rocaneyāḥ</s>, the <s>Anapekṣāḥ</s>, and the <s>Agniveśyāḥ</s>.
331.019. Among these: the <s>Kāśyapāḥ</s> include the <s>Jātukarṇyāḥ</s>, the <s>Dhānyāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Pārāśarāḥ</s>, the <s>Vyāghranakhāḥ</s>, the <s>Āṇḍāyanāḥ</s>, and the <s>Aupamanyavāḥ</s>.
331.021. Among these: the <s>Māṇḍavyāḥ</s> include the <s>Bhāṇḍāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Dhomrāyaṇāḥ</s>, the <s>Kātyāyanāḥ</s>, the <s>Khalvavāhanāḥ</s>, the <s>Sugandhārāyaṇāḥ</s>, and the <s>Kāpiṣṭhalāyanāḥ</s>.
331.022. These, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, are the forty-nine lineages correctly perceived by the ancient <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, in the <s>Chandas</s>, in grammar, and in the examination of words.
331.023. And other lineages too have been declared by me at length.
331.024. Those are not known by others.'

body.text:
331.025. yadutaikatvamiti viditvā bhavān bandhurbhavitumarhati/
331.025. tasmātte brāhmaṇa bravīmi sāmānyaṃ saṃjñāmātrakamidaṃ lokasya yaduta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
331.027. ekamidaṃ sarvamidamekam/
331.027. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaramutsṛja bhāryārthāya/
331.028. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvantamanupradāsyāmi//
body.translated_text:
331.025. 'Knowing their oneness, you should be willing to become a kinsman.
331.025. Therefore I say to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — this designation in the world is merely a common label, namely "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>" or "<s>Kṣatriya</s>" or "<s>Vaiśya</s>" or "<s>Śūdra</s>."
331.027. All this is one; all this is the same.
331.027. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as a wife.
331.028. Whatever bride-price you think fitting, I shall pay.'

body.text:
331.029. idaṃ punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī tūṣṇīmbhūto madgubhūtaḥ srastaskandho 'dhomukho niṣpratibhaḥ pradhyānaparaḥ sthito 'bhūt/
331.030. adrākṣīt triśaṅkurmātaṅgarājah <332>puskarasāriṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tūṣṇīmbhūtaṃ madgubhūtaṃ srastaskandhamadhomukhaṃ niṣpratibhaṃ pradhyānaparaṃ sthitam/ dṛṣṭvā ca punaridamavocat--
body.translated_text:
331.029. Having heard this speech, the brāhmaṇa <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> of King <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> (outcaste) stood silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in thought.
331.030. King <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s> saw the brāhmaṇa <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> standing silent, dejected, with drooping shoulders, face downward, without reply, absorbed in thought. Having seen him, he spoke again as follows:

body.text:
332.003. yādṛśaṃ vāpyate bījaṃ tādṛśaṃ labhyate phalam/
332.004. prajāpaterhi caikatve nirviśeṣo bhavatyataḥ//72//
body.translated_text:
332.003. 'As is the seed that is sown, so is the fruit that is obtained;
332.004. since all beings are one in <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures), there is no distinction among them.' //72//

body.text:
332.005. na cendriyāṇāṃ nānātvaṃ kriyābhedaśca dṛśyate/
332.006. brāhmaṇe vānyajātau vā naiṣāṃ kiṃcidviśiṣyate//73//
body.translated_text:
332.005. 'No difference in the sense-faculties and no distinction in activity is seen
332.006. between a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and one of another birth — in nothing are they distinguished.' //73//

body.text:
332.007. na hyātmanaḥ samutlarṣaḥ śreṣṭhatvamiha yujyate/
332.008. śukraśoṇitasambhūtam yonito hyubhayaṃ samam//74//
body.translated_text:
332.007. 'Self-exaltation and superiority are not justified in this world;
332.008. born from semen and blood, both are equal from the womb.' //74//

body.text:
332.009. cāturvarṇyaṃ pravakṣyāmi paśudharmakathāṃ tava/
332.010. bhavette bhavinī bhāryā naitad brāhmaṇa yujyate//75//
body.translated_text:
332.009. 'I shall proclaim to you the four <s>varṇas</s> (classes) — a discourse on the nature of animals.
332.010. That she should become your future wife — this is not proper, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>!' //75//

body.text:
332.011. yadi tāvadayaṃ loko brahmaṇā janitaḥ svayam/
332.012. brāhmaṇī brāhmaṇasvasā kṣatriyā kṣatriyasvasāa//76//
body.translated_text:
332.011. 'If indeed this world was created by <s>Brahmā</s> himself,
332.012. then a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman would be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s sister, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman a <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s sister.' //76//

body.text:
332.013. atha vaiśyasya vaiśyā vai śūdrā vā punaḥ/
332.014. na bhāryā bhaginī yuktā brahmaṇā janitā yadi//77//
body.translated_text:
332.013. 'And a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman would be a <s>Vaiśya</s>'s, and a <s>Śūdra</s> woman likewise;
332.014. a wife who is also a sister would not be proper, if beings were created by <s>Brahmā</s>.' //77//

body.text:
332.015. na sattvā brahmaṇo jātāḥ kleśajāḥ karmajāstvamī/
332.016. nīcaiścoccaiśca dṛśyante sattvā nānāśrayāḥ pṛthak//78//
body.translated_text:
332.015. 'Beings are not born from <s>Brahmā</s>; they are born from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s> (actions).
332.016. They are seen high and low, beings of various abodes, separate.' //78//

body.text:
332.017. teṣāṃ ca jātisāmānyād brāhmaṇe kṣatriye tathā/
332.018. atha vaiśye ca śūdre ca samaṃ jñānaṃ pravartate//79//
body.translated_text:
332.017. 'Among them, by commonality of birth, whether in <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or <s>Kṣatriya</s>,
332.018. or in <s>Vaiśya</s> or <s>Śūdra</s>, knowledge operates equally.' //79//

body.text:
332.019. ṛgvedo 'tha yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'pyatharvaṇam/
332.020. itihāso nighaṇṭaśca kutaśchando nirarthakam//80//
body.translated_text:
332.019. 'The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the <s>Atharvaveda</s>,
332.020. the <s>Itihāsa</s> (history) and the <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> (glossary) — of what use is meter devoid of meaning?' //80//

body.text:
332.021. asmākamapyadhyayane maitrī vidyā tathā śikhī/
332.022. saṃkrāmaṇī prakrāmaṇī stambhanī kāmarūpiṇī//81//
body.translated_text:
332.021. 'Among us too there are studies: <s>Maitrī Vidyā</s> (the Science of Friendship), and <s>Śikhī</s> (the Crested One),
332.022. <s>Saṃkrāmaṇī</s> (the Transferring One), <s>Prakrāmaṇī</s> (the Advancing One), <s>Stambhanī</s> (the Paralyzing One), and <s>Kāmarūpiṇī</s> (the Shape-Shifting One).' //81//

body.text:
332.023. manojavā ca gāndhārī ghorī vidyā vaśaṃkarī/
332.024. kākavāṇī ca mantraṃ ca indrajālaṃ ca bhañjanī//82//
body.translated_text:
332.023. '<s>Manojavā</s> (Swift-as-Thought), <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Ghorī</s> (the Terrible), <s>Vidyā Vaśaṃkarī</s> (the Subjugating Science),
