332.024. <s>Kākavāṇī</s> (Crow-Speech), and <s>Mantra</s>, and <s>Indrajāla</s> (magic), and <s>Bhañjanī</s> (the Breaking One).' //82//

body.text:
332.025. asmākamāsītpuruṣā vidyāsvākhyātapaṇḍitāḥ/
332.026. maṇipuṣpāśca ṛṣayo bhāsvarāśca maharṣayaḥ//83//
body.translated_text:
332.025. 'Among us there were men, renowned scholars in these sciences;
332.026. <s>Maṇipuṣpa</s> and other <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), and the radiant <s>Maharṣis</s> (great sages).' //83//

body.text:
332.027. saṃlprāptā devatāṛddhiṃ kiṃ cikitsasi vidyayā/
332.028. aśikṣitāśca caṇḍālā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ//84//
body.translated_text:
332.027. 'They attained the supernatural powers of the gods — why do you doubt their science?
332.028. The uneducated are <s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcastes), while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are those who have mastered the <s>Vedas</s>.' //84//

body.text:
332.029. kipiṃjalādyo janito mantrāṇāṃ pāramiṃ gataḥ/
332.030. na hyasau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa manyase//85//
body.translated_text:
332.029. '<s>Kipiñjala</s> (the Francolin) was born — he who attained the perfection of <s>mantras</s>;
332.030. he was not the son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman — what then do you think, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>?' //85//

body.text:
333.001. <333>niṣadyajanayatkālī putraṃ dvaipāyanaṃ munim/
333.002. ugraṃ tejasvinaṃ bhīṣmaṃ pañcābhijñaṃ mahātapam/
333.003. na hyasau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//86//

333.004. kṣatriyā reṇukā nāma jajñe rāmaṃ mahāmunim/
333.005. paṇḍitaṃ ca vinītaṃ ca sarvaśāstraviśāradam/
333.006. na hyasau brāhmaṇīputraḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//87//

333.007. ye ca te manujā āsaṃs tejasā tapasā yutāḥ/
333.008. paṇḍitāśca vinītāśca loke ca ṛṣisaṃmatāḥ/
333.009. na hi te brāhmaṇīputrāḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇa vakṣyasi//88//
body.translated_text:
333.007. 'Those men who were endowed with brilliance and austerity,
333.008. learned and disciplined, esteemed in the world as <s>ṛṣis</s> —
333.009. they were not the sons of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women — what then will you say, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>?' //88//

body.text:
333.010. saṃjñā kṛteyaṃ lokasya brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāstathā/
333.011. vaiśyāścaiva tathā śūdrāḥ saṃjñeyaṃ saṃprakīrtitā//89//
body.translated_text:
333.010. 'This is merely a designation of the world: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
333.011. <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and likewise <s>Śūdras</s> — this designation has been proclaimed.' //89//

body.text:
333.012. tasmātte brāhmaṇa bravīmi saṃjñāmātrakamidaṃ lokasya yaduta brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
333.013. ekamidaṃ sarvamidamekam/
333.013. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaramanuprayaccha bhāryārthāya/
333.014. yāvantaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvantamanupradāsyāmi//
body.translated_text:
333.012. 'Therefore I say to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this is merely a designation of the world — that is, "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>," or "<s>Kṣatriya</s>," or "<s>Vaiśya</s>," or "<s>Śūdra</s>."
333.013. All this is one; all this is the same.
333.013. Give my daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as his wife.
333.014. Whatever bride-price you consider appropriate, I shall pay that much.'

body.text:
333.015. idaṃ ca punarvacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅgarājamidamavocat--kiṃgotro bhavān? āha--ātreyagotro 'smi/
333.016. kimpūrvah? āha--ātreyaḥ/
333.017. kiṃcaraṇam? āha--kāleya--maitrāyaṇīyaḥ/
333.017. kati pravarāh? āha--trayaḥ pravarāḥ/
333.017. tadyathā vātsyāḥ kautsyā bharadvājāśca/
333.018. ke bhavantaḥ sabrahmacāriṇah? chandogāḥ/
333.018. kati cchandogānāṃ bhedāh? ṣaṭ/
333.019. te katame? āha--tadyathā/
333.019. kauthumāḥ/
333.019. cārāyaṇīyāḥ/
333.019. lāṅgalāḥ/
333.019. sauvarcasāḥ/
333.020. kāpiṃjaleyāḥ/
333.020. ārṣṭiṣeṇā iti//
body.translated_text:
333.015. Having heard this speech of King <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s>, the brāhmaṇa <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said this to King <s>Triśaṅku</s> the <s>Mātaṅga</s>: 'What is your <s>gotra</s> (lineage)?' He replied: 'I am of the <s>Ātreya</s> lineage.'
333.016. 'What is your original line?' He replied: '<s>Ātreya</s>.'
333.017. 'What is your tradition?' He replied: '<s>Kāleya-Maitrāyaṇīya</s>.'
333.017. 'How many <s>pravaras</s> (distinguished ancestors) do you have?' He replied: 'Three <s>pravaras</s> —
333.017. namely, <s>Vātsya</s>, <s>Kautsya</s>, and <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.'
333.018. 'Who are your fellow students of sacred knowledge?' '<s>Chandogas</s> (chanters of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>).'
333.018. 'How many divisions of the <s>Chandogas</s> are there?' 'Six.'
333.019. 'Which are they?' He replied: 'Namely —
333.019. <s>Kauthumas</s>,
333.019. <s>Cārāyaṇīyas</s>,
333.019. <s>Lāṅgalas</s>,
333.019. <s>Sauvarcasas</s>,
333.020. <s>Kāpiñjaleyas</s>,
333.020. and <s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇas</s>.'

body.text:
333.021. kiṃ bhavato mātṛjaṃ gotram? āha--pārāśarīyam/
333.021. paṭhatu bhavān sāvitrīm/
333.021. kathaṃ bhavati? katyakṣarā sāvitrī? katigaṇḍā? katipadā?
333.023. caturviṃśatyakṣarā sāvitrī/
333.023. trigaṇḍā/
333.023. aṣṭākṣarapadā/
333.023. uccārayatu bhavān sāvitrīm/
333.024. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin, sotpattikāṃ sāvitrīṃ pravakṣyāmi/
333.024. tacchrūyatām/
333.024. kathayatu bhavān/
333.025. bhūtapūrvaṃ brāhmaṇa atīte 'dhvani vasur nāma ṛṣirbabhūva/
333.026. pañcābhijña ugratejā mahānubhāvo dhyānānāṃ lābhī/
333.026. tena tatra takṣakaduhitā kapilā nāma āsaditā bhāryārtham/
333.026. sa tatra saṃraktacittastayā kanyayā sārdhaṃ maithunamagacchat/
333.027. sa ṛṣirṛddhyā bhraṣṭo dhyānebhyo vañcitaḥ/
333.028. ṛddhiparihīnaḥ sa vipratisārī ātmano duścaritaṃ vigarhāṇastasyāṃ velāyāṃ sāvitrīṃ bhāṣate sma/
333.029. tadyathā--
333.030. bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ/
333.030. tatsaviturvireṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi/
333.030. dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt/
333.031. iti hi brāhmaṇa ajñānaśodhanārthamimameva mantraṃ sa brāhmaṇo divārātraṃ japati sma/
333.032. iyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sāvitrī/
333.032. pūrvajaḥ prajāpatih--
body.translated_text:
333.021. 'What is your maternal <s>gotra</s>?' He replied: '<s>Pārāśarīya</s>.'
333.021. 'Recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (sacred verse).
333.021. How does it go? How many syllables has the <s>Sāvitrī</s>? How many sections? How many feet?'
333.023. 'The <s>Sāvitrī</s> has twenty-four syllables,
333.023. three sections,
333.023. and feet of eight syllables each.'
333.023. 'Pronounce the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.'
333.024. 'Well then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall proclaim the <s>Sāvitrī</s> together with its origin.
333.024. Listen to that.'
333.024. 'Speak, sir.'
333.025. 'Once upon a time, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the past, there was a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) named <s>Vasu</s>.
333.026. He possessed the five supernatural knowledges, was of fierce brilliance and great power, and had attained the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions).
333.026. There he took a girl named <s>Kapilā</s>, the daughter of a <s>Takṣaka</s> (serpent), as his wife.
333.026. With mind inflamed by passion for that maiden, he engaged in sexual intercourse.
333.027. That <s>ṛṣi</s>, fallen from his supernatural powers, was deprived of his <s>dhyānas</s>.
333.028. Bereft of supernatural powers, filled with remorse, condemning his own misconduct, at that very time he uttered the <s>Sāvitrī</s>:
333.029. Namely —
333.030. "<s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ</s>.
333.030. We meditate upon the most excellent splendor of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>;
333.030. may he inspire our thoughts."
333.031. Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, for the purpose of purifying ignorance, that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> recited this very <s>mantra</s> day and night.
333.032. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
333.032. The progenitor <s>Prajāpati</s> was the first-born —

body.text:
334.001. <334>jaṭilastāpaso bhūtvā gahanaṃ vanamāśritaḥ/
334.002. gambhīrāvabhāse tatra hyātmastaporataḥ//90//
body.translated_text:
334.001. 'Having become a <s>jaṭila</s> (matted-hair ascetic), an ascetic, he resorted to a dense forest.
334.002. There, in deep contemplation, he was devoted to self-austerity.' //90//

body.text:
334.003. devasya śreṣṭakaṃ bhojanamupanāmyopaviṣṭa imaṃ mantramajapat/
334.003. iyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ sāvitrī/
334.004. citraṃ hi vaiśyakanyakā/
334.004. atha sā kanyā arthataḥ pravīṇā/
334.004. iyaṃ vaiśyānāṃ sāvitrī/
334.005. atapaḥ sutapaḥ/
334.005. jīvema śaradāṃ śatam/
334.005. paśyema śaradāṃ śatam/
334.005. iyaṃ śūdrāṇāṃ sāvitrī/
334.006. bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ/
334.007. kāmā hi loke paramāḥ prajānāṃ kleśaprahāṇe bhūtā antarāyāḥ/
334.009. tasmādbhavantaḥ prajahantu kāmāṃs tato 'tulaṃ prāpsyatha brahmalokam//91//
body.translated_text:
334.003. 'Offering the best food to the god, having sat down, he recited this <s>mantra</s>.
334.003. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.
334.004. And then, a <s>Vaiśya</s> (merchant-class) maiden — <s>Citrā</s> was her name.
334.004. That maiden was skilled in worldly matters.
334.004. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Vaiśyas</s>.
334.005. "<s>Atapaḥ</s>, <s>Sutapaḥ</s>.
334.005. May we live a hundred autumns.
334.005. May we see a hundred autumns."
334.005. This is the <s>Sāvitrī</s> of the <s>Śūdras</s>.
334.006. <s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ</s>.
334.007. Desires are indeed the highest in the world for living beings, and obstacles to the abandonment of suffering.
334.009. Therefore, let the venerable ones abandon desires; then you shall attain the incomparable <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of <s>Brahmā</s>).' //91//

body.text: 334.011. itīyaṃ brāhmaṇa brahmaṇā sahāpatinā sāvitrī bhāṣitā, pūrvakaiśca samyaksambuddhairabhyanumoditā//
body.translated_text: 334.011. 'Thus, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, this <s>Sāvitrī</s> was spoken by <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> (the Lord Companion), and was approved by the former Perfectly Awakened Ones.'

body.text:
334.013. paṭha bhostriśaṅko nakṣatravaṃśam/
334.013. atha kim? bhoḥ kathayatu bhavān/
334.013. śrūyatām/
334.014. bhoḥ puṣkarasārin, nakṣatravaṃśaṃ kathayiṣyāmi/
334.014. tadyathā--
334.015. kṛttikā rohiṇī mṛgaśirā ārdrā punarvasuḥ puṣyah āśleṣā maghā pūrvaphalgunī uttaraphalgunī hastā citrā svātī viśākhā anurādhā anurādhā jyeṣṭā mūlā pūrvāṣāḍhā uttarāṣāḍhā abhijit śravaṇā dhaniṣṭhā śatabhiṣā pūrvabhādrapadā uttarabhādrapadā revatī aśvinī bharaṇī/
334.017. ityetāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatinakṣatrāṇi//
body.translated_text:
334.013. 'Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lineage of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions).'
334.013. 'Very well, sir. Speak, sir.'
334.013. 'Listen.'
334.014. 'O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall proclaim the lineage of the <s>nakṣatras</s>.
334.014. Namely —
334.015. <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśirā</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūlā</s>, <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>, <s>Śravaṇā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>.
334.017. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>.'

body.text:
334.019. katitārakāṇi katisaṃsthānāni katimuhūrtayogāni kimāhārāṇi kiṃdaivatāni kiṃgotrāṇi?
334.021. kṛttikā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatraṃ ṣaṭtāraṃ kṣurasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ dadhyāhāramagnidaivataṃ vaiśyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
334.022. rohiṇīnakṣatraṃ pañcatārakaṃ śakaṭākṛtisaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ mṛgamāṃsāhāraṃ prajāpatidaivataṃ bhāradvājaṃ gotreṇa/
334.023. mṛgāśirānakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ mṛgaśīrṣasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ phalamūlāhāraṃ somadaivataṃ mṛgāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/
334.024. ārdrānakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcadaśamuhūrtayogaṃ sarpirmaṇḍāhāraṃ sūryadaivataṃ hārītāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
334.026. punarvasunakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padasaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ madhyāhāram aditidaivataṃ vāsiṣṭhaṃ gotreṇa/
334.027. puṣyanakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ vardhamānasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ madhumaṇḍāhāraṃ bṛhaspatidaivatam aupamanyavīyaṃ gotreṇa/
334.028. āśleṣānakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcadaśamuhūrtayogaṃ pāyasabhojanaṃ sarpadaivataṃ maitrāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/
334.029. itīmāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta nakṣatrāṇi pūrvadvārakāṇi//
body.translated_text:
334.019. 'How many stars does each have? What are their configurations? What are their <s>muhūrta</s> (time-unit) conjunctions? What are their foods? What are their deities? What are their <s>gotras</s> (lineages)?'
334.021. '<s>Kṛttikā</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of six stars, razor-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with yogurt as its food, <s>Agni</s> (Fire) as its deity, and <s>Vaiśyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.022. <s>Rohiṇī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of five stars, cart-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with deer-meat as its food, <s>Prajāpati</s> as its deity, and <s>Bhāradvāja</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.023. <s>Mṛgāśirā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, deer-head-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with fruits and roots as its food, <s>Soma</s> as its deity, and <s>Mṛgāyaṇīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.024. <s>Ārdrā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, with clarified butter as its food, <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) as its deity, and <s>Hārītāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.026. <s>Punarvasu</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, foot-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with honey as its food, <s>Aditi</s> as its deity, and <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.027. <s>Puṣya</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, increasing-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with honey-cream as its food, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) as its deity, and <s>Aupamanyavīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.028. <s>Āśleṣā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, with milk-rice as its food, <s>Sarpa</s> (the Serpent) as its deity, and <s>Maitrāyaṇīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
334.029. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the eastern gate.'

body.text: 334.031. maghānakṣatraṃ pañcatāraṃ nadīkubjasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ tilakṛsarāhāraṃ titṛdaivatam <335>piṅgalāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
body.translated_text: 334.031. '<s>Maghā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of five stars, river-bend-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with sesame-rice as its food, <s>Pitṛ</s> (the Ancestors) as its deity, and <s>Piṅgalāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.'

body.text:
335.001. pūrvaphalgunīnakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padakasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ bilvabhojanaṃ bhavadaivataṃ gautamīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.002. uttaraphalgunīnakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ godhūmamatsyāhāramaryamādaivataṃ kauśikaṃ gotreṇa/
335.003. hastanakṣatraṃ pañcatāraṃ hastasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ śyāmākabhojanaṃ sūryadaivataṃ kāśyapaṃ gotreṇa/
335.004. citrānakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ mudgakṛsaraghṛtapūpāhāraṃ tvaṣṭṛdaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.005. svātīnakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcadaśamuhūrtayogaṃ mudgakṛsaraphalāhāraṃ vāyudaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.007. viśākhānakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ viṣāṇasaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ tilapuṣpāhāramindrāgnidaivataṃ śākhāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.008. ityetāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin saptanakṣatrāṇi dakṣiṇadvārakāṇi//
body.translated_text:
335.001. '<s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, foot-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruit as its food, <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) as its deity, and <s>Gautamīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.002. <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, foot-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with wheat and fish as its food, <s>Aryamā</s> as its deity, and <s>Kauśika</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.003. <s>Hastā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of five stars, hand-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with millet as its food, <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) as its deity, and <s>Kāśyapa</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.004. <s>Citrā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with mung-bean rice, ghee, and cakes as its food, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.005. <s>Svātī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, with mung-bean rice and fruits as its food, <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.007. <s>Viśākhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, horn-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with sesame-flower food, <s>Indrāgni</s> (<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>) as its deity, and <s>Śākhāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.008. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the southern gate.'

body.text:
335.009. anurādhānakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ ratnāvalīsaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ surāmāṃsāhāraṃ mitradaivatamālambāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.010. jyeṣṭhānakṣatraṃ tritāram yavamadhyasaṃsthānaṃ pañcadaśamuhūrtayogaṃ śāliyavāgūbhojanamindradaivataṃ dīrghakātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.011. mūlanakṣatraṃ saptatāraṃ vṛścikasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ mūlaphalāhāraṃ nairṛtidaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.012. pūrvāṣāḍhānakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ govikramasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ nyagrodhakaṣāyāhāraṃ toyadaivataṃ darbhakātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.013. uttarāṣāḍhānakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ gajavikramasaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ madhulājāhāraṃ viśvadaivataṃ maudgalāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.015. abhijinnakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ gośīrṣasaṃsthānaṃ ṣaṇmuhūrtayogaṃ vāyvāhāraṃ brahmadaivataṃ brahmāvatīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.016. śravaṇānakṣatraṃ tritāram yavamadhyasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ pakṣimāṃsāhāraṃ viṣṇudaivataṃ kātyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.017. ityetāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta nakṣatrāṇi paścimadvārakāṇi//
body.translated_text:
335.009. '<s>Anurādhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of four stars, jewel-necklace-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with liquor and meat as its food, <s>Mitra</s> (Friend) as its deity, and <s>Ālambāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.010. <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, barley-grain-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, with rice-gruel as its food, <s>Indra</s> as its deity, and <s>Dīrghakātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.011. <s>Mūla</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of seven stars, scorpion-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with roots and fruits as its food, <s>Nirṛti</s> (Destruction) as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.012. <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of four stars, cow-stride-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with banyan-tree decoction as its food, <s>Toya</s> (Water) as its deity, and <s>Darbhakātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.013. <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of four stars, elephant-stride-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with honey and parched grain as its food, <s>Viśva</s> (the All-Gods) as its deity, and <s>Maudgalāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.015. <s>Abhijit</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, bull-head-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of six <s>muhūrtas</s>, with air as its food, <s>Brahmā</s> as its deity, and <s>Brahmāvatīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.016. <s>Śravaṇā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, barley-grain-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with bird-meat as its food, <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity, and <s>Kātyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.017. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the western gate.'

body.text:
335.019. dhaniṣṭhānakṣatraṃ catustāraṃ śakunasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ kulatthapūpāhāraṃ vasudaivataṃ kauṇḍinyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.020. śatabhiṣānakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcadaśamuhūrtayogam yavāgubhojanaṃ varuṇadaivataṃ tāṇḍyāyanīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.021. pūrvabhādrapadānakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padakasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ māṃsarudhirāhāramahirbudhnyadaivataṃ jātūkarṇyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.022. uttarabhādrapadānakṣatraṃ dvitāraṃ padakasaṃsthānaṃ pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ māṃsāhāram aryamādaivataṃ dhyānadrāhyāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.024. revatīnakṣatramekatāraṃ tilakasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ madhupāyasabhojanaṃ gandharvadaivataṃ maitrāyaṇīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.026. bharaṇīnakṣatraṃ tritāraṃ bhagasaṃsthānaṃ triṃśanmuhūrtayogaṃ tilataṇḍulāhāram yamadaivataṃ bhārgavīyaṃ gotreṇa/
335.027. ityetāni bhoḥ puṣkarasārin sapta nakṣatrāṇi uttaradvārakāṇi//
body.translated_text:
335.019. '<s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of four stars, bird-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with horse-gram cakes as its food, <s>Vasu</s> (the Vasus) as its deity, and <s>Kauṇḍinyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.020. <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s>, with barley-gruel as its food, <s>Varuṇa</s> as its deity, and <s>Tāṇḍyāyanīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.021. <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, foot-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with flesh and blood as its food, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> (the Serpent of the Deep) as its deity, and <s>Jātūkarṇya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.022. <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of two stars, foot-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s>, with meat as its food, <s>Aryamā</s> as its deity, and <s>Dhyānadrāhyāyaṇīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.024. <s>Revatī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of one star, mole-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with honey-milk-rice as its food, <s>Gandharva</s> as its deity, and <s>Maitrāyaṇīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.026. <s>Bharaṇī</s> is a <s>nakṣatra</s> of three stars, pudendum-shaped in configuration, with a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>, with sesame and rice as its food, <s>Yama</s> (Death) as its deity, and <s>Bhārgavīya</s> by <s>gotra</s>.
335.027. These, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, are the seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the northern gate.'

body.text:
335.028. amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭaviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ ṣaṇnakṣatrāṇi pañcacatvāriṃśanmuhūrtayogāni/
335.029. tadyathā--rohiṇī punarvasu uttaraphalgunī viśākhā uttarāṣāḍhā uttarabhādrapadā ceti/
335.030. pañcanakṣatrāṇi pañcadaśamuhūrtayogāni/
335.030. tadyathā--ārdrā āśleṣā svātī jyeṣṭhā śatabhiṣā ceti/
335.031. eko 'bhijit ṣaṇmuhūrtayogam/
335.031. avaśiṣṭāni triṃśanmuhūrtayogāni//
body.translated_text:
335.028. 'Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, six <s>nakṣatras</s> have a conjunction of forty-five <s>muhūrtas</s> —
335.029. namely, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, and <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>.
335.030. Five <s>nakṣatras</s> have a conjunction of fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s> —
335.030. namely, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>.
335.031. One, <s>Abhijit</s>, has a conjunction of six <s>muhūrtas</s>.
335.031. The remaining ones have a conjunction of thirty <s>muhūrtas</s>.'

body.text:
336.001. <336>amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ pūrvadvārikāṇāṃ kṛttikā prathamā nāmā, āśleṣā paścimā nāma/
336.002. amīṣāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ dakṣiṇadvārīkāṇāṃ maghā prathamā nāma, viśākhā paścimāa nāma/
336.003. amīṣāṃ paścimadvārikāṇāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāmanurādhā prathamā nāma, śravaṇā paścimā nāma/
336.004. amīṣāṃ saptānāṃ nakṣatrāṇāmuttaradvārikāṇāṃ dhaniṣṭhā prathamā nāma, bharaṇī paścimā nāma//
body.translated_text:
336.001. 'Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the eastern gate, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s> is named the first, and <s>Āśleṣā</s> the last.
336.002. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the southern gate, <s>Maghā</s> is named the first, and <s>Viśākhā</s> the last.
336.003. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the western gate, <s>Anurādhā</s> is named the first, and <s>Śravaṇā</s> the last.
336.004. Of these seven <s>nakṣatras</s> of the northern gate, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is named the first, and <s>Bharaṇī</s> the last.'

body.text:
336.006. amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ sapta balāni/
336.006. katamāni sapta? yaduta trīṇi pūrvāṇi viśākhānurādhā punarvasuḥ punarvasuḥ svātiśca/
336.007. triṇi dāruṇāni/
336.007. ārdrā āśleṣā bharaṇī ceti/
336.008. catvāri saṃmānanīyāni/
336.008. yaduta trīṇi uttarāṇi rohiṇī ceti/
336.008. pañca mṛdukāni/
336.009. śravaṇā dhaniṣṭhā śatabhiṣā jyeṣṭhā mūlā iti/
336.009. pañca dhāraṇīyāni/
336.009. hastā citrā āśleṣā maghā abhijicceti/
336.010. catvāri kṣiprakaraṇīyāni/
336.010. yaduta kṛttikā mṛgaśirā puṣyā aśvinī ceti//
body.translated_text:
336.006. 'Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, there are seven powers.
336.006. Which seven? Three are auspicious — <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, and <s>Svātī</s>.
336.007. Three are fierce —
336.007. <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>.
336.008. Four are to be honored —
336.008. namely, the three <s>Uttarā</s> <s>nakṣatras</s> and <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
336.008. Five are gentle —
336.009. <s>Śravaṇā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Mūlā</s>.
336.009. Five are to be sustained —
336.009. <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and <s>Abhijit</s>.
336.010. Four are for swift action —
336.010. namely, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Mṛgaśirā</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Aśvinī</s>.'

body.text:
336.011. amīṣāṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭhāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ trayo yogā bhavanti--ṛṣabhānusārī yogaḥ/
336.012. vatsānusārī yogaḥ/
336.012. yuganaddho yogaḥ/
336.012. tatra nakṣatram yadi purastādgacchati candraśca pṛṣṭhataḥ, ayamucyate ṛṣabhānusārī yoga iti/
336.013. yaduta candraḥ purastād gacchati nakṣatraṃ ca pṛṣṭhataḥ, tadā bhavati vatsānusārī yogaḥ/
336.014. yadi punaścandro nakṣatraṃ cobhau samau yugapad gacchataḥ, tadāyamucyate yoga iti//
body.translated_text:
336.011. 'Of these twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, there are three conjunctions (<s>yogas</s>) —
336.012. the bull-following conjunction,
336.012. the calf-following conjunction,
336.012. and the yoked conjunction.
336.012. When the <s>nakṣatra</s> goes in front and the moon follows behind, this is called the bull-following conjunction.
336.013. When the moon goes in front and the <s>nakṣatra</s> follows behind, then it is the calf-following conjunction.
336.014. When the moon and the <s>nakṣatra</s> both go together equally and simultaneously, then this is called the yoked conjunction.'

body.text:
336.016. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin grahān pravakṣyāmi/
336.016. tacchrūyatām/
336.016. tadyathā śukro bṛhaspatiḥ śanaiścaro budho 'ṅgārakaḥ sūryastārādhipatiśceti//
body.translated_text:
336.016. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall proclaim the planets.
336.016. Listen to that.
336.016. Namely: <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), and the Lord of the Stars (the Moon).'

body.text:
336.018. evaṃ viparivartamāne loke nakṣatreṣu pravibhakteṣu kathaṃ rātridivasānāṃ hrāso vṛddhiśca bhavati? taducyate/
336.019. hemantānāṃ dvitīye māsi rohiṇyāmaṣṭabhyāṃ dvādaśamuhūrto divaso bhavati/
336.020. aṣṭādaśamuhūrtā rātriḥ/
336.020. grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse rohiṇyāmaṣṭabhyāmaṣṭādaśamuhūrto divaso bhavati/
336.021. dvādaśamuhūrto rātriḥ/
336.021. varṣāṇāṃ paścime māse rohiṇyāmaṣṭabhyāṃ caturdaśamuhūrto divase bhavati/
336.022. ṣoḍaśamuhūrtā rātriḥ//
body.translated_text:
336.018. 'As the world revolves and the <s>nakṣatras</s> are distributed, how do the day and night increase and decrease? This is explained:
336.019. In the second month of winter, on the eighth day from <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day is twelve <s>muhūrtas</s> long.
336.020. The night is eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s>.
336.020. In the last month of summer, on the eighth day from <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day is eighteen <s>muhūrtas</s> long.
336.021. The night is twelve <s>muhūrtas</s>.
336.021. In the last month of the rains, on the eighth day from <s>Rohiṇī</s>, the day is fourteen <s>muhūrtas</s>.
336.022. The night is sixteen <s>muhūrtas</s>.'

body.text:
336.023. kiṃ bhostriśaṅko rātridivasānāṃ prasthānam? divasānudivasam/
336.023. kiṃ pakṣasya prasthānam? pratipad/
336.024. kiṃ saṃvatsarasya prasthānam? pauṣaḥ/
336.024. kimṛtūnāṃ prasthānam? prāvṛṭ//
body.translated_text:
336.023. 'What, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, is the starting point of night and day? Day after day.
336.023. What is the starting point of the fortnight? The first day (<s>pratipad</s>).
336.024. What is the starting point of the year? The month of <s>Pauṣa</s>.
336.024. What is the starting point of the seasons? The rainy season (<s>Prāvṛṭ</s>).'

body.text:
336.025. kiṃ bhostriśaṅko kṣaṇasya parimāṇam? kiṃ lavāsya? kiṃ muhūrtasya? tadyathā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin striyā nātidīrghahrasvaḥ kartinyāḥ sūtrodyāmaḥ/
336.026. evaṃ dīrghastatkṣaṇam/
336.026. viṃśatyadhikaṃ tatkṣaṇaśatamekaḥ kṣaṇaḥ/
336.027. triṃśallavā eko muhūrtaḥ/
336.027. etena kramasambandhena triṃśanmuhūrtamekaṃ rātridivasamanumīyate/
336.028. teṣāṃ muhūrtānāmimāni nāmāni bhavanti--
336.029. āditya udayati ṣaṇṇavatipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ caturojā nāma muhūrto bhavati/
336.029. ṣaṣṭipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ śveto nāma muhūrto bhavati/
336.030. dvādaśapauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ samṛddho nāma muhūrto bhavati/
336.031. ṣaṭpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ śarapathe nāma muhūrto bhavati/
336.031. pañcapauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāmatisamṛddho<337> nāma muhūrto bhavati/
body.translated_text:
336.025. 'What, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, is the measure of an instant (<s>kṣaṇa</s>)? What is that of a <s>lava</s>? What is that of a <s>muhūrta</s>? As follows, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>: the length of thread drawn out by a woman spinner, neither too long nor too short —
336.026. that long is one <s>tatkṣaṇa</s> (sub-instant).
336.026. One hundred and twenty <s>tatkṣaṇas</s> make one <s>kṣaṇa</s> (instant).
336.027. Thirty <s>lavas</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.
336.027. By this sequential relation, thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> are reckoned as one day-and-night.
336.028. These <s>muhūrtas</s> have the following names:
336.029. When the sun rises, at a shadow of ninety-six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Caturojā</s> (Four-Vigor).
336.029. At a shadow of sixty man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Śveta</s> (White).
336.030. At a shadow of twelve man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Samṛddha</s> (Prosperous).
336.031. At a shadow of six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Śarapatha</s> (Arrow-Path).
336.031. At a shadow of five man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Atisamṛddha</s> (Most Prosperous).'

body.text:
337.001. catuḥpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāmudgato nāma muhūrto bhavati/
337.002. tripauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sumukho nāma muhūrto bhavati/
337.002. sthite madhyāhne vajrako nāma muhūrto bhavati/
337.003. parivṛto madhyāhne tripuruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ rohito nāma muhūrto bhavati/
337.003. catuḥpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ balo muhūrtaḥ/
337.004. pañcapauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ vijayo nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.004. ṣaṭpauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sarvaraso nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.005. dvādaśapauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ vasur nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.005. ṣaṣṭipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ sundaro nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.006. avataramāṇa āditye ṣaṇṇavatipauruṣāyāṃ chāyāyāṃ parabhayo nāma muhūrto bhavati/
337.007. ityetāni divasasya muhūrtāni//
body.translated_text:
337.001. 'At a shadow of four man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Udgata</s> (Risen).
337.002. At a shadow of three man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Sumukha</s> (Fair-Faced).
337.002. At midday, when the shadow is stationary, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Vajraka</s> (Thunderbolt).
337.003. When midday has turned, at a shadow of three man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Rohita</s> (Red).
337.003. At a shadow of four man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is <s>Bala</s> (Strength).
337.004. At a shadow of five man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Vijaya</s> (Victory).
337.004. At a shadow of six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Sarvarasa</s> (All-Flavored).
337.005. At a shadow of twelve man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Vasu</s> (Wealth).
337.005. At a shadow of sixty man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Sundara</s> (Beautiful).
337.006. As the sun sets, at a shadow of ninety-six man-lengths, the <s>muhūrta</s> is called <s>Parabhaya</s> (Supreme Fear).
337.007. These are the <s>muhūrtas</s> of the day.'

body.text:
337.008. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin rātryā muhūrtāni vyākhyāsyāmi/
337.008. astaṃgata āditye raudro nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.009. tatastārāvacaro nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.009. samyamo nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.009. sāmpraiyako nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.010. ananto nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.010. gardabho nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.010. rākṣaso nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.010. sthite 'rdharātre 'vayavo nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.011. atikrānte 'rdharātre brahmā nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.011. ditir nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.011. arko nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.012. vidhamano nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.012. āgneyo nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.012. ātapāgnir nāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.013. abhijinnāma muhūrtaḥ/
337.013. ityetāni rātrermuhūrtanāmāni/
337.013. iti bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn imāni triṃśanmuhūrtāni yairahorātraṃ prajñāyate//

337.015. tatkṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇo lavo muhūrtaḥ/
337.015. tatra triṃśatitamo bhāgo muhūrtasya lavaḥ/
337.015. ṣaṣṭitamo bhāgo lavasya kṣaṇaḥ/
337.016. viṃśatyuttarabhāgaśataṃ kṣaṇasya tatkṣaṇaḥ/
337.016. tadyathā striyā nātidīrghahrasvaḥ kartinyāḥ sūtrodyāmaḥ/
337.017. evaṃ dīrghastatkṣaṇaḥ/
337.017. viṃśatyuttarakṣaṇaśataṃ tatkṣaṇasyaikaḥ kṣaṇaḥ/
337.017. ṣaṣṭiḥ kṣaṇā eko lavaḥ/
337.018. triṃśallavā eko muhūrtaḥ/
337.018. etena kramayogena triṃśanmuhūrtamekamahorātram/
337.019. triṃśadahorātrāṇyeko māsaḥ/
337.019. dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ/
337.019. caturojāḥ śvetaḥ samṛddhaḥ śarapatho 'tisamṛddha udgataḥ sumukho vajrako rohito balo vijayaḥ sarvaraso vasuḥ sundaraḥ parabhayaḥ/
337.020. raudrastārāvacaraḥ samyamaḥ sāmpraiyako 'nanto gardabho rākṣaso 'vayavo brahmā ditirarko vidhamano āgneya ātapāgnirabhijit/
337.022. itīmāni muhūrtānāṃ nāmāni//
body.translated_text:
337.015. 'Sub-instant (<s>tatkṣaṇa</s>), instant (<s>kṣaṇa</s>), <s>lava</s>, <s>muhūrta</s> —
337.015. therein, the thirtieth part of a <s>muhūrta</s> is a <s>lava</s>;
337.015. the sixtieth part of a <s>lava</s> is a <s>kṣaṇa</s>;
337.016. the one-hundred-and-twentieth part of a <s>kṣaṇa</s> is a <s>tatkṣaṇa</s>.
337.016. As for a woman spinner, neither too long nor too short — the length of thread drawn out —
337.017. that long is one <s>tatkṣaṇa</s>.
337.017. One hundred and twenty <s>tatkṣaṇas</s> make one <s>kṣaṇa</s>.
337.017. Sixty <s>kṣaṇas</s> make one <s>lava</s>.
337.018. Thirty <s>lavas</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.
337.018. By this sequential connection, thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> make one day-and-night.
337.019. Thirty day-and-nights make one month.
337.019. Twelve months make one year.
337.019. <s>Caturojā</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Samṛddha</s>, <s>Śarapatha</s>, <s>Atisamṛddha</s>, <s>Udgata</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Vajraka</s>, <s>Rohita</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Sarvarasa</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Sundara</s>, <s>Parabhaya</s>;
337.020. <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Tārāvacara</s>, <s>Samyama</s>, <s>Sāmpraiyaka</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Gardabha</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, <s>Avayava</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Arka</s>, <s>Vidhamana</s>, <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Ātapāgni</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>.
337.022. These are the names of the <s>muhūrtas</s>.'

body.text:
337.023. kālotpattimapi te brāhmaṇa vakṣyāmi, śṛṇu--
337.024. kālasya kiṃ pramāṇamiti taducyate/
337.024. dvāvakṣinimeṣāveko lavaḥ/
337.024. aṣṭau lavā ekā kāṣṭhā/
337.025. ṣoḍaśa kāṣṭhā ekā kalā/
337.025. kalānāṃ triṃśadekā nāḍikā/
337.025. tatra dve nāḍike eko muhūrtaḥ//
body.translated_text:
337.023. 'I shall also tell you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of time — listen:
337.024. What is the measure of time? This is explained:
337.024. Two winks of the eye make one <s>lava</s>.
337.024. Eight <s>lavas</s> make one <s>kāṣṭhā</s>.
337.025. Sixteen <s>kāṣṭhās</s> make one <s>kalā</s>.
337.025. Thirty <s>kalās</s> make one <s>nāḍikā</s>.
337.025. Therein, two <s>nāḍikās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.'

body.text:
337.026. nāḍikāyāḥ punaḥ kiṃ pramāṇam? taducyate--
337.027. droṇaṃ salilasyaikam/
337.027. tadvaraṇato dve palaśate bhavataḥ/
337.027. nālikāchidrasya kiṃ pramāṇam? suvarṇamātram/
337.028. upari caturaṅgalā suvarṇaśalākā kartavyā/
337.028. vṛttaparimaṇḍalā samantāccaturasrā āyatā/
337.029. yadā caivaṃ śīryeta tat toyaṃ ghaṭasya tadaikā nāḍikā/
337.029. etena nāḍikāpramāṇena vibhakte dve nāḍike eko muhūrtaḥ/
337.030. etena bho brāhmaṇa triṃśanṃhūrtāḥ, yai rātridivasā anumīyanta iti//
body.translated_text:
337.026. What then is the measure of a <s>nāḍikā</s> (time-unit)? It is stated:
337.027. One <s>droṇa</s> (measure) of water.
337.027. By weight, that amounts to two hundred <s>palas</s>.
337.027. What is the measure of the hole of the <s>nālikā</s> (water-clock)? The size of a gold piece.
337.028. Above, a gold rod four finger-breadths long should be made,
337.028. round and circular, square on all sides, and elongated.
337.029. When the water of the vessel drains away thus, that is one <s>nāḍikā</s>.
337.029. By this measure of a <s>nāḍikā</s>, when divided, two <s>nāḍikās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.
337.030. By this, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> are measured, by which a day and night are reckoned.

body.text:
338.001. <338>tataḥ ṣoḍaśa nimeṣā ekā kāṣṭhā/
338.001. ṣoḍaśa kāṣṭhā ekā kalā/
338.001. ṣaṣṭiḥ kalā eko muhūrtaḥ/
338.002. triṃśanmuhūrtā ekamahorātram/
338.002. triṃśadahorātrāṇyeko māsaḥ/
338.002. dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvatsaraḥ//
body.translated_text:
338.001. Then: sixteen eye-blinks make one <s>kāṣṭhā</s>.
338.001. Sixteen <s>kāṣṭhās</s> make one <s>kalā</s>.
338.001. Sixty <s>kalās</s> make one <s>muhūrta</s>.
338.002. Thirty <s>muhūrtas</s> make one day-and-night.
338.002. Thirty day-and-nights make one month.
338.002. Twelve months make one year.

body.text:
338.003. etena punarakṣinimeṣeṇa ṣoḍaśakoṭyo 'ṣṭapañcāśañca śatasahasrāṇi aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi sa evaṃ māpitaḥ/
338.004. tacca brāhmaṇa kālotpattirvyākhyātā//
body.translated_text:
338.003. Furthermore, by this eye-blink measure, sixteen <s>koṭis</s> and fifty-eight hundred-thousands and eighty-eight thousand — thus it has been calculated.
338.004. And thus, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of time-measurement has been explained.

body.text:
338.005. śṛṇu brāhmaṇa trośayojanānāmutpattim/
338.006. vātāyanarajāṃsi sapta, śaśakrajaḥ/
338.006. sapta śaśakarajāṃsi eḍakarajaḥ/
338.007. sapta eḍakarajāṃsi ekaṃ gorajaḥ/
338.007. sapta gorajāṃsi ekā yūkā/
338.007. sapta yūkā ekā likṣā/
338.008. sapta likṣā eko yavaḥ/
338.008. sapta yavā ekāṅguliḥ/
338.008. dvādaśāṅgulayo vitastiḥ/
338.008. dve vitastī eko hastaḥ/
338.009. catvāro hastā ekaṃ dhanuḥ/
338.009. dhanuḥsahasramekaḥ krośaḥ/
338.009. catvāraḥ krośā eko māgadhayojanaḥ/
338.010. yojanasya pramāṇaṃ piṇḍitam/
338.010. paramāṇūnāṃ koṭiśatasahasrāṇi caturviṃśatiścaikonatriṃśatkoṭisahasrāṇi dvādaśa ca śatasahasrāṇi/
338.011. evaṃ māpitam yojanamiti//
body.translated_text:
338.005. Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the <s>krośa</s> and <s>yojana</s> measures.
338.006. Seven window-dust motes make one hare-dust.
338.006. Seven hare-dusts make one sheep-dust.
338.007. Seven sheep-dusts make one cow-dust.
338.007. Seven cow-dusts make one louse.
338.007. Seven lice make one nit.
338.008. Seven nits make one barley-grain.
338.008. Seven barley-grains make one finger-breadth.
338.008. Twelve finger-breadths make one span.
338.008. Two spans make one cubit.
338.009. Four cubits make one bow-length.
338.009. A thousand bow-lengths make one <s>krośa</s>.
338.009. Four <s>krośas</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>yojana</s>.
338.010. The measure of a <s>yojana</s> in total:
338.010. one hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of atoms, plus twenty-four, and twenty-nine thousand <s>koṭis</s>, and twelve hundred-thousands.
338.011. Thus has the <s>yojana</s> been measured.

body.text:
338.012. śṛṇu brāhmaṇa suvarṇasya parimāṇotpattim/
338.012. tatkathayatu bhavān--
338.013. dvādaśa yavā māṣakaḥ/
338.013. ṣoḍaśa māṣakā ekaḥ karṣaḥ/
338.013. suvarṇasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitamiti/
338.014. dve koṭī pañcaviṃśatiśca sahasrāṇi pañcaśatānyaṣṭau ca paramāṇavaḥ/
338.014. evaṃ māpitā brāhmaṇa suvarṇasya parimāṇotpattiḥ//
body.translated_text:
338.012. Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the measure of gold.
338.012. Let it be stated:
338.013. Twelve barley-grains make one <s>māṣaka</s>.
338.013. Sixteen <s>māṣakas</s> make one <s>karṣa</s>.
338.013. The measure of gold in total:
338.014. two <s>koṭis</s> and twenty-five thousand, five hundred and eight atoms.
338.014. Thus, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the measure of gold has been calculated.

body.text:
338.016. śṛṇu brāhmaṇa palapramāṇam/
338.016. catuḥṣaṣṭimāṣakāḥ palaṃ māgadhakam/
338.016. māgadhakayā tulayā palasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitam/
338.017. paramāṇūnāmaṣṭakoṭayaḥ saptacatvāriṃśacca śatasahasrāṇi sapta ca sahasrāṇi dve śate aśītiśca paramāṇavaḥ/
338.018. evaṃ māpitaṃ brāhmaṇa palasya parimāṇamiti/
338.019. śṛṇu brāhmaṇa rasaparimāṇasyotpattim/
338.019. caturviṃśatipalāni māgadhakaḥ prasthaḥ/
338.019. tat rasaparimāṇam/
338.020. māgadhakayā tulayā prasthasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitam/
338.020. dve koṭiśate tisraśca koṭaya ekonatriṃśacca śatasahasrāṇi catuḥsaptatisahasrāṇi sapta ca śatāni viṃśatiśca paramāṇavaḥ/
338.022. evaṃ māpitā brāhmaṇa rasamānasyotpattiriti//
body.translated_text:
338.016. Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the measure of a <s>pala</s> (weight-unit).
338.016. Sixty-four <s>māṣakas</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>pala</s>.
338.016. By the <s>Māgadha</s> balance, the measure of a <s>pala</s> in total:
338.017. eight <s>koṭis</s> of atoms, forty-seven hundred-thousands, seven thousand, two hundred, and eighty atoms.
338.018. Thus, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the measure of a <s>pala</s> has been calculated.
338.019. Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the measure of liquid.
338.019. Twenty-four <s>palas</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>prastha</s>.
338.019. That is the liquid measure.
338.020. By the <s>Māgadha</s> balance, the measure of a <s>prastha</s> in total:
338.020. two hundred <s>koṭis</s> and three <s>koṭis</s>, twenty-nine hundred-thousands, seventy-four thousand, seven hundred and twenty atoms.
338.022. Thus, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the measure of liquid has been calculated.

body.text:
338.023. śṛṇu brāhmaṇa dhānyaparimāṇasyotpattim/
338.023. ekonatriṃśatipalānyekakarṣeṇonāni māgadhaḥ prasthaḥ/
338.024. māpitaṃ dhānyaparimāṇam/
338.024. māgadhakayā tulayā prasthasya parimāṇaṃ piṇḍitam/
338.024. koṭiśatamaṣṭapañcāśacca koṭayo dviraśītiśca śatāshasrāṇi ekaṣaṣṭiśca sahasrāṇi pañcaśatāni triṃśacca paramāṇavaḥ/
338.026. evaṃ māpitaṃ brāhmaṇa dhānyasya parimāṇamiti//
body.translated_text:
338.023. Hear, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the origin of the grain measure.
338.023. Twenty-nine <s>palas</s> less one <s>karṣa</s> make one <s>Māgadha</s> <s>prastha</s>.
338.024. The grain measure has been calculated.
338.024. By the <s>Māgadha</s> balance, the measure of a <s>prastha</s> in total:
338.024. one hundred <s>koṭis</s>, fifty-eight <s>koṭis</s>, eighty-two hundred-thousands, sixty-one thousand, five hundred and thirty atoms.
338.026. Thus, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the grain measure has been calculated.

body.text:
338.027. paṭha bhostriśaṅko nakṣatravyākaraṇaṃ nāmādhyāyam/
338.027. atha khalu bho brāhmaṇa nakṣatravyākaraṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi tacchrūyatām/
338.028. kathayatu bhavān--
338.029. kṛttikāsu jāto mānavo yaśasvī bhavati/
338.029. rohiṇyāṃ jātaḥ subhago bhavati bhogavāṃśca/
338.030. mṛgaśirasi jāto yuddhārthī bhavati/
338.030. ārdrāyāṃ jāta utso 'nnapānānāṃ bhavati/
338.031. punarvasau jāto bhavati gorakṣaśca/
338.031. puṣye jātaḥ śīlavān bhavati/
338.031. āśleṣāyām <339>jātaḥ kāmuko bhavati/
body.translated_text:
338.027. 'Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called "Explanation of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>" (Lunar Mansions).'
338.027. 'Now then, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, I shall expound the chapter called "Explanation of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>" — let it be heard.'
338.028. 'Let it be stated.'
338.029. 'One born under <s>Kṛttikā</s> becomes renowned.
338.029. One born under <s>Rohiṇī</s> becomes fortunate and wealthy.
338.030. One born under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> becomes a lover of battle.
338.030. One born under <s>Ārdrā</s> becomes a source of food and drink.
338.031. One born under <s>Punarvasu</s> becomes a protector of cattle.
338.031. One born under <s>Puṣya</s> becomes virtuous.
338.031. One born under <s>Āśleṣā</s> becomes lustful.

body.text:
339.001. maghāyāṃ jāto matimān bhavati, mahātmā ca/
339.001. pūrvaphalgunyāṃ jāto 'lpāyuṣko bhavati/
339.002. uttaraphalgunyāṃ jāta upavāsaśīlo bhavati, svargaparāyaṇaśca/
339.003. haste jātaścauro bhavati/
339.003. citrāyāṃ jāto nṛtyagītakuśalo bhavati, ābharaṇavidhijñaśca/
339.004. svātyāṃ jāto gaṇako bhavati, gaṇakamahāmātro vā/
339.004. viśākhāyāṃ jāto rājabhaṭo bhavati/
339.005. anurādhāyāṃ jāto vāṇijako bhavati sārthikaḥ/
339.005. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ jāto 'lpāyuṣko bhavati, alpabhogaśca/
339.006. mūle jātaḥ putravān bhavati, yaśasvī ca/
339.006. pūrvāṣāḍhāyāṃ jāto yogācāro bhavati/
339.007. uttarāṣāḍhāyāṃ jāto bhakteśvaraḥ kulīnaśca bhavati/
339.007. abhijiti jātaḥ kīrtimān puruṣo bhavati/
339.008. śravaṇe jāto rājapūrjito bhavati/
339.008. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ jāto dhanāḍhyo bhavati/
339.008. śatabhiṣāyāṃ jāto mūliko bhavati/
339.009. pūrvabhādrapadāyāṃ jātaścaurasenāpatirbhavati/
339.009. uttarabhādrapadāyāṃ jāto gandhiko bhavati, gandharvaśca/
339.010. revatyāṃ jāto nāviko bhavati/
339.010. aśvinyāṃ jāto 'śvavāṇijako bhavati/
339.011. bharaṇyāṃ jāto vadhyaghātako bhavati/
339.011. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatravyākaraṇo nāma//
body.translated_text:
339.001. One born under <s>Maghā</s> becomes wise and great-souled.
339.001. One born under <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> becomes short-lived.
339.002. One born under <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> becomes devoted to fasting and destined for heaven.
339.003. One born under <s>Hasta</s> becomes a thief.
339.003. One born under <s>Citrā</s> becomes skilled in dance and song, and knowledgeable in the art of ornaments.
339.004. One born under <s>Svātī</s> becomes a reckoner or a chief accountant.
339.004. One born under <s>Viśākhā</s> becomes a royal officer.
339.005. One born under <s>Anurādhā</s> becomes a merchant and caravan-leader.
339.005. One born under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> becomes short-lived and of meager enjoyments.
339.006. One born under <s>Mūla</s> becomes endowed with sons and fame.
339.006. One born under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> becomes a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>.
339.007. One born under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> becomes a lord of provisions and of noble birth.
339.007. One born under <s>Abhijit</s> becomes a person of great fame.
339.008. One born under <s>Śravaṇa</s> becomes honored by the king.
339.008. One born under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> becomes rich in wealth.
339.008. One born under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> becomes a herbalist.
339.009. One born under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> becomes a chief of thieves.
339.009. One born under <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> becomes a perfumer and musician.
339.010. One born under <s>Revatī</s> becomes a boatman.
339.010. One born under <s>Aśvinī</s> becomes a horse-trader.
339.011. One born under <s>Bharaṇī</s> becomes an executioner.
339.011. This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "Explanation of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>."

body.text:
339.012. paṭha bhostriśaṅko nakṣatranirdeśaṃ nāmādhyāyam/
339.012. atha bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatranirdeśaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
339.013. tacchrūyatām/
339.013. kathayatu bhavān--
339.014. kṛttikāsu niviṣṭaṃ vai nagaraṃ jvalati śriyā/
339.015. prabhūtaratnojjvalaṃ caivaṃ tannagaraṃ vinirdiśet//92//
body.translated_text:
339.012. 'Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called "Description of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>."'
339.012. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called "Description of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>."'
339.013. 'Let it be heard.'
339.013. 'Let it be stated.'
339.014. 'A city established under <s>Kṛttikā</s> blazes with glory,
339.015. ablaze with abundant jewels — thus shall that city be described.' //92//

body.text:
339.016. rohiṇyāṃ tu niviṣṭaṃ vai nagaraṃ tad vinirdiśet/
339.017. dhārmiko 'tra jano bhūyātprabhūtadhanasaṃcayaḥ/
339.018. vidyāprakṛtisampannaḥ svadārābhirato 'pi ca//93//
body.translated_text:
339.016. 'A city established under <s>Rohiṇī</s> shall be described thus:
339.017. the people there are righteous, with great accumulations of wealth,
339.018. endowed with learning and good character, and devoted to their own wives.' //93//

body.text:
339.019. mṛgaśīrṣe niviṣṭaṃ tu strībhirgobhirdhanaistathā/
339.020. mālyabhogaiśca saṃkīrṇamadbhutaiśca puraskṛtam//94//
body.translated_text:
339.019. 'One established under <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s> is teeming with women, cattle, and wealth,
339.020. filled with garlands and enjoyments, and adorned with wondrous things.' //94//

body.text:
339.021. ārdrāyāṃ matsyamāṃsāni bhakṣyabhojyadhanāni ca/
339.022. bhavanti krūrapuruṣā mūrkhaprakṛtayaḥ pure//95//
body.translated_text:
339.021. 'Under <s>Ārdrā</s>, there are fish and meat, food, drink, and wealth,
339.022. but the people in the city are cruel, and foolish by nature.' //95//

body.text:
339.023. punarvasau niviṣḍe tu nagaraṃ dīpyate śriyā/
339.024. prabhūtadhanadhānyaṃ ca bhūtvā cāpi viniśyati//96//
body.translated_text:
339.023. 'A city established under <s>Punarvasu</s> blazes with glory,
339.024. abounding in wealth and grain, but eventually it also perishes.' //96//

body.text:
339.025. śrīmatpuṣye niviṣṭe tu prajā duṣṭā prasīdati/
339.026. yuktāḥ śriyā ca dharmiṣḍhāstathaiva cirajīvinaḥ//97//
body.translated_text:
339.025. 'Under the glorious <s>Puṣya</s>, even wicked people become calm;
339.026. they are endowed with prosperity and righteous, and also long-lived.' //97//

body.text:
339.027. tejasvinaśca dīrghāyurdhanadhānyarasānvitāḥ/
339.028. vanaspatistathā kṣipraṃ puṣyettatra punaḥ punaḥ//98//
body.translated_text:
339.027. 'They are radiant, long-lived, endowed with wealth, grain, and flavors;
339.028. and trees there flourish swiftly, again and again.' //98//

body.text:
339.029. āśleṣāyāṃ niviṣṭe tu durbhagāḥ kalahapriyāḥ/
339.030. duḥśīlā duḥkhabhājaśca nivasanti narādhamāḥ//99//
body.translated_text:
339.029. 'Under <s>Āśleṣā</s>, the people are unfortunate and quarrelsome;
339.030. the lowest of men dwell there — of bad conduct and destined for suffering.' //99//

body.text:
339.031. maghāyāṃ ca niviṣṭe tu vidyāvanto mahādhanāḥ/
339.032. svadārābhiratā martyā jāyante suparākramāḥ//100//
body.translated_text:
339.031. 'Under <s>Maghā</s>, they are learned, of great wealth,
339.032. devoted to their own wives, and mortals of great prowess are born there.' //100//

body.text:
340.001. <340>phālgunyāṃ tu striyo mālyaṃ bhojanācchādanaṃ śubham/
340.002. gandhopetāni dhānyāni niviṣṭe nagare bhavet//101//
body.translated_text:
340.001. 'Under <s>Phalgunī</s>, there are women, garlands, fine food and clothing,
340.002. and grains accompanied by perfumes in a city so established.' //101//

body.text:
340.003. uttarāyāṃ tu phalgunyāṃ dhānyāni ca dhanāni ca/
340.004. mūrkhā janā strībhir niviṣṭe nagare bhavet//102//
body.translated_text:
340.003. 'Under <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, there are grains and wealth,
340.004. but the people are foolish with regard to women, in a city so established.' //102//

body.text:
340.005. haste ca viniviṣṭe tu vidyāvanto mahādhanāḥ/
340.006. parasparaṃ ca rucitaṃ śayanaṃ nagare bhavet//103//
body.translated_text:
340.005. 'Under <s>Hasta</s>, the people are learned, of great wealth,
340.006. with pleasant lodgings among themselves in the city.' //103//

body.text:
340.007. citrāyāṃ ca niviṣṭe tu strījitāḥ sarvamānavāḥ/
340.008. śrīmatkāntaṃ ca nagaraṃ jvalantaṃ tadvinirdiśet//104//
body.translated_text:
340.007. 'Under <s>Citrā</s>, all men are conquered by women;
340.008. the city is glorious, beautiful, and blazing — thus it is described.' //104//

body.text:
340.009. svātyāṃ pure niviṣṭe tu prabhūtadhanasaṃcayāḥ/
340.010. lubdhāḥ krūrāśca mūrkhāśca prabhūtā nagare bhavet//105//
body.translated_text:
340.009. 'In a city established under <s>Svātī</s>, there are great accumulations of wealth;
340.010. but the greedy, cruel, and foolish are abundant in the city.' //105//

body.text:
340.011. viśākhāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu nagaraṃ jvalati śriyā/
340.012. yāyajūkajanākīrṇaṃ śastrāntaṃ ca vinirdiśet//106//
body.translated_text:
340.011. 'A city established under <s>Viśākhā</s> blazes with glory,
340.012. filled with people devoted to sacrifice, but it is described as ending in weapons.' //106//

body.text:
340.013. anurādhāniviṣṭe tu dharmaśīlā jitendriyāḥ/
340.014. svadāraniratāḥ puṇyā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ//107//
body.translated_text:
340.013. 'Under <s>Anurādhā</s>, the people are righteous, with senses controlled,
340.014. devoted to their own wives, meritorious, and devoted to prayer and fire-offerings.' //107//

body.text:
340.015. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ saṃniviṣṭaṃ tu bahuratnadhanānvitaiḥ/
340.016. sattvairvedavidaiḥ pūrṇaṃ śaśvatsamabhivardhate//108//
body.translated_text:
340.015. 'A city established under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, filled with beings rich in jewels and wealth,
340.016. learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, it eternally increases.' //108//

body.text:
340.017. mūlena saṃniviṣṭaṃ tu puraṃ dhānyadhanānvitam/
340.018. duḥśīlajanasaṃkīrṇaṃ pāṃsunā ca vinaśyati//109//
body.translated_text:
340.017. 'A city established under <s>Mūla</s> is endowed with grain and wealth,
340.018. but teeming with people of bad conduct, it perishes through dust.' //109//

body.text:
340.019. pūrvāṣāḍhāniviṣṭaṃ tu puraṃ syāddhanadhānyabhāk/
340.020. lubdhāḥ krūrāśca mūrkhāśca nivasanti narādhamāḥ//110//
body.translated_text:
340.019. 'Under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, the city possesses wealth and grain,
340.020. but the greedy, cruel, and foolish, the lowest of men, dwell there.' //110//

body.text:
340.021. niviṣṭe tūttarāyāṃ ca dhanadhānyasamuccayaḥ/
340.022. vidyāprakṛtisampanno janaśca kalahapriyaḥ//111//
body.translated_text:
340.021. 'Under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, there is an accumulation of wealth and grain;
340.022. the people are endowed with learning and good character, but are fond of quarrels.' //111//

body.text:
340.023. abhijiti niviṣṭe tu nagare tatra moditāḥ/
340.024. narāḥ sarve sadā hṛṣṭāḥ parasparānurāgiṇaḥ//112//
body.translated_text:
340.023. 'In a city established under <s>Abhijit</s>, the people are delighted;
340.024. all men are always joyful and mutually affectionate.' //112//

body.text:
340.025. śravaṇāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu paraṃ dhānyadhanānvitam/
340.026. arogijanabhūyiṣṭhasahitaṃ tadvinirdiśet//113//
body.translated_text:
340.025. 'A city established under <s>Śravaṇā</s> is supremely rich in grain and wealth,
340.026. teeming with healthy people and harmonious — thus it is described.' //113//

body.text:
340.027. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ niviṣṭaṃ tu strījitaṃ puramādiśet/
340.028. prabhūtavastramālyaṃ ca kāmabhogavivarjitam//114//
body.translated_text:
340.027. 'A city established under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is described as conquered by women,
340.028. abounding in cloth and garlands, but devoid of sensual enjoyments.' //114//

body.text:
340.029. pure śatabhiṣāyukte mūrkhaśāṭhyapriyā janāḥ/
340.030. strīṣu pāneṣu saṃsaktāḥ salilena vinaśyati//115//
body.translated_text:
340.029. 'In a city under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, the people are fond of foolishness and deceit,
340.030. addicted to women and drink — it perishes through water.' //115//

body.text:
341.001. <341>pure proṣṭhapadādhyakṣe narāstatra sukhapriyāḥ/
341.002. paropatāpino mūrkhā mānakāmavivarjitāḥ//116//
body.translated_text:
341.001. 'In a city presided over by <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, the men there are pleasure-loving,
341.002. harming others, foolish, devoid of honor and desire.' //116//

body.text:
341.003. uttarāyāṃ niviṣṭe tu śaśvadvṛddhiranuttarā/
341.004. pūrṇaṃ ca dhanadhānyābhyāṃ ratnāḍhyaṃ ca vinirdiśet//117//
body.translated_text:
341.003. 'Under <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, there is ever-increasing, unsurpassed growth;
341.004. it is described as full of wealth and grain, and rich in jewels.' //117//

body.text:
341.005. pure niviṣṭe revatyāṃ sundarī janatā bhavet/
341.006. kharoṣṭraṃ caiva gāvaśca prabhūtadhanadhānyatā//118//
body.translated_text:
341.005. 'In a city established under <s>Revatī</s>, the people are beautiful;
341.006. there are donkeys, camels, and cattle, and abundant wealth and grain.' //118//

body.text:
341.007. aśvinyāṃ viniviṣṭaṃ tu nagaraṃ śivamādiśet/
341.008. arogijanasampūrṇaṃ darśanīyajanākulam//119//
body.translated_text: 'A city established under <s>Aśvinī</s> is declared auspicious, filled with healthy people, teeming with people beautiful to behold.' //119//

body.text:
341.009. bharaṇyāṃ saṃniviṣṭe tu durbhagāḥ kalahapriyāḥ/
341.010. duḥśīlā duḥkhabhājaśca vasanti puruṣādhamāḥ//120//
body.translated_text: 'But in one established under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, the unfortunate, the quarrelsome, the ill-conducted, and wretched, the sharers of suffering, the lowest of men, dwell.' //120//

body.text:
341.011. purāṇi rāṣṭrāṇi tathā gṛhāṇi nakṣatrayogaṃ prasamīkṣya vidvān/
341.013. iṣṭe praśaste ca niveśayettu pūrve ca janme 'dhigataṃ mayedam//121//
body.translated_text: 'Cities, kingdoms, and houses — having examined the conjunction of <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), the wise man should establish them in an auspicious and favorable one. This I have mastered in a former birth.' //121//

body.text: 341.015. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinnakṣatranirdeśo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the chapter called the Designation of <s>Nakṣatras</s>.'

body.text:
341.016. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn aṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ sthānanirdeśaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi/
341.017. tacchrūyatām/
341.017. kathayatu bhagavān--
341.018. kṛttikā bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatraṃ kaliṅgamagadhānām/
341.018. rohiṇī sarvaprajāyāḥ/
341.019. mṛgaśirā videhānāṃ rājopasevakānāṃ ca/
341.019. evamārdrā kṣatriyāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca/
341.019. punarvasuḥ sauparṇānām/
341.020. puṣyanakṣatraṃ sarveṣāmavadātavasanānāṃ rājapadasevakānāṃ ca/
341.020. āśleṣā nāgānāṃ haimavatānāṃ ca/
341.021. maghānakṣatraṃ gauḍikānām/
341.021. pūrvaphalgunī caurāṇām/
341.021. uttaraphalgunī avantīnām/
341.022. hastā saurāṣṭrikāṇām/
341.022. citrā pakṣiṇāṃ dvipadānām/
341.022. svātī sarveṣāṃ pravarajyāsamāpannānām/
341.023. viśākhā audakānām/
341.023. anurādhā vāṇijakānāṃ śākaṭikānāṃ ca/
341.023. jyeṣṭhā dauvālikānām/
341.024. mūlā pathikānām/
341.024. pūrvāṣāḍhā bāhlīkānāṃ ca/
341.024. uttarāṣāḍhā kāmbojānām/
341.025. abhijitsarveṣāṃ dakṣiṇāpathikānāṃ tāmraparṇikānāṃ ca/
341.025. śravaṇā ghātakānāṃ caurāṇāṃ ca/
341.025. dhaniṣṭhā kurupāñcālānām/
341.026. śatabhiṣā maulikānāmātharvaṇikānāṃ ca/
341.026. pūrvabhādrapadā gandhikānām yavanakāmbojānāṃ ca/
341.027. uttarabhādrapadā gandharvāṇām/
341.027. revatī nāvikānāṃ ca/
341.027. aśvinī aśvavāṇijānāṃ ca/
341.028. bharaṇī bhadrapadakarmaṇāṃ bhadrakāyakānāṃ ca//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, I shall expound the chapter called the Designation of the Locations of the twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>. Hear it.' 'Let the lord speak.' '<s>Kṛttikā</s>, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of the <s>Kaliṅgas</s> and <s>Magadhans</s>. <s>Rohiṇī</s> belongs to all peoples. <s>Mṛgaśirā</s> belongs to the <s>Videhans</s> and those who serve kings. Likewise <s>Ārdrā</s> belongs to <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. <s>Punarvasu</s> belongs to the <s>Suparṇas</s> (Garuḍa-folk). The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Puṣya</s> belongs to all those who wear white garments and to royal servants. <s>Āśleṣā</s> belongs to the <s>Nāgas</s> and those of the <s>Himālayan</s> region. The <s>nakṣatra</s> <s>Maghā</s> belongs to the <s>Gauḍikas</s>. <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> belongs to thieves. <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s> belongs to the people of <s>Avantī</s>. <s>Hastā</s> belongs to the <s>Saurāṣṭrians</s>. <s>Citrā</s> belongs to two-footed birds. <s>Svātī</s> belongs to all those who have taken to the ascetic life. <s>Viśākhā</s> belongs to water-dwellers. <s>Anurādhā</s> belongs to merchants and cart-drivers. <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> belongs to gatekeepers. <s>Mūlā</s> belongs to travelers. <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> belongs to the <s>Bāhlīkas</s>. <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> belongs to the <s>Kāmbojas</s>. <s>Abhijit</s> belongs to all southerners and the <s>Tāmraparṇikas</s>. <s>Śravaṇā</s> belongs to killers and thieves. <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> belongs to the <s>Kuru-Pāñcālas</s>. <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> belongs to herbalists and <s>Atharvanic</s> practitioners. <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> belongs to perfumers, <s>Yavanas</s>, and <s>Kāmbojas</s>. <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> belongs to the <s>Gandharvas</s>. <s>Revatī</s> belongs to boatmen. <s>Aśvinī</s> belongs to horse-traders. <s>Bharaṇī</s> belongs to those engaged in <s>bhadrapada</s> rites and <s>bhadrakāyakas</s>.'

body.text: 341.028. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatrāṇāṃ sthānanirdeśavyākaraṇo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the chapter called the Explanation of the Designation of the Locations of the <s>Nakṣatras</s>.'

body.text:
341.030. paṭha bhostriśaṅko ṛtuvaṣa nāmādhyāyam/
341.030. tadahaṃ vakṣye śrūyatām/
341.030. kathayatu bhagavān--
body.translated_text: 'Recite, Ho <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called Seasonal Rainfall.' 'I shall declare it — hear it.' 'Let the lord speak.'

body.text:
342.001. <342>kṛttikāsu grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.002. varṣo daśarātrikaḥ/
342.002. śravaṇāyuktaproṣṭhapadāyām agrodako varṣārātro bhavati/
342.003. agnibhayaṃ śastrabhayaṃ codakabhayaṃ ca bhavati/
342.004. uktaṃ kṛttikāsu//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Kṛttikā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. The rainy season lasts ten nights. On the <s>Śravaṇā</s>-combined <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>, the rain is water-fronted and the night is rainy. There will be danger from fire, danger from weapons, and danger from floods. This is stated for <s>Kṛttikā</s>.'

body.text:
342.005. rohiṇyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ekaviṃśatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.006. tatra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
342.006. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
342.006. eṣa ca varṣārātraḥ sāroparodhaḥ sasyaṃ ca saṃpādayati/
342.007. dvau cātra rogau prabalau bhavataḥ/
342.007. kukṣirogaścakṣūrogaśca/
342.007. caurabahulāścātra diśo bhavanti/
342.008. uktaṃ ca rohiṇyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Rohiṇī</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains twenty-one <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided. This rainy night brings an obstruction of essential supplies, yet it matures the crops. Two diseases become prevalent there — stomach disease and eye disease. Thieves also become numerous in the regions. This is stated for <s>Rohiṇī</s>.'

body.text:
342.009. mṛgaśīrṣe grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.010. sāroparodho varṣārātraḥ/
342.010. paścādvarṣaṃ saṃjanayati/
342.010. nikṣiptaśastrāścātra rājāno bhavanti/
342.010. kṣemiṇaḥ sunītikāśca diśo bhavanti/
342.011. muditāścātra janapadā bhavanti/
342.011. uktaṃ mṛgaśirasi//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There is an obstruction of essential supplies during the rainy night, but later it produces rain. Kings there put down their weapons. The regions are secure and well-governed. The people of the countryside are joyful there. This is stated for <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>.'

body.text:
342.012. ārdrāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, aṣṭādaśāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.013. tatra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
342.013. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
342.013. nidhayaśca rakṣayitavyāḥ/
342.014. caurabahulāścātra diśo bhavanti/
342.014. nikṣiptaśastrāśca rajāno bhavanti/
342.014. trayaścātra rogāḥ prabalā bhavanti--jvaraḥ śvāso galagrahaśca/
342.015. bālānāṃ dārakadārikāṇāṃ ca maraṇaṃ bhavati/
342.015. ityuktamārdrāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Ārdrā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains eighteen <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided; and stores should be guarded. Thieves become numerous in the regions. Kings put down their weapons. Three diseases become prevalent there — fever, asthma, and throat-seizure. There is death among infants, boys, and girls. This is stated for <s>Ārdrā</s>.'

body.text:
342.016. punarvasau grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, navatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.017. mahāmeghānutpādayati/
342.017. āṣāḍhāyāṃ praviṣṭāyāṃ mṛdūni pravarṣati/
342.017. anantaraṃ ca nirantareṇa pravarṣati/
342.018. nikṣiptaśastrāścātra rājāno bhavanti/
342.018. uktaṃ punarvasau//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Punarvasu</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains ninety <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. He produces great cloud-masses. When <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> has commenced, he rains gently. And he rains continuously without interruption. Kings there put down their weapons. This is stated for <s>Punarvasu</s>.'

body.text:
342.019. puṣye grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, dvātriṃśadāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.019. atra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
342.020. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
342.020. vyaktaṃ pradhānavarṣāṇi bhavanti/
342.020. sasyaṃ ca niṣpādayati/
342.021. brāhmaṇakṣatriyāṇāṃ ca virodho bhavati/
342.021. daṃṣṭriṇaścātra prabalā bhavanti/
342.021. tatra trayo rogāśca bhavanti--gāṇḍāḥ piṭakāḥ pāmāni ca/
342.022. ityuktaṃ puṣye//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Puṣya</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains thirty-two <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided. The rains are clearly the principal ones and they mature the crops. Conflict arises between <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. Fanged creatures become powerful there. Three diseases arise there — boils, abscesses, and scabies. This is stated for <s>Puṣya</s>.'

body.text:
342.023. āśleṣāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ekaviṃśatyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.024. tatra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
342.024. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
342.024. viṣamāśca vāyavo vānti/
342.025. saṃvignāścātra jñānino rājānaśca bhavanti/
342.025. eṣo varṣaḥ sarvasasyāni saṃpādayati/
342.025. jāyāpatikānāṃ rājāmātyānāṃ ca virodho bhavati/
342.026. uktamāśleṣāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Āśleṣā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains twenty-one <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided. Irregular winds blow. The wise, the learned, and kings become agitated there. This rainfall matures all crops. Conflict arises between husbands and wives, and between kings and ministers. This is stated for <s>Āśleṣā</s>.'

body.text:
342.027. maghāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.028. eṣo varṣaḥ sarvasasyāni saṃpādayati/
342.028. mṛgapakṣipaśumanuṣyāṇāṃ cātra garbhā vinaśyanti/
342.029. janamaraṇaṃ cātra bhaviṣyatīti/
342.029. uktaṃ maghāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Maghā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. This rainfall matures all crops. There, the fetuses of wild animals, birds, livestock, and humans are destroyed. Mass death of people will occur. This is stated for <s>Maghā</s>.'

body.text:
342.030. pūrvaphalgunyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
342.031. eṣo varṣaḥ sarvasasyāni saṃpādayati/
342.031. tacca sasyaṃ janayitvā paracakrapīḍitā manuṣyā na sukhenopabhuñjate/
342.032. paśūnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cātra garbhāḥ sukhino bhavanti/
342.032. uktaṃ pūrvaphalgunyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. This rainfall matures all crops. But having produced those crops, people, afflicted by hostile forces, do not enjoy them happily. The fetuses of livestock and humans are fortunate there. This is stated for <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>.'

body.text:
343.001. <343>uttaraphalgunyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, aśītyāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.002. eko varṣaḥ sarvasyāni ca saṃpādayati/
343.002. nikṣiptaśastrāścātra rājāno bhavanti/
343.003. brahmakṣatriyayośca virodho bhavati/
343.003. kṣipraṃ ca anītikāḥ prajā vinaśyanti/
343.003. uktamuttaraphalgunyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains eighty <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. This single rainfall matures all crops. Kings there put down their weapons. Conflict arises between <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. People who are without calamity perish quickly. This is stated for <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>.'

body.text:
343.005. haste grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse devaḥ pravarṣati, ekonapañcāśadāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.006. devaśca tadyathā parikṣipti/
343.006. patitāni ca sasyārasāgrāṇi anudagrāṇi alpasāraṇyalpodakāni/
343.007. durbhikṣaścātra bhaviṣyati/
343.007. uktaṃ haste//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Hastā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains forty-nine <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. But the rain-god scatters it about. The fallen crops are sapless at their tips, stunted, of little substance, and with little water. Famine will occur there. This is stated for <s>Hastā</s>.'

body.text:
343.008. citrāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.009. sāroparodhāstataḥ paścādvarṣaṃ saṃjanayati/
343.009. nikṣiptaśastrāśca rājāno bhavanti/
343.009. muditāścātra janapadā bhavanti/
343.010. uktaṃ citrāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Citrā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There is an obstruction of essential supplies, but later it produces rain. Kings put down their weapons. The people of the countryside are joyful there. This is stated for <s>Citrā</s>.'

body.text:
343.011. svātyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ekaviṃśatyāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.012. nikṣiptaśastrāśca rājāno bhavanti/
343.012. caurāścātra balavattarā bhavanti/
343.012. uktaṃ svātyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Svātī</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains twenty-one <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. Kings put down their weapons. Thieves become especially powerful there. This is stated for <s>Svātī</s>.'

body.text:
343.013. viśākhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, aśītyāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.014. eko varṣaḥ sarvasyāni saṃpādayati/
343.014. rājānaścātra cchidrayuktā bhavanti/
343.014. agnidāhāścātra prabalā bhavanti/
343.015. daṃṣṭriṇaścātra balavanto 'pi kṣayaṃ gacchanti/
343.015. uktaṃ viśākhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Viśākhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains eighty <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. This single rainfall matures all crops. Kings there become vulnerable. Fires become prevalent there. Even powerful fanged creatures perish there. This is stated for <s>Viśākhā</s>.'

body.text:
343.016. anurādhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ṣaṣṭyāḍakāni pravarṣati/
343.017. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse cātra dṛḍāni bhavanti/
343.017. uktamanurādhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Anurādhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. In <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, in the last month of summer, the conditions become firm. This is stated for <s>Anurādhā</s>.'

body.text:
343.018. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ṣoḍaśāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
343.019. tatra kṛṣikarmāntāni pratisaṃhartavyāni/
343.019. yugavaratrāṇi varjayitavyāni/
343.019. svadhānyāni upasaṃhartavyāni/
343.020. agnayaḥ pratisaṃhartavyāḥ/
343.020. lā.ṅgalāni pratisaṃhartavyāni/
343.020. avaśyamanena janapadena vinaṣṭavyaṃ bhavati/
343.021. paracakrapīḍito bhavati/
343.021. uktaṃ jyeṣṭhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixteen <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, agricultural operations should be suspended. Yokes and straps should be set aside. One's own grain should be stored away. Fires should be banked. Plows should be put away. That country will inevitably be destroyed. It will be afflicted by hostile forces. This is stated for <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.'

body.text:
343.022. mūle grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
343.022. ekaḥ sasyaṃ saṃpādayati/
343.022. caurabahulāścātra diśo bhavanti/
343.023. trayaścātra vyādhayo balavanto bhavanti--vātagaṇḍaḥ pārśvaśūlamakṣirogaśca/
343.024. puṣpaphalāni cātra samṛddhāni bhavanti/
343.024. nikṣiptaśastrāścātra rājāno bhavanti/
343.025. uktaṃ mūle//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Mūla</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. This single rainfall matures the crops. Thieves become numerous in the regions. Three diseases become powerful there — wind-boils, side-pain, and eye disease. Flowers and fruits become abundant there. Kings put down their weapons. This is stated for <s>Mūla</s>.'

body.text:
343.026. pūrvasyāmāṣāḍhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
343.027. dvau cātra grāhau bhavataḥ/
343.027. proṣṭhapade vā āśvayujau vā pakṣe/
343.027. eko varṣaḥ sarvasasyāni saṃpādayati/
343.028. dvau cātra rogau prabalau bhavatah--kukṣirogo 'kṣirogaśca/
343.028. uktaṃ pūrvāṣāḍhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. Two eclipses occur there, in the <s>Proṣṭhapada</s> or <s>Āśvayuja</s> fortnight. This single rainfall matures all crops. Two diseases become prevalent there — stomach disease and eye disease. This is stated for <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>.'

body.text:
343.029. uttarasyāmāṣāḍhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, pūrṇamāḍhakaśataṃ pravarṣati/
343.030. tatra sthalāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
343.030. niṃnāni parivarjayitavyāni/
343.030. mahāsrotāṃsi cātra pravahanti/
343.031. agrodakā cātra bhavanti/
343.031. sarvasasyāni niṣpādayati/
343.031. trayaścātra rogāḥ prabalā bhavanti--gaṇḍaḥ kacchaḥ kaṇṭharoga iti/
343.032. uktamuttarāṣāḍhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains a full hundred <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, high ground should be cultivated; low-lying lands should be avoided. Great torrents flow there. The rains are water-fronted. All crops are matured. Three diseases become powerful there — boils, scabies, and throat disease. This is stated for <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>.'

body.text:
344.001. <344>abhijiti grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakani pravarṣati/
344.002. maṇḍalavarṣaṃ ca devaḥ pravarṣati/
344.002. paścād varṣaḥ sasyaṃ janayati/
344.002. audakānāṃ bhūtānāmutsargo bhavati/
344.003. uktamabhijiti//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Abhijit</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. The rain-god rains in circular showers. Later the rainfall produces crops. There is an eruption of aquatic creatures. This is stated for <s>Abhijit</s>.'

body.text:
344.004. śravaṇe tu grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
344.005. maṇḍalavarṣaṃ ca devo varṣati/
344.005. paścād varṣā sasyaṃ saṃpādayati/
344.005. audakānāṃ bhūtānāmutsargo bhavati/
344.006. vyādhibahulāśca narā bhavanti/
344.006. rājānaśca tīvradaṇḍā bhavanti/
344.006. uktaṃ śravaṇe//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. The rain-god rains in circular showers. Later the rainfall matures crops. There is an eruption of aquatic creatures. People become prone to many diseases. Kings impose severe punishments. This is stated for <s>Śravaṇa</s>.'

body.text:
344.007. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, ekapañcādāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
344.008. vibhaktāścātra varṣā bhavanti/
344.008. tatra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
344.008. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
344.009. durmukho rātrau varṣo bhavati/
344.009. sasyāni saṃpādayati/
344.009. ekaścātra rogo bhavati--gaṇḍavikāraḥ/
344.010. śastrasamādānāśca rājāno bhavanti/
344.010. uktaṃ dhaniṣṭhāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains fifty-one <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. The rains are divided there. Low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided. The night-rain has an unfavorable appearance. It matures the crops. One disease arises there — boil-disorder. Kings take up weapons. This is stated for <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>.'

body.text:
344.011. śatabhiṣāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra pravarṣati, ṣoḍaśāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
344.012. tatra niṃnāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
344.012. sthalāni parivarjayitavyāni/
344.012. eko varṣaḥ sarvasasyāni saṃpādayati/
344.013. cakrasamārūḍhā janapadā bhavanti/
344.013. manuṣyā dārakadārikāśca skandhe kṛtvā deśāntaraṃ gacchanti/
344.014. uktaṃ śatabhiṣāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixteen <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. There, low-lying lands should be cultivated; high ground should be avoided. This single rainfall matures all crops. The countryfolk are subjected to the wheel of war. People, carrying boys and girls on their shoulders, go to other lands. This is stated for <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>.'

body.text:
344.015. pūrvasyāṃ bhādrapadāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime māse yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, catuḥṣaṣṭyāḍhakāni pravarṣati/
344.016. varṣāmukhe cātra ekonaviṃśatirātriko 'vagraho bhavati/
344.016. puṣpasasyaṃ ca nāśayati/
344.017. etāścād varṣā bahucaurā bhavanti/
344.017. dvau cātra mahāvyādhī bhavatah--prathamaṃ pittatāpajvaro bhavati, paścād balavān mahāgraho bhavati/
344.018. martyānāṃ nārīṇāṃ ca maraṇaṃ bhavati/
344.019. uktaṃ pūrvabhādrapadāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains sixty-four <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. At the onset of the rainy season, there is a drought of nineteen nights. It destroys the flower-crops. These rains are marked by many thieves. Two great diseases arise there — first comes bile-fever, and then comes a powerful great eclipse-seizure. Death of men and women occurs. This is stated for <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>.'

body.text:
344.020. uttarasyāṃ bhādrapadāyāṃ grīṣmāṇāṃ paścime yadyatra devaḥ pravarṣati, pūrṇamāḍhakaśataṃ pravarṣati/
344.021. mahāsrotāṃsi pravahanti/
344.021. grāmanagaranigamāḥ srotasā uhyante/
344.021. catvāraścātra vyādhayaḥ prabalā bhavanti/
344.022. tadyathā--kukṣirogo 'kṣirogaḥ kāso jvaraśceti/
344.022. bālānāṃ dārakadārikāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ bhavati/
344.023. atra sthalāni kṛṣikartavyāni/
344.023. niṃnāni parivarjayitavyāni/
344.024. etāśca varṣāḥ puṣpāṇi phalāni ca saṃpādayanti/
344.024. uktamuttarabhādrapadāyām//
body.translated_text: 'If the rain-god rains in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, in the last month of summer, he rains a full hundred <s>āḍhaka</s> measures. Great torrents flow. Villages, cities, and towns are carried away by the currents. Four diseases become powerful there — namely, stomach disease, eye disease, cough, and fever. Death of infants, boys, and girls occurs.
