359.004. āśleṣāyāṃ caledbhūmir nāgāḥ sarve sarīsṛpāḥ/
359.005. kīṭāḥ pipīlikāḥ śvānā ekakhurāśca ye mṛgāḥ//256//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Āśleṣā</s>, all <s>Nāgas</s> and serpents, insects, ants, dogs, and single-hoofed animals —' //256//

body.text:
359.006. vaidyā viṣakarāścāpi ye ca sattvā darīśrayāḥ/
359.007. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//257//
body.translated_text: 'Physicians, poison-makers, and creatures dwelling in caves — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //257//

body.text:
359.008. maghāsu calitā bhūmirmahārājo 'tra tapyate/
359.009. ye ca śrāddhā nivartante samājā utsavāstathā/
359.010. yajñāśca devakṛtyaṃ ca sarvamatra nivartate//258//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Maghā</s>, the great king suffers there. Funerary feasts cease, as do assemblies and festivals; sacrifices and divine worship — all cease there.' //258//

body.text:
359.011. ye jātā ye ca saṃvṛddhā ye cānye 'pyagrapaṇḍitāḥ/
359.012. gandharvāśca vinaśyanti narā ye ca mahākulāḥ/
359.013. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//259//
body.translated_text: 'Those who were born, those who grew up, and other foremost scholars too, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and men of great families perish — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //259//

body.text:
359.014. phalgunyāṃ calitā bhūmirṛturvyāvartate tadā/
359.015. tiryagvātaścaiva vāti kṛtaṃ naśyati śāśvatam/
359.016. pathikāścopatapyanti māṣayācyopajīvikāḥ//260//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Phalgunī</s>, the seasons are reversed. Cross-winds blow; what was established is permanently destroyed. Travelers suffer, and those who live by begging for beans.' //260//

body.text:
359.017. dharme ratā āsanikā ye ca śulkopajīvinaḥ/
359.018. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//261//
body.translated_text: 'Those devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, gamblers, and those who live by tolls — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //261//

body.text:
359.019. calatyuttaraphalgunyāṃ vaṇijā dvīpayātrikāḥ/
359.020. sārthavāhā āsanikā ye ca śilpopajīvinaḥ//262//
body.translated_text: 'When it quakes in <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, merchants who travel to islands, caravan-leaders, gamblers, and those who live by crafts —' //262//

body.text:
359.021. aṅgā videhamagadhā nairṛtāḥ strīparigrahāḥ/
359.022. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//263//
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Aṅgas</s>, <s>Videhans</s>, <s>Magadhans</s>, <s>Nairṛtas</s>, and those who have women in their households — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //263//

body.text:
359.023. hastena calitā bhūmiḥ kumbhakāracikitsakāḥ/
359.024. gaṇamukhyā mahāmātrāḥ senādhyakṣāśca ye narāḥ//264//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Hastā</s>, potters, physicians, guild-leaders, high officials, and military commanders —' //264//

body.text:
359.025. tāramakā(?) nārapaṭā(?) vipsarah(?) kauṭikā api/
359.026. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//265//
body.translated_text: 'Astrologers, cloth-dealers, courtesans, and deceivers too — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //265//

body.text:
359.027. citrāyāṃ calitā bhūmiḥ kārukā upakalpakāḥ/
359.028. kumāryaḥ sarvaratnaṃ ca sasyānāṃ bījakaiḥ saha//266//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Citrā</s>, artisans, preparers, maidens, all jewels, and crops along with their seeds —' //266//

body.text:
359.029. vaṅgā daśārṇakuravaścedimāhiṣakāstathā/
359.030. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//267//
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Daśārṇas</s>, <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Cedis</s>, and <s>Māhiṣakas</s> — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //267//

body.text:
360.001. <360>svātau pracalitā bhūmiścaurā ye ca kuśīlakāḥ/
360.002. hiṃsakā ye ca tatkarmaratā^bhyarthitamūṣakāḥ//268//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Svātī</s>, thieves and those of ill-conduct, those who are violent and devoted to such deeds, and those who extort through intimidation —' //268//

body.text:
360.003. himavata uttareṇa vāyubhakṣāstapasvinaḥ/
360.004. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//269//
body.translated_text: 'North of <s>Himavat</s>, wind-eating ascetics — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //269//

body.text:
360.005. viśākhāyāṃ caled bhūmirmahāśailakṣayo bhavet/
360.006. ugrā vātāḥ pravāntyatra aśmakairakuśalinaḥ//270//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Viśākhā</s>, great mountains are destroyed. Fierce winds blow; those of the stony regions are imperiled.' //270//

body.text:
360.007. anurādhe caled bhūmirdasyūnāmanayo mahān/
360.008. viṭā dyūtakarāścaiva granthibhedāśca ye narāḥ//271//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Anurādhā</s>, great destruction comes to bandits, pimps, gamblers, and pickpockets —' //271//

body.text:
360.009. andhrāḥ puṇḍrāḥ pulindāśca bhaye tiṣṭhantyanāśritāḥ/
360.010. mitrabhedaśca balavāṃs tadā jagati jāyate//272//
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Andhras</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, and <s>Pulindas</s> stand in fear, without refuge. A powerful breaking of alliances then arises in the world.' //272//

body.text:
360.011. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ calitā bhūmirmahārāja pratapyate/
360.012. vāyasā vṛṣabhā vyāḍāstathā caṇḍamṛgāśca ye//273//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, the great king suffers. Crows, bulls, fierce beasts, and savage wild animals —' //273//

body.text:
360.013. kuravaḥ śūrasenāśca mallā bāhlīkanigrahāḥ/
360.014. pratyarthikena śīghreṇa ye ca tadbhaktibhājanāḥ/
360.015. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//274//
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Śūrasenas</s>, <s>Mallas</s>, and those subjugated by the <s>Bāhlīkas</s> — with their adversary swift, and those devoted to their cause — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //274//

body.text:
360.016. mūlena calitā bhūmiścatuṣpaddvipadāstathā/
360.017. grahāśrayāḥ piśācāśca ye ca sattvā darīśrayāḥ/
360.018. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//275//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Mūla</s>, four-footed and two-footed beings, those possessed by planets, <s>Piśācas</s>, and creatures dwelling in caves — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //275//

body.text:
360.019. durbhikṣaṃ ca karotyāśu dhānyamalpodakaṃ bhavet/
360.020. darīparvatamūlāni gacchanti ca tadā bhuvi//276//
body.translated_text: 'It quickly brings famine; grain becomes scarce in water. They go then to cave-bases and mountain-roots on the earth.' //276//

body.text:
360.021. pūrvāṣāḍhe caled bhūmirjalajā matsyaśuktikāḥ/
360.022. śiśumārā udrakāśca nakrā makarakacchapāḥ//277//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, aquatic beings — fish, oysters, crocodiles, otters, <s>makara</s> sea-creatures, and turtles —' //277//

body.text:
360.023. jātigotrapradhānāśca dhanino 'tha vicakṣaṇāḥ/
360.024. dvitīyābhijātāśca mahāvidyākarāśca ye/
360.025. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//278//
body.translated_text: 'Those distinguished by birth and lineage, the wealthy, the wise, those of the second rank of birth, and those great in learning — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //278//

body.text:
360.026. uttarasyāṃ caled bhūmiḥ śilpināmanayo mahān/
360.027. ayaskārāḥ sthapatayastrapukārāśca takṣakāḥ//279//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, great destruction comes to craftsmen. Iron-workers, architects, tin-workers, and carpenters —' //279//

body.text:
360.028. daridrā dhaninaścāpi śilpino vividhā api/
360.029. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ/
360.030. grāmakūṭāni ca ghnanti sacalasthāvarāṇi ca//280//
body.translated_text: 'The poor and the rich alike, and various artisans — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes. They destroy village-tops, both moving and stationary things.' //280//

body.text:
361.001. <361>vaiṣṇave calitā bhūmistadeti yadanīpsitam/
361.002. adhyāpakāḥ śāstravidaḥ kavayo mantrapāragāḥ/
361.003. yugaṃdharāḥ śūrasenā abhirājāḥ paṭaccarāḥ//281//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Abhijit</s> (the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> nakṣatra), what is undesired comes about. Teachers, knowers of <s>śāstras</s>, poets, those who have crossed to the far shore of <s>mantras</s>, yoke-bearers, <s>Śūrasenas</s>, paramount kings, and wanderers —' //281//

body.text:
361.004. kuśaṇḍāḥ śaradaṇḍāśca ye narā rājapūjitāḥ/
361.005. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//282//
body.translated_text: '<s>Kuśaṇḍas</s>, <s>Śaradaṇḍas</s>, and men honored by kings — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //282//

body.text:
361.006. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ caled bhūmirdhanināmanayo mahān/
361.007. maheśvarāstathā mahānāgarāḥ śreṣṭhinastathā//283//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, great destruction comes to the wealthy. Great lords, great citizens, guild-masters likewise —' //283//

body.text:
361.008. pracaṇḍāḥ svastimantaśca bhadrakārā yugaṃdharāḥ/
361.009. pārikūlāśca bhojyāśca hyanye sannāgarā api/
361.010. ete vyasanamarcchanti bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//284//
body.translated_text: 'The fierce, the prosperous, the auspicious-doers, the yoke-bearers, the hostile, the subjects, and other city-dwellers too — all these meet with calamity, shaken by earthquakes.' //284//

body.text:
361.011. vāruṇye calitā bhūmiraudakeṣvanayo mahān/
361.012. hastino 'śvakharoṣṭrāśca sparśamarcchanti dāruṇam//285//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in the <s>Vāruṇa</s> (nakṣatra), great destruction comes to aquatic beings. Elephants, horses, donkeys, and camels receive a terrible blow.' //285//

body.text:
361.013. tadāsau vīrakān madrān bāhlīkān kekayānapi/
361.014. anāśrayāṃścakravākāñ janasthānapi pīḍayet//286//
body.translated_text: 'At that time it afflicts the <s>Vīrakas</s>, <s>Madras</s>, <s>Bāhlīkas</s>, <s>Kekayas</s>, homeless <s>Cakravākas</s>, and even the people of <s>Janasthāna</s>.' //286//

body.text:
361.015. sājena calitā bhūmī rākṣasān ghātakāṃstathā/
361.016. aurabhrikān saukarikān sauvīrāṃśca nipātayet//287//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> (the <s>Āja</s> nakṣatra), it brings down <s>Rākṣasas</s> and killers, sheep-breeders, pig-herders, and the <s>Sauvīras</s>.' //287//

body.text:
361.017. vaṇijyajīvino vaiśyāñ śūdrāṃśca karītīnapi/
361.018. yavanān mālavādyāṃśca ganthibhedāṃśca nāśayet//288//
body.translated_text: 'Merchants, <s>Vaiśyas</s> who live by trade, <s>Śūdras</s> and servants, <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Mālavas</s> and the like, and pickpockets — it destroys them.' //288//

body.text:
361.019. ahirbudhnye caled bhūmirvaṇijāmanayo mahān/
361.020. dharme ratāśca ye siddhā ye ca śauktikakarmiṇaḥ//289//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> (the <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> nakṣatra), great destruction comes to merchants. Those devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, accomplished ones, and those who work with shells —' //289//

body.text:
361.021. śibīn vatsāaṃs tathā vātsyān kṣatriyānārjunāyanān/
361.022. sindhurājadhanuṣpāṇīn sarvānardayate 'cirāt//290//
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Śibis</s>, <s>Vatsas</s>, <s>Vātsyas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> of <s>Ārjunāyana</s>, the kings of <s>Sindh</s> with bows in hand — all of them it afflicts without delay.' //290//

body.text:
361.023. revatyāṃ calitā bhūmiḥ saṃgrāmaḥ syātsudāruṇaḥ/
361.024. grāmaghātāśca vartante grāmo grāmaṃ ca hiṃsati//291//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Revatī</s>, a terrible battle arises. Village-raids occur; village destroys village.' //291//

body.text:
361.025. naucarānudakājīvān ramaṭhān bharukacchakān/
361.026. sudhanvānabhisārāṃśca sarvasenāṃśca nirdahet//292//
body.translated_text: 'Sailors, those who live by water, <s>Ramaṭhas</s>, <s>Bharukacchakas</s>, <s>Sudhanvāns</s>, <s>Abhisāras</s>, and all armies — it burns them.' //292//

body.text:
361.027. aśvinyāṃ calitā bhūmiraśvānāmanayo mahān/
361.028. grāmaghātaśca vartante bhrātā bhrātṛñ jighāṃsati//293//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Aśvinī</s>, great destruction comes to horses. Village-raids occur; brother seeks to kill brother.' //293//

body.text:
361.029. yā cātra garbhamādhatte ye ca jātāśca tāniha/
361.030. trīṇi varṣāṇyato duḥkhamupaiti ca nirantaram//294//
body.translated_text: 'Whatever conceives there and whatever is born — for three years hence, suffering comes upon it continuously.' //294//

body.text:
362.001. <362>sahitāścitragarbhāśca ye hyanye cāṅganājanāḥ/
362.002. ārjunāyanā rājanyāḥ suṣṭhu trīṃścāpi hiṃsati//295//
body.translated_text: 'Those united, those with pregnant women, and other women-folk, the <s>Ārjunāyana</s> kings — it truly afflicts three of them.' //295//

body.text:
362.003. bharaṇyāṃ calitā bhūmiścaurāṇāmanayo mahān/
362.004. viṭā dyūtakarāścaiva granthibhedāśca ye narāḥ//296//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth quakes in <s>Bharaṇī</s>, great destruction comes to thieves. Pimps, gamblers, and pickpockets —' //296//

body.text:
362.005. ādarśacakrāṭā dhūrtāstathā bandhanarakṣakāḥ/
362.006. antāvaśāyinaḥ pāpāścaranti ye tu durjanāḥ/
362.007. te 'pi tatra vipadyante bhūmicālavicālitāḥ//297//
body.translated_text: 'Mirror-swindlers, cheats, prison-guards, wretched outcaste-dwellers, and those wicked people who wander about — even they perish there, shaken by earthquakes.' //297//

body.text:
362.008. vepitāyāṃ tu medinyāṃ bhavedrūpamanantaram/
362.009. saptāhābhyantarāttatra megho bhavati prārthitaḥ//298//
body.translated_text: 'When the earth has trembled, immediately afterward a phenomenon appears: within seven days, a rain-cloud arrives as desired.' //298//

body.text:
362.010. snigdho hyañjanasaṃkāśo mahāparvatasannibhaḥ/
362.011. indraśca vaṣate tatra maharṣervacanam yathā/
362.012. {eva nigaditaṃ nāthairindraścātra pravarṣati//299//}
362.013. svastikākārasaṃkāśā indravajradhvajopamāḥ/
362.014. dṛśyante 'bhrā hi saṃdhyāyāṃ grastvā candradivākarau//300//
body.translated_text: Glossy and resembling collyrium, like a great mountain; and <s>Indra</s> rains there, as the great sage has spoken. {Thus it is declared by the lords, and <s>Indra</s> rains here.} //299// Resembling the <s>svastika</s> shape, like the banner and <s>vajra</s> of <s>Indra</s>, clouds are seen at twilight, having swallowed the moon and sun. //300//

body.text:
362.015. tadā nabhasi jāyante meghā dāḍimasaṃnibhāḥ/
362.016. lakṣaṇaṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyāttānindrakampitān/
362.017. sa nirdeśo bhavettatra maharṣervacanam yathā//301//
body.translated_text: Then clouds resembling pomegranates appear in the sky. Seeing such a sign, one should know them as <s>Indra</s>-quakes. That is the prediction there, as the great sage has spoken. //301//

body.text:
362.018. atīva tatra viśvastaḥ sarvabījāni vāpayet/
362.019. vyavahārāṃśca kurvīrannirbhayāstatra vāṇijāḥ/
362.020. sarveṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ praśastā indrakampitāḥ//302//
body.translated_text: One should be very confident there and sow all seeds; merchants should conduct their business there without fear. Of all earthquakes, <s>Indra</s>-quakes are the most auspicious. //302//

body.text:
362.021. vepitāyāṃ tu medinyāṃ bhavedrūpamanantaram/
362.022. saptāhābhyantare tatra meghāḥ saṃchādayennabhaḥ//303//
body.translated_text: When the earth trembles, the next sign appears: within seven days, clouds will cover the sky there. //303//

body.text:
362.023. tato 'nubaddhā jāyante abhrāḥ kauśeyasaṃnibhāḥ/
362.024. anulomaṃ ca samyānti carantaḥ paścimāṃ diśam//304//
body.translated_text: Then connected clouds appear, resembling silk; and they move favorably, traveling toward the western direction. //304//

body.text:
362.025. śiśumāra-udrakāṇāṃ matsyamakarasannibhāḥ/
362.026. dṛśyante 'bhrāśca saṃdhyāyāṃ grastvā candradivākarau//305//
body.translated_text: Resembling porpoises, otters, fish, and <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), clouds are seen at twilight, having swallowed the moon and sun. //305//

body.text:
362.027. lakṣaṇaṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidyāttāñjalakampitān/
362.028. sa nirdeśo bhavettatra maharṣervacanam yathā//306//
body.translated_text: Seeing such a sign, one should know them as water-quakes. That is the prediction there, as the great sage has spoken. //306//

body.text:
362.029. sthaleṣu girikūṭeṣu kṣetreṣūpavaneṣu ca/
362.030. sthāpyante tatra bījāni niṃne naśyanti vai tadā//307//
body.translated_text: On high ground, mountain peaks, fields, and gardens, seeds should be placed there; in low-lying places, they will perish then. //307//

body.text:
363.001. <363>paṅkenāpi jalenāpi naśyeyū rajasāpi vā/
363.002. eteṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ praśastā jalakampitāḥ//308//
body.translated_text: By mud, by water, or by dust they may perish. Of all earthquakes, water-quakes are the most auspicious. //308//

body.text:
363.003. vepitāyāṃ tu medinyāṃ bhavedrūpamanantaram/
363.004. saptāhābhyantare tatra vātā vānti sudāruṇāḥ//309//
body.translated_text: When the earth trembles, the next sign appears: within seven days, terribly fierce winds blow there. //309//

body.text:
363.005. dṛśyate kapilā saṃdhyā candrasūryau tu lohitau/
363.006. lakṣaṇaṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā jānīyādvāyukampitān//310//
body.translated_text: The twilight appears tawny; the moon and sun appear red. Seeing such a sign, one should know them as wind-quakes. //310//

body.text:
363.007. tato bhavati nirdeśo maharṣervacanam yathā/
363.008. na tatra pravasetprājña ātmānaṃ cātra gopayet//311//
body.translated_text: Then comes the prediction, as the great sage has spoken: the wise one should not travel there; one should protect oneself here. //311//

body.text:
363.009. guhyamāvaraṇaṃ kuryātprākāraparikhāṃ khanet/
363.010. prātisīmā virudhyante narāṇāṃ jāyate bhayam//312//
body.translated_text: One should make a hidden shelter and dig a rampart with a moat. Boundary disputes arise, and fear befalls people. //312//

body.text:
363.011. eteṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kīrtitā guṇāḥ/
363.012. viśeṣeṇa manuṣyāṇāṃ nirmitā vāyukampitāḥ//313//
body.translated_text: The qualities of all these earthquakes have been declared. Wind-quakes are especially [dangerous] for human beings. //313//

body.text:
363.013. kampitāyāṃ tu medinyāṃ bhavedrūpamanantaram/
363.014. saptāhābhyantarāttatra ulkāpātāḥ sudāruṇāḥ//314//
body.translated_text: When the earth trembles, the next sign appears: within seven days there, terribly fierce meteor-falls [occur]. //314//

body.text:
363.015. saṃdhyā ca lohitā bhāti candrasūryau tu lohitau/
363.016. lakṣaṇaṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vijñeyā agnikampitāḥ//315//
body.translated_text: The twilight appears red; the moon and sun appear red. Seeing such a sign, one should know them as fire-quakes. //315//

body.text:
363.017. agnirdahati kāṣṭhāni rakṣitāni dhanāni ca/
363.018. dṛśyante dhūmaśikharāḥ śastraṃ ca svidyate bhṛśam//316//
body.translated_text: Fire burns timbers and stored wealth; smoke-crested [flames] are seen, and weapons sweat profusely. //316//

body.text:
363.019. vīṇāśca divi dṛśyante nava māsānna varṣati/
363.020. eteṣāṃ bhūmikampānāṃ jaghanyā agnikampitāḥ//317//
body.translated_text: Lutes are seen in the sky; for nine months it does not rain. Of all earthquakes, fire-quakes are the worst. //317//

body.text:
363.021. jayati ahani pūrve kṣatriyān pārthivāṃśca hayagajarathamukhyān mantriṇo madhyamāhne/
363.023. vyathayati aparāhṇe gopaśūn vaiśyaśūdrān pradahati niśisaṃdhyā taskarānantavāsān//318//
body.translated_text: At daybreak it conquers <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and kings, the foremost of horses, elephants, and chariots, and ministers at midday; it afflicts at afternoon the cowherds, servants, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>; it burns at the evening twilight thieves and border-dwellers. //318//

body.text:
363.025. rajanimiha pradoṣe hiṃsate mlecchasaṃghān striyamapi ca napuṃsaścārdharātreṣvanantān/
363.027. kṛṣivaṇigupajīvyān hanti yāme tṛtīye vyathayati surapakṣaṃ raudrakarmāntakṛṣṇe//319//
body.translated_text: At nightfall it harms the hosts of <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians); and women and the innumerable neuter-gendered ones at midnight; in the third watch it slays those who live by agriculture and trade; it afflicts the divine host in the terrible, dark final [watch]. //319//

body.text:
363.029. pradahati śaśipakṣe yājñikaṃ brahmakṣatra śrapayati śucivṛttāneva dharme pradhānān/
363.031. viduṣi ca mṛdubhāvaṃ vindate yo hyadhīte sa bhavati nṛpapūjyo brāhmaṇo vedadarśī//320//
body.translated_text: In the bright fortnight it burns the sacrificers and the <s>Brahma-Kṣatra</s>; it scorches those of pure conduct, the foremost in <s>dharma</s>; and whoever studies with a gentle disposition among the learned — he becomes honored by kings, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sees the <s>Vedas</s>. //320//

body.text:
364.001. <364>bṛhaspateśca catvāri samāni śubhakarmaṇā/
364.002. catvāri sūryakarmāṇi tulyāni śukrakarmaṇā/
364.003. somakarmāṇi catvāri brahmakarma ca tatsamam//321//
body.translated_text: Four [actions] of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) with auspicious deeds, four actions of <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) equal to the actions of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), four actions of <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) and the action of <s>Brahman</s> equal to that. //321//

body.text: 364.004. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin bhūmikampanirdeśo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Prediction of Earthquakes.' //

body.text:
364.005. atha bhoḥ puṣkarasārinn abhiṣāmaṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ nakṣatrāṇāṃ rogotpattiṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāmi/
364.006. tacchrūyatām/
364.006. kathayatu bhagavān--
364.007. kṛttikāsūtthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.008. catūrātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//322//
body.translated_text: Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'The Arising of Diseases from the Twenty-eight <s>Nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions).' Listen to it. Let the blessed one speak — A disease arising under <s>Kṛttikā</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of four nights; thereafter one is freed. //322//

body.text:
364.009. agnirhi devatā tatra dadhnā hyasya baliṃ haret/
364.010. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//323//
body.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> (Fire) is the deity there; one should make an offering with curds. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //323//

body.text:
364.011. rohiṇyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.012. pañcarātraṃ bhavedvyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//324//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of five nights; thereafter one is freed. //324//

body.text:
364.013. devaḥ prajāpatistatra śuddhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
364.014. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//325//
body.translated_text: The god <s>Prajāpati</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with pure garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //325//

body.text:
364.015. vyādhirmṛgaśirobhūtaḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.016. aṣṭarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//326//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of eight nights; thereafter one is freed. //326//

body.text:
364.017. somo hi devatā tatra maṇḍena tu baliṃ haret/
364.018. anena balidānena tasmādrogādvimucyate//327//
body.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> (the Moon) is the deity there; one should make an offering with <s>maṇḍa</s> (rice-water). By this gift of offering, one is freed from that disease. //327//

body.text:
364.019. ārdrāyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.020. daśarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//328//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Ārdrā</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of ten nights; thereafter one is freed. //328//

body.text:
364.021. rudro hi devatā tatra pāyasena baliṃ haret/
364.022. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//329//
body.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //329//

body.text:
364.023. punarvasau bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.024. aṣṭarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//330//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Punarvasu</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of eight nights; thereafter one is freed. //330//

body.text:
364.025. ādityo devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
364.026. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//331//
body.translated_text: <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //331//

body.text:
364.027. puṣye samutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
364.028. stokakālaṃ bhavettasya pañcarātrādvimucyate//332//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Puṣya</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be of brief duration; one is freed after five nights. //332//

body.text:
364.029. devo bṛhaspatistatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
364.030. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//333//
body.translated_text: The god <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //333//

body.text:
365.001. <365>āśleṣāyāṃ bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.002. na taṃ vaidyāścikitsantu sarpastatra tu daivataḥ//334//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Āśleṣā</s>, whether in a woman or a man — physicians cannot cure it; the Serpent is the deity there. //334//

body.text:
365.003. maghāsamutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.004. aṣṭarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//335//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Maghā</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of eight nights; thereafter one is freed. //335//

body.text:
365.005. pitaro devatāstatra kṛsareṇa baliṃ haret/
365.006. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//336//
body.translated_text: The Ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>) are the deities there; one should make an offering with <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-sesame dish). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //336//

body.text:
365.007. pūrvaphālgunijo vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.008. saptarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//337//
body.translated_text: A disease born of <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of seven nights; thereafter one is freed. //337//

body.text:
365.009. aryamā devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
365.010. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucayte//338//
body.translated_text: <s>Aryaman</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //338//

body.text:
365.011. uttarāyāṃ bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.012. na taṃ vaidyāścikitsantu bhago 'pyatra tu devatā//339//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Uttarā</s> [Phālgunī], whether in a woman or a man — physicians cannot cure it; <s>Bhaga</s> is the deity there. //339//

body.text:
365.013. hastenāpyutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya va/
365.014. pañcarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//340//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Hasta</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of five nights; thereafter one is freed. //340//

body.text:
365.015. ravirhi devatā tatra gandhapuṣpairbaliṃ haret/
365.016. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//341//
body.translated_text: <s>Ravi</s> (the Sun) is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and flowers. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //341//

body.text:
365.017. citrāyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.018. aṣṭarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//342//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Citrā</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of eight nights; thereafter one is freed. //342//

body.text:
365.019. tvaṣṭā hi devatā tatra ghṛtamudgairbaliṃ haret/
365.020. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//343//
body.translated_text: <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with ghee and <s>mudga</s> (mung beans). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //343//

body.text:
365.021. svātyāṃ samutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya/
365.022. kleśito hi bhaved vyādhiḥ pañcaviṃśatirātrikaḥ//344//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Svātī</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a distressing disease of twenty-five nights. //344//

body.text:
365.023. devatātra bhaved vāyuścitramālyairbaliṃ haret/
365.024. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//345//
body.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) is the deity there; one should make an offering with various garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //345//

body.text:
365.025. viśākhāyāṃ bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.026. guruko 'sau bhaved vyādhirahānyekonaviṃśatiḥ//346//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Viśākhā</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a severe disease of nineteen days. //346//

body.text:
365.027. indrāgnī devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
365.028. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucayte//347//
body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> are the deities there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //347//

body.text:
365.029. anurādhotthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
365.030. ardhamāsaṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//348//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Anurādhā</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of a half-month; thereafter one is freed. //348//

body.text:
366.001. <366>mitro hi devatā tatra ghṛtapātraṃ baliṃ haret/
366.002. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//349//
body.translated_text: <s>Mitra</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with a vessel of ghee. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //349//

body.text:
366.003. jyeṣṭhāyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.004. kleśiko hi bhaved vyādhirahorātratrayodaśa//350//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a distressing disease of thirteen day-and-nights. //350//

body.text:
366.005. indro hi devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
366.006. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//351//
body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //351//

body.text:
366.007. mūle samutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.008. māsiko hi bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//352//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Mūla</s>, whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of one month; thereafter one is freed. //352//

body.text:
366.009. naiṛtirdevatā tatra madyamāṃsairbaliṃ haret/
366.010. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//353//
body.translated_text: <s>Nirṛti</s> (goddess of destruction) is the deity there; one should make an offering with liquor and meat. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //353//

body.text:
366.011. pūrvāṣāḍhe bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.012. sāṃkleśiko bhaved vyādhiraṣṭau māsānna saṃśayaḥ//354//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a distressing disease of eight months, without doubt. //354//

body.text:
366.013. āpo hi devatāstatra kṛsareṇa baliṃ haret/
366.014. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//355//
body.translated_text: The Waters (<s>Āpas</s>) are the deities there; one should make an offering with <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-sesame dish). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //355//

body.text:
366.015. uttarāyāṃ bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.016. saptarātraṃ bhavet vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//356//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Uttarā</s> [Āṣāḍhā], whether in a woman or a man, shall be a disease of seven nights; thereafter one is freed. //356//

body.text:
366.017. viśvo hi devatā tatra pāyasena baliṃ haret/
366.018. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//357//
body.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> (the All-gods) is the deity there; one should make an offering with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //357//

body.text:
366.019. abhijidutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.020. ṣaṇmāsān saṃbhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//358//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Abhijit</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a disease of six months; thereafter one is freed. //358//

body.text:
366.021. viṣṇuśca devatā tatra dadhimaṇḍaṃ baliṃ haret/
366.022. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//359//
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with <s>dadhimaṇḍa</s> (whey). By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //359//

body.text:
366.023. śravaṇenotthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.024. guruko hi bhaved vyādhiḥ pūrṇaṃ dvādaśamāsikam//360//
body.translated_text: A disease arising under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, whether in a woman or a man — it shall be a severe disease of a full twelve months. //360//

body.text:
366.025. viṣṇurhi devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
366.026. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//361//
body.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is freed from that disease. //361//

body.text:
366.027. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ bhaved vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
366.028. trayodaśadivastatra tataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//362//
body.translated_text: In <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, disease will arise for a woman or a man. For thirteen days there, and after that one is released. //362//

body.text:
366.029. varuṇo devatā tatra pāyasena baliṃ haret/
366.030. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//363//
body.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with milk-porridge (<s>pāyasa</s>). By this offering-rite, one is released from that disease. //363//

body.text:
367.001. <367>pūrvabhadrotthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
367.002. na taṃ vaidyāścikitsantu ahirbudhnyo 'tra daivataḥ//364//
body.translated_text: A disease arising in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, whether for a woman or a man — physicians should not treat it. <s>Ahirbudhnya</s> is the deity here. //364//

body.text:
367.003. uttarābhādrajo vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
367.004. saptarātraṃ bhaved vyādhistataścordhvaṃ vimucyate//365//
body.translated_text: A disease arising in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, whether for a woman or a man — the disease lasts seven nights, and after that one is released. //365//

body.text:
367.005. aryamā devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
367.006. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//366//
body.translated_text: <s>Aryaman</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is released from that disease. //366//

body.text:
367.007. revatyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
367.008. mṛduko hi bhaved vyādhiraṣṭāviṃśatirātrikaḥ//367//
body.translated_text: A disease arising in <s>Revatī</s>, whether for a woman or a man — the disease is mild, lasting twenty-eight nights. //367//

body.text:
367.009. pūṣā hi devatā tatra gandhamālyairbaliṃ haret/
367.010. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//368//
body.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with fragrance and garlands. By this offering-rite, one is released from that disease. //368//

body.text:
367.011. aśvinyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
367.012. sāṃkleśiko bhaved vyādhiḥ pañcaviṃśatirātrikaḥ//369//
body.translated_text: A disease arising in <s>Aśvinī</s>, whether for a woman or a man — the disease is distressing, lasting twenty-five nights. //369//

body.text:
367.013. gandharvo devatā tatra yāvakena baliṃ haret/
367.014. anena balikarmeṇa tasmādrogādvimucyate//370//
body.translated_text: A <s>Gandharva</s> is the deity there; one should make an offering with barley-gruel. By this offering-rite, one is released from that disease. //370//

body.text:
367.015. bharaṇyāmutthito vyādhiḥ striyā vā puruṣasya vā/
367.016. na taṃ vaidyāścikitsantu yamastatra tu daivataḥ/
367.017. śīlaṃ rakṣatu medhāvī tataḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyati//370//
body.translated_text: A disease arising in <s>Bharaṇī</s>, whether for a woman or a man — physicians should not treat it. <s>Yama</s> is the deity there. The wise one should preserve his virtue; then he will go to heaven. //370//

body.text: 367.018. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vyādhisamutthāno nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Arising of Diseases.'

body.text:
367.019. ayaṃ khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin bandhananirmokṣaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
367.019. tacchrūyatām/
367.020. kathayatu bhagavān--
367.021. kṛttikāsu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin baddho vā ruddho vā trirātreṇa mokṣyatīti vaktavyaḥ/
367.021. rohiṇyāṃ baddho vā ruddho vā trirātreṇa mokṣyatīti/
367.022. mṛgaśirasi baddho vā ruddho vā ekaviṃśatirātreṇa mokṣyatīti/
367.023. ārdrāyāṃ baddho vā ruddho vā ardhamāsena mokṣyatīti/
367.023. punarvassau ruddho vā baddho vā saptarātreṇa/
367.024. puṣye trirātreṇa/
367.024. āśleṣāyāṃ triṃśadrātreṇa/
367.024. maghāsu ṣoḍaśarātreṇa/
367.024. pūrvaphālgunīṣu daśarātreṇa/
367.025. viśākhāyāṃ ṣaḍviṃśadrātreṇa/
367.026. anurādhāyāmekatriṃśadrātreṇa/
367.026. jyeṣṭhāyāmaṣṭādaśarātreṇa/
367.027. abhijiti ṣaḍrātreṇa/
367.027. pūrvāṣāḍhāyāṃ caturdaśarātreṇa/
367.027. uttarāṣāḍhāyāṃ caturdaśarātreṇa/
367.028. abhijiti ṣaḍrātreṇa/
367.028. śravaṇe dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ śatabhiṣāyāṃ pūrvabhādrapade uttarabhādrapade revatyāṃ caturdaśarātreṇa/
367.029. aśvinyāṃ trirātreṇa/
367.029. bharaṇyāṃ baddho vā ruddho vā parikleśamāvāpsyatīti vaktavyaḥ//
body.translated_text:
Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Release from Imprisonment.' Listen to it. Let the blessed one speak —
O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, one who is bound or imprisoned in <s>Kṛttikā</s> will be released after three nights — so it should be declared. One bound or imprisoned in <s>Rohiṇī</s> will be released after three nights. One bound or imprisoned in <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> will be released after twenty-one nights. One bound or imprisoned in <s>Ārdrā</s> will be released after a half-month. One imprisoned or bound in <s>Punarvasu</s>, after seven nights. In <s>Puṣya</s>, after three nights. In <s>Āśleṣā</s>, after thirty nights. In <s>Maghā</s>, after sixteen nights. In <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>, after ten nights. In <s>Viśākhā</s>, after twenty-six nights. In <s>Anurādhā</s>, after thirty-one nights. In <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, after eighteen nights. In <s>Abhijit</s>, after six nights. In <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, after fourteen nights. In <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, after fourteen nights. In <s>Abhijit</s>, after six nights. In <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>, <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s>, and <s>Revatī</s>, after fourteen nights. In <s>Aśvinī</s>, after three nights. One who is bound or imprisoned in <s>Bharaṇī</s> — it should be declared that he will suffer distress.

body.text: 367.031. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin bandhananirmokṣo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Release from Imprisonment.'

body.text:
367.032. atha bhoḥ puṣkarasāriṃs tilakādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
367.032. tacchrūyatām/
367.032. kathayatu bhagavān--
body.translated_text: Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter on <s>Tilakas</s> (beauty-marks). Listen to it. Let the blessed one speak —

body.text:
368.001. <368>mūrdhni tu yasyāstilako 'sti sūkṣmaḥ knigdho bhavet padmasamānavarṇaḥ/
368.003. rājā tu tasyā bhavatīha bhartā stanopariṣṭātpratibimbamāhuḥ//372//
body.translated_text: She who has a fine <s>tilaka</s> (beauty-mark) on the crown of the head, smooth and lotus-colored — a king will be her husband; they call it a reflection above the breast. //372//

body.text:
368.005. śīrṣe tu yasyāstilakālakaḥ syāt sūkṣmo bhavedañjanacūrṇavarṇaḥ/
368.007. senāpatistasyā bhaveddhi bhartā stanāntare 'syāḥ pratibimbakaṃ syāt//373//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the head, fine and the color of collyrium-powder — a general (<s>senāpati</s>) will be her husband; between her breasts will be its reflection. //373//

body.text:
368.009. bhruvontare 'syāstilakālakaḥ syād duścāriṇīṃ tāṃ pramadāṃ vadanti/
368.011. pañcaiva tasyāḥ patayo bhavanti bahvannapānaṃ labhate nārī//374//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark between the eyebrows — they call that woman unchaste. She will have five husbands, and the woman will obtain much food and drink. //374//

body.text:
368.013. gaṇḍasya nāsādikamadhyadeśe bhavecca bimbaṃ tilakasya yasyāḥ/
368.015. tāṃ śokabhājaṃ pramadāṃ vadanti romapradeśe pratibimbamāhuḥ//375//
body.translated_text: She who has the mark of a <s>tilaka</s> in the middle region between the cheek and nose — they call that woman a bearer of sorrow; they say its reflection is in the body-hair region. //375//

body.text:
368.017. karṇe tu yasyāstilakālakaḥ syād bahuśrutāṃ tāṃ pramadāṃ vadanti/
368.019. bahuśrutāṃ tāṃ śrutidhāriṇīṃ ca trike tu yasyāḥ pratibimbakaṃ syāt//376//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the ear — they call that woman learned. She is learned and a retainer of what she has heard; and she who has its reflection on the sacrum. //376//

body.text:
368.021. yasyottaroṣṭhe tilakālakaḥ syāttāṃ bhinnasatyāṃ pramadāṃ vadanti/
368.023. kṛcchreṇa sā vai labhate hi vṛttimūrau tu tasyāstilabimbamāhuḥ//377//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the upper lip — they call that woman a breaker of truth. She obtains her livelihood with difficulty; they say the mark's reflection is on her thigh. //377//

body.text:
368.025. yasyādharoṣṭhe tilakālakaḥ syād duścāriṇīṃ tāṃ pramadāṃ vadanti/
368.027. miṣṭānnapānaṃ bahu ṛcchate sā tathā hi guhye pratibimbakaṃ syāt//378//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the lower lip — they call that woman unchaste. She obtains much sweet food and drink; and its reflection will be on her private parts. //378//

body.text:
368.029. cibuke tu yasyāstilakālakaḥ syād duścāriṇīṃ tāṃ pramadāṃ vadanti/
368.031. miṣṭānnapānaṃ bahu sā labheta guhye dvitīyaṃ pratibimbakaṃ syāt//379//
body.translated_text: She who has a dark <s>tilaka</s>-mark on the chin — they call that woman unchaste. She will obtain much sweet food and drink; a second reflection will be on her private parts. //379//

body.text: 368.033. ayaṃ bho puṣkarasāriṃstilakādhyāyo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Chapter on <s>Tilakas</s>.'

body.text:
369.001. <369>atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatrajanmaguṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
369.001. tacchrūyatām/
369.002. kathayatu bhavāṃs triśaṅko--
369.003. kṛttikāsu naro jātastejasvī priyasāhasaḥ/
369.004. bhavecchūrastathā caṇḍaḥ priyavādī ca mānavaḥ//380//
body.translated_text:
Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Qualities According to Birth-<s>Nakṣatra</s>.' Listen to it. Speak, <s>Triśaṅku</s> —
A man born in <s>Kṛttikā</s> is brilliant, fond of daring deeds, brave, fierce, and sweet-speaking. //380//

body.text:
369.005. rohiṇyāṃ puruṣo jāto dhanavān dhārmikastathā/
369.006. vyavasāyī sthiraḥ śūro dhruvaṃ cāsya sadā sukham//381//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Rohiṇī</s> is wealthy, righteous, industrious, steadfast, brave, and his happiness is always assured. //381//

body.text:
369.007. jāto mṛgaśire yastu mṛduḥ saumyastu mānavaḥ/
369.008. darśanīyo bhaveccāsau strīkāntastu viśeṣataḥ//382//
body.translated_text: One who is born in <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> — that person is gentle and mild. He will be handsome, and especially attractive to women. //382//

body.text:
369.009. ārdrājātastu hiṃsātmā caṇḍaḥ paramajalpakaḥ/
369.010. raudrakarmā bhaveccāsāvīśvaraśca śatairmahān//383//
body.translated_text: One born in <s>Ārdrā</s> is violent by nature, fierce, and excessively talkative. He will engage in cruel deeds, and will be a lord great among hundreds. //383//

body.text:
369.011. jātaḥ punarvasau yastu hyalolo buddhimānnaraḥ/
369.012. dharmaśīlo bhaveccāsau jātakrodhaśca mānavaḥ//384//
body.translated_text: One who is born in <s>Punarvasu</s> is a man free from fickleness, intelligent. He will be of righteous disposition, and also a man of quick anger. //384//

body.text:
369.013. puṣyeṇa puruṣo jātastejasvī brāhmaṇo bhavet/
369.014. kṣatriyaśca bhavedrājā vaiśyaśūdrau ca pūjitau//385//
body.translated_text: A man born under <s>Puṣya</s> will be a brilliant <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. If a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, he will become a king; <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s> will be honored. //385//

body.text:
369.015. śvasanaḥ krodhanaḥ krūto hyāśleṣāsambhavo naraḥ/
369.016. durmanuṣyaśca caṇḍaśca iti sarvamihādiśet//386//
body.translated_text: A man born of <s>Āśleṣā</s> is a breather (panting), angry, and cruel. He is a wicked person and fierce — one should declare all this here. //386//

body.text:
369.017. bahuprajñaḥ śrāddhakaro bahubhāgyastathaiva ca/
369.018. dhanavān dhānyavān bhogī maghāsu puruṣo bhavet//387//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Maghā</s> will be of great wisdom, a performer of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), and likewise of great fortune, wealthy, rich in grain, and a man of enjoyment. //387//

body.text:
369.019. pūrvaphālgunījātastu yaḥ kaścitpuruṣo bhavet/
369.020. adharmabuddhiśīlaśca gurudārābhimardakaḥ//388//
body.translated_text: Whatever man is born in <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s> will be of unrighteous disposition and intellect, and an oppressor of his teacher's wife. //388//

body.text:
369.021. uttarāyāṃ tu phālgunyāṃ jāto bhavati bhogavān/
369.022. divyajñānaśca vijñāne puruṣaḥ subhago bhavet//389//
body.translated_text: One born in <s>Uttaraphālgunī</s> will be a man of enjoyment, possessed of divine knowledge in matters of learning, and a fortunate person. //389//

body.text:
369.023. haste jātaśca śuddhātmā vikrānto mṛdubhojanaḥ/
369.024. senāpatyaṃ ca kurute 'steyakarmā bhavedasau//390//
body.translated_text: One born in <s>Hasta</s> is pure-souled, valiant, a gentle eater, holds the position of general (<s>senāpati</s>), and will be one who does not steal. //390//

body.text:
369.025. catrāsu jātaścitrākṣastathā citrakathākaraḥ/
369.026. darśanīyo bahustrīkaścitraśīlo bhavennaraḥ//391//
body.translated_text: One born in <s>Citrā</s> has beautiful eyes, is a teller of wonderful tales, handsome, having many women, and will be a man of varied character. //391//

body.text:
369.027. svātyāṃ ca puruṣo jāto bandhuślāghī vicakṣaṇaḥ/
369.028. mṛdukaḥ pānaśauṇḍaśca mitrakārī vicāravān//392//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Svātī</s> is one who praises his kinsmen, discerning, gentle, fond of drinking, a maker of friends, and thoughtful. //392//

body.text:
369.029. viśākhāsu naro jātastejasvī dravyavān mahān/
369.030. śūro vikramavān dakṣaḥ subhagaśca bhavedasau//393//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Viśākhā</s> is brilliant, wealthy, great, brave, bold, skilled, and will be fortunate. //393//

body.text:
369.031. anurādhodbhavo martyo mitravān saṃgrahī naraḥ/
369.032. śuciścaiva kṛtajñaśca dharmātmā ca bhavecca saḥ//394//
body.translated_text: A mortal born in <s>Anurādhā</s> is a man with friends, one who gathers [wealth], pure, grateful, righteous in soul — so he will be. //394//

body.text:
370.001. <370>jyeṣṭhāsu puruṣo jāto mitravānabhijāyate/
370.002. dhanurvedābhirāmaśca nārīṣu kurute manaḥ//395//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is born with friends, delighting in the science of archery, and sets his mind on women. //395//

body.text:
370.003. mūleṣu puruṣo jāto 'kṛtajñaḥ syādadhārmikaḥ/
370.004. dṛḍho vīro bhaveccāsau kilbiṣī ca sa mānavaḥ//396//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Mūla</s> will be ungrateful and unrighteous. He will be firm and heroic, and that person will also be sinful. //396//

body.text:
370.005. āṣāḍhāsu ca pūrvāsu matsarī calitendriyaḥ/
370.006. matsyamāṃsapriyaścāpi ghātakaḥ syātsa mānavaḥ//397//
body.translated_text: One [born] in <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> is envious and of unsteady senses, fond of fish and meat, and that person will be a killer. //397//

body.text:
370.007. sānukrośaśca dātā ca vidyāniṣṭhaḥ suhṛjjanaḥ/
370.008. viśvadaive naro jāto bhavedapi ca niścitaḥ//398//
body.translated_text: Compassionate, generous, devoted to learning, a friend to all — a man born in <s>Viśvadeva</s> (i.e., <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>) will be also resolute. //398//

body.text:
370.009. ācāryaḥ śāstrakartā ca viścvāsī ca kriyāparaḥ/
370.010. śravaṇe jāta āyuṣmāñ śrīmāṃśca puruṣo bhavet//399//
body.translated_text: A teacher, a maker of treatises, trustworthy, and devoted to ritual action — one born in <s>Śravaṇa</s> will be long-lived and a prosperous man. //399//

body.text:
370.011. anavasthitacittaśca citradravyaśca mānavaḥ/
370.012. dhaniṣṭhāsu bhavejjātaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvaśaṅkitaḥ//400//
body.translated_text: A man of unsteady mind, possessing various kinds of wealth — one born in <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> will be a person suspicious of everything. //400//

body.text:
370.013. vāruṇe yadi nakṣatre jāto bhavati mānavaḥ/
370.014. puruṣo dveṣaśīlaśca parivādī ca sarvaśaḥ//401//
body.translated_text: If a man is born under the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Varuṇa</s> (<s>Śatabhiṣā</s>), that man will be of hateful disposition and slanderous in every way. //401//

body.text:
370.015. jāto bhādrapadāyāṃ tu pūrvasyāmiha mānavaḥ/
370.016. cāritraguṇayuktaśca kṛtajño mukharastathā//402//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> here will be endowed with good conduct and virtues, grateful, and also talkative. //402//

body.text:
370.017. uttarasyāṃ naro jāto bhaviṣyati vicakṣaṇaḥ/
370.018. medhāvī bahvapatyaśca dharmaśīlo mahādhanaḥ//403//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> will be discerning, wise, having many offspring, of righteous disposition, and greatly wealthy. //403//

body.text:
370.019. revatyāṃ puruṣo jāto dharmātmā jñātisevakaḥ/
370.020. daridro 'lpadhano nityaṃ dāyako nānasūyakaḥ//404//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Revatī</s> is righteous in soul and a servant of his kinsmen, always poor and of little wealth, generous and not envious. //404//

body.text:
370.021. aśvinyāṃ puruṣo jāto bhavatyativicakṣaṇaḥ/
370.022. mahājanapriyaścāpi śūraśca subhagaśca saḥ//405//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Aśvinī</s> will be extremely discerning, dear to the great people, brave, and fortunate. //405//

body.text:
370.023. bharaṇyāṃ puruṣo jātaḥ pāpācāro 'vicakṣaṇaḥ/
370.024. kandarpe dātukāmaśca parataścopajīvakaḥ//406//
body.translated_text: A man born in <s>Bharaṇī</s> is of sinful conduct and unwise, desirous of giving in [matters of] love, and one who lives off others. //406//

body.text: 370.025. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatrajanmaguṇo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Qualities According to Birth-<s>Nakṣatra</s>.'

body.text:
371.001. <371>paṭha bhostriśaṅko utpātacakraṃ nāmādhyāyam/
371.001. kathayati ca--
  utpātacakranirdeśaḥ/
371.002. aṣṭāviṃśatiparyantakṛtsne nakṣatramaṇḍale/
371.003. divyā vikārā dṛśyante sūryacandragrahādiṣu//407//
body.translated_text:
Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter called 'The Wheel of Portents.' And he speaks —
Instruction on the Wheel of Portents:
In the entire circle of twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s>, celestial disturbances are seen in the sun, moon, planets, and so forth. //407//

body.text:
371.004. māghasya prathame pakṣe śailo vā pārthivo yadi/
371.005. dhūmavṛṣṭirhi āditye udayati pradṛśyate/
371.006. vidyuto vātha dṛśyante tadā vidyājjanakṣayam//408//
body.translated_text: In the first fortnight of <s>Māgha</s>, whether on a mountain or on the earth, if a rain of smoke is seen when the sun rises, or if lightning flashes are seen, then one should know there will be destruction of the people. //408//

body.text:
371.007. aśvinyāamarkato dhūmo nirgacchannapi cchādayet/
371.008. anāvṛṣṭiṃ tadā vidyātpūrṇavarṣāṇi dvādaśa//409//
body.translated_text: If in <s>Aśvinī</s>, smoke issuing from the sun covers [the sky], then one should know there will be drought for a full twelve years. //409//

body.text:
371.009. bharaṇyāṃ māghamāse tu pītasūryo 'tha dṛśyate/
371.010. samantādvadhyate rāṣṭraṃ madhye durbhikṣamādiśet//410//
body.translated_text: If in <s>Bharaṇī</s>, in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, the sun is seen as yellow, the kingdom is slaughtered on all sides — one should predict famine in the midst. //410//

body.text:
371.011. phālgune kṛttikāyāṃ tu āditye parikho yadi/
371.012. naśyanti karvaṭāstatra yadi devo na varṣati//411//
body.translated_text: If in <s>Phālguna</s>, in <s>Kṛttikā</s>, there is a halo around the sun, the market-towns there are destroyed if the rain-god does not rain. //411//

body.text:
371.013. caitramāse yadā puṣye sūrye kṛṣṇaṃ pradṛśyate/
371.014. acirodayakāle tu kṣitipālo 'varudhyate//412//
body.translated_text: If in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, when [the moon is] in <s>Puṣya</s>, blackness is seen on the sun, shortly after the time of sunrise, the ruler of the earth will be besieged. //412//

body.text:
371.015. vaiśākhamāse cārdrāyāmādityaḥ pratisūryakaḥ/
371.016. saṃgrāmaṃ tatra jānīyādubhau ghātyete pārthivau//413//
body.translated_text:
371.015. 'In the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, when the sun is a mock-sun under <s>Ārdrā</s>,
371.016. one should know there will be battle — both kings will be slain.' //413//

body.text:
371.017. gṛhyetāṃ candrasūryau vā jyaiṣṭe bharaṇijyeṣṭhayoḥ/
371.018. sāmātyo vadhyate rājā rāṣṭre durbhikṣamādiśet//414//
body.translated_text:
371.017. 'When the moon and sun are seized together in <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>, under <s>Bharaṇī</s> and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>,
371.018. the king together with his ministers is slain; one should declare famine in the realm.' //414//

body.text:
371.019. āṣāḍhe ca yadāditye pūrvabhādrapade sthite/
371.020. sāyāhne dṛśyate 'tyarthaṃ lohito maṇḍale vraṇaḥ//415//
body.translated_text:
371.019. 'In <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, when the sun is stationed in <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>,
371.020. and is seen excessively red with a wound in its disc at evening —' //415//

body.text:
371.021. paracakreṇa tadrāṣṭraṃ ṣaṇmāsān pīḍyate tadā/
371.022. kṣitipālaśca sāmātyaḥ putradāreṇa vadhyate//416//
body.translated_text:
371.021. 'then that kingdom is afflicted by an enemy army for six months,
371.022. and the king together with his ministers is slain along with his sons and wives.' //416//

body.text:
371.023. pūrvāyāṃ cottarāṣāḍhāyāmāṣāḍhe gṛhyate śaśī/
371.024. vidyād durbhikṣakalaharogāṃścātra vinirdiśet//417//
body.translated_text:
371.023. 'When the moon is seized under <s>Pūrvā</s> and <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>,
371.024. one should know and declare famine, strife, and diseases.' //417//

body.text:
371.025. māse 'tha śrāvaṇe mūle candrasūryau na bhāsataḥ/
371.026. sphuliṅgāścātra dṛśyante vidyādrogabhayaṃ mahat//418//
body.translated_text:
371.025. 'In the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, under <s>Mūla</s>, when the moon and sun do not shine,
371.026. and sparks are seen — one should know there is great fear of disease.' //418//

body.text:
371.027. māse 'śvayuji gṛhyetāmekapakṣendubhāskarau/
371.028. rājaputrasahasrāṇāṃ tadā jāyet saṃkṣayaḥ//419//
body.translated_text:
371.027. 'In the month of <s>Aśvayuj</s> (Āśvina), when the moon and sun are seized in the same fortnight,
371.028. then destruction of thousands of princes would arise.' //419//

body.text:
371.029. alakṣaṇo niḥprakāśaḥ pūrṇamāsyāṃ tu kārtike/
371.030. candrasūryāvagnivarṇau raktavarṇe nabhastale//420//
body.translated_text:
371.029. 'Without marks, without radiance, on the full moon in <s>Kārtika</s>,
371.030. when the moon and sun are fire-colored, red-hued in the sky —' //420//

body.text:
372.001. <372>ravivadbhāti tadrāṣṭraṃ vinaśyeta punaḥ punaḥ/
372.002. rājñāṃ vidyāddhatānāṃ vai bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam//421//
body.translated_text:
372.001. 'that kingdom shines like the sun, but is destroyed again and again;
372.002. one should know: the earth will drink the blood of slain kings.' //421//

body.text:
372.003. bharaṇyaṃ māghamāse tu kṛṣṇo vāyuḥ samutthitaḥ/
372.004. chādayeccandrasūryau tu śīghraṃ rāṣṭraṃ vinaśyati//422//
body.translated_text:
372.003. 'In the month of <s>Māgha</s>, under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, when a black wind arises
372.004. and covers the moon and sun — the kingdom is swiftly destroyed.' //422//

body.text:
372.005. māse tu phālgune vāyuḥ pāṃśuvarṣaṃ savidyutam/
372.006. vadhyante pūrvarājānaḥ pratiṣṭhante tathāpare//423//
body.translated_text:
372.005. 'In the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, when there is a dust-storm with lightning,
372.006. the former kings are slain and others are established in their place.' //423//

body.text:
372.007. sahādityena candre 'tha yadā kaścid grahaścaret/
372.008. vāyurvā viṣamo vāti vidyādrājavadhaṃ tadā//424//
body.translated_text:
372.007. 'When any planet moves together with the sun and the moon,
372.008. or an uneven wind blows — one should know the king will be slain.' //424//

body.text:
372.009. aśanyulke tu vaiśākhe ādityena sahotthite/
372.010. ṣaṇmāsābhyantareṇātha rāṣṭre vyasanamādiśet//425//
body.translated_text:
372.009. 'When in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, thunderbolts and meteors arise together with the sun,
372.010. within six months one should declare calamity in the realm.' //425//

body.text:
372.011. jyeṣṭhamāse yadādityo grahato nirgato bhavet/
372.012. ādityasyopaghātena grahāḥ sarve 'tha pīḍitāḥ//426//
body.translated_text:
372.011. 'In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when the sun emerges from a planet's grasp,
372.012. by the sun's injury all the planets are afflicted.' //426//

body.text:
372.013. jyeṣṭhe ca pāṃśuvarṣeta ādityaḥ pariviṣyate/
372.014. kṣitipālasahasrāṇāmeka ekastu vadhyate//427//
body.translated_text:
372.013. 'In <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when there is a dust-storm and the sun is encircled by a halo,
372.014. among thousands of kings, each one is slain.' //427//

body.text:
372.015. āṣāḍhe vāyavo vānti gacchanto bharaṇīsthitāḥ/
372.016. udapānāti śuṣyante sarvaśasyaṃ ca puṣyati//428//
body.translated_text:
372.015. 'In <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, winds blow stationed in <s>Bharaṇī</s>,
372.016. wells dry up, and all crops flourish.' //428//

body.text:
372.017. śrāvaṇe vāyavaḥ pītāḥ sadā kṛṣṇaṃ nabhastalam/
372.018. bhayaṃ tatra vijānīyātsamantāt samupasthitam//429//
body.translated_text:
372.017. 'In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the winds are yellow and the sky is always black;
372.018. one should know that fear is approaching from all sides.' //429//

body.text:
372.019. śrāvaṇe varṣate hyagniḥ pūrvabhādrapade divā/
372.020. meghāḥ śabdamutkurvanti rogadurbhikṣamādiśet//430//
body.translated_text:
372.019. 'In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, when fire rains under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> during the day,
372.020. and clouds make loud sounds — one should declare disease and famine.' //430//

body.text:
372.021. yadā bhādrapade māse nabhaḥ syācchannagarjitam/
372.022. paracakraṃ tadā rāṣṭre harate dhanasaṃcayam//431//
body.translated_text:
372.021. 'When in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, the sky is covered with thunder,
372.022. then an enemy army in the realm carries away the accumulated wealth.' //431//

body.text:
372.023. aśvayuji vātavṛṣṭiḥ syādāgatyottarāṃ diśam/
372.024. pātayeccaivamāghātaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vinaśyati//432//
body.translated_text:
372.023. 'In <s>Aśvayuj</s>, there would be wind and rain coming from the northern direction,
372.024. causing destruction by impact — the entire kingdom is destroyed.' //432//

body.text:
372.025. kārtike śuklatrayodaśyām yadā candre dhanurbhavet/
372.026. samantānnaśyate rāṣṭraṃ madhye durbhikṣamādiśet//433//
body.translated_text:
372.025. 'In <s>Kārtika</s>, on the bright thirteenth, when there is a rainbow around the moon,
372.026. the kingdom is destroyed on all sides; one should declare famine in the midst.' //433//

body.text:
372.027. ulkāpātā hyaśanayo māghamāse bhavanti vā/
372.028. aśvinyāṃ viṣaye tatra prajā śvāsena vadhyate//434//
body.translated_text:
372.027. 'Meteor-falls and thunderbolts occur in the month of <s>Māgha</s>;
372.028. in the territory under <s>Aśvinī</s>, the people are slain by pestilence.' //434//

body.text:
372.029. māse tu phālgune yatra agnivarṣaṃ nabhastalāt/
372.030. bhavecchabdastadākāśe tadrāṣṭraṃ naśyate laghu//435//
body.translated_text:
372.029. 'In the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, when there is fire-rain from the sky,
372.030. and a sound arises in the atmosphere — that kingdom is swiftly destroyed.' //435//

body.text:
372.031. svātyāṃ caitre yadā varṣaṃ niruddhaṃ vātavarṣitam/
372.032. dṛśyatendradhanuḥ kṣipraṃ nagaraṃ tadvinaśyati//436//
body.translated_text:
372.031. 'Under <s>Svātī</s> in <s>Caitra</s>, when rain is obstructed and driven by wind,
372.032. and a rainbow is seen — that city is quickly destroyed.' //436//

body.text:
373.001. <373>bharaṇyāṃ jyeṣṭhamāse tu śabda uttarato bhavet/
373.002. pītavarṇaṃ tadākāśaṃ paracakrabhayaṃ bhavet//437//
body.translated_text:
373.001. 'Under <s>Bharaṇī</s> in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, when a sound comes from the north,
373.002. and the sky becomes yellow — there will be fear of an enemy army.' //437//

body.text:
373.003. āṣāḍhe māsi puṇye 'tha dṛśyante vyoṃni vidyutaḥ/
373.004. satṛṇodakavṛṣṭibhistribhāgaṃ mucyate prajā//438//
body.translated_text:
373.003. 'In the auspicious month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, when lightning is seen in the sky
373.004. with rain of grass and water, one-third of the people are saved.' //438//

body.text:
373.005. śrāvaṇe tu yadā mūle bahu devaḥ pravarṣati/
373.006. dṛśyatendradhanustatra kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahadbhayam//439//
body.translated_text:
373.005. 'In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, when the god rains abundantly under <s>Mūla</s>,
373.006. and a rainbow is seen — there is great fear for the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.' //439//

body.text:
373.007. māse bhādrapade yatra nirghātaḥ patati kṣitau/
373.008. sukṛcchrā vāyavo vānti mahadrogabhayaṃ tadā//440//
body.translated_text:
373.007. 'In the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, when a thunderbolt falls upon the earth,
373.008. and harsh winds blow — there is then great fear of disease.' //440//

body.text:
373.009. māse bhādrapade puṣye vidigbhyo niścared dhvaniḥ/
373.010. kṣatriyaḥ kupyate kṣipraṃ vipakṣā tu tadā prajā//441//
body.translated_text:
373.009. 'In the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, under <s>Puṣya</s>, when a sound issues from the intermediate directions,
373.010. the <s>Kṣatriya</s> is quickly angered, and the people become hostile.' //441//

body.text:
373.011. bharaṇyāmaśvayuje śabda upariṣṭādbhavedyadi/
373.012. satṛṇaṃ cotsṛjetpāṃśu tāpasānāṃ mahadbhayam//442//
body.translated_text:
373.011. 'Under <s>Bharaṇī</s> in <s>Aśvayuj</s>, if a sound comes from above,
373.012. and dust is released along with grass — there is great fear for ascetics.' //442//

body.text:
373.013. kārtike tu yadārdrāyāṃ śabdaḥ śrūyeta bhairavaḥ/
373.014. catuṣpadaḥ kārṣakāṇāṃ mṛtyuṃ tatra vinirdiśet//443//
body.translated_text:
373.013. 'In <s>Kārtika</s>, under <s>Ārdrā</s>, when a terrifying sound is heard,
373.014. one should declare death of cattle and of cultivators.' //443//

body.text:
373.015. mārgaśīrṣe dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ tūryaśabdo 'mbare bhavet/
373.016. vātāturastadā rāṣṭre vyādhirbhavati dāruṇaḥ//444//
body.translated_text:
373.015. 'In <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, when the sound of drums arises in the sky,
373.016. then a disease caused by wind-affliction, severe, arises in the realm.' //444//

body.text:
373.017. pauṣamāse yadā svātyāṃ śabdo bhavati bhairavaḥ/
373.018. abhīkṣṇaṃ viṃdyudākāśe paṇḍitānāṃ mahadbhayam//445//
body.translated_text:
373.017. 'In the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, under <s>Svātī</s>, when a terrifying sound arises,
373.018. and frequent lightning appears in the sky — there is great fear for the learned.' //445//

body.text:
373.019. māghe śukle tu nirghāto nityaṃ śāmyedvasuṃdharām/
373.020. jānīyāttṛtīye varṣe sakalaṃ rāṣṭravibhramam//446//
body.translated_text:
373.019. 'In <s>Māgha</s>, in the bright fortnight, when a thunderbolt constantly strikes the earth,
373.020. one should know: in the third year, there will be total upheaval of the kingdom.' //446//

body.text:
373.021. jyeṣṭhāyāṃ phālgune māse kṛṣṇavāyuḥ samākulaḥ/
373.022. abhīkṣṇaṃ kampate bhūmirbrahmacāribhayaṃ tadā//447//
body.translated_text:
373.021. 'Under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> in the month of <s>Phālguna</s>, when a black wind rages in turmoil,
373.022. and the earth trembles frequently — there is then fear for celibate students.' //447//

body.text:
373.023. pūrvabhādrapadāyāṃ tu caitre kampetkṣitirdivā/
373.024. tasmin varṣe ca tadrāṣṭre parasainyānmahadbhayam//448//
body.translated_text:
373.023. 'Under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> in <s>Caitra</s>, if the earth trembles during the day,
373.024. in that year, in that kingdom, there is great fear from an enemy army.' //448//

body.text:
373.025. pūrvāyāṃ cedāṣāḍhāyāṃ rātrau caitre ca niścalet/
373.026. asibhirhanyate rājā hanyate ca mahājanaḥ//449//
body.translated_text:
373.025. 'Under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>, if the earth quakes at night in <s>Caitra</s>,
373.026. the king is slain by swords, and the great populace is slain.' //449//

body.text:
373.027. vaiśākhe kampitā bhūmiḥ kṛṣṇapakṣe hyabhīkṣṇaśaḥ/
373.028. anāvṛṣṭyā tu durbhikṣaṃ māsān ṣaṭ tatra nirdiśet//450//
body.translated_text:
373.027. 'In <s>Vaiśākha</s>, when the earth trembles frequently in the dark fortnight,
373.028. one should declare famine from drought for six months.' //450//

body.text:
373.029. jyeṣṭhe māse bharaṇyāṃ tu divā kampedvasuṃdharā/
373.030. vidyādyodhasahasrāṇāṃ mahī pāsyati śoṇitam//451//
body.translated_text:
373.029. 'In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, when the earth trembles during the day,
373.030. one should know: the earth will drink the blood of thousands of warriors.' //451//

body.text:
373.031. jyeṣṭhe māse yadā mūle rātrau bhūmiḥ prakampate/
373.032. pratyanto vadhyate rājā rāṣṭre baliṃ samādiśet//452//
body.translated_text:
373.031. 'In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, under <s>Mūla</s>, when the earth trembles at night,
373.032. the border-king is slain; one should declare tribute in the realm.' //452//

body.text:
374.001. <374>āṣāḍhe kampate bhūmiḥ puṣyanakṣatrasaṃsthite/
374.002. śasyaṃ vinaśyate tatra kalikarma ca jāyate//453//
body.translated_text:
374.001. 'In <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the earth trembles when stationed under the <s>Puṣya</s> <s>nakṣatra</s>;
374.002. crops are destroyed there, and strife arises.' //453//

body.text:
374.003. prakampante yadā caityā ārdrāyāṃ vā maghāsu vā/
374.004. jvaleyuḥ prapateyurvā naśyedrāṣṭraṃ tadā laghu//454//
body.translated_text:
374.003. 'When shrines tremble under <s>Ārdrā</s> or <s>Maghā</s>,
374.004. or when they burn or fall — the kingdom is swiftly destroyed.' //454//

body.text:
374.005. caityā yatra prakampante hasanti ca namanti ca/
374.006. sarāṣṭraḥ kṣitipastatra nacirānnāśamarcchati//455//
body.translated_text:
374.005. 'Where shrines tremble, laugh, and bow,
374.006. the king together with his realm swiftly approaches destruction.' //455//

body.text:
374.007. śrāvaṇe kampate bhūmiḥ pūrvabhādrapadāsthite/
374.008. sadā parājito rājā caurai rāṣṭre ca vadhyate//456//
body.translated_text:
374.007. 'In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the earth trembles when stationed under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s>;
374.008. the king is always defeated, and the realm is plagued by thieves.' //456//

body.text:
374.009. kārtike kṣitikampena yadā caityaṃ viśīryate/
374.010. dvāraṃ vā nagarasyātha bhūyiṣṭhaṃ naśyate prajā//457//
body.translated_text:
374.009. 'In <s>Kārtika</s>, when a shrine crumbles from an earthquake,
374.010. or the gate of the city — the greater part of the people perishes.' //457//

body.text:
374.011. vāme vā dakṣiṇe cendoḥ śṛṅge tiṣṭhed bṛhaspatiḥ/
374.012. mahābhogā vinaśyeyuḥ prakāśāḥ pṛthivīśvarāḥ//458//
body.translated_text:
374.011. 'When <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) stands at the left or right horn of the moon,
374.012. mighty and illustrious rulers of the earth perish.' //458//

body.text:
374.013. sūryācandramasoḥ śṛṅge lohitāṅgo yadāruhet/
374.014. śrūrākṣamantrikātpīḍāṃ pratyantānāṃ vinirdiśet//459//
body.translated_text:
374.013. 'When <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars) ascends to the horn of the sun and moon,
374.014. one should declare affliction from a fierce-eyed sorcerer upon the border regions.' //459//

body.text:
374.015. śanaiścaro yadā śṛṅge somasyābhiruhettadā/
374.016. jñeyaṃ rogabhayaṃ ghoraṃ durbhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet//460//
body.translated_text:
374.015. 'When <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) ascends to the horn of the moon,
374.016. one should know there is terrible fear of disease, and one should declare famine.' //460//

body.text:
374.017. rāhuṇā nigṛhītastu colkayā hanyate śaśī/
374.018. ṣaṇmāsābhyantarāttatra rājño vyasanamādiśet//461//
body.translated_text:
374.017. 'When the moon is seized by <s>Rāhu</s> and struck by a meteor,
374.018. within six months one should declare calamity for the king.' //461//

body.text:
374.019. yasya caivātha nakṣare śaśī sūryo vigṛhyate/
374.020. rāhuṇā kṣitipo rājyaiḥ saha pīḍāmavāpnuyāt//462//
body.translated_text:
374.019. 'In whichever <s>nakṣatra</s> the moon or sun is seized
374.020. by <s>Rāhu</s>, the king suffers affliction together with his kingdom.' //462//

body.text:
374.021. rājño vai cātha nakṣatre candraṃ keturyadā viśet/
374.022. pratyantarājabhiḥ sārdhaṃ śastramūrcchāṃ vinirdiśet//463//
body.translated_text:
374.021. 'When <s>Ketu</s> enters the moon in the king's <s>nakṣatra</s>,
374.022. one should declare the surging of weapons together with border-kings.' //463//

body.text:
374.023. candramadhyagataḥ śukraḥ phālgunyātha maghā yadā/
374.024. sarvadhānyāni śuṣyeyustadā rogaṃ vinirdiśet//464//
body.translated_text:
374.023. 'When <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) is situated in the middle of the moon under <s>Phalgunī</s> or <s>Maghā</s>,
374.024. all grains would dry up; one should then declare disease.' //464//

body.text:
374.025. bṛhaspatiśca śukraśca lohitāṅgaḥ śanaiścaraḥ/
374.026. likhyanti somaśṛṅgasya tadā vidyānmahadbhayam//465//
body.translated_text:
374.025. 'When <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars), and <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn)
374.026. scratch the horn of the moon — then one should know great fear.' //465//

body.text:
374.027. dhūmaketurmahābhāgaḥ puṣyamāruhya tiṣṭhati/
374.028. caturdiśaṃ tadā vidyātparacakraiḥ prābhavam//466//
body.translated_text:
374.027. 'When the great comet (<s>Dhūmaketu</s>) ascends <s>Puṣya</s> and stands there,
374.028. one should know: dominion of enemy armies from the four directions.' //466//

body.text:
374.029. maghāyāṃ lohitāṅgo vā śravaṇe vā bṛhaspatiḥ/
374.030. tiṣṭhetsaṃvatsarastrīṇi bhayaṃ vidyātsamāgatam//467//
body.translated_text:
374.029. 'When <s>Lohitāṅga</s> (Mars) stands in <s>Maghā</s>, or <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) in <s>Śravaṇa</s>,
374.030. for three years one should know that fear has arrived.' //467//

body.text:
374.031. tiṣṭhecchukro 'tha rohiṇyāṃ jyeṣṭhe māse kathaṃcana/
374.032. vyākuryānniyatamatra kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahadbhayam//468//
body.translated_text:
374.031. 'When <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) stands in <s>Rohiṇī</s> in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, in any manner,
374.032. it would certainly bring about great fear for the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.' //468//

body.text:
375.001. <375>viśākhāyāṃ samīpasthau bṛhaspatiśanaiścarau/
375.002. somo vā raviṇā sārdhaṃ paracakrabhayaṃ tadā//469//
body.translated_text:
375.001. 'When <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) and <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) are close together in <s>Viśākhā</s>,
375.002. or the moon with the sun — there is then fear of an enemy army.' //469//

body.text:
375.003. kākāḥ śyenāśca gṛdhrāśca vaseyuḥ sahitā mudā/
375.004. maithunaṃ vāritaṃ veyuḥ paraiḥ saha raṇastadā//470//
body.translated_text:
375.003. 'When crows, hawks, and vultures dwell together in joy,
375.004. or mating is checked — there will be battle with enemies.' //470//

body.text:
375.005. śyeno hastinivāse vā abhirohetpunaḥ punaḥ/
375.006. paracakreṇa yuddhaṃ tu bhaveccāpi punaḥ punaḥ//471//
body.translated_text:
375.005. 'When a hawk repeatedly mounts an elephant stable,
375.006. there will be battle with an enemy army again and again.' //471//

body.text:
375.007. kanyā prasūyate yatra caturhastā catuḥstanī/
375.008. strīṇāmeva bhavettatra maraṇaṃ hyatidāruṇam//472//
body.translated_text:
375.007. 'Where a girl is born with four arms and four breasts,
375.008. there will be exceedingly terrible death of women.' //472//

body.text:
375.009. garbhasthā dārakā yatra hasanti ca vadanti ca/
375.010. tasya deśasya jānīyādvināśaṃ samupasthitam//473//
body.translated_text:
375.009. 'Where children in the womb laugh and speak,
375.010. one should know destruction is approaching that country.' //473//

body.text:
375.011. ekapādāṃstripādāṃśca caturaṅgāṃstathaiva ca/
375.012. nāryo yatra prasūyante rājño vyasanamādiśet//474//
body.translated_text:
375.011. 'Where women give birth to one-footed, three-footed,
375.012. or four-limbed beings — one should declare calamity for the king.' //474//

body.text:
375.013. sūyante vikṛtān garbhān saṃtānān bhayavyañjanān/
375.014. pramadā yatra deśe tu rājā tatra vinaśyati//475//
body.translated_text:
375.013. 'Where women give birth to deformed offspring, progeny marked by fear,
375.014. in that region the king perishes.' //475//

body.text:
375.015. laghuhastaśīrṣamukhān mānuṣaṃ kāyamāśritān/
375.016. pramadā yatra sūyante rāṣṭraṃ tatra vinaśyati//476//
body.translated_text:
375.015. 'Where women give birth to beings with small hands, heads, and faces but human bodies,
375.016. in that kingdom there is destruction.' //476//

body.text:
375.017. kharāśca mahiṣāścāpi paśavo 'tha tathāvidhāḥ/
375.018. dvitriśīrṣāḥ prasūyante deśe yatra sa naśyati//477//
body.translated_text:
375.017. 'When donkeys, buffaloes, and other such animals
375.018. are born with two or three heads — the country where this occurs is destroyed.' //477//

body.text:
375.019. śṛgālaśvānamakarahayarūpāśca mānavāḥ/
375.020. jāyante yatra deśe tu sa deśo laghu naśyati//478//
body.translated_text:
375.019. 'Where humans are born in the forms of jackals, dogs, <s>makaras</s>, and horses,
375.020. that country is quickly destroyed.' //478//

body.text:
375.021. pādāvubhau yadā vaiśyā gurviṇī saṃprasūyate/
375.022. deśasya vilayaṃ brūyātparacakreṇa dāruṇam//479//
body.translated_text:
375.021. 'When a pregnant <s>Vaiśya</s> woman gives birth to only both feet,
375.022. one should declare terrible destruction of the country by an enemy army.' //479//

body.text:
375.023. pūrvārdhaḥ pakṣinarayorgarbho yatra prasūyate/
375.024. rājā vā rājāmātyo vā saha deśena naśyati//480//
body.translated_text:
375.023. 'Where the front half of a bird-human hybrid is born,
375.024. the king or the king's minister perishes together with the country.' //480//

body.text:
375.025. kumbhāṇḍo jāyate yatra dvimukho 'tha caturmukhaḥ/
375.026. trinetrastrimukho vāpi vidyāttatra mahadbhayam//481//
body.translated_text: 'Where a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> (gourd-headed being) is born, or a two-faced or four-faced one, or a three-eyed or three-faced one — know that there is great danger.' //481//

body.text:
375.027. saukareṇa tu vaktreṇa śarīraṃ mānuṣam yadi/
375.028. sūtaṃ caturdiśaṃ rāṣṭraṃ hanyāttatra na saṃśayaḥ//482//
body.translated_text: 'If a human body with a boar's face is born there, it destroys the kingdom in the four directions — of this there is no doubt.' //482//

body.text:
375.029. ādityasya tu rūpeṇa mānuṣo yatra jāyate/
375.030. vibhramātsakalaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vināśamupagacchati//483//
body.translated_text: 'Where a human is born with the form of the sun, the entire kingdom, through confusion, goes to destruction.' //483//

body.text:
376.001. <376>uttānaśāyī bālastu deśe yatra dvijottamaḥ/
376.002. dṛṣṭaḥ pravyāharan vedān kṣipraṃ deśo vinaśyati//484//
body.translated_text: 'Where, O best of twice-born, an infant lying on its back is seen reciting the <s>Vedas</s>, that land is quickly destroyed.' //484//

body.text:
376.003. kukṣiṃ bhittvā yadā bālo garbhānniṣkramate svayam/
376.004. atrāṇāṃ mātaraṃ kṛtvā sa deśo naśyate laghu//485//
body.translated_text: 'When an infant, splitting the belly, emerges from the womb by itself, having left the mother without protection — that land is destroyed swiftly.' //485//

body.text:
376.005. garbhasthāḥ sūkarā uṣṭrāḥ sarpāśca śakunistathā/
376.006. strīṇāṃ garbhātprasūyante deśe tu bhayamādiśet//486//
body.translated_text: 'When boars, camels, serpents, or birds in embryo are born from the wombs of women — danger for that land should be declared.' //486//

body.text:
376.007. pauruṣaṃ gārdabhaṃ cātha saukaraṃ cārthavigraham/
376.008. gāvo yatra prasūyante nirdiśedbhayamāgatam//487//
body.translated_text: 'Where cows give birth to offspring of human, donkey, or boar form — declare that danger has arrived.' //487//

body.text:
376.009. nārī gṛhṇāti garbhaṃ vā adṛṣṭastanarūpiṇī/
376.010. vināśaṃ tasya deśasya sanṛpasya vinirdiśet//488//
body.translated_text: 'Where a woman conceives a child or is seen with an unseen breast-form — declare the destruction of that land along with its king.' //488//

body.text:
376.011. jaṭī dīrghanakho yatra sukṛṣṇaḥ paruṣacchaviḥ/
376.012. sa jano jāyate yatra rāṣṭraṃ sādhipatiṃ dahet//489//
body.translated_text: 'Where a person is born matted-haired, long-nailed, very dark, and rough-skinned — that kingdom will burn along with its ruler.' //489//

body.text:
376.013. agrīvā dantasahitā jāyante yatra bālakāḥ/
376.014. śuṣyeta sakalaṃ śasyaṃ janaśca vilayaṃ vrajet//490//
body.translated_text: 'Where infants are born neckless and with teeth — all crops will wither and the people will perish.' //490//

body.text:
376.015. ekabāhuraśīrṣo 'tha garbho yatra prasūyate/
376.016. svayaṃ kṣubhyeta tadrāṣṭraṃ vinaśyeta na saṃśayaḥ//491//
body.translated_text: 'Where an embryo is born with one arm and without a head — that kingdom will be agitated of its own accord and will be destroyed without doubt.' //491//

body.text:
376.017. phale phalam yadā paśyetpuṣpe vā puṣpamāśritam/
376.018. garbhāḥ sraveyur nārīṇām yuvarājaśca vadhyate//492//
body.translated_text: 'When one sees fruit within fruit, or a flower attached to a flower — the wombs of women will miscarry and the crown-prince will be killed.' //492//

body.text:
376.019. akāle pādapā yatra puṣpyanti ca phalanti ca/
376.020. latā gulmo 'tha vallī vā deśe tatra bhayaṃ bhavet//493//
body.translated_text: 'Where trees flower and bear fruit out of season — whether creeper, bush, or vine — in that land danger will arise.' //493//

body.text:
376.021. vṛkṣopariṣṭātpaśyedvā sravantamātmaśoṇitam/
376.022. kūjamānaṃ pataṅgaṃ vā tadā vidyānmahadbhayam//494//
body.translated_text: 'If one sees from the top of a tree its own blood flowing, or a moth buzzing — then know there is great danger.' //494//

body.text:
376.023. vṛkṣāṇāṃ maṇḍapānāṃ vā chāyā na parivartate/
376.024. caturvarṇabhayaṃ tatra kalikarma ca jāyate//495//
body.translated_text: 'Where the shadows of trees or canopies do not revolve — there is danger for all four <s>varṇas</s>, and deeds of the age of <s>Kali</s> arise.' //495//

body.text:
376.025. puṣpyeyuḥ pādapā yatra vividhāḥ puṣpajātayaḥ/
376.026. kalpavṛkṣaprakṛtayastato vidyānmahadbhayam//496//
body.translated_text: 'Where trees bloom with various kinds of flowers, resembling the nature of wish-fulfilling trees — from that, know there is great danger.' //496//

body.text:
376.027. anāvartam yadā puṣpaṃ phalaṃ cāpi pradṛśyate/
376.028. vināśaṃ tasya deśasya durbhikṣaṃ kalahaṃ vadet//497//
