body.translated_text: 'When flowers and fruits are seen that do not return — declare destruction, famine, and strife for that land.' //497//

body.text:
376.029. sthānāsthānaṃ gatā vṛkṣā dṛśyeyuryatra kutracit/
376.030. pūrvapratiṣṭhito rājā nacireṇa vicālyate//498//
body.translated_text: 'Where trees are seen moved from their proper to improper places, anywhere — the formerly established king is displaced before long.' //498//

body.text:
377.001. <377>daivāsuraṃ ca saṃgrāmaṃ paśyedadbhutadarśanam/
377.002. śastraṃ mūrcchayate tatra taskaraiścāpi pūrvavat//499//
body.translated_text: 'When one sees the wondrous spectacle of a battle between gods and <s>Asuras</s>, weapons become powerless there, and so too with thieves as before.' //499//

body.text:
377.003. kampate rudate śāstā gacchan vā yatra dṛśyate/
377.004. paracakrāttadā vidyādatyarthaṃ tatparājayam//500//
body.translated_text: 'Where a teacher-image is seen trembling, weeping, or moving — know from hostile forces that there will be extreme defeat.' //500//

body.text:
377.005. devatā yatra deśe tu nṛtyanti ca hasanti ca/
377.006. aśrūṇi pātayeyurvā tadā vidyānmahadbhayam//501//
body.translated_text: 'Where in a land the deities dance and laugh, or shed tears — then know there is great danger.' //501//

body.text:
377.007. devatā yatra krīḍanti jvalanti nimiṣanti vā/
377.008. caleyurathavā yatra kṣitipo 'nyo bhavettadā//502//
body.translated_text: 'Where deities play, blaze, blink, or move about — at that time, a different king will arise.' //502//

body.text:
377.009. śivaliṅgam yadā kampedgagane vātha dṛśyate/
377.010. nimajjate dharaṇyāṃ vā dhruvaṃ rājavadho bhavet//503//
body.translated_text: 'When a <s>Śivaliṅga</s> trembles, or is seen in the sky, or sinks into the earth — certainly the king will be killed.' //503//

body.text:
377.011. pratimāḥ parivartante dhūmāyante rudanti ca/
377.012. prasvidyeyuḥ pradhāveyuranyo rājā bhaviṣyati//504//
body.translated_text: 'When images reverse their position, emit smoke, weep, sweat, or run — a different king will arise.' //504//

body.text:
377.013. acalo vā caletsthānāccalaṃ vāpyacalaṃ bhavet/
377.014. amātyo hanti rājānaṃ kalahaṃ cātra nirdiśet//505//
body.translated_text: 'When the immovable moves from its place, or the movable becomes immovable — a minister kills the king, and strife should be declared.' //505//

body.text:
377.015. vamanti rudhiraṃ kanyā namante vā diśo daśa/
377.016. ayuktā vā pravartante kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahadbhayam//506//
body.translated_text: 'When maidens vomit blood, or bow to the ten directions, or move about improperly — there is great danger for the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.' //506//

body.text:
377.017. varṣate kusumam yatra raktabindumathāpi vā/
377.018. prāṇino vividhān vāpi vidyāccaurabhayaṃ tadā//507//
body.translated_text: 'Where flowers rain down, or drops of blood, or various living creatures — know that there is danger from thieves.' //507//

body.text:
377.019. yūpāḥ purāṇā nigamā devāgārāṇi cetiyāḥ/
377.020. nagarāṇyatha dhūmyante kṣipraṃ rājā vinaśyati//508//
body.translated_text: 'When ancient sacrificial posts, market-towns, temples, and shrines, and cities emit smoke — the king will be quickly destroyed.' //508//

body.text:
377.021. indurvā dīpavṛkṣo vā dīpo yatra na dīpyate/
377.022. rājyakāmaḥ kumāro vā kṣubhyedviṭapako 'pi vā//509//
body.translated_text: 'Where a lamp on a lamp-tree or any lamp does not burn, or a prince desiring the kingdom becomes agitated, or even a branch —' //509//

body.text:
377.023. antaḥpure yadā nīḍaṃ kurvate madhumakṣikāḥ/
377.024. astraṃ vāpi gṛhaṃ dahyād rājño vyasanamādiśet//510//
body.translated_text: 'When honeybees build a nest in the inner palace, or a weapon or house is burned — declare calamity for the king.' //510//

body.text:
377.025. patedantaḥpure vidyud vṛkṣo vāpyāśrame tathā/
377.026. puri caityacchāyāyāṃ vā rājārthe patitā hi sā//511//
body.translated_text: 'If lightning strikes in the inner palace, or on a tree in the hermitage, or in the shadow of a shrine in the city — it has fallen for the king's sake.' //511//

body.text:
377.027. prākāre vāyudhāgāre gopurāsthānakeṣu vā/
377.028. vāyasaḥ kurute nīḍaṃ sāmātyo dhvaṃsate nṛpaḥ//512//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow builds a nest on the rampart, the armory, the gateway, or in stalls — the king will fall together with his ministers.' //512//

body.text:
377.029. anāhatebhyastūryebhyaḥ svayaṃ śabdo viniścaret/
377.030. svacakrakṣobhadoṣeṇa sarvaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vilupyate//513//
body.translated_text: 'When from unbeaten drums a sound issues forth of its own accord — by the fault of disturbance from its own forces, the entire kingdom is plundered.' //513//

body.text:
378.001. <378>māsaśoṇitavarṣaṃ vā patrapuṣpaphalāni vā/
378.002. yadābhivarṣettadvarṣaṃ cakrai rāṣṭraṃ vilupyate//514//
body.translated_text: 'When for a month it rains blood, or leaves, flowers, and fruits — if it rains thus, the kingdom will be plundered by hostile forces.' //514//

body.text:
378.003. madhuphāṇitapuṣpāṇi gandhavarṣāṇyathāpi vā/
378.004. diśo dāhāśca dṛśyeyurmāradurbhikṣalakṣaṇam//515//
body.translated_text: 'When honey, sugar, flowers, and fragrant rains fall, and burning of the horizons is seen — these are signs of death and famine.' //515//

body.text:
378.005. meghaḥ samantato garjedupavarṣetsacātakam/
378.006. śoṇitaṃ sakarakaṃ syāttadā vidyātparādbhayam//516//
body.translated_text: 'When clouds thunder all around and rain with hail, and there is blood with stony precipitation — then know there is danger from enemies.' //516//

body.text:
378.007. vidyucca patate ghorā karakāṇāṃ ca varṣaṇam/
378.008. gandharvanagaraṃ cātha dṛṣṭvā vidyānmahadbhayam//517//
body.translated_text: 'When terrible lightning falls and hailstones rain down, and a <s>Gandharva</s>-city (mirage) is seen — know there is great danger.' //517//

body.text:
378.009. śaśī śoṇitasaṃkāśo madhye kṛṣṇo vivarṇavān/
378.010. sāmantakena pīḍyate vidyādrāṣṭre mahadbhayam//518//
body.translated_text: 'When the moon appears blood-colored, black in the middle, discolored — when it is oppressed by <s>Sāmantaka</s> — know there is great danger in the kingdom.' //518//

body.text:
378.011. pradīpitāgnisaṃkāśo yadā dṛśyeta candramāḥ/
378.012. gaganaṃ dahyate tatra lokapīḍā jvareṇa ca//519//
body.translated_text: 'When the moon appears like a blazing fire — the sky burns there, and the people are afflicted by fever.' //519//

body.text:
378.013. yadā gairikasaṃkāśaḥ kṣipramevopaśāmyati/
378.014. varṣaṇasyāgamo vidyādyadi vāyuḥ pravāyate//520//
body.translated_text: 'When it appears ochre-colored and quickly fades — know that the arrival of rain is imminent, even if winds are blowing.' //520//

body.text:
378.015. saṃdhyāyāṃ dhūmravārṇāyāṃ dṛśyetenduśca bhāskaraḥ/
378.016. vicchinno brahmarūpeṇa varṣaṃ tatra vinirdiśet//521//
body.translated_text: 'When at twilight, in a smoke-colored sky, both the moon and the sun are seen — cut off by a divine form — declare rain there.' //521//

body.text:
378.017. nāpsu majjati nāpyagnau pūrvavacca na dṛśyate/
378.018. agnirutpatsyate tatra koṣṭhāgāraṃ daheta saḥ//522//
body.translated_text: 'When it neither sinks in water nor burns in fire, and cannot be seen as before — fire will arise there and it will burn the granary.' //522//

body.text:
378.019. dhvajāgre vāyaso yatra lambapakṣo vidhāvate/
378.020. udakaṃ saṃharetkṣipramagnitaḥ sumahadbhayam//523//
body.translated_text: 'Where a crow runs with drooping wings on the top of a flagstaff — gather water quickly; there is very great danger from fire.' //523//

body.text:
378.021. jalaṃ jājvalyamānaṃ tu matsyo nirdahati svayam/
378.022. anāvṛṣṭiṃ tadā brūyād durbhikṣaṃ ca mahadbhayam//524//
body.translated_text: 'When water blazes forth and a fish burns itself — then declare drought, famine, and great danger.' //524//

body.text:
378.023. puradvāre yadāgacchetsvayamāraṇyako mṛgaḥ/
378.024. cakradvaye 'pi durbhikṣaṃ rāṣṭre rogaṃ ca nirdiśet//525//
body.translated_text: 'When a wild forest animal comes of its own accord to the city-gate — declare famine from both forces in the kingdom, and disease.' //525//

body.text:
378.025. triśīrṣaḥ pañcaśīrṣo vā yadā sarpo 'tha dṛśyate/
378.026. anāvṛṣṭyā tadā vidyātsarvaśasyaṃ vinaśyati//526//
body.translated_text: 'When a three-headed or five-headed serpent is seen — know that by drought all crops will perish.' //526//

body.text:
378.027. kuśūlo yatra dṛśyeta kampayastu vasuṃdharām/
378.028. koṣṭhāgārāṇi naśyeyurye cānye dhanasaṃcayāḥ//527//
body.translated_text: 'Where a whirlwind is seen, shaking the earth — granaries will perish, and all other stores of wealth.' //527//

body.text:
378.029. sarpa udyataśīrṣastu yudhyate puruṣaiḥ saha/
378.030. cakradvayādrogataśca vidyāttatra mahadbhayam//528//
body.translated_text: 'When a serpent with raised head fights with men — from both forces, and from disease, know there is great danger.' //528//

body.text:
379.001. <379>bila ekatra bahavaḥ sarpāḥ supariveṣṭitāḥ/
379.002. śastramṛtyuṃ tadā vidyāt kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahadbhayam//529//
body.translated_text: 'When many serpents are closely intertwined in one hole — then know there will be death by weapons; great danger for the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.' //529//

body.text:
379.003. niścarantyavadhānena khaḍgāḥ prajvalitā yadā/
379.004. tatastaṃ nacirātpaśyetsaṃgrāmaṃ pratyupasthitam//530//
body.translated_text: 'When swords issue forth blazing, heedlessly — soon afterward, see that battle has arrived.' //530//

body.text:
379.005. kākaḥ śyenaśca gṛdhro vā yasya nīyeta mūrdhani/
379.006. ṣaṇmāsābhyantare rājā mriyate sapurohitaḥ//531//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow, hawk, or vulture alights upon someone's head — within six months, the king together with his chaplain will die.' //531//

body.text:
379.007. prāsādāśca prakampante śaraṇāni gṛhāṇi ca/
379.008. mahābalaṃ ca vadhyeta rāṣṭrasya rājapālakaḥ//532//
body.translated_text: 'When palaces tremble, and shelters and houses likewise — the mighty one will be killed, the protector-king of the realm.' //532//

body.text:
379.009. vajroddhṛtā diśaḥ sarvāḥ kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdiśam/
379.010. varṣeyuḥ śoṇitam yatra kṣitipālo 'tra vadhyate//533//
body.translated_text: 'When all the directions are lit up by lightning, and in the dark fortnight blood rains in the four directions — the ruler of the earth will be killed.' //533//

body.text:
379.011. sūryasyodayakāle tu maholkā nipatedyadā/
379.012. rājaputrāshasrāṇāṃ bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam//534//
body.translated_text: 'When at the time of sunrise a great meteor falls — the earth will drink the blood of thousands of princes.' //534//

body.text:
379.013. vṛkṣāḥ sarpāḥ prakampeyurmucyeyustvaco vā tathā/
379.014. sarvasminneva rāṣṭre tu vidyācchatrubhayaṃ mahat//535//
body.translated_text: 'When trees and serpents tremble, or shed their bark — in that entire kingdom, know there is great danger from enemies.' //535//

body.text:
379.015. dine hyulkāprayuktirvā jvalantī yadi dṛśyate/
379.016. raktotpādaṃ tadā vidyātsaṃgrāmaṃ bhīmadarśanam//536//
body.translated_text: 'When by day a blazing meteor is seen applied or falling — then know there will be bloodshed and a battle terrible to behold.' //536//

body.text:
379.017. asiṃ prajvalitaṃ praśyettomaraṃ cakrameva ca/
379.018. vidyātpaśyanti śastrāṇi saṃgrāmaṃ bhīmadarśanam//537//
body.translated_text: 'When one sees a blazing sword, a lance, and a discus — know that they see weapons; a battle terrible to behold.' //537//

body.text:
379.019. dīrghamucchvasate vāśvah aśrūṇi ca nipātayet/
379.020. pādena karṣate śīghram yuddhe rājavadho dhruvam//538//
body.translated_text: 'When a horse sighs deeply and sheds tears, and paws the ground quickly — in battle, the king's death is certain.' //538//

body.text:
379.021. kākaśced gṛhamāruhya hā putra iti vāśati/
379.022. sarvaḥ praṇaśyate deśo nagaragrāmakarvaṭaḥ//539//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow, mounting a house, cries out "Alas, son!" — the entire land will perish, city, village, and hamlet.' //539//

body.text:
379.023. anagnau jāyate dhūmaḥ sthale padmāni vā yadā/
379.024. vināśaṃ tasya deśasya niyamācchīghramādiśet//540//
body.translated_text: 'When smoke arises without fire, or lotuses appear on dry land — declare the destruction of that land, with certainty and speed.' //540//

body.text:
379.025. āravanti yadā ghoraṃ meghā vṛkamṛgāstathā/
379.026. vināśaṃ tasya deśasya vidyācchīghramupasthitam//541//
body.translated_text: 'When clouds roar terribly, and wolves and wild beasts likewise — know that the destruction of that land has swiftly arrived.' //541//

body.text:
379.027. chinnasrotā bhavennadyaścirakālavahā api/
379.028. gṛhāḥ śūnyodakenāpi śuṣkāstatra bhayaṃ bhavet//542//
body.translated_text: 'When rivers of long-standing current are cut off — houses empty of water, dried up — danger will arise there.' //542//

body.text:
379.029. pratisrotā yadā nadyo vahantyaprativāritāḥ/
379.030. nityodvignā janapadā nirdiśecca janakṣayam//543//
body.translated_text: 'When rivers flow against their current, unimpeded — the countryfolk are constantly in distress; declare the destruction of the people.' //543//

body.text:
380.001. <380>dhanūṃṣyākṛṣyamāṇāni dhūmāyanti jvalanti ca/
380.002. anyadvāpi praharaṇaṃ parebhyo jāyate bhayam//544//
body.translated_text: 'When bows being drawn emit smoke and blaze, and other weapons too — danger arises from enemies.' //544//

body.text:
380.003. mayūragrīvasaṃkāśaḥ pariveśo niśākare/
380.004. vidyādrājasahasrāṇāṃ mahī pāsyati śoṇitam//545//
body.translated_text: 'When a halo around the night-maker (moon) has the color of a peacock's neck — know that the earth will drink the blood of thousands of kings.' //545//

body.text:
380.005. narāṇāṃ pramadānāṃ ca ratiharṣo na jāyate/
380.006. sarvatra śokacintā vā mahattatra bhayaṃ bhavet//546//
body.translated_text: 'When neither joy nor pleasure in love arises among men and women, and sorrow and anxiety are everywhere — there will be great danger.' //546//

body.text:
380.007. nirgranthā ṛṣayaḥ santo deśātprakrameyuryataḥ/
380.008. nadīṃ bhittvā nikuñjān vā sa deśo naśyate 'cirāt//547//
body.translated_text: 'When unclad sages, being pure, depart from the land — and when a river breaks through or thickets are broken — that land will perish before long.' //547//

body.text:
380.009. yatrauṣadhyaśca virasā jalaṃ ca parihīyate/
380.010. vidyāddeśaṃ tamutsṛṣṭaṃ devatā-ṛṣisādhubhiḥ//548//
body.translated_text: 'Where herbs become tasteless and water diminishes — know that land to be abandoned by deities, sages, and holy men.' //548//

body.text:
380.011. matsyāḥ kūrmāśca sarpāśca mriyante yatra jāṅgalāḥ/
380.012. dhanaskandhaḥ striyāstatra sapatnairvipralopsyate//549//
body.translated_text: 'Where fish, turtles, and serpents die in dry land — the wealth and the woman there will be seized by rivals.' //549//

body.text:
380.013. apūrvāḥ pakṣiṇo yatra sthale vāriṇi eva vā/
380.014. dṛśyeyuḥ paracakreṇa dhanaskandho vilopsyate//550//
body.translated_text: 'Where unprecedented birds are seen, whether on land or in water, the wealth-store will be plundered by an enemy army.' //550//

body.text:
380.015. mahāpatho yadā kakṣaiḥ prasṛtairapatho bhavet/
380.016. sagrāmakarvaṭaṃ rāṣṭraṃ putreṇa saha naśyati//551//
body.translated_text: 'When the great highway becomes impassable due to spreading thickets, the kingdom along with its villages and market-towns perishes together with its prince.' //551//

body.text:
380.017. nānotpātacakranirdeśo nāmādhyāyaḥ/
380.018. paṭha bhostriśaṅko puruṣapinyādhyāyam/
380.018. atha kim/
380.018. kathayatu bhagavān--atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin puruṣapinyādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāmi/
380.019. tacchrūyatām/
380.019. kathayatu bhagavān--
380.020. aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ puṣkarasārin nakṣatrāṇi prakīrtitāni, yāni candrasūryaniḥsṛtānyanuvahanti/
380.021. tatra sukugṛṣṭyā aṣṭāṅgalapramāṇayā dvādaśākṣagṛṣṭayaḥ svaśarīraṃ dairdhyeṇa jñātavyam//
body.translated_text: This is the chapter called 'Instruction on the Wheel of Various Portents.' 'Recite, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the chapter on body-marks of a person.' 'What then?' 'Let the lord speak.' 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter on body-marks of a person — let it be heard.' 'Let the lord speak.' 'Twenty-eight <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) have been proclaimed, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, which follow the course of the moon and the sun. Therein, by a good finger-breadth of eight finger-widths as measure, twelve finger-breadth units — one should know one's own body by its length.'

body.text:
380.022. ekākṣagṛṣṭiḥ śīrṣamūrdhni ekapādatalaṃ bhavet/
380.022. caturdaśagṛṣṭayo nakṣatrāṇāṃ padam yatra saṃdṛśyante, tadanyathā na bhavati/
380.023. nakṣatre yatra yo jātastatra tatra saṃdṛśyate//
body.translated_text: 'One finger-breadth unit corresponds to the crown of the head; one sole of the foot is equivalent. Fourteen finger-breadths are where the stations of the <s>nakṣatras</s> are seen — it is not otherwise. In whichever <s>nakṣatra</s> one is born, there it is seen.'

body.text:
380.024. puruṣapinyaḥ/
380.025. kṛttikāyāṃ hi jātasya mukhe vai caturaṅgalaḥ/
380.026. pinyo dakṣiṇato yasya lomaśaḥ kṛṣṇalohitaḥ//552//
body.translated_text: 'The body-marks of a person: One born under <s>Kṛttikā</s> has a four-finger-breadth mark on the face. His mark is on the right side — he is hairy and dark-reddish.' //552//

body.text:
380.027. bhogavān yaśasā yuktaḥ piṇḍato jvalati śriyā/
380.028. kṛttikāsvatha jātasya bhavatyetaddhi lakṣaṇam//553//
body.translated_text: 'He is wealthy, endowed with fame, and blazes with glory in his body. This indeed is the characteristic of one born under <s>Kṛttikā</s>.' //553//

body.text:
380.029. dṛśyate vraṇa evāyam yasya vai caturaṅgalaḥ/
380.030. rohiṇyāṃ jātakaḥ so 'pi vidvān dharmarataḥ sadā//554//
body.translated_text: 'A scar is seen on this one that is four finger-breadths. One born under <s>Rohiṇī</s>, he too is learned and always devoted to <s>Dharma</s>.' //554//

body.text:
380.031. maṇḍito bhogasampanno hrīyuktaścāpi sarvataḥ/
380.032. śūro vijayasampanno nityaṃ śatrupramardakaḥ//555//
body.translated_text: 'Adorned, endowed with enjoyments, and modest in every way, heroic, endowed with victory, and always a crusher of enemies.' //555//

body.text:
381.001. <381>grīvāyāmardhagṛṣṭyā tu dāho yasya pradṛśyate/
381.002. mṛgaśīrṣe hyasau jātaḥ śūro bhogasamarpitaḥ//556//
body.translated_text: 'On the neck, by half a finger-breadth, a burn-mark is seen on him — one born under <s>Mṛgaśīrṣa</s>, heroic and devoted to enjoyments.' //556//

body.text:
381.003. ardhadvitīyagṛṣṭyā tu pinyo vāme hi yasya tu/
381.004. ārdrāyāṃ krodhano jāto mūrkho gopatikaśca saḥ//557//
body.translated_text: 'By two-and-a-half finger-breadths, one whose mark is on the left side — one born under <s>Ārdrā</s>, he is wrathful, foolish, and a lord of cattle.' //557//

body.text:
381.005. vāme kakṣe vraṇo yasya kṛṣṇaścaiva punarvasau/
381.006. dhanadhānyasamṛddho hi jāyate svalpamedhasaḥ//558//
body.translated_text: 'One whose scar is in the left armpit, dark, born under <s>Punarvasu</s> — he is born rich in wealth and grain, but of little intelligence.' //558//

body.text:
381.007. tathaiva puṣye jāto 'sau dṛśyate varalakaṇaḥ/
381.008. cakramadhye ca haste ca sūryaścandro virājate//559//
body.translated_text: 'Likewise, one born under <s>Puṣya</s> — an excellent mark is seen on him: in the middle of the palm and on the hand, the sun and moon shine forth.' //559//

body.text:
381.009. ardhapradakṣiṇāvartāḥ keśāḥ sarve hi saṃsthitāḥ/
381.010. parimaṇḍalaśca kāyena jitakleśo 'pi nāyakaḥ//560//
body.translated_text: 'All his hairs are arranged in half-clockwise whorls. He is round-bodied, one who has conquered afflictions, and a leader.' //560//

body.text:
381.011. hṛdaye yasya dāhaḥ syādāśleṣāyāṃ kalipriyaḥ/
381.012. duḥśīlo duḥkhasaṃvāso maithunābhirataśca saḥ//561//
body.translated_text: 'One who has a burn-mark on the heart, born under <s>Āśleṣā</s> — he is fond of quarrels, of bad conduct, difficult to live with, and devoted to sexual intercourse.' //561//

body.text:
381.013. adha urasi pṛṣṭhe vā yasya vraṇaḥ pradṛśyate/
381.014. maghāyāṃ dhanavāñ jāto mahātmā dhārimiko naraḥ//562//
body.translated_text: 'One whose scar is seen below on the chest or on the back — born under <s>Maghā</s>, he is wealthy, great-souled, and a righteous man.' //562//

body.text:
381.015. nābhyāṃ dakṣiṇavāmābhyāṃ vraṇo yasya pradṛśyate/
381.016. pūrvaphālgunījāte 'sau matsarī cālpajīvitaḥ//563//
body.translated_text: 'One whose scar is seen on the right or left side of the navel — born under <s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s>, he is envious and short-lived.' //563//

body.text:
381.017. caturaṅgulato nābhyā yasya pinyaḥ pradṛśyate/
381.018. uttaraphālgunījāto bhogaśīlaḥ śrutodyataḥ//564//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark is seen four finger-breadths from the navel — born under <s>Uttaraphalgunī</s>, he is devoted to enjoyments and zealous in learning.' //564//

body.text:
381.019. śroṇyāmalohitaḥ pinyo haste jātasya dṛśyate/
381.020. cauraḥ śaṭhaśca māyāvī mandapuṇyo 'lpamedhasaḥ//565//
body.translated_text: 'On the hip, a blood-red mark is seen on one born under <s>Hasta</s> — he is a thief, deceitful, and cunning, of little merit and little intelligence.' //565//

body.text:
381.021. vyañjane yasya pinyastu dṛśyate niyamena hi/
381.022. citrājātaḥ sa cedrogī nṛtyagītaratastathā//566//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark is seen invariably on the private parts — born under <s>Citrā</s>, he is indeed sickly, and devoted to dancing and singing.' //566//

body.text:
381.023. vyañjane 'pi ca ūrdhve vā pītaḥ pinyaḥ pradṛśyate/
381.024. jātaḥ svātyāmasau lubdho guṇadviṣṭo hyapaṇḍitaḥ//567//
body.translated_text: 'On the private parts or above them, a yellow mark is seen — one born under <s>Svātī</s>, he is greedy, hostile to good qualities, and unlearned.' //567//

body.text:
381.025. kugṛṣṭyā yasya ūrubhyāṃ pinyo lohita eva hi/
381.026. ākīrṇo naranārībhirviśākhāyāṃ bhaṭo 'graṇīḥ//568//
body.translated_text: 'By a small finger-breadth on the thighs, one whose mark is indeed blood-red, surrounded by men and women — born under <s>Viśākhā</s>, he is a soldier and a leader.' //568//

body.text:
381.027. vidvāñ śūro jitāmitro nityaṃ saukhyaparāyaṇaḥ/
381.028. śriyā dhṛtyā ca saṃpanno 'cyutaḥ svarupapadyate//569//
body.translated_text: 'Learned, heroic, having conquered enemies, always devoted to happiness, endowed with glory and steadfastness, unfallen — he attains his own true nature.' //569//

body.text:
381.029. dvitīyagṛṣṭyāmūrubhyāmaṅge yasya pradṛśyate/
381.030. śīlavānanurādhāyāṃ dharmabhogasamanvitaḥ//570//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark is seen by two finger-breadths on the thighs, on the body — born under <s>Anurādhā</s>, he is virtuous and endowed with righteous enjoyments.' //570//

body.text:
382.001. <382>adho yasyeha corubhyāṃ pinyo jyeṣṭhe sa jāyate/
382.002. alpāyurapriyo duḥkhī duḥśīlaḥ kṛpaṇastathā//571//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark is below on both thighs — he is born under <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>: short-lived, unloved, miserable, of bad conduct, and wretched.' //571//

body.text:
382.003. jānubhyāmūrdhvataḥ sūkṣmo vraṇo yasyeha dṛśyate/
382.004. mūlena bhāgyavāñ jātaḥ svagṛhaṃ nāśayellaghu//572//
body.translated_text: 'One whose fine scar is seen here above both knees — born under <s>Mūla</s>, he is fortunate, but quickly destroys his own house.' //572//

body.text:
382.005. pūrvāṣāḍhāsu jātasya pinyaḥ syājjānumaṇḍale/
382.006. dāyako dharma āsaṅgyacyutaḥ svargaparāyaṇaḥ//573//
body.translated_text: 'One born under <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> has a mark on the knee-cap: he is generous, devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, unattached, unfallen, and destined for heaven.' //573//

body.text:
382.007. uttarāyāmāṣāḍhāyāṃ jātasya tilakastrike/
382.008. yadi dṛśyetsa medhāvī bhogavānsyājjanapriyaḥ//574//
body.translated_text: 'One born under <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> has a beauty-mark on the shin — if it is seen, he is intelligent, wealthy, and dear to the people.' //574//

body.text:
382.009. dvitīyaḥ pinyo dṛśyeta dhanavān bhogavān sadā/
382.010. satyapriyastathārogo 'cyutaḥ svargaṃ ca gacchati//575//
body.translated_text: 'If a second mark is seen, he is always wealthy and prosperous, truth-loving, healthy, unfallen, and goes to heaven.' //575//

body.text:
382.011. dhaniṣṭhāyāṃ ca jaṅghāyām yasya pinyaḥ pradṛśyate/
382.012. krodhano mandarāgaśca prājño bhogavivarjitaḥ//576//
body.translated_text: 'One born under <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, whose mark is seen on the calf of the leg — he is wrathful, of mild passion, wise, but devoid of enjoyments.' //576//

body.text:
382.013. dvikugṛṣṭyā ca jaṅghāyāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pinyaḥ pradṛśyate/
382.014. mūrkhaḥ śatabhiṣāyāṃ tu mriyate hyudakena saḥ//577//
body.translated_text: 'By two small finger-breadths on the calf, a dark mark is seen — a fool born under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, he dies by water.' //577//

body.text:
382.015. adho jaṅghāṃ kugṛṣṭyā tu pūrvabhādrapade vraṇaḥ/
382.016. paropatāpako mūrkho daridraścaura ityapi//578//
body.translated_text: 'Below the calf, by a small finger-breadth, one born under <s>Pūrvabhādrapadā</s> has a scar — he is one who harms others, foolish, destitute, and also a thief.' //578//

body.text:
382.017. kugṛṣṭyā yasya pinyaḥ syājjāto bhādrapadottare/
382.018. dānaśīlaḥ smṛtiprāpto dayāpanno viśāradaḥ//579//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark is by a small finger-breadth, born under <s>Uttarabhādrapadā</s> — he is charitable, possessed of mindfulness, compassionate, and skilled.' //579//

body.text:
382.019. ubhayoḥ pādayoḥ sūkṣmaḥ pinyo yasya pradṛśyate/
382.020. revatyāṃ jāyate nīco nāpitaḥ sa bhavatyapi//580//
body.translated_text: 'One whose fine mark is seen on both feet — born under <s>Revatī</s>, he is base and becomes even a barber.' //580//

body.text:
382.021. aṅguṣṭhavivare pinyo nīlo yasya pradṛśyate/
382.022. arogo balavānnityamaśvinyāṃ jāta eva saḥ//581//
body.translated_text: 'One whose dark mark is seen in the gap between the big toes — he is always healthy and strong, born indeed under <s>Aśvinī</s>.' //581//

body.text:
382.023. atha pāṇitale pinyo bharaṇyāmakṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ/
382.024. vadhyaghātaśca duḥśīlaḥ syānnarakaparāyaṇaḥ//582//
body.translated_text: 'Now, a mark in the palm of the hand — one born under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, it is said to be imperishable. He is a killer and executioner, of bad conduct, and destined for hell.' //582//

body.text:
382.025. nakṣatrāṇāṃ padaṃ hyetadyena caryā prajāyate/
382.026. etaddhi lokaprajñānaṃ loko yatra samāśritaḥ//583//
body.translated_text: 'This indeed is the station of the <s>nakṣatras</s> by which one's destiny is born. This indeed is the worldly knowledge upon which the world relies.' //583//

body.text: 382.027. iti pinyādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on body-marks.

body.text:
382.028. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin piṭakādhyāyaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
382.028. tacchrūyatām/
382.029. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
382.030. piṭakādhyāyaḥ/
382.031. ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvasthānagataṃ punaḥ/
382.032. strīṇāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ ca piṭakaṃ sarvakarmakam//584//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called the <s>Piṭaka</s> (Boil) Chapter — let it be heard.' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'The <s>Piṭaka</s> Chapter: Henceforth I shall declare, regarding all bodily locations, for women and for men, the <s>piṭaka</s> (boil/mole) that determines all outcomes.' //584//

body.text:
383.001. <383>lābhālābhaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā/
383.002. prājñā yenābhijānanti taṃ ca sarvaṃ nibodhatām//585//
body.translated_text: 'Gain and loss, happiness and sorrow, life and death likewise — that by which the wise know all this, let it be understood.' //585//

body.text:
383.003. tatrābhighātadagdhā vā tilāstadrūpakā api/
383.004. visphoṭavarṇabhedāśca piṭakābhihitāḥ smṛtāḥ//586//
body.translated_text: 'Therein, those caused by injury or burning, those resembling sesame seeds, blisters, and discolorations — these are called <s>piṭakas</s> (moles/marks).' //586//

body.text:
383.005. śvetavarṇena piṭako viprāṇāṃ pūjito bhavet/
383.006. kṣatopamaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ vaiśyānāṃ pītakaḥ smṛtaḥ//587//
body.translated_text: 'A <s>piṭaka</s> of white color is honored among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Among <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, it resembles a wound; among <s>Vaiśyas</s>, it is said to be yellowish.' //587//

body.text:
383.007. śūdrāṇāmasitaḥ śreṣṭho vivarṇo mlecchajātiṣu/
383.008. yadā savarṇapiṭako mūrdhni rājā mahān smṛtaḥ//588//
body.translated_text: 'Among <s>Śūdras</s>, the best is dark; among <s>Mleccha</s> (barbarian) castes, it is discolored. When a <s>piṭaka</s> of matching color appears on the crown, a great king is proclaimed.' //588//

body.text:
383.009. śīrṣe tu dhanadhānyābhyāṃ kāntaye subhagāya ca/
383.010. upaghātaṃ bhruvorvidyātstrīlābho bhruvasaṃgame//589//
body.translated_text: 'On the head, it brings wealth, grain, beauty, and good fortune. One should know a mark between the eyebrows as distress; at the juncture of the brows, there is gain of a woman.' //589//

body.text:
383.011. akṣisthāne tu piṭakaḥ karoti priyadarśanam/
383.012. akṣibhrūbhāge śokāya gaṇḍe putravadho dhruvam//590//
body.translated_text: 'A <s>piṭaka</s> located at the eye makes one pleasing to behold. On the region between eye and brow, it brings sorrow; on the cheek, the death of a son is certain.' //590//

body.text:
383.013. aśrupāto dhruvaṃ śokaḥ śravaṇe goṣu nāśakaḥ/
383.014. karṇapīṭhe vibhūṣāya nāsāvaṃśe tu jātaye//591//
body.translated_text: 'Tears are certain, and sorrow; on the ear, it causes destruction of cattle. On the ear-lobe, it brings adornment; on the bridge of the nose, it brings progeny.' //591//

body.text:
383.015. nāsāgaṇḍe putralābhaṃ vastralābhaṃ dhruvaṃ vadet/
383.016. nāsāgre jāte nāpnoti gandhabhogānabhīpsitān//592//
body.translated_text: 'On the nose-cheek, one should declare gain of a son and certainly gain of garments. When arising on the nose-tip, one does not obtain the desired enjoyments of fragrance.' //592//

body.text:
383.017. uttaroṣṭhe tathādhare cānnapānaṃ śubhāśubham/
383.018. cibuke hanudeśe ca dhanaṃ gāvaḥ satāṃ śriyaḥ//593//
body.translated_text: 'On the upper lip and lower lip — food and drink, auspicious and inauspicious. On the chin and jaw region — wealth, cattle, and the splendor of the virtuous.' //593//

body.text:
383.019. gale tu dānamāpnoti pānamābharaṇāni ca/
383.020. śiraḥsaṃdhau ca grīvāyāṃ śiraśchedanamādiśet//594//
body.translated_text: 'On the throat, one obtains gifts, beverages, and ornaments. At the junction of the head and at the neck, one should predict beheading.' //594//

body.text:
383.021. jāto 'yaṃ śiraso mūle hanuni ca dhanakṣayaḥ/
383.022. bhaikṣacaryā bhavetsaṃdhau hṛdaye priyasaṃgamaḥ//595//
body.translated_text: 'Arising at the base of the head and on the jaw — loss of wealth. At the junction, there will be begging for alms; on the heart, there is meeting with a beloved.' //595//

body.text:
383.023. pṛṣṭhe tu duḥkhaśayyāyai annapānakṣayāya ca/
383.024. pārśve tu sukhaśayyāyai stane tu sutajanyatā//596//
body.translated_text: 'On the back — an uncomfortable bed and loss of food and drink. On the side — a comfortable bed. On the breast — birth of a son.' //596//

body.text:
383.025. jātena śivamāpnoti na cāpriyasamāgamaḥ/
383.026. bāhvoḥ śatruvināśāya yuktaṃ strīlābha eva ca//597//
body.translated_text: 'By one arising there, one obtains auspiciousness and no meeting with the unwanted. On the arms — for the destruction of enemies, coupled with the gain of a woman.' //597//

body.text:
383.027. dadātyābharaṇaṃ jātaḥ prabāhvoḥ kūrpare kṣudhā/
383.028. maṇibandhe niyamanamaṃsābhyāṃ harṣa eva ca//598//
body.translated_text: 'One arising on the forearms gives ornaments. At the elbow — hunger. At the wrist — restraint. On the shoulders — joy indeed.' //598//

body.text:
383.029. saubhagaṃ dhanalābhaṃ ca jātaḥ pāṇau dadāti ca/
383.030. puṣpito hyekadeśe tu daśaneṣu nakheṣu ca//599//
body.translated_text: 'Good fortune and gain of wealth — one arising on the hand bestows these. And when blossoming in a particular area, on the teeth or the nails —' //599//

body.text:
384.001. <384>jātena hṛdi jānīyād bhrātṛputrasamāgamam/
384.002. jaṭhare somadānāya nābhyāṃ strīlābhamādiśet//600//
body.translated_text: 'By one arising on the heart, one should know reunion with brothers and sons. On the belly — for the giving of <s>Soma</s>. At the navel — one should predict gain of a woman.' //600//

body.text:
384.003. jaghane vyasanaṃ vidyānnāryā dauḥśīlyameva ca/
384.004. putrotpattistu vṛṣaṇe liṅge bhāryā tu śobhanā//601//
body.translated_text: 'On the buttock, one should know calamity and also the unchastity of a woman. On the testicles — birth of a son. On the penis — a beautiful wife.' //601//

body.text:
384.005. pṛṣṭhānte sukhabhāgitvaṃ sphici cāpi dhanakṣayaḥ/
384.006. ūrujātāśca piṭakā dhanasaubhāgyadāyakāḥ//602//
body.translated_text: 'At the end of the back — enjoyment of happiness. On the hip — loss of wealth. Boils arising on the thigh are givers of wealth and good fortune.' //602//

body.text:
384.007. jānau śatrubhayaṃ vidyāttathaiva ca dhanakṣayam/
384.008. jānusaṃdhau vijānīyānmeḍhrake hyatha jātakaiḥ/
384.009. vijayaṃ jñānalābhaṃ ca putrajanma vinirdiśet//603//
body.translated_text: 'On the knee, one should know fear from enemies and also loss of wealth. At the knee-joint, one should know — and by those arising on the male organ — victory, gain of knowledge, and the birth of a son should be predicted.' //603//

body.text:
384.010. strīlābhaṃ vakṣasi caiva bhavedanyo nirarthakaḥ/
384.011. jaṅghāyāṃ parasevā tu paradeśāttu bhujyate//604//
body.translated_text: 'Gain of a woman on the chest, but another one is meaningless. On the calf — servitude to others, and one is sustained from a foreign land.' //604//

body.text:
384.012. maṇibandhe tu piṭako bandhanaṃ nirdiśed dhruvam/
384.013. paribādhaṃ sa labhate bandhanaṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ//605//
body.translated_text: 'A <s>piṭaka</s> at the wrist should be predicted as certainly indicating bondage. He obtains suffering, and bondage without doubt.' //605//

body.text:
384.014. pārśve gulphe ca jānīyācchastreṇa maraṇaṃ dhruvam/
384.015. aṅgulīṣu dhruvaṃ śoko vyādhiścāṅguliparvasu/
384.016. pravāsaṃ pravasennityaṃ tathaivottarapādake//606//
body.translated_text: 'On the side and the ankle, one should know death by a weapon is certain. On the fingers — sorrow is certain, and disease on the finger-joints. One always goes abroad, and likewise on the upper foot.' //606//

body.text:
384.017. yasya pādatale jātastathā hastale 'pi ca/
384.018. dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ sutā gāvaḥ striyo yānāni cāpnuyāt//607//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mark arises on the sole of the foot and also on the palm of the hand — he shall obtain wealth, grain, sons, cattle, women, and vehicles.' //607//

body.text:
384.019. snigdhaṃ snigdheṣu vijñeyaṃ caleṣu ca calaṃ phalam/
384.020. sthānasthe vipulaṃ dadyāt phalaṃ nṛṇāṃ śubhodayam//608//
body.translated_text: 'Among the smooth-skinned, the result should be known as smooth; among the unstable, the result is unstable. For one in a fixed position, it gives abundant fruit — an auspicious arising for men.' //608//

body.text:
384.021. vivarṇo viparītaśca phalaṃ sarvaṃ prayacchati/
384.022. puṃsāṃ madhye ye snigdhāśca deśe dakṣiṇataśca ye/
384.023. tathā cābhyantare caiva sthāne tu pratipūjitāḥ//609//
body.translated_text: 'One that is discolored or contrary gives entirely opposite results. For men, those that are smooth and in the middle, those that are on the right side, and likewise those that are on the inner side — these are honored in their respective positions.' //609//'

body.text:
384.024. strīṇāṃ mṛduṣu deśeṣu vaktrānteṣu ca parvataḥ/
384.025. tattvaṃ vijñāya pinyānāṃ sthānaṃ varṇaṃ ca janma ca//610//
body.translated_text:
On women's soft spots and at the corners of the mouth, [there are] moles.
Having ascertained the reality of the moles — their location, color, and origin — // 610 //

body.text:
384.026. sthānāsthānaṃ ca matimān vikāraṃ gatimeva ca/
384.027. ādiśettu naraḥ paścādyathaivaṃ samudāhṛtam//611//
body.translated_text:
their proper and improper placement, their change, and their movement —
the wise man should afterward declare, just as has been stated. // 611 //

body.text:
384.028. vāmabhāge tu nārīṇāṃ vijñeyāḥ piṭakāḥ śubhāḥ/
384.029. dakṣiṇe tu manuṣyāṇāṃ bhavanti hyarthasādhakāḥ//612//
body.translated_text:
On the left side of women, moles are to be known as auspicious;
on the right side of men, they serve to accomplish [their] purposes. // 612 //

body.text:
384.030. viparītāstu piṭakā moghāstu bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ/
384.031. yathoktānāṃ ca saṃdhisthāḥ sarve viphaladāḥ smṛtāḥ//613//
body.translated_text:
But reversed moles are declared to be fruitless and many;
and those situated at the joints of the [body parts] mentioned are all declared to give no fruit. // 613 //

body.text:
385.001. <385>siddhā dhruvā vraṇā bhidyāstathā sadyaḥkṛtāśca ye/
385.002. dharmakīlasamāścaiva sarve te piṭakāḥ smṛtāḥ//614//
body.translated_text:
Established, fixed, wound-bursting, and those that are freshly formed,
and those resembling pegs of <s>dharma</s> — all these are classified as moles. // 614 //

body.text:
385.003. guṇadoṣāśca sarveṣāṃ tathāpyanye prakīrtitāḥ/
385.004. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ śiṣyebhyo nityadarśanam//615//
body.translated_text:
The merits and defects of all [moles], as well as others, have been declared.
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> to his disciples — the perpetual observation. // 615 //

body.text:
385.005. na nakhena na śastreṇa nāyasena kathaṃcana/
385.006. kāñcanena suvarṇena dahedviprāṃśca bhojayet//616//
body.translated_text:
Not with a nail, not with a blade, not with iron in any way —
with gold [alone should one cauterize]; and one should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // 616 //

body.text: 385.007. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin piṭakādhyāyanāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'The Study of Moles.'

body.text:
385.008. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin svapnādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
385.008. tacchrūyatām/
385.008. atha kim/
385.009. kathayatu bhagavān--
385.010. svapnādhyāyaḥ/
385.011. śubhāśubhaṃ ca svapnānām yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam/
385.012. devatābrāhmaṇau gāvau vahniṃ prajvalitaṃ tathā/
385.013. yastu paśyati svapnānte kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//617//
body.translated_text:
Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter on dreams.
Listen to it.
Now what?
Let the blessed one speak —
The Chapter on Dreams.
The auspicious and inauspicious fruits of dreams that have been declared:
he who sees at the end of a dream a deity, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, cows, or a blazing fire —
his household prospers. // 617 //

body.text:
385.014. yastu paśyati svapnānte rājānaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayam/
385.015. suvarṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ caiva kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//618//
body.translated_text:
He who sees at the end of a dream a king, an elephant, a horse,
gold, or a bull — his household prospers. // 618 //

body.text:
385.016. sārasāṃśca śukān haṃsān krauñjāñ śvetāṃśca pakṣiṇaḥ/
385.017. yastu paśyati svapne vai kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//619//
body.translated_text:
<s>Sārasa</s> cranes, parrots, geese, <s>krauñca</s> herons, and white birds —
he who sees [these] in a dream, his household prospers. // 619 //

body.text:
385.018. samṛddhāni ca śasyāni navāni surabhīṇi ca/
385.019. padminīṃ puṣpitāṃ cāpi pūrṇakumbhāṃstathaiva ca//620//
body.translated_text:
Flourishing crops, fresh and fragrant,
a lotus pond in bloom, and full water-pots as well — // 620 //

body.text:
385.020. prasannamudakaṃ caiva puṣpāṇi vividhāni ca/
385.021. yastu paśyati svapnānte kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//621//
body.translated_text:
clear water and various flowers —
he who sees [these] at the end of a dream, his household prospers. // 621 //

body.text:
385.022. pāṇau pāde 'tha vā jānau śastreṇa dhanuṣāpi vā/
385.023. prahārā yasya dīyante tasyāmbaro 'bhivardhate//622//
body.translated_text:
On the hand, or on the foot, or on the knee —
he to whom blows are given with a weapon or a bow, his garments increase. // 622 //

body.text:
385.024. tārācandramasau sūryaṃ nakṣatrāṇi grahāṃstathā/
385.025. yastu paśyati svapnānte kuṭumbaṃ tasya vardhate//623//
body.translated_text:
The stars, the moon, the sun, the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), and the planets —
he who sees [these] at the end of a dream, his household prospers. // 623 //

body.text:
385.026. aśvapṛṣṭhaṃ gajaskandham yānāni śayanāni ca/
385.027. yo 'bhirohati svapnānte mahadaiśvaryamāpnuyāt//624//
body.translated_text:
The back of a horse, the shoulder of an elephant, vehicles and couches —
he who mounts [these] at the end of a dream shall attain great sovereignty. // 624 //

body.text:
385.028. patitaścāruhed bhūyastatrasthaśca vibudhyate/
385.029. eśvaryadhanalābhāya naṣṭalābhāya nirdiśet//625//
body.translated_text:
One who has fallen and climbs up again, and one who awakens while standing there —
one should predict [this as indicating] the gain of sovereignty and wealth, and the recovery of what was lost. // 625 //

body.text:
385.030. goyutaṃ ca rathaṃ svapne hayaṃ vā yo 'bhirohati/
385.031. tatrasthaśca vibudhyeta eśvaryamadhigacchati//626//
body.translated_text:
He who, in a dream, mounts a chariot yoked with oxen, or a horse,
and awakens while standing thereon — he attains sovereignty. // 626 //

body.text:
386.001. <386>prapātaṃ parvataṃ caiva yo 'bhirohati mānavaḥ/
386.002. tatrasthaśca vibudhyeta eśvaryamadhigacchati//627//
body.translated_text:
A man who climbs a precipice or a mountain,
and awakens while standing thereon — he attains sovereignty. // 627 //

body.text:
386.003. āsane śayane yāne teṣāmārohaṇātkṣayaḥ/
386.004. yeṣāmārohaṇaṃ śastaṃ teṣāmārohaṇātkṣayaḥ//628//
body.translated_text:
From [ascending] a seat, a couch, or a vehicle, there is decline.
For those whose ascent is auspicious, [the reverse] — from ascending, decline. // 628 //

body.text:
386.005. yeṣāmārohaṇāddoṣāsteṣāmārohaṇād guṇāḥ/
386.006. trisāhasraṃ bhavetkaṇṭhe daśa śīrṣasya cchedane/
386.007. rājyaṃ śatasahasraṃ vā labhate śīrṣabhakṣaṇe//629//

386.008. śuṣkāṃ nadīṃ hradaṃ vāpi śūnyāgārapraveśanam/
386.009. śuṣkodapānaṃ tu labhate svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ bhayam//630//
body.translated_text:
A dry river, a dry pond, entry into an empty house,
a dry well — seeing [these] in a dream, one certainly [experiences] fear. // 630 //

body.text:
386.010. śṛgālaṃ mānuṣaṃ nagnaṃ godhāvṛścikasūkaram/
386.011. ajāṃ vā paśyataḥ svapne vyādhikleśaṃ vinirdiśet//631//
body.translated_text:
A jackal, a naked human, a monitor lizard, a scorpion, a pig,
or a goat — for one who sees [these] in a dream, one should predict illness and distress. // 631 //

body.text:
386.012. kākaṃ śyenamulūkaṃ vā gṛdhraṃ vāpyatha vartakam/
386.013. mayūraṃ paśyataḥ svapne tasya vyasanamādiśet//632//
body.translated_text:
A crow, a hawk, an owl, a vulture, or indeed a quail,
a peacock — for one who sees [these] in a dream, one should predict calamity for him. // 632 //

body.text:
386.014. nagnaṃ paśyati hyātmānaṃ pāṃśunā dhvastameva vā/
386.015. kardamenopaliptaṃ vā vyādhikleśamavāpnuyāt//633//
body.translated_text:
If one sees oneself naked, or covered with dust,
or smeared with mud — one shall experience illness and distress. // 633 //

body.text:
386.016. kuṣṭhāḥ striyo 'tha saṃlokya caurān dyūtakarāṃstathā/
386.017. kuśīlāṃścāraṇān dhūrtān svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ bhayam//634//
body.translated_text:
Lepers, women, thieves, gamblers,
low-performers, wandering entertainers, and rogues — seeing [these] in a dream, fear is certain. // 634 //

body.text:
386.018. vamimūtrapurīṣāṇi virekaṃ vasāno janaḥ/
386.019. udvartanaṃ vā kurvāṇaḥ svapnānte rogamarcchati//635//
body.translated_text:
A person [engaged in] vomiting, urinating, defecating, taking purgatives,
or performing an oil-massage at the end of a dream — he encounters disease. // 635 //

body.text:
386.020. dhvajaṃ chatraṃ vitānaṃ vā svapnānte yasya dhāryate/
386.021. tatrastho 'pi vibudhyeta mahadaiśvaryamādiśet//636//
body.translated_text:
A banner, an umbrella, or a canopy — for whom [these] are held at the end of a dream,
and he awakens while standing thereon — one should predict great sovereignty. // 636 //

body.text:
386.022. antraistu yasya nagaraṃ samantātparivāryate/
386.023. grasate candrasūryau tu mahadaiśvaryamādiśet//637//
body.translated_text:
If a city is entirely encircled by intestines,
or if one swallows the moon and sun — one should predict great sovereignty. // 637 //

body.text:
386.024. manuṣyaṃ bhūmibhāgaṃ vā svapnānte grasate yadi/
386.025. hradaśca vā samudro 'yaṃ mahadaiśvaryamāpnuyāt//638//
body.translated_text:
If at the end of a dream one swallows a human being or a portion of earth,
or a lake or an ocean — one shall attain great sovereignty. // 638 //

body.text:
386.026. dhanuḥ praharaṇaṃ śastraṃ raktamābharaṇaṃ dhvajam/
386.027. kavacaṃ vā labhetsvapne dhanalābhaṃ vinirdiśet//639//
body.translated_text:
A bow, a weapon, a blade, a red ornament, a banner,
or armor — if obtained in a dream, one should predict the gain of wealth. // 639 //

body.text:
386.028. prapātaṃ parvataṃ tālaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ kuñjaraṃ hayam/
386.029. toraṇaṃ nagaraṃ dvāraṃ candrādityau satārakau/
386.030. svapne prapatitau dṛṣṭvā rājñāṃ vyasanamādiśet//640//
body.translated_text:
A precipice, a mountain, a palm tree, a bull, an elephant, a horse,
a gateway, a city, a door, the moon and sun with stars —
seeing [these] fallen in a dream, one should predict calamity for kings. // 640 //

body.text:
386.031. udayaṃ candrasūryāṇāṃ svapne dṛṣṭaṃ praśasyate/
386.032. tayorastaṃ gataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājño vyasanamādiśet//641//
body.translated_text:
The rising of the moon and sun, seen in a dream, is praised;
seeing their setting, one should predict calamity for the king. // 641 //

body.text:
387.001. <387>śmaśānavṛkṣayūpaṃ vā naro yadyabhirohati/
387.002. valmīkaṃ bhasmarāśiṃ vā svapne vyasanamādiśet//642//
body.translated_text:
If a man climbs a cremation-ground tree or a sacrificial post,
an anthill or a heap of ashes — in a dream, one should predict calamity. // 642 //

body.text:
387.003. kṛṣṇavastrā tu yā nārī kālī kāmayate naram/
387.004. karavīrasrajā svapne tadantaṃ tasya jīvitam//643//
body.translated_text:
A woman clad in black garments, dark-complexioned, who desires a man,
wearing a garland of <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) in a dream — that is the end of his life. // 643 //

body.text:
387.005. tamasi praviśet svapne śambhorvā cāmaraṃ tathā/
387.006. vṛkṣādvā prapatet svapne maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//644//
body.translated_text:
If one enters darkness in a dream, or [sees] the <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
or falls from a tree in a dream — one should predict his death. // 644 //

body.text:
387.007. vṛkṣaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ tṛṇaṃ vāpi virucam yastu paśyati/
387.008. svapne śīrṣaṃ śarīraṃ vā maraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//645//
body.translated_text:
He who sees a tree, wood, or grass, or a creeper
growing on [his own] head or body in a dream — one should predict his death. // 645 //

body.text:
387.009. devo vā varṣate yatra yatra caivāśaniḥ patet/
387.010. bhūmirvā kampate yatra svapne vyasanamādiśet//646//
body.translated_text:
Where a god rains, where lightning falls,
or where the earth trembles — in a dream, one should predict calamity. // 646 //

body.text:
387.011. candradityau yadi svapne khaṇḍau bhinnau ca paśyati/
387.012. patitau patamānau vā cakṣustasya vinaśyati//647//
body.translated_text:
If in a dream one sees the moon and sun broken, shattered,
fallen or falling — his eyesight will be destroyed. // 647 //

body.text:
387.013. kāṣāyaprāvṛtāṃ muṇḍāṃ nārīṃ malinavāsasam/
387.014. nīlaraktāmbarāṃ dṛṣṭvā āyāsamadhigacchati//648//
body.translated_text:
Seeing a woman clad in ochre robes, shaven-headed, wearing dirty garments,
or dressed in dark-blue or red garments — one encounters distress. // 648 //

body.text:
387.015. trapusīse ayastāmraloharajatamañjanam/
387.016. labdhvā tu puruṣaḥ svapne dhananāśaṃ samarcchati//649//
body.translated_text:
Tin, lead, iron, copper, base metal, silver, or antimony —
if a man obtains [these] in a dream, he encounters the loss of wealth. // 649 //

body.text:
387.017. gāyantī vā hasantī vā nṛtyantī vā vibudhyate/
387.018. vāditravādyamānairvā āyāsaṃ tatra nirdiśet//650//
body.translated_text:
If a woman awakens singing, laughing, or dancing,
or with musical instruments being played — one should predict distress there. // 650 //

body.text:
387.019. kardame yadi vā paṅke sikatāsvavasīdati/
387.020. tatrastho vā vibudhyeta vyādhiṃ samadhigacchati//651//
body.translated_text:
If one sinks in mud, or in a mire, or in sand,
or awakens while standing therein — one encounters disease. // 651 //

body.text:
387.021. aṣṭāpadairathānyairvā krīḍejjayaparājaye/
387.022. krīḍedakuśalāṅkairvā svapne dṛṣṭvā dhruvaṃ kaliḥ//652//
body.translated_text:
If one plays [games of] chess or other [games] involving victory and defeat,
or plays with unskilled [dice] markings — seeing [this] in a dream, quarrel is certain. // 652 //

body.text:
387.023. āsane śayane yāne vastre sābharaṇe gṛhe/
387.024. naṣṭe bhraṣṭe viśīrṇe vā āyāsamadhigacchati//653//
body.translated_text:
When a seat, couch, vehicle, garment, ornament, or house
is lost, dropped, or shattered — one encounters distress. // 653 //

body.text:
387.025. surāmaireyapānāni śārkaramāsavaṃ madhu/
387.026. pibate puruṣaḥ svapne āyāsamadhigacchati//654//
body.translated_text:
If a man in a dream drinks liquor, <s>maireya</s> (fermented drink), sugar-wine, <s>āsava</s> (distilled spirits), or honey —
he encounters distress. // 654 //

body.text:
387.027. prasanne 'mbhasi cādarśe chāyāṃ paśyati nātmanaḥ/
387.028. utpadyate dhruvaṃ tasya skandhanyāso na saṃśayaḥ//655//
body.translated_text:
If in clear water or in a mirror one does not see one's own reflection,
there certainly arises for him the placing of the shoulder[-bier] — without doubt. // 655 //

body.text:
387.029. abhīkṣṇaṃ varṣate devo jalaṃ pāṃśumathāpi vā/
387.030. aṅgāraṃ vāpi varṣeta maraṇaṃ tatra nirdiśet//656//
body.translated_text:
If a god incessantly rains water, or dust,
or rains embers — one should predict death there. // 656 //

body.text:
387.031. janaghātaṃ vijānīyāttatra deśe mahābhayam/
387.032. rajjujālena vā svapne paracakrād vinirdiśet//657//
body.translated_text:
One should know the slaughter of people — great danger in that region.
Or, in a dream, [if one sees] a net of ropes — one should predict [danger] from a foreign army. // 657 //

body.text:
388.001. <388>udakena samantādvai nagaraṃ parivāryate/
388.002. jālenānyena vā svapne paracakrodgamo bhavet//658//
body.translated_text:
If a city is entirely surrounded by water,
or by another net in a dream — there will be an invasion by a foreign army. // 658 //

body.text:
388.003. tailakardamaliptāṅgo raktakaṇṭhaguṇo naraḥ/
388.004. gāyate hasate caiva prahāraṃ tasya nirdiśet//659//
body.translated_text:
A man whose body is smeared with oil and mud, wearing a red garland around his neck,
who sings and laughs — one should predict a blow for him. // 659 //

body.text:
388.005. yaṃ kṛṣṇavasanā nārī ārdrā vā malinātha vā/
388.006. pariṣvajennaraṃ svapne bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//660//
body.translated_text:
If a woman clad in black garments, wet or dirty,
embraces a man in a dream — one should predict imprisonment for him. // 660 //

body.text:
388.007. kṛṣṇasārpo yadi svapne hyabhirohati yaṃ naram/
388.008. gātrāṇi veṣṭayedvāpi bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//661//
body.translated_text:
If a black serpent in a dream climbs upon a man,
or coils around his limbs — one should predict imprisonment for him. // 661 //

body.text:
388.009. latābhiḥ sthāṇuvṛndairvā yantrairvā parivāryate/
388.010. svapnānte puruṣo yastu bandhanaṃ tasya nirdiśet//662//
body.translated_text:
If a man at the end of a dream is surrounded by creepers, groups of tree-stumps,
or by fetters — one should predict imprisonment for him. // 662 //

body.text:
388.011. yantrāṇi yadi sarvāṇi vāgurābandhanāni vā/
388.012. yasya cchidyeran svapnānte bandhanātsa vimucyate//663//
body.translated_text:
If all fetters, traps, and bonds
are cut asunder for someone at the end of a dream — he is released from bondage. // 663 //

body.text:
388.013. viṣamāṇi ca niṃnāni parvatānnagarāṇi ca/
388.014. yastu paśyati svapnānte kṣipraṃ kleśādvimucyate//664//
body.translated_text:
Rough terrain, hollows, mountains, and cities —
he who sees [these] at the end of a dream is quickly freed from distress. // 664 //

body.text:
388.015. pūtanā vā piśācā vā duścalā malinātha vā/
388.016. evamrūpāṇi rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā svapne dhruvaṃ kaliḥ//665//
body.translated_text:
<s>Pūtanās</s> (demonesses), <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), the unsteady, the dirty —
seeing such forms in a dream, quarrel is certain. // 665 //

body.text:
388.017. susnātaṃ ca suveśaṃ ca sugandhaṃ śuklavāsasam/
388.018. puruṣaṃ vātha nārīṃ vā dṛṣṭvā svapne mahatsukham/
388.019. tṛṇaṃ vṛkṣamatho kāṣṭhaṃ virūḍham yatra dṛśyate/
388.020. gṛhe vā yadi vā kṣetre kṣipraṃ dravyakṣayo bhavet//667//
body.translated_text:
A well-bathed, well-dressed, fragrant person wearing white garments —
whether man or woman — seeing [such a one] in a dream brings great happiness.
Grass, a tree, or wood — wherever [these] are seen sprouting
in a house or in a field — there will quickly be a loss of wealth. // 667 //

body.text:
388.021. bhadrāsane vābhyāsīno śayane vā susaṃskṛte/
388.022. naro vā labhate nārīṃ nārī vā labhate naram//668//
body.translated_text:
Seated upon an auspicious seat, or lying on a well-prepared couch —
a man obtains a wife, or a woman obtains a husband. // 668 //

body.text:
388.023. naraḥ śuklamatho vastraṃ śuklagandhānulepitam/
388.024. svapnānte yastu paśyeta strīlābhaṃ tasya nirdiśet//669//
body.translated_text:
A man [who sees] white cloth or white fragrant unguent
at the end of a dream — one should predict for him the gain of a wife. // 669 //

body.text:
388.025. yastu hyannāni paśyeta bhūṣaṇaṃ nigaḍaistathā/
388.026. narastu labhate bhāryāṃ nārī vā labhate patim//670//
body.translated_text:
He who sees foods, ornaments, or fetters —
a man obtains a wife, or a woman obtains a husband. // 670 //

body.text:
388.027. mekhalāṃ karṇikāṃ mālāṃ strīṇāmābharaṇāni ca/
388.028. labdhvā naro labhed bhāryāṃ nārī ca labhate patim//671//
body.translated_text:
A girdle, an ear-ornament, a garland, and women's ornaments —
a man who obtains [these] shall gain a wife, and a woman shall gain a husband. // 671 //

body.text:
388.029. kuñjaraṃ vṛṣabhaṃ nāgaṃ candrādityau satārakau/
388.030. abhivandeta yā nārī patiṃ sā labhate 'cirāt//672//
body.translated_text:
An elephant, a bull, a serpent, the moon and sun with stars —
a woman who salutes [these] shall soon obtain a husband. // 672 //

body.text:
388.031. eṣāmanyatamaḥ kukṣau praviśecca yadi striyāḥ/
388.032. sā kāle sarvapūrṇāṅgaṃ śrīmatputraṃ prasūyate//673//
body.translated_text:
If any one of these enters the womb of a woman,
she shall, in due time, give birth to a son of full and beautiful limbs, endowed with <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity). // 673 //

body.text:
389.001. <389>phalāni ca samagrāṇi vanāni haritāni ca/
389.002. svapnānte labhate nārī śrīmatputraṃ prasūyate//674//
body.translated_text:
Complete fruits and green forests —
a woman who obtains [these] at the end of a dream gives birth to a prosperous son. // 674 //

body.text:
389.003. utpalaṃ kumudaṃ padmaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ sakuḍmalam/
389.004. labdhvā nārī tu svapnānte śrīmatputraṃ prasūyate//675//
body.translated_text:
A woman who obtains a lotus, water-lily, lotus, white lotus, or bud
at the end of a dream gives birth to a glorious son. // 675 //

body.text:
389.005. upāyanasūtrayorantaḥ sajjaṃ tatra tu piṇḍakam/
389.006. svapne yā labhate nārī sāpi putraṃ prasūyate/
389.007. yamaṃ tu bhājanaṃ cāpi yamaṃ tu sā prasūyate///676//

389.008. mlāyantīmatha grīṣmānte taruṇīmātmikāmapi/
389.009. śuṣkāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā svapne svapakṣamaraṇaṃ bhavet//677//
body.translated_text:
Seeing in a dream a [plant] withering at the end of summer, a young [woman] of her own [family],
or a dried-up [one] — there will be death in one's own group. // 677 //

body.text:
389.010. bāhavo yasya vardhante cakṣuraṅgulayopi vā/
389.011. jñātayastasya vardhante śatrūṇāṃ maraṇaṃ bhavet//678//
body.translated_text:
He whose arms increase [in dream], or eyes and fingers —
his kinsmen increase, and there will be death of enemies. // 678 //

body.text:
389.012. badhyante bāhavo yasya cakṣuśca vyākulaṃ bhavet/
389.013. bāhurvā prapatedyasya svapakṣamaraṇaṃ bhavet//679//
body.translated_text:
He whose arms are bound [in dream], or whose eye becomes disturbed,
or whose arm falls off — there will be death in one's own group. // 679 //

body.text:
389.014. devo vā yadi vā preto nāryā vastraṃ phalāni vā/
389.015. svapne prayacchate yasyāḥ putrastasyāḥ prajāyate//680//
body.translated_text:
If a god or a departed spirit gives a woman garments or fruits
in a dream — a son is born to her. // 680 //

body.text:
389.016. apakṛṣṭo rudan yo vā nagno 'tha malinaḥ kṛśaḥ/
389.017. krodhaṃ vā .................. vinirdiśet//681//
body.translated_text:
One who is dragged away weeping, or is naked, dirty, and emaciated,
or [shows] anger — one should predict [accordingly]. // 681 //

body.text:
389.018. carma yantraṃ gaṇitaṃ vā kīlaṃ vātha kilāṭakam/
389.019. svapne labdhvā ca prāpnu{jānī}yād dhruvaṃ vastrāgamo bhavet//682//
body.translated_text:
If in a dream one obtains leather, a machine, an account, a peg, or a piece of cheese,
one should know that there will certainly be the arrival of garments. // 682 //

body.text:
389.020. amānuṣo 'tha rājā vā devaḥ preto 'tha brāhmaṇaḥ/
389.021. svapne yathā te jalpante sa tathārtho bhaviṣyati//683//
body.translated_text:
A non-human, a king, a god, a departed spirit, or a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> —
whatever they speak in a dream, that very meaning will come to pass. // 683 //

body.text:
389.022. .................. pūrvavicintitam/
389.023. yaccānusmarate dṛṣṭvā yaccāpi bahu paśyati//684//
body.translated_text:
[...what was] previously thought about,
and what one remembers upon seeing, and what one sees in abundance — // 684 //

body.text:
389.024. abhyutthito yathā mārge svapnānte pratibudhyate/
389.025. viṣamaṃ vā tathādhvānaṃ chidraṃ vā pratipadyate//685//
body.translated_text:
Just as one who rises up as if on a road, awakens at the end of a dream,
or traverses a rough path or arrives at a gap — // 685 //

body.text:
389.026. agniṃ prajvalitaṃ taptaṃ śamitvā tu praśasyate/
389.027. gṛhāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ śastaṃ bhedanaṃ na praśasyate//686//
body.translated_text:
To quench a blazing, heated fire is praised;
the building of houses is auspicious, but their destruction is not praised. // 686 //

body.text:
389.028. nirmalaṃ gaganaṃ śastaṃ samedhaṃ na praśasyate/
389.029. prasannamudakaṃ śastaṃ kaluṣaṃ na praśasyate//687//
body.translated_text:
A clear sky is auspicious; one with fuel [i.e., clouds] is not praised;
clear water is auspicious; turbid [water] is not praised. // 687 //

body.text:
389.030. adhvānaṃ gamanaṃ śastaṃ na kvacitsaṃnivartanam/
389.031. suvarṇadarśanaṃ śastaṃ dhāraṇaṃ na praśasyate//688//
body.translated_text:
Traveling on a road is auspicious; turning back at any point is not;
seeing gold is auspicious; holding it is not praised. // 688 //

body.text:
390.001. <390>māṃsasya darśanaṃ sādhu bhakṣaṇaṃ na praśasyate/
390.002. madyasya darśanaṃ śastaṃ pānaṃ tu na praśasyate//689//
body.translated_text:
Seeing meat is good; eating it is not praised;
seeing liquor is auspicious; drinking it is not praised. // 689 //

body.text:
390.003. pṛthivī haritā śastā vivarṇā na praśasyate/
390.004. yānasyārohaṇaṃ śāstaṃ patanaṃ na praśasyate//690//
body.translated_text:
Green earth is auspicious; discolored [earth] is not praised;
mounting a vehicle is auspicious; falling from it is not praised. // 690 //

body.text:
390.005. svapneṣu ruditaṃ śastaṃ hasitaṃ na praśasyate/
390.006. pracchannadarśanaṃ śastaṃ nagnaṃ naiva praśasyate//691//
body.translated_text:
Weeping in dreams is auspicious; laughing is not praised;
seeing [oneself] clothed is auspicious; [seeing oneself] naked is never praised. // 691 //

body.text:
390.007. mālyasya darśanaṃ śastaṃ dhāraṇaṃ na praśasyate/
390.008. gātraṃ vikartitaṃ sādhu prokṣitaṃ na praśasyate//692//
body.translated_text:
Seeing a garland is auspicious; wearing it is not praised;
the body being cut is good; being sprinkled is not praised. // 692 //

body.text:
390.009. mṛduḥ praśasyate vāto nātivātaḥ praśasyate/
390.010. vyādhito malinaḥ śasto bhūṣito na praśasyate/
390.011. parvatārohaṇaṃ śastaṃ na tu tatrāvatāraṇam//693//

390.012. dhūmrā ghanā dundubhiśaṅkhaśabdo vāto 'bhravṛṣṭiśca tathā samantāt/
390.014. sarvasthirāṇāṃ ca calaśca yaḥ syādye cāntare doṣakṛtā vikārāḥ//694//
body.translated_text:
Smoke, clouds, the sound of drums and conches, wind and cloudbursts all around,
and the shaking of all that is stable, and whatever disturbances are caused by defects internally — // 694 //

body.text:
390.016. pūrveṣu rūpeṣu yathāvadiṣṭā rājarṣayo devagaṇāśca sarve/
390.018. yad brāhmaṇa gātravikartanaṃ ca etāni sarvāṇyapi śobhanāni//695//
body.translated_text:
In the aforementioned forms, as declared, royal sages and all the hosts of gods,
and the cutting of the body by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — all these too are auspicious. // 695 //

body.text:
390.020. yatpūrvarūpeṣu bhavetpraśastaṃ duḥsvapnametāni śamaṃ nayanti/
390.022. gāvaḥ pradānaṃ dvijapūjanaṃ ca duḥsvapnametena parājitaṃ syāt//696//
body.translated_text:
What would be praised in the aforementioned forms — these bring bad dreams to peace;
cows, giving gifts, and honoring <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — by these, a bad dream would be defeated. // 696 //

body.text:
390.024. devaṃ ca yaṃ bhaktigato manuṣyastaṃ tu parāṃścārcayitum yatena/
390.026. svapnaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā prathame pradoṣe saṃvatsarānte 'sya vipākamāhuḥ//697//
body.translated_text:
Whichever deity a person approaches with devotion — let him worship that one and others with effort;
a dream seen in the first watch of the night — they say its ripening comes at the end of a year. // 697 //

body.text:
390.028. ṣaṇmāsikam yacca bhaved dvitīye ṣaṭpākṣikam yattu bhavet tṛtīye/
390.030. adhyardhamāsetarameva yatsyāt phaleccaturthe rajanīprabhāte//698//
body.translated_text:
What occurs in the second [watch] ripens in six months; what occurs in the third, in a fortnight;
what would be in the remaining period of a month and a half — the fruit [manifests] at dawn after the fourth [watch] of the night. // 698 //

body.text:
391.001. <391>dvijottame vā tilapātradānaṃ śāntikriyāḥ svastyayanaprayogāḥ/
391.003. pūjā gurūṇāṃ parimiṣṭamannaṃ duḥsvapnametāni vināśayanti//699//
body.translated_text:
Giving sesame and a vessel to the best of the twice-born, performing pacification rites and auspicious ceremonies,
honoring elders, [offering] thoroughly cleansed food — these destroy a bad dream. // 699 //

body.text:
391.005. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin svapnādhyāyanāmādhyāyaḥ/
391.006. atha khalu bho puṣkarasārinn aparamapi svapnādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
391.006. tacchrūyatām/
391.007. atha kim/
391.007. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuh--
391.008. aparaḥ svapnādhyāyaḥ/
391.009. śubhāśubhānāṃ svapnānām yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam/
391.010. nimittam yādṛśam yasya śṛṇu vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ//700//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Dream Interpretation.' Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound yet another dream chapter. Listen to it. Now what? Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak — The Second Dream Chapter: The fruit that has been declared for auspicious and inauspicious dreams, and whatever omen belongs to each — listen, I shall declare it in truth. // 700 //

body.text:
391.011. jāgrato yadi vā trasto divā svapnāni paśyati/
391.012. na tu bhayaṃ bhavettasya jānīyādeva buddhimān//701//
body.translated_text:
If a waking person, or one who is frightened, sees dreams during the day,
there will be no danger for him — a wise person should know this. // 701 //

body.text:
391.013. yasya tu yo bhavecchatruryasya vidheyamicchati/
391.014. svapne tu kalahaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣipraṃ prītirbhaviṣyati//702//
body.translated_text:
Whoever is an enemy to whomever, and whoever wishes to control another —
having seen a quarrel in a dream, friendship will soon arise. // 702 //

body.text:
391.015. rajanyāṃ purime yāme yo 'drākṣītsukhaduḥkhadam/
391.016. adhvānaṃ cirakālena tathā hyeṣa nivartate//703//
body.translated_text:
He who in the first watch of the night saw [a dream] giving happiness or sorrow —
it returns after a long time, for thus it works. // 703 //

body.text:
391.017. madhyame bhavate naiva kṣipraṃ bhavati paścime/
391.018. vaimārgaṃ tvaritaṃ dṛṣṭvā strīlābhamabhinirdiśet//704//
body.translated_text:
In the middle [watch] it does not come to pass; in the last [watch] it comes quickly;
having seen a wrong path quickly [in a dream], one should predict the gain of a woman. // 704 //

body.text:
391.019. dṛṣṭvā jalacarān matsyānevaṃ jānīta buddhimān/
391.020. yatkiṃcidārabhiṣyāmi kṣiprameva bhaviṣyati//705//
body.translated_text:
Having seen aquatic fish [in a dream], the wise person should know:
'Whatever I am about to undertake will quickly come to pass.' // 705 //

body.text:
391.021. campāyāṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ haste ghṛṣetsvapnāntareṣu vā/
391.022. pratibuddho vijānīyād varṇamevaṃ bhaviṣyati//706//
body.translated_text:
If in a dream one rubs a testicle in the hand with <s>campā</s> [flowers],
upon awakening one should know that complexion will improve accordingly. // 706 //

body.text:
391.023. sarvāṇi khalu pānāni madhurāṇi sukhāni ca/
391.024. yastu pibati svapnānte sa ca lābhaiḥ prayujyate//707//
body.translated_text:
All sweet and pleasant drinks —
he who drinks them at the end of a dream is joined with gains. // 707 //

body.text:
391.025. śvaśṛgālairbhakṣyate 'tra svapne saṃparivāryate/
391.026. pratibuddhastu jānīyāt śatrureva pramūrcchati//708//
body.translated_text:
If in a dream one is eaten by dogs and jackals, or surrounded [by them],
upon awakening one should know that an enemy is growing in strength. // 708 //

body.text:
391.027. upari kākā gṛdhrāśca dhāvantyupari yānti ca/
391.028. pratibuddho vijānīyācchatrurmā vadhayiṣyati//709//
body.translated_text:
If crows and vultures fly above and circle overhead,
upon awakening one should know: 'An enemy intends to slay me.' // 709 //

body.text:
391.029. yasya paragṛhaśvāno dvāre mūtraṃ prakurvate/
391.030. pratibuddho vijānīyādbhāryā me jāramicchati//710//
body.translated_text:
He at whose door another's household dogs urinate —
upon awakening he should know: 'My wife desires a lover.' // 710 //

body.text:
391.031. ekaśca dharaṇau pādo dvitīyaḥ śirasi sthitaḥ/
391.032. pratibuddho vijānīyādrājyalābho bhaviṣyati//711//
body.translated_text:
One foot on the ground, the second standing on [one's own] head —
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be the attainment of a kingdom.' // 711 //

body.text:
392.001. <392>samudram yadi paśyedvā pātumicchati tajjalam/
392.002. pratibuddho vijānīyādrājyalābho bhaviṣyati//712//
body.translated_text:
If one sees the ocean or wishes to drink its water,
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be the attainment of a kingdom.' // 712 //

body.text:
392.003. vṛkṣaṃ parvatamāruhya nāgaṃ ca turagaṃ tathā/
392.004. pratibuddho vijānīyādrājyalābho bhaviṣyati//713//
body.translated_text:
Climbing a tree, a mountain, or mounting an elephant or horse —
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be the attainment of a kingdom.' // 713 //

body.text:
392.005. yastu svapnāntare paśyet pitṛrn yāniha cānyathā/
392.006. tathā mātā pitā caiva tasya jīvanti te ciram//714//
body.translated_text:
He who in a dream sees his ancestors, or others [who have departed] in this world,
or his mother and father — they will live for a long time. // 714 //

body.text:
392.007. yastu svapnāntare paśyetkeśaśmaśru vikartitam/
392.008. pratibuddho vijānīyādarthasiddhirbhaviṣyati//715//
body.translated_text:
He who in a dream sees his hair and beard being cut —
upon awakening he should know: 'There will be the accomplishment of purpose.' // 715 //

body.text:
392.009. anānaṃ codake dṛṣṭvā madhye 'gnau ca vidhāvitam/
392.010. pratibuddho vijānīyāt kulavṛddhirbhaviṣyati//716//
body.translated_text:
Having seen [one's own] face in water and having run through the midst of fire,
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be increase of the family.' // 716 //

body.text:
392.011. dhāvanaṃ laṅghanaṃ caiva grāmāṇāṃ parivartanam/
392.012. pratibuddho vijānīyādātmānaṃ śātitamiti//717//
body.translated_text:
Running, leaping, and the revolving of villages —
upon awakening one should know: 'I am being calmed.' // 717 //

body.text:
392.013. caurāṇāmapi sāmagrīṃ svapnānte yastu paśyati/
392.014. pratibuddho vijānīyādātmānaṃ śātitamiti//718//
body.translated_text:
He who at the end of a dream sees a gathering of thieves —
upon awakening he should know: 'I am being calmed.' // 718 //

body.text:
392.015. kṛṣṇasarpagṛhītaṃ tu svapnānte yastu paśyati/
392.016. pratibuddho vijānīyācchatrupīḍā bhaviṣyati//719//
body.translated_text:
He who at the end of a dream sees [himself] seized by a black serpent —
upon awakening he should know: 'There will be affliction from an enemy.' // 719 //

body.text:
392.017. kaṭakān karṇikāścaiva haṃsakeyūrakuṇḍalam/
392.018. yastu cābharaṇaṃ paśyed bandhuvargo bhaviṣyati//720//
body.translated_text:
Bracelets, ear-ornaments, <s>haṃsa</s>-armlets, and earrings —
he who sees such ornaments [in a dream] — there will be [a gathering of] relatives. // 720 //

body.text:
392.019. kuḍye ca gṛhaprākāre dhāvatīha parasparam/
392.020. nāvike dhanasamyoge aṅgate kṣaṇayam(?) khajaḥ//721//
body.translated_text:
On a wall and on a house-rampart, running to and fro;
in a boat at a confluence of wealth, on the body [...]. // 721 //

body.text:
392.021. yastu svapnāntare paśyeccātmānamagnitāpitam/
392.022. pratibuddho vijānīyājjvaraṃ kṣipraṃ bhaviṣyati//722//
body.translated_text:
He who at the end of a dream sees himself heated by fire —
upon awakening he should know: 'Fever will soon come.' // 722 //

body.text:
392.023. rājānaṃ kupitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ātmānaṃ malinīkṛtam/
392.024. pratibuddho vijānīyātkuṭumbaṃ tasya naśyati//723//
body.translated_text:
Having seen an angry king, [or] oneself made dirty —
upon awakening one should know: 'His family will be destroyed.' // 723 //

body.text:
392.025. kāṣṭhabhāraṃ tṛṇaṃ caiva bahubhāramabhīkṣṇaśaḥ/
392.026. ātmanaḥ śiraso dṛṣṭvā guruvyādhirbhaviṣyati//724//
body.translated_text:
Having seen a load of wood, grass, or a heavy burden repeatedly
upon one's own head — there will be a serious illness. // 724 //

body.text:
392.027. yastu vānarayuktena gacchate purimāṃ diśam/
392.028. pratibuddho vijānīyādrātrireṣā hyapaścimā//725//
body.translated_text:
He who travels eastward in a vehicle yoked with monkeys —
upon awakening he should know: 'This is the last night [of his life].' // 725 //

body.text:
392.029. candrasūryau ca saṃgṛhya pāṇinā parimārjati/
392.030. pratibuddho vijānīyādāyadharmāgamo hi saḥ//726//
body.translated_text:
Grasping the moon and sun with one's hand and wiping them —
upon awakening one should know: 'This is the acquisition of inherited wealth.' // 726 //

body.text:
392.031. sumanāṃ vārṣikam {kīm} caiva kumudānyutpalāni ca/
392.032. yastu paśyati svapnānte dakṣiṇīyasamāgamaḥ//727//
body.translated_text:
Jasmines, seasonal [flowers], water-lilies, and blue lotuses —
he who sees them at the end of a dream — there will be a meeting with a venerable person. // 727 //

body.text:
393.001. <393>brāhmaṇaṃ śramaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣapaṇaṃ suranāyakam/
393.002. pratibuddho vijānīyādyakṣā me hyanukampakāḥ//728//
body.translated_text:
Having seen a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, an ascetic (<s>śramaṇa</s>), a Jain monk (<s>kṣapaṇa</s>), or a leader of the gods —
upon awakening one should know: 'The <s>Yakṣas</s> are indeed compassionate toward me.' // 728 //

body.text:
393.003. rudhireṇa viluptasya snātvā caivātmalohitaiḥ/
393.004. pratibuddho vijānīyādaiśvaryādhisamāgamaḥ//729//
body.translated_text:
If one is covered with blood, or bathes in one's own blood —
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be an encounter with sovereignty.' // 729 //

body.text:
393.005. mudgamāṣayavāṃścaiva dhānyaṃ jvalanadarśanam/
393.006. yastu svapnānatare paśyetsubhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//730//
body.translated_text:
Mung beans, black gram, barley, grain, and the sight of fire —
he who sees these at the end of a dream — one should predict abundance of food there. // 730 //

body.text:
393.007. suvarṇaṃ ca tathā rūpyaṃ muktāhāraṃ tathaiva ca/
393.008. yastu svapnāntare paśyennidhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet//731//
body.translated_text:
Gold, silver, and a string of pearls likewise —
he who sees these at the end of a dream — one should predict a [hidden] treasure there. // 731 //

body.text:
393.009. bandhanaṃ bahu dṛṣṭvā tu cchedanaṃ kuṭṭanaṃ tathā/
393.010. pratibuddho vijānīyādarthasiddhirbhaviṣyati//732//
body.translated_text:
Having seen many bonds, cutting, and beating —
upon awakening one should know: 'There will be the accomplishment of purpose.' // 732 //

body.text: 393.011. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārinnaparaḥ svapnādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the second dream chapter.

body.text:
393.012. atha khalu puṣkarasārin māsaparīkṣānāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
393.012. tacchrūyatām/
393.013. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuh--
393.014. māsaparīkṣā/
393.015. yadi phālgune māse nirghoṣa upari bhavet, manuṣyāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ codayati/
393.015. navacandro lohitābhāso dṛśyate, sarvasasyānutpattiṃ codayati/
393.016. yadi devo garjati, prathamaṃ mahāsasyāni bhavanti/
393.017. paścimasasyaṃ na bhavet/
393.017. kalahaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text: Now then, <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called 'Monthly Prognostication.' Listen to it. Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak — Monthly Prognostication: If in the month of <s>Phālguna</s> a thunderclap occurs above, it predicts death for humans. If the new moon appears reddish in hue, it predicts the non-production of all crops. If the sky thunders, first there will be great crops; but the later crops will not come. It predicts quarrel.

body.text:
393.018. yadi caitre māse devo garjati, tadā sarvasasyamutpattiṃ codayati/
393.018. yadi candragraho bhavati, mahān saṃnipāto bhavati/
393.019. śūnyāni grāmakṣetrāṇi bhaviṣyanti/
393.019. yadi nīhāraṃ bhūmiṃ chādayati, subhikṣaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text:
393.018. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, then it stimulates the growth of all crops.
393.018. If a lunar eclipse occurs, a great assembly arises.
393.019. Villages and fields will become deserted.
393.019. If mist covers the earth, it portends abundance.

body.text:
393.021. yadi vaiśākhe māase devo garjati, subhikṣaṃ codayati/
393.021. yadi pūrve paścime śaṅkhe candragraho bhavati, kṣemaṃ codayati/
393.022. yadi colkāpāto bhavati, yasmiṃśca janapade nipatati, tatra deśe pradhānapuruṣasya vināśo bhavati/
393.023. yadi bhūmicālo bhavati, subhikṣaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text:
393.021. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, it portends abundance.
393.021. If a lunar eclipse occurs in the first or last quarter, it portends well-being.
393.022. If a meteor falls, in whatever region it falls, the leading man of that land meets destruction.
393.023. If an earthquake occurs, it portends abundance.

body.text:
393.024. yadi jyeṣṭhe māse devo garjati, rogaṃ codayati/
393.024. yadi sūryagraho bhavati, manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśaṃ codayati/
393.025. pūrve paścime vā śaṅkhe yadi candrasya sūryasya kiṃcinnimittaṃ lakṣyate, tadā kṣemaṃ codayati/
393.026. yadi madhyarātrau candragraho bhavati, manuṣyāṇāmanyonyaghātaṃ codayati/
393.026. yadi copari nirghoṣo bhavati, adhyakṣapuruṣasya pīḍāṃ codayati, paracakrāgamaṃ ceti//
body.translated_text:
393.024. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, it portends disease.
393.024. If a solar eclipse occurs, it portends the destruction of people.
393.025. If in the first or last quarter some portent of the moon or sun is observed, then it portends well-being.
393.026. If a lunar eclipse occurs at midnight, it portends mutual slaughter among people.
393.026. If a thundering sound is heard above, it portends trouble for the chief administrator, and the invasion of a foreign army.

body.text: 393.028. āṣāḍhe māse yadi sūryagraho rucirābhāso bhavati, subhikṣaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text: 393.028. If a solar eclipse of brilliant appearance occurs in the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, it portends abundance.

body.text:
393.028. yadi candragraho bhavati, rogaṃ codayati/
393.029. yadi vidyunniścarati, kalyāṇaṃ codayati/
393.029. yadi nīhāraṃ bhūmiṃ chādayati, subhikṣaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text:
393.028. If a lunar eclipse occurs, it portends disease.
393.029. If lightning flashes forth, it portends auspiciousness.
393.029. If mist covers the earth, it portends abundance.

body.text:
393.031. śrāvaṇamāse yadi sūryagraho bhavati, rājyaṃ parivartate/
393.031. yadi candragraho bhavati, prathame māse durbhikṣaṃ codayati/
393.032. śarabhaiḥ śobhanaśasyanāśo bhaviṣyati/
393.032. yadi tārakā yatra deśe patanti, <394>tatra yuddhaṃ codayati/
body.translated_text:
393.031. If a solar eclipse occurs in the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the kingdom is overturned.
393.031. If a lunar eclipse occurs, it portends famine in the first month.
393.032. Locusts will cause the destruction of good crops.
393.032. If stars fall upon a particular region, it portends war there.

body.text:
394.001. yadi cātiśayaṃ bhūmicālo bhavati, rogaṃ codayati/
394.001. yadi nirghoṣo bhavati, tatra gṛhe yo gṛhasvāmī bhavati tasya vināśaṃ codayati/
394.002. atra ca māse 'bhinavaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ na prāvaritavyam/
394.003. āvāho vivāho na kartavyaḥ/
394.003. paribhūto bhavati//
body.translated_text:
394.001. If an extraordinary earthquake occurs, it portends disease.
394.001. If a thundering sound occurs, it portends the destruction of the householder of that house.
394.002. In this month, new garments should not be worn.
394.003. Marriages and wedding ceremonies should not be performed.
394.003. One who does so will be humiliated.

body.text:
394.004. yadyāśvayuje māse devo garjati, manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśaṃ codayati/
394.004. yadi sūryoparāgo bhavati, mahāpuruṣavināśaṃ codayati/
394.005. yadi pūrve yāme candrasya nimittaṃ dṛśyate, subhikṣaṃ codayati/
394.006. yadi bhūmicālo bhavati, ākulaṃ codayati/
394.006. pararājā deśaṃ haniṣyati/
394.006. tatra ca manuṣyā anyonyaṃ vadhayiṣyantīti codayati//
body.translated_text:
394.004. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, it portends the destruction of people.
394.004. If a solar eclipse occurs, it portends the destruction of a great man.
394.005. If a portent of the moon is observed in the first watch, it portends abundance.
394.006. If an earthquake occurs, it portends confusion.
394.006. A foreign king will destroy the land.
394.006. People there will slay one another — so it portends.

body.text:
394.008. yadi kārtike māse devo varṣati, mahadākulaṃ codayati/
394.008. prāṇakāśca dhānyaṃ khādiṣyanti/
394.009. yadyekāntarūpaṃ vāto vāti, tatra ca manuṣyā jalena vibhramiṣyanti/
394.009. mahātmanaḥ puruṣasya vināśaṃ codayati/
394.010. yadi pūrve yāme utpāto bhavati, mahāvarṣaṃ bhavati/
394.010. mahāpuruṣasya ca maraṇaṃ bhavati/
394.011. yadi nirghoṣo bhavati rogaṃ codayati//
body.translated_text:
394.008. If the rain-god rains in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, it portends great confusion.
394.008. Vermin will devour the grain.
394.009. If a wind of singular form blows, the people there will be swept away by water.
394.009. It portends the destruction of a great-souled man.
394.010. If a portent occurs in the first watch, there will be great rain.
394.010. The death of a great man will occur.
394.011. If a thundering sound occurs, it portends disease.

body.text:
