394.012. yadi mārgaśīrṣe māsi devo garjati, śasyavināśo bhavati/
394.012. anyaśca tatra svāmī bhavati/
394.013. yadi cākāśe nirghoṣo bhavati, yatpūrvabhāgīyā manuṣyāsteṣāmāmayaṃ codayati/
394.013. yadi bhūmicālo bhavati, yastatra janapade pradhānapuruṣaḥ sa vadhānmokṣyati//
body.translated_text:
394.012. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, the crops are destroyed.
394.012. Another ruler will arise there.
394.013. If a thundering sound occurs in the sky, it portends illness for those of the eastern quarter.
394.013. If an earthquake occurs, the leading man of that region will be freed from execution.

body.text:
394.015. yadi pauṣe māse devo garjati, prathame janapadanāśo bhavati/
394.015. dvitīye mahātmanaḥ puruṣasya bandhanaṃ codayati/
394.016. prathame yāme ca yadi candroparāgo bhavati lohitavarṇaśca dṛśyate, udakāgamaṃ codayati/
394.017. mahātmamanuṣyaṃ codayti/
394.017. yadi sūryagraho bhavati, śuddhapuruṣāṇāṃ raṇam/
394.018. yadi tārakāḥ patantyo vidṛśyante, tatra janapade ākulaṃ codayati/
394.018. yadyākāśe nirghoṣo bhavati, manuṣyāṇāṃ maraṇaṃ codayati/
394.019. yadi dvitīye nirghoṣo bhavati, manuṣyāścaurairhanyante/
394.020. yadyatraiva māse tārakā utsṛṣṭā na candro dṛśyate, sasyaṃ saṃcodayati/
394.020. yadi bhūmicālo bhavati, mahāmanuṣyasya maraṇaṃ bhavati/
394.021. atraiva māse devasthānaṃ kartavyam/
394.021. vṛkṣā ropayitavyāḥ/
394.022. mūlavāstu pratiṣṭhāpayitavyam/
394.023. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin māsaparīkṣānāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text:
394.015. If the rain-god thunders in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, the first effect is the destruction of the region.
394.015. The second is that it portends the imprisonment of a great-souled man.
394.016. If a lunar eclipse occurs in the first watch and a reddish color is observed, it portends a flood.
394.017. It portends harm to a great man.
394.017. If a solar eclipse occurs, there is battle for men of purity.
394.018. If falling stars are seen, it portends confusion in that region.
394.018. If a thundering sound occurs in the sky, it portends the death of people.
394.019. If a thundering sound occurs a second time, people are slain by thieves.
394.020. If in this very month stars are scattered and the moon is not visible, it stimulates the crops.
394.020. If an earthquake occurs, the death of a great man occurs.
394.021. In this very month, a place for the gods should be established.
394.021. Trees should be planted.
394.022. The root-foundation should be consecrated.
394.023. This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called 'Examination of the Months.'

body.text:
394.024. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin khañjarīṭakajñānaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
394.024. tacchrūyatām/
394.025. atha kim/
394.025. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
394.026. khañjarīṭakajñānam/
394.027. khañjarīṭakaśāstraṃ vai parvate gandhamādane/
394.028. kucarairdṛśyate saumya kucarasya mahābhayam//733//
body.translated_text:
394.024. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called "Knowledge of the Wagtail."
394.024. Listen to that.'
394.025. 'Very well.'
394.025. 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak —'
394.026. 'Knowledge of the Wagtail.'
394.027. 'The treatise on the wagtail, on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
394.028. is seen by wanderers, O gentle one — great is the danger of a wanderer.' //733//

body.text:
394.029. yāni tāni nimittāni darśayetkhañjarīṭakaḥ/
394.030. pracarato bhaved dṛṣṭvā pañcottarapado dvijaḥ//734//
body.translated_text:
394.029. 'Whatever omens the wagtail displays —
394.030. seeing it moving about, the bird with five extra steps.' //734//

body.text:
395.001. <395>tatra sarve pravarteyuryatra yeṣu bhavedbhavet/
395.002. śādvale bahucelatvaṃ gomayeṣu prabandhatā//735//
body.translated_text:
395.001. 'All those omens should be applied wherever and in whichever cases they may occur.
395.002. On green grass, it portends abundance of clothing; on cow-dung, it portends steadiness.' //735//

body.text:
395.003. kañcāre bahucelatvaṃ kardame bahubhakṣatā/
395.004. kṛkare svalpacelatvaṃ purīṣe tu kṛśaṃ śravaḥ//736//
body.translated_text:
395.003. 'On metal, abundance of clothing; on mud, abundance of food;
395.004. on a black partridge, scanty clothing; on excrement, a lean livelihood.' //736//

body.text:
395.005. bhasme vivādamaphalaṃ vālukāyāṃ tu saṃbhramaḥ/
395.006. devadvāre tu saṃmānaṃ padmeṣu bahuvittatā/
395.007. phale 'rthānuguṇaṃ proktaṃ puṣpeṣu priyasaṃgamaḥ//737//

395.008. bhayaṃ prākāraśṛṅgeṣu kaṭakeṣvaridarśanam/
395.009. pakṣayā carate vyādhiḥ patito mṛtyumādiśet//738//
body.translated_text:
395.008. 'On rampart-tops, danger; on encampments, the sight of an enemy;
395.009. moving on one wing, disease; fallen down, it portends death.' //738//

body.text:
395.010. sugandhatailabhūtāni maithune nidhidarśanam/
395.011. vṛkṣāgre vidyate pānaṃ gṛheṣvatha ........ lasaḥ//739//
body.translated_text:
395.010. 'On fragrant oil and such substances, sexual union and the sight of a treasure;
395.011. on a treetop, there is drinking; in houses, then ... enjoyment.' //739//

body.text:
395.012. deśabhaṅgapravāde ca bandhanaṃ vigrahīkṛte/
395.013. amṛtaṃ ca sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā odanaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ//740//
body.translated_text:
395.012. 'In talk of a region's ruin, imprisonment; in a quarrel,
395.013. if seen standing still, food is certain — there is no doubt.' //740//

body.text:
395.014. gavāṃ pṛṣṭhe dhruvaṃ siddhiraśvapṛṣṭhe dhruvaṃ jayaḥ/
395.015. avikānāmajānāṃ ca pṛṣṭhe sarvatra śasyate//741//
body.translated_text:
395.014. 'On the back of a cow, success is certain; on the back of a horse, victory is certain;
395.015. on the backs of sheep and goats, it is praised in all cases.' //741//

body.text:
395.016. uṣṭrapṛṣṭhe dhruvaṃ kleśaḥ śvānapṛṣṭhe ca vidravaḥ/
395.017. pṛṣṭhe ca gardabhasyeha maraṇaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ//742//
body.translated_text:
395.016. 'On a camel's back, hardship is certain; on a dog's back, flight;
395.017. and on the back of a donkey here, death — there is no doubt.' //742//

body.text:
395.018. kīle tu maraṇaṃ vidyād yūpāgre ca na saṃśayaḥ/
395.019. kumbhasthāne śmaśāne vā mṛto vā yatra dṛśyate//743//
body.translated_text:
395.018. 'On a stake, one should know death; on a sacrificial post, without doubt;
395.019. at a pot-place, or at a cremation ground, or where a dead person is seen.' //743//

body.text:
395.020. antarīkṣe praḍīnaṃ tu aphalaṃ tu vinirdiśet/
395.021. dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ vāsaṃ prahṛṣṭaṃ khañjarīṭakam//744//
body.translated_text:
395.020. 'Flying through the sky, it should be predicted as fruitless;
395.021. seeing a wagtail that has arrived joyfully at its place.' //744//

body.text:
395.022. yathāsthānam yathāvarṇaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vinirdiśet/
395.023. viṣame svalpakakṣeṣu prasaktaḥ kalaho bhavet/
395.024. sameṣu samake kṣetre samān varṇān vinirdiśet/
395.025. nadyāṃ tu śailavāhinyāṃ pravāsamabhinirdiśet//745//

395.026. kāṣṭheṣu nātikā cintā tathāsthiṣu dhanakṣayaḥ/
395.027. yāṃ diśaṃ samudāgacchat pañcottarapadaḥ khagaḥ/
395.028. tāṃ diśaṃ gamanaṃ vidyādyathā tasya tathā punaḥ//746//

395.029. kīṭā vātha pataṅgā vā bhayam yadiha dṛśyate/
395.030. pracurāpi yadājñeyā narasyāsthīni nirdiśet//747//
body.translated_text:
395.029. 'If insects or moths are seen, there is danger;
395.030. if they are known to be numerous, predict skeletal remains for the person.' //747//

body.text:
396.001. <396>apāṃ samīpe gajamastake vā sūryodaye brāhmaṇasaṃnidhau vā/
396.003. mukhyaprakāśe 'pyahimastake vā yaḥ paśyate khañjanakaṃ sa dhanyaḥ//748//
body.translated_text:
396.001. 'Near water, on an elephant's head, at sunrise, in the presence of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
396.003. or in the light of the face, or on a serpent's head — whoever sees the wagtail there is blessed.' //748//

body.text:
396.005. mātaṅgarājo matimāṃstriśaṅkaḥ provāca tattvaṃ khañjanaṃ ca śāstram/
396.007. snigdhe sarūkṣe viṣame same ca odeśayed doṣaguṇairyathoktaiḥ/
396.009. tamādiśettatra samīkṣya vidvāñ śubhāśubhaṃ tatphalamādiśecca//749//
396.011. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin khañjarīṭakajñānaṃ nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 396.011. 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "Knowledge of the Wagtail."'

body.text:
396.011. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasāriñ śivārutaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
396.012. tacchrūyatā/
396.012. atha kim/
396.013. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
396.014. śivārutam/
396.015. namaḥ sarveṣāmāryāṇām/
396.015. namaḥ sarveṣāṃ satyavādinām/
396.015. teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ tapasā vīryeṇa ca imaṃ śivārutaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
396.016. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ/
396.016. śāṇḍilyamidamabravīt/
396.017. yādṛśaṃ ca yathā vāśetteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vāśāñ śṛṇotha me/
396.017. pūrvasyāṃ diśi yadi vāśet, śivā pūrvamukhaṃ sthitvā trīn vārān vāśet, vṛddhiṃ nivedayati/
396.018. caturo vārān yadi vāśet, atra maṅgalaṃ nivedayati/
396.019. pañca vārān vāśet, varṣāṃ nivedayati/
396.019. ṣaḍvārān vāśet, paracakrabhayaṃ nivedayati/
396.020. saptavārān vāśet, bandhanaṃ nivedayati/
396.020. aṣṭa vārān vāśet, priyasamāgamaṃ nivedayati/
396.021. abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśet, paracakrabhayaṃ nivedayati/
396.021. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text:
396.011. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called "The Cry of the Jackal."
396.012. Listen to that.'
396.012. 'Very well.'
396.013. 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak —'
396.014. 'The Cry of the Jackal.'
396.015. 'Homage to all the Noble Ones.
396.015. Homage to all speakers of truth.
396.015. By the austerity and power of all of them, I shall expound this chapter called "The Cry of the Jackal."
396.016. Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
396.016. He declared this to <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>.
396.017. Whatever kind and however the jackal cries — hear from me the cries of all of them.
396.017. If a jackal cries in the eastern direction, standing facing east, three times, it announces increase.
396.018. If it cries four times, it announces auspiciousness.
396.019. If it cries five times, it announces rain.
396.019. If it cries six times, it announces the danger of a foreign army.
396.020. If it cries seven times, it announces imprisonment.
396.020. If it cries eight times, it announces the meeting of loved ones.
396.021. If it cries incessantly, it announces the danger of a foreign army.
396.021. Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
396.022. dakṣiṇāyāṃ dakṣiṇamukhaṃ sthitvā trivārān vāśet, 'atṛ atṛ' kurute maraṇaṃ tatra nivedayati/
396.023. caturo vārān vāśati, dakṣiṇamukhaṃ sthitvā dakṣiṇāyā eva diśāyāḥ priyasamāgamaṃ nivedayati/
396.024. arthalābhaṃ ca nivedayati/
396.024. pañcavārān vāśet, arthaṃ nivedayati/
396.024. ṣaḍvārān vāśet, siddhiṃ nivedayati/
396.025. saptavārān vāśet vivādakalahaṃ nivedayati/
396.025. aṣṭavārān vāśet, bhayaṃ nivedayati/
396.026. abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśet, ākulaṃ nivedayati/
396.026. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text:
396.022. 'Standing in the south facing south, if it cries three times making "atṛ atṛ," it announces death there.
396.023. If it cries four times, standing facing south, from the southern direction itself, it announces the meeting of loved ones.
396.024. It also announces the gain of wealth.
396.024. If it cries five times, it announces wealth.
396.024. If it cries six times, it announces success.
396.025. If it cries seven times, it announces dispute and quarrel.
396.025. If it cries eight times, it announces danger.
396.026. If it cries incessantly, it announces confusion.
396.026. Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.'

body.text:
396.027. paścimāyāṃ paścimābhimukhaṃ sthitvā śivā trivārān vāśati, maraṇaṃ nivadayati/
396.028. caturvārān vāśati, bandhanaṃ nivedayati/
396.028. pañcavārān vāśati, varṣaṃ nivedayati/
396.028. ṣaḍvārān vāśati, annapānaṃ nivedayati/
396.029. saptavārān vāśati, maithunaṃ nivedayati/
396.029. aṣṭavārān vāśati, arthasiddhiṃ nivedayati/
396.030. abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśati, mahāmeghaṃ nivedayati/
396.030. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text:
396.027. 'Standing in the west facing west, if the jackal cries three times, it announces death.
396.028. If it cries four times, it announces imprisonment.
396.028. If it cries five times, it announces rain.
396.028. If it cries six times, it announces food and drink.
396.029. If it cries seven times, it announces sexual union.
396.029. If it cries eight times, it announces the accomplishment of aims.
396.030. If it cries incessantly, it announces a great rain-cloud.
396.030. Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.'

body.text:
397.001. <397>uttarasyāṃ diśi uttarābhimukhaṃ sthitvā trivārān vāśati, puruṣasya prasthitasya nirarthakaṃ gamanaṃ bhavati/
397.002. caturvārān vāśati, rājapratibhayaṃ nivedayati/
397.002. pañcavārān vāśati, vivādaṃ nivedayati/
397.003. ṣaḍvārān vāśati, kuśalaṃ nivedayati/
397.003. saptavārān vāśati, varṣāṃ nivedayati/
397.004. aṣṭavārān vāśati, rājakuladaṇḍaṃ nivedayati/
397.004. abhīkṣṇaṃ vāśati, yakṣarākṣasapiśācakumbhāṇḍabhayaṃ nivedayati/
397.005. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: 'Standing facing north in the northern direction, if it cries three times — a man's journey will be fruitless. If it cries four times, it announces danger from the king. If it cries five times, it announces a dispute. If it cries six times, it announces welfare. If it cries seven times, it announces rain. If it cries eight times, it announces punishment from the royal court. If it cries repeatedly, it announces danger from <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>.' Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
397.006. diśi vidiśi caiva giriprāgbhāreṣu śikhareṣu nirdeśaṃ taṃ ca śṛṇotha me/
397.006. "amūṃ tuṣyet pipāsārtāṃ vidyāsiddhyai tathaiva ca"/
397.008. vidyālambhaṃ dhanalambhaṃ nirdiśecca vicakṣaṇaḥ/
397.009. tīrthākāravṛkṣamūle vāśatī yadi dṛśyate//750//
body.translated_text: 'Now hear from me the designation regarding directions, intermediate directions, mountain-slopes, and peaks. "Satisfy that thirsty one, and likewise for the success of the science." The wise man should declare the gain of knowledge and the gain of wealth. When a <s>śivā</s> (jackal) is seen crying at a ford, at a temple, or at the root of a tree —' //750// 'he should declare success everywhere. And one should not approach the <s>śivā</s> with the fear of a jackal — with vigilance and mindfulness, the <s>śivā</s> should always be worshipped with offerings of fragrance and flowers; service should be rendered to her. When thus worshipped, she will announce complete success. Thus "all one's aims succeed, as the word of <s>Triśaṅku</s> declares." If a jackal cries, it announces gain of wealth. If it cries face-down, it announces a hidden treasure there. If it cries face-up, it announces rain there. If it cries at a crossroads, standing facing east, it announces gain of wealth. If facing south, it announces a meeting with a beloved. If at a crossroads facing west, it announces quarrel, dispute, conflict, and death. If it cries at the rim of a well, it announces wealth there. If it cries on green grass, it announces success in gain. If it cries very softly, it announces disease there. If it cries with a melodious voice, it announces both gain and loss. With three cries — gain; with four — loss; with five — meeting with a beloved; with six — a meal; with seven — danger; with eight — conflict and dispute.' Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
397.010. sarvatra siddhiṃ nirdiśet/
397.010. na ca śṛgālabhaye śivā (vā)me sameti apramattena smṛtimatā pūjayitavyā śivā nityam/
397.011. gandhapuṣpopahāreṇa śuśrūṣā kartavyā/
397.011. evamarcyamānā sarvasiddhiṃ nivedayiṣyati/
397.012. evam "sarve 'rthāstasya sidhyanti triśaṅkorvacanam yathā"/
397.012. krauṣṭriko yadi vāśati, arthalambhaṃ nivedayati/
397.013. adhomukho yadi vāśati, nidhānaṃ tatra nivedayati/
397.013. ūrdhvamukho yadi vāśati, varṣāṃ tatra nivedayati/
397.014. dvipathe yadi vāśati, pūrvamukhaṃ sthitvā arthalābhaṃ nivedayati/
397.015. dakṣiṇābhimukho yadi vāśati, yathāpriyasamāgamanaṃ nivedayati/
397.015. dvipathe pañcimābhimukho yadi vāśati, kalahaṃ vivādaṃ vigrahaṃ maraṇaṃ ca nviedayati/
397.016. kūpakaṇaṭhake yadi vāśati, arthaṃ tatra nivedayati/
397.017. śādvale yadi vāśati, arthasiddhiṃ nivedayati/
397.017. atimṛdukam yadi vāśati, vyādhikaṃ tatra nivedayati/
397.018. gītahāreṇa yadi vāśati, arthamanarthaṃ ca nivedayati/
397.019. tribhirvārairarthaṃ caturbhiranarthaṃ pañcabhiḥ priyasamāgamaṃ ṣaḍbhirbhojanaṃ saptabhirbhayamaṣṭabhirvigrahaṃ vivādaṃ ca/
397.020. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: 'Now I shall further declare — hear from me in sequence.' 'If it cries over various foods, or while standing on the road — I shall tell all; hear it from me. When a man has set out on a journey and the <s>śivā</s> cries, standing facing east — she announces swift travel and success in gaining wealth. If she cries facing south — she announces success in gaining wealth. If she cries facing west — she announces danger. If she cries facing north — she announces gain of wealth. If she cries standing in front of one who has set out — she announces a minor affliction. If she cries on the right side, if indeed facing southward — she announces success in the undertaking. If she cries from the west — she announces misfortune and suffering from thieves. If she cries on the right side of one walking along the road — she announces a great disease, loss, and that thieves will rob — she announces this. If she cries for a sick person, facing south — "he cannot be treated; he is impelled by the messenger of death." If she cries for a sick person, standing facing north — she announces gain of health and wealth. If she cries overhead — she announces a minor affliction. If standing facing west, she talks back and forth — she announces the decree of <s>Yama</s> (death). If she cries over various foods — she announces agitation.' Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
397.021. "atha bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi anupūrvaṃ śṛṇotha me"/
397.021. nānāhāre yadi vāśati, mārge saṃsthitasyāpi sarvaṃ vakṣyāmi taṃ śṛṇotha me/
397.022. saṃprasthitasya puruṣasya śivā vāśati vā, yā pūrvamukhaṃ sthitvā kṣipragamanamarthasiddhiṃ nivedayati/
397.023. atha dakṣiṇamukhaṃ vāśati, yā arthasiddhiṃ nivedayati/
397.024. paścānmukhaṃ vāśati, bhayaṃ nivedayati/
397.024. athottaramukhaṃ vāśati, arthalābhaṃ nivedayati/
397.025. atha saṃprasthitasya vāśati, yā purataḥ sthitvā upakleśaṃ nivedayati/
397.025. atha dakṣiṇe vāśati, yadi dakṣiṇāmukhā eva diśaḥ karmasiddhiṃ ca nivedayati/
397.026. paścimato yadi vāśati, caurato 'hitamasya duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ nivedayati/
397.027. atha mārge vrajato dakṣiṇato vāśati, mahāvyādhimanarthaṃ caurā muṣanti tannivedayati/
397.028. glānasya yadi vāśati, dakṣiṇamukham, "na sa cikitsituṃ śakyo mṛtyudūtena coditah"/
397.029. glānasya yadi vāśati, uttaramukhaṃ sthitvā ārogyadhanalābhaṃ ca nivedayati/
397.030. atha mūrdhnā vāśati, yā upakleśaṃ nivedayati/
397.030. atha paścimamukhaṃ sthitvā yā anyonyaṃ vyāharate, yamaśāsanam {nivedayati}/
397.031. nānāhāre yadi vāśati, yā saṃkṣobhaṃ nivedayati/
397.032. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: 'If the <s>śivā</s> cries in front of a man traveling on the road — she announces a safe path ahead, and success in gaining wealth. When a man walking on the road is approached by the <s>śivā</s> from the left and she goes to the right, facing south — one should know the path is safe and she announces success in gaining wealth. When a man walking on the road is approached by the <s>śivā</s> from the left and she cries in front — she announces that the path is dangerous. The wise man should turn back. Going south to the left, one should turn around from the left side — "One should not go by that path, as the word of <s>Triśaṅku</s> declares." If the <s>śivā</s>, having gone in front, sits down ahead — one should know the path is dangerous. The wise man should turn back. If the <s>śivā</s>, having come from the front, turns around to the left — "Fear approaches here" — even by that, the wise man should know there is danger. When an army has been assembled and the <s>śivā</s> cries — she announces retreat westward. If it proceeds, there will be defeat. The army should not proceed. When an army is marching and the <s>śivā</s> comes in front — she announces victory for the army and defeat of the enemy forces. When a caravan is traveling and the <s>śivā</s> goes ahead — she announces a safe path and success in gaining wealth likewise. When a man is traveling on a path and she cries on the left — she announces the road. "One should go by that path, as the word of <s>Triśaṅku</s> declares."'

body.text:
398.001. <398>śivā purataḥ puruṣasya mārgaprayātasya yadi vāśati, yā agrataḥ kṣemamārgaṃ vijñāpayati/
398.002. arthasiddhiṃ nivedayati/
398.002. mārgaṃ vrajato 'sya śivā vāmenāgatya gacchate, dakṣiṇamukhaṃ kṣemamārgaṃ vijānīyādarthasiddhiṃ ca nivedayati/
398.003. mārge vrajataḥ puruṣasya śivā vāmenāgatya purato vāśati, yā tathā sabhayaṃ mārgaṃ vijñāpayati/
398.004. nivarteta vicakṣaṇaḥ/
398.004. dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ vāmaṃ gatvā vāmataḥ parivarteta "na tanmārgeṇa gantavyaṃ triśaṅkuvacanam yathā"/
398.005. purataḥ śivā gatvā agrataśca niṣīdati, sabhayaṃ mārgaṃ vijānīyāt/
398.006. nivarteta vicakṣaṇaḥ/
398.006. śivā purata āgatya vāmena parivartate, 'bhayametīha' tenāpi bhayaṃ jānīyādvicakṣaṇaḥ/
398.007. senāyāmāvāhitāyāṃ śivā vāśati, paścimaṃ nivartanaṃ nivedayati/
398.008. yadi gacchetparājayaḥ/
398.008. senā na gacchet/
398.008. senāyāṃ vrajamānāyāṃ śivā āgacchedagrataḥ senājayaṃ nivedayati/
398.009. paracakraparājayaṃ ca nivedayati/
398.009. sārthasya vrajamānasya śivā gacchatyagrataḥ kṣemamārgaṃ nivedayati/
398.010. arthasiddhiṃ tathaiva ca/
398.011. puruṣasya pathi vrajato vāmato vāśati, mārgaṃ nivedayati/
398.011. "tanmāgeṇa {hi} gantavyaṃ triśaṅkuvacanam yathā"//
body.translated_text: '"For a village, a city, or at a shrine-place likewise" — if the <s>śivā</s> cries to the east or north, she announces welfare there. If she cries to the south or west — she announces danger there. From the left, they do not praise; likewise in the intermediate directions. An excessively long or excessively harsh cry, or one at the end of a month — I shall declare the lower one as danger, as the word of <s>Triśaṅku</s> declares.' //751//

body.text:
398.012. "grāmasya nagarasyāpi caityasthāne tathaiva ca"/
398.012. pūrveṇottareṇāpi śivā vāśati, kṣemaṃ tatra nivedayati/
398.013. dakṣiṇe paścime yadi vāśati, yā bhayaṃ tatra nivedayati/
398.014. vāmato na praśaṃsanti tathaiva vidiśāsu ca/
398.015. atidīrghātirūkṣā vā kāle māsāntike tathā/
398.016. adharāṃ tu bhayaṃ vakṣye triśaṅkuvacanam yathā//751//
body.translated_text: 'Knowing the <s>śivā</s> with a honey-sweet voice, when the proper time and occasion have arrived — welfare and success in gaining wealth should be contemplated by the wise.' //752//

body.text:
398.017. madhusvarāṃ śivāṃ jñātvā kāle vele upasthite/
398.018. kṣemaṃ caivārthasiddhiśca cintitavyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ//752//
body.translated_text: 'Diseases and misfortunes — "all come to peace, as the word of <s>Triśaṅku</s> declares." The practice of interpreting the <s>śivā's</s> cry: omens should be observed in directions and intermediate directions. Whichever day belongs to the <s>śivā</s>, that day should be known. Offerings of flowers, fragrance, and garlands should be prepared on that day. One should always be devoted to the deity. One should be devoted to the goddess. Service should be rendered to the goddess. She will fulfill all purposes. She announces all undertakings.'

body.text:
398.019. vyādhirupadravāśca, "sarvaṃ tu praśamam yānti triśaṅkuvacanam yathā"/
398.020. śivārutasyopacāro digvidiśāsu nimittā grahītavyāḥ/
398.020. yaḥ śivāyā divaso bhavati, sa divaso jñātavyaḥ/
398.021. puṣpagandhamālyopahārastaddivase upapādayitavyaḥ/
398.021. nityaṃ devatāgurukeṇa bhavitavyam/
398.021. devyā gurukeṇa bhavitavyam/
398.022. devyai śuśrūṣā kartavyā/
398.022. sarvārthān saṃpādayiṣyati/
398.022. sarvakāryāṇi nivedayati//
body.translated_text: 'Whatever undertaking one shall begin, she announces all of it. <s>Sarjarasa</s> (sal-tree resin) and <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) incense should be offered to the goddess. And flower-offerings should be presented at the proper times.' Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

body.text:
398.024. yatkiṃcitkāryamārabhiṣyati, tatsarvaṃ nivedayati/
398.024. devyai sarjaraso guggulu ca dhūpayitavyam/
398.025. puṣpabaliśca yathākāle dāpayitavyaḥ/
398.025. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ//
body.translated_text: 'In the discourse on the <s>śivā's</s> cry, I shall now declare the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) as it truly shall be. Homage to the Forest-dweller! To the Bark-clad one, <s>svāhā</s>! — with <s>sarjarasa</s> incense. This, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the chapter called the Cry of the <s>Śivā</s>.'

body.text:
398.026. śivārutakathane 'tra vidyāṃ vakṣyāmi yathāsatyaṃ bhaviṣyati/
398.027. nama āraṇyāyai/
398.027. cīriṇyai svāhā sarjarasadhūpam/
398.028. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasāriñ śivārutanāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, I shall expound the chapter called Palm-Lines (<s>pāṇilekhā</s>). Hear it.' 'What is it?' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'Palm-Lines. Now I shall declare what is situated on the hands of men — the marks of happiness and suffering, of life and death likewise.' //753//

body.text:
399.001. <399>athātaḥ puṣkarasārin pāṇilekhānāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
399.001. tacchrūyatām/
399.001. atha kim/
399.002. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuh--
399.003. pāṇilekhā/
399.004. athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi narāṇāṃ karasāṃsthitam/
399.005. lakṣaṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā//753//
body.translated_text: 'A line extending upward from the base of the thumb — from it is born great happiness; the second is in the middle, pertaining to knowledge.' //754//

body.text:
399.006. aṅguṣṭhamūlamāśritya ūrdhvarekhā pravartate/
399.007. tatra jātaṃ sukhataraṃ dvitīyā jñānamantare//754//
body.translated_text: 'The third is that line which extends toward the index finger. There the causes stated in the <s>śāstra</s> are fourfold in brief.' //755//

body.text:
399.008. tṛtīya sā lekhā yatra pradeśinyā pravartate/
399.009. tatroktā hetavaḥ śāstre samāsena caturvidhāḥ//755//
body.translated_text: 'Where joints appear on jointless areas — disturbance of the <s>nakṣatras</s>. One born under a double emergence, of purified soul, shall live a hundred years.' //756//

body.text:
399.010. aparvasu ca parvāṇi nakṣatrāṇāmupadravaḥ/
399.011. dviniḥsṛto viśuddhātmā jīvedvarṣaśataṃ hi saḥ//756//
body.translated_text: 'By one-third of thirty, one should know fifty years of life; seventy in three-part divisions, and when it extends to the very end, a hundred.' //757//

body.text:
399.012. triṃśat gtribhāgena jānīyādardhe pañcāśadāyuṣaḥ/
399.013. saptatistryaṃśabhāgeṣu atyantānugate śatam//757//
body.translated_text: 'When the life-line is visible, the obstacle is revealed. It should be known by the designation of <s>nakṣatras</s>, as well as by wealth, by wise men.' //758//

body.text:
399.014. āyurlekhā pradṛśyaiva vyantarāyaḥ prakāśyate/
399.015. nakṣatrasaṃjñayā jñeyā manujairarthaśastathā//758//
body.translated_text: 'On the path of the thumb's belly, however many strokes one has — one should know that many offspring; there is no doubt in this.' //759//

body.text:
399.016. aṅguṣṭhodaramārge tu yāvatyo yasya rājayaḥ/
399.017. tasyāpatyāni jānīyāt tāvanti nātra saṃśayaḥ//759//
body.translated_text: 'One whose line is long should be known as long-lived; one whose line is short should be known as short-lived.' //760//

body.text:
399.018. dīrghāyuṣaṃ vijānīyād dīrghalekhā tu yā bhavet/
399.019. hrasvāyuṣaṃ vijānīyāddhrasvalekhā tu yā bhavet//760//
body.translated_text: 'A barley-grain mark at the base of the thumb indicates birth at night. Birth during the day is certainly indicated by a barley-grain on the thumb.' //761//

body.text:
399.020. aṅguṣṭhamūle yavako rātrau janmābhinirdiśet/
399.021. divā tu janma nirdiṣṭamaṅguṣṭhayavake dhruvam//761//
body.translated_text: 'Where the barley-grain is indistinct — there declare the <s>lagna</s> (ascendant). The <s>lagna</s> known by the male sign indicates the day-and-night cycle.' //762//

body.text:
399.022. avyakto yavako yatra tatra lagnaṃ vinirdiśet/
399.023. lagnaṃ puṃsaṃjñako jñeyo 'horātraṃ vinirdiśet//762//
body.translated_text: 'One should indicate birth during the day; at night, the female sign prevails. Night is declared as twilight, by other divisions without doubt. From the male sign, one should state the rising and the end of the day-and-night cycle.' //763//

body.text:
399.024. divasaṃ janma nirdiśed rātrau strīsaṃjñako bhavet/
399.025. rātriḥ saṃdhyā samākhyātā bhāgairanyair na saṃśayaḥ/
399.026. puṃsaṃjñādudayaṃ teṣāmahorātrāntikaṃ vadet//763//
body.translated_text: 'On the barley-grain and rice-grain at the base of the thumb — happiness is ordained. From a horse-mark, one should know auspiciousness, through the barley-grains on the thumb.' //764//

body.text:
399.027. aṅguṣḍhamūle yavake śale saukhyaṃ vidhīyate/
399.028. aśvād bhadraṃ vijānīyādaṅguṣṭhayavakeṣviha//764//
body.translated_text: 'A barley-garland and a fish-mark on the thumb's barley-grain indicate love. Declare happiness at the beginning, middle, and end of childhood, youth, and old age.' //765//

body.text:
399.029. yavamālā ca matsyaḥ syādaṅguṣṭhayavako ratau/
399.030. bālayauvanamadhyānte sukhaṃ tasyābhinirdiśet//765//
body.translated_text: 'One who has a barley-grain, or a bow, or a <s>svastika</s> — on whose palms these are seen — blessed indeed are those men!' //766//

body.text:
399.031. yasya syād yavakaścāpi cāpo vā svastikastathā/
399.032. taleṣu yeṣu dṛśyante dhanyante dhanyāste puruṣā hyamī//766//
body.translated_text: 'A fish-mark brings grain; at the beginning of a meat-like mark, the barley-grain brings wealth. One should know enjoyment and good fortune from a fish-mark at the start; there is no doubt.' //767//

body.text:
400.001. <400>matsyo dhānyaṃ bhaved bhogāyāmiṣādau yave dhanam/
400.002. bhogasaubhāgyaṃ jānīyānmīnādau nātra saṃśayaḥ//767//
body.translated_text: 'One who has banners, flags, spears, lances, and goads on the palms should be known as a ruler of the earth. Born in a royal lineage, he should be declared a sovereign.' //768//

body.text:
400.003. patākābhirdhvajairvāpi śaktibhistomaraistathā/
400.004. talasthairaṅkuśaiścāpi vijñeyaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ/
400.005. rājavaṃśaprasūtaṃ ca rājamātraṃ vinirdiśet//768//
body.translated_text: 'Five branches extend on the hand, and four as well. He is either a <s>Kṣatriya</s> or an enjoyer, and honored by kings.' //769//

body.text:
400.006. preṣkyante śākhayā pañca haste catvāra eva ca/
400.007. kṣatriyo vā bhaved bhogī rājabhiścāpi satkṛtaḥ//769//
body.translated_text: 'A <s>Vaiśya</s> or a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, eloquent, with wealth and grain — without doubt. A <s>Śūdra</s> shall have abundant share, devoted to festivals and steadfast in vows.' //770//

body.text:
400.008. vaiśyo 'tha kṣatriyo vāgmī dhanadhānyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ/
400.009. śūdro vipulabhāgī syāt parvaśīlo 'tha naiṣṭhikaḥ//770//
body.translated_text: "He is a <s>Vaiśya</s> or a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, eloquent, with wealth and grain — without doubt. A <s>Śūdra</s> shall have abundant share, steadfast in vows, devoted to the final goal." (770)

body.text:
400.010. satatamabhipūjyaḥ syāt sarveṣāṃ ca priyaṃvadaḥ/
400.011. viśīlaḥ śīlakuñco vā bahubhir na bahustathā//771//
body.translated_text: 'He should always be honored and should be sweet-spoken to all. Whether lacking in virtue or deficient in conduct, he is not esteemed by many.' //771//

body.text:
400.012. śyāmavarṇātha bhinnā vā sā lekhā duḥkhabhāginī/
400.013. trilekhā yasya dṛśyante yasya pūrṇāḥ karasthitāḥ/
400.014. mahābhogo mahāvidvāñ jīvedvarṣaśataṃ ca saḥ//772//
body.translated_text: 'If a line is dark-colored or broken, she is a sharer of suffering. One whose three lines are seen full and situated on the hand — he is of great enjoyments, greatly learned, and lives a hundred years.' //772//

body.text:
400.015. ajapadaṃ rājacchatraṃ śaṅkhacakrapuraskṛtam/
400.016. taleṣu yasya dṛśyante taṃ vidyāt pṛthivīpatim//773//
body.translated_text: 'Goat-hoofprints, a royal parasol, preceded by a conch and a discus — one on whose palms these are seen, know him to be a lord of the earth.' //773//

body.text:
400.017. bhagastu bhāgyāya dhvajaiḥ patākairhastyaśvamālāṅkuśataśca rājā/
400.019. matsyo nu pānāya yavo dhanāya vedistu yajñāya gavāṃ ca goṣṭhaḥ//774//
body.translated_text: 'A vulva-mark brings fortune; with banners and flags, elephants, horses, garlands, and goads — he is a king. A fish indeed brings drink; a barley-grain brings wealth; an altar brings sacrifice and a cow-pen brings cattle.' //774//

body.text:
400.021. anāmikāparva atikramed yadi kaniṣṭhikā varṣaśataṃ sa jīvati/
400.023. same tvaśītirvarṣāṇi saptabhiryathā nadīnāṃ bharitāya nirdiśed//775//
body.translated_text: 'If the little finger surpasses the joint of the ring finger, he lives a hundred years. If they are equal, eighty years. With seven, one should predict the filling of rivers.' //775//

body.text:
400.025. śarīravarṇaprabhavāṃ tu lekhāṃ savaiśikhāṃ varṇavihīnakāṃ ca/
400.027. samīkṣya nīcottamamadhyamānāṃ dāridryamadhye caratāṃ vijānatām//776//
body.translated_text: 'Examining lines arising from the body's complexion, with a topknot-mark, and those devoid of color — whether low, high, or middle — one should know those who wander in the midst of poverty.' //776//

body.text:
400.029. abhyañjanodvartanasatkarī{ṣai}radhyakṣacurṇaiśca vimṛjya pāṇim/
400.031. prakṣālya caikāntaraghṛṣṭalekhāmekāgracittastu karaṃ parīkṣet//777//
body.translated_text: 'Having cleansed the hand with ointments, massage treatments, powders, and washed it, one should examine the hand with single-pointed mind, rubbing the lines in a solitary place.' //777//

body.text:
401.001. <401>valayasamanarādhipaṃ bhajantyaḥ samanugatā maṇibandhane tu tisraḥ/
401.003. dvirapi ca {sa} bhavāntare mahātmā vipuladhanaśriya āha vastralābhaḥ//778//
body.translated_text: 'Three lines like bracelets at the wrist, following and serving the lord of men — and if also in a second life, the great soul has abundant wealth and splendor; he is declared to gain garments.' //778//

body.text:
401.005. dadati satatamunnatastu pāṇirbhavati cirāya tu dīrghapīnapāṇiḥ/
401.007. paripatati śirāviruddhapāṇirdhanamadhigacchati māṃsagūḍhapāṇiḥ//779//
body.translated_text: 'A hand that is always raised and giving — one with such a long, plump hand lives for a long time. One with veins visible and hands crossed stumbles. One with fleshy, concealed hands obtains wealth.' //779//

body.text:
401.009. sudṛśa {karatalaiśca} sādhavaste kuṭilakṛtairvinimīlitaiśca dhūrtāḥ/
401.011. bhavati rudhirasaṃnibhaḥ suraktaściramiha piṇḍitapāṇirīśvaraḥ syāt//780//
body.translated_text: 'Those with good, visible palms are virtuous; those with crooked and closed palms are deceitful. One who is blood-red in color, deeply flushed — one with round, fleshy palms would be a lord.' //780//

body.text:
401.013. dhṛtaruciramanāḥ śilāravindairjvalanakaṣāyasuvarṇapāṇirā{jih}/
401.015. bhavati bahudhano nigūḍhapāṇiściramiha jīvati pānabhogabhogī//781//
body.translated_text: 'One whose mind is firm and delightful, with hands like lotuses of rock, with hands fiery, astringent, and golden — he is a tongue. He is of great wealth, with concealed palms, lives long here, and enjoys drink and pleasures.' //781//

body.text:
401.017. subhaga iha tathoṣṇadīrghapāṇirdhruvamiha śītalapāṇikastu ṣaṇḍhaḥ/
401.019. iha hi bahudhano balena yuktaḥ sutanususaṃcitapāṇirekhako yaḥ//782//
body.translated_text: 'A handsome man here with warm, long palms; one with cool palms is certainly a eunuch here. Here one who is wealthy and endowed with strength — he whose palm-lines are fine and well-drawn.' //782//

body.text:
401.021. dhanamupanayatīha pāṇilekhā kṛtajanitā jalavacca yā sudīrghā/
401.023. jalavadanugatā suvarṇavarṇā dhanamadhigacchati niṃnaśonnatā yā//783//
body.translated_text: 'A palm-line brings wealth here — one that is born well-formed and long like water. Following like water, of golden color — one obtains wealth whose line is sunken and raised.' //783//

body.text:
401.025. dhanamupalabhate suraktapāṇirvipulamatho ca nirantarāṅguliḥ syāt/
401.027. balipuruṣamapi tyajeddhi vittaṃ ditavivaśā (?) ca viśīrṇavarṇalekhā//784//
body.translated_text: 'One with deep-red palms obtains wealth, and one with broad, gapless fingers. But even a powerful man may lose his wealth — one whose line is discolored and crumbling.' //784//

body.text:
401.029. apagataghṛtavarṇapāṇilekho bhavati naro dhanavān balena yuktaḥ/
401.031. asubhṛtisadṛśā bhavettathā bhūṣaṇavṛta {rūpavatī subhā} ekabhāryā//785//
body.translated_text: 'One whose palm-line has departed from the color of ghee — that man is wealthy and endowed with strength. A line resembling a breath of life — she has one adorned, beautiful, and auspicious wife.' //785//

body.text:
402.001. <402>bhavati bahudhano dhanairvihīnaḥ śrutamadhigamya viśālapāṇilekhaḥ/
402.003. {su}ṛjubhirahinīlanirmalā{bhih} karatalarāji {bhirīśvaraḥ sa dhanyah}//786//
body.translated_text: 'One becomes wealthy or deprived of wealth, having attained learning — one with broad palm-lines. With lines on the palm that are straight, serpent-dark, and unblemished, he is a lord and fortunate.' //786//

body.text: 402.005. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin karatalalekhānāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter on palm-lines.'

body.text:
402.006. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vāyasarutaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
402.006. tacchrūyatām/
402.007. atha kim/
402.007. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ/
402.007. namo 'rhatām/
402.007. teṣāṃ namaskṛtvā--
402.008. vāyasarutam/
402.009. idaṃ śāstraṃ pravakṣyāmi vāyasānāṃ śubhāśubham/
402.010. jayaṃ parājayaṃ caiva lābhālābhaṃ tathaiva ca//787//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called \"Crow-Omens.\" Let it be heard.' 'What then?' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'Homage to the <s>Arhats</s>.' Having paid homage to them: 'Crow-Omens. I shall declare this science of the auspicious and inauspicious signs of crows — victory and defeat, gain and loss likewise.' //787//

body.text:
402.011. sukhaduḥkhaṃ priyāpriyaṃ jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā/
402.012. vāyasānāṃ vacaḥsiddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvidhi//788//
body.translated_text: 'Happiness and sorrow, the pleasant and unpleasant, life and death likewise — I shall declare the fulfilled speech of crows according to the proper rules.' //788//

body.text:
402.013. devāḥ pravadanti śreṣṭhā vāyasānāṃ namo namaḥ/
402.014. āgatā mānuṣaṃ lokaṃ vāyasā balibhojanāḥ//789//
body.translated_text: 'The excellent gods declare: homage, homage to the crows! They have come to the human world — crows who feed on offerings.' //789//

body.text:
402.015. prasthitasya yadādhvānamagrato vāyaso bhavet/
402.016. vyāharan kṣīrivṛkṣastho nirdiśedarthasiddhitām//790//
body.translated_text: 'When one has set out on a journey, if a crow appears ahead, cawing while perched on a milk-sap tree — one should predict the accomplishment of one's purpose.' //790//

body.text:
402.017. svareṇa parituṣṭena phalavṛkṣasamāśritaḥ/
402.018. punarāgamanaṃ caiva siddhamarthaniveditam//781//
body.translated_text: 'With a contented voice, perched on a fruit-bearing tree — it indicates return again and the announced purpose as accomplished.' //791//

body.text:
402.019. vivṛddhavṛkṣapatrāṇi madhuraṃ cānuvāsati/
402.020. asūpaṃ nirdiśed bhojyaṃ guḍamiśraṃ tu gorasam//782//
body.translated_text: 'Pulling at the leaves of a luxuriant tree and calling sweetly — one should predict unseasoned food, milk-products mixed with <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery).' //792//

body.text:
402.021. dṛṣṭastu tuṇḍapādena ātmanaḥ parimārjati/
402.022. pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā miśraṃ tatra vidyānna saṃśayaḥ//783//
body.translated_text: 'And when seen cleaning itself with beak and feet — one should know there will be <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) mixed with ghee, without doubt.' //793//

body.text:
402.023. rūkṣaṃ nirgharṣate tuṇḍaṃ śiraśca parimārjati/
402.024. saphalaṃ vṛkṣamāsthāya dhruvaṃ māṃsena bhojanam//784//
body.translated_text: 'When it harshly scrapes its beak and cleans its head, perching on a fruit-bearing tree — there will certainly be a meal of meat.' //794//

body.text:
402.025. locayati vyāharati phalavṛkṣasamāśritaḥ/
402.026. vyādhena ca hataṃ māṃsaṃ nivedayati bhojanam//785//
body.translated_text: 'When it pecks and caws while perched on a fruit-bearing tree — it announces food of meat killed by a hunter.' //795//

body.text:
402.027. ghoraṃ vyāharate kāryaṃ vāyaso vṛkṣamāśritaḥ/
402.028. kalahaṃ saṃgrāmabhayaṃ tatra vidyānna saṃśayaḥ//786//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow caws a terrible omen while perched on a tree — one should know there will be quarrel and fear of battle, without doubt.' //796//

body.text:
402.029. śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
402.030. kalahaṃ sumahat kṛtvā na cārthaṃ tatra sidhyati//787//
body.translated_text: 'When perched on a dry tree it caws weakly and pitifully — after a great quarrel, one's purpose is not accomplished there.' //797//

body.text:
402.031. kṣīrivṛkṣe niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
402.032. krameṇa yugamātreṇa na cārthaṃ tatra sidhyate//788//
body.translated_text: 'When perched on a milk-sap tree it caws weakly and pitifully — in due course, within a yoke-measure of time, one's purpose is not accomplished there.' //798//

body.text:
403.001. <403>śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā 'kāmukākam' pravāśati/
403.002. tatkṣaṇaṃ saṃnivedeti tatra caurabhayaṃ bhavet//799//
body.translated_text: 'When perched on a dry tree it calls \"kāmukākam\" — at that very moment it announces: there will be fear of thieves.' //799//

body.text:
403.003. śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā 'kāmukākam' pravāśati/
403.004. pṛṣṭhena darśayedbhāraṃ kṣudhāpīḍāṃ ca nirdiśet//800//
body.translated_text: 'When perched on a dry tree it calls \"kāmukākam\" and shows its back as a burden — one should predict affliction by hunger.' //800//

body.text:
403.005. pakṣaṃ vidhūyamāno yaḥ paśyan pathasya vāśati/
403.006. na tatra gamanaṃ kuryāccauraiḥ pathamupadrutam//801//
body.translated_text: 'One that shakes its wings while watching and caws at the road — one should not travel there; the path is beset by robbers.' //801//

body.text:
403.007. rajjuṃ vā phalakaṃ vāpi yadi karṣati vāyasaḥ/
403.008. na tatra gamanaṃ śreyaścauraiḥ pathamupadrutam//802//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow drags a rope or a plank — it is not good to travel there; the path is beset by robbers.' //802//

body.text:
403.009. gomaye śuṣkakāṣṭhe vā yadi vāśati vāyasaḥ/
403.010. kalahaḥ kuvaco vyādhir na cārthaṃ tatra sidhyati//803//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow caws upon cow-dung or dry wood — quarrel, harsh words, and disease; one's purpose is not accomplished there.' //803//

body.text:
403.011. tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā kāṣṭhaṃ darśayecca sadā khagaḥ/
403.012. purataḥ śuṣkapāṇistu tatra caurabhayaṃ bhavet//804//
body.translated_text: 'If the bird constantly shows grass or wood, and ahead one's hand is empty — there will be fear of thieves.' //804//

body.text:
403.013. sārthopari niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
403.014. nipatet sārthamadhye 'smiṃś caurasainyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ//805//
body.translated_text: 'When perched upon a caravan it caws weakly and pitifully, and falls into the midst of the caravan — there is a robber army, without doubt.' //805//

body.text:
403.015. yadā pradakṣiṇaṃ trastaṃ vāśanti vividhaṃ khagāḥ/
403.016. śuṣkavṛkṣe niṣīditvā tatra vidyānmahābhayam//806//
body.translated_text: 'When birds caw in various ways, frightened and turning clockwise, perched on a dry tree — one should know there is great danger.' //806//

body.text:
403.017. bhītastrastaḥ parītaśca yastu vyāharate khagaḥ/
403.018. paribādhan diśaḥ sarvāstatra bhayamupasthitam//807//
body.translated_text: 'When a bird caws frightened, terrified, and surrounded — harassment from all directions; danger is at hand there.' //807//

body.text:
403.019. gacchantaṃ samanugacchetpuraḥ sthitvā tu vyāharet/
403.020. na tatra gamanaṃ kuryānmārgamatra praśātanam//808//
body.translated_text: 'If it follows one who is going and caws while standing ahead — one should not travel there; the path ahead should be pacified.' //808//

body.text:
403.021. vāstumadhye pratisthāne kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ ca vyāharet/
403.022. vyādhiṃ tatra vijānīyād vāse vā gṛhasvāminām//809//
body.translated_text: 'In the middle of a dwelling or at a resting-place, if it caws weakly and pitifully — one should know there will be disease there, or at the residence of the householder.' //809//

body.text:
403.023. śakaṭasya yathā śabdaṃ viśrabdhaṃ vāśati vāyasaḥ/
403.024. dūrādabhyāgataṃ jñātvā prasiddhiṃ cābhinirdiśet//810//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow caws with a sound like a cart's creaking — knowing someone is arriving from afar, one should predict accomplishment.' //810//

body.text:
403.025. gargare ghaṭake caiva sthālikapiṭhareṣu vā/
403.026. niṣaṇṇo vāśati kākaḥ prasiddhaṃ gamanaṃ dhruvam//811//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow sits cawing upon a water-jar, a pot, a cooking-vessel, or a basin — the journey is certainly accomplished.' //811//

body.text:
403.027. āsane śayane vāpi sthito vāśati vāyasaḥ/
403.028. prasiddhaṃ gamanaṃ brūyātproṣitena samāgamaḥ//812//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow stands cawing on a seat or on a bed — one should declare the journey is accomplished; there will be reunion with one who was abroad.' //812//

body.text:
403.029. brahmasthāne niṣīditvā dhruvaṃ vāśati vāyasaḥ/
403.030. arthalābhaṃ vijānīyāddhanalābhaṃ ca ākaret//813//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow sits cawing at the <s>Brahma</s>-station — one should know gain of purpose, and it brings gain of wealth.' //813//

body.text:
403.031. brahmasthāne niṣīditvā kṣāmaṃ dīnaṃ vāśati/
403.032. saṃdhisthāne hareccaurastatra vai nāsti saṃśayaḥ//814//
body.translated_text: 'When a crow sits at the <s>Brahma</s>-station cawing weakly and pitifully — at the junction-point a thief steals; there is indeed no doubt.' //814//

body.text:
404.001. <404>devatādevatānāṃ ca devasyopavanāni ca/
404.002. yasya vācaṃ vadettasya arthalābhaṃ vinirdiśet//815//
body.translated_text: 'At the shrines of gods and divinities, and at the pleasure-groves of a deity — for whomever it utters its voice, one should predict gain of purpose for that person.' //815//

body.text:
404.003. lākṣāharidrāmañjiṣṭhāharitālamanaḥśilāḥ/
404.004. yasyāharetpurastasya svarṇalābhaṃ vinirdiśet//816//
body.translated_text: '<s>Lākṣā</s> (lac), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) — before whomever it brings these, one should predict gain of gold for that person.' //816//

body.text:
404.005. pātraṃ ca pātrakaṃ caiva mṛttikāvarabhājanam/
404.006. yasya yasya harettasya dravyalābhaṃ vinirdiśet//817//
body.translated_text: 'A vessel, a small pot, an earthen water-jar — from whomever it takes these, one should predict gain of goods for that person.' //817//

body.text:
404.007. saṃghībhūtvā yugamātraṃ śubhaṃ tiṣṭhati vāyasaḥ/
404.008. kāṣṭhaṃ vā vāyasā yatra gṛhamāropayanti ca/
404.009. nigadantyatra vijānīyād yācakāttu mahābhayam//818//
body.translated_text: 'When crows gather together and a crow stands for the duration of a yoke-measure in an auspicious position, or where crows place a piece of wood on a house — one should know it announces here: there is great danger from a supplicant.' //818//

body.text:
404.010. nīlaṃ pītaṃ lohitaṃ ca pratisaṃharaṇāni ca/
404.011. nigṛhṇanti yatra kākā vyādhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet//819//
body.translated_text: 'Blue, yellow, and red things, and collected objects — wherever crows seize these, one should predict disease there.' //819//

body.text:
404.012. grāmānte bhayamākhyāti kāko vā vāśati dhruvam/
404.013. pratyekato vā vāśati vidyāttatra mahābhayam//820//
body.translated_text: 'At the village boundary, a crow cawing certainly announces danger. Or if it caws individually, one should know there is great danger there.' //820//

body.text:
404.014. vāyaso 'stha gṛhītvā vai pragacchedanudakṣiṇam/
404.015. niṣīdan saphale vṛkṣe sa vadenmāṃsabhojanam//821//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow, having taken a bone, goes in a counter-clockwise direction, and sits on a fruit-bearing tree — it declares a meal of meat.' //821//

body.text:
404.016. yasya śīrṣe niṣīditvā karṇaṃ karṣati vāyasaḥ/
404.017. abhyantare saptarātrānmaraṇaṃ tasya nirdiśet//822//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow, having sat upon someone's head, pulls the ear — within seven nights, one should predict the death of that person.' //822//

body.text:
404.018. karake codake caiva snigdhadeśeṣu vāśati/
404.019. ūrdhvamukhaṃ nirīkṣaṃstu jagad vṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//823//
body.translated_text: 'On a water-pot or in water, and in moist places it caws; looking upward — one should predict rain for the world.' //823//

body.text:
404.020. svareṇa parituṣṭena tīrthavṛkṣeṣu vāśati/
404.021. ūrdhvamukhaṃ tathā vakti vātavṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//824//
body.translated_text: 'With a contented voice it caws on trees at sacred fords; speaking thus with face upward — one should predict rain with wind.' //824//

body.text:
404.022. kāyaṃ kilakilāyaṃstu snigdhadeśeṣu vāśati/
404.023. vakṣo vidhunvan vāyasaḥ sadyo vṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet//825//
body.translated_text: 'Making a rattling cry with its body and cawing in moist places, a crow shaking its chest — one should predict immediate rain.' //825//

body.text:
404.024. svareṇa parituṣṭena snigdhaṃ madhuraṃ vāśati/
404.025. sakṣarasadravaṃ bhāgaṃ vāśati bhojanaṃ bhavet//826//
body.translated_text: 'With a contented voice, it caws moistly and sweetly — when it caws a portion rich with liquid drops, there will be food.' //826//

body.text:
404.026. prakāre toraṇāgre vā yadi vāśati vāyasaḥ/
404.027. abhīkṣṇaṃ gharṣate tuṇḍaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ tatra nirdiśet//827//
body.translated_text: 'If a crow caws on a rampart-wall or at the top of a gateway, and frequently scrapes its beak — one should predict battle there.' //827//

body.text:
404.028. maṇḍalāni vāvartāni bahirvā nagarasya ca/
404.029. vairaṃ ca vigrahaṃ ghoraṃ tatra caiva vinirdiśet//828//
body.translated_text: 'Circles and whirlwinds outside the city — one should predict fierce enmity and conflict there.' //828//

body.text:
404.030. grāme vā nagare vāpi kurvate yatra maṇḍalam/
404.031. ūrdhvamukhaṃ vāśanto vai viṣaṇṇatvaṃ samutthitam//829//
body.translated_text: 'In a village or in a city, wherever crows make circles, cawing with faces upward — despondency has arisen.' //829//

body.text:
405.001. <405>pūrveṇa caiva grāmasya yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.002. alpodakenotplavanti vanāni nagarāṇi ca//830//
body.translated_text: 'When a she-crow nests to the east of the village — with little water, the forests and cities are flooded.' //830//'

body.text:
405.003. purastāddakṣiṇe pārśve yadi sūyati vāyasī/
405.004. varṣati prathame māse paścāddevo na varṣati/
405.005. kṛṣṭadhānyāni vardhante māṣadhānyaṃ vinaśyati//831//
body.translated_text:
405.003. 'If a she-crow nests on the front southern side,
405.004. it rains in the first month; afterwards the god does not rain.
405.005. Crops grown from ploughed land increase, but bean-crops are destroyed.' //831//

body.text:
405.006. dakṣiṇe vṛkṣaśikhare yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.007. maṇḍūkakīṭakamakṣā cauraśca bahulībhavet//832//
body.translated_text:
405.006. 'When a she-crow nests on the top of a southern tree,
405.007. frogs, insects, and flies increase, and thieves become numerous.' //832//

body.text:
405.008. paścimottarapāśva tu yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.009. aśanir nipatettatra bhayaṃ ca mṛgapakṣiṇām//833//
body.translated_text:
405.008. 'When a she-crow nests on the western-northern side,
405.009. a thunderbolt falls there, and there is fear for animals and birds.' //833//

body.text:
405.010. uttare vṛkṣaśikhare yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.011. pūrvamuptaṃ vijānīyācchasyaṃ samupajāyate//834//
body.translated_text:
405.010. 'When a she-crow nests on the top of a northern tree,
405.011. one should know: the crop that was sown first will grow.' //834//

body.text:
405.012. upari vṛkṣaśikhare yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.013. alpodakaṃ vijānīyātsthale bījāni ropayet//835//
body.translated_text:
405.012. 'When a she-crow nests on the very top of a tree,
405.013. one should know there will be little water; seeds should be sown on high ground.' //835//

body.text:
405.014. yadā tu madhye vṛkṣasya nilayaṃ karoti vāyasī/
405.015. madhyaṃ varṣate varṣaṃ madhyaśasyaṃ prajāyate//836//
body.translated_text:
405.014. 'When a she-crow makes her nest in the middle of a tree,
405.015. rain falls moderately, and a moderate crop is produced.' //836//

body.text:
405.016. skandhamūle tu vṛkṣasya yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.017. anāvṛṣṭirbhaved ghorā durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//837//
body.translated_text:
405.016. 'When a she-crow nests at the base of a tree trunk,
405.017. there will be terrible drought; one should declare famine.' //837//

body.text:
405.018. caturaḥ pañca vā potān yadā sūyati vāyasī/
405.019. subhikṣaṃ ca bhavettatra phalānāmuditaṃ bhavet//838//
body.translated_text:
405.018. 'When a she-crow lays four or five chicks,
405.019. there will be abundance of food, and fruits will flourish.' //838//

body.text: 405.020. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vāyasarutaṃ nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 405.020. 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "The Cry of the Crow."'

body.text:
405.021. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvāralakṣaṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
405.021. tacchrūyatām/
405.022. atha kim/
405.022. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
405.023. dvāralakṣaṇam/
405.024. mohendramatha divyaṃ ca māṅgalyaṃ pūrvataḥ smṛtam/
405.025. dakṣiṇe tu diśo bhāge pūṣā ca pitryameva ca//839//
body.translated_text:
405.021. 'Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called "Characteristics of Doors."
405.021. Listen to it.
405.022. What then?
405.022. Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak:
405.023. "Characteristics of Doors."
405.024. <s>Mohendra</s> and the divine and the auspicious are remembered on the eastern side.
405.025. On the southern side: <s>Pūṣā</s> and the ancestral.' //839//

body.text:
405.026. sugrīvaṃ puṣpadantaṃ ca paścimenātra nirdiśet/
405.027. bhallātakaṃ rājayakṣmaṃ vidyāduttarataḥ śubham//840//
body.translated_text:
405.026. '<s>Sugrīva</s> and <s>Puṣpadanta</s> are declared on the western side.
405.027. <s>Bhallātaka</s> and <s>Rājayakṣma</s> are known as auspicious on the northern side.' //840//

body.text:
405.028. janmasampadvipatkṣetrakṣemapratyarisādhanam/
405.029. atha vai dhanamitraṃ ca paramaṃ mairameva ca//841//
body.translated_text:
405.028. 'Birth, prosperity, adversity, field, security, means against enemies,
405.029. wealth-and-friends, and the supreme friendship —' //841//

body.text:
405.030. uvāca vidhivatprājño viśvakarmā mahāmatiḥ/
405.031. vāstūnāṃ guṇadoṣau ca pravakṣyāmyanupūrvaśaḥ//842//
body.translated_text:
405.030. 'The wise <s>Viśvakarman</s>, of great intellect, spoke according to rule:
405.031. "I shall declare the merits and defects of building sites in order."' //842//

body.text:
406.001. <406>samaṃ syāccaturasraṃ ca vistīrṇā caiva mṛttikā/
406.002. kṣīrivṛkṣākulaṃ dhanyaṃ brāhmaṇasya praśasyate//843//
body.translated_text:
406.001. 'A site should be level, quadrilateral, with expansive soil,
406.002. abounding in milky trees — such a prosperous site is recommended for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' //843//

body.text:
406.003. pūrvāyatanatayā vāstu rathacakrākṛti ca yat/
406.004. raktapāṃśurbhavedyatra rājñāṃ tattu praśasyate//844//
body.translated_text:
406.003. 'A site elongated toward the east, shaped like a chariot wheel,
406.004. where the soil is red — that is recommended for kings.' //844//

body.text:
406.005. trikoṇaṃ kuśasaṃstrīrṇamuttānaṃ madhuraṃ ca yat/
406.006. vyāyamato jalaṃ caiva vāstu tasya dhanauṣadhī//845//
body.translated_text:
406.005. 'Triangular, strewn with <s>kuśa</s> grass, open, and sweet,
406.006. with water obtained by effort — that site yields wealth and medicines.' //845//

body.text:
406.007. aṅgārākārasaṃsthānaṃ gomukhaṃ śakaṭākṛti/
406.008. anāvāsyaṃ ca tat proktam yacca putrakṣayāvaham//846//
body.translated_text:
406.007. 'A site shaped like charcoal, cow-mouthed, or cart-shaped,
406.008. is declared uninhabitable, and one that causes the destruction of sons.' //846//

body.text:
406.009. yattu kañjarakakṣaistat tyaktaṃ varṣodakena ca/
406.010. apasavyodakaṃ caiva dūrataḥ parivarjayet//847//
body.translated_text:
406.009. 'A site covered with thorny bushes, abandoned by rainwater,
406.010. with water flowing counter-clockwise — should be avoided from afar.' //847//

body.text:
406.011. viprasya caturasraṃ tu kṣātriyaṃ parimaṇḍalam/
406.012. daśadvādaśakaṃ vaiśye śūdrasya tatra lekhanam//848//
body.translated_text:
406.011. 'For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a quadrilateral site; for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a circular one;
406.012. for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, a ten-or-twelve-sided one; for a <s>Śūdra</s>, a drawn site.' //848//

body.text:
406.013. vāstupūrvottare deśe gokulaṃ tatra kārayet/
406.014. tathaiva cāgniśālāṃ tu pūrvadakṣiṇato diśi//849//
body.translated_text:
406.013. 'In the northeastern part of the building-site, a cow-pen should be built.
406.014. And likewise, the fire-hall should be in the southeastern direction.' //849//

body.text:
406.015. varṣavṛṣyāyudhāgārān dakṣiṇena niveśayet/
406.016. paścimottarataścātra vaṇigbhāṇḍaṃ niveśayet//850//
body.translated_text:
406.015. 'The armories for rain-equipment and weapons should be placed to the south.
406.016. And merchandise for trade should be placed to the northwest.' //850//

body.text:
406.017. uttarāyāṃ tu kartavyaṃ varcaḥsthānamanuttaram/
406.018. eśānyāmeva sarvāṇi prāsādaśca puromukhaḥ//851//
body.translated_text:
406.017. 'The privy should be made to the north, the best arrangement.
406.018. All structures in the northeast, and the palace should face forward.' //851//

body.text:
406.019. avidhiparivarteta tatra vairaṃ vadho bhavet/
406.020. racitasarvadvārāṇāmāyāmo dviguṇo mataḥ//852//
body.translated_text:
406.019. 'If this arrangement is reversed, there will be enmity and slaughter.
406.020. The length of all constructed doors is considered to be double.' //852//

body.text:
406.021. kuryātsurabhavanānām yatheṣṭaṃ dvārakāṇyapi/
406.022. taddvārabāhuparyante striyo dṛṣṭā doṣāvahāḥ//853//
body.translated_text:
406.021. 'One should make doors of divine residences as desired.
406.022. Women seen at the ends of the door-arms are inauspicious.' //853//

body.text:
406.023. vidviṣasya salokasya dvāre syānnu karagraha/
406.024. mahendre pure vā rājyaṃ sūrye sūraprabhāvatā//854//
body.translated_text:
406.023. 'At the door of an enemy's abode, there should be a seizure of tribute.
406.024. In <s>Mahendra</s>'s city, there is sovereignty; in <s>Sūrya</s>'s, the radiance of heroes.' //854//

body.text:
406.025. satye mṛdurmṛgo śūro 'ntarīkṣe dhanakṣayaḥ/
406.026. vāyavye tu bahuvyādhirbhage bhāgyaviparyayaḥ//855//
body.translated_text:
406.025. 'In <s>Satya</s>, one is gentle; in <s>Mṛga</s>, heroic; in <s>Antarīkṣa</s>, loss of wealth.
406.026. In the northwestern quarter, many diseases; in <s>Bhaga</s>, reversal of fortune.' //855//

body.text:
406.027. puṣpe tu subhago nityaṃ vitathe 'pyaśubho bhavet/
406.028. śoke bhūtavikāraḥ syāt śoṣe tasya viṣaṇṇatā//856//
body.translated_text:
406.027. 'In <s>Puṣpa</s>, always fortunate; in <s>Vitatha</s>, inauspicious.
406.028. In <s>Śoka</s>, there is disturbance by spirits; in <s>Śoṣa</s>, dejection.' //856//

body.text:
406.029. bhallātake gṛhe vāso rājayakṣme samāvṛtiḥ/
406.030. hrade reṇupariśrāva āditye tu kalirdhruvam//857//
body.translated_text:
406.029. 'In <s>Bhallātaka</s>, dwelling in the house; in <s>Rājayakṣma</s>, enclosure.
406.030. In <s>Hrada</s>, dust and noise; in <s>Āditya</s>, strife is certain.' //857//

body.text:
406.031. nāgarāje nāgabhayaṃ mahaśced dīrghamāyuṣam/
406.032. bhavedasya ca yad dvāraṃ tatrāgnibhayamādiśet//858//
body.translated_text:
406.031. 'In <s>Nāgarāja</s>, fear of serpents; in <s>Mahat</s>, long life.
406.032. Whatever door one may have — one should declare fire-danger there.' //858//

body.text:
407.001. <407>kṣayaṃ vidyāttasya tasya dhanasya kulasya ca/
407.002. yame mṛtyuṃ vijānīyātkule śreṣṭhottamasya ca/
407.003. bhṛṅgirāje tu matimān gandharve gandhamālyatā//859//
body.translated_text:
407.001. 'One should know the decline of that wealth and that family.
407.002. In <s>Yama</s>, one should know death in the family of the best and highest.
407.003. In <s>Bhṛṅgirāja</s>, one is wise; in <s>Gandharva</s>, there is fragrance and garlands.' //859//

body.text:
407.004. bhṛṅge krodhaḥ kaliścaiva pitari bhogasampadaḥ/
407.005. dauvārike svalpadhanaṃ sugrīve rājapūjitaḥ//860//
body.translated_text:
407.004. 'In <s>Bhṛṅga</s>, anger and strife; in <s>Pitṛ</s>, prosperity of enjoyment.
407.005. In <s>Dauvārika</s>, little wealth; in <s>Sugrīva</s>, honored by the king.' //860//

body.text:
407.006. puṣpadante dhanāvāptirvaruṇe jalacitratā/
407.007. asure maraṇaṃ ghoraṃ roge tu bahudoṣatā//861//
body.translated_text:
407.006. 'In <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, acquisition of wealth; in <s>Varuṇa</s>, beauty of water.
407.007. In <s>Asura</s>, terrible death; in <s>Roga</s>, many faults.' //861//

body.text:
407.008. baliṃśca upahārāṃśca pravakṣyāmi yathāgṛham/
407.009. vicitrairvidiśairgandhaiḥ paripūjya baliṃ haret//862//
body.translated_text:
407.008. 'I shall declare the offerings and oblations for each house.
407.009. Having worshipped with various fragrant offerings from the intermediate directions, one should make an oblation.' //862//

body.text:
407.010. kalatre hetubījāni madhyame 'rjitameva tu/
407.011. mahendre muktapuṣpāṇi pāvake ca payo dadhi//863//
body.translated_text:
407.010. 'For the wife, causal seeds; in the middle, what is earned.
407.011. For <s>Mahendra</s>, loose flowers; for the fire, milk and curds.' //863//

body.text:
407.012. āditye parideyaṃ tu bhaktaṃ caiva priyaṅgavaḥ/
407.013. antarīkṣe jalaṃ divyaṃ puṣpāṇi jalajāni ca//864//
body.translated_text:
407.012. 'For <s>Āditya</s>, rice and millet should be given.
407.013. For <s>Antarīkṣa</s>, divine water and aquatic flowers.' //864//

body.text:
407.014. nandā pratipadā jñeyā ṣaṣṭhī trayodaśī jayā/
407.015. tāsu tāsu dhruvaṃ kuryātprājño hyevaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ//865//
body.translated_text:
407.014. 'The first <s>tithi</s> is known as <s>Nandā</s>; the sixth and thirteenth as <s>Jayā</s>.
407.015. On those respective days, the wise and discerning one should surely perform the rites.' //865//

body.text: 407.016. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvāralakṣaṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 407.016. 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "Characteristics of Doors."'

body.text:
407.017. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvādaśarāśikaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
407.017. tacchrūyatām/
407.018. atha kim/
407.018. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
407.019. dvādaśarāśikaḥ/
407.020. ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi cittavijñānakāṇḍakam/
407.021. yathādṛṣṭāntenaivenaṃ narāṇāṃ samudāhṛtam//866//
body.translated_text:
407.017. 'Now, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called "The Twelve Signs."
407.017. Listen to it.
407.018. What then?
407.018. Let the blessed <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak:
407.019. "The Twelve Signs."
407.020. Hereafter I shall declare the section on mind-knowledge,
407.021. as it was set forth by example for mankind.' //866//

body.text:
407.022. tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi cittavijñānamuttamam/
407.023. dvādaśaiva tu cittāste ye loke pracaranti vai//867//
body.translated_text:
407.022. 'I shall declare the supreme mind-knowledge.
407.023. There are twelve states of mind that operate in the world.' //867//

body.text:
407.024. tānahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvena me tataḥ/
407.025. dvādaśaiva tu kuryācca maṇḍalāni vicakṣaṇaḥ//868//
body.translated_text:
407.024. 'I shall declare them; listen to me regarding the truth of this.
407.025. The discerning one should make twelve circles.' //868//

body.text:
407.026. prathamaṃ meṣo nāma syād dvitīyaṃ tu vṛṣaḥ smṛtaḥ/
407.027. tṛtīyaṃ mithunaṃ nāma caturthaṃ cāpi karkaṭaḥ//869//
body.translated_text:
407.026. 'The first is called <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries); the second is known as <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus);
407.027. the third is called <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini); and the fourth is <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer).' //869//

body.text:
407.028. pañcamaṃ cāpi siṃhastu ṣaṣṭhaṃ kanyā iti smṛtam/
407.029. tulā tu saptamaṃ jñeyā vṛścikastu tathāṣṭamam//870//
body.translated_text:
407.028. 'The fifth is <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo); the sixth is known as <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo);
407.029. the seventh is to be known as <s>Tulā</s> (Libra); and the eighth, <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio).' //870//

body.text:
407.030. dhanvī tu navamaṃ jñeyā daśamaṃ makaraḥ smṛtaḥ/
407.031. kumbhaścaikādaśaṃ jñeyo dvādaśaṃ mīna ucyate//871//
body.translated_text:
407.030. 'The ninth is to be known as <s>Dhanvī</s> (Sagittarius); the tenth is known as <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn);
407.031. the eleventh is to be known as <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius); the twelfth is called <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces).' //871//

body.text:
408.001. <408>horā śarīraṃ jātasya dvitīye cintitaṃ dhanam/
408.002. tṛtīye bhrātaraścaiva caturthe svajanastathā//872//
body.translated_text:
408.001. 'The <s>horā</s> (ascendant) signifies the body of the person born; the second house signifies contemplated wealth;
408.002. the third signifies brothers; and the fourth, one's own people.' //872//

body.text:
408.003. cintyate pañcame putraḥ ṣaṣṭhe maṇḍale śatrutā/
408.004. saptame dārasamyogo hyaṣṭame naidhanaṃ smṛtam//873//
body.translated_text:
408.003. 'The fifth concerns a son; the sixth circle signifies enmity;
408.004. the seventh, union with a spouse; the eighth is known as death.' //873//

body.text:
408.005. navame cintyate dharmo daśame karmajaṃ phalam/
408.006. ekādaśe cārthalābho dvādaśe vyarthasambhavaḥ//874//
body.translated_text:
408.005. 'The ninth concerns <s>Dharma</s>; the tenth, the fruit of one's actions;
408.006. the eleventh, acquisition of wealth; the twelfth, futile expenditure.' //874//

body.text:
408.007. ete dvādaśa cittāstu yathā dṛṣṭā maharṣibhiḥ/
408.008. sarvabhūtātmabhūtāśca yathājñeyāsta dehinām//875//
body.translated_text:
408.007. 'These are the twelve states of mind as seen by the great sages,
408.008. pertaining to the souls of all beings, as they are to be known by the embodied.' //875//

body.text:
408.009. āgatya pṛcchate kaścit prathamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
408.010. śirastu spṛśate yaśca śabdaśca upalakṣyate//876//
body.translated_text:
408.009. 'When someone comes and asks, touching the first circle —
408.010. if he touches his head, and a sound is perceived —' //876//

body.text:
408.011. vyādhitaṃ caiva hyātmānamāgneyāśca vinaṣṭayaḥ/
408.012. yadi brūyāttadā tasya ātmārthaṃ cintitaṃ bhavet//877//
body.translated_text:
408.011. 'and if he speaks of his own illness and losses by fire,
408.012. then his concern is for himself.' //877//

body.text:
408.013. kāñcanaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ lohaṃ caiva bhṛśaṃ bhavet/
408.014. sa ca sarvagataścaiva agniraśnāti niścitam//878//
body.translated_text:
408.013. 'Whether gold, silver, copper, or iron — it would be considerable;
408.014. and it is all-pervading; fire certainly consumes it.' //878//

body.text:
408.015. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātamāgneyaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
408.016. yādṛśaśca bhavecchabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//879//
body.translated_text:
408.015. 'Seeing such a portent, one should declare a fire-related omen for him.
408.016. And whatever kind of sound there is, such is his concern.' //879//

body.text:
408.017. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya dvitīyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
408.018. grīvāṃ vā parimārjayed galaṃ ca cibukaṃ punaḥ//880//
body.translated_text:
408.017. 'When some person comes and touches the second circle,
408.018. or wipes his neck, throat, and chin —' //880//

body.text:
408.019. yadi śabdaśca śrūyeta dṛṣṭā gāvastathaiva ca/
408.020. īdṛśaṃ ca dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ gośabdaṃ tatra nirdiśet/
408.021. atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//881//
body.translated_text:
408.019. 'and if a sound is heard, and cows are also seen —
408.020. seeing such a portent, one should declare the cry of cattle for him.
408.021. Or whatever kind of sound there is, such is his concern.' //881//

body.text:
408.022. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya tṛtīyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
408.023. mārjayenmukhadeśaṃ tu strīcittaṃ tasya nirdiśet//882//
body.translated_text:
408.022. 'When some person comes and touches the third circle,
408.023. and wipes the area of the face — one should declare that his concern is about a woman.' //882//

body.text:
408.024. atha śabdo bhavettatra śrūyantāṃ tādṛśāstu te/
408.025. jātaṃ prajātamupajātaṃ tathā jāto bhaviṣyati//883//
body.translated_text:
408.024. 'And if a sound occurs there — listen to what it signifies:
408.025. "Born, newly born, just born" — thus a birth will occur.' //883//

body.text:
408.026. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ garbhaṃ tasya vinirdiśet/
408.027. atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//884//
body.translated_text:
408.026. 'Seeing such a portent, one should declare pregnancy for him.
408.027. Or whatever kind of sound there is, such is his concern.' //884//

body.text:
408.028. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya caturthaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
408.029. kacchapaṃ spṛśate yastu kalahaṃ tatra nirdiśet/
408.030. svajanavyavahārastu sati kalaha na saṃśayaḥ//885//
body.translated_text:
408.028. 'When some person comes and touches the fourth circle,
408.029. and if he touches a tortoise — one should declare quarrel there.
408.030. There is no doubt of a quarrel involving dealings with one's own people.' //885//

body.text:
408.031. ākaṭṭā kaṭṭeti śabdā bhavanti ca nirantaram/
408.032. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ kalahaṃ tatra nirdiśet//886//
body.translated_text:
408.031. 'Harsh grating sounds arise continuously;
408.032. seeing such a portent, one should declare quarrel there.' //886//

body.text:
409.001. <409>puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya pañcamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
409.002. hṛdayaṃ spṛśate yastu apatyaṃ tatra cintitam//887//
body.translated_text:
409.001. 'When some person comes and touches the fifth circle,
409.002. and if he touches his heart — his concern is about offspring.' //887//

body.text:
409.003. pravāsakaśca vijñeyaḥ paragrāmagato mṛtaḥ/
409.004. śastradravyaṃ ca yattasya brāhmaṇānāṃ kule sthitam//888//
body.translated_text:
409.003. 'And one should know he is a traveler; having gone to another village, he died.
409.004. And his weapon-property remains in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family.' //888//

body.text:
409.005. atha śabdo bhavettatra yaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu maharṣibhiḥ/
409.006. putraputreti yacchabdo yadgataṃ gatameva ca/
409.007. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ maraṇaṃ tatra nirdiśet//889//
body.translated_text:
409.005. 'And if a sound occurs there — which the great sages observed:
409.006. if the sound is "son, son" — what is gone is gone indeed.
409.007. Seeing such a portent, one should declare death there.' //889//

body.text:
409.008. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
409.009. spṛśate cāpi pārśvāni gātracintā tu cintitā//890//
body.translated_text:
409.008. 'When some person comes and touches the sixth circle,
409.009. and touches his sides — his concern is about the body.' //890//

body.text:
409.010. vigrahastu mahāghoraḥ śatruścāpi pravadhyate/
409.011. atha vā tatra ye śabdāḥ śrotavyāste na saṃśayaḥ//891//
body.translated_text:
409.010. 'A great and terrible conflict will arise, and the enemy is slain.
409.011. Or whatever sounds occur there — they should be listened to without doubt.' //891//

body.text:
409.012. ayaṃ tu prakṣaraścaivaṃ hataśca vihatastathā/
409.013. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātamarivigrahamādiśet/
409.014. atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//892//
body.translated_text:
409.012. 'This one is an assailant, and thus he is struck and beaten.
409.013. Seeing such a portent, one should declare conflict with an enemy.
409.014. Or whatever kind of sound there is, such is his concern.' //892//

body.text:
409.015. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya saptamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
409.016. hastena mardayed hastaṃ tathā nāḍīṃ ca mardayet//893//
body.translated_text:
409.015. 'If some man comes and touches the seventh circle,
409.016. rubbing his hand with his hand and likewise rubbing his pulse —' //893//

body.text:
409.017. niveśacintā vijñeyā anyagrāmagatā bhavet/
409.018. tatreme bhavanti śabdāḥ śrotavyā bhūmimicchatā//894//
body.translated_text:
409.017. 'A concern about settling is to be understood; she has gone to another village.
409.018. These are the sounds to be heard by one who desires land.' //894//

body.text:
409.019. sthitaṃ niviṣṭaṃ vartaṃ ca kṛtaṃ hastagataṃ tathā/
409.020. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ niveśaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
409.021. yādṛśo vā śrutaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//895//
body.translated_text:
409.019. '"Standing," "settled," "turning," "done," "in hand" —
409.020. seeing such a portent, one should predict settlement for him.
409.021. Whatever sound is heard, such is what he has been thinking.' //895//

body.text:
409.022. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya aṣṭamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
409.023. udaraṃ caiva phicakaṃ dve ime parimārjayet//896//
body.translated_text:
409.022. 'If some man comes and touches the eighth circle,
409.023. rubbing his belly and his back — these two he rubs.' //896//

body.text:
409.024. nidhanaṃ dṛśyate tasya maraṇaṃ cāpi dṛśyate/
409.025. yadi bhaved bhavenmṛtyuryaścānyapriyasaṃgamaḥ//897//
body.translated_text:
409.024. 'Destruction is seen for him, and death too is seen;
409.025. if it is to be, death shall come, or separation from a loved one.' //897//

body.text:
409.026. tatreme śabdāḥ śrotavyā mṛta eva bhaviṣyati/
409.027. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ vyāpattiṃ tasya nirdiśet//898//
body.translated_text:
409.026. 'These are the sounds to be heard — he will certainly die.
409.027. Seeing such a portent, one should predict calamity for him.' //898//

body.text:
409.028. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya navamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
409.029. ūruṃ ca spṛśate bhūyo dharmacintā ca cintitā//899//
body.translated_text:
409.028. 'If some man comes and touches the ninth circle,
409.029. and again touches his thigh — he has been thinking about <s>Dharma</s> (religious duty).' //899//

body.text:
409.030. tatra śabdāśca śrotavyā bhavanti hi na saṃśayaḥ/
409.031. yajan hi yājakaścaiva yajamānastathaiva ca/
409.032. śabdānevaṃvidhāñ śrutvā yajñacintāṃ tu nirdiśet//900//
body.translated_text:
409.030. 'The sounds to be heard there are indeed these, without doubt:
409.031. "sacrificing," "one who causes sacrifice," and "the one who performs the sacrifice" —
409.032. hearing such sounds, one should predict a concern about sacrifice.' //900//

body.text:
410.001. <410>puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya daśamaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
410.002. karmacintā vicintyeti gṛhakarma na saṃśayaḥ//901//
body.translated_text:
410.001. 'If some man comes and touches the tenth circle,
410.002. his concern is about work — domestic work, without doubt.' //901//

body.text:
410.003. spṛśate jānunī caiva karmacintāṃ tu nirdiśet/
410.004. tatra śabdā bhavantīme śrotavyāśca na saṃśayaḥ//902//
body.translated_text:
410.003. 'He touches both his knees — one should predict a concern about work.
410.004. The sounds that arise there are to be heard, without doubt.' //902//

body.text:
410.005. bhūmikarma ca kṣetraṃ ca kṣetrakarma tathaiva ca/
410.006. etādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvotpātaṃ karmacintāṃ vinirdiśet//903//
body.translated_text:
410.005. '"Land-work," "field," and "field-work" likewise —
410.006. seeing such a portent, one should predict a concern about work.' //903//

body.text:
410.007. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya ekādaśaṃ tu saṃspṛśet/
410.008. jaṅghe tu spṛśate bhūyo hyarthalābhaṃ vinirdiśet//904//
body.translated_text:
410.007. 'If some man comes and touches the eleventh circle,
410.008. touching again his shanks — one should predict gain of wealth.' //904//

body.text:
410.009. tatreme śabdāḥ śrotavyā bhavantīha na saṃśayaḥ/
410.010. paṇasuvarṇacelāni dhānyaṃ samaṇikuṇḍalam//905//
body.translated_text:
410.009. 'These are the sounds to be heard there, without doubt:
410.010. coins, gold, garments, grain, an earring, and a ring.' //905//

body.text:
410.011. etādṛśaṃ ravaṃ śrutvā hiraṇyaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
410.012. atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ phalamādiśet//906//
body.translated_text:
410.011. 'Hearing such a sound, one should predict gold for him;
410.012. or whatever kind of sound it is, one should predict a corresponding result.' //906//

body.text:
410.013. puruṣaḥ kaścidāgatya dvādaśaṃ maṇḍalaṃ spṛśet/
410.014. pādau ca spṛśate pṛcchaṃś cittaṃ cāpyanarthikam//907//
body.translated_text:
410.013. 'If some man comes and touches the twelfth circle,
410.014. touching his feet and asking, his mind is on something futile.' //907//

body.text:
410.015. yastu taccintito hyartha āśā āgantukā ca yā/
410.016. atha vā śabdāḥ śrotavyā nimittajñānapāragaiḥ//908//
body.translated_text:
410.015. 'That matter which he has thought about — those are vain hopes;
410.016. or the sounds to be heard by those accomplished in omen-knowledge.' //908//

body.text:
410.017. nirāśaścaiva ghoṣaśca nirāśaṃ tasya nirdiśet/
410.018. atha vā yādṛśaḥ śabdastādṛśaṃ tena cintitam//909//
body.translated_text:
410.017. '"Hopeless" and a cry — one should predict hopelessness for him;
410.018. or whatever kind of sound it is, such is what he has been thinking.' //909//

body.text: 410.019. aya bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dvādaśarāśiko nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 410.019. 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called "The Twelve Circles."'

body.text:
410.020. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin kanyālakṣaṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
410.020. tacchrūyatām/
410.021. atha kim/
410.021. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuh--
410.022. kanyālakṣaṇam/
410.023. tattvaṃ vijñāyate yena yena śubhamupasthitam/
410.024. ninditaṃ ca praśastaṃ ca strīṇāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam//910//
body.translated_text:
410.020. 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall explain the chapter called "Characteristics of Maidens."
410.020. Listen to that.'
410.021. 'Very well.'
410.021. 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak —'
410.022. 'Characteristics of Maidens.'
410.023. 'That by which the truth is known, by which the auspicious is at hand —
410.024. the censured and the praised characteristics of women I shall declare.' //910//

body.text:
410.025. pitaraṃ mātaraṃ caiva mātulaṃ bhrātaraṃ tathā/
410.026. vimbādvimbaṃ parīkṣyeta triśaṅkuvacanam yathā//911//
body.translated_text:
410.025. 'The father, the mother, the maternal uncle, and the brother too —
410.026. from generation to generation one should examine them, as <s>Triśaṅku</s> has declared.' //911//

body.text:
410.027. muhūrte tithisampanne nakṣatre cāpi pūjite/
410.028. tadvijñaiḥ saha saṃgamya kanyāṃ paśyeta śāstravit//912//
body.translated_text:
410.027. 'On a <s>muhūrta</s> that is endowed with a favorable <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) and honored <s>nakṣatra</s>,
410.028. meeting with experts, the one versed in the treatise should examine the maiden.' //912//

body.text:
410.029. hastau pādau nirīkṣata nakhāni hyaṅgulīstathā/
410.030. pāṇilekhāśca jaṅghe ca kaṭi nābhyūrumeva ca//913//
body.translated_text:
410.029. 'He should examine the hands, feet, nails, and fingers;
410.030. the palm-lines, the shanks, the waist, the navel, and the thighs.' //913//

body.text:
411.001. <411>oṣṭhau jihvāṃ ca dantāṃśca kapolau nāsikāṃ tathā/
411.002. akṣibhruvau lalāṭaṃ ca karṇau keśāṃstathaiva ca//914//
body.translated_text:
411.001. 'The lips, the tongue, the teeth, the cheeks, and the nose;
411.002. the eyes, the eyebrows, the forehead, the ears, and the hair.' //914//

body.text:
411.003. romarājīṃ svaraṃ varṇaṃ mantritaṃ gītameva ca/
411.004. matiṃ sattvaṃ samīkṣeta kanyānāṃ śāstrakovidaḥ/
411.005. tatra pūrvaṃ parīkṣeta svayameva vicakṣaṇaḥ//915//

411.006. haṃsasvarā meghavarṇā nārī madhuralocanā/
411.007. aṣṭau putrān prasūyeta dāsīdāsaiḥ samāvṛtā//916//
body.translated_text:
