411.006. 'A woman with the voice of a goose, the complexion of a cloud, and sweet eyes
411.007. gives birth to eight sons, surrounded by male and female servants.' //916//

body.text:
411.008. vyāvartāścatvāro yasyāḥ sarve caiva pradakṣiṇāḥ/
411.009. samagātravibhaktāṅgī putrānaṣṭau prasūyate//917//
body.translated_text:
411.008. 'She whose four hair-whorls all turn clockwise,
411.009. whose limbs are evenly proportioned and well-distributed — she gives birth to eight sons.' //917//

body.text:
411.010. maṇḍūkakukṣiryā nārī saiśvaryamadhigacchati/
411.011. dhanyān sā janayetputrāṃsteṣāṃ prītiṃ ca bhuñjate//918//
body.translated_text:
411.010. 'A woman whose belly is like a frog's attains sovereignty;
411.011. she produces fortunate sons and enjoys their affection.' //918//

body.text:
411.012. yasyāḥ pāṇitale vyaktaḥ kacchapaḥ svastiko dhvajaḥ/
411.013. aṅkuśaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ mālā dṛśyante supratiṣṭhitāḥ/
411.014. ekaṃ sā janayetputraṃ taṃ ca rājānamādiśet//919//
body.translated_text:
411.012. 'She on whose palm are clearly seen a tortoise, a <s>svastika</s>, a banner,
411.013. a goad, an earring, and a garland, well-established —
411.014. she gives birth to one son, and that son should be predicted as a king.' //919//

body.text:
411.015. yasyāḥ pāṇau pradṛśyeta koṣṭhāgāraṃ satoraṇam/
411.016. api dāsakule jātā rājapatnī bhaviṣyati//920//
body.translated_text:
411.015. 'She on whose palm is seen a granary with an arched gateway —
411.016. even if born in a slave family, she will become a queen.' //920//

body.text:
411.017. dvātriṃśaddaśanā yasyāḥ sarve gokṣīrapāṇḍarāḥ/
411.018. samaśikharisnigdhābhā rājānaṃ sā prasūyate//921//
body.translated_text:
411.017. 'She who has thirty-two teeth, all white as cow's milk,
411.018. even, smooth-tipped, and lustrous — she gives birth to a king.' //921//

body.text:
411.019. snigdhā kāraṇḍavaprekṣā hariṇākṣī tanutvacā/
411.020. raktoṣṭhajihvā sumukhī rājānamupatiṣṭhati//922//
body.translated_text:
411.019. 'Glossy, with the gaze of a <s>kāraṇḍava</s> duck, deer-eyed, with delicate skin,
411.020. with red lips and tongue, fair-faced — she attends upon a king.' //922//

body.text:
411.021. sūkṣmā ca tuṅganāsā ca muktamāraktimodarī/
411.022. subhrūḥ suvarakeśāntā sā tu kanyā bahuprajā//923//
body.translated_text:
411.021. 'Delicate, with a prominent nose, pearl-like and slender-waisted,
411.022. with beautiful eyebrows and fine hair-ends — that maiden will have many offspring.' //923//

body.text:
411.023. aṅgulyaḥ saṃhitāḥ kāntā nakhāḥ kamalasaṃnibhāḥ/
411.024. suṛjuraktacaraṇā sā kanyā sukhamedhate//924//
body.translated_text:
411.023. 'Fingers well-joined and lovely, nails resembling lotuses,
411.024. with straight, red feet — that maiden thrives in happiness.' //924//

body.text:
411.025. yasyāvartau samau snigdhau ubhau pārśvau susaṃsthitau/
411.026. ...............ṛājapatnī tu sā bhavet//925//
body.translated_text:
411.025. 'She whose two hair-whorls are even, smooth, and well-positioned on both sides —
411.026. ............... she will become a queen.' //925//

body.text:
411.027. pradakṣiṇaṃ prakrameta prekṣate ca pradakṣiṇam/
411.028. pradakṣiṇasamācārāṃ kanyāṃ bhāryarthamāvahet//926//
body.translated_text:
411.027. 'She who steps to the right and looks to the right,
411.028. whose conduct is rightward — such a maiden should be taken as a wife.' //926//

body.text:
411.029. ūrū jaṅghe ca pārśve ca tathā vikramaḥ saṃsthitaḥ/
411.030. raktānte vipule netre sā kanyā sukhamedhate//927//
body.translated_text:
411.029. 'Thighs, shanks, sides, and gait well-proportioned,
411.030. with reddish, wide eyes — that maiden thrives in happiness.' //927//

body.text:
411.031. mṛgākṣī mṛgajaṅghā ca mṛgagrīvā mṛgodarī/
411.032. yuktanāmā tu yā nārī rājānamupatiṣṭhate//928//
body.translated_text:
411.031. 'Deer-eyed, deer-shanked, deer-necked, deer-bellied —
411.032. a woman with a fitting name attends upon a king.' //928//

body.text:
412.001. <412>yasyāgralalitāḥ keśā mukhaṃ ca parimaṇḍalam/
412.002. nābhiḥ pradakṣiṇāvartā sā kanyā kulavardhinī//929//
body.translated_text:
412.001. 'She whose hair is curled at the tips, whose face is round,
412.002. whose navel-whorl turns clockwise — that maiden increases the family.' //929//

body.text:
412.003. nātidīrghā nātihrasvā supratiṣṭhatanutvacā/
412.004. sukhasaṃsparśakeśāgrā saubhāgyaṃ nātivartate//930//
body.translated_text:
412.003. 'Neither too tall nor too short, with well-proportioned, delicate skin,
412.004. with hair-tips pleasant to touch — her good fortune does not wane.' //930//

body.text:
412.005. kāntajihvā tu yā nārī raktoṣṭhī priyabhāṣiṇī/
412.006. tādṛśīṃ varayetprājño gṛhārthaṃ sukhamedhinīm//931//
body.translated_text:
412.005. 'A woman with a lovely tongue, red lips, and pleasant speech —
412.006. a wise man should choose such a one for his household, one who thrives in happiness.' //931//

body.text:
412.007. nīlotpalasuvarṇābhā dīrghāṅgulitalā tu yā/
412.008. sahasrāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ tu svāminī sā bhaviṣyati//932//
body.translated_text:
412.007. 'She who has the hue of a blue lotus and gold, with long fingers and palms —
412.008. she will become the mistress of many thousands.' //932//

body.text:
412.009. dhanadhānyaiḥ samāyuktāmāyuṣā yaśasā śriyā/
412.010. kanyāṃ lakṣaṇasampannāṃ prāpya vardhati mānavaḥ//933//
body.translated_text:
412.009. 'A man who obtains a maiden endowed with auspicious marks, possessed of
412.010. wealth, grain, long life, fame, and prosperity — he prospers.' //933//

body.text:
412.011. kīrtitāstu mayā dhanyā maṅgalyakṣaṇāḥ striyaḥ/
412.012. apraśastaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathoddeśena lakṣaṇam//934//
body.translated_text:
412.011. 'I have declared the auspicious women with fortunate, auspicious marks.
412.012. Now I shall declare the unpraised characteristics, by way of summary.' //934//

body.text:
412.013. ūrdhvaprekṣī adhaḥprekṣī yā ca tiryak ca prekṣiṇī/
412.014. udbhrāntā vipulākṣī ca varjanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ//935//
body.translated_text:
412.013. 'She who looks upward, she who looks downward, she who looks sideways,
412.014. she who is restless, and she who is wide-eyed — these should be avoided by the discerning.' //935//

body.text:
412.015. bhinnāgraśatikā rūkṣāḥ keśā yasyāḥ pralambikāḥ/
412.016. citrāvalī citragātrā bhavati kāmacāriṇī//936//
body.translated_text:
412.015. 'She whose hair is split at the tips, rough, and hanging down,
412.016. with a mottled waist-line and mottled body — she is a woman of loose conduct.' //936//

body.text:
412.017. kāmukā piṅgalā caiva gaurī caivātikālikā/
412.018. atidīrghā atihrasvā varjanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ//937//
body.translated_text:
412.017. 'Lustful, tawny, fair-skinned yet excessively dark,
412.018. excessively tall or excessively short — these should be avoided by the discerning.' //937//

body.text:
412.019. yasyāstrīṇi pralambanti lalāṭamudaraṃ sphicau/
412.020. trīṃśca sā puruṣān hanti devaraṃ śvaśuraṃ patim//938//
body.translated_text:
412.019. 'She whose three parts hang down — the forehead, the belly, and the buttocks —
412.020. she destroys three men: the brother-in-law, the father-in-law, and the husband.' //938//

body.text:
412.021. pārśvato romarājī tu vinatā ca kaṭirbhavet/
412.022. dīrghamāyuravāpnoti dīrghakālaṃ ca duḥkhitā//939//
body.translated_text:
412.021. 'She whose line of body-hair is on the side, and whose waist is bent —
412.022. she attains long life, but is miserable for a long time.' //939//

body.text:
412.023. kākajaṅghā ca yā nārī raktākṣī ghargharasvarā/
412.024. niḥsukhā ca nirāśā ca varjitā naṣṭabāndhavā//940//
body.translated_text:
412.023. 'A woman with crow-like shanks, red eyes, and a harsh voice —
412.024. without happiness, without hope, shunned, her kinsmen destroyed.' //940//

body.text:
412.025. atisthūlodaram yasyāḥ pralambo niṃnasaṃnibhaḥ/
412.026. atyantamavaśā nārī bahuputrā suduḥkhitā//941//
body.translated_text:
412.025. 'She whose belly is excessively thick, hanging down like a low place —
412.026. utterly helpless, that woman, though having many sons, is greatly miserable.' //941//

body.text:
412.027. yā tu sarvasamācārā mṛdvaṅgī samatāṃ gatā/
412.028. sarvaiḥ samairguṇairyuktā vijñeyā kāmacāriṇī//942//
body.translated_text:
412.027. 'She who is uniform in all her conduct, soft-limbed, attaining evenness,
412.028. endowed with all equal qualities — she should be known as a woman of loose conduct.' //942//

body.text:
412.029. yasyā romacite jaṅghemukhaṃ ca parimaṇḍalam/
412.030. putraṃ vā bhrātaraṃ vāpi jāramicchati tādṛśī//943//
body.translated_text:
412.029. 'She whose shanks are covered with hair and whose face is round —
412.030. such a one desires a son, or a brother, or a paramour.' //943//

body.text:
412.031. yasyā bāhuprakoṣṭhau dvau romarājīsamāvṛtau/
412.032. uttaroṣṭhe ca romāṇi sā tu bhakṣayate patim//944//
body.translated_text:
412.031. 'She whose two forearms are covered with a line of hair,
412.032. and who has hair on the upper lip — she devours her husband.' //944//

body.text:
413.001. <413>yasyā hastau ca pādau ca cchidrau dantāntarāṇi ca/
413.002. patinopārjitaṃ dravyaṃ na tasyā ramate gṛhe//945//
body.translated_text:
413.001. 'She whose hands and feet have holes, and whose teeth have gaps —
413.002. the wealth earned by her husband does not remain in her house.' //945//

body.text:
413.003. yasyāstu vrajamānāyāḥ sphuṭante parvasaṃdhayaḥ/
413.004. sā jñeyā duḥkhabahulā sukhaṃ naivādhigacchati//946//
body.translated_text:
413.003. 'She whose joints crack as she walks —
413.004. she should be known as one full of suffering; she never attains happiness.' //946//

body.text:
413.005. yasyā kaniṣṭhikā pāde bhūmiṃ na spṛśate 'ṅguliḥ/
413.006. kaumāraṃ sā patiṃ tyaktvā ātmanaḥ kurute priyam//947//
body.translated_text:
413.005. 'She whose little toe on the foot does not touch the ground —
413.006. she abandons her youthful husband and takes a lover of her own choosing.' //947//

body.text:
413.007. anāmāṅguliḥ pādasya mahīṃ na spṛśate 'ṅguliḥ/
413.008. na sā ramati kaumāraṃ bandhakītvena jīvati//948//
body.translated_text:
413.007. 'The ring-finger toe of her foot does not touch the ground —
413.008. she does not enjoy youth; she lives by the profession of a courtesan.' //948//

body.text:
413.009. yasyāḥ pradeśinī pāde 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ samatikramet/
413.010. kumārī kurute jāram yauvanasthā viśeṣataḥ//949//
body.translated_text:
413.009. 'She whose second toe on the foot extends beyond the big toe —
413.010. as a maiden she takes a paramour, especially when in the prime of youth.' //949//

body.text:
413.011. āvartaḥ pṛṣṭhato yasyā nābhī sā cānubandhati/
413.012. na sā ramati kaumāraṃ dvitīyaṃ labhate patim//950//
body.translated_text:
413.011. 'She whose hair-whorl is on the back, and whose navel follows suit —
413.012. she does not enjoy youth; she obtains a second husband.' //950//

body.text:
413.013. vikṛtā sthirajālā ca rūkṣagaṇḍaśiroruhā/
413.014. api rājakule jātā dāsītvamadhigacchati//951//
body.translated_text:
413.013. 'Deformed, with thick webbed skin, with rough hair on the cheeks and head —
413.014. even if born in a royal family, she attains servitude.' //951//

body.text:
413.015. yasyāstu hasamānāyā gaṇḍe jāyati kūpakam/
413.016. agnikārye 'pi sā gatvā kṣipraṃ doṣaṃ kariṣyati//952//
body.translated_text:
413.015. 'She on whose cheek a dimple appears when she laughs —
413.016. even if she attends to the sacred fire, she will quickly commit a fault.' //952//

body.text:
413.017. samāsamagatā subhrūrgaṇḍāvartā ca yā bhavet/
413.018. pralamboṣṭhī tu yā nārī naikatra ramate ciram//953//
body.translated_text:
413.017. 'She who is of uneven and even gait, with beautiful eyebrows, with cheek-whorls,
413.018. and with hanging lips — that woman does not delight in one place for long.' //953//

body.text:
413.019. lambodarī sthūlaśirā raktakṣī piṅgalānanā/
413.020. aṣṭau bhakṣayate vīrānnavame tiṣṭhate ciram//954//
body.translated_text:
413.019. 'Pot-bellied, thick-headed, red-eyed, tawny-faced —
413.020. she devours eight heroes, and with the ninth she remains for a long time.' //954//

body.text:
413.021. na devikā na nadikā na ca daivatanāmikā/
413.022. vṛkṣagulmasanāmā ca varjanīyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ//955//
body.translated_text:
413.021. 'Named after a goddess, named after a river, or bearing a deity's name,
413.022. or named after a tree or shrub — these should be avoided by the discerning.' //955//

body.text:
413.023. nakṣatranāmā yā nārī yā ca gotrasanāmikā/
413.024. suguptā rakṣitā vāpi manasā pāpamācaret//956//
body.translated_text:
413.023. 'A woman named after a <s>nakṣatra</s>, or one who bears the same name as her <s>gotra</s> —
413.024. even if well-guarded and protected, she commits sin in her mind.' //956//

body.text:
413.025. dārān vivarjayedetān yā mayā parikīrtitāḥ/
413.026. praśastā yāstu pūrvoktāstādṛśīyānnarah(?) sadā//957//
body.translated_text:
413.025. 'One should avoid such wives as I have enumerated.
413.026. Those praised earlier are the ones a man should always choose.' //957//

body.text:
413.027. padmāṅkuśasvastikavardhamānaiścakradhvajābhyāṃ kalaśena pāṇau/
413.029. śaṅkhātapatrottamalakṣaṇaiśca saṃpattaye sādhu bhavanti kanyāḥ//958//
body.translated_text: 'With lotus, goad, <s>svastika</s>, <s>vardhamāna</s> (prosperity symbol), wheel, flag, and water-pot on the hand; with conch, parasol, and excellent marks — maidens bring prosperity.' //958//

body.text: 413.031. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin kanyālakṣaṇaṃ nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the chapter called Maiden-Marks.'

body.text:
414.001. <414>atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vastrādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
414.001. tacchrūyatām/
414.001. atha kim/
414.002. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
414.003. vastrādhyāyaḥ/
414.004. kṛttikāsu dahatyagnirarthalābhāya rohiṇī/
414.005. mṛgaśirā mūṣīdaṃśā ārdrā prāṇavināśinī//959//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, I shall expound the Garment Chapter. Hear it.' 'What then?' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'The Garment Chapter. In <s>Kṛttikā</s>, fire burns it; <s>Rohiṇī</s> is for gain of wealth. <s>Mṛgaśirā</s> means moth-damage; <s>Ārdrā</s> is life-destroying.' //959//

body.text:
414.006. punarvasuśca dhanyā syātpuṣye vai vastravān bhavet/
414.007. āśleṣāsu bhavenmoṣaḥ śmaśānaṃ maghayā vrajet//960//
body.translated_text: '<s>Punarvasu</s> is auspicious; in <s>Puṣya</s>, one becomes possessed of garments. In <s>Āśleṣā</s>, there is theft; by <s>Maghā</s>, one goes to the cremation ground.' //960//

body.text:
414.008. phālgunīṣu bhaved vidyā uttarāsu ca vastravān/
414.009. hastāsu hastakarmāṇi citrāyāṃ gamanaṃ dhruvam//961//
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Phalgunī</s>, there is learning; in <s>Uttarā</s>, one becomes possessed of garments. In <s>Hastā</s>, hand-work; in <s>Citrā</s>, certainly a journey.' //961//

body.text:
414.010. svātyāṃ ca śobhanaṃ vastraṃ viśākhā priyadarśanam/
414.011. bahuvastrā cānurādhā jyeṣṭhā vastravināśinī//962//
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Svātī</s>, beautiful garments; <s>Viśākhā</s> is pleasing to behold. <s>Anurādhā</s> gives many garments; <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is a destroyer of garments.' //962//

body.text:
414.012. mūlena kledayedvāsa āṣāḍhā rogasambhavā/
414.013. uttarā mṛṣṭabhojī syācchravaṇe cakṣuṣo rujam//963//
body.translated_text: 'By <s>Mūla</s>, one wets the garment; <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> produces disease. <s>Uttarā</s> gives refined food; in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, pain of the eyes.' //963//

body.text:
414.014. dhaniṣṭhā dhānyabahulā vidyācchatabhiṣe bhayam/
414.015. pūrvabhādrapade toyaṃ putralābhāya cottarā//964//
body.translated_text: '<s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is abundant in grain; in <s>Śatabhiṣā</s>, know there is danger. In <s>Pūrvabhādrapada</s>, water; <s>Uttarā</s> is for gain of a son.' //964//

body.text:
414.016. revatī dhanalābhāya aśvinī vastralābhadā/
414.017. bharaṇī ca bhayākīrṇā cauragamyā ca sā bhavet//965//
body.translated_text: '<s>Revatī</s> is for gain of wealth; <s>Aśvinī</s> gives gain of garments. <s>Bharaṇī</s> is filled with danger and frequented by thieves.' //965//

body.text: 414.018. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin vastrādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, is the Garment Chapter.'

body.text:
414.019. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasāriṃl luṅgādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi/
414.019. tacchrūyatām/
414.019. atha kim/
414.020. kathayatu bhagavāṃs triśaṅkuh--
414.021. luṅgādhyāyaḥ/
414.022. kutrotpannā ime bījāh(?) śasyānāṃ ca yavādayaḥ/
414.023. yairidaṃ dhriyate viśvaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam//966//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, Ho <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, I shall declare the Sprout Chapter (<s>Luṅgādhyāya</s>). Hear it.' 'What then?' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'The Sprout Chapter. From where did these seeds originate — barley and other grains — by which this entire world of moving and stationary beings is sustained?' //966//

body.text:
414.024. vāpayet tu kathaṃ bījaṃ lāṅgalam yojayetkatham/
414.025. keṣu nakṣatrayogeṣu tithiyogeṣu keṣu ca//967//
body.translated_text: 'How should one sow the seed? How should one yoke the plow? Under which <s>nakṣatra</s> conjunctions and under which <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) conjunctions?' //967//

body.text:
414.026. śāradaṃ vātha graiṣmaṃ tu kasmin māse tu vāpayet/
414.027. nimittaṃ kati śasyante kāni vā parivarjayet/
414.028. kasya vā dāpayed dhūpaṃ kena mantreṇa dāpayet//968//
body.translated_text: 'Whether autumn-sown or summer-sown — in which month should one sow? How many omens are recommended? Which should be avoided? To whom should incense be offered? With what <s>mantra</s> should it be offered?' //968//

body.text:
414.029. pradakṣiṇasamāvṛttā yadi luṅgā prajāyate/
414.030. tadā nāgamukhī luṅgā dahati citramukhyapi//969//
body.translated_text: 'If the sprout arises turning clockwise — then a serpent-faced sprout; it burns even the foremost of varied sprouts.' //969//

body.text:
415.001. <415>darbhasūcīmukhī vāpi kāraṇaṃ tatra ko bhavet/
415.002. kati saubhikṣiko luṅgāḥ kati daurbhikṣikāḥ smṛtāḥ/
415.003. kativarṇāḥ samākhyātāḥ kativarṇā nidarśitāḥ//970//
body.translated_text: 'Or a <s>darbha</s>-needle-faced one — what would be the reason there? How many sprouts indicate abundant harvests? How many are declared to indicate famine? How many colors are stated? How many colors are shown?' //970//

body.text:
415.004. naṣṭāpanaṣṭabījasya varṣati yadi vāsavaḥ/
415.005. nirghāto vā bhavettīvro 'thavāpi medinī calet//971//
body.translated_text: 'If <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) rains on seed that is lost or not yet lost, or if a severe earthquake occurs, or if the earth quakes —' //971//

body.text:
415.006. śasyaṃ phalasya kiṃ tatra nimittamupalakṣayet/
415.007. sarvametatsamāsena śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ//972//
body.translated_text: 'What omen should one observe for the crop's fruiting? All this, in brief, I wish to hear in truth.' //972//

body.text:
415.008. puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā triśaṅkurmātaṅgādhipatiridaṃ vacanamabravīt--
415.009. purā devāsurair nāgairyakṣarākṣasakinnaraiḥ/
415.010. sāgarādamṛtaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ manthite tu samudbhavam//973//
body.translated_text: Having heard the words of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke these words: 'Formerly, by gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) was seen arising from the churning of the ocean.' //973//

body.text:
415.011. amṛte bhakṣyamāṇe tu bhāgaṃ prārthitavān dvijaḥ/
415.012. tato dattāḥ surairbhāgā amṛtāddaśabindavah //974//
body.translated_text: 'While the <s>amṛta</s> was being consumed, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> requested a share. Then the gods gave shares — ten drops from the <s>amṛta</s>.' //974//

body.text:
415.013. tata utpannā ime bījā bhuvi lokasukhāvahāḥ/
415.014. yavavrīhitilāścaiva godhūmā mudgamāṣakāḥ//975//
body.translated_text: 'From those were born these seeds upon the earth, bringing happiness to the world — barley, rice, sesame, wheat, mung beans, and black gram.' //975//

body.text:
415.015. śyāmakaṃ saptamaṃ vidyādikṣuścāṣṭamakaḥ smṛtaḥ/
415.016. śeṣāstu saṃgatā jātā bahavaḥ śasyajātayaḥ//976//
body.translated_text: 'Know <s>śyāmaka</s> (millet) as the seventh; sugarcane is declared the eighth. The rest arose from their combinations — many varieties of crops.' //976//

body.text:
415.017. haritakeṣu sarveṣu ye cānye sattvajātayaḥ/
415.018. parito navamo binduḥ sarvadehe 'mṛto 'bhavat/
415.019. mūleṣu caiva sarveṣu bindurekaḥ prapātitaḥ//977//
body.translated_text: 'Among all green things and other species of beings — the ninth drop became <s>amṛta</s> throughout the entire body. And one drop was let fall upon all roots.' //977//

body.text:
415.020. āṣāḍhe śuklapakṣe 'sya vrīhidhānyāni vāpayet/
415.021. śāradādīni sarvāṇi māse bhādrapade tathā//978//
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, during the bright fortnight, one should sow rice and grain. All autumn crops likewise in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>.' //978//

body.text:
415.022. kārtike mārgaśīrṣe vā grīṣmadhānyāni vāpayet/
415.023. pañcamyāṃ śuklasaptamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhyāmekādaśīṣu ca//979//
body.translated_text: 'In <s>Kārtika</s> or <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, one should sow summer grains. On the fifth, the bright seventh, the sixth, and the eleventh —' //979//

body.text:
415.024. trayodaśyāṃ dvitīyāyāṃ tathā hi navamīṣu ca/
415.025. viśeṣatastu niṃneṣu sarvabījāni hyutsṛjet//980//
body.translated_text: 'On the thirteenth, the second, and likewise on the ninths. Especially in low-lying areas, one should scatter all seeds.' //980//

body.text:
415.026. bharaṇīpuṣyamūleṣu hastāśvinīmaghāsu ca/
415.027. kṛttikāsu viśākhāsu viśeṣeṇa tu śāradam//981//
body.translated_text: 'Under <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Hastā</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Maghā</s>; under <s>Kṛttikā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s> — especially for autumn sowing.' //981//

body.text:
415.028. saumye maitre 'nurādhe ca dhaniṣṭhāśravaṇāsu ca/
415.029. utsargaḥ sarvabījānāmuttareṣu praśasyate/
415.030. varjayejjanmanakṣatraṃ saṃgrahaṃ ca vivarjayet//982//
body.translated_text: 'Under the gentle <s>Saumya</s> (<s>Mṛgaśiras</s>), the friendly <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Śravaṇā</s> — the sowing of all seeds is praised under the <s>Uttara</s> (northern) nakṣatras. One should avoid one's birth-nakṣatra and avoid hoarding.' //982//

body.text:
415.031. grāmakṣetre ca yad bījaṃ gṛhe ca gṛhadevatā/
415.032. nimittamupalakṣeta maṅgalāni śubhāni ca//983//
body.translated_text: 'Whatever seed is for the village-field, and the household deity for the house — one should observe omens and auspicious signs.' //983//

body.text:
416.001. <416>brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ kanyāmarciṣmantaṃ ca pāvakam/
416.002. vāraṇendraṃ vṛṣaṃ caiva hayaṃ vā svabhyalaṃkṛtam//984//
body.translated_text: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a maiden, a blazing fire, a lordly elephant, a bull, or a well-adorned horse —' //984//

body.text:
416.003. pūrṇakumbhaṃ dhvajaṃ chatramāmamāṃsaṃ surāṃ tathā/
416.004. uddhṛtāṃ dhāraṇīṃ caiva baddhamekapaśuṃ dadhi//985//
body.translated_text: 'A full water-pot, a flag, a parasol, raw meat, liquor, plowed earth, a single tethered animal, and yogurt —' //985//

body.text:
416.005. cakrārūḍhaṃ ca śakaṭaṃ kākārūḍhāṃ ca sūkarīm/
416.006. parasyāropaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā sasyasampattimādiśet//986//
body.translated_text: 'A cart mounted on wheels, and a sow mounted by a crow — seeing the ascent of another upon these, one should predict success of crops.' //986//

body.text:
416.007. sarve dakṣiṇato dhanyāḥ puraśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ/
416.008. darśanaṃ śuklapuṣpāṇāṃ phalānāṃ caiva śasyate//987//
body.translated_text: 'All animals and birds to the right and in front are auspicious. The sight of white flowers and fruits is also praised.' //987//

body.text:
416.009. ajo vā vāmataḥ śasyo jambukaśca praśasyate/
416.010. vikṛtaṃ kubjakuṣṭhiṃ ca mukhaṃ śmaśrudharaṃ tathā//988//
body.translated_text: 'A goat on the left is auspicious for crops, and a jackal is praised. But deformed, hunchbacked, leprous, bearded faces —' //988//

body.text:
416.011. naraṃ nirbhartsitaṃ dīnaṃ śokārtaṃ vyādhipīḍitam/
416.012. varāhavṛndaṃ sarpaṃ ca gardabhaṃ bhārahīnakam/
416.013. dṛṣṭvā nivartayed bījaṃ punargrāmaṃ praveśayet//989//
body.translated_text: 'A man who is rebuked, wretched, grief-stricken, or afflicted by disease; a herd of boars, a serpent, or an unladen donkey — seeing these, one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.' //989//

body.text:
416.014. tilasya bahupūrṇasya bhāṇ:e syādvapanaṃ tathā/
416.015. śrutvā hyetāni vrajatāṃ sasyasampattimādiśet//990//
body.translated_text: 'Sowing should be done with a vessel full of sesame. Having heard these, for those who proceed — one should predict success of crops.' //990//

body.text:
416.016. rāśisthaṃ grathitaṃ dhautaṃ svasthamaṅkuritaṃ tathā/
416.017. śrutvā saṃmārjitaṃ caiva ityāśukṛtinaṃ viduḥ//991//
body.translated_text: 'Heaped, bound, washed, in good condition, sprouted — having heard of these, and swept clean — these they know as the quick results.' //991//

body.text:
416.018. śrutvā mlānaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca mandavṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet/
416.019. śrutvā nivartayed bījaṃ punargrāmaṃ praveśayet//992//
body.translated_text: 'Having heard of it being withered or dried — one should predict scanty rain. Having heard this, one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.' //992//

body.text:
416.020. nīyamānaṃ ca yad bījaṃ varṣate yadi vāsavaḥ/
416.021. svayameva tu tacchasyaṃ kāmaṃ kālena bhujyate//993//
body.translated_text: 'If <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) rains upon seed that is being transported — that crop itself, at the desired time, is enjoyed.' //993//

body.text:
416.022. nīyamānaṃ ca yad bījaṃ kampate yadi medinī/
416.023. bhramyate karṣakaḥ sthānānna tacchakyaṃ tu vāpitum//994//
body.translated_text: 'If the earth quakes while seed is being transported — the farmer is displaced from his place; that seed cannot be sown.' //994//

body.text:
416.024. nīyamānasya bījasya nirghāto dāruṇo bhavet/
416.025. svāmino maraṇaṃ kṣipraṃ śasyapālasya nirdiśet//995//
body.translated_text: 'If a terrible thunderbolt falls upon seed being transported — one should predict the quick death of the owner or the crop-guardian.' //995//

body.text:
416.026. atha vā vyākulaṃ karyādrājadaṇḍaṃ nikṛntati/
416.027. dṛṣṭvā nivartayed bījaṃ punargrāmaṃ niveśayet//996//
body.translated_text: 'Or one should confuse the matter — the king's punishment cuts it off. Seeing this, one should turn back the seed and re-enter the village.' //996//

body.text:
416.028. brāhmaṇebhyo yathāśakti datvā tu saṃprayojayet/
416.029. kṛtvā suvipulāṃ vedīṃ darbhānāstīrya sarvataḥ//997//
body.translated_text: 'Having given gifts to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> according to one's ability, one should then proceed. Having made a large altar and strewing <s>darbha</s> grass all around —' //997//

body.text:
416.030. samidbhiragniṃ prajvālya juhuyād ghṛtasarṣapam/
416.031. vedaśāntiṃ japetpūrvaṃ śasyaśāntimataḥ param//998//
body.translated_text: 'Having kindled the fire with kindling-sticks, one should offer ghee and mustard. One should first recite the Vedic peace-chant, then the crop peace-chant afterward.' //998//

body.text:
417.001. <417>japetpārāśaraṃ pūrvaṃ priyatāṃ vācayed dvijaiḥ/
417.002. prathamaṃ prānmukhaṃ bījaṃ prakṣipeduttare 'tha vā//999//
body.translated_text: 'One should first recite the <s>Pārāśara</s> hymn; the <s>priyatā</s> verse should be recited by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. The first seed should be cast facing east, or to the north.' //999//

body.text:
417.003. pipīlikā yadā kṣetre bījaṃ kurvanti saṃcayam/
417.004. suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarvasasyeṣu saṃpadā//1000//
body.translated_text: 'When ants in the field make stores of seed — good rain, good harvests, and prosperity in all crops.' //1000//

body.text:
417.005. haranti cet tṛṇād bījaṃ tṛṇe śasyāpahā api/
417.005. parasparaṃ ca hiṃsanti dhānyaṃ ca nidhanaṃ vrajet//1001//
body.translated_text: 'But if they carry seed from the stalks, and if they also destroy the crop from the stalks, and if they harm each other — the grain will meet destruction.' //1001//

body.text:
417.006. sthaleṣu saṃcayaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāvṛṣṭiṃ vinirdiśet/
417.007. dṛṣṭvā tu saṃcayaṃ niṃne 'nāvṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet//1002//
body.translated_text: 'Seeing them storing on high ground — one should predict heavy rain. But seeing them storing in low ground — one should predict drought.' //1002//

body.text:
417.008. yadā tu preṣitaṃ bījaṃ saptarātreṇa jāyate/
417.009. suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarvaśasyeṣu saṃpadā//1003//
body.translated_text: 'When dispatched seed germinates in seven nights — good rain, good harvests, and prosperity in all crops.' //1003//

body.text:
417.010. yadā tu proṣitaṃ bījamardhamāsena jāyate/
417.011. alpaṃ niṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ cātra jāyate//1004//
body.translated_text: 'When dispatched seed germinates in half a month — little crop is produced; famine arises there.' //1004//

body.text:
417.012. trirātrāccatūrātrādvā yadi luṅgaḥ prajāyate/
417.013. ativṛṣṭirbhavettatra paracakrabhayaṃ viduḥ//1005//
body.translated_text: 'If a sprout arises in three or four nights — there will be excessive rain there; they know there is danger from hostile forces.' //1005//

body.text:
417.014. luṅgasya tu ye pādāḥ pañca sapta nava tathā/
417.015. suvṛṣṭiṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca sarvasasyeṣu saṃpadā//1006//
body.translated_text: 'If the sprout has five, seven, or nine shoots — good rain, good harvests, and prosperity in all crops.' //1006//

body.text:
417.016. syālluṅgasya tu ye pādāścatvāro 'ṣṭapadātha vā/
417.017. alpaṃ niṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet//1007//
body.translated_text: 'If the sprout has four or eight shoots — little crop is produced; one should predict famine there.' //1007//

body.text:
417.018. luṅgasya yadi pādāstu dṛśyante dvādaśa kvacit/
417.019. kvacinniṣpadyate śasyaṃ dubhikṣaṃ kvacidādiśet/
417.020. vāmāvartāḥ pradṛśyante durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//1008//
body.translated_text: 'If the sprout's shoots are seen to be twelve anywhere — crops are produced only in some places; one should predict famine in others. If counter-clockwise turnings appear — one should predict famine there.' //1008//

body.text:
417.021. yadā pūrvamukhī luṅgā kṣemaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet/
417.022. yadā paścānmukhī luṅgā ativṛṣṭiṃ ca nirdiśet//1009//
body.translated_text: 'When the sprout faces east — one should predict safety and rain. When the sprout faces west — one should predict excessive rain.' //1009//

body.text:
417.023. kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ caivātra yadā luṅgottarāmukhī/
417.024. haritālasuvarṇābhā bhadraśocirivotthitā//1010//
body.translated_text: 'Safety and abundant harvests — when the sprout faces north, with the color of orpiment and gold, risen like an auspicious flame.' //1010//

body.text:
417.025. darbhasūcīmukhī cāpi dṛśyate yatra kutracit/
417.026. kvacinniṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ tatra nirdiśet//1011//
body.translated_text: 'And a <s>darbha</s>-needle-faced one is seen anywhere — crops are produced only in some places; one should predict famine there.' //1011//

body.text:
417.027. yadā nāgamukhī luṅgā dṛśyate yatra vā kvacit/
417.028. kvacinniṣpadyate śasyaṃ durbhikṣaṃ cātra nirdiśet/
417.029. tatrāśanibhayaṃ cāpi bhayaṃ meghānna saṃśayaḥ//1012//
body.translated_text: 'When a serpent-faced sprout is seen anywhere — crops are produced only in some places; one should predict famine there. And there is danger from lightning; danger from clouds without doubt.' //1012//

body.text:
417.030. kṛṣimūlamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram/
417.031. nāsti kṛṣisamāvṛttiḥ svayamuktaṃ svayambhuvā//1013//
body.translated_text: 'All this triple world of moving and stationary beings is rooted in agriculture. There is no livelihood equal to agriculture — this was declared by the Self-existent one himself.' //1013//

body.text:
418.001. <418>nākṛṣerdharmamāpnoti nākṛṣeḥ sukhamāpnuyāt/
418.002. dharmamarthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ sarvaṃ prāpnoti karṣakaḥ//1014//
body.translated_text: 'Without agriculture, one does not attain <s>Dharma</s>; without agriculture, one does not obtain happiness. <s>Dharma</s>, wealth, and pleasure alike — the farmer obtains all.' //1014//

body.text: 418.003. iti luṅgādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the Sprout Chapter.

body.text:
418.004. punarapi puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇastriśaṅkur mātaṅgādhipatimetadavocat--
418.005. kathaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nāgāśca kena vā vinivāritāḥ/
418.006. kuto mūlasamutthānaṃ nirghātaḥ kutra jāyate//1015//
body.translated_text: Then again the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s> said to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>: 'How are the <s>Nāgas</s> on the earth, and by whom are they restrained? From where does the earthquake originate? Where does the thunderbolt arise?' //1015//

body.text:
418.007. kutaścābhrāṇi jāyante nānāvarṇā diśo daśa/
418.008. kasyaiṣa mahataḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate dundubhisvaraḥ//1016//
body.translated_text: 'From where do clouds of various colors in the ten directions arise? Whose is this great sound heard, like the booming of a drum?' //1016//

body.text:
418.009. ko hi sṛjati durbhikṣaṃ subhikṣaṃ caiva prāṇinām/
418.010. kastatra sa muniśreṣṭho nāma gotraṃ bravīhi me//1017//
body.translated_text: 'Who indeed creates famine and also prosperity for living beings? Who is that best of sages? Tell me his name and lineage.' //1017//

body.text:
418.011. daivatāni ca me brūhi vidhānāni svayambhuvaḥ/
418.012. yajñaṃ ca yajñabhāgaṃ ca hotavyaśca yathā baliḥ//1018//
body.translated_text: 'Tell me the deities and the ordinances of the Self-Born One — the sacrifice and the shares of the sacrifice, and how the offering should be made.' //1018//

body.text:
418.013. pṛthivyāṃ daivataṃ brūhi āśrame daivataṃ brūhi/
418.014. deve tu daivataṃ brūhi kena devī sā kalpitā//1019//
body.translated_text: 'Tell me the deity of the earth; tell me the deity of the <s>āśrama</s> (hermitage). Tell me the deity of the sky; by whom was that goddess established?' //1019//

body.text:
418.015. pātrasya daivataṃ brūhi pūrṇakumbhasya daivatam/
418.016. karake daivataṃ brūhi tathā sthālyāṃ ca daivatam//1020//
body.translated_text: 'Tell me the deity of the vessel; the deity of the full water-pot. Tell me the deity of the water-jar; and likewise the deity of the cooking-pot.' //1020//

body.text:
418.017. śasyasya daivataṃ brūhi śasyapālasya daivatam/
418.018. vāyuskandhaiśca katibhiḥ śukro vegaṃ pramuñcati//1021//
body.translated_text: 'Tell me the deity of grain; the deity of the grain-protector. And by how many wind-masses does <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) release its speed?' //1021//

body.text:
418.019. atha triśaṅkurmātaṅgādhipatirbrāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇametadavocat--
418.020. pṛthvī vā vāyurākāśamāpo jyotiśca pañcamam/
418.021. tatra saṃvartate piṇḍaṃ tato meghaḥ pravartate//1022//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke thus to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>: 'Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth — therein the mass gathers, and from that the cloud arises.' //1022//

body.text:
418.022. eṣa vyāpnoti cākāśaṃ vāyunā janyate ghanaḥ/
418.023. ādityaraśmayo vāri samudrasya nabhastale//1023//
body.translated_text: 'It pervades the sky; the dense cloud is produced by wind. The rays of the sun draw water from the ocean to the sky.' //1023//

body.text:
418.024. tajjalaṃ nāgasaṃkṣiptaṃ tato varuṇasaṃkṣayaḥ/
418.025. vāyur nabho garjayate agnirvidyotate diśaḥ//1024//
body.translated_text: 'That water is collected by the <s>Nāgas</s>, and then by the dissolution of <s>Varuṇa</s>. The wind makes the sky thunder; fire illuminates the directions.' //1024//

body.text:
418.026. marutā kṣipyate piṇḍaṃ saṃnipātaśca garjate/
418.027. virodhanaṃ tu vāyośca agneśca anilasya ca//1025//
body.translated_text: 'The mass is hurled by the wind, and the concurrence thunders. There is a conflict of wind, fire, and air.' //1025//

body.text:
418.028. ākāśe vartate piṇḍaṃ paścātpatati medinīm/
418.029. yad grahāṇāmadhipatir nakṣatrajyotiṣāmapi/
418.030. tato mārutasaṃsargātparjanyamapi varṣṣati//1026//
body.translated_text: 'The mass revolves in the sky and afterward falls upon the earth. He who is the lord of the planets and of the stars and luminaries — then by contact with the wind, the rain-cloud also rains.' //1026//

body.text:
418.031. varṣate śailaśikhare yatra saṃprasthito janaḥ/
418.032. yatra satyaṃ ca dharmaśca havirmeghaśca vartate//1027//
body.translated_text: 'It rains on mountain peaks where people have set forth, where truth and <s>Dharma</s>, oblation and clouds prevail.' //1027//

body.text:
419.001. <419>tatra bījāni rohanti annapānaṃ samṛdhyati/
419.002. evaṃ piṇḍāśanirādyā tato vātāśanī smṛtā/
419.003. dantāśanī tṛtīyā tu aśanistu caturthikā//1028//
body.translated_text: 'There seeds sprout and food and drink flourish. Thus the first is the mass-thunderbolt; then the wind-thunderbolt is recorded; the tooth-thunderbolt is the third, and the thunderbolt proper is the fourth.' //1028//

body.text:
419.004. pañcamī krimayaḥ proktāḥ ṣaṣṭhī tu śalabhāstathā/
419.005. saptamī syādanāvṛṣṭirativṛṣṭistastathāṣṭamī//1029//
body.translated_text: 'The fifth is said to be worms; the sixth is locusts likewise. The seventh would be drought; the eighth is excessive rain.' //1029//

body.text:
419.006. navamī saṃbaraḥ proktā ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ/
419.007. etāstvaśanyo vyākhyātāstāsāṃ vai devatāḥ śṛṇu/
419.008. piṇḍāśanī brahmasṛṣṭā eṣā jyeṣṭhādyadevatā//1030//
body.translated_text: 'The ninth is said to be plague,' thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>. 'These thunderbolts have been explained; now hear their deities. The mass-thunderbolt was created by <s>Brahmā</s>; this is the foremost deity.' //1030//

body.text:
419.009. dantāśanī tu sainyānāṃ grahā vātāśanī smṛtā/
419.010. adeśa.......................ḍevatāḥ//1031//
body.translated_text: 'The tooth-thunderbolt belongs to armies; the planets are the wind-thunderbolt. The deities of the placeless... [text damaged].' //1031//

body.text:
419.011. śalabhāḥ ketudaivatyā ādityā ditidevatāḥ/
419.012. śaṃsakāmativarṣasya anāvṛṣṭestu jyoti{ṣah}//1032//
body.translated_text: 'Locusts have <s>Ketu</s> as their deity; the <s>Ādityas</s> have <s>Diti</s> as deity. The indicator of excessive rain; the luminaries are the deity of drought.' //1032//

body.text:
419.013. {samba}rasya tu parjanyamākhyātā nava devatāḥ/
419.013. aśanyā devatāḥ proktā ākāśagamanārthaṃ bodhata/
419.015. pūrvamadhīndradaivatyaṃ dakṣiṇe yamadaivatam/
419.016. varuṇaṃ paścime vidyāduttare dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ/
419.017. ..ṭyā daivataṃ viṣṇurāśramaṃ viśvadaivatam//1033//
body.translated_text: '<s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god) is declared as the deity of plague — thus the nine deities. The deities of the thunderbolts have been proclaimed. For the purpose of traversing the sky, understand: In the east, <s>Indra</s> is the presiding deity; in the south, <s>Yama</s> is the deity; <s>Varuṇa</s> should be known in the west; in the north, <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) is recorded. <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the deity of...; the <s>āśrama</s> has the All-Gods as deity.' //1033//

body.text:
419.018. samidhādaivatā devāstebhyo devī prakalpitā/
419.019. samidhādaivatā...........ṭognihutāśanam//1034//
body.translated_text: 'The gods are the deities of the sacrificial fuel-sticks; the goddess was established from them. The deities of the sacrificial fuel-sticks... fire, the eater of oblations.' //1034//

body.text:
419.020. vedyāṃ tu daivatam ............kārādityadaivatam/
419.021. pātrasya devatā dharmaḥ pūrṇakumbhe janārdanaḥ//1035//
body.translated_text: 'On the altar, the deity is... the sun as deity. <s>Dharma</s> is the deity of the vessel; <s>Janārdana</s> (Viṣṇu) is the deity of the full water-pot.' //1035//

body.text:
419.022. caruṃ ceti.....ḍhūpasthānasya jyotiṣaḥ/
419.023. śasya......śasyapālo mahāmatiḥ/
419.024. vāyuskandhaiścaturbhistu śukro vegaṃ pramuñcati//1036//
body.translated_text: 'The oblation-offering and... the place of incense has the luminaries as deity. Grain... the grain-protector of great wisdom. And by four wind-masses, <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) releases its speed.' //1036//

body.text:
419.025. atra madhye pṛthivyāpa āśramo viśvadaivataḥ/
419.026. tasmin deśe......yasmin prīto vṛṣadhvajaḥ//1037//
body.translated_text: 'In the midst here, the earth and water; the <s>āśrama</s> has the All-Gods as deity. In that region... in which the Bull-Bannered One (<s>Śiva</s>) is pleased.' //1037//

body.text:
419.027. ityāha bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuḥ/
419.027. punarapi puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇastriśaṅkumevamāha--
419.028. kimarthamāśrame nityaṃ hūyate havyavāhanaḥ/
419.029. tṛṇakāṣṭhāni saṃhṛtya meghaṃ dṛṣṭvā samutthitam//1038//
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s>. Again, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> spoke thus to <s>Triśaṅku</s>: 'For what purpose is the fire-bearer always offered oblations in the <s>āśrama</s>? Having gathered grass and wood, seeing a cloud that has risen —' //1038//

body.text:
419.030. ati.....ṇyate agniṃ sudāruṇam/
419.031. sarvalokahitārthāya dhyātvā divyeta cakṣuṣā/
419.032. praśamecca samāsena tadbhavārthaṃ tu ......//1039//
body.translated_text: '... [text damaged] the terrible fire is kindled. For the benefit of all the world, having meditated, one should proceed with the divine eye, and pacify in brief — for the purpose of that existence...' //1039//

body.text:
420.001. <420>evamukte triśaṅkurmātaṅgādhipatirbrāhmaṇaṃ puṣkarasāriṇametadavocat--
420.002. dhūmikādhyāyaḥ/
420.003. purā hi khāṇḍavadvīpamarjunena mahātmanā/
420.004. .........jvalitaṃ jātavedasā//1040//
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the lord of the <s>Mātaṅgas</s>, spoke this to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>: 'The Smoke Chapter. Formerly indeed, the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest was... by the great-souled <s>Arjuna</s>, blazing with <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire).' //1040//

body.text:
420.005. .........prasannamānānnidhigatam/
420.006. tatra dagdhā anekā hi nāgāḥ koṭisahasraśaḥ//1041//
body.translated_text: '... with pleased minds... obtained as treasure. There many <s>Nāgas</s> were burned — thousands of <s>koṭis</s>.' //1041//

body.text:
420.007. purā mahoragagaṇā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ/
420.008. pādahīnāḥ kṛtāḥ kecid bāhuhīnāḥ kṛtāpare//1042//
body.translated_text: 'Formerly the great serpent-hosts, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and serpent-beings — some were made footless; others were made armless.' //1042//

body.text:
420.009. vaikalyaṃ karṇanāsābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ caivākṣipātanam/
420.010. tadāprabhṛti bhūtānāṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vai trāsitaṃ manaḥ//1043//
body.translated_text: 'Mutilation of ears and noses was done, and also the gouging out of eyes. From that time forth, the minds of beings were seen to be terrified.' //1043//

body.text:
420.011. agninā tāpitāḥ kecidbāṇairanye ca sūditāḥ/
420.012. vācāṭakenāpi purā kādraveyāḥ prapātitāḥ//1044//
body.translated_text: 'Some were burned by fire; others were slain by arrows. Formerly, even by the clever one, the sons of <s>Kadrū</s> (serpents) were brought down.' //1044//

body.text:
420.013. arciṣā havigandhena muhyamānā nabhontare/
420.014. tadvihīnāḥ patantyanye guhyakā dharaṇītale//1045//
body.translated_text: 'Bewildered by the flame and the smell of oblation in the midst of the sky — bereft of that, other <s>Guhyakas</s> (hidden beings) fall upon the surface of the earth.' //1045//

body.text:
420.015. sahāmpatistu nāṃnā sa śasyakāle tadāśrame/
420.016. śasyapālaistu satataṃ hotavyo havyavāhanaḥ//1046//
body.translated_text: 'One named <s>Sahāmpati</s>, in that <s>āśrama</s> during the crop season — by the grain-protectors, the fire-bearer should always be offered oblations.' //1046//

body.text:
420.017. gṛhamedhī jvālayedagniṃ nirmale 'pi nabhontare/
420.018. digbhāgeṣu ca bhūtānāṃ teṣāmarthaṃ dine dine//1047//
body.translated_text: 'A householder should kindle fire even when the sky is clear, in the directions of the quarters for the sake of those beings, day after day.' //1047//

body.text:
420.019. jāgrataṃ satataṃ vahnimāśramastho 'pi dhārayet/
420.020. meghaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśeṣeṇa jvālitavyo hutāśanaḥ//1048//
body.translated_text: 'One dwelling in the <s>āśrama</s> should always keep the fire awake and maintain it. Seeing a cloud especially, the sacrificial fire should be kindled.' //1048//

body.text:
420.021. sadhūmaṃ jvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānaṃ tu pāvakam/
420.022. bhayamāpatate teṣāṃ nāgasainyaṃ vimuhyate//1049//
body.translated_text: 'Seeing the fire blazing with smoke and shining — fear falls upon them, and the army of <s>Nāgas</s> is bewildered.' //1049//

body.text:
420.023. agniṃ paricarato 'sya śasyapālasya cāśrame/
420.024. agninā hūyamānena sidhyate sarvakarma ca//1050//
body.translated_text: 'For one who tends the fire in the <s>āśrama</s> of the grain-protector — by the fire being offered oblations, all work is accomplished.' //1050//

body.text: 420.025. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasārin dhūmikādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the Smoke Chapter.'

body.text:
420.026. atha khalu bhoḥ puṣkarasāriṃs tithikarmanirdeśaṃ nāmādhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi/
420.026. tacchrūyatām/
420.027. atha kim/
420.027. kathayatu bhagavāṃstriśaṅkuh--
420.028. tithikarmanirdeśaḥ/
420.029. nandāṃ pratipadāmāhuḥ praśastāṃ sarvakarmasu/
420.030. vijñānasya samārambhe pravāse ca vigarhitā//1051//
body.translated_text: 'Now then, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, I shall expound the chapter called \"Instruction on Lunar-Day Activities.\" Let it be heard.' 'What then?' 'Let the lord <s>Triśaṅku</s> speak.' 'Instruction on Lunar-Day Activities: The first <s>tithi</s> (lunar day) is called <s>Nandā</s> (Joyful) — it is praised for all activities, but condemned for the commencement of learning and for travel.' //1051//

body.text:
420.031. dvitīyā kathitā bhadrā śastā bhūṣaṇakarmasu/
420.032. jayā tṛtīyā vyākhyātā praśastā jayakarmasu//1052//
body.translated_text: 'The second is called <s>Bhadrā</s> (Auspicious) — praised for adornment-work. The third is declared <s>Jayā</s> (Victorious) — praised for activities of conquest.' //1052//

body.text:
421.001. <421>caturthī kathitā riktā grāmasainyavadhe hitā/
421.002. cauryābhicārakūṭāgnidāhagorasasādhane//1053//
body.translated_text: 'The fourth is called <s>Riktā</s> (Empty) — suitable for the destruction of villages and armies, for theft, sorcery, treachery, arson, and the preparation of poisons.' //1053//

body.text:
421.003. pūrṇā tu pañcamī jñeyā cikitsāgamanādhvasu/
421.004. dānādhyayanaśilpeṣu vyāyāme ca praśasyate//1054//
body.translated_text: 'The fifth should be known as <s>Pūrṇā</s> (Full) — praised for medical treatment, travel, roads, giving, study, crafts, and exercise.' //1054//

body.text:
421.005. jayeti saṃjñitā ṣaṣṭhī garhitādhvasu śasyate/
421.006. gṛhe kṣetre vivāhe vā āvāhakarmasu mitreti//1055//
body.translated_text: 'The sixth is designated <s>Jayā</s> (Victorious) — condemned for roads but praised for houses, fields, marriage, and invitation ceremonies — it is called <s>Mitrā</s> (Friendly).' //1055//

body.text:
421.007. bhadrā ca saptamī khyātā śreṣṭhā sā saukṛte 'dhvani/
421.008. nṛpāṇāṃ śāsane chatre śayyānāṃ karaṇeṣu ca//1056//
body.translated_text: 'The seventh is known as <s>Bhadrā</s> (Auspicious) — best for good deeds and roads, for the governance and parasols of kings, and for the making of beds.' //1056//

body.text:
421.009. mahābalāṣṭamī sā ca prayojyā parirakṣaṇe/
421.010. bhayamandarabaddheṣu yogeṣu haraṇeṣu ca//1057//
body.translated_text: 'The eighth is <s>Mahābalā</s> (Greatly Powerful) — to be employed for protection, in matters of fear, resistance, and bondage, in unions and abductions.' //1057//

body.text:
421.011. ugrasenā tu navamī tasyāṃ kuryādripukṣayam/
421.012. tathā viṣadhnāvaskandavidyābandhavadhakriyāḥ//1058//
body.translated_text: 'The ninth is <s>Ugrasenā</s> (Fiercely Armed) — under it one should bring about the destruction of enemies, and likewise poisoning, assault, magical arts, bondage, and execution.' //1058//

body.text:
421.013. sudharmā daśamī śastā śāstrārambhe dhanodyate/
421.014. śāntisvastyayanārambhe dānayajñodyateṣu ca//1059//
body.translated_text: 'The tenth, <s>Sudharmā</s> (Well-Righteous), is praised for the commencement of <s>śāstras</s> (sciences) and undertaking of wealth, for the commencement of pacification and benediction rites, and for undertaking giving and sacrifice.' //1059//

body.text:
421.015. ekādaśī punarmānyā strīṣu ca māṃsamadyayoḥ/
421.016. kārayennagaraṃ guptaṃ vivāhaṃ śāstrakarma ca//1060//
body.translated_text: 'The eleventh is again honored — in matters of women, meat, and liquor. One should build a fortified city, perform a marriage, and carry out work according to the <s>śāstras</s>.' //1060//

body.text:
421.017. yaśeti dvādaśīmāhurvaire 'dhvani ca garhitā/
421.018. vivāhe ca girau kṣetre gṛhakarmasu pūjitā//1061//
body.translated_text: 'The twelfth is called <s>Yaśā</s> (Glorious) — condemned for enmity and roads, but honored for marriage, in the mountains, in fields, and in house-works.' //1061//

body.text:
421.019. jayā trayodaśī sādhvī maṇḍaleṣu ca yoṣitām/
421.020. kanyāvaraṇavāṇijyavivāhādiṣu ceṣyate//1062//
body.translated_text: 'The thirteenth is <s>Jayā</s> (Victorious) and virtuous — for women's circles, choosing a maiden, trade, marriage, and the like — it is favored.' //1062//

body.text:
421.021. ugrā caturdaśī tu syātkārayedabhicārikam/
421.022. vadhabandhaprayogāṃśca pūrvaṃ ca praharedapi//1063//
body.translated_text: 'The fourteenth is <s>Ugrā</s> (Fierce) — one should perform sorcery, employ acts of killing, bondage, and assault, and strike first.' //1063//

body.text:
421.023. siddhā pañcadaśī sādhvī devatāgnividhau hitā/
421.024. gosaṃgrahavṛṣotsargabalijapyavrateṣu ca//1064//
body.translated_text: 'The fifteenth is <s>Siddhā</s> (Accomplished) and virtuous — suitable for worship of deities and fire, for the collection of cattle, release of bulls, offerings, <s>japa</s> (recitation), and vows.' //1064//

body.text:
421.025. nandādīnāṃ kriyā pūrve ṣaṣṭhyādīnāṃ tu madhyame/
421.026. sunandāyāśca saṃdhyābhirdinarātryoḥ prasidhyati//1065//
body.translated_text: 'The activities of <s>Nandā</s> and the rest succeed in the first watch; those of <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s> and the rest in the middle watch; and those of <s>Sunandā</s> succeed at the twilight junctures of day and night.' //1065//

body.text: 421.027. ayaṃ bhoḥ puṣkarasāriṃs tithikarmanirdeśo nāmādhyāyaḥ//
body.translated_text: 'This, O <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, is the chapter called \"Instruction on Lunar-Day Activities.\"'

body.text: 421.028. api ca mahābrāhmaṇa idaṃ pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkriyāyāṃ vidyāyāṃ cittamabhinirṇayāmi nivartayāmi, anekavidhapūrvanivāsaṃ samanusmarāmi//
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, I bring my mind to bear upon, and turn it toward, that knowledge and direct realization of the recollection of former lives — I recall my manifold former existences.'

body.text:
421.030. syātte brāhmaṇa kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmā devānāṃ pravaro 'bhūt/
421.031. nahyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
421.031. ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena brahmā devānāṃ pravaro 'bhūvam/
421.032. so 'haṃ tataścyutaḥ samāna indraḥ kauśiko 'bhūvam/
421.032. tataścyutaḥ samāno 'raṇemirgautamo 'bhūvam<422>/
body.translated_text: 'You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: \"Another was he who at that time, in that era, was <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost of the gods.\" It should not be seen thus. I myself at that time, in that era, was <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost of the gods. Having fallen from that state, I became <s>Indra</s> <s>Kauśika</s>. Having fallen from that state, I became <s>Araṇemi</s> <s>Gautama</s>.'

body.text:
422.001. tataścyutaḥ samānaḥ śvetaketur nāma maharṣirabhūvam/
422.001. tataścyutaḥ samānaḥ śukapaṇḍito 'bhūvam/
422.002. mayā te tadā brāhmaṇa catvāro vedā vibhaktāḥ/
422.002. tadyathā puṣyo bahvṛcānāṃ paṅktiśchandogānām/
422.003. ekaviṃśaticaraṇā adhvaryavaḥ/
422.003. kraturatharvaṇikānām//
body.translated_text: 'Having fallen from that state, I became the great sage named <s>Śvetaketu</s>. Having fallen from that state, I became the scholar <s>Śuka</s>. At that time, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the four <s>Vedas</s> were divided by me — namely: <s>Puṣya</s> for the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (Ṛg-Vedins), <s>Paṅkti</s> for the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāma-Vedins), twenty-one branches for the <s>Adhvaryus</s> (Yajur-Vedins), and <s>Kratu</s> for the <s>Ātharvaṇikas</s> (Atharva-Vedins).'

body.text:
422.004. syāttava brāhmaṇa kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena vasur nāma maharṣirabhūt/
422.005. na hyevaṃ draṣṭavyam/
422.005. ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena vasur nāma maharṣirabhūvam/
422.006. mayā sā takṣakavadhūkāyāḥ kapilā nāma māṇavikā duhitā āsāditā bhāryārthāya/
422.007. so 'haṃ tatra saṃraktacitta ṛddhyā bhraṣṭo dhyānebhyo vañcitaḥ parihīnaḥ/
422.007. so 'hamātmānaṃ jugupsamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāṃ babhāṣe--oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ/
422.008. tatsavituvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi/
422.009. dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt//
body.translated_text: 'You might have doubt or uncertainty, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: \"Another was he who at that time, in that era, was the great sage named <s>Vasu</s>.\" It should not be seen thus. I myself at that time, in that era, was the great sage named <s>Vasu</s>. By me, the maiden named <s>Kapilā</s>, the daughter of the <s>Takṣaka</s>-serpent's bride, was taken as a wife. With my mind infatuated there, I fell from my supernatural power, was cheated out of my <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and declined. Reproaching myself, at that moment I uttered this verse: <s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s> — \"Let us meditate upon that excellent glory of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>; may he inspire our thoughts.\"'

body.text:
422.010. so 'haṃ brāhmaṇa tvāṃ bravīmi--sāmānyasaṃjñāmātrakamidaṃ lokasya brāhmaṇa iti vā kṣatriya iti vā vaiśya iti vā śūdra iti vā/
422.011. ekamevedaṃ sarvaṃ sarvamidamekam/
422.011. putrāya me śārdūlakarṇāya prakṛtiṃ duhitaramanuprayaccha bhāryārthāya/
422.012. yāvatakaṃ kulaśulkaṃ manyase tāvatakamanupradāsyāmi/
422.013. idaṃ ca vacanaṃ punaḥ śrutvā triśaṅkormātaṅgarājasya brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī idamavocat--
422.014. bhagavāñ śrotriyaḥ śreṣṭhastvatto bhūyānna vidyate/
422.015. sadevakeṣu lokeṣu mahābrahmasamo bhavān//1066//
body.translated_text:
422.010. 'Therefore I say to you, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — this designation in the world is merely a common label: "<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>" or "<s>Kṣatriya</s>" or "<s>Vaiśya</s>" or "<s>Śūdra</s>."
422.011. All this is one; all this is the same.
422.011. Give your daughter <s>Prakṛti</s> to my son <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> as a wife.
422.012. Whatever bride-price you think fitting, I shall pay.'
422.013. Having heard these words again from <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said:
422.014. 'You, blessed one, are the foremost Vedic scholar — none greater than you exists.
422.015. In the worlds with their gods, you are equal to the great <s>Brahmā</s>.' //1066//

body.text:
422.016. putrāya te bhoḥ prakṛtiṃ dadāmi śīlena rūpeṇa guṇairupetaḥ/
422.018. śārdūlakarṇaḥ prakṛtistu bhadrā ubhau rametāṃ rucitaṃ mamedam//1067//
body.translated_text:
422.016. 'To your son I give <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed with virtue, beauty, and qualities.
422.018. <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> and the noble <s>Prakṛti</s> — may both delight; this pleases me.' //1067//

body.text:
422.020. tatra tāni pañcamātrāṇi māṇavakaśatāni uccaiḥśabdāni procurmahāśabdāni--mā tvaṃ bho upādhyāya vidyamāneṣu brāhmaṇeṣu cāṇḍālena sārdhaṃ saṃbandhaṃ rocaya/
422.021. nārhasi bho upādhyāya vidyamāneṣu brāhmaṇeṣu cāṇḍālena sārdhaṃ saṃbandhaṃ kartum//
body.translated_text:
422.020. Then those five hundred young students cried out loudly with great voices: 'O teacher, do not favor an alliance with a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are available!
422.021. It is not fitting, O teacher, to make an alliance with a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> while <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are available!'

body.text:
422.023. atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī teṣāṃ nidānaṃ nidāya śabdaṃ saṃsthāpya nipatya ślokenaitānarthānabhāṣata--
422.025. evametadyathā hyeṣa triśaṅkurbhāṣate giram/
422.026. tattvaṃ hyavitathaṃ bhūtaṃ satyaṃ nityaṃ tathā dhruvam//1068//

422.027. atha brāhmaṇaḥ puṣkarasārī teṣāṃ māṇavakānāṃ taṃ mahāntaṃ śabdaṃ saṃsthāpya triśaṅkuṃ mātaṅgarājamidamavocat--ayaṃ bhostriśaṅko brahmaṇā sahāpatinā cātrumahābhaitiko mahāpuruṣaḥ prajñaptaḥ/
422.029. yasya
422.030. śiraḥ satāraṃ gaganamākāśamudaraṃ tathā/
422.031. parvatāścāpyubhāvūrū pādau ca dharaṇītalam//1069//
body.translated_text:
422.027. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, having silenced the great outcry of those students, said to <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king: 'This great being, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, was designated by <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Sahāpati</s> as the <s>Cāturmahābhautika</s> (one composed of four great elements), the <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s> (Great Being).
422.029. Whose:
422.030. Head is the sky with stars; space is his belly;
422.031. the mountains are his two thighs; and his feet are the surface of the earth.' //1069//

body.text:
423.001. <423>sūryācandramasau netre roma tṛṇavanaspatī/
423.002. sāgarāścāpyamedhyaṃ vai nadyo mūtrasravo 'sya tu//1070//
body.translated_text:
423.001. 'The sun and moon are his eyes; grass and trees are his body-hair;
423.002. the oceans are his excrement; and the rivers are his flow of urine.' //1070//

body.text:
423.003. aśrūṇi varṣaṇaṃ cāsya eṣa brahmā sahāpatiḥ/
423.004. bhavāṃstu paramajño 'si tanme brūhi yathā tathā//1071//
body.translated_text:
423.003. 'His tears are the rain — this is <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>.
423.004. You are supreme in knowledge — tell me the truth of this.' //1071//

body.text:
423.005. iha bhostriśaṅko kimāha svalakṣaṇaṃ brahmaṇaḥ pratyavekṣasva/
423.005. pitrā ca mātrā ca kṛtāni karmāṇi bhavanti/
423.006. aśvastanāstena vañcitāḥ/
423.007. gacchanti sattvā bahugarbhayoniṃ na caiva kaścinmanujo hyayoniḥ/
423.009. samastajātau pracaranti sattvā na mārutājjāyate kaścideva//1072//
body.translated_text:
423.005. 'Here, O <s>Triśaṅku</s>, examine the characteristic nature of <s>Brahmā</s>.
423.005. The deeds done by father and mother exist.
423.006. Those who are impermanent are deceived.
423.007. Beings go to many a womb-birth, and no human is without birth.
423.009. Beings of all births move about — no one is born from the wind alone.' //1072//

body.text:
423.010. svabhāvabhāvyaṃ hyavagaccha loke ke brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ/
423.013. sarvatra kāṇāḥ kuṇinaśca khañjāḥ kuṣṭhī kilāsī hyapasmāriṇo 'pi//1073//
body.translated_text:
423.010. 'Understand the nature of things as they naturally are in the world — who are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>?
423.013. Everywhere there are the one-eyed, the crippled, the lame, lepers, those with white-spot disease, and epileptics.' //1073//

body.text:
423.015. kṛṣṇāśca gaurāśca tathaiva śyāmāḥ sattvāḥ prajā hyanyatame viśiṣṭāḥ/
423.017. sahāsthicarmāḥ sanakhāḥ samāṃsā duḥkhī sukhī mūtrapurīṣayuktāḥ/
423.019. na cendriyāṇāṃ praviviktirasti tasmānna varṇāścaturo bhavanti//1074//

423.021. mantrairhi yadi labhyeta svargaṃ tu gamanaṃ dvijaḥ/
423.022. kṛṣṇaśuklāni karmāṇi bhaveyur niṣphalāni hi//1075//
body.translated_text:
423.021. 'If heaven could be attained by mantras alone, the twice-born would find
423.022. that dark and bright deeds would be without fruit.' //1075//

body.text:
423.023. yasmātkṛṣṇāni śuklāni karmāṇi saphalāni hi/
423.024. pacyamānāni dṛśyante gatiṣvetāni pañcasu//1076//
body.translated_text:
423.023. 'Since dark and bright deeds do bear fruit,
423.024. and are seen ripening in the five destinies —' //1076//

body.text:
423.025. māṇavakaśateṣu sa tatra vinihato mahāyaśasā triśaṅkunā puṣkarasārī brāhmaṇo 'bravīt--brāhmaṇo 'sau mātaṅgarājo hi triśaṅkur nāma/
423.026. bhavān hi brahmā indraśca kauśikaḥ/
423.026. tvamaraṇemiśca gautamaḥ/
423.027. tvaṃ śvetaketuśca śukapaṇḍitaḥ/
423.027. vedaḥ samākhyātastvayā caturdhā/
423.027. bhagavānvasū rājarṣirmahāyaśā bhagavān/
423.029. jñānena hi tvaṃ parameṇa yuktaḥ sarveṣu śāstreṣu bhavān kṛtārthaḥ/
body.translated_text:
423.025. Defeated in the presence of those hundreds of students by the greatly renowned <s>Triśaṅku</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> said: 'That <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s> is indeed a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
423.026. You are <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Indra Kauśika</s>.
423.026. You are <s>Araṇemi-Gautama</s>.
423.027. You are <s>Śvetaketu</s> and the wise <s>Śuka</s>.
423.027. The four <s>Vedas</s> were proclaimed by you.
423.027. You are the blessed <s>Vasu</s>, the royal sage of great renown.
423.029. You are endowed with the supreme knowledge and accomplished in all the sciences.

body.text: 424.001. <424>śreṣṭho viśiṣṭo paramo 'si loke bhavān hi vidyācaraṇena yuktaḥ//1077//
body.translated_text: 424.001. You are the best, the most distinguished, the highest in the world; you are endowed with knowledge and conduct.' //1077//

body.text:
424.003. dadāmi te 'haṃ prakṛtiṃ mamāmalāṃ śīlena rūpeṇa guṇairupetaḥ/
424.005. śārdūlakarṇaḥ prakṛtiśca bhadrā ubhau rametāṃ rucitaṃ mamedam//1078//
body.translated_text:
424.003. 'I give you my pure <s>Prakṛti</s>, endowed with virtue, beauty, and qualities.
424.005. <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> and the noble <s>Prakṛti</s> — may both delight; this pleases me.' //1078//

body.text:
424.007. pragṛhya bhṛṅgāramudakaprapūrṇamāvarjito brāhmaṇo hṛṣṭacittaḥ/
424.008. anupradāsīdudakena kanyakāṃ śārdūlakarṇasya iyamastu bhāryā//1079//
body.translated_text:
424.007. 'Taking a water-vessel filled with water, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, with joyful mind, inclined,
424.008. poured the water and gave the maiden — "May this be the wife of <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>."' //1079//

body.text:
424.011. udagracitta āsīnmātaṅgarājaḥ/
424.012. kṛtvā niveśaṃ sa tadātmajasya gatvāśrame 'sau nagaram yaśasvī/
424.014. dharmeṇa vai kārayati svarājyaṃ kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca sadotsavāḍhyam//1080// iti/
424.016. syād bhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena triśaṅkur nāma mātaṅgarājo 'bhūt? naivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
424.017. ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena triśaṅkur nāma mātaṅgarājo 'bhūvam/
424.018. syādevaṃ ca bhikṣavo yuṣmākam--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena śādūlakarṇo nāma mātaṅgarājakumāro 'bhūt/
424.019. naivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
424.019. eṣa sa ānando bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena śārdūlakarṇo nāma mātaṅgarājakumāro 'bhūt/
424.021. syādevam yuṣmākam--anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇo 'bhūt/
424.021. naivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
424.022. eṣa śāradvatīputro bhikṣuḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasārī nāma brāhmaṇo 'bhūt/
424.023. nānyā sā tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitābhūt/
424.024. naivaṃ draṣṭavyam/
424.024. eṣā sā prakṛtirbhikṣuṇī tena kālena tena samayena puṣkarasāriṇo brāhmaṇasya prakṛtir nāma māṇavikā duhitābhūt/
424.025. sā etarhi tenaiva snehena tenaiva premṇā ānandaṃ bhikṣuṃ gacchantamanugacchati tiṣṭhantamanutiṣṭhati/
424.026. yadyadeva kulaṃ piṇḍāya praviśati, tatra tatraiva dvāre tūṣṇīmbhūtā asthāt//
body.translated_text:
424.011. The <s>Mātaṅga</s> king was elated in mind.
424.012. Having made the dwelling for his son, the renowned one went to his city from the hermitage.
424.014. He governed his kingdom righteously — secure, prosperous, and always rich in festivals.' //1080//
424.016. 'Perhaps, O monks, you have doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity, thinking: "That <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s> at that time was someone else." It should not be seen thus.
424.017. I myself at that time was the <s>Mātaṅga</s> king named <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
424.018. And perhaps you monks think: "That <s>Mātaṅga</s> prince named <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s> at that time was someone else."
424.019. It should not be seen thus.
424.019. This monk <s>Ānanda</s> was at that time the <s>Mātaṅga</s> prince named <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>.
424.021. Perhaps you think: "That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s> at that time was someone else."
424.021. It should not be seen thus.
424.022. This monk, the son of <s>Śāradvatī</s>, was at that time the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>.
424.023. "That maiden <s>Prakṛti</s>, the daughter of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>, at that time was someone else."
424.024. It should not be seen thus.
424.024. This nun <s>Prakṛti</s> was at that time the maiden named <s>Prakṛti</s>, the daughter of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasārin</s>.
424.025. Even now, with that very affection, with that very love, she follows the monk <s>Ānanda</s> when he goes, and stands when he stands.
424.026. Whatever household he enters for alms, there at the door she stood in silence.'

body.text:
424.028. atha khalu bhagavānetasminnidāne etasmin prakaraṇe tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata--
424.029. parvakeṇa nivāsena pratyutpannena tena ca/
424.030. etena jāyate prema candrasya kumude yathā//1081//
body.translated_text:
424.028. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, at that time, spoke this verse:
424.029. 'By former dwelling together and by this present one,
424.030. love arises, as it does in the water-lily for the moon.' //1081//

body.text:
425.001. <425>tasmāttarhi bhikṣavo 'nabhisamitānāṃ caturṇāmāryasatyānāmabhisamayāya, adhimātraṃ vīryaṃ tīvracchando vīryaṃ śabdāpayāmi/
425.002. utsāha unnatiraprativāṇiḥ/
425.002. smṛtyā saṃprajanyena apramādato yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
425.003. drutameṣāṃ caturṇāṃ duḥkhasyāryasatyasya duḥkhasamudayasya nirodhasya nirodhagāminyāḥ pratipada āryasatyasya amīṣāṃ caturṇāmāryasatyānāmanabhisamitānāmabhisamayāya adhimātraṃ tīvracchando vīryaṃ vyāyāma utsāha unnatiraprativāṇiḥ smṛtyā saṃprajanyenāpramādato yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ//

425.007. asmiṃśca khalu punardharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe bhikṣūṇāṃ ṣaṣṭimātrāṇāmanupādāya āsravebhyaścittāani vimuktāni/
425.008. saṃbahulānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ brahmaṇāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ ca virajaskaṃ vigatamalaṃ dharmacakṣurudapādi viśuddham//
body.translated_text:
425.007. And while this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, the minds of sixty monks were liberated from the defilements without clinging.
425.008. And for a great number of disciples, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders, the eye of <s>Dharma</s> arose — dustless, free from stain, pure.

body.text:
425.010. idamavocadbhagavān/
425.010. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
425.010. Thus spoke the Blessed One.
425.010. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 425.011. iti śrīdivyāvadāne śārdūlakarṇāvadānam//
body.translated_text: 425.011. Thus, in the sacred <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Śārdūlakarṇa</s>) is concluded.

body.text: 426.001. div34 dānādhikaraṇamahāyānasūtram/
body.translated_text: 426.001. Chapter 34: The <s>Dānādhikaraṇamahāyānasūtra</s> (The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Grounds of Giving).

body.text:
426.001. evaṃ mayā śrutam/
426.002. ekasmin samaye bhagavāñchrāvastyāṃ viahrati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham/
426.003. tatra {bhagavān} bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--saptagtriṃśatā bhikṣava ākāraiḥ paṇḍito dānaṃ dadāti/
426.004. kāle dānaṃ dadāti tathāgatānujñātam/
426.005. kalpitaṃ dānaṃ dadāti trivastupariśuddham/
426.005. satkutya dānaṃ dadāti sarvadoṣavikṣepavigamārtham/
426.006. svahastena dānaṃ dadātyasārātkāyātsārasaṃgrahārtham/
426.006. skandhaṃ dānaṃ dadāti mahātyāgabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.007. varṇasampannaṃ dānaṃ dadāti prāsādikavipākapratisaṃvartanīyam/
426.007. gandhasampannaṃ dānaṃ dadāti gandhavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.008. rasasampannaṃ dānaṃ dadāti rasarasāgravyañjanavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.009. praṇītaṃ dānaṃ dadāti praṇītabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.010. vipulaṃ dānaṃ dadāti vipulabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.010. annadānaṃ dadāti kṣuttarṣavicchedavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.011. pānadānaṃ dadāti sarvatra jātiṣu tṛḍvicchedavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.012. vastradānaṃ dadāti praṇītavastrabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.012. pratiśrayaṃ dānaṃ dadāti harmyakūṭāgāraprāsādabhavanavimānodyānārāmaviśeṣavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.014. śayyādānaṃ dadātyuccakulabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.014. yānaṃ dānaṃ dadāti ṛddhipādavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.015. bhaiṣajyadānaṃ dadāti ajarāmaraṇaviśokasaṃkliṣṭanirodhanivāṇavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.016. dharmadānaṃ dadāti jātismarapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.016. puṣpadānaṃ dadāti bodhyaṅgapuṣpavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.017. mālyadānaṃ dadāti rāgadveṣamohaviśuddhavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.018. gandhadānaṃ dadāti divyagandhasukhopapattivipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.019. dhūpadānaṃ dadāti saṃkleśadaurgandhaprahāṇavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.019. chatradānaṃ dadāti dharmaiśvaryādhipatyavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.020. ghaṇṭādānaṃ dadāti manojñasvaravipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.021. vādyadānaṃ dadāti brahmasvaranirghoṣavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.021. paṭṭadānaṃ dadāti devamanuṣyābhiṣekapaṭṭabandhavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.022. tathāagatacaityeṣu tathāgatabimbeṣu ca sugandhodakasnānaṃ dānaṃ dadāti dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāśītyanuvyañjanavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.023. sūtradānaṃ dadāti sarvatra jātiṣūtpasyatā grāhyakuleṣūpapadya samantaprāsādikavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.025. pañcasāradānaṃ dadāti sarvatra jātiṣu mahābalavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.025. maitryātmakadānaṃ dadāti vyāpādaprahāṇavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.026. karuṇāśritadānaṃ dadāti mahāsukhavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.027. muditāśritadānaṃ dadāti sarvathā muditānandavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.028. upekṣāśritaṃ dānaṃ dadāti aratiprahāṇavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.028. vicitropacitraṃ dānaṃ dadāti nānābahuvidhavicitropabhogavipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.029. sarvārthaparityāgaṃ dānaṃ dadāti anuttarasamyaksambodhivipākapratilābhasaṃvartanīyam/
426.030. ebhirbhikṣavaḥ saptatriṃśatprakāraiḥ paṇḍito dānaṃ dadāti//
body.translated_text:
426.001. Thus have I heard.
426.002. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks.
426.003. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'By thirty-seven modes, O monks, the wise one gives a gift.
426.004. He gives a gift at the proper time — one sanctioned by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
426.005. He gives a prepared gift, purified in three aspects.
426.005. He gives a gift with respect — for the purpose of removing all faults and defilements.
426.006. He gives a gift with his own hand — for the purpose of extracting the essential from the inessential body.
426.006. He gives a shoulder-gift — conducive to obtaining the fruit of great renunciation and enjoyment.
426.007. He gives a gift endowed with color — conducive to obtaining a pleasing result.
426.007. He gives a gift endowed with fragrance — conducive to obtaining the result of fragrance.
426.008. He gives a gift endowed with taste — conducive to obtaining the result of the finest flavors, tastes, and seasonings.
426.009. He gives an excellent gift — conducive to obtaining the result of excellent enjoyments.
426.010. He gives an abundant gift — conducive to obtaining the result of abundant enjoyments.
426.010. He gives the gift of food — conducive to obtaining the result of the cessation of hunger and thirst.
426.011. He gives the gift of drink — conducive to obtaining the result of the cessation of thirst in all births.
426.012. He gives the gift of clothing — conducive to obtaining the result of excellent clothing.
426.012. He gives the gift of shelter — conducive to obtaining the result of mansions, tower-halls, palaces, dwellings, celestial abodes, gardens, and special parks.
426.014. He gives the gift of bedding — conducive to obtaining the result of enjoyment in a high-born family.
426.014. He gives the gift of a vehicle — conducive to obtaining the result of the bases of supernatural power.
426.015. He gives the gift of medicine — conducive to obtaining the result of the cessation of agelessness, deathlessness, sorrowlessness, freedom from affliction, and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
426.016. He gives the gift of <s>Dharma</s> — conducive to obtaining the result of remembering past lives.
426.016. He gives the gift of flowers — conducive to obtaining the result of the flowers of the factors of awakening.
426.017. He gives the gift of garlands — conducive to obtaining the result of purification from passion, hatred, and delusion.
426.018. He gives the gift of fragrance — conducive to obtaining the result of rebirth in divine fragrance and happiness.
426.019. He gives the gift of incense — conducive to obtaining the result of the abandonment of the foul smell of affliction.
426.019. He gives the gift of a parasol — conducive to obtaining the result of sovereignty over the <s>Dharma</s>.
426.020. He gives the gift of a bell — conducive to obtaining the result of a pleasing voice.
426.021. He gives the gift of musical instruments — conducive to obtaining the result of the sound of <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice.
426.021. He gives the gift of a silk banner — conducive to obtaining the result of the tying of the consecration-banner among gods and humans.
426.022. He gives the gift of bathing <s>Tathāgata</s> shrines and <s>Tathāgata</s> images with fragrant water — conducive to obtaining the result of the thirty-two marks of a great man and the eighty minor characteristics.
426.023. He gives the gift of thread — conducive to obtaining the result of being born in all births in distinguished families, with an all-around pleasing appearance.
426.025. He gives the gift of the five essences — conducive to obtaining the result of great strength in all births.
426.025. He gives a gift imbued with loving-kindness — conducive to obtaining the result of the abandonment of ill-will.
426.026. He gives a gift founded on compassion — conducive to obtaining the result of great happiness.
426.027. He gives a gift founded on sympathetic joy — conducive to obtaining the result of joy and delight in every way.
426.028. He gives a gift founded on equanimity — conducive to obtaining the result of the abandonment of discontent.
426.028. He gives a varied and elaborate gift — conducive to obtaining the result of many diverse and varied enjoyments.
426.029. He gives the gift of the renunciation of all possessions — conducive to obtaining the result of unsurpassed perfect awakening.
426.030. By these thirty-seven modes, O monks, the wise one gives a gift.'

body.text:
426.031. idamavocadbhagavān/
426.031. āttamanasaste bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan//
body.translated_text:
426.031. This the Blessed One spoke.
426.031. Delighted, those monks rejoiced in the Blessed One's words.

body.text: 426.032. iti śrīdivyāvadāne dānādhikaraṇamahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: 426.032. Thus concludes the <s>Dānādhikaraṇa Mahāyāna Sūtra</s> (the Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Basis of Giving) in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text:
********** Avadāna 35 **********
427.001. div35 cūḍāpakṣāvadānam /
body.translated_text:
********** <s>Avadāna</s> 35 **********
427.001. The <s>Cūḍāpakṣāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Lock of Hair).

body.text:
427.002. buddho bhagavāñ śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme/
427.002. śrāvastyāmanyatamo brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati/
427.003. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
427.003. sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati tamate paricārayati/
427.004. tasyāpatyaṃ jātaṃ jātaṃ kālaṃ karoti/
427.004. athāpareṇa samayena tasya patnī āpannasattvā/
427.005. sa kare kapolaṃ dattvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ/
427.005. tasya nātidūre vṛddhayuvatiḥ prativasati/
427.006. tayā dṛṣṭaḥ/
427.006. sā kathayati--kasmāttvaṃ brāhmaṇa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitah? sa kathayati--mamāpatyaṃ jātaṃ jātaṃ kālaṃ karoti/
427.007. mama cedānīṃ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
427.008. yadapyanyadapatyaṃ janayiṣyati, tadapi kālaṃ kariṣyati/
427.008. sa kathayati--yadā tava patvyāḥ prasavakālaḥ syāt, tadā māṃ śabdāpayethā iti/
427.009. athāpareṇa samayena tasya patnyāḥ prasavakāle jātaḥ/
427.010. tena sā vṛddhayuvatiḥ śabdāpitā/
427.010. tayā sā prasavāpitā/
427.010. putro jātaḥ/
427.011. tayā sa dārakaḥ snāpayitvā śuklena veṣṭayitvā navanītenāsyaṃ pūrayitvā dārikāyā haste 'nupradattaḥ/
427.012. sā dārikoktā--imaṃ dārakaṃ caturmahāpathe dhāraya/
427.012. yaṃ kaṃcit paśyasi brāhmaṇaṃ vā, sa vaktavyah--ayaṃ dārakaḥ pādābhivandanaṃ karotīti/
427.013. astaṃ gate āditye yadi jīvati, gṛhītvā āgaccha/
427.014. atha kālaṃ karoti, tatraivāropayitavyaḥ/
427.014. sā tamādāya caturmahāpathe gatvā sthitā/
427.015. ācaritaṃ tīrthyānāṃ kalyamevotthāya tīrthopasparśanāya gacchanti/
427.016. sā dārikā sagauravā sapratīśā pādabhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--ayaṃ dāraka āryāṇāṃ pādābhivandanaṃ karoti/
427.017. te kathayanti--ciraṃ jīva, dīrghamāyuḥ pālayatu, mātāpitrormanorathaṃ pūrayatu/
427.018. sthavirasthvirā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍāya praviśanti/
427.019. sā dārikā sagauravā sapratīśā pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--ayaṃ dāraka āryāṇāṃ pādābhivandanaṃ karotīti/
427.020. sthavirāḥ kathayanti--suciraṃ jīvatu, dīrghamāyuḥ pālayatu, mātāpitromanorathaṃ pūrayatu/
427.021. bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya praviśati sma/
427.022. sā dārikā sagauravā sapratīśā pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--bhagavān, ayaṃ dārako bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ karotīti/
427.023. bhagavānāha--ciraṃ jīvatu, dīrghamāyuḥ pālayatu, mātāpitromanorathaṃ pūrayatu/
427.024. vikālībhūte paśyati--yāvajjīvati/
427.025. sā taṃ gṛhītvā gṛhamāgatā/
427.025. sā taiḥ pṛṣṭā--jīvati dārakah? sā kathayati--jīvati/
427.026. te kathayanti--kutra dhāritah? asmin mahāpathe/
427.026. te kathayanti--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma? ayaṃ dārako mahāpathe dhāritaḥ/
427.027. bhavatu dāraksya mahāpanthaka iti nāma/
427.027. mahāpanthako dāraka unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttaḥ/
427.028. sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyāmupanyastaḥ, saṃkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāṃ brāhmaṇikāyāmīryāyāṃ śauce samudācāre bhasmagrahe autkare bhoskāre ṛgvede yajurvede sāmavede 'tharvavede yajane yājane 'dhyayane 'dhyāpane dāne pratigrahe/
427.030. ṣaṭkarmanirato brāhmaṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
427.031. sa pañcaśatagaṇaṃ brāhmaṇakarma oṃ vācayitumārabdhaḥ/
427.031. tasya bhūyaḥ krīḍato ramataḥ paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
427.032. tasyāḥ prasavakālo jātaḥ/
427.032. tena sā vṛddhayuvatih<428> śabdāpitā/
body.translated_text:
427.002. The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.
427.002. A certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was residing in <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
427.003. He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing.
427.003. He played with her, delighted in her, and was attended by her.
427.004. Each child born to him died.
427.004. Then, on another occasion, his wife became pregnant.
427.005. He placed his cheek on his hand and stood absorbed in worry.
427.005. Not far from him lived an elderly woman.
427.006. She saw him.
427.006. She said: 'Why, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, do you stand with cheek on hand, absorbed in worry?' He said: 'Each child born to me dies.
427.007. Now my wife has become pregnant again.
427.008. Even if she bears another child, that too will die.'
427.008. She said: 'When your wife's time of delivery comes, then send for me.'
427.009. Then, on another occasion, when his wife's time of delivery came,
427.010. he sent for that elderly woman.
427.010. She delivered the child.
427.010. A son was born.
427.011. She bathed the boy, wrapped him in white cloth, filled his mouth with fresh butter, and placed him in a girl-servant's hands.
427.012. She instructed the girl-servant: 'Hold this boy at the crossroads.
427.012. Whomever you see — be it a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or other — you should say to him: "This boy pays homage at your feet."
427.013. When the sun has set, if he is still alive, bring him back.
427.014. But if he dies, leave him right there.'
