427.014. She took him and went to stand at the crossroads.
427.015. It is the custom of the heretics to rise early and go to the holy bathing places to perform ritual ablutions.
427.016. The girl-servant, with respect and deference, made obeisance at their feet and said: 'This boy pays homage at the feet of the noble ones.'
427.017. They said: 'May he live long! May he enjoy a long life! May he fulfill the heart's desire of his parents!'
427.018. Elder monks, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.
427.019. The girl-servant, with respect and deference, made obeisance at their feet and said: 'This boy pays homage at the feet of the noble ones.'
427.020. The elders said: 'May he live very long! May he enjoy a long life! May he fulfill the heart's desire of his parents!'
427.021. The Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.
427.022. The girl-servant, with respect and deference, made obeisance at his feet and said: 'Blessed One, this boy pays homage at the feet of the Blessed One.'
427.023. The Blessed One said: 'May he live long! May he enjoy a long life! May he fulfill the heart's desire of his parents!'
427.024. When evening came, she saw that the boy was still alive.
427.025. She took him and returned home.
427.025. They asked her: 'Does the boy live?' She said: 'He lives.'
427.026. They said: 'Where was he kept?' 'At the great crossroads.'
427.026. They said: 'What should be the boy's name?' 'This boy was kept at the great road.
427.027. Let the boy's name be <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> (Great Roadside).'
427.027. The boy <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> was raised and nurtured and grew up.
427.028. When he had grown up, he was set to learning — writing, arithmetic, calculation, seals, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> conduct, deportment, purification, good manners, ash-taking, heap-offering, the exclamation "<s>bhoḥ</s>," the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, sacrificing, causing others to sacrifice, study, teaching, giving, and receiving.
427.030. He became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> devoted to the six duties.
427.031. He began teaching <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> rites with the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> to a group of five hundred.
427.031. Once again, while he was playing, delighting, and being attended by his wife, she became pregnant.
427.032. Her time of delivery came.
427.032. He sent for that elderly woman.

body.text:
428.001. tayā prasavitā/
428.001. tasyāḥ putro jātaḥ/
428.001. tayā sa dārakaḥ snāpayitvā śuklena vastreṇa veṣṭayitvā navanītenāsyaṃ pūrayitvā dārikāyā haste dattaḥ/
428.002. sā dārikoktā--imaṃ tvaṃ dārakaṃ caturmahāpathe dhāraya/
428.003. yadi kaṃcitpaśyasi śramaṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā, sa vaktavyah--ayaṃ dāraka āryasya pādābhivandanaṃ karoti/
428.004. astaṃ gata āditye yadi jīvati, gṛhītvā āgaccha/
428.005. atha kālaṃ karoti, tatraivāropayitvā āgaccha/
428.005. sā dārikā alasajātīyā taṃ dārakamādāya panthalikāyāṃ sthitā/
428.006. ācaritaṃ tīrthyānāṃ kalyamevotthāya tīrthopasparśakā gacchanti/
428.006. sā dārikā sagauravā sapratīśā pādabhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--ārya, ayaṃ daraka āryāṇāṃ pādābhivandanaṃ karoti/
428.008. te kathayanti--ciraṃ jīvatu, dīrghamāyuḥ pālayatu, mātāpitromanorathaṃ pūrayatu/
428.009. sā taṃ vikālībhūte paśyati--yāvajjīvati/
428.009. sā taṃ gṛhītvā gṛhamāgatā/
428.009. sā taiḥ pṛṣṭā--jīvati dārakah? sā kathayati--jīvatīti/
428.010. te kathayanti--kutra tvayaiṣa dhāritah? sā kathayati--amuṣyāṃ panthalikāyām/
428.011. te kathayanti--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma? ayaṃ dārakaḥ panthalikāyāṃ dhāritaḥ/
428.012. bhavatu dārakasya nāmadheyaṃ panthaka iti/
428.012. panthako dāraka unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttiḥ/
428.013. sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttastadā lipyamupanyastaḥ/
428.013. tasya sītyukte dhamiti vismarati/
428.014. atha tasyācāryaḥ kathayati--brāhmaṇa, mayā prabhūtadārakāḥ pāṭhayitavyāḥ/
428.015. na śakṣyāmyahaṃ panthakaṃ pāṭhayitum/
428.015. mahāpanthakasyālpamucyate prabhūtaṃ gṛhṇāti, asya tu panthakasya sītyukte dhamiti vismarati/
428.016. brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--sarve brāhmaṇā lipyakṣarakuśalā bhavanti, vedabrāhmaṇa eṣa bhaviṣyati/
428.017. sa tenādhyāpakasya vedaṃ pāṭhayituṃ samarpitaḥ/
428.017. tasya omityukte bhūriti vismarati, bhūrityukta omiti vismarati/
428.018. adhyāpakaḥ kathayati--prabhūtā māṇavakāḥ pāṭhayitavyā mayā/
428.019. na śakyāmyahaṃ panthakaṃ pāṭhayitum/
428.019. asya omityukte bhūriti vismarati, bhūrityukta omiti vismarati/
428.020. brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--na sarve brāhmaṇā vedapāragā bhavanti/
428.021. jātibrāhmaṇa evāyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
428.021. sa yatra kvacinnimantritako gacchati, tameva panthakamādāya gacchati/
428.022. atha tena samayena sa brāhmaṇo glānībhūtaḥ/
428.022. sa mūlagaṇḍapatraphalabhaiṣajyairupasthīyamāno hīyata eva/
428.023. sa tena mahāpanthaka uktah--putra, tvaṃ mamātyayādaśocyo 'si/
428.024. api tu tvayā panthakasya yogodvahanaṃ kartavyamiti/
428.024. ityuktvā--
428.025. sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ/
428.026. samyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ ca jīvitam//1//
body.translated_text: She gave birth. A son was born to her. Having bathed the boy, wrapped him in white cloth, and filled his mouth with fresh butter, she placed him in the hands of a servant girl. She instructed the servant girl: 'You are to hold this boy at the crossroads. If you see any <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he should be told: "This boy makes obeisance at the feet of the venerable one." When the sun has set, if he lives, bring him back. But if he dies, place him right there and return.' The servant girl, being of a lazy nature, took the boy and stood at a path-junction. It was the custom of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics) to rise early in the morning and go to bathe at the sacred ford. The servant girl, with respect and reverence, having made obeisance at their feet, said: 'Venerable sir, this boy makes obeisance at the feet of the venerable ones.' They said: 'May he live long, may he enjoy a long life, may he fulfill the heart's desire of his parents.' She looked at him when evening came — and he was still alive. She took him and came home. She was asked by them: 'Does the boy live?' She said: 'He lives.' They said: 'Where did you hold him?' She said: 'At such-and-such a path-junction.' They said: 'What should be the boy's name? This boy was held at the path-junction. Let the boy's name be <s>Panthaka</s> (Path-born).' The boy <s>Panthaka</s> was raised, nourished, and grew up. When he had grown up, he was set to learning letters. But when he was taught 'si,' he forgot 'dha.' Then his teacher said: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, I have many boys to teach. I am unable to teach <s>Panthaka</s>. When <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> is told a little, he grasps much; but this <s>Panthaka</s>, when told "si," forgets "dha."' The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> reflected: 'All <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> become skilled in letters and writing; this one will be a Veda-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' He then entrusted him to a Vedic instructor to teach the <s>Vedas</s>. But when he was told 'Oṃ,' he forgot '<s>Bhūḥ</s>'; when told '<s>Bhūḥ</s>,' he forgot 'Oṃ.' The instructor said: 'I have many students to teach. I am unable to teach <s>Panthaka</s>. When told "Oṃ," he forgets "<s>Bhūḥ</s>"; when told "<s>Bhūḥ</s>," he forgets "Oṃ."' The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> reflected: 'Not all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> become masters of the <s>Vedas</s>. This one will simply be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by birth.' Wherever he went to an invitation, he would take <s>Panthaka</s> along. Then at that time, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> fell ill. Though treated with medicines of roots, swellings, leaves, and fruits, he only deteriorated. He said to <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>: 'Son, after my passing you need not grieve for yourself. But you must undertake the responsibility of caring for <s>Panthaka</s>.' Having said this — 'All accumulations end in exhaustion; all heights end in falling; all unions end in separation; and life ends in death.' //1//

body.text:
428.027. iti sa kāladharmeṇa samyuktaḥ/
428.027. te taṃ nīlapītalohitāvadātairvastraiḥ śibikāmalaṃkṛtya mahatā satkāreṇa śmaśāne dhmāpayitvā śokavinodaṃ kṛtvā avasthitāḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus he was joined with the law of death. They adorned the bier with blue, yellow, red, and white cloths, and with great ceremony cremated him at the cremation ground. Having performed the consolation of grief, they remained.

body.text:
428.029. āyuṣmantau śāriputramaudgalyāyanau pañcaśataparivārau kosaleṣu jānapadeṣu cārikāṃ carantau śrāvastīmanuprāptau/
428.030. śrāvastyāṃ janakāyena śrutam--āyuṣmantau śāriputramaudgalyāyanau pañcaśataparivārau kosaleṣu jānapadeṣu cārikāṃ carantau śrāvastīmanuprāptau/
428.031. śrutvā ca punaḥ sa janakāyo bahir nirgantumārabdhaḥ/
428.032. mahāpanthako 'pi bahiḥ śrāvastyāmanyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle <429>pañcamātrāṇi māṇavakaśatāni brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayati/
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, attended by five hundred [monks], while wandering on a preaching tour through the <s>Kosala</s> country, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The people of <s>Śrāvastī</s> heard: 'The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, attended by five hundred, while wandering on a preaching tour through the <s>Kosala</s> country, have arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' Having heard this, the crowd of people began to go out. <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> too, outside <s>Śrāvastī</s>, at the foot of a certain tree, was teaching five hundred young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> students their sacred texts.

body.text:
429.001. tena sa janakāyaḥ śrāvastyā nirgacchan dṛṣṭaḥ/
429.002. sa tān māṇavakān pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, ka eṣa mahājanakāyo nirgacchati? te tasya kathayanti--upādhyāya, bhadantau śāriputramaudgalyāyanau pañcaśataparivārau kosaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caritvā iha śrāvastīmanuprāptau, taddarśanāyopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
429.004. kiṃ nu tau draṣṭavyau? yatredānīṃ tadagraṃ varṇamapahāya dvitīyavarṇasya śramaṇasya gautamasyāntike pravrajitau/
429.005. ekastatra māṇavakaḥ śrāddhaḥ/
429.006. sa kathayati--upādhyāya, maivaṃ vocaḥ/
429.006. mahānubhāvau tau/
429.006. yadyupādhyāyasteṣāṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇuyāt, sthānametadvidyate yadupādhyāyasyāpi rocate/
429.007. ācaritaṃ teṣāṃ māṇavakānām yadā apāṭhā bhavanti, te kadācinnagarāvalokanayā gacchanti/
429.008. kadācittīrthopasparśakā gacchanti/
429.009. kadācitsamidhāhārakā gacchanti/
429.009. apareṇa samayena te sarve apāṭhāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ/
429.009. te samidhāhārakāḥ saṃprasthitāḥ/
429.010. so 'pi mahāpanthako 'nyatamavṛkṣamūle caṃkramya sthitaḥ/
429.010. tatraikaṃ bhikṣumadrākṣīt/
429.011. sa tamupasaṃkramyaivamāha--bho bhikṣo, ucyatāṃ tāvatkiṃcidbuddhavacanam/
429.011. tena tasya daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā vistareṇa saṃprakāśitāḥ/
429.012. so 'bhiprasannaḥ kathayati--bho bhikṣo, punarapyākhyāhi vistaram/
429.013. ityuktvā prakrāntaḥ/
429.013. apareṇa samayena bhūyaste apāṭhāḥ saṃvṛtāḥ/
429.014. te samidhāhātakāḥ saṃprasthitāḥ/
429.014. mahāpanthako 'pi bhikṣusakāśamupasaṃkrāntaḥ/
429.014. tena tasya dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo 'nulomapratilomo vistareṇa prakāśitaḥ/
429.015. so 'bhiprasannaḥ kathayati--bho bhikṣu, labheyāhaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
429.016. careyamahaṃ śramaṇasya gautamasyāntike brahmacaryam/
429.017. sa bhikṣuḥ saṃlakṣayati--pravrājayāmi śāsane, dhuramunnāmayatīti/
429.018. sa tenoktah--brāhmaṇa, evaṃ kuruṣva/
429.018. mahāpanthakaḥ kathayati--bhikṣo, vayaṃ prajñātā brāhmaṇāḥ/
429.019. na śakṣyām ihaiva pravrajitum/
429.019. janapadaṃ gatvā pravrajāmaḥ/
429.019. sa tena janapadaṃ nītvā pravrajitah upasampāditaḥ, uktaśca/
429.020. dve bhikṣukarmaṇī dhyānamadhyayanaṃ ca/
429.020. kiṃ kariṣyasi? ubhayaṃ kariṣyāmi/
429.021. tena divā uddiśatā yoniśo bhāvayatā trīṇi piṭakāni, rātrau cintayatā tulayatā upaparīkṣamāṇena sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
429.022. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhatukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāḍbhukhaḥ/
429.024. sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ mānyaḥ pūjyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: He saw that crowd of people coming out of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He asked those students: 'Gentlemen, what is this great crowd going out for?' They told him: 'Teacher, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, attended by five hundred, having wandered on a preaching tour through the <s>Kosala</s> country, have arrived here at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The crowd is approaching to see them.' 'Are those two worth seeing? They who have abandoned the foremost <s>varṇa</s> and gone forth as <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) in the company of the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> of the second <s>varṇa</s>!' One student there was full of faith. He said: 'Teacher, do not speak thus. They are of great power. If the teacher were to hear their <s>Dharma</s>, it is possible that even the teacher would be pleased.' It was the custom of those students that when they had no lessons, they would sometimes go sightseeing in the city, sometimes go to bathe at the sacred ford, and sometimes go to gather firewood. At another time, they all found themselves without lessons. They set out to gather firewood. <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> too was walking up and down at the foot of a certain tree. There he saw a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk). He approached him and said: 'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, please recite some word of the <s>Buddha</s>.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> then explained to him the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>kuśala karmapatha</s>) in detail. Deeply impressed, he said: 'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, please tell me again in detail.' Having said this, he departed. At another time, again they found themselves without lessons. They set out to gather firewood. <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> also went to the <s>bhikṣu</s>. The <s>bhikṣu</s> then explained to him the twelvefold chain of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), in forward and reverse order, in detail. Deeply impressed, he said: 'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, may I obtain the going forth, the full ordination, and <s>bhikṣu</s>-status in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline). May I practice the holy life in the company of the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> reflected: 'I shall ordain him into the teaching; he will shoulder the burden.' He told him: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, do so.' <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> said: 'O <s>bhikṣu</s>, we are well-known <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. I am unable to go forth right here. Let me go to the countryside and go forth there.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> then took him to the countryside and ordained him, gave him full ordination, and said: 'There are two duties of a <s>bhikṣu</s>: meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and study. Which will you do?' 'I will do both.' By day, studying and meditating wisely, he [mastered] the three <s>Piṭakas</s> (baskets of scripture); by night, reflecting, examining, and investigating, he directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of the worthy one) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements). He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding gold and a clod of earth as equal, with a mind as even as the sky and the palm of a hand, like a sandalwood log and an axe, with the egg-shell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of honor, veneration, and salutation even by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

body.text:
429.026. yadā panthakasya bhogāstanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatāḥ, sa kṛcchreṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayitumārabdhaḥ/
429.027. atha panthakasyaitadabhavat--yattāvanme śrutena prāptavyaṃ tanmayā.../
429.027. yannvahaṃ śrāvastīṃ gatvā bhagavantaṃ paryupāāsyāmi/
429.028. athāyuṣmān mahāpanthakaḥ pañcaśataparivāro yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
429.029. anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
429.029. śrāvastyāṃ janakāyena śrutam--āryo mahāpanthakaḥ pañcaśataparivāraḥ kosaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
429.031. śrutvā ca punar nirgantumārabdhaḥ/
429.031. panthakena dṛṣṭaḥ/
429.031. sa pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, kutreṣu mahājanakāyo gacchati? te kathayanti--āryo mahāpanthakaḥ pañcaśataparivātaḥ kosaleṣu <430>janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carañ śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
body.translated_text: When <s>Panthaka</s>'s possessions had diminished, wasted away, and were exhausted, he began to eke out a difficult livelihood. Then <s>Panthaka</s> thought: 'What is to be gained through learning, that I have [failed to gain]... Let me go to <s>Śrāvastī</s> and attend upon the Blessed One.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, attended by five hundred, set out on a preaching tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Wandering gradually, he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The people of <s>Śrāvastī</s> heard: 'The noble <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, attended by five hundred, while wandering on a preaching tour through the <s>Kosala</s> country, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.' Having heard this, the crowd began to go out. <s>Panthaka</s> saw them. He asked: 'Gentlemen, where is this great crowd going?' They said: 'The noble <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, attended by five hundred, while wandering on a preaching tour through the <s>Kosala</s> country, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.'

body.text:
430.001. tameṣu mahājanakāyo darśanāyopasaṃkrāmati/
430.002. panthakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--eṣāmasau na bhrātā na jñātiḥ/
430.002. mamāsau bhrātā bhavati/
430.002. ahaṃ kasmāttaṃ na darśanāyopasaṃkrāmāmi? so 'pi taddarśanāyopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
430.003. sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaśca--panthaka, katham yāpayasi? kṛcchreṇa yāpayāmi? kiṃ na pravrajasi? sa kathayati--ahaṃ cūḍaḥ paramacūḍo dhanvaḥ paramadhanvaḥ/
430.005. ko māṃ pravrājayiṣyatīti? āyuṣmān mahāpanthakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--santyasya kānicitkuśalamūlāni? santi/
430.006. kenāyaṃ na yogyah? āgaccha, ahaṃ tvāṃ pravrājayiṣyāmi/
430.007. tena pravrājita upasampāditaḥ/
430.007. tena tasyoddeśo dattah--
430.008. pāpaṃ na kuryānmanasā na vācā kāyena vā kiṃcana sarvaloke/
430.010. riktaḥ kāmaiḥ smṛtimān saṃprajānan duḥkhaṃ na sa vidyādanarthopasaṃhitam//1//
body.translated_text: This great crowd is approaching to see him. <s>Panthaka</s> reflected: 'He is neither brother nor kinsman to these people. But he is my brother. Why should I not go to see him?' He too approached to see him. He was seen by <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, who asked: '<s>Panthaka</s>, how are you getting on?' 'With difficulty.' 'Why do you not go forth [as a monk]?' He said: 'I am a fool, supremely foolish, a dullard, supremely dull. Who would ordain me?' The venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> reflected: 'Does he have any wholesome roots?' He does. 'Then why is he not fit?' 'Come, I shall ordain you.' He ordained him and gave him full ordination. He gave him this lesson to learn: 'One should not commit evil by mind, by speech, or by body in any way in the whole world; empty of sense-desires, mindful and clearly comprehending, one would not undergo suffering connected with what is unprofitable.' //1//

body.text:
430.012. tasyaiṣā gāthā traimāsyenāpi na vṛttā jātā/
430.012. anyeṣāṃ gopālakānāṃ paśupālakānāṃ śrutvā pravṛttā jātā/
430.013. sagauravaḥ sapratīśa upasaṃkramya praṣṭuṃ pravṛttaḥ/
430.013. te upasaṃharanti/
430.013. dharmatā khalu yathā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dvau śrāvakāṇāṃ saṃnipātau bhavataḥ, āṣāḍhyāṃ varṣopanāyikāyāṃ kārtikapūrṇamāsyām/
430.015. evaṃ mahāśrāvkāṇāmapi/
430.015. tatra ye āṣāḍhīvarṣopanāyikāyāmupasaṃkrāmanti, te tāṃstān manasikāraviśeṣānādāya tāsu tāsu grāmanigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu varṣā upagacchanti/
430.017. ye kārtikyāṃ ca pūrṇamāsyāmupasaṃkramanti, te svādhyāyanikāṃ paripṛcchanikāṃ ca yācanti, yathādhigataṃ cārocayanti/
430.018. āyuṣmato mahāpanthakasya sārdhaṃvihāryantevāsikā bhikṣavo janapade varṣoṣitāḥ, te 'pyeva kārtikyāṃ pūrṇamāsyām yenāyuṣmān mahāpanthakastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
430.019. tatra kecitsvādhyāyinikām yācanti, kecitparipṛcchanti, kecidyathādhigatamārocayanti/
430.020. tatra ye cūḍā bhavanti paramacūḍā dhanvāḥ paramadhanvāḥ, te ṣaḍvargīyān sevante bhajante paryupāsante/
430.022. āyuṣmān panthakaḥ ṣaḍvargīyān sevate bhajate paryupāsate/
430.022. sa ṣaḍvargīyairucyate--āyuṣman panthaka, tava samānopādhyāyā upādhyāyasyāntikātsvadhyāyinikāṃ paripṛcchinikām yācanti/
430.024. gaccha, tvamapi tvadupādhyāyasyāntikātsvādhyāyinikāṃ paripṛcchanikām yācasva/
430.024. sa kathayati--mayā na kiṃcitpaṭhitaṃ traimāsye, na tvekā gāthā mama vṛttā jātā, kimahaṃ svādhyāyinikām yāceyamiti? te kathayanti--nanūktaṃ bhagavatā--asvādhyāyamānā mattā iti/
430.026. kiṃ tavāsvādhyāyamānasya gāthā anupravṛttā bhaviṣyati? gaccha, yācāhi/
430.027. sa gatvā kathayati--upādhyāya, svādhyāyinikāṃ tāvanme dehi/
430.028. āyuṣmān mahāpanthakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kimasyedaṃ svaṃ pratibhānamāhosvit kenacitprayuktah? sa paśyati--yāvatprayuktaḥ/
430.029. āyuṣmān mahāpanthakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ nvayamutsahanāvineya āhosvidavasāadanāvineyah? sa paśyati--yāvadavasādanāvineyaḥ/
430.031. sa tena grīvāayāṃ gṛhītvā bahirvihārasya niṣkāsitaḥ/
430.031. tvaṃ tāvaccūḍaḥ paramacūḍo dhanvaḥ paramadhanvaḥ/
430.032. kiṃ tvamasmiñ śāsane kariṣyasi? sa roditumārabdhaḥ/
430.032. idānīmahaṃ na <431>gṛhī na pravrajitaḥ/
body.translated_text: This verse of his was not mastered even in three months. Other cowherds and cattle-keepers had mastered it upon hearing it. With respect and reverence, he approached to ask. They withdrew. It is indeed the natural order that for the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavats</s> (Blessed Ones), there are two assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples): on the <s>Āṣāḍhī</s> (full moon of Āṣāḍha), the <s>varṣopanāyikā</s> (rainy season commencement), and on the full moon of <s>Kārttika</s>. So too for the great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples). Those who come at the <s>Āṣāḍhī varṣopanāyikā</s> (rainy season commencement), having taken up their respective subjects of meditation, go to spend the rains in various villages, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals. Those who come at the full moon of <s>Kārttika</s> request recitation lessons and catechism, and report what they have attained. The monks who were co-residents and pupils of the venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, having spent the rains in the countryside, came to the venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> at the full moon of <s>Kārttika</s>. There, some requested recitation lessons, some asked questions, and some reported what they had attained. Among them, those who were the dullest of the dull, the most barren of the barren, attended upon and served the <s>ṣaḍvargīyas</s> (the group of six monks). The venerable <s>Panthaka</s> attended upon and served the <s>ṣaḍvargīyas</s>. The <s>ṣaḍvargīyas</s> said to him: "Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, those who share your preceptor are requesting recitation lessons and catechism from your preceptor. Go, you too should request recitation lessons and catechism from your preceptor." He said: "I have not learned anything in three months; not even one verse has been mastered by me. Why should I request recitation lessons?" They said: "Did not the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) say: 'Those who do not recite are intoxicated'? How will a verse be mastered by you who do not recite? Go, ask!" Having gone, he said: "Preceptor, please give me a recitation lesson." The venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> reflected: "Is this his own initiative, or has someone put him up to it?" He saw that someone had put him up to it. The venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s> reflected: "Can this one be trained by encouragement, or is he to be trained by humiliation?" He saw that he was to be trained by humiliation. Seizing him by the neck, he expelled him from the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery). "You are the dullest of the dull, the most barren of the barren. What will you accomplish in this teaching?" He began to weep. "Now I am neither a householder nor one gone forth."

body.text:
431.001. adrākṣīdbhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ pathakaṃ bahirvihārasya bhramantam/
431.001. dṛṣṭvā ca punarāgacchantamidamavocat--kasmāttvaṃ pathaka vahirvihārasya rodiṣyasi, aśrūṇi vartayasi? ahamasmi bhadanta upādhyāyena niṣkāsitaḥ/
431.003. idānīmahaṃ na gṛhī na pravrajitaḥ/
431.004. bhagavānāha--nedaṃ vatsa maunīndraṃ vacanaṃ tavopādhyāyena tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairaneikairduṣkaraśatasahasraiḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya samudānītam, api tu mayedaṃ maunīndraṃ pravacanaṃ tribhiḥ kalpāsaṃkhyeyairanaikairduṣkaraśatasahasraiḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya samudānītam/
431.006. na śakyasi tvaṃ tathāgatasyāntikātpaṭhitum? ahamasmi bhadanta cūḍaḥ paramacūḍo dhanvaḥ paramadhanvaḥ/
431.007. atha bhagavānasyāmutpattau gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
431.009. yo bālo bālabhāvena paṇḍitastatra tena saḥ/
431.010. bālaḥ paṇḍitamānī tu sa vai bāla ihocyate//2//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) saw the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> wandering outside the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery). Having seen him, he approached and said this: "Why do you, <s>Panthaka</s>, weep outside the <s>vihāra</s>, shedding tears?" "I have been expelled by my preceptor, Venerable Sir. Now I am neither a householder nor one gone forth." The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: "Child, this word of the <s>Maunīndra</s> (Chief of Sages) was not brought forth by your preceptor through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) and innumerable hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds, having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections); rather, this proclamation of the <s>Maunīndra</s> was brought forth by me through three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> and innumerable hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds, having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Are you not able to learn from the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" "I am, Venerable Sir, the dullest of the dull, the most barren of the barren." Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> spoke this verse regarding his potential: "He who, being foolish, knows his own foolishness — he is wise in that regard. But the fool who thinks himself learned — he is truly called a fool." (2)

body.text:
431.011. asthānamanavakāśo yadbuddhā bhagavantaḥ padaśo dharmaṃ vācayiṣyanti nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate/
431.012. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma--imaṃ pāṭhaya tvamānanda panthakam/
431.012. āyuṣmānānandastaṃ pāṭhayitumārabdhaḥ/
431.013. sa na śaknoti pāṭhayitum/
431.013. āyuṣmānānando bhagavantamidamavocat--mayā tāvadbhadanta śāsturupasthānaṃ karaṇīyam, śrutamudgrahītavyam, gaṇo vācayitavyaḥ/
431.014. āgatagatānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ dharmo deśayitavyam/
431.015. nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi panthakaṃ pāṭhayitum/
431.015. bhagavatā tasya dve pade datte--rajo harāmi, malaṃ harāmīti/
431.016. tasyaitatpadadvayaṃ na lebhe/
431.016. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati/
431.017. karmāpanayo 'sya kartavyamiti/
431.017. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--śakṣyasi tvaṃ panthaka bhikṣūṇāmupānahānmūlācca proñchitum/
431.018. paraṃ bhadanta śakṣyāmi/
431.018. gaccha proñchasva/
431.019. sa bhikṣūṇāmupānahānmūlācca proñchitumāradhaḥ/
431.019. tasya te bhikṣavo nānuprayacchanti/
431.019. bhagavānāha--anuprayacchata, karmāpanayo 'sya kartavya iti/
431.020. padadvayasya dāsye svādhyāyanikām, anuprayacchata/
431.021. sa bhikṣūṇāmupānahānmūlaṃ kramataśca proñchate/
431.021. tasya te bhikṣavaḥ padadvaysya svādhyāyanikāmanuprayacchanti/
431.022. tasyaitatpadadvayaṃ svādhyāyataḥ kālāntareṇa pravṛttaṃ jātam/
431.023. athāyuṣmataḥ panthakasya rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaye etadabhavat--bhagavānevamāha--rajo harāmi, malaṃ harāmīti/
431.024. kiṃ nu bhagavānādhyātmikaṃ rajaḥ saṃdhāyāha āhosvidbāhyam? tasyaivaṃ cintayatastasyāṃ velāyāmaṣrutapūrvāstisro gāthā āmukhīpravṛttā jātāh--
431.026. rajo 'tra rāgo na hi reṇureṣa rajo rāgasyādhivacanaṃ na reṇoḥ/
431.028. etadrajaḥ prativinudanti paṇḍitā na ye pramattāḥ sugatasya śāsane//3//
body.translated_text: It is impossible and inconceivable that <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavats</s> (Blessed Ones), would teach the <s>Dharma</s> word by word — this does not occur. There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "<s>Ānanda</s>, you teach this <s>Panthaka</s>." The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> began to teach him. He was unable to teach him. The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: "Venerable Sir, I must attend upon the Teacher, I must retain what is heard, I must instruct the community, I must teach the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders who come and go. I am not able to teach <s>Panthaka</s>." The <s>Bhagavat</s> gave him two words: '<s>rajo harāmi</s>' (I remove dust), '<s>malaṃ harāmi</s>' (I remove stain). Even this pair of words he could not grasp. The <s>Bhagavat</s> reflected: "A removal of his <s>karma</s> (karmic obstruction) must be performed." There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "<s>Panthaka</s>, will you be able to wipe the monks' sandals and dust their feet?" "Yes, Venerable Sir, I will be able." "Go, wipe them." He began to wipe the monks' sandals and dust their feet. But those monks would not give them to him. The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: "Give them to him; a removal of his <s>karma</s> must be performed. I shall give him a recitation lesson of two words — give them to him." He wiped the monks' sandals and dusted their feet in turn. Those monks gave him a recitation lesson of two words. In time, through recitation, that pair of words was mastered by him. Then, at the last watch of the night, at the break of dawn, this occurred to the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>: "The <s>Bhagavat</s> said thus: '<s>rajo harāmi</s>' (I remove dust), '<s>malaṃ harāmi</s>' (I remove stain). Does the <s>Bhagavat</s> speak referring to internal dust or to external dust?" As he was reflecting thus, at that very moment, three verses never heard before came forth from his lips: "'Dust' here means <s>rāga</s> (passion), not physical dust; 'dust' is a designation for <s>rāga</s>, not for particles of dirt. The wise who are not heedless in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) dispel this dust." (3)

body.text: 431.030. rajo 'tra dveṣo na hi reṇureṣa rajo dveṣasyādhivacanaṃ na reṇoḥ/
body.translated_text: "'Dust' here means <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), not physical dust; 'dust' is a designation for <s>dveṣa</s>, not for particles of dirt."

body.text: 432.001. <432>etadrajaḥ prativinudanti paṇḍitā na ye pramattāḥ sugatasya śāsane//4//
body.translated_text: "The wise who are not heedless in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) dispel this dust." (4)

body.text:
432.003. rajo 'tra moho na hi reṇureṣa rajo mohasyādhivacanaṃ na reṇoḥ/
432.005. etadrajaḥ prativinudanti paṇḍitā na ye pramattāaḥ sugatasya śāsane//5//
body.translated_text: "'Dust' here means <s>moha</s> (delusion), not physical dust; 'dust' is a designation for <s>moha</s>, not for particles of dirt. The wise who are not heedless in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) dispel this dust." (5)

body.text:
432.007. tenodyacchamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
432.008. arhan saṃvṛttas traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhaḥ/
432.010. sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ mānyaśca pūjyaścābhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
432.010. dhyāne niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmatā mahāpanthakena dṛṣṭaḥ/
432.011. asamanvāhṛtyārhatāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate/
432.011. sa tena bāhau gṛhītvoktah--āgaccha svādhyāyinikāṃ tāvatkuru, tataḥ paścāddhyāyiṣyasīti/
432.012. athāyuṣmatā panthakena sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, gajabhujasadṛśo bāhurutsṛṣṭaḥ/
432.013. āyuṣmatā mahāpanthakena pṛṣṭato mukhaṃ vyavalokayatā dṛṣṭaḥ/
432.014. sa kathayati--āyuṣman panthaka, evaṃ te tvayā guṇagaṇā adhigatāh? adhigatāḥ//
body.translated_text: By him, striving, exerting, and endeavoring, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship) was directly realized. He became an <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), free from passion toward the three realms of existence, equal-minded toward clods of earth and gold, regarding space and the palm of the hand as equal, like sandalwood and an axe alike, with the eggshell of ignorance split open by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), having attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural powers), and <s>pratisaṃvits</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from attachment to existence, gain, honor, and reverence. He became worthy of respect, worship, and salutation by the <s>devas</s> (gods) including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Seated in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he was seen by the venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>. Not having considered that he had attained the knowledge and vision of an <s>Arhat</s>, he seized him by the arm and said: "Come, first do your recitation lesson; you can meditate afterward." Then the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, having directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, released the arm that was like the trunk of an elephant. The venerable <s>Mahāpanthaka</s>, looking back at his face, saw him. He said: "Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, have such multitudes of virtues been attained by you?" "They have been attained."

body.text:
432.016. yadā āyuṣmatā panthakena sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, anyatīrthikā avadhyāyanti dhriyanti vivācayanti/
432.017. śramaṇo gautama evamāha--gambhīro me dharmo gambhīrāvabhāso durdṛśo durnubodho 'tarko 'tarkāvacaraḥ, sūkṣumo nipuṇapaṇḍitavijñavedanīyaḥ/
432.018. atredānīṃ kiṃ gambhīro 'sya, yasyedānīṃ panthakaprabhṛtayaścūḍāḥ paramacūḍā dhanvāḥ paramadhanvāḥ pravrajanti/
432.020. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--sumeruprakhye mahāśrāvake mahājanakāyaḥ kṣāntiṃ gṛhṇāti/
432.020. guṇodbhāvanā asya kartavyā/
432.021. tatra bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--gaccha ānanda, panthakasya kathaya--bhikṣuṇyaste avavaditavyā iti/
432.022. evaṃ bhadantetyāyuṣmānānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yenāyuṣmān panthakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
432.023. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ panthakamidamavocat--śāstā tvāmāyuṣman panthaka evamāha--bhikṣuṇyaste avavaditavyā iti/
432.024. āyuṣmān panthakaḥ kathayati--kimarthaṃ sthavirasthavirān bhikṣūnapahāya māṃ bhagavān bhikṣuṇyavavādakamājñāpayati? mamaiva guṇodbhāvanā kartavyeti śāsturmanorathaṃ paripūrayiṣyāmīti/
432.026. bhikṣuṇyaśchandahānisah(?) jetavanamāgatāḥ/
432.027. tā bhikṣūn pṛcchanti--bhagavatā ko 'smākamavavādaka ājñaptah? te kathayanti--āyuṣmān panthakaḥ/
432.028. tāḥ kathayanti--bhaginyaḥ, paśyata kathaṃ mātṛgrāmaḥ paribhūtaḥ/
432.028. yena tribhirmāsairekā gāthā paṭhitā, sāpi na pravṛttā/
432.029. bhikṣuṇyastripiṭā dhārmakathikā yuktamuktapratibhānāḥ/
432.030. sa kila bhikṣuṇīravavadiṣyatīti/
432.030. tāḥ parṣadamāgatā bhikṣuṇībhiḥ pṛṣṭāh--bhaginyaḥ, ko 'smākamavavaditumāgamiṣyati? tāḥ kathayanti--āryapanthakaḥ/
432.031. kimāryo mahāpanthakah? na hyayam, sa tvanyaścūḍāpanthakaḥ/
432.032. dvādaśavargīyābhiḥ śrutam/
432.032. tāvadavadhyāyanti/
body.translated_text: When <s>Arhattva</s> (Arhatship) was directly realized by the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the heretics of other sects spoke ill of him, persisted, and disputed: "The <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) <s>Gautama</s> says thus: 'My <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) is profound, of profound appearance, hard to see, hard to comprehend, beyond reasoning, not within the range of reasoning, subtle, to be known only by the wise, the skilled, the learned.' Now what is profound about this, when nowadays the likes of <s>Panthaka</s> — dullards, utter dullards, fools, utter fools — go forth?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) considered: "Toward the great disciple, lofty as <s>Sumeru</s>, the great multitude of people takes offense. His virtues must be made manifest." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, tell <s>Panthaka</s>: 'You are to admonish the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns).'" "So be it, Venerable Sir," the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, assenting to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approached the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>: "The Teacher says this to you, Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>: 'You are to admonish the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>.'" The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> said: "Why does the <s>Bhagavān</s> pass over the elder and senior <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and command me as instructor of the nuns? It is my own virtues that are to be made manifest — I shall fulfill the Teacher's wish." The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, without loss of resolve, came to the <s>Jetavana</s>. They asked the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Whom has the <s>Bhagavān</s> appointed as our instructor?" They said: "The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>." They said: "Sisters, look how womankind is held in contempt! He who in three months recited a single verse, and even that did not succeed — and yet the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> are versed in the <s>Tripiṭaka</s> (Three Baskets), <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, with apt and fluent eloquence — and he, it seems, is to admonish the nuns!" The twelve-group nuns (<s>dvādaśavargīyāḥ</s>) heard this and took offense to that extent.

body.text:
433.001. <433>bhaginyaḥ paśyata, kathaṃ mātṛgrāmaḥ paribhūtah? yena tribhirmāsairekā gāthā paṭhitā, sāpi na pravṛttā/
433.002. imā bhikṣuṇyastripiṭā dharmakathikā yuktamuktapratibhānāḥ, sa kila kimāsāmavavadiṣyatīti? tāḥ kathayanti--bhaginyaḥ, ṣaḍjanyo dvādaśahastikābhirlatābhiḥ siṃhāsanaṃ prajñapayantu/
433.004. ṣaḍjanyaḥ śrāvastyāṃ praviśya rathya rathyāvīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣvārocayantu--so 'smākaṃ tādṛśo 'vavādaka āgamiṣyati, yo 'smākaṃ tanusatyāni na drakṣyati/
433.005. tena saṃsāre ciraṃ vastavyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
433.006. yena na kaścit putramoṭikāputro 'lpaśruta utsahate bhikṣuṇīravavaditum/
433.007. tāsāṃ ṣaḍbhir janībhir dvādaśahastikābhir latābhiḥ saṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptam, ṣaḍbhikṣuṇībhiḥ śrāvastīṃ praviśya rathyāvīthicatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣvārocitam--so 'smākaṃ tādṛśo 'vavādaka āgamiṣyati, yo 'smākaṃ tanusatyāni na drakṣyati/
433.009. tena saṃsāre ciraṃ vastavyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti/
433.010. āyuṣmān panthakaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
433.011. kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktāpiṇḍapātrapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamayya pādau prakṣālya vihāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ pratisamlayanāya/
433.012. athāyuṣmān panthakaḥ sāyāhne pratisamlayanāya vyutthāya saṃghāṭīmādāya anyatamena bhikṣuṇā paścāccramaṇena saṃprasthitaḥ/
433.013. anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi--kāni ca kutūhalajātāni, kānicit pūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni/
433.014. adrākṣīt sā pariṣat āyuṣmantaṃ panthakaṃ dūrādeva/
433.015. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ parasparaṃ pṛcchati--kataro 'tra bhikṣuṇyavavādakah? kiṃ puraḥśramaṇaḥ, āhosvit paścācchramaṇah? tatraike kathayanti--puraḥśramaṇaḥ/
433.016. te 'vadhyāyitumārabdhāh--paśyata bhadanta, saṃcintya vayaṃ bhikṣuṇībhirviheṭhitāḥ/
433.017. yena tribhirmāsairekā gāthā paṭhitā, sāpi na pravṛttā, sa kiṃ bhikṣuṇīravavadiṣyati, dharmaṃ vā vācayiṣyati? gacchāmaḥ/
433.019. apare kathayanti--tiṣṭhāmo yadi dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati, śroṣyāmaḥ/
433.019. atha na, gacchāmaḥ/
433.019. iti sā parṣat samavasthitā/
433.020. āyuṣmatā panthakena siṃhāsanaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ prajñaptakaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ tāvat prasādajātābhiḥ prajñaptamāhosvit viheṭhanābhiprāyābhih? paśyati--yāvat viheṭhanābhiprayābhiḥ/
433.020. dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ tāvat prasādajātābhiḥ prajñaptamāhosvit viheṭhanābhiprasāyābhih? paśyati--yāvat viheṭhanābhiprāyābhiḥ/
433.022. āyuṣmatā panthakena gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya taṃ siṃhāsanam yathāsthāne sthāpitam/
433.023. āyuṣmān panthakastatra niṣaṇṇaḥ/
433.023. sa niṣīdan kaiścit dṛṣṭah. kaiścit na dṛṣṭaḥ/
433.024. athātrastha āyuṣmān panthakastadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte sve āsane 'ntarhitaḥ, pūrvasyāṃ diśi uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya pūrvavat yāvat ṛddhiprātihāryāṇi vidarśya tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
433.026. niṣadya āyuṣmān panthakastā bhikṣuṇīrāmantrayate--mayā bhaginyastribhirmāsairekā gāthā paṭhitā/
433.027. utsahetavyāni(?) śrotumekagāthāyāḥ saptarātriṃdivasānyanyaiḥ padairvyañjanairarthaṃ vibhaktum?
433.029. pāpaṃ na kuryānmanasā na vācā kāyena vā kiṃcana sarvaloke/
433.031. riktaḥ kāmeiḥ smṛtimān saṃprajānan duḥkhaṃ na sa vidyādanarthopasaṃhitam//6//iti/
body.translated_text: "Sisters, look at how womankind has been insulted! He who in three months studied one verse, and even that did not succeed — these <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) are learned in the <s>Tripiṭaka</s> (Three Baskets), skilled <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, with ready and apt eloquence — what indeed will he teach them?" They said: "Sisters, let six women prepare a lion-seat with creepers twelve arm-lengths high. Let six women enter <s>Śrāvastī</s> and announce in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads: 'Such an instructor is coming to us, one who will not even perceive our subtle truths. Because of him, one will have to dwell long in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). So that no son of a slave-woman's son, of little learning, will dare to instruct the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns).'" By six women a lion-seat was prepared with creepers twelve arm-lengths high; by six <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), having entered <s>Śrāvastī</s>, it was announced in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads: "Such an instructor is coming to us, one who will not even perceive our subtle truths. Because of him, one will have to dwell long in <s>saṃsāra</s>." The venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Having finished his meal, having returned from the after-meal alms-round, having put away his bowl and robe, having washed his feet, he entered the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) for seclusion. Then the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, having risen from seclusion in the afternoon, having taken up his outer robe, set out accompanied by a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) as an attendant following behind. Many hundreds of thousands of beings — some born of curiosity, some impelled by previous roots of merit — that assembly saw the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> from afar. Having seen him, they asked one another: "Which one here is the instructor of the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns)? Is it the one walking in front, or the one walking behind?" Some among them said: "The one in front." They began to murmur disapprovingly: "Look, venerable sirs, we have been deliberately harassed by the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>. He who in three months studied one verse, and even that did not succeed — will he instruct the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, or teach the <s>Dharma</s>? Let us go." Others said: "Let us stay — if he will teach the <s>Dharma</s>, we shall listen. If not, we shall go." Thus that assembly remained assembled. The venerable <s>Panthaka</s> saw the lion-seat that had been prepared; having seen it, he considered: "Was this prepared by those who have faith, or by those with the intention of harassment?" He perceived: "It was by those with the intention of harassment." The venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, extending his arm resembling an elephant's trunk, placed that lion-seat in its proper position. The venerable <s>Panthaka</s> sat down upon it. As he sat down, he was seen by some and not seen by others. Then the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, seated there, entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) that, with his mind composed, he vanished from his own seat, rose up into the sky in the eastern direction, and as before displayed various <s>ṛddhi-prātihārya</s> (miraculous feats of supernatural power), then, having relaxed those supernatural transformations, sat down again on that very prepared seat. Having sat down, the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> addressed those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns): "Sisters, by me in three months one verse was studied. Can you endure to hear the meaning of that one verse expounded with different words and expressions for seven days and nights? 'One should not commit evil by mind, nor by speech, nor by body — nothing at all in the entire world. Empty of desires, mindful and clearly comprehending, one should not pursue suffering connected with what is harmful.'" (6)

body.text:
434.001. <434>sarvapāpasya bhagavān kāraṇamāha--yāvadgāthārthasyārthamadhītam yāti, tāvad dvādaśabhiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ satyāni dṛṣṭāni/
434.002. kaiścicchrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam, kaiścidanāgāmiphalam, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittānyutpāditāni/
434.005. yadbhūyasā sā pariṣad buddhaniṃnādharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā/
434.006. athāyuṣmān panthakastāṃ pariṣadaṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣyotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ/
434.007. sa bhikṣubhirāgacchan dṛṣṭaḥ/
434.007. te saṃlakṣayanti--adyāyuṣmatā panthakena mahājanakāyaḥ prasādito bhaviṣyati/
434.008. te na ṣaknuvantyāyuṣmantaṃ panthakaṃ saṃmukhamapriyaṃ praṣṭum/
434.008. taiḥ paścācchramaṇaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ/
434.009. āyuṣman, adya āyuṣmatā panthakena kiṃ mahājanakāyo na prasādito vā prasāditah? āyuṣmatā na kaścit aprasāditaḥ/
434.010. bhagavatā vārāṇasyām ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāraṃ dharmyaṃ cakraṃ pravartitam, tadadyāyuṣmatā panthakenānupravartitam/
434.011. yāvadgāthārthaṃ na vibhajati, tāvad dvādaśabhiḥ praṇisahasraiḥ satyāni dṛṣṭāni//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) explained the cause of all evil: as long as the meaning of the verse's meaning was being expounded, twelve thousand beings perceived the truths. By some, the fruit of <s>Srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry) was directly realized; by some, the fruit of <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning); by some, the fruit of <s>Anāgāmin</s> (non-returning); by some, having gone forth, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat) was directly realized; by some, minds were set upon <s>Śrāvaka-bodhi</s> (the awakening of a disciple); by some, upon <s>Pratyeka-bodhi</s> (solitary awakening); by some, minds were set upon <s>Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). For the most part, that assembly stood inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Then the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted that assembly with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed. He was seen by the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) as he arrived. They considered: "Today the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> must have pleased the great multitude." They were unable to ask the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> anything unpleasant to his face. So they asked the attendant monk who followed behind: "Venerable one, today did the venerable <s>Panthaka</s> please the great multitude or not?" "There was no one not pleased by the venerable one. The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at the Deer Park in <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>, turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of three turnings and twelve aspects — that has today been set in motion again by the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>. As long as he expounded the meaning of the verse, twelve thousand beings perceived the truths."

body.text:
434.013. tatra bhagavāan bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikcūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ cetovivartakuśalānām yaduta panthako bhikṣuḥ/
434.014. bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--paśya bhadanta dvādaśavargīyābhirāyuṣmataḥ panthakasyānarthaṃ kariṣyāmi ityatha eva kṛtaḥ/
434.015. bhagavānāha--na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'pyadhvani ābhiranarthaṃ kariṣyāma ityartha eva kṛtaḥ/
434.016. tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks): "This one, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, is the foremost among my <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) disciples who are skilled in <s>cetovivarta</s> (mental transformation), namely the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Panthaka</s>." The <s>bhikṣus</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One): "Look, Venerable Sir, the group of twelve <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) said 'We shall bring harm to the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>,' and yet the very opposite was accomplished." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Not only now, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, but in the past as well, they said 'We shall bring harm to him,' and yet the very opposite was accomplished. Listen to that story."

body.text:
434.017. bhūtapūrvamevaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake brāhmaṇaḥ prativasati/
434.017. tena sadṛśātkulātkalatramānītam/
434.018. sa tayā sardhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati/
434.018. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato bhūyaḥ krīḍati ramate paricārayati yāvar dvādaśa putrā jātāḥ/
434.019. tena teṣāṃ niveśaḥ kṛtaḥ/
434.020. apareṇa samayena tasya patnī kālagatā/
434.020. so 'pi brāhmaṇo vṛddhāvasthāyāṃ jātaḥ/
434.020. andhībhūtasya snaṣā duścāriṇyaḥ/
434.021. yadā tāsāṃ svāmino bahir nirgatā bhavanti, tadā tāḥ parapuruṣaiḥ sārdhaṃ paricārayanti/
434.022. sa brāhmaṇaḥ śabde kṛtāvī/
434.022. sa jānāti--ayaṃ mama putrasya śabdaḥ, ayaṃ parapuruṣayeti/
434.023. sa puruṣāṇāṃ padaśabdāñ śrutvā tāḥ snuṣā garjayati.
434.023. tāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--ayaṃ brāhmaṇp^smākamanarthāya pratipannaḥ/
434.024. tāstasya cakaṭyodanaṃ kāñjitakacchiṭiṃ cānuprayacchanti/
434.026. taistā uktāh--kiṃ kāraṇam yūyaṃ tātasya cakaṭyodanaṃ kāñjikacchiṭiṃ cānuprayacchata? tāḥ kathayanti--tasya puṇyāni parikṣīṇāni, asyārthe piparīkāyāṃ ta:ḍulāḥ prakṣiptā bhavanti, cakaṭyodanaṃ parivartate, dadhi prakṣiptaṃ kāñjikaṃ parivartate/
434.028. te kathayanti--kimetadevaṃ bhaviṣyati? tāḥ kathayanti--vayam yuṣmākaṃ pratyakṣīkariṣyāmaḥ/
434.029. tāḥ kathayanti--asmābhiḥ pratijñātamidānīṃ nirvoḍhavyam/
434.030. tābhiḥ kumbhakāara uktah--śakṣyasi tvaṃ bhadramukham ekamukhike dve sthālyau kartum? sa kathayati--śakṣyāmi/
434.031. tenaikamukhike dve sthālyau kṛte/
434.031. tābhirekasyāṃ sthālyāṃ cakaṭitaṇḍulāḥ prakṣiptāḥ, dvitīyāyāṃ kāñjikam/
434.032. tābhiḥ svāmināṃ purastādekasya <435>sthālyāṃ taṇḍulāḥ prakṣiptā ekasyāṃ dadhi/
body.translated_text: In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), in a certain small town there lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (brahmin). He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He played with her, enjoyed her company, and lived intimately with her. As he played, enjoyed, and lived intimately with her, again and again he played, enjoyed, and lived intimately until twelve sons were born. He arranged their marriages. After some time, his wife passed away. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> too reached old age. When he became blind, his daughters-in-law were unchaste. Whenever their husbands went out, they would consort with other men. That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was skilled in recognizing sounds. He knew: "This is the sound of my son, this is that of another man." Hearing the footsteps of the men, he would scold those daughters-in-law. They considered: "This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is set on bringing us harm." They gave him rice mixed with chaff and the dregs of sour gruel. Their husbands said to them: "Why do you give father rice mixed with chaff and the dregs of sour gruel?" They replied: "His merit is exhausted. When rice is put in the pot for his sake, it turns into rice mixed with chaff; when yogurt is put in, it turns into sour gruel." They said: "Will it really be so?" The daughters-in-law said: "We will demonstrate it before your eyes." They said: "We have made a promise; now it must be carried out." They told a potter: "Can you, good sir, make two cooking vessels with a single opening?" He replied: "I can." He made two cooking vessels with a single opening. In one vessel they placed rice mixed with chaff, in the other sour gruel. Then, before their husbands' eyes, into one vessel rice was placed, and into the other yogurt.

body.text:
435.001. tābhiḥ sādhitam/
435.001. kathayanti--āryaputrasya kiṃ tāvattātastatprathamataḥ paribhuktāmāhosvit yūyam/
435.002. te kathayanti--tātastāvatparibhuktām/
435.003. tābhisteṣāṃ purastāttasyaukasyāḥ sthālyā uddhṛtya cakaṭyodanaṃ dattaṃ dvitīyāyāḥ kañjikam/
435.004. tata evaṃ tābhisteṣāmekasyāḥ sthālyā uddhṛtya śālyodanaṃ dattaṃ dvitīyāyā dadhi uddhṛtam/
435.004. te tasya kathayanti--tāta, tava puṇyāni parikṣīṇāni/
435.005. yata ekasyāṃ sthālyāṃ śālitaṇḍulāḥ prakṣiptāḥ, dvitīyasyāṃ dadhi, taccakaṭyodanaṃ kāñjikaṃ ca parivṛttam/
435.006. brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--mayā hastocchrayaśatairbhogāḥ samudānītāḥ/
435.007. kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mama puṇyāni parikṣīṇāni? tena tāsāmapratyakṣaṃ mahānasaṃ praviśya paryeṣamāṇena hastasaṃspatśenaikamukhe dve sthālyau labdhe/
435.008. tena gopāyite/
435.009. tena etṣāṃ putrāṇāmāgatānāṃ te pradarśite--paśyata, mama puṇyāni parikṣīṇāni/
435.010. gatvā paśyadhvamasmākaṃ gṛha eva ekamukhī sthālī/
435.010. putraka, anyeṣu geheṣu na shālīdvayaṃ tvakamukhamasmākaṃ mandabhāgyānām/
435.011. taistāḥ patnyaḥ sutāḍitāḥ/
435.011. tāḥ saṃlakṣayanti--ayaṃ brāhmaṇo 'smākamanarthāya pratipannakaḥ//
body.translated_text: By them it was accomplished. They said: "Of our noble lord, which did the father first partake of, or did you?" They said: "The father partook first." Before them, taking from one of those pots, she gave him coarse rice, and from the second, gruel. Then likewise, taking from one pot, she gave them fine rice, and from the second she took curds. They said to him: "Father, your merits are exhausted. Since in one pot fine rice grains were placed and in the second curds, that has turned into coarse rice and gruel." The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (brahmin) considered: "By the hundreds of efforts of my hands I gathered these enjoyments. What is the reason my merits are exhausted?" Then, unseen by them, entering the kitchen and searching, by the touch of his hand he found two pots with a single mouth. He hid them. When his sons came, he showed them to them: "Look, my merits are exhausted. Go and see — in our very house there is a single-mouthed pot. Son, in other houses there is no double pot; ours, the unlucky ones', is single-mouthed." By them those wives were beaten severely. They considered: "This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has set himself to our ruin."

body.text:
435.012. praghātayāma iti/
435.012. tena ca pradeśenāhituṇḍika āgataḥ/
435.013. tāḥ pṛcchanti--asti sarpa iti? sa kathayati--kīdṛśaṃ sarpaṃ mṛgayatha jīvantamāhosvit mṛtakamiti? tāḥ kathayanti--mṛtakam/
435.014. sa saṃlakṣayati--kemetā mṛtakena sarpeṇa kariṣyanti? nūnametā etaṃ vṛddhaṃ mārayitukāmā bhaviṣyanti/
435.015. dharmatā khalu sarpasya ruṣitasya dvayoḥ sthānayorviṣaṃ saṃkrāmati--śirasi pucche ca/
435.016. tena roṣitvā śiraḥ pucchaṃ svayaṃ chittvā tāsāṃ madhye sarpā dattaḥ/
435.017. tābhirjomāṃ sādhayitvā sa brāhmaṇa uktah--tāta, hilimāṃ joma pāsyasi? sa brāhmaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kimetā me hilimāṃ jomāṃ dāsyanti? nūnaṃ kiṃcit abhaiṣajyaṃ dattaṃ bhaviṣyati/
435.019. sa saṃlakṣayati--pibāmi, yathā ca tathā marāmi/
435.019. tābhistasya hilimā jomā dattā/
435.020. tena pītā/
435.020. tasya bāṣpeṇa paṭale sphuṭite/
435.020. sa draṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
435.020. sa nipatyāvasthitaḥ/
435.021. kathayati ca--marāmi marāmīti/
435.021. tāḥ kathayanti--śīghraṃ mā pātu/
435.021. tāḥ kathayanti--tāta, bhūyaḥ pāsyasi? sa kathayati--pāsyāmīti/
435.022. tābhistasya bhūyo hilimā jomā dattā/
435.023. tena bhūyaḥ pītā/
435.023. tasya tena bāṣpeṇa bhūyasyā mātrayā paṭale sphuṭite/
435.023. sa spaṣṭataraṃ draṣṭumārabdhaḥ/
435.024. tāḥ pūrvam yathā tasyāndhasya tato viśvastā vihṛtavantyastathaiva vihartumārabdhāḥ/
435.025. sa daṇḍaṃ gṛhītvā utthitaḥ/
435.025. kathayati ca--kim yūyaṃ jānītha idānīmapyahaṃ na paśyāmi? paśyāmyahamidānīmiti/
435.026. tāḥ salajjā niṣpalāyitāḥ//
body.translated_text: "Let us have him killed." And by that road a snake-charmer (<s>āhituṇḍika</s>) came along. They asked him, "Do you have a snake?" He replied, "What kind of snake are you looking for — a living one or a dead one?" They said, "A dead one." He thought to himself, "What will these women do with a dead snake? Surely they must want to kill this old man." Now it is a natural law that when a snake is angered, its venom concentrates in two places — in the head and in the tail. So, having angered the snake, he himself cut off the head and tail and gave the snake to those women. They prepared a broth from it and said to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, "Father, will you drink this broth?" The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> thought to himself, "Why would they give me broth? Surely they must have put some poison in it." He thought, "I shall drink it; however it turns out, let me die." They gave him the broth, and he drank it. From the steam, the films over his eyes burst open, and he began to see. He fell down and lay there, crying out, "I am dying, I am dying!" They said, "Let him drink it quickly!" They said, "Father, will you drink more?" He replied, "I will drink." They gave him more broth, and he drank again. From that steam, the films over his eyes burst open even more, and he began to see even more clearly. Those women, just as before when he was blind they had carried on freely trusting that he could not see, began to carry on in the same way again. He seized his staff and stood up, saying, "Do you think that even now I cannot see? I can see now!" They fled away in shame.

body.text:
435.027. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ/
435.027. yo 'sau brāhmaṇaḥ, eṣa evāsau panthakastena kālena tena samayena/
435.028. yāstāstasya dvādaśa snuṣāḥ, etā eva tā dvādaśavargīyāḥ/
435.028. tadāpyābhirasyānarthaṃ kariṣyāma ityartha eva kṛtaḥ/
435.029. etarhyapi ābhirasyānarthaṃ kariṣyāma ityartham eva kṛtaḥ//
body.translated_text: What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)? That <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — he was none other than <s>Panthaka</s> at that time, in that era. And those twelve daughters-in-law of his — they are none other than the <s>dvādaśavargīyāḥ</s> (group of twelve nuns). Even then, thinking "let us do him harm," they accomplished the very opposite. And even now, thinking "let us do him harm," they have accomplished the very opposite.

body.text:
435.030. bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--paśya bhadanta bhagavatā āyuṣmān panthakaḥ parīttenāvavādenācodya saṃsārakāntārāduttārya atyantaniṣṭhe anuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭāpitaḥ/
435.032. bhagavānāha--na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'pyadhvanyeṣo mayā parīttenāvavādenācodya mahatyaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ/
435.033. tacchrayatām//
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One): "Behold, Venerable Sir! The <s>Bhagavān</s> has, with just a brief admonition, exhorted the venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, brought him across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), and established him in the ultimate, supreme <s>yogakṣema</s> (security from bondage) — <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation)." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Not only now, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, but in the past as well, I exhorted him with just a brief admonition and established him in great sovereignty and lordship. Listen to that story."

body.text:
436.001. <436>bhūtabhūtaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin kartavaṭake gṛhapariḥ prativasati āḍyo sahādhano mahābhogaḥ/
436.002. tena sadṛśātkulātkalatramānītam/
436.002. sa tayā sārdhaṃ trīṭati ramate paticārayati/
436.002. tasya putro jātaḥ/
436.003. sa parnīmāmantrayate--bhadre, jāto 'smākam ṛṇaharaḥ/
436.003. gacchāmi, ahaṃ paṇyamādāya mahāsamudramavatarāmi/
436.004. sā āha--evaṃ kuruṣva/
436.004. sa gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati--yadahamasyai prabhūtānaṃ kārṣāpaṇān dāsyāmi, parapuruṣaiḥ sārdhaṃ vihariṣyati/
436.005. tena tasyāḥ kārṣāpaṇā na dattāḥ/
436.006. tasmin karpaṭake śreṣṭhī prativasati tasya gṛhapatervayasyaḥ/
436.006. tasya haste prabhūtāḥ kārṣāpaṇāḥ sthāpitāh--yadi mama patnyā bhaktācchādena yogodvahanaṃ kuryāḥ/
436.007. sa paṇyamādāya mahāsamudramavatīrṇaḥ/
436.008. tarraivānayena vyasanamāpannah.
436.008. tayā sa dārako jñātibakena svahastabalena vā āyāpitā(payitvā) pālito vardhitaḥ/
436.009. sa mātaraṃ pṛcchati--amba, kimasmākaṃ pitā pitāmahāśca karmākārṣuh? sā saṃlakṣayati--yadyasya vakṣyāmi mahāsamudre potasaṃvyavahāriṇa āsann iti, sthānametadvidyate yadeṣo 'pi mahāsamudramavatariṣyatīti, tatraiva anayena vyasanamāpatsyate/
436.011. śrutamāhitastava putā ca pitāmahāśca ihaiva vāṇijyamakārṣuḥ/
436.012. sa kathayati--kārṣāpaṇān mamānuprayaccha, yairihaiva vāṇijyaṃ kariṣyāmi/
436.013. mātā kathayati--kuto mama kārṣāpaṇāh? tvaṃ mayā kathaṃcit jñātibalena svahastabakena āyāpitaḥ poṣitaḥ saṃvardhitaḥ/
436.014. kuto me kārṣāpaṇānāṃ vibhavah? api tvayaṃ śroṣṭī tava pitṛvayasyo bhavati/
436.015. asya sakāśāt kārṣāpaṇān gṛhītvā karma kuru/
436.016. sa tasya gṛhaṃ gataḥ/
436.016. tasyānyatamena puruṣeṇa yāvat dvirapi vināśitaḥ/
436.017. sa tamavasādayati/
436.017. tasya ca gṛhāt preṣyadārikāyāḥ saṃkāratalasyopari mṛtamūṣikāṃ dṛṣṭvā prayacchati cchorayitum/
436.018. sa śreṣṭhī tasya puruṣasya kathayati--yaḥ puruṣaḥ syāt, śakyate anayā mṛtamūṣikayā ātmānamuddhartum/
436.019. tena dārakeṇa śrutam/
436.019. sa saṃlakṣayati--mahātmaiṣaḥ/
436.019. na śakyamanena yadvā tadvā vaktum/
436.020. nūnaṃ śakyamanayā mṛtamūṣikayā ātmānamuddhartum/
436.020. sa tasyā dārikāyāḥ pṛṣṭhato nirgataḥ/
436.021. tayā dātikayā saṃkāre choritā/
436.021. sa tāṃ mṛtamūṣikāmādāya vīthīṃ gataḥ/
436.022. tatra vāṇijako biḍākena krīḍitvā sthitaḥ/
436.022. tena tasya biḍālasya mṛtamūṣikā darśitā/
436.023. sa tāṃdṛṣṭvā utpatitumārabdhaḥ/
436.023. tena vāṇijakena dāraka ucyate--anuprayaccha asya biḍālasya mṛtamūṣikām/
436.024. sa kathayati--kimayaṃ kalikayā dīyate? mūlyamanuprayaccha/
436.025. tena tasya kalāyānāmañjalipūroo dattaḥ/
436.025. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadyetān bhakṣayiṣyāmi, mūlameva bbhikṣitaṃ bhaviṣyati/
436.026. sa tān bhrāṣṭre bharjayitvā śītalasya pānīyasya vardhanīyasya pūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadgṛhya tasmātsthānakānniṣkramya yasmin pradeśe kāṣṭhahārakā viśrāmyanti, tasmin pradeśe gatvāvasthitaḥ/
436.028. kāṣṭhahārakā āgatāḥ/
436.028. tenoktāh--mātulāḥ, arpayata kāṣṭhabhārakāḥ, muhūrtaṃ viśrāmyatām/
436.029. taiḥ kāṣṭhabhārāḥ sthipitāḥ/
436.029. tena teṣāṃ kalāyānāṃ stoktaṃ dattaṃ śītalaṃ ca pānīyaṃ pātam/
436.030. te kathayanti--bhāgineya, kva yāsyasi? kāṣṭhānām/
436.030. bhāgineya, vayaṃ tāvat kalyamevotthāya gatvā idānīmāgacchāmaḥ/
436.031. tvamidānīṃ gacchan kiyatā āgamiṣyasi? taistasyaikaikaṃ kāṣṭhamanupradattam/
436.032. tasya kāṣṭhamūlikā saṃpannā/
436.032. sa tāṃ gṛhītvā pratinivṛttaḥ/
436.032. sa tāṃ vikrīya <437>kalāyānāṃ gṛhītvā bharjayitvā udakasya kumbhaṃ pūrayitvā tasminneva praveśe gatvāvasthitaḥ/
body.translated_text: In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), in a certain small town there lived a householder, prosperous, with great wealth and great enjoyments. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He played, rejoiced, and lived intimately with her. A son was born to him. He said to his wife: "Good lady, a debt-remover has been born to us. I shall go, take goods, and set out upon the great ocean." She said: "Do so." The householder considered: "If I give her abundant <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), she will consort with other men." So he did not give her the <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>. In that town there lived a <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-master), a friend of that householder. In his hands he deposited abundant <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>: "If you would maintain my wife with food and clothing, support her." He took goods and set out upon the great ocean. There, through misfortune, he met with calamity. By her that boy was reared and brought up by the strength of kinsmen or by the strength of her own hands. He asked his mother: "Mother, what work did our father and grandfather do?" She considered: "If I tell him that they were sea-faring traders on the great ocean, it is possible that he too would set out upon the great ocean, and there through misfortune meet with calamity." "It is heard, my son, that your father and grandfather carried on trade right here." He said: "Give me <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), with which I shall carry on trade right here." The mother said: "Whence have I <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>? You were somehow reared and supported and brought up by me by the strength of kinsmen and the strength of my own hands. Whence the wealth of <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> for me? But this <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-master) is your father's friend. Take <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> from him and do work." He went to his house. By some man of his he was twice ruined. He despaired of him. And from his house, seeing a dead mouse upon a heap of refuse, a servant girl was about to throw it away. The <s>śreṣṭhin</s> said to that man: "A man who is capable could lift himself up by this dead mouse." The boy heard this. He considered: "This is a great man. He would not say just anything. Surely one can lift oneself up by this dead mouse." He went out behind that servant girl. The girl threw it onto the refuse heap. He took that dead mouse and went into the street. There a trader stood, playing with a cat. He showed the dead mouse to that cat. Seeing it, the cat began to leap up. The trader said to the boy: "Give the dead mouse to this cat." He said: "Is this given for nothing? Pay the price." He gave him a handful of peas. He considered: "If I eat these, the capital itself will be eaten up." So he roasted them in a pan, filled a jar with cool, refreshing water, took it, went out from that place, and went and stood in a place where the woodcutters rest. The woodcutters came. He said to them: "Uncles, set down your loads of wood; rest a moment." They set down their loads of wood. He gave them a little of those peas and cool water to drink. They said: "Nephew, where will you go? For wood." "Nephew, we, having risen at dawn and gone, now return." "How far will you go now in coming?" Each of them gave him one piece of wood. His stock of wood was complete. He took it and returned. Having sold it, he took peas, roasted them, filled a jar with water, and went and stood in that very entrance.

body.text:
437.002. te kāṣṭhahārakāstathaiva tena kalāyaiḥ saṃvibhaktāḥ, śītalena pānīyena saṃtarpitāḥ/
437.002. te tasya kathayati--bhāgineya, divase divase tvaṃ kalāyān pānīyaṃ ca gṛhītvā āgamya atraiva tiṣṭham/
437.004. vayaṃ tavopari kāṣṭhamūlikāmānayiṣyāmaḥ/
437.004. sa divase divase tayaiva kartumārabdhaḥ/
437.004. sa teṣāṃ kathayati--mātula, mā yūyaṃ kāṣṭhabhārān vīrthāṃ nayatha/
437.005. mama gṛhe sthāpayata/
437.005. yuṣmākamevaṃ piṇḍitamūlyaṃ dāsyāmi/
437.006. taistasya gṛhe kāṣṭhabhārakāṇi sthāpitāḥ/
437.006. apareṇa samayena saptāhavardalikā jātāḥ/
437.007. tena tāni kāṣṭhabhārakāṇi vikrītāni/
437.007. tasya prabhūto lābhaḥ saṃpannaḥ/
437.008. sa saṃlakṣayati--etatpratikruṣṭataraṃ vāṇijyānām yaduta kāṣṭhavāṇijyam/
437.008. sa saṃlakṣayati--api candanakāṣṭhena kāṣṭhavāṇijyameva/
437.009. yannvahamukkarikāpaṇaṃ prasārayeyam/
437.009. tena ukkarikāpaṇaḥ prasāritaḥ/
437.010. sa dharmeṇa vyavaharati/
437.010. tasya tatprabhūto lābhaḥ sa saṃlakṣayati--etat pratikruṣṭataraṃ vāṇijyānām yaduta ukkarikāpaṇaḥ/
437.011. yannvahaṃ gāndhikāpaṇaṃ prasārayeyam/
437.012. tena gāndhikāpaṇaḥ prasāritaḥ/
437.012. tasya prabhūto lābhaḥ saṃpannaḥ/
437.012. sa saṃlakṣayati--etadapi pratikraṣṭataraṃ ca tadvāṇijyānāṃ pūrvavat/
437.013. tena sarve hairaṇyakā abhibhūtāḥ/
437.013. tasya mūṣikāhairaṇyako mūṣikāhairaṇyaka iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
437.014. te hairaṇyakāḥ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, sarve vayamanena mūṣikāhairaṇyakenābhibhūtāḥ/
437.015. vayamenaṃ mānaṃ prāhayāmaḥ, yathā mahāsamudramavataret tatraivānayena vyasanamāpatsyate tathā kariṣyāma iti/
437.016. te tasya nātidūre sthitvā svaiḥ kathāsamlāpena tiṣṭhanti--yathāpi nāma bhavantaḥ puruṣo hastigrīvāyāṃ gatvā aśvapṛṣṭhena gacchet, aśvapṛṭhena gatvā śibikāyāṃ gacchet, śibikāyāṃ gatvā padbhyāṃ gacchet, evamevāsya mūṣkikāhairaṇyikasya pitā ca pitāmahāśca samudre potasaṃvyavahātiṇa āsan/
437.019. eṣa idānīṃ kuṛcchreṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayati hairaṇyikāpaṇaṃ vāhayatīti/
437.020. śrutvā sa kathayati--kiṃ kathayata? te kathayanti--tava pitā ca pitāmahāśca potasaṃvyavahāriṇa āsan/
437.021. sa tvamidānīṃ kṛcchreṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayasi, hairaṇyikāpaṇaṃ vāhayasi? sa gṛhaṃ gatvā mātaraṃ pṛcchati--amba, satyamasmākaṃ pitā ca pitāmahāśca mahāsamudre petasaṃvyavahāriṇa āsan? sā saṃlakṣayati--nūnamanena kiṃcitkutaścit śrutaṃ syāt/
437.024. tadapratirūpaṃ syāt, yadahaṃ mṛṣāvādena vañcayeyam/
437.024. satyaṃ putra/
437.024. sa kathayati--anujānīṣva, ahamapi mahāsamudramavatariṣyāmi/
437.025. sā kathayati--putra, ihaiva tiṣṭha/
437.025. sa bhūyo bhūyaḥ kathayati--gacchāmi/
437.026. tasya nirbandhaṃ jñātvā anujñātaḥ/
437.026. tena ghaṇṭāvadhoṣaṇaṃ kṛtam--yo yuṣmākamutsahate mūṣikāhairaṇyena sārdhamaśulkenāgulmenātarapaṇyena mahāsamudramavataritum, sa mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānayatu/
437.028. pañcamātrairvaṇikśatairmahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānītam/
437.028. atha mūṣilāhairaṇyikaḥ kṛtamaṅgalakaitūhalasvastyayanaḥ śakaṭairbhārairmūṭaiḥ piṭakairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiḥ paṇyamāropya mahāsamudraṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
437.030. so 'nupūrveṇa mahāsamudramavatarannanuprāptaḥ/
437.030. te vaṇijo mahāsamudraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaītaḥ/
437.031. notsahante vahanamabhiroḍum/
437.031. sārthavāhaḥ karṇadhārasya kathayati--kathaya kathaya bhoḥ puruṣa yathābhūtaṃ mahāsamudrasya varṇam/
437.032ṭataḥ karṇadhāra uddhoṣayitumārabdhah--santyetasmin <438>mahāsamudre imānyevamrūpāṇi ratnāni tadyathā--maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāla rajatajātarūpamaśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitakā dakṣiṇāvartaḥ/
body.translated_text: Those woodcutters were likewise shared with by him with peas, and refreshed with cool water. They said to him: "Nephew, day after day you bring peas and water and stand right here. We shall bring a load of wood on your behalf." He began doing that very thing day after day. He said to them: "Uncles, do not carry the wood-loads in vain. Store them at my house. I will give you the lump-sum price." The wood-loads were stored at his house. After some time, a seven-day rainstorm occurred. He sold those wood-loads. His profit was abundant. He reflected: "This is the lowest of trades, namely the wood trade." He reflected: "Even dealing in sandalwood is still just wood trade. What if I should open a sugar-cake shop?" He opened a sugar-cake shop. He conducted business righteously. His profit from that was abundant. He reflected: "This too is a lowly trade, namely the sugar-cake shop. What if I should open a perfumer's shop?" He opened a perfumer's shop. His profit was abundant. He reflected: "This too is a lowly trade among trades, as before." He surpassed all the goldsmiths. He came to be known by the name <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s> (Mouse Goldsmith). Those goldsmiths said: "Sirs, we have all been surpassed by this <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s>. Let us send him a challenge, so that he descends into the great ocean and meets with disaster there — thus shall we act." They stood not far from him and spoke among themselves in conversation: "How indeed, sirs, a man who has ridden on an elephant's neck should then go on horseback, having gone on horseback should go in a palanquin, having gone in a palanquin should go on foot! Just so, this <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s>'s father and grandfathers were sea-vessel traders. He now ekes out a living with difficulty, running a goldsmith's shop." Hearing this, he said: "What are you saying?" They said: "Your father and grandfathers were sea-vessel traders. Yet you now eke out a living with difficulty, running a goldsmith's shop?" He went home and asked his mother: "Mother, is it true that our father and grandfathers were sea-vessel traders on the great ocean?" She reflected: "Surely he must have heard something from somewhere. It would be improper if I were to deceive him with falsehood." "It is true, son." He said: "Give me leave, I too shall descend into the great ocean." She said: "Son, stay right here." He said again and again: "I shall go." Knowing his insistence, she gave permission. He made a bell-proclamation: "Whoever among you is willing to descend into the great ocean together with <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s>, without tax, without toll, without transit duty, let him gather merchandise suitable for an ocean voyage." About five hundred merchants gathered merchandise for the ocean voyage. Then <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s>, having performed the auspicious rites, festivities, and benedictions, loading merchandise onto carts, loads, bales, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, set forth for the great ocean. Proceeding gradually, he reached the great ocean. The merchants, seeing the great ocean, were frightened. They did not dare to board the vessel. The caravan-leader said to the helmsman: "Describe, describe, good man, the true nature of the great ocean." Then the helmsman began to proclaim: "In this great ocean there are jewels of such kinds, namely: gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), conch-shells, crystal, coral, silver, gold, cat's-eye, <s>musāragalva</s> (a precious stone), rubies, and right-spiraling conches."

body.text:
438.002. yo yuṣmākamutsahate evamrūpai ratnairātmānaṃ samyaksukhena pratiṇayitum, mātāpitarau putradārān dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ motrāmātyajñātisālohitaṃ kālena kālaṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayitum, mūrdhagāminīṃ saubhāsikīṃ sukhavipākāmāyatyāṃ svargasaṃvartanīm, sa mahāsamudramavataratu/
sampattikāmo lokaḥ/
438.006. mahājanakāyo 'bhirūḍho yatastadvahanamasahyaṃ jātam/
438.006. sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kimidānīṃ vakṣyāmi avatarateti? sa karṇadhārasya kathayati--ghoṣaya bhoḥ puruṣa mahāsamudrasya yathābhūtaṃ varṇam/
438.008. tataḥ karṇadhāra uddhoṣitumāravdhah--śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā vaṇijaḥ/
438.009. santyasmin mahāsamudre imānyevaṃtūpāṇi mahānti mahābhayāni, tadyadhā timibhayaṃ timiṃgalabhayaṃ timitimiṃgalabhayamāvartabhayaṃ kumbhīrabhayaṃ śiśumārabhayamantarjalagatānāṃ parvatānāmāghātabhayam/
438.011. caurā apyatrāgavvhanti nīlaiḥ sitairvanacāriṇaḥ, asmākaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ jīvitādvyavaropayiṣyanti/
438.012. yena yuṣmākaṃ priyamātmānaṃ parityaktvā mātāpitarau putradāraṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaṃ mitrāmātyañjātisālohitaṃ mahāsamudramavataratu/
438.013. alpāḥ śūrā bahavaḥ kātarāḥ/
438.013. mahājanakāyo 'vatīrṇaḥ, yatastadvahanaṃ sahyaṃ saṃvṛtam/
438.014. tataḥ karṇadhārastriruddḥpṣaṇāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ paścādekāṃ vastrāṃ muñcati, dvitrivastrāṃ muñjati, yatastadvahanaṃ mahākarṇadhārasaṃdhānabalavadvāyusampreritaṃ mahāmegha iva saṃprasthito 'nuguṇena vāyunā yāvad ratnadvīpamanuprāptam/
438.016. tataḥ karṇadhāra uddhoṣayitumārabdhah--śṛṇvantu bhavanto jambudvīpakā vaṇijaḥ, santyasmin ratnadvīpe kācamaṇayo ratnasadṛśāḥ/
438.018. te bhavadbhirupaparīkṣyopaparikṣya grahītavyāḥ/
438.018. mā vaḥ paścājjambudvīpaprāptānāṃ paścāttāpo bhaviṣyati/
438.019. asminneva ca ratnadvīpe kroñjakumārikā nāma rākṣasyaḥ prativasanti/
438.020. tāḥ puruṣaṃ tathā upalālayanti yathā tatraivānayena vyasanamāpadyante/
438.020. asminneva ratnadvīpe madanīyāni phaṇāni santi/
438.021. tāni yaḥ paribhuṅkte, sa saptarātraṃ mūrcchitastiṣṭhati/
438.021. tāni bhavadbhir na paribhoktavyāni/
438.022. asminneva ca ratnadvīpe 'manuṣyāḥ prativasanti/
438.022. te muṣyāṇāṃ saptāhaṃ marṣayanti/
438.023. saptāahasyātyayāt tādṛśaṃ vāyumutsṛjanti yena vahanamapahriyate yathāpi tadkṛtakāryāṇām/
438.024. yaṃ śrutvā te vaṇijo 'vahitā apramattā avasthitāḥ/
438.024. taistadvahanaṃ ratnānamupaparīkṣyopaparīkṣya pūritaṃ tadyathā tilataṇḍulakolakulatthānām/
438.025. te anuguṇena vāyunā jambudvīpamanuprāptāaḥ/
438.026. evam yāvat saptakṛtvaḥ saṃsiddhayāanapātra āgataḥ/
438.026. sa mātrā^bhihitah--putra, atra niveśas triyatāmiti/
438.027. sa kathayati--agradhanikaṃ tāvacchinadbhi, tataḥ paścānniveśaṃ kariṣyāmi/
438.028. sa tathā uktah--putra na tava putā na putāmaho dhanikaḥ kṛtaḥ, kutastava dhaniko jātah? sa kathayati--amba, ahameva jānāmi/
438.029. tena cāturatnamayyaścatasro mūṣikāḥ kāritāḥ/
438.030. tena suvarṇasya phelāṃ pūrayitvā catasno mūṣikāścaturṣu pārśveṣu sthāpayitvā śroṣṭhigṛhaṃ gataḥ/
438.031. sa śreṣṭhī tadā tasyaiva tadvarṇaṃ bhāṣamāṇastiṣṭhati--paśyata bhavanto mūṣikāhairaṇyikaḥ kathaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyo yam yameva gṛhṇāti tṛṇaṃ vā loṣṭaṃ vā sarvaṃ tat suvarṇaṃ saṃpadyate/
438.032. sa ca <439>tathā kathāsamlāpena tiṣṭhati/
body.translated_text: "Whoever among you is willing to fully gratify himself with such jewels, to provide for mother and father, sons and wives, female and male servants, workers and attendants, friends, ministers, kinsmen and blood-relatives, and from time to time to establish offerings to <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins) — offerings that ascend to the crown of the head, that bring happiness, that ripen into bliss, and that in the future lead to heaven — let him descend into the great ocean." People desire prosperity. A great multitude boarded, so that the vessel became overloaded. The caravan-leader reflected: "What shall I now say, 'disembark'?" He said to the helmsman: "Proclaim, good man, the true nature of the great ocean." Then the helmsman began to proclaim: "Hear, O merchants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent)! In this great ocean there are great and terrible dangers of such kinds, namely: the danger of <s>timi</s> (whales), the danger of <s>timiṅgala</s> (whale-swallowers), the danger of <s>timitimiṅgala</s> (great whale-swallowers), the danger of whirlpools, the danger of crocodiles, the danger of <s>śiśumāra</s> (sea-monsters), and the danger of striking against submerged mountains. Pirates also come here — the blue ones, the white ones, the forest-dwellers — who will deprive us of everything, down to our very lives. Whoever among you would abandon his dear self, mother and father, sons and wife, female and male servants, workers and attendants, friends, ministers, kinsmen and blood-relatives, let him descend into the great ocean." The brave are few, the cowardly are many. A great multitude disembarked, so that the vessel became manageable. Then the helmsman, having made three proclamations and counter-proclamations, afterwards released one sail, then a second and third sail, whereupon that vessel, propelled by a powerful wind fitting the great helmsman's rigging, set forth like a great cloud, and with a favorable wind arrived at the Jewel Island. Then the helmsman began to proclaim: "Hear, O merchants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>! On this Jewel Island there are glass gems resembling real jewels. These must be examined and re-examined by you before taking them. Lest upon reaching <s>Jambudvīpa</s> you have cause for regret afterwards. Also on this very Jewel Island dwell <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses) called <s>Kroñcakumārikā</s> (Heron Maidens). They so pamper a man that he meets with disaster right there. Also on this very Jewel Island there are intoxicating fruits. Whoever eats them remains unconscious for seven nights. Those must not be consumed by you. Also on this very Jewel Island dwell non-human beings. They tolerate humans for seven days. After the passing of seven days, they release such a wind that the vessel is carried away — as if for those whose task is already accomplished." Hearing this, those merchants remained attentive, vigilant, and alert. They filled that vessel with jewels, having examined and re-examined them, packed as tightly as sesame seeds, rice grains, jujubes, and horse-gram. With a favorable wind they reached <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Thus he returned seven times with successful voyages. His mother said to him: "Son, let a marriage be arranged here." He said: "Let me first outdo the chief wealthy man, then afterwards I shall arrange a marriage." She said: "Son, neither your father nor your grandfather was made the chief wealthy man; how would you become the chief wealthy man?" He said: "Mother, I myself know." He had four mice fashioned from the four kinds of jewels. Then, filling a plate with gold and placing the four mice on the four sides, he went to the guild-master's house. That guild-master was at that very time speaking of his qualities: "Look, sirs, how <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s> is one of great merit and majesty! Whatever he takes up, be it a blade of grass or a clod of earth, it all turns to gold." And he stood there in such conversation.

body.text:
439.001. daivārikeṇa cāsya gatvā ārocitam--mūṣikāhairaṇyiko dvāritiṣṭhati/
439.002. sa kathayati--praviśatu, mūṣikāhairaṇyakaṃ vā ānayeti/
439.002. sa praviśya kathayati--idaṃ te mūlam, ayaṃ lābhaḥ/
439.003. pratigṛhyatām/
439.003. sa āha--vismarāmi, satyam yattva kiṃciddattakamiti/
439.003. ahaṃ te smārayiṣyāmi/
439.004. tena smāritam/
439.004. sa pṛcchati--kasya tvaṃ putra iti/
439.004. amukasya gṛhapateḥ/
