439.004. śreṣṭhī kathayati--tvaṃ mama vayasyaputro bhavasi/
439.005. mayaiva tava dātavyam/
439.005. tava pitrā gacchatā mama hasto kārṣāpaṇāḥ sthāpitāḥ/
439.006. tena śreṣṭhinā duhitā sarvlamlāravibhūṣitā tasya bhāryārthamanupradattā//
body.translated_text: The doorkeeper went and informed him: "<s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s> stands at the door." He said: "Let him enter, or bring <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s> in." He entered and said: "Here is your principal, and here is the profit. Please accept it." He replied: "I forget; is it true that you were given something?" "I shall remind you." He was reminded. He asked: "Whose son are you?" "Of such-and-such a householder." The guild-master said: "You are the son of my friend. It is I who should give to you. Your father, when departing, deposited <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins) in my hand." That guild-master gave his daughter, adorned with all ornaments, to him as a wife.

body.text:
439.007. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau śreṣṭhī, ahameva tena kālena tena samayena/
439.007. yo 'sau mūṣikāhairaṇyakaḥ, eṣa eva panthakastena kālena tena samayena/
439.008. tadāpyeṣa mayā parīttenāvavādenācodya mahatyaiśvarye pratiṣṭhapitaḥ/
439.009. etarhyapyeṣa mayā parittenāvavādenāvavādya saṃsārakāntārāduttārya atyantaniṣṭhe 'nuttare yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ//
body.translated_text: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)? That <s>śreṣṭhin</s> (guild-master) — it was I myself at that time, in that era. That <s>Mūṣikāhairaṇyaka</s> — he is this very <s>Panthaka</s> at that time, in that era. Then too, with but a slight admonition, having urged him on, I established him in great lordship. And now too, with but a slight admonition, having admonished him, having brought him across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, I established him in the utterly final, unsurpassed security from bondage, <s>nirvāṇa</s>."

body.text:
439.011. bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--kiṃ bhadanta panthakena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena dhanvaḥ paramadhanvaścūḍaḥ paramacūḍo jātah? panthakenaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni/
439.012. na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
439.015. na praṇaśyanti karmaṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
439.016. sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//7//
body.translated_text: The monks asked the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, did <s>Panthaka</s> do, by the ripening of which deed he was born as <s>Dhanvan</s>, the supreme <s>Dhanvan</s>, <s>Cūḍa</s>, the supreme <s>Cūḍa</s>?' 'It was <s>Panthaka</s> himself, O monks, who performed those deeds. Deeds that have been done and accumulated, O monks, do not ripen externally, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element — rather, they ripen in the very <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) that have been appropriated, whether wholesome or unwholesome. Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; reaching the proper conjunction and time, they certainly bear fruit for embodied beings.' //7//

body.text:
439.017. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma śastā loka utpannastathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho vidyāciraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān/
439.019. sa viṃśatibhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ parivāro vārāṇasīmupaniśritya viharati sma/
439.020. tasyaiva pravacane bhikṣurāsīt tripiṭaḥ/
439.020. anena tatra mātsaryeṇa na kasyaciccatuṣpadikāpi gāthā uddiṣṭo/
439.021. bhūyo 'nyasmin karpaṭake saukarika āsīt/
439.022. tasmāt karpaṭakānnadīpāre dvitīyaṃ karpaṭakam/
439.022. tatra parvaṇī pratyupasthitā/
439.022. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi sūkarān praghātya nayiṣyāmi, māṃsasya krayiko na bhaviṣyati, kledaṃ gamiṣyati/
439.023. jīvantameva gṛhītvā gacchāmi/
439.024. tatra tatra praghātya neṣyāmi, yatra yatra krāyiko 'sti/
439.025. sa prabhūtān sūkarāñ jānuṣu buddhvā nāvamāropya saṃprasthitaḥ/
439.025. sā naistaiḥ parispandamānairbāḍitā/
439.025. tatraivānayena vyasanamāpannaḥ/
439.026. so 'pi saukariko 'tra snotenohyamānaḥ/
439.026. tasyā nadyāstīre pañcapratyekabuddhaśatāni prativasanti/
439.027. teṣāmekaḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ pānīyasyārthe nadīṃ gataḥ/
439.027. tena sa dṛṣṭaḥ/
439.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ tāvadayaṃ mṛtah āhosvijjīvatīti? paśyati yāvajjīvati/
439.028. sa tena gajamujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya uddhṛtya vālukāyāḥ shalaṃ kṛtvā tatrāvamūrdhakaḥ sthāpitāḥ/
439.030. tasya kāyāt pānīyaṃ niḥsṛtam/
439.030. sa vyutthitaḥ/
439.030. manuṣyapadāni paśyati/
439.030. sa tena pādānusāreṇa gato yāvatpaśyati pañcamātrāṇi pratyekabuddhaśatāni/
439.031. sa teṣāṃ patreṇa puṣpeṇa phalena dantakāṣṭhena copasthānaṃ kartumārabdhaḥ/
439.032. te tasya pātraśoṣamanuprayacchanti/
439.032. tena bhuktam/
439.032. atha <440>te pratyekabuddhāḥ paryaṅka buddhvā dhyāyanti/
body.translated_text: In the past, O monks, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, a charioteer who tames men, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. Attended by twenty thousand monks, he dwelt near <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. In his very dispensation there was a monk who knew the <s>Tripiṭaka</s> (Three Baskets). But out of stinginess, he did not teach even a single four-line verse to anyone. Furthermore, in another small town there was a pig-butcher. Across the river from that town was a second small town. There, a festival day had arrived. He thought: 'If I slaughter the pigs and take them, there will be no buyer for the meat — it will rot. I shall take them alive instead. Wherever there is a buyer, there I shall slaughter and sell them.' Having bound many pigs at the knees, he loaded them onto a boat and set forth. That boat, buffeted by them thrashing about, was overwhelmed. There, through this mishap, he met with disaster. That pig-butcher too was being swept away by the current. On the bank of that river dwelt five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. One of those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> had gone to the river for water. He saw him. He thought: 'Is this man dead, or is he alive?' He saw that he was indeed alive. Extending an arm as mighty as an elephant's trunk, he pulled him out, made a bed of sand, and placed him there head-downward. Water flowed out from his body. He revived. He saw human footprints. Following those footprints, he went and saw fully five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. He began to attend upon them with leaves, flowers, fruits, and tooth-sticks. They gave him the remains from their alms-bowls. He ate. Then those <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, having crossed their legs, meditated.

body.text:
440.001. tadā so 'pyekānte sthitvā paryaṅkaṃ buddhcā dhyāyati/
440.002. sa tatrāsaṃjñikamutpādya asaṃjñisattveṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then he too, standing apart, crossed his legs and meditated. There he generated the state of non-perception and was reborn among the gods of the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> (Non-Percipient Beings) realm.

body.text:
440.003. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ/
440.003. yo 'sau kāśyapasya samyaksambuddhasya pravacane bhikṣastripiṭah āsīt, paścādasau saukarikaḥ, eṣa eva panthako bhikṣuḥ/
440.004. yadanena mātsaryeṇa na kasyaciccatuṣpadikā gāthā uddiṣṭā, yacca sūkarān praghātya yaccāsaṃjñisattvebhya ihopapannaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena cūḍaḥ paramacūḍo dhanvaḥ paramadhanvaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ//
body.translated_text: What do you think, O monks? He who was the <s>Tripiṭaka</s>-knowing monk in the dispensation of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and who afterward was the pig-butcher — that is this very monk <s>Panthaka</s>. Because out of stinginess he did not teach even a four-line verse to anyone, and because he slaughtered pigs, and because from the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> realm he was reborn here — by the ripening of those deeds, he became <s>Cūḍa</s>, the supreme <s>Cūḍa</s>, <s>Dhanvan</s>, the supreme <s>Dhanvan</s>.

body.text:
440.007. yadā āyuṣmān panthakaḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajitaḥ, jīvakena śrutam--panthakaḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajita iti/
440.008. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi bhagavān rājagṛhamāgamiṣyati, ahaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayiṣyāmi sthāpayitvā bhadantaṃ panthakam/
440.009. bhagavān yathābhiramyaṃ śrāvastīṃ vihṛtya yena rājagṛhe tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
440.010. anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caran rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
440.011. rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe/
440.011. aśrauṣījjīvakaḥ kumārabhūtah--bhagavān magadheṣu janapadacārikāṃ caran rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe/
440.012. śrutvā punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
440.013. apasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānto niṣaṇṇaḥ/
440.013. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ jīvakaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
440.015. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm/
440.015. atha jīvakaḥ kumārabhūtah utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadvocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñchvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
440.017. dūrāsadā buddhā bhagavanto duṣprasahāḥ/
440.018. sa na śaknoti bhagavantaṃ vaktuṃ sthāpayitvā bhadantaṃ panthakam/
440.018. atha jīvakaḥ kumārabhūto bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yenāyuṣmānāndastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
440.020. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vinditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
440.021. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo jīvakaḥ kumārabhūta āyucmantamānandimadamavocat--yatkhalu bhadanta ānanda jānīyāh--mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargehe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ sthāpayitvā bhadantaṃ panthakam/
440.023. yathā te jīvaka kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vṛddhirbhavati/
440.023. atha jīvakaḥ kumārabhūta āyuṣmata ānandasya bhāṣitamabhinandyānumodya āyuṣmata ānandasya pādau śirasā vanditvā prakrāntaḥ/
440.025. athāyuṣmānānando 'ciraprakrāntaṃ jīvakaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ viditvā yenāyuṣmān pathakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
440.026. upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ panthakamidamavocat--yatkhalvāyuṣman panthaka jānīyāh--jīvakena kumārabhūtena buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopapanimantritaḥ shāpyitvā āyuṣmantaṃ panthakam/
440.028. yathāsya bhdantānanda kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vṛddhirbhavati/
440.028. sa jīvakaḥ kumārabhūtastāmeva rātriṃ śuciṃ praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kalyamevotthāya āsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samaye bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate/
440.031. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena jīvakasya kumārabhūtasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text: When the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> went forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s> heard: '<s>Panthaka</s> has gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' He thought: 'If the Blessed One comes to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, I shall feed the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, excluding the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>.' The Blessed One, having dwelt in <s>Śrāvastī</s> as long as he wished, set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Wandering by stages, he arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He dwelt in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground). <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince heard: 'The Blessed One, wandering through the <s>Magadha</s> country, has arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s> and dwells in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.' Having heard, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince, seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and extending his joined palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept from me a meal tomorrow in my house, together with the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks.' <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are difficult to approach and hard to overcome. He was unable to say to the Blessed One: 'excluding the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>.' Then <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince, having rejoiced in and approved of the words of the Blessed One, departed from the Blessed One's presence and approached the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Please know, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, that I have invited the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal tomorrow in my house, excluding the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>.' 'As it may be for the growth of your wholesome qualities, <s>Jīvaka</s>.' Then <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince, having rejoiced in and approved of the words of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and departed. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, knowing that <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince had recently departed, approached the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>: 'Please know, Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, that <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince has invited the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal tomorrow in his house, excluding the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>.' 'As it may be for the growth of his wholesome qualities, Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.' Then <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent hard and soft foods, rising early in the morning, laid out seats, set up water vessels, and sent a messenger to announce the time to the Blessed One: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready — may the Blessed One come at whatever time he thinks fit.' Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, attended by the assembly of monks, preceded by the <s>Saṅgha</s> of monks, approached the residence of <s>Jīvaka</s> the Prince.

body.text:
441.001. <441>upasaṃkramya purastādbhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
441.001. niṣadya bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate--panthakasyānugantī moktavyā/
441.002. jīvakaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sauvarṇabhṛṅgāraṃ gṛhītvā vṛddhānte tiṣṭhati/
441.003. bhagavān vāridhārāṃ na pratigṛhṇāti/
441.003. jīvikaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ kathayati--kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavan vāridhārāṃ na pratigṛhṇāti/
441.004. bhagavānāha--na tāvadbhikṣusaṃgham iti samagra iti/
441.005. jīvakaḥ kathayati--bhagavān, ko 'nāgata iti/
441.005. bhagavānāha--na panthako bhikṣuḥ saṃghaḥ/
441.006. jīvakaḥ kathayati--bhagavan, nāsau mayā nimantrita iti/
441.006. bhagavānāha--na tvayā jīvaka buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho nimantritah? bhagavan, nimantritaḥ/
441.007. kimasau bhikṣusaṃghādbahir na vā? bhagavān kathayati jīvakam--gaccha tvaṃ śabdāpaya/
441.008. jīvakaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpyahaṃ bhagavato gauraveṇa śabdāpayāmi, na satkṛtya pariveṣayiṣyāmi/
441.009. tena dūto 'nupreṣitah--gaccha, śabdāpayasva/
441.010. āyuṣmānapi panthakaśca trayodaśabhikṣuśatāni nirmāyāvasthitaḥ/
441.010. tena dūtena gatvā panthaka iti śabdo muktaḥ/
441.011. anukairbhikṣubhiḥ prativacanaṃ dattam/
441.011. sa dūta āgatya jīvakasya kathayati--tathaiva veṇuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpo bhikṣūṇāṃ pūrṇastiṣṭhati/
441.012. bhagavānāha--gaccha tvaṃ kathaya yo bhūtapanthakaḥ sa āgacchatu/
441.013. sa gatvā kathayati--yo bhūtapanthakaḥ sa āgacchatu/
441.014. āyuṣmān panthakastatra gatvā svasyāṃ gatyāṃ niṣaṇṇāḥ/
441.014. jīvakaḥ kumārabhūto buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ pariveṣayitumārabdhaḥ/
441.015. āyuṣmantaṃ panthakaṃ na satkṛtya pativeṣayati/
441.015. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--sumeruprakhye mahāśrāvake jīvakaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ kṣāntiṃ gṛhṇāti/
441.016. guṇodbhāvanā asya kartavyā/
441.016. bhagavatā āyuṣmat ānandasya pātraṃ nānupradattam/
441.017. dharmatā khalu na tāvat sthabirashtavirāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātrāṇi pratigṛhyante, yāvadbhagavataḥ pātrapratigrahī na bhaviṣyati/
441.018. āyuṣmān panthakaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavataḥ sthavirasthavirāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pātrāṇi na gṛhyante? mayā atra guṇodbhāvanā kartavyā/
441.020. āyuṣmatā panthakenādharmāsanaṃ kṛtvā gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhumabhiprasārya bhagavataḥ pātraṃ gṛhītam/
441.021. kumārabhūtena jīvakena vṛddhānte sthitena dṛṣṭham/
441.021. sa saṃlakṣayati--ko 'pyayaṃ sthaviro bhikṣuḥ/
441.022. ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayati/
441.022. sa pātrānusāreṇa gato yāvatpaśyatyāyuṣmataṃ panthakam/
441.023. sa dṛṣṭvā mūrchitakastiṣṭhati/
441.023. sa jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇa āyuṣmataḥ panthakasya pādayor nipatya kṣamāpayati, gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
441.025. nityaṃ caityaguṇo hi candanaraso nityaṃ sugandhayutpalaṃ nityaṃ bhāsati kāñcanasya vimalaṃ vaiḍūryaśuddham/
441.027. nityaṃ pāpajane hi krodhamatulaṃ pāṣāṇarekhopamaṃ nityaṃ cāryajaneṣu prātirvasate kṣāntirdhruvā hyarhatām//8//
body.translated_text:
441.001. He approached and sat down on the seat prepared at the front of the assembly of monks.
441.001. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: '<s>Panthaka</s>'s companion should be released.'
441.002. <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince stood at the end of the row, holding a golden water-vessel.
441.003. The Blessed One did not accept the pouring of water.
441.003. <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince said: 'Why, Blessed One, do you not accept the pouring of water?'
441.004. The Blessed One said: 'The assembly of monks is not yet complete.'
441.005. <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Blessed One, who has not come?'
441.005. The Blessed One said: 'The monk <s>Panthaka</s> is not with the assembly.'
441.006. <s>Jīvaka</s> said: 'Blessed One, he was not invited by me.'
441.006. The Blessed One said: 'Did you not, <s>Jīvaka</s>, invite the assembly of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>?' 'I did, Blessed One.'
441.007. 'Is he outside the assembly of monks or not?' The Blessed One said to <s>Jīvaka</s>: 'Go, summon him.'
441.008. <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince reflected: 'I shall summon him out of respect for the Blessed One, but I shall not serve him with honor.'
441.009. He sent a messenger: 'Go, summon him.'
441.010. The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> had created thirteen hundred monks and stood there.
441.010. The messenger went and called out '<s>Panthaka</s>!'
441.011. The manifested monks all answered.
441.011. The messenger returned and told <s>Jīvaka</s>: 'The <s>Veṇuvana</s>, the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>, is filled with monks.'
441.012. The Blessed One said: 'Go, say: "Let the real <s>Panthaka</s> come."'
441.013. He went and said: 'Let the real <s>Panthaka</s> come.'
441.014. The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> went there and sat in his proper seat.
441.014. <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince began to serve the assembly of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.
441.015. He served the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> without respect.
441.015. The Blessed One reflected: '<s>Jīvaka</s> the prince is showing disregard to a great disciple who is like <s>Sumeru</s>.
441.016. His qualities must be made manifest.'
441.016. The Blessed One did not hand his bowl to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>.
441.017. It is a rule that the bowls of the most senior monks are not accepted until the Blessed One's bowl has been accepted.
441.018. The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> reflected: 'Why are the bowls of the Blessed One and the most senior monks not being accepted? I must make a display of qualities here.'
441.020. The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, making a firm seat, extended his arm like the trunk of an elephant and took the Blessed One's bowl.
441.021. <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince, standing at the end of the row, saw this.
441.021. He reflected: 'Who is this senior monk?
441.022. He is displaying a miracle of supernatural power.'
441.022. Following the bowl, he went and saw the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>.
441.023. Seeing him, he stood there stunned.
441.023. Revived by a sprinkling of water, he fell at the feet of the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>, begged forgiveness, and spoke a verse:
441.025. 'Always the quality of a shrine is like sandalwood fragrance; always like a sweet-scented lotus; always shines the spotless pure luster of gold and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>.
441.027. Always among wicked people, boundless anger is like a line on stone; but always among noble people, forbearance dwells — for the <s>Arhats</s> it is constant.' //8//

body.text: 441.029. āyuṣmān panthakaḥ kathayati--kṣāntaṃ jīvaka//
body.translated_text: 441.029. The Venerable <s>Panthaka</s> said: 'It is forgiven, <s>Jīvaka</s>.'

body.text: 441.030. bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti--paśya bhadanta, yadā jīvakaḥ kumārabhūta āyuṣmataḥ panthakasya guṇānāmanabhijñastadā asatkāraḥ prayuktaḥ, yadā guṇānāmabhijñastadā pādayor nipatya <442>kṣamāpayati/
body.translated_text: 441.030. The monks asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: 'See, Venerable Sir, when <s>Jīvaka</s> the prince was ignorant of the Venerable <s>Panthaka</s>'s qualities, he showed disrespect; when he recognized his qualities, he fell at his feet and begged forgiveness.'

body.text:
442.001. bhagavānāh--na bhikṣava etarhi yathātīte 'dhvanyeṣo 'sya guṇānāmanabhijñah,tadā asatkāraṃ prayuktavān/
442.002. yadā guṇānāmabhijñastadā pādayor nipatya kṣamāpitavān/
442.002. tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text:
442.001. The Blessed One said: 'Not only now, O monks; in a past age as well, this one, being ignorant of his qualities, showed disrespect.
442.002. When he recognized his qualities, he fell at his feet and begged forgiveness.
442.002. Listen to this.'

body.text:
442.003. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣava uttarāpathāt sārthavāḥ pañcaśatamaśvapaṇyamādāya madhyadeśamāgataḥ/
442.004. tasya ca vaḍavāyāḥ kukṣāvaśvājāneyo 'vakrāntaḥ/
442.004. sa yameva divasamavakrāntastameva divasamupādāya te 'śvā na bhūyo heṣante/
442.005. sārthavahaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ ca mamāśvānāṃ kaścid rogaḥ prādurbhūto bhaviṣyati yena te na heṣante? apareṇa samayenāśvā vaḍavā prasūtā/
442.006. tasyāḥ kiśorako jātaḥ/
442.007. sa yameva divasamupādāya te 'śvāḥ saṃcartumapi nārabdhāḥ/
442.007. sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--nūnamayaṃ daurbhāgyasattvo jātah asya doṣaṇa mamāśvānāṃ rogaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ/
442.008. sa tāṃ vaṭavāṃ nityameva vāhayati/
442.009. tasyā navayavasampannayogyāśanamanuprayacchati/
442.009. so 'nupūrveṇa pūjitaṃ nāmādhiṣṭhānamanuprāptaḥ/
442.010. tasya tatra vārṣāratryaḥ pratyupasthitāḥ/
442.010. sa saṃlakṣayati--yadi gamiṣyāmi, aśvānāṃ khurāḥ kledaṃ gamiṣyanti, apaṇyoobhaviṣyanti/
442.011. ihaiva varṣāṃ tiṣṭhāmi/
442.011. sa tasyaiva varṣāmuṣitasya tadvāsino yo śilpinaste svena śilpenopasthānaṃ kurvānti/
442.012. tasya gamanakāle śilpinn upasaṃkrāntāḥ/
442.013. teṣāṃ tena saṃvibhāgaḥ kṛtaḥ/
442.013. tatraikaḥ kumbhakāraḥ prativasati/
442.013. tenāpi tasya svena śilpenopasthānaṃ kṛtam/
442.014. sa patnyābhihitah--āryaputra, sa sārthavāho gacchati/
442.014. gaccha, tvaṃ gatvā kiṃcidyācasva/
442.015. tasmāccalitasya mṛtpiṇḍaṃ gṛhītvopasthitaḥ/
442.015. sa tena sārthavāhena dṛṣṭaḥ/
442.015. sa tasya kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, aticireṇa tvamāgataḥ/
442.016. mama kiṃciddātavyam/
442.016. sa āha--sarvaṃ gatam/
442.017. tasyāpi sārthavāhasya tasya kiśorasyāntike 'maṅgalabuddhiḥ/
442.017. sa kathayati--api tvayamekaḥ kiśorastiṣṭhati, yadi prayo 'si, gṛhītvā gaccha/
442.018. kumbhakāraḥ kathayati--śobhanam/
442.018. ahaṃ bhāṇḍāni kariṣyāmi, eṣa bhetsyate/
442.019. sa kiśorakastasya pādau jihvayā leḍhumārabdhaḥ/
442.020. tasyāśvasyāntike 'nunaya utpannaḥ/
442.020. sa taṃ gṛhītvā gataḥ/
442.020. sa patnyā uktah--asti kiṃcittvayā tasya sakāśāllabdham? labdham/
442.021. ayaṃ kiśorakaḥ/
442.021. tvaṃ bhāṇḍāni kariṣyasi, eṣa bhetsyate/
442.021. sa kiśorako 'syāḥ pādāni leḍhumārabdhaḥ/
442.022. tasyā api tasyāntike 'nunaya utpannaḥ/
442.023. sa pakkamānānāṃ bhāṇḍānāṃ madhye parisarpanna kiṃcidbhāṇḍaṃ bhinatti/
442.023. sā tasya patnī kathayati--śobhanam/
442.024. ayaṃ kiśorakaḥ saṃprajānan parisarpati/
442.024. apareṇa samayena kumbhakāro mṛttikārthamāgataḥ/
442.025. sa kiśorakastasya pṛṣṭhato 'nusarannanubaddhaḥ/
442.025. tena kumbhakāreṇa mṛttikāprasevakaḥ pūritaḥ/
442.026. tena kiśorakena pṛṣṭhamavanāmitam/
442.026. tena tasya mṛttikāyāḥ prasevakaḥ pṛṣṭhamāropitaḥ/
442.027. sa taṃ gṛhītvā gṛhamāgataḥ/
442.027. tena kumbhakāreṇa patnī uktā--bhadre, śobhanaḥ kiśorakaḥ/
442.028. na bhūyo mayā mṛttikā voḍhavyā bhaviṣyati/
442.028. ahamasya tatrāropayiṣyāmi, tvamihāvatārayiṣyasi/
442.029. sa tasya tuṣān kuṭiṃ cānuprayacchati//
body.translated_text:
442.003. 'In a former time, O monks, a caravan-leader came from the northern region to the central country, bringing five hundred horses as merchandise.
442.004. In the belly of his mare, a thoroughbred horse had been conceived.
442.004. From the very day it was conceived, those horses ceased to neigh.
442.005. The caravan-leader reflected: "Has some disease befallen my horses, that they do not neigh?" On another occasion, the mare gave birth.
442.006. A colt was born.
442.007. From that very day, those horses would not even begin to stir.
442.007. The caravan-leader reflected: "Surely this is an unlucky creature; due to his fault, disease has befallen my horses."
442.008. He kept driving that mare constantly.
442.009. He gave her excellent food, rich with fresh barley.
442.009. Gradually, he reached a place of worship called <s>Pūjita</s>.
442.010. There the rainy season arrived.
442.010. He reflected: "If I travel, the horses' hooves will become sodden, and they will be unsaleable.
442.011. I shall stay here for the rains."
442.011. He stayed there for the rains, and the local craftsmen served him each with their own craft.
442.012. At the time of his departure, the craftsmen came to him.
442.013. He distributed shares among them.
442.013. There lived a potter.
442.014. He too had served him with his craft.
442.014. His wife said to him: "Noble husband, the caravan-leader is departing.
442.014. Go, and ask for something."
442.015. He came, having taken a lump of clay, and presented himself.
442.015. The caravan-leader saw him.
442.015. He said to him: "Good sir, you have come too late.
442.016. I have something to give you."
442.016. He said: "Everything is gone."
442.017. Now the caravan-leader also had an unlucky feeling about that colt.
442.017. He said: "There is this one colt standing here; if you wish, take him and go."
442.018. The potter said: "Excellent!
442.018. I shall make pots; this one will break them."
442.019. The colt began to lick his feet with his tongue.
442.020. Affection arose in him for that horse.
442.020. He took him and went.
442.020. His wife asked: "Did you get something from him?" "I did.
442.021. This colt.
442.021. You will make pots; this one will break them."
442.021. The colt began to lick her feet too.
442.022. Affection arose in her as well for him.
442.023. He moved among the vessels being baked without breaking a single one.
442.023. His wife said: "Excellent!
442.024. This colt moves about with full awareness."
442.024. On another occasion, the potter went to get clay.
442.025. The colt followed behind him.
442.025. The potter filled the basket with clay.
442.026. The colt bent its back.
442.026. The potter placed the basket of clay upon its back.
442.027. He took him and came home.
442.027. The potter told his wife: "Dear, this is a fine colt.
442.028. I shall no longer have to carry clay myself.
442.028. I shall load it there; you shall unload it here."
442.029. He gave it chaff and a shed.'

body.text:
442.030. tena kālena tena samayena vārāṇasyāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca bahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
442.031. tasyāśvājāneyaḥ kālagataḥ/
442.031. sāmantarājyaiḥ śrutam--brahmadattasya rājño 'śvājāneyaḥ kālagata iti/
442.032. taistasya saṃdiṣṭam--karapratyāyān vā anuprayaccha udyānam <443>vā/
body.translated_text:
442.030. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling — his kingdom was prosperous, flourishing, and full of many people.
442.031. His thoroughbred horse had died.
442.031. The vassal kingdoms heard: "King <s>Brahmadatta</s>'s thoroughbred horse has died."
442.032. They sent him word: "Either pay tribute or surrender your territory."

body.text:
443.001. te nirgatakaṇṭake 'nuvarodhya ānayiṣyāmaḥ/
443.001. sa teṣāṃ karapratyāyān nānuprayacchati, nāpi taṃ sa udyānaṃ samāgataḥ/
443.002. sārthavāho 'śvapaṇyamādāya vārāṇasīmanuprāpta/
443.002. brahmadattena rājñā śrutam--uttarāpathāt sārthavāho 'śvapaṇyamādāya vārāṇasīmanuprāpta iti/
443.003. so 'mātyānāmantrayate sma--bhavantaḥ, kiyacciraṃ mayehaṃ praviṣṭena sthātavyam? gacchata, aśvājāneyaṃ paryeṣadhvam/
443.005. te sārthavāhasya sakāśaṃ gatāḥ/
443.006. taiste 'śvāḥ/
443.006. na cātra kaścidaśvājāneyo vidyate/
443.006. sārthavāhaṃ dṛṣṭvā te kathayanti--bhavanto 'śvāvaḍavāyā aśvājāneyo jātaḥ/
443.007. sa ca na dṛśyate/
443.007. sārthavāhamupasaṃkramya pṛcchanti--asti kaścidaśvastvayā vikrītaḥ kasyacidvā datta iti? sa kathayati--nāsti kaścidvikrītaḥ/
443.008. api tvasti mayā pūjitake 'dhiṣṭhāne 'maṅgalakaḥ kiśorakaḥ kumbhakārasya datta iti/
443.009. te 'nyonyaṃ kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, mahāmūrkho 'yaṃ sārthavāhaḥ, yo 'yaṃ maṅgalamapahāyāmaṅgalānevādāyāgata iti/
443.010. te rājānamavalokya pūjitakaṃ gatāḥ/
443.011. te taṃ kumbhakāramupasaṃkrāntāḥ/
443.011. upasaṃkramya kathayanti--kimanena kiśorakena karoṣi? sa āha--eṣa mama mṛttikāṃ vahati/
443.012. te kathayati--vayaṃ te tathā gardabhamanuprayacchāmaḥ, tvamasmākamamumanuprayacchasva/
443.013. kathayati--eṣa me śobhana iti/
443.013. caturgavayuktaṃ śakaṭamanuprayacchāmaḥ/
443.014. sa kathayati--eṣa mama śobhana iti/
443.014. te kathayanti--evaṃ cet saṃpradhāraya vayaṃ śvo bhūya āgamiṣyāmaḥ/
443.015. ityuktvā prakrāntāḥ/
443.015. sa kiśorakaḥ kathayati--kimarthaṃ nānuprayacchasi? kiṃ tvaṃ jānāsi mayā mṛttikā voḍhavyā tuṣāśca kuṭisakaṇṭaṃ bhakṣitavyam/
443.017. mayā rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto vāḍhavyaḥ, sauvarṇasthāle madhumrākṣitakā mūlakā bhakṣitavyāḥ/
443.018. te yadi saṃkathayanti keśoraka iti, vaktavyāh--kiṃ lajjadhvaṃ vaktumaśvājāneya iti? śvaḥ punarāgatvā te kathayiṣyanti mūlyenānuprayaccheti/
443.020. vaktavyāh--suvarṇalakṣaṃ vānuprayacchatha yāvadvā dakṣiṇena sakthnā kariṣyati tāvadanuprayacchati/
443.021. te 'parasmin divase upasaṃkramya pṛcchanti--bhoḥ puruṣa, saṃpradhāritaṃ tvayā? saṃpradhāritam--kiṃ lajjadhvaṃ vaktumaśvājāneya iti? te kathayanti--mūrkhaḥ sa eṣaḥ/
443.022. kimeṣa jñāsyati? eṣa aśvājāneyo dhārayati/
443.023. etadeva tena sārthavāhenāsyārocitaṃ bhaviṣyati/
443.023. te kathayanti--aśvājāneyo bhavatu/
443.024. mūlyenānuprayaccha/
443.024. sa kathayati--suvarṇalakṣaṃ vānuprayaccḥ, yāvadvā suvarṇalakṣaṃ dakṣiṇena sakthnā kariṣyati/
443.025. te saṃlakṣayanti--balavāneṣaḥ/
443.025. sthānametadvidyate yat prabhūtataramākarṣayati/
443.026. suvarṇalakṣamanuprayacchāmaḥ/
443.026. tairbrahmadattasya rājñaḥ saṃdiṣṭaṃ suvarṇalakṣeṇa aśvājāneyo labhyate/
443.027. rājñāpi saṃdiṣṭam--yūyam yāvatā mūlyena tāvatā gṛhṇīta/
443.027. taiḥ suvarṇalakṣeṇa gṛhītaḥ/
443.028. te tamādāya vāraṇasīmāgatāḥ/
443.028. sa taiśca mandurāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
443.028. tasya paramayogyāśanaṃ dīyate/
443.029. sa taṃ na paribhuṅkte/
443.029. kiṃ sarogo bhavadbhiraśvājāneya ānītah? api tu samanuyuñjyāmahe tāvadenam/
443.030. atha sūto gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
443.032. smarasi turaga ghaṭikarasya śālāṃ kimiha vidhairya viprayukraḥ/
body.translated_text:
443.001. 'We shall bring him by obstructing him once the thorn is removed.'
443.001. But the merchant did not hand over the taxes to them, nor did he come to the garden.
443.002. The caravan-leader, having taken the horse merchandise, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
443.002. King <s>Brahmadatta</s> heard: 'A caravan-leader has arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> from the northern road with horse merchandise.'
443.003. He addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, how long must I remain here? Go and seek a thoroughbred horse.'
443.005. They went to the caravan-leader.
443.006. Those were his horses.
443.006. But among them there was no thoroughbred.
443.006. Seeing the caravan-leader, they said: 'Sir, a thoroughbred was born from your mare,
443.007. but it is not to be seen.'
443.007. Approaching the caravan-leader, they asked: 'Has any horse been sold or given by you to anyone?' He said: 'No horse has been sold.
443.008. However, an inauspicious colt was given by me to a potter at a holy shrine.'
443.009. They said to one another: 'Sirs, this caravan-leader is a great fool — he left behind what was auspicious and brought only the inauspicious!'
443.010. They looked to the king and went to the shrine.
443.011. They approached that potter.
443.011. Approaching, they said: 'What do you do with this colt?' He said: 'He carries clay for me.'
443.012. They said: 'We shall give you a donkey in exchange; you give us this one.'
443.013. He said: 'This one is fine for me.'
443.013. 'We shall give you a cart yoked with four oxen.'
443.014. He said: 'This one is fine for me.'
443.014. They said: 'If so, think it over — we shall come again tomorrow.'
443.015. Having said this, they departed.
443.015. The colt said: 'Why do you not hand me over? Do you know that I must carry clay and eat chaff and thorn-stalks?
443.017. I should carry a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king, anointed and consecrated, and eat honey-smeared radishes from a golden plate.
443.018. If they address me as "colt," tell them: "Are you ashamed to say 'thoroughbred'?" Tomorrow when they come again, they will say "give him for a price" —
443.020. tell them: "Either give a <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000) of gold, or give as much as he will produce with his right thigh."
443.021. The next day they approached and asked: 'Good man, have you deliberated?' 'I have deliberated — are you ashamed to say "thoroughbred"?' They said: 'This fool!
443.022. How would he know? This is a thoroughbred.
443.023. The caravan-leader must have told him.'
443.023. They said: 'Let him be a thoroughbred.
443.024. Give him for a price.'
443.024. He said: 'Either give a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold, or as much gold as he will produce with his right thigh.'
443.025. They thought: 'He is powerful.
443.025. It is possible he will produce even more.'
443.026. 'Let us give a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold.'
443.026. They reported to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>: 'The thoroughbred can be obtained for a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold.'
443.027. The king commanded: 'Take him for whatever price.'
443.027. They took him for a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold.
443.028. They brought him to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
443.028. They installed him in the stable.
443.028. The finest suitable food was given to him.
443.029. But he would not eat it.
443.029. 'Is the thoroughbred you brought ill? Let us inquire of him.'
443.030. Then the charioteer spoke a verse:
443.032. 'Do you remember the potter's shed, O horse? Why do you stand here despondent and disheartened?'

body.text: 444.001. <444>pariśithilaśirāsthicarmagātraḥ svadaśānacūrṇitaghāsasya cārī//9//
body.translated_text: 444.001. 'With loosened head-bones and skin-and-frame body, you who used to graze on chaff ground by your own teeth —' //9//

body.text:
444.003. na carasi bahumatastadarthe māsidiha hi cara yānasahasrapūrṇayāyī/
444.005. hyavasanamidaṃ tṛṣāpanītaṃ na carasi kiṃ vada me 'dya sādhu pṛṣṭaḥ//10//
body.translated_text:
444.003. 'You do not eat, though highly esteemed for that purpose. Eat here, O one who shall ride with a thousand vehicles!
444.005. This provision removes thirst — why do you not eat? Tell me now, being properly asked.' //10//

body.text:
444.007. tamakathayadamarṣitaḥ sakopaṃ paramayavārjavadhairyasamprayuktaḥ/
444.009. upaśamamatha saṃpracintya tasmāt turagavaro narasūtamaitrabuddhiḥ//11//
body.translated_text:
444.007. 'Him the best of horses addressed, angered and indignant, yet endowed with the utmost sincerity, straightforwardness, and fortitude;
444.009. then, reflecting on tranquility, with a mind of friendliness toward the human charioteer —' //11//

body.text:
444.011. tvamiha vidhihitapradābhimānī na ca vihito bhavato yathāvadasmi/
444.013. nidhanamahamiha prayāyamāśu na ca biduṣāya taraya pūrvyām//12//
body.translated_text:
444.011. 'You here are proud of giving what is prescribed, but I have not been served as is proper.
444.013. I shall quickly go to destruction here, and not because I do not know the ancient way.' //12//

body.text:
444.015. suciramapi hi na sajjanāvamāno yadi guṇavānasi saumya nāvamānaḥ/
444.017. kṣaṇamāpi khalu sajjanāvamāno yadi guṇavānasi nāvamānaḥ//13//
body.translated_text:
444.015. 'Even for a long time, there is no contempt from good people — if you are virtuous, O gentle one, there is no disgrace.
444.017. Even for a moment, indeed, contempt from good people — if you are virtuous, there is no disgrace.' //13//

body.text:
444.019. sūto rājñaḥ kathayati--devasyānupūrvī na kṛtā yanaiṣa yavasayogyāśanaṃ na gṛhṇāti/
444.020. kāsyānupūrvī kṛtā? asyāyamupacāraḥ/
444.020. sārdhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kartavyā/
444.020. rājābhiṣiktaścaturaṅgena balakāyena sārdhaṃ pratyudgacchati/
444.021. yasmin pradeśe sthāpyate, sa pradeśastāmrapaṭṭairbadhyate/
444.022. rājño jyeṣṭhaputraḥ/
444.022. sa tasya śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ mūrdhni dhārayati/
444.022. rājño jyeṣṭhā duhitā sauvarṇena maṇivyajanena makṣikān vārayati/
444.023. rājño 'gramahiṣī sauvargasthāle madhumrakṣitakān mūlān bhakṣayato dhārayati/
444.024. rājño 'grāmātyaḥ sauvarṇena lakṣaṇena laḍḍīśchorayati/
444.024. rājā kathayati--eṣa nāma rājā, nāhaṃ sa rājeti/
444.025. sūtaḥ kathayati--deva, nāsya sarvakālameṣa upacāraḥ kriyate/
444.026. api tu saptāhasyātyayādvidheyo bhavati/
444.026. rājā kathayati--yattāvadatītaṃ na śakyaṃ tatpunaḥ kartum, yadavaśiṣṭaṃ tatkriyatām/
444.027. yasmin pradeśe tāmrapaḍḍairbaddhaḥ, tasya rājño jyeṣṭhaḥ putraḥ śataśalākāṃ dhārayati, rājño jyeṣṭhā duhitā sauvarṇamaṇimayavālavyajanena makṣikān vārayati, rājño 'gramāhiṣī sauvarṇena sthālena madhumrakṣitakān mūlān bhakṣayato dhārayati, rājño 'mātyaḥ sauvarṇena lakṣaṇena laḍḍīśchorayati/
444.030. tamanunayati pārthivaḥ/
444.030. sasṛtaparamasugandhivilepanānudhārī madhuramadhurakṛtāntarānurāgā nṛpamahiṣī turagottamāya dattā rājñā/
444.031. udyānabhūmiṃ nirgantukāmo 'syāścājāneya upagamya pṛṣṭhamunnāmayati/
444.031. rājā sūtaṃ pṛcchati--rājā asya pṛṣṭhaṃ duḥkhayati/
444.031. sa kathayati--kiṃ tu rājā <445>duḥkhamadhirokṣyatīti/
body.translated_text:
444.019. The charioteer told the king: 'The proper protocol has not been followed for His Majesty's horse — that is why he does not accept the suitable barley and food.'
444.020. 'What is his proper protocol?' 'This is the treatment for him:
444.020. For three and a half <s>yojanas</s>, the road must be adorned.
444.020. The king, anointed and consecrated, together with the fourfold army, should go out to meet him.
444.021. The place where he is stationed should be hung with copper plates.
444.022. The king's eldest son should hold a hundred-ribbed parasol over his head.
444.022. The king's eldest daughter should fan away flies with a golden gem-studded yak-tail whisk.
444.023. The king's chief queen should hold a golden plate of honey-smeared radishes for him to eat.
444.024. The king's chief minister should brush off flies with a golden <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (insignia).'
444.024. The king said: 'He, then, is the king — not I!'
444.025. The charioteer said: 'Sire, this treatment is not performed for him at all times.
444.026. Rather, after seven days he becomes obedient.'
444.026. The king said: 'What is past cannot be done again; let what remains be done.'
444.027. At the place hung with copper plates, the king's eldest son held the hundred-ribbed parasol, the king's eldest daughter fanned away flies with a golden gem-studded yak-tail whisk, the king's chief queen held a golden plate of honey-smeared radishes for him to eat, and the king's minister brushed off flies with a golden insignia.
444.030. The king conciliated him.
444.030. The king's chief queen, bearing the finest sweet fragrant unguents, with a voice of sweet and tender inner affection, was given by the king to attend the best of horses.
444.031. When the king wished to go out to the garden, the thoroughbred approached and lowered his back.
444.031. The king asked the charioteer: 'Will the king hurt his back?'
444.031. He said: 'No — the king will mount painlessly.'

body.text:
445.001. yato 'nenāvanāmitaṃ sa rājā tamabhiruhya saṃprasthitaḥ/
445.001. tasya gacchataḥ pānīyamāgatam/
445.002. sa tatra nāvatarati/
445.002. rājā sūtaṃ pṛcchati--eṣo bibheti? deva, naiṣa bibheti/
445.002. api tu mā rājānaṃ pucchodakena sekṣyāmīti/
445.003. tasya tatpucchaṃ sauvarṇāyāṃ nālikāyāṃ prakṣiptam/
445.003. sa taṃ pānīyamuttīrṇaḥ/
445.004. sa udyānaṃ gatvā pramatto 'vasthitaḥ/
445.004. sāmantarājaiḥ śrutam--yathā rājā brahmadatta udyānaṃ gata iti/
445.005. tairāgatya nagarasya dvārāṇi bandhayanti/
445.005. rājñā brahmadattena śrutaṃ sāmantarājair nagaradvārāṇi nigṛhītānīti/
445.006. so 'śvājāneyamabhirūḍhaḥ/
445.006. antarā ca vārāṇasyantarā codyānamatrāntarā brahmavatī nāma puṣkiriṇyutpalakuṃdapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannā/
445.007. so 'śvājāneyaḥ padmopari saran vārāṇasīṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
445.008. rājā tuṣṭo 'matyānāṃ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yorājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhnābhiṣiktasya jīvitamanuprayacchati, kiṃ tasya kartavyam? deva, upārdharājyaṃ dātavyam/
445.009. rājā kathayati--tiryageṣaḥ/
445.010. kimasyopārdharājyena? api tvenamāgamya saptāhaṃ dānāni dīyantām, puṇyāni kriyantām, akālakaumudī ca kriyatām/
445.011. amātyaiḥ saptāahaṃ dānāni dātumārabdhāni, puṇyāni kartumārabdhāni, saptāhamakālakaumudī prasthāpitā/
445.012. sārthavāhaḥ puruṣān pṛcchati--bhavantaḥ, kimakālakaumudī vartate? te 'sya kathayanti--pūjitaṃ nāmādhiṣṭhānam/
445.013. tataḥ kumbhakārasya sakāśāt suvarṇalakṣeṇāśvājāneyaṃ gṛhītvā ihānītam/
445.014. tenādya rājño jīvitaṃ dattam/
445.014. tamāgamya saptāhaṃ dānāni dātumārabdhāni, puṇyāni kriyante, akālakaumudī ca prasthāpitā/
445.015. sārthavāhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--yo mayā chorito nāma, sa eṣa kiśorako 'śvājāneyaḥ syāt? tattāvadgatvā paśyāmi/
445.017. sa tasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
445.017. sa tenāśvājāneyenoktah--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ tvayā teṣāmaśvānāṃ sakāśāllabdham? mayaikākinaiva tasya kumbhakārasya suvarṇalakṣaṃ dattam/
445.018. sa mūrchitakaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ/
445.019. jalapariṣekena pratyāgataprāṇaḥ pādayor nipatya kṣamāpitavān//
body.translated_text:
445.001. When the horse had lowered himself, the king mounted and set forth.
445.001. As he went, water was encountered.
445.002. He did not descend there.
445.002. The king asked the charioteer: 'Is he afraid?' 'Sire, he is not afraid.
445.002. But he thinks: "I must not splash the king with tail-water."'
445.003. His tail was placed in a golden tube.
445.003. He crossed that water.
445.004. He went to the garden and remained at leisure.
445.004. The neighboring kings heard that King <s>Brahmadatta</s> had gone to the garden.
445.005. Coming, they blockaded the city gates.
445.005. King <s>Brahmadatta</s> heard that the neighboring kings had seized the city gates.
445.006. He mounted the thoroughbred.
445.006. Between <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and the garden there was a lotus pond called <s>Brahmavatī</s>, covered with lotuses, white lotuses, and water-lilies.
445.007. The thoroughbred, treading upon the lotuses, entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
445.008. The king, pleased, said to his ministers: 'Sirs, to one who saves the life of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king, anointed and consecrated — what should be done for him?' 'Sire, half the kingdom should be given.'
445.009. The king said: 'He is an animal.
445.010. What use is half a kingdom to him? Rather, in his honor, for seven days let gifts be given, let merit be made, and let an out-of-season <s>Kaumudī</s> (moonlight) festival be held.'
445.011. The ministers began giving gifts for seven days, making merit for seven days, and a seven-day out-of-season moonlight festival was proclaimed.
445.012. The caravan-leader asked some men: 'Sirs, why is there an out-of-season moonlight festival?' They told him: 'There is a shrine called <s>Pūjitaka</s>.
445.013. From there, a thoroughbred was taken from the potter for a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold and brought here.
445.014. Today he saved the king's life.
445.014. In his honor, gifts are being given for seven days, merit is being made, and an out-of-season moonlight festival has been proclaimed.'
445.015. The caravan-leader thought: 'Could it be that the colt I discarded is this very thoroughbred? Let me go and see.'
445.017. He went to him.
445.017. The thoroughbred said to him: 'Good man, what did you gain from those horses? I alone gave that potter a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold.'
445.018. He fainted and fell to the ground.
445.019. Revived by a sprinkling of water, he fell at his feet and begged forgiveness.

body.text:
445.020. kiṃ manyadhve bḥkṣavo yo 'sau sārthavāhaḥ, eṣa eva jīvakastena kālena tena samayena/
445.021. yo 'śvājāneyaḥ, eṣa eva panthakastena kālena tena samayena/
445.021. tadāpi yadā asyaiṣa guṇānāmanabhijñaḥ, tadāsyāsatkāraṃ prayuktavān/
445.022. yadā tu guṇānāmabhijñaḥ, tadā pādayor nipatya kṣamāpitavān/
445.023. etarhyapyeṣa yadā guṇānāmanabhijñaḥ, tadā asatkāraṃ prayuktavān/
445.023. yadā guṇānāmabhijñaḥ, tadā pādayor nipatya kṣamapayati//
body.translated_text:
445.020. 'What do you think, O monks? That caravan-leader — he is this very <s>Jīvaka</s>, at that time, in that era.
445.021. That thoroughbred — he is this very <s>Panthaka</s>, at that time, in that era.
445.021. Then too, when he was unaware of his virtues, he treated him with disrespect.
445.022. But when he recognized his virtues, he fell at his feet and begged forgiveness.
445.023. Now too, when he was unaware of his virtues, he treated him with disrespect.
445.023. When he recognized his virtues, he fell at his feet and begged forgiveness.'

body.text: 445.025. iti śrīdivyāvadāne cūḍāpakṣāvadānaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: 445.025. Thus concludes the <s>Cūḍāpakṣāvadāna</s> (The Story of the Lock of Hair) in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text: 446.001. div36 mākandikāvadānam/
body.translated_text: 446.001. The <s>Mākandikāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Mākandikā</s>).

body.text:
446.002. buddho bhagavān kuruṣu janapadacārikāṃ carat kalmāṣadamyamanuprāptaḥ/
446.002. tena khalu punaḥ samayena kalmāṣadamye mākandiko nāma parivrājakaḥ prativasati/
446.003. tasya sākalir nāma patnī/
446.004. tasya duhitā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā/
446.004. tasyā asthīni sūkṣmāṇi susūkṣmāṇi, na śakyata upamā kartum/
446.005. tasyāstrīṇi saptāhānyekaviṃśatiṃ divasān vistareṇa jātimahī saṃvṛttā yāvajjātamahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate--kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti? jñātaya ūcuh--iyaṃ dārikā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā/
446.008. tasyā asthīni sūkṣmāṇi susūkṣmāṇi, na śakyate upamā kartum/
446.008. bhavatu dārikāyā anupameti nāma/
446.009. tasyā anupameti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
446.009. sonnītā vardhitā/
446.009. mākandikaḥ saṃlakṣayati--iyaṃ dārikā na mayā kasyacit kulena dātavyā na dhanena nāpi śrutena, kiṃ tu yo 'syā rūpeṇa samo vāpyadhiko vā, tasya mayā dātavyeti//
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, wandering on a tour of the countryside among the <s>Kurus</s>, arrived at <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s>. Now at that time, in <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s>, there dwelt a wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājaka</s>) named <s>Mākandika</s>. His wife was named <s>Sākalī</s>. A daughter was born to him — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. Her bones were fine, exceedingly fine — no comparison could be made. For three weeks — twenty-one days — an elaborate birth-celebration took place. When the birth-celebration was completed, a name was to be determined: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The relatives said: 'This girl is beautiful, lovely, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. Her bones are fine, exceedingly fine — no comparison can be made. Let the girl's name be <s>Anupamā</s> (Incomparable).' Thus her name was established as <s>Anupamā</s>. She was nurtured and raised. <s>Mākandika</s> reflected: 'This girl of mine should not be given to anyone for family, nor for wealth, nor for learning. Rather, whoever is equal to or surpasses her in beauty — to him I shall give her.'

body.text:
446.012. atrāntare bhagavān kuruṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran kalmāṣadamyamanuprāptaḥ/
446.012. kalmāṣadamye viharati kurūṇāṃ nigame viharati/
446.013. atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya kalmāṣadamyaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
446.014. kalmāṣadamyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātraḥ pratikrāntaḥ/
446.015. pātracīvaraṃ pratiśāmya pādau prakṣāmya anyatamavṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇaḥ suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍīkṛtaṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā/
446.016. tena khalu samayena mākandikaḥ parivrajakaḥ puṣpasamidhasyārthe nirgato 'bhut/
446.017. adrākṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājako bhagavantaṃ dūradevānyataravṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍīkṛtaṃ paryaṅka baddhvā niṣaṇṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ dūrādevānyataravṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍīlṛtaṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā niṣaṇṇaṃ prāsādikaṃ pradarśanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ parameṇa cittavyupaśamena samanvāgataṃ suvarṇayūpamiva śriyā jvalantam/
446.020. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prītiprāmodyajātaḥ/
446.020. sa saṃlakṣayati--yādṛśo 'yaṃ śramaṇaḥ prāsādikaḥ pradarśanīyaḥ sakalajanamanohārī, durlabhastu sarvastrījanasya patiḥ pratirūpaḥ prāgeva anupamāyāḥ/
446.022. labdho me jāmāteti/
446.022. yena svaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
446.022. upasaṃkramya patnīmāmantrayate--yatkhalu bhadre jānīyāh--labdho me duhiturjāmātā/
446.023. alaṃkuruṣva, anupamāṃ dadāmīti/
446.024. sā kathyati--kasya prayacchasīti? sa kathayati--śramaṇasya gautamasyeti/
446.024. sā kathayati--gacchāvastāvatpaśyāva iti/
446.025. mākandikastayā sārdhaṃ gataḥ/
446.025. dūrāttayā dṛṣṭaḥ/
446.025. tasyā antarmārge smṛtirupapannā/
446.026. gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
446.027. dṛṣṭo mayā vipra sa piṇḍahetoḥ kalmāṣadamye vicaranmaharṣiḥ/
446.029. bhūratnabhā santi tasya pragacchato 'tyunnamate na caiva(?)//1//
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, the Blessed One, wandering on a tour of the countryside among the <s>Kurus</s>, arrived at <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s>. He dwelt in <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s>, in the settlement of the <s>Kurus</s>. Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s> for alms. Having gone for alms in <s>Kalmāṣadamya</s>, having finished his meal, after eating and returning from his alms-round, he put away his bowl and robe, washed his feet, and sat down at the foot of a certain tree, having crossed his legs like the coils of a sleeping serpent-king. At that time, the wanderer <s>Mākandika</s> had gone out to gather flowers and kindling-wood. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer saw the Blessed One from afar, seated at the foot of a certain tree, cross-legged like the coils of a sleeping serpent-king — pleasing, beautiful to behold, with senses calmed, mind calmed, endowed with the supreme tranquility of mind, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post. Seeing him, he was filled with joy and gladness. He reflected: 'Such a <s>śramaṇa</s> — so pleasing, so beautiful to behold, captivating the minds of all people — a suitable husband is hard to find for any woman, let alone for <s>Anupamā</s>. I have found a son-in-law!' He went to his own dwelling. Having approached, he addressed his wife: 'Know this, good lady — I have found a son-in-law for our daughter. Adorn her! I shall give <s>Anupamā</s> away.' She asked: 'To whom will you give her?' He said: 'To the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.' She said: 'Let us go and see first.' <s>Mākandika</s> went with her. She saw him from afar. On the way, recollection arose in her. She spoke a verse:

body.text:
446.031. nāsau bhaktāṃ bhajate kumārikām/
446.031. nivarta, yāsyāmaḥ svakaṃ niveśanam/
446.031. so 'pi gāthāṃ bhāsate--
body.translated_text: 'He does not desire a maiden who is devoted to him. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' He too spoke a verse:

body.text:
447.001. <447>amaṅgale sākalike tvaṃ māṃgalayakāle vadase hyamaṅgalam/
447.003. saceddruta samadhikṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati punarapyasau kāmaguṇyeṣu raṃsyate//2// iti/
447.005. sā ānupamāṃ vastrāmlakārairalaṃkṛtya saṃprasthitā/
447.005. bhagavānapi tasnādvanaṣaṇḍādanyavanaṣaṇḍaṃ saṃprashtitaḥ/
447.006. adrākṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājako bhagavantaṃ tṛṇasaṃstaraṇakam/
447.006. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ patnīmāmantrayate--yatkhalu bhavati jānīyāh--eṣa te duhitustṛṇasaṃstaraka iti/
447.007. sā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
447.009. raktasya śayyā bhavatativikopitā dviṣṭasya śayyā sahasā nipīḍitā/
447.011. sūḍhasya śayyā khalu pādato gatā suvītarāgeṇa nisevitā nviyam/
447.013. nāsau bhartā bhajate kumārikāṃ nirvata, yāsyāmaḥ svaṃ niveśanam//3//
body.translated_text: 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>! At an auspicious time you speak what is inauspicious. If the matter is quickly brought to a conclusion, he will again delight in the pleasures of the senses.' //2// She adorned <s>Anupamā</s> with garments and ornaments and set out. The Blessed One too departed from that grove to another grove. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer saw the Blessed One's grass-mat seat. Seeing it, he addressed his wife: 'Know this, good lady — this is your daughter's son-in-law's grass-mat seat.' She spoke a verse: 'A man who is passionate has a bed that is greatly disheveled; a man who is hateful has a bed that is violently compressed;'

body.text:
447.015. amaṅgale sākalike tvaṃ maṅgalyakāle vadase hyamaṅgalam/
447.017. sāceddrutaṃ samadhikṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati punarapyasau kāmaguṇeṣu raṃsyate//4//
body.translated_text: 'A deluded man's bed is in disarray; but this bed was used by one who is perfectly free from passion. He does not desire a maiden as a husband. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' //3//

body.text:
447.019. adrākṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājakaḥ/
447.019. bhagavataḥ padāni dṛṣṭvā punaḥ patnīmāmantrayate--imāni te bhavanti bhadre duhiturjāmātuḥ padāni/
447.020. gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
447.021. raktasya puṃsaḥ padamutpaṭaṃ syānnipīḍitaṃ dveṣavataḥ padaṃ ca/
447.023. padaṃ hi mūḍhasya visṛṣṭadehaṃ suvītarāgasya padaṃ tvihedṛśam/
447.025. nāsau bhartā bhajate kumārikām/
447.026. nivarta, yāsyāmaḥ svakaṃ niveśanam//5//
body.translated_text: 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>! At an auspicious time you speak what is inauspicious. If the matter is quickly brought to a conclusion, he will again delight in the pleasures of the senses.' //4//

body.text:
447.027. amaṅgale sākalike pūrvavat/
447.028. bhagavatotkaśaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ/
447.028. aśrauṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājako bhagavata utkāśanaśabdaṃ śuśrāva/
447.029. śrutvā ca punaḥ punaḥ patnīmāmantrayate--eṣa te bhavati huhiturjāmāturutkāśanaśabda iti/
447.030. sā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
447.031. rakto naro bhavati hi gadadasvaro dviṣṭo naro bhavati hi khakkhaṭāsvaraḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer saw the Blessed One's footprints. Seeing them, he again addressed his wife: 'These, good lady, are the footprints of your daughter's son-in-law.' She spoke a verse: 'A passionate man's footprint is raised up; a hateful man's footprint is pressed down;'

body.text:
448.001. <448>mūḍho naro hi bhavati samākulasvaro buddho hyayaṃ brāhmaṇadundubhisvaraḥ/
448.003. nāsau bhartā bhajate kumārikāṃ nivarta yāsyāmaḥ svakaṃ niveśanam//3//
body.translated_text: 'A deluded man's footprint is loose-bodied; but one who is perfectly free from passion has a footprint like this. He does not desire a maiden as a husband. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' //5//

body.text:
448.005. amaṅgale sākalike pūrvavat/
448.006. bhagavatā mākandikaḥ parivrājako dūrādivalokitaḥ/
448.006. adrākṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājako bhagavantamavalokayantam/
448.007. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ patnīmāmantrayate sma--eṣa te bhavati duhiturjāmātā nirīkṣata iti/
448.008. sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
448.009. rakto naro bhavati hi cañcalekṣaṇo dviṣṭo bhujagaghoraviṣo yathekṣate/
448.011. mūḍo naraḥ saṃtamasīva paśyati dvijavītarāgo yugamātradarśī/
448.013. na eṣa bhartā bhajate kumārikāṃ nivarta yāsyāmaḥ svakaṃ niveśanam//7//
body.translated_text: 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>!' — as before. The Blessed One cleared his throat. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer heard the Blessed One's throat-clearing sound. Having heard it, he again addressed his wife: 'This, good lady, is the throat-clearing sound of your daughter's son-in-law.' She spoke a verse: 'A passionate man has a hoarse, cracking voice; a hateful man has a harsh, grating voice;'

body.text:
448.015. amaṅgale sākalike pūrvavat/
448.016. bhagavāṃścakramyate/
448.016. adrākṣīnmākandikaḥ parivrājako bhagavantaṃ caṃkramyamāṇam/
448.017. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ patnīmāmantrayate--eṣa duhiturjāmātā caṃkramyata iti/
448.017. sā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
448.018. yathāsya tetre ca yathāvalekitam yathāsya kāle sthita eva gacchataḥ/
448.020. yathaiva padmaṃ stimite jale 'sya netraṃ viśiṣṭe vadane virājate/
448.022. na eṣa bhartā bhajate kumārikāṃ nivarta yāsyāmaḥ svakaṃ niveśanam//8//
body.translated_text: 'A deluded man has a confused, agitated voice; but this one has a voice like the drum of <s>Brahmā</s>. He does not desire a maiden as a husband. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' //6// 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>!' — as before. The Blessed One gazed upon <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer from afar. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer saw the Blessed One gazing. Seeing him, he again addressed his wife: 'This, your daughter's son-in-law, is looking!' She spoke a verse: 'A passionate man has restless, darting eyes; a hateful one gazes like a terrible, venomous serpent;'

body.text:
448.024. amaṅgale sākalike tvaṃ maṅgalakāle vadase hyamaṅgalam/
448.026. saceddrutaṃ samadhikṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati punarapyayaṃ kāmaguṇeṣu raṃsyate//9//
body.translated_text: 'A deluded man sees as if in utter darkness; but one free from passion sees only a yoke's length ahead. He does not desire a maiden as a husband. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' //7// 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>!' — as before. The Blessed One walked back and forth. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer saw the Blessed One walking. Seeing him, he again addressed his wife: 'Your daughter's son-in-law is walking!' She spoke a verse: 'How he stretches and how he looks about, how he walks steadily at the proper pace,'

body.text:
448.028. vaśiṣṭhośīramaunalāyanā(?) apatyahetoratatkāmamohitāḥ/
448.030. dharmo munīnāṃ hi sanātano hyayamapatyamutpāditavān sanātanaḥ//10//
body.translated_text: 'Just as a lotus in still water, so his eye shines in his distinguished face. He does not desire a maiden as a husband. Turn back — let us return to our own dwelling.' //8//

body.text:
449.001. atha mākandikaḥ parivrājako yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
449.001. upasaṃkramya bhagavantamidamavocat--
449.003. imāṃ bhagavān paśyatu me sūtāṃ satīṃ rūpopapannāṃ pramadāmalaṃkṛtām/
449.005. kāmārthinīm yadbhavate pradīyate sahānayā sādhurivācaratāṃ bhavān/
449.007. sametya candro nabhasīva rohiṇīm//11//
body.translated_text: 'Inauspicious <s>Sākalī</s>! At an auspicious time you speak what is inauspicious. If the matter is quickly brought to a conclusion, he will again delight in the pleasures of the senses.' //9// '<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Uśīra</s>, <s>Mauna</s>, <s>Lāyana</s> — for the sake of offspring, not deluded by desire for it — the <s>Dharma</s> of sages is indeed eternal; he who begot offspring is the eternal one.' //10//

body.text:
449.008. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--yadyahamanupamāyā anunayavacanaṃ brūyām, sthānametadvidyate yadanupamā rāgeṇa svinnā kālaṃ kurvāṇā bhaviṣyati/
449.009. tattasyāḥ pratighavacanaṃ brūyāmiti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
449.011. dṛṣṭā mayā mārasutā hi vipra tṛṣṇā na me nāpi tathā ratiśca/
449.013. chando na me kāmaguṇeṣu kaścit/
449.014. tasmādimāṃ mūtrapurīṣapūrṇāṃ praṣṭuṃ hi yattāmapi notsaheyam//12//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: 'Behold, Blessed One, my daughter — well-born, endowed with beauty, an adorned young woman, seeking a lover — she is offered to you. Together with her, may the Blessed One conduct himself well, like the moon meeting <s>Rohiṇī</s> in the sky.' //11// The Blessed One reflected: 'If I were to speak words of affection to <s>Anupamā</s>, it is possible that <s>Anupamā</s>, drenched with passion, would die. Therefore I shall speak words of aversion to her.' Knowing this, he spoke a verse: 'I have seen, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the daughters of <s>Māra</s> — <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (Craving), and likewise <s>Rati</s> (Delight);'

body.text:
449.016. mākandiko gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
449.017. sutāmimāṃ paśyasi kiṃ madīyāṃ hīnāṅginīṃ rūpaguṇairviyuktām/
449.019. chandaṃ na yenātra karoṣi cārau viviktabhāveṣviva kāmabhogī//13// iti/
449.021. bhagavānapi gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
449.022. yasmādihārthī viṣayeṣu mūṭaḥ sa prārthayedvipra sutāṃ tavemām/
449.024. rūpopapannāṃ viṣayeṣu saktāmavītarāgo 'tra janaḥ pramūḍaḥ//14//
body.translated_text: 'I have no desire whatsoever for the pleasures of the senses. Therefore this one, filled with urine and excrement — I would not even wish to touch her with my foot.' //12// <s>Mākandika</s> spoke a verse: 'Do you see this daughter of mine as deficient in limbs, lacking beauty and virtues? You have no desire for her beauty — like one who delights in solitude, indifferent to sensual pleasures.' //13// The Blessed One also spoke a verse: 'Since one who is deluded, desiring sense-objects, would seek your daughter, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — endowed with beauty, attached to sense-objects — the person without passion here is bewildered.' //14//

body.text:
449.026. ahaṃ tu buddho munisattamaḥ kṛtī prāptā mayā bodhiranuttarā śivā/
449.028. padmam yathā vārikaṇairaliptaṃ carāmi loke 'nupalipta eva//15//
body.translated_text: 'But I am the <s>Buddha</s>, the best of sages, accomplished. I have attained unsurpassed, auspicious awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>). Just as a lotus is untouched by drops of water, so I move through the world, entirely unstained.' //15//

body.text:
449.030. nīlāmbujaṃ kardamavārimadhye yathā ca paṅkena va nopaliptam/
449.032. tathā hyahaṃ brāhmaṇa lokamadhye carāmi kāmeṣu viviktah {eva}//16// iti/
body.translated_text: 'Just as a blue lotus in the midst of muddy water is not stained by the mud, so too I, O <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, move through the world, detached from sensual pleasures.' //16//

body.text:
450.001. athānupamā bhagavatā mūtrapurīṣavādena samudācaritā vītaharṣā durmanāḥ saṃvṛttā/
450.001. tasyā yadrāgaparyavasthānaṃ tadvigatam, dveṣaparyavasthānamutpannam, sthūlībhūtāryasthītikāvarībhūtekṣiṇī(?)/
450.003. tena sa khalu samayenānyatamo mahallo, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthito 'bhūt/
450.003. atha mahallo bhagavantamidamavocat--
450.005. samantadṛṣṭe pratigṛhya nārīmasmatsametāṃ bhagavan prayaccha/
450.007. ratā vayaṃ hi pramadāmalaṃkṛtāṃ bhokṣyāmahe ghīra yathānulomam//17// iti/
450.009. evamukte bhaganāṃstaṃ mahallamidamavocat--apehi puruṣa, mā me puratastiṣṭheti/
450.009. sa ruṣito gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
450.011. idaṃ ca te pātramidaṃ ca cīvaram yaṣṭiśca kuṇḍī ca vrajantu niṣṭhām/
450.013. imāṃ ca śikṣāṃ svayameva dhāraya dhātrī yathā hyaṅkagataṃ kumārakam//18// iti/
450.015. evamukte sa mahallaḥ śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāya mahānanāryo 'yamiti matvā yena mākandikaḥ parivrājakastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
450.016. upasaṃkramya mākandikaṃ parivrājakamidamavocat--anuprayacchamamāntike 'nupamāmiti/
450.017. sa paryavasthitaḥ kathayati--mahalla, draṣṭamapi te na prayacchāmi, prāgeva sparcṭumiti/
450.018. evamuktasya mākandikasya parivrājakasyāntike tādṛśaṃ paryavasthānamupannam yenoṣṇaṃ śoṇitaṃ chardayitvā kālagato narakeṣūpapannaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Anupamā</s>, having been addressed by the Blessed One with talk of urine and excrement, became joyless and downcast. Whatever obsession of passion she had — that departed; an obsession of hatred arose. She became coarsened, her noble composure diminished, her vision clouded. At that time, a certain old man was standing behind the Blessed One. Then the old man said this to the Blessed One: 'O All-Seeing One, accept this woman who has come with us, and give her to us, O Blessed One. We who delight in an adorned woman will enjoy her properly and fittingly.' //17// When this was said, the Blessed One said to that old man: 'Go away, fellow! Do not stand before me.' He, angered, spoke this verse: 'Let this bowl of yours, this robe of yours, this staff and water-pot meet their end! Keep this training for yourself, as a nurse would a child held in her lap.' //18// When this was said, that old man, having rejected the training and thinking 'This one is indeed ignoble,' approached the wanderer <s>Mākandika</s>. Having approached, he said to the wanderer <s>Mākandika</s>: 'Give me <s>Anupamā</s> to my care.' He, overwhelmed with emotion, replied: 'Old man, I will not give her even for you to look at, let alone touch.' When these words were spoken, such an obsession arose in the wanderer <s>Mākandika</s> that, vomiting hot blood, he died and was reborn in the hells.

body.text:
450.020. tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--paśya bhadanta, bhagavatā anupamā labhyamānā na pratigṛhīteti/
450.021. bhagavānāha--na bhikṣava etarhi, yathā atīte 'pyadhvanyeṣā mayā labhyamānā na pratigṛhītā/
450.022. tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text: Then the monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'Behold, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One did not accept <s>Anupamā</s> even when she was available.' The Blessed One said: 'Not only now, O monks — even in a past life this woman, though available to me, was not accepted by me. Listen to this.'

body.text:
450.023. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmiṅkarvaṭake 'yaskāraḥ prativasati/
450.023. tena sadṛśātkulāt kalatramānītam/
450.024. pūrvavadyāvadduhitā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā/
450.024. unnītā vardhitā mahānītaṃ saṃvṛttā/
450.025. ayaskāraḥ saṃlakṣayati--mayaiṣā duhitā na kasyacit kulena dātavyā, na rūpeṇa na dhanena, api tu yo mama śilpena samo 'bhyadhiko vā, tasyāhamenāṃ dāsyāmīti/
450.027. yāavadanyatamo māṇavo bhikṣārthī tasya gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
450.027. sā dārikā bhaikṣamādāya nirgatā/
450.027. sa māṇavastāṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati--dārike, tvaṃ kasyaciddattā āhosvinna datteti? sā kathayati--yadā jātāhaṃ tadaiva matpitaivāṅgīkṛtya vadati--duṣkaramasau māṃ kasyaciddāsyati/
450.029. kiṃ tava pitā vadati? yo mama śilpena samo 'bhyadhiko vā, asyāhamenāṃ dāsyāmīti/
450.030. tava pitā kīdṛśaṃ śilpaṃ jānīte? sūcīmīdṛśāṃ karoti yāvadudake plavate/
450.031. sa māṇavaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpyahamanayānarthī, madāpanayo 'sya kartavya iti/
450.032. kuśalo 'sau teṣu teṣu śilpasthānakarmasthāneṣu/
body.translated_text: In the past, O monks, in a certain small town there lived an ironsmith. He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing. As before, in due course a daughter was born — beautiful, lovely, and charming. She was raised and nurtured and grew up to full womanhood. The ironsmith thought: 'I shall not give this daughter of mine to anyone by family, nor by beauty, nor by wealth — rather, whoever equals or surpasses me in craftsmanship, to him I shall give her.' In time, a certain young man entered his house seeking alms. That girl came out carrying the alms-food. That young man, seeing her, said: 'Girl, have you been given to anyone or not?' She said: 'From the time I was born, my father himself declared: "It would be difficult for him to give me to anyone."' 'What does your father say?' 'Whoever equals or surpasses me in craftsmanship — to him I shall give her.' 'What kind of craft does your father know?' 'He makes needles of such quality that they float on water.' The young man thought: 'Though I have no interest in this girl, I should bring down his pride.' He was skilled in various craft-stations and work-stations.

body.text:
451.001. <451>tenāyaskārabhāṇḍikām yācitvā anyatra gṛhe susūkṣmāḥ sūcyo ghaṭitāḥ, yā udake plavante/
451.002. ekā ca mahatī ghaṭitā yasyāṃ sapta sūcyaḥ pratikṣiptāḥ saha tayā plavante/
451.002. sa tāḥ kṛtvā tasyāyaskārasya gṛhamāgataḥ/
451.003. sa kathayati--sūcyaḥ sūcya iti/
451.003. tayā dārikayā dṛṣṭāḥ/
451.003. sā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
451.005. unmattakastvaṃ kaṭuko 'tha vāsi acetanaḥ/
451.006. ayaskāragṛhe yastvaṃ sūcīṃ viktretumāgataḥ//19// iti/
451.007. so 'pi gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
451.008. nāhamunmattako vāsmi kaṭuko 'hamacetanaḥ/
451.009. mānāvatāraṇārthaṃ tu mayā śilpaṃ pradṛśyate//20//
body.translated_text: Having borrowed ironsmith's tools, he fashioned in another house extremely fine needles that floated on water. He also fashioned one large needle into which seven needles were inserted — together with it, they floated. Having made these, he came to the house of that ironsmith. He said: 'Needles! Needles!' The girl saw them. She spoke this verse: 'You are a madman, or a bitter fool, or a witless one — you who have come to an ironsmith's house to sell needles!' //19// He too spoke a verse: 'I am neither a madman, nor bitter, nor witless. It is to bring down your pride that I display my craft.' //20//

body.text:
451.010. sacetpitā te jānīyācchilpaṃ mama hi yādṛśam/
451.011. tvāṃ caivānuprayaccheta anyacca vipratam (vipulam?) dhanam//21// iti/
451.012. sā kathayati--kīdṛśaṃ tvaṃ śilpaṃ jānīṣe? īdṛṣīṃ sūcīṃ karomi yodake plavate/
451.013. tayā mātur niveditam--amba, śilpakarmātrāgata iti/
451.013. sā kathayati--praveśayeti/
451.013. tayā praveśitaḥ/
451.014. ayaskārabhāryā kathayati--kīdṛśaṃ tvaṃ śilpaṃ jānīṣe? tena samākhyātam/
451.014. tayā svāmine niveditaḥ/
451.015. āryaputra, ayaṃ śilpadārakaḥ/
451.015. īdṛśaṃ jānīta iti/
451.015. sa kathayati--yadyevamānaya pānīyam, paśyāmīti/
451.016. tayā pānīyasya bhājanaṃ pūrayitvopanāmitam/
451.016. tenaikā sūcī prakṣiptā/
451.017. sā plotumārabdhā/
451.017. evaṃ dvitīyā, tṛtīyā/
451.017. tataḥ sā mahatī sūcī prakṣiptā/
451.017. sāpi plotumārabdhā/
451.018. punastasyāmekā sūcī prakṣiptā/
451.018. tathāpi plotumārabdhā/
451.018. evaṃ dvitīyāṃ tṛtīyām yāvat saptasūcīṃ prakṣipya prakṣiptāstathāpi plotumārabdhāḥ/
451.019. ayaskāraḥ saṃlakṣayati--mamaiṣo 'dhikataraḥ śilpena/
451.020. asmai duhitaramanuprayacchām/
451.020. iti viditvā tāṃ dārikāṃ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitāṃ kṛtvā vāmena pāṇinā gṛhītvā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā bhṛṅgārakamādāya māṇavasya purataḥ sthitvā kathayati--imāṃ te 'haṃ māṇavaka duhitaramanuprayacchāmi bhāryārthāyeti/
451.022. sa kathayati--nāhamanayārthī, kiṃ tu tavaiva madāpanayaḥ kartavya iti mayā śilpamupadarśitamiti//
body.translated_text: 'If your father knew what manner of craft is mine, he would give you to me and abundant wealth besides.' //21// She said: 'What kind of craft do you know?' 'I make needles of such quality that they float on water.' She reported this to her mother: 'Mother, a craftsman has come here.' She said: 'Let him enter.' She let him in. The ironsmith's wife said: 'What kind of craft do you know?' He told her. She reported to her husband: 'My lord, here is a craft-lad. He knows such-and-such.' He said: 'If so, bring water — let me see.' She filled a vessel with water and presented it. He cast one needle in — it began to float. Likewise a second and a third. Then the large needle was cast in — it too began to float. Then one more needle was cast into it — it too began to float. Likewise a second, a third — until, having cast in seven needles, all of them began to float. The ironsmith thought: 'This one surpasses me in craftsmanship. I shall give him my daughter.' Having decided this, he adorned that girl with all ornaments, took her by the left hand, and holding a golden water-ewer in his right hand, stood before the young man and said: 'I give you, young man, this my daughter as a wife.' He said: 'I have no interest in her. Rather, it was only to bring down your pride that I displayed my craft.'

body.text:
451.024. bhagavānāha--kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau māṇavaḥ, ahameva sa tena kālena tena samayena/
451.025. yo 'sāvayaskāraḥ, eṣa eva mākandikastena kālena tena samayena/
451.025. yāsāvayaskārabhāryā, eṣaivāsau mākandikabhāryā tena kālena tena samayena/
451.026. yāsāvayaskāraduhitā, eṣaivāsāvanupamā tena kālena tena samayena/
451.027. tadāpyeṣā mayā labhyamānā na pratigṛhītā/
451.028. etarhyapyeṣā mayā labhyamānā na pratigṛhītā//
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, O monks? That young man — that was I myself at that time, in that era. That ironsmith — that was this very <s>Mākandika</s> at that time, in that era. That ironsmith's wife — that was this very wife of <s>Mākandika</s> at that time, in that era. That ironsmith's daughter — that was this very <s>Anupamā</s> at that time, in that era. At that time too, though available to me, she was not accepted by me. Now too, though available to me, she has not been accepted by me.'

body.text:
451.029. punarapi bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--paśya bhadanta ayaṃ mahallako 'nupamāmāgamyānayena vyasanamāpanna iti/
451.030. bhagavānāha--bhikṣava etarhi yathātīte 'pyadhvanyeṣa anupamāmāgamya sāntaḥpuro 'nayena vyasanamāpannaḥ/
451.031. tacchrūyatām//
body.translated_text: Again, the monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'Behold, Venerable Sir, this old man, having come after <s>Anupamā</s>, met with disaster through this mishap.' The Blessed One said: 'O monks, not only now — even in a past life, this one, having come after <s>Anupamā</s>, met with disaster together with his retinue through a mishap. Listen to this.'

body.text:
452.001. <452>bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ siṃhakalpāyāṃ siṃhakesarī nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanaṃ pūrvavadyāvaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
452.002. tena khalu samayena siṃhakalpāyāṃ siṃhako nāma sārthavāhaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigrahaḥ pūrvavadyāvattena kalatramānītam/
452.004. sā āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā/
452.004. na cāsyāḥ kiṃcidamano 'jñaśabdaśravaṇam yāvadgarbhasya paripākāya/
452.005. sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūtā/
452.005. dārako jātah abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇah chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhurvidtīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṇa saṃgatabhrūs tuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ/
452.007. tasya trīṇi saptakānyekaviṃśatiṃ divasān vistareṇa tasya jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate--kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti? jñātaya ūcuh--ayaṃ dārakaḥ siṃhasya sārthavahasya putraḥ/
452.009. bhavatu siṃhala iti nāma/
452.009. tasya siṃhala iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
452.010. siṃhalo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattaḥ pūrvavadyāvadaṣṭāsu parīkṣāsu ghaṭako vācakaḥ piṇḍitaḥ paṭupracāraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ/
452.011. tasya pitrā trīṇi vāsagṛhāṇi māpitāni haimantikaṃ graiṣmikaṃ vārṣikam/
452.012. trīṇyantaḥpurāṇi vyavasthāpitāni jyeṣṭhaṃ madhyaṃ kanīyasam/
452.013. so 'pareṇa samayena pitaramāhvayate--tāta, anujānīhi, mahāsamudramavatarāmīti/
452.014. sa kathayati--putra, tāvatprabhūtaṃ me dhanajātamasti yadi tvaṃ tilataṇḍulakulatthādiparibhogena ratnāni me paribhokṣyase, tathāpi me bhogā na tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gamiṣyanti/
452.015. tadyāvadahaṃ jīvāmi, tāvat krīḍa ramasva paricāraya/
452.016. mamātyayād dhanenopārjitaṃ kariṣyasīti/
452.016. sa bhūyo bhūyaḥ kathayati--tāta, anujānīhi, mahāsamudramavatarāmīti/
452.017. sa tenāvaśyanirbandhaṃ jñātvā uktah--putra, evaṃ kuru/
452.018. kiṃ tu bhayabhairavasahiṣṇunā te bhavitavyamiti/
452.018. tena siṃhakalpāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ siṃhakalpanivāsino vaṇijo nānādeśābhyāgatāśca/
452.020. siṃhalasārthavāho mahāsamudramavatariṣyatīti/
452.020. yo yuṣmākamutsahate siṃhalena sārthavāhena sārdhamaśulkenātarapaṇyena mahāsamudramavatartum, sa mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānayatviti/
452.022. tataḥ pañcabhirvaṇikśatairmahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānītam/
452.022. mātāpitarau bhṛtyāṃśca suhṛtsambandhibāndhavānavalokya divasatithimuhūrtaprayogeṇa kṛtakautukama.ṅgalasvastyayanaḥ śakaṭairbhāraiḥ piṭakair mūṭairuṣṭrairgobhirgardabhaiḥ prabhūtaṃ mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyamādāya pañcabhirvaṇikśataiḥ saparivāraḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
452.025. so 'nupūrveṇa grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrājadhānīṣu cañcūryamāṇaḥ pattanānyavalokayan samudratīramanuprāptaḥ/
452.026. vistareṇa rākṣasīsūtraṃ sarvaṃ vācyam/
452.026. sarve te vaṇijo bālahāśvarājātpatitāḥ, tābhiśca rākṣasībhirbhakṣitāḥ/
452.027. siṃhalaka ekaḥ svastikṣemābhyāṃ jambudvīpamanuprāptaḥ/
452.028. siṃhalabhāryā yā rākṣasī sā rākṣasībhirucyate--bhagini, asmābhiḥ svakasvakāḥ svāmino bhikṣitāḥ, tvayā svāmī nirvāhitaḥ/
452.029. yadi tāvattamānayiṣyasītyevaṃ kuśalam, no cetvāṃ bhakṣayām iti/
452.030. sā saṃtrastā kathayati--yadi yuṣmākameṣa nirbandho māṃ dhariṣyatha ānayāmīti/
452.031. tāḥ kathayanti--śobhanam/
452.031. evaṃ kuruṣveti/
452.031. sā paramabhīṣaṇarūpamabhinirmāya laghuladhveva gatvā siṃhalasya sārthavāhasya purato gatvā sthitā/
452.032. siṃhalena sārthavahena niṣkoṣamasiṃ kṛtvā <453>saṃtrāsitā apakrāntā/
body.translated_text:
452.001. 'In a former time, O monks, in <s>Siṃhakalpā</s>, a king named <s>Siṃhakesarin</s> ruled a prosperous, flourishing, secure, abundant kingdom, and so on as before, governing righteously.
452.002. At that time in <s>Siṃhakalpā</s>, there dwelt a caravan-leader named <s>Siṃhaka</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, of wide and extensive household, and so on as before, until he took a wife.
452.004. She became pregnant.
452.004. There was nothing displeasing to her, no hearing of inauspicious words, until the maturation of the embryo.
452.005. After eight or nine months, she gave birth.
452.005. A boy was born — handsome, beautiful, pleasing, fair, golden-complexioned, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a tall nose, joined brows, a prominent nose, endowed with all limbs and appendages.
452.007. For three periods of seven — twenty-one days — they celebrated his birth festival in grand style and established his name: "What shall be the boy's name?" The relatives said: "This boy is the son of the caravan-leader <s>Siṃha</s>.
452.009. Let his name be <s>Siṃhala</s>." His name was established as <s>Siṃhala</s>.
452.010. The boy <s>Siṃhala</s> was given to eight nurses, and so on as before, until he became skilled, articulate, learned, and accomplished in the eight evaluations.
452.011. His father had three residential palaces built: for winter, summer, and the rainy season.
452.012. Three inner courts were established: the senior, the middle, and the junior.
452.013. On another occasion, he addressed his father: "Father, give me leave — I wish to set out to sea."
452.014. He said: "Son, I have such abundant wealth that even if you consumed my riches along with sesame, rice, horse-gram, and other provisions, my possessions would not diminish, be exhausted, or be depleted.
452.015. So long as I live, sport, delight, and amuse yourself.
452.016. After my death, you may earn wealth."
452.016. He asked again and again: "Father, give me leave — I wish to set out to sea."
452.017. Knowing his insistent determination, he said: "Son, do as you wish.
452.018. But you must be one who endures fear and terror."
452.018. He had the bell-proclamation made in the royal capital <s>Siṃhakalpā</s>: "Let the merchants dwelling in <s>Siṃhakalpā</s> and those come from various countries hear!
452.020. The caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s> intends to set out to sea.
452.020. Whoever among you is willing to set out to sea with the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>, free of charge and with untaxed merchandise, let him gather goods suitable for the ocean voyage."
452.022. Then five hundred merchants gathered goods suitable for the ocean voyage.
452.022.
