Having seen his parents, servants, friends, relatives, and kinsmen, and at the proper conjunction of day, lunar date, and hour, having performed the auspicious rites, blessings, and benedictions, with carts, loads, baskets, bundles, camels, cattle, and donkeys, taking abundant merchandise suitable for the ocean voyage, accompanied by the five hundred merchants and their retinues, he set out.
452.025. Gradually, wandering through villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, inspecting the ports, he reached the shore of the ocean.
452.026. The entire <s>Rākṣasī</s> narrative should be told in detail.
452.026. All those merchants fell from the horse-king <s>Bālāha</s>, and were devoured by those <s>Rākṣasīs</s>.
452.027. <s>Siṃhala</s> alone reached <s>Jambudvīpa</s> safely and securely.
452.028. <s>Siṃhala</s>'s wife, who was a <s>Rākṣasī</s>, was told by the other <s>Rākṣasīs</s>: "Sister, we each devoured our own husbands, but you let your husband escape.
452.029. If you will bring him back, well and good; otherwise, we shall devour you."
452.030. She, frightened, said: "If this is your insistence, support me and I shall bring him back."
452.031. They said: "Very well. Do so."
452.031. She assumed a supremely terrifying form, and going swiftly, she stood before the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>.
452.032. <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader drew his sword from its sheath and frightened her away.

body.text:
453.001. yāvanmadhyadeśāt sārtha āgataḥ/
453.001. sā rākṣasī sārthavāhasya pādayor nipatyāha--sārthavāha, ahaṃ tāmradvīpakasya rājño duhitā/
453.002. tenāhaṃ siṃhalasārthavāhasya bhāryārthaṃ dattā/
453.003. tasya mahāsamudramadhyagatasya makareṇa matsyajātena yānapātraṃ bhagnam/
453.003. tenāhamamaṅgaleti kṛtvā choritā/
453.004. tadarhasi taṃ mamopasaṃvarayitumiti/
453.004. tenādhivāsitaṃ kṣamāpayāmīti/
453.004. sa tasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
453.005. viśrambhakathālāpena muhūrtaṃ sthitvā kathayati--vayasya, rājaduhitāsau tvayā pariṇitā/
453.006. mā tāmasthāne parityaja, kṣamasveti/
453.006. sa kathayati--vayasya, nāsau rājaduhitā, tāmradvīpādasau rākṣasī/
453.007. atha kathamihāgatā? tena vṛttamārocitam/
453.007. sa tūṣṇīmavasthitaḥ/
453.008. siṃhalaḥ sārthavāho 'nukramataḥ svagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
453.008. sāpi rākṣasī svayamatīvarūpayauvanasampannamahāsundarīmānuṣīrūpamāsthāya siṃhalasadṛśanirviśeṣasundaraṃ putraṃ nirmāya taṃ putramādāya siṃhakalpāṃ rājadhānīmanuprāptā/
453.010. siṃhalasya sārthavāhasya svagṛhadvāramūle 'vasthitā/
453.010. janakāyenāsau mukhabimbakena pratyabhijñātaḥ/
453.011. te kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, jñāyantāmayaṃ dārakaḥ siṃhalasya sārthavāhasya putra iti/
453.012. rākṣasī kathayati--bhavantaḥ, parijñāto yuṣmābhiḥ/
453.012. tasyaivāyaṃ putra iti/
453.013. te kathayanti--bhagini, kuta āgatā, kasya vā duhitā tvamiti? sā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, ahaṃ tāmradvīparājasya duhitā siṃhalasya sārthavāhasya bhāryārthaṃ dattā/
453.014. mahāsamudramadhyagatasya sārthavāhasya matsyajātena yānapātraṃ bhagnam/
453.015. tenāhamamaṅgaleti kṛtvā asthāne chotitā, kathaṃcidiha saṃprāptā/
453.016. kṣudraputrāham/
453.016. arhatha siṃhalaṃ sārthavāhaṃ kṣamayitumiti/
453.016. taistasya mātāpitror niveditam/
453.017. sa tābhyāmuktah--putra, mainām {tyaja}duhitaraṃ rājñaḥ, kṣudraputreyaṃ tapasvinī, kṣameti/
453.018. sa kathayati--tāta, naiṣā rājaduhitā, rākṣasyeṣā tāmradvīpādihāgateti/
453.018. tau kathayatah--putra, sarvā eva striyo rākṣasyaḥ/
453.019. kṣameti/
453.019. tāta, yadyeṣā yuṣmākamabhipretā, etāṃ gṛhe dhārayata/
453.020. ahamapyanyatra gacchāmīti/
453.020. tau kathayatah--putra, sutarāṃ vayamenāṃ tavaivārthāya dhārayāmaḥ/
453.020. yadyeṣā tava nābhipretā, kimasmākamanayā? na dhārayāma iti/
453.021. tābhyāṃ niṣkāsitā/
453.021. sā siṃhakesaiṇo rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatā/
453.022. amātyai rājño niveditam--deva, īdṛśī rūpayauvanasampannā strī rājadvāre tiṣṭhatīti/
453.023. rājā kathayati--praveśayeti/
453.023. paśyāma iti/
453.023. sā taiḥ praveśitā/

body.translated_text:
453.001. Meanwhile, a caravan arrived from the central country.
453.001. The <s>Rākṣasī</s>, falling at the caravan-leader's feet, said: "Caravan-leader, I am the daughter of the king of <s>Tāmradvīpa</s> (Copper Island).
453.002. I was given as a wife to the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>.
453.003. When the caravan-leader was in the midst of the great ocean, his vessel was wrecked by a sea-creature.
453.003. Considering me unlucky, he abandoned me.
453.004. Please persuade him to take me back."
453.004. He agreed: "I shall ask his pardon."
453.004. He went to <s>Siṃhala</s>.
453.005. After standing for a while in friendly conversation, he said: "Friend, that princess was married by you.
453.006. Do not abandon her in an improper place; forgive her."
453.006. He said: "Friend, she is no king's daughter — she is a <s>Rākṣasī</s> from <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>."
453.007. "Then how has she come here?" He told him what had happened.
453.007. The man stood in silence.
453.008. The caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s> gradually reached his own home.
453.008. The <s>Rākṣasī</s> too, assuming of her own accord the form of a supremely beautiful young human woman, creating a boy as handsome as <s>Siṃhala</s> himself, and taking that child, reached the royal capital <s>Siṃhakalpā</s>.
453.010. She stood at the doorstep of the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>'s house.
453.010. The crowd recognized the child by his facial features.
453.011. They said: "Sirs, recognize this child — he is the son of the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>!"
453.012. The <s>Rākṣasī</s> said: "Sirs, you have recognized him correctly.
453.012. He is indeed his son."
453.013. They said: "Sister, where have you come from, and whose daughter are you?" She said: "Sirs, I am the daughter of the king of <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>, given as a wife to the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>.
453.014. When the caravan-leader was in the midst of the great ocean, his vessel was wrecked by a sea-creature.
453.015. Considering me unlucky, he abandoned me without cause; somehow I have arrived here.
453.016. I am a mother with a small child.
453.016. Please persuade the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s> to forgive me."
453.016. They informed his parents.
453.017. They said to him: "Son, do not abandon this princess, the king's daughter; she is a poor woman with a small child — forgive her."
453.018. He said: "Father, she is no king's daughter — she is a <s>Rākṣasī</s> who has come here from <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>."
453.018. They said: "Son, all women are <s>Rākṣasīs</s>!
453.019. Forgive her."
453.019. "Father, if she is agreeable to you, keep her in the house.
453.020. I too shall go elsewhere."
453.020. They said: "Son, we keep her only for your sake.
453.020. If she is not agreeable to you, what use is she to us? We will not keep her."
453.021. She was turned out by them.
453.021. She went to King <s>Siṃhakesarin</s>.
453.022. The ministers informed the king: "Sire, such a woman, endowed with beauty and youth, stands at the palace gate."
453.023. The king said: "Let her enter.
453.023. Let us see."
453.023. She was brought in.
453.023. Her senses were captivating.
453.024. The king, seeing her, was inflamed with passion.
453.024. Greeting her with words of welcome, he said: "From where and how have you come, and whose are you?"
453.025. She fell at his feet and said: "Sire, I am the daughter of the king of <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>, given as a wife to the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>.
453.026. When the caravan-leader was in the midst of the great ocean, his vessel was wrecked by a sea-creature.
453.027. Hearing that I was unlucky, he abandoned me without cause; somehow I have arrived here.
453.028. I am a mother with a small child.
453.028. May Your Majesty please persuade the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s> to forgive me."
453.028. The king comforted her.
453.029. He ordered the ministers: "Go, sirs, summon the caravan-leader <s>Siṃhala</s>."
453.029. They summoned him.
453.030. The king said: "<s>Siṃhala</s>, keep this king's daughter; forgive her."
453.030. He said: "Sire, she is no king's daughter — she is a <s>Rākṣasī</s> who has come here from <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>."
453.031. The king said: "Caravan-leader, all women are <s>Rākṣasīs</s>; forgive her.
453.032. If she is not agreeable to you, give her to me."
453.032. The caravan-leader said: "Sire, she is a <s>Rākṣasī</s>!"

body.translated_text: 'I do not give her; I do not choose a husband.' She was brought by the king into the inner palace. By her, the king was brought under her power. Then on another occasion, having given a sleeping potion to the king together with the inner palace, she went to those <s>Rākṣasīs</s> and said: 'Sisters, what use is <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader to you? I have given a sleeping potion to King <s>Siṃhakesarin</s> together with the inner palace. Come, let us devour him.' They, having fashioned themselves in a supremely terrifying form with distorted hands, feet, and noses, came at night to <s>Siṃhakalpa</s>. By them, that king together with the inner palace retinue was devoured. When dawn broke, the palace gates were not opened. Corpse-eating birds began to circle above the royal palace. The ministers, officers, military commanders, townsmen, and countryfolk stood at the palace gate. This report spread throughout the royal capital of <s>Siṃhakalpa</s>: 'The palace gates are not opened. Corpse-eating birds are circling above the royal palace. The ministers, officers, military commanders, townsmen, and countryfolk stand at the palace gate.' <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader heard this. He hurried swiftly, taking his sword, and went. He said: 'Sirs, think clearly — the king has been devoured by that <s>Rākṣasī</s>.' The ministers asked: 'What should be done here?' He said: 'Bring a ladder — I shall see.' They brought one. <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader, taking his sword, climbed up. By him they were terrified. Some of them fled, seizing hands and feet; some fled with their heads. Then <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader seized the gates of the royal palace. The ministers cleansed the royal palace. The citizens, ministers, and countryfolk, assembling together, said: 'Sirs, the king together with the inner palace retinue has been devoured by the <s>Rākṣasīs</s>. He has no prince — whom shall we consecrate here?' Some said: 'One who is brave and wise.' Others said: 'Who other than <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader is brave and wise? Let us consecrate <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader.' 'Let us do so.' They said to <s>Siṃhala</s> the caravan-leader: 'Caravan-leader, accept the kingdom.' He said: 'I live by the trade of a merchant. What use is a kingdom to me?' They said: 'Caravan-leader, no one else is able to maintain the kingdom. Accept it.' He said: 'I accept on one condition — if you follow my commands.' 'Accept; we shall follow — excellent for you.' Then, having made a great city-decoration in his honor, he was consecrated as king with great pomp. He summoned learned masters of various arts from various countries and trained himself further in many skills, and likewise archery-masters in archery. He gave orders to the ministers: 'Sirs, prepare and equip the fourfold army.' King <s>Siṃhala</s>, selecting the finest elephants, horses, chariots, and men from the fourfold army, loaded them onto ships and set out for <s>Tāmradvīpa</s> (Copper Island). Proceeding gradually, he reached the seashore. The market-flag of those <s>Rākṣasīs</s> began to tremble. They began to discuss among themselves: 'Ladies, the market-flag is trembling. Surely humans from <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, delighting in battle, have come. Let us investigate.' They went to the seashore. They saw many hundreds of ships that had reached the seashore. Having seen them, half of them went out to meet them. Then, by the <s>vidyā</s>-holders they were possessed, and by the archery-masters they were struck down. The survivors fell at the feet of King <s>Siṃhala</s> and said: 'Lord, forgive us.' He said: 'I forgive on one condition — if you uproot this city and go elsewhere, and do not harm anyone in my dominion.'

body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O monks? He who was <s>Siṃhala</s> — that was I myself, at that time, in that era. He who was King <s>Siṃhakesarin</s> — that is this very elder, at that time, in that era. She who was the <s>Rākṣasī</s> — that is this very <s>Anupamā</s>, at that time, in that era. Then too, <s>Anupamā</s> brought disaster and ruin upon him. Now too, she has brought disaster and ruin upon him because of <s>Anupamā</s>.'

body.translated_text: <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer took <s>Anupamā</s> and went to <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. He stayed in a certain park. The park-keeper reported to King <s>Udayana</s>, the <s>Vatsa</s> king: 'Lord, a beautiful, lovely, and pleasing woman stands in the park. She is worthy of His Majesty.' Hearing this, the king went to that park. He saw her — she captivated his senses. At the very sight, his heart was seized. He said to <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer: 'Whose is this girl?' He said: 'Lord, she is my daughter — she belongs to no one, Lord.' 'Why is she not given to me?' 'Lord, let her be given to the king.' 'Excellent.' The great king had many wives obtained by purchase. She was given to <s>Puṣpadanta</s> (a section of the palace). For her <s>Puṣpadanta</s> Palace, funds were given; five hundred attendant women were given, and five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> daily for flowers and garlands. <s>Mākandika</s> the wanderer was appointed chief minister. Now at that time, King <s>Udayana</s> had three chief ministers: <s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s>, <s>Ghoṣila</s>, and <s>Mākandika</s>. On another occasion, a man approached King <s>Udayana</s>. The king asked him: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Lord, I am a bringer of good news.' The ministers were ordered: 'Sirs, provide a livelihood for the bringer of good news.' They gave him a livelihood. Then another man approached. He too was asked by the king: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Lord, I am a bringer of bad news.' The king ordered the ministers: 'Sirs, provide a livelihood for this bringer of bad news as well.' They said: 'May the lord never hear bad news!' He said: 'Sirs, the affairs of kings are extensive. Provide it.' They gave him a livelihood as well. On another occasion, King <s>Udayana</s>, <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, and <s>Anupamā</s> were standing in one place. Then the king sneezed. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> said: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!' <s>Anupamā</s> said: 'Homage to His Majesty!' <s>Anupamā</s> said: 'Great king, <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> eats your food and makes obeisance to the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>!' The king said: '<s>Anupamā</s>, it is not like that. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> is a lay-devotee (<s>upāsikā</s>). She must make obeisance to the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>.' She fell silent. Her maid-servant was instructed: 'Girl, when the lord, <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, and I are in private, you shall drop a bronze vessel on the staircase.' 'So be it.' She dropped the bronze vessel on the staircase when they were standing in private. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> said: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!' <s>Anupamā</s>, having said 'Homage to His Majesty!' said: 'She eats your food and makes obeisance to the <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>!' The king said: '<s>Anupamā</s>, do not create agitation over this — she is a lay-devotee; there is no fault here.' King <s>Udayana</s> ate one day at <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s quarters, and the next day at <s>Anupamā</s>'s.

body.text:
456.001. rājñā śākunikasyājñā dattā--yasmin divase śyāmāvatyā bhojanavāraḥ, tasmin divase jīvantaḥ kapiṃjalā ānetavyā iti/
456.002. śākunikena jīvantaḥ kapiṃjalā rājña upanītāḥ/
456.003. rājā kathayati--anupamāyāḥ samarpayeti/
456.003. anupamayā śrutam/
456.004. sā kathayati--deva, na mama vāraḥ/
456.004. śyāmāvatyā vāra iti/
456.004. rājā kathayati--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, śyāmāvatyāḥ samarpayeti/
456.005. tena śyāmāvatyāḥ sakāśamupanītah--devasyārthāya sādhayeti/
456.005. sā kathayati--kimahaṃ śākunikāyinī? na mama prāṇātipātaḥ kalpate/
456.006. gaccheti/
456.006. tena rājñe gatvā niveditam--deva, śyāmāvatī kathayati--kimahaṃ śākunikāyinī? na mama prāṇātipātaḥ kalpate/
456.008. gaccheti/
456.008. anupamā śrutvā kathayati--deva, yadyasāvucyate śramaṇasya gautamasyārthāya sādhayeti sāmprataṃ saparivārā sādhayet/
456.009. rājā saṃlakṣayati--syādevam/
456.009. tenāsau puruṣa uktah--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, evaṃ vada--bhagavato 'rthāya sādhayeti/
456.010. saṃprasthito 'nupamayā pracchannamuktah--praghātayitvānayeti/
456.011. tena praghātayitvā śyāmāvatyā upanītāḥ/
456.011. deva kathayati--bhagavato 'rthāya sādhayeti/
456.012. sā saparivārā udyuktā/
456.012. śākunikena gatvā rājñe niveditam--sā deva saparivārā udyukteti/
456.013. anupamā kathayati--śrutaṃ devena? yadi tāvatprāṇātipāto na kalpate, śramaṇasyārthāya na kalpate, devasyāpi kalpate? devasya na kalpate iti kuta etat? rājā paryavasthito dhanuḥ pūrayitvā saṃprathitaḥ/
456.015. mitāmitramadhyamo lokaḥ/
456.015. aparayā śyāmāvatyā niveditam--devo 'tyarthaṃ paryavasthito dhanuḥ pūrayitvā āgacchati, kṣamayeti/
456.016. tayā svopaniṣaduktā--bhaginyaḥ, sarvā yūyaṃ maitrīṃ samāpadyadhvamiti/
456.017. tāḥ sarvā maitrīsamāpannāḥ/
456.018. rājñā ā karṇāddhanuḥ pūrayitvā śaraḥ kṣiptaḥ/
456.018. so 'rdhamārge patitaḥ/
456.018. dvitīyaḥ kṣiptaḥ/
456.018. sa nivartya rājñaḥ samīpe patitaḥ/
456.019. tṛtīyaṃ kṣeptumārabdhaḥ/
456.019. śyāmāvatī kathayati--deva, mā kṣepsyasi/
456.019. mā sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyatīti/
456.020. rājā vinītaḥ kathayati--tvaṃ devī nāgī yakṣiṇī gandharvī kinnarī mahoragīti? sā kathayati--na/
456.021. atha kā tvam? bhagavataḥ śrāvikā anāgāminī/
456.021. maya bhagavato 'ntike 'nāgāmiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, ebhiśca pañcabhiḥ strīśataiḥ satyāni dṛṣṭānīti/
456.022. rājā abhiprasannaḥ kathayati--varaṃ te 'nuprayacchāmīti/
456.023. sā kathayati--yadi devo 'bhiprasannaḥ, yadā devo 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśati, tadā mamāntike dharmānvayamupasthāpayediti/
456.024. rājā kathayati--śobhanam/
456.025. evaṃ bhavatviti/
456.025. so 'nupamāyāḥ śyāmāvatyā antike dharmānvayaṃ prasādayati/
456.025. yānyasya navasasyāni navaphalāni navartukāni samāpadyante, tāni tatprathamataḥ śyāmāvatyāḥ prayacchati/
456.027. īṣryāprakṛtirmātṛgrāmaḥ/
456.027. anupamā saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ rājā maya sārthaṃ ratikrīḍāṃ pratyanubhavati/
456.028. śyāmāvatyā navaiḥ phalair navaiḥ sasyakair navartukaiḥ kārāṃ karoti/
456.028. tadupāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam yenaiṣā praghātyata iti/
456.029. sā ca tasyāḥ praghātanāya randhrānveṣaṇatatparā avasthitā/
456.029. rājñaścānyatamaḥ kārvaṭiko viruddhaḥ/
456.030. tenaikaṃ daṇḍasthānaṃ preṣitam/
456.030. taddhatuprahatamāgatam/
456.031. evaṃ dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam/
456.031. amātyāḥ kathayanti--devasya balaṃ hīyate, kārvaṭikasya balaṃ varthate/
456.032. yadi devaḥ svayameva na gacchati, sthānametadvidyate yat sarvathāsau durdamyo <457>bhaviṣyati/
body.translated_text:
456.001. The king gave orders to the fowler: 'On the day when it is <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s turn to prepare the meal, living francolins are to be brought.'
456.002. The fowler brought live francolins to the king.
456.003. The king said: 'Deliver them to <s>Anupamā</s>.'
456.003. <s>Anupamā</s> heard.
456.004. She said: 'Sire, it is not my turn.
456.004. It is <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s turn.'
456.004. The king said: 'Go, good man, deliver them to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>.'
456.005. They were brought to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>: 'Prepare them for the king's use.'
456.005. She said: 'Am I a fowler's woman? Taking of life is not fitting for me.
456.006. Go away.'
456.006. He went and reported to the king: 'Sire, <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> says: "Am I a fowler's woman? Taking of life is not fitting for me.
456.008. Go away."'
456.008. <s>Anupamā</s>, having heard, said: 'Sire, if she is told "prepare them for the <s>Śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s>'s use," she together with her retinue will prepare them at once.'
456.009. The king thought: 'That may be so.'
456.009. He instructed the man: 'Go, good man, and say this: "Prepare them for the Blessed One's use."'
456.010. As he departed, <s>Anupamā</s> secretly instructed him: 'Kill them first and then bring them.'
456.011. He killed them and brought them to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>.
456.011. 'The king says: "Prepare them for the Blessed One's use."'
456.012. She and her retinue set to work.
456.012. The fowler went and reported to the king: 'She, Sire, and her retinue have set to work.'
456.013. <s>Anupamā</s> said: 'Has the king heard? If taking life is not fitting for her, if it is not fitting for the <s>Śramaṇa</s>'s use — is it fitting for the king too? Whence comes this notion that it is not fitting for the king?'
456.013. The king became furious and, drawing his bow fully, set out.
456.015. The world is divided into friends, enemies, and neutrals.
456.015. Another woman reported to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>: 'The king is extremely furious and comes with bow drawn — appease him.'
456.016. She instructed her companions: 'Sisters, all of you enter the <s>maitrī samāpatti</s> (attainment of loving-kindness).'
456.017. They all entered the attainment of loving-kindness.
456.018. The king, having drawn his bow to the ear, shot an arrow.
456.018. It fell halfway.
456.018. He shot a second.
456.018. It turned back and fell near the king.
456.019. He began to shoot a third.
456.019. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> said: 'Sire, do not shoot.
456.019. Otherwise, all will be lost for everyone.'
456.020. The king, humbled, said: 'Are you, O queen, a <s>Nāgī</s>, a <s>Yakṣiṇī</s>, a <s>Gandharvī</s>, a <s>Kinnarī</s>, or a <s>Mahoragī</s>?' She said: 'No.
456.021. What then are you?' 'I am a disciple of the Blessed One, a non-returner (<s>anāgāminī</s>).
456.021. I have directly realized the fruit of non-returning in the Blessed One's presence, and these five hundred women have seen the truths.'
456.022. The king, deeply pleased, said: 'I grant you a boon.'
456.023. She said: 'If the king is pleased, whenever the king enters the inner quarters, let him establish a <s>Dharma</s> connection in my presence.'
456.024. The king said: 'Excellent.
456.025. So be it.'
456.025. He established a <s>Dharma</s> connection with <s>Anupamā</s> in <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s presence.
456.025. Whatever new crops, new fruits, and new seasonal produce arose, he gave them first to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>.
456.027. Women are jealous by nature.
456.027. <s>Anupamā</s> thought: 'This king enjoys amorous sport with me,
456.028. yet he shows favor to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> with new fruits, new crops, and new seasonal produce.
456.028. A stratagem must be devised by which she may be destroyed.'
456.029. She stood ready, intent on finding an opening for her destruction.
456.029. A certain provincial chief had rebelled against the king.
456.030. A punitive force was sent against him.
456.030. It came back defeated.
456.031. A second and a third likewise.
456.031. The ministers said: 'The king's forces are declining; the provincial chief's forces are growing.
456.032. If the king himself does not go, it is possible that he will become wholly unconquerable.'

body.text:
457.001. tena kauśāmbyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--yo mama vijite kaścicchastropajīvī prativasati, tena sarveṇa gantavyamiti/
457.002. tena saṃprasthitena yogandharāyaṇa uktah--tvamiha tiṣṭheti/
457.003. sa na saṃpratipadyate/
457.003. sa kathayati--devenaiva sārdhaṃ gacchāmīti/
457.003. ghoṣilo 'pyukta evameva kathayati/
457.004. rājñā mākandikaḥ sthāpita uktaśca--śyāmāvatyā yogodvahanaṃ kartavyamiti/
457.005. saṃprasthitenāpyanuvrajan sa evamevoktaḥ/
457.005. nivartamānenāpi tena saṃpratipannam/
457.005. so 'nupamāyāḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
457.006. tayā pṛṣṭah--tāta, ka iha devena sthāpitah? aham/
457.006. sā saṃlakṣayati--śobhanam/
457.007. śakyamanena sahāyena vairaniryātanaṃ kartumiti viditvā kathayati--nānujānīṣe śyāmāvatī kā mama bhavatīti/
457.008. putri, jāne sapatnīti/
457.008. tāta satyamevam/
457.008. nānujānīṣe kataro dharmo 'tyarthaṃ bādhata iti? putri, jāne īrṣyā mātsaryaṃ ca/
457.009. tāta yadyevam, śyāmāvatīṃ praghātaya/
457.010. sa kathayati--kiṃ me dve śirasī? yāvat trirapyahaṃ rājñā siṃdiṣṭah--śyāmāvatyā yogodvāhanaṃ kariṣyasīti/
457.011. bhavatu nāmāpi na gṛhītumiti/
457.011. sā kathayati--tāta, īdṛśo 'pi tvaṃ mūrkhah? asti kaścitpitā duhiturarthe vimukhaḥ, yaḥ sapatnyāḥ sakāśe atīva snehaṃ karoti? praghātayasītyevaṃ kuśalam/
457.013. no cedahaṃ paurāṇe sthāne sthāpayāmīti/
457.013. sa bhītaḥ saṃlakṣayati--strīvaśagā rājānaḥ/
457.014. syādevamiti/
457.015. sā kathayati--śobhanam/
457.015. evaṃ kuru/
457.015. sa śyāmāvatyāḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ/
457.016. sa kathayati--devi, kiṃ te karaṇīyamasti? sā kathayati--mākandika, na kiṃcitkaraṇīyamasti/
457.017. api tvetā dārikā rātrau pradīpena buddhavacanaṃ paṭhanti, atra bhūrjena prayojanaṃ tailena masinā kalamayā tulena/
457.018. sa kathayati--devi, śobhanam/
457.018. upāvartayāmīti/
457.018. tena prabhūtamupāvartya praveśitam, dvārakoṣṭhake rāśirvyavasthāpitaḥ/
457.019. śyāmāvatī kathayati--mākandika, alaṃ paryāptaṃtī/
457.020. mākandikaḥ kathayati--devi praveśayāmi, na bhūyo bhūyaḥ praveśitavyam/
457.021. tenapaścime bhūrjabhārake 'gniṃ prakṣipya śaraḥ praveśitaḥ/
457.021. etna saṃdhukṣitena dvārakoṣṭhakaḥ prajvālitaḥ/
457.022. kauśāmbīnivāsī janakāyaḥ pradhāvito nirvāpayitum/
457.022. mākandiko niṣkoṣamasiṃ kṛtvā janakāyaṃ nirvāsayitumārabdhaḥ/
457.023. tiṣṭhata, kim yūyaṃ rājño 'ntaḥpuraṃ draṣṭum? kauśāmbyām yantrakarācāryaḥ kathayati--ahamenaṃ dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ jvalantam yantreṇānyasthānaṃ saṃkramayāmīti/
457.024. so 'pi mākandikenaivamevokto nivartitaḥ/
457.025. śyāmāvatī ṛddhyā ākāśamutplutya kathayati--bhaginyaḥ, asmābhirevaitāni karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayānyoghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
457.027. asmābhireva kṛtyānyupacitāni/
457.027. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? uktaṃ ca bhagavatā--
457.029. naivāntarikṣe na samudramadhye na parvatānāṃ vivaraṃ praviśya/
457.031. na vidyate pṛthivīpradeśo yatra sthitaṃ na prasaheta karma//22// iti/
body.translated_text:
457.001. The king had a bell-proclamation made in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>: 'Whoever in my domain lives by the profession of arms — all must march forth.'
457.002. Setting out, he told <s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s>: 'You stay here.'
457.003. He did not agree.
457.003. He said: 'I shall go with the king himself.'
457.003. <s>Ghoṣila</s> too, when told likewise, said the same.
457.004. The king stationed <s>Mākandika</s> and instructed him: 'You must maintain <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s provisions.'
457.005. Though the departing king told him likewise while following, he agreed only when the king turned back.
457.005. He went to <s>Anupamā</s>.
457.006. She asked: 'Father, who has the king stationed here?' 'I.'
457.006. She thought: 'Excellent.
457.007. With this ally it is possible to carry out revenge.' Knowing this, she said: 'Do you not know what <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> is to me?'
457.008. 'Daughter, I know — a co-wife.'
457.008. 'Father, truly so.
457.008. Do you not know which passion torments most?' 'Daughter, I know — jealousy and envy.'
457.009. 'Father, if so, destroy <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>.'
457.010. He said: 'Do I have two heads? Three times the king instructed me: "You must maintain <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>'s provisions."
457.011. So be it — I refuse to accept this.'
457.011. She said: 'Father, are you truly such a fool? Is there any father who is indifferent to his daughter's interests, who shows excessive affection to a co-wife? That you would destroy her — that would be excellent.
457.013. If not, I shall put you back in your former position.'
457.013. He was frightened and thought: 'Kings are slaves to their women.
457.014. It may be so.'
457.015. She said: 'Excellent.
457.015. Do it.'
457.015. He went to <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>.
457.016. He said: 'Queen, is there anything you need?' She said: '<s>Mākandika</s>, there is nothing I need.
457.017. But these girls recite the <s>Buddha</s>'s words at night by lamplight. For that, there is need of birch-bark, oil, ink, reed-pens, and brushes.'
457.018. He said: 'Queen, excellent.
457.018. I shall arrange it.'
457.018. He gathered large quantities and brought them in, piling them up in the doorway chamber.
457.019. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> said: '<s>Mākandika</s>, enough — that is sufficient.'
457.020. <s>Mākandika</s> said: 'Queen, let me bring it in — it need not be brought again and again.'
457.021. He secretly placed fire in the last bundle of birch-bark and brought it in.
457.021. When it caught fire, the doorway chamber was set ablaze.
457.022. The people of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> rushed to extinguish it.
457.022. <s>Mākandika</s>, drawing his sword, began to drive the people away.
457.023. 'Stop! Why do you want to see the king's inner quarters?' In <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, a master of mechanical arts said: 'I shall move this burning doorway chamber to another place with a machine.'
457.024. He too was driven away by <s>Mākandika</s> in the same way.
457.025. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, rising into the sky by supernatural power, said: 'Sisters, these <s>karmas</s> were done and accumulated by us ourselves; their conditions have come together, their causes have ripened, and they stand before us overwhelmingly, inevitably.
457.027. We ourselves did and accumulated them.
457.027. Who else will experience their results? And the Blessed One has said:
457.029. "Neither in the sky, nor in the midst of the ocean, nor entering a mountain cave —
457.031. there exists no place on earth where one could stand and not be overpowered by <s>karma</s>." //22//'

body.text:
458.001. <458>tatkarmaparāyaṇairvo bhavitavyamityuktvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
458.002. dṛṣṭo mayā sa bhagavāṃs tiryakprākārasaṃnibhaḥ/
458.003. ājñātāni ca satyāni kṛtaṃ buddhasya śāsanam//23// iti/
458.004. śyāmāvatīpramukhāstāḥ striyaḥ pataṅga ivotplutyāgnau nipatitāḥ/
458.004. iti tatra śyāmāvatīpramukhāni pañca strīśatāni dagdhāni/
458.005. kubjottarā sasambhrameṇa niṣpalāyitā/
458.005. mākandikena teṣāṃ pañcānāṃ strīśatānāṃ kalevarāṇi śmaśāne choritāni/
458.006. rājakulaṃ sāntarbahiḥ śodhitam/
458.007. kauśāmbīnivāsī janakāyo nānādeśābhyāgataśca vikrośannivāritaḥ//
body.translated_text:
458.001. 'You must be devoted to <s>karma</s>.' Having said this, she spoke a verse:
458.002. 'I have seen that Blessed One, resembling a sideways rampart;
458.003. the truths have been understood, the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching has been fulfilled.' //23//
458.004. <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> and the women, like moths, leapt up and fell into the fire.
458.004. Thus <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> and five hundred women were burned there.
458.005. <s>Kubjottarā</s> (the hunchbacked elder) escaped in haste.
458.005. <s>Mākandika</s> threw the bodies of those five hundred women into the cremation ground.
458.006. The royal palace was cleaned inside and out.
458.007. The people of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> and visitors from various lands were crying out but were restrained.

body.text:
458.008. atha saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya kauśāmbīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣan/
458.009. aśrauṣuḥ saṃbahulā bhikṣavaḥ kauśāmbīnagare udayanasya vatsarājasya janapadān gatasya antaḥpuramagninā dagdhaṃ pañcamātrāṇi strīśatāni śyāmāvatīpramukhāni/
458.010. śrutvā ca punaḥ kauśāmbīṃ piṇḍāya praviśyā caritvā pratikramya punaryena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntā etadūcuh--aśrauṣma vayaṃ bhadanta saṃbahulā bhikṣavo kauśāmbīṃ piṇḍāya caranta udayanasya vatsarājasyāntaḥpuramagninā dagdhaṃ pañcamātrāṇi strīśatāni śyāmāvatīpramukhāni dagdhāni//
body.translated_text:
458.008. Then a number of monks, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken their bowls and robes, entered <s>Kauśāmbī</s> for alms.
458.009. Those monks heard in the city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> that the inner quarters of King <s>Udayana</s> of <s>Vatsa</s>, who had gone to the countryside, had been burned by fire — some five hundred women led by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> had been burned.
458.010. Having heard this, and having gone for alms in <s>Kauśāmbī</s> and returned, they approached the Blessed One and said: 'We have heard, Venerable Sir — we, a number of monks, while going for alms in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, heard that the inner quarters of King <s>Udayana</s> of <s>Vatsa</s> have been burned by fire — some five hundred women led by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> have been burned.'

body.text:
458.014. bhagavānāha--bahu bhikṣavastena mohapuruṣeṇāpuṇyaṃ prasūtam yenodayanasya vatsarājasya janapadagatasyāntaḥpuramagninā dagdhaṃ pañcamātrāṇi strīśatāni śyāmāvatīpramukhāni/
458.015. kiṃ cāpi bhikṣavastena mohapuruṣeṇa bahvapuṇyaṃ prasūtam, api tu na tā durgatiṃ gatāḥ/
458.016. sarvāḥ śuddhapudgalāḥ kālagatāḥ/
458.017. tatkasya hetoh? santi tasminnantaḥpure striyo yāḥ pañcānāmavarabhāgīyānāṃ samyojanānāṃ prahāṇādupapādukāḥ/
458.018. tatra parinirvāyiṇyo 'nāgāminyo 'nāvṛttikadharmiṇyaḥ punarimaṃ lokam/
458.019. evamrūpāstasminnantaḥpure striyaḥ santi/
458.019. santi tasminnantaḥpure striyo yāstrayāṇāṃ samyojanānāṃ prahāṇādrāgadveṣamohānāṃ kālaṃ kṛtvā sakṛdāgāminyaḥ, sakṛdimaṃ lokamāgamya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyanti/
458.021. evamrūpāstasminnantaḥpure striyaḥ santi/
458.021. santi tasminnantaḥpure striyo yāstrayāṇāṃ samyojanānāṃ prahāṇācchrotāpannā avinipātadharmiṇyo niyatasamādhiparāyaṇāḥ saptakṛtvo bhavaparamāḥ saptakṛtvo devāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtya duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyanti/
458.024. evamrūpāstasminnantaḥpure striyaḥ santi/
458.024. santi tasminnantaḥpure striyo yāḥ svajīvitahetorapi śikṣāṃ na vyatikrāntāḥ/
458.025. ityevamrūpāstasminnantaḥpure striyaḥ santi/
458.025. santi tasminnantaḥpure striyo yā mamāntike prasannacittālaṃkāraṃ kṛtvā kāyasya bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapannāḥ/
458.027. evamrūpāstasminnantaḥpure striyaḥ santi/
458.027. āgamyata bhikṣavo yena śyāmāvatīpramukhānāṃ pañcastrīśatānāṃ kalevarāṇi/
458.028. evaṃ bhadanteti bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ/
458.028. atha khalu bhagavān saṃbahulairbhikṣubhiḥ sārdham yena tāsāṃ pañcānāṃ strīśatāṇāṃ kalevarāṇi tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
458.030. upasaṃkramya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--etāni bhikṣavastāni pañcaśatakalevarāṇi yatra udayano vatsarājo raktaḥ sakto gṛddho grathito mūrcchito 'dhyavasāyamāpannaḥ/
458.031. tatra naiva prājñadhīḥ pādenāpi spṛśet/
458.032. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Much demerit, O monks, was generated by that deluded man, by whom the inner palace of King <s>Udayana</s> of <s>Vatsa</s>, while he was away in the countryside, was burned by fire — five hundred women headed by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>. Yet even though, O monks, that deluded man generated much demerit, those women did not go to a bad rebirth. They all died as purified individuals. For what reason? There are women in that inner palace who, through the abandonment of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth — attaining final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> there, they are non-returners, not destined to return again to this world. Women of such quality exist in that inner palace. There are women in that inner palace who, through the abandonment of the three fetters, having reduced passion, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners — coming once more to this world, they will make an end of suffering. Women of such quality exist in that inner palace. There are women in that inner palace who, through the abandonment of the three fetters, are stream-enterers — not destined for a bad rebirth, certain in their attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, with at most seven more existences; after traversing seven times among gods and humans, they will make an end of suffering. Women of such quality exist in that inner palace. There are women in that inner palace who would not transgress the training even for the sake of their own lives. Women of such quality exist in that inner palace. There are women in that inner palace who, with minds of faith in me, having adorned their bodies, upon the breakup of the body, were reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world among the gods. Women of such quality exist in that inner palace. Come, O monks, to where the corpses of the five hundred women headed by <s>Śyām��vatī</s> are.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the monks replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with many monks, approached where the corpses of those five hundred women were. Having approached, he addressed the monks: 'These, O monks, are the five hundred corpses to which King <s>Udayana</s> of <s>Vatsa</s> was attached, infatuated, greedy, clinging, deluded, and devoted. A wise person would not touch them even with his foot.' And he spoke a verse:

body.text:
459.001. <459>mohasaṃvardhano loko bhavyarūpa iva dṛśyate/
459.002. upadhibandhanā balāstamasā parivāritāḥ/
459.003. asatsaditi paśyanti paśyatāṃ nāsti kiṃcana//24// iti/
459.004. evaṃ cāha--tasmāttarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam, yaddagdhasthūṇāyāmapi cittaṃ na pradūṣayiṣyāmaḥ prāgeva savijñānake kāye/
459.005. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam//
body.translated_text: 'The world is an increaser of delusion, appearing as if it were truly real. Fools, bound by their attachments, are surrounded by darkness. They see what is unreal as real; for those who truly see, nothing exists at all.' //24// And he said this: 'Therefore, O monks, you should train thus: "We shall not corrupt our minds even with regard to a burnt post, let alone a conscious body." Thus, O monks, you should train.'

body.text:
459.006. atha kauśāmbīnivāsinaḥ paurāḥ saṃnipatya saṃjalpitumārabdhāh--bhavantaḥ, rājña īdṛśo 'narthaḥ saṃvṛtta/
459.007. tatko nvasmākaṃ rājña ārocayiṣyatīti? tatrekai kathayanti--yo 'sāvapriyākhyāyī sa ārocayiṣyati/
459.008. taṃ śabdayāma iti/
459.008. apare kathayanti--evaṃ kurmaḥ/
459.008. tairasāvāhūyoktah--devasyedamīdṛśamapriyamanupūrvyā nivedayeti/
459.009. vṛttirdiyatām/
459.009. kimapriyākhyāyino vṛttirdīyata ityayaṃ sa kālaḥ/
459.010. yūyameva nivedayata/
459.010. te kathayanti--atorthameva tava vṛttirdattā/
459.010. kāryaṃ nivedayeti/
459.011. samayato nivedayāmi yadahaṃ bravīmi tatkurudhvam? brūhi, kariṣyāmaḥ/
459.011. evamanupūrveṇāsya nivedayitavyam--pañcahastiśatāni prayacchata, pañcahastinīśatāni pañcāśvaśatāni pañcavaḍavāśatāni pañcakumāraśatāni pañcakumārikāśatāni suvarṇalakṣaṃ kauśāmbyadhiṣṭhānam/
459.013 paṭe lekhayata puṣpadantaprāsādam yathā mākandikena bhūrjaṃ kalamā tailaṃ tūlamasirapaścime ca bhūrjabhāge 'gniḥ prakṣiptaḥ/
459.015. yathā dvārakoṣṭhakaḥ prajvālitaḥ, yathā kauśāmbīnivāsī janakāyo nirvāpayituṃ pradhāvitaḥ, yathā mākandikena niṣkoṣamasiṃ kṛtvā nivāritaḥ/
459.016. yathā yantrakalācārya āgatya kathayati--dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ jvalantamanyat sthānaṃ saṃkramayāmīti/
459.017. so 'pi mākandikena nivāritaḥ/
459.017. yathā śyamāvatīpramukhāni pañcastrīśatānyutplutya nipatitāni/
459.018. te kathayati--evaṃ kurmaḥ/
459.018. taiḥ pañcahastiśatānyupasthāpitāni pañcahastinīśatāni pañcāśvaśatāni pañcavaḍavāśatāni pañcakumāraśatāni pañcakumārikāśatāni suvarṇasya lakṣaṃ kauśāmbyadhiṣṭhānaṃ paṭe likhitaṃ puṣpadantaprāsādaḥ/
459.020. yathā mākandikena bhūrjaṃ kalamā tailaṃ tūlamasirapaścime bhūrjabhārake 'gniḥ prakṣipto yathā dvārako 'ṣṭhake prajvālitaḥ/
459.022. yathā kauśāmbīnivāsī janakāyo nivārpayituṃ pradhāvitaḥ/
459.022. yathā mākandikena niṣkoṣamasiṃ kṛtvā nivāritaḥ/
459.023. yathā yantrakalācārya āgatah--ahamenaṃ dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ jvalantamanyat sthānaṃ saṃkramayāmīti, so 'pi mākandikena nivāritaḥ/
459.024. yathā śyāmāvatīpramukhāni pañcastrīśatānyagnāvutplutya nipatitāni, tatsarvaṃ paṭe likhitam/
459.025. tato 'priyākhyāyino 'mātyānāṃ lekho 'nupreṣito rājña īdṛśo 'nartha utpanno 'hamasyānenopāyena nivedayiṣyāmi/
459.026. yuṣmābhiḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpayitavyamiti/
459.027. sa teṣāṃ lekhāṃ lekhayitvā caturaṅgabalakāyayukto 'nyatamasmin pradeśe gatvāvasthitaḥ/
459.028. udayanasya ca lekho 'nupreṣitah--deva, ahamanuṣmin pradeśe rājā/
459.028. mama ca putro mṛtyunāpahṛtaḥ/
459.029. tadahaṃ tena sārthaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ saṃgrāmayiṣyāmi/
459.029. yadi tāvattvaṃ śaknoṣi yuddhena niyoktumityevaṃ kuśalam, no cetpañcahastinīśatāni pañcāśvaśatāni pañcavaḍavāśatāni pañcakumāraśatāni pañcakumārikāśatāni suvarṇasya lakṣaṃ datvā tamāneṣyāmīti/
459.032. rājña udayanasya sa kārvaṭiko balavān saṃnāmaṃ na gacchati/
459.032. so 'mātyānāṃ kathayati--
body.translated_text: Then the citizens of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, having assembled, began to confer: 'Sirs, such a calamity has befallen the king. Who then will inform our king?' Some said: 'The one who is the bearer of unwelcome news — he shall inform him. Let us summon him.' Others said: 'Let us do so.' They summoned him and said: 'You must inform His Majesty of this unwelcome event in proper sequence.' 'Let a livelihood be given.' 'Is a livelihood given to a bearer of unwelcome news? — this is the time for it. You yourselves inform him.' They said: 'It is precisely for this purpose that a livelihood was given to you. Inform him of the matter.' 'I shall inform him on the condition that you do what I say. Shall you?' 'Speak — we shall do it.' 'In this manner it must be gradually communicated to him: Provide five hundred bull-elephants, five hundred cow-elephants, five hundred stallions, five hundred mares, five hundred boys, five hundred girls, a <s>lakṣa</s> (100,000) of gold, and the sovereignty of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. Have painted on a canvas the <s>Puṣpadanta</s> Palace — how <s>Mākandika</s> placed birch-bark, reed-grass, oil, cotton, a sword, and at the far end of the birch-bark, placed fire; how the door-chamber was set ablaze; how the citizens of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> rushed to extinguish it; how <s>Mākandika</s>, having drawn his unsheathed sword, stopped them; how the master of mechanical arts came and said: "I can move this burning door-chamber to another location" — and he too was stopped by <s>Mākandika</s>; how the five hundred women headed by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> leapt up and fell into the fire.' They said: 'Let us do so.' They prepared five hundred bull-elephants, five hundred cow-elephants, five hundred stallions, five hundred mares, five hundred boys, five hundred girls, a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold, the sovereignty of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, and had painted on a canvas the <s>Pu���padanta</s> Palace — how <s>Mākandika</s> placed birch-bark, reed-grass, oil, cotton, and a sword, and at the far end of the birch-bark bundle placed fire; how the door-chamber was set ablaze; how the citizens of <s>Kauśāmbī</s> rushed to extinguish it; how <s>Mākandika</s>, having drawn his unsheathed sword, stopped them; how the master of mechanical arts came — 'I can move this burning door-chamber to another location' — and he too was stopped by <s>Mākandika</s>; how the five hundred women headed by <s>��yāmāvatī</s> leapt up and fell into the fire — all of this was painted on the canvas. Then a written message was sent from the bearer of unwelcome news to the ministers: 'Such a calamity has befallen the king. I shall inform him by the following stratagem. You must render assistance.' He had them write the letter, and equipped with a fourfold army, stationed himself at a certain location. He also sent a letter to <s>Udayana</s>: 'Sire, in a certain territory I am a king. My son has been carried off by death. I shall wage war against Death itself. If you are able to deploy your forces in battle, very well — if not, give five hundred cow-elephants, five hundred stallions, five hundred mares, five hundred boys, five hundred girls, and a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold, and I shall bring him back.' King <s>Udayana</s>'s townsman was powerful and would not submit. He said to his ministers:

body.text:
460.001. <460>bhavantaḥ, īdṛśo 'pi rājā mūrkhah? asti kaśṣinmṛtyunāpahṛtaḥ śakyata ānetum? tadgatam/
460.002. etattasyaivaṃ likhitam--mamaivaṃnāmā kārvaṭikaḥ saṃnāmaṃ na gacchati/
460.002. sa tvamasmākaṃ tāvatsāhāyyaṃ kalpaya, paścāttavāpi sāhayyaṃ karomīti/
460.003. so 'mātyaistasyaivaṃ lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ/
460.003. sa lekhaśravaṇādevāgatya kārvaṭikasya nātidūre vyavasthāpitaḥ/
460.004. kārvaṭikena śrutam/
460.004. sa saṃlakṣayati--ekena tāvadahaṃ rājñā daśa diśo viśrāntaḥ, ayaṃ ca dvitīyaḥ/
460.005. sarvathā punarapi viṣayānna tu prāṇānnirgacchāmīti/
460.006. sa kaṇṭhe 'siṃ baddhvā nirgatya rājña udayanasya pādayor nipatitaḥ/
460.006. sa rājñā udayanena karado vyavasthāpitaḥ/
460.007. athasāvapriyākhyāyī rājalīlayā rājña udayanasya sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--deva, mama putro mṛtyunā apahṛtaḥ/
460.008. tvaṃ mama devaḥ sāhāyyaṃ kalpayatu/
460.009. ahaṃ tena sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ saṃgrāmayiṣyāmīti/
460.009. yadi tāvattvaṃ śaknoṣi yuddhena nirjetumiyevaṃ kuśalam, no cetpañcahastiśatāni pañcahastinīśatāni pañcavaḍavāśatāni pañcakumāraśatāni pañcakumārikāśatāni suvarṇasya lakṣaṃ datvā tamāneṣyāmīti/
460.011. udayano rājā kathayati--priyavayasya, mūrkhastvam/
460.012. asti kaścicchakyate mṛtyoḥ sakāśādānetumiti? sa kathayati--deva, na śakyate/
460.013. yadyevam, imaṃ paṭaṃ paśyeti/
460.013. tena paṭaḥ prasātitaḥ/
460.013. rājā paṭaṃ nirīkṣya marmavedhaviddha iva ruṣyamāṇaḥ kathayati--bhoḥ kim? kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ kathayasi śyāmāvatīpramukhāni pañca strīśatānyagninā dagdhānīti? sa paṭṭaṃ mauliṃ cāpanīya gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
460.016. nāhaṃ narendro na narendraputraḥ pādopajīvī tava deva mṛtyaḥ/
460.018. athāpriyasyeva nivedanārthamihāgato 'haṃ tava pādamūlam//25// iti/
460.020. rājā sutarāṃ nirīkṣya vicārayati/
460.020. iyaṃ kauśāmbī nagarī, idaṃ rājakulam, ayaṃ mākandikaḥ puṣpadantaṃ prāsādaṃ bhūrjādinā prayogeṇa dahati, imāni śyāmāvatīpramukhāni pañca strīśatānyagninā dahyamānānyutplutya nipatitānīti/
460.022. vicārya kathayati--bhoḥ puruṣa, kiṃ kathayasi śyāmāvatī dagdheti? deva, nāhaṃ kathayāmi api tu deva eva kathayati/
460.023. bhoḥ puruṣa, upāyena me tvayā niveditam, anyathā te mayāsinā nikṛntitamūlaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ nipātitamanvabhavisyadityutkvā mūrcchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ/
460.025. tato jalapariṣekeṇa pratyāgataprāṇaḥ kathayati--saṃnāhayata bhavantaścaturaṅgabalakāyam/
460.026. kauśāmbīṃ gacchāma iti/
460.026. amātyaiścaturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhitam/
460.027. rājā kauśāmbīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ/
460.027. anupūrveṇa saṃprāptaḥ/
460.027. tena paurāṇāṃ sakāśāt sarvaṃ śrutam/
460.028. tairamarṣitam/
460.028. tamārāgitam/
460.028. tato yogandharāyaṇasyājñā dattā--gaccha mākandikamanupamayā saha yantragṛhe prakṣipya dahyatām/
460.029. tato yogandharāyaṇena suguptaṃ bhūmigṛhe prakṣipya sthāpitaḥ/
460.030. rājñaḥ saptame divase śoko vigataḥ/
460.030. sa vigataśokaḥ/
460.030. sa kathayati--yogandharāyaṇa, kutrānupameti? tena yathāvṛttaṃ niveditam/
460.031. rājā kathayati--śobhanam/
460.031. mākandikena śyāmāvatī praghātitā, tvayāpyanupamayā saparivārayā sārdhaṃ mayā pravrajitavyaṃ jātamiti/
460.032. yogandharāyaṇaḥ kathayati--deva, ityarthameva mayā asau bhūmigṛhe prakṣipya sthāpitā/
460.032. paśyāmi tāvadyadi jīvatīti/
body.translated_text: 'Sirs, is even such a king so foolish? Can anyone who has been seized by death be brought back? That is past.' This is what was written to him: 'A certain chieftain of mine does not submit. You arrange your assistance for us now; afterward I shall also render assistance to you.' Such a letter was sent to him by the ministers. Upon hearing the letter, he came and was stationed not far from the chieftain. The chieftain heard this. He reflected: 'By one king alone I was already exhausted in all ten directions, and now there is a second. In any case, I shall depart from my territories but not from my life.' He tied a sword to his neck, came out, and fell at the feet of King <s>Udayana</s>. He was established by King <s>Udayana</s> as a tributary. Then that bringer of bad news, assuming a royal bearing, went to King <s>Udayana</s> and said: 'Lord, my son has been seized by death. May His Majesty arrange assistance for me. I shall wage war against him.' 'If you can conquer him by battle, very well; if not, give five hundred elephants, five hundred female elephants, five hundred mares, five hundred boys, five hundred girls, and a <s>lakṣa</s> of gold, and I shall bring him back.' King <s>Udayana</s> said: 'Dear friend, you are a fool. Can anyone be brought back from the presence of death?' He said: 'Lord, it cannot be done.' 'If so, look at this cloth.' He spread out the cloth. The king, gazing at the cloth, as if struck in a vital spot, said angrily: 'What? What is this?' He said: 'Sir, what are you saying — that five hundred women headed by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> were burned by fire?' He removed his turban-cloth and crown and spoke a verse: 'I am not a king, nor the son of a king — I am one who lives at your feet, O lord Death. But for the purpose of reporting bad news, I have come here to the base of your feet.' //25// The king, examining it more carefully, deliberated: 'This is the city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>; this is the royal palace; this is <s>Mākandika</s> setting fire to the <s>Puṣpadanta</s> palace by means of birch-bark and other devices; these are the five hundred women headed by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> being burned by fire, leaping up and falling down.' Having deliberated, he said: 'Sir, what are you saying — that <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> has been burned?' 'Lord, I am not saying it — rather, His Majesty himself is saying it.' 'Sir, you have reported it to me by a stratagem; otherwise, your head, its root cut off by my sword, would have been cast down upon the earth' — having said this, he fainted and fell to the ground. Then, revived by a sprinkling of water, he said: 'Prepare the fourfold army! We go to <s>Kauśāmbī</s>.' The ministers equipped the fourfold army. The king set out for <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. He arrived in due course. From the citizens he heard everything. They were enraged. They were infuriated. Then <s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s> was ordered: 'Go — throw <s>Mākandika</s> together with <s>Anupamā</s> into the machine-house and burn them.' Then <s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s> secretly threw her into an underground chamber and kept her there. On the seventh day, the king's grief subsided. His grief having subsided, he said: '<s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s>, where is <s>Anupamā</s>?' He reported the matter as it occurred. The king said: 'Excellent. <s>Mākandika</s> had <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> killed, and you too, together with <s>Anupamā</s> and her retinue — now I must go forth as a renunciant.' <s>Yogandharāyaṇa</s> said: 'Lord, for this very purpose I threw her into the underground chamber and kept her there. Let me see if she is still alive.'

body.text:
461.001. <461>tenāsau bhūmigṛhādānītā tadavasthānākliṣṭā amlānaśarīrā/
461.001. rājā dṛṣṭvā saṃlakṣayati--yatheyamamlānā, neiṣā nirāhārā/
461.002. nūnamanayā parapuruṣeṇa sārdhaṃ paricāritamiti viditvā kathayati--anupame, anyena paricāritamiti? sā kathayati--śāntaṃ pāpam, nāhamevaṃkāriṇī/
461.003. kathaṃ jāne? abhiśraddadhasi tvaṃ bhagavatah? abhiśraddadhe gautame/
461.004. tatttadā śramaṇo gautamaḥ, idānīṃ bhagavān/
461.004. api tu kiṃ navaśavāyā arthe bhagavantaṃ pravakṣyāmi, śyāmāvatyā arthe pravakṣyāmīti viditvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
461.006. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
461.006. udayano vatsarājo bhagavantamidamavocat--kiṃ bhadanta śyāmāvatīpramukhaiḥ pañcabhiḥ strīśataiḥ karma kṛtam yenāgninā dagdhāni? kubjottarā anukrameṇa niṣpalāyiteti/
461.008. bhagavānāha--ābhireva mahārāṭ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni pūrvavadyāvatphalanti khalu dehinām//
body.translated_text: He brought her out of the underground chamber — she was in the same condition, unafflicted, her body unfaded. The king, seeing her, reflected: 'Since she is so unfaded, she is not without sustenance. Surely she has been consorting with another man.' Knowing this, he said: '<s>Anupamā</s>, have you been attended by another?' She said: 'Heaven forbid! I am not one who does such things.' 'How do I know? Do you have faith in the Blessed One?' 'I have faith in <s>Gautama</s>.' 'That <s>śramaṇa</s> <s>Gautama</s> of the past is now the Blessed One.' 'But shall I speak to the Blessed One on account of a new corpse, or on account of <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>?' Knowing this, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat to one side. King <s>Udayana</s>, the <s>Vatsa</s> king, said this to the Blessed One: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, was done by the five hundred women headed by <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, that they were burned by fire? <s>Kubjottarā</s> (the Hunchback) managed to escape in time.' The Blessed One said: 'By these very women, O great king, deeds were done and accumulated, having reached their full conditions, having matured in their causes — as before, up to: deeds certainly bear fruit for embodied beings.'

body.text:
461.010. bhūtapūrvaṃ mahārāja vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryā brahmadatto rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca pūrvavadyāvaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
461.011. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
461.012. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīmanuprāptaḥ/
461.013. so 'nyatamasminnudyāne kuṭikāyāmavasthitaḥ/
461.014. rājā ca brahmadattaḥ sāntaḥpuraparivārastadudyānaṃ nirgataḥ/
461.014. tā antaḥpurikās trīḍāpuṣkiriṇyāṃ snātvā śītenānubaddhāḥ/
461.015. tato 'gramāhiṣyā preṣyadārikoktā--dārike, śītenātīva bādhyāmahe/
461.016. gaccha, etasyāaṃ kuṭikāyāmagniṃ prajvalayeti/
461.016. sā ulkāṃ prajvalya gatā/
461.016. paśyati taṃ pratyekabuddham/
461.017. tayā tasyā niveditam--devi, pravrajito 'syāṃ tiṣṭhatīti/
461.017. sā kathayati--pravrajito vā tiṣṭhatu, agniṃ datvā tāṃ prajvalayeti/
461.018. tayā na dattam/
461.018. tatastayā kupitayā svayameva dattam/
461.019. sa pratyekabuddho nirgataḥ/
461.019. ābhiḥ sarvābhirantaḥpurikābhiranumoditam/
461.019. devi, śobhanaṃ tvayā yadagnirdattaḥ/
461.020. sarvā vayaṃ prataptā iti/
461.020. sa pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--kṣatā etāstapasvinya upahatāśca/
461.021. mā atyantakṣatā etā bhaviṣyanti/
461.021. anugrahamāsāṃ karomīti/
461.021. sa tāsāmanukampārthaṃ tata evākāśamutplutya tapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ/
461.022. āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhirāvarjanakarī/
461.023. tā mūlanikṛntita iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kṣamayitumārabdhāḥ/
461.023. avatarāvatara sadbhūtadakṣiṇīya, asmākaṃ kāmapaṅkanimagnānāṃ hastoddhāramanuprayaccheti/
461.024. sa tāsāmanukampārthamavatīrṇaḥ/
461.025. tāni tasmin kārāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kārtumārabdhāh--yadasmābhirevaṃ sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye 'pakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, mā asya karmaṇo vipākamanubhavema/
461.026. yattu kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, anena vayaṃ kuśalamūlenaivaṃvidhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābhinyo, bhavema, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāramāragayema iti//
body.translated_text: 'In former times, O great king, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, King <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling the kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, and secure — as before, up to: he governed the kingdom righteously. When <s>Buddhas</s> do not arise in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of remote dwellings and beds, worthy of individual offerings, a boon to the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a countryside tour, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. He stayed in a hut in a certain park. King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, together with his inner palace retinue, went out to that park. The women of the inner palace, having bathed in the pleasure-pool, were afflicted by the cold. Then the chief queen told a maid-servant: "Girl, we are exceedingly troubled by the cold. Go, kindle a fire in that hut." She went, having lit a torch. She saw that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. She reported to the queen: "My lady, a renunciant is staying in that hut." She said: "Let the renunciant stay or not — set fire to it and light it up." She did not set fire to it. Then the queen, angered, set fire to it herself. That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> came out. All those women of the inner palace expressed their approval: "My lady, well done that you set the fire! We have all been warmed." That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> reflected: "These poor wretched women are damaged and ruined. Let them not be damaged forever. I shall show them favor." Out of compassion for them, from that very spot he rose up into the sky and began to perform the miracles of burning, raining, and flashing. Quickly, the supernatural power of a commoner wins over others. They, like a tree cut at the root, fell at his feet and began to beg forgiveness: "Come down, come down, O truly worthy recipient of offerings! Extend to us, who are sunk in the mire of desire, a hand of rescue!" Out of compassion for them, he descended. Having performed services for him, they began to make a resolve: "Whatever harm we have done to this truly worthy recipient of offerings — may we not experience the ripening of this deed. But by the merit of the services we have performed, may we become recipients of such <s>Dharmas</s>, and may we encounter a teacher even more distinguished than this one."'

body.text:
461.028. kiṃ manyase mahārāja tadā sāsau rājño brahmadattasyāgramahiṣī, eṣaiva sā śyāmāvatī tena kālena tena samayena/
461.029. yāni pañca strīśatāni, etānyeva tāni pañca strīśatāni tāni tena kālena tena samayena/
461.030. yā sā preṣyadārikā, eṣaivāsau kubjottarā tena kālena tena samayena/
461.031. yadābhiḥ pratyekabuddhasya kuṭikāṃ dagdhvā anumoditam, tasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣāṇi narakeṣu patkā yāvadetarhyapi dṛṣṭasatyā agninā dagdhāḥ/
461.032. kubjottarā anukrameṇa <462>niṣpalāyitā/
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O great king? She who was the chief queen of King <s>Brahmadatta</s> at that time — that is this very <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, at that time, in that era. Those five hundred women — those are these very five hundred women, at that time, in that era. She who was the maid-servant — that is this very <s>Kubjottarā</s>, at that time, in that era. Because they burned the hut of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and expressed their approval, by the ripening of that deed, for many years they cooked in the hells; and even now, though they had realized the truth, they were burned by fire. <s>Kubjottarā</s> managed to escape in time.'

body.text:
462.001. yatpraṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ mamāntike satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam/
462.001. iti hi mahārāja ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmāṇāṃ pūrvavadyāvadevamābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
462.002. ityevaṃ te mahārāja śikṣitavyam/
462.003. atrodayano vatsarājo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinindyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikātprakrāntaḥ/
462.005. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta kubjottarayā karma kṛtam yena kubjā saṃvṛttā? bhagavānāha--kubjottarayaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni pūrvavadyāvad phalanti khalu dehinām/
462.008. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati pūrvavadyāvaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati/
462.009. naimittikairdvādaśavārṣikā anāvṛṣṭirādiṣṭā/
462.009. rājñā vārāṇasyāmevaṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--yasya dvādaśavārṣikaṃ bhaktamasti, tena sthātavyam/
462.010. yasya nāsti tenānyatra gantavyamiti yataḥ kolenāgantavyamiti/
462.011. tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ saṃdhāno nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhoga iti vistaraḥ pūrvavadyāvad vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī/
462.013. tena koṣṭhāgārika āhūyoktah--bhoḥ puruṣa, bhaviṣyati mama saparivārasya dvādaśa varṣāṇi bhaktamiti? sa kathayati--ārya, bhaviṣyatīti/
462.014. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante pūrvavadyāvadbhoḥ puruṣa, vinyasya pravrajitasahasrasya mama dvādaśa varṣāṇi bhaktamiti/
462.016. sa kathayati--ārya, bhabiṣyatīti/
462.016. tena teṣāṃ pratijñātam/
462.016. dānaśālā māpitāḥ/
462.017. pūrvavattatra dine dine pratyekabuddhasahasraṃ bhuṅkte/
462.017. tatraikaḥ pratyekabuddho glānaḥ/
462.018. so 'nyatamasmin dine nāgacchati/
462.018. sandhānasya duhitā kathayati--tāta, eko 'dya pravrajito nāgata iti/
462.019. sa kathayati--putri, kīdṛśa iti/
462.019. sā pṛṣṭhaṃ vināmayitvā kathayati--tāta, īdṛśa iti/
462.020. yadanayā pratyekabuddho vināḍitaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena kubjā saṃvṛttā/
462.021. punarapi bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta, kubjottarayā karma kṛtam yena śrutadharāa jāteti? bhagavānāha--tena kālena tena samayena pratyekabuddhānām yaḥ saṃghasthaviraḥ sa vāyvādhikaḥ/
462.023. tasya muñjānasya pātraṃ kampate/
462.023. tasya saṃdhānaduhitrā hastāt kaṭānavatārya sa pratyekabuddha uktah--ārya, taistatpātraṃ sthāpayeti/
462.024. tena tatra sthāpitam/
462.024. niṣkampamavasthitam/
462.025. tayā pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam/
462.025. yathaiva tatpātraṃ niṣkampamavasthitam, evameva mamāpi saṃtāne ye dharmāḥ praviśeyuḥ, te niṣkrampaṃ tiṣṭhantvati/
462.026. yattayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena śrutadharā saṃvṛtā//
body.translated_text:
462.001. 'The vow that was made in my presence, the vision of truth that was gained —'
462.001. Thus, O Great King, regarding deeds that are entirely black, as before, up to: 'thus should one reflect.'
462.002. Thus, O Great King, you should train yourself.
462.003. Thereupon <s>Udayana</s>, the king of <s>Vatsa</s>, having praised and approved the words of the Blessed One, and having bowed at the Blessed One's feet with his head, departed from the Blessed One's presence.
462.005. The monks, in whom doubts had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what deed did <s>Kubjottarā</s> do that she was born hunchbacked?' The Blessed One said: 'O monks, the deeds were done and accumulated by <s>Kubjottarā</s> herself, as before, up to: deeds certainly ripen for the embodied.
462.008. In a former time, O monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled his kingdom, as before, up to: he governed righteously.
462.009. The soothsayers predicted a drought of twelve years.
462.009. The king had the bell-proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: "Whoever has provisions for twelve years, let him stay;
462.010. whoever does not, let him go elsewhere; but let no one come here from outside."
462.011. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there dwelt a householder named <s>Saṃdhāna</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, and so on in detail as before, up to: rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth.
462.013. He summoned his granary-keeper and said: "Good sir, will there be provisions for twelve years for me and my household?" He said: "Noble sir, there will."
462.014. When no <s>Buddhas</s> have arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> appear in the world, as before, up to: "Good sir, set aside provisions for twelve years for a thousand renunciants as well."
462.016. He said: "Noble sir, there will."
462.016. He made the pledge to them.
462.016. Alms-halls were built.
462.017. As before, every day a thousand <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> ate there.
462.017. One <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> among them was ill.
462.018. On a certain day, he did not come.
462.018. <s>Saṃdhāna</s>'s daughter said: "Father, one renunciant has not come today."
462.019. He said: "Daughter, what does he look like?"
462.019. She bent her back and said: "Father, he looks like this."
462.020. Because she mimicked the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, by the ripening of that deed, she was born hunchbacked.
462.021. The monks again asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, what deed did <s>Kubjottarā</s> do that she was born able to retain what she heard?" The Blessed One said: "At that time, the senior monk among the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> suffered from a wind-ailment.
462.023. His bowl trembled while he ate.
462.023. <s>Saṃdhāna</s>'s daughter took the bowl from his hand, lowering it from the frame, and said to that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>: "Noble sir, please set your bowl down there."
462.024. He set it there.
462.024. It stood without trembling.
462.025. She fell at his feet and made a vow:
462.025. "Just as this bowl stands without trembling, so may the teachings that enter my continuum remain without trembling."
462.026. By the ripening of that vow, she was born with the ability to retain all that she heard.'

body.text:
462.028. punarapi bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta kubjottarayā karma kṛtam yena dāsīsaṃvṛtteti? bhagavānāha--anayā bhikṣavastatraiśvaryamadamattayā parijano dāsīvādena samudācaritaḥ/
462.030. tasya karmavipākena dāsī saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text:
462.028. The monks again asked the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, what deed did <s>Kubjottarā</s> do that she was born a servant?' The Blessed One said: 'O monks, she, intoxicated with the pride of her wealth, addressed her household servants with the word "slave."
462.030. By the ripening of that deed, she was born a servant.'

body.text:
462.031. punarapi bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta anupamayā karma yadeṣā nirāhārā bhūmigṛhe sthāpitā amlānagātrī cotthitā/
462.032. bhagavānāha--anupamayaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni pūrvavadyāvatphalanti khalu dehinām//
body.translated_text:
462.031. The monks again asked the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, what deed did <s>Anupamā</s> do that when she was placed without food in an underground chamber, she arose with her body unwithered?'
462.032. The Blessed One said: 'O monks, the deeds were done and accumulated by <s>Anupamā</s> herself, as before, up to: deeds certainly ripen for the embodied.'

body.text:
463.001. <463>bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake dve dārike anyonyasaṃstutike kṣatriyadārikā brāhmaṇadārikā ca/
463.002. asti buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
463.003. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho 'nyatamasmiñchānte pradeśe rātriṃ vāsamupagataḥ/
463.004. aparasmin divase pūrvāhṇe nivāsya piṇḍārthī pracalitaḥ/
463.004. taṃ dṛṣṭvā te dārike prasādite, asmai praṇītānnapūrṇaṃ pātraṃ prayacchataḥ/
463.005. tatkarmaṇo vipālenānupamā jātā, ekā ghoṣilasya gṛhapaterduhitā jātā mahāsundarī śrīmatī nāma/
463.006. ekasmin samaye rājñā dṛṣṭā pṛṣṭā ca--kasyeyaṃ kanyā? māntribhiḥ kathiyam--ghoṣilasya gṛhapateḥ/
463.007. tato ghoṣilo gṛhapatiḥ samāhūyoktah--gṛhapate, tava duhiteyaṃ kanyā? sa prāha--mama deva/
463.008. kasmānmama na dīyate? dīyatāṃ mahyam/
463.009. sa prāha--deva, dattā bhavatu/
463.009. ghoṣilena gṛhapatinā dattā/
463.009. udayanena vatsarājenāntaḥpuraṃ praveśya mahatā śrīsamudayena pariṇītā/
463.010. apareṇa samayena rājā uktah--deva, bhikṣudarśanamabhikāṅkṣāmīti/
463.011. sa kathayati--ākāṅkṣase kiṃ tu bhikṣavo rājakulaṃ praviśānti/
463.012. deva, ahaṃ nāma dārakaṃ praveśitā/
463.012. sarvathā yadi bhikṣudarśanaṃ na labhe, adyāgreṇa na bhokṣye na pāsya iti/
463.013. sā anāhāratāṃ pratipannā/
463.013. rājñā ghoṣilo gṛhapatiruktah--gṛhapate, na tvaṃ duhitaraṃ pratyavekṣase? deva, kim? anāhāratāṃ pratipannā/
463.014. kimartham? bhikṣudarśanamākāṅkṣate/
463.015. tadātmano gṛhe bhaktaṃ sādhitvā kāyām(?) bhikṣusaṃghamupanimantrya bhojaya, antareṇa ca dvāraṃ chedayeti/
463.016. rājño ghoṣilasya ca saṃsaktasīmaṃ gṛham/
463.016. ghoṣilena gṛhapatinā dvāraṃ chinnam/
463.017. tato bhūri karma kārayitvā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
463.017. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
463.018. ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ ghoṣilaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
463.019. anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tuṣṇīm/
463.020. atha ghoṣilo gṛhapatirutthāyāsanādyena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamidamavocat--adhivāsayatu me bhagavāñchvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena mama nimantritaṃ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena/
463.022. pūrvavadyāvadbhagavato dūtena kālamārocayati--samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālāṃ manyata iti/
463.0bhagavānaupadhike sthitaḥ/
463.023. śāriputrapramukho bhiṣusaṃghaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ/
463.024. pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairbuddhā bhagavanta aupadhike tiṣṭhanti--abhinirhṛtaṃ manrtayate sma/
463.025. caturṇāmāyuṣmanta ājñā akopyā tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya, arahato bhikṣoḥ kṣīṇāśravasya upadhivārakasya, rājñaśca kṣatriyasya mūrdhnābhiṣiktasya/
463.026. smṛtimupasthāpayati--praviśāmeti/
463.027. sa praviśya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
463.027. atha śrīmatī devī sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ śāriputrapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā pūrvavadyāvannīcataramāsanaṃ gṛhītvā purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
463.029. athāyuṣmāñchāriputraḥ śrīmatīṃ devīṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati/
463.030. sā satyāni na paśyati/
463.030. āyuṣmāñchāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati--kimāsyāḥ santi kānicitkuśalamūlāni? na santīti paśyati/
463.031. santi kasyāntike pratibaddhāni? paśyatyātmanaḥ/
463.032. tasya dharmaṃ deśayato vicārayataśca sūryāstaṃgamanasamayo <464>jātaḥ/
body.translated_text:
463.001. 'In a former time, O monks, in a certain hamlet, there were two girls who were friends — a <s>Kṣatriya</s> girl and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> girl.
463.002. When no <s>Buddhas</s> have arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> appear in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, content with secluded lodgings and food, singularly worthy of offerings to the world.
463.003. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> spent the night at a certain secluded spot.
463.004. The next day, in the forenoon, having dressed, he set out for alms.
463.004. Seeing him, those two girls were filled with faith and gave him a bowl full of excellent food.
463.005. By the ripening of that deed, <s>Anupamā</s> was born, and one was born as the daughter of the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s>, a great beauty named <s>Śrīmatī</s>.
463.006. On one occasion, the king saw her and asked: "Whose is this maiden?" The ministers said: "The householder <s>Ghoṣila</s>'s."
463.007. Then the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s> was summoned and asked: "Householder, is this your daughter?" He said: "She is, Sire."
463.008. "Why has she not been given to me? Let her be given to me."
463.009. He said: "Sire, let her be given."
463.009. The householder <s>Ghoṣila</s> gave her.
463.009. <s>Udayana</s>, the king of <s>Vatsa</s>, took her into the inner palace and married her with great pomp.
463.010. On another occasion, she said to the king: "Sire, I desire to see monks."
463.011. He said: "You desire it, but monks enter the royal palace."
463.012. "Sire, I was merely admitted as a girl.
463.012. In any case, if I do not obtain the sight of monks, from today I shall neither eat nor drink."
463.013. She undertook a fast.
463.013. The king said to the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s>: "Householder, do you not look after your daughter?" "Sire, what is it?" "She has undertaken a fast."
463.014. "Why?" "She desires to see monks."
463.015. "Then let her have food prepared in your own house, and having invited the assembly of monks, feed them; and let a door be cut through the partition wall."
463.016. The houses of the king and <s>Ghoṣila</s> shared a common boundary.
463.016. The householder <s>Ghoṣila</s> had a door cut through.
463.017. Then, having made extensive preparations, he approached the Blessed One.
463.017. Approaching, he bowed at the Blessed One's feet with his head and sat down to one side.
463.018. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s>, seated to one side, with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>.
463.019. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent.
463.020. Then the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s>, rising from his seat and making a salutation with joined palms toward the Blessed One, said: "May the Blessed One consent to a meal tomorrow in my inner house, together with the assembly of monks, as my invitation."
463.022. As before, up to: a messenger announced the time to the Blessed One: "It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready; may the Blessed One go at his convenience."
463.023. The Blessed One remained in his lodging.
463.023. The assembly of monks headed by <s>Śāriputra</s> set out.
463.024. For five reasons, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, remain in their lodging: [he reflected upon what had been produced].
463.025. The commands of four are inviolable — of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One; of the <s>Arhat</s> monk whose defilements are destroyed, the guardian of the lodging; and of the king, the anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
463.026. He established mindfulness: "I shall enter."
463.027. He entered and sat on the seat prepared at the front of the assembly of monks.
463.027. Then Queen <s>Śrīmatī</s>, knowing the assembly of monks headed by <s>Śāriputra</s> to be comfortably seated, as before, up to: she took a lower seat and sat in front for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.
463.029. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened Queen <s>Śrīmatī</s> with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>.
463.030. She did not see the Truths.
463.030. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: "Does she have any roots of merit?" He saw that she did not.
463.031. "Under whose guidance are they bound?" He saw: under his own.
463.032. While he was teaching and reflecting on the <s>Dharma</s>, the time of sunset arrived.'

body.text:
464.001. bhikṣava utthāyāsanātprakrāntāḥ/
464.001. āyuṣmāñchāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati--kiṃ cāpi bhagavatā nānujñātam, sthānametadvidyate yadetadeva pratyakṣaṃ kṛtvā anujñāsyatīti/
464.002. sa vineyāpekṣayā tatraivāvasthitaḥ/
464.003. tena tasyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ ca prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā śrīmatyā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ pūrvavadyāvatsarvaṃ vādyaṃ triśaraṇagamabhiprasannam/
464.005. athāyuṣmāñchāriputraḥ śrīmatīṃ satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpya prakrānto yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
464.006. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
464.006. ekānte niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmāñchāriputra etatprakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavate vistaraṇārocayati/
464.007. bhagavānāha--sādhu sādhu śāriputra, saptānāmājñā akopyā--tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya, arhato bhikṣoḥ kṣīṇāśravasya, rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhnābhiṣiktasya, saṃghasthavirasya, upadhivārikasya, ācāryasya, upādhyāyasya/
464.010. atha bhagavāñchikṣākāmatayā varṇaṃ bhāṣitvā pūrvavadyāvat pūrvikā prajñaptaḥ/
464.011. iyaṃ cābhyanujñātā--evaṃ ca me śrāvakairvinayaśikṣāpadamupadeṣṭavyam/
464.011. yaḥ punarbhikṣuranirgatāyāṃ rajanyāmanudgate 'ruṇe anirhṛteṣu ratneṣu ratnasaṃmateṣu vā rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhnābhiṣiktasya indrakīlaṃ vā idrakīlasāmantaṃ vā samatikrāmedanyatra tadrūpātpratyayāt pāpāntiketi/
464.013. yaḥ punarbhikṣurityudāyī iti, so vā punaranyo 'pyevaṃjātīyah anirgatāyāṃ rajanyāmityaprabhātāyām, anudgata ityanudite aruṇe iti, aruṇo nīlāruṇaḥ pītāruṇas tāmrāruṇaḥ/
464.016. tatra nīlāruṇo nīlābhāsaḥ, pītāruṇaḥ pītābhāsaḥ, tāmrāruṇas tāmrābhāsaḥ/
464.016. iha tu tāmrāruṇo 'bhipretaḥ/
464.017. ratneṣu veti ratnānyucyante maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaṃ pūrvavadyāvaddakṣiṇāvartaḥ/
464.018. ratnasaṃmateṣu veti ratnasaṃmatamucyate sarvaṃ saṃgrāmāvacaraśastraṃ sarvaṃ ca gandharvāvacaraṃ bhāṇḍam/
464.019. rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasyeti vā rājye stryapi rājyābhiṣikeṇābhiṣiktā bhavati, rājā sā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ/
464.020. kṣatriyo 'pi brāhmaṇo 'pi vaiśyo 'pi śūdro 'pi rājyābhiṣekeṇābhiṣikto bhavati rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ/
464.021. indrakīlaṃ veti traya indrakīlaḥ/
464.021. nagare indrakīlo rājakule indrakīlo 'ntaḥpura indrakīlaśca/
464.022. indrakīlasāmantaṃ veti tatsamīpam/
464.023. samatikramedapi vigacchet/
464.023. anyatra tadrūpātpratyayāditi tadrūpaṃ pratyayaṃ sthāpayitvā/
464.024. pāpāntiketi dahati pacati yātayati pūrvavat/
464.024. tatrāpattiḥ kathaṃ bhavati? bhikṣuraprabhāte prabhātasaṃjñī nagarendrakīlaṃ samatikrāmati, āpadyate duṣkṛtām/
464.025. aprabhāte vaimatikaḥ, āpadyate duṣkṛtam/
464.026. prabhāte aprabhātasaṃjñī, athāpadyate duṣkṛtam/
464.026. prabhāte vaimatikaḥ, āpadyate duṣkṛtam/
464.027. bhikṣuraprabhāte aprabhātasaṃjñī antaḥpurendrakīlam asmatikrāmati āpadyate pāpāntikam/
464.028. prabhāte 'prabhātasaṃjñī āpadyate duṣkṛtam/
464.028. prabhāte vaimatikaḥ, āpadyate duṣkṛtam/
464.028. anāpattih--rājā śabdayati--devyaḥ kumārā āmātyā aṣṭānāmantarāyāṇāmantyatamānyatamamupathitaṃ bhavati rājā cauramanuṣyāmanuṣyavyālāgnyudakānām/
464.030. anāpattirādikarmikasyeti pūrvavat//
body.translated_text: The monks rose from their seats and departed. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'Even though this was not sanctioned by the Blessed One, there exists the possibility that, having made this matter manifest, he will sanction it.' With regard to those to be disciplined, he remained there. Having understood her disposition and latent tendencies, her element and nature, he gave such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching that, upon hearing it, <s>Śrīmatī</s>'s mountain of the view of the composite self, risen up with twenty peaks — as before, up to the point where all music became an expression of faith in the Three Refuges. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having established <s>Śrīmatī</s> in the Truths, departed and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reported this entire matter in full to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Śāriputra</s>! The commands of seven are inviolable: of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One; of an <s>Arhat</s> monk whose defilements are exhausted; of a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the crown; of the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s>; of the stores-keeper; of the preceptor; and of the teacher.' Then the Blessed One, having spoken in praise of the desire for training, as before up to the point where the preliminary rule was established, and this was sanctioned: 'Thus shall my disciples teach this <s>Vinaya</s> training rule: Whatever monk, when the night has not yet departed, when dawn has not yet risen, when the jewels and objects regarded as jewels of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king anointed on the crown have not been removed, should cross the <s>Indra</s>-post or the vicinity of the <s>Indra</s>-post, except for a proper reason — this is a <s>pāpāntika</s> (grave) offense.' The term 'whatever monk' means <s>Udāyin</s>, or anyone else of such a kind. 'When the night has not yet departed' means when it has not yet dawned. 'When dawn has not risen' — dawn is of three kinds: blue-dawn, yellow-dawn, and copper-dawn. The blue-dawn has a bluish hue; the yellow-dawn has a yellowish hue; the copper-dawn has a coppery hue. Here, the copper-dawn is intended. 'Jewels' means gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, as before up to right-spiraling conch. 'Objects regarded as jewels' means all weapons used in battle and all musical instruments of the <s>Gandharvas</s>. 'A <s>Kṣatriya</s> king anointed on the crown' — in a kingdom, even a woman, if anointed with the royal consecration, is a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the crown. Whether <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, or <s>Śūdra</s> — one anointed with the royal consecration is a king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the crown. 'The <s>Indra</s>-post' — there are three <s>Indra</s>-posts: the <s>Indra</s>-post of the city, the <s>Indra</s>-post of the royal palace, and the <s>Indra</s>-post of the inner palace. 'The vicinity of the <s>Indra</s>-post' means its neighborhood. 'Should cross' means should go beyond. 'Except for a proper reason' means setting aside a proper reason. '<s>Pāpāntika</s>' means it burns, cooks, and torments, as before. How does the offense arise? If a monk, when it has not dawned, with the perception that it has dawned, crosses the city's <s>Indra</s>-post — he commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s> (misdeed). When it has not dawned and he is uncertain — he commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s>. When it has dawned and he perceives it as not having dawned — he then commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s>. When it has dawned and he is uncertain — he commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s>. If a monk, when it has not dawned, with the perception that it has not dawned, crosses the <s>Indra</s>-post of the inner palace — he commits a <s>pāpāntika</s> offense. When it has dawned and he perceives it as not having dawned — he commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s>. When it has dawned and he is uncertain — he commits a <s>duṣkṛta</s>. There is no offense when: the king summons him; the queens, princes, or ministers summon him; one of the eight emergencies has arisen — emergencies involving the king, thieves, humans, non-humans, wild beasts, fire, or water. There is no offense for one who is a beginner — as before.

body.text: 464.031. iti śrīdivyāvadāne mākandikāvadānaṃ samāptam//
