body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Mākandikāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Mākandikā</s>) in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>.

body.text: 465.001. div37 rudrāyaṇāvadānam/
body.translated_text: Chapter 37: The <s>Rudrāyaṇāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>).

body.text:
465.002. buddho bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe/
465.002. dve mahānagare pāṭaliputraṃ rorukaṃ ca/
465.003. yadā pāṭaliputraṃ saṃvartate, tadā rorukaṃ vivartate/
465.003. roruke mahānagare rudrāyaṇo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
465.005. sadāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣāḥ/
465.005. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
465.005. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
465.006. tasya candraprabhā nāma devī, śikhaṇḍī putraḥ kumāraḥ, hirubhirustasyāgrāmātyau/
465.007. rājagṛhe rājā bimbisāro rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
465.008. tasya vaidehī mahādevī, ajātaśatruḥ putraḥ kumāraḥ, varṣakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmātyo 'grāmātyaḥ/
465.009. sadāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣāḥ/
465.009. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
465.010. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/ rājagṛhādvaṇijaḥ paṇyamādāya rorukamanuprāptāḥ/
465.010. atha rājā rudrāyaṇo 'mātyagaṇaparivṛto 'mātyānāmantrayate--bhavantaḥ, asti kasyacidanyasyāpi rājña evamavidhā janapadā ṛddhāśca sphītāśca kṣemāṣca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyāśca? sadāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣāh? devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati? atīva śasyasampattirbhavati? te vaṇijaḥ kathayanti--asti deva pūrvadeśe rājagṛhaṃ nagaram/
465.014. tatra rājā bimbisāro rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca/
465.015. tasyāpi sadāpuṣpaphalavṛkṣāḥ/
465.016. devaḥ kālena kālaṃ samyagvāridhārāmanuprayacchati/
465.016. atīva śasyasampattirbhavati/
465.017. tasya mahaśravaṇādeva tasyāntike 'nunaya utpannaḥ/
465.017. so 'mātyānāmantrayate--kiṃ bhavantastasya rājño durlabham? te kathayanti--devo ratnādhipatiḥ, sa rājā vastrādhipatiḥ/
465.018. tasya ratnāni durlabhāni/
465.019. tena tasya ratnānāṃ peṭāṃ pūrayitvā prābhṛtamanupreṣitaṃ lekhaśca dattah--priyavayasya, tvaṃ mamādṛṣṭasakhā/
465.020. yadā tava kiṃcid roruke nagare karaṇīyaṃ bhavati, mama lekho dātavyaḥ/
465.021. sarvaṃ tat pariprāpayiṣyāmi/
465.021. te taṃ prābhṛtamādāya yena rājagṛhaṃ tena prakrāntāḥ/
465.022. anupūrveṇa rājagṛhamanuprāptāḥ/
465.022. taiḥ sā ratnapeṭā rājño bimbisārasyopanāmitā lekhaśca/
465.022. rājā bimbisāro lekhaṃ vācayitvā amātyānāmantrayate--kiṃ bhavantastadrājño durlabham? amātyāḥ kathayanti--devo vastrādhipatiḥ, sa rājā ratnādhipatiḥ/
465.024. tasya vastrāṇi durlabhāni/
465.024. tena tasya mahārhāṇāṃ vastrāṇāṃ vastrāṇāṃ peṭāṃ pūrayitvā prābhṛtamanupreṣitaṃ lekhaśca dattah--priyavayasya, tvaṃ mamādṛṣṭasakhā/
465.026. yatkiṃcittava rājagṛhe prayojanaṃ bhavati, mama lekho dātavyaḥ/
465.026. tatsarvaṃ pariprāpayiṣyāmi/
465.027. te taṃ prābhṛtamādāya yena rorukaṃ tena prakrāntāḥ/
465.027. anupūrveṇa rorukamanuprāptāḥ/
465.028. taiḥ sā vastrapeṭā rājño rudtāyaṇasyopanāmitā lekhaṣca/
465.028. sa dūtaḥ pratyāgataḥ/
465.028. athāpareṇa samayena rājā rudrāyaṇo 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ/
465.029. so 'mātyānāmantrayate--bhavantaḥ, kīdṛśastasya rājño ānāhapariṇāhah? te kathayanti--yādṛśa eva devasya, api tu sa rājā svayaṃ prahartā/
465.030 prātisīmaiḥ kīdṛśaṃ rajabhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmayati? rudrāyaṇasya rājño maṇivarma pañcāṅgepetośītam uṣṇasaṃsparśamuṣṇe śootasaṃsparśaṃ duśchedaṃ durbhedaṃ viṣaghnamavabhāsātmakaṃ ca/
465.032. tena tasya taṃ prābhṛtamanupreṣitam <466>lekhaśca dattah--priyavayasya, idaṃ mayā ca tava maṇivarma prābhṛtamanupreṣitaṃ pañcāṅgopetaṃ śīte uṣṇasaṃsparśamuṣṇe śītasaṃsparśaṃ duśchedaṃ durbhedaṃ viṣaghnamavabhāsātmakam/
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground). There were two great cities: <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> and <s>Roruka</s>. When <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> wanes, <s>Roruka</s> flourishes. In the great city of <s>Roruka</s>, a king named <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> was ruling — his kingdom was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. The trees always bore flowers and fruit. The rain-god gave timely and proper showers. There was exceedingly abundant harvest. His queen was named <s>Candraprabhā</s>; his son, the prince <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>; <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s> were his chief ministers. In <s>Rājagṛha</s>, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was ruling — his kingdom was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. His chief queen was <s>Vaidehī</s>; his son, the prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s>; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Varṣakāra</s>, the chief minister of <s>Magadha</s>, was his principal minister. The trees always bore flowers and fruit. The rain-god gave timely and proper showers. There was exceedingly abundant harvest. Merchants from <s>Rājagṛha</s>, carrying merchandise, arrived at <s>Roruka</s>. Then King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, surrounded by his council of ministers, addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, does any other king also have such a territory — prosperous, flourishing, secure, and teeming with many people? With trees that always bear flowers and fruit? Where the rain-god gives timely and proper showers? Where there is exceedingly abundant harvest?' The merchants said: 'There is, Sire — in the eastern region, the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. There, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> rules — his kingdom is prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. His trees also always bear flowers and fruit. The rain-god gives timely and proper showers. There is exceedingly abundant harvest.' From hearing of his greatness, affection arose in him toward that king. He addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, what is rare for that king?' They said: 'Your Majesty is the lord of jewels; that king is the lord of garments. Jewels are rare for him.' He then filled a casket with jewels and sent it as a gift, along with a letter: 'Dear friend, you are my unseen companion. Whenever you have any business in the city of <s>Roruka</s>, you should send me word. I shall accomplish everything.' They took the gift and departed for <s>Rājagṛha</s>. In due course, they arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. They presented the casket of jewels and the letter to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, having read the letter, addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, what is rare for that king?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty is the lord of garments; that king is the lord of jewels. Garments are rare for him.' He then filled a casket with precious garments and sent it as a gift, along with a letter: 'Dear friend, you are my unseen companion. Whenever you have any business in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, you should send me word. I shall accomplish everything.' They took the gift and departed for <s>Roruka</s>. In due course, they arrived at <s>Roruka</s>. They presented the casket of garments and the letter to King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>. The envoy returned. Then on another occasion, King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, surrounded by his council of ministers, addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, what is the stature and girth of that king?' They said: 'Just like Your Majesty's, but that king is himself a warrior on the battlefield. What sort of neighboring kings does he fight?' King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> had a jewel-armor, possessing five qualities — cool to the touch in heat, warm to the touch in cold, hard to cut, hard to pierce, an antidote to poison, and luminous. He sent this as a gift, along with a letter: 'Dear friend, this jewel-armor is sent to you by me as a gift — it possesses five qualities: warm to the touch in cold, cool to the touch in heat, hard to cut, hard to pierce, an antidote to poison, and luminous.'

body.text:
466.002. na tvayaitatkasyaciddātavyam/
466.003. sa dūtastanmaṇivarma ādāya lekhaṃ ca, yena rājagṛhaṃ tena prakrāntaḥ/
466.003. anupūrveṇa rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
466.004. tena tanmaṇivarma rājño bimbisārasyopanītaṃ lekhaśca/
466.004. rājā bimbisārastaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayamāpannaḥ/
466.005. tena ratnaparīkṣakā āhūtāh--mūlyamasya kuruta/
466.005. te kathayanti--deva, ekaikaratnamanardho 'yam/
466.006. dharmatā khalu yasya na śakyate mūlyaṃ kartum, tasyaikaikasya koṭimūlyaṃ kriyate/
466.007. rājā bimbisāro vyathitaḥ kathayati--kiṃ mayā tasya prābhṛtamanupreṣitavyaṃ bhaviṣyati? sa saṃlakṣayati--ayaṃ buddho bhagavān/
466.008. sa rājñaḥ sarvadasyānuttarajñānajño vaśiprāptaḥ/
466.009. gacchāmi, buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchāmi/
466.009. sa tamādāya yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
466.009. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
466.010. rājā bimbisāro bhagavantamidamavocat--roruke bhadanta nagare rājā rudrāyaṇo nāma prativasati mamādṛṣṭasakhā/
466.011. tena mama pañcāṅgopatamaṇivarma prābhṛtamanupreṣitam/
466.012. ahaṃ tasya kiṃ prābhṛtamanupraṣeyāmi? bhagavānāha--tathāgatapratimāṃ paṭe likhāpayitvā prābhṛtamanupreṣaya/
466.013. tena citrakarā āhūyotkāh--tathāgatapratimāṃ peṭe citrayatha/
466.014. durāsadā buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
466.014. te na śaknuvanti bhagavato nimittamudgrahītum/
466.015. te kathayanti--yadi devo bhagavantamantargṛhe bhojayet, evaṃ svayaṃ saṃjñāpaya bhagavato nimittamudgrahītum/
466.016. rājñā bimbisāreṇa bhagavānantargṛhe upanimantrya bhojitaḥ/
466.016. asecanakadarśanā buddhā bhagavantaḥ/
466.017. te yamevāvayavaṃ bhagavataḥ paśyanti, tameva paśyanto na tṛptiṃ gacchanti/
466.018. te na śaknuvanti bhagavato nimittamudgrahītum/
466.019. bhagavānāha--mahārāja, khedamāpatsyante, na śakyate tathāgatasya nimittamudgrahītum/
466.019. api tu paṭakamānaya/
466.019. tena paṭaka ānītaḥ/
466.020. tatra bhagavatā chāyā utsṛṣṭā, uktāśca--raṅgaiḥ pūrayata/
466.020. tasyādhastāccharaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni lakhitavyāni/
466.021. anulomapratilomadvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo likhitavyaḥ/
466.021. gāthādvayaṃ ca likitavyam--
466.023. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
466.024. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//1//
body.translated_text:
466.002. 'You must not give this to anyone.'
466.003. That messenger, taking the jewel-armor and the letter, set out toward <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
466.003. Gradually he reached <s>Rājagṛha</s>.
466.004. By him, that jewel-armor was presented to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, along with the letter.
466.004. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, seeing it, was filled with wonder.
466.005. He summoned jewel-appraisers: 'Determine its value.'
466.005. They said: 'Sire, each individual gem is priceless.'
466.006. Indeed, by convention, that which cannot be valued is assigned a price of a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million) for each gem.
466.007. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, troubled, said: 'What return gift shall I send him?' He reflected: 'Here is the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.
466.008. He knows all things for every king, having attained unsurpassed knowledge and mastery.'
466.009. 'I shall go and ask the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'
466.009. Taking it, he approached the Blessed One.
466.009. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet and sat down to one side.
466.010. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'In the city of <s>Roruka</s>, Venerable Sir, there dwells a king named <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, a friend I have never met.
466.011. He has sent me a jewel-armor of five components as a gift.
466.012. What gift shall I send him in return?' The Blessed One said: 'Have a <s>Tathāgata</s> image painted on cloth and send it as a gift.'
466.013. He summoned painters: 'Paint a <s>Tathāgata</s> image on cloth.'
466.014. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are difficult to approach.
466.014. They were unable to capture the Blessed One's likeness.
466.015. They said: 'If His Majesty were to invite the Blessed One for a meal in the inner chamber, then we ourselves could attempt to capture the Blessed One's likeness.'
466.016. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> invited the Blessed One to the inner chamber and served him a meal.
466.016. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are of inexhaustible beauty.
466.017. Whatever feature of the Blessed One they gazed upon, gazing at that very feature they could not be satisfied.
466.018. They were unable to capture the Blessed One's likeness.
466.019. The Blessed One said: 'Great king, they will become exhausted — the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s likeness cannot be captured.
466.019. Rather, bring a cloth.'
466.019. A cloth was brought by him.
466.020. There the Blessed One cast his shadow and said: 'Fill it in with colors.'
466.020. Beneath it, the formulas of taking refuge and the rules of training were to be written.
466.021. The twelve-fold <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) in forward and reverse order was to be written.
466.021. And a pair of verses was to be written:
466.023. 'Arise, set forth, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!
466.024. Shatter the army of Death, as an elephant shatters a reed-hut!' //1//

body.text:
466.025. asmin yo dharmavinaye hyapramattaścariṣyati/
466.026. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//2//
body.translated_text:
466.025. 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> shall conduct himself heedfully,
466.026. having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall make an end of suffering.' //2//

body.text:
466.027. yadi kathayati--kimidam? vaktavyam--iyamabhyupapattiriyaṃ śikṣā iyaṃ lokasaṃvṛtiriyamatyutsāhatā/
466.028. tairyathāsaṃdiṣṭaṃ sarvamabhilikhitam/
466.028. bhagavatā rājā bimbisāra uktah--mahārāja, rudrāyaṇasya lekhamanuprayaccha--priyavaysya, idaṃ te mayā trailokyaprativiśiṣṭaṃ prābhṛtamanupreṣitam/
466.029. asya tvayā ardhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kartavyam/
466.030. svayameva caturaṅgena balakāyena pratyudgantavyam/
466.031. vistīrṇāvakāśe pradeśe sthāpayitvā mahatīṃ pūjāṃ satkāraṃ kṛtvodghāṭayitavyam/
466.031. tataste mahataḥ puṇyasyāvāptirbhaviṣyatīti/
466.032. rājñā bimbisāreṇa yathāsaṃdiṣṭaṃ lekho likhitvā saṃpreṣitaḥ/
466.032. rājño <467>rudrāyaṇasya lekha upanāmitaḥ/
body.translated_text:
466.027. 'If he asks "What is this?" — he should be told: "This is the higher rebirth; this is the training; this is the convention of the world; this is the supreme exertion."
466.028. Everything was inscribed by them as instructed.
466.028. The Blessed One said to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Great king, send <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> a letter as follows: "Dear friend, I am sending you a gift that surpasses the three worlds.
466.029. For this, you must adorn the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>.
466.030. You yourself must go out to meet it with the fourfold army.
466.031. Having placed it in a spacious, open area, you must offer great worship and honor, and then unveil it.
466.031. Thereby you will obtain great merit."
466.032. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> had the letter written as instructed and dispatched it.
466.032. The letter was presented to King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>.

body.text:
467.001. tena vācitaḥ/
467.001. tasyāmarṣaḥ/
467.001. so 'mātyānāṃ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kīdṛśaṃ mama tena prabhṛtamanupreṣitam yasya satkāraḥ kartavyo bhaviṣyati? saṃnāhayata caturaṅgabalakāyam/
467.003. rāṣṭrāpamardanamasya kariṣyāmaḥ/
467.003. amātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, mahātmāsau rājā śrūyate/
467.004. na śakyaṃ tena yadvā tadvā pratiprābhṛtamanupreṣayitum/
467.004. ānupūrvī tāvatkriyatām/
467.005. yadi devasya na cittaparitoṣo bhaviṣyati, tatra kālajñā bhaviṣyāmaḥ/
467.005. evaṃ kriyatām/
467.006. tenārdhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kṛtā/
467.006. svayameva caturaṅgabalakāyena pratyudgamya praveśitaḥ/
467.007. vistīrṇāvakāśe pradeśe sthāpayitvā mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvoddhāṭitā/
467.007. madhyadeśādvaṇijaḥ paṇyamādāya tatrānuprāptaḥ/
467.008. tairbuddhapratimāṃ dṛṣṭvā ekaraveṇa nādo muktah--namo buddhāyeti/
467.009. tasya buddha ityaśrutapūrvaṃ ghoṣaṃ śrutvā sarvaromakūpāṇyāhṛṣṭāni/
467.009. sa kathayati--ka eṣa bhavanto buddho nāma? te kathayanti--deva, śākyānāṃ kumāra utpanno 'sti himavatpārśve nadyā bhāgīrathyāstīre kapilasya ṛṣerāśramapadasya nātidūre/
467.011. sa brāhamaṇair naimittikairvipaścikairvyākṛtaḥ/
467.012. sacedgṛhī agāramadhyāvasiṣyati, rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī caturaṅgairvijetā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ/
467.013. tasyemānyevamrūpāṇi saptaratnāni bhavanti, tadyathā--cakraratnaṃ hastiratnamaśvaratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ strīratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnameva saptamam/
467.014. pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām/
467.015. sa imāmeva samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthvīṃkhilāmalaṇṭakāmanutpīḍāmadaṇḍenāśastreṇa dharmeṇa śamenābhinirjitya adhyāvasiṣyati/
467.016. sacet keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyati, tathāgato bhaviṣyatyarhan samyaksambuddho vighuṣṭaśabdo loke/
467.018. sa eṣa buddho nāma/
467.018. tasyaiṣā pratibhā/
467.019. idaṃ kim? abhyupapattiḥ/
467.019. idaṃ kim? śikṣāpadam/
467.019. idaṃ kim? lokasya pravṛttinivṛttī/
467.020. idaṃ kim? atyutsāhanā/
467.020. tena pratītyasamutpādo 'nulomapratilomaḥ sugṛhītaḥ kṛtaḥ//
body.translated_text:
467.001. He had it read.
467.001. He was filled with indignation.
467.001. He said to his ministers: 'Sirs, what kind of gift has he sent me, for which such honor must be shown? Muster the fourfold army!
467.003. We shall lay waste to his kingdom.'
467.003. The ministers said: 'Sire, he is known to be a great-souled king.
467.004. He would not be able to send just any trifling return gift.
467.004. Let the proper sequence be followed first.
467.005. If it does not satisfy Your Majesty's mind, we shall know the right course at that time.'
467.005. 'Let it be done so.'
467.006. He adorned the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>.
467.006. He himself went out with the fourfold army to receive it and had it brought in.
467.007. Having placed it in a spacious, open area, he offered great worship and then unveiled it.
467.007. Merchants from the central country (<s>Madhyadeśa</s>) had arrived there with goods.
467.008. Upon seeing the <s>Buddha</s>-image, they cried out with one voice: '<s>Namo Buddhāya</s>!' (Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!)
467.009. Having heard the word '<s>Buddha</s>' — a sound never heard before — all the hair on his body stood on end.
467.009. He said: 'Sirs, who is this one called the <s>Buddha</s>?' They said: 'Sire, a prince was born among the <s>Śākyas</s>, on the slope of the <s>Himālayas</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>.
467.011. He was declared by <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> soothsayers and seers:
467.012. "If he remains a householder, dwelling in a house, he will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> king — a universal monarch, a righteous conqueror, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, endowed with the seven treasures.
467.013. These are his seven treasures, namely: the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh.
467.014. He will have a full thousand sons — heroes, warriors, of beautiful form, destroyers of enemy armies.
467.015. He will conquer this great earth, bounded by the ocean, without thorns and defilements, without oppression, by means not involving punishment or weapons, but through <s>Dharma</s> and peace, and will dwell therein.
467.016. But if he shaves his hair and beard, dons the saffron robes, and with perfect faith goes forth from the household life into homelessness, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, renowned throughout the world."
467.018. He is that very <s>Buddha</s>.
467.018. This is his likeness.
467.019. What is this? The higher rebirth.
467.019. What is this? The rule of training.
467.019. What is this? The way the world arises and ceases.
467.020. What is this? The supreme exertion.'
467.020. By him, the <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) in forward and reverse order was thoroughly grasped and comprehended.

body.text:
467.021. atha rudrāyaṇo rājā sāmātyaḥ pratyūṣasamaye sarvārthān sarvakarmāntān pratiprasrabhya niṣaṇṇaḥ paryaṅkamābhujya ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhāṃ smṛtimupasthāpya/
467.022. sa imameva dvādaśāṅgaṃ pratītyasamutpādamanulomapratilomaṃ vyavalokayati, yaduta asmin satīdaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvatsamudayo nirodhaśca bhavati/
467.024. tenemaṃ dvādaśāṅgaṃ pratītyasamutpādamanulomapratilomaṃ vyavalokayatā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
467.026. sa dṛṣṭasatyo gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
467.027. bhūratnena hi buddhena prajñācakṣurviśodhitam/
467.028. namastasmai suvaidyāya cikitsā yasya hīdṛśī//3//
body.translated_text:
467.021. Then King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, together with his ministers, at the time of early dawn, having set aside all duties and all works, sat down cross-legged, with body erect, establishing mindfulness before him.
467.022. He contemplated this very twelve-fold <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) in forward and reverse order, namely: 'When this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises — that is, with ignorance as condition, formations arise,' and so on up to 'both arising and cessation occur.'
467.024. As he contemplated the twelve-fold dependent origination in forward and reverse order, he shattered the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), towering with its twenty peaks, with the thunderbolt of knowledge, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
467.026. Having seen the truths, he spoke a verse:
467.027. 'By the <s>Buddha</s>, who is a jewel of the earth, the eye of wisdom has been purified.
467.028. Homage to that supreme physician whose treatment is of such a nature!' //3//

body.text:
467.029. tena rājño bimbisārasya saṃdiṣṭam--priyavayasya, tvāmāgamya mayodddhṛto narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ pādaḥ, pratiṣṭhāpito devamanuṣyeṣu/
467.030. ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, anādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
467.032. bhikṣudarśanamākāṅkṣāmi/
467.032. tadarhasi bhikṣuṃ preṣayitum/
467.032. atha sa rājā bimbisāro yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
body.translated_text:
467.029. He sent word to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Dear friend, thanks to you I have been lifted out of the realm of hells, animals, and hungry ghosts, and established among gods and humans.
467.030. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed, the mountain of the view of the personal self — accumulated since beginningless time — has been shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge, and the fruit of stream-entry has been directly realized.
467.032. I desire to see a monk.
467.032. Therefore, please send a monk.'
467.032. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s> approached the Blessed One.

body.text:
468.001. <468>upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
468.001. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo bhagavantamidamavocat--rudrāyaṇena bhadanta rājñā satyāni dṛṣṭāni/
468.002. tena mama saṃdiṣṭam--bhikṣudarśanamākāṅkṣāmīti/
468.003. bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--katamasya bhikṣo rudrāyaṇo rājā saparivāro vineyo rairukanivāsī ca janakāyah? kātyāyanasya bhikṣoḥ/
468.004. tatra bhgavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamāmantrayate--samanvāhara kātyāyana rauruke nagare rudrāyaṇaṃ rājānaṃ saparivāraṃ raurukanivāsinaṃ ca janakāyam/
468.006. adhivāsayatyāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ/
468.006. bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikātprakrāntaḥ/
468.007. athāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastasyā eva rātryā atyayātpūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
468.008. rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ paribhuktaṃ śayanaṃ pratiśāmya samādāya pātracīvaraṃ pañcaśataparivāro yena raurukaṃ tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
468.010. rājñā bimbisāreṇa rudrāyaṇasya rājño lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ/
468.011. priyavayasya, eṣa te bhikṣurmayā śāstṛkalpo mahāśrāvako 'nupreṣitaḥ/
468.012. asya tvayārdhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kartavyā nagaraśobhā ca/
468.012. svayameva caturaṅgena balakāyena pratyudgantavyaḥ/
468.013. pañca vihāraśatāni kartavyāni/
468.013. pañca mañcapīṭhavṛṣikoccakabimbopadhānacaturasrakaśatāni dātavyāni/
468.014. pañca piṇḍaśatāni prajñāpayitavyāni/
468.015. ataste mahataḥ puṇyasyāvāptirbhaviṣyati/
468.015. tenārdhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kṛtā, nagaraśobhā kṛtā, pañca vihāraśatāni, yena ekajanasahasraparivāreṇa ca svayameva pratyudgamya mahatā satkāreṇa rorukaṃ nagaraṃ praveśitaḥ/
468.017. bahir nagarasya pañca vihāraśatāni kāritāni, pañca mañcapīṭhavṛṣikoccakabimbopadhānacaturasrakaśatāni dāpitāni, pañca piṇḍapātaśatāni prajñaptāni, vistīrṇāvakāśe ca pṛthivīpradeśe āsanaprajñaptiḥ kāritā/
468.019. ayuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ/
468.020. anekāni praṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni/
468.021. kānicitkutūhalajātāni, kānicitpūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni/
468.021. tata āyuṣmatā mahākātyāyanena tasyāḥ pariṣada āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairmahāviśeṣo 'dhigataḥ/
468.023. kaiścicchrotāpattiphalam, kaiścidnāgāmiphalam, kaiścitpravrahya sarvalkeśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, kaiścicchrāvakabodhau cittānyutpāditāni, kaiścitpratyekāyāṃ bodhau, kaiścidanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau/
468.026. yadbhūyasā sā pariṣadbuddhaniṃnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitā//
body.translated_text: Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat to one side. Seated to one side, he said this to the Blessed One: 'King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, Venerable Sir, has seen the truths. He has instructed me thus: "I wish to see a monk."' The Blessed One reflected: 'Of which monk is King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> together with his retinue, and the populace of <s>Rauruka</s>, the disciple to be trained?' Of the monk <s>Kātyāyana</s>. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: 'Take charge, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, of King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> together with his retinue, and the populace of <s>Rauruka</s> city.' The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> consented. Having bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he departed from the Blessed One's presence. Then the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, on the morning after that night, having dressed in the forenoon and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Having gone for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having finished his meal, after eating and returning from his alms-round, he put away his bedding, took his bowl and robe, and with a retinue of five hundred set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Rauruka</s>. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> sent a letter to King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>: 'Dear friend, I am sending you this monk — a great disciple, equal to the Teacher himself. You should adorn the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s> and adorn the city. You yourself should go out to meet him with the fourfold army. Five hundred monasteries should be built. Five hundred sets of beds, seats, cushions, pillows, bolsters, and square mats should be given. Five hundred alms-meals should be arranged. From this you will obtain great merit.' He adorned the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>, adorned the city, built five hundred monasteries, and with a retinue of one thousand people went out himself to meet him and brought him into the city of <s>Rauruka</s> with great honor. Outside the city, five hundred monasteries were built, five hundred sets of beds, seats, cushions, pillows, bolsters, and square mats were provided, five hundred alms-meals were arranged, and in a spacious open area a seating arrangement was made. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> sat upon the prepared seat at the head of the assembly of monks. Many hundreds of thousands of beings gathered — some out of curiosity, some impelled by previous roots of merit. Then the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having understood the disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character of that assembly, gave such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great distinction. Some attained the fruit of stream-entry; some the fruit of non-returning; some, having gone forth and abandoned all defilements, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>; some generated the aspiration for the enlightenment of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>; some for <s>Pratyeka</s>-enlightenment; some for unsurpassed perfect awakening. For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text:
468.027. rauruke nagare tiṣyaḥ puṣyaśca gṛhapatī vasataḥ/
468.027. tau yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenopasaṃkrāntau/
468.028. upasaṃkramya āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇau/
468.029. tiṣyapuṣyau gṛhapatī āyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamidamavocatām--labhevahi āryamahākātyāyana svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
468.030. careva āryamahākātyāyana bhavato 'ntike brahmacaryamiti/
468.031. tāvayuṣmatā kātyāyanena pravrajitāvupasampāditau, avavādo dattaḥ/
468.031. tābhyām yujyamānābhyāṃ vyāyacchamānābhyāṃ ghaṭamānābhyāmidameva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalam <469>viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śataśaḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
469.002. arhantau saṃvṛttau traidhātukavīrāgau samaloṣṭakāñcanāvākāśapāṇisamacittau vāsīcandanakalpau vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośau vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptau bhvalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhau/
469.004. sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyau mānyavabhivādyau ca saṃvṛttau/
469.004. tau jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtau/
469.006. tayorjñātṛbhiḥ śarīrapūjāṃ kṛrtvā dvau stūpau kāritau--ekastiṣyasya, dvitīyaḥ puṇyasya//
body.translated_text: In the city of <s>Rauruka</s>, two householders named <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s> dwelt. They approached the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> and sat to one side. The householders <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: 'May we, Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, obtain the going-forth, the full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May we practice the holy life in the presence of the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.' They were ordained and given full ordination by the Venerable <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and instruction was given. As they applied themselves, exerted themselves, and strove — having understood this five-knotted wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> as unstable and wavering, having struck down the courses of all <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) as subject to the nature of shattering, crumbling, scattering, and destruction hundreds of times over — they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the complete abandonment of all defilements. They became <s>Arhats</s> — free from passion toward the three realms, their minds equal toward clods of earth and gold, their consciousness equal toward open space and the palm of the hand, like sandalwood and an axe — their egg-shells of ignorance broken by knowledge; having attained knowledge, the higher knowledges, and the analytical powers; turned away from worldly gain, profit, and honor; worthy of being worshipped, honored, and saluted by gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Having performed the miracles of burning, heating, raining, and flashing, they attained final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder. Their kinsmen, having performed the worship of their bodily relics, built two <s>stūpas</s> — one for <s>Tiṣya</s> and the second for <s>Puṣya</s>.

body.text:
469.007. rudrāyaṇo rājā dine dine āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasyāntikād dharmaṃ śrutvā antaḥpurasyārocayati--āryo mahākātyāyano madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudramiva madhuraṃ praprīṇayatīti/
469.009. tāḥ kathayanti--devasya saphalo buddhotpādaḥ/
469.009. katham? yena tvaṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoṣi/
469.010. yadyevam, yūyaṃ kasmāñ śṛṇutha? deva, vayaṃ hrīmantyaḥ/
469.010. kathaṃ vayaṃ tatra gatvā dharmaṃ śṛṇumah? yadyāryo mahākātyāyana ihaivāgatya dharmaṃ deśayet, evaṃ vayamapi śṛṇuyām iti/
469.011. rudrāyaṇena rājñā āyuṣmān mahākātyāyana uktah--mama ārya sāntaḥpuramicchati śrotum/
469.012. sa kathayati--mahārāja, na bhikṣavo 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśya dharmaṃ deśayanti/
469.013. pratikṣipto bhagavatā antaḥpurapraveśaḥ/
469.014. ārya, atra ko 'ntaḥpurasya dharmaṃ deśayati? mahārāja, bhikṣuṇyaḥ/
469.014. rudrāyaṇarājñā bimbisārasya rājño lekho 'nupreṣitah--priyavayasya, antaḥpuramicchati dharmaṃ śrotum/
469.015. tadarhasi kāṃcidbhikṣuṇīṃ preṣayitum/
469.016. bimbisāro rājā taṃ lekhaṃ vācayitvā yena bhagvāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
469.016. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
469.017. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo rājā bimbisāro bhagavantamidamavocat--rudrāyaṇena bhagavan rājñā lekho 'nupreṣitah--antaḥpuramicchati dharmaṃ śrotum/
tadarhasi kāṃcidbhikṣuṇīṃ preṣayitumiti/
469.019. tadatra kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti? bhagavān saṃlakṣayati--katarasyā bhikṣuṇyā rudrāyaṇasya rājño antaḥpuraparijano vineyo raurukanivāsī ca strījana iti? paśyati śailāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ/
469.021. tatra bhagavāñchailāṃ bhikṣuṇīmāmantrayate--samanvāhara śaile rauruke nagare rudrāyaṇasya rājño 'ntaḥpurajanaṃ raurukanivāsinaṃ strījanamiti/
469.022. evaṃ bhadanteti śailā bhikṣuṇī bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntā/
469.024. atha śailā bhikṣuṇī tasyā eva rātrertyayātpūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhakrakṛtyā pañcādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntā yathāparibhuktaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratisamayya samādāya pātracīvaraṃ pañcaśataparivārā yena raurukaṃ nagaraṃ tena cārikāṃ prakrāntā/
469.027. bimbisāreṇa ca rājñā rudrāyaṇasya rājño lekho 'nupreṣitah--priyavayasya, eṣā te mayā mahāśrāvikā śāstrānugatā pañcaśataparivārā preṣitā/
469.028. asyāṃ tvayārdharṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kartavyā nagaraśobhā ca/
469.029. svayameva ca caturaṅgena balakāyena pratyudgantavyam/
469.029. abhyantare ca nagarasya pañca vihāraśatāni kārayitavyāni, pañca mañcapīṭhaśatāni, vṛṣikoccabimbopadhānacaturasrakaśatāni dātavyāni, pañca piṇḍapātaśatāni prajñāpayitavyāni/
469.031. ataste puṇyasyāvāptirbhaviṣyatīti/
469.032. rudrāyaṇena rājñā lekhaṃ vācayitvā prāmodyajātenārdhatṛtīyāni yojanāni mārgaśobhā kāritā/
body.translated_text: King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, day after day, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, reported to the inner palace: 'The Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> sweetly and sweetly — sweet like honey, it fills one with delight.' They said: 'The arising of a <s>Buddha</s> has been fruitful for His Majesty.' 'How so?' 'Because you hear the <s>Dharma</s>.' 'If so, why do you not hear it?' 'Lord, we are modest women. How can we go there and hear the <s>Dharma</s>? If the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> would come here and teach the <s>Dharma</s>, then we too might hear it.' King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said to the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: 'Noble Sir, my inner palace wishes to hear the teaching.' He said: 'Great king, monks do not enter the inner palace to teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Entry into the inner palace is prohibited by the Blessed One.' 'Noble Sir, who then teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the inner palace?' 'Great king, nuns do.' King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> sent a letter to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Dear friend, the inner palace wishes to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Please be so good as to send a nun.' King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, having had the letter read, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, Blessed One, has sent a letter: "The inner palace wishes to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Please be so good as to send a nun." How should this be handled?' The Blessed One reflected: 'Of which nun is King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>'s inner palace retinue and the women of <s>Rauruka</s> the disciple to be trained?' He saw — of the nun <s>Śailā</s>. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the nun <s>Śailā</s>: 'Take charge, <s>Śailā</s>, of King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>'s inner palace populace and the women of <s>Rauruka</s> city.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the nun <s>Śailā</s> assented to the Blessed One, bowed her head at his feet, and departed from the Blessed One's presence. Then the nun <s>Śailā</s>, on the morning after that night, having dressed in the forenoon and taken her bowl and robe, went for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Having finished her meal, after eating and returning from her alms-round, she put away her bedding, took her bowl and robe, and with a retinue of five hundred set out on a wandering tour toward the city of <s>Rauruka</s>. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> sent a letter to King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>: 'Dear friend, I am sending you this great disciple who follows the Teacher, with a retinue of five hundred. You should adorn the road for two and a half <s>yojanas</s> and adorn the city. You yourself should go out to meet her with the fourfold army. Inside the city, five hundred monasteries should be built; five hundred sets of beds, seats, cushions, pillows, bolsters, and square mats should be given; five hundred alms-meals should be arranged. From this you will obtain merit.' King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, having had the letter read, filled with joy, had the road adorned for two and a half <s>yojanas</s>.

body.text:
470.001. anekajanasahasraparivāreṇa ca svayameva pratyudgamya mahatā satkāreṇa raurukaṃ nagaraṃ praveśitā/
470.002. abhyantare ca nagarasya pañca vihāraśatāni kāritāni, pañca mañcapīṭhavṛṣikoṣabimbopadhānacaturasrakaśatāni dāpitāni, pañca piṇḍapātaśatāni prajñaptāni/
470.003. śailā bhikṣuṇī rudrāyaṇasya rājño 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśya dine dinai dharmaṃ deśayati/
470.004. rudrāyaṇo rājā vīṇāyāṃ kṛtāvī, candraprabhā devī nṛtye/
470.005. yāvadapareṇa samayena rudrāyaṇo rājā vīṇāṃ vādayati, candraprabhā devī nṛtyati/
470.005. tena tasyā nṛtyantyā bināśalakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam/
470.006. sa tāmitaścāmutaśca nirīkṣya saṃlakṣayati--saptāhasyātyayātkālaṃ kariṣyati/
470.007. tasya hastādvīṇā srastā, bhūmau nipatitā/
470.007. candraprabhā devī kathayati--deva, mā mayā durnṛtyam? devi, na tvayā dunṛtyam/
470.008. api tu mayā tava nṛtyantyā vināśalakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam--saptame divase tava kālatriyā bhavatīti/
470.009. candraprabhā devī pādayor nipatya kathayati--deva yadyevam, kṛtopasthānāhaṃ devasya/
470.010. yadi devo 'nujānīyāt, ahaṃ pravrajeyamiti/
470.010. sa kathayati--candraprabhe, samayato 'nujānāmi/
470.011. yadi tāvatpravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkaroṣi, eṣa eva te duḥkhāntaḥ/
470.012. atha sāvaśeṣasamyojanā kālaṃ kṛtvā deveṣūpapadyase, devabhūtayā te mamopadarśayitavyamiti/
470.013. sā kathayati--deva, evaṃ bhavatviti/
470.013. sā rudrāyaṇena rājñā śailāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ samarpitā--āryacandraptabhā devī ākāṅkṣati svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikcuṇībhāvam/
470.015. tadarhasi tāṃ pravrājayitumupasampādayitumiti/
470.015. śailā bhikṣuṇī kathayati--evaṃ bhavatu, prabrājayāmīti/
470.016. tayāsau pravrājitā upasampāditā ca/
470.016. samanvāhṛtya cāvavādo dattah--maraṇasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayeti/
470.017. candraprabhā devī maraṇasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayitumārabdhā/
470.017. sā saptame divase kālagatā cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannā/
470.018. dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya, trīṇi cittānyutpadyante--kutaścyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ, kena karmaṇeti/
470.019. candraprabhā devakanyā saṃlakṣayati--kṛto 'haṃ cyutā? manuṣyebhyaḥ/
470.020. kutropapannā? cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣu/
470.021. kena karmaṇā? bhagavataḥ śāsane brāhmacaryaṃ caritveti/
470.021. tasyā etadabhavat--tadapratirūpaṃ syādyadahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitum/
470.022. yannvahamaparyuṣitaparivāsaiva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyamiti/
470.023. atha candraprabhā devakanyā calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrī tāmeva rātrīṃ divyānāmutpalakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndāravāṇāmutsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ veṇuvanaṃ kalandakakanivāpamudāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpairavakīrya bhagavataḥ purastānniṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya/
470.026. bhagavatā tasyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā candraprabhayā devakanyayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃsatkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā śrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
470.028. sā dṛṣṭasatyā trirudānamudānayati--idamasmākaṃ bhadanta, na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭair nasvajanabandhuvargair na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇairyadbhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam/
470.030. ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitānyapāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭāpitā devamanuṣyeṣu/
470.032. āha ca--
body.translated_text:
470.001. Accompanied by many thousands of people, he himself went out to greet her and had her enter the city of <s>Rauruka</s> with great honor.
470.002. Inside the city, five hundred monasteries were built, five hundred sets of beds, chairs, mats, pillows, cushions, and bolsters were provided, and five hundred alms-meals were arranged.
470.003. The nun <s>Śailā</s> entered the inner palace of King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> and taught the <s>Dharma</s> day by day.
470.004. King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> was skilled in the <s>vīṇā</s>, and Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> in dance.
470.005. On another occasion, King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> played the <s>vīṇā</s> while Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> danced.
470.005. While she was dancing, he perceived in her the signs of destruction.
470.006. Looking at her from this side and that, he reflected: 'After seven days, she will die.'
470.007. The <s>vīṇā</s> slipped from his hand and fell to the ground.
470.007. Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> said: 'Sire, have I danced badly?' 'Queen, you have not danced badly.
470.008. But I perceived in your dancing the signs of destruction — on the seventh day, the time of death will come for you.'
470.009. Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s>, falling at his feet, said: 'Sire, if this is so, I have served Your Majesty.
470.010. If Your Majesty permits, I would go forth into homelessness.'
470.010. He said: '<s>Candraprabhā</s>, I permit you on one condition:
470.011. If, having gone forth, you realize <s>Arhatship</s> by the abandonment of all defilements — that itself will be the end of suffering for you.
470.012. But if you die with fetters remaining and are reborn among the gods, as a divine being you must appear to me.'
470.013. She said: 'Sire, so be it.'
470.013. She was entrusted by King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> to the nun <s>Śailā</s>: 'The noble Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> desires the going-forth, ordination, and the state of a nun in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.
470.015. Please ordain and give her full ordination.'
470.015. The nun <s>Śailā</s> said: 'So be it; I shall ordain her.'
470.016. She was ordained and given full ordination.
470.016. And having reflected, she gave this instruction: 'Cultivate the perception of death.'
470.017. Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> began to cultivate the perception of death.
470.017. On the seventh day, she died and was reborn among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven.
470.018. It is a rule that when a god or a goddess has newly been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?'
470.019. The goddess <s>Candraprabhā</s> reflected: 'From where did I pass away? From among humans.
470.020. Where have I been reborn? Among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.
470.021. By what deed? By having lived the holy life in the Blessed One's teaching.'
470.021. She thought: 'It would be improper for me to visit the Blessed One after spending the night in my new abode.
470.022. Let me visit the Blessed One for an audience before the night has passed.'
470.023. Then the goddess <s>Candraprabhā</s>, wearing sparkling, pure earrings, her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, that very night filling her lap with divine lotuses — <s>utpala</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>māndārava</s> flowers — illuminating the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s>, the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>, with a magnificent radiance, and scattering flowers upon the Blessed One, she sat before the Blessed One for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.
470.026. The Blessed One, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the goddess <s>Candraprabhā</s>, shattering the mountain of the view of the transient composite — peaked with twenty summits — with the thunderbolt of knowledge, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry.
470.028. Having seen the Truths, she uttered three times the solemn declaration: 'This was not done for us by our mother, not done by our father, not by a king, not by deities, not by loved ones, not by kinsmen and relatives, not by the departed ancestors, not by ascetics or <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us.
470.030. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones surmounted, the doors to the lower realms closed, the doors to heaven and liberation opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.'
470.032. And she said:

body.text:
471.001. tavānubhāvātpihitaḥ sughoro hyapāyamārgo bahuduḥkhayuktaḥ/
471.003. apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaśca mayopalabdhaḥ//4//
body.translated_text:
471.001. 'By your majesty, the dreadful path to the lower realms, full of much suffering, has been closed;
471.003. the meritorious path to heaven has been opened, and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been attained by me.' //4//

body.text:
471.005. tvadāśrayādāptamapetadoṣaṃ mamādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ/
471.007. prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padamāryakāntaṃ tīrṇaśca duḥkhārṇavapāramasmi//5//
body.translated_text:
471.005. 'By relying on you, my pure, thoroughly cleansed eye of insight, free from fault, has been obtained today;
471.007. the peaceful state, beloved of the Noble Ones, has been attained, and I have crossed to the other shore of the ocean of suffering.' //5//

body.text:
471.009. jagati daityanarāmarapūjita vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya/
471.011. bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana sphalamadya mune tava darśanam//6//
body.translated_text:
471.009. 'Worshipped by <s>Daityas</s>, humans, and immortals in the world, free from birth, old age, death, and disease,
471.011. exceedingly rare to behold through thousands of existences — fruitful today, O Sage, is the sight of you.' //6//

body.text:
471.013. avanamya tataḥ pralambahārā caraṇau dvāvabhivandya jāraharṣā/
471.015. parigamya pradakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ suralokābhimukhī divaṃ jagāma//7//
body.translated_text:
471.013. 'Then, bowing down with her long necklace swaying, having saluted both feet with tears of joy,
471.015. circumambulating the Conqueror of enemies to the right, she departed toward the divine world, facing the heavens.' //7//

body.text:
471.017. atha candraprabhā devakanyā vaṇigiva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasampanna iva karṣakaḥ, śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturaḥ, yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśāmāgatā tayaiva vibhūtyā svarbhavanaṃ saṃprasthitā/
471.019. tasyā etadabhavat--mayā rudrāyaṇasya rājñaḥ pratijñātamupadarśayiṣyāmīti/
471.020. atha candraprabhā devakanyā yena rājā rudrāyaṇastenopasaṃkrāntā/
471.020. tena khalu samayena rudrāyaṇo rājā ekākī gṛhasyoparitalake śayitaḥ/
471.021. sa tayā udārāvabhāsaṃ kṛtvā acchaṭāśabdena pratibodhitaḥ/
471.022. sa middhāvasthalocanāparisphuṭo 'vijñātaḥ kathayati--kā tvamiti? sā kathayati--ahaṃ candraprabheti/
471.023. rājā kathayati--āgaccha, paricārayāma iti/
471.023. sā kathayati--deva, cyutāhaṃ kālagatā cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannā/
471.024. yadīcchasi mayā sārdhaṃ samāgamam, bhagavato 'ntike pravraja/
471.025. yadi tāvaddṛṣṭadharmā sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyase, sa eva te 'nto dukhasya/
471.026. atha sāvaśeṣasamyojanaḥ, kālaṃ kṛtvā cārturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapatsyase/
471.026. tatra te mayā sārdhaṃ samāgamo bhaviṣyati/
471.027. ityuktvā tatraivāntarhitā/
471.027. rudrāyaṇo rājā kṛtsnāṃ rātriṃ pravrajyāmanuvicintayan kālyamevotthāya amātyānāmantrayate--paśyata bhavantaḥ, candraprabhā devī kva tiṣṭhatīti? te kathayanti--deva, kālagateti/
471.029. rudrāyaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--na mama pratirūpaṃ syādyadahaṃ devatācodito 'ham agāramadhyāvaseyam/
471.030. saṃnidhānī kālaparibhogena vā kāmān paribhuñjīyam/
471.031. yannvahaṃ śikhaṇḍinaṃ kumāraṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajeyamiti/
471.032. tena hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau ddutanāhūtoktau <472>bhavantau, yādṛśa eva mama śikhaṇḍī kumāraḥ putraḥ, tādṛśa eva yuvayoḥ/
body.translated_text:
471.017. Then the goddess <s>Candraprabhā</s> — like a merchant who has gained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won a battle, like a sick person freed from all diseases — departed for her heavenly abode with the same splendor with which she had come to the Blessed One.
471.019. She thought: 'I promised King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> that I would appear to him.'
471.020. Then the goddess <s>Candraprabhā</s> approached King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>.
471.020. At that time, King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> was sleeping alone on the rooftop of his palace.
471.021. She awakened him with a magnificent radiance and the sound of a finger-snap.
471.022. He, with eyes still blurred from sleep and unaware, said: 'Who are you?' She said: 'I am <s>Candraprabhā</s>.'
471.023. The king said: 'Come, let us enjoy each other's company.'
471.023. She said: 'Sire, I have passed away and been reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.
471.024. If you desire union with me, go forth into homelessness in the Blessed One's presence.
471.025. If in this very life you realize <s>Arhatship</s> by the abandonment of all defilements, that itself will be the end of your suffering.
471.026. But if you die with fetters remaining, you will be reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods.
471.026. There you will have union with me.'
471.027. Having spoken thus, she vanished right there.
471.027. King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, reflecting on going-forth throughout the entire night, rose at dawn and addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, see where Queen <s>Candraprabhā</s> is.' They said: 'Sire, she has passed away.'
471.029. <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> reflected: 'It would not be proper for me, having been urged by a deity, to continue dwelling in a household.
471.030. Or to enjoy pleasures with stored-up goods that will decay with time.
471.031. Let me anoint the prince <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> as king, shave off my hair and beard, don the yellow robes, and with perfect faith go forth from the household life into homelessness.'
471.032. He summoned the two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s> and said: 'Sirs, just as my son, the prince <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, is to me, so is he to you both.'

body.text:
472.001. sa eṣa yuvābhyāmahitānnivārayitavyo hite ca saṃniyojayitavyaḥ/
472.002. ahaṃ pravrajāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye iti/
472.002. etau sāśrukaṇṭhau byavasthitau/
472.003. śikhaṇḍyapi kumāro 'bhihitah--putra, yathaiva tvaṃ mama vacanaṃ śrotavyaṃ kartavyaṃ manyase, tathā anayorapi hirubhirukayoragrāmātyayorvacanaṃ śrotavyaṃ kartavyaṃ manyathāḥ/
472.004. ahaṃ pravrajāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye/
472.005. iti śrutvā so 'pi sāśrukaṇṭho vyavasthitaḥ/
472.005. tato rudrāyaṇena rājñā rauruke nagare ghaṇṭāvadhoṣaṇaṃ kāritam--śṛṇvantu bhavanto raurukanivāsinaḥ paurā nānādeśābhyāgataśca janakāyaḥ/
472.007. ahaṃ keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇyācchādya samyageva śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajiṣyāmi/
472.008. bhūyaśaḥ putramāha--putra, tvayā rājyaṃ kārayatā kasyacidaparādhyaṃ na kṣantavyamiti/
472.009. anuraktapaurajanapado 'sau rājā/
472.009. śrutvā sarva eva raurukanivāsī janakāyo 'nyaśca nānādeśābhyāgātaḥ sāśrukaṇṭho vyavasthitaḥ/
472.010. tato rudrāyaṇo rājā śikhaṇḍinaṃ kumāraṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpya bandhujanaṃ kṣamāpayitvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyo dānāni datvā paṇyāni kṛtvā ekena puruṣeṇopasthāyakena rājagṛhābhimukhah {samprasthitah}/
472.012. tataḥ śikhaṇḍī rājā sāntaḥpurāmātyapaurajanapado 'nyaśca nānādeśābhyāgato janakāyaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ/
472.013. so 'nekaiḥ praṇiśatasahasrairanugamyamāno raurukānnagarānniṣkramya anyatamāsminnudyāne vividhataruṣaṇḍamaṇḍite nānāpuṣpasalilasampanne haṃsakroñcamayūraśukasārikākokilajīvaṃjīvakanirghoṣite muhūrtamāsthāya raurukaṃ nagaramavalokya śikhaṇḍinaṃ rājānamāmantrayate--putra, mayā dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāritam, yena me iyanti praṇiśatasahasrāṇi pṛṣṭhato 'nuvaddhāni/
472.017. tattvayāpi dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitavyamiti/
472.017. so 'pi janakāyaḥ samāśvāsyoktah--bhavantaḥ, eṣa yuṣmākaṃ rājā samanuyukto mayā/
472.018. nivartate, sukhaṃ prativatsyatha, ityuktvā saṃprasthitaḥ/
472.019. rājā śikhaṇḍī sāntaḥpurakumārāmātyapaurajanapado 'śruparuyākulekṣaṇo muhūrmuhūr nivartya nirīkṣamāṇo raurukaṃ nagaraṃ pratinivṛttaḥ/
472.020. tato rudrāyaṇo rājā anupūrveṇa rājagṛhaṃ nagaramanuprāptaḥ/
472.021. tenodyāne sthitvā sa puruṣa uktah--gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, rājño bimbisārasya gatvā nivedaya--rudrāyaṇo nāma udyāne tiṣṭhatīti/
472.022. tena puruṣeṇa gatvā rājño bimbisārasya niveditam--deva, rudrāyaṇo rājā udyāane tiṣṭhatīti, sa rājā śrutvā sahasaivotthitaḥ pauruṣānāmantrayate--bhavantaḥ, mahāsādhano rājā apratisaṃvidita evāgataḥ/
472.024. na yuṣmākaṃ kenacidvijñāt iti? sa kathayati--deva, kuto 'sya sādhanam? ātmanā dvitīya āgata iti/
472.025. rājā bimbisāraḥ saṃlakṣayati--na mama pratirūpaṃ syādyadahaṃ rāhānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhnāmiṣiktamevameva praveśayeyam/
472.027. mahatā satkāreṇa praveśayāmīti viditvā mārgaśobhāṃ bagaraśobhāṃ ca kārayitvā caturaṅgena balakāyena pratyudgataḥ/
472.028. kaṇṭhe pariṣvajya hastiskandhe āropya rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ praveśitaḥ/
472.029. nānāgandhaparibhāvitenodakena snāpitaḥ/
472.029. rājārhaivastrairgandhamālyavilepanaiśca samalaṃkṛtya bhojitaḥ/
472.030. mārgaśrame prativinodite uktah--priyavayasya, sphītaṃ rājyamapāsya antaḥpuraṃ kumārānāmātyān paurajanapadān kimihāgamanaprayojanam? mā kenacidbhūmyantareṇa rājñā rāṣṭrāvamardanaḥ kṛtah? kumāreṇa vā kenacidduṣṭāmātyavigrāhitena rājyābhinandinā parākrāntamiti? sa kathayati--vayasya, <473>ākaṅkṣāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
body.translated_text: 'He must be restrained by you two from what is harmful and engaged in what is beneficial. I am going forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' The two ministers stood there, their throats choked with tears. The prince <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> too was addressed: 'Son, just as you think my words should be heard and obeyed, so also you should think the words of these two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s> should be heard and obeyed. I am going forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Hearing this, he too stood with throat choked with tears. Then King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> had a bell-proclamation made throughout the city of <s>Roruka</s>: 'Hear, good citizens of <s>Roruka</s> and people who have come from various lands! Having shaved off my hair and beard, donning the saffron robes, with perfect faith, I shall go forth from the household life to homelessness.' He again told his son: 'Son, while you rule the kingdom, no offense against anyone should be tolerated.' That king was beloved by the citizens and country-folk. Having heard, all the citizens of <s>Roruka</s> and the people who had come from various lands stood with throats choked with tears. Then King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, having established Prince <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> in the kingdom, having begged forgiveness of his kinsmen, having given gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and wayfarers, and having made arrangements, set forth toward <s>Rājagṛha</s> with a single attendant. Then King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, together with the inner palace, ministers, citizens, and country-folk, and people who had come from various lands, followed behind him, step after step. Followed by many hundreds of thousands of beings, he departed from the city of <s>Roruka</s> and paused for a moment at a certain garden adorned with groves of various trees, rich in diverse flowers and pools, resounding with geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>sārikā</s>-birds, cuckoos, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s>-birds. Looking back at the city of <s>Roruka</s>, he addressed King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>: 'Son, I ruled the kingdom righteously, which is why these hundreds of thousands of beings follow behind me. You too must rule the kingdom righteously.' Having comforted the people, he said: 'Good people, here is your king, entrusted by me. Turn back — you will live happily.' Having spoken thus, he set forth. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, together with the inner palace, princes, ministers, citizens, and country-folk, with tear-filled and clouded eyes, turning back again and again to look, returned to the city of <s>Roruka</s>. Then King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, traveling by stages, arrived at the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Having stayed at a garden, he told his attendant: 'Go, good man, to King <s>Bimbisāra</s> and announce: "<s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> is waiting at the garden."' That man went and announced to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Sire, King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> is waiting at the garden.' Hearing this, the king rose up immediately and addressed his courtiers: 'Sirs, a king of great resources has arrived quite unannounced. Was he not recognized by any of you?' He said: 'Sire, what resources could he have? He has come with just one companion.' King <s>Bimbisāra</s> reflected: 'It would not be fitting for me to receive a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king anointed on the crown just like that. I shall receive him with great honor.' Having decided this, he had the roads and city adorned, and went out to meet him with a fourfold army. Embracing him around the neck, he placed him on the back of an elephant and led him into the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He had him bathed with water infused with various fragrances, adorned with royal garments, perfumes, garlands, and unguents, and fed. When the fatigue of the journey had subsided, he said: 'Dear friend, having abandoned a prosperous kingdom, inner palace, princes, ministers, and citizens and country-folk — what is the purpose of your coming here? Has some neighboring king caused devastation of your territory? Or has some prince, instigated by treacherous ministers, hungry for kingship, launched an attack?' He replied: 'Friend, I desire going forth, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.'

body.text:
473.001. iti śrutvā rājā bimbisāra āttamanāḥ pūrvakāyamabhyunnamayya dakṣiṇabāhumābhiprasāryodānamudānayati--aho buddhaḥ, aho dharmaḥ, aho saṃghah aho dharmasya svākhyātatā, yatredānīmevaṃvidhāḥ puruṣāḥ sphītaṃ rājyamapahāya sphītamantaḥpuraṃ vistīrṇasvajanabandhuvargaṃ sphītāni ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇyapahāya ākāṅkṣante svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
473.005. ityuktvā rājānaṃ rudrāyaṇaṃ samādāya yena bhagavāṃsetnopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
473.006. tena khalu samayena bhagavānanekaśatāyā bhikṣuparṣadaḥ purastānniṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati/
473.007. adrākṣīdbhagavān rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dūrādeva/
473.007. dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhikṣūnāmantrayate sma--eṣa bhikṣavo rājā bimbisāraḥ saprābhṛta āgacchati/
473.008. nāstitathāgatasyaivaṃvidhaḥ prābhṛto yathā vineyaprābhṛtaḥ/
473.009. ityuktvā tūṣṇīmavasthitaḥ/
473.009. rājā bimbisāro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ/
473.010. ekāntaniṣaṇṇo rājā biṃvisāro bhagavantamidamavocat--ayaṃ bhadanta rājā rudrāyaṇa ākāṅkṣate svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasampadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam/
473.011. taṃ bhagavān pravrājayatu, upasampādayatu anukampāmupādāyeti/
473.012. sa bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitah--ehi bhikṣo, cara brāhmacaryamiti/
473.013. sa bhagavato vācāvasāne eva muṇḍaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ pātrakaravyagrahasto varṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣorīryāpathenāvasthitaḥ//
body.translated_text: Hearing this, King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, delighted, raising his upper body and extending his right arm, uttered this solemn utterance: 'Wonderful is the <s>Buddha</s>! Wonderful is the <s>Dharma</s>! Wonderful is the <s>Saṅgha</s>! Wonderful is the well-proclaimedness of the <s>Dharma</s>, that now such men, having abandoned a prosperous kingdom, a prosperous inner palace, an extensive circle of kinsmen and relatives, and prosperous treasuries and granaries — desire going forth, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>!' Having spoken thus, he took King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> and approached the Blessed One. At that time, the Blessed One was seated before an assembly of many hundreds of monks, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One saw King <s>Śreṇya</s> <s>Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> from afar. Having seen him, he addressed the monks: 'This, O monks, is King <s>Bimbisāra</s> coming with a gift. There is no gift for a <s>Tathāgata</s> such as the gift of one who is to be disciplined.' Having said this, he remained silent. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and sat to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said to the Blessed One: 'This, Venerable Sir, is King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>. He desires going forth, full ordination, and the status of a monk in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May the Blessed One ordain and give full ordination to him, out of compassion.' He was addressed by the Blessed One with the 'Come, monk' ordination: 'Come, monk, practice the holy life.' At the very conclusion of the Blessed One's words, he became tonsured, clad in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, with bowl and hand-vessel, standing in the deportment of a monk who had been fully ordained for a hundred rainy seasons.

body.text:
473.015. ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaśca saṃghāṭiparivṛtadehaḥ/
473.017. sadyaḥ praśāntendraya eva tasthau evaṃ sthito buddho manorathena//8//
body.translated_text: 'Called \"Come\" by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured, his body wrapped in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, immediately he stood with senses perfectly calmed — thus established by the <s>Buddha</s>'s intention.' //8//

body.text:
473.019. āyuṣmān rudrāyaṇaḥ pūrvāhne nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇṭāya prāvikṣat/
473.020. sa mahājanakāyena dṛṣṭaḥ/
473.020. eṣa ca śabdo rājagṛhe nagare samantato visṛtah--rudrāyaṇo rājā bhagavatā pravrajitaḥ, sa rājagṛhaṃ bhikṣārthī praviṣṭaḥ/
473.021. iti śrutvā anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni/
473.022. antarbhavanavicāriṇyo 'pi yoṣito vātāyanagavākṣavedikāsvavasthitā nirīkṣitumārabdhāḥ/
473.023. amātyai rājño bimbisārasya niveditam--deva, rudrāyaṇo rājā rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭo 'nekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtastiṣṭhatīti/
473.024. śrutvā ca punā rājā bimbisāro yena rudrāyaṇo bhikṣustenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
473.025. upasaṃkramya rudrāyaṇaṃ bhikṣumidamavocat--
473.026. bhuktvā grāmasahasrāṇi raurukaṃ ca narādhipa/
473.027. utsṛṣṭaṃ piṇḍameṣāṇaḥ kaccinna paritapyase//9//
body.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. He was seen by the great multitude. This report spread throughout the entire city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>: 'King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> has been ordained by the Blessed One and has entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> seeking alms.' Hearing this, many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled. Even the women dwelling within their houses stood at windows, lattice-openings, and balconies, and began to gaze. The ministers reported to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Sire, King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> has entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms and stands surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of beings.' Hearing this, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> approached the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>. Having approached, he said this to the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>: 'Having enjoyed thousands of villages and <s>Roruka</s>, O lord of men, you have abandoned them and now seek alms — do you not grieve?' //9//

body.text:
473.028. bhuktvā śatapale pātre sauvarṇe rājate 'tha vā/
473.029. bhuñjāno mṛnmaye pātre kaccinna paritapyase//10//
body.translated_text: 'Having eaten from a hundred-<s>pala</s>-weight plate, golden or silver, and now eating from a clay bowl — do you not grieve?' //10//

body.text:
473.030. śālīnāmodanaṃ bhuktvā śuci māṃsopasevitam/
473.031. bhuñjānaḥ śuṣkakulmāṣān kaccinna paritapyase//11//
body.translated_text: 'Having eaten rice and sweet foods, pure and accompanied by meat, and now eating dried barley-gruel — do you not grieve?' //11//

body.text:
474.001. <474>hitvā kauśeyakarpāsān kṣaumaṃ kauṭumbakāśikān/
474.002. dhārayan pāṃśukūlāni kaccinna paritapyase//12//
body.translated_text: 'Having left behind silks, cottons, linens, and fine <s>Kauṭumbaka</s> and <s>Kāśika</s> fabrics, and now wearing refuse-rag robes — do you not grieve?' //12//

body.text: 474.003. kūṭāgāre śāyitvā tvaṃ nirvāte sparśitāgate//
body.translated_text: 'Having slept in a mansion, sheltered from wind and pleasant to the touch —'

body.text: 474.004. āsīno vṛkṣamūleṣu kaccinna paritapyase//13//
body.translated_text: 'And now sitting at the roots of trees — do you not grieve?' //13//

body.text:
474.005. paryaṅke 'vaśayitvā tvaṃ mṛduke tūlasaṃnibhe/
474.006. tṛṇasaṃstare śayānaḥ kaccinna paritapyase//14//
body.translated_text: 'Having lain on a couch, soft and cotton-like, and now lying on a grass-mat — do you not grieve?' //14//

body.text:
474.007. bhāryāṃ sadṛśikāṃ gṛdyāmāśravāṃ vai priyaṃvadām/
474.008. rudantīṃ viprahāya tvaṃ kaccinna paritapyase//15//
body.translated_text: 'Having abandoned a wife who is your equal, desirable, charming, and sweet-spoken, weeping — do you not grieve?' //15//

body.text:
474.009. yānaistvaṃ hastigrīvābhiraśvairapi rathairapi/
474.010. padbhyāṃ paribhraman bhūmau kaccinna paritapyase//16//
body.translated_text: 'Having traveled by vehicles, on the backs of elephants, on horses, and in chariots, and now wandering on foot upon the earth — do you not grieve?' //16//

body.text:
474.011. koṣṭhāgārāṇi kośaṃ ca bahuvittaṃ prahāya vai/
474.012. ākiṃcanyamanuprāptaḥ kaccinna paritapyase//17// iti/
474.013. rudrāyaṇaḥ prāha--
474.014. anṛddhirdamayatyenaṃ sacedbhavati durdamaḥ/
474.015. parabhojanabhuñjānaḥ kathaṃ damayate yugam//18// iti/
474.016. rājā bimbisāraḥ prāha--
474.017. kiṃ nu tvaṃ durmanā rājan kiṃ dīna iva bhāṣase/
474.018. dadāmyupārdharājyaṃ te bhuṅkṣva bhogaparāyaṇa//19//
body.translated_text: 'Having abandoned granaries and treasuries, and great wealth — having attained possessionlessness, do you not grieve?' //17// <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Non-prosperity tames this person if he is hard to tame. One who eats the food of others — how does he tame the yoke?' //18// King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said: 'Why are you downcast, O king? Why do you speak as if dejected? I shall give you half my kingdom — enjoy it, O you who are devoted to pleasures!' //19//

body.text:
474.019. kiṃ nu tvaṃ durmanā rāhan kiṃ dīna iva bhāṣase/
474.020. dadāmi pravarān bhogān yān kāṃścinmanasecchasi//20// iti/
474.021. rudrāyaṇa prāha--
474.022. na rājan kṛpaṇo loke dharmakāyena saṃspṛśet/
474.023. deva tripathanirāśī(?) dhruvaṃ tasya vidhīyate//21//
body.translated_text: 'Why are you downcast, O king? Why do you speak as if dejected? I shall give you the finest enjoyments — whichever ones your mind desires!' //20// <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Not wretched in the world, O king, is one who touches the <s>Dharma</s>-body. The god who is free from longing for the three paths — his destiny is firmly established.' //21//

body.text:
474.024. yastu dharmavirāgārthamadharme nirato nṛpaḥ/
474.025. sa rājan kṛpaṇo jñeyastamastamaḥparāyaṇaḥ//22//
body.translated_text: 'But one who, O king, for the sake of aversion to <s>Dharma</s>, is devoted to <s>Adharma</s> — he, O king, should be known as wretched, heading from darkness to darkness.' //22//

body.text:
474.026. śṛṇu me tvaṃ mahārāja dharmatā deśayāmyaham/
474.027. śrutvā dharmaṃ tato jñeyo yadi tvaṃ prītimeṣyasi//23//
body.translated_text: 'Hear me, O great king — I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>. Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, it should be understood, if you shall find delight.' //23//

body.text:
474.028. nirguṇasya śarīrasya eka eva mahāguṇaḥ/
474.029. yathā yathā vidhāryaṃ te tattathaivānuvartate//24//
body.translated_text: 'For this body devoid of qualities, there is but one great quality: however it should be directed, just so it follows accordingly.' //24//

body.text:
474.030. daśeme varṣadaśāḥ puruṣasyāsu nirucyate/
474.031. trīṭā tatra ratiḥ kā vā putraparadhaneṣu vā//25//
body.translated_text: 'These ten decades of a man's life are quickly told — among those three, what delight is there in sons, the wealth of others?' //25//

body.text:
475.001. <475>putrādveṣiṇīyāmāhurbhāryayā kṛtirucyate/
475.002. śaurā dhanaṃ prārthayante rājan mukto 'smi bandhanāt//26//
body.translated_text: 'Sons become hostile, they say; the wife's devotion is said to be transient. Heroes covet one's wealth — O king, I am freed from bondage!' //26//

body.text:
475.003. na bhaiṣajyāni trāyante na dhanaṃ jñātayo na ca/
475.004. na sarvavidyā na balaṃ na śauryaṃ trāyate 'ntakāt//27/
475.005. devāpi santīha mahānubhāvāḥ sthānecvihocceṣu cirāyuṣo 'pi/
475.007. āyuḥkṣayānte 'pi tataścyavante mucyeta ko neha śarīrabhedāt//28//
body.translated_text: 'Neither medicines protect, nor wealth, nor kinsmen, nor all knowledge, nor strength, nor valor — nothing saves from Death.' //27// 'Even gods of great power exist here, in high and supreme stations, long-lived too — yet at the end of their lifespan, even they fall from there. Who can escape from the breakup of the body?' //28//

body.text:
475.009. rājyāni kṛtvāpi mahānubhāvā vṛṣṇyandhakāḥ kuravaśca pāṇḍavāśca/
475.011. saṃpannacittā yaśasā jvalantas te na śaktā maraṇaṃ nopagantum//29//
body.translated_text: 'Even having held kingdoms, the greatly powerful <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s>, the <s>Kurus</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, accomplished in mind and blazing with glory — they were not able to escape death.' //29//

body.text:
475.013. na samyamena tapasā na rājan na karmaṇā na rājan na karmaṇā vīryaparākrameṇa vā/
475.015. na vittapūgair na dhanairudāraiḥ śakyaṃ kadācinmaraṇādvimoktam//30//
body.translated_text: 'Not by restraint, not by <s>tapas</s> (austerity), O king, not by deeds, not by valor and heroism, not by heaps of wealth, not by abundant riches — can one ever be freed from death.' //30//

body.text:
475.017. naivāntarīkṣe na samudramadhye na parvatānāṃ vivaraṃ praviśya/
475.019. na vidyate sa pṛthivīpradeśo yatra sthitaṃ na prasaheta mṛtyuḥ//31//
body.translated_text: 'Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor by entering the crevices of mountains — there exists no place on earth where one could stand and death would not overpower him.' //31//

body.text:
475.021. naivāntarīkṣe na samudramadhye na parvatānāṃ vivaraṃ praciśya/
475.023. na vidyate sa pṛthivīpradeśo yatra sthitaṃ na prasaheta karma//32//
body.translated_text: 'Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor by entering the crevices of mountains — there exists no place on earth where one could stand and <s>karma</s> would not overpower him.' //32//

body.text:
475.025. yānīmānyapaviddhāni vikṣiptāni diśo diśa/
475.026. kapotavarṇānyasthīni tāni dṛṣṭveha kā ratiḥ//33//
body.translated_text: 'These bones, cast away and scattered in every direction, pigeon-colored — seeing them, what delight is there here?' //33//

body.text:
475.027. imāni yānyupasthānāni alāburiva serabhe/
475.028. śaṅkhavarṇāni śīrṣāṇi tāni dṛṣṭveha kā ratiḥ//34//
body.translated_text: 'These skulls that lie about like gourds at a festival, conch-white — seeing them, what delight is there here?' //34//

body.text:
475.029. yamātape chādayase śīte yamupagūhase/
475.030. evaṃ te priyamātmānaṃ rājan mṛtyurhaniṣyati//35//
body.translated_text: 'The self that you shelter from the heat, that you embrace in the cold — that very dear self of yours, O king, death shall destroy.' //35//

body.text:
476.001. <476>yāvanmṛtyorvaśaṃ bhuṅkte paridhatte dadāti vā/
476.002. taddhi tasya svakaṃ jñeyamanyannityaṃ vigacchati//36//
body.translated_text: 'So long as one is under the power of death — whatever one eats, puts on, or gives away — that alone should be known as one's own; all else is constantly perishing.' //36//

body.text:
476.003. asādhāraṇamanyeṣāmaśaurāharaṇaṃ nidhim/
476.004. martyo nidahyāddānena anyena sukṛtena vā//37//
body.translated_text: 'A treasure that is not shared with others, that cannot be carried off by thieves — a mortal should lay it up through giving or other meritorious deeds.' //37//

body.text:
476.005. purā hi tvāṃ vyāghra iva mṛgaṃ nihatya vyādhirjarā karṣati antakaśca/
476.007. na te mitrāṇyapaneṣyanti rogaṃ saṃgamya sodaryagaṇāśca sarve//38//
body.translated_text: 'Before disease, old age, and the Destroyer drag you away, striking you down like a tiger strikes a deer — neither friends nor all your kinsmen assembled together can remove your disease.' //38//

body.text:
476.009. yadeva labdhādhikamasya bhavati dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ rajataṃ jātarūpam/
476.011. dāyādyamevānuvicintayanti putrāḥ sadārā anujīvinaśca//39//
body.translated_text: 'Whatever additional wealth, grain, silver, and gold one has obtained — only the inheritance do sons with their wives, and dependents, think about.' //39//

body.text: 476.013. sacedṛṇaṃ bhvati piturmṛtasya priyāḥ sutā nāsya vahṇiṃ viśanti mṛtyau na vāpyaśrumukhā rudanti rāhuḥ pitā mama kāryateti(?)//40//
body.translated_text: 'If the father has debts when he dies, the beloved sons do not enter his funeral pyre; nor do they weep with tear-stained faces at his death — "The debt of my father is my burden!"' //40//

body.text:
476.017. āyāntu sattvāḥ pitā mameti prakīrṇakeśāśrumukhā rudanti/
476.019. jyotiścāsya purato haranti hyaho batāyamamaro bhavediti//41//
body.translated_text: 'The relatives come saying "He is my father," weeping with disheveled hair and tear-stained faces. They carry the funeral fire before him, thinking: "Alas, if only he were immortal!"' //41//

body.text:
476.021. dūṣyairenaṃ prāvṛtaṃ nirharanti jyotiḥ samādāya {ca tam} dahanti/
476.023. sa dahyate jñātibhī rudyamāna ekena vastreṇa vihāya bhogam//42//
body.translated_text: 'Wrapped in cloth, they carry him out; taking the fire, they burn him. He is burned while his kinsmen weep — with a single garment, having abandoned all enjoyments.' //42//

body.text:
476.025. eko hyayaṃ jāyate jāyamānastathā mriyate mriyamāṇo 'yamekaḥ/
476.027. eko duḥkhānanubhavatīha jantur na vidyate saṃsarataḥ sahāyaḥ//43//
body.translated_text: 'Alone indeed is one born when being born; likewise alone does one die when dying. Alone does a creature experience suffering here — there is no companion for one who wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>.' //43//

body.text:
476.029. etacca dṛṣṭveha parivrajanti kulāyakāste na bhavanti santaḥ/
476.031. te sarvasaṃgānabhisamprahāya na garbhaśayyāṃ punarāvasānti//33// iti/
body.translated_text: 'Seeing this, the wise go forth into homelessness and are no longer nesters. Having struck off all attachments, they do not again enter the womb-bed.' //44//

body.text: 477.001. <477>atha bimbisāro rājā rudrāyaṇena bhikṣuṇā uttarottareṇa pratibhānena nirākṛtastūṣṇīṃ niṣpratibhaḥ prakrāntaḥ//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, refuted by the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> with ever-higher eloquence, fell silent, without reply, and departed.

body.text:
477.003. atha śikhaṇḍī rājā yāvatkaṃciddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā adharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitumārabdhaḥ/
477.004. sa hirubhirukābhyāmuktah--deva, dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kāraya, mā adharmeṇa/
477.004. tatkasya hetoh? puṣpaphalavṛkṣasadṛśā deva janapadāḥ/
477.005. tadyathā deva puṣpavṛkṣāḥ phalavṛkṣāśca kālena kālaṃ samyakparipālyamānā anuparataprayogeṇa yathākālaṃ puṣpāṇi phalāni cānuprayacchanti, evameva janapadāḥ pritipālyamānā anuparataprayogeṇa yathākālaṃ karapratyāyānanuprayacchantīti/
477.007. sa tābhyāṃ nivārito yāvattāvaddharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā punarapyadharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitumārabdhaḥ/
477.009. sa tābhyām yāvat trirapyuktaḥ/
477.009. visāriṇī kṛ(tṛ?)ṣṇā/
477.009. nivāryamāṇā nāvatiṣṭhate/
477.009. ruṣito 'mātyānāmantrayate--yo bhavanto rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya yāvat trirapyājñāṃ prativahati, tasya kīdṛśo daṇḍa iti/
477.011. tatra kecidduṣṭāmātyāḥ kathayanti--deva, kimatra jñātavyam? tasya vadho daṇḍa iti/
477.012. gāthe ca bhāṣante--
477.013. amātyasya ca duṣṭasya dantasya calitasya ca/
477.014. bhojanasya ca {ajīrṇasya} nānyatroddharaṇātsukham//45//
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, having governed the kingdom righteously for some time, began to govern unrighteously. He was told by <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s>: 'Lord, govern the kingdom righteously, not unrighteously. Why so? Territories, Lord, are like trees bearing flowers and fruit. Just as trees bearing flowers and fruit, when properly tended at the right time with unceasing effort, yield flowers and fruits in due season, so too territories, when properly protected with unceasing effort, yield taxes and revenues in due season.' Having been restrained by those two, he governed righteously for a time, then again began to govern unrighteously. He was thus admonished by them three times. Desire is far-reaching — when restrained, it does not subside. Angered, he addressed the ministers: 'Sirs, whoever thrice disobeys the command of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> king, anointed and consecrated — what punishment should he receive?' Thereupon certain wicked ministers said: 'Lord, what is there to deliberate? The punishment for him is death.' And they spoke verses: 'A corrupt minister, a loose tooth, and undigested food — there is no comfort except by extraction.' //45//

body.text:
477.015. amātyaṃ buddhisampattiprajñāvinayakovidam/
477.016. kośasthaṃ ca balasthaṃ ca yo na hanyātsa ghātyate//43// iti/
477.017. śikhaṇḍī rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, mamaitau pitrā saṃnyastau/
477.017. nāhametau praghātayāmi/
477.018. kiṃ tvābhyāṃ mama darśanapathe na sthātavyamiti/
477.018. tayordvāraṃ nivāritam/
477.018. anyau dvau duṣṭāmātyau sthāpitau/
477.019. tau kathayatah--deva, nākranditā nāluñcitā nātaptā notpīḍitāstilāstailaṃ prayacchanti, tadvannarapate janapadā iti/
477.020. rājā kathayati--yadetābhyāṃ kṛtam, tatparaṃ pramāṇamiti/
477.021. tau janapadān pīḍayitumārabdhau/
477.021. yāvadanyatamo vaṇik paṇyamādāya raurukānnagarād rājagṛhamanuprāptaḥ/
477.022. sa āyuṣmatā rudrāyaṇena dṛṣṭaḥ/
477.023. kaccicchikhaṇḍī khalu raurukeṣu sabhtyavargo balavānarogaḥ/
477.025. dharmeṇa vā kārayati svarājyaṃ na cāsya kaścitparatopasargaḥ//47// iti/
477.027. sa kathayati--
477.028. tathyaṃ śikhaṇḍī khalu raurukeṣu sabhṛtyavargo balavānarogaḥ/
477.030. na cāsya kaścitparatopasargo adharmeṇa tu rājyaṃ karoti nityam//48//
body.translated_text: 'A minister endowed with wisdom, ability, knowledge, and discipline, one stationed in the treasury and stationed in the army — whoever does not slay him, that one is slain.' //43// King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> said: 'Sirs, these two were entrusted to me by my father. I will not have them killed. But they shall not remain within my sight.' Their access was barred. Two other wicked ministers were installed. They said: 'Lord, like sesame seeds that do not yield oil unless they are wailed at, pounded, heated, and pressed — so too are the territories, O lord of men.' The king said: 'What those two did before is the greater authority.' They began to oppress the territories. A certain merchant, having taken merchandise from the city of <s>Rauruka</s>, arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He was seen by the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, who asked: 'Is <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> in <s>Rauruka</s> well, with his retinue, powerful, and in good health? Does he govern his kingdom righteously?
