And is there no external threat to him?' //47// He replied: 'Indeed, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> is in <s>Rauruka</s> with his retinue, powerful, and in good health. Nor is there any external threat to him. But he always governs the kingdom unrighteously.' //48//

body.text:
478.001. <478>athāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇo 'nupūrvyā praṣṭumārabdhah--kastatrāmātyapradhānah? kasya śikhaṇḍī vaśena janapadān pīḍayatīti? sa kathayati--deva, hirubhirukayoramātyayordvāraṃ nivārya anyau duṣṭāmātyau sthāpitau/
478.003. tadvaśena śikhaṇḍī janapadān pīḍayatīti/
478.003. rudrāyaṇaḥ kathayati--gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa, raurukanivāsinaṃ janakāyaṃ samāścāsaya/
478.004. ahamapi tatra pracārite gamiṣyāmi/
478.005. ahamenaṃ śikhaṇḍinamahitānnivārayiṣyāmi, hite ca saṃniyojayiṣyāmīti/
478.006. sa vaṇik paṇyaṃ visarjayitvā pratipaṇyamādāya saṃprasthito 'nupūrveṇa raurukamanuprāptaḥ/
478.007. tena jñātīnāṃ rahasi niveditam--bhavantaḥ, ahaṃ paṇyamādāya rājagṛhaṃ gataḥ/
478.007. tatra mayā vṛddharājo dṛṣṭaḥ/
478.008. sa kathayati--ahaṃ pracāritaṃ raurukaṃ gamiṣyāmi, śikhaṇḍinaṃ cāhitānnivārayiṣyāmi, hite ca saṃniyojayiṣyāmi yathā janapadānna pīḍayatīti/
478.009. tairapareṣāmārocitam, tairapyapareṣām/
478.010. evaṃ karṇaparamparayā sa śabdastayorduṣṭāmātyayoḥ karṇaṃ gataḥ/
478.010. tau saṃlakṣayatah--yadi vṛddharājā āgamiṣyati, niyatamasau bhūyo hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau sthāpayiṣyati, āvayoścānarthaṃ kārayiṣyati/
478.012. tadupāyasaṃvidhānaṃ ca kartavyam yenāsavantarmārga eva praghātyata iti/
478.013. tābhyāṃ rājñaḥ śikhaṇḍina ārocitam--deva, śrūyate vṛddharājā āgacchatīti/
478.013. sa kathayati--pravrajito 'sau/
478.014. kimarthaṃ tasyāgamanaprayojanamiti? tau kathayatah--deva, yenaikadivasamapi rājyaṃ kāritam, sa vinā rājyenābhiraṃsyata iti kṛta etat? punarapyasau rājyaṃ kārayitukāma iti/
478.016. śikhaṇḍī kathayati--yadyasau rājā bhaviṣyati, ahaṃ sa eva kumāraḥ/
478.016. ko nu virodha iti? tau kathayatah--deva, apratirūpametat/
478.017. kathaṃ nāma kumārāmātyapaurajanapadairañjalisahasrair namasyamānena rājyaṃ kārayitvā punarapi kumāravāsena vastavyam? varaṃ deśaparityāgo na tu kumāravāsena vāsam/
478.019. tadyathāpi nāma puruṣo hastigrīvāyāṃ gatvā aśvapṛṣṭhena gacchet,aśvapṛṣṭhena gatvā rathena gacchet, rathena gatvā pādābhyāmeva gacchet, evameva rājyaṃ kārayitvā punaḥ kumāravāsena vāsa iti/
478.021. sa tābhyāṃ vipralabdhaḥ kathayati--kimatra yuktam? kathaṃ pratipattavyamiti? tau kathayatah--deva, praghātayitavyo 'sau/
478.022. yadi na praghātyate, niyataṃ duṣṭāmātyavigrāhito devaṃ praghātayatīti/
478.023. sa evamukte hīnadīnavadano mūhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīṃ sthitvā bāṣpoparudhyamānahṛdayaḥ karuṇadīnavilambitairakṣaraiḥ sa kathayati--bhavantau, kathaṃ pitaraṃ praghātayāmīti? tau kahtayatah--na devena śrutam?
478.026. pitā vā yadi vā bhrātā putro vā svāṅganiḥsṛtaḥ/
478.027. pratyanīkeṣu varteta kartavyā bhūmivardhanā(?)//49// iti/
478.028. punarapyāha--
478.029. yasya putrasahasraṃ syādekanāvādhirūḍhakam/
478.030. ekaśca tatra śatruḥ syāttadarthe tānnimajjayet//50// iti/
478.031. anyatrāpyuktam--
478.032. tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet/
478.033. grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet//51// iti/
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> began to inquire in detail: 'Who is the chief among the ministers there? Under whose influence is <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> oppressing the territories?' He said: 'Lord, having barred the access of the ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s>, he installed two other wicked ministers. Under their influence, <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> oppresses the territories.' <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Go, good man, and reassure the people of <s>Rauruka</s>. When the news has spread, I too shall go there. I shall restrain this <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> from wrongdoing and engage him in what is beneficial.' The merchant, having disposed of his merchandise and taken return goods, set out and in due course arrived at <s>Rauruka</s>. He told his kinsmen in private: 'Sirs, I took merchandise and went to <s>Rājagṛha</s>. There I saw the elder king. He says: "I shall go to <s>Rauruka</s> when the news has spread, and I shall restrain <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> from wrongdoing and engage him in what is beneficial, so that he does not oppress the territories."' They told others, and those told still others. Thus, by word of mouth, that report reached the ears of those two wicked ministers. They reflected: 'If the elder king comes, he will certainly again install <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s> as chief ministers, and he will cause harm to us both. Therefore, a stratagem must be devised so that he is killed on the road itself.' They reported to King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>: 'Lord, it is heard that the elder king is coming.' He said: 'He has gone forth as a renunciant. What purpose does he have in coming?' They said: 'Lord, has anyone who has governed a kingdom even for a single day ever been content without the kingdom? Has such a thing ever happened? He again wishes to govern the kingdom.' <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> said: 'If he becomes king, then I shall simply remain as the prince. What conflict is there?' They said: 'Lord, this is not proper. How can one who has governed the kingdom, being saluted by thousands of joined palms from princes, ministers, citizens, and countryfolk, again live as a mere prince? Better to abandon the country than to live as a prince. Just as a man who has ridden on an elephant's neck would then go on horseback, and having gone on horseback would go by chariot, and having gone by chariot would go on foot — just so is governing a kingdom and then living as a prince.' He, deceived by them, said: 'What is proper here? What should be done?' They said: 'Lord, he must be killed. If he is not killed, he will certainly, incited by wicked ministers, have Your Majesty killed.' When this was said, his face fell and he stood silent for a moment, his heart choked with tears, and in a pitiful, sorrowful, halting voice he said: 'Sirs, how can I kill my father?' They said: 'Has Your Majesty not heard? "Whether father or brother, or a son born from one's own body — when he stands as an adversary, one must increase one's territory."' //49// And again: '"If one has a thousand sons, all embarked on a single boat, and one among them is an enemy — for his sake one should sink them all."' //50// And elsewhere it is said: '"One should abandon one person for the sake of a family; a family for the sake of a village; a village for the sake of a territory; and the earth itself for the sake of oneself."' //51//

body.text:
479.001. <479>deva, nātra kiṃcittapanīyam/
479.001. vadhārho 'sau praghātayitavyaḥ/
479.001. yadi devo 'tra vilambate, yaddevasyānuraktāḥ kumārāmātyapaurajanapadāste kṣobhamāpannā niyatamanarthaṃ kurvantīti/
479.002. kāmān khalu pratisevamānasya nāsti kiṃcitpāpaṃ karmākaraṇīyamiti tenādhivāsitam--evaṃ kriyatāmiti/
479.004. tau duṣṭāmātyau hṛṣṭatuṣṭau pramuditau vadhakapuruṣānutsāhayatah--bhavantaḥ, gacchata, vṛddharājaṃ praghātayata/
479.005. bhogairvaḥ saṃvibhāgaṃ kariṣyāma iti/
479.005. anuraktapaurajānapadaḥ sa rājā/
479.005. na kaścidutsahate praghātayitum/
479.006. tābhyāṃ te hiraṇyasuvarṇagrāmapradānādinā protsāhitā na pratipadyante/
479.007. tatastābhyāṃ krodhaparyavasthitābhyāṃ cārapālānāmājñā dattā--gacchantu, bhavantah etān puruṣān saputradārān sasuhṛtsambandhibāndhavāṃścārake baddhvā sthāpayateti/
479.008. te śrutvā bhītāḥ saṃpratipannāḥ kathayanti--deva, alaṃ krodhena/
479.009. bhṛtyā vayamājñākarāḥ/
479.009. gacchāma iti/
479.009. te tīkṣṇānasīn kakṣeṇādāya saṃprasthitāḥ/
479.010. āyuṣmānapi rudrāyaṇastrayāṇāṃ māsānāmatyayātkṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ samādāya pātracīvaram yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
479.011. upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantamidamavocat--icchāmyahaṃ bhadanta raurukaṃ nagaraṃ janapadacārikāṃ caritumiti/
479.013. bhagavānāha--gaccha rudrāyaṇa, karmasvakatā te manasikartavyeti/
479.013. athāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ/
479.014. āyuṣmān rudrāyaṇastasyā eva rātreratyayāt pūrvāhne nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
479.015. rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātraḥ pratikrānto yathāparibhuktaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratisāmayya samādāya pātracīvaraṃ karmabalapreritam--
479.018. dūraṃ hi karṣate karma dūrātkarma prakarṣate/
479.019. tatra prakarṣate jantum yatra karma vipacyate//52//
body.translated_text:
479.001. 'Sire, there is nothing here to deliberate.
479.001. He deserves death and must be executed.
479.001. If Your Majesty delays, those princes, ministers, and townspeople devoted to Your Majesty will become agitated and will certainly cause harm.'
479.002. 'There is no evil deed that cannot be done by one who indulges in pleasures' — with this, he consented: 'Let it be done.'
479.004. The two wicked ministers, delighted and pleased, urged the executioners: 'Sirs, go and kill the old king.
479.005. We shall share the rewards with you.'
479.005. But the king was beloved by the townspeople and countryfolk.
479.005. No one was willing to kill him.
479.006. Though offered gold, silver, and village-grants by the two, they would not comply.
479.007. Then the two, overcome with anger, gave orders to the police chiefs: 'Go, sirs; seize these men together with their sons, wives, friends, relatives, and kinsmen, and imprison them.'
479.008. Hearing this, they were frightened and submitted, saying: 'Sire, enough of anger.
479.009. We are your servants who obey orders.
479.009. We shall go.'
479.009. They took sharp swords at their sides and set out.
479.010. The Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> too, after three months, having finished making his robes, and taking his bowl and robe, approached the Blessed One.
479.011. Approaching, he bowed at the Blessed One's feet with his head and said: 'Venerable Sir, I wish to go on a wandering tour to the city of <s>Rauruka</s> in the countryside.'
479.013. The Blessed One said: 'Go, <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>; you must bear in mind that you are the owner of your own deeds.'
479.013. Then the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, having bowed at the Blessed One's feet with his head, departed from the Blessed One's presence.
479.014. The Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, after that night had passed, in the forenoon, dressed and taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms.
479.015. Having walked for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having attended to the meal-duty, after his meal, returning, having put away his bedding as it was used, taking his bowl and robe, impelled by the force of karma —
479.018. 'For karma draws one from afar, and from afar karma pulls;
479.019. it draws the being there where the karma ripens.' //52//

body.text:
479.020. iti yena raurukaṃ tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ/
479.020. anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carannantarmārge 'nyatamaṃ karvaṭakaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ/
479.021. sa ca tasmāt piṇḍapātamaṭitvā niṣkrāmati/
479.021. te ca vadhakapuruṣāḥ saṃprāptāḥ/
479.022. sa tairdṛṣṭaḥ/
479.022. tenāpi te pratyabhijñātāḥ/
479.022. sa taiḥ puruṣaiḥ sārdhamekasminnevodyāne rātriṃdevā samupagataḥ/
479.023. sa tān praṣṭumārabdhah--
479.024. kaccicchikhaṇḍī khalu raurukeṣu sabhṛtyavargo balavānarogaḥ/
479.026. dharmeṇa vā kārayati svakaṃ rājyaṃ na cāsya kaccitparatopasargaḥ//53// iti/
479.028. te kathayanti--
479.029. deva, tathyaṃ śikhaṇḍī khalu raurukeṣu sabhṛtyavargo bakavānarogaḥ/
479.031. na cāsya kaścitparatopasargah adharmarājyaṃ tu karoti nityam//54//
body.translated_text:
479.020. Thus he set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Rauruka</s>.
479.020. Gradually, wandering on the journey, he entered a certain hamlet on the road for alms.
479.021. Having gone about for alms, he was coming out.
479.021. And those executioners had arrived.
479.022. He was seen by them.
479.022. He too recognized them.
479.022. He spent the night with those men in a certain garden.
479.023. He began to ask them:
479.024. 'Is <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> well among the <s>Raurukas</s>, together with his servants and retinue, strong and healthy?
479.026. Does he govern his kingdom righteously? And is there no trouble from enemies for him?' //53//
479.028. They said:
479.029. 'Sire, indeed <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> among the <s>Raurukas</s>, together with his servants and retinue, is strong and healthy.
479.031. And there is no trouble from enemies for him; but he always governs unrighteously.' //54//

body.text:
480.001. <480>naravara yattava sadṛśaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā āryaparābhavacihnakaram/
480.002. tasyāpi tu yatsadṛśaṃ tadadya upalapsyase saubhyeti//55//
body.translated_text:
480.001. 'O best of men, what was fitting for you, you did — bearing the mark of not harming the noble.
480.002. But what is fitting for him, that you shall now receive, O lord.' //55//

body.text:
480.003. āyuṣmān rudrāyaṇaḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kimasau mama tatra gamanaṃ nābhinandatīti? te kathayati--deva, nābhinandatīti/
480.004. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yadevaṃ na gacchāmi, pratinivartāmīti/
480.005. te gāthāṃ bhāṣante--
480.006. kva yāsyasi tvaṃ naravīra bhūyo na te suto nandati jīvitena/
480.008. vayaṃ hyadhanyā nṛpasamprayuktā ihābhyupetāstava ghātanāya //56// iti//
body.translated_text:
480.003. The Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Sirs, does he not welcome my going there?' They said: 'Sire, he does not welcome it.'
480.004. He said: 'Sirs, if it is so, I shall not go; I shall turn back.'
480.005. They spoke a verse:
480.006. 'Where will you go now, O hero among men? Your son does not rejoice in your being alive.
480.008. We unfortunate ones, bound to the king's service, have come here for your slaughter.' //56//

body.text:
480.010. āyuṣmān rudrāyaṇaḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yūyaṃ nāma mama vadhakapuruṣāh? deva, vadhakapuruṣāḥ/
480.011. sa saṃlakṣayati--yattaduktaṃ bhagavatā karmasvakatā te rudrāyaṇa manasikartavyeti, idaṃ tat/
480.012. sarvathā dhik saṃsārabhaṅguramiti viditvā teṣāṃ kathayati--bhadramukhāḥ, ahamasmi yadarthaṃ pravajitaḥ, so 'rtho mayā na saṃprāptaḥ/
480.013. tiṣṭhata tāvanmuhūrtam yāvatkhakāryamanurūpaṃ gacchāmīti/
480.014. te parasparaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kṛtvā kathayanti--deva, evaṃ kuru/
480.014. athāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇo 'nyatamaṃ vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍataṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā śānteneryāpathenāvasthitaḥ/
480.015. uktaṃ bhagavatā--pañcānuśaṃsā bāhuśrutye--skandhakuśalo bhavati dhātukuśala āyatanakuśalaḥ pratītyasamutpādakuśalaḥ, aparapratibaddhā cāsya bhavatyavavādānuśāsanīti/
480.017. tena vīryamārabhya idameva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
480.019. arhan saṃvṛttastraidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisavitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparānmukhaḥ/
480.021. sendropaindrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaśca saṃvṛttaḥ/
480.022. athāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇo 'rhattvaprāpto vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedī tasyā velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate--
480.024. mukto granthaiśca yogauśca śalyair nīvaraṇaistathā/
480.025. adyāpyudrāyaṇo bhikṣū rājadharmair na mucyate//57// iti/
480.026. ityuktvā tān vadhakapuruṣānuvāca--bhadramukhāḥ, yaṃ mayā prāptavyaṃ tatprāptam/
480.026. idānīm yadartham yūyamāgatāstadarthaṃ saṃprāpayateti/
480.027. te kathayati--deva, yadi śikhaṇḍī rājā asmān pṛcchati--kiṃ vṛddharājena maraṇasamaye vyākṛtamiti, kimasmābhirvaktavyam? bhadramukhāḥ, sa vaktavyah--
480.030. bahvapuṇyaṃ prasavase rājyahetoḥ piturvadhāt/
480.031. ahaṃ ca parinirvāsye tvaṃ cāvīciṃ gamiṣyasi//58// iti/
body.translated_text:
480.010. The Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Sirs, you are my executioners?' 'Sire, we are executioners.'
480.011. He reflected: 'That which the Blessed One said — "<s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, you must bear in mind that you are the owner of your own deeds" — this is that.'
480.012. Knowing that 'all of <s>saṃsāra</s> is perishable — alas!', he said to them: 'Good sirs, I have not yet attained that for which I went forth.
480.013. Wait a moment while I fulfill my final task.'
480.014. They conferred among themselves and said: 'Sire, do so.'
480.014. Then the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, sitting under a certain tree, bound his legs in the cross-legged posture like the coils of the king of serpents, and remained in a peaceful deportment.
480.015. The Blessed One said: 'There are five advantages of great learning: one becomes skilled in the aggregates, skilled in the elements, skilled in the sense-bases, skilled in dependent origination, and one's instruction and admonition become unimpeded.'
480.017. Exerting effort, knowing this five-knotted wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, having struck at all conditioned states with the quality of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all defilements.
480.019. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from desire in all three realms, equal toward a lump of earth and gold, with a mind like space and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the eggshell of ignorance split by knowledge, having attained the knowledges, higher powers, and analytical insights, turned away from the gains, profits, honor, and respect of existence.
480.021. He became worthy of worship, honor, and salutation by <s>Indra</s> and the gods.
480.022. Then the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, experiencing the bliss of liberation's joy, spoke a verse at that moment:
480.024. 'Freed from bonds, fetters, thorns, and hindrances,
480.025. even today the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> is not free from the duties of a king.' //57//
480.026. Having said this, he addressed the executioners: 'Good sirs, I have attained what was to be attained.
480.026. Now accomplish the purpose for which you have come.'
480.027. They said: 'Sire, if King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> asks us: "What did the old king declare at the time of death?" — what shall we say?' 'Good sirs, tell him this:
480.030. "You engender much demerit by killing your father for the sake of the kingdom.
480.031. I shall attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and you shall go to <s>Avīci</s>."' //58//

body.text:
481.001. <481>idaṃ cāparaṃ vaktavyah--dve ānantarye karmaṇī kṛte--yacca pitā jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, yaccārhan bhikṣuḥ kṣīṇāśravaḥ/
481.002. te 'vīcau mahānarake vastavyam/
481.002. atyayamatyayato deśaya, apyetatkarma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchediti/
481.003. punarāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇaḥ saṃlakṣayati--ṛddhyā gacchāmi/
481.004. mamāsau sattvo narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyatīti/
481.004. yam yam ṛddhyupāyaṃ prārabhate, tasya dharmavinaṣṭatvād ṛkaro 'pi na pratibhāti prāgeva ṛddhiḥ/
481.005. tatasteṣāmekena puruṣeṇa nirghṛṇahṛdayena tyaktaparalokena kakṣādasiṃ niṣkṛṣya utkṛttamūlaṃ śiraḥ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ nipātitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
481.001. 'And say this also: "Two deeds of immediate retribution have been committed — a father has been deprived of life, and an <s>Arhat</s> monk whose defilements were destroyed.
481.002. For these, one must dwell in the great hell <s>Avīci</s>.
481.002. Confess the transgression as a transgression; perhaps this karma may be diminished, exhausted, and consumed."'
481.003. Then the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> reflected: 'I shall go by supernatural power.
481.004. That being of mine will be destined for hell.'
481.004. Whatever means of supernatural power he attempted, because his <s>Dharma</s> was destined to be destroyed, not even the syllable 'ṛ' appeared to him, let alone supernatural power.
481.005. Then one of those men, with a pitiless heart and heedless of the next world, drew his sword from his side and, having cut off his head at the root, cast it to the ground.

body.text:
481.008. atha bhavavān smitamakārṣīt/
481.008. dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītakohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhānniścārya kāścidadhastādgacchanti, kāścidupariṣṭādgacchanti/
481.010. yā adhastādgacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanamavīcimarbudaṃ nirarbudamaṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvamutpalaṃ padman mahāpadmaṃ narakaṃ gatvā ye uṣṇanarakāsteṣu śītībhūtvā nipatanti, ye śītanarakāsteṣūṣpībhūtvā nipatanti/
481.013. tena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante/
481.013. teṣāmevaṃ bhavati--kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, āhosvidanyatropapannā iti/
481.014. teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavānnirmitaṃ visarjayati/
481.015. teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati--na hyeva vayaṃ bhavanta itaścyutāḥ, nāpyanyatropapannāḥ/
481.016. api tvayamapūrvadarśanaḥ sattvaḥ/
481.016. asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti/
481.016. te nirmite cittamabhiprasādya taṃ narakanivedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti/
481.018. yā upariṣṭādgacchanti, tāścāturmahārājikāṃstrāyastriṃśān yāmāṃstuṣitānnirmāṇaratīn parinirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān brahmapārṣadyān mahabrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhānapramāṇābhānābhāsvarān parīttaśubhānapramāṇaśubhāñchubhakṛtsnānanabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalānabṛhānatapān sudṛśān sudarśanānakaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyamanātmetyuddhoṣayanti/
481.022. gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante--
481.023. ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane/
481.024. dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ saunyaṃ naḍāgāramiva kuñjaraḥ//59//
body.translated_text:
481.008. Then the Blessed One smiled.
481.008. It is a rule that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that moment, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward.
481.010. Those that go downward enter the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — and in the hot hells they fall down cooling them, and in the cold hells they fall down warming them.
481.013. Thereby the various torments of those beings are allayed.
481.013. They think: 'Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?'
481.014. The Blessed One, to generate faith in them, releases a magical creation.
481.015. Seeing the creation, they think: 'We have not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere.
481.016. Rather, this is a being of unprecedented appearance.
481.016. By his power our various torments have been allayed.'
481.016. They, having produced faith in the creation, exhaust the karma that destined them for hell, and take rebirth among gods and humans where they become vessels for the Truths.
481.018. Those rays that go upward pass through the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛhatapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!'
481.022. And they speak two verses:
481.023. 'Strive! Go forth! Exert yourselves in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!
481.024. Shake off <s>Mṛtyu</s>'s army, as an elephant shakes off a reed-hut.' //59//

body.text:
481.025. yo hyasmin dharmavinaye apramattaścariṣyati/
481.026. prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati//60//
body.translated_text:
481.025. 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live diligently,
481.026. having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s>, shall make an end of suffering.' //60//

body.text:
481.027. atha tā arciṣastrisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokaghātumanvāhiṇḍya bhagavantameva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti/
481.028. tadyadi bhagavānatītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante/
481.029. anāgataṃ cet purastāt/
481.029. narakopapattiṃ cet pādatale/
481.029. tiryagupapattiṃ cet pārṣṇyām/
481.030. pretopapattiṃ cet pādāṅguṣṭhe/
481.030. manuṣyopapattiṃ cejjānunoḥ/
481.030. balacakravartirājyaṃ cedvāme karatale/
481.031. cakravartirājyaṃ ceddakṣiṇe karatale/
481.031. devopapattiṃ cennābhyām/
481.031. śrāvakabodhiṃ cedāsye/
481.032. pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ cedūrṇāyām/
481.032. yadyanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati <482>uṣṇīṣe 'ntardhīyante/
body.translated_text:
481.027. Then those rays, having wandered through the great trichiliocosm (the billion-fold world-system), followed behind the Blessed One.
481.028. If the Blessed One wishes to declare a past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One.
481.029. If a future one, in front.
481.029. If rebirth in a hell, at the soles of his feet.
481.029. If rebirth as an animal, at his heels.
481.030. If rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), at his big toe.
481.030. If rebirth as a human, at his knees.
481.030. If sovereignty as a <s>Balacakravartin</s>, in his left palm.
481.031. If sovereignty as a <s>Cakravartin</s>, in his right palm.
481.031. If rebirth as a god, at his navel.
481.031. If the awakening of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple), at his mouth.
481.032. If the awakening of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows).
481.032. If he wishes to declare the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

body.text:
482.001. atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādatale 'ntarhitāḥ/
482.002. athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha--
482.003. nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro vaktrāntarānniṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ/
482.005. avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantāddivākareṇodayatā yathaiva//61//
body.translated_text:
482.001. Then those rays circumambulated the Blessed One three times and disappeared at the soles of the Blessed One's feet.
482.002. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:
482.003. 'A cluster of diverse rays, adorned with a thousand colors, has issued from your mouth;
482.005. by which the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the sun at its rising.' //61//

body.text:
482.007. gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate--
482.008. vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā buddhājagatyuttamahetubhūtāḥ/
482.010. nākaraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ smitamupadarśayanti jivā jitārayaḥ//62//

482.013. tatkālaṃ svayamadhigamya dhīra buddyā śrotṛrṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām/
482.014. dhīrabhirmunivṛṣa vāgmiruttamābhirutpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ//63//
body.translated_text:
482.013. 'Having yourself realized that truth in due time through wisdom, O steadfast one, for the sake of listeners who are desirous, O lord of ascetics, O <s>Jinendra</s>,
482.014. with your words — steadfast, eloquent, supreme, and auspicious — dispel, O bull among sages, the doubt that has arisen.' //63//

body.text:
482.016. nākasmāllavaṇajalādritājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitamupadarśayanti nāthāḥ/
482.018. yasyārthe smitamupadarśayanti dhīrāstaṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ//64// iti/
482.020. bhagavānāha--evametadānanda, evametad/
482.020. nāhetvapratyayamānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti/
482.021. api tvānanda,
482.022. mukto granthaiśca yogaiśca śalyair nīvaraṇaistathā/
482.023. athāpi rudrāyaṇo bhikṣurjīvitād vyaparopitaḥ//65//
body.translated_text:
482.016. 'Not without cause do the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, steadfast as the ocean and mountains, display a smile, O protectors.
482.018. The multitudes of people desire to hear for whose sake the steadfast ones display their smile.' //64// Thus.
482.020. The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is.
482.020. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile.
482.021. However, <s>Ānanda</s>:
482.022. "Freed from bonds, fetters, thorns, and hindrances alike,
482.023. the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> has been deprived of life." //65//

body.text:
482.024. rudrāyaṇa ānanda arhattvaṃ prāpto jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ/
482.024. śrutvā āyuṣmānāndaḥ sāśrukaṇṭho vyavasthitaḥ/
482.025. atha te vadhakapuruṣā āyuṣmato rudrāyaṇasya pātracīvaraṃ khikkhitaṃ cādāya raurukamanuprāptāḥ/
482.026. taistayorduṣṭamātyayor niveditam--vṛddharājaḥ praghātita iti/
482.026. tau śrutvā prītiprāmodyajātau yena śikhaṇḍī rājā tenopasaṃkrāntau/
482.027. kathayatah--deva, diṣṭyā vardhase/
482.028. idānīṃ devasyākaṇṭakaṃ rājyam/
482.028. kathaṃ kṛtvā? yo devasya śatruḥ, sa praghātitaḥ/
482.029. ko nāma śatruh? deva, vṛddharājaḥ/
482.029. kathaṃ jñāyate 'sau? praghātita iti? tābhyāṃ te vadhakapuruṣā darśitāh--deva, ime te badhakapuruṣā yaurasau praghātitaḥ/
482.030. śokhaṇḍanā rājñā te pṛṣṭāh--bhavantaḥ, kiyadvṛddharājasya balam/
482.031. deva, kutastasya balam? idaṃ pātracīvaraṃ khikkhiraṃ ceti/
482.031. śikhaṇḍī <483>rājā mūrcchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatito jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇaḥ kathayati--bhavantaḥ, kiṃ vṛddharājena maraṇakāle vyākṛtam? deva, vṛddharājaḥ prāṇaviyogaḥ kathayati--
body.translated_text:
482.024. '<s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, having attained <s>Arhattva</s> (the state of an <s>Arhat</s>), has been deprived of life.'
482.024. Upon hearing this, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> stood with tears in his throat.
482.025. Then those assassins, taking the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>'s bowl, robe, and staff, arrived at <s>Roruka</s>.
482.026. They reported to the two wicked ministers: 'The old king has been slain.'
482.026. Those two, filled with joy and delight, approached King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>.
482.027. They said: 'Sire, congratulations!
482.028. Now Your Majesty's kingdom is free of thorns.
482.028. How so? He who was Your Majesty's enemy has been slain.'
482.029. 'Who was the enemy?' 'Sire, the old king.'
482.029. 'How is it known that he has been slain?' They showed him the assassins: 'Sire, these are the assassins by whom he was slain.'
482.030. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> asked them: 'Sirs, how great was the old king's army?'
482.031. 'Sire, what army did he have? Only this bowl, robe, and staff.'
482.031. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> fainted and fell to the ground. Revived by a sprinkling of water, he said: 'Sirs, what did the old king declare at the time of death?' 'Sire, the old king, at the moment of parting with life, said:'

body.text:
483.003. bahvapuṇyaṃ prasavase rājyahetoḥ piturvadhāt/
483.004. ahaṃ ca parinirvāsye tvaṃ cāvīciṃ gamiṣyase//66// iti/
483.005. idaṃ cāparaṃ vaktavyah--dve tvayā ānantarye karmaṇī kṛte--yacca pitā jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, yaccārhan bhikṣuḥ kṣīṇāśravaśca/
483.006. ciraṃ te 'vīcau mahānarake vastavyam/
483.006. atyayamatyayato deśaya/
483.007. apyevaitatkarma tanutvaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchediti/
483.007. manaḥśokaśalyenābhyāhato haritalūna uva na:o mlāyitumārabdhaḥ/
483.008. tena hirubhirukāvagrāmātyāvāhūtoktaubhavantau, na yuvābhyāmahamīdṛśakarma kurvāṇo nivārita iti? tau kathayatah--vayaṃ devenādarśanapathe vyavasthāpitāḥ/
483.010. kathaṃ nivārayāma iti? tena tau duṣṭāmātyau adarśanapathe vyavasthāpitau/
483.011. bhūyo hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau sthāpitau/
483.011. tābhyāmapi duṣṭāmātyābhyāṃ pracchannaṃ tiṣyapuṣyastūpayordve bale kṛtvā dvau biḍālapotakau sthāpitau/
483.012. tayordine dine māṃsapeśīrdattvā śikṣayatah--tiṣyapuṣyau,yena satyena satyavacanena yuvābhyāṃ māyayā lokaṃ vañcayitvā śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātya pratyavarāyāṃ biḍālayonāvupapannau, tena satyena satyavacanena māṃsapeśīṃ kṛtvā svakasvakaṃ stūpaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svakasvakaṃ balaṃ praviśatāmiti/
483.015. tau yadā suśikṣitau saṃvṛttau, tadā tābhyāṃ duṣṭāmātyābhyāṃ rudrāyaṇasya rājño devī uktā--devi, putraste kṛśāluko durbalako mlāno 'prāptakāyaḥ/
483.017. kimadhyupekṣasa iti? sā kathayati--kimahaṃ karomīti? yuvābhyāmevāsāvīdṛśakarma kārita iti/
483.018. tau kathayati--devi, yatra gha{aḥ patitaḥ, kiṃ tatra rajjurapi pātayitavyā? sā kathayati--satyametatpiturvadham/
483.019. tadahaṃ tasya prativinodayāmi iti/
483.020. sā kathayati--yadyevam, śobhanam/
483.021. sā tasya sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayati--putra, kasmātvamutpāṇḍūtpāḍuḥ kṛśāluko durbalako mlāno 'prāptakāya iti? sa kathayati--amba, tvamapyevaṃ kathayasi--kasmāttvamutpāḍūtpāṇḍuḥ kṛśāluko durbako mlāno 'prāptakāya iti, kathamahaṃ notpāṇḍūtpāṇḍuko bhavāmi kṛśāluko dubalako mlāno 'prāptakāya iti, yena mayā duṣṭāmātyavigrāhitena dve ānantarye karmaṇī kṛte--yacca pitā jīvitādvyaparopito yaccārhan bhikṣuḥ kṣīṇāśravah? ciramavīcau mahānarake vastavyamiti/
483.026. sā kathayati--putra, abhayaṃ tāvatprayaccha, yatsatyaṃ tatkathayāmīti/
483.026. sa kathayati--dattaṃ bhavatu/
483.027. sā kathayati--yathābhūtaṃ putra, nāsau tava pitā, kiṃ tu mayā ṛtusnātayā anyena puruṣeṇa sārthaṃ paricaritam, tatastvaṃ jāta iti/
483.028. sa saṃlakṣayati--pitṛvadhastāvanna jātaḥ/
483.029. iti viditvā kathayati--amba, yadyevaṃ pitṛvadho nāsti, athadvadho 'sti/
483.029. sa kathaṃ nistārya iti? sā kathayati--putra, jñānakocidāḥ praṣṭavyāḥ/
483.030. te etadekāntīkariṣyantīti uktvā prakrāntā/
483.031. tayā tau duṣṭāmātyau āhūyoktau--mayā asya pitṛvadho vinoditaḥ/
483.031. yuvāmidānīmarhadvadhaṃ prativinodayatāmiti/
483.032. śikhaṇḍinā rājñā amātyānāmājñā dattā, sarvāmātyān <484>saṃnipātayata ye ca kecijjñānakovidā iti/
body.translated_text:
483.003. '"You generate much demerit — from killing your father for the sake of kingship.
483.004. I shall attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, and you shall go to <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell)." //66//
483.005. And this further was to be told: "Two deeds of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya karman</s>) have been committed by you — that your father was deprived of life, and that he was an <s>Arhat</s> monk, one whose defilements were destroyed.
483.006. For a long time you must dwell in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell.
483.006. Confess your transgression as a transgression.
483.007. Perhaps this <s>karma</s> may be weakened, diminished, and exhausted."'
483.007. Struck by the arrow of mental grief, he began to wither like a green plant cut down.
483.008. He summoned the two ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s> and said: 'Sirs, was I not led astray by you two into committing such a deed, and you did not restrain me?' They said: 'We were placed by His Majesty out of sight.
483.010. How could we have restrained you?'
483.010. By him, the two wicked ministers were placed out of sight.
483.011. Again, the ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s> were appointed.
483.011. But those two wicked ministers had secretly made two images at the <s>stūpas</s> of <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s>, and placed two kittens inside them.
483.012. Day after day, feeding them pieces of meat, they trained them thus: '<s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s>, by the truth of this true statement — that you two, having deceived the world through illusion and caused the squandering of gifts given in faith, were reborn in the miserable existence of cats — by that truth and true statement, take the piece of meat, circumambulate your respective <s>stūpas</s>, and enter your respective images.'
483.015. When they were well-trained, the two wicked ministers said to King <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>'s queen: 'Queen, your son is pale, thin, weak, withered, and underdeveloped.
483.017. Why do you remain indifferent?' She said: 'What can I do?' 'It was you who caused him to commit such a deed.'
483.018. They said: 'Queen, where the pot has fallen, should the rope be thrown down too?' She said: 'True — there is the murder of his father.
483.019. I shall console him about that.'
483.020. She said: 'If so, very well.'
483.021. She went to him and said: 'Son, why are you so pale, thin, weak, withered, and underdeveloped?' He said: 'Mother, even you speak thus — "Why are you so pale, thin, weak, withered, and underdeveloped?" How should I not be pale, thin, weak, withered, and underdeveloped, when I, led astray by wicked ministers, have committed two deeds of immediate retribution — that my father was deprived of life, and that he was an <s>Arhat</s> monk, one whose defilements were destroyed? For a long time I must dwell in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell.'
483.026. She said: 'Son, first grant me safety, and I shall tell you the truth.'
483.026. He said: 'It is granted.'
483.027. She said: 'In truth, son, he was not your father. Rather, when I had bathed after my menstrual period, I consorted with another man, and from that you were born.'
483.028. He reflected: 'Then the murder of a father has not occurred.'
483.029. Knowing this, he said: 'Mother, if so, there is no patricide, but there is the murder of an <s>Arhat</s>.
483.029. How can that be atoned for?' She said: 'Son, those skilled in knowledge should be asked.
483.030. They will resolve this matter.' Having spoken, she departed.
483.031. She summoned the two wicked ministers and said: 'I have consoled him regarding the patricide.
483.031. Now you two must console him regarding the murder of the <s>Arhat</s>.'
483.032. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> gave orders to his ministers: 'Assemble all the ministers and all who are skilled in knowledge.'

body.text:
484.001. taiḥ sarvāmātyāḥ saṃnipātitāḥ, ye ca kecijjñānakovidāḥ/
484.002. tāvapi suṣṭāmātyau tatraiva saṃnipatitau/
484.002. sarva eva jājopajīvī loko 'nukūlaṃ vaktumārabdhaḥ/
484.003. tatra kecitkathayanti--deva, kenāsau dṛṣṭo 'rhattvam iti? apare kathayanti--deva, arhantaḥ sarvajñānakalpā ākāśagāmina iti/
484.004. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--deva, kimatra śokaḥ kriyate? sa kathayati--yuvāmapyevaṃ kathayatha--kimarthaṃ śokaḥ kriyate iti, nanu yuvābhyāmevāhamarhadvadhaṃ kātitaḥ/
484.006. deva, na santyarhantaḥ/
484.006. kuto 'rhadvadhah? sa kathayati--mayā pratyakṣadṛṣṭau tiṣyapuṣyau arhantau jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau nirvātau/
484.008. yuvāmevaṃ kathayatha--na santyarhanataḥ, kuto 'rhadvadha iti? tau kathayatah--vayaṃ devasya pratyakṣīkurmo yathā māyayā lokaṃ vañcayitvā śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātya pratyavarāyāṃ biḍālayonāvupapannau adyatve 'pi stūpe tiṣṭhata iti/
484.010. rājā amātyānāmantrayate--bhavantaḥ, yadyevamāgacchata gacchāmaḥ, paśyāmaḥ kiṃ bhūtamabhūtaṃ veti/
484.011. eṣa ca śabdo rauruke nagare samantato visṛtaḥ/
484.012. tataste sarve janapadanivāsino lokāstaddraṣṭuṃ niṣkrāntāḥ/
484.012. tatastau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--yathā tiṣyapuṣyau yena satyena satyavacanena yuvāṃ māyayā lokaṃ vañcayitvā śraddhādeyaṃ vinipātya pratyavarāyāṃ biḍālayonāvupapannau svakasvake stūpe tiṣṭhataḥ/
484.014. anena satyena satyavacanena imāṃ māṃsapeśīmādāya svakasvakaṃ stūpaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svakasvakaṃ bilaṃ praviśatāmiti/
484.015. tāvevamuktau svakasvakāt stūpānnirgatau/
484.016. tāvevānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrairdṛṣṭau/
484.016. tau māṃsapeśīmādāya svakasvakastūpaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svakasvakabilaṃ praviṣṭau/
484.017. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayata--dṛṣṭaṃ deveneti? sa kathayati--dṛṣṭam/
484.018. deva, na santi loke 'rhantaḥ/
484.018. kevalaṃ tvayaṃ janapravāda iti/
484.018. tasya yāsau dṛṣṭih--santi loke 'rhanta iti, sā prativigatā/
484.019. tatra ye 'śraddhāsteṣāmasaddarśanamutpannam, ye madhyasthāsteṣāṃ kāṅkṣā, ye śraddhāsteṣāmadbhutaṃ saṃvṛttam/
484.020. anubhāvodagrā aviśāradāḥ/
484.020. śikhaṇḍī rājā saṃlakṣayati--yadi na santyeva loke 'rhantaḥ, kimarhtamāryakāśyapasya kātyāyanasya pañcaśataparivārasya śaulāyā bhikṣuṇyāḥ plañcaśataparivārāyāḥ piṇḍakamanuprayacchāmīti? tena bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ ca piṇḍapātaḥ samucchinnaḥ/
484.023. bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaśca raurukātprakrāntāḥ/
484.023. athāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ śaulā ca bhikṣuṇī vinayāpekṣayā tatraivāvasthatau/
484.024. yāvadapareṇa samayena rājā śikhaṇḍī raurukānnagarānnirgacchati/
484.025. āyuṣmāṃśca mahākātyāyano raurukaṃ nagaraṃ piṇḍāya praviśati/
484.026. sa rājānaṃ dṛṣṭvaikānte 'pakramyāvasthitah--mā ayamaprasādaṃ pravedayiṣyatīti/
484.027. sa rājñā śikhaṇḍinā ekānte 'vasthito dṛṣṭaḥ/
484.027. dṛṣṭvā ca punarāmantrayate--bhavantaḥ, kimarthamayamāryo mahākātyāyano māṃ dṛṣṭvā ekānte 'pakramyāvasthita iti/
484.028. tasya pṛṣṭhato hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau gacchataḥ/
484.029. tau kathayatah--deva, āryo mahākātyāyanaḥ saṃlakṣayati--devaḥ kṛtakautukamaṅgalo gacchati, mā aprasādaṃ vedayiṣyati, duḥkhaṃ caradgacchati, karma kriyate, pātracīvarāṇi pāṃśunā avatariṣyatīti/
484.031. rājā tūṣṇīmavasthita iti/
484.031. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano raurukaṃ nagaraṃ piṇḍāya caritvā nirgacchati, rājā ca śikhaṇḍī praviśati/
body.translated_text: They assembled all the ministers and whoever was learned in knowledge. Those two good ministers also assembled there. The whole world of dependents began to speak favorably. Some said: 'Sire, who has seen that one attain Arhatship?' Others said: 'Sire, <s>Arhats</s> are virtually omniscient and can travel through the sky.' The two wicked ministers said: 'Sire, why is grief being made here?' He said: 'You too speak thus — "Why is grief being made?" — yet it was you two who instigated me to kill the <s>Arhats</s>!' 'Sire, <s>Arhats</s> do not exist. How then could there be the killing of an <s>Arhat</s>?' He said: 'I saw with my own eyes the <s>Arhats</s> <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s> perform miracles of blazing, burning, raining, and illuminating, and then attain final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder. Yet you say: "<s>Arhats</s> do not exist — how could there be the killing of an <s>Arhat</s>?"' They said: 'We shall demonstrate to Your Majesty that, having deceived the world through magic, having brought down the faithful, they have been reborn in a lowly cat-womb — they still live in the <s>stūpas</s> to this day.' The king addressed his ministers: 'Sirs, if so, come, let us go and see whether it is true or false.' This report spread throughout the city of <s>Roruka</s>. All the country-dwelling people went out to see it. Then those two wicked ministers said: 'As <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Puṣya</s> — by this truth, by this truthful word — you who, having deceived the world through magic, having brought down the faithful, were reborn in a lowly cat-womb, you live in your respective <s>stūpas</s>. By this truth, by this truthful word, take this piece of meat, circumambulate your respective <s>stūpas</s>, and enter your respective holes.' Being thus addressed, those two emerged from their respective <s>stūpas</s>. They were seen by many hundreds of thousands of beings. Having taken the piece of meat, they circumambulated their respective <s>stūpas</s> and entered their respective holes. The two wicked ministers said: 'Has Your Majesty seen?' He said: 'I have seen.' 'Sire, <s>Arhats</s> do not exist in the world. This is merely popular hearsay.' His view that '<s>Arhats</s> exist in the world' was dispelled. Among them, the faithless developed a wrong view; the neutral developed doubt; the faithful were astounded — struck by the power of it, they became bewildered. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> reflected: 'If <s>Arhats</s> truly do not exist in the world, why should I provide alms to the Noble <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>Kātyāyana</s> with his five hundred attendants and to the nun <s>Śaulā</s> with her five hundred attendants?' By him, the alms-food of the monks and nuns was cut off. The monks and nuns departed from <s>Roruka</s>. But the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> and the nun <s>Śaulā</s>, out of regard for the <s>Vinaya</s>, remained there. On another occasion, King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> was going out from the city of <s>Roruka</s>. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> was entering <s>Roruka</s> for alms. Seeing the king, he withdrew to one side and stood there, thinking: 'Let this one not become displeased.' He was seen standing to one side by King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>. Seeing him, the king addressed his retinue: 'Sirs, why has this Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, seeing me, withdrawn to one side and stood there?' Behind him walked the two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s>. They said: 'Sire, the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> reflects: "His Majesty goes out on an auspicious festival occasion. Let him not become displeased. It is painful to wander about begging; work is being done; the bowl and robes will become soiled with dust."' The king remained silent. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having wandered for alms in the city of <s>Roruka</s>, was going out, and King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> was entering.

body.text:
485.001. <485>āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastathaiva ekānte 'pakramyāvasthitaḥ/
485.001. śikhaṇḍī rājā kathayati--bhavantaḥ, pūrvamapyayamāryo mahākātyāyano māṃ dṛṣṭvā ekānte 'pakramyāvasthitaḥ, sāmpratimapi/
485.003. ko 'tra heturiti? tasya pṛṣṭhatastau duṣṭāmātyau gacchataḥ/
485.003. tau kathayatah--deva, eṣa kathayati--mā ahamasya pitṛmārakasya rajasā pravrajyāmīti/
485.004. aparīkṣako 'sau/
485.004. śrutvā paryavasthitaḥ/
485.005. sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, yasyāhaṃ priyaḥ, so 'sya muṇḍakasya śramaṇakasyoparyekaikaṃ pāṃśumusṭiṃ kṣipatviti/
485.006. sarveṇa janakāyenaikaikā pāṃśumuṣṭiḥ kṣiptā/
485.006. mahāsādhano 'sau rājā/
485.006. ekaikayā pāṃśumuṣṭyā āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasyopari mahān pāṃśurāśirvyavasthitaḥ/
485.007. so 'pi ṛddhyā parṇikāṃ kuṭimabhinirmāyāvashitaḥ/
485.008. sa gopālakaiḥ paśupālakaiścāvaṣṭabhyamāno dṛṣṭaḥ/
458.008. te buddhyāyamānāh(?) parivāryāvasthitāḥ/
485.009. hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau pṛṣṭhato 'nuhiṇḍya taṃ pradeśamanuprāptau/
485.010. tau pṛcchatah--bhavantaḥ, kimidamiti? te kathayanti--tena kalirājena pitṛmārakeṇa āryo mahākātyāyano 'duṣyanayakārī pāṃśunā avaṣṭabdha iti/
485.011. tau sāśrukaṇṭhau rudanmukhau gopālakapaśupālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ pāṃśūnapanetumārabdhau/
485.011. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano nirgataḥ/
485.012. tau pādayor nipatya pṛcchatah--ārya, kimidamiti? sa kathayati--kimanyadbhaviṣyatīti? tau kathayatah--ārya, yadidaṃ śikhaṇḍinā mahākātyāyane janakāyasahāyena karma kṛtam/
485.014. asya ko bhaviṣyatīti/
485.015. itaḥ saptame divase raurukaṃ nagaraṃ pāṃśunā avaṣṭapsyate/
485.015. ārya, kā āvupūrvī bhaviṣyatīti? āyuṣmantau, prathame divase mahāvāyurāgatya raurukaṃ nagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ vyavasthāpayiṣyati/
485.017. dvitīye divase puṣpavarṣaṃ patiṣyati/
485.017. tṛtīye vastravarṣam, caturthe hiraṇyavarṣam, pañcame suvarṇavarṣam, paścādyai raurukasāmāntanivāsibhiḥ sāmavāyikaṃ karma kṛtam, te raurukaṃ nagaraṃ prevakṣyanti/
485.019. teṣu praviṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭhe divase ratvavarṣaṃ patiṣyati, saptame divase pāṃśuvarṣamiti/
485.019. tau kathayatah--ārya, kimāvāmasya karmaṇo bhāvinau? bhadramukhau, na yuvāmasya karmaṇo bhāginau/
485.021. ārya, yadevaṃ kathamasmābhirasmānnagarānniṣkramitavyamiti? sa kathayati--yuvām yāvacca gṛham yāvacca nadī atrāntare suruṅgāṃ khānayitvā gṛhasamīpe nāvaṃ sthāpayitvā tiṣṭhata/
485.023. yadā ratnavarṣaṃ patet, tadā ratnānāṃ nāvaṃ pūrayitvā niṣpalāyitavyamiti/
485.023. tau tasya pādayor nipatya raurukaṃ praviṣṭau/
485.024. rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ praviṣṭau kathayatah--kiṃ devenāryo mahākātyāyanaḥ kiṃciduktaḥ pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdhah? sa kathayati--bhavantaḥ, jīvatyasau? deva, jīvati/
485.025. kiṃ kathayati--deva, evaṃ kathayati--itaḥ saptame divase raurukaṃ nagaraṃ pāṃśunā avaṣṭapsyata iti/
485.026. kānupūrvī? kathayati--deva, sa evaṃ kathayati, prathame tāvaddivase mahavāyurāgatya raurukaṃ nagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ vyavasthāpayiṣyati, dvitīye divase puṣpavarṣaṃ patiṣyati, tṛtīye divase vastravarṣam, caturthe hiraṇyavarṣam, pañcame suvarṇavarṣam, paścādyai raurukasāmantakanivāsibhiḥ sāmavāyikaṃ karma kṛtaṃ te raurukaṃ nagaraṃ pravekṣyanti, teṣu praviṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭhe divase ratnavarṣaṃ patiṣyati, saptame divase pāṃśuvarṣamiti/
485.031. tau kathayatah--ārya, kimāvāmapyasya karmaṇo bhāginau? bhadramukhau, na yuvāmasya karmaṇo bhāginau/
485.032. ārya, yadyevaṃ kathamasmānnāgrānniṣkramitavyamiti? sa kathayati--<486>yuvām yāvacca gṛham yāvacca nadī atrāntare suruṅgāṃ khānayitvā gṛhasamīpe nāvaṃ sthāpayitvā tiṣṭhata/
body.translated_text: The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, just as before, withdrew to one side and stood there. King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> said: 'Sirs, previously too this Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, seeing me, withdrew to one side and stood there, and now again. What is the reason?' Behind him walked the two wicked ministers. They said: 'Sire, he says: "Let me not be defiled by the dust of this patricide."' He did not investigate. Hearing this, he was overwhelmed with anger. He said: 'Sirs, whoever loves me, let him throw a fistful of dust upon this shaveling ascetic!' Every person threw a fistful of dust. That king had great power. By each fistful of dust, a great heap of dust was piled up over the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. But he, by his supernatural power, conjured a leaf-hut and remained within it. He was found by cowherds and shepherds who dug around him. They gathered around and stood there. The two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s>, following behind, arrived at that spot. They asked: 'Sirs, what is this?' They said: 'That sinful king, the patricide, has buried the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the blameless doer of no wrong, under dust.' The two ministers, with throats choked with tears and weeping faces, together with the cowherds and shepherds, began to remove the dust. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> emerged. They fell at his feet and asked: 'Noble One, what is this?' He said: 'What else could it be?' They said: 'Noble One, this deed that <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> has done to <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, with the people as his accomplices — what will become of him?' 'From today, on the seventh day, the city of <s>Roruka</s> will be buried under dust.' 'Noble One, what will be the sequence?' 'Venerable sirs, on the first day a great wind will come and make the city of <s>Roruka</s> free of stones, gravel, and broken pottery. On the second day, a rain of flowers will fall. On the third, a rain of garments; on the fourth, a rain of silver; on the fifth, a rain of gold. Afterward, those who live in the neighboring regions of <s>Roruka</s>, whose collective <s>karma</s> has been done, will enter the city of <s>Roruka</s>. Once they have entered, on the sixth day a rain of jewels will fall; on the seventh day, a rain of dust.' They said: 'Noble One, will we two also share in the consequences of this deed?' 'Good-faced ones, you two will not share in the consequences of this deed.' 'Noble One, if so, how should we escape from this city?' He said: 'You two should dig a tunnel from your house to the river, station a boat near the house, and wait. When the rain of jewels falls, fill the boat with jewels and flee.' They fell at his feet and entered <s>Roruka</s>. Having entered the king's presence, they said: 'Did Your Majesty say something to the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, burying him under dust?' He said: 'Sirs, does he live?' 'Sire, he lives.' 'What does he say?' 'Sire, he says thus: "From today, on the seventh day, the city of <s>Roruka</s> will be buried under dust."' 'What is the sequence?' 'Sire, he says thus: On the first day a great wind will come and make the city of <s>Roruka</s> free of stones, gravel, and broken pottery. On the second day, a rain of flowers will fall; on the third, a rain of garments; on the fourth, a rain of silver; on the fifth, a rain of gold. Afterward, those who live in the neighboring regions of <s>Roruka</s>, whose collective <s>karma</s> has been done, will enter the city of <s>Roruka</s>. Once they have entered, on the sixth day a rain of jewels will fall; on the seventh day, a rain of dust.' They said: 'Noble One, will we two also share in the consequences of this deed?' 'Good-faced ones, you two will not share in the consequences of this deed.' 'Noble One, if so, how should we escape from this city?' He said: 'You two should dig a tunnel from your house to the river, station a boat near the house, and wait.'

body.text:
486.002. yadā ratnavarṣaṃ patet, tadā ratnānāṃ nāvaṃ pūrayitvā niṣpalayitavyamiti/
486.002. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--samucchinnapiṇḍapātaḥ pāṃśuvarṣeṇāvaṣṭabadhaḥ sa kimanyadvadatu? īdṛśaṃ vā vadate, devato vā pāpanaramiti(?)/
486.004. rājā śikhaṇḍī saṃlakṣayati--syādevamiti/
486.004. hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau mukhaṃ vibhaṇḍya hastān saṃparivartya prakrāntau/
486.005. tatra hitukasya śyāmāko dārakaḥ putraḥ/
486.006. bhirukasya śyāmāvatī nāma dārikā duhitā/
486.006. hitukena śyāmāko dāraka āyuṣmate mahākātyāyanāya dattah--ārya, yadyasya kānicitkuśalamūlāni syuḥ, pravrājayethāḥ/
486.007. no cet tavaivāyamupasthāyaka iti/
486.008. bhirukenāpi śyāmāvatī dārikā śailāyā bhikṣuṇyā dattā--ārye, yadyasyāḥ kānicit kuśalamūlāni syuḥ, pravrājayethāḥ/
486.009. no cet kauśāmbyāṃ ghoṣilo nāma gṛhapatirmama vayasyastasya samarpayiṣyasīti/
486.010. tayādhivāsitam/
486.010. atha śailā bhikṣuṇī śyāmāvatīmādāya ṛddhyā raurukānnagarāt prakrāntā/
486.011. tadā kauśāmbyāṃ ghoṣilasya gṛhapaterdattā/
486.012. yathā ca saṃdiṣṭaṃ samākhyātam/
486.012. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastatraivāvasthitaḥ/
486.012. hirubhirukābhyāmagrāmātyābhyām yāvacca gṛham yāvacca nadī atrāntare suruṅgāṃ khānayitvā gṛhasamīpe ca nauḥ sthāpitā/
486.014. yāvadanyatamasmin divase mahāvāyurāgataḥ, yena taṃ raurukaṃ nagaramapagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakapālaṃ vyavasthāpitam/
486.015. dvitīye divase puṣpavarṣaṃ patitam/
486.015. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--deva, śrūyate rājño māndhātuḥ saptāhaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patitamiti/
486.016. devasyedaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ patitam, nacirādvastravarṣaṃ patiṣyati/
486.017. tṛtīye divase vastravarṣaṃ patiam/
486.017. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--devasyedaṃ vastravarṣaṃ patitam, nacirādvirāddhiraṇyavarṣaṃ patiṣyatīti/
486.018. caturthe divase hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patitam/
486.019. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--devasyedaṃ hiraṇyavarṣaṃ patitam, nacirādeva suvarṇavarṣaṃ patiṣyatīti/
486.020. pañcame divase suvarṇavarṣaṃ patitam/
486.020. tau duṣṭāmātyau kathayatah--devasyedaṃ suvarṣaṃ ptatitam, nacirādeva ratnavarṣaṃ patiṣyatīti/
486.021. yau raurukasāmantakanivāsibhiḥ sāmavāyikaṃ karma kṛtam, te raurukaṃ nagaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ/
486.022. teṣu praviṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭhe divase ratnavarṣaṃ patitam/
486.022. hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau ratnānāṃ nāvaṃ pūrayitvā niṣpalāyitau/
486.023. tatra hirukeṇānyatamasmin pradeśe hirukaṃ nāma nagaraṃ māpitam/
486.024. tasya hirukaṃ hirukamiti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
486.024. bhirukeṇānyatamasmin pradeśe bhirukaṃ nāma nagaraṃ māpitam/
486.025. tasyāpi bhirukacchaṃ bhirukacchamiti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
486.025. saptame divase pāṃśuvarṣaṃ patitumārabdham/
486.026. amanuṣyakairdvārāṇyavaṣṭabdhāni/
486.026. śyāmākaḥ kathayati--ārya, kimeṣa uccaśabdo mahāśabda iti/
486.027. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ kathayati--putra, vātāyanena kāśikāṃ niṣkāsayeti/
486.028. tena vātāyanena kāśikā niṣkāsitā/
486.028. pāṃśubhiranavīkṛtā/
486.028. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ saṃlakṣayati--sāvaśeṣāgocara iti/
486.029. yāvadbhūyo niṣkāsitā, pūrṇā cūḍikābaddhā saṃvṛttā/
486.030. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ saṃlakṣayati--agocarībhūtam/
486.030. idānīṃ gacchamīti/
486.030. atha yā raurukanivāsinī devatā sā yenāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastenopasaṃkrāntā/
486.031. upasaṃkramya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā kathayati--ārya, ahamapyāgachāmi/
486.032. āryasyopasthānaṃ kariṣyāmīti/
body.translated_text: 'When a rain of jewels falls, fill a boat with the jewels and escape.' The two wicked ministers said: 'His alms-food has been cut off; he is afflicted by the rain of dust — what else would he say? Either he speaks such things, or the lord should dismiss this wicked man.' King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> reflected: 'Perhaps so.' The chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s>, pulling faces and wringing their hands, departed. Now <s>Hiru</s> had a son, a boy named <s>Śyāmāka</s>. <s>Bhiruka</s> had a daughter, a girl named <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>. <s>Hiru</s> gave the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s> to the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: 'Noble Sir, if he has any roots of merit, ordain him. If not, let him be your attendant.' <s>Bhiruka</s> also gave the girl <s>Śyāmāvatī</s> to the nun <s>Śailā</s>: 'Noble Lady, if she has any roots of merit, ordain her. If not, in <s>Kauśāmbī</s> there is a householder named <s>Ghoṣila</s>, my friend — you will entrust her to him.' She consented. Then the nun <s>Śailā</s>, taking <s>Śyāmāvatī</s>, departed from the city of <s>Rauruka</s> by her supernatural power. At that time, she was given to the householder <s>Ghoṣila</s> in <s>Kauśāmbī</s>. And the instructions were conveyed as directed. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> remained there. The chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s> had a tunnel dug from their house to the river, and a boat was stationed near the house. Then on a certain day, a great wind came, which left the city of <s>Rauruka</s> swept clean of stones, gravel, and potsherds. On the second day, a rain of flowers fell. The two wicked ministers said: 'Lord, it is heard that for King <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, a rain of gold fell for seven days. For Your Majesty this rain of flowers has fallen; soon a rain of garments will fall.' On the third day, a rain of garments fell. The two wicked ministers said: 'For Your Majesty this rain of garments has fallen; soon a rain of silver will fall.' On the fourth day, a rain of silver fell. The two wicked ministers said: 'For Your Majesty this rain of silver has fallen; soon a rain of gold will fall.' On the fifth day, a rain of gold fell. The two wicked ministers said: 'For Your Majesty this rain of gold has fallen; soon a rain of jewels will fall.' Those who had been recruited from the neighboring regions of <s>Rauruka</s> entered the city of <s>Rauruka</s>. When they had entered, on the sixth day, a rain of jewels fell. The chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s>, having filled a boat with jewels, escaped. <s>Hiru</s> built a city called <s>Hiruka</s> in a certain region. It came to be known as <s>Hiruka</s>. <s>Bhiruka</s> built a city called <s>Bhiruka</s> in another region. It too came to be known as <s>Bhirukaccha</s> (Bharuch). On the seventh day, a rain of dust began to fall. The gates were blocked by non-human beings. <s>Śyāmāka</s> said: 'Noble Sir, what is this loud, great sound?' The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> said: 'Son, push a <s>Kāśika</s> cloth out through the window.' He pushed the <s>Kāśika</s> cloth out through the window. It was not covered by the dust. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> reflected: 'There is still a remnant of my alms-range.' When it was pushed out again, it became full, tied in a bundle. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> reflected: 'The alms-range has been exhausted. Now I shall depart.' Then the deity dwelling in <s>Rauruka</s> approached the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. Having approached and bowed at his feet, she said: 'Noble Sir, I too am coming. I shall attend upon the Noble One.'

body.text:
487.001. <487>tenādhivāsitam/
487.001. āyṣmatā mahākātyāyanena śyāmāka uktah--putra, gṛhāṇa cīvarakarṇikam/
487.002. gacchāma iti/
487.002. tena cīvarakarṇiko gṛhītaḥ/
487.002. sa ṛddhyā uparivihāyasā śyāmākaṃ dārakamādāya saṃprasthitaḥ/
487.003. raurukanivāsinyapi devatā svarddhyā tasya pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhā/
487.004. raurukamapi nagaraṃ pāṃśunāvaṣṭabaddham/
487.004. te 'nupūrveṇa kharaṃ mama karvaṭakamanuprāptāḥ/
487.004. tena tatra khalābhidhāne 'vasthitāḥ/
487.005. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanaḥ śyāmākaṃ dārakaṃ khalabhidhāne sthāpayitvā pinṇḍapātraṃ praviṣṭaḥ/
487.006. devatānubhāvāttasmin khalābhidhāne dhānyaṃ vardhitumārabdham/
487.007. yastatra puruṣo 'vasthitaḥ, sa taṃ dārakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya sakāśamupasaṃkramya kathayati--bho dāraka, tava prabhāvātkhalābhidhāne dhānyaṃ vardhata iti/
487.008. sa kathayati--na mama prabhāvāt khalabhidhāne dhānyaṃ vardhata iti, api tu raurukanivāsinī devatā ihāgatā amuṣmin pradeśe tiṣṭhati, tasyāḥ prabhāvāt khalābhidhāne dhānyaṃ vardhata iti/
487.010. sa tasyāḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā pādayor nipatya kathayati--devate, tāḍakaṃ kuñcikāṃ ca tāvaddhāraya, yāvadgrāmam {gatvā} āgacchāmi/
487.011. na ca tvayā māṃ muktvā anyasya kasyaciddātavyamiti/
487.012. tenāpi karvaṭakaṃ gatvā karvaṭakanivāsī janakāyaḥ saṃnipātitaḥ/
487.013. uktaśca--bhavantaḥ, raurukanivāsinī devatā ihāgatā khalābhidhāne tiṣṭhati/
487.014. tatprabhāvāt khalabhidhāne dhānyaṃ vardhate/
487.014. tasyā haste mayā tāḍakaṃ kuñcikā ca dattā/
487.015. {uktam} ca--devate, tāḍakaṃ kuñcikāṃ ca tāvaddhāraya yāvad grāmaṃ gatvā āgacchāmi/
487.016. na ca tvayā māṃ muktvā anyasya kasyaciddātavyamiti/
487.016. tadadhiṣṭhānaṃ vijñāpayāmi--yadi mama putraṃ śreṣṭhinamabhiṣiñcatha, ahamātmānaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayāmīti/
487.017. devatā asmādadhiṣṭhānānna kvacidgamiṣyati, yuṣmākaṃ bhogābhivṛddhirbhaviṣyati, sarvāśca ītayo vyupaśamaṃ gamiṣyantīti/
487.019. taustasya putraḥ śreṣṭhī tenātmā jīvitādvyaparopitaḥ/
487.019. tataḥ sarvaṃ tadadhiṣṭhānaṃ gandhapuṣpośobhitaṃ chatradhvajapatākāśobhitaṃ ca balimādāya yena devatā tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ/
487.021. upasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya kathayati--devate, adhiṣṭhā bhava, ihaiva tiṣṭheti/
487.022. nāsti mamehāvasthānam/
487.022. āryasyāhaṃ mahākātyāyanasyopasthāyiketi/
487.022. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyana iti kathayati--devate, samanvāhara asya yasya sakāśāt tāḍakaḥ kuñcikā ca gṛhīteti/
487.024. sā samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttā paśyati, yāvatkālagataḥ/
487.024. tayāsāvadhiṣṭhānanivāsī janakāyo 'bhihitah--bhavantaḥ, samayato 'haṃ tiṣṭhāmi/
487.025. tauryādṛśameva tasyā devatāyāḥ sthaṇḍilaṃ kāritaṃ tādṛśamevāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya/
487.027. tasyā devatāyā yo 'dhiṣṭhāne pradīpaḥ prajñaptaḥ, tamasau gṛhītvā āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya sthaṇḍile sthāpayati/
487.028. sā anyatamena puruṣeṇa prākārakaṇṭake sthitena pradīpaṃ gṛhītvā gacchantī dṛṣṭā/
487.029. sa saṃlakṣayati--eṣā devatā āryasya mahākātyāyanasyābhisātikā gacchatīti/
487.030. tayā tasya cittamupalakṣitam/
487.030. sā ruṣitā--pāpacittasamudācāro 'yaṃ karvaṭakanivāsī janakāyaḥ/
487.031. āryasya mahākātyāyanasya nirāmagandhasyātṛptapuṇyasyāpavādamanuprayacchatīti/
487.032. tasmāttasmin karvaṭake mārirutsṛṣṭā/
487.032. mahājanamarako jātaḥ/
487.032. mṛtajane <488>niṣkāsyamāne mañcakāmañcake saḍtkumārabdhāḥ/
body.translated_text: He consented. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> said to <s>Śyāmāka</s>: 'Son, take the robe-corner. Let us go.' He took the robe-corner. Rising by supernatural power into the air, taking the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s>, he set out. The deity of <s>Rauruka</s> also followed behind him by her own supernatural power. The city of <s>Rauruka</s> was buried by the dust. They gradually arrived at a settlement called <s>Khara</s>. There, he established himself at the threshing-floor. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having placed the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s> at the threshing-floor, went for alms. By the deity's power, grain began to increase at that threshing-floor. The man stationed there, seeing the boy, approached him and said: 'Boy, by your power the grain at the threshing-floor is increasing.' He said: 'The grain at the threshing-floor is not increasing by my power; rather, the deity of <s>Rauruka</s> has come here and stands at such-and-such a spot — by her power the grain at the threshing-floor is increasing.' He went to her, fell at her feet, and said: 'Deity, hold this key and lock for me until I go to the village and return. And you must not give them to anyone other than me.' He went to the settlement and gathered the inhabitants together. He said: 'Sirs, the deity of <s>Rauruka</s> has come here and stands at the threshing-floor. By her power, the grain at the threshing-floor is increasing. I have placed the key and lock in her hands. I said: "Deity, hold the key and lock until I go to the village and return. And you must not give them to anyone other than me." I make this known to the council: if you consecrate my son as the head-merchant, I shall put an end to my own life. The deity will not leave this place because of this arrangement; your prosperity will increase, and all calamities will be pacified.' They consecrated his son as head-merchant, and he put an end to his own life. Then all the people of that settlement, having adorned the place with fragrance and flowers, decorated with parasols, banners, and pennants, and bringing offerings, approached the deity. Having approached and fallen at her feet, they said: 'Deity, be our patron; stay right here.' 'I have no reason to stay here. I am an attendant of the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.' The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> said: 'Deity, take charge of the one from whom the key and lock were received.' She began to take charge and saw that he had already died. She addressed the inhabitants of that settlement: 'Sirs, I shall stay on one condition.' They made for that deity a platform of such kind, and one of the same kind for the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>. The lamp that was placed at the deity's platform — she would take it and place it at the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>'s platform. She was seen by a certain man standing on the wall, taking the lamp and going. He reflected: 'This deity is going as a lover to the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.' She perceived his thought. She was angered: 'This inhabitant of the settlement has arisen with evil thoughts. He ascribes slander to the Noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, who is free from the smell of defilements and whose merit is unsatiated.' Therefore she unleashed a plague in that settlement. A great epidemic arose among the people. As the dead were being carried out, the funeral biers began to collide with one another.

body.text:
488.001. adhiṣṭhānanivāsinā janakāyena naimittikā āhūya pṛṣṭāh--kimetaditi? te kathayanti devatāprakopa iti/
488.002. te tāṃ kṣamayitumārabdhāḥ/
488.002. sākathayati--yūyamāryasya mahākātyāyanasya nirāmagandhasyāsatkāramanuprayacchatheti? te bhūyaḥ kathayanti--kṣamakha devate, na kaścidasatkāraṃ kariṣyatīti/
488.004. sā kathayati--yadi yūyam yādṛśamevāryasya mahākātyāyanasyeti/
488.005. te kathayanti--devate kṣamakha, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ kurma iti/
488.006. tayā teṣāṃ kṣāntam/
488.006. tairapyāyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya prativiśiṣṭataraḥ satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ/
488.006. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastatra varṣoṣitaḥ śyāmākaṃ dārakamādāya devatāmupāmantrya saṃprasthitaḥ/
488.007. sā kathayati--ārya, mama kiciccihnamanuprayaccha, yatrāhaṃ kārāṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhāmīti/
488.008. tena tasyāṃ kāśikā dattā/
488.009. tayātra prakṣipya stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpito mahaśca prasthāpitah--kāśīmaha kāśīmaha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
488.010. adyāpi caityavandakā bhikṣavo vandante/
488.010. śyāmāko dārakaścīvarakarṇike lagnaḥ pralambamāno gopālakapaśupālakairdṛṣṭaḥ/
488.011. tairlambate lambata iti uccair nādo muktaḥ/
488.011. tasmiñ janapade manuṣyāṇāṃ lambakapāla iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
488.012. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano 'nyatamaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
488.013. tatra śyāmākaṃ dārakaṃ vṛkṣamūle sthāpayitvā piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ/
488.013. tasmiṃśca karvaṭake 'putro rājā kālagataḥ/
488.014. paurajānapadāḥ saṃnipatya kathayanti--bhavantaḥ, kaṃ rājānamabhiṣiñcāma iti? tatraike kathayanti--yaḥ puṇyamaheśākhya iti/
488.015. apare kathayanti--kathamasau prajñāyata iti? anye kathayanti--parīkṣakāḥ prayujyantāmiti/
488.016. taiḥ parīkṣakāḥ prayuktāḥ/
488.016. te itaścāmutaśca paryāṭitumārabdhāḥ/
488.017. tairasau vṛkṣasyādhastānmiddhamavakrānto dṛṣṭaḥ/
488.017. te tasya nimittamudgṛhītumārabdhā yāvatpaśyanti/
488.018. anyeṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ chāyā prācīnapravaṇā prācīnaprāgbhārā/
488.018. tasya vṛkṣasya cchāyā asya śyāmākasya dāraksya kāyaṃ na vijahātīti/
488.019. dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ saṃjalpitumārabdhāh--bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ sattvaḥ, etamabhiṣiñcāma iti/
488.020. sa taiḥ prabodhyoktah--dāraka, rājyaṃ pratīccheti/
488.021. sa kathayati--nāhaṃ rājyenārthī/
488.021. ahamāryasya mahākātyāyanasyopasthāpaka iti/
488.022. āyuṣmatā mahākātyāyanena śrutam/
488.022. samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ/
488.022. kimasya dārakasya rājñaḥ saṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi na veti/
488.023. paśyati, santi/
488.023. sa kathayati--putra, pratīccha rājyam, kiṃ tu dharmeṇa te kārayitavyamiti/
488.024. tena taṃ pratīṣṭam/
488.024. sa tai rājye 'bhiṣikraḥ/
488.024. śyāmākena dārakeṇa tasmin rājyaṃ kāritamiti/
488.025. śyāmākarājyaṃ śyāmākarājyamiti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā//
body.translated_text:
488.001. The inhabitants of that region summoned soothsayers and asked: 'What is happening?' They said: 'It is the wrath of a deity.'
488.002. They began to propitiate her.
488.002. She said: 'You are showing disrespect to the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the faultless one!' They further said: 'Please be patient, O deity — no one will show disrespect.'
488.004. She said: 'If you treat the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> as you should —'
488.005. They said: 'O deity, please be patient — we shall show him even greater honor.'
488.006. She was appeased by them.
488.006. They then showed the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> even greater honor.
488.006. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having spent the rains-retreat there, took the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s>, bade farewell to the deity, and set out.
488.007. She said: 'Noble one, give me some token, where I may make a shrine and remain.'
488.008. He gave her a Kāśī cloth.
488.009. She enshrined it and established a <s>stūpa</s>, and a great festival was held — thus the designation '<s>Kāśī</s> festival, <s>Kāśī</s> festival' came to be.
488.010. Even today, monks who pay homage to <s>caityas</s> venerate it.
488.010. The boy <s>Śyāmāka</s>, clinging to the hem of the robe, dangling, was seen by cowherds and shepherds.
488.011. They cried out loudly: 'He's dangling! He's dangling!'
488.011. In that region, the designation '<s>Lambakapāla</s>' (Dangling-skull) came to be for the people.
488.012. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> arrived at a certain market-town.
488.013. There, having placed the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s> at the foot of a tree, he entered the town for alms.
488.013. In that market-town, the childless king had died.
488.014. The townspeople and country-folk assembled and discussed: 'Sirs, whom shall we consecrate as king?' Some said: 'One who is known as greatly meritorious.'
488.015. Others said: 'How is such a person to be recognized?' Others said: 'Let examiners be employed.'
488.016. Examiners were employed by them.
488.016. They began to roam here and there.
488.017. They saw him fallen asleep beneath a tree.
488.017. They began to observe his signs — and they saw:
488.018. The shadows of other trees had shifted eastward, leaning to the east,
488.018. but the shadow of that tree did not leave the body of the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s>.
488.019. Having seen this, they began to confer: 'Sirs, this being is known as greatly meritorious — let us consecrate him.'
488.020. He was awakened and told: 'Boy, accept the kingdom.'
488.021. He said: 'I have no use for a kingdom.
488.021. I am the attendant of the noble <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.'
488.022. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> heard this.
488.022. He began to investigate:
488.022. 'Does this boy have <s>karmas</s> conducive to becoming a king or not?'
488.023. He saw that he did.
488.023. He said: 'Son, accept the kingdom, but you must rule righteously.'
488.024. He accepted it.
488.024. He was consecrated as king by them.
488.024. Since the boy <s>Śyāmāka</s> ruled that kingdom,
488.025. the designation '<s>Śyāmāka</s> Kingdom, <s>Śyāmāka</s> Kingdom' came to be.

body.text:
488.026. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano vokkāṇamanuprāptaḥ/
488.026. vokkāṇe āyuṣmato mahākātyāyanasya mātā upapannā/
488.027. sā āyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati--dṛṣṭvā cirasya bara putrakaṃ paśyāmi, cirasya bata putrakaṃ paśyāmīti/
488.028. stanābhyāṃ cāsyāḥ kṣīradhārāḥ prasṛtāḥ/
488.028. āyuṣmatā mahākātyāyanena amba ambeti samāśvāsitā/
488.029. tayā āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano bhojitaḥ/
488.029. tasyā āyuṣmatā mahākātyāyanenāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasamprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam/
488.032. sā dṛṣṭasatyā trirudānamudānayati sma--idamasmākaṃ bhadanata na mātrā <489>kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇairyadbhavatā asmākaṃ kṛtam/
body.translated_text:
488.026. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> arrived at <s>Vokkāṇa</s>.
488.026. In <s>Vokkāṇa</s>, the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>'s mother had been reborn.
488.027. Seeing the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, she said: 'After so long I see my dear son! After so long I see my dear son!'
488.028. And from her breasts, streams of milk flowed forth.
488.028. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> consoled her, saying: 'Mother, mother.'
488.029. She served a meal to the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.
488.029. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> concerning the penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, she shattered the mountain of the view of the personal self — towering with its twenty peaks — with the thunderbolt of knowledge, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>).
488.032. Having seen the truths, she uttered an inspired exclamation three times: 'This was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by a king, nor by deities, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what has been done for us by you, Venerable Sir.

body.text:
489.002. smucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitānyapāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamauṣyeṣu/
489.003. āha ca--
489.004. yatkartavyaṃ suputreṇa mānurduṣkarakāriṇā/
489.005. tatkṛtaṃ bhavatā mahyaṃ cittaṃ mokṣaparāyaṇam//67//
body.translated_text:
489.002. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed, the doors to the lower realms have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.'
489.003. And she said:
489.004. 'What should be done by a good son, a man who performs difficult deeds —
489.005. that you have done for me: my mind is directed toward liberation.' //67//

body.text:
489.006. durgatibhyaḥ samuddhṛtya svarge ca te aham/
489.007. sthāpitā putra yatnena sādhu te duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam//68//
body.translated_text:
489.006. 'Having rescued me from the lower realms and established me in heaven,
489.007. with effort, O son — well done is the difficult deed you have performed.' //68//

body.text:
489.008. athāyuṣmān mahākātyāyanastāṃ bhadrakanyāṃ satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpya kathayati--amba, avalokitā bhava, gacchāmīti/
489.009. sā kathayati--putra, yadyevaṃ mama kiṃcidanuprayaccha, yatrāhaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhāmīti/
489.010. tena tasyā yaṣṭirdattā/
489.010. tayā stūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sā tasmin pratimāropitā/
489.011. yaṣṭistūpa iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
489.011. adyāpi caityavandakā bhikṣavo vandante//
body.translated_text:
489.008. Then the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, having established that good woman in the truths, said: 'Mother, be watchful — I am leaving.'
489.009. She said: 'Son, if so, give me something where I may make an offering and remain.'
489.010. He gave her his staff.
489.010. She established a <s>stūpa</s> and enshrined it there.
489.011. The designation '<s>Yaṣṭi-stūpa</s>' (Staff <s>Stūpa</s>) came to be.
489.011. Even today, monks who pay homage to <s>caityas</s> venerate it.

body.text:
489.012. athāyuṣmān mahākātyāyano madhyadeśamāgantukāmaḥ sindhumanuprāptaḥ/
489.012. atha yā uttarāpathanivāsinī devatā, sā āyuṣmantaṃ mahākātyāyanamidamavocat--ārya, mamāpi kiṃciccihnamanuprayaccha, yatrāhaṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhāmīti/
489.014. sa saṃlakṣayati--uktaṃ bhagavatā madhyadeśe pule na dhārayitavye iti/
489.015. tadete anuprayacchāmīti/
489.015. tena tasyaite datte/
489.015. tayā sthaṇḍile kārayitvā te pratiṣṭhāpite itaścarasantisaṃjñā saṃvṛttā/
489.016. āyuṣmān mahākātyāyano 'nupūrveṇa śrāvastīmanuprāptaḥ/
489.017. bhikṣubhirdṛṣṭa uktaśca--svāgataṃ svāgatamāyuṣman/
489.017. kiccitkuśalacaryeti? sa kathayati--āyuṣmantaḥ, kiṃcit sukhacaryā kiṃcidduḥkhacaryeti/
489.018. bhikṣavaḥ kathayanti--kiṃ sukhacaryā kiṃ duḥkhacaryeti? sa kathayati--yatsattvakāryaṃ kṛtam, iyaṃ sukhacaryā/
489.019. yad rājā śikhaṇḍī raurukanivāsī ca janakāya ahaṃ ca pāṃśunāvacṭabdhaḥ, hirubhirukau cāgrāmātyau kṛcchreṇa palāyitau, iyaṃ duḥkhacaryeti/
489.021. atha pāthābhikṣavo 'vadhyāyantaḥ kathayanti--pitṛmārako 'sau/
489.022. tenāyuṣmān rudrāyaṇo 'rhattvaṃ prāptaḥ/
489.022. aduṣyanayakārī praghatita iti/
489.022. idaṃ tasya puṣpamātram/
489.023. anyatphalaṃ bhaviṣyatīti//
body.translated_text:
489.012. Then the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, wishing to come to <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the central country), arrived at <s>Sindhu</s>.
489.012. Then the deity dwelling in the northern region said to the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>: 'Noble one, give me too some token, where I may make an offering and remain.'
489.014. He reflected: 'The Blessed One has said that in <s>Madhyadeśa</s>, flowers are not to be kept.
489.015. Therefore, I shall give her these.'
489.015. He gave them to her.
489.015. She had them placed on a platform and enshrined them — the designation '<s>Itaścarasanti</s>' came to be.
489.016. The Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> gradually arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.
489.017. He was seen by the monks, who said: 'Welcome, welcome, Venerable one!
489.017. Has your journey been pleasant?' He said: 'Venerable ones, partly pleasant and partly painful.'
489.018. The monks asked: 'What was pleasant and what was painful?' He said: 'That the work of benefiting beings was accomplished — that is the pleasant part.
489.019. That King <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the people of <s>Roruka</s>, and I were pelted with dust, and that the chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiruka</s> barely escaped — that is the painful part.'
489.021. Then the other monks, reproaching him, said: 'He is a patricide.
489.022. Through him, the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, who had attained <s>Arhattva</s>,
489.022. an innocent man, was slain.
489.022. This is only the flower of his deed.
489.023. The fruit is yet to come.'

body.text:
489.024. bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā rudrāyaṇena karma kṛtam yenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule pratyājātah? bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam? arhattvaprāptaśca śastreṇa praghātita iti? bhagavānāha--rudrāyaṇena bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtānyupacittāni labdhasambhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayānyoghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
489.028. rudrāyaṇena karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
489.028. ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
body.translated_text:
489.024. The monks, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, was performed by the Venerable <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>, that he was born in a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions? That, having gone forth in the Blessed One's teaching, he directly realized <s>Arhattva</s> through the abandonment of all defilements? And that, having attained <s>Arhattva</s>, he was slain by a weapon?' The Blessed One said: 'The <s>karmas</s> done and accumulated by the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s> — their conditions have come together, their causes have ripened, and they stand before him overwhelmingly, inevitably.
489.028. The <s>karmas</s> were done and accumulated by <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>.
489.028. Who else will experience their results? O monks, <s>karmas</s> done and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> done and accumulated — both wholesome and unwholesome — ripen in the very aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that are appropriated.'

body.text:
490.001. <490>na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
490.002. sāmagarīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//69// iti/
490.003. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīti^dhvani asti buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā lola utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktāḥ khaṅgaviṣāṇakalpā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
490.005. yāvadanyatamasmin karvaṭake labdhuḥ prativasati/
490.005. tasya karvaṭakasya ca nātidūre udapānaṃ prabhūtānāṃ mṛgāṇāmāvāsaḥ/
490.006. tatrāsau lubdhakaḥ pratidinaṃ prabhūtān kūṭān pāśālepāṃśca pratikṣipati prabhūtānāṃ mṛgānāmutsādāya vināśāya anayena vyasanāya/
490.007. tasya cāmoghāste kūṭāḥ pāśālepāśca/
