490.008. yāvadanyataraḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāaṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāpto devatāyatane rātiṃdivā samupāgataḥ/
490.009. sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya taṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
490.009. tan karvaṭakaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat/
490.010. tataḥ piṇḍapātamaṭitvā saṃlakṣayati--idaṃ devāyatanaṃ divā ākīrṇam/
490.011. bahiḥ karvaṭakasya śānte sthāne piṇḍapātaṃ velāṃ karomīti/
490.011. sa karvaṭakānniṣkramyedaṃ śāntamidaṃ śāntamiti yena tadudapānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
490.012. upasaṃkramya pātrasnāvaṇamekānta upanikṣipya pādau prakṣālya hastau nirmādya pānīyaṃ parisrāvya śīrṇaparṇakāni samudānīya niṣadya bhaktaketyaṃ kṛtvā hastau nirmādya mukhaṃ pātraṃ ca pātraparisrāvaṇam yathāsthāne sthāpya pādau prakṣālya anyatamavṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍīkṛtaṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā śānteneryāpathena niṣaṇṇaḥ/
490.016. tasmin divase mānuṣagandhenaikamṛgo 'pi na grahaṇānugataḥ/
490.016. atha sa lubdhakaḥ kālyamevotthāya yena tadudapānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ/
490.017. sa tān kūṭān pāśāṃśca pratyevekṣitumārabdhaḥ/
490.018. ekamṛgamapi nādrakṣīt/
490.018. tasyaitadabhavat--mamāmī kūṭāḥ pāśālepāścāvandhyāḥ/
490.018. kimatra kāraṇam yenādya ekamṛgo 'pi na baddha iti?/
490.019. tadudapānaṃ sāmantakena paryaṭitumārabdhaḥ/
490.019. paśyati manuṣyapadam/
490.020. sa tena padānusāreṇa gataḥ/
490.020. paśyati taṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ śānteneryāpathena niṣaṇṇam/
490.021. sa saṃlakṣayati--ete pravrajitāḥ śāntātmāna īdṛśeṣu sthāneṣvabhiramante/
490.021. yadyadyāhamasya jīvitāpacchedaṃ na karomi, niyatameṣa mama vṛttisamucchedaṃ karoti/
490.022. sarvathā praghātyo 'yamiti/
490.023. tenāsau nirghṛṇahṛdayena tyaktaparalokena karākārasadṛśaṃ dhanurākarṇaṃ pūrayitvā saviṣeṇa śareṇa marmaṇi tāḍitaḥ/
490.024. sa mahātmā pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati--mā ayaṃ tapasvī lubdho 'tyantakṣataśca bhaviṣyati, upahataśca/
490.025. hastoddhāramasya dadāmīti/
490.025. sa vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarāja uparivihāyasamabhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartumārabdhaḥ/
490.026. āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhirāvarjanakarī/
490.027. sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati--avatarāvatara sadbhūtadakṣiṇīya, mama kleśapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāramanuprayaccheti/
490.028. sa tasyānukampārthamavatīrṇaḥ/
490.028. tatastena viśalyī kṛtaḥ/
490.029. upanāho dattaḥ/
490.029. uktaśca--ārya, niveśanaṃ gacchamaḥ/
490.029. yadyatra suvarṇapaṇo 'pi dātavyaḥ, ahaṃ pariprāpayāmīti/
490.030. sa saṃlakṣayati--yanmayā anena pūtikāyena prāptavyaṃ tadidānīṃ śāntaṃ nirupadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇadhātuṃ praviśāmīti/
490.031. sa tasyaiva purastātpunargaganatalamabhyudgamya vicitrāṇi pratihāryāṇi vidarśya nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ/
490.032. dhanavānasau <491>labdhaḥ/
body.translated_text:
490.001. 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;
490.002. attaining the right conjunction and time, they certainly ripen for the embodied.' //69//
490.003. 'In a former time, O monks, in a past age, when no <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, had arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> appeared in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, content with secluded lodgings and food, like the horn of a rhinoceros, singularly worthy of offerings to the world.
490.005. In a certain hamlet there lived a hunter.
490.005. Not far from that hamlet was a water-well, the haunt of many deer.
490.006. There the hunter daily set out many traps, snares, and bird-lime for the destruction, annihilation, calamity, and ruin of the many deer.
490.007. His traps, snares, and bird-lime were never in vain.
490.008. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a countryside tour, reached that hamlet and spent the night at a temple.
490.009. In the forenoon, dressing and taking his bowl and robe, he reached that hamlet.
490.009. He entered the hamlet for alms.
490.010. Having gone about for alms, he reflected: "This temple is crowded during the day.
490.011. Let me take my meal at a quiet place outside the hamlet."
490.011. Coming out of the hamlet, saying "This is quiet, this is quiet," he approached that water-well.
490.012. Approaching, he set down his bowl-washing cloth to one side, washed his feet, cleaned his hands, strained his drinking water, gathered some dried leaves, sat down, performed the meal-duty, cleaned his hands, face, bowl, and bowl-strainer, placed them in their proper positions, washed his feet, sat under a certain tree with his legs crossed like the coils of the king of serpents, and remained in a peaceful deportment.
490.016. On that day, because of the human scent, not a single deer came near for capture.
490.016. The next morning, the hunter rose early and approached the water-well.
490.017. He began to inspect his traps and snares.
490.018. He did not see a single deer.
490.018. He thought: "My traps, snares, and bird-lime have never been in vain.
490.018. What is the reason that today not a single deer has been caught?"
490.019. He began to wander around the vicinity of the water-well.
490.019. He saw human footprints.
490.020. Following the footprints, he went.
490.020. He saw the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> seated in a peaceful deportment.
490.021. He reflected: "These renunciants, of peaceful nature, delight in such places.
490.021. If today I do not take his life, he will surely destroy my livelihood.
490.022. He must be killed at all costs."
490.023. With a pitiless heart, heedless of the next world, drawing his bow to the fullest like the shape of a hook, he struck the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> in a vital spot with a poisoned arrow.
490.024. The great <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> reflected: "May this wretched hunter not be utterly ruined and destroyed.
490.025. I shall give him a helping hand."
490.025. Like a royal goose with spread wings, he rose up into the sky and began to perform miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and illuminating.
490.026. The supernatural power of a saint quickly captivates an ordinary person.
490.027. The hunter, falling at his feet like a tree cut at the root, said: "Descend, descend, O truly worthy one! Give a helping hand to me who am sunk in the mire of defilements!"
490.028. Out of compassion for him, he descended.
490.028. Then he extracted the arrow.
490.029. A bandage was applied.
490.029. He said: "Noble sir, let us go to my dwelling.
490.029. Even if a gold coin must be given for treatment, I shall provide it."
490.030. He reflected: "What was to be attained with this putrid body — that is now done. Let me enter the peaceful, remainderless <s>nirvāṇa</s> element."
490.031. Rising again into the sky before the hunter, displaying various miracles, he attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the remainderless <s>nirvāṇa</s> element.
490.032. That hunter was wealthy.

body.text:
491.001. tena sarvagandhakāṣṭhaiścitāṃ citvā dhmāpitaḥ/
491.001. sā citā kṣīreṇa nirvāpitā/
491.001. tānyasthīni nave kumbhe prakṣipya śārīrastūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ/
491.002. chatradhvajapatākāścāropitāḥ/
491.002. gandhairmālyairdhūpaśca kumbhe kṛtvā pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam--yanmayaivaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye 'pakāro kṛtaḥ, mā ahamasya karmano bhāgī syām/
491.004. yattu kārā kṛtā, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlenāḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeyam, evaṃvidhānāṃ ca guṇānāṃ lābhī syām, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātuḥ śāstāramārāgayeyaṃ na virāgayoyamiti//
body.translated_text:
491.001. He built a pyre with all kinds of fragrant woods and cremated him.
491.001. He quenched the pyre with milk.
491.001. He placed those bones in a new vessel and established a reliquary <s>stūpa</s>.
491.002. Parasols, banners, and flags were raised.
491.002. Having placed fragrances, garlands, and incense in the vessel, falling at its feet, he made a vow: 'That I committed an offense against such a truly worthy one — may I not be a partaker of the fruit of that deed.
491.004. But the honor that was done — by this root of merit, may I be born in a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions, may I obtain such qualities, and may I find an even more distinguished teacher whom I shall not turn away from but toward.'

body.text:
491.007. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena lubdhakaḥ, eṣa evāsau rudrāyaṇo bhikṣuḥ/
491.008. yadanena pratyekabuddhaḥ saviṣeṇa śareṇa marmaṇi tāḍitaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena bahūni varṣaśatāni bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi narakeṣu paktaḥ, tasminnapi codapāne saviṣeṇa śareṇa marmaṇi tāḍitaḥ, tenaiva ca karmāvaśeṣeṇaitarhyapyarhattvaprāptaḥ śastreṇa praghātitaḥ//
body.translated_text:
491.007. 'What do you think, O monks? He who at that time was the hunter — that was none other than the monk <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>.
491.008. Because he struck the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> in a vital spot with a poisoned arrow, by the ripening of that deed, he was cooked in the hells for many hundreds and thousands of years; at that very water-well too he was struck in a vital spot with a poisoned arrow; and by the residual force of that very deed, even now, having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he was killed by the sword.'

body.text:
491.011. punarapi bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuh--kiṃ bhadanta śikhaṇḍinā raurukanivāsinā janakāyenāyucmatā mahākātyāyanena ca karma kṛtam yena pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdhāḥ, hirubhirukau tvagrāmātyau niṣpalayitāviti? bhagavānāha--ebhireva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni labdhasambhārāṇi prariṇatapratyayānyoghavatpratyupasthitānyavaśyambhāvīni/
491.014. ebhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtānyupacitāni/
491.015. ke 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bḥkṣavaḥ karmaṇi kṛtānyupacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣveva skandhadhātvāayataneṣu karmaṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhānyaśubhāni ca/
491.018. na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatairapi/
491.019. samagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām//70//
body.translated_text:
491.011. Again the monks, in whom doubts had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what deed was done by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the people of <s>Rauruka</s>, and the Venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s> that they were buried under dust, while the two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s> were saved?' The Blessed One said: 'O monks, the deeds were done and accumulated by them — with all conditions gathered, with causes matured, standing before them like a flood, inevitable.
491.014. By them the deeds were done and accumulated.
491.015. Who else would experience the result? O monks, deeds done and accumulated do not ripen externally in the earth-element, nor in the water-element, nor in the fire-element, nor in the wind-element; rather, deeds done ripen in these very appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — both wholesome and unwholesome.
491.018. Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;
491.019. attaining the right conjunction and time, they certainly ripen for the embodied.' //70//

body.text:
491.020. bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatarasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati/
491.020. tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatramānītam/
491.021. sa tayā saha krīḍate ramate paricārayati/
491.021. tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ/
491.022. punarasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato dārikā jātā/
491.022. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
491.023. yā janmikā dārikāḥ, tāsām yācanakā āgacchanti/
491.024. tasyā na kaścidāgacchati/
491.024. asati buddhānāmutpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanasanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya/
491.025. yāvadanyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caraṃstaṃ karvaṭakamanuprāptaḥ/
491.026. yāvattayā dārikayā gṛhaṃ saṃmṛjya vāṭasyopariṣṭāt saṃkāraśchoritaḥ/
491.027. tasya pratyekabuddhasya piṇḍapātamaṭataḥ śirasi patitaḥ/
491.028. tayāsau dārikayā patan dṛṣṭaḥ/
491.028. na cāsya vipratisāracittamutpannam/
491.028. neivam/
491.029. tasyāstameva divasam yācanaka āgataḥ/
491.029. sā bhrātrā pṛṣṭā--kiṃ tvayādya kṛtam yena te yācanakā nāgatā iti/
491.030. tayā samākhyātam--mayā tasyopari saṃskāraśachoritaḥ/
491.030. tena vipuṣpitam/
491.031. tadā dārikayā anyasyā dārikāyā niveditam/
491.031. tayāpyasyā lokasyedaṃ pāpakaṃ dṛṣṭigatamutpannam/
491.032. yasyā yasyā yācanakā āgacchanti, sā sā tasya pratyekabuddhasyopari saṃkāram <492>chorayatviti/
body.translated_text:
491.020. 'In a former time, O monks, in a certain hamlet, a householder dwelt.
491.020. He took a wife from an equal family.
491.021. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her.
491.021. While sporting, delighting, and amusing himself, a son was born.
491.022. Again while sporting, delighting, and amusing himself, a daughter was born.
491.022. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a countryside tour, reached that hamlet.
491.023. For the local-born girls, suitors would come.
491.024. For that girl, none came.
491.024. When no <s>Buddhas</s> have arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> appear in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, content with secluded lodgings and food, singularly worthy of offerings to the world.
491.025. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, wandering on a countryside tour, reached that hamlet.
491.026. That girl, having swept the house, threw refuse from atop the wall.
491.027. It fell on the head of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> as he was walking for alms.
491.028. She saw it falling upon him.
491.028. But no mind of regret arose in her.
491.028. Not at all.
491.029. On that very day, a suitor came for her.
491.029. She was asked by her brother: "What did you do today that your suitors had not been coming?"
491.030. She told him: "I threw refuse upon that one."
491.030. He was delighted by this.
491.031. Then that girl told another girl.
491.031. In that one too, this wicked wrong view arose:
491.032. "Whoever wants suitors to come, let her throw refuse upon that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>."'

body.text:
492.001. asatkārabhītavaste mahātmānaḥ sarve pratyekabuddhāḥ/
492.001. sa tasmāt karvaṭakātprakrāntaḥ/
492.002. pañcābhijñāmṛṣīṇāmupari kṣeptumārabdhāḥ/
492.002. te 'pi prakrāntāḥ/
492.002. tato mātāpitrorupari kṣeptumārabdhāḥ/
492.003. tasmin karvaṭake dvau gṛhapatī samakau prativasataḥ/
492.003. sā ābhyāmuktā--bhavantaḥ, asaddharmo 'yaṃ vardhate, viramateti/
492.004. tābhyāṃ nivāritāḥ prativiratāḥ//
body.translated_text:
492.001. 'Those great beings, all the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, are afraid of disrespect.
492.001. He departed from that hamlet.
492.002. They began to throw refuse upon the sages of the five higher knowledges.
492.002. They too departed.
492.002. Then they began to throw refuse upon their own parents.
492.003. In that hamlet, two householders of equal status dwelt.
492.003. She was told by them: "Sirs, this wrong practice is growing — stop it!"
492.004. Having been restrained by those two, they desisted.'

body.text:
492.005. kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau dārikā yayā pratyekabuddhasyopari saṃkāraśchoritaḥ, eṣa evāsu śikhaṇḍī/
492.006. yo 'sau karvaṭakanivāsī janakāyaḥ, eṣa evāsau raurukanivāsī janakāyaḥ/
492.007. yadebhiḥ pratyekabuddhānāmupari pāpakaṃ dṛṣṭigaramutpannaṃ kṛtam, asya karmaṇo vipākena pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdhāḥ/
492.008. yo 'sau gṛhapatī yābhyāṃ nivāritam, etāvetau hirubhirukāvagrāmātyau/
492.009. tasya karmaṇo vipākena niṣpalāyitau/
492.009. yo 'sau dārikāyā bhrātā yena vipuṣpitam, eṣa evāsau kātyāyano bhikṣuḥ/
492.010. yadanena bipuṣpitaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdhaḥ/
492.011. yadi tena na vipuṣpitam (cittam) na pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdho 'bhaviṣyaditi/
492.011. yadi tasya pāpakaṃ dṛṣṭigatamutpannamabhaviṣyat, kātyāyano 'pi bhikṣuḥ pāṃśunāvaṣṭabdho 'nayena vyasanamāpanno 'bhaviṣyaditi/
492.013. iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇāmekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāmekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ/
492.014. tasmāttarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇyapāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśuleṣveva karmasvābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ/
492.015. ityevaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyamiti/
492.016. bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti//
body.translated_text:
492.005. 'What do you think, O monks? She who threw refuse upon the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> — that was none other than <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>.
492.006. Those hamlet-dwelling people — they are the same as the people of <s>Rauruka</s>.
492.007. Because they generated the wicked wrong view of throwing refuse upon <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, by the ripening of that deed they were buried under dust.
492.008. Those two householders who restrained them — they are the two chief ministers <s>Hiru</s> and <s>Bhiru</s>.
492.009. By the ripening of that deed, they were saved.
492.009. The brother of that girl, who was delighted — that is the monk <s>Kātyāyana</s>.
492.010. Because he was delighted, by the ripening of that deed, he was buried under dust.
492.011. Had he not been delighted, he would not have been buried under dust.
492.011. But had the wicked wrong view arisen in him too, the monk <s>Kātyāyana</s> also would have been buried under dust and met with calamity and disaster.'
492.013. 'Thus, O monks, for deeds that are entirely black, the result is entirely black; for deeds that are entirely white, entirely white; for deeds that are mixed, mixed.
492.014. Therefore, O monks, abandoning entirely black deeds and mixed deeds, one should apply oneself only to entirely white deeds.
492.015. Thus, O monks, you should train yourselves.'
492.016. The monks rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

body.text: 492.017. iti śrīdivyāvadāne rudrāyaṇāvadānaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: 492.017. Thus, in the sacred <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Rudrāyaṇāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Rudrāyaṇa</s>) is concluded.

body.text: 493.001. div38 maitrakanyakāvadānam/
body.translated_text: <s>Maitrakanyakāvadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>) — Chapter 38.

body.text:
493.002. mātaryapakāriṇaḥ prāṇina ihaiva vyasanaprapātapātālāvalambino bhavantīti satatasamupajāyamānapremaprasādabahumānamānasaiḥ satpuruṣairmātaraḥ śuśrūṣaṇīyāḥ/
493.003. tadyathānuśrūyate--vikasitasitakumudendukundakusumāvalīguṇagaṇavibhūṣitaḥ pūrvajanmāntaropāttāprameyānavadyavipulasakalasambhāro dhanadasamānaratnāśrayaḥ svajanakṛpaṇavanīpakabhujyamānodāravibhavasāranicayo mitro nāma sārthavāho babhūva/
493.007. paropakāraikarasābhirāmā vibhūtayaḥ sphītatarā babhūvuḥ/
493.009. tasyāryasattvasya nabhasyarātre karā navendoḥ kumudāvadātāḥ//1//
body.translated_text: Those beings who wrong their mothers fall into the abyss, the chasm, the pit of calamity in this very life — therefore mothers should be served with devotion by virtuous men whose minds are ever filled with arising love, faith, and reverence. As is heard in tradition: There was a caravan-leader named <s>Mitra</s>, adorned with garlands of virtues like blooming white night-lilies, moonlight, and jasmine blossoms, endowed with immeasurable, faultless, and abundant provisions acquired through previous births, a repository of jewels equal to <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera), whose magnificent wealth of noble substance was consumed by his own needy kinsmen like creeping vines. The splendid prosperities of that noble being were exceedingly abundant, delighting solely in the taste of helping others, like the rays of the new moon on an autumn night, white as water-lilies. //1//

body.text:
493.011. tṛṣṇānilaiḥ śokaśikhāpracaṇḍaiścittāni dagdhāni bahuprakāram/
493.013. āśāvatāṃ sapraṇayābhirāmairdānāmbuṣekaiḥ śamayāmbabhūva//2//
body.translated_text: The minds of the hopeful, burnt in many ways by the fierce flames of grief fanned by the winds of craving, he was able to cool with showers of the water of giving, lovely with affection. //2//

body.text:
493.015. dṛṣṭvā lokamimaṃ dhanakṣayabhayāt saṃtyaktadānotsavaṃ lokakleśapiśācikāvaśatayā saṃdūṣitādhyāśayam/
493.017. kāruṇyāt sa dadāvanāthakṛpaṇaklībāturebhyo dhanaṃ matvā ca prahatārṇavormicapalaṃ svaṃ jīvitaṃ bhūyasā//3//
body.translated_text: Seeing this world, which had abandoned the festival of giving out of fear of losing wealth, whose inner resolve was corrupted by subjugation to the demons of worldly affliction, out of compassion he gave wealth to the helpless, wretched, impotent, and distressed, reflecting moreover that his own life was as unstable as waves on the ocean. //3//

body.text:
493.019. yeṣu vyāsajjacetā bhujagavaravadhūbhogabhīmeṣu labdhā gāhante pāpagartaṃ sphuṭadahanaśikhābhīmaparyantarandhram/
493.021. vātāghātapranṛttapravaranaravadhūnetrapakṣmāgralolāṃs tānarthānarthiduḥkhavyupaśamapaṭubhiḥ protsasarja pradānaiḥ//4//
body.translated_text: Those riches, upon which when one's mind is fixed, the obtained ones plunge into the pit of sin with its fearsome boundaries of blazing, crackling flames — and whose dancing, swaying, and flickering resemble the eyelash-tips of the finest women dancing in gusts of wind — those riches he lavished through gifts skilled in alleviating the suffering of the needy. //4//

body.text:
493.023. tasmāt putradhanatvāt putrābhilāṣiṇo yadā manorathaśatairasakṛdunmiṣitonmiṣitāḥ putraśriyaḥ prasahya sphītataravairabhārendhanavahninaiva vigatanikhilapratīkāradāruṇaprabhāvamahatā sukṛtāntalayaīkaparāyaṇāḥ kriyante sma, yadāsau lokapravādamātrayāpi panthānaṃ samavatīrya dhanadavaruṇakuberaśaṃkarajanārdanapitāmahādīn devatāviśeṣān putrārtham yācitumārebhe/
493.027. yasmin yasmiṃstanayasarasi svacchapūrṇāmbupūrṇe vane(jāte)vṛddhiḥ samuditamahāvaṃśalakṣmyambujasya/
493.029. tattattasya prabalavirasam yāti tīkṣṇāṃśumālaiḥ śoṣaṃ manye raviriva jalaṃ bhāgadheyārkabimbam//5//
body.translated_text: Since from that wealth of sons, when the glories of sons — though repeatedly glimpsed through hundreds of wishes by one desirous of a son — were forcibly brought to an end, as if by the fire fueled by ever-more-abundant enmity, whose terrible power admitted no remedy whatsoever, solely devoted to the destruction of merit; since he, having descended to the path of mere popular hearsay, began to entreat various deities — <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, and others — for the sake of a son. In whichever clear, full-watered lake of a son a lotus of great lineage-glory arose and grew, that very one, I think, is dried up by the fierce rays of the sun-disc of fate, just as the sun dries up water, with its scorching heat that bitterly withers. //5//

body.text:
494.001. <494>rudraṃ naikakapālaśekharadharaṃ cakrāyudhaṃ vajriṇaṃ sraṣṭāraṃ makaradhvajaṃ girisutāputraṃ mayūrāsanam/
494.003. gaṅgāśaṅkhadalāvadātasalilāṃstāṃstāṃśca devānasau putrārthī śaraṇam yayau bahu punardānaṃ dvijebhyo dadau//6//
body.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> who bears a chaplet of skulls, the discus-armed <s>Vajrin</s> (Indra), the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>), the crocodile-bannered one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), the son of the mountain's daughter (<s>Skanda</s>), the peacock-seated one (<s>Kārttikeya</s>), and those various gods with waters pure as the Ganges, conch-shells, and white petals — to them all he, desiring a son, went for refuge, and he gave much wealth to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. //6//

body.text:
494.005. yadyajjano maṅgaladeśanābhirvratopavāsādhigataiśca duḥkhaiḥ/
494.007. putrārthasaṃsiddhinimagnabuddhirvikṣipya khedaṃ sa cakāra tāṃstān//7//
body.translated_text: Whatever auspicious observances, vows, fasts, and hardships people prescribed, with his mind absorbed in the pursuit of obtaining a son, casting off weariness, he performed them all. //7//

body.text:
494.009. evamanekaprakārakāyacetasorāyāsakāribhirapi vratopavāsamaṅgalairyadā naiva kadācit kāle 'sya putrā jīvino babhūvuḥ, tadainamativipule pragāḍhaśokāpagāmbhasi nimajjantaṃ kaścit sādhupuruṣo 'bravīt--
494.012. karmāṇyevāvalambanti dehināṃ sarvasampadaḥ/
494.013. bhūtānāṃ tuṅgaśṛṅgādvā vinipāto na bhūtaye//8//
body.translated_text: Thus, though he performed vows, fasts, and auspicious rites that caused suffering to both body and mind in manifold ways, when still at no time did his sons survive, then a certain virtuous man addressed him as he was sinking in the deep waters of the river of overwhelming grief: 'Only <s>karmas</s> sustain all prosperities of embodied beings; even a fall from a lofty peak does not lead to prosperity for beings.' //8//

body.text:
494.014. saṃkleśaṃ bahavaḥ prāptāḥ putratṛṣṇārtabuddhinā/
494.015. na ca te 'dyāpi jīvanti tatra kiṃ parikhidyase//9//
body.translated_text: 'Many have reached affliction with minds tormented by the craving for sons, yet they do not live even to this day — why then do you grieve over that?' //9//

body.text:
494.016. karmāṇi nirmucya kathaṃ bhavebhyaḥ svargaukasastuṣṭivaśādiheyuḥ/
494.018. ye yairvinā nātmabhavaṃ labhante te tairvinā janma kathaṃ bhajeran//10//
body.translated_text: 'How could the heavenly beings, freed from <s>karmas</s> by their own satisfaction, come here to worldly existences? Those without whom they cannot obtain birth — how could they take birth without them?' //10//

body.text:
494.020. ye sāṃsārikanaikaduḥkhadahanajvālālatāliṅgitāste vāñchanti narāmaroragasukhaṃ prāyeṇa dānādibhiḥ/
494.022. tvaṃ kenāpi viḍambase jaḍamatiḥ putrāśayonmattako yastvaṃ dyāmadhigantumicchasi bṛhatsopānamālāśrayāt//12//
body.translated_text: 'Those who are embraced by the creeping flames of the fire of the manifold sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s> — they generally desire the happiness of humans, gods, and serpents through giving and the like. You are being mocked by some force, O dull-witted one, crazed with the desire for a son — you who wish to ascend to heaven by relying on a great staircase of ladders!' //12//

body.text:
494.024. vidhimaparamahaṃ te bodhayāmi prasiddhyai tvamapi ca kuru tāvat saṃprasiddhyai kadācit/
494.026. yadi bhavati sutaste kanyakānāma tasya sakalajanapade 'smin khyāpayasva prasiddhyā//13//
body.translated_text: 'I shall teach you another method for success; and you too should try it sometime for its fulfillment: if a son is born to you, proclaim his name as <s>Kanyaka</s> (Maiden) throughout the entire land with publicity.' //13//

body.text:
494.028. atha tasya kālāntare gaganatalamaṃśumālīva svakiraṇanikarairvirājamānaṃ svavaṃśalakṣmīḥ putraṃ janayāmbabhūva/
494.029. sa ca--
494.030. nirvāntāmalahemaśailaśirasaḥ pracchedagauradyutiḥ saṃpūrṇāmalacandramaṇḍalasamacchatrorubhāsvacchirāḥ/
body.translated_text: Then, after some time, his lineage-glory bore him a son, radiant like the sun illuminating the sky's vault with its cluster of rays. And he —, with a complexion bright as a fragment from the peak of a pure golden mountain newly cooled,

body.text: 495.001. <495>mattairāvaṇacārupuṣkarakaravyālambabāhudvayo bhinnendīvaraphullapatranicayaśyāmāruṇāntekṣaṇaḥ//14//
body.translated_text: with a head resplendent like a full, spotless moon-orb under a brilliant white parasol, with two long arms like the beautiful trunk of a magnificent rutting elephant <s>Airāvaṇa</s>, and with eyes dark-red at the edges like the petals of a freshly blooming blue lotus, //14//

body.text:
495.003. bhūyaḥ kalpasahasrasaṃcitamahāpuṇyaprabhāvodbhavaiḥ pravyaktasphuritendracāparuciraiḥ prahlādibhirlakṣaṇaiḥ/
495.005. mūrtistasya rarāja cāruśikharāddhemam yathā bhūcyutaṃ prodgīrṇasvamayūkhajālajaṭilai ratnāṅkurairveṣṭitam//15//
body.translated_text: his body shone furthermore with delightful auspicious marks, lovely as a clearly arching rainbow, born from the splendor of great merit accumulated over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — like gold fallen from a beautiful peak of the earth, encircled by shoots of jewels bristling with their own radiating nets of rays. //15//

body.text:
495.007. bhramaracamarapaṅktiśyāmakeśābhirāmaṃ samavipulalalāṭaṃ śrīmaduttuṅganāsam/
495.009. tanayamuditacetā maitrakanyābhidhānaṃ daśadivasapareṇa khyāpayāmāsa loke//16//
body.translated_text: With joy in his heart, the father proclaimed to the world the son named <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, charming with his dark hair like rows of bees serving as fly-whisks, with an even, broad forehead, a handsome, prominent nose, on the tenth day after birth. //16//

body.text:
495.011. śarīriṇāṃ vṛddhikaraiḥ samṛddhairviśeṣayuktairvividhānnapānaiḥ/
495.013. sudhāvadātaiḥ sphuṭacandrapādaiḥ payodhiveleva yayau samṛddhim//17//
body.translated_text: Nourished with abundant and special varieties of food and drink that promote the growth of the body, white as ambrosia, bright as rays of the full moon, he grew in prosperity like the ocean at high tide. //17//

body.text:
495.015. dhātrībhiḥ sa samunnītaḥ kṣīraiśca sarpimaṇḍakaiḥ/
495.016. pupoṣa sundaraṃ dehaṃ hradasthamiva paṅkajam//18//
body.translated_text: Raised by wet-nurses with milk and clarified-butter cream, he nourished his beautiful body like a lotus in a lake. //18//

body.text:
495.017. atha tasya pitā mitraḥ sārthavāho vaṇigjanaiḥ/
495.018. dravyairvahanamāropya jagāhe codadhiṃ mudā//19//
body.translated_text: Then his father <s>Mitra</s>, the caravan-leader, together with merchants, having loaded goods onto a vessel, cheerfully plunged into the ocean. //19//

body.text:
495.019. timiṃgilakṣobhavivardhitormipayodadhau mīnavipannapātre/
495.021. pitaryatīte jananīṃ jagāda cakāra kiṃ karma pitā mameti//20//
body.translated_text: When his father had perished in the ocean whose waves swelled from the thrashing of <s>Timiṅgila</s> sea-monsters, the vessel with its fish destroyed, the son asked his mother: 'What work did my father do?' //20//

body.text:
495.023. tato 'sya jananī pativiyogaśokaglapitahṛdayā cintāmāpede/
495.024. āśāpāśaśatākṛṣṭo vāraṇasyeva mṛtyaṃ na paśyati/
495.025. viṣayāsvādakṛpaṇo vāraṇasyeva bandhanam//21//
body.translated_text: Then his mother, her heart withered by the grief of her husband's separation, fell into anxious reflection: 'Dragged by hundreds of nooses of desire, like an elephant he does not see death; wretched through savoring sense-pleasures, his captivity is like an elephant's.' //21//

body.text:
495.026. yadyapi kathayiṣyāmi pitaram yānapātrikam/
495.027. eṣo 'pi mama mandāyā nāśameṣyati toyadhau//22//
body.translated_text: 'Even if I tell him that his father was a sea-trader, this son of unfortunate me will also meet his end in the ocean.' //22//

body.text:
495.028. yāvaccāyaṃ janapadamimaṃ tasya vṛttiṃ na bhūtāṃ pṛcchatyasmai kathayati na vā sarva evaiṣa lokaḥ/
495.030. tāvadyuktaṃ mama sutamimaṃ mṛtyuvaktrāntarālaṃ nānāduḥkhavyasanagahanaṃ vyādhiṣaktaṃ niṣeddhum//23//
body.translated_text: 'So long as this son does not ask anyone in the land about his father's true occupation, and so long as the whole world does not tell him either, it is fitting for me to prevent my son from entering the jaws of death, that dense thicket of manifold sufferings and calamities.' //23//

body.text:
496.001. <496>paro 'pi yaḥ sādhujanānujuṣṭaṃ vihāya mārgaṃ śrayate vimārgam/
496.003. nivāraṇīyaḥ sa svamatājjanena prayatnataḥ kiṃ punareva putraḥ//24//
body.translated_text: 'Even a stranger who abandons the path frequented by virtuous people and resorts to a wrong path should be restrained by one's own people with effort — how much more so one's own son?' //24//

body.text:
496.005. tato jananī kathayāṃcakre--
496.006. putra aukarikatvena pitā te māmapūpuṣat/
496.007. yadyahaṃ sukhitā kāryā kārṣīraukāribhūṣaṇam//25//
body.translated_text: Then the mother said: 'Son, your father maintained me as a baker. If you wish me to be happy, take up the baker's ornament (trade).' //25//

body.text:
496.008. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo māturvacanaṃ kusumamālāmiva śirasā samabhivandya anyasminnahani aukarikāpaṇaṃ prasasāra/
496.010. puṇyasambhāramahatastasya sattvadayāvataḥ/
496.011. prathame 'hani saṃpannaṃ catuḥkārṣāpaṇaṃ dhanam//26//
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, reverently accepting his mother's words upon his head like a garland of flowers, went the next day to the baker's shop. On the very first day, by the greatness of his merit-accumulation and his compassion for beings, wealth of four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> was earned. //26//

body.text:
496.012. svagarbhasaṃdhāraṇaduḥkhitāyai dadau sa tasyai mudito jananyai/
496.014. dāridryaduḥkhavyasanacchidāyai dhanaṃ mahābhogaphalaprasūtyai//27//
body.translated_text: He joyfully gave that wealth to his mother, who had suffered in carrying him in her womb — for the cutting off of the afflictions of poverty, for the bearing of the fruit of great enjoyment. //27//

body.text:
496.016. atha ye tasmin puravare ciraṃtanā aukarikāḥ, te tasya tāmabhivardhamānāṃ kriyavikrayalokamaviṣamavyavahāranītyā prakṛtipremapeśalatayā cāvarjitamanasastasmin mahāsattve vyavahārārthamāpatantamavalokya taṃ tasmātkarmaṇo vinivartanārthamāhuh--
496.019. gāndhikāpaṇikaḥ śreṣṭhī pitaitasmin pure purā/
496.020. sa tvaṃ tāṃ vṛttimujjhatvā śrayase 'nyāṃ kayā dhiyā//28//
body.translated_text: Then the established bakers of that fine city, seeing the great being's ever-increasing trade and commercial activity conducted with fair, impartial business ethics, and with their minds won over by the charm of his natural affection — seeing him advancing in commerce, they told him, in order to turn him away from that trade: 'Your father was formerly a perfumer-merchant, a leading trader in this city. Why do you, abandoning that livelihood, resort to another — by what reasoning?' //28//

body.text:
496.021. atha bodhisattvastāmāpi jīvikāmapahāya gāndhikāpaṇaṃ cakāra--
496.022. yasminneva dine cakre sa sādhurgāndhikāpaṇam/
496.023. kārṣāpaṇāṣṭakaṃ tasya tasminnevopapadyate//29//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, giving up even that livelihood, set up a perfumer's shop. On the very day that noble man established the perfumer's shop, eight <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> accrued to him on that same day. //29//

body.text:
496.024. tamapi mātre pratipāditavān/
496.024. atha gāndhikāpaṇikāḥ puruṣāḥ sametyāgatya ca taṃ mahāsattvaṃ vicchandayāmāsuh--
496.026. gāndhāpaṇaṃ klībajanābhipannaṃ pitā na vai mādya pure(?) cakāra/
496.028. tatraiva hairaṇyikatāṃ sa kṛtvā dhanāni bhūyāṃsi samāpa sādho//30//
body.translated_text: That too he handed over to his mother. Then the perfumer-merchants, coming together and approaching, urged that great being: 'Your father in this city formerly did not run a perfumer's shop, which is frequented by weak folk. Rather, there in the goldsmith's trade, he earned abundant wealth, O noble one.' //30//

body.text:
496.030. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvastāmapi jīvikāmapahāya hairaṇyikāpaṇaṃ cakrāra/
496.031. tayāpi tasmin vyavahāranītyā hairaṇyikāṃstānabhibhūya sarvān/
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, giving up even that livelihood, established a goldsmith's shop. By his fair business ethics in that trade too, surpassing all those goldsmiths,

body.text: 497.001. <497>lebhe dine sa prathame mahārhaḥ kārṣāpaṇān ṣoḍaśa tān dadau ca//31//
body.translated_text: the worthy one earned sixteen <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> on the first day and gave them away. //31//

body.text:
497.003. dine dvitīye dvātriṃśat kārṣāpaṇamupārjya saḥ/
497.004. dakṣiṇīyaviśeṣāyai mātre tānapi dattavān//32//
body.translated_text: On the second day, having earned thirty-two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, he gave those too to his mother, worthy of the highest offerings. //32//

body.text:
497.005. atha hairaṇyikāpaṇikāḥ puruṣā sametyāgatya ca taṃ tasmātkarmaṇo vinivartanārthamāhuh--
497.006. śaraccandrāṃśudhavale labdhvā janma kule katham/
497.007. kṛpaṇāṃ jīvikāhetorvṛttimāśrayate bhavān//33//
body.translated_text: Then the goldsmith-merchants, coming together and approaching, told him, in order to turn him away from that trade: 'How can one born in a family white as the rays of the autumn moon, for the sake of a livelihood, resort to a wretched occupation?' //33//

body.text:
497.008. prabhañjanoddhūtaśikhākarāle hutāśane visphuritasphuliṅge/
497.010. vivartitaṃ ślāghyamatīva puṃsāṃ na tu svavṛtteścyavanaṃ pravṛttam//34//
body.translated_text: 'In a fire whose flames are terrifyingly whipped up by the hurricane, with sparks flying and crackling, what is truly praiseworthy for men is fortitude, not the abandonment of one's own proper calling.' //34//

body.text:
497.012. mahoragāśvāsavighūrṇitograistaraṃgabhaṅgairviṣamaṃ payodhim/
497.014. agādhapātālavilagnamūlaṃ pitā vigāhyārjitavān dhanaṃ te//35//
body.translated_text: 'Your father earned his wealth by plunging into the ocean, treacherous with towering waves churned by the breathing of great sea-serpents, whose depths reach down to the netherworld.' //35//

body.text:
497.016. yadāśritaṃ karma janānuvarjinā tvayā vidagdhena dhanepsunādhunā/
497.018. kathaṃ na saṃprāpsyasi bhāgyasampadaṃ piturvyatīte 'pi viśālinīṃ śriyam//36//
body.translated_text: 'When you, a clever man eager for wealth, have resorted to the same trade that was followed by your father, a man whom people followed — how shall you not attain the prosperity of fortune, the expansive glory of your father, even though he has passed away?' //36//

body.text:
497.020. vitteśvaro 'pyarthavibhūtivistarair nāśāṃ sadarthāṃ vibabhāra yasya/
497.022. tasyā mahendrāmalatulyakīrteḥ sūnuḥ kathaṃ tvaṃ na bibharṣi lajjām//37//
body.translated_text: 'Even <s>Vitteśvara</s> (the Lord of Wealth, Kubera) could not sustain with all his extensive displays of affluence the purpose of the wealth of him whose fame was pure as great <s>Indra</s>'s. How then do you, his son, not bear shame?' //37//

body.text:
497.024. ye mṛtyuṃ gaṇayanti naiva vipadi grāsaṃ bhajante 'nagha gehe bandhuṣu sūnuṣu vyapagatasnehātmanodyoginaḥ/
497.026. ye nītvā jaladhīnagādhasalilānāvartabhīmān budhāḥ prāpyārthān gajadantabhaṅgasitayāsinvanta kīrtyā jagat//38//
body.translated_text: 'Those who do not even reckon with death in adversity, who partake of but a morsel, O sinless one, who are free from attachment to home, kinsmen, and sons, self-exerting — those wise ones, having navigated the fathomless, whirlpool-fearsome oceans, having obtained riches, inundate the world with fame white as the breaking of elephant tusks.' //38//

body.text:
497.028. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvastebhyo 'pi tathānuguṇinīṃ kathāmavadhārya samudrāvataraṇakṛtavyavasāyo mātaramupasṛtyovāca--amba, sārthavāhaḥ kilāsmākaṃ pitā purā/
497.029. tadanujñāṃ prayaccha, yadahamapi mahāsamudramavatariṣyāmīti/
497.030. sā pūrvameva bhartṛmaraṇaduḥkhena vigatajīvitāśā svasya tanayasya tenāsamlakṣitadāruṇena viyogaśokaśastreṇa bhṛśataraṃ pravidāryamāṇahṛdayeva svatanayamāha--
497.032. vatsa kena tavākhyātaṃ vinākāraṇaśatrunā/
497.033. jīvitaṃ kasya te 'niṣṭaṃ tvayā krīḍāṃ karoti kaḥ//39//
body.translated_text:
497.028. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, having heard from them too a suitably corresponding account, resolved to embark on the ocean and approached his mother, saying: 'Mother, our father was formerly a caravan-leader.
497.029. Grant me permission, for I too wish to cross the great ocean.'
497.030. She, who had already lost all hope of life through the grief of her husband's death, her heart torn asunder even more deeply by the terrible weapon of separation-sorrow — unforeseen by her own son — said to her child:
497.032. 'Son, who has told you this — that enemy without cause?
497.033. Whose life is displeasing to him? Who plays games with yours?' //39//

body.text:
498.001. <498>daivāt kathaṃcitsamprāptaṃ cakṣurekaṃ tvamadya me/
498.002. putrakleśābhāginyā mṛtyunā hriyase 'dhunā//40//
body.translated_text:
498.001. 'By fate, somehow, you, my one remaining eye, have come to me;
498.002. now, from me who has known only the torments of a son, you are being snatched away by death.' //40//

body.text:
498.003. na yāvadevaṃ mama duḥkhaśalyaṃ prayāti nāśaṃ pravidārya śokam/
498.005. kathaṃ nu tasyopari me dvitīyaṃ nipātyate pāpamayairamitraiḥ//41//
body.translated_text:
498.003. 'Before this arrow of grief in me has come to its end, rending my sorrow apart,
498.005. how is it that a second one is hurled upon it by sinful enemies?' //41//

body.text:
498.007. yeṣāṃ ceto vividhavirasāyāsaduḥkhāprakampyam yaiḥ saṃtyaktaṃ kṛpaṇahṛdayairjīvitaṃ bhogalubdhaiḥ/
498.009. te saṃtyaktvā nayanagalitāśrupravāhārdravaktrān bandhūnajñā makaranilaye mṛtyave yānti nāśam//42//
body.translated_text:
498.007. 'Those whose minds are unshaken by the manifold weariness and suffering of diverse miseries, who — wretched-hearted and greedy for enjoyment — have abandoned life itself,
498.009. they, forsaking their kinsmen whose faces are moist with streams of tears flowing from their eyes, go ignorantly to destruction at the abode of sea-creatures, surrendering themselves to death.' //42//

body.text:
498.011. tanmāmanāthāṃ pratipālanīyāṃ tvajjīvitāśaikanibandhajīvām/
498.013. saṃtyajya yātuṃ kathamudyamaste mā sā kathā mā nu vaco madīyam(?)//43//
body.translated_text:
498.011. 'Therefore, me — helpless, deserving of care, living only by the bond of hope in your life —
498.013. how can you be eager to abandon and depart? Let there be no such talk — heed my words!' //43//

body.text:
498.015. svaprāṇasaṃdehakarīmavasthāṃ praviśya naikāntasukhaṃ prasādhyam/
498.017. saṃpattayo yena vaṇigjanasya tato 'hamevaṃ suta vārayāmi//44//
body.translated_text:
498.015. 'By entering a state that endangers one's own life, prosperity is not to be secured with certainty for a merchant;
498.017. it is for this reason, O son, that I restrain you thus.' //44//

body.text:
498.019. sa tasyā hitārthaṃ madhurāṇyapi vacanakusumāni tṛṇamivāvadhūya sapragalbhatayā samavalambitavikatthāśobhaṃ kiṃcidīdṛśaṃ pratyāha--
498.021. varaṃ naiva tu jāyeran ye jātā nirdhanā janāḥ/
498.022. jātasya yadi duḥkhāni varaṃ mṛtyur na jīvitam//45//
body.translated_text:
498.019. He, casting aside her words — though sweet as flower-blossoms and spoken for his benefit — as if they were mere grass, replied with boldness adorned with a certain self-assurance, speaking thus:
498.021. 'Better indeed that those people who are born destitute should never be born at all.
498.022. If the born one must suffer, better death than life.' //45//

body.text:
498.023. āśayā gṛhamāgatya dīnadīnāstapasvinaḥ/
498.024. arthino mama pāpasya yānti niḥśvasya durmanāḥ//46//
body.translated_text:
498.023. 'Coming home with hope, the wretched and pitiable,
498.024. seeking aid from wretched me, depart sighing and downcast.' //46//

body.text:
498.025. ye śaktihīnā vibhavārjanādau te dehino duḥkhaśataṃ sahante/
498.027. lokaṃ punarduḥkhaśatopataptaṃ draṣṭaṃ na śaknomi cirāyamāṇaḥ//47//
body.translated_text:
498.025. 'Those who are powerless in the matter of acquiring wealth — those embodied ones endure a hundred sorrows.
498.027. And I cannot bear to look upon the world, afflicted by a hundred sorrows, for much longer.' //47//

body.text:
498.029. tasmādvilaṅghāmi vacastvadīyam yāsyāmi taṃ tvaṃ prajahīhi śokam/
498.031. tatraiva yāyāṃ nidhanaṃ samudre chinnaṃ mayā vā vyasanaṃ janasya//48//
body.translated_text:
498.029. 'Therefore I shall transgress your words — I shall go. Abandon your grief.
498.031. Either I shall meet my end in that very ocean, or I shall cut short the misery of the people.' //48//

body.text:
499.001. <499>atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo mātaramapramāṇīkṛtya nirgatya gṛhādvārāṇasyāṃ puryāmātmānaṃ sārthavāhamityuddhoṣayāmāsa/
499.003. asyāmeva purā puraṃdarapurīpratispardhipuryāṃ vaṇik mitro nāma babhūva yatsuranaraprakhyātakīrtidhvajaḥ/
499.005. putrastasya mahāsamudramacirādyāsyatyamuṣmindine yātum ye vaṇijaḥ kṛtopakaraṇāste santu sajjā iti//49//
body.translated_text:
499.001. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, disregarding his mother, went out from his house and in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> made a proclamation declaring himself caravan-leader:
499.003. 'In this very city — a rival to the city of <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) — there was formerly a merchant named <s>Mitra</s>, whose banner of fame was renowned among gods and men.
499.005. His son will set out for the great ocean on this very day — let those merchants who have prepared their goods be ready to depart.' //49//

body.text:
499.007. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo vividhopakaraṇasambhārasādhanānāṃ samāgṛhītapuṇyāhaprasthānabhadrāṇāmupahṛtamaṅgalavividhānāṃ vaṇijāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ kṛtaparivāraḥ prasasāra/
499.008. mātā cainaṃ gacchatīti śrutvāha--mamaikaputraka, kva yāsyasīti karuṇakaruṇākranditamātraparāyāṇā komalavimalakamaladalavilāsālasābhyāṃ pāṇikamalābhyāṃ rucirakanakaghaṭitaghaṭavikaṭapayodharavarorubhāsuramuraḥ pragāḍhamabhitāḍayati/
499.011. bāṣpasaliladhārāparamparodbhavoparudhyamānakaṇṭhī anilabalākulitagalitasajalajaladapaṭalāvalīmalinakeśapāśā satvaratvaramabhigamya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya pādayoḥ pariṣvajyaivamāha--mā māṃ putraka parityajaya yāsīti/
499.014. anartharāgagrahamūḍhabuddhayo narā hi paśyanti na kevalaṃ hitam/
499.016. satāṃ hitādhānavidhānacetasāṃ giro 'pi śṛṇvanti na bhūtavādinām//50//
body.translated_text:
499.007. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, accompanied by five hundred merchants who had gathered diverse supplies and provisions, performed the auspicious departure-rites and blessings, and offered various auspicious items, set forth.
499.008. His mother, hearing that he was leaving, cried out: 'My only son! Where will you go?' — with nothing but piteous, piteous wailing as her recourse, she struck her chest — beautiful, radiant, adorned with breasts like ornate golden jars — with her lotus-like hands, soft and pure as lotus petals.
499.011. With her throat choked by an unbroken succession of flowing tears, her tresses of hair darkened and disheveled like a mass of rain-clouds scattered and loosened by the force of the wind, she hastened swiftly and, embracing the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, spoke thus: 'Do not abandon me, my son, and go!'
499.014. 'Indeed, men whose minds are deluded by the grip of passion for what is harmful do not see what is truly beneficial;
499.016. nor do they heed the words of the truthful — those good people whose minds are intent on bestowing benefit.' //50//

body.text:
499.018. maitrakanyako 'pi dharaṇi{tala}niṃnāṃ mātaraṃ śokavaśyāṃ śirasi kupitacittaḥ pādavajreṇa hatvā/
499.021. muhurupacitaśokaḥ karmaṇā preryamāṇas tvaritamatirabhūt saṃprayātuṃ vaṇigbhiḥ//51//
body.translated_text:
499.018. <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> too, with mind enraged, struck his mother — who had fallen to the ground, overcome by grief — on the head with the thunderbolt of his foot;
499.021. then, with sorrow greatly accumulated, impelled by his <s>karma</s>, he was eager in mind to depart swiftly with the merchants. //51//

body.text:
499.023. tataḥ sā mātā samutthāyāha--putraka,
499.024. mayi gamananivṛttiṃ kartumatyudyatāyām yadupacitamapuṇyaṃ macchirastāḍanātte/
499.026. vyasanaphalamanantaṃ mā tu bhūt karmaṇo 'sya punarapi guruvākyaṃ mātigāḥ svapnato 'pi//52//
body.translated_text:
499.023. Then that mother, rising up, said: 'My son,
499.024. whatever demerit has been accumulated from your striking my head, while I was striving with utmost effort to prevent your departure —
499.026. may the fruit of this evil deed not be endless! And never again, even in a dream, transgress the words of your elders.' //52//

body.text: 499.028. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvo vividhavihārāyatanaparvatopavanagahvarasarittaḍāgārāmaramaṇīyatarānanekanagaranigamarkaṭagrāmādīnanuvicaran krameṇa samudratīraṃ saṃprāpya sajjīkṛtayānapātro bhujagapativadanavisṛtaśvasanacapalabalavilulitavipulavimalasalilamaruṇataruṇakiraṇanikararucirapadmarāgapuñjaprabhārāgarañjitormimālājalamasurasvarasamasuraparasureśvarakarodarasphuritahutavahaśikhāvalīkarālavajrapatanabhayanilīnadharaṇīdharaśikharaparāhatajaloddhatottuṅgataraṃgabhaṅgaraudraṃ samudramavatatāra/
body.translated_text: 499.028. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, wandering gradually through various monastery-grounds, mountain groves, caverns, rivers, lakes, and gardens of delightful beauty, through many cities, towns, market-villages, and hamlets, reached the ocean shore. Having made ready his vessel, he crossed the ocean — whose vast, pure waters were agitated by the restless, powerful breath issuing from the mouths of serpent-kings, whose waves were colored with the splendor of heaps of rubies radiant as the rays of the young rising sun, whose wave-garlands were tinted with passionate hues, whose waters sounded like the voice of <s>Asuras</s>, and resounded with the roar of great <s>Asura</s> and <s>Sura</s> lords, whose terrifyingly fierce and thunderbolt-like waves — raised by the churning of mountain-like sea-creatures and elephantine <s>makaras</s> — struck the cowering mountain peaks, making the flames of submarine fire flicker from their palms.

body.text:
500.001. <500>mahāanilotkṣiptataraṃgabhaṅgaiḥ samullasadbhiḥ khamivotpatantam/
500.003. saritsahasrāmburayapravāhairbhujairvilāsairiva gṛhyamāṇam//53//
body.translated_text:
500.001. 'With its towering wave-crests hurled up by the great wind, surging as if leaping into the sky,
500.003. seized as if by the playful arms of the currents of a thousand rivers pouring their waters into it —' //53//

body.text:
500.005. prakṣubdhaśīrṣoragabhīmabhogavyāvartitodvartitatoyarāśim/
500.007. tanmūrdhni ratnodgataraśmipuñjaṃ jvālākalāpocchruritormicakram//54//
body.translated_text:
500.005. 'A mass of waters whirled and churned by the terrible coils of agitated great serpents,
500.007. with clusters of rays from gems rising on their crests, and circles of waves shooting up like garlands of flames —' //54//

body.text:
500.009. ahipativadanādvimuktatīvrajvalitaviṣānaladāhabhīmaśaṅkham/
500.011. timinakhakuliśāgradāritādriṃ tadacalapādahatāmbumīnavṛndam//55//
body.translated_text:
500.009. 'Fearful as conch-shells from the fierce blazing poison-fire released from the mouths of serpent-kings,
500.011. with mountains split open by the adamantine tips of the claws of great fish, and shoals of fish struck down by the feet of those immovable ones —' //55//

body.text:
500.013. tuṅgataraṃgasamudgatatīraṃ tīranilīnakalasvanahaṃsam/
500.015. haṃsanakhakṣatadāruṇamīnaṃ mīnavivartitakampitavelam//56//
body.translated_text:
500.013. 'With shores from which high waves surge forth, with geese resting along the shores singing sweetly,
500.015. with fish cruelly wounded by the claws of the geese, and with coastlines trembling from the turning of the fish —' //56//

body.text:
500.017. ratnalatāvṛtabhāsuraśaṅkhaṃ śaṅkhasitendugabhastivivṛddham/
500.019. vṛddhabhujaṃgamahābhavaraudraṃ raudramahāmakarāhatacakram//57//
body.translated_text:
500.017. 'With radiant conch-shells entwined by creepers of gems, illuminated by the moonbeam-white rays of the conch-shells,
500.019. terrible with the great existences of aged serpents, and with its circles struck by great <s>makaras</s> —' //57//

body.text:
500.021. khagapatisavilāsapāṇivajraṃ prahatavipāṭitadṛṣṭimūlarandhram/
500.023. pramuditajaladantidantakoṭipramathitanaikavilāsakalpavṛkṣam//58//
body.translated_text:
500.021. 'With the playful thunderbolt-hands of <s>Garuḍa</s> (the king of birds), by which the eye-sockets of serpents are shattered and split open,
500.023. with the tips of the tusks of joyful cloud-elephants crushing many a playful wishing-tree —' //58//

body.text:
500.025. tadeva sa saṃlakṣya tīraparyantarekhaṃ prakaṭavikaṭārtagartodarabhramadbhramitajhaṣabhujagakulamaṇḍalaṃ naikavicitrādbhutāścaryamatiśayamambhasāmālayamatikrāmatastasya dharaṇīdharaśikharavipulātmabhāvasya makarakaripatervivartamānasya samutthitairurvīdharākāradāruṇaiḥ pramuktakalakalārāvaraudrairmahadbhiḥ salilanivahairutpīḍyamānaṃ tadyānapātraṃ maraṇabhayaviṣādabhraśyamānagātrairdīnaruditākranditamātraparāyaṇaiḥ samyānapātrakaiḥ saha sahaiva salilanidheradhaḥ praveṣṭumārabdham/
500.030. urvīdharākārataraṃgatuṅgairugrairyugāntānilacaṇḍavegaiḥ/
500.032. tadyānapātraṃ jaladherjalaughairāsphālyamānaṃ vidadāra madhye//59//
body.translated_text:
500.025. Having observed that very ocean, with its shoreline border, its circles of fish and serpent-schools whirling and spinning in the belly of its frightful, gaping, exposed abysses — a most wondrous, marvelous, extraordinary, and surpassing abode of waters — as they were crossing it, a great sea-creature, mountain-like in its vast frame, an elephant-lord of <s>makaras</s>, churned upward, and from its terrible, mountain-shaped movements, tremendous masses of water, accompanied by fearsome roaring sounds, began to overwhelm that vessel. The crew — their bodies collapsing with the despair and terror of death, with nothing but piteous weeping and wailing as their recourse — together with the vessel, began to sink beneath the waters of the ocean.
500.030. 'By the towering, mountain-like waves, fierce as the violent winds at the end of an age,
500.032. that vessel, battered by the floods of the ocean, was split apart in the middle.' //59//

body.text:
501.001. <501>daṃṣṭrākarāle jhaṣavavaktrarandhre kaścinmamārārtaravastapasvī/
501.003. kecijjalodgāraniruddhakaṇṭhā jagmur nirucchvāsagirā vyasutvam//60//
body.translated_text:
501.001. 'Some poor wretches died in the crevice-like mouths of fish with fangs like swords, screaming in agony;
501.003. some, their throats blocked by surging water, met their end without breath or voice.' //60//

body.text:
501.005. gatvāpi kecitphalakairmahadbhirambhonidhestīramavekṣamāṇāḥ/
501.007. dūrāmbusaṃtānapariśramārtāstrāsākulā nedurudīrṇanādāḥ//61//
body.translated_text:
501.005. 'Some, though they reached large planks, gazing at the shore of the ocean,
501.007. exhausted by the long stretch of water, cried out in great distress, agitated with terror.' //61//

body.text:
501.009. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvastena mahatā vyasanopanipātenāpyanāpatitabhayaviṣādadainyāyāsamanāḥ samavalambya mahaddhairyaparākramaṃ sasambhramaṃ phalakamādāya prasasāra/
501.010. tato 'sau samapavanagamanajavajanitasavilāsagatibhiḥ salilaplavairitastataḥ samākṣipyamāṇo nirāhāratayā ca parimlāyamānanayanavadanakamalaścānyairbahubhirahorātrairyathākathaṃcittasya durvagāhasalilasya mahārṇavasya dakṣiṇaṃ tīradeśamāsasāda/
501.014. tīrtvā tamambhonidhimapragādhamāsādya tīraṃ phalakaṃ mumoca/
501.016. saṃsmṛtya māturvacanaṃ sa pāṇā vyāsajya mūrdhānamidaṃ jagāda//62//
body.translated_text:
501.009. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, though struck by that great calamity, with a mind free from the falling away of fear, despair, wretchedness, and weariness, summoning his great fortitude and valor, hurriedly seized a plank and set forth.
501.010. Then he, being tossed here and there by the water-waves moving with the speed and playful grace of a windstorm, and with the lotus of his face and eyes wilting from lack of food, after many days and nights somehow reached the southern shore of that unfathomable, vast ocean.
501.014. 'Having crossed that fathomless ocean and reaching the shore, he released the plank;
501.016. remembering his mother's words, he placed his hands upon his head and spoke thus:' //62//

body.text:
501.018. śṛṇvanti ye nātmahitaṃ gurūṇāṃ vākyaṃ hitārthodayakāryabhadram/
501.020. teṣāmimāni vyasanāni puṃsāmāvāhayanti prabhavanti mūrdhni//63//
body.translated_text:
501.018. 'Those who do not heed the words of their elders — beneficial, auspicious, spoken for one's own good and well-being —
501.020. for those men, these calamities come and prevail upon their heads.' //63//

body.text:
501.022. taireva naikavyasanapradasya toyendubimbasthitabhaṅgurasya/
501.024. prāptaṃ phalaṃ janmataroḥ sudhībhirye mānayantīha giro gurūṇām//64//
body.translated_text:
501.022. 'By those very wise ones who honor the words of their elders here,
501.024. the fruit of the tree of birth — as fragile as a moon's reflection in water, a provider of manifold calamities — is attained.' //64//

body.text:
501.026. māturhitāyaiva sadodyatāyāḥ prollaṅghya vākyaṃ mama duṣkṛtasya/
501.028. puṣpam yadīdṛgbharapāpadāruṇaṃ prāntaṃ gamiṣyāmi kadā phalasya//65//
body.translated_text:
501.026. 'Having transgressed the words of my mother — who was ever striving for my benefit —
501.028. if the flower of my evil deed is so terribly burdensome, when shall I reach the end of its fruit?' //65//

body.text:
501.030. hutavahahatalekhātyantaparyantaraudraṃ gamanapatitamugraṃ vismayātyantavajram/
501.032. guruśirasi dadhānaḥ pādavajraṃ khalo 'haṃ kathamavanividāryaśvabhrarandhre na lagnaḥ//66//
body.translated_text:
501.030. 'Terrible beyond measure at its edges like streaks of blazing fire, having fallen in motion, fierce, a thunderbolt of utter astonishment —
501.032. I, the villain, bearing the thunderbolt of my foot upon my elder's head — how is it that I have not sunk into the crevice of a chasm in the earth?' //66//

body.text:
502.001. <502>ye santo hitavādināṃ sphuṭadhiyāṃ saṃpādayante giriḥ śreyaste samavāpnuvanti niyataṃ kravyādapuryām yathā/
502.003. ye tūtsṛjya mahārthasāradayitāṃ vācaṃ śrayante 'nyathā dustāre vyasanodadhau nipatintāḥ śocanti te 'ham yathā//67//
body.translated_text:
502.001. 'Those good people who fulfill the words of the clear-minded, well-speaking ones assuredly attain what is beneficial, as surely as one reaches the city of carrion-eaters.
502.003. But those who, casting aside the beloved words so rich in great meaning, follow another path — they fall into the hard-to-cross ocean of calamity and grieve, just as I do.' //67//

body.text:
502.005. tato 'sau krameṇa khadiravarasaralaniculabakulatamālatālanālikeradrumavanagahanaṃ pravaravāraṇavarāhacamaraśarabhaśambaramahiṣaviṣāṇakarṣaṇapatitamathitavividhamālulatājāladuḥsaṃcaraṃ kvacitkṣubhitakesarininādabhayacakitavanacarakulākīrṇacaraṇaṃ kathaṃcidapi śabaramanujajanacaraṇākṣuṇṇaparyantamanucaran kvacit sthitvaivamāha--
502.009. ete dāḍimapuṣpalohitamukhāḥ pronmuktakolāhalā hāsādarśitadantapaṅktivirasāḥ śākhāmṛgā nirbhayāḥ/
502.011. sarpān bhīmaviṣānalasphuradurujvālākarālasphuṭān hatvā pāṇitalaiḥ prayānti vivaśāḥ phūtkārabhītā nunaḥ//68//
body.translated_text:
502.005. Then he, gradually making his way through dense forests of <s>khadira</s>, <s>śāla</s>, <s>sarala</s>, <s>nicula</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>tamāla</s>, <s>tāla</s>, <s>nālikera</s>, and other trees — difficult to traverse due to the tangled creeper-nets of various vines crushed and trampled by the horn-rubbing of mighty elephants, boars, yaks, <s>śarabhas</s>, <s>śambaras</s>, and buffaloes — in some places with paths trodden by frightened forest-dwelling creatures alarmed by the roar of enraged lions, somehow following the trail along edges trodden by the feet of <s>Śabara</s> tribesmen, he stopped at a certain place and said:
502.009. 'These tree-monkeys, with mouths red as pomegranate blossoms, unrestrained in their uproar,
502.011. with hideous grins baring their rows of teeth — fearlessly they kill serpents blazing with terrible, fiery, flaming poison-flames, and then, overcome, they depart, surely frightened by their own hissing.' //68//

body.text:
502.013. ramye kuṅkumaśākhināmaviralacchāyākuthāśītale mūle komalanīlaśādvalavati pravyaktapuṣpotkare/
502.015. vaṃśaistālaravaiḥ sagītamadhuraiḥ pracchedasampādibhiḥ saṃgītāhitacatasaḥ pramuditā gāyantyamī kinnarāḥ//69//
body.translated_text: At the lovely, cool base of saffron trees, in the unbroken shade of thick canopies, upon soft blue-green grass with clusters of full-blooming flowers, with bamboo flutes and palm-leaf sounds, sweetly musical and rhythmic — joyful <s>Kinnaras</s> sing, their voices blended in harmony. //69//

body.text:
502.017. tato nātidūramatisṛtya mahīdharavarākāraṃ parvataṃ dadarśa/
502.018. kvacidugrataracārumaṇiprabhayā surabhīkṛtabhīmaguhāvicaram/
502.020. kvaciduddhatakinnaragītaravaṃ pratibuddhasasambhramanāgakulam//70//
body.translated_text: Then, having gone not far beyond, he beheld a mountain in the form of a great mountain-king — in some places, with the brilliance of fierce and beautiful gems perfuming its terrifying cave-passages,

body.text:
502.022. capalānilavellitapuṣpataruṃ tatumandiramūrdhni caladbhramaram/
502.024. bhramaradhvanipūrṇaguhākuharaṃ kuharasthitaraudrabhujaṃgakulam//71//
body.translated_text: in some places, with the sound of <s>Kinnara</s> songs rising up, and herds of <s>Nāgas</s> awakened in alarm; with flower-trees swayed by fitful breezes, bees hovering on the rooftops of their dwellings, cave hollows filled with the hum of bees, and fierce serpent-clans dwelling in the caverns. //71//

body.text:
502.026. pakṣivirājitaparvataśṛṅgaṃ śṛṅgaśilātalasaṃsthitasiddham/
502.028. siddhavadhūjanaramyanikuñjaṃ kuñjanisevitamattaśakuntam//72//
body.translated_text: Mountain peaks adorned with birds, <s>Siddhas</s> established on the rock-ledges of the peaks, lovely bowers where <s>Siddha</s> women dwell, intoxicated birds frequenting the groves. //72//

body.text:
502.030. mattaśikhaṇḍikalasvararamyaṃ ramyaguhāmukhanirgatasiṃha/
502.032. siṃhaninādabhayākulanāgaṃ nāgamadāmbusugandhisamīram//73//
body.translated_text: Charming with the melodious calls of intoxicated peacocks, with lions emerging from the mouths of beautiful caves, <s>Nāgas</s> agitated with fear at the lions' roars, breezes fragrant with the ichor-water of <s>Nāgas</s>. //73//

body.text:
503.001. <503>kvacidupacitavāraṇadantaśikhāśanidāritaśikharatataṃ pravirūḍhavilāsaśikhāgaruvṛkṣavanam/
503.002. kvaciduparipayodharabhārataraladhvanirañjitaśikhikulāviṣkṛtapicchakalāpavicitritacārutaṭam/
503.003. kvacidanilavikampitapuṣpataruṃ skhalitojjvalasurabhibalaṃ kusumaprabalaprativāsitasānuśikham//74//
body.translated_text: In some places, peak-slopes split by thunderbolts from the tusks of massed elephants, with forests of luxuriant aloe and agalloch trees grown upon them; in some places, beautiful slopes adorned with the display of peacock-tail plumes swaying to the undulating rhythm of the clouds above; in some places, flower-trees shaken by the wind, with fallen, brilliant, fragrant petals, the mountain-ridges and peaks perfumed by the profusion of blossoms. //74//

body.text:
503.004. tathāparaṃ dadarśa--
503.005. likhantaṃ karālair nabhaḥ śṛṅgajālaiḥ kṣipantaṃ mayūkhaistamaḥ sāgarāṇām/
503.007. vahantaṃ samabhrāmbarāmadrigurvīṃ kṣarantaṃ kvacit kāñcanāmbhaḥpravāham//75//
body.translated_text: And then he saw another mountain — scratching the sky with its web of peaks and sharp claws, dispelling the darkness of the oceans with its rays, bearing the heavy, cloud-veiled mountain-mass, and in places flowing with streams of golden water. //75//

body.text:
503.009. phalitāmalakāsanakalpataruṃ tarukhaṇḍavirājitasānuśikham/
503.011. śikharasthitadevavadhūmithunaṃ mithunairdahatāṃ vayasā madhuram//76//
body.translated_text: With fruiting <s>āmalaka</s> trees, <s>āsana</s> trees, and wish-fulfilling trees, its ridges and peaks radiant with groves, divine couples dwelling on its summit, sweet in youth as they blaze with pairs. //76//

body.text:
503.013. kvacidarkamahārathacakranipātavikhaṇḍitamayūkhakalāpakarālitanaikamahāmaṇipallavasaṃcayaṃ maulibharāvanatonnatabhāsuravajradharam/
503.015. kvacidindrakarīndravimardataraṃganayabhramitapracalatkalahaṃsakulāvalihāranabhassaridambuvidhautaśilam/
503.017. kvacidaṇḍajarājavilāsasamucchritayakṣamahābhujavajravipāṭitasāgaravāritaloddhṛtapannagabhogadharam/
503.019. kvacideva surāsurasamyugaśastravipannamahāsuravidrutaśoṇitaraṅgamahāvalayam//77//
body.translated_text: In some places, the peak-slopes split by the fall of the chariot-wheel of the great sun, fearsome with masses of great jewels bursting forth in splendid shoots, bearing brilliant <s>vajra</s>-gems heavy with diadems on high; in some places, its rocks washed by the waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>, stirred by the surge of <s>Indra</s>'s chief elephant churning the waves, with flocks of swans fluttering about; in some places, great-armed <s>Yakṣas</s> standing erect in lordly splendor like serpent-shafts, bearing serpent-hoods drawn up from the ocean-waters by <s>vajra</s>-split; in some places, with a great circle of blood-red waves from the wounded great <s>Asuras</s> fled in the battle-clash of gods and <s>Asuras</s>. //77//

body.text:
503.021. dṛṣṭvaivamāha--
503.022. ete parvataśṛṅgavandanatarucchāyāsthalaṃ saṃsṛtāḥ karṇaprāvaraṇaṃ navāruṇakaracchāyāsamānaśriyaḥ/
503.024. prekṣante madavārilolamadhuliṭprollīḍhagaṇḍasthalaṃ darpāt kesariṇo balena mahatā pronmathyamānā gajam//78//
body.translated_text: Seeing this, he said: 'These lions have reached the shade at the base of trees honored by mountain peaks, with ears as mantles, their splendor equal to the glow of fresh dawn-rays; they gaze at the elephant whose temple-region is licked by bees maddened by the flow of ichor — with pride and great strength they assail the elephant.' //78//

body.text:
503.026. ityevamasāvatikāntāradurgaṃ salilaphalāhāramātraparāyaṇaḥ paribhrannajñānatamaḥpaṭalāvaguṇṭhitamiva jagat saṃsārapaṅke tribhuvanasvāmīvodayad ramaṇakaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa/
503.028. samucchritottuṅgacalatpatākaiḥ patatpatatrisvanavāvadūkaiḥ/
503.030. suvarṇasālairmaṇihemaśṛṅgairmahīdharākāragṛhaiḥ suguptaiḥ//79//
body.translated_text: Thus he, subsisting only on water and fruit, wandering through that impassable wilderness, as though the world were enveloped in a curtain of the darkness of ignorance — like the lord of the three worlds rising from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> — beheld a city called <s>Ramaṇaka</s> (Delightful): with lofty, soaring, waving banners, with birds alighting and calling on the pinnacles, with golden halls crowned with gem-and-gold spires, and mansions like mountains, well-guarded. //79//

body.text: 503.031. nilīnapadmālikulālipadmaiḥ samunmiṣatpadmarajaḥpiśaṅgaiḥ/
body.translated_text: With lotuses in which clusters of bees nestled, dusted with yellow pollen from opening lotuses,

body.text: 504.001. <504>kalapralāpāṇḍajarāvaramyairmandānilairāvasthīkṛtaṃ sadā//80//
body.translated_text: charming with the cooing of <s>Aṇḍaja</s> cranes, always enveloped by gentle breezes. //80//

body.text:
504.003. surakarikarajadhnakalpavṛkṣairmarakataratnatṛṇaiḥ śukāṃśunīlaiḥ/
504.005. maṇikanakalatānibaddhaśākhaiḥ kvacidurubhistarubhiḥ prakāmahāri//81//
body.translated_text: In some places, with great trees like the tusks of the elephants of the gods, with emerald-gem grasses, blue-green as parrots' plumage, branches bound with garlands of gold and gems — magnificent with their broad trunks, delighting beyond measure. //81//

body.text:
504.007. vikasitanavakarṇikāragauraiḥ kanakagṛhairbahuratnaśṛṅgacitraiḥ/
504.009. svakiraṇaruciroruratnasānoracalapateḥ sakalaśriyaṃ dadhānam//82//
body.translated_text: With golden mansions bright with newly blooming petals, adorned with many gem-crested spires, bearing the complete splendor of a steadfast mountain-king with brilliant great jewels on its slopes. //82//

body.text:
504.011. kvacidamaravilāsinīkarāgraprahatamahāmurajasvanābhirāmam/
504.013. kvaciduparipayodatūryanādapramuditamattaśikhaṇḍivṛndakīrṇam//83//
body.translated_text: In some places, delightful with the sound of great <s>muraja</s> drums struck by the hands of celestial women; in some places, filled with flocks of intoxicated peacocks, delighted by the sound of celestial trumpets from the clouds above. //83//

body.text:
504.015. tatastaddarśanāt samutpannajīvitāśo 'sau ramaṇaṃ nagaramupasasarpa/
504.015. tasmānnagarādviniḥsṛtya catasro 'psaraso dravitanavakanakarasarāgāvadātamūrtayaḥ pravikasitāmbujakusumarucakarucinayanayugalotpalavilāsāḥ kvaṇadruciravividhamaṇimekhalāpabhā(prāgbhā)ramandavilāsagatayaḥ kanakakalaśākārapṛthutarapaodharabharāvanamitatanumadhyā divasakarakarasparśavibodhitāmlānakamalapalāśabhāsurādharakisalayā vividhavibhūṣaṇaśatā nirāmayadarśanāḥ śirasi viracitobhayakamalāñjalayo maitrakanyasya bodhisattvasya pādayorvinyasitaśirasaḥ prāhuh--
504.021. susvāgataṃ candrasamānanāya nārījanaprītivivardhanāya/
504.023. kṛpāmṛtāhlāditamānasāya bodhau cirābaddhaviniścyayāya//84//
body.translated_text: Then, his hope of survival revived by that sight, he approached the city of <s>Ramaṇaka</s>. From that city, four <s>Apsaras</s> came forth — their forms radiant as molten fresh gold, their paired lotus-eyes lovely as blossoming water-lily buds, walking with slow, graceful gaits tinkling with various jeweled girdles, their slender waists bent under the weight of ample breasts like golden vessels, their lip-petals brilliant as lotus-leaves awakened by the sun's rays, adorned with hundreds of various ornaments, their appearance free from blemish — with double lotus-bud <s>añjalis</s> raised upon their heads, they placed their brows at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanya</s> and said: 'Welcome to you, O moon-faced one, you who increase the delight of women, whose mind is gladdened by the nectar of compassion, whose resolve for awakening was long ago firmly fixed!' //84//

body.text:
504.025. adyaiva duḥkhāni śamaṃ gatāni adyaiva no jīvitamāttasāram/
504.027. niratyayapremaviśeṣabhadrāṇyadyaiva saukhyāni puraḥ sthitāni//85//
body.translated_text: 'Today indeed our sufferings have come to peace; today indeed our life has found its essence. Today indeed before us stand beautiful blessings of surpassing, imperishable love.' //85//

body.text:
504.029. imāni duḥkhāṅkuśakhaṇḍitāni manāṃsi naḥ śokaparikṣatāni/
504.031. bhavantamāsādya vasantakāle vanāntarāṇīva vijṛmbhitāni//86//
body.translated_text: 'These minds of ours, pierced by the goad of suffering, wounded by sorrow — upon finding you, like forest groves in the season of spring, they have blossomed forth.' //86//

body.text:
505.001. <505>yānyarjitānyanyabhavāntareṣu karmāṇi śuklāni śubhodayāni/
505.003. teṣāṃ phalaṃ vīkṣaṇameva te 'laṃ saṅgastvayā kiṃ punareva dīghyam (rgha?) //87//
body.translated_text: 'The bright deeds of auspicious result that were gathered in other lifetimes — to behold you is the fruit of those. How much more then, long companionship with you!' //87//

body.text:
505.005. adyaiva mā bandhusuhṛdviyogaśokaṃkathāḥ kasya na santyapāyāḥ/
505.007. dāsyo vayaṃ te 'psarasaścatasrah chāyā na te laṅghayituṃ samarthāḥ//88//
body.translated_text: 'Do not today speak of the grief of separation from kinsmen and friends — for whom do misfortunes not exist? We four <s>Apsaras</s> are your servants. Even your shadow we are unable to overstep.' //88//

body.text:
505.009. ratnāni vāsāṃsi samujjvalāni śayyāśrayāścārutarā vayaṃ ca/
505.011. saṃtyabhartāḥ surarājayogyā śaktirvidheneha(?) sukhaṃ bhajasva//89//
body.translated_text: 'Gems, radiant garments, beautiful couches and seats, and we ourselves — all are present, without a husband, worthy of the king of the gods. You have the power — enjoy happiness here in the manner that pleases you.' //89//

body.text:
505.013. api ca/
505.014. duḥkhe mahatyapratikāraghore ye vartamānāściramudvahanti/
505.016. te duḥkhabhāropanipātamūḍhāstatraiva śīghraṃ nidhanaṃ prayānti//90//
body.translated_text: 'Moreover: Those who, while suffering in great, irremediable, terrible affliction, endure for a long time — they, bewildered by the weight of that burden of suffering, quickly meet their end right there.' //90//

body.text:
505.018. nitye viyoge maraṇāt puraḥsthite śocanti te deśakṛte viyoge/
505.020. saṃsmṛtya rogopanipātamūḍhāḥ kāmaprahārādviṣamaṃ prapannāḥ//91//
body.translated_text: 'When separation is eternal, with death standing before them — they grieve over separation caused by distance. Bewildered by the onslaught of illness, stricken by the blows of desire, they fall into misery.' //91//

body.text:
505.022. śabdāyamānavaranūpuramekhalābhirādiśyamānabhavanaṃ pravarāpsarobhiḥ/
505.024. haimādriśṛṅgamiva tatpuramāviśantaṃ nemuḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭā bahavo 'pi tatra//92//
body.translated_text: With the tinkling of their finest anklets and girdles, directed to the mansion by the excellent <s>Apsaras</s>, as he entered that city like a golden mountain-peak — many there bowed with joined palms. //92//

body.text:
505.026. anyaiśca punah--
505.027. kiṃ dīptaraśmirvinigūḍharaśmiḥ kiṃ puṣpaketuḥ sahasāvatīrṇaḥ/
505.029. hā kiṃ vinikṣipya kharāgravajro nāthaḥ surāṇāmiti tarkito 'bhūt//93//
body.translated_text: And others wondered: 'Is this the blazing-rayed sun with his rays hidden? Has <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (the flower-bannered god of love) suddenly descended? Or has the lord of the gods descended, having cast aside his sharp-tipped <s>vajra</s>?' — thus he was speculated upon. //93//

body.text: 505.031. timiranikaralekhyāḥ śyāmalopakṣmalekhyāh(?) sphuṭitakanakahārā nyastaratnojvalāṅgāḥ/
body.translated_text: Dark-lidded, to be painted by the brush of darkness, with shimmering golden necklaces, their limbs glowing with set jewels,

body.text: 506.001. <506>vipulabhavanamālājālavātāyanasthāḥ pramuditamanaso 'nyāścikṣipuḥ srastakāñcayaḥ//94//
body.translated_text: standing at the lattice-windows of the rows of broad mansions, other women, with joyful minds and loosened girdles, gazed at him. //94//

body.text:
506.003. ratnapradīpaprahatāndhakāraṃ muktāphalapraruciroruharmyam/
506.005. calatpatākāgravibhinnameghaṃ gehaṃ viveśāpsarasāṃ hi tāsām//95//
body.translated_text: Into the mansion of those <s>Apsaras</s> — its darkness dispelled by jewel-lamps, its upper chamber bright with lustrous pearls, its clouds pierced by the tips of waving banners — he entered. //95//

body.text:
506.007. tāsāṃ vilāsairgamanaiḥ salīlairhāsaiḥ kaṭākṣairmadhuraiḥ pralāpaiḥ/
506.009. krīḍan sa kālaṃ na viveda yātaṃ sarvātmanā rāgaparītacetāḥ//96//
body.translated_text: Playing with their graceful movements, their playful laughs, their sidelong glances, their sweet words — absorbed in passion with all his being, he did not perceive time passing. //96//

body.text:
506.011. pratyahaṃ ca dakṣiṇena gamanaṃ vārayanti sma/
506.011. so 'pi yathā yathā nivāryate, tathā tathā tayā diśā gamanāyautsukyamanā babhūva/
506.013. yatrāyaṃ vāryate loko janena hitabuddhinā/
506.014. viparyastamatistatra janaḥ sa paridhāvati//97//
body.translated_text: Every day they tried to prevent him from going southward. But the more he was restrained, the more eager he became to go in that direction. 'Where this person is restrained by well-meaning people, there the person, his mind turned contrarily, runs.' //97//

body.text:
506.015. yadi kuryādayaṃ loke suhṛdāṃ vacanaṃ hitam/
506.016. paraiti svargaṃ pātāle śvabhre vā svapnato 'pi na//98//
body.translated_text: 'If this person in the world would follow the beneficial counsel of friends, he would not fall into hell, the abyss, or the netherworld, even in a dream.' //98//

body.text:
506.017. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvastāsāmapsarasāmaparijñātagamanaprayojano dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi padavīmāruhya vrajan sadāmattakaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa/
506.018. tasmādapi nagarādaṣṭāpsarasaḥ sasambhramaṃ niḥsṛtya taṃ mahāsattvaṃ praveśayāmāsuḥ/
506.019. tatrāpyaticiraṃ ratimanubhūya pratiṣiddhamānagamanakriyastenaiva dakṣiṇena pathā gacchannandanaṃ nāma nagaraṃ dadarśa/
506.020. tasmādapi ṣoḍaśāpsarobhirabhigamya satkṛtya praveśayāmāse/
506.021. tatrāpi ciraṃ krīḍāṃ sevitvā tasmādapi brahmottaraṃ nāma nagaraṃ prayayau/
506.021. tatrāpi dvātriṃśatāpsarobhiḥ prabhūtasatkāraṃ viṣayasukhaṃ bhuktvā tāḥ prāha--
506.023. icchāmi gantuṃ tadahaṃ bhavantyo mā matkṛte śokahrade śayīdhvam/
506.025. saṃpātabhadrāṇi hi kasya nāma viśleṣaduḥkhāni na santi loke//99//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanya</s>, not having understood the purpose of their prohibition from going, set out on the southern path and saw a city called <s>Sadāmatta</s> (Ever-Intoxicated). From that city too, eight <s>Apsaras</s> came forth hurriedly and brought that great being inside. There too, having enjoyed pleasures for a very long time, and being restrained from going further, he continued south and saw a city called <s>Nandana</s> (Delightful). From that city too, sixteen <s>Apsaras</s> came forth, honored him, and brought him inside. There too, having sported for a long time, he departed from it and went to a city called <s>Brahmottara</s> (Supreme <s>Brahmā</s>). There too, having enjoyed abundant sense-pleasures with elaborate honors from thirty-two <s>Apsaras</s>, he said to them: 'I wish to go. Do not, on my account, lie in a lake of grief. For whom, indeed, are the blessings of companionship without the sorrow of separation in this world?' //99//

body.text:
506.027. sthitvāpi yenaiva ciraṃ viyogaḥ śatroḥ kṛtāntādbhavitāntakāle/
506.029. tenaiva netrāśrujalārdragaṇḍān yuṣmān vihāyādya yiyāsurasmi//100//
body.translated_text: 'Even having stayed long with one, separation must come at the end from the enemy Death. So today, leaving you with tears wetting your cheeks, I wish to depart.' //100//

body.text: 506.031. vātāhatāmbhodhitaraṃgalole ye jīvaloke bahuduḥkhabhīme/
body.translated_text: 'Those who, in this world of the living — tossed like waves on a wind-struck ocean, full of great suffering and dread —'

body.text: 507.001. <507>viśleṣaduḥkhāya ratiṃ prayānti teṣāṃ paro nāsti vimūḍhacetāḥ//101//
body.translated_text: 'take delight destined for the sorrow of separation — none is more deluded in mind than they.' //101//

body.text:
507.003. athāpsarasastāḥ samastāstadgamanaviyogaśokaropitahṛdayāḥ sasambhramāḥ kamalakuvalayakunmalavilāsā nalinya iva śirasi viracitobhayakamalāñjalayaḥ prāhuh--
507.005. asmāsu te kartumaniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ kathaṃ hi bhaktipraṇayārpitāsu/
507.007. so 'nyena ekagrahaṇīyarūpaḥ śarīradānena vayo 'grahītte//102//
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Apsaras</s>, their hearts pierced by the grief of his departing, trembling, like lotus and water-lily buds, like lotuses — with double lotus-bud <s>añjalis</s> raised upon their heads, said: 'How could you wish to do what is unwished for us who are devoted to you with love and devotion? He whose form is to be grasped by no other — with the gift of your body, he has seized your youth.' //102//

body.text:
507.009. gatvā tannagaratrayam yadapi he svāminnihāpyāgataḥ saṃprāptā viṣayopabhogamadhurāḥ saṃpattayaste ciram/
507.011. gantavyaṃ na punastvayā subahunā proktena kim yāsi cet saṃsmartāsi vipatsamudrapatito vākyaṃ hi no duḥkhitaḥ//103//
body.translated_text: 'Having gone to those three cities and come back here too, O master — the sweet pleasures of sense-enjoyment have long been yours. You need not go again. What more need be said? If you do go, you will remember, fallen into an ocean of calamity, these our words spoken in sorrow.' //103//

body.text:
507.013. bodhisattvaḥ prāha--
507.014. yadabhyāsavaśānnṛrṇāmudayaḥ saṃpadasthirā/
507.015. kathaṃ teṣu nivāryerannivarteran kathaṃ nu vā//104//
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'The prosperity and fortune that arise by the power of habit in people — how could they be restrained? How indeed could they be turned away?' //104//

body.text:
507.016. niyojanīyāḥ suhṛdo 'suhṛdbhir yasmin hite karmaṇi nityakālam/
507.018. nivāraṇaṃ tatra tu ye prakurvate te śatravo mitratayā bhavanti//105//
body.translated_text: 'Friends should be directed always to that beneficial deed by which they are not led by enemies. But those who obstruct such deeds — they are enemies in the guise of friends.' //105//

body.text:
507.020. divyaṃ prāpya sukhaṃ pure ramaṇake saṃcoditaḥ karmaṇā āyāto 'smi niṣevaṇāya paraṃ saukhyaṃ sadāmattakam/
507.022. saṃprāpto 'smi tataḥ svakarmakuśaleneṣṭaṃ puraṃ nandanaṃ tasmādāgatakasya yūyamadhunā pronmūlitā bhūmayaḥ//106//
body.translated_text: 'Having obtained divine happiness in the city of <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, impelled by my deeds, I came to enjoy supreme happiness in <s>Sadāmattaka</s>. Then I reached the cherished city of <s>Nandana</s>, by the excellence of my own <s>karma</s>. And from there, having come [here], you who are my very grounds have now been uprooted.' //106//

body.text:
507.024. tasmādato me gamanaṃ bhavantyo mā vārayadhvaṃ na hi no 'styapāyaḥ/
507.026. asmādviśeṣāṇi sukhāni manye lapsye 'hamityuccalito 'hamadya//107// iti/
507.028. atha maitrakanyako bodhisattvastāsāmapsarasāṃ hitamapi vākyamahitamivāvajñayā tiraskṛtya tenaiva dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan dadarśa mahārgalapraghaṭitaprakaṭapuṭacaturdvāradāruṇaṃ sureśvareṇāpyabhedyottuṅgāyasaviśālaprākārapariveṣṭitamantarbhramaccakramaṇḍalālokapramuktadamadamāśabdagambhīrabhairavamāyasaṃ nagaram/
507.031. tasya ca dvāradeśamupacakrāma/
body.translated_text:
