'Therefore, do not restrain my departure from here, O ladies, for there is no downfall for us. I think I shall obtain pleasures even more excellent than these — so I am setting forth today.' //107//
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, dismissing with contempt the words of those <s>Apsarases</s> — beneficial though they were — as if they were harmful, proceeding by that very southern path, beheld an iron city — terrifying with its four doors whose massive bolts were thrown wide open, surrounded by lofty, broad iron ramparts impenetrable even by the lord of the gods, with a revolving wheel-circle (<s>cakramaṇḍala</s>) spinning within, emitting deep and dreadful sounds of 'dama dama.' And he approached the area of its gate.

body.text:
508.001. <508>samprāptamātrasya tu tatkṣaṇena dvāraṃ ca pusphoṭa kapāṭabhāram/
508.003. vajrāgradhāroparibhinnasānorvindhyācalasyeva nitambakukṣiḥ//108//
body.translated_text: No sooner had he arrived than the gate burst open its heavy door-panels, like the flank and belly of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain whose peak has been split by the cutting edge of a <s>vajra</s>. //108//

body.text:
508.005. tato maitrakanyako bodhisattvo 'tra viveśa/
508.006. praviṣṭamātrasya tu tatkṣaṇena dvāraṃ parikṣiptakapāṭayantram/
508.008. tatkarmavāyuprabhavairmahadbhiḥ kṣaṇādbhujāgrairiva saṃjaghāṭa//109//
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> entered there. No sooner had he entered than the gate, with its door-panel mechanisms thrown shut, instantly slammed together as if by great arms born from the wind of that [accumulated] <s>karma</s>. //109//

body.text:
508.010. aśrauṣīcca pragāḍhavedanāviklavahṛdayapuruṣasyāntaḥprākārāntaratiraskṛtaparamabhīṣaṇanirnādaṃ sakalajanottrāsanamuccarantam/
508.011. śrutvā ca dvāradeśaṃ tvaritamatirlalaṅgha/
508.012. praviṣṭamātrasya tato dvitīyamāsphālitaṃ dvāramivāparuddham/
508.014. paryantakālānilavegaviddhaṃ dvāraṃ surāṇāmiva vajrakalpam//110//
body.translated_text: And he heard, emanating from within the inner rampart, the supremely horrifying cry of a man whose heart was distraught with excruciating pain — a cry that would terrify all people. Having heard it, he swiftly leaped toward the area of the gate. No sooner had he entered than a second gate was slammed shut as if barred,

body.text:
508.016. tato maitrakanyako bodhisattvaḥ praviveśa/
508.017. praviṣṭamātrasya punastṛtīyaṃ dvāraṃ parikṣiptakapāṭayantram/
508.019. kṣaṇādabhūttannagaraṃ ca sarvaṃ bhrāntaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ sa dadarśa bhītaḥ//111//
body.translated_text: struck by the force of the wind at the end of an eon — a gate as hard as the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) of the gods. //110// Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> entered further. No sooner had he entered than a third gate, with its door-panel mechanisms thrown shut, [was sealed]. In an instant, all of that city appeared — and he, frightened, saw it all in disarray. //111//

body.text:
508.021. tato maitrakanyako bodhisattvaḥ paśyati sma tamatidāruṇākārapramāṇaṃ krūrājvalanamālāliṅgitamudāreṇa paṭupavanavikīryamāṇadhūmapaṭalāndhakāradurdinena sphuratkphuliṅgāvalikarāladarśanenāyasena mahatā bhramatā cakreṇa dārviva pravidāryamāṇamūrdhānaṃ svaśiraḥpravigalitaśoṇitavasārasāhāramātravidhṛtaprāṇaśeṣam/
508.024. samīpaṃ copagamyainaṃ paryapṛcchat--
508.025. kiṃ nāgo 'si suro 'si kinnaravaro yakṣo 'si kiṃ mānuṣaḥ kiṃ vidyādharasainikaḥ kimasi vā daityaḥ piśāco 'si vā/
508.027. kiṃ vākāri bhavāntareṣu bhavatā karmātiraudraṃ svayam yāsyāmi vyasanaṃ duruttaramidaṃ bhujyaṃ phalaṃ krandayat//112//
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> saw [a man] of exceedingly terrible form and proportion, embraced by garlands of cruel, blazing flames, enveloped in the gloom of a dark, foul day with sheets of smoke scattered by a fierce, sharp wind, frightful to behold with its flickering rows of sparks — with a great iron wheel revolving [on his head], his skull being split open as though it were wood, his life sustained only by the nourishment of blood, fat, and fluid streaming from his own head. And having approached him, he asked:
'Are you a <s>Nāga</s>? A god? A <s>Kinnara</s> chief? A <s>Yakṣa</s>? Are you human? Are you a <s>Vidyādhara</s> soldier? Or are you a <s>Daitya</s>? Or a <s>Piśāca</s>? Or what exceedingly cruel <s>karma</s> was performed by you yourself in past lives, that you endure this unbearable calamity — this fruit that makes one weep?' //112//

body.text:
508.029. puruṣaḥ prāha--
508.030. nāhaṃ nāgo naiva yakṣo na devo daityo nāhaṃ nāpi gandharvarājaḥ/
body.translated_text:
The man replied:
'I am not a <s>Nāga</s>, nor a <s>Yakṣa</s>, nor a god; I am not a <s>Daitya</s>, nor indeed the king of <s>Gandharvas</s>.'

body.text: 509.001. <509>rakṣo nāhaṃ nāpi vidyādharo 'pi jātistulyā saṃpratīhi tvayā naḥ//113//
body.translated_text: 'I am not a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>Vidyādhara</s> either. Know now that our birth is the same as yours.' //113//

body.text:
509.003. bodhisattvaḥ prāha--
509.004. kiṃ karma bhramatā tvayā kumatinā saṃsāradurge kṛtam yenedaṃ jvalitānalaṃ śirasi cakraṃ bhramatyāyasam/
509.006. puruṣaḥ prāha--
509.007. nānāduṣkarakārikā bhagavatī saṃsārasaṃdarśikā tatra śreyaḥsukhopapādanaparā matsnehabaddhāśayā//114//
body.translated_text:
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:
'What deed was done by you, wandering with wicked mind in the perilous [realm of] <s>saṃsāra</s>, that this blazing, fiery iron wheel revolves on your head?'
The man replied:
'That blessed [mother] who shows the way of <s>saṃsāra</s> through various hardships, who is devoted to providing well-being and happiness, whose heart is bound by affection for me —' //114//

body.text:
509.009. yāṃ loke pravadanti sādhumatayaḥ kṣetraṃ paraṃ prāṇināṃ daivāveśavaśādakāryagurukastasyā jananyā mahat/
509.011. sādho prāskhalayaṃ śiraḥpraharaṇaṃ pādena pāpāśayas tenedaṃ jvalitānalaṃ śirasi me cakraṃ bhramatyāyasam//115//
body.translated_text: 'She whom the wise in this world call the supreme field for living beings — against that mother, a great [offense]: by the irresistible force of fate, with heavy sinful deeds, O good one, I stumbled and struck her head with my foot, with evil intent. Because of that, this blazing, fiery iron wheel revolves upon my head.' //115//

body.text:
509.013. atha bodhisattvastasya puruṣasya pravacanapratodena saṃcoditahṛdayastāṃ parajugupsāmātmanyanupaśyannāha--
509.015. anyaṃ jugupsāmyahamalpabuddhirātmānamevādya nininda ajñaḥ/
509.017. yeṣu svayaṃ doṣaguṇeṣu magnas taireva lokaṃ kathamaṅkayāmi//116//
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his heart stirred by the goad of that man's words, seeing in himself that very same cause for self-reproach, said:
'I, of little wisdom, reproach another, while I myself, ignorant, should condemn only myself today. In those very faults and virtues in which I myself am sunk — how can I brand the world with them?' //116//

body.text:
509.019. mayāpi yanmātari dakṣiṇīyaih (ṇāyām?) kṛto 'parādhaḥ puruṣādhamena/
509.021. tasyaiva pāpasya phalāni bhoktumullaṅghya toyāvalimāgato 'smi//117//
body.translated_text: 'I too, the lowest of men, committed an offense against my mother, who is worthy of reverence. To experience the fruits of that very sin, I have come, having crossed the expanse of waters.' //117//

body.text:
509.023. atha tasya vacanānantarameva prabhinnanavakuvalayadalanirmalānnabhastalāt sajalajaladaninādagambhīradhīro dhvaniruccacāra--
509.025. kiṃ na paśyati karmāṇi balavanti śarīriṇām/
509.026. lokālokāntarasthāyī pāśeneva vikṛṣyate//118//
body.translated_text:
Then, immediately after his words, from the sky — clear as the petals of a freshly split blue water-lily — there arose a voice, deep and solemn as the rumbling of a rain-laden cloud:
'Does one not see that the <s>karmas</s> of embodied beings are powerful? One who stands between the world of light and the world of darkness is dragged as if by a noose.' //118//

body.text:
509.027. ye baddhā viṣayeṇa duḥkhanigaḍenāyāsakarmotkaṭe ye tyaktvā guruvākyamandhamatayaḥ pāpāśrayaṃ kurvate/
509.029. muktāḥ karmabhireva duḥkhanigaḍapracchedaśūraiḥ śubhair mānuṣyam yadavāpya mūḍhamatayo dūre sthitā jarmiṇah (janminah?) //119//
body.translated_text: 'Those who are bound by the fetter of suffering in the shackles of sense-objects, in the painful <s>karma</s>-factory — those who, abandoning the words of their elders, with blind minds take refuge in sin — are freed by those very <s>karmas</s> that are auspicious, valiant in severing the fetters of suffering. Having obtained human birth, those of deluded minds — the embodied ones — stand far [from liberation].' //119//

body.text:
509.031. atha tasya vacanānantarameva karmānilāvegotkṣiptamiva taccakraṃ ciṭiciṭāyamānadahanakaṇacayodgāraraudraṃ tasya mūrdhnaḥ samabhyudgamya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya śiraḥ pravidārayad bhramitumārabdham/
509.034. kṣaṇātsa reje rudhirapravāhairmūrdhnā cyutaiḥ snātasamastamūrtiḥ/
body.translated_text: Then, immediately after those words, that wheel — as if flung upward by the force of the wind of <s>karma</s> — terrifying with its discharge of showers of crackling, burning sparks, having risen up from that man's head, began to revolve upon the head of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, tearing it open. In an instant, he shone — his entire body bathed in streams of blood flowing from his head,

body.text: 510.001. <510>prabhinnacakrāgravibhinnamūrdhnā airāvaṇasyeva tanuḥ patantī//120//
body.translated_text: his skull split by the edge of the revolving wheel — like the body of [the elephant] <s>Airāvaṇa</s> falling, its head cloven. //120//

body.text:
510.003. tataḥ sa puruṣo hā heti mūrdhnā pravidāhajena tīvreṇa duḥkhena samākramyamāṇaśarīrakaṃ maitrakanyakaṃ bodhisattvamāha--
510.005. divyāṅganāgītamanoharāṇi cittapramododayasādhanāni/
510.007. saṃtyajya karmāda parāṇi tāni prāptastvidaṃ sthānamanantaduḥkham//121//
body.translated_text:
Then that man said 'Alas!' to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, whose body was being assailed by the intense pain from the burning of his skull:
'Having abandoned those other [pleasures of] <s>karma</s> — the enchanting songs of divine women, which produce the arising of delight in the mind — you have arrived at this place of endless suffering.' //121//

body.text:
510.009. devālayaṃ divyasukhopabhogaṃ ko nāma saṃprāpya śubhairatulyaiḥ/
510.011. nityaṃ jvaladvahniśikhākareṇa saṃprārthayedbhīmamapāyagartam//122//
body.translated_text: 'Having reached, through unequaled merits, the abode of the gods with divine, happy enjoyments — who in the world would then desire this terrible pit of perdition, with its ever-blazing fiery flames?' //122//

body.text:
510.013. bodhisattvaḥ prāha--
510.014. sattālikolāhalasaṃkulāni vanāni puṣpojjvalamastakāni/
510.016. saṃtyajya nāgā vyasanaṃ sahante yayā tayecchālatayā gato 'ham//123//
body.translated_text:
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied:
'Abandoning forests teeming with the tumult of flocks of <s>sārikā</s> birds, their crowns brilliant with blossoms, elephants endure calamity — by that very force of desire's impulse have I come.' //123//

body.text:
510.018. rājyāni vistīrṇadhanojjvalāni vihāya nārīmukhapaṅkajāni/
510.020. yuddhe mriyante bahavo narendrā yayā tayecchālatayā gato 'ham//124//
body.translated_text: 'Abandoning kingdoms blazing with vast wealth, [forsaking] the lotus-faces of women, many kings die in battle — by that very force of desire's impulse have I come.' //124//

body.text:
510.022. samutpatattuṅgataraṃgarodrau bhramajjalāvartavimuktanāde/
510.024. mahodadhau yānti narāḥ praṇāśam yayā tayecchālatayā gato 'ham//125//
body.translated_text: 'In the great ocean, with its towering waves raging, roaring with the sound of whirling water-eddies, men go to destruction — by that very force of desire's impulse have I come.' //125//

body.text:
510.026. niratyayātyantikasaukhyasādhanaṃ narāmaraśrīsukhasiddhimārgam/
510.028. munīśvarāṇāṃ vratamutsṛjanti yayā tayecchālatayā gato 'ham//126//
body.translated_text: 'The vow of the great sages — the means of attaining imperishable, ultimate, supreme happiness, the path to the glory, joy, and perfection of men and gods — [even that] they abandon: by that very force of desire's impulse have I come.' //126//

body.text:
510.030. teṣāṃ munīnāṃ vigatavyathānāṃ deyaṃ kathaṃ pādarajena mūrdhni/
510.032. yairlaṅghitāstīvraviṣapracaṇḍā āśāprapātā bahuduḥkhabhīmāḥ//127//
body.translated_text: 'How can the dust of the feet of those sages, free from all affliction, be placed upon one's head — those who have surmounted the precipices of desire, fierce with terrible poison, full of the terror of much suffering?' //127//

body.text:
511.001. <511>kiṃ tadbhavedduḥkhamatīva tīvraṃ kā vā vipattirbahuduḥkhayoniḥ/
511.003. tṛṣṇāviṣāgnikṣatacittavṛtteryā dūrataḥ saṃparivartinī syāt//128//
body.translated_text: 'What suffering could be so exceedingly intense, or what misfortune such a source of much suffering, that it could remain far from one whose mental activity has been wounded by the fire-poison of craving?' //128//

body.text:
511.005. api ca he sādho,
511.006. karmaṇā parikṛṣṭo 'smi vartamāno 'pi dūrataḥ/
511.007. karṣati prāṇinastatra phalam yatra prayacchati//129//
body.translated_text: 'Moreover, O good one, I have been dragged by <s>karma</s>, though standing at a distance. <s>Karma</s> drags living beings to the very place where it bestows its fruit.' //129//

body.text:
511.008. api ca--
511.009. kati varṣasahasrāṇi kati varṣaśatāni ca/
511.010. pradīptamāyasaṃ cakraṃ mama mūrdhni bhramiṣyati//130//
body.translated_text: 'Moreover: For how many thousands of years and how many hundreds of years will this blazing iron wheel revolve upon my head?' //130//

body.text:
511.011. puruṣaḥ prāha--
511.012. ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca/
511.013. pradīptamāyasaṃ cakraṃ tava mūrdhni bhramiṣyati//131//
body.translated_text:
The man replied:
'For sixty thousand years and six thousand years, the blazing iron wheel will revolve upon your head.' //131//

body.text:
511.014. bodhisattvaḥ prāha--
511.015. etadbhāsuravahnipiṅgalaśikhājvālākalāpojjvalaṃ ko 'nyo 'vabhramitaṃ prayāsyati samaṃ chittvā paraścaiṣyati/
511.017. puruṣaḥ prāha--
511.018. yo mātaryapakārakartumanasaḥ kṛtvā samāyāsyati tasyedaṃ śirasi bhramiṣyati punarmūrdhnā tava pracyutam//132//
body.translated_text:
The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said:
'This [wheel], blazing with clusters of flames, glowing bright yellow with terrible fire — who else will endure its unceasing revolutions, having cut [it free] and going beyond?'
The man replied:
'He who, having done wrong to his mother with an evil mind, shall come [here] — upon his head this [wheel] will revolve again, having departed from your head.' //132//

body.text:
511.020. atha bodhisattvastena mūrdhnā pravidāhajena tīvreṇa duḥkhena samākulahṛdayo 'pi sattveṣvananteṣu samutpāditatīvrakāruṇyāśayastaṃ puruṣamābabhāṣe--
511.022. kṣapitasakalarāgakleśajālāndhakārā gaganatalanilīnā yogino ye namasyāḥ/
511.024. sphuritakaṭakahārāḥ prajvalanmaulayo ye punaramarasamūhāste 'pi śeṇvantu santaḥ//133//
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, though his heart was troubled by the intense pain from the burning of his skull, having generated in himself a profound disposition of compassion toward infinite beings, addressed that man:
'Those <s>yogins</s> who have destroyed the entire web of darkness of passion and affliction, who are hidden in the firmament of the sky, who are worthy of homage — those whose flashing girdles and necklaces blaze, whose diadems shine forth — and the hosts of the immortals also — may those good ones listen!' //133//

body.text:
511.026. kṛtvā duścaritaṃ svamātari jagatkṛtsnam yadi prodvahedetatprajvalitāgnirāgakapilaṃ cakraṃ bṛhanmūrdhani/
511.028. kalpaṃ kalpasamairahobhirayutān voḍhuṃ cirāyotsahe sattvārthaṃ pratipadyamānamasya hi me cittaṃ na saṃkhidyate//134//
body.translated_text: 'Having committed misconduct toward my own mother, if the entire world should be lifted up [by my suffering] — this wheel, blazing with fire, tawny with the glow of passion, great upon my head — for an eon, with days equal to eons, ten thousand [of them], I am ready to bear it for a long time. For the sake of all beings, my mind does not become crushed in undertaking this.' //134//

body.text:
511.030. atha tasya sarvasattvapriyasya maitrakanyakasya bodhisattvasya vacanānantarameva mūrdhnā samutpāṭyotkṣiptamiva taccakraṃ saptatālocchrayāccakraṃ nabhastalaṃ samutpatyāvatasthe/
511.032. reje taccapalānilāhatacalajjvālākalāpojjvalaṃ cakraṃ khe parivartamānamasakṛtpronmuktabhīmasvanam/
511.034. udyadbimbamivāruṇasya sakalapronmuktaraśmyutkaraṃ ratnādyaiḥ pravilambamānamamalairvaiḍūryabhittyāśrayaiḥ//135//
body.translated_text: Then, immediately after the words of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, the friend of all beings, that wheel — as if torn from his head and flung upward — soared to the height of seven palm trees into the sky and remained there. That wheel, blazing with clusters of flames flickering in the unsteady wind, revolving in the sky, repeatedly releasing terrifying sounds, shone like the rising orb of the sun with all its rays unleashed, suspended with pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-gem panels adorned with jewels and the like. //135//

body.text:
512.001. <512>tataḥ sravannirjharavāricāriṇaḥ samīraṇollāsitapuṣpaśākhinaḥ/
512.003. nabho vicumbyāyataśṛṅgabāhavaścakampire bhūmibhṛto hatā iva//136//
body.translated_text: Then the mountains — with their streaming waterfall-waters, their blossom-laden branches swayed by the breeze, their long peak-arms kissing the sky — trembled as if struck. //136//

body.text:
512.005. bhujaṃgavikṣobhasamudgatormayaḥ payodharadhvānagabhīranādinaḥ/
512.007. jalālayā ratnaśikhānivāsinastadātivelāsalilairlalaṅghire//137//
body.translated_text: The oceans — their waves surging from the agitation of the serpents [below], deep-sounding as the rumble of thunderclouds — their jewel-crowned crest-dwellers overflowed with waters beyond their shores at that time. //137//

body.text:
512.009. pramuktaniḥśeṣamayūkhabhāsuraṃ rarāja khe maṇḍalamaṃśumālinaḥ/
512.011. ravermayūkhāṅkuradanturāntarāddiśaḥ samantāddadṛśuḥ sphuṭaśriyaḥ//138//
body.translated_text: The orb of the sun shone in the sky, radiant with all its released rays. Through the gaps between the sun's ray-sprouts, the directions on all sides appeared in manifest splendor. //138//

body.text:
512.013. sphurattaḍiddāmavirājitorasaḥ surendracāpapratibaddhakaṅkaṇāḥ/
512.015. payomucaḥ kiṃcidavāsrutāmbhaso vitānavadvyomani te virejire//139//
body.translated_text: The rain-clouds — their chests adorned with garlands of flashing lightning, wearing the rainbow of <s>Indra</s> as their bracelets, shedding just a little water — shone in the sky like a canopy. //139//

body.text:
512.017. srajo vicitrā vinipeturambarāt vituṣṭuvurhṛṣṭatarā divaukasaḥ/
512.019. cirapragāḍhavyasanā hatārtayaḥ kṣaṇādabhūvan bahavo nirāmayāḥ//140//
body.translated_text: Wondrous garlands fell from the sky; the overjoyed gods uttered praises. Those who had long been in deep calamity, their afflictions destroyed — in an instant, many became free from suffering. //140//

body.text:
512.021. jvalati viṣamacakre prāntadīrṇordhvakāyo galitarudhiradhārāsiktasarvāṅgakāyaḥ/
512.023. bhagavati guṇarāśau saṃprasādya svacittaṃ svagṛhamiva sa sādhurdyāmayāttatkṣaṇena//141//
body.translated_text:
Burning on the crooked wheel, his body torn apart at the edges and raised aloft,
his entire body drenched by streams of flowing blood —
having composed his mind in faith toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), that treasury of virtues,
that virtuous one at that very instant went to heaven as if to his own home. // 141 //

body.text:
512.025. dānodakamahattīrthe śīlaśaucasunirmale/
512.026. kṣamāsurabhiśītācche vīryāgādhapravāhake//142//
body.translated_text:
In the great <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) of the water of generosity (<s>dāna</s>), beautifully pure with the purity of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>),
fragrant and cool with patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), with a current deep and unfathomable through vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) — // 142 //

body.text:
512.027. dhyānastimitagambhīre prajñāpadmaprabodhake/
512.028. tasmin bodhimahātīrthe sthitvā bodhipurotsukaḥ//143//
body.translated_text:
still and profound with meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), awakening the lotuses of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) —
having stood in that great <s>tīrtha</s> of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), eager for enlightenment — // 143 //

body.text:
512.029. prakṣālayeccheṣapāpaṃ tuṣite 'sau yayau mudā/
512.030. tatrastho 'pyaciraṃ reme dṛṣṭvā lokaṃ kṛpānvitaḥ//144//
body.translated_text:
he washed away his remaining sins; he went joyfully to <s>Tuṣita</s> [heaven].
Even while dwelling there, he did not delight for long; seeing the world, filled with compassion — // 144 //

body.text: 512.031. tatkimidamupanītam? evaṃ hi mātaryapakāriṇaḥ prāṇinah ihaiva vyasanaprapātapātālāvalambino bhavantīti satatasamupajāyamānapremaprasādabahumānasānasaiḥ satpuruṣairmātaraḥ śuśrūṣaṇīyā iti//
body.translated_text: What has been conveyed by this? Thus indeed, beings who wrong their mothers become, in this very life, those who cling to the precipice of the abyss of calamity. Therefore, mothers should be served with devoted care by virtuous people, with constantly arising love, faith, reverence, and respect.

body.text: 512.033. iti śrīdivyāvadāne maitrakanyakāvadānaṃ samāptam//
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Divyāvadāna</s>, the <s>Maitrakanyakāvadāna</s> is concluded.

body.text: == End of the DivyAvadAna ==
body.translated_text: == End of the <s>Divyāvadāna</s> ==
